m.2.1.3.1: The sages said: O Sūta, Sūta, greatly fortunate one, disciple of Vyāsa, salutations to you. Dear one, this wondrous story has indeed been narrated to us out of your kindness.
m.2.1.3.2: Dear one, when the sage had gone, what did Hari do after that? And where did Nārada go? You should explain that to me.
m.2.1.3.3: Vyāsa said: Having heard their words thus, Sūta, the wise one, foremost of Purāṇa-narrators, remembered Śiva, the maker of manifold creations, and replied.
m.2.1.3.4: Sūta said: When that sage Nārada had gone off as he pleased, Viṣṇu, expert in illusion, quickly created an illusion by Śiva's will.
m.2.1.3.5: In the middle of the sage's path he fashioned a great city, a hundred yojanas in extent, wondrous and most charming,
m.2.1.3.6: more delightful than his own world, resplendent with various things, rich in the pleasures of men and women, and teeming with the four classes — an excellent city.
m.2.1.3.7: There a king named Śīlanidhi, endowed with sovereignty, was engaged in arranging his daughter's svayaṃvara, accompanied by a great festival.
m.2.1.3.8: The city was filled with princes who had come from the four directions, in various garb, splendid, and eager to win that maiden.
m.2.1.3.9: Seeing such a city, Nārada then fell into delusion; full of curiosity and inflamed by love, he went to the door of that king.
m.2.1.3.10: Seeing that best of sages arrive, King Śīlanidhi seated him on an excellent jewelled throne and worshipped him.
m.2.1.3.11: Then the king brought his excellent daughter, Śrīmatī by name, and made her fall at Nārada's feet.
m.2.1.3.12: Looking at that maiden, the sage Nārada, astonished, said: O king, who is this greatly fortunate maiden, like a daughter of the gods?
m.2.1.3.13: Hearing his words, the king, with joined palms, said: O sage, this is my daughter, named Śrīmatī.
m.2.1.3.14: She has reached the time for being given in marriage and is seeking an auspicious husband; she has come to her svayaṃvara, marked with all auspicious signs.
m.2.1.3.15: O sage, kindly tell her fortune, her whole horoscope. What kind of husband will this daughter of mine obtain? Tell me that.
m.2.1.3.16: Thus addressed, Nārada, tiger among sages, desiring her and overcome by lust, spoke to the king and said these words:
m.2.1.3.17: O protector of the earth, this daughter of yours is marked with all auspicious signs, greatly fortunate, blessed, an abode of virtues like Lakṣmī.
m.2.1.3.18: Her husband will certainly be the lord of all, unconquered, heroic, equal to Girīśa, all-pervading, conqueror of Kāma, the best of gods.
m.2.1.3.19: Having said this and taken leave of the king, the sage, who roams at will, departed. He became helpless before desire, deluded by Śiva's māyā.
m.2.1.3.20: The sage pondered in his mind: How may I obtain the maiden? How would she choose me alone among the kings at the svayaṃvara?
m.2.1.3.21: Beauty is always dear to all women. Just on seeing that, she will be pleased and under my control; there is no doubt about this.
m.2.1.3.22: Having resolved thus, Nārada, best of sages, tormented by love, quickly went to Viṣṇu's world to obtain Viṣṇu's form.
m.2.1.3.23: Bowing to Hṛṣīkeśa, he spoke these words: In private I shall tell you my whole story.
m.2.1.3.24: When the lord of Śrī, the doer of what Śiva wills, had said, so be it, and it was so, and had said, speak, the sage addressed Keśava.
m.2.1.3.25: Nārada said: Your devotee, King Śīlanidhi, is devoted to dharma. His daughter is large-eyed Śrīmatī, of excellent complexion.
m.2.1.3.26: Renowned as the enchantress of the world, exceedingly beautiful even in the three worlds — O Viṣṇu, I wish to marry her today, without delay.
m.2.1.3.27: That king has held a svayaṃvara out of his wish for his daughter; princes have come by the thousands from the four directions.
m.2.1.3.28: If you give me your form, then I would surely win her. Without your form she will not place the victory garland on my neck.
m.2.1.3.29: Give me your own form, O Lord; I am your dear servant — so that Śrīmatī, the king's daughter, will indeed choose me.
m.2.1.3.30: Sūta said: Hearing the sage's words thus, Madhusūdana laughed, and, understanding Śaṅkara's sovereign power at work, the compassionate one replied.
m.2.1.3.31: Viṣṇu said: Go to the place you desire, O sage. I shall do what is good for you, as the best of physicians does for a sick man, since you are very dear to me.
m.2.1.3.32: Having said this, Viṣṇu gave that sage the face of a hari (monkey), and, granting him his own form for the rest, he vanished.
m.2.1.3.33: Thus addressed, the sage was delighted; having obtained, as he thought, the form of Hari, he considered himself fulfilled, and he did not understand that contrivance.
m.2.1.3.34: Then Nārada, best of sages, quickly went there, where the king had held the svayaṃvara, crowded with princes.
m.2.1.3.35: O chief brahmins, the divine svayaṃvara hall, surrounded by princes, shone exceedingly, like a second assembly-hall of Śakra.
m.2.1.3.36: Nārada sat down in that royal assembly; staying there, he thought thus with a delighted mind:
m.2.1.3.37: She will surely choose me, bearing Viṣṇu's form, and no other. The best of sages did not know the ugliness of his face.
m.2.1.3.38: All the people there saw the sage in his former form; O brahmins, the princes and others did not perceive that difference.
m.2.1.3.39: Two attendants (gaṇas) of Rudra had come there to guard her, disguised in the form of brahmins; they alone knew that difference.
m.2.1.3.40: Thinking the sage a fool, those two gaṇas went near him and mocked him, talking with each other.
m.2.1.3.41: Look at Nārada's form: it is most excellent, like Viṣṇu's, but his face is like a monkey's, hideous and frightening.
m.2.1.3.42: Deluded by Kāma, this man desires the king's daughter in vain. Having spoken these deceitful words, the two mocked him.
m.2.1.3.43: But the sage, overwhelmed by Kāma, did not hear those words for what they truly were; deluded and longing to win her, he kept gazing at that Śrīmatī.
m.2.1.3.44: Meanwhile that king's daughter, of lovely complexion, came there from the inner apartments, surrounded by women.
m.2.1.3.45: Taking a lovely golden garland, she who bore auspicious marks shone there at the svayaṃvara, standing in the midst of the assembly like Ramā (Lakṣmī).
m.2.1.3.46: Holding the garland, that virtuous princess wandered through the whole assembly, searching there for a bridegroom dear to her own heart.
m.2.1.3.47: Seeing the sage with a monkey's face and Viṣṇu's body, she became angry; then, turning her gaze away, she moved on with a pleased heart.
m.2.1.3.48: Not seeing there her own bridegroom, the one her heart desired, she became anxious; standing within the assembly, she placed the garland on no one.
m.2.1.3.49: Meanwhile Viṣṇu came there in the form of a king; he was not seen by any others—only she saw him.
m.2.1.3.50: Then, seeing him, the fair lady, her lotus face beaming with joy, placed that garland around his neck.
m.2.1.3.51: Then Lord Viṣṇu, bearing a king's form, took her and at once vanished; he went, it is said, to his own abode.
m.2.1.3.52: All the princes lost hope regarding Śrīmatī, while the sage, tormented by love, became exceedingly distraught.
m.2.1.3.53: Then at once the two attendants of Rudra, disguised as brahmins and skilled in knowledge, spoke to Nārada, who was overwhelmed by Kāma.
m.2.1.3.54: The two attendants said: O sage Nārada, you are deluded by Kāma in vain, longing for her. Look at your own face — contemptible, like a monkey's.
m.2.1.3.55: Sūta said: Hearing these words of the two, Nārada was astonished; deluded by Śiva's māyā, he looked at his face in a mirror.
m.2.1.3.56: Seeing his own face like a monkey's, he quickly grew angry, and the deluded sage there cursed those two attendants.
m.2.1.3.57: You two have mocked me, a brahmin. Therefore become rākṣasas, born of a brahmin's seed, of that very form.
m.2.1.3.58: Hearing their curse thus, the two attendants of Hara, foremost among the wise, said nothing at all, understanding that the sage was deluded.
m.2.1.3.59: The two in brahmin guise went to their own abode, unperturbed, and sang Śiva's praise, ever regarding everything as Śiva's will.
m.2.1.3.iti: Thus ends the third adhyāya, named Nārada's delusion, in the account of creation, in the first khaṇḍa of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.1.4.1: The sages said: O Sūta, O Sūta, most wise one, a wondrous story has indeed been told. Blessed is Śambhu's māyā; the moving and unmoving world is subject to it.
m.2.1.4.2: When the two gaṇas of Śambhu, the all-pervading Lord, had gone away of their own will, what did the angry sage Nārada, overwhelmed by love, do?
m.2.1.4.3: Sūta said: The deluded sage, having given the two a fitting curse, then, by the will of Giriśa, looked at his face, his own form, in the water.
m.2.1.4.4: By Śiva's will he was not awakened to the truth; remembering the trick played by Hari, and becoming unbearably angry, he went to Viṣṇu's world.
m.2.1.4.5: Angry like a blazing fire, his wisdom lost by Śiva's will, he spoke words full of abuse and sarcasm.
m.2.1.4.6: Nārada said: O Hari, you are very wicked, a deceiver, the deluder of the world; you cannot bear another's success, you trickster of impure heart.
m.2.1.4.7: Long ago, taking the form of Mohinī, you practised deceit: you made the asuras drink liquor (vāruṇī), not nectar.
m.2.1.4.8: Had Rudra, the Great Lord, not drunk the poison out of compassion, all your māyā would have been destroyed, O Hari, you who delight in trickery.
m.2.1.4.9: A deceitful course is especially dear to you, O Viṣṇu. You are not of good nature, yet you were made independent by the Lord.
m.2.1.4.10: What Śiva, the Supreme Self, did was not at all proper; relying on the strength of his power, you act independently.
m.2.1.4.11: Having fully understood your conduct, he felt remorse; he, who established the authority of the Veda he himself had spoken, declared the brahmin to be above all.
m.2.1.4.12: Knowing that, O Hari, today I shall teach you a lesson by that strength, so that you never do such a deed anywhere.
m.2.1.4.13: Until now you have been fearless, for you have not met with one who is powerful. Now, O Viṣṇu, you will reap the fruit of your own deed.
m.2.1.4.14: Having spoken thus to Hari, the sage, deluded by māyā and wrought up with anger, then cursed him, displaying his brahminical power.
m.2.1.4.15: O Viṣṇu, deluder, you made me distraught for the sake of a woman; the form in which you imitated me, O doer of deceitful deeds—
m.2.1.4.16: —in that form become a human, O Hari, and suffer that sorrow; and those whose face you gave me, may they be your helpers.
m.2.1.4.17: You, who give sorrow to others, receive the sorrow born of separation from your wife; living a human life, be for the most part deluded by ignorance.
m.2.1.4.18: Thus Nārada, bewildered by ignorance, cursed Hari out of delusion; Viṣṇu accepted that curse, praising Śambhu's unborn māyā.
m.2.1.4.19: Then Śambhu, of great sport, withdrew his own deluding māyā, by which even the wise Nārada had become deluded.
m.2.1.4.20: When the māyā vanished, Nārada became clear-minded as before; astonished at heart, he regained understanding and was calm.
m.2.1.4.21: Feeling deep remorse, he reproached himself again and again, and then praised Śambhu's māyā, which deludes even the wise.
m.2.1.4.22: Then, realising the whole confusion of his own mind caused by māyā, the sage Nārada, foremost of Viṣṇu's devotees, fell at Viṣṇu's feet.
m.2.1.4.23: Raised up by Hari, he, his evil-mindedness gone, said: Abusive words were spoken by me, deluded and of wicked understanding.
m.2.1.4.24: A curse too was given to you, O Lord; make it void, O Master. I have indeed committed a great sin; I shall surely go to hell.
m.2.1.4.25: What remedy should I undertake, O Hari? I am your servant; instruct me in that by which the mass of my sins may perish and hell may not be my lot.
m.2.1.4.26: Having said this, that best of sages, now right-minded and overcome with remorse, again fell at Viṣṇu's feet in devotion.
m.2.1.4.27: Then Viṣṇu, raising him up, spoke kind and true words: Do not grieve; you are my foremost devotee, there is no doubt of this.
m.2.1.4.28: Listen, dear one; I shall tell you what is truly good for you. You will certainly not go to hell; Śiva will grant you welfare.
m.2.1.4.29: Because, deluded by pride, you made Śiva's words false, he who bestows the fruits of action gave you such a fruit.
m.2.1.4.30: All this happened by Śiva's will; make your mind firm in this. That master, Śaṅkara, the Supreme Lord, is the remover of pride.
m.2.1.4.31: He is the supreme Brahman, the Supreme Self, revealed as existence-consciousness-bliss, without qualities, changeless, and beyond rajas, sattva and tamas.
m.2.1.4.32: He alone, taking up his own māyā, becomes threefold in form, as Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Maheśa; though without qualities, he is also with qualities.
m.2.1.4.33: In his qualityless state he is called Śiva, the Supreme Self, Maheśvara, the supreme Brahman, imperishable and infinite; he is sung of as Mahādeva.
m.2.1.4.34: By serving him, Vidhi (Brahmā) is the creator and I am the protector of the worlds; he himself, in the form of Rudra, is ever the destroyer of all.
m.2.1.4.35: In his own form as Śiva he is the witness, distinct from māyā, without qualities, acting at his own will, sporting freely, and bestowing grace on his devotees.
m.2.1.4.36: Listen, O sage Nārada, to an excellent remedy that gives happiness, removes all sins, and always grants enjoyment and liberation.
m.2.1.4.37: Casting off all your doubts, singing the true glory of Śaṅkara, always recite the hymn of Śiva's hundred names with undivided mind.
m.2.1.4.38: By reciting it, all your sin will quickly perish. Having said this to Nārada, Viṣṇu, full of compassion, spoke again:
m.2.1.4.39: O sage, do not grieve; nothing at all was done by you. Śambhu did all this of his own will; there is no doubt.
m.2.1.4.40: He took away your divine understanding and gave you the torment of desire; that Maheśvara caused the curse on me to be uttered from your mouth.
m.2.1.4.41: In this way Mṛtyuñjaya, the Conqueror of Death, the Death of Death (Kāla), who is wholly intent on uplifting his devotees, himself made his own deeds known in the world.
m.2.1.4.42: For me there is no beloved master, giver of happiness, equal to Śiva. He alone, the Supreme Lord, is the one who grants me all powers.
m.2.1.4.43: Worship him, O sage; adore him alone continually. Listen to his glory and sing it, and perform his worship every day.
m.2.1.4.44: He who approaches Śaṅkara with body, mind and speech, O sage, should be known as truly wise; he is called liberated while living.
m.2.1.4.45: By the forest-fire of the name Śiva, mountains of great sins are reduced to ashes effortlessly — this is true, true, there is no doubt.
m.2.1.4.46: Sorrows rooted in sin, manifold though they are, are therefore destroyed by the worship of Śiva alone, and by nothing else at all.
m.2.1.4.47: He is a true follower of the Veda, he is of meritorious soul, he is blessed, he is wise, O sage, who always takes refuge in Śaṅkara with body, speech and mind.
m.2.1.4.48: Those whose various merits (dharmas) are on the point of bearing fruit immediately — they come to have faith in the worship of Tripurāntaka, the Destroyer of Tripura.
m.2.1.4.49: As many sins as are destroyed by the worship of Śiva — so many sins do not even exist on earth, O great sage.
m.2.1.4.50: Even immeasurable heaps of sins such as killing a brāhmaṇa are destroyed by the remembrance of Śiva, O sage — I speak the truth, the truth.
m.2.1.4.51: Having obtained the boat of Śiva's name, they cross the ocean of saṃsāra; the sins that are the root of saṃsāra of such a one perish without doubt.
m.2.1.4.52: O great sage, by the axe of Śiva's name the destruction of the sins that are the very root of saṃsāra certainly takes place.
m.2.1.4.53: The nectar of Śiva's name should be drunk by those tormented by the forest-fire of sin; for those scorched by the fire of sin there is indeed no peace without it.
m.2.1.4.54: Those drenched by the streaming showers of the nectar of the name Śiva do not grieve even in the midst of the forest-fire of saṃsāra; there is no doubt.
m.2.1.4.55: Men whose minds delight in attachment and hatred have no devotion to Śaṅkara; but for people opposed to these passions, liberation comes about in every way.
m.2.1.4.56: Only he by whom austerity has been performed through endless births gains devotion to the beloved of Bhavānī's life.
m.2.1.4.57: Even when devotion to Śaṅkara has arisen, if it is shared with others it is futile; rather, devotion to Śiva that is unswerving is what is required.
m.2.1.4.58: Liberation is easily attained only by him whose devotion to Śambhu is exclusive and unswerving, and not by anyone else — such is my view.
m.2.1.4.59: Even having committed endless sins, if one has devotion to Maheśvara, one becomes freed from all sins; there is no doubt.
m.2.1.4.60: Just as trees in a forest burnt by a forest-fire are reduced to ashes, so too the sins of Śaṅkara's devotees are burnt up.
m.2.1.4.61: He who, his limbs purified with ash, is always intent on the worship of Śiva, surely crosses the boundless and most dreadful saṃsāra.
m.2.1.4.62: Even having stolen a brāhmaṇa's property, even having killed many brāhmaṇas, a man who is a servant of Virūpākṣa is not tainted by sins.
m.2.1.4.63: Having examined all the Vedas, the ancients concluded that the worship of Śiva alone is the supreme means of destroying saṃsāra.
m.2.1.4.64: From today onward, with effort, attentively and according to rule, worship with devotion every day Sāmba Sadāśiva, the great Lord (Maheśvara).
m.2.1.4.65: Having properly and reverently smeared yourself with ash from feet to head, repeat the six-syllabled Śaiva mantra proclaimed in all the śrutis.
m.2.1.4.66: With care, wear on all your limbs rudrākṣas, dear to Śiva, with the deepest devotion, accompanied by mantra and according to rule.
m.2.1.4.67: Listen daily to stories of Śiva, always recount stories of Śiva, and honour the devotees of Śiva with great care again and again.
m.2.1.4.68: Without negligence, be constantly one whose sole refuge is Śiva, since through the worship of Śiva bliss is perpetually attained.
m.2.1.4.69: Placing Śiva's lotus-feet in your pure heart, first wander through the holy places of Śiva, O best of sages.
m.2.1.4.70: Beholding the incomparable greatness of Śaṅkara, the Supreme Self, then go to Ānandavana, most beloved of Śambhu, O sage.
m.2.1.4.71: There, having seen Viśveśvara, perform worship with devotion; having bowed and praised him especially, you will become free from all doubt.
m.2.1.4.72: And after that, O sage, you should certainly go to Brahmaloka for your own desired purpose, by my command, with devotion.
m.2.1.4.73: Having bowed to and especially praised Vidhi (Brahmā), your own father, O sage, you should ask him repeatedly, with a pleased mind, about the greatness of Śiva.
m.2.1.4.74: That Brahmā, foremost among Śaivas, will with great affection recite to you the greatness of Śaṅkara and also the hymn of a hundred names.
m.2.1.4.75: From today, O sage, be a Śaiva wholly devoted to Śiva; you will especially be a partaker of liberation, and Śiva will bestow well-being upon you.
m.2.1.4.76: Having thus lovingly instructed the sage, Viṣṇu, serene of mind, remembered Śiva, bowed to him and praised him, and then vanished.
m.2.1.4.iti: Thus ends the fourth adhyāya, named Viṣṇu's teaching to Nārada, in the account of creation, in the first khaṇḍa of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.1.5.1: Sūta said: O Brāhmaṇas, when Hari had vanished, Nārada, the best of sages, wandered over the earth, devoutly visiting the Śiva-liṅgas.
m.2.1.5.2: O Brāhmaṇas, having roamed the earth, he lovingly beheld the many forms of Śiva that grant worldly enjoyment and liberation.
m.2.1.5.3: Then the two attendants of Śambhu, learning that Nārada of divine aspect was wandering on the earth, approached him, who was now of tranquil mind.
m.2.1.5.4: Bowing quickly and deeply with their heads and clasping his feet, the two attendants spoke respectfully, desiring release from the curse.
m.2.1.5.5: The two attendants of Śiva said: O son of Brahmā, O divine sage, kindly hear our words. We two who offended you are not really Brāhmaṇas.
m.2.1.5.6: O Brāhmaṇa, O sage, we two are attendants of Hara who offended you at the princess's svayaṃvara, when your mind was deluded by Māyā.
m.2.1.5.7: And the curse was given to us by you, impelled by the Supreme Lord. Knowing it was an unfavourable moment, silence alone was our safety.
m.2.1.5.8: We have reaped the fruit of our own deeds; no one else is to blame. Be fully gracious, O lord; show us favour today.
m.2.1.5.9: Sūta said: Having heard these words spoken with devotion and respect by the two attendants, the sage, filled with remorse, replied kindly.
m.2.1.5.10: Nārada said: Listen, O attendants of Mahādeva, most honoured among the good, to my words, which are pleasing, free from delusion and true.
m.2.1.5.11: Formerly my mind was surely led astray by the will of Śiva; wholly overcome by delusion and of perverse understanding, I cursed you two.
m.2.1.5.12: What was said will come to pass; still, listen, O attendants: I shall tell you the release from the curse. Forgive my sin today.
m.2.1.5.13: Born from the seed of an eminent sage, you shall attain lordship over the Rākṣasas, as I ordain; may you be endowed with splendour, mighty and of great valour.
m.2.1.5.14: Kings of the whole universe, devotees of Śiva, with senses controlled, you shall meet death at the hands of Śiva's other form Viṣṇu and then regain your own station.
m.2.1.5.15: Sūta said: Having heard these words of the great-souled sage Nārada, both attendants of Hara, pleased, joyfully went to their own abode.
m.2.1.5.16: Nārada too, supremely pleased, meditating on Śiva with single-minded focus, roamed the earth, repeatedly visiting Śiva's holy places.
m.2.1.5.17: Then the sage reached Kāśī, which shines above all, dear to Śiva, giving joy to Śambhu, the very embodiment of Śambhu.
m.2.1.5.18: Seeing Kāśī he felt his purpose fulfilled; he beheld Kāśīnātha and, filled with supreme bliss, worshipped him with the greatest love.
m.2.1.5.19: Joyfully having resorted to Kāśī, the best of sages felt fulfilled—bowing, praising devoutly, remembering Śiva, overwhelmed with love.
m.2.1.5.20: Then Nārada, his good mind set on remembering Śiva and wishing to know the truth of Śiva in particular, went to Brahmaloka.
m.2.1.5.21: There, having devoutly bowed to Brahmā and praised him with various hymns, he, his mind united with Śiva, asked about the true nature of Śiva.
m.2.1.5.22: Nārada said: O Brahmā, knower of the nature of Brahman, Grandsire, lord of the world, by your grace I have heard the whole supreme greatness of Viṣṇu,
m.2.1.5.23: I have heard of the path of devotion, the path of knowledge, the very arduous path of austerity, the path of charity, and the path of pilgrimage to holy places.
m.2.1.5.24: But I have not known the truth of Śiva. Therefore, O lord, explain to me in order the method of his worship and his various deeds.
m.2.1.5.25: Dear father, how is Śiva, though without attributes, Śaṅkara with attributes? Deluded by Śiva's Māyā, I do not know the truth of Śiva.
m.2.1.5.26: How did Śambhu abide in his own nature before creation? And how does the Lord continue, sporting, in the midst of creation?
m.2.1.5.27: And at its end, how does that god Maheśvara remain? How does Śaṅkara, the benefactor of the worlds, become pleased?
m.2.1.5.28: And when pleased, what fruit does Maheśvara bestow on his own devotees and on others? O Creator, tell me all that.
m.2.1.5.29: It is heard that the Lord becomes pleased at once; that great one, intent on compassion, does not look at the devotee's toil.
m.2.1.5.30: Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Maheśa—the three gods—are born of portions of Śiva; among them Maheśa is the full portion, the supreme Śiva himself.
m.2.1.5.31: Tell me of his manifestation and especially his deeds; tell me also, O lord, of Umā's manifestation and her marriage to him.
m.2.1.5.32: Especially his household life, and likewise his other sports too—all this and more should be narrated by you, O sinless one.
m.2.1.5.33: Tell me in particular, O lord of creatures, of Śivā's origin and marriage, and likewise of the birth of Guha.
m.2.1.5.34: I have heard it before from many, but I am not satisfied, O lord of the world. Therefore I have come to you for refuge; show me your grace.
m.2.1.5.35: Having heard these words of Nārada, his own son, Brahmā, the Grandsire of the worlds, spoke there.
m.2.1.5.iti: Thus ends the fifth adhyāya, named Nārada's question, in the account of creation, in the first khaṇḍa of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.1.6.1: Brahmā said: O Brahman (Nārada), best among the wise gods, you have asked me well, you who are ever a benefactor of the worlds, out of a desire for the welfare of the worlds.
m.2.1.6.2: I shall now tell you that flawless truth of Śiva, by hearing which the destruction of all sins may come about for all the worlds.
m.2.1.6.3: The truth of Śiva has not been truly known by me, nor even by Viṣṇu; nor has his supreme and wondrous form been known by anyone else.
m.2.1.6.4: At the time of the great dissolution, when everything moving and unmoving had perished, all was made of darkness, without sun, planets or stars,
m.2.1.6.5: without moon, without day and night, without fire, wind, earth or water, without primordial matter, the sky empty, devoid of any other light,
m.2.1.6.6: lacking visibility and the like, devoid of sound and touch, with smell and form unmanifest, bereft of taste, and without directions.
m.2.1.6.7: When it was thus, in blinding darkness so dense it could be pierced only by a needle, unbroken, there was that which is heard of in scripture as That, the Existent, Brahman, by which one comes to know the one Existent.
m.2.1.6.8: When there was nothing of this kind, there was that which is of the nature of both being and non-being, which yogins constantly behold in the inner space of the heart,
m.2.1.6.9: which is beyond the reach of the mind and never the object of words, without name, form or colour, neither gross nor subtle,
m.2.1.6.10: neither short nor long, not light, devoid of heaviness, in which there is no increase whatsoever, nor any decrease,
m.2.1.6.11: which the Śruti, as if awestruck, declares again simply as that which is — truth, knowledge, the infinite, supreme bliss, the supreme light,
m.2.1.6.12: immeasurable, without support, changeless, formless, beyond the guṇas, attainable by yogins, all-pervading, the sole cause,
m.2.1.6.13: free from differentiation, without beginning of activity, free from illusion, untroubled, without a second, without beginning or end, not unfolding, of the nature of consciousness—
m.2.1.6.14: of which the wise thus conceive by means of names and designations. After some time, it is said, a desire for a second arose in it.
m.2.1.6.15: By that formless one, through its own play, a form of its own was fashioned—endowed with all lordly powers and qualities, consisting of all knowledge, auspicious,
m.2.1.6.16: going everywhere, having all forms, all-seeing, the doer of all, the one to be worshipped by all, the first of all, at all times the refinement of all.
m.2.1.6.17: Having thus conceived that lordly form of pure nature, that which is called the Supreme Brahman—without a second, without beginning or end, illuminating all, of the nature of consciousness, all-pervading and imperishable—vanished.
m.2.1.6.18: The form of that formless one which is called the Supreme is Sadāśiva. The wise, of later and of earlier times, have called him Īśvara.
m.2.1.6.19: Then by him, though alone, sporting at will, Śakti—a body—was created by himself from his own form, never separating from his own body.
m.2.1.6.20: They call her Pradhāna, Prakṛti, and Māyā—supreme, possessed of the guṇas, the mother of the principle of intellect (buddhi), herself free from modification.
m.2.1.6.21: That Śakti is called Ambikā, Prakṛti, the sovereign of all, the mother of the three gods, eternal, and the root cause.
m.2.1.6.22: She had eight arms; auspicious, with a wondrous face, and in her face shone constantly the radiance of a thousand full moons.
m.2.1.6.23: The goddess was adorned with various ornaments, endowed with various movements, bearing various weapons, with eyes like full-blown lotuses.
m.2.1.6.24: Endowed with inconceivable splendour, the source of all, ever active—Māyā, who is single when alone, yet manifold through union.
m.2.1.6.25: He is the Supreme Person, the Lord, Śiva, Śambhu, who has no lord over him, bearing the Mandākinī (Gaṅgā) on his head, with the moon on his forehead and three eyes,
m.2.1.6.26: five-faced, serene in spirit, ten-armed, bearing the trident, very white, fair as camphor, his body smeared with ash.
m.2.1.6.27: And simultaneously, together with that Śakti, by that Brahman whose very nature is Time, a region named Śivaloka was created.
m.2.1.6.28: That very region is called Kāśikā, the most excellent sacred field, the supreme abode of liberation (nirvāṇa), shining above all.
m.2.1.6.29: And by those two, whose form is supreme bliss, sporting in that charming field, the field was made to be of the form of supreme bliss.
m.2.1.6.30: O sage, even at the time of dissolution, that field is never abandoned by Śiva and Śivā; therefore they know it as Avimukta ('never abandoned').
m.2.1.6.31: Formerly the Pināka-bearer (Śiva) named this field Ānandavana ('Forest of Bliss') because it is the cause of bliss, and afterwards Avimukta.
m.2.1.6.32: Then, O divine sage, as Śiva and Śivā were sporting in that Forest of Bliss, a desire arose: Some other being should be created.
m.2.1.6.33: On whom we two may place the great burden, and, moving freely at our own will, solely abiding in Kāśī, enjoy the state of liberation.
m.2.1.6.34: May he alone do everything, may he alone protect, and may he alone withdraw everything at the end, always by my grace.
m.2.1.6.35: Having contracted the ocean of the mind, tossed by waves of anxiety, with sattva as its jewel, tamas as its crocodile, and entwined with rajas as its coral,
m.2.1.6.36: by whose grace we two may dwell happily in the Forest of Bliss, for there is little happiness when the mind's activity is scattered and troubled by outward cares.
m.2.1.6.37: Having thus resolved, that all-pervading supreme Lord, together with that Śakti, applied nectar-elixir to the tenth limb on his left side.
m.2.1.6.38: Then a single Person appeared, the most beautiful in the three worlds, tranquil, abounding in the quality of sattva, an immeasurable ocean of profundity.
m.2.1.6.39: And, O sage, endowed with forbearance, he was beyond compare; he had the lustre of sapphire, was glorious, with eyes like the finest white lotus.
m.2.1.6.40: Bearing a golden radiance, clad in a pair of excellent silk garments, with a pair of shining, mighty staff-like arms, he was unconquerable.
m.2.1.6.41: Then that Puruṣa bowed to Śambhu, the supreme Lord, and said: O master, give me names, and tell me my task.
m.2.1.6.42: Hearing those words, the Lord Śaṅkara, the great Ruler, laughing, spoke to that Puruṣa in a voice deep as a thundercloud.
m.2.1.6.43: Śiva said: Because you are all-pervading, your name will be renowned as Viṣṇu; you will also have many other names that bring happiness to devotees.
m.2.1.6.44: Being steadfast, perform penance, the supreme means of accomplishing your task. Having said this, he then gave him the Veda by way of his breath.
m.2.1.6.45: Then Acyuta, having bowed to Śiva, performed extensive penance; the Supreme Lord, together with Śakti and his world, vanished.
m.2.1.6.46: Even after performing penance for twelve thousand divine years, Acyuta did not obtain the vision of Śambhu that he longed for, which grants everything.
m.2.1.6.47: Then, falling into doubt, Viṣṇu, remembering Śiva, reflected earnestly in his heart: What should I do now?
m.2.1.6.48: Meanwhile an auspicious voice arose from Śiva: Penance must be performed again to dispel the doubt.
m.2.1.6.49: Then, having heard that, he, intent on the path of meditation on Brahman, performed very severe penance for a long time.
m.2.1.6.50: Then that Puruṣa Viṣṇu, awakened through the path of meditation, was greatly delighted and struck with wonder, saying, what is this? Oh!
m.2.1.6.51: From the very limbs of that toiling Viṣṇu, various streams of water flowed forth through Śiva's māyā.
m.2.1.6.52: O great sage, the whole of that void was pervaded; the water became of the form of Brahman, destroying sin by its touch.
m.2.1.6.53: Then the weary Puruṣa Viṣṇu himself, supremely delighted and deluded by māyā, slept in that water for a long time.
m.2.1.6.54: His name Nārāyaṇa also arose, approved by the Veda. At that time nothing else existed apart from the primordial Puruṣa.
m.2.1.6.55: At that time the principles (tattvas) came forth from the great-souled one. Hear how, O wise one, O great-minded one, as I tell it.
m.2.1.6.56: From Prakṛti arose Mahat, and from Mahat the three guṇas; from that was born Ahaṅkāra, threefold by the division of the guṇas.
m.2.1.6.57: From that the subtle elements (tanmātras) were born, and from them the five gross elements; at the same time arose the senses, consisting of organs of knowledge and action.
m.2.1.6.58: Thus the enumeration of the principles has been told to you, O best of sages. All of that, arising from Prakṛti, is inert by nature, apart from the Puruṣa.
m.2.1.6.59: Then, by Śiva's will, he took up that principle numbering twenty-four, made into one, and slept in the water of Brahman's form.
m.2.1.6.iti: Thus ends the sixth adhyāya, named The origin of Viṣṇu, in the exposition of creation, in the first khaṇḍa of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.1.7.1: Brahmā said: While the god Nārāyaṇa was asleep, an excellent and huge lotus suddenly appeared from his navel by the will of Śaṅkara.
m.2.1.7.2: It had an endless stalk, shone like the karṇikāra flower, was endless yojanas in length and possessed of endless height.
m.2.1.7.3: It was radiant like ten million suns, beautiful, endowed with the principles (tattvas), most wonderful, exceedingly charming, worth beholding and unsurpassed.
m.2.1.7.4: Making an effort as before, that Śaṅkara, the supreme Lord, Śambhu together with Ambā, generated me from his own right side.
m.2.1.7.5: O sage, that Maheśa, quickly making me deluded by māyā, caused me, in sport, to appear from the lotus of his (Viṣṇu's) navel.
m.2.1.7.6: Thus I was then born from the lotus as a son, Hemagarbha (the golden-wombed), four-faced, red in colour, my forehead marked with the tripuṇḍra.
m.2.1.7.7: Deluded by his māyā and weak in knowledge, I did not know, dear one, any father, the begetter of my body, other than the lotus.
m.2.1.7.8: Who am I, or whence have I come? What is my task? Whose son am I, born here? By whom have I now been made?
m.2.1.7.9: To me, fallen into such doubt, a thought occurred: Why do I fall into delusion? Surely knowing that is easy.
m.2.1.7.10: Below lies the place from which the petals of this lotus flower rise; and my maker will surely be there, no doubt.
m.2.1.7.11: Resolving thus, I descended from the lotus and went down there through tube after tube of the stalk for a hundred years, O sage.
m.2.1.7.12: But I did not find there the excellent base of the lotus; falling into doubt again, I became eager to go back to the lotus.
m.2.1.7.13: Then, O sage, I climbed up the lotus by way of the stalk; but, deluded, I did not reach the bud of the lotus.
m.2.1.7.14: As I wandered along the stalk, another hundred years passed. Then I stayed there for a moment, bewildered.
m.2.1.7.15: Then, O sage, by Śiva's will, a supreme, auspicious, excellent voice arose from the sky, saying, perform austerity, destroying delusion.
m.2.1.7.16: Having heard that voice from the sky, I then performed severe austerity with effort for twelve years, in order to see my own begetter.
m.2.1.7.17: Then indeed the blessed Viṣṇu, four-armed and fair-eyed, quickly appeared in order to show grace to me alone.
m.2.1.7.18: Holding the conch and discus as weapons in his hands, bearing the mace and lotus, supreme, with all his limbs dark as a rain cloud, wearing yellow garments, the highest,
m.2.1.7.19: adorned with a crown and other great ornaments, his lotus-face serene, resembling ten million Kandarpas — he was seen by me, the deluded one.
m.2.1.7.20: Seeing that beautiful form — dark like Kāla and yet golden in radiance, the Self of all, four-armed — I was filled with supreme wonder.
m.2.1.7.21: Seeing mighty-armed Nārāyaṇa in such a form, comprising in himself both the existent and the non-existent, I then became delighted.
m.2.1.7.22: Deluded then by the māyā of Lord Śambhu, whose nature is sport, and not recognising my own begetter, I joyfully spoke to him.
m.2.1.7.23: Brahmā said: Who are you? Speak. So saying, I roused the Eternal One with my hand, with a sharp and very firm blow of the hand.
m.2.1.7.24: Awakening and rising from his bed, the self-controlled one sat for a moment; with his spotless lotus-eyes moist with sleep he saw
m.2.1.7.25: me standing there. The blessed Hari, invested with radiance, rising up and smiling, spoke sweetly once to me, Brahmā.
m.2.1.7.26: Viṣṇu said: Welcome, welcome, child, O Grandsire of great splendour. Be fearless; I shall grant all your desires, no doubt.
m.2.1.7.27: Hearing his words spoken with a smile, I, the foremost of gods, bound in enmity by rajas, spoke to Janārdana.
m.2.1.7.28: Brahmā said: O sinless one, smiling broadly, you address me here as child, child — me, the cause of the dissolution of all — like a teacher addressing a pupil,
m.2.1.7.29: me, the very maker of the worlds and impeller of Prakṛti, the eternal, unborn, all-pervading Viriñci, sprung from Viṣṇu,
m.2.1.7.30: the Self of the universe, the ordainer, the creator, the lotus-eyed. Why do you speak thus out of delusion? You should tell me at once.
m.2.1.7.31: The Veda invariably calls me the Self-born, the unborn, the all-pervading, the Grandsire, the self-ruling, and the supreme Parameṣṭhin.
m.2.1.7.32: Hearing these words of mine, Hari, the lord of Ramā, grew angry; he too said to me: I know you as the creator with respect to the worlds.
m.2.1.7.33: Viṣṇu said: You descended from my imperishable body in order to create and sustain. You have forgotten me, Nārāyaṇa, lord of the world, free from affliction,
m.2.1.7.34: the Puruṣa, the supreme Self, invoked by many, praised by many, Viṣṇu, Acyuta, the Lord, the source and origin of the universe,
m.2.1.7.35: Nārāyaṇa, the mighty-armed, the all-pervading Lord. For you were born from the lotus of my navel; there is no doubt about this.
m.2.1.7.36: There is no fault of yours in this; it has been brought about in you by my māyā. Hear the truth, O four-faced one: I am indeed the lord of all the gods.
m.2.1.7.37: I am the creator, the destroyer and the sustainer; there is no lord equal to me. I alone am the supreme Brahman, the supreme reality, O Grandsire.
m.2.1.7.38: I alone am the supreme light; I am the supreme Self, the all-pervading. Whatever moving and unmoving is seen and heard today in this world —
m.2.1.7.39: know all that, O four-faced one, to be made of me. Long ago the Unmanifest, with its twenty-four principles, was created by me.
m.2.1.7.40: In them the atoms are eternally bound; anger, fear and the like were created; and by my power you were produced here, along with many bodies, in sport.
m.2.1.7.41: The intellect (buddhi) was created by me; in it arose ego (ahaṅkāra) in three forms; then the group of five subtle elements (tanmātras); from that, the mind, the body and the senses;
m.2.1.7.42: and the elements beginning with ether, and the things made of the elements — all this I created in play. Knowing this, O lord of creatures, O Vidhi, take refuge in me.
m.2.1.7.43: I will protect you from all sorrows; there is no doubt. Hearing his words, I, Brahmā, filled with anger and bewildered by māyā, rebuked him and said, who are you?
m.2.1.7.44: Why do you speak so much, words that cause great harm? You are not the Lord, the supreme Brahman; there must be some creator of you.
m.2.1.7.45: Deluded by the māyā of Śaṅkara, the great Lord, I waged a most terrible battle with that Hari.
m.2.1.7.46: Thus there was a hair-raising fight between me and Hari in the midst of the ocean of dissolution, the two of us bound in enmity by rajas.
m.2.1.7.47: Meanwhile a Liṅga appeared before us both, to quell the dispute and likewise to awaken us two.
m.2.1.7.48: It was rich with thousands of garlands of flames, like a hundred fires of universal destruction, free from decrease and growth, devoid of beginning, middle and end,
m.2.1.7.49: incomparable, indescribable, unmanifest, the source of the universe. By its thousand flames the blessed Hari was bewildered.
m.2.1.7.50: And he said to me, who was also bewildered: Why do you contend here now? A third has come here; let our battle cease.
m.2.1.7.51: From where has it arisen here? Let us two examine this fire-born thing. I shall go downward along this incomparable pillar of fire,
m.2.1.7.52: to examine it, O lord of creatures; you should go upward with effort, quickly, with the speed of the wind.
m.2.1.7.53: Brahmā said: Having spoken thus, the Soul of the universe then assumed the form of a boar; and I too, O sage, quickly attained the state of a swan.
m.2.1.7.54: From that time they call me Haṃsa-haṃsa and Virāṭ. Whoever says Haṃsa, haṃsa will then become a Haṃsa.
m.2.1.7.55: Very white, resembling fire, furnished with wings on all sides, becoming swift as mind and wind, I went upward, ever higher, in that former time.
m.2.1.7.56: Nārāyaṇa too, the Soul of the universe, then became very white, ten yojanas wide and a hundred yojanas long,
m.2.1.7.57: with a body like Mount Meru, with white, sharp, fierce tusks, shining like the sun at the time of dissolution, long-snouted, loud-roaring,
m.2.1.7.58: short-legged, with wondrous limbs, victorious, firm, incomparable — assuming such a boar form, he swiftly went below it.
m.2.1.7.59: Thus moving for a thousand years, Viṣṇu went downward. From then on in the worlds there was the kalpa named Śvetavārāha,
m.2.1.7.60: the kalpa came into being, O divine sage, a designation of time for men. Viṣṇu, the mighty one, having gone down, roamed about in many ways.
m.2.1.7.61: The boar did not see even the slightest trace of the base of this Liṅga. For that same length of time, O slayer of foes, I too went upward,
m.2.1.7.62: quickly, with every effort, wishing to know its end. Weary, not having seen its end, I came down after a time.
m.2.1.7.63: Likewise the blessed lotus-eyed Viṣṇu, wearied, resembling all the gods, of mighty body, quickly rose up.
m.2.1.7.64: He came together with me and, bowing again and again to Bhava, stood deluded by the māyā of Śambhu, his mind agitated.
m.2.1.7.65: Bowing along with me to the Supreme Lord from behind, from the sides and from the front, he pondered, what is this?
m.2.1.7.66: That form was indescribable, nameless, devoid of action; the signless had attained the state of a sign (liṅga), beyond reach even on the path of meditation.
m.2.1.7.67: Then, making our minds composed, we both — I and Hari too — became wholly devoted to obeisance.
m.2.1.7.68: We do not know your form; whoever you are, that you are, O great Lord. Salutation to you, O Maheśāna; show your form to us quickly.
m.2.1.7.69: Thus, O tiger among sages, a hundred years passed while we two, who had been given to pride, kept making obeisance.
m.2.1.7.iti: Thus ends the seventh adhyāya, named The dispute between Viṣṇu and Brahmā, in the account of creation, in the first khaṇḍa of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.1.8.1: Brahmā said: Thus, O best of sages, while we two gods, now free of pride and longing for a sight of him, remained there continually, O sage,
m.2.1.8.2: Śambhu became compassionate — he who protects the afflicted, takes away the pride of the proud, and is the imperishable lord of all.
m.2.1.8.3: Then there arose there, from the best of gods, a resonance having the character of speech — Om, Om — very distinct, with the quality of a prolonged (pluta) sound.
m.2.1.8.4: While I pondered — what indeed is this? — and the great sound persisted, Viṣṇu — adored by all the gods, free from enmity — with a contented mind
m.2.1.8.5: saw on the right side of the liṅga the eternal first letter called A, and then U on the northern side,
m.2.1.8.6: and M in the middle, and at its end the resonance Om. Having seen the first letter on the right like the orb of the sun,
m.2.1.8.7: U on the north resembling fire, O best of seers, and M in its middle resembling the orb of the moon,
m.2.1.8.8: then above it he saw the Supreme, shining brightly like pure crystal, beyond the fourth state, stainless, partless, free of affliction,
m.2.1.8.9: beyond dualities, absolute, void, devoid of outer and inner, yet present in the outer and inner, abiding both without and within,
m.2.1.8.10: without beginning, middle or end, the primal cause of bliss — truth, bliss, immortality, the supreme, the highest goal, Brahman.
m.2.1.8.11: From where indeed has this arisen here? Let us two examine this fire-born pillar. I shall go below the incomparable pillar of fire.
m.2.1.8.12: He contemplated the Soul of the universe, pervaded by both the Veda and sound. Then a seer appeared there, regarded as the very essence of seerhood.
m.2.1.8.13: Through that very seer Viṣṇu came to know the Supreme Lord, Mahādeva, the supreme Brahman, the supreme one whose body is the Word-Brahman.
m.2.1.8.14: Rudra is beyond thought; he from whom words, together with the mind, turn back without reaching him — he is denoted by the single syllable.
m.2.1.8.15: By the single syllable is that expressed: the cosmic order, the supreme cause, truth, bliss, immortality, the supreme Brahman, higher than the highest.
m.2.1.8.16: From the single syllable called A came the Lord, the egg-born bearer of the seed Brahmā; from the single syllable called U, Hari, the supreme cause;
m.2.1.8.17: from the single syllable called M, the Lord Nīlalohita. The one called A is the creator, and the one called U is the deluder;
m.2.1.8.18: and the one called M became the constant bestower of grace. The one called M is the all-pervading seed-holder; A is said to be the seed.
m.2.1.8.19: The one called U is Hari, the womb, lord of Pradhāna and Puruṣa. The seed-holder, the seed, and its womb — and Maheśvara, called Nāda.
m.2.1.8.20: The seed-holder, dividing himself by his own will, remained established. From the liṅga of this lord, the seed-holder, came forth the seed, A.
m.2.1.8.21: Deposited in the womb U, it grew on all sides and became a golden egg; that was only to be indicated, devoid of distinguishing marks.
m.2.1.8.22: Thus the divine egg remained in the waters for many years. Then at the end of a thousand years, the egg from which the Unborn Brahmā arises was split in two —
m.2.1.8.23: the egg lying in the waters — by a blow from the Lord himself. Then its very auspicious golden upper shell, situated above,
m.2.1.8.24: became the sky; the other half became the earth with its five characteristics. From that egg was born the lord called Ka, the four-faced one.
m.2.1.8.25: He is the creator of all the worlds; he alone is the threefold lord. Thus has Om Om been declared — so said the foremost of the Yajus hymns.
m.2.1.8.26: Hearing the words of the Yajus, the Ṛks and Sāmans respectfully said to us two then: Just so, O Hari, O Brahmā.
m.2.1.8.27: Then, having rightly understood the Lord of gods, he praised the god Maheśvara of supreme glory with mantras arising from his own power.
m.2.1.8.28: Meanwhile the Lord, protector of the universe, together with me, saw another form, wondrous and beautiful:
m.2.1.8.29: five-faced, ten-armed, fair like camphor, O sage, endowed with manifold radiance, adorned with various ornaments,
m.2.1.8.30: most magnanimous, of great valour, bearing the marks of a great being. Seeing that supreme form, Hari, together with me, became fulfilled.
m.2.1.8.31: Then the Lord Maheśa, the Supreme Lord, pleased, having revealed his divine form made of sound, stood smiling.
m.2.1.8.32: A is his head; the long Ā is said to be the forehead; I is the right eye, Ī the left eye.
m.2.1.8.33: U is the right ear, Ū is said to be the left; Ṛ is the right cheek of that Supreme One.
m.2.1.8.34: Ṝ is the left cheek; Ḷ and Ḹ are the two nostrils; E is the upper lip and Ai the lower lip of the Lord.
m.2.1.8.35: O and Au are the two rows of teeth respectively; Aṃ and Aḥ are the two palates of that trident-bearing God of gods.
m.2.1.8.36: The five letters beginning with Ka are his five hands on the right; likewise the five letters beginning with Ca are the five hands on the left.
m.2.1.8.37: The five letters beginning with Ṭa and likewise the five beginning with Ta are the feet; Pa is his belly; Pha is said to be the right flank.
m.2.1.8.38: Ba is the left flank, Bha is said to be the shoulder, and Ma is the heart of Śambhu, Mahādeva, the yogin.
m.2.1.8.39: The letters from Ya to Sa are the seven bodily constituents of the Lord; Ha is in the form of the navel, and Kṣa is said to be the nose.
m.2.1.8.40: Having thus seen, together with Umā, this form made of sound of him who is without attributes and yet whose nature is the attributes, Hari, along with me, became fulfilled.
m.2.1.8.41: Having thus seen Maheśāna, Śiva whose body is the Word-Brahman (śabdabrahman), and having bowed to him, Viṣṇu together with me again looked upward and saw:
m.2.1.8.42: a mantra arising from Oṃkāra, endowed with five kalās, resembling pure crystal, of thirty-eight auspicious syllables.
m.2.1.8.43: Next there appeared a mantra in the form of intelligence, accomplishing all dharma and artha: a mantra arising from the Gāyatrī, complete with its parts, bringing about subjugation,
m.2.1.8.44: rich in twenty-four syllables, to be used at the four times of day, unsurpassed. Then a mantra of five whites (pañcasita), joined with eight kalās,
m.2.1.8.45: exceedingly potent for abhicāra rites, of about thirty auspicious syllables; and another connected with the Yajurveda, of twenty-five auspicious syllables,
m.2.1.8.46: joined with eight kalās, very white and pacifying; and another joined with thirteen kalās, red, together with Bālā and the others.
m.2.1.8.47: These became the cause of its origination, growth and dissolution; and the syllables of this excellent mantra are sixty-one.
m.2.1.8.48: Again, the Mṛtyuñjaya mantra; after that the five-syllabled mantra; likewise the Cintāmaṇi mantra, and the one called Dakṣiṇāmūrti;
m.2.1.8.49: then the great saying of Hara, expressed as tat tvam asi (That thou art). Having thus obtained the five mantras, the blessed Hari recited them.
m.2.1.8.50: Then, having seen him whose form is the kalās and letters, whose form is the Ṛg, Yajus and Sāman, who has Īśāna as his crown, the ancient one called Puruṣa,
m.2.1.8.51: whose heart is Aghora, lovely, the secret of all, Sadāśiva, whose feet are Vāmadeva, Mahādeva, adorned with the great serpent-king,
m.2.1.8.52: him, Śiva, having feet on all sides, eyes and hands on all sides, the overlord of Brahmā, the cause of creation, maintenance and dissolution —
m.2.1.8.53: the blessed Viṣṇu, together with me, with a delighted mind, praised with pleasing words the boon-giving Lord, Sāmba (Śiva with Ambā).
m.2.1.8.iti: Thus ends the eighth adhyāya, named The form of Brahman as sound, in the account of creation, in the first khaṇḍa of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.1.9.1: Brahmā said: Then, having heard the praise of himself composed by Viṣṇu, Maheśvara, the treasure of compassion, greatly pleased, appeared together with his consort.
m.2.1.9.2: He was five-faced, three-eyed, with the moon on his forehead, wearing matted locks, fair in complexion, large-eyed, his body smeared with ash;
m.2.1.9.3: ten-armed, blue-throated, adorned with every ornament, beautiful in every limb, his forehead marked with the triple stripe (tripuṇḍra) of ash.
m.2.1.9.4: Seeing that god, the Supreme Lord, in such a form together with his consort, Viṣṇu, along with me, again praised him with pleasing words.
m.2.1.9.5: Then Hara, Maheśa, the mine of compassion, gracious at heart, gave the Veda to him, to Viṣṇu, in the form of his breath.
m.2.1.9.6: Then he gave secret knowledge to him, the Supreme Self Viṣṇu; and the Supreme Self in turn, out of kindness, gave it to me, O sage.
m.2.1.9.7: Having received the Veda, Viṣṇu, his purpose fulfilled, bowing with joined palms along with me, questioned Maheśvara once more.
m.2.1.9.8: Viṣṇu said: How are you pleased, O God? How are you to be worshipped by me, O Lord? How should meditation be performed? How do you come under a devotee's control?
m.2.1.9.9: What should we two do by your command, O Mahādeva? Always, always command us; act for our delight, O Śaṅkara.
m.2.1.9.10: All this, O great king, O Lord, showing kindness to us two, should be told to us, and other things as well, O Śiva, knowing us to be your own followers.
m.2.1.9.11: Brahmā said: Hearing these words, the blessed Hara, pleased, the treasure of compassion, most gracious, spoke affectionately.
m.2.1.9.12: Śrī Śiva said: Truly I am pleased by the devotion of you both, O best of gods. Beholding me, Mahādeva, cast off all fear.
m.2.1.9.13: My liṅga is always to be worshipped, and this form of mine is to be meditated upon; just as it is seen now, so should it be done with care.
m.2.1.9.14: Worshipped in the form of the liṅga and pleased, I shall grant to all the worlds various fruits and the desires of their hearts in many ways.
m.2.1.9.15: Whenever sorrow arises for you two there, O best of gods, then, when my liṅga is worshipped, there will be destruction of sorrow.
m.2.1.9.16: You two mighty ones were born from my Prakṛti, from the left and right limbs of me, the Lord of all.
m.2.1.9.17: This Brahmā, grandsire of the worlds, arose from my right side, and you, Viṣṇu, from the left side of me, the Supreme Self.
m.2.1.9.18: I am thoroughly pleased with you both; I would grant you a boon as you wish. By my consent, may your devotion to me be firm.
m.2.1.9.19: Making an earthen image of me, O wise ones, perform various kinds of service to it; having done so, you will attain happiness.
m.2.1.9.20: O Brahmā, carry out creation, as the keeper of my command; and you, dear child, dear child Hari, likewise protect the moving and unmoving world.
m.2.1.9.21: Brahmā said: Having said this, the Lord gave to us two the auspicious method of worship, by which Śambhu, when worshipped, bestows fruit in many ways.
m.2.1.9.22: Having heard these words of Śambhu, Hari, together with me, bowing down with joined palms, replied to Maheśāna.
m.2.1.9.23: Viṣṇu said: If love for us has arisen, and if a boon is to be given to us, may our devotion to you be constant and unwavering.
m.2.1.9.24: You too, though beyond attributes, descend now in sport; be our helper, dear father, for you are the highest, the Supreme Lord.
m.2.1.9.25: O Lord of the god of gods, even our dispute was auspicious, since you have come here to settle our dispute.
m.2.1.9.26: Brahmā said: Hearing those words of his, Hara himself spoke again to Hari, who stood having bowed with his head, with palms joined.
m.2.1.9.27: Śrī Maheśa said: I am the maker of dissolution, preservation and creation; with attributes and without; the Supreme Brahman, changeless, characterized by being, consciousness and bliss.
m.2.1.9.28: O Viṣṇu, I am divided threefold under the names Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Hara, through the qualities of creation, protection and dissolution; yet I am always partless, O Hari.
m.2.1.9.29: Since I have been praised by you, O Viṣṇu, and by Brahmā, for my descent, I shall make that prayer come true, for I am loving toward devotees.
m.2.1.9.30: O Brahmā, a supreme form of mine, just like this, will become manifest in the world from your body, celebrated by the name Rudra.
m.2.1.9.31: Being from my portion, his power will not be any less. What I am, he is; there is no difference, even in the ordinance of the rite of worship.
m.2.1.9.32: Just as light, by its association with water and the like, does not truly come into contact with them, so for me too, being beyond attributes, there is no bondage through association.
m.2.1.9.33: This is my Śiva form, and Rudra too will then be like Śiva; no distinction of other should be made there, O great sage.
m.2.1.9.34: In reality it is of one form, though in the world it is divided in two; therefore no difference should ever be recognised between Śiva and Rudra.
m.2.1.9.35: Just as one and the same gold does not lose its substance when it is made into ornaments, O god, the difference is in name, not in substance.
m.2.1.9.36: Just as one clay's difference in various vessels is not real, so here; this is the illustration: in the effect there is nothing present but the cause itself.
m.2.1.9.37: This should be understood by the best of the wise, by those of pure knowledge, O gods; knowing thus, you two should see no ground for difference.
m.2.1.9.38: All that is seen, like the one substance, is held by me to be the form of Śiva: I, you, the Unborn Brahmā, and this Rudra who will come to be.
m.2.1.9.39: We are of one form; there is no difference, for in difference there would be bondage. Even so, my Śiva form is the eternal one,
m.2.1.9.40: the root of all, ever declared to be truth, knowledge and the infinite. Knowing thus, it should always be meditated upon in the mind, in its true nature.
m.2.1.9.41: And listen, O Brahmā, to what is being told by me, which is secret: you two have arisen from Prakṛti, but this one Rudra is not, again, from Prakṛti.
m.2.1.9.42: By my command I shall be born there from Brahmā's brow. Even among the guṇas, as it is declared, Hara is conventionally called tāmasa.
m.2.1.9.43: And he should be known as vaikārika, that which is spoken of as ahaṅkāra; only in name, not in reality, is he called tāmasa.
m.2.1.9.44: For this reason, O Brahmā, this is to be done by you: be the maker of creation, O Brahmā, and Hari shall be the protector of creation.
m.2.1.9.45: And likewise that portion of mine which will be the maker of dissolution. This goddess who is Prakṛti, called Umā, the supreme sovereign —
m.2.1.9.46: — her power, the goddess of speech, will attend upon Brahmā. Another power of Prakṛti will arise there again.
m.2.1.9.47: She will then take refuge with Viṣṇu in the form of Lakṣmī. And again she, by the name Kālī, will surely attain my portion.
m.2.1.9.48: She will arise there in the form of light for the sake of the task. Thus have the supreme, auspicious powers of the Goddess been declared.
m.2.1.9.49: Their task, in order, is surely that of creation, preservation and dissolution. They are portions of this Prakṛti, my beloved, O best of gods.
m.2.1.9.50: And you Viṣṇu, taking Lakṣmī as your support, should carry out the work here. And you, O Brahmā, having obtained the goddess of speech, a portion of Prakṛti,
m.2.1.9.51: should carry out here, with your whole heart, the work of creation at my direction. I, taking Kālī as support — the portion of my beloved, higher than the highest —
m.2.1.9.52: shall in the form of Rudra carry out dissolution, the supreme task. The world made up of the four varṇas, together surely with all the āśramas,
m.2.1.9.53: and with various other works — having accomplished these, you two will attain happiness. Endowed with knowledge and realisation, working for the good of the worlds,
m.2.1.9.54: be you, from today, the giver of liberation here in the world by my command. Whatever fruit there is in seeing me, that very fruit is in seeing you.
m.2.1.9.55: Thus a boon has been given to you today — truly, truly, there is no doubt. Viṣṇu is in my very heart, and I am in Viṣṇu's heart.
m.2.1.9.56: He who knows no difference between the two is dear to my mind. Hari is born from my left side; Vidhi Brahmā has arisen from my right side;
m.2.1.9.57: Rudra, the maker of the great dissolution, the soul of the universe, has arisen from my heart. O Viṣṇu, I am divided threefold, under the names Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Bhava,
m.2.1.9.58: performing creation, protection and dissolution through the three guṇas beginning with rajas. Śiva himself is distinct from the guṇas, beyond Prakṛti and Puruṣa,
m.2.1.9.59: the supreme Brahman, non-dual, eternal, infinite, complete, stainless. Inwardly tamas, outwardly sattva, is Hari, the protector of the three worlds.
m.2.1.9.60: Inwardly sattva, outwardly tamas, is Hara, the maker of the dissolution of the three worlds.
m.2.1.9.61: Rajas both inwardly and outwardly is Vidhi, the creator of the three worlds. Thus are the guṇas in the three gods; Śiva is declared to be distinct from the guṇas.
m.2.1.9.62: O Viṣṇu, lovingly protect this Grandsire, the maker of creation. By my command you will be worshipped in the three worlds.
m.2.1.9.63: Rudra alone will be the one to be served by you and by Vidhi too; for he is Śiva's full incarnation, the maker of the dissolution of the three worlds.
m.2.1.9.64: In the Pādma kalpa the Grandsire will be your son. Then you will see me, and he too, the lotus-born, will see me.
m.2.1.9.65: Having spoken thus and shown incomparable grace, Hara, the great lord, the master, lord of all, again spoke to Viṣṇu with great affection.
m.2.1.9.iti: Thus ends the ninth adhyāya, named The truth of Śiva, in the account of creation, in the first khaṇḍa of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.1.10.1: The Supreme Lord said: Hear another command of mine, O Hari, O Viṣṇu, you of good vows: you will always be honoured and worshipped in all the worlds.
m.2.1.10.2: Whenever sorrow arises in the world created by Brahmā, then you must be intent on destroying all sorrows.
m.2.1.10.3: I will give you help in every task, even an unbearable one. I will slay your enemies, who are hard to overcome and exceedingly fierce.
m.2.1.10.4: Taking up various incarnations, O Hari, spread your supreme fame in the world, and be intent on delivering beings.
m.2.1.10.5: I, Rudra, having the form of a guṇa, will always, with this body, accomplish the work of the worlds that is impossible for you; there is no doubt.
m.2.1.10.6: You are to be meditated upon by Rudra, and likewise Hara is to be meditated upon by you. Between you two—you and Rudra—there is no difference whatsoever.
m.2.1.10.7: In reality there is oneness, and likewise by my boon too, even in divine play, O great Viṣṇu—truly, truly, there is no doubt.
m.2.1.10.8: The man who, being a devotee of Rudra, reviles you—all his merit will quickly turn to ashes.
m.2.1.10.9: Because of his hatred toward you, O Puruṣottama, he will fall into hell by my command, O Viṣṇu—truly, truly, there is no doubt.
m.2.1.10.10: In this world, as giver of liberation to men and especially as giver of enjoyment, to be meditated upon and worshipped by devotees, exercise restraint and grace.
m.2.1.10.11: Having said this, he himself took me, the Creator, and Hari by the hand and said: Always be a helper in times of sorrow.
m.2.1.10.12: Be always the overseer of all, the bestower of devotion and liberation upon all, the best, the fulfiller of all desires.
m.2.1.10.13: By my command, be the very life-breath of all. In distress, O Hari, that Rudra, who is my own body, is indeed to be worshipped.
m.2.1.10.14: Whoever takes refuge in you surely takes refuge in me alone; and whoever sees a difference between us certainly falls into hell.
m.2.1.10.15: Now hear in particular the lifespan and strength of the three gods, Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Hara; no doubt should be entertained about this.
m.2.1.10.16: A thousand sets of four yugas is called a day of Brahmā, and his night is of equal length; this is his measure in due order.
m.2.1.10.17: Thirty of those days make a month, and twelve of those months a year; Brahmā's lifespan is declared to measure a hundred such years.
m.2.1.10.18: A single year of Brahmā is called a day of Viṣṇu; he too lives for a hundred years by his own measure.
m.2.1.10.19: A year of Viṣṇu is certainly a day of Rudra. When a hundred such years have passed, Hara remains established in human form.
m.2.1.10.20: He remains so as long as the out-breath arising from Sadāśiva is in his mouth; afterwards he goes into Śakti, until the in-breath occurs.
m.2.1.10.21: Of the inhalations and exhalations of all embodied beings—of Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Hara, and of Gandharvas, serpents and Rākṣasas—
m.2.1.10.22: —twenty-one thousand and six hundred are declared the measure of a day and night, O best of gods.
m.2.1.10.23: Six exhalations and inhalations make one pala; a ghaṭī is said to be sixty palas, and sixty of those make a day and night.
m.2.1.10.24: But of the inhalations and exhalations arising from Sadāśiva there is no counting; therefore he is held to be imperishable.
m.2.1.10.25: By my command you must preserve this form for that long, and for that long the work of creation must be carried out through the various guṇas.
m.2.1.10.26: Brahmā said: Having heard these words of Śambhu, Lord Hari, the self-controlled, together with me, bowed to the Lord of the universe and spoke very softly.
m.2.1.10.27: Viṣṇu said: O Śaṅkara, ocean of compassion, Lord of the world, please hear this: I shall do all this, following the authority of your command.
m.2.1.10.28: You will always be the object of my meditation, and never otherwise. All my power was obtained by me from you long ago.
m.2.1.10.29: O Master, may supreme meditation on you never depart far from my mind even for a moment.
m.2.1.10.30: And, O Master, whoever, being my devotee, reviles you—grant him, surely and without fail, a dwelling in hell.
m.2.1.10.31: O Master, whoever is your devotee is indeed dearer to me. For one who understands this, liberation is not hard to attain.
m.2.1.10.32: My greatness has surely been increased by you today. If ever some fault arises in me, may it be forgiven.
m.2.1.10.33: Brahmā said: Then Śambhu, having heard his excellent words, said to Viṣṇu with great affection: Your fault will be forgiven by me.
m.2.1.10.34: Having spoken thus, the Supreme Lord, the treasury of compassion, out of compassion touched both of us, Hari and me, on all our limbs with his hands.
m.2.1.10.35: Having taught various dharmas, Hara, the remover of all sorrows, gave us two many boons, wishing our welfare.
m.2.1.10.36: Then the Lord Śambhu, compassionate and loving to his devotees, quickly vanished right there while we two looked on with our eyes.
m.2.1.10.37: From then on, the rite of liṅga worship has been established in this world. Śambhu, established in the liṅga, bestows enjoyment and liberation.
m.2.1.10.38: The pedestal of the liṅga is the Great Goddess, and the liṅga is Maheśvara himself. It is called liṅga because of dissolution (layana), for in it the whole universe dissolves.
m.2.1.10.39: Whoever daily recites the narrative of the liṅga in the presence of a liṅga becomes of Śiva's form within six months; there should be no doubt about this.
m.2.1.10.40: And whoever performs any act at all near a liṅga—I cannot describe the fruit of his merit, O great sage.
m.2.1.10.iti: Thus ends the tenth adhyāya, named The supreme truth of Śiva, in the account of creation, in the first khaṇḍa of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.1.11.1: The sages said: O Sūta, O Sūta, most fortunate one, disciple of Vyāsa, salutation to you. Today you have made us hear the wondrous, supremely purifying story of Śiva.
m.2.1.11.2: In it we heard the wondrous, most divine and auspicious account of the origin of the liṅga, by hearing whose power the destruction of sorrow would come about here in this world.
m.2.1.11.3: O treasure of compassion, following the dialogue of Brahmā and Nārada, tell us the method of worshipping Śiva, by which Śiva becomes pleased.
m.2.1.11.4: Śiva is worshipped by brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas or śūdras; how should that worship be performed? Tell it as you heard it from the mouth of Vyāsa.
m.2.1.11.5: Having heard their words, which brought welfare and accorded with the Veda, he spoke everything with affection, in keeping with the sages' questions.
m.2.1.11.6: Sūta said: Well have you asked about that secret, O lords among sages. I shall tell it today according to my understanding and as I have heard it.
m.2.1.11.7: Just as it is asked by you, so it was formerly asked by Vyāsa of Sanatkumāra; and that was heard by Upamanyu.
m.2.1.11.8: Then whatever concerns the worship of Śiva and so on, having been heard by Vyāsa, was taught to me by him out of desire for the welfare of the worlds.
m.2.1.11.9: That was also heard by Kṛṣṇa from the great-souled Upamanyu. I shall tell it as Brahmā spoke it of old.
m.2.1.11.10: Brahmā said: Listen, Nārada, I shall describe the worship of the liṅga in brief; O sage, it cannot be told in detail even in a hundred years.
m.2.1.11.11: Thus one should worship, with supreme devotion, the form of Śaṅkara, blissful, pure and eternal, to obtain the fruit of all desires.
m.2.1.11.12: Poverty, the suffering of disease, affliction arising from enemies, and the fourfold sin persist only so long as one does not worship Śiva.
m.2.1.11.13: When the god Śiva is fully worshipped, all sorrow dissolves, every happiness comes about, and afterwards liberation is attained.
m.2.1.11.14: Whoever, having attained human birth, seeks the chief happiness that comes from progeny, by him Mahādeva, the accomplisher of all undertakings and aims, should be worshipped.
m.2.1.11.15: Brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas and śūdras should perform the worship of Śaṅkara according to rule and in due order, for the fulfilment of all desires and aims.
m.2.1.11.16: Rising in the early morning, in the period called Brāhma-muhūrta, one should remember the guru and then also Śambhu.
m.2.1.11.17: Having remembered the holy places and meditated on Hari too, and likewise on me, on the gods, and on the sages and others, O sage,
m.2.1.11.18: then one should take up a hymn and the names of Śambhu according to rule. Then, getting up, one should void excrement in the southern direction.
m.2.1.11.19: One should perform the rite of evacuation in a secluded place, as has been taught; that very thing I now describe—listen with attentive mind, O sage.
m.2.1.11.20: For purification a brāhmaṇa should apply pure earth five times; a kṣatriya four times, and a vaiśya likewise three times.
m.2.1.11.21: A śūdra should take earth twice for ritual purity—this at the anus; and on the genital organ once, a single time, with care.
m.2.1.11.22: Ten times on the left hand, seven times on both hands, dear one, on each foot three times, and again three times on the hands.
m.2.1.11.23: Women should perform the excellent taking of earth as a śūdra does. Having washed the hands and feet, one should take earth as before.
m.2.1.11.24: Then a man should use a tooth-stick according to the order of his own varṇa.
m.2.1.11.25: A brāhmaṇa should use a tooth-stick twelve finger-breadths in measure; a king, eleven finger-breadths; a vaiśya should use one of ten finger-breadths.
m.2.1.11.26: A śūdra should use one of nine finger-breadths—this is the measure laid down in tradition. Considering faults of time, one should avoid a stick defective in measure.
m.2.1.11.27: The sixth, the first and the new-moon days, the ninth, a vow-day, sunset, Sunday, and likewise the day of a śrāddha, dear one, are forbidden for cleaning the teeth.
m.2.1.11.28: Bathing should be done according to rule, in due order, at holy waters and the like; according to the particulars of place and time, the bath should be done with mantras.
m.2.1.11.29: Having first sipped water there, one should put on washed garments; then, staying in a secluded, pleasant spot, one should perform the rite of sandhyā.
m.2.1.11.30: Having performed the rite as is fitting, one should then begin the procedure of worship, making the mind quite steady and entering the worship-room.
m.2.1.11.31: Taking up the requisites of worship and sitting on one's own seat, one should first perform nyāsa and the rest, and then worship Hara in due order.
m.2.1.11.32: First, having duly worshipped the lord of the gaṇas, the door-keepers and likewise the guardians of the directions, one should afterwards arrange the seat of the deity.
m.2.1.11.33: Or else, having made an eight-petalled lotus, with the articles of worship close by, one should sit there and seat the Lord Śiva upon it.
m.2.1.11.34: Having sipped water three times and washed the hands again, and having done three prāṇāyāmas, one should meditate on the Three-eyed One in the centre.
m.2.1.11.35: He is five-faced, ten-armed, resembling pure crystal, adorned with all ornaments, with a tiger-skin as his upper garment.
m.2.1.11.36: Contemplating one's identity of form with him, a man should always burn away sin. Then, having raised up Śiva in meditation, one should worship the Supreme Lord.
m.2.1.11.37: Then, having performed purification of the body, one should place the root-mantra on the limbs in order, and everywhere perform the six-limbed nyāsa with the praṇava alone.
m.2.1.11.38: Having made the application in the heart, one should then begin the worship, and arrange vessels for water for the feet, arghya and ācamana.
m.2.1.11.39: The wise one should set up nine jars of various kinds according to rule, covering them with darbha grass, placing them on darbha and sprinkling them with water.
m.2.1.11.40: Into each and every one of them he should pour very cool water; and the intelligent one, examining the substances, should put them into them with the praṇava.
m.2.1.11.41: He should place vetiver (uśīra) and sandal in the foot-water (pādya). Jasmine, kaṅkola, camphor, banyan root and tamāla —
m.2.1.11.42: having powdered these properly, he should put them into the water for sipping (ācamanīya). He should have this, mixed with sandal, placed in all the vessels.
m.2.1.11.43: On both sides of the God of gods he should worship Nandīśa. With perfumes, incense and various lamps he should worship Śiva.
m.2.1.11.44: Then, having purified the liṅga, the man, filled with joy, should proceed as is fitting with a multitude of mantras beginning with the praṇava and ending with namaḥ.
m.2.1.11.45: he should conceive the seat — svastika, lotus and the like — with the praṇava. From it, the eastern petal is the imperishable power consisting of aṇimā itself;
m.2.1.11.46: laghimā is the southern, mahimā likewise the western, prāpti the northern petal, and prākāmya the petal of Pāvaka (south-east);
m.2.1.11.47: īśitva is the south-western petal, vaśitva in the region of Vāyu (north-west), and sarvajñatva likewise the north-eastern; the pericarp is said to be Soma (the moon).
m.2.1.11.48: Below the moon is the sun, and below it this fire; below that too he should conceive, in order, Dharma and the rest for Bhava's seat.
m.2.1.11.49: He should conceive Avyakta and the rest in the four directions, and the three guṇas at the edge of the moon. Having invoked the Supreme Lord with sadyojātaṃ prapadyāmi,
m.2.1.11.50: with the Vāmadeva mantra he should make him stay upon the seat; with the Rudra-gāyatrī secure his presence, and with the Aghora mantra he should fix him there.
m.2.1.11.51: He should worship with the mantra īśānaḥ sarvavidyānām. Having offered water for the feet and for sipping, he should present the arghya.
m.2.1.11.52: He should duly bathe Rudra with water mixed with perfume and sandal, and, according to the rule of the pañcagavya, having consecrated it with mantras in a household vessel,
m.2.1.11.53: with the praṇava alone he should bathe him with cow's milk, with curd, with honey, and with sugarcane juice,
m.2.1.11.54: and likewise with ghee, bathing the Worshipful One who brings the welfare of all desires; with holy substances he should anoint Mahādeva with the praṇava.
m.2.1.11.55: Then he should pour water with mantras into the pure water-vessels. Having purified it properly with a white cloth, the practitioner —
m.2.1.11.56: should not put it away until he has applied the sandal. Then there he should joyfully worship Śaṅkara with beautiful rice grains,
m.2.1.11.57: with kuśa, apāmārga, camphor, jasmine, campaka and pāṭala, with white karavīra, with mallikā, lotuses and water-lilies,
m.2.1.11.58: with various rare flowers, and likewise with sandal and the rest. With water he should arrange a stream of water upon the Supreme Lord.
m.2.1.11.59: With various vessels he should bathe the god Maheśvara. Worship, which grants all fruits, should be performed preceded by mantras.
m.2.1.11.60: Those mantras, dear one, for the accomplishment of all desires and aims, I shall tell you briefly; listen attentively.
m.2.1.11.61: With the Pavamāna mantra, and with the Vāṅmaya, with the Rudra, the Nīlarudra, the auspicious Suśukla,
m.2.1.11.62: with the Hotāra, likewise the Śīrṣa, the auspicious Atharvaṇa, the Śānti and again the Śānti, with the Bhāruṇḍa and the Aruṇa,
m.2.1.11.63: with the Arthābhīṣṭa sāman and likewise with the Devavrata,
m.2.1.11.64: with the Rathantara, the Puṣpa hymn and the Puruṣa hymn, with the Mṛtyuñjaya mantra and likewise with the Five-syllabled mantra —
m.2.1.11.65: the streams of water should be made a thousand times or a hundred and one, in the Vedic manner, or else with the divine names.
m.2.1.11.66: Then sandal, flowers and the rest should be placed upon Śiva; likewise with the praṇava he should offer mouth-perfume and the like.
m.2.1.11.67: Then the god resembling crystal, partless, imperishable, the cause of all worlds, consisting of all worlds, supreme,
m.2.1.11.68: beyond the reach even of the gods Brahmā, Indra, Upendra, Viṣṇu and others — indeed declared by the knowers of the Veda in the Vedānta to be beyond perception,
m.2.1.11.69: without beginning, middle or end, the medicine for all the sick, renowned as the Śiva-principle — this Śivaliṅga established there,
m.2.1.11.70: he should worship on the top of the liṅga with the praṇava mantra alone, with incense, lamps, food-offerings and beautiful betel,
m.2.1.11.71: then with a lovely waving of lights (nīrājana) according to the prescribed rule, with salutations, hymns and other mantras of various kinds.
m.2.1.11.72: Having offered arghya, scattered flowers at his feet and bowed down to the Lord of gods, he should worship Śiva with his whole self.
m.2.1.11.73: Taking flowers in hand, rising up with joined palms, he should again entreat Īśāna, Śaṅkara, with this mantra:
m.2.1.11.74: Whether out of ignorance or knowingly, whatever japa, worship and the like has been done by me, may it bear fruit by your grace, O Śaṅkara.
m.2.1.11.75: Having recited thus, he should joyfully place the flowers on Śiva. Then, having performed the svastyayana rite and likewise various blessings,
m.2.1.11.76: then the sprinkling (mārjana) should again be done over Śiva; then salutation, the asking of forgiveness, and the request for his coming again.
m.2.1.11.77: Uttering the Aghora mantra, he should make salutation, and there he should pray again with all his heart:
m.2.1.11.78: Devotion to Śiva, devotion to Śiva, devotion to Śiva, birth after birth. There is no other refuge; you alone are my refuge.
m.2.1.11.79: Having thus entreated the Lord of gods, the bestower of all accomplishments, he should worship him with supreme devotion, especially with sounds from the throat.
