m.2.1.19.15: Hearing these words of his, Umā's lord, the god of gods, touched him with his palm and gave him the power of sight.
m.2.1.19.16: Opening wide his eyes, he first looked at Umā alone. Then this son of Yajñadatta, having gained that power, thought:
m.2.1.19.17: Who is this woman beside Śambhu, beautiful in every limb? What austerity has she performed, greater even than mine?
m.2.1.19.18: Ah, what beauty! Ah, what love! Ah, what good fortune and splendour, exceedingly! So this son spoke again and again, intensely.
m.2.1.19.19: As he kept staring with an unkind gaze, repeating this again and again, his left eye burst from looking at the lovely lady.
m.2.1.19.20: Then the Goddess said to the god: What is this wicked ascetic saying, looking at me again and again? Tell me the power of his austerity.
m.2.1.19.21: Again and again, with his right eye, he looks at me alone, envious of my wealth of beauty, love and good fortune.
m.2.1.19.22: Hearing the Goddess's words, the Lord laughed and said to her: Umā, this is your son; he does not, with a cruel eye,
m.2.1.19.23: look at you; rather he would extol the splendour of your austerity. Having thus addressed the Goddess, the Lord spoke to him again:
m.2.1.19.24: I give you boons, child, pleased by this austerity. Be the master of the treasures and lord of the Guhyakas.
m.2.1.19.25: Be king of the Yakṣas and Kinnaras, king of kings, O you of good vows, lord of the Puṇyajanas, and giver of wealth to all.
m.2.1.19.26: You shall have constant friendship with me, and I shall dwell near you, close to Alakā, O friend, to increase your joy.
m.2.1.19.27: Come, fall at her feet, for she is your mother, O son of Yajñadatta, great devotee, with a fully gladdened heart.
m.2.1.19.28: Brahmā said: Having given these boons, god Śiva again spoke to Śivā: O Queen of the gods, show favour here to this ascetic, your son.
m.2.1.19.29: Hearing Śambhu's words, Pārvatī, Mother of the world, spoke to that son of Yajñadatta with a fully gladdened heart.
m.2.1.19.30: The Goddess said: Child, may your pure devotion to Bhava last forever. Be one-eyed-tawny (Ekapiṅga) by your burst left eye.
m.2.1.19.31: May the boons the god has given you be just so. Be Kubera by name, son, on account of your envy of my beauty.
m.2.1.19.32: Having thus given boons to Dhanada, the god Maheśvara, together with the Goddess, then entered the abode called Vaiśveśvara.
m.2.1.19.33: In this way Dhanada attained friendship with the glorious Śambhu, and near the city of Alakā stood Kailāsa, the abode of Śaṅkara.
m.2.1.19.iti: Thus ends the nineteenth adhyāya, named Kubera's friendship with Śiva, in the account of the going to Kailāsa, in the first khaṇḍa of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.1.20.1: Brahmā said: O Nārada, O sage, listen to the account of Śiva's excellent coming to Kailāsa, the best of mountains, brought about by the power of Kubera's penance.
m.2.1.20.2: Having granted Kubera the boon of lordship over the treasures and having gone to his own excellent abode, the Lord of the universe, the bestower of boons on Kubera, reflected in his heart:
m.2.1.20.3: Rudra, born from the body of Vidhi (Brahmā), is my own complete form, the one who performs the work of dissolution. In that form I shall go to Kailāsa, the abode of the Guhyakas.
m.2.1.20.4: Rudra, born of my heart, is indeed my complete portion, the partless Brahman, to be worshipped by Hari, Brahmā and others, not different from me, stainless.
m.2.1.20.5: In that form, becoming Kubera's friend, I, the sportive one, shall dwell right there and shall perform great penance.
m.2.1.20.6: Having thus reflected on Śiva's wish, that Rudra, eager to go, sounded there his own drum (ḍhakkā), of auspicious movement, whose very form is sound.
m.2.1.20.7: Its sound pervaded the three worlds, rousing enthusiasm, carrying the force of a summons, wondrous and densely resonant.
m.2.1.20.8: Hearing that, the gods headed by Viṣṇu and Brahmā, and likewise the sages, the Āgamas and Nigamas in embodied form, and the Siddhas went there.
m.2.1.20.9: All the gods, demons and others went there joyfully; all the Pramathas too went, wherever they had been stationed.
m.2.1.20.10: And so did the illustrious leaders of the Gaṇas, revered by all the worlds. I shall tell their number; listen attentively.
m.2.1.20.11: The Gaṇa-lord Śaṅkhakarṇa came with a crore of Gaṇas; Kekarākṣa with ten crores, and Vikṛta with eight.
m.2.1.20.12: Viśākha with sixty-four, Pāriyātraka with nine, the glorious Sarvāntaka with six, and Dundubha with eight.
m.2.1.20.13: Jālaṅka, the foremost of Gaṇas, with twelve crores; the glorious Samada with seven, and likewise Vikṛtānana.
m.2.1.20.14: Kapālī with five, the auspicious Sandāraka with six, and here Kaṇḍuka and Kuṇḍaka with crores upon crores.
m.2.1.20.15: Viṣṭambha came with eight, and Candratāpana with eight.
m.2.1.20.16: The Gaṇa-lord Mahākeśa came, surrounded by a thousand crores.
m.2.1.20.17: Kuṇḍī with twelve, likewise Vāha and the auspicious Parvataka; Kāla, Kālaka and Mahākāla with a hundred.
m.2.1.20.18: Agnika with a hundred crores, Abhimukha with a crore, Ādityamūrdhā with a crore, and likewise Dhanāvaha.
m.2.1.20.19: Sannāha with a hundred, Kumuda likewise with crores; Amogha, Kokila and Sumantraka with crores of crores.
m.2.1.20.20: Another, Kākapāda, with sixty; lord Santānaka with sixty; Mahābala with nine, and Madhupiṅga and Piṅgala.
m.2.1.20.21: Nīla with ninety came to the Lord of gods, and likewise Pūrṇabhadra; and the mighty Caturvaktra with seven crores.
m.2.1.20.22: Surrounded by twenty hundreds of thousands of crores of crores, the lord of all Gaṇas came there for the journey to Kailāsa.
m.2.1.20.23: Kāṣṭhāgūḍha with sixty-four, likewise Sukeśa and Vṛṣabha; Caitra with seven crores, and Nakulīśa, the lord himself.
m.2.1.20.24: Lokāntaka, of radiant self, and likewise lord Daityāntaka; the divine Bhṛṅgī, the glorious Riṭi, and Devadevapriya.
m.2.1.20.25: Aśani and Bhānuka, and Sanātana with sixty-four; and Nandīśvara, the mighty overlord of the Gaṇas, with a hundred crores.
m.2.1.20.26: These and other mighty Gaṇa-leaders, countless—all thousand-armed and bearing crowns of matted hair—
m.2.1.20.27: all with the moon as crest-ornament, blue-throated, three-eyed, adorned with necklaces, earrings, armlets, crowns and the like,
m.2.1.20.28: resembling Brahmā, Indra and Viṣṇu, attended by the hosts of powers such as aṇimā, shining like ten million suns—these Gaṇa-lords came there.
m.2.1.20.29: These and other great-souled Gaṇa-chiefs of spotless splendour went there with great delight, longing to see Śiva.
m.2.1.20.30: Having gone there and seen Śiva, they bowed and offered supreme praise—all of them, headed by Viṣṇu, with joined palms and bowed heads.
m.2.1.20.31: Thus, together with Viṣṇu and the others, Maheśa, the supreme Lord, went to Kailāsa out of affection for the great-souled Kubera.
m.2.1.20.32: Kubera too, together with his retinue, worshipped Śambhu who had arrived, reverently, with devotion and with various offerings.
m.2.1.20.33: Then he also duly honoured the gods headed by Viṣṇu and the other Gaṇas, the followers of Śiva, in order to please Śiva.
m.2.1.20.34: Then Śambhu, delighted at heart, embraced Kubera and, smelling his head affectionately, stayed near Alakā with all his followers.
m.2.1.20.35: The Lord commanded Viśvakarman to build on the mountain dwellings for his various devotees, as befitting his own and others.
m.2.1.20.36: Then Viśvakarman, O sage, went there and swiftly constructed works of many kinds at Śambhu's command.
m.2.1.20.37: Then Śambhu, delighted, at the request of Hari,
m.2.1.20.38: having bestowed his grace on Kubera, went to Mount Kailāsa. At an auspicious moment that supreme Lord entered his own abode,
m.2.1.20.39: and he, affectionate to his devotees, lovingly made all of them protected. Then all the gods headed by Viṣṇu, delighted, and the sages and other Siddhas joyfully consecrated Śiva.
m.2.1.20.40: All of them, with various gifts in their hands, worshipped him in turn, and performed the waving of lights (nīrājana) accompanied by a great festival.
m.2.1.20.41: Then, O sage, there was a shower of flowers, the abode of auspiciousness; and the celestial nymphs, greatly delighted and intent on singing, danced there.
m.2.1.20.42: Cries of victory and salutation, uttered by all, arose there. Then there was a great festivity that increased everyone's happiness.
m.2.1.20.43: Seated on the throne, Śambhu then shone all the more, constantly attended by all, by Viṣṇu and the others, as was fitting.
m.2.1.20.44: Then all the gods and others praised him, Śaṅkara, the benefactor of the worlds, each separately, with meaningful and pleasing words.
m.2.1.20.45: Hearing the praise, Śiva, pleased at heart, the Lord of all, the master, lovingly granted them their desires, the boons longed for in their minds.
m.2.1.20.46: Then, O sage, at Śiva's command, all of them, their desires fulfilled and delighted, went each to his own abode; and I too stayed with Viṣṇu.
m.2.1.20.47: Having seated Viṣṇu and me on a seat, Śambhu, the supreme Lord, addressing us at length and blessing us with great affection, spoke.
m.2.1.20.48: Śiva said: O Hari, O Vidhi (Brahmā), dear ones, you two are most beloved to me, the best of gods, ever the protector and creator of the three worlds.
m.2.1.20.49: Go fearlessly to your own abodes at my command, forever. I am indeed the giver of happiness to you both, and always especially watch over you.
m.2.1.20.50: Hearing these words of Śambhu, bowing deeply, at his command Hari and I went to our own abodes, gladdened in mind.
m.2.1.20.51: Right then the greatly pleased Śaṅkara joyfully seated the lord of treasures (Kubera), and, taking him by the hand, spoke auspicious words.
m.2.1.20.52: Won over by your love, friend, I have entered into friendship with you. Go fearlessly to your own place; I am always your helper, O sinless one.
m.2.1.20.53: Hearing these words of Śambhu, Kubera, gladdened in mind and full of joy, went to his own abode at his command.
m.2.1.20.54: That Śambhu dwelt on Mount Kailāsa, the best of mountains, with his attendants, devoted to yoga, free, and intent on meditation.
m.2.1.20.55: At times he meditated on his own Self; at times he was absorbed in yoga; with a free mind he lovingly narrated ancient tales to the gaṇas.
m.2.1.20.56: At times Maheśvara, skilled in sport, joyfully roamed with the gaṇas in the various lovely spots of Mount Kailāsa.
m.2.1.20.57: Thus that Śaṅkara, the supreme Lord in the form of Rudra, though the foremost of yogins, performed various sports on his own mountain.
m.2.1.20.58: Having spent some time without a wife, the supreme Lord afterwards obtained his own wife, born of Dakṣa's wife.
m.2.1.20.59: Maheśvara sported with her, Satī, the daughter of Dakṣa, and became happy, O divine sage, devoted to worldly conduct.
m.2.1.20.60: Thus, O lord of sages, this incarnation of Rudra has been described to you, and his coming to Kailāsa, and indeed his friendship with the lord of treasures.
m.2.1.20.61: The sport contained within it has also been described, which increases knowledge and which always grants the fruit of all desires here and hereafter.
m.2.1.20.62: Whoever reads this story or listens to it attentively attains enjoyment here and obtains liberation in the next world.
m.2.1.20.iti: Thus ends the twentieth adhyāya, named Śiva goes to Kailāsa, in the account of Kailāsa within the account of creation, in the first khaṇḍa of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.2.1.1: Nārada said: O Vidhi (Brahmā), by the grace of Śaṅkara you know everything. Wonderful and auspicious stories of Śiva and Śivā have indeed been told to me by you.
m.2.2.1.2: Having heard the supreme story of Śiva that came forth from your lotus-mouth, I am still not satisfied; O lord, I wish to hear it again.
m.2.2.1.3: O Vidhi, that Rudra whom you described earlier as the full portion of Śaṅkara himself — the great lord, dwelling on Kailāsa, self-controlled —
m.2.2.1.4: he, the yogin, to be served by all the gods headed by Viṣṇu, the refuge of the good, free from the pairs of opposites, ever sports, unchanging, the great lord.
m.2.2.1.5: And he again became a householder, having gladly married, at Hari's request, the supreme woman, auspicious and rich in austerity.
m.2.2.1.6: First she was Dakṣa's daughter, afterwards she was the mountain's daughter. How, with a single body, is she regarded as the daughter of both?
m.2.2.1.7: How did Satī, as Pārvatī, come back to Śiva again? O Brahman, please tell all this and whatever else there is.
m.2.2.1.8: Sūta said: Having heard these words of that divine sage, whose soul was devoted to Śaṅkara, Brahmā, pleased in mind, spoke.
m.2.2.1.9: Brahmā said: Listen, dear one, best of sages: I shall tell the auspicious story, by hearing which one's birth becomes fruitful — there is no doubt.
m.2.2.1.10: Long ago, dear one, on seeing my own daughter named Sandhyā, I, together with my sons, became agitated, tormented by the arrows of Kāma.
m.2.2.1.11: Then, when Dharma called him to mind, Rudra — the great yogin, the supreme lord — came, and having rebuked me along with my sons, dear one, he went back to his own abode.
m.2.2.1.12: Deluded by his māyā, I — the speaker of the Vedas, yet dull-minded — therefore acted improperly toward the supreme lord Śambhu.
m.2.2.1.13: Out of jealousy of him, I, foolish and deluded by Śiva's māyā, devised with my sons many means to bring about his infatuation.
m.2.2.1.14: Then all those means, both theirs and mine too, O lord of sages, proved fruitless against that Śambhu, the supreme lord.
m.2.2.1.15: Then, my means having failed, I with my sons remembered the lord of Ramā (Viṣṇu); he, wise and devoted to Śiva, came and enlightened us.
m.2.2.1.16: Enlightened by the lord of Ramā, who revealed the truth of Śiva, I gave up my jealousy of him; yet, deluded, I did not give up that obstinacy.
m.2.2.1.17: Having worshipped Śakti, through her favour I then caused her to be born, for the enchanting of Hara, from my son Dakṣa in his wife Asiknī Vīriṇī.
m.2.2.1.18: She, Umā, having become Dakṣa's daughter and performed austerity hard to endure, became through devotion the wife of Rudra — she who works the welfare of her devotees.
m.2.2.1.19: The lord Rudra, together with Umā, having become a householder, performed a supreme play; and there at his own wedding he, unchanging in mind, deluded me.
m.2.2.1.20: Having married her and come to his own mountain, he, the maker of creation, sported with her — he who enchants many, independent, having assumed a form by his own will.
m.2.2.1.21: As he sported with her, O sage, a long and happy time passed for Śambhu, the unchanging one who delights in the good.
m.2.2.1.22: Then, by Rudra's own will, rivalry arose between Rudra and Dakṣa, who was greatly foolish, deluded by his māyā, and very proud.
m.2.2.1.23: Under its influence Dakṣa, exceedingly arrogant, his mind deluded and greatly bewildered, reviled Hara, the supremely calm and unchanging.
m.2.2.1.24: Then Dakṣa himself, proud, performed a sacrifice without Hara, having invited all the gods and others, Viṣṇu and me — he being the lord of all.
m.2.2.1.25: Being in that state, overcome with anger, he did not invite Rudra; likewise, deluded by fate, he did not invite there his own daughter named Satī.
m.2.2.1.26: When she was not invited by her father, whose mind was deluded by māyā, then Śivā, the all-knowing and supremely chaste, performed a play.
m.2.2.1.27: Then Satī, having obtained Śiva's permission, went there to her father's house, though uninvited by proud Dakṣa.
m.2.2.1.28: Seeing no share for Rudra and receiving contempt from her father, she rebuked them all there and then gave up her body.
m.2.2.1.29: Hearing that, the lord of the gods of gods, becoming unbearably angry, tore out a great matted lock and produced Vīrabhadra.
m.2.2.1.30: Having produced him together with his troops, as he asked what he should do, Śiva commanded the destruction of the sacrifice, preceded by the humiliation of all.
m.2.2.1.31: That lord of the gaṇas, having received his command, endowed with great forces, of mighty strength and valour, went there swiftly and at once.
m.2.2.1.32: At his command the gaṇas wrought great havoc there; he punished everyone, and no one was spared.
m.2.2.1.33: Having with effort defeated Viṣṇu together with the gods, the best of gaṇas cut off Dakṣa's head and offered that head into the fire.
m.2.2.1.34: Wreaking great havoc, he swiftly destroyed the sacrifice; then he went to his own mountain and bowed to the lord Śiva.
m.2.2.1.35: Thus the destruction of the sacrifice took place while the world of the gods looked on, carried out there by Rudra's attendants, Vīrabhadra and the others.
m.2.2.1.36: O sage, this principle should be understood, accepted in the Śrutis and Smṛtis: when Rudra, the good lord, is angered, how can there be happiness in the world?
m.2.2.1.37: Then Rudra became pleased on hearing that supreme hymn of praise; compassionate to the afflicted, he made the petition of all fruitful.
m.2.2.1.38: And as before, compassion was shown by that great-souled Śaṅkara, the great lord who sports in manifold plays.
m.2.2.1.39: By him Dakṣa was restored to life, and all there were honoured; and the sacrifice was caused to be performed again by the compassionate Śaṅkara.
m.2.2.1.40: And Rudra was especially worshipped there in the sacrifice with devotion by all the gods, headed by Viṣṇu, whose hearts were fully gladdened, O sage.
m.2.2.1.41: The flame that arose from Satī's body, bringing happiness to the worlds, fell there upon a mountain; worshipped there, it bestows happiness.
m.2.2.1.42: She became the supreme goddess renowned as Jvālāmukhī, granting the fruits of all desires, who removes sins merely by being seen.
m.2.2.1.43: Even now she is worshipped in the world, with many rites and accompanied by great festivals, for the attainment of the fruits of all desires.
m.2.2.1.44: And thereafter that goddess Satī became the daughter of Himālaya, and then her name became famous as Pārvatī.
m.2.2.1.45: And she, having again propitiated him through severe austerity, took that very Supreme Lord as her husband.
m.2.2.1.46: All this that I was asked about, O lord of sages, has been narrated; hearing it, one is freed from all sins; there is no doubt about this.
m.2.2.1.iti: Thus ends the first adhyāya, named A brief account of the life of Satī, in the second khaṇḍa, the Satī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.2.2.1: Sūta said: O dwellers of the Naimiṣa forest, having heard his words thus, the best of sages Nārada asked Brahmā for the story that destroys sin.
m.2.2.2.2: Nārada said: O Vidhi, O Vidhi, most fortunate one, though I keep hearing the auspicious story of Śambhu from the lotus of your mouth, I am not satisfied, O great lord.
m.2.2.2.3: Therefore tell all of it — the auspicious, divine life-story of Śiva joined with the glory of Satī; I wish to hear it, O maker of the universe.
m.2.2.2.4: How indeed was the lovely Satī born of Dakṣa's wife? How did Hara set his mind on the act of taking a wife?
m.2.2.2.5: And how did Satī, who long ago gave up her body because of anger at Dakṣa, come to be born again as the daughter of Himavat, or how did she reach the sky realm?
m.2.2.2.6: And how did Pārvatī's most severe austerity and her marriage come about? How did she come to dwell in half the body of the destroyer of Smara?
m.2.2.2.7: Relate all this in detail, O great-minded one. There is no other dispeller of doubts, nor will there be one equal to you.
m.2.2.2.8: Brahmā said: Listen, O sage, to the whole auspicious glory of Satī and Śiva — purifying, supreme, divine, the most secret of secrets, the highest.
m.2.2.2.9: Long ago Śambhu told this to Viṣṇu, the foremost of devotees, when asked by him with great devotion for the benefit of others, O sage.
m.2.2.2.10: Then that wise Viṣṇu, best of Śiva's devotees, being asked by me, lovingly narrated it to me in detail, O best of sages.
m.2.2.2.11: I shall tell you this ancient story, filled with the glory of Śivā and Śiva, which grants the fruit of all desires.
m.2.2.2.12: Long ago, when the god Śiva — without attributes, beyond all distinctions, formless, devoid of Śakti, pure consciousness, beyond existent and non-existent —
m.2.2.2.13: — became endowed with attributes, the Lord took a twofold form, possessed of Śakti, together with Umā (sa-uma), of divine form, O brahmin, changeless, higher than the highest.
m.2.2.2.14: From his left side Viṣṇu was born; I, Brahmā, was born from his right side; and Rudra was born from his heart, O best of sages.
m.2.2.2.15: I, Brahmā, became the creator; Viṣṇu the preserver; Rudra himself the dissolver — thus Sadāśiva became threefold.
m.2.2.2.16: Having worshipped him alone, I, Brahmā, grandsire of the worlds, created all those beings — gods, demons, humans and the rest.
m.2.2.2.17: Having created the Prajāpatis headed by Dakṣa, the best of the gods, I, greatly pleased, regarded myself as the most exalted of all.
m.2.2.2.18: Marīci, Atri, Pulaha, Pulastya and Aṅgiras, Kratu, Vasiṣṭha, Nārada, Dakṣa and Bhṛgu — these great lords —
m.2.2.2.19: When I, Brahmā, created these mind-born sons, O sage, then from my mind was born a beautiful woman of lovely form.
m.2.2.2.20: She was Sandhyā by name — the close of day, the evening twilight, the time of muttered prayer (japantikā) — exceedingly beautiful, with fine brows, bewildering the minds of sages.
m.2.2.2.21: Neither in the world of the gods, nor among mortals, nor in Rasātala, nor in all three times, is there any woman like her, so fully endowed with virtues.
m.2.2.2.22: Seeing her, I rose up, brooding in my heart on her who had entered my heart; and so did Dakṣa and the other creators, and Marīci and the rest, my sons.
m.2.2.2.23: While I, Brahmā, was thinking thus, O best of sages, a charming, most wondrous mind-born man appeared.
m.2.2.2.24: He had the lustre of refined gold, a full chest, a fine nose, well-rounded thighs, hips and shanks, and dark curling hair.
m.2.2.2.25: His pair of brows met together; he was restless, his face like the full moon, his fine chest broad as a door-panel, adorned with a line of hair.
m.2.2.2.26: His form was like that of the cloud-elephant; he was stout, wearing fine dark-blue garments, with reddish palms, eyes, face, feet and fingers.
m.2.2.2.27: Slender-waisted, with lovely teeth, smelling like an elephant in rut, with eyes like the petals of a full-blown lotus, delighting the nose like kesara blossoms.
m.2.2.2.28: Conch-necked, with the fish as his emblem, tall, with the makara as his mount, bearing five flower-arrows, swift, adorned with a bow of flowers.
m.2.2.2.29: Handsome, rolling his two eyes with sidelong glances, accompanied by a fragrant breeze, dear one, and attended by the sentiment of love (śṛṅgāra).
m.2.2.2.30: Seeing that man, all my sons, Dakṣa and the others, became extremely eager, their minds filled with amazement.
m.2.2.2.31: Quickly the minds of those sons of mine became disturbed; dear one, with their hearts agitated by desire they could not keep their composure.
m.2.2.2.32: That man too, seeing me, Vedhas, the creator and lord of the worlds, bowed and spoke, his neck bent in humility.
m.2.2.2.33: The being said: What work shall I do, O Brahman? Appoint me to it, since a person who has a task is honoured today, fitting and resplendent, O Vidhi.
m.2.2.2.34: Tell me my identity (abhimāna), my fitting place, and who will be my wife, O lord of the three worlds, for you are the creator and lord of the worlds.
m.2.2.2.35: Brahmā said: Hearing these words of that great-souled man, the creator, greatly astonished, said nothing for a moment.
m.2.2.2.36: Then, firmly restraining his mind and fully setting aside his amazement, Brahmā spoke to the man, fulfilling that wish of his.
m.2.2.2.37: Brahmā said: With this form of yours and your five flower-arrows, enchanting men and women, carry on the eternal creation.
m.2.2.2.38: In these three worlds with their moving and unmoving beings, all these creatures, gods and the rest, will be unable to transgress you.
m.2.2.2.39: Even I, or Vāsudeva, or Sthāṇu, O best of men, shall be under your sway — what then of other living beings?
m.2.2.2.40: In hidden form, ever entering the hearts of creatures, becoming yourself the cause of their pleasure, carry on the eternal creation.
m.2.2.2.41: The mind, wondrous as it is, is always an easy target for your flower-arrows; you are ever and constantly the cause of intoxication for all living beings.
m.2.2.2.42: Thus your function, which sets creation in motion, has been told to you. Now these sons of mine will tell you your names truly.
m.2.2.2.43: Brahmā said: Having said this, O best of gods, and having looked at the faces of my own sons, I sat down for a moment on my lotus seat.
m.2.2.2.iti: Thus ends the second adhyāya, named The appearance of Kāma, in the second khaṇḍa, the Satī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.2.3.1: Brahmā said: Then all those sages, my sons headed by Marīci, who understood my intention, gave him a fitting name.
m.2.2.3.2: Having learned the situation merely by looking at my face, and from other signs, Dakṣa and the other creators gave him a place and a wife.
m.2.2.3.3: Then, having settled on the names, the twice-born headed by Marīci, my sons, spoke fittingly to this being.
m.2.2.3.4: The sages said: Since, as soon as you were born, you agitate that mind of ours, as also of the Creator, therefore you will be famed in the world by the name Manmatha.
m.2.2.3.5: In the worlds you assume forms at will; none equal to you exists. Therefore, O Manobhava, be famed also by the name Kāma.
m.2.2.3.6: From intoxicating (madana) you are called Madana; being born of pride (darpa), you are full of pride; therefore you will be famed in the world also by the name Kandarpa.
m.2.2.3.7: Since the might of all the gods will not be equal to yours, therefore all places are your domain; hence you are all-pervading.
m.2.2.3.8: This Dakṣa, who is the first Prajāpati, will himself give you a charming wife as you wish, O best of beings.
m.2.2.3.9: And this maiden of lovely form, born from Brahmā's mind, will be renowned in the whole world by the name Sandhyā.
m.2.2.3.10: Since this fair lady was born perfectly from Brahmā as he meditated (sam-dhyā), she is renowned as Sandhyā, of captivating radiance, like the jasmine.
m.2.2.3.11: Brahmā said: Then Manobhava, taking up his five flowery weapons, with his form concealed, pondered his resolve right there.
m.2.2.3.12: Harṣaṇa, the one called Rocana, Mohana, Śoṣaṇa, and Māraṇa—so they are named, able to delude even a sage.
m.2.2.3.13: The eternal task that Brahmā has assigned to me I shall perform right here, in the presence of the sages and of the Creator.
m.2.2.3.14: The sages are standing here, and Prajāpati himself too; today they will be witnesses of my resolve.
m.2.2.3.15: And Sandhyā too, spoken of by Brahmā, is here; now let my word be sent forth. Testing my work right here, I shall delude them by applying my arrows.
m.2.2.3.16: Brahmā said: Having thus pondered in his mind and resolved, Manobhava fitted his flower-born bow with flower-born arrows.
m.2.2.3.17: Taking the ālīḍha stance and drawing the bow with effort, Kāma, best of archers, then bent it into the shape of a ring.
m.2.2.3.18: When he had set the arrow on the bow, fragrant breezes blew there, O best of sages, thoroughly delightful.
m.2.2.3.19: Then the Deluder deluded them all—the Creator and the others, and all the mind-born sons—each separately with sharp flower-arrows.
m.2.2.3.20: Then all those sages were deluded, and I too, O sage; joined with them in mind, they experienced some agitation from the very outset.
m.2.2.3.21: All of them, gazing at Sandhyā again and again with agitation, became inflamed with passion, since a woman is the kindler of passion.
m.2.2.3.22: Then Madana, deluding them all again and again, made them such that they reached agitation of the senses.
m.2.2.3.23: When I, the Creator, with senses aroused, looked at her, at that very moment forty-nine feelings (bhāvas) arose from my body.
m.2.2.3.24: And she too, being gazed at by them, owing to the fall of Kandarpa's arrows, displayed again and again gestures such as sidelong glances and covering herself.
m.2.2.3.25: Sandhyā, naturally beautiful, making those gestures born of the mind-born god, shone exceedingly, like the celestial river with gentle ripples.
m.2.2.3.26: Then, seeing Sandhyā full of these gestures, I, Prajāpati, my body filled with passion, conceived desire, O sage.
m.2.2.3.27: Then all those sages headed by Marīci and Atri, and Dakṣa and the rest, O best of the twice-born, came to have agitated senses.
m.2.2.3.28: Seeing Dakṣa, Marīci and the rest, and me, and Sandhyā in such a state, Madana then gained confidence in his own work.
m.2.2.3.29: This task that Brahmā assigned to me can indeed be accomplished by me: so the self-born Kāma then firmly concluded.
m.2.2.3.30: Seeing thus the sinful course of his brothers and likewise of his father, Dharma then remembered Śambhu, the Lord who protects dharma.
m.2.2.3.31: Remembering in his mind Śaṅkara, guardian of dharma, Dharma, son of the Unborn (Brahmā), grew distressed and praised him with various words.
m.2.2.3.32: Dharma said: O God of gods, O Mahādeva, protector of dharma, salutation to you. You alone, O Śambhu, are the maker of creation, preservation and destruction.
m.2.2.3.33: In creation you are Brahmā, in preservation Viṣṇu, in dissolution you bear the form of Hara—through the three guṇas, rajas, sattva and tamas—yet you are beyond the guṇas, O Lord.
m.2.2.3.34: Free from the three guṇas, you are Śiva himself, the Fourth, beyond Prakṛti; you are without attributes, changeless, and skilled in manifold divine plays.
m.2.2.3.35: Protect, protect me, O Mahādeva, from this sin so hard to overcome. This is my father, and these are my brothers, whose minds are set on sin.
m.2.2.3.36: Brahmā said: Thus praised by Dharma, Maheśāna, the supreme Lord, the self-existent, quickly came there to protect Dharma.
m.2.2.3.37: Śambhu, appearing in the sky and seeing Vidhi in such a state—me, and Dakṣa and the others—laughed inwardly and mocked us.
m.2.2.3.38: Laughing at them all again and again and mockingly saying well done, the bull-bannered Lord spoke thus, O best of sages, putting them to shame.
m.2.2.3.39: Śiva said: Ah, Brahmā! How did lustful feeling arise in you on seeing your own daughter? It is not at all proper for those who follow the Vedas.
m.2.2.3.40: Mother, sister, brother's wife, and likewise daughter—these should never be looked upon with an improper gaze by a wise man.
m.2.2.3.41: This indeed is the settled conclusion of the Vedic path, and it abides in your own mouth. How then, O Vidhi, has it been made to slip from your memory by mere desire?
m.2.2.3.42: Why was firmness not awakened in your mind, O four-faced one, so that by this petty Kāma your composure was shattered into the wish to dally, O Vidhi?
m.2.2.3.43: How then are the mind-born sons, Dakṣa, Marīci and the rest — yogins devoted to solitude, ever beholding the supreme Sun — lustful toward women?
m.2.2.3.44: How has Kāma too, dull-souled, ignorant of the proper time and of little sense, just now by sheer force made them perverted with his arrows?
m.2.2.3.45: Fie upon the scriptural learning of him whose mind a beloved woman has carried away; dragging the mind away from steadiness, she even plunges it into lusts.
m.2.2.3.46: Brahmā said: Having heard these words of Śiva spoken before the world, I, my shame doubled, at once became drenched in sweat.
m.2.2.3.47: Then, O sage, restraining the agitation of desire, I let go of that Sandhyā, who bore the form of desire, though I longed to seize her — out of fear of him.
m.2.2.3.48: From the sweat that fell from my body, O best of the twice-born, were born the hosts of Pitṛs, the Agniṣvāttas, and other hosts of Pitṛs.
m.2.2.3.49: All of them resembled crushed collyrium, with eyes like full-blown lotuses; utterly ascetic, holy, supreme, turned away from worldly existence.
m.2.2.3.50: Sixty-four thousand Agniṣvāttas are proclaimed, and likewise eighty-six thousand Barhiṣads, O sage.
m.2.2.3.51: Then sweat fell to the ground from Dakṣa's body, and from it was born an excellent woman endowed with every virtue.
m.2.2.3.52: She was slender-limbed, with a well-proportioned waist and a fine line of hair on her belly, renowned, soft-bodied, with lovely teeth, radiant like fresh gold.
m.2.2.3.53: Charming in every limb, with a lotus-face like the full moon, she was known by the name Rati, bewitching even to sages.
m.2.2.3.54: The six headed by Marīci restrained the activity of their senses — except Kratu and Vasiṣṭha, and likewise Pulastya and Aṅgiras.
m.2.2.3.55: The seed of those four, Kratu and the others, fell upon the ground, and from them were born other hosts of Pitṛs, O best of sages.
m.2.2.3.56: The Somapas and Ājyapas by name, and likewise others, the Sukālins and Haviṣmants — all these sons are proclaimed as bearers of kavya, the offerings to the ancestors.
m.2.2.3.57: The Somapas are the sons of Kratu, likewise the Kālins descend from Vasiṣṭha, those called Ājyapas are Pulastya's, and the Haviṣmants are the sons of Aṅgiras.
m.2.2.3.58: When these, the Agniṣvāttas and the rest, had been born, O chief of brahmins, the office of bearer of kavya was established everywhere among the ancestral classes of the worlds.
m.2.2.3.59: Sandhyā, having become the mother of the Pitṛs, became joined with their purpose; faultless, looked upon graciously by Śambhu, she was devoted to dharma and sacred rites.
m.2.2.3.60: Meanwhile Śambhu, having shown favour to all the twice-born and duly protected dharma, swiftly vanished.
m.2.2.3.61: Then I, the Grandfather, shamed by Śaṅkara's words, grew angry with Kandarpa, my face twisted with a frown.
m.2.2.3.62: Seeing my face and grasping my intent, Manmatha too, afraid of Paśupati, quickly withdrew his arrows, O sage.
m.2.2.3.63: Then I, the lotus-born, filled with anger, blazed up, exceedingly mighty, like a fire eager to consume.
m.2.2.3.64: Kandarpa, deluded by pride, will be burnt up by the fire of Bhava's eye, having attempted a most difficult deed against Mahādeva.
m.2.2.3.65: Thus I, the Creator, cursed Kāma, O best of the twice-born, in the presence of the host of Pitṛs and of the self-controlled sages.
m.2.2.3.66: Frightened thus, Rati's lord, having heard the most terrible curse, at that very moment cast aside his arrows and appeared in visible form.
m.2.2.3.67: With his pride gone from his mind, he spoke this to me, Brahmā, who was accompanied by Dakṣa and my other sons, O sage, while the hosts of Pitṛs and Sandhyā listened.
m.2.2.3.68: Kāma said: Why have I been cursed so terribly by you, O Brahman, O lord of the world, I who am guiltless toward you and follow the right path?
m.2.2.3.69: The task you assigned me, O Brahman, that I have done; therefore a curse is not fitting for me, since I did nothing else.
m.2.2.3.70: I, Viṣṇu and likewise Śambhu — all are within the range of your arrows — what you declared thus, that I merely put to the test.
m.2.2.3.71: There is no fault of mine in this, O Brahman; upon me, who am blameless, this curse, O god, lord of the world, is a terrible decree.
m.2.2.3.72: Brahmā said: Having heard his words, I, Brahmā, lord of the worlds, replied to Madana, now self-controlled, repeatedly restraining my anger.
m.2.2.3.73: Brahmā said: This Sandhyā is my daughter; since you made me a target of desire toward her, therefore I pronounced the curse.
m.2.2.3.74: Now, my anger calmed, I speak to you, O mind-born one: listen, free of doubt; be happy and cast off fear.
m.2.2.3.75: Having been turned to ashes by the fire of Bharga's eye, O Madana, you will afterward quickly regain a body just like this one.
m.2.2.3.76: When Hara readily takes a wife, then he himself will cause you to regain your body.
m.2.2.3.77: Having spoken thus to Madana, I, the Grandfather of the worlds, vanished as the chief sages, my mind-born sons, looked on.
m.2.2.3.78: Having heard these words of mine, Madana and those mind-born sons all became happy and promptly went home.
m.2.2.3.iti: Thus ends the third adhyāya, named The curse on Kāma and the favour shown to him, in the second khaṇḍa, the Satī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.2.4.1: Nārada said: O disciple of Viṣṇu, O greatly wise one, O Vidhi, maker of the worlds, O lord, this wondrous story you have told is filled with the nectar of Śiva's divine play.
m.2.2.4.2: What happened after that, dear father? Tell me that account now, since it is connected with Śambhu's story; I am full of faith and eager to hear it.
m.2.2.4.3: Brahmā said: When Śambhu had gone to his own abode and I, the Creator, had vanished, Dakṣa then spoke to Kandarpa, remembering those words of mine.
m.2.2.4.4: Dakṣa said: O Kandarpa, this maiden born from my body is endowed with fine form and virtues. Take her as your wife; she is your equal in qualities.
m.2.2.4.5: This greatly radiant one will always be your companion, obedient to you as you wish, in accordance with dharma.
m.2.2.4.6: Brahmā said: Having said this, he gave to Kandarpa her who had arisen from the sweat-water of his body, placing her before him and naming her Rati.
m.2.2.4.7: Having married her, Smara too rejoiced greatly, O Nārada — Dakṣa's lovely daughter, who could bewitch even sages.
m.2.2.4.8: Then Madana, gazing at his auspicious wife named Rati, was pierced by his own power and, captivated by Rati, was infatuated.
m.2.2.4.9: The fair, doe-eyed beloved, with tremulous eye-corners, joyfully became a giver of delight; and she was his very wife, his match in love-play.
m.2.2.4.10: Seeing the pair of her brows, Madana began to doubt: Has the Creator set my bow in her, to my undoing?
m.2.2.4.11: Seeing the swift movement of her side-glances, O best of the twice-born, he no longer trusted the swiftness of his own arrows in flight, nor their charm.
m.2.2.4.12: Smelling her natural fragrance and the gentle breeze of her breath, Madana gave up his faith in the Malaya breeze.
m.2.2.4.13: Seeing her face, like the full moon and well marked with a beauty-mark, Madana could not decide the difference between her face and the moon.
m.2.2.4.14: Her two breasts, like golden lotus buds, shone with their pair of nipples as if encircled by bees.
m.2.2.4.15: Seeing the middle of her bosom, firm, full and high, and the slender, lovely, moon-like garland hanging down to her navel —
m.2.2.4.16: Kāma forgot the string of his flower-bow, a whirling row of bees, because, abandoning it, he gazes at this garland.
m.2.2.4.17: The inside of her deep navel-hollow was enclosed by skin on all four sides; her lotus-face with its pair of eyes was like a reddish lotus.
m.2.2.4.18: With her slender-waisted body, of natural golden lustre, that lovely woman appeared to Kāma like a golden altar.
m.2.2.4.19: Kāma gazed at her pair of thighs, long like plantain stems, smooth, soft and charming, equal to his own power.
m.2.2.4.20: Her two feet, with reddened heels and toe-tips at their edges — the Mind-born regarded them as his friend, as if dyed with passion by him.
m.2.2.4.21: Her pair of hands was red, charming with nails like kiṃśuka flowers and with round fingers tapering to fine tips.
m.2.2.4.22: Her pair of arms was lovely, long like a pair of lotus stalks, soft and smooth, ever shining like lustrous metal and coral.
m.2.2.4.23: Her charming mass of hair, like a dark rain-cloud, resembled a heavy load of yak-tail hair; thus Smara's beloved shone.
m.2.2.4.24: Such a one, named Rati, Kāma took with eyes wide open in delight, as Mahādeva received Gaṅgā born from the snowy mountain —
m.2.2.4.25: her who, like the river, had cakravāka birds and lotuses, whose lovely arms were pieces of lotus stalk, and who shone with slender waves formed by the many playful movements of her brows;
m.2.2.4.26: whose falling side-glances were lofty currents, who had blue lotuses in her own eyes, the fine hairs of her body as water-moss, and who played about the tree of the mind;
m.2.2.4.27: whose deep navel was a pool, slender, lovely in every limb, abode of all beauty, shining like Ramā (Lakṣmī);
m.2.2.4.28: adorned with the twelve ornaments and the sixteen embellishments, enchanting all the worlds and illuminating the ten directions.
m.2.2.4.29: Seeing Rati thus, Madana eagerly took her, as Hṛṣīkeśa took the excellent Lakṣmī who approached him out of love.
m.2.2.4.30: Then Kāma, bewildered by the joy that arose, did not speak to Dakṣa, having forgotten the terrible curse given by Vidhi.
m.2.2.4.31: Then, dear son, there was a great festival that increased happiness; Dakṣa was most pleased, and my sons rejoiced.
m.2.2.4.32: Kāma, attaining great happiness, reached the end of all sorrow; and Rati, Dakṣa's daughter, having obtained Kāma, also rejoiced.
m.2.2.4.33: And sweet-spoken Smara, smitten with love, shone together with her like a cloud at twilight with charming lightning.
m.2.2.4.34: Thus Rati's lord, deeply infatuated, held Rati to his heart as a seer of yoga holds sacred knowledge; and Rati too, her face like the full moon, having obtained the foremost husband, shone like Kamalā beside Hari.
m.2.2.4.iti: Thus ends the fourth adhyāya, named The marriage of Kāma, in the second khaṇḍa, the Satī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.2.5.1: Sūta said: Having heard these words of Brahmā, that best of sages, his mind delighted, remembered Śaṅkara and spoke joyfully.
m.2.2.5.2: Nārada said: O Brahmā, O Creator, O greatly fortunate one, disciple of Viṣṇu, O wise one, you have narrated the wonderful sport of the moon-crested Śiva.
m.2.2.5.3: When Madana, having taken a wife, went joyfully to his own home, and Dakṣa too went to his own home, and likewise you, the creator, went to yours,
m.2.2.5.4: and when the mind-born sons had gone to their respective abodes, where did that Sandhyā go, the daughter of Brahmā and mother of the Pitṛs?
m.2.2.5.5: What did she do, and by what man was she married? Tell me all this, the story of Sandhyā, in detail.
m.2.2.5.6: Sūta said: Having heard these words of his wise son, Brahmā, knower of the truth, remembered Śaṅkara with devotion and spoke.
m.2.2.5.7: Brahmā said: Listen, O sage, to the whole auspicious story of Sandhyā, hearing which all women with desires may always become chaste, O sage.
m.2.2.5.8: That Sandhyā was formerly my mind-born daughter. Having performed austerity and given up her body, she herself was born as Arundhatī.
m.2.2.5.9: Becoming the daughter of Medhātithi, the best of sages, the wise one, who observed vows at the word of Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Maheśa,
m.2.2.5.10: chose as husband the great-souled Vasiṣṭha of praiseworthy vows. She became foremost among devoted wives, worthy of homage and worship, and gentle.
m.2.2.5.11: Nārada said: How did Sandhyā perform austerity, for what purpose, and where? How, having given up her body, did she become the daughter of Medhātithi?
m.2.2.5.12: Or how did she choose as husband the great-souled Vasiṣṭha of praiseworthy vows, as ordained by the gods Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śiva?
m.2.2.5.13: O Grandfather, tell me, who am eager to hear, this story of Arundhatī in detail and truly; I have great curiosity.
m.2.2.5.14: Brahmā said: Formerly, having seen my own daughter Sandhyā, I quickly set my mind on desire, and then abandoned it out of fear of Śiva; and she—
m.2.2.5.15: seeing that Sandhyā's mind was shaken, agitated by Kāma's arrows, as were also the minds of the great sages whose minds had been restrained,
m.2.2.5.16: having heard Bharga's mocking words directed at me, and knowing her own improper agitation toward the sages,
m.2.2.5.17: and having seen again and again such a state of Kāma that deludes sages, Sandhyā herself there became extremely distressed and turned to self-restraint.
m.2.2.5.18: Then, O sage, when Madana had been cursed by Brahmā, that is by me, when I had withdrawn and Śiva too had gone to his own abode,
m.2.2.5.19: that Sandhyā, my daughter, O best of sages, overcome by indignation, reflected thus and then became absorbed in meditation.
m.2.2.5.20: Meditating for a moment on what had happened before, the high-minded Sandhyā quickly pondered this, as was fitting at that time:
m.2.2.5.21: Sandhyā said: Seeing me a young woman as soon as I was born, this father of mine, impelled by Madana and full of passion, conceived desire for me.
m.2.2.5.22: And while the mind-born sages of purified selves looked on, their minds too became improperly filled with desire on merely seeing me.
m.2.2.5.23: My own heart too was churned by the wicked Madana, by whom my mind was greatly agitated on seeing all the sages.
m.2.2.5.24: Madana himself has obtained the fruit of this sin, since the Grandfather in anger cursed him in the presence of Śambhu.
m.2.2.5.25: I, the doer of my own sin, should obtain the fruit of this sin; and I quickly desire the means whose fruit is its purification.
m.2.2.5.26: Since my father and brothers, openly seeing me full of desire, conceived longing for me, there is therefore no greater sinner than I.
m.2.2.5.27: I too, seeing them, had improper desire, as towards a husband, for my own father and for all my brothers.
m.2.2.5.28: I myself will perform expiation for this sin; I will offer myself into the fire according to the Vedic path.
m.2.2.5.29: But I will establish one rule here on earth: that embodied beings shall not be filled with desire as soon as they are born.
m.2.2.5.30: For this purpose, having performed extremely severe austerity, I will establish the rule, and afterwards I will give up my life.
m.2.2.5.31: That body for which desire was felt by my father himself and by my brothers—with that body I have no purpose at all.
m.2.2.5.32: The body with which I aroused the feeling of desire towards my fathers and brothers is not a means for good deeds.
m.2.2.5.33: Having thus reflected in her mind, Sandhyā then went to the excellent mountain called Candrabhāga, from which the river Candrabhāgā flows.
m.2.2.5.34: Then, knowing that Sandhyā had gone to that excellent mountain for austerity, I, Brahmā, spoke to my son of controlled self,
m.2.2.5.35: Vasiṣṭha, self-restrained, all-knowing, a yogin of knowledge, master of the Vedas and Vedāṅgas, seated near me.
m.2.2.5.36: Brahmā said: Vasiṣṭha, my son, go to the high-minded Sandhyā, who is resolved upon austerity, and initiate her according to rule.
m.2.2.5.37: Earlier she became ashamed on seeing you all and me full of lust, and likewise herself full of desire, O best of sages.
m.2.2.5.38: Reflecting on that deed of yours and of herself—unspoken yet manifest—as akin to an earlier death, she wishes to give up her life.
m.2.2.5.39: By austerity she will establish a rule among those without rule. The virtuous one has gone to perform austerity on the mountain called Candrabhāga.
m.2.2.5.40: She does not know any method of austerity, dear son; therefore act so that, through instruction, she may attain what she desires.
m.2.2.5.41: O sage, give up this form of yours, take on another form, and going near her, teach her the practice of austerity.
m.2.2.5.42: Since she has already seen this form of yours here, just as she saw the two of us, she may not gain anything from you; therefore take on a different form.
m.2.2.5.43: Brahmā said: O Nārada, thus was the compassionate Vasiṣṭha instructed by me, and the sage said to me, so be it, and went to Sandhyā.
m.2.2.5.44: There Vasiṣṭha then saw a divine lake, full of water, equal to the Mānasa in its qualities, and also Sandhyā, who had come to its shore.
m.2.2.5.45: With her standing on the bank, that lake, bright with lotuses, shone like the evening sky with the rising moon and lovely stars.
m.2.2.5.46: Then the sage, full of curiosity, having seen her there of noble bearing, looked at the lake there named Bṛhallohita.
m.2.2.5.47: And he also saw the river Candrabhāgā flowing from that rampart toward the southern ocean, descending from the great ridge of the mountain.
m.2.2.5.48: That river, breaking through the western side of the mountain Candrabhāga, goes to the ocean just as the Gaṅgā flows from the Himavat.
m.2.2.5.49: Then, having seen Sandhyā on the shore of Bṛhallohita on that mountain Candrabhāga, Vasiṣṭha respectfully questioned her.
m.2.2.5.50: Vasiṣṭha said: For what purpose have you come, good lady, to this deserted mountain? Whose daughter are you, and what is it that you wish to do?
m.2.2.5.51: This I wish to hear; tell me, if it is not a secret. And why is your face, radiant like the full moon, so motionless?
m.2.2.5.52: Brahmā said: Having heard those words of the great-souled Vasiṣṭha, and having seen that great soul blazing like fire,
m.2.2.5.53: like celibacy embodied, resplendent, wearing matted locks — Sandhyā then bowed respectfully and spoke to that ascetic rich in austerity.
m.2.2.5.54: Sandhyā said: Learn from me why I have come to the mountain — a purpose already fulfilled, which will indeed be accomplished for me by the mere sight of you, O lord.
m.2.2.5.55: O brahmin, I have come to this deserted mountain to perform austerity. I was born the daughter of Brahmā, and am known by the name Sandhyā.
m.2.2.5.56: If it is fitting and not burdensome for you, instruct me. This is my secret intention; there is nothing else.
m.2.2.5.57: Without knowing the nature of austerity, I have resorted to this penance grove. I am withering with anxiety; indeed my mind trembles.
m.2.2.5.58: Brahmā said: Having heard her words, Vasiṣṭha, foremost among knowers of Brahman, who himself knew all that was to be done, asked nothing further.
m.2.2.5.59: Then, remembering in his mind Śaṅkara, who is loving to his devotees, he spoke to her, self-controlled and resolved upon austerity.
m.2.2.5.60: Vasiṣṭha said: He who is the supreme great splendour, who is the supreme great austerity, the Supreme, supremely worthy of worship — let that Śambhu be held in the mind.
m.2.2.5.61: He who alone is the primal cause of dharma, wealth, desire and liberation — worship that One, the origin of the worlds, the Supreme Person.
m.2.2.5.62: With this mantra, O fair-faced one, worship Śambhu, lord of the gods. Through that you will attain everything; there is no doubt.
m.2.2.5.63: The mantra is Om namaḥ śaṅkarāya, ending with Om, repeated continually. Hear from me as I explain the undertaking of the austerity of silence.
m.2.2.5.64: Bathing should be done in silence, and worship of Hara in silence. At first, during the two sixth periods of the day, the food should be water alone.
m.2.2.5.65: At the third sixth period one should be devoted to complete fasting. Thus it proceeds, and at the completion of the austerity the rite should take place at the sixth period.
m.2.2.5.66: This, called the austerity of silence, bestows the fruit of celibacy and grants all one's desires, O goddess — truly, truly; there is no doubt.
m.2.2.5.67: Thus, fixing your desire in your mind, meditate on Śaṅkara. Pleased, he will very soon grant you the object you desire.
m.2.2.5.68: Brahmā said: Then Vasiṣṭha, having sat down and duly explained to Sandhyā the procedure of austerity, addressed her, and the sage vanished right there.
m.2.2.5.iti: Thus ends the fifth adhyāya, named The life of Sandhyā, in the second khaṇḍa, the Satī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.2.6.1: Brahmā said: O best of sons, O greatly wise one, listen to the great austerity of Sandhyā, by hearing which a mass of sins is surely destroyed at that very moment.
m.2.2.6.2: When Vasiṣṭha, having instructed her in the nature of austerity, had gone to his own abode, Sandhyā too, having understood the nature of austerity, attained joy.
m.2.2.6.3: Then, joyful in mind, having put on the appropriate attire, she, staying on the bank of Bṛhallohita, began to perform austerity.
m.2.2.6.4: With the mantra that Vasiṣṭha had taught as the means in austerity — with that mantra she worshipped Śaṅkara with true devotion.
m.2.2.6.5: As she, single-minded, performed very great austerity with her mind fixed on Śambhu, one cycle of four yugas passed.
m.2.2.6.6: Then Śambhu, gratified by that austerity, became pleased, having revealed his own form within, without, and in the sky.
m.2.2.6.7: In that very form which she was contemplating, he became visible to her.
m.2.2.6.8: Then, seeing before her the Lord Śaṅkara whom she had contemplated in her mind, with a gracious face and calm, she rejoiced exceedingly.
m.2.2.6.9: With awe, what shall I say? How shall I praise Hara? Thus absorbed in anxious thought, she closed her eyes.
m.2.2.6.10: Hara, entering the heart of her whose eyes were closed, gave her divine knowledge, divine speech, and divine eyes.
m.2.2.6.11: She obtained divine knowledge, divine sight and divine speech; seeing directly the Lord of Durga, the master of the worlds, she praised him.
m.2.2.6.12: Sandhyā said: Whose form is formless, reachable by knowledge, supreme, neither gross nor subtle nor high, to be contemplated inwardly by yogins — to you, that maker of the worlds, let there be salutation.
m.2.2.6.13: I bow to you, the gracious one, whose form is all, peaceful, stainless, changeless, beyond the reach of ordinary knowledge, unchanging in its own light, resembling the path of the sky, beyond the path of darkness.
m.2.2.6.14: Whose form is one, pure, shining, without Māyā, consciousness-bliss, innate and unchanging, eternal bliss, gracious with true glory, bestower of fortune — to him, to you, salutation.
m.2.2.6.15: Whose form is to be realised as the shape of knowledge, distinct from all, free in purity (sattva), to be meditated upon, the very nature of the Self, the essence, the beyond, the purifier of purifiers — to him, to you, salutation.
m.2.2.6.16: Salutation to you, joined with yoga, whose shape is of pure form, charming, adorned with jewels, fair as clear camphor, bearing in the hands the boon-giving and fear-dispelling gestures, the trident and the skull.
m.2.2.6.17: Sky, earth, the directions, water, fire, and again time are your forms — salutation be to you.
m.2.2.6.18: From whom Pradhāna and Puruṣa came forth as his body — therefore to Śaṅkara of unmanifest form, salutation again and again.
m.2.2.6.19: You who as Brahmā create, who as Viṣṇu maintain, who as Rudra will destroy — to you, salutation again and again.
m.2.2.6.20: Salutation again and again to the cause of causes, the giver of the glory of divine nectar-like knowledge, the giver of prosperity to all the worlds, whose form is light, higher than the highest.
m.2.2.6.21: Of whom the world is said to be nothing other; from whose feet arose the earth, and from him the directions, the sun, the moon, Manoja (Kāma), the outward-facing senses, and from the navel the atmosphere — to you, that Śambhu, let my salutation be.
m.2.2.6.22: You are the supreme and the supreme Self; you, Hara, are the manifold knowledge; you are the true Brahman and the supreme Brahman, devoted to reflection.
m.2.2.6.23: He who has no beginning, no middle and no end, from whom the world arises — how shall I praise that god Hara, beyond the reach of speech and mind?
m.2.2.6.24: O god, whose forms Brahmā and the other gods and the sages rich in austerity cannot describe — how can he be described by me?
m.2.2.6.25: O Lord, how can your qualities, you who are without qualities, be known by me, a woman, when even the gods and demons together with Indra do not know your form?
m.2.2.6.26: Salutation to you, O Maheśāna; salutation to you, O one made of austerity. Be gracious, O Śambhu, lord of gods; again and again salutation be to you.
m.2.2.6.27: Brahmā said: Hearing these words of hers, the Supreme Lord Śaṅkara, thus praised, affectionate to his devotees, became exceedingly pleased.
m.2.2.6.28: Then seeing her body clad in bark garments and deerskin, covered by masses of matted hair shining on her pure head,
m.2.2.6.29: and then seeing her face, like a lotus blighted by frost, Hara, filled with compassion, spoke this to her.
m.2.2.6.30: Maheśvara said: O good lady, I am pleased with your supreme austerity and with your praise, O one of auspicious wisdom; choose a boon now.
m.2.2.6.31: Whatever purpose you have in mind to be accomplished by this boon, that I will do. May good befall you; I am pleased by your vows.
m.2.2.6.32: Brahmā said: Hearing these words of Maheśa, whose mind was pleased, Sandhyā, very delighted, bowing again and again, then spoke.
m.2.2.6.33: Sandhyā said: If a boon is to be given out of love, if I am worthy of a boon, if I have become purified from that sin, O Maheśvara,
m.2.2.6.34: if, O god, you are now pleased with my austerity, then let this first boon chosen by me be granted:
m.2.2.6.35: O lord of gods, let living beings on this earth not become filled with desire at once, as soon as they are born; let them become so only later.
m.2.2.6.36: And may I become renowned for virtuous conduct in all three worlds, such that no other woman is so: this is the one boon chosen by me.
m.2.2.6.37: My created being shall nowhere fall to anyone in desire; O Lord, whoever becomes my husband, he too shall be my dearest friend.
m.2.2.6.38: Any man who looks at me with desire — his manhood shall then be destroyed, and he shall become impotent.
m.2.2.6.39: Brahmā said: Hearing these words spoken by her, the sinless one, Śaṅkara, affectionate to his devotees, spoke with a very pleased heart.
m.2.2.6.40: Maheśvara said: Listen, O goddess Sandhyā: your sin has been reduced to ashes. I have given up my anger towards you; you have become pure through the practice of austerity.
m.2.2.6.41: Whatever you have chosen, O gentle lady, all of it has been granted by me, for I am well pleased with your austerity, O Sandhyā, and I grant it as a boon indeed.
m.2.2.6.42: The first stage of life is infancy, the second is called childhood, the third stage is youth, and likewise the fourth is old age.
m.2.2.6.43: When the third stage of life has been reached, embodied beings will become filled with desire; at the end of the second it will happen only here and there.
m.2.2.6.44: Through your austerity I have established this rule in the world: that embodied beings should not be filled with desire as soon as they are born.
m.2.2.6.45: And may you attain in the world such chastity as will arise for no other woman in the three worlds.
m.2.2.6.46: Whoever, except your husband, looks at you with desire, he will at once become impotent and fall into weakness.
m.2.2.6.47: Your husband will be highly fortunate, endowed with austerity and beauty, and will live together with you until the end of seven kalpas.
m.2.2.6.48: Thus the boons that you asked of me have been granted by me. And I shall tell you something else, established in a former birth.
m.2.2.6.49: The abandoning of your body in fire was promised by you earlier. I tell you the means for it; do that, without doubt.
m.2.2.6.50: And let that be done by you soon, in the fully blazing fire at the twelve-year sacrifice of the sage Medhātithi.
m.2.2.6.51: In the valley at the foot of this mountain, on the bank of the river Candrabhāgā, Medhātithi is performing a great sacrifice in the hermitage of ascetics.
m.2.2.6.52: Going there of your own will, unnoticed by the sages, you will, by my grace, be born from the fire and become his daughter.
m.2.2.6.53: Whatever lord you desire in your mind as a husband, placing him in your own heart, give up your body in the fire.
m.2.2.6.54: While you, O Sandhyā, were practising severe austerity on the mountain for the span of a four-yuga cycle, when its Kṛta age had passed,
m.2.2.6.55: in the first part of the Tretā age daughters were born to Dakṣa, who, endowed with good character, were married as was fitting.
m.2.2.6.56: Among them he gave twenty-seven daughters to the Moon (Vidhu); but the Moon, abandoning the others, became fond of Rohiṇī alone.
m.2.2.6.57: For that reason, when the Moon was cursed by the angry Dakṣa, then all the gods came near you.
m.2.2.6.58: But those gods together with Brahmā were not seen by you, O Sandhyā, since your mind was fixed on me; and having looked at the sky, the Moon would regain his state again.
m.2.2.6.59: Then, for the release of the Moon from the curse, the river Candranadī came into being, created by the Creator; at that very time Medhātithi arrived here.
m.2.2.6.60: There is none equal to him in austerity; none has been nor will be. By him the sacrifice Jyotiṣṭoma, of grand ritual, has been begun.
m.2.2.6.61: There the fire is blazing; in it give up your own body. Now you are utterly pure; may your vow be fulfilled.
m.2.2.6.62: This has been arranged by me for the sake of your own purpose, O ascetic lady. Do that, O fortunate one; go to the sacrifice of the great sage. Having done her this good, the Lord of the gods vanished right there.
m.2.2.6.iti: Thus ends the sixth adhyāya, named The life of Sandhyā, in the second khaṇḍa, the Satī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.2.7.1: Brahmā said: O sage, when Śambhu had granted the boon and then vanished, Sandhyā too went to the very place where the sage Medhātithi was.
m.2.2.7.2: There, by Śambhu's grace unnoticed by anyone, she remembered that celibate student who had instructed her in austerity.
m.2.2.7.3: Earlier, O great sage, she had been instructed by Vasiṣṭha, who had taken the form of a celibate student, to perform austerity, at the word of Parameṣṭhin Brahmā.
m.2.2.7.4: Then Sandhyā, in her mind making that very brāhmaṇa celibate, the instructor of her austerity, her husband,
m.2.2.7.5: the daughter of Vidhi Brahmā, delighted, unnoticed by the sages through Śambhu's grace, entered the blazing fire at the great sacrifice.
m.2.2.7.6: Then at that very moment her body, turned into sacrificial cake (puroḍāśa), was burnt and spread a fragrance of oblation, which went unnoticed.
m.2.2.7.7: Having burnt her body, Fire then, again by Śambhu's command, made it enter, purified, into the orb of the Sun.
m.2.2.7.8: Then the Sun, dividing that body into two halves, placed it in his own chariot for the pleasure of the Pitṛs and the gods.
m.2.2.7.9: The upper part of her body, O lord of sages, became the morning twilight, lying at the juncture at the beginning of day and night.
m.2.2.7.10: The remaining part of her, lying at the juncture at the end of day and night, became the evening twilight, ever bestowing pleasure on the Pitṛs.
m.2.2.7.11: When dawn breaks first, before the sunrise, then the morning twilight rises, giving pleasure to the gods.
m.2.2.7.12: Then, when the Sun, resembling a red lotus, has set, the evening twilight too always rises, bringing delight to the Pitṛs.
m.2.2.7.13: Her vital breaths were made embodied with a divine body by the compassionate Lord Śambhu through his mind.
m.2.2.7.14: When the end of the sage's sacrifice came, she was obtained by the sage as a daughter in the midst of the fire, shining like molten gold.
m.2.2.7.15: Then the sage, filled with joy, took that daughter; having bathed her for the sake of the sacrifice, he placed her on his own lap, O sage.
m.2.2.7.16: The great sage gave her the name Arundhatī; surrounded by his disciples there, he attained great joy.
m.2.2.7.17: Since she does not obstruct dharma for any reason whatsoever, she herself therefore obtained that name, renowned in the three worlds.
m.2.2.7.18: Having completed the sacrifice, the sage, attaining the state of one whose aim is fulfilled and full of joy at gaining a daughter, constantly cherished her alone in that hermitage of his, together with his groups of disciples, O divine sage.
m.2.2.7.19: Then that goddess grew up in that hermitage of the best of sages, on the bank of the river Candrabhāgā, in the place called Tāpasāraṇya.
m.2.2.7.20: When her fifth year arrived, that virtuous one by her qualities made the Candrabhāgā and Tāpasāraṇya too holy.
m.2.2.7.21: Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Maheśvara arranged the marriage of Arundhatī with Vasiṣṭha, the son of Brahmā.
m.2.2.7.22: At her wedding there was a great festival that increased happiness; all the gods and sages attained supreme happiness, O sage.
m.2.2.7.23: From the water that flowed from the hands of Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Maheśa, seven very holy rivers arose, beginning with the Śiprā.
m.2.2.7.24: Arundhatī, the greatly chaste one, foremost among chaste women, daughter of Medhātithi, shone having obtained Vasiṣṭha, O sage.
m.2.2.7.25: She of whom were born excellent, auspicious sons beginning with Śakti shone, having obtained that beloved Vasiṣṭha, O best of sages.
m.2.2.7.26: Thus, O best of sages, the story of Sandhyā has been told to you — holy, supreme, divine, bestowing the fruit of all desires.
m.2.2.7.27: Whoever, woman or man of auspicious vows, listens to this attains all desires; there need be no doubt about this.
m.2.2.7.iti: Thus ends the seventh adhyāya, named The marriage of Arundhatī and Vasiṣṭha, in the second khaṇḍa, the Satī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.2.8.1: Sūta said: Having heard these words of Brahmā, the Prajāpati, Nārada, his mind delighted, spoke to him.
m.2.2.8.2: Nārada said: O Brahmā, O Creator, most fortunate one, disciple of Viṣṇu, of great intellect, you are blessed, a devotee of Śiva indeed, a revealer of the supreme truth.
m.2.2.8.3: You have made me hear a fine, divine story that increases devotion to Śiva, and likewise the story of Arundhatī, who was that very Sandhyā in her next birth.
m.2.2.8.4: Now, O knower of dharma, tell me the supreme, sacred story of Śiva, which destroys the gravest sins, bestows auspiciousness, and is most excellent.
m.2.2.8.5: When Kāma had taken a wife and was joyful, and when they had departed, and when Sandhyā had gone to perform austerities, what happened then?
m.2.2.8.6: Sūta said: Hearing these words of the sage of purified self, Brahmā became exceedingly pleased and spoke these words.
m.2.2.8.7: Brahmā said: Listen, O Nārada, chief of brahmins, to that very auspicious story, filled with Śiva's divine play, with devotion; you are blessed, a servant of Śiva.
m.2.2.8.8: Dear son, when Śiva had vanished earlier, I, deluded and tormented by the poison of Śambhu's words, kept constantly brooding on that.
m.2.2.8.9: Having brooded long in my mind, deluded by Śiva's māyā, I conceived jealousy towards Śiva; hear that — I shall tell you.
m.2.2.8.10: Then I went to where Dakṣa and the others were. Seeing Madana with Rati, I became somewhat intoxicated with pride.
m.2.2.8.11: O Nārada, addressing Dakṣa and my other sons with great affection, I, deluded by Śiva's māyā, spoke these words.
m.2.2.8.12: Brahmā said: O Dakṣa, O sons led by Marīci, hear my words; having heard, you must devise a means to remove my distress.
m.2.2.8.13: Seeing merely my desire for a woman, Śambhu reproached me; the great yogin heaped much scorn on me and on you.
m.2.2.8.14: Burning with grief because of that, I find no peace anywhere. An effort must surely be made so that he takes a wife.
m.2.2.8.15: If he takes a wife, I would be happy and free of grief. But on reflection I think that wish of mine is extremely hard to attain.
m.2.2.8.16: Seeing merely my desire for a woman, Śambhu reproached me before the sages; how then will he himself accept a wife?
m.2.2.8.17: Or which woman in these three worlds could dwell in his mind, and, making him disregard the path of yoga, delude him?
m.2.2.8.18: Even Manmatha will not be able to delude him; that utter yogin cannot bear even the name of women.
m.2.2.8.19: And without the acceptance of a wife by Hara, the primal one, creation would remain only half-accomplished; this is so by his word, which no one else can obstruct.
m.2.2.8.20: On earth there will arise some great asuras to be slain by me, some surely to be slain by Hari, and some by Śambhu's means.
m.2.2.8.21: While Śambhu remains averse to worldly life and utterly dispassionate, without this marriage he will undertake no other task — there is no doubt.
m.2.2.8.22: Having said this and looked closely at my sons Dakṣa and the others, I then joyfully addressed Madana, who was there with Rati.
m.2.2.8.23: Brahmā said: O Kāma, best of my sons, you bring happiness in every way. Hear my words gladly, together with your wife, O you who love your father.
m.2.2.8.24: O mind-born one, you shine with this companion, and she, united with you as husband, is greatly resplendent.
m.2.2.8.25: Just as Hṛṣīkeśa shines with his consort and Ramā with Hari, as the night with the moon and the moon with her,
m.2.2.8.26: so too is the beauty of you two, and your married union is honoured. Therefore you will be the banner of the world — Viśvaketu.
m.2.2.8.27: For the welfare of the world, dear son, delude the wielder of Pināka, so that Śambhu, with a gladdened heart, may quickly accept a wife.
m.2.2.8.28: In solitary, pleasant places, on mountains and by lakes — wherever the Lord goes, there go with her,
m.2.2.8.29: and delude Hara, who is self-controlled and averse to women. Apart from you there is no one else who can delude him.
m.2.2.8.30: When Hara has become passionate, O mind-born one, your curse too will be pacified; therefore do what is good for yourself.
m.2.2.8.31: If Maheśvara, filled with passion, desires a fair-hipped woman, then Bhava, worthy and noble, will also deliver you.
m.2.2.8.32: Therefore, accompanied by your wife, strive to delude Hara; by deluding Maheśvara, become the banner of the universe.
m.2.2.8.33: Brahmā said: Hearing these words of mine, his father and lord of the world, Manmatha then spoke truthfully to me, the lord of the worlds.
m.2.2.8.34: Manmatha said: O lord, at your word I will delude Śambhu. But woman is my weapon; therefore, O Blessed One, create a beloved for him.
m.2.2.8.35: When Śambhu has been enchanted by me, there must be a woman by whom his further enchantment is to be accomplished; now, O Creator, devise the best means for that.
m.2.2.8.36: Brahmā said: When Kandarpa spoke thus, I, the Creator and Prajāpati, fell into thought: By whom can he be enchanted?
m.2.2.8.37: From the breath that issued from me as I was absorbed in thought, Vasanta (Spring) was born, adorned with masses of flowers.
m.2.2.8.38: He resembled a red lotus, had eyes like blooming lotuses, a face like the full moon risen at twilight, and a fine nose.
m.2.2.8.39: His feet were curved like the Śārṅga bow, his hair dark and curly; he resembled the twilight sun and was adorned with a pair of earrings.
m.2.2.8.40: His gait was like that of an elephant in rut; his arms stout and long, his shoulders high; his neck like a conch; his chest very broad; his face full and handsome.
m.2.2.8.41: He was beautiful in every limb, dark-complexioned, complete with all auspicious marks, most handsome to behold, enchanting to all, and a heightener of desire.
m.2.2.8.42: When such a Vasanta, the mine of flowers, had arisen, a very fragrant breeze blew, and the trees too burst into bloom.
m.2.2.8.43: Cuckoos in hundreds, sweet-voiced, sang out the fifth note (pañcama); the lakes, with clear waters, became full of blooming lotuses.
m.2.2.8.44: Then I, Hiraṇyagarbha, seeing him thus arisen, so excellent, spoke sweet words to Madana.
m.2.2.8.45: Brahmā said: Thus he, resembling Manmatha, has become your constant companion; this god will do everything favourable for your sake.
m.2.2.8.46: Just as the wind, friend of fire, will assist it everywhere, so this one, your friend, will always follow you.
m.2.2.8.47: Because he is the cause of the end of dwelling at home (vasati), let him be called Vasanta. Following you is his task, and likewise delighting the worlds.
m.2.2.8.48: This adornment of spring and the vernal Malaya breeze — may they ever be in the role of friends, remaining under your control.
m.2.2.8.49: Vivvoka and the other amorous gestures, likewise the hāvas, and likewise the sixty-four arts — may they show friendship to Rati, just as your friends do to you.
m.2.2.8.50: O Kāma, with these companions headed by Vasanta, together with Rati and with great effort, do you enchant Mahādeva.
m.2.2.8.51: I, dear son, after careful reflection in my mind, shall diligently bring into being that lovely woman who will enchant Hara.
m.2.2.8.52: Brahmā said: Thus addressed by me, the eldest of the gods, Kāma was delighted; then he, together with his wife, bowed at my feet.
m.2.2.8.53: Having bowed to Dakṣa and saluted all those mind-born sons, Manmatha went to the place where Śambhu himself had gone.
m.2.2.8.iti: Thus ends the eighth adhyāya, named The form of Vasanta, in the second khaṇḍa, the Satī-khaṇḍa, within the life of Satī, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.2.9.1: Brahmā said: When Manmatha, with his attendants, had gone to Śiva's abode, a wondrous event took place. Hear it, O lord of sages.
m.2.2.9.2: Having gone there, the great hero Manmatha, the causer of delusion, quickly spread his power and deluded living beings.
m.2.2.9.3: Vasanta too exerted his own power to bewitch Hara; all the trees burst into bloom at once, O sage.
m.2.2.9.4: Manobhava, together with Rati, made many kinds of efforts. All living beings fell under his control—but not Śiva, together with the lord of the gaṇas.
m.2.2.9.5: The efforts of Madana, along with Madhu, were fruitless, O sage. Then, his pride gone, he turned back and went to his own place.
m.2.2.9.6: Having bowed to me, Vidhi (Brahmā), Madana—dejected and humbled—spoke to me in a faltering voice, O sage.
m.2.2.9.7: Kāma said: O Brahmā, Śambhu, devoted wholly to yoga, cannot be deluded. Neither I nor anyone else has the power to delude that Śambhu.
m.2.2.9.8: O Brahmā, I with my friend Vasanta and with Rati employed various means, but all of them proved fruitless with regard to Śiva.
m.2.2.9.9: Hear, O Brahmā, dear one, O sage, as I recount them, the various efforts we made to delude Hara.
m.2.2.9.10: When Śambhu remained self-controlled, absorbed in samādhi, then with a fragrant, cool, very swift breeze—
m.2.2.9.11: —a breeze that causes infatuation, I constantly and strenuously tried to disturb Rudra, the three-eyed Mahādeva, who was established in samādhi.
m.2.2.9.12: Likewise, taking up my five arrows and my bow, I wandered all around him, deluding his gaṇas.
m.2.2.9.13: By my mere entry all creatures became fully subject to me, but Lord Śaṅkara with his gaṇas was not in the least affected.
m.2.2.9.14: When that lord of the pramathas went to the plateau of Himavat, I arrived there at that very time with Rati and Madhu, O Vidhi.
m.2.2.9.15: When Rudra went to Meru, or to Nāgakeśara, or when he went to Kailāsa, I went there at that time.
m.2.2.9.16: Whenever Hara, having left off his samādhi, stayed awake, I created before him a pair of cakravāka birds.
m.2.2.9.17: And that pair, O Brahmā, with brows repeatedly playing in amorous gestures, displayed various moods and the excellent sequence of conjugal love.
m.2.2.9.18: Deer and birds, standing in front of the blue-throated Mahādeva and his gaṇas, displayed enamoured feelings.
m.2.2.9.19: A pair of peacocks there, adopting various movements at his side and in front of him, displayed a mood eager for love.
m.2.2.9.20: My arrow never found an opening in him. I tell you the truth, O lord of the worlds: I have no power to delude him.
m.2.2.9.21: Madhu too did what was fitting for deluding him. Hear that, O fortunate one; I tell you truly, truly.
m.2.2.9.22: Campakas, keśaras, young kāraṇa trees, pāṭalas, nāgakeśaras, punnāgas, kiṃśukas and excellent ketakas—
m.2.2.9.23: —mālatīs, mallikās laden with leaves, and kurabakas he made blossom wherever Hara stayed.
m.2.2.9.24: Fanning them with Malaya breezes, he diligently made the lakes, with their full-blown lotuses, exceedingly fragrant in Giriśa's hermitage.
m.2.2.9.25: And there all the flowering creepers, with clusters of dhattūra shoots, embraced the bodies of the trees with lasting affection.
m.2.2.9.26: Seeing those trees laden with masses of fine flowers, fanned by those fragrant breezes, even sages fell under the sway of desire—what then of others?
m.2.2.9.27: Even so, no cause of delusion was seen in Śambhu. Śaṅkara showed not even a trace of emotion—not even anger toward me.
m.2.2.9.28: Having seen all this and understood his disposition, I have turned away from deluding Śambhu; this I tell you with certainty.
m.2.2.9.29: When he has left his samādhi, we cannot remain within his sight even for a moment. Who could delude that Rudra?
m.2.2.9.30: Seeing the horned one, whose eyes blaze like burning fire and who is terrifying with his mass of matted locks, who, O Brahmā, can stand before him?
m.2.2.9.31: Brahmā said: Having heard these words of Manobhava, I, the four-faced one, though wishing to speak, said nothing; I then became absorbed in worry.
m.2.2.9.32: Hearing Manobhava's words, that he was not able to delude Hara, I sighed out of great distress, O sage.
m.2.2.9.33: From the breath of my sighs were born gaṇas of many forms, very mighty, with lolling tongues, restless and exceedingly terrifying.
m.2.2.9.34: All of them played countless musical instruments of many kinds—kettledrums and the like—frightful and loud-sounding.
m.2.2.9.35: Then those great gaṇas born of my breath, standing before me, Brahmā, cried, kill, cut.
m.2.2.9.36: Hearing the words of those gaṇas there, as they kept saying to me, kill, cut, Kāma began to speak to Vidhi.
m.2.2.9.37: Then, O sage, Madana, having seen those gaṇas, addressed me; Smara spoke, restraining them, in front of the gaṇas, O Brahmā.
m.2.2.9.38: Kāma said: O Brahmā, O lord of creatures, initiator of all creation, who are these heroes that have arisen, frightful and terrifying?
m.2.2.9.39: What work will they do, or where will they dwell, O Vidhi? What are their names? Tell me that, and appoint them to their tasks.
m.2.2.9.40: Having appointed them to their own tasks and given them a place and a name, command me, O lord of gods, showing me fitting kindness.
m.2.2.9.41: Brahmā said: Having heard these words of his, O sage, I, the maker of the worlds, spoke to Madana, assigning their duties and so on.
m.2.2.9.42: As soon as they were born, these uttered again and again the word kill (māraya); therefore let their name be Māra.
m.2.2.9.43: These gaṇas will always create obstacles for creatures whose minds delight in various desires, O Kāma, unless they themselves are worshipped.
m.2.2.9.44: Following you is their chief task, O Manobhava; they will always be your helpers, there is no doubt.
m.2.2.9.45: Wherever and whenever you go for your work, there and then these will go to assist you.
m.2.2.9.46: They will cause confusion of mind in those who fall under the power of your weapons, and will in every way obstruct the path of knowledge of the wise.
m.2.2.9.47: Brahmā said: Having heard these words of mine, that Manobhava, together with Rati, became somewhat cheerful of face, O best of sages.
m.2.2.9.48: Having heard this, all those gaṇas too surrounded Madana and me on all sides and stood there as they pleased, in their own forms.
m.2.2.9.49: Then I, Brahmā, said affectionately to Smara: Carry out my command; go again together with these to delude Hara.
m.2.2.9.50: Setting your mind on it, make efforts with the Māra-gaṇas so that Śambhu may be deluded into taking a wife.
m.2.2.9.51: Having heard these words, Kāma, O divine sage, regarding them as weighty and bowing to me with humility, spoke again.
