m.2.2.9.52: Kāma said: I performed the task of deluding him properly and with effort; yet he was not deluded, dear father, nor will he be — not now.
m.2.2.9.53: Respecting the weight of your words, and having seen the Māra-gaṇas too, I shall go there again with my wife at your command.
m.2.2.9.54: My mind is certain of this: he will not be deluded. And I have this fear, O Creator, that he may reduce my body to ashes.
m.2.2.9.55: Having said this, Kāma, with Madhu and with Rati, and fearful, then went with the Māra-gaṇas to Śiva's abode, O lord of sages.
m.2.2.9.56: Then the mind-born one exerted his power as before; and Madhu too, bringing forth many kinds of ingenuity, used many stratagems.
m.2.2.9.57: He made great efforts there, and the Māra host as well; yet no delusion whatever arose in Śambhu, the supreme Self.
m.2.2.9.58: Turning back, Smara then came again to my abode; the Māra host, stripped of pride and joyless, also stood before me.
m.2.2.9.59: Then Kāma, dejected, bowed and, standing before me humbled, together with the Māras and Madhu, spoke to me, dear one.
m.2.2.9.60: O Creator, the effort to delude him was made even more than before; yet no delusion at all came upon him, whose mind is absorbed in meditation.
m.2.2.9.61: Nor was my body burnt there by that compassionate one; the reason is my former merit — and that Lord is indeed free from all change.
m.2.2.9.62: If your wish is that Hara should take a wife, O Lotus-born, then, setting aside pride, devise another means — this is my view.
m.2.2.9.63: Brahmā said: Having said this and bowed to me, Kāma went with his retinue to his own abode, remembering Śambhu, the curber of pride, who is kind to the humble.
m.2.2.9.iti: Thus ends the ninth adhyāya, named The power of Kāma and the birth of the Māra gaṇas, in the account of Satī in the Satī-khaṇḍa of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.2.10.1: Nārada said: O Brahmā, O Creator, O greatly fortunate one, you are blessed, your mind attached to Śiva. You have narrated the excellent story of Śaṅkara, the Supreme Self.
m.2.2.10.2: After Kāma had gone to his own hermitage with his attendants and with Rati, what happened then? What did you do? Tell that story now.
m.2.2.10.3: Brahmā said: Listen, O Nārada, with great delight, to the story of the Moon-crested Śiva, by merely hearing which a man becomes free from passion.
m.2.2.10.4: When Kāma had gone to his own hermitage accompanied by his retinue, learn from me the story of what happened then.
m.2.2.10.5: My pride was destroyed, O Nārada, and astonishment arose in my heart; I was joyless, O sage, my own wish being unfulfilled.
m.2.2.10.6: I grieved in many ways in my mind: How would he take a wife, that Śaṅkara, free from passion, self-controlled, devoted to yoga?
m.2.2.10.7: Having reflected thus in many ways, O sage, I, then devoid of pride, remembered with devotion that Hari, whose self is Śiva, the giver of my own body.
m.2.2.10.8: And I praised him with auspicious hymns full of humble words. Hearing that, the Lord quickly became manifest before me.
m.2.2.10.9: Hari, four-armed, lotus-eyed, bearing conch, lotus and mace, with a shining yellow garment and a dark body, the lover of his devotees.
m.2.2.10.10: Seeing him in such a form, the excellent refuge, I praised him again and again with love, in a voice choked with tears.
m.2.2.10.11: Hearing that hymn, Hari, the remover of his devotees' sorrow, being well pleased, spoke to me, Brahmā, who had come to him for refuge.
m.2.2.10.12: Hari said: O Vidhi, O Brahmā, O greatly wise one, blessed are you, maker of the worlds. For what purpose have you remembered me today, and why is praise being offered?
m.2.2.10.13: What great sorrow has befallen you? Tell it to me now. I shall allay all of it; there need be no hesitation about this.
m.2.2.10.14: Brahmā said: Hearing these words of Viṣṇu, my face somewhat relieved, I bowed and, with joined palms, spoke these words to Viṣṇu.
m.2.2.10.15: O God of gods, O lord of Ramā, O giver of honour, hear my account; and having heard it, show compassion, remove my sorrow and bring me happiness.
m.2.2.10.16: For the purpose of infatuating Rudra, O Viṣṇu, I sent Kāma together with his retinue, with the Māras and his friend Madhu (Spring).
m.2.2.10.17: They employed various means, and they were fruitless; no infatuation arose in that yogin who sees all equally.
m.2.2.10.18: Hearing these words of mine, Hari—the all-knowing bestower, the wise one, expert in the truth of Śiva—spoke to me in astonishment.
m.2.2.10.19: Viṣṇu said: For what reason did this idea arise in you, O Grandsire? Having considered everything with a sound mind, O Brahmā, tell me the truth of it.
m.2.2.10.20: Brahmā said: Hear that story, dear one. Your Māyā is the deluder; the whole world is subject to it, absorbed in pleasure, pain and the like.
m.2.2.10.21: Impelled by that very Māyā, I was intent on committing a sin. Hear that, O lord of gods; I tell it at your command.
m.2.2.10.22: At the time of the beginning of creation, ten sons were born, Dakṣa and the others, and also one daughter born of speech, exceedingly beautiful.
m.2.2.10.23: Dharma was born from my chest, Kāma from my mind, and others from my body. Then, seeing my daughter, delusion came over me, O Hari.
m.2.2.10.24: Deluded by your Māyā, I looked at her with an evil gaze. At that very moment Hara came and reproached me and my sons too.
m.2.2.10.25: He censured all of us, regarding himself as the supreme lord—wise, a yogin, the master, an enjoyer yet with senses conquered.
m.2.2.10.26: Though being my son, O Hari, he reproached me to my face. This is my great sorrow, which I have told in your presence.
m.2.2.10.27: If he would take a wife, I would be happy, my mind freed from sorrow. For this purpose I have come to you for refuge, O Keśava.
m.2.2.10.28: Brahmā said: Hearing these words of mine, Brahmā's, Madhusūdana laughed and quickly spoke to me, gladdening the maker of the world.
m.2.2.10.29: Viṣṇu said: O Vidhi, listen to my words, which entirely dispel error and which are, in ultimate truth, wholly in accord with the Vedas, Āgamas and the rest.
m.2.2.10.30: How have you become so greatly deluded in mind today, O Vidhi? Though you are the speaker of the Vedas and the maker of all the worlds, you are of foolish mind.
m.2.2.10.31: Abandon your dullness, O dull-witted one; do not hold such a notion. Recall with a good mind what all the Vedas declare in their praise.
m.2.2.10.32: O foolish one, you take Rudra, the Supreme Lord, to be your own son. Though you are the speaker of the Vedas, you have forgotten all your knowledge, O Vidhi.
m.2.2.10.33: Considering Śaṅkara an ordinary god, you commit hostility against him. Your good understanding has left you today, and evil thinking has appeared instead.
m.2.2.10.34: Hear the established doctrine of truth that is declared, and take up right understanding, having ascertained Śiva, the cause of existence, as truly proclaimed by the Vedas.
m.2.2.10.35: Śiva is indeed the maker of all, the sustainer and the destroyer, higher than the highest, the Supreme Brahman and Supreme Lord, beyond the guṇas and eternal.
m.2.2.10.36: He is indescribable, changeless, the Supreme Self, without a second, imperishable, infinite, the bringer of the end, the master, all-pervading, the Supreme Lord.
m.2.2.10.37: The all-powerful one, taking on the three guṇas, is the agent of creation, preservation and destruction; called Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Maheśa, associated with rajas, sattva and tamas, he is yet beyond them.
m.2.2.10.38: He is distinct from Māyā, free from desire, the possessor of Māyā, skilled in Māyā; though endowed with qualities, he is independent, blissful in himself, free from differentiation.
m.2.2.10.39: He delights in the Self, is beyond the pairs of opposites, is subject to his devotees, of beautiful form; a yogin ever devoted to yoga, the revealer of the path of yoga.
m.2.2.10.40: He is the remover of pride, the lord of the worlds, ever compassionate to the afflicted. Such is that Master, and you consider him your own son.
m.2.2.10.41: Abandon such wrong understanding and go to him for refuge. Worship Śambhu with your whole being; when pleased, he will bring about your welfare.
m.2.2.10.42: If the thought is in your heart that Śaṅkara should take a wife, then, O Brahmā, perform a fine austerity directed toward Śivā, while remembering Śiva.
m.2.2.10.43: Meditate on Śivā, holding your own desire in your heart. If that Goddess of the gods is pleased, she will accomplish the whole task.
m.2.2.10.44: If Śivā, taking an incarnation endowed with attributes, becomes a human woman, the daughter of someone in the world, she will surely become his wife.
m.2.2.10.45: O Brahmā, instruct Dakṣa that he should perform austerity with great effort, with devotion and of his own accord, in order to beget her as a wife for Śiva.
m.2.2.10.46: And, dear one, those two, Śivā and Śiva, should be clearly understood to be subject to their devotees; though of the nature of the supreme Brahman, by their own will they have become endowed with attributes.
m.2.2.10.47: Brahmā said: Having said this, the Lord of Mā (Viṣṇu) at that very moment remembered Śiva, his own master; and having gained knowledge by his grace, he then spoke to me.
m.2.2.10.48: Viṣṇu said: O Creator, remember the words spoken long ago by Śaṅkara, when he was entreated by the two of us, who had been brought forth by his will.
m.2.2.10.49: You have forgotten all that. Blessed is the supreme Śāmbhavī power, by whom everything is deluded; she is hard to comprehend for anyone but Śiva.
m.2.2.10.50: When the attributeless Śiva, by his own will, became endowed with attributes, and, engaging in fine sport, brought forth me and then you through his own power,
m.2.2.10.51: then Lord Śambhu instructed you in the work of creation, and me, O Brahmā, in its preservation — he who is with Umā (Soma), the cause of origination, the imperishable.
m.2.2.10.52: Then we two, having come to his abode with folded hands and bowed heads, said: O Bhava, you are the Lord of all, the one who incarnates, assuming forms with attributes.
m.2.2.10.53: Thus addressed, that Lord, full of compassion and skilled in many sports, laughed, looked up toward the sky with great delight, and spoke.
m.2.2.10.54: O Viṣṇu, such a supreme form of mine will become manifest in the world from the body of Vidhi (Brahmā), renowned by the name Rudra.
m.2.2.10.55: He is my complete form, always to be worshipped by you two, fulfiller of all desires, the agent of dissolution, presiding over the guṇas, free of distinctions, accomplisher of true yoga.
m.2.2.10.56: The three gods are also my form, but Hara in particular is complete. Of Umā too there will be forms, threefold, O sons.
m.2.2.10.57: Hari's wife will be named Lakṣmī, Brahmā's wife Sarasvatī, and the complete form, named Satī, will be Rudra's wife.
m.2.2.10.58: Viṣṇu said: Having said this and shown his grace, Maheśvara vanished. We two became happy, devoted each to our own tasks.
m.2.2.10.59: In due time, O Brahmā, we two have come to have wives, but not Śaṅkara, who has himself descended under the name Rudra and dwells on Kailāsa.
m.2.2.10.60: Śivā too is to become incarnate, she who is named Satī, O lord of creatures; therefore effort must indeed be made for the sake of bringing her into being.
m.2.2.10.61: Having said this and shown supreme compassion, Viṣṇu disappeared. Then I attained even greater joy, my jealousy gone.
m.2.2.10.iti: Thus ends the tenth adhyāya, named The dialogue of Brahmā and Viṣṇu, in the second khaṇḍa, the Satī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.2.11.1: Nārada said: O Brahmā, dear father, greatly wise one, best of speakers, tell us: after Viṣṇu had gone, what happened? What did you do, O Creator?
m.2.2.11.2: Brahmā said: O best of the sons of brāhmaṇas, listen attentively to what I did when the lord Viṣṇu had gone.
m.2.2.11.3: I ever praise the goddess Durgā, beloved of Śambhu, who is of the nature of both knowledge and ignorance, pure, whose very form is the supreme Brahman, the sustainer of the world.
m.2.2.11.4: I bow to her who pervades everywhere, eternal, without support, undisturbed, mother of the three gods, the grossest of the gross and yet formless.
m.2.2.11.5: You are consciousness, supreme bliss, whose form is the supreme Self. Be gracious, O sovereign of the gods; accomplish my task. Salutation to you.
m.2.2.11.6: Being thus praised by me, O sage, that Yoganidrā, Caṇḍikā, appeared visibly before me, O divine sage.
m.2.2.11.7: She had the lustre of glossy collyrium, a lovely form, four divine arms; she was seated on a lion, her hand in the boon-giving gesture, and resplendent with pearls and gems in her hair.
m.2.2.11.8: Her face was like the autumn moon, a bright moon was on her forehead, she had three eyes, was charming in every limb, and the nails of her lotus feet gleamed.
m.2.2.11.9: Seeing that Umā, the Śakti of Śiva, before me, O sage, I bowed down deeply with my lofty shoulders lowered in devotion and praised her.
m.2.2.11.10: Brahmā said: Salutation, salutation to you whose form is the activity and the withdrawal of the world, whose form is maintenance and creation. You are the excellent power of all moving and unmoving beings, eternal, the deluder of all.
m.2.2.11.11: You who are Śrī, ever the garland on Keśava's form; who as Viśvambharā (the Earth) bear all; you who of old were the maker of creation, the great sovereign, the destroyer of the three worlds, beyond the guṇas.
m.2.2.11.12: You who are honoured by yogins and dear to their minds — salutation to you, O essence of the subtlest atom; you who dwell in the hearts of yogins purified by yama and the other disciplines, who are realised on the yogins' path of meditation.
m.2.2.11.13: Endowed with illumination, purity and the like, free of passion, you are indeed Knowledge, the support of many. Bearing the immutable, unmanifest one of infinite form, you, made of time, bear the worlds.
m.2.2.11.14: Endowed with the guṇas, you constantly produce the seed of transformation in all beings indeed. You, O Śivā, are the primal cause of the three guṇas, and you are beyond them.
m.2.2.11.15: Of these — sattva, rajas and tamas — you are free of modification, the fourth state together with the worlds. You, abiding within Brahman, set in motion the one cause of the world made of the guṇas; you consume and you protect.
m.2.2.11.16: O seed of all the worlds, whose form is both the knowable and knowledge, O consort of Śiva, ever devoted to the welfare of the world, salutation to you.
m.2.2.11.17: Having heard these words of mine, that Kālī, who brings the worlds into being, lovingly spoke to me, the creator of the worlds, in human speech.
m.2.2.11.18: The Goddess said: O Brahmā, consider for what purpose I have been praised by you. If you are bold enough, let it be stated quickly before me.
m.2.2.11.19: Now that I have appeared before you visibly, the success of the task is certain. Therefore tell me your wish, which I, being propitiated, will fulfil.
m.2.2.11.20: Brahmā said: Listen, O goddess, great sovereign, showing compassion towards me; O all-knowing one, at your command I shall declare the wish that lies in my heart.
m.2.2.11.21: Your husband, O sovereign of the gods, who formerly arose from my forehead — Śiva the yogin, called Rudra — has settled on Kailāsa.
m.2.2.11.22: The Lord of beings practises austerity all alone, free of mental distinctions; wifeless and unchanging, he desires no companion.
m.2.2.11.23: Enchant him so that he looks upon another as his companion, O Satī. Apart from you, no woman will ever captivate his mind.
m.2.2.11.24: Therefore you yourself, by your beauty, become the enchantress of Hara; becoming Dakṣa's daughter, become Rudra's wife, O Śivā.
m.2.2.11.25: Just as you, having taken a body in the form of Lakṣmī, delight Keśava, so do for him, for the welfare of the universe.
m.2.2.11.26: The bull-bannered one rebuked me on merely seeing my longing for a beloved. How then, O goddess, will he of his own accord take a woman?
m.2.2.11.27: Only when Hara has taken a wife can creation be auspicious; how otherwise, when he, its cause at the beginning, middle and end, remains dispassionate?
m.2.2.11.28: Thus absorbed in anxiety, I see no beneficial refuge other than you. I am in distress; therefore do this for me, for the welfare of the universe.
m.2.2.11.29: Neither Viṣṇu, nor Lakṣmī, nor Kāma, nor even I, O Mother of the world, can delude him — no one at all apart from you.
m.2.2.11.30: Therefore, O Great Goddess, being born as Dakṣa's daughter in divine form, become his wife out of regard for my devotion, and enchant the yogin Lord.
m.2.2.11.31: Dakṣa, O sovereign of the gods, is performing austerities on the northern shore of the Ocean of Milk, with you as his aim, his mind fixed on you, firm in his vow.
m.2.2.11.32: Brahmā said: Hearing these words, Śivā then became thoughtful, and the Mother of the world, astonished, said within her mind:
m.2.2.11.33: The Goddess said: Ah, what a great wonder! Though he is the speaker of the Vedas and maker of the universe, devoted to great knowledge, what is this Creator saying?
m.2.2.11.34: A great delusion, bringing unhappiness, has arisen in the Creator's mind, since he wishes to enchant that supreme, changeless one.
m.2.2.11.35: This Vidhi desires from me the boon of enchanting Hara. What gain is there for him in this? That Lord is free of delusion and beyond mental distinctions.
m.2.2.11.36: Śambhu, who is called the supreme Brahman, beyond qualities and changeless — I am ever his servant, always subject to his command.
m.2.2.11.37: That very Śiva, the independent supreme Lord, became the one named Rudra in his full form, for the sake of uplifting his devotees.
m.2.2.11.38: He is the master of Hari and Vidhi, never in any way inferior to Śiva; devoted to yoga, standing beyond māyā, the lord of māyā, higher than the highest.
m.2.2.11.39: Regarding him as his own son, like an ordinary god, this Brahmā wishes to enchant him; hence he is deluded by ignorance.
m.2.2.11.40: If I do not grant the boon, the Vedic norm would be broken. What should I do so that the Lord Maheśvara will not be angry with me?
m.2.2.11.41: Brahmā said: Having reflected thus, Śivā remembered that Maheśa in her mind; then, having obtained Śiva's permission, Durgā spoke to me.
m.2.2.11.42: Durgā said: O Brahmā, all that you have said is indeed true. Apart from me, there is no one here who can enchant Śaṅkara.
m.2.2.11.43: If Hara does not take a wife, this eternal creation will not continue — that truth you have set forth.
m.2.2.11.44: Even the effort I had for enchanting this great Lord — through your words that effort of mine has today become doubled and intense.
m.2.2.11.45: I shall strive in such a way, O Creator, that Hara, himself enchanted, will take a wife.
m.2.2.11.46: Assuming the form of Satī, I, the greatly fortunate one, shall be subject to him alone, his beloved, as Lakṣmī is to Viṣṇu.
m.2.2.11.47: And I shall make an effort, O Creator, by his own grace, so that he too may always be subject to me alone here.
m.2.2.11.48: Born from the wife of Dakṣa in the form of Satī, I shall playfully win over and honour that Śaṅkara, O Grandfather.
m.2.2.11.49: Just as any other creature on earth lives under the sway of a woman, so through devotion to me that Hara will become subject to his wife.
m.2.2.11.50: Brahmā said: Having spoken thus to me, that Śivā, the Mother of the world, while I was watching, dear one, then vanished right there.
m.2.2.11.51: When she had vanished, I, the Grandfather of the worlds, went to where my sons were and described everything to them.
m.2.2.11.iti: Thus ends the eleventh adhyāya, named The praise of Durgā and Brahmā's receiving a boon, in the second khaṇḍa, the Satī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.2.12.1: Nārada said: O Brahmā, best devotee of Śambhu, O wise and sinless one, you have rightly narrated the story of Śiva and Śivā. My birth has been purified and blessed.
m.2.2.12.2: Now tell me: having performed austerity, what boon did Dakṣa, firm in his vows, obtain from the Goddess, and how did she become Dakṣa's daughter?
m.2.2.12.3: Brahmā said: Listen, O Nārada, with devotion, together with all the sages — you are blessed — how Dakṣa of good vows performed austerity and obtained the boon.
m.2.2.12.4: Instructed by me, the wise Dakṣa, the great lord, composing his mind and longing for her, went to worship that Goddess Jagadambikā.
m.2.2.12.5: Placing in his heart her who abides on the northern shore of the Milk Ocean, he began to perform austerity in order to see Ambikā face to face.
m.2.2.12.6: Dakṣa, disciplined, self-controlled and firm in his vows, practised austerity for three thousand years by the reckoning of divine years.
m.2.2.12.7: Living on air, fasting, subsisting on water, and eating leaves, he thus spent that time meditating on her who pervades the world.
m.2.2.12.8: Absorbed in meditation on Durgā and devoted to austerity for a long time, he of good vows worshipped the Goddess with many observances.
m.2.2.12.9: Then, O best of sages, Śivā became manifest before Dakṣa, who, endowed with yama and the other disciplines, was worshipping the Mother of the world.
m.2.2.12.10: Then, having seen with his own eyes the Mother of the world who pervades the world, Dakṣa the Prajāpati considered himself to have fulfilled his purpose.
m.2.2.12.11: He saw her seated on a lion, Kālikā, dark in hue, lovely-faced, four-armed, her hands showing the boon-giving and fear-dispelling gestures and holding a blue lotus and a sword, captivating —
m.2.2.12.12: — with reddish eyes, beautiful loosened hair, the mother of the world, radiant; having bowed deeply, he then praised her with wonderful words.
m.2.2.12.13: Dakṣa said: O Mother of the world, O Great Māyā, O Ruler of the world, O Great Goddess, salutations to you, who out of compassion have shown me your own form.
m.2.2.12.14: Be gracious, O primordial Bhagavatī; be gracious, O you whose form is Śiva; be gracious, O granter of boons to devotees; O Māyā of the world, salutations to you.
m.2.2.12.15: Brahmā said: Thus praised by Dakṣa of restrained mind, O sage, Maheśānī spoke to Dakṣa, though she herself already knew what he desired.
m.2.2.12.16: The Goddess said: O Dakṣa, I am greatly pleased by this true devotion of yours. Choose the boon you desire; there is nothing that cannot be given to you.
m.2.2.12.17: Brahmā said: Hearing the words of the Mother of the world, Dakṣa the Prajāpati, overjoyed, bowed again and again to Śivā and spoke.
m.2.2.12.18: Dakṣa said: O Mother of the world, O Great Māyā, if you are to grant me a boon, listen to my words with kindness and fulfil my wish.
m.2.2.12.19: Śiva, who is my master, has been born as the son of Brahmā, named Rudra, the complete incarnation of the Supreme Self.
m.2.2.12.20: Your incarnation has not taken place; so who could be his wife? O Śivā, descend to earth and enchant that Great Lord.
m.2.2.12.21: Apart from you, no other woman is ever able to enchant him. Therefore, becoming my daughter, now become Hara's wife.
m.2.2.12.22: Thus, performing a beautiful divine play, become the enchantress of Hara. This alone is my boon, O Goddess; I have spoken truly before you.
m.2.2.12.23: This is not for my own sake alone, but for all the worlds too, and for Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śiva; indeed, I have been urged by Brahmā.
m.2.2.12.24: Brahmā said: Hearing these words of the lord of creatures, Jagadambikā smiled and, remembering Śiva in her mind, replied thus.
m.2.2.12.25: The Goddess said: Dear Dakṣa, O Prajāpati, listen to my supreme words. I speak the truth: greatly pleased by your devotion, I am the giver of everything.
m.2.2.12.26: I, Maheśvarī, shall become your daughter, O Dakṣa, born of your wife — there is no doubt — being subject to your devotion.
m.2.2.12.27: I shall make such an effort, performing austerity very hard to endure, and, obtaining that boon from him, O sinless one, I shall become Hara's wife.
m.2.2.12.28: For otherwise the task cannot be accomplished, since that Lord is free from change; Sadāśiva, to be served by Vidhi and Viṣṇu, is indeed complete.
m.2.2.12.29: I am ever his servant and beloved, birth after birth; that Śambhu is indeed my master, even though he bears many forms.
m.2.2.12.30: By the power of a boon he descended from the brow of Vidhi; I too, by his boon, shall descend here at his command.
m.2.2.12.31: Go to your own abode, dear one; your role as messenger is understood by me. Becoming your daughter before long, I shall become Hara's wife.
m.2.2.12.32: Having spoken these true words to Dakṣa and having received Śiva's command in her mind, the Goddess, remembering Śiva's lotus feet, spoke again.
m.2.2.12.33: But, O Prajāpati, a pledge must be kept in your mind. I shall make you hear it; know it to be true, not false.
m.2.2.12.34: When you again become lacking in respect towards me, then I shall truly abandon my own body, and either abide in my own Self or take another form.
m.2.2.12.35: This boon is granted to you, O Prajāpati, for every creation: becoming your daughter, I shall become Hara's beloved.
m.2.2.12.36: Brahmā said: Having spoken thus to Dakṣa, the chief Prajāpati, Maheśānī quickly vanished completely right there, while Dakṣa looked on.
m.2.2.12.37: When Durgā had vanished, Dakṣa too went to his own hermitage and rejoiced that she would become his daughter.
m.2.2.12.iti: Thus ends the twelfth adhyāya, named Dakṣa receives a boon, in the second khaṇḍa, the Satī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.2.13.1: Nārada said: O Brahmā, O Creator (Vidhi), O greatly wise one, best of speakers, tell us: after Dakṣa had gone home gladly, what happened next?
m.2.2.13.2: Brahmā said: Dakṣa the Prajāpati, having gone to his own hermitage with a joyful mind, carried out mind-born creation in many ways at my command.
m.2.2.13.3: Seeing that this creation of beings did not increase, Dakṣa the Prajāpati reported it to me, Brahmā, his father.
m.2.2.13.4: Dakṣa said: O Brahmā, father, lord of creatures, O master, the beings do not increase. All those created by me have remained just as many as I made.
m.2.2.13.5: What shall I do, O lord of creatures? How may they increase by themselves? Tell me the means for that; I shall produce beings, no doubt.
m.2.2.13.6: Brahmā said: O Dakṣa, Prajāpati, my son, hear my supreme counsel. Do that, O best of gods; Śiva will grant you welfare.
m.2.2.13.7: The lovely daughter of Prajāpati Pañcajana, named Asiknī — let her be accepted as your wife, O lord of creatures.
m.2.2.13.8: Adopting the practice of union with a woman, you will again bring about this creation of beings abundantly in that lovely woman of such kind.
m.2.2.13.9: Brahmā said: Then, in order to produce beings by the law of sexual union, he married the daughter of Vīraṇa at my direction.
m.2.2.13.10: Then in her, his own wife Vīriṇī, Dakṣa the Prajāpati begot ten thousand sons called the Haryaśvas.
m.2.2.13.11: All those sons, O sage, were of one and the same virtuous disposition, ever devoted to their father and dedicated to the path of the Vedas.
m.2.2.13.12: Told by their father, all the sons of Dakṣa went to the western direction to perform austerities for the purpose of creating beings, my son.
m.2.2.13.13: There is the supremely purifying sacred place, Lake Nārāyaṇa, where the confluence of the divine river and the ocean has arisen.
m.2.2.13.14: Merely by touching its waters their minds awakened, their inner impurities were washed away, and they became inclined towards the dharma of the paramahaṃsas.
m.2.2.13.15: There those excellent sons of Dakṣa, firm of mind and well restrained by their father's command, performed austerities for the increase of beings.
m.2.2.13.16: And you, Nārada, knowing that they were doing austerities for the sake of creation, went there, having fully understood the heart's intent of Viṣṇu (Mā-pati).
m.2.2.13.17: Without having seen the end of the earth, how are you, Haryaśvas, sons of Dakṣa, intent on making creation? Thus you spoke to them respectfully.
m.2.2.13.18: Brahmā said: Then, having heard what you said, all those Haryaśvas, alert and of innate wisdom, reflected on it deeply by themselves.
m.2.2.13.19: One who does not know the command of the father — the good scripture — which leads to cessation from worldly action, how could he, trusting in the guṇas, undertake to make creation?
m.2.2.13.20: Having decided thus, those wise and single-minded sons bowed to him, circumambulated him, and went on the path of no return.
m.2.2.13.21: O Nārada, O sage, you — being as it were the mind of Śambhu — then roamed the worlds, devoted to none other, unperturbed, acting according to the will of Maheśāna.
m.2.2.13.22: After a very long time had passed, my son the Prajāpati, hearing from Nārada of the loss of his sons, was grieved.
m.2.2.13.23: Again and again he said that having good offspring is a seat of sorrows. Deluded by Śiva's māyā, Dakṣa grieved greatly.
m.2.2.13.24: I came with great affection and consoled my son Dakṣa, showing him a peaceful attitude and saying that fate is mighty.
m.2.2.13.25: Then Dakṣa, consoled by me, begot in Pañcajanī a thousand sons called the Sabalāśvas.
m.2.2.13.26: Those sons too, firm in their vows and directed by their father, went to that place where their elder brothers had gone and attained perfection, for the sake of creating beings.
m.2.2.13.27: Merely by touching its waters their sins were destroyed and their hearts became pure; there, those of good vows performed great austerity, repeating the Brahman (sacred syllable).
m.2.2.13.28: Knowing they were intent on creating beings, O Nārada, you went there and, remembering the Lord's design, spoke words as before.
m.2.2.13.29: Having pointed out their brothers' path, O sage of unfailing vision, you went on your upward course; and those sons too went the way of their brothers.
m.2.2.13.30: At that very time the Prajāpati saw many ill omens; my son Dakṣa was astonished and distressed in mind.
m.2.2.13.31: Dakṣa, greatly alarmed, heard that, as before, it was your doing; swooning with grief for his sons, he lamented their loss exceedingly.
m.2.2.13.32: That Dakṣa became angry with you and said, this one is wicked. Then, by fate, you arrived there, bent on bestowing grace.
m.2.2.13.33: Dakṣa, overcome with grief, his lip quivering with rage, finding you, accosted you and, crying shame, shame, reviled you:
m.2.2.13.34: Dakṣa said: What have you done, O best of the vile, in the guise of the virtuous? You have shown our young boys the path of a mendicant — an evil deed against us.
m.2.2.13.35: By you, merciless rogue, the welfare in both worlds of these boys, not yet freed from the three debts, has been destroyed.
m.2.2.13.36: A man who, setting aside the three debts, renounces home, abandoning mother and father in desire of liberation, goes downward.
m.2.2.13.37: You are merciless and utterly shameless, a corrupter of children's minds and a destroyer of reputation; foolish-minded, you move in vain among the attendants of Hari.
m.2.2.13.38: Again and again you have done me harm, O vilest of the vile; therefore, as you wander, there shall be no fixed abode for you in the worlds.
m.2.2.13.39: Thus Dakṣa, in his grief, then cursed you, who are honoured by the virtuous; deluded by Śiva's māyā, he did not understand the Lord's will.
m.2.2.13.40: And you, O sage, with unperturbed mind, accepted the curse. This indeed is the way of the good, O saintly brāhmaṇa: one endures it oneself.
m.2.2.13.iti: Thus ends the thirteenth adhyāya, named The curse on Nārada in Dakṣa's creation, in the second khaṇḍa, the Satī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.2.14.1: Brahmā said: Meanwhile, O divine sage, I, the grandfather of the worlds, having learned of that incident, quickly came there out of affection.
m.2.2.14.2: Being very discerning, I pacified Dakṣa as before, and, bringing about great pleasure for you, I established close friendship between you and him.
m.2.2.14.3: Having consoled you, my own son, the best of sages, dear to the gods, and taking you along with great affection, I returned to my own abode.
m.2.2.14.4: Then Prajāpati Dakṣa, persuaded by me, begot in his own wife sixty lovely daughters.
m.2.2.14.5: Untiring, he arranged their marriages with Dharma and others. Listen to that with pleasure; I shall relate it, O lord of sages.
m.2.2.14.6: Dakṣa duly gave ten daughters to Dharma, O sage, thirteen to the sage Kaśyapa, and twenty-seven to the Moon.
m.2.2.14.7: To Bhūta, Aṅgiras and Kṛśāśva he gave two daughters each, and the remaining maidens to Tārkṣya; since by their offspring and progeny…
m.2.2.14.8: …the three worlds were filled, that is not described in detail, for fear of prolixity.
m.2.2.14.9: Some say that Śivā was the eldest, others the middle one, some the last-born of all; owing to the difference of kalpas, all three are true.
m.2.2.14.10: After the birth of the daughters, Prajāpati Dakṣa together with his wife meditated in his mind with great love on that Jagadambikā.
m.2.2.14.11: Then with love he praised her in a faltering voice, bowing again and again, with joined palms, full of humility.
m.2.2.14.12: Then the goddess, pleased, reflected in her mind thus: I shall take incarnation in Vīriṇī to fulfil my promise.
m.2.2.14.13: Then Jagadambikā dwelt in Dakṣa's mind, and Dakṣa then shone exceedingly, O best of sages.
m.2.2.14.14: At an auspicious moment Dakṣa joyfully deposited his seed in his wife; then compassionate Śivā dwelt in the mind of Dakṣa's wife.
m.2.2.14.15: All the signs of pregnancy indeed appeared.
m.2.2.14.16: Dear one, Vīriṇī shone all the more, her heart delighted, embodying great auspiciousness through the power of Śivā's dwelling within her.
m.2.2.14.17: Following the traditions of his family and of the Veda, and from loftiness of mind, Dakṣa lovingly performed the sacred rites beginning with puṃsavana.
m.2.2.14.18: A great festival arose then at those rites; the Prajāpati gave wealth to the twice-born as much as they desired.
m.2.2.14.19: Then at that time all the gods, Hari and the rest, knowing that the goddess had entered the womb in Vīriṇī, rejoiced.
m.2.2.14.20: Coming there, they all praised Jagadambikā, the benefactress of the world, bowing again and again.
m.2.2.14.21: Then, with delighted minds, having praised Dakṣa Prajāpati and Vīriṇī in many ways, they went to their own homes.
m.2.2.14.22: When nine months had passed, Śivā, having let the worldly course of gestation take place, when the tenth month was complete, O Nārada,…
m.2.2.14.23: …then immediately appeared before her mother, O sage, at a pleasant moment favourable as to moon, planets and stars.
m.2.2.14.24: As soon as she was born, that Prajāpati, greatly pleased, seeing her blazing with radiance, regarded her as Śiva's goddess.
m.2.2.14.25: Then there was a fine shower of flowers, the clouds rained water, and the directions at once became calm when she was born, O lord of sages.
m.2.2.14.26: The gods, stationed in the sky, played auspicious instruments; the quiet fires blazed up; everything was most auspicious.
m.2.2.14.27: Seeing Jagadambikā born of Vīriṇī, Dakṣa bowed to her, joined his hands, and praised her at length with devotion.
m.2.2.14.28: Dakṣa said: O Maheśānī, salutation to you, O Mother of the world, eternal one. Show mercy, O Mahādevī, O true one, whose very form is truth.
m.2.2.14.29: I bow to you, the bringer of welfare, who are called by the knowers of the Veda Śivā, Śāntā, Mahāmāyā, Yoganidrā and Jaganmayī.
m.2.2.14.30: Appointed by you for the creation of the world, the Creator (Dhātṛ) performed it of old; to you, that supreme Maheśvarī, sustainer of the world, I bow.
m.2.2.14.31: Appointed by you for the preservation of the world, Viṣṇu always carries it out; to you, that supreme Maheśvarī, sustainer of the world, I bow.
m.2.2.14.32: Appointed by you for the dissolution of the world, Rudra always carries it out; to you, that supreme Maheśvarī, sustainer of the world, I bow.
m.2.2.14.33: I bow to you, that goddess Śivā, whose form is rajas, sattva and tamas, who ever accomplishes all works, the mother of the three gods.
m.2.2.14.34: O goddess, whoever meditates on you, the supreme one whose nature is both knowledge and nescience, for him enjoyment and liberation always lie in the palm of his hand.
m.2.2.14.35: O goddess, whoever beholds you directly as the purifying Śivā, revealer of knowledge and nescience, for him liberation will certainly come.
m.2.2.14.36: O Mother of the world, those who praise you as Bhavānī, Ambikā, Jaganmayī and Durgā will obtain everything.
m.2.2.14.37: Brahmā said: Thus praised by the wise Dakṣa, Śivā, the Mother of the world, then spoke to Dakṣa in such a way that her mother did not hear.
m.2.2.14.38: Having deluded everyone, the Supreme Goddess Śivā spoke the truth in such a way that Dakṣa alone should hear it and no one else; thus she of manifold forms spoke.
m.2.2.14.39: The Goddess said: O Prajāpati, I was worshipped by you formerly for the sake of a daughter; your wish is now fulfilled, so take up austerity now.
m.2.2.14.40: Brahmā said: Having thus spoken to Dakṣa, the goddess then, by her own māyā, assumed the state of infancy and cried near her mother.
m.2.2.14.41: Then, hearing that crying and that speech, the women came there in excitement and with great joy, and the maidservants too, in haste.
m.2.2.14.42: Seeing the form of Asiknī's daughter, all the women rejoiced, and all the townspeople too then raised cries of victory.
m.2.2.14.43: And there was a great festival, with singing and instrumental music leading it. Dakṣa and Asiknī felt joy on seeing their daughter's auspicious face.
m.2.2.14.44: Then Dakṣa duly performed the rites prescribed by the Veda and family custom; he gave gifts to the twice-born, and wealth to others as well.
m.2.2.14.45: Everywhere there was singing and dancing, as was fitting; instruments sounded in abundance, accompanied by great auspiciousness.
m.2.2.14.46: Then all the gods, Hari and the rest, with their attendants, arriving together with hosts of sages, celebrated the festival according to rule.
m.2.2.14.47: Seeing Dakṣa's daughter, the Mother, supreme Goddess of the world, all bowed with humility and praised her with auspicious hymns.
m.2.2.14.48: All, delighted, uttered words of victory, victory, and joyfully praised Dakṣa, and Vīriṇī especially.
m.2.2.14.49: Then at their bidding Dakṣa, filled with joy, gave the name Umā to her, who was excellent in all virtues and in her sattva too.
m.2.2.14.50: Other names of hers arose later among people, all bestowing great auspiciousness and especially destroying sorrow.
m.2.2.14.51: Then Dakṣa, bowing to Hari, to me, to all the immortals and to the sages too, with joined palms praised and worshipped them with devotion.
m.2.2.14.52: Then Viṣṇu and all the others, having warmly praised the son of Aja (Dakṣa), went with joy to their own abodes, remembering Śiva together with Śivā.
m.2.2.14.53: Then the mother, having properly performed the purificatory rites for that daughter as was fitting, gave her breast-milk and the like according to the method of nursing infants.
m.2.2.14.54: Nurtured by Vīriṇī and by the great-souled Dakṣa, she grew day by day like the crescent of the moon in the bright fortnight.
m.2.2.14.55: All good qualities entered her, O best of the twice-born, even in childhood, as all the charming digits enter the moon.
m.2.2.14.56: Whenever, acting by her own nature, she was among her companions, she would draw the image of Bharga again and again, day after day.
m.2.2.14.57: When she, Śivā, sang lovely songs befitting childhood, then she remembered Sthāṇu, Hara, Rudra, the chastiser of Smara.
m.2.2.14.58: Every day the incomparable tenderness of the couple grew exceedingly, constantly and again and again, for her who was devoted to them even in childhood.
m.2.2.14.59: Endowed with all the virtues of a child and always attending to her own home, she delighted her parents continually, again and again.
m.2.2.14.iti: Thus ends the fourteenth adhyāya, named The birth of Satī and her childhood play, in the Satī-khaṇḍa of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.2.15.1: Brahmā said: Then one day, O sage, I, together with you, saw that Satī standing beside her father, she who was the very essence of the three worlds.
m.2.2.15.2: Seeing you and me saluted and honoured by her father, Satī, who in her play conformed to the ways of the world, bowed to us with joy and devotion.
m.2.2.15.3: At the end of her salutation, O Nārada, as I and you sat on the fine seats given by Dakṣa, I looked at the humble Satī and said:
m.2.2.15.4: O Satī, obtain as your husband that god, the all-knowing Lord of the world, who desires you alone and whom you desire.
m.2.2.15.5: He who has taken no other wife, does not take one, and will not take one—may he, who has no equal, be your husband, O auspicious one.
m.2.2.15.6: Having said this to her and stayed a long while in Dakṣa's house, we two, given leave by him, went back to our own abodes, O Nārada.
m.2.2.15.7: Hearing that, Dakṣa became very pleased, his anxiety gone, and he took his daughter to himself, regarding her as the Supreme Goddess.
m.2.2.15.8: Thus, through charming childhood pastimes, she who is loving to her devotees and had assumed human form by her own will passed beyond the state of girlhood.
m.2.2.15.9: Passing beyond childhood, Satī attained the first bloom of youth; with a body made exceedingly radiant by austerity, she was captivating in all her limbs.
m.2.2.15.10: Dakṣa, lord of the worlds, seeing her established in budding youth, pondered: How shall I give this daughter to Bharga?
m.2.2.15.11: Then she too, of her own accord, longed day after day to win Bharga; knowing her father's mind, she came to her mother.
m.2.2.15.12: Then that Satī, the auspicious Supreme Goddess of vast intellect, asked her mother Vīriṇī for permission to perform austerity for the sake of Śaṅkara.
m.2.2.15.13: Then Satī, firm in her vow to obtain Maheśāna as husband, worshipped him at home with her mother's permission.
m.2.2.15.14: In the month of Āśvina, on the Nandā lunar day, she worshipped Hara with devotion, with rice cooked with jaggery and with salt; bowing to him, she passed that month.
m.2.2.15.15: On the fourteenth of Kārtika, having worshipped him with cakes and milk-rice heaped up, she meditated on the Supreme Lord.
m.2.2.15.16: In Mārgaśīrṣa, on the dark eighth, having worshipped Hara with sesame, barley-rice and kīla offerings, Satī passed the days.
m.2.2.15.17: In Pauṣa, on the bright seventh, having kept vigil through the night, Satī worshipped Śiva in the morning with kṛśara (rice cooked with sesame).
m.2.2.15.18: In Māgha, on the full-moon day, having kept vigil through the night, she performed the worship of Śaṅkara on a river bank in wet clothes.
m.2.2.15.19: In the month of Tapas (Phālguna), on the dark fourteenth, having kept vigil through the night, she specially worshipped him with bilva leaves in every watch.
m.2.2.15.20: In Caitra, on the bright fourteenth, she worshipped Śiva day and night with palāśa flowers and damana; remembering him, she passed that month.
m.2.2.15.21: On the bright third of Māgha, having worshipped Rudra with sesame food and barley-rice and with cow products, Satī passed that month.
m.2.2.15.22: On the full-moon of Jyeṣṭha, having worshipped Śaṅkara at night with garments and bṛhatī flowers, she passed that month fasting.
m.2.2.15.23: Likewise, on the bright fourteenth of Āṣāḍha, the worship of Rudra was performed by her, clad in black garments, with bṛhatī flowers.
m.2.2.15.24: On the bright eighth and the fourteenth of Śrāvaṇa, she worshipped Śiva with sacred threads, garments and pavitras (purificatory strings).
m.2.2.15.25: In Bhādra, on the dark thirteenth, having worshipped him with various flowers and fruits, on the fourteenth she took only water as food.
m.2.2.15.26: With various fruits, flowers and grains produced in that season, she, strictly regulated in diet and doing japa, performed the worship of Śiva each month.
m.2.2.15.27: In every month and on every day, the goddess Satī, who had assumed human form by her own will, remained devoted to the worship of Śiva and firm in her vow.
m.2.2.15.28: Having thus completed the entire Nandā vow, Satī, fully concentrated, meditated on Śiva with love and became motionless, her mind on nothing else.
m.2.2.15.29: Meanwhile, O sage, all the gods and sages, placing Viṣṇu and me at their head, went to see Satī's austerity.
m.2.2.15.30: Having arrived, the gods saw Satī, like another embodied Siddhi (Perfection), deeply immersed in meditation on Śiva, having then reached the state of perfection.
m.2.2.15.31: All the gods, with joined palms, joyfully bowed to Satī, and the sages too, with bent shoulders, Viṣṇu and the others, delighted at heart.
m.2.2.15.32: Then all, Viṣṇu and the others, gods and sages, very gladdened and filled with wonder, praised that austerity of Satī.
m.2.2.15.33: Then, having again bowed to that goddess, those sages and gods went at once to Kailāsa, the best of mountains, dear to Śiva.
m.2.2.15.34: And I, accompanied by Sāvitrī, and the blessed Vāsudeva too, with Lakṣmī, full of joy, then went into Hara's presence.
m.2.2.15.35: Going there and seeing the Lord, they bowed deeply in reverent haste and, humble with folded hands, praised him with various hymns.
m.2.2.15.36: The gods said: Salutation to you, the Blessed One, from whom this moving and unmoving world arises; to the Puruṣa, the Great Lord, the Supreme Lord, the Great Soul.
m.2.2.15.37: To the primal seed of all, of Prakṛti and of Puruṣa; to the one whose form is consciousness, the Supreme, to Brahman, the changeless.
m.2.2.15.38: You who, having brought forth this universe, are this; by whom this shines forth; from whom this comes, whence this is, to whom this belongs, and in whom it rests—that you are.
m.2.2.15.39: He who is beyond this and beyond the higher, the changeless great Lord, who beholds this universe within his own Self—to him, the Self-born, we bow.
m.2.2.15.40: Of unobstructed vision, supreme, the witness, the Self of all, bearing many forms, the inmost Self, the Supreme Brahman, the one who shines—we have gone to him for refuge.
m.2.2.15.41: Whose state not even the gods, the sages and the Siddhas know, what other creature, then, is able to know and comprehend it?
m.2.2.15.42: You, whose state the truly virtuous, freed from attachment, long to see, and whose conduct they follow, observing a flawless vow together with the world — you are our good refuge.
m.2.2.15.43: No sorrow-giving modifications such as birth exist for you at all; even so, through māyā and out of compassion, you take them on.
m.2.2.15.44: Salutation to you, that supreme Lord of wondrous deeds; salutation to the Brahman, the Supreme Self, who is far beyond words.
m.2.2.15.45: To the formless one who has vast forms, to the transcendent one of infinite power, to the lord of the three worlds, the witness of all, and the all-pervading one;
m.2.2.15.46: Salutation to the self-illumining lamp, the wealth of the bliss of liberation; salutation be to you, whose nature is knowledge, the all-pervading Lord.
m.2.2.15.47: Salutation to the lord of liberation (kaivalya), easily attained through freedom from action; salutation to you, the Puruṣa, the supreme Lord, the giver of all.
m.2.2.15.48: To the knower of the field, whose form is the Self, the cause of all cognitions;
m.2.2.15.49: Salutation to the overseer of all, the great one, the root Prakṛti; salutation to you, the Puruṣa, the supreme Lord, the giver of all.
m.2.2.15.50: Salutation to you, the three-eyed, five-faced, ever-shining one; salutation be to you, the seer of the qualities of all the senses, O causeless one.
m.2.2.15.51: Salutation again and again to the cause of the three worlds, and to the one who is final release; to the giver of release, who swiftly rescues those who come for refuge;
m.2.2.15.52: Salutation be to you, the ocean of all Vedic traditions and Āgamas, the supreme one (Parameṣṭhin), the final resort of devotees and of all virtues.
m.2.2.15.53: Salutation, O Maheśvara, to you whose fire of consciousness is hidden in the fire-stick of the guṇas, whose form is hard for the deluded to attain, and who ever dwells in the hearts of the wise.
m.2.2.15.54: To the releaser of the bound souls (paśu) from their bonds (pāśa), the giver of true liberation to devotees, the self-luminous, eternal, imperishable one of unceasing awareness;
m.2.2.15.55: To the inner seer, the changeless one, the bearer of supreme lordship, whom people worship, desiring the four aims of life and the good goal they wish for: you, that Lord, have been without compassion towards us; be gracious now; salutation to you.
m.2.2.15.56: Whose single-minded devotees desire no object whatever; they only sing your supremely auspicious deeds.
m.2.2.15.57: We praise you, the imperishable supreme Brahman, the all-pervading one of unmanifest form, attainable through the yoga of the Self, the perfectly full.
m.2.2.15.58: We bow to you, the Lord of all, beyond the senses, without support yet the support of all, causeless, infinite, primordial and subtle.
m.2.2.15.59: All the gods beginning with Hari, and likewise the worlds of moving and unmoving beings, have been made by a trifling portion of you, through distinctions of name and form.
m.2.2.15.60: Just as flames from a fire, or rays from the sun, go forth and return again and again, so this stream of creation is said to be secondary.
m.2.2.15.61: You are not a god, a demon or a mortal, nor an animal, nor a twice-born, O Lord; not woman, not neuter, not man; neither being nor non-being, nor anything at all.
m.2.2.15.62: You are what remains after all negation, yet you are everything — maker of the universe, protector of the universe, dissolver of the universe, the Self of the universe; we bow to that Lord.
m.2.2.15.63: We bow to you, the Lord of yoga, whom yogins, their karma burnt away by yoga, behold in a mind purified by yoga.
m.2.2.15.64: Salutation be to you, O one of irresistible force, possessor of the three powers, embodiment of the three Vedas; salutation to the protector of those who seek you; salutation to you of abundant power.
m.2.2.15.65: O Lord hard to reach, salutation to you whose supreme path is unattainable for those with base senses, who delights in uplifting devotees, and whose splendour is hidden.
m.2.2.15.66: By whose power, through the notion of I, the deluded-minded one, alas, does not know the Self — to you, that great Lord of insurmountable greatness, we have bowed.
m.2.2.15.67: Brahmā said: Having thus praised Mahādeva, all the gods headed by Viṣṇu stood silent before the Lord, their necks bowed in true devotion.
m.2.2.15.iti: Thus ends the fifteenth adhyāya, named The rite of the Nandā vow and the praise of Śiva, in the second khaṇḍa, the Satī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.2.16.1: Brahmā said: Having heard this praise offered by Hari and the others, Śaṅkara became exceedingly pleased, and the maker of creation laughed.
m.2.2.16.2: Seeing Brahmā and Viṣṇu come together with their wives, Hara addressed them fittingly and asked them the reason for their coming.
m.2.2.16.3: Rudra said: O Hari, O Vidhi, O gods and sages, now, without fear, tell me truly the reason for your coming.
m.2.2.16.4: For what purpose have you come, and what task is there here? I wish to hear all that, my mind pleased by your praise.
m.2.2.16.5: Brahmā said: When Hara asked thus, O sage, I, the grandsire of all worlds, urged on by Viṣṇu, spoke to Mahādeva.
m.2.2.16.6: O God of gods, Mahādeva, ocean of compassion, Lord, hear the purpose for which we two have come, together with the gods and sages.
m.2.2.16.7: We have come especially for your sake, O Vṛṣabhadhvaja; for those who share a common purpose it is always fitting to act together; otherwise the world could not exist.
m.2.2.16.8: Some asuras, O Maheśvara, will be slayable by me; likewise some by Hari, and some also by you.
m.2.2.16.9: Some, O great Lord, will be slain by the son born of your seed; and some asuras, O Lord, will always be slain by Māyā.
m.2.2.16.10: By your grace alone, O Śambhu, there will be supreme happiness for the gods; having destroyed the terrible asuras, the world will enjoy well-being, ever free from fear.
m.2.2.16.11: But if you remain ever absorbed in yoga, free from attachment and aversion, devoted solely to compassion, then they would not be slain by you at all.
m.2.2.16.12: If they are favoured by you, O Lord, how will creation and preservation go on? Therefore it will be proper for you to act constantly, O Vṛṣadhvaja.
m.2.2.16.13: If the acts of creation, preservation and dissolution are not to be done, then our division into separate bodies, and that of Māyā, is pointless.
m.2.2.16.14: For we are of one essential form, distinct only by the distinction of function; if the distinction of function is not fulfilled, the distinction of form is purposeless.
m.2.2.16.15: The one Supreme Self, Maheśvara, has divided himself threefold solely by reason of Māyā; independent, the Lord does this in play.
m.2.2.16.16: Hari is born from his left side, and I from his right side; and you, born from Śiva's heart, are Śiva in complete form.
m.2.2.16.17: Thus, O Lord, we have become threefold, of distinct forms, sons of Śivā and Śiva; know this truth in your heart, O eternal one.
m.2.2.16.18: I and Viṣṇu, together with our wives, have come into being for the sake of the work, gladly performing the work of the world at your command, O Lord.
m.2.2.16.19: Therefore, for the welfare of the universe and the happiness of the gods, take as your wife one most beautiful woman.
m.2.2.16.20: Hear something more, O Maheśāna: a past event I have recalled, which you yourself, in the form of Śiva, once declared before us.
m.2.2.16.21: O Brahmā, a supreme form of mine like this will become manifest in the world from your body, celebrated by the name Rudra.
m.2.2.16.22: Brahmā became the creator, Hari the preserver; I, in the form of Rudra, an embodiment of the guṇa, shall be the agent of dissolution.
m.2.2.16.23: Having married a woman, I shall accomplish the highest work for the world. Remembering this, which you yourself said, fulfil your own pledge.
m.2.2.16.24: By your command, O Master, I am the creator and Hari the preserver; and you, Śiva himself manifested, are the cause of dissolution.
m.2.2.16.25: Without you we two are not capable in our respective tasks; therefore take one beloved woman devoted to the work of the world.
m.2.2.16.26: Just as Padmālayā Lakṣmī is Viṣṇu's and Sāvitrī is mine, so, O Śambhu, take now a beloved companion.
m.2.2.16.27: Brahmā said: Hearing these words of mine, Brahmā, in Hari's presence, Hara, lord of the worlds, with a smiling face, spoke to me.
m.2.2.16.28: Īśvara said: O Brahmā, O Hari, you two are always most dear to me; on seeing you, my joy indeed becomes exceedingly great.
m.2.2.16.29: You two are indeed pre-eminent among the gods, the masters of the three worlds; the word of you two, whose minds are devoted to the affairs of the world, is weighty.
m.2.2.16.30: Yet marriage is not fitting for me, O best of gods, who am devoted to austerity, detached, and ever known as a yogin.
m.2.2.16.31: One who stands on the good path of renunciation, delights in his own Self, is stainless, of the body of an avadhūta, a knower, a seer of the Self, devoid of desire—
m.2.2.16.32: unchanging, not given to enjoyment, ever impure and inauspicious—tell me now, what need has such a one for a woman in the world?
m.2.2.16.33: For me, absorbed solely in yoga, there is always bliss; it is the man devoid of knowledge who considers desire to be of much worth.
m.2.2.16.34: Marriage in the world should be known as a great bondage; therefore I have no liking for it—I speak the truth, the truth.
m.2.2.16.35: My engagement in this is not for my own sake, having rightly reflected on my own interest; nevertheless I shall do what you have said, for the good of the world.
m.2.2.16.36: Considering your words weighty, and to fulfil my own declaration, I shall indeed marry, for I am always subject to my devotees.
m.2.2.16.37: But hear, O Hari, O Brahmā, what kind of beloved I shall take according to my condition; my words are indeed fitting.
m.2.2.16.38: She who is able to receive my energy in divided portions—point her out to me as a wife: a yoginī who can assume any form at will.
m.2.2.16.39: When I am absorbed in yoga, she too must be a yoginī; when I am given to love, she too must be a loving woman.
m.2.2.16.40: That Imperishable which the wise knowers of the Veda proclaim—the eternal Śiva in the form of light—that I shall contemplate.
m.2.2.16.41: When, absorbed in contemplation of That Brahman, O Brahmā, I approach a woman, she who would produce obstacles there must not be my wife; such a one would be struck down by me.
m.2.2.16.42: You, or Viṣṇu, or I too, O greatly fortunate ones, are portions of Śiva who has the form of Brahman; contemplation of him is fitting.
m.2.2.16.43: I shall remain in that contemplation even without marriage, O lotus-seated one. Therefore, you designate for me a wife who will always conform to my activity.
m.2.2.16.44: Even so, O Brahmā, hear from me one condition concerning myself: if she has distrust in my words, she will be abandoned by me.
m.2.2.16.45: Brahmā said: Having heard these words of Hara, I, and that Viṣṇu, with glad minds, smiling, humbly spoke thus.
m.2.2.16.46: Listen, O Lord, O Maheśāna: with great affection I shall tell you of a woman such as you have sought, O master.
m.2.2.16.47: That Umā, accomplishing the divine purpose, was born in separate forms: formerly, O Lord, as Sarasvatī and likewise as Lakṣmī, in a twofold form.
m.2.2.16.48: Padmā became the beloved of Viṣṇu, and likewise Sarasvatī mine; in a third form she came into being for us, desiring the welfare of the world's work.
m.2.2.16.49: She who was born as the daughter of Dakṣa, Satī by name, O all-pervading one — she alone would be such a wife, for she would bring benefit.
m.2.2.16.50: She, O lord of the gods, firm in her vow, is performing austerities for your sake — Satī, of great splendour, desiring to obtain you as her husband.
m.2.2.16.51: Go to grant her a boon; show her grace, O Maheśvara. Having given her such a boon, marry her with great joy.
m.2.2.16.52: This is the wish of Hari, of me and of the gods, O Śaṅkara: fulfil it with your gracious glance, so that we may reverently behold the festival.
m.2.2.16.53: May there be supreme auspiciousness, bringing happiness in the three worlds; the affliction of all would surely perish — there is no doubt here.
m.2.2.16.54: Then, at the close of our words, Madhusūdana Acyuta spoke to Īśāna, whose form arises from his sport and who is affectionate to his devotees.
m.2.2.16.55: Viṣṇu said: O God of gods, Mahādeva, mine of compassion, Śaṅkara, all that Brahmā has said is said by me too; there is no doubt.
m.2.2.16.56: Do that, O Maheśāna, showing grace to me; by marrying her duly, make the three worlds protected through your gracious glance.
m.2.2.16.57: Brahmā said: Having said this, O sage, the wise Lord Viṣṇu fell silent. That Lord, affectionate to his devotees, laughed and said, so be it.
m.2.2.16.58: Then we two, having received his command, went with the sages and gods to our desired abodes, accompanied by our wives and supremely delighted.
m.2.2.16.iti: Thus ends the sixteenth adhyāya, named The prayer to Śiva made by Viṣṇu and Brahmā, in the second khaṇḍa, the Satī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.2.17.1: Brahmā said: Having spoken thus, supreme praise of Śambhu was offered by all the gods. Now listen attentively, O sage, to how she obtained the boon from Śiva.
m.2.2.17.2: Then Satī, having again fasted on the eighth day of the bright fortnight in the month of Āśvina, worshipped the Lord of all with devotion.
m.2.2.17.3: When the Nandā vow had thus been completed, on the ninth day, during the daytime, Hara became manifest before her as she was absorbed in meditation.
m.2.2.17.4: Beautiful in every limb, fair-complexioned, five-faced, three-eyed, the moon on his forehead, gracious of spirit, dark-throated and four-armed;
m.2.2.17.5: holding the trident, Brahmā's skull, and the gestures of boon and fearlessness, gleaming with ash, his head resplendent with the heavenly river, charming in all his limbs;
m.2.2.17.6: an abode of great loveliness, his face like ten million moons, his radiance equal to ten million Kāmas, his form in every way pleasing to women.
m.2.2.17.7: Seeing Hara, the Lord of such a form, before her eyes, Satī bowed at his feet, her face lowered in deep modesty.
m.2.2.17.8: Then Mahādeva, the giver of the fruit of austerity, though himself desiring her as his wife, spoke to Satī, the observer of that vow.
m.2.2.17.9: Mahādeva said: O daughter of Dakṣa, O you of excellent vows, I am pleased with this vow. Choose a boon; I shall grant whatever is your wish.
m.2.2.17.10: Brahmā said: Though he knew her feeling, Mahādeva, lord of the world, said, choose a boon, wishing to hear her words.
m.2.2.17.11: She too, overcome by bashfulness, could not speak what lay in her heart; what she desired was once more veiled by modesty.
m.2.2.17.12: Hearing Śiva's dear words, she became utterly immersed in love. Knowing this, Śaṅkara, affectionate to his devotees, was greatly pleased.
m.2.2.17.13: Tell the boon, tell the boon, he said again quickly — Śambhu, swayed by Satī's devotion, the inner controller, the refuge of the good.
m.2.2.17.14: Then, when Satī, restraining her bashfulness, said to Hara, O giver of boons, grant me the boon as I wish, without hindrance...,
m.2.2.17.15: then, without waiting for the end of her sentence, the bull-bannered one, affectionate to devotees, said to her, be my wife.
m.2.2.17.16: Hearing his words, which brought about the fruit she desired, she stood silent, overjoyed, having obtained the boon in her heart.
m.2.2.17.17: Standing before Hara, who was full of desire, she of the lovely smile displayed her own feelings and the amorous gestures that heighten love.
m.2.2.17.18: Then the sentiment called śṛṅgāra, taking up those feelings, swiftly entered the minds of both, along with its graces and gestures, as described in the treatises.
m.2.2.17.19: Through its entry, O divine sage, a certain splendour came over those two who were following the play of the world, like the conjunction of the star Citrā and the moon.
m.2.2.17.20: Satī, having won Hara, whose body gleamed like crystal, shone with the lustre of glossy, ground collyrium, like a streak of cloud near the moon.
m.2.2.17.21: Then Dākṣāyaṇī, greatly pleased, folding her hands and bowing, said this again and again to Hara, affectionate to devotees:
m.2.2.17.22: Satī said: O God of gods, Mahādeva, Lord, O master of the world, make it known to my father and take me by the rite of marriage.
m.2.2.17.23: Brahmā said: Hearing Satī's words thus, Maheśa, affectionate to devotees, looked at her lovingly and said, so be it.
m.2.2.17.24: Dākṣāyaṇī too, bowing to Śambhu and respectfully taking leave, having received permission, went to her mother, filled with infatuation and joy.
m.2.2.17.25: Hara too, entering his own hermitage on the ridge of Himavat, with difficulty became intent on meditation because of his separation from Dākṣāyaṇī.
m.2.2.17.26: Composing his mind and adopting the ways of the world, Śambhu, the bull-bannered, thought of me in his mind, O divine sage.
m.2.2.17.27: Then I, being thought of by Maheśa the trident-bearer, quickly arrived before him, impelled by Hara's power.
m.2.2.17.28: Where Hara, separated from her, stayed on the ridge of Himavat, there indeed I arrived, dear child, accompanied by Sarasvatī.
m.2.2.17.29: Seeing me with Sarasvatī, O divine sage, the Lord Śambhu, eager and bound by love for Satī, spoke.
m.2.2.17.30: Śambhu said: O Brahmā, I have become intent on my own interest; since I am engaged in taking a wife, a sense of ownership, as it were, now appears in me regarding my own purpose.
m.2.2.17.31: I was worshipped with devotion by Satī, the daughter of Dakṣa, and through the power of the Nandā vow I granted her a boon.
m.2.2.17.32: Be my husband — this boon was chosen from me by her, O Brahmā; and I, wholly pleased, said, be my wife.
m.2.2.17.33: Then Satī, the daughter of Dakṣa, said to me thus: Make it known to my father and take me, O lord of the world.
m.2.2.17.34: That too I accepted, O Brahmā, pleased by her devotion. She has gone to her mother's house, and I have come here, O Vidhi.
m.2.2.17.35: Therefore, at my command, go to Dakṣa's house and speak in such a way that Dakṣa gives that maiden to me without delay.
m.2.2.17.36: Act so that my separation from Satī may come to an end; reassure that Dakṣa, you who are skilled in all knowledge.
m.2.2.17.37: Brahmā said: Having said this, Mahādeva, in my presence — mine, the Prajāpati — looked at Sarasvatī and at once fell under the sway of separation.
m.2.2.17.38: Thus commanded by him, I, feeling fulfilled and full of joy, spoke thus to that lord of the worlds, affectionate to devotees:
m.2.2.17.39: Brahmā said: What you say, O blessed Śambhu, has been well considered and firmly decided. It is indeed the chief interest of the gods, and of mine as well, O bull-bannered one.
m.2.2.17.40: Dakṣa will himself give his own daughter to you, and I too will convey your words in his presence.
m.2.2.17.41: Brahmā said: Having spoken thus to Mahādeva, the lord of all, the master, I went to Dakṣa's abode in a very swift chariot.
m.2.2.17.42: Nārada said: O Creator, wise and greatly fortunate one, best of speakers, tell us: what did Dakṣa then do for Satī when she had come home?
m.2.2.17.43: Brahmā said: Having performed austerities and obtained the boon her mind desired, Satī went home and then bowed to her father and mother.
m.2.2.17.44: Then, through her own friend, she related all that to her mother and father — Satī's obtaining of a boon from Maheśvara, who was pleased by her devotion.
m.2.2.17.45: The mother and father, hearing the whole account from the friend's mouth, attained supreme joy and held a great festival.
m.2.2.17.46: The generous-minded Dakṣa gave wealth to the twice-born as they desired, and so did the great-hearted Vīriṇī, to others too, the blind and the poor.
m.2.2.17.47: Vīriṇī, embracing her own daughter who increased their joy, and delightedly kissing her on the head, praised her again and again.
m.2.2.17.48: Then, after some time had passed, Dakṣa, foremost of knowers of dharma, pondered: How is this daughter of mine to be given to Śambhu?
m.2.2.17.49: Though Mahādeva came and was pleased, he went away. How will he come here again for the sake of my daughter?
m.2.2.17.50: Should someone be sent by me quickly to Śambhu's presence? That is not proper: if he does not accept, the entreaty would thus be fruitless.
m.2.2.17.51: Or else I shall worship that very bull-bannered one, so that he of his own accord may become husband of my daughter through devotion.
m.2.2.17.52: Worshipped by her too with noble effort, he also desires it; her wish, may Śambhu be my husband, has been sanctioned by the boon he gave.
m.2.2.17.53: As that Dakṣa was pondering thus day after day, I suddenly appeared before him then, accompanied by Sarasvatī.
m.2.2.17.54: Seeing me, his father, Dakṣa bowed and stood with head lowered, and gave a seat to me, his own source, as was fitting.
m.2.2.17.55: Then Dakṣa, though anxious yet delighted, quickly asked me, the lord of all worlds, the reason for my coming there.
m.2.2.17.56: Dakṣa said: What is the reason for your coming and entering here, O Creator? Showing great grace toward me, tell it, O preceptor of the world.
m.2.2.17.57: Have you come to my hermitage out of affection for your son, or because of some task, O maker of the worlds? I am delighted at the sight of you.
m.2.2.17.58: Brahmā said: Thus asked by my own son Dakṣa, O best of sages, I, smiling, spoke these words, gladdening that Prajāpati.
m.2.2.17.59: Brahmā said: Listen, Dakṣa, to the purpose for which I have come to you: a benefit to come from you, which is desired by me and by you as well.
m.2.2.17.60: Your daughter propitiated Mahādeva, lord of the world; the time for the boon she requested has now arrived.
m.2.2.17.61: I have certainly been sent to you by Śambhu for the sake of your daughter; determine what is to be done that is beneficial.
m.2.2.17.62: Since Rudra Śaṅkara departed after granting the boon, from that time on he truly finds no peace because of separation from your daughter.
m.2.2.17.63: Madana, finding no weak point, could not conquer Giriśa, even after trying many times with all his flowery arrows.
m.2.2.17.64: Yet he, pierced by Kāma's arrows, has abandoned contemplation of the Self and remains thinking of Satī, agitated like an ordinary man.
m.2.2.17.65: Forgetting, through separation, the words he had uttered before the Gaṇas, he keeps asking all around where Satī is, even in his abasement.
m.2.2.17.66: What was desired earlier by me, by you, by Madana and by the great sages beginning with Marīci has now been accomplished, my son.
m.2.2.17.67: Śambhu, propitiated by your daughter, is himself, from thinking of her, desirous of seeking her out, and stays on the Himavat mountain.
m.2.2.17.68: Just as Śambhu was propitiated by her with various sentiments, with sincerity and with that vow, so in the same way is Satī being propitiated by him.
m.2.2.17.69: Therefore, Dakṣa, give him without delay your daughter, destined for Śambhu; your purpose will then be fulfilled.
m.2.2.17.70: I shall bring him to your abode with Nārada; give her to him, she who has been destined for that purpose.
m.2.2.17.71: Brahmā said: Hearing my words thus, my son Dakṣa was overjoyed, and, supremely delighted, he said to me, so be it.
m.2.2.17.72: Then, O sage, I, exceedingly delighted and eager, went to where Giriśa, devoted to the welfare of the worlds, was staying.
m.2.2.17.73: When I had gone, O Nārada, Dakṣa too, together with his wife and daughter, became one whose desires were fulfilled, as if filled with nectar.
m.2.2.17.iti: Thus ends the seventeenth adhyāya, named Satī obtains her boon, in the second khaṇḍa, the Satī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.2.18.1: Nārada said: When you had gone to Rudra's side, what happened then? What news was there, dear father? What did Hara himself do?
m.2.2.18.2: Brahmā said: Then I, gladdened, went to the great god Śiva, the supreme lord dwelling on the Himavat mountain, in order to bring him.
m.2.2.18.3: Seeing me, the creator of the worlds, approaching, the bull-bannered god kept turning over in his mind, again and again, doubts about obtaining Satī.
m.2.2.18.4: Then Hara, playfully adopting the way of the world, out of affection and devotion to Satī quickly spoke to me like an ordinary man.
m.2.2.18.5: Īśvara said: O eldest of the gods, what has that son of yours done for me in the matter of Satī? Tell me, so that my heart may not be torn apart by Manmatha.
m.2.2.18.6: Separation, rushing on, strikes me alone, on account of Satī, O eldest of the gods, sparing every other living being.
m.2.2.18.7: Satī, Satī, I cry constantly, O Brahmā; tell me, and I will do what must be done. Being non-different from me, she is to be won by me; so, O Creator, let it be done accordingly.
m.2.2.18.8: Brahmā said: Hearing these words spoken by Rudra, full of worldly convention, I, O sage Nārada, said to Śiva, consoling him:
m.2.2.18.9: Brahmā said: O bull-bannered one, hear what my son said concerning Satī, and know that your aim is accomplished.
m.2.2.18.10: Dakṣa said: My daughter is to be given by me to him; she was conceived for that very purpose. This deed is my own wish, and all the more so because of your word.
m.2.2.18.11: Śambhu has been worshipped by my daughter for this very purpose; and since he himself now seeks her from me, she is then to be given by me to Hara.
m.2.2.18.12: Let him come to me at an auspicious lagna and a favourable muhūrta; then, O Vidhi, I shall give my daughter to Śambhu as alms.
m.2.2.18.13: So Dakṣa told me. Therefore, O bull-bannered one, go to his house at an auspicious moment and bring her.
m.2.2.18.14: Brahmā said: Hearing my words, Rudra, kind to his devotees, adopting the worldly manner, spoke to me with a smile, O sage:
m.2.2.18.15: Rudra said: I shall go to his house together with you and Nārada. O creator of the world, therefore call Nārada to mind.
m.2.2.18.16: Call to mind also your mind-born sons, Marīci and the rest; with them and my gaṇas I shall go to Dakṣa's abode, O Vidhi.
m.2.2.18.17: Brahmā said: Thus commanded by the Lord, who was intent on worldly custom, I called to mind you, Nārada, and likewise my sons Marīci and the others.
m.2.2.18.18: Then all the mind-born sons, together with you, came quickly and with reverence, delighted, at my mere remembering of them.
m.2.2.18.19: Viṣṇu, the king among Śiva's devotees, remembered by Rudra, came swiftly with his own hosts and with Kamalā, mounted on Garuḍa.
m.2.2.18.20: Then in the bright fortnight of Caitra, under the constellation presided over by Bhaga, on the thirteenth day, a Sunday, the great Lord set out.
m.2.2.18.21: Going along with all the hosts of gods led by Brahmā and Viṣṇu, and with those sages, Śaṅkara shone on the road.
m.2.2.18.22: On the way a great festivity arose among the gods and others as they went, and likewise among Hara's gaṇas, whose minds were exceedingly joyful.
m.2.2.18.23: The elephant -hide, the bull, the tiger -skin, the serpents, the matted locks and the crescent moon all became ornaments, as was fitting, by Śiva's will.
m.2.2.18.24: Then in a moment, on his strong and swift bull, Hara, with Viṣṇu and the other leaders, joyfully reached Dakṣa's abode.
m.2.2.18.25: Then Dakṣa, humble in spirit, his hair bristling with delight, went forth to meet him, accompanied by all his own people.
m.2.2.18.26: All the hosts of gods there were honoured by Dakṣa himself and, with the sages, were seated in due order beside the Supreme One.
m.2.2.18.27: Having all the gods and gaṇas, along with the sages, surround him properly, Dakṣa led Śiva into the interior of the house.
m.2.2.18.28: Then Dakṣa, glad at heart, himself worshipped Hara, lord of all, according to the rites, having offered him an excellent seat.
m.2.2.18.29: Then he worshipped Viṣṇu, me, the brahmins, all the gods and the gaṇas with true devotion, according to the proper rites.
m.2.2.18.30: Having performed fitting worship of them, with the worshipful ones and others, Dakṣa then held consultation with the mind-born sages.
m.2.2.18.31: Then Dakṣa, my son, bowing, lovingly said to me, his father: O lord, the wedding rite should be performed by you.
m.2.2.18.32: Saying, very well, with a delighted heart I rose and then performed that entire rite accordingly.
m.2.2.18.33: Then at an auspicious moment, in a lagna endowed with planetary strength, Dakṣa joyfully gave his own daughter Satī to Śambhu.
m.2.2.18.34: And the bull-bannered one, delighted, then took the hand of the fair-bodied daughter of Dakṣa according to the marriage rite.
m.2.2.18.35: I, Hari, you and the others, the sages, gods and gaṇas — all bowed and pleased the Lord with hymns of praise.
m.2.2.18.36: There was a great festival, with dancing and singing; all the hosts of sages and the gods attained supreme joy.
m.2.2.18.37: Having given away his daughter, Dakṣa, my son, then felt his purpose fulfilled; Śiva and Śivā were pleased, and everything became an abode of auspiciousness.
m.2.2.18.iti: Thus ends the eighteenth adhyāya, named The giving away of the bride, in the second khaṇḍa, the Satī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.2.19.1: Brahmā said: Having performed the gift of his daughter, Dakṣa, greatly pleased, gave Hara a dowry of many kinds, and gave the brahmins wealth of many kinds.
m.2.2.19.2: Then Garuḍadhvaja Viṣṇu, together with Kamalā, approached Śambhu, rose, and with joined palms said this:
m.2.2.19.3: Viṣṇu said: O God of gods, O Mahādeva, O ocean of compassion, O Lord, you, dear one, are the father of the worlds, and Satī is the mother of all.
m.2.2.19.4: You two are indeed playful incarnations, always for the welfare of the good and for the restraint of the wicked; this is the eternal teaching of the Veda.
m.2.2.19.5: O Hara, you shine with Dākṣāyaṇī, whose beauty is dark like glossy blue collyrium, just as I shine with Padmā, in the reverse way.
m.2.2.19.6: Together with this Satī, protect the gods and men, the virtuous; and likewise, O Śambhu, always grant auspiciousness to those who move in worldly existence.
m.2.2.19.7: Whoever, having seen or heard of her, becomes filled with desire for her—him you should slay, O Lord of all beings. This is my request, O Lord.
m.2.2.19.8: Brahmā said: Hearing these words of Viṣṇu, the all-knowing Supreme Lord laughed and said to Madhusūdana, so be it.
m.2.2.19.9: Hari, returning to his own place, remained there, O lord of sages; he had a festival held and kept that matter guarded.
m.2.2.19.10: I approached the Goddess and, by the procedure stated in the Gṛhya texts, performed the entire fire-rite as prescribed, in full detail.
m.2.2.19.11: Then Śivā and Śiva, joyfully and according to rule, circumambulated the fire at the command of me, the officiating teacher, and of the brahmins.
m.2.2.19.12: Then a wonderful great festival took place there, O best of brahmins, with music, preceded by song and dance, delightful to all.
m.2.2.19.13: At that time an exceedingly wondrous event took place there, most astonishing, dear one; listen to it, I shall tell you.
m.2.2.19.14: Śambhu's māyā is hard to understand; by it the world, with all moving and unmoving things, gods, demons and humans, is utterly deluded.
m.2.2.19.15: I, who once wished to delude Śambhu by trickery—me Śaṅkara, dear one, deluded in turn through his play.
m.2.2.19.16: Whoever wishes harm to another, that harm surely comes to him alone; thinking thus, a person should not do harm to another.
m.2.2.19.17: As Satī was circumambulating the fire, her two feet became visible from beneath her garment, and I saw them, O sage.
m.2.2.19.18: With my mind possessed by Madana, deluded by Śiva's māyā, I gazed at Satī's limbs, O best of brahmins.
m.2.2.19.19: The more I eagerly looked at Satī's lovely limbs, the more excited and tormented by desire I became.
m.2.2.19.20: Having thus seen Dakṣa's daughter, the devoted wife, I, my mind possessed by Smara, became eager to see her face, O sage.
m.2.2.19.21: Out of shame before Śambhu, her face could not be looked at directly; nor did she, overcome with modesty, reveal her face.
m.2.2.19.22: Then, considering a good means of seeing it, I, tormented by desire, afterwards accomplished it by means of dreadful smoke.
m.2.2.19.23: Throwing much wet fuel into the fire there, and offering only a little ghee as oblation, smoke arising from the wet material was produced.
m.2.2.19.24: Then dense smoke arose there on all sides, such that the ground built for the altar was turned into darkness.
m.2.2.19.25: Then Maheśa, the Supreme Lord, the master of many sports, covered his smoke-troubled eyes with his hands.
m.2.2.19.26: Then, lifting the veil, I, tormented by desire, looked at Satī's face, O sage, with a thrilled inner heart.
