m.2.2.27.56: Thus the curse on that sacrifice has been described by me, O lord of sages. Now the account of the sacrifice's destruction is being told; listen attentively.
m.2.2.27.iti: Thus ends the twenty-seventh adhyāya, named The beginning of the sacrifice, in the second khaṇḍa, the Satī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.2.28.1: Brahmā said: When the gods and sages went with festivity to Dakṣa's sacrifice, at that very time the goddess, on Mount Gandhamādana,
m.2.2.28.2: in a fountain-house with a canopy, surrounded by her friends, Satī, the daughter of Dakṣa, engaged in many kinds of grand play.
m.2.2.28.3: Then the goddess Satī, absorbed in play, joyfully saw the Moon, having taken leave, hastening with Rohiṇī toward Dakṣa's sacrifice.
m.2.2.28.4: Having seen this, Satī spoke to the fortunate Vijayā, her own foremost friend, dear to her as life, and ever bringing her good.
m.2.2.28.5: Satī said: O best of friends, O Vijayā, dear to me as life, where is this Moon going with Rohiṇī? Ask quickly.
m.2.2.28.6: Brahmā said: Thus addressed by Satī, Vijayā went quickly into his presence and fittingly asked the Moon, where are you going?
m.2.2.28.7: Then, having heard what Vijayā said, he respectfully told her first of his own journey—all about Dakṣa's sacrificial festival and the rest.
m.2.2.28.8: Hearing that, Vijayā, hurried and agitated, told the goddess Satī all that the Moon had said.
m.2.2.28.9: Hearing that, the goddess Kālikā Satī was then astonished; reflecting, and not finding the reason for it, she pondered in her mind:
m.2.2.28.10: Dakṣa is my father and Vīriṇī my mother; why have they not invited us two? Have they forgotten me, their beloved daughter? So thought Satī.
m.2.2.28.11: I shall respectfully ask Śaṅkara the whole reason for this. Having thought thus, she became firmly resolved to go there.
m.2.2.28.12: Then the goddess Dākṣāyaṇī, leaving her foremost friend Vijayā there, quickly went to Śiva's presence.
m.2.2.28.13: She saw him seated in the midst of the assembly with many gaṇas—Nandin and other great heroes, the foremost leaders of troops.
m.2.2.28.14: Having seen him, the Lord Īśāna, her own husband, Dakṣa's daughter then quickly approached Śaṅkara to ask the reason for that.
m.2.2.28.15: Śiva, full of affection, placed his beloved on his lap and delighted her with words, showing her great honour.
m.2.2.28.16: Then Śambhu, of great sport, lord of all, giver of happiness to the good, seated amid the gaṇas, quickly and respectfully spoke to Satī.
m.2.2.28.17: Śambhu said: Why have you come here into the midst of the assembly, looking astonished? Tell me the reason quickly and gladly, O slender-waisted one.
m.2.2.28.18: Brahmā said: Thus addressed then by Maheśa, O lord of sages, Satī—Śivā—with folded hands, bowing deeply at once, spoke to the Lord.
m.2.2.28.19: Satī said: I have heard that a great sacrifice of my father is taking place. There is a great festival there; the gods and sages have assembled.
m.2.2.28.20: Why does going to my father's great sacrifice not please you, O Lord of the god of gods? Tell me all of it, O master.
m.2.2.28.21: This indeed is the way of kinsfolk: friends keep company with friends, O Mahādeva, which increases affection.
m.2.2.28.22: Therefore, with every effort, go with me today, O Lord, to my father's sacrificial ground, O master, at my request.
m.2.2.28.23: Brahmā said: Hearing those words of Satī, the god Maheśvara, his heart pierced by the arrows of Dakṣa's words, spoke kind words.
m.2.2.28.24: Maheśvara said: Dakṣa, your father, O goddess, is especially hostile to me.
m.2.2.28.25: All those who honour him—the others, headed by the gods and sages—who have gone to your father's sacrifice are fools, devoid of wisdom.
m.2.2.28.26: And those who go uninvited to another's house, O goddess, meet with dishonour worse than death.
m.2.2.28.27: Even Indra, going in that way to another's house, becomes belittled; what then to speak of others? Such a journey is indeed disgraceful.
m.2.2.28.28: Therefore neither you nor I should by any means go to Dakṣa's sacrifice; I have told you the truth, my dear.
m.2.2.28.29: A man is not so pained even when wounded by enemies' arrows as he is when struck in his vitals by the harsh words of his own people.
m.2.2.28.30: When their discernment is destroyed by the six qualities—learning and the rest—which in the good are virtues but in the wicked are otherwise, the wicked do not see the glory of the great, my dear.
m.2.2.28.31: Brahmā said: Thus addressed by the great-souled Maheśa, Satī, filled with anger, spoke to Śiva, the best of those skilled in speech.
m.2.2.28.32: Satī said: You, O Śambhu, Lord of all, by whom a sacrifice becomes fruitful—you have not been invited today by that evil-doing father of mine.
m.2.2.28.33: I wish to know all that, O Bhava—the intention of that wicked one, and of all the wicked gods and sages who have come there.
m.2.2.28.34: Therefore I am going this very day to my father's sacrifice, O Lord. Give me permission to go there, O master, Maheśvara.
m.2.2.28.35: Brahmā said: Thus addressed by that goddess, the blessed Rudra, Śiva himself—the seer whose vision knows all, the cause of creation—spoke to Satī.
m.2.2.28.36: Śiva said: If such is your desire, O goddess, that you must go there, then, O you of good vows, go quickly to your father's sacrifice with my consent.
m.2.2.28.37: Mount this bull Nandin, made ready with care, and, furnished with great royal honours, endowed with many excellences, go.
m.2.2.28.38: Told by Rudra to mount the adorned bull, Satī, finely adorned and fully equipped, went to her father's house.
m.2.2.28.39: Great royal insignia were given to her by the Supreme Self—a fine umbrella, chowries and the like, and excellent garments and ornaments.
m.2.2.28.40: Sixty thousand fierce gaṇas of Rudra went by Śiva's command, full of curiosity, delighted, and in high festive spirit.
m.2.2.28.41: Then a great festivity arose there on all sides during the journey of Satī, Śiva's beloved, made by the gaṇas of Vāmadeva.
m.2.2.28.42: The gaṇas made merriment and sang aloud the glory of Śiva and Śivā; those great heroes, dear to Śiva, leapt about vigourously out of joy.
m.2.2.28.43: In every way there was great splendour at the departure of the Mother of the world; a joyful clamour arose, and the three worlds were filled with it.
m.2.2.28.iti: Thus ends the twenty-eighth adhyāya, named Satī's journey, in the second khaṇḍa, the Satī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.2.29.1: Brahmā said: Dākṣāyaṇī went there, where the greatly splendid sacrifice was being held, full of the excitement of gods, asuras, chief sages and others.
m.2.2.29.2: There she saw her father's mansion, full of many wonders, very splendid and lovely, crowded with hosts of gods and sages.
m.2.2.29.3: Then the goddess, standing at the gate, dismounted from her own seat, Nandin, and quickly went inside, alone, into the sacrifice.
m.2.2.29.4: Seeing Satī arrive, her illustrious mother Asiknī honoured her, and so did her sisters, as was fitting.
m.2.2.29.5: Dakṣa, though he saw her, showed her no respect at all; nor did anyone else there, out of fear of him, deluded by Śiva's māyā.
m.2.2.29.6: Then the goddess Satī, O sage, bowed to her mother and father, greatly astonished at the slight from everyone.
m.2.2.29.7: In that sacrifice she saw the shares of the gods, Hari and the rest, but no share for Śambhu; Satī conceived an unbearable anger.
m.2.2.29.8: Then Satī, insulted and intensely filled with rage, as if burning Dakṣa, looked at all of them with a fierce glance and spoke.
m.2.2.29.9: Satī said: Why was Śambhu, the supremely auspicious, not invited by you—he by whom this whole universe, moving and unmoving, is purified?
m.2.2.29.10: Śambhu, who is the sacrifice, the best of those who know sacrifice, the limb of sacrifice, the sacrificial fee and the performer of sacrifice—without him, how can there be a sacrifice?
m.2.2.29.11: Ah! By the mere remembrance of him everything becomes pure; whatever is done without him will all be impure.
m.2.2.29.12: All the materials, mantras and the like, the offerings to the gods and to the ancestors, consist of him; without that Śambhu, how has the sacrifice been started?
m.2.2.29.13: Did you show this disrespect thinking Śiva to be an ordinary god? You have become corrupt in mind today, O vilest of fathers.
m.2.2.29.14: Do you not know, you, that Hara, the Great Lord, by serving whom Viṣṇu, Brahmā and all the other gods attained their own positions?
m.2.2.29.15: How have these gods, Viṣṇu, Brahmā and others, and likewise the sages, come to your sacrifice without Śambhu, their own lord?
m.2.2.29.16: Brahmā said: Having said this, the supreme Goddess, whose very self is Bhava's, addressed Viṣṇu and all the others one by one, rebuking them.
m.2.2.29.17: Satī said: O Viṣṇu, do you not truly know Mahādeva, whom the Śrutis declare to be both with attributes and without attributes?
m.2.2.29.18: Although Maheśvara, laying his hand on you, taught you many times in the past, O Hari, through forms such as Śālva and others,
m.2.2.29.19: still knowledge has not entered your mind, O evil-minded one, since you seek a share in this sacrifice of Dakṣa without Śiva, your own master.
m.2.2.29.20: O Brahmā, formerly, having become five-faced, you were arrogant towards Sadāśiva; you were made four-faced by him—have you forgotten that marvel?
m.2.2.29.21: Indra, do you not know Mahādeva's prowess? Your thunderbolt was reduced to ashes by Hara of fierce deeds.
m.2.2.29.22: O gods, do you not know Mahādeva's prowess? O Atri, O Vasiṣṭha, O sages, what have you done here?
m.2.2.29.23: Formerly the all-pervading Lord went about begging in the Dāruvana, when Rudra, as a mendicant, was cursed by you sages.
m.2.2.29.24: How have you forgotten what Rudra did even when cursed? By his liṅga the whole world, moving and unmoving, was burnt.
m.2.2.29.25: All of you have become deluded—the gods Viṣṇu, Brahmā and others, and the other sages—since you have come here to the sacrifice without Śambhu.
m.2.2.29.26: From whom all the Vedas with their limbs, the śāstras and speech arose—that Śambhu, who is reached through the Vedānta, cannot be known by just anyone.
m.2.2.29.27: Brahmā said: Thus Satī, Mother of the World, filled with anger, spoke words of many kinds there, with an anguished heart.
m.2.2.29.28: Viṣṇu and all the gods, and the sages who were there, hearing her words, fell silent, their minds agitated by fear.
m.2.2.29.29: Then Dakṣa, hearing such words from his daughter, looked at Satī with a fierce glance and angrily spoke.
m.2.2.29.30: Dakṣa said: What is the use of your saying so much? You have no business here now. Go or stay, good lady—why indeed have you come?
m.2.2.29.31: That husband of yours, Śiva, is known by the wise to be inauspicious, of no good family, outside the Vedas, lord of bhūtas, pretas and piśācas.
m.2.2.29.32: Therefore, O daughter, knowing this as a wise man, I did not invite Rudra, who wears a most vile garb, to the sacrifice in the assembly of gods and sages.
m.2.2.29.33: Urged by Vidhi (Brahmā), I—dull and sinful—gave you to Rudra, whose aims are unknown, arrogant and wicked-souled.
m.2.2.29.34: Therefore give up your anger and be at ease, O sweetly smiling one. Since you have come to this sacrifice, take your share yourself.
m.2.2.29.35: Brahmā said: Thus addressed by Dakṣa, his daughter Satī, worshipped by the three worlds, seeing her father full of censure, became extremely enraged.
m.2.2.29.36: Then she thought thus: How shall I go back to Śaṅkara? I came wishing to see Śaṅkara (and my family); when asked, what answer shall I give?
m.2.2.29.37: Then Satī, mother of the three worlds, sighing and possessed by rage, spoke to her father Dakṣa, who was wicked-minded.
m.2.2.29.38: Satī said: He who reviles Mahādeva, or hears him being reviled—both go to hell for as long as the moon and sun endure.
m.2.2.29.39: Therefore I shall abandon this body; I shall enter the fire. What use is life to me, father, when I hear disrespect towards the Lord?
m.2.2.29.40: If one is able, he should himself forcibly cut out the tongue of a reviler of Śambhu in particular; then he would be purified, no doubt.
m.2.2.29.41: If a person there is unable to stop the blasphemer, the wise one should leave, having firmly closed his ears; then he becomes pure — so the best of the learned declare.
m.2.2.29.42: Brahmā said: Having thus spoken the rule of dharma, she was filled with remorse; with an anguished mind she remembered Śaṅkara's words.
m.2.2.29.43: Then, enraged, Satī spoke fearlessly and firmly to Dakṣa, and also to all of them — the gods headed by Viṣṇu and the sages.
m.2.2.29.44: Satī said: Father, you, the reviler of Śambhu, will come to remorse; having suffered great misery here, in the end you will go to torment in hell.
m.2.2.29.45: For this Śarva, the Supreme Self, to whom no one in the world is disliked or specially dear, who is without enmity — who but you is hostile to him?
m.2.2.29.46: Envious reviling of the great is no wonder among the wicked at all times; but among those whose darkness has been destroyed by the dust of the feet of the great, it is not at all becoming.
m.2.2.29.47: He whose two-syllabled name Śiva, uttered by the voice of men even once, even incidentally, swiftly destroys all sin —
m.2.2.29.48: — him, of pure fame, stainless, whose command cannot be transgressed, Śambhu the Lord of all, you hate, being opposed to Śiva. Alas, you are wicked!
m.2.2.29.49: Whose lotus-feet, well served by the bees of the minds of the great, bestow every aim and are worshipped with reverence by those seeking the bliss of Brahman and by all seekers —
m.2.2.29.50: and since Śiva lovingly and swiftly showers boons on the supplicants of the world — against him, the friend of all, you bear malice out of folly.
m.2.2.29.51: Or do the wise other than you — Brahmā and the rest, the sages Sanaka and others, and others besides — not know that the one called Śiva is inauspicious?
m.2.2.29.52: They know well that he, the skull-bearer, with matted locks dishevelled, dwelt gladly with the ghosts in the cremation ground, wearing such garlands and ashes — and knowing this, still honour the magnanimous one.
m.2.2.29.53: He whose discarded offering, cast off from his feet, the sages and gods reverently bear on their heads — he is Śiva, the Supreme Lord.
m.2.2.29.54: Action enjoined in the Veda is of two kinds — of engagement (pravṛtti) and of withdrawal (nivṛtti); having been distinguished, its conduct should be examined by the wise.
m.2.2.29.55: And likewise the two, being contradictory, cannot be done simultaneously by one agent; but in Śambhu, the Supreme Brahman, no action whatever takes hold.
m.2.2.29.56: O father, the states always resorted to by us are not yours; yours are in sacrificial halls, enjoyed and then abandoned by those following the smoky path.
m.2.2.29.57: Ours is of unmanifest mark, ever well served by the avadhūtas; therefore, father, holder of a wicked mind, do not be proud.
m.2.2.29.58: What use are many words? You are wicked, evil-minded in every way. I have no use whatever for this body born of you.
m.2.2.29.59: Fie on the birth from that wicked one who in every way offends the great! The wise should especially renounce any connection with him.
m.2.2.29.60: When the Lord with the bull-banner calls me by your lineage, Dākṣāyaṇī, I at once become deeply distressed.
m.2.2.29.61: Therefore, casting off now this body born of your limbs — a corpse, ever contemptible — I shall surely be at ease.
m.2.2.29.62: O gods and sages, all of you, hear my words: the deed of you wicked-minded ones is improper in every way.
m.2.2.29.63: All of you are deluded, revilers of Śiva, lovers of strife; such ones will surely receive full punishment from Hara without fail.
m.2.2.29.64: Brahmā said: Having spoken thus to Dakṣa at that sacrifice, Satī then fell silent, and, contemplating in her mind, she remembered Śambhu, the beloved of her life.
m.2.2.29.iti: Thus ends the twenty-ninth adhyāya, named The words of Satī, in the second khaṇḍa, the Satī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.2.30.1: Nārada said: When Satī, the beloved of Śaṅkara, had fallen silent, what happened there, O Creator? Kindly tell me that.
m.2.2.30.2: Brahmā said: Having become silent, the goddess Satī, remembering her own husband with reverence, suddenly sat down on the ground on the northern side, her mind completely calm.
m.2.2.30.3: Having sipped water according to rule, pure and wrapped in her garment, closing her eyes and remembering her husband, she entered the path of yoga.
m.2.2.30.4: The bright-faced one, having made the two vital airs, prāṇa and apāna, equal, then with effort raised the udāna from the navel-cakra,
m.2.2.30.5: and having placed it in the heart, the blameless Satī, dear as life to Śaṅkara, by her intellect led what was established in the chest through the throat to the middle of the eyebrows.
m.2.2.30.6: Thus, wishing to cast off her own body at once out of anger at Dakṣa, she, purified by the vital air, held the fire-concentration through the path of yoga, so that her limbs were burnt.
m.2.2.30.7: Then, meditating on her own husband's feet and on nothing else, Satī, her mind fixed on the path of yoga, saw nothing else there.
m.2.2.30.8: Her body, its impurities destroyed, fell, and by that fire it at once turned to ashes, O best of sages, by her own will.
m.2.2.30.9: Then, among those who saw this, in the sky and on earth, a very great outcry of alas, alas arose, wondrous and strange, frightening to the gods and others.
m.2.2.30.10: Alas! Satī, the supreme beloved of Śambhu, the goddess who is indeed his very deity, has given up her life. By what utterly wicked one was she enraged?
m.2.2.30.11: Ah, behold the very great heartlessness of this Dakṣa, the Prajāpati whose progeny is the whole moving and unmoving world, and whose daughter she was!
m.2.2.30.12: Ah, today the high-minded goddess Satī became dejected — she, the beloved of the Bull-bannered Śiva, who was always and ever worthy of honour from the good.
m.2.2.30.13: This Prajāpati, with his intolerant heart, hostile to Brahman, will surely earn great infamy throughout the whole world,
m.2.2.30.14: since he, the hater of Śambhu, did not stop his own daughter, born of his body, when she was set on death because of his offence. He will suffer great hell.
m.2.2.30.15: While people were speaking thus, having seen Satī's wondrous giving-up of life, her attendants quickly rose up in anger with weapons raised.
m.2.2.30.16: All the gaṇas stationed at the door, sixty thousand in number, exceedingly mighty, became enraged through the power of Śaṅkara.
m.2.2.30.17: All those heroic leaders of Śaṅkara's gaṇas raised a cry of lament, repeatedly shouting aloud, shame, shame on us, no, no.
m.2.2.30.18: The space between the quarters was filled with that great cry of lament; all the gods were seized with fear, and so were the sages and the others present there.
m.2.2.30.19: Having consulted together, all those gaṇas became furious, with weapons raised, creating a tumult like the dissolution with their instruments; the space between the quarters was filled with weapons.
m.2.2.30.20: Some of them there, overcome with grief, struck their own limbs, heads and faces with very sharp, life-destroying weapons, O divine sage.
m.2.2.30.21: In this way twenty thousand gaṇas then perished along with Dākṣāyaṇī; that seemed a marvel.
m.2.2.30.22: Those gaṇas of the great-souled Śaṅkara who survived the destruction rose up, weapons raised, to kill that Dakṣa who had provoked their anger.
m.2.2.30.23: Perceiving the rush of those attackers, the venerable Bhṛgu offered an oblation into the southern fire with a Yajus formula that slays the destroyers of sacrifice, O sage.
m.2.2.30.24: As the oblation was being offered by Bhṛgu, great and powerful beings, heroes called Ṛbhus, sprang up there by the thousands.
m.2.2.30.25: Between them, armed with firebrands, and the Pramathas there arose a most terrible battle, O lord of sages, hair-raising to those who hear of it.
m.2.2.30.26: Struck on all sides by those mighty heroic Ṛbhus, blazing with brahminical power, the Pramathas fled without resistance.
m.2.2.30.27: Thus those gaṇas of Śiva were struck and swiftly put to flight by that great power, through Śiva's will; that seemed a marvel.
m.2.2.30.28: Seeing that, the sages, the gods headed by Śakra together with the hosts of Maruts, the Viśvedevas, the two Aśvins and the guardians of the worlds then fell silent.
m.2.2.30.29: Some there, anxious, kept beseeching Lord Viṣṇu from all sides, and deliberated again and again on how to avert the obstacle.
m.2.2.30.30: Having carefully considered the eventual outcome, the wise gods, Viṣṇu and the rest, became greatly troubled again and again over the destruction and rout of those gaṇas.
m.2.2.30.31: Such then was the sacrifice, and an obstacle arose for the wicked Dakṣa, a brahmin in name only and hostile to Śaṅkara, O sage.
m.2.2.30.iti: Thus ends the thirtieth adhyāya, named The tumult at Satī's giving up her body, in the account of Satī, in the second khaṇḍa, the Satī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.2.31.1: Brahmā said: Meanwhile, O lord of sages, a voice from the sky spoke there truthfully, while Dakṣa, the gods and the others were listening.
m.2.2.31.2: The heavenly voice said: Ho, ho, Dakṣa, you of wicked conduct, given wholly to hypocritical behaviour, what have you done, great fool — a deed that brings calamity?
m.2.2.31.3: You did not accept as authoritative the word of Dadhīci, king among Śaivas — a word which, if acted upon, would have been auspicious and brought joy to all, O fool.
m.2.2.31.4: The brahmin left your sacrifice after pronouncing a curse very hard to bear; even then nothing at all was grasped in your mind, fool that you are.
m.2.2.31.5: Then why did you not show the highest honour to your own daughter, auspicious Satī, who came to your house of her own accord?
m.2.2.31.6: Satī and Bhava were not worshipped — what is this, you who are weak in wisdom? Deluded, you are vainly proud, thinking, I am Brahmā's son.
m.2.2.31.7: That Satī is ever to be worshipped; she bestows the fruit of all merit, she is the mother of the three worlds, the auspicious one, who shares half of Śaṅkara's body.
m.2.2.31.8: That Satī, when worshipped always, grants all good fortune; she is Māheśvarī, who gives every blessing to her devotees.
m.2.2.31.9: That Satī, when worshipped always, destroys the fear of worldly existence; the goddess grants the mind's desires and removes all calamities.
m.2.2.31.10: That Satī, when worshipped always, bestows fame and wealth; she is the supreme one, the supreme Ruler, who grants enjoyment and liberation.
m.2.2.31.11: That Satī is the sustainer of the world, the protector of the world, the beginningless Power who at the end of the aeon brings about the world's dissolution.
m.2.2.31.12: That Satī is the mother of the world, the mother of Viṣṇu, the playful one; she is remembered as the begetter of Brahmā, Indra, the Moon, Fire, the Sun and the other gods.
m.2.2.31.13: That Satī bestows the fruits of austerity, dharma, charity and the like; she is Śambhu's Power, the great Goddess, slayer of the wicked, higher than the highest.
m.2.2.31.14: Such is the goddess Satī, the ever-beloved wife of Śiva; yet you, fool of wicked judgement, gave her no share.
m.2.2.31.15: For Śambhu is the supreme Lord, master of all, higher than the highest, to be served by Viṣṇu, Brahmā and the rest, the doer of all good.
m.2.2.31.16: Austerity is practised by the perfected ones longing to see him; yoga is undertaken by yogins, through their disciplines, longing to see him.
m.2.2.31.17: The sight of Śaṅkara alone is declared to be the great fruit of gifts of endless wealth and grain, and likewise of sacrifices and the like.
m.2.2.31.18: Śiva alone is the sustainer of the world, the lord of all knowledge, the master, the excellent lord of primal knowledge, the auspiciousness of all that is auspicious.
m.2.2.31.19: Since today you, villain, have shown no honour to his Power, for that very reason this sacrifice will surely be destroyed.
m.2.2.31.20: Misfortune surely arises from not worshipping those worthy of worship; and she was not worshipped, though Śivā is the most worthy of worship.
m.2.2.31.21: Satī, the auspicious one, is the Power of him the dust of whose feet Śeṣa joyfully bears day after day even on his thousand heads.
m.2.2.31.22: Satī is the beloved of that Śambhu by constantly meditating on whose lotus feet and worshipping them with reverence Viṣṇu attained his Viṣṇu-hood.
m.2.2.31.23: Satī is the beloved of that Śambhu by constantly meditating on whose lotus feet and worshipping them with reverence Brahmā attained his Brahmā-hood.
m.2.2.31.24: By constantly meditating on his lotus feet and worshipping them with reverence, Indra and the other guardians of the worlds attained each his own supreme position.
m.2.2.31.25: Śiva is the father of the world and his Power, that Satī, is the mother of the world; you did not honour them, fool — how will any good come to you?
m.2.2.31.26: Ill fortune has passed into you and calamities have come upon you, since those two, Bhavānī and Śaṅkara, were not worshipped with devotion.
m.2.2.31.27: Without worshipping Śiva Śambhu I shall attain welfare — is there such irresistible pride? That pride will perish today.
m.2.2.31.28: Having turned away from the Lord of all, who among these gods will help you? I see no such helper for you at all.
m.2.2.31.29: If the gods now give you help, they will meet destruction like moths in a fire.
m.2.2.31.30: Let your face burn today; let the sacrifice be destroyed. Let all those who are your helpers burn swiftly today.
m.2.2.31.31: And on all the immortals I lay a solemn oath: it will be to their misfortune if they give help today to this wicked one.
m.2.2.31.32: Let the immortals leave this sacrificial pavilion for their own abodes; otherwise your destruction will surely come today.
m.2.2.31.33: Let all the others too — sages, Nāgas and the rest — leave the sacrifice; otherwise your destruction will surely come today.
m.2.2.31.34: O Hari, leave this sacrificial pavilion quickly; otherwise your destruction will surely come today.
m.2.2.31.35: O Vidhi (Brahmā), leave this sacrificial pavilion quickly; otherwise your destruction will surely come today.
m.2.2.31.36: Brahmā said: Having said this to all those seated throughout the whole sacrificial hall, that voice from the sky, the bringer of all good, fell silent.
m.2.2.31.37: Hearing those words from the sky, all the gods headed by Hari were struck with wonder, dear son, and so were the sages and the others.
m.2.2.31.iti: Thus ends the thirty-first adhyāya, named The voice from the sky, in the account of Satī, in the second khaṇḍa, the Satī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.2.32.1: Nārada said: Having heard the voice from the sky, what did the foolish Dakṣa do then? And what did the others do, and what happened after that? Tell me.
m.2.2.32.2: The Śiva-gaṇas, defeated by the power of Bhṛgu's mantra — what did they do, and where did they go? Tell me the truth of it, O greatly wise one.
m.2.2.32.3: Brahmā said: Having heard the voice from the sky, all the gods and the others were astonished; they said nothing at all, but stood there bewildered.
m.2.2.32.4: Those heroes who were fleeing because of the power of Bhṛgu's mantra — those remaining Śiva-gaṇas — went to Śiva for refuge.
m.2.2.32.5: Having bowed down deeply with reverence, they reported everything to Rudra of immeasurable splendour, and the events just as they had happened.
m.2.2.32.6: The attendants said: O God of gods, Mahādeva, protect us who have come for refuge. O Lord, listen attentively to the news of Satī in detail.
m.2.2.32.7: O Maheśāna, the arrogant and most wicked Dakṣa committed an insult; and likewise Satī was shown disrespect by the gods.
m.2.2.32.8: He did not give a share to you, but gave shares to the gods. The wicked, very arrogant Dakṣa spoke harsh words loudly.
m.2.2.32.9: Then, seeing no share for you in the sacrifice, Satī grew angry, O Lord; having reproached her father many times, she then burned her own body.
m.2.2.32.10: Gaṇas numbering ten thousand died there out of shame, cutting off their own limbs with weapons; we others became enraged.
m.2.2.32.11: Armed and fearsome, we set out to destroy that sacrifice swiftly, but we were repulsed by Bhṛgu, the adversary, through his own power.
m.2.2.32.12: We have come to you for refuge, O sustainer of the universe, O Lord. Therefore, O compassionate one, make us free from the fear that has arisen.
m.2.2.32.13: In that sacrifice, O great Lord, Dakṣa and all those wicked ones, exceedingly arrogant, committed an insult in particular.
m.2.2.32.14: Thus the whole account concerning ourselves, Satī, and those dull-witted ones has been told, O Śaṅkara. Do as you wish.
m.2.2.32.15: Brahmā said: Having heard these words of his own gaṇas, the Lord called Nārada to mind, in order to learn that whole affair quickly.
m.2.2.32.16: You came there swiftly, O divine sage of divine vision; having bowed to Śaṅkara with devotion, you stood there with joined palms.
m.2.2.32.17: Then the Lord, having praised you, asked for news of Satī who had gone to Dakṣa's sacrifice, and also about what followed.
m.2.2.32.18: Dear one, being asked by Śambhu, you, whose mind is fixed on Śiva, quickly told all that had happened at Dakṣa's sacrifice.
m.2.2.32.19: Having heard that statement spoken from your mouth, O sage, the Lord Rudra, of very fierce valour, became angry at once.
m.2.2.32.20: Rudra, the destroyer of the worlds, plucked out one matted lock and in fury dashed it then upon the mountain.
m.2.2.32.21: From the striking, that lock of the Lord split in two, O sage, and a great roar arose, terrifying like the great dissolution.
m.2.2.32.22: From the front part of that lock, O divine sage, arose the mighty Vīrabhadra, most terrible, foremost of the gaṇas.
m.2.2.32.23: Enveloping the earth on all sides, he stood ten fingers' breadth beyond it — like the fire of dissolution, towering high, with a thousand arms.
m.2.2.32.24: There, from the angry breath of the Lord Mahārudra, a hundred fevers were born, and thirteen sannipāta fevers.
m.2.2.32.25: From the other part of that lock arose Mahākālī, most terrifying, dear one, surrounded by millions of bhūtas.
m.2.2.32.26: All the fevers were embodied, cruel, terrifying to the world, blazing with their own energy as though burning everything around.
m.2.2.32.27: Then the hero Vīrabhadra, skilled in speech, bowed to the Supreme Lord and with joined palms spoke these words.
m.2.2.32.28: Vīrabhadra said: O Mahārudra, most fierce one, whose eyes are the moon, sun and fire, what task is to be done by me? Command me quickly, O Lord.
m.2.2.32.29: Are the oceans to be dried up in half a moment, O Īśāna? Are the mountains to be crushed in half a moment, O Īśāna?
m.2.2.32.30: Shall I reduce the cosmic egg to ashes in a moment, O Hara? Or shall I reduce the gods or the lords of sages to ashes in a moment?
m.2.2.32.31: Is the breath of all the worlds to be stopped, O Śaṅkara? Or, O Īśāna, is the slaughter of all living beings to be carried out?
m.2.2.32.32: By your grace, O Maheśvara, nothing anywhere is impossible for me; in valour, none equal to me has been, nor will be.
m.2.2.32.33: Wherever, for whatever task you send me, O Lord, I shall surely accomplish that task swiftly by your grace.
m.2.2.32.34: By your command, O Śaṅkara, even the lowly cross the ocean of the world; so, O Hara, am I not able to cross a great ocean of calamity?
m.2.2.32.35: Even with a blade of grass sent by you, a great task can be done in a moment without effort, O Śaṅkara; of this there is no doubt.
m.2.2.32.36: Though the task would be accomplished by your mere play, O Śambhu, still I should be sent; this indeed is your grace.
m.2.2.32.37: Such power is mine too, O Śambhu, through your grace; without your grace, O Śaṅkara, no one has any power.
m.2.2.32.38: Without your command, no one can in truth move even a blade of grass or the like; this is true, without doubt.
m.2.2.32.39: O Śambhu, all the gods and others are subject to your control, O Maheśvara; likewise I am subject to you, the controller of all embodied beings.
m.2.2.32.40: I bow to you, O Mahādeva; again and again I bow. Send me now, swiftly, O Hara, to accomplish your desired purpose.
m.2.2.32.41: O Śambhu, my right limbs keep throbbing again and again. Victory will come today, so send me, O Lord.
m.2.2.32.42: A special kind of joy and eagerness is also rising in me, and, O Śambhu, my mind is fixed on your lotus feet.
m.2.2.32.43: At every step there will be an unbroken succession of auspicious results.
m.2.2.32.44: Victory always belongs to him alone, and good fortune day after day to him alone, whose devotion to Śambhu, to you, the excellent refuge, is firm.
m.2.2.32.45: Brahmā said: Hearing these words he had spoken, the lord of Maṅgalā Pārvatī, pleased, gave the blessing, Vīrabhadra, be victorious, and spoke to him again.
m.2.2.32.46: Maheśvara said: Listen with an attentive mind to my words, dear Vīrabhadra. What pleases me must be done with effort, and quickly.
m.2.2.32.47: Dakṣa, the wicked son of Brahmā, has set about performing a sacrifice. He is especially hostile to me, extremely arrogant, and now devoid of understanding.
m.2.2.32.48: Reduce his sacrifice to ashes together with all who attend it, and come back quickly to my abode, O best of the Gaṇas.
m.2.2.32.49: Whether they are gods, Gandharvas, Yakṣas or any others, reduce them too to ashes, this very day, suddenly and swiftly.
m.2.2.32.50: Whether Viṣṇu, Brahmā, the lord of Śacī Indra or even Yama be there, strike them all down with effort this very day.
m.2.2.32.51: Whether they are gods, Gandharvas, Yakṣas or any others, reduce them too to ashes, this very day, suddenly and swiftly.
m.2.2.32.52: Those who remain there, having disregarded the oath sworn by Dadhīci concerning me, must certainly be burnt by you with every effort.
m.2.2.32.53: The Pramathas too will come with you. If Viṣṇu and the others are there out of delusion, draw them in with the mantra of manifold attraction and burn them swiftly.
m.2.2.32.54: Those who stand there in their arrogance, having violated my oath, are my enemies; therefore burn them with a garland of fire.
m.2.2.32.55: Burn those present at the site of Dakṣa's sacrifice, together with their wives and their possessions, reduce them to ashes, and come back quickly.
m.2.2.32.56: When you have gone there, even the gods, the Viśvas and others, will praise you respectfully; even then, quickly burn them with flame.
m.2.2.32.57: Quickly burn the gods too who have acted with hostility, with fires crowded with wreaths of flame; do not give thought to the guardian of the Vedic recitation.
m.2.2.32.58: Having burnt Dakṣa and all the others there, with their wives and kinsmen, O hero, drink Dakṣa down playfully as if he were water.
m.2.2.32.59: Brahmā said: Having spoken thus to the great hero, the enemy of Kāla, lord of all, guardian of the bounds of the Veda, his eyes red with anger, fell silent.
m.2.2.32.iti: Thus ends the thirty-second adhyāya, named The birth of Vīrabhadra and Śiva's instruction, in the second khaṇḍa, the Satī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.2.33.1: Brahmā said: Having respectfully heard these words spoken by the glorious Maheśa, Vīrabhadra, greatly delighted, bowed down to Maheśvara.
m.2.2.33.2: Bearing on his head the command of the trident-bearing God of gods, Vīrabhadra then set out swiftly towards the sacrifice.
m.2.2.33.3: Then Śiva sent with him, for added splendour, gaṇas by the crore—great heroes resembling the fire of the cosmic dissolution.
m.2.2.33.4: Then those mighty gaṇas went in front of Vīrabhadra, and heroic gaṇas, causing wonder, went behind as well.
m.2.2.33.5: The gaṇas who accompanied Vīrabhadra, by hundreds of thousands, were attendants of the Death of Death, all having the very form of Rudra.
m.2.2.33.6: Accompanied indeed by those gaṇas, the great-souled Vīrabhadra—wearing Hara's garb and ornaments, thousand-armed, adorned with lords of serpents, mighty and exceedingly terrifying—went forth seated on a chariot.
m.2.2.33.7: The measure of the chariot was two thousand nalvas, and it was drawn with effort by ten thousand lions as its draught-animals.
m.2.2.33.8: Likewise many mighty lions were guards at the sides, and there were tigers, makaras, fishes and elephants there by the thousands.
m.2.2.33.9: When Vīrabhadra had set out swiftly for Dakṣa's destruction, a shower of flowers released by the wish-fulfilling trees then fell.
m.2.2.33.10: The gaṇas praised the hero who was acting for Śipiviṣṭa Śiva, and all of them made merry at that festive march.
m.2.2.33.11: Kālī, Kātyāyanī, Īśānī, Cāmuṇḍā, Muṇḍamardinī, Bhadrakālī, likewise Bhadrā, Tvaritā and Vaiṣṇavī—
m.2.2.33.12: accompanied by these nine Durgās, Mahākālī went forth for the destruction of Dakṣa together with all the hosts of bhūtas.
m.2.2.33.13: Ḍākinīs and Śākinīs, bhūtas, pramathas and guhyakas, kūṣmāṇḍas, parpaṭas, caṭakas and brahmarākṣasas—
m.2.2.33.14: Bhairavas and Kṣetrapālas, destroyers of Dakṣa's sacrifice, heroes upholding Śiva's command, went forth quickly.
m.2.2.33.15: Likewise the circle of Yoginīs, joined by its sixty-four hosts, went forth suddenly in wrath to destroy Dakṣa's sacrifice.
m.2.2.33.16: Hear, O Nārada, the numbering of all those gaṇas—the host of the chief ones, of great strength and full of fortitude.
m.2.2.33.17: Śaṅkukarṇa, lord of gaṇas, advanced with ten crores; Kekarākṣa with ten, and Vikṛta with eight.
m.2.2.33.18: Viśākha with sixty-four, Pāriyātrika with nine, the hero Sarvāṅkaka with six, and likewise Vikṛtānana.
m.2.2.33.19: Jvālakeśa, the best of gaṇas, with twelve crores; Samadajjīmān with seven, and Dudrabha with eight.
m.2.2.33.20: Kapālīśa with five, the gaṇa Sandāraka with six, and here likewise Koṭikuṇḍa with crores upon crores.
m.2.2.33.21: Viṣṭambha, the best of gaṇas, with sixty-four crores of heroes; and, dear son, Sannāda and Pippala with a thousand crores.
m.2.2.33.22: Āveśana likewise with eight, Candratāpana with eight, and the gaṇa-leader Mahāveśa surrounded by a thousand crores.
m.2.2.33.23: Kuṇḍī with twelve crores, and likewise Parvataka, O sage, the best of gaṇas, went forth to destroy Dakṣa's sacrifice.
m.2.2.33.24: Kāla, Kālaka and likewise Mahākāla went towards Dakṣa's sacrifice with a hundred crores.
m.2.2.33.25: Agnikṛt with a hundred crores, Agnimukha with a crore, Ādityamūrdhā with a crore, and likewise Ghanāvaha.
m.2.2.33.26: Sannāha with a hundred crores, the gaṇa Kumuda with a crore, and Amogha and Kokila, lords of gaṇas, with crores of crores.
m.2.2.33.27: Kāṣṭhāgūḍha with sixty-four, Sukeśa, Vṛṣabha, and likewise Sumantraka, lord of gaṇas, went forth well, dear son.
m.2.2.33.28: Kākapādodara, best of gaṇas, with sixty crores; likewise Santānaka, foremost of gaṇas, with sixty crores.
m.2.2.33.29: And likewise Mahābala, a foremost one, with nine crores.
m.2.2.33.30: Likewise, dear son, Madhupiṅga, lord of gaṇas, went forth; Nīla with ninety crores, and likewise Pūrṇabhadra.
m.2.2.33.31: Caturvaktra, lord of gaṇas, went forth with a hundred crores.
m.2.2.33.32: Virūpākṣa, lord of gaṇas, with sixty-four crores; Tālaketu, Ṣaḍāsya, and Pañcāsya, lord of gaṇas;
m.2.2.33.33: likewise Saṃvartaka, and Kulīśa, himself a lord; Lokāntaka, of blazing self, and likewise Daityāntaka, O sage;
m.2.2.33.34: the glorious gaṇa Bhṛṅgīriṭi, dear to the God of gods; and Aśani, Bhālaka, and Sahasraka with sixty-four crores.
m.2.2.33.35: Surrounded by twenty hundreds of thousands of crores of crores, the hero Vīrabhadra, lord of heroes, advanced at Śiva's command.
m.2.2.33.36: He set forth with thousands of crores of bhūtas and with three crores more; and with the hair-born ones and the hosts of dogs the hero went swiftly.
m.2.2.33.37: Then arose the great roar of kettledrums, conches of various sounds, jaṭāharas and mukhas, and horns of many kinds.
m.2.2.33.38: Those instruments, stretched skin instruments, bound ones and pleasing ones—various musical instruments—resounded at that great festival.
m.2.2.33.39: On the march of Vīrabhadra with his army, O great sage, many auspicious omens bringing happiness appeared there.
m.2.2.33.iti: Thus ends the thirty-third adhyāya, named The march of Vīrabhadra, in the second khaṇḍa, the Satī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.2.34.1: Brahmā said: When Vīrabhadra, accompanied by the gaṇas, had thus set out, evil omens were seen by Dakṣa and also by the gods.
m.2.2.34.2: While Vīrabhadra advanced with the gaṇas, various portents appeared, O divine sage, of all three kinds, foretelling the destruction of the sacrifice.
m.2.2.34.3: A throbbing of Dakṣa's left eye, arm and thigh occurred, O dear one, bringing many troubles and in every way signifying ill fortune.
m.2.2.34.4: Then an earthquake took place there at the site of Dakṣa's sacrifice, and at midday Dakṣa saw strange stars.
m.2.2.34.5: The quarters became very murky; the sun became spotted and, encircled by a thousand halos, terrifying.
m.2.2.34.6: Stars, shining like lightning and fire, kept falling; and then the course of the stars became crooked and turned downward.
m.2.2.34.7: Vultures by the thousands rose up after touching Dakṣa's head, and the sacrificial pavilion was overshadowed by the shadows of the vultures' wings.
m.2.2.34.8: Then jackals and netrakas howled on the sacrificial ground; and a shower of meteors fell there, together with white scorpions born from it.
m.2.2.34.9: Harsh winds blew there, accompanied by showers of dust; and locusts arose, tossed about by whirlwinds.
m.2.2.34.10: And that pavilion of Dakṣa's sacrifice, new and wondrous, which Dakṣa had built together with the gods, was carried upward by the winds.
m.2.2.34.11: Then Dakṣa and all the others vomited blood in a strange way; and again and again they vomited pieces of flesh with bone splinters.
m.2.2.34.12: They trembled like lamps struck by the wind, and all were in anguish as if struck by the edges of weapons.
m.2.2.34.13: Then at that very moment showers of tears burst forth with loud cries, like lotuses shedding dew in the morning within a forest.
m.2.2.34.14: The eyes of Dakṣa and the others, though bright before, suddenly became dim, like lotuses at night and like night-lilies in the forenoon.
m.2.2.34.15: The sky-god rained blood, the quarters were covered in darkness, and the horizons blazed exceedingly, terrifying all people.
m.2.2.34.16: The gods and others saw such evil omens, and then, O sage, Viṣṇu and the rest were seized by extreme fear.
m.2.2.34.17: They fell senseless to the ground, crying, alas, we are slain, like trees growing on a bank struck down by the river's current.
m.2.2.34.18: Having fallen, they lay on the ground like cruel serpents that had been struck; then, like balls, they fell and rose up again and again.
m.2.2.34.19: Then, scorched by anguish, they wept like ospreys, as though their loud cries and answering cries had merged into a single sound of wailing.
m.2.2.34.20: Then all of them, Viṣṇu (Vaikuṇṭha) included, their powers blunted, rolled about beside one another, heads drawn in up to the neck, like tortoises.
m.2.2.34.21: Meanwhile a bodiless voice arose there, making all the gods, and Dakṣa especially, hear it.
m.2.2.34.22: The heavenly voice said: Shame on your birth, Dakṣa! Today you are a great fool, sinful-minded, and great, unavoidable misery will come, springing from Hara.
m.2.2.34.23: Those fools, the gods and others, who stand here as your helpers — great misery will befall them too; there is no doubt.
m.2.2.34.24: Brahmā said: Hearing that voice from the sky and seeing those evil omens, Dakṣa fell into great fear, and so did the others, the gods and the rest.
m.2.2.34.25: Then Dakṣa, trembling and greatly agitated in mind, went for refuge to Viṣṇu, his own lord, the husband of Indirā.
m.2.2.34.26: Overcome by fear and bewildered, he bowed down deeply, praised him, and spoke to that Viṣṇu, god of gods, who is loving towards his own people.
m.2.2.34.iti: Thus ends the thirty-fourth adhyāya, named The sight of evil omens, in the second khaṇḍa, the Satī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.2.35.1: Dakṣa said: O God of gods, O Hari, O Viṣṇu, friend of the afflicted, treasure-house of compassion, you must grant protection to me and to my sacrifice.
m.2.2.35.2: You alone are the protector of the sacrifice; you are the rite of sacrifice and the very soul of sacrifice. Show mercy to the sacrifice; let there be no disruption of it, O Lord.
m.2.2.35.3: Brahmā said: Having thus made many kinds of entreaty with reverence, Dakṣa, his mind distraught with fear, fell at his feet.
m.2.2.35.4: Then Viṣṇu raised up Dakṣa, whose mind was overwhelmed, and having heard those words of that ill-minded one, he remembered Śiva.
m.2.2.35.5: Having remembered Śiva, the great Lord, his own master, the supreme Īśvara, Hari, who knew the truth of Śiva, spoke, instructing Dakṣa.
m.2.2.35.6: Hari said: Listen, Dakṣa, I shall explain in truth; hear my words, which are in every way beneficial to you and bestow happiness like a great mantra.
m.2.2.35.7: For, O Dakṣa, not knowing the truth, you have shown disrespect to Śaṅkara, the supreme Self, the sovereign Lord of all.
m.2.2.35.8: Through disrespect to the Lord every undertaking becomes, in every way, not merely fruitless—there is also calamity at every step.
m.2.2.35.9: Where those unworthy of worship are worshipped and the one worthy of worship is not worshipped, there three things will arise: poverty, death and fear.
m.2.2.35.10: Therefore the bull-bannered one (Śiva) must be honoured with every effort; and from Maheśa, who was not honoured, great danger has now arrived.
m.2.2.35.11: Even now, all of us, though lords, are not able to prevail—solely because of your misconduct. I am telling you the truth.
m.2.2.35.12: Brahmā said: Having heard those words of Viṣṇu, Dakṣa became absorbed in anxiety; his face turning pale, he stood on the ground and remained silent.
m.2.2.35.13: Meanwhile Vīrabhadra, leader of the Gaṇas, urged on by Rudra, came to the sacrifice accompanied by his army.
m.2.2.35.14: Some came behind, some came through the sky, and others, all of them, came enveloping the cardinal and intermediate directions.
m.2.2.35.15: By Śarva's command the Gaṇas—heroic, fearless, mighty as Rudra, countless, the best of warriors—came roaring lion-roars.
m.2.2.35.16: With that mighty roar the three worlds resounded; the sky was covered with dust and the directions with darkness.
m.2.2.35.17: The earth with its seven continents, together with its mountains and forests, shook violently, stricken with fear; and all the oceans were churned up.
m.2.2.35.18: Seeing that vast army, of such a kind and capable of destroying the worlds, all the gods and others were astonished.
m.2.2.35.19: Then, seeing the army's advance, Dakṣa, distraught, with blood rushing to his face, fell prostrate like a staff together with his wife and addressed Viṣṇu.
m.2.2.35.20: Dakṣa said: It was on the strength of your power alone that I began this great sacrifice. For the success of this holy rite, O Viṣṇu, you are the authority, O great Lord.
m.2.2.35.21: O Viṣṇu, you are the witness of all actions and the protector of sacrifices; you are the guardian of dharma and of Brahman that holds the Vedas within it, O great Lord.
m.2.2.35.22: Therefore, O Lord, you must protect this sacrifice of mine. Who other than you is capable, since you are the Lord of all?
m.2.2.35.23: Brahmā said: Having heard Dakṣa's most piteous words, Viṣṇu then spoke, instructing him who had turned away from the truth of Śiva.
m.2.2.35.24: Viṣṇu said: Indeed, O Dakṣa, I ought to protect your sacrifice; my vow is well known and true—the protection of dharma.
m.2.2.35.25: What you have said is indeed true; but what of its violation by you? Listen, I tell you, Dakṣa: abandon your cruel intent now.
m.2.2.35.26: The wondrous event that took place at Naimiṣa, the field of the gods (Animiṣa-kṣetra)—do you not remember it, Dakṣa? Has it been forgotten by your foolish mind?
m.2.2.35.27: Who here is capable of protecting you from Rudra's wrath? O Dakṣa, whoever protects you without his consent is ill-minded.
m.2.2.35.28: What is action and what is non-action—that you do not see, O ill-minded one. Action alone will never be efficacious.
m.2.2.35.29: Know that to be one's proper action through which efficacy arises. There is no other bestower of the fruit of action; there can be no welfare without the Lord.
m.2.2.35.30: He who, through devotion to the Lord, is tranquil, his mind fixed on him—to him Śiva then grants the fruit of action.
m.2.2.35.31: Men who rely on knowledge alone and are devoted to godlessness go to hell for hundreds of crores of kalpas.
m.2.2.35.32: Again, bound by the fetters made of karma birth after birth, those who are mere embodiments of karma are tormented in the hells.
m.2.2.35.33: This Vīrabhadra, lord of Rudra's Gaṇas, crusher of foes, born of the fire of Rudra's wrath, has arrived in the sacrificial arena.
m.2.2.35.34: He has come for our destruction—there is no doubt. Nothing at all is impossible for him, whatever it may be, in truth.
m.2.2.35.35: This great lord will surely burn us all up; only then will his heart be pacified—there is no doubt.
m.2.2.35.36: Since, out of delusion, I have transgressed the oath of the glorious Mahādeva and remained here, I must therefore suffer misery together with you.
m.2.2.35.37: O Dakṣa, I have no power today to avert this, since by transgressing the oath I have become an enemy of Śiva.
m.2.2.35.38: Since there is no happiness in any of the three times for those hostile to Maheśa, I must surely suffer misery today together with you.
m.2.2.35.39: The discus named Sudarśana will not strike him, since this is Śiva's discus, the cause of the destruction of non-Śaivas.
m.2.2.35.40: Indeed, even without Vīrabhadra, this divine discus, having slain us, will now swiftly go back to Hara's presence.
m.2.2.35.41: Though I stand here having transgressed the oath sworn by Śiva, this discus of such power has not suddenly destroyed me; out of compassion alone it has remained steady so far.
m.2.2.35.42: Beyond this, even this discus will certainly not remain; it will now quickly depart, enveloped in garlands of flames.
m.2.2.35.43: Even if Vīrabhadra is promptly worshipped by us with reverence, overcome by great wrath he will not protect us.
m.2.2.35.44: An untimely dissolution has come upon us today, alas, alas! Alas, alas, now destruction has arrived for you and for us.
m.2.2.35.45: There is now no refuge at all for us in the three worlds. Who in the world will be a refuge for one hostile to Śaṅkara?
m.2.2.35.46: Even after the body perishes, the torments of Yama must be undergone by them; those torments, giving great suffering, cannot be endured at all.
m.2.2.35.47: On seeing one hostile to Śiva, Yama himself, gnashing his teeth, hurls him into cauldrons of heated oil—and not otherwise.
m.2.2.35.48: I was fully prepared to leave right after hearing the oath; yet I did not go quickly, owing to the sin of association with the wicked.
m.2.2.35.49: If we now flee from here, then Śarva's warrior, even if not yet pursuing, will drag us back with his weapons.
m.2.2.35.50: For whether in heaven, on earth, or in the nether world—wherever it may be—the reach of Śrī Vīrabhadra's weapons is by no means hard to attain.
m.2.2.35.51: As many gaṇas as there are of Śrī Rudra, the trident-bearer, all of them certainly possess such power.
m.2.2.35.52: Long ago at Kāśī, Śrī Kālabhairava, merely with the tip of his nail and in sport, cut off Brahmā's fifth head—this is certain.
m.2.2.35.53: Having said this, Viṣṇu stood still, his lotus-face deeply frightened. At that very moment Vīrabhadra too arrived at the sacrificial pavilion.
m.2.2.35.54: While Govinda was speaking thus, the gods and others saw the ocean of an army that had arrived, together with Vīrabhadra.
m.2.2.35.iti: Thus ends the thirty-fifth adhyāya, named The words of Viṣṇu, in the account of Satī, in the second khaṇḍa, the Satī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.2.36.1: Brahmā said: Then Indra too, the thunderbolt-wielder, laughing at Viṣṇu, who was absorbed in boasting about himself, became eager to fight together with the gods.
m.2.2.36.2: Then Indra mounted his elephant, and Agni likewise mounted a goat; Yama mounted a buffalo, and Nirṛti a ghost.
m.2.2.36.3: Varuṇa, holder of the noose, mounted a makara; Vāyu, the ever-moving, mounted a deer; Kubera, mounted on the Puṣpaka, stood armed and alert.
m.2.2.36.4: Likewise the other hosts of gods, and the mighty Yakṣas, Cāraṇas and Guhyakas, mounted each their own vehicles.
m.2.2.36.5: Seeing their preparation, Dakṣa, his face smeared with blood, came near them with his wife and spoke.
m.2.2.36.6: Dakṣa said: It is on the strength of you alone that I have begun this great sacrifice. O you of great splendour, may you be the guarantors for the success of this good rite.
m.2.2.36.7: Brahmā said: Hearing those words of Dakṣa, all the gods along with Indra quickly went forth there, ready to do battle.
m.2.2.36.8: Then all those hosts of gods, full of strength, fought—the guardians of the worlds headed by Śakra, deluded by Śiva's māyā.
m.2.2.36.9: Then there was a great battle between the gods and the gaṇas; they fought each other with sharp lances and iron arrows.
m.2.2.36.10: Conches and kettledrums sounded in that great festival of battle; great war-drums, paṭahas, ḍiṇḍimas and the like resounded.
m.2.2.36.11: Encouraged then by that great sound, the gods, together with the guardians of the worlds, struck down those servants of Śiva.
m.2.2.36.12: O tiger among sages, Śambhu's gaṇas were turned back by the world-guardians headed by Indra, and by the power of Bhṛgu's mantras.
m.2.2.36.13: Bhṛgu, the sacrificing priest, then performed an uccāṭana, a rite of expulsion, on them, for the sake of the sacrifice to the gods and for the satisfaction of the consecrated sacrificer.
m.2.2.36.14: Seeing his own troops defeated, Vīrabhadra, filled with anger, placed the bhūtas, pretas and piśācas behind,
m.2.2.36.15: and putting those mounted on bulls in front, he himself, of great strength, took up his great trident and felled the immortals.
m.2.2.36.16: Gods, Yakṣas, hosts of Sādhyas, Guhyakas and Cāraṇas too—all the gaṇas swiftly struck them with blows of tridents.
m.2.2.36.17: Some were cut in two with swords, others crushed with maces; and the gods were then torn apart by the gaṇas with other weapons too.
m.2.2.36.18: Thus defeated, all the gods, intent on flight, abandoned one another and went to heaven.
m.2.2.36.19: Only those world-guardians headed by Śakra, of great strength, remained eager in that terrible battle, holding on to their courage.
m.2.2.36.20: All the gods headed by Śakra gathered together there on the battlefield and then, bowed in humility, questioned Bṛhaspati.
m.2.2.36.21: The guardians of the worlds said: O teacher Bṛhaspati, dear one, greatly wise, ocean of compassion, tell us quickly, as we ask: how may victory be ours?
m.2.2.36.22: Brahmā said: Hearing their words, Bṛhaspati, with effort, remembered Śambhu and said this to the great Indra, who was weak in understanding.
m.2.2.36.23: Bṛhaspati said: What Viṣṇu said earlier has all come to pass today. I shall explain that very thing, O Indra; listen attentively.
m.2.2.36.24: Whatever Lord there is who bestows the fruits of all actions, he too resorts to the doer of the action; he is indeed not master of the fruit apart from its own doer.
m.2.2.36.25: Neither all mantras and herbs, nor sorcery, nor worldly means, nor rites, nor the Vedas, nor the two Mīmāṃsās—
m.2.2.36.26: nor other scriptures connected with the various Vedas, are able to know the Lord; so the ancients say.
m.2.2.36.27: Maheśāna is not easily known even through myriads of all the Vedas; he is known by devotees who have no other refuge, and not otherwise—so declares the great scripture.
m.2.2.36.28: Sadāśiva is surely to be known through peace and a supreme vision wholly free from change, by his grace.
m.2.2.36.29: But further I shall tell you, regarding what is to be done and not to be done as intended, and the part that leads to success, O lord of gods; listen to it for your own good.
m.2.2.36.30: You, Indra, being foolish, have come today with the world-guardians to Dakṣa's sacrifice; what valour will you show?
m.2.2.36.31: These gaṇas, Rudra's helpers, extremely wrathful, have come to obstruct the sacrifice; they will do it without doubt.
m.2.2.36.32: In truth, there is no means at all here, for anyone, to remove the obstruction of the sacrifice; I speak the truth, the truth.
m.2.2.36.33: Brahmā said: Hearing these words of Bṛhaspati, all those heaven-dwellers, the world-guardians with Indra, fell into anxiety.
m.2.2.36.34: Then Vīrabhadra, surrounded by gaṇas of great heroism, remembering Śaṅkara in his mind, spoke to those world-guardians headed by Indra.
m.2.2.36.35: Vīrabhadra said: All of you, out of foolishness, have come for your sacrificial portions. I shall give you your portion—come near me.
m.2.2.36.36: O Śakra, O Agni (Śuci), O Sun, O Moon, O lord of wealth, O noose-bearer, O Vāyu, Nirṛti, Yama, O Śeṣa,
m.2.2.36.37: O hosts of gods and asuras, you clever ones, come here. I shall give portions today to satiety to you, the best of the wicked.
m.2.2.36.38: Brahmā said: Having spoken thus, Vīrabhadra, leader of the gaṇas, full of rage, at once struck all those gods with white arrows. Struck by those arrows, all the lords of the gods headed by Vāsava
m.2.2.36.39: became intent on flight and went off in the ten directions; and when the world-guardians had gone and the gods had fled, Vīrabhadra went with the gaṇas to the vicinity of the sacrificial enclosure.
m.2.2.36.40: Then all those sages, greatly frightened and wishing to petition the Lord of Ramā, at once spoke quickly, bowing low.
m.2.2.36.41: The sages said: O God of gods, Lord of Ramā, Lord of all, great Master, protect Dakṣa's sacrifice, for you are the Sacrifice itself; there is no doubt.
m.2.2.36.42: You are the performer of sacrifice, the form of sacrifice, the limb of sacrifice, the protector of sacrifice. Therefore protect the sacrifice, protect it, for there is no protector other than you.
m.2.2.36.43: Brahmā said: Hearing these words of the sages, Hari Viṣṇu became eager to fight with that Vīrabhadra.
m.2.2.36.44: Four-armed, fully armed, holding the discus and other weapons in his hands, the mighty one went forth from the sacrificial enclosure with the hosts of gods.
m.2.2.36.45: Vīrabhadra, trident in hand and accompanied by various gaṇas, saw the great Lord Viṣṇu armed and eager to fight.
m.2.2.36.46: Seeing him, Vīrabhadra's face became twisted with a frown, like Death facing a most sinful man, like a lion facing an elephant.
m.2.2.36.47: Seeing Hari in such a state, Vīrabhadra, crusher of foes, surrounded by heroic gaṇas, spoke swiftly in anger.
m.2.2.36.48: Vīrabhadra said: Ho, ho, Hari, how have you today transgressed the oath of Mahādeva? Has pride arisen in your mind?
m.2.2.36.49: Do you have the power to transgress the oath of the glorious Rudra? Who are you, and who is your protector in the three worlds?
m.2.2.36.50: Why have you come here? That we do not know at all. How have you become the protector of Dakṣa's sacrifice? Tell that.
m.2.2.36.51: Did you not see what Dākṣāyaṇī did? Did you not hear what Dadhīci declared?
m.2.2.36.52: You too have come to this sacrifice of Dakṣa for your share of the offering; I shall give you your share too, O mighty-armed one.
m.2.2.36.53: I shall tear open your chest with my trident, O Hari. Who is the protector that has come with you today before me?
m.2.2.36.54: I shall fell you to the ground, burn you with fire, and then quickly grind you, burnt, to powder.
m.2.2.36.55: Ho, ho, Hari, of wicked conduct, vilest of those hostile to Maheśa, do you not know the purifying greatness of the glorious Mahārudra?
m.2.2.36.56: Even so, O mighty-armed one, you stand before me eager to fight. If you stand against me of your own will, I shall make you turn back.
m.2.2.36.57: Brahmā said: Hearing those words of Vīrabhadra, the wise Viṣṇu, lord of the gods, laughing, spoke there with affection.
m.2.2.36.58: Viṣṇu said: Listen, Vīrabhadra; I shall now speak before you. Do not call me hostile to Rudra, for I am a servant of Śaṅkara.
m.2.2.36.59: I was earlier entreated again and again for the sacrifice by this Dakṣa, who, devoted to ritual action, does not know the real purpose, out of folly.
m.2.2.36.60: I am subject to my devotees, and so too is Maheśvara. Dakṣa is my devotee, dear one; therefore I came here to the sacrifice.
m.2.2.36.61: Hear my vow, O hero born of Rudra's wrath, you who are the very form of Rudra's splendour, abode of great valour, O lord.
m.2.2.36.62: I will hold you back, and you hold me back. What is to be will be; I shall display my prowess.
m.2.2.36.63: Brahmā said: When Govinda had spoken thus, the mighty-armed one laughed and said: I am well pleased, knowing you to be dear to our Lord.
m.2.2.36.64: Then Vīrabhadra, chief of the gaṇas, smiling and very pleased, bowing in humility, spoke truly to the god Viṣṇu.
m.2.2.36.65: Vīrabhadra said: O great Lord, I spoke thus to test your disposition. Now I speak the truth; listen attentively.
m.2.2.36.66: As Śiva is, so are you; and as you are, so is Śiva. Thus the Vedas describe, by Śiva's decree, O Hari.
m.2.2.36.67: By Śiva's command we are all servants of Śaṅkara; even so, O Lord of Ramā, what I said was fitting for the dispute, and is said with respect.
m.2.2.36.68: Brahmā said: Hearing those words of Vīrabhadra, Acyuta laughed and spoke these words to Vīrabhadra.
m.2.2.36.69: Viṣṇu said: Fight with me without hesitation, O great hero. Covered by your missiles, I shall go to my own abode.
m.2.2.36.70: Brahmā said: Having said this, he fell silent and made ready for battle; mighty Vīrabhadra too, with his gaṇas, made ready.
m.2.2.36.iti: Thus ends the thirty-sixth adhyāya, named The dialogue of Viṣṇu and Vīrabhadra, in the second khaṇḍa, the Satī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.2.37.1: Brahmā said: Then that mighty Vīrabhadra, engaged in battle with Viṣṇu, having remembered in his mind Śaṅkara, the remover of all calamities,
m.2.2.37.2: having mounted a divine chariot, he, the crusher of all enemies, taking up supreme weapons, roared a lion's roar.
m.2.2.37.3: Viṣṇu too, the mighty, blew his own great conch named Pāñcajanya, of tremendous sound, as if gladdening his own side.
m.2.2.37.4: Hearing that blast of the conch, the gods who had fled, having abandoned the battle and gone off earlier, quickly came back again.
m.2.2.37.5: Those guardians of the worlds, together with Vāsava, full of strength, raised lion's roars and fought with Vīrabhadra's gaṇas.
m.2.2.37.6: There arose there a fearful, tumultuous duel between the gaṇas and the guardians of the worlds, as they roared with lion's roars.
m.2.2.37.7: Śakra fought with Nandin, and likewise Anala (Fire) with Aśman; the mighty Kubera too fought with the lord of the Kūṣmāṇḍas.
m.2.2.37.8: Then Nandin was struck by Indra with the hundred-jointed thunderbolt.
m.2.2.37.9: And Śakra was struck by Nandin with a trident in the middle of the chest.
m.2.2.37.10: Both mighty ones, Nandin and Śakra, fought each other with zest, dealing various blows, eager for victory.
m.2.2.37.11: Śuci (Fire), exceedingly wrathful, struck Aśman with a spear; and he too swiftly struck that Pāvaka with a sharp-edged lance.
m.2.2.37.12: Mahāloka, the heroic foremost of the gaṇas, waged a tumultuous battle with Yama, joyfully remembering Mahādeva.
m.2.2.37.13: And Caṇḍa, exceedingly mighty, encountering Nairṛta, fought with supreme weapons, thoroughly mocking Nairṛti.
m.2.2.37.14: And the hero Muṇḍa, of great strength, fought with Varuṇa with supreme might, as though astonishing the three worlds.
m.2.2.37.15: Bhṛṅgī was struck by Vāyu with his own weapon of supreme force, and Vāyu was struck by Bhṛṅgin with a blazing trident.
m.2.2.37.16: The lord of the Kūṣmāṇḍas, encountering Kubera, fought eagerly, a mighty hero, meditating in his heart on Maheśvara.
m.2.2.37.17: The great leader of the Bhairavīs, accompanied by the circle of Yoginīs, tore apart all the gods and drank their blood — a wondrous sight.
m.2.2.37.18: Likewise the Kṣetrapālas there, hungry, tore apart the foremost gods; and Kālī too, tearing them apart, drank much blood.
m.2.2.37.19: Then Viṣṇu of great splendour, slayer of foes, fought with them; he hurled his discus with force, as though burning the ten directions.
m.2.2.37.20: A Kṣetrapāla, seeing the discus coming swiftly, rushed there — the mighty hero — and suddenly swallowed it.
m.2.2.37.21: Seeing the discus swallowed, Viṣṇu, conqueror of enemy cities, squeezed that foe's mouth and made him disgorge it.
m.2.2.37.22: Taking back his discus, the great-souled one, sole sustainer of the world, became exceedingly angry; the very mighty one, bearing various weapons in his rage, fought those great heroes with missiles.
m.2.2.37.23: Viṣṇu made a great battle; he fought with them joyfully, hurling various weapons — a tumultuous fight of fearsome valour.
m.2.2.37.24: Then Bhairava and the others fought him fiercely, discharging various missiles, enraged, with supreme might.
m.2.2.37.25: Seeing their battle thus with Hari of matchless splendour, the mighty one Vīrabhadra, turning back and coming forward, himself fought them.
m.2.2.37.26: Then Viṣṇu of great splendour, the lord Mādhava, inflamed with wrath, raising his discus, fought with that Vīrabhadra.
m.2.2.37.27: Between those two — the great hero and the lord of the ocean, both bearing various weapons — there arose a most terrible, hair-raising battle, O sage.
m.2.2.37.28: Through Viṣṇu's yogic power, from his very body there were born countless, most fierce beings holding conch, discus and mace in their hands.
m.2.2.37.29: Those hosts too, mighty like Viṣṇu and bearing various weapons, fought with the shouting Vīrabhadra.
m.2.2.37.30: All of them, equal in radiance to Nārāyaṇa, that hero slew with his trident and reduced to ashes, remembering Śiva the Lord.
m.2.2.37.31: Then on the battlefield the very mighty Vīrabhadra, as if in sport, struck that Viṣṇu on the chest with his trident.
m.2.2.37.32: Struck suddenly by that blow, Puruṣottama fell then to the ground; Hari became unconscious, O sage.
m.2.2.37.33: Then arose a wondrous radiance like the fire of cosmic dissolution, intense, capable of burning the three worlds, terrifying even to heroes.
m.2.2.37.34: With eyes red with anger, that glorious lord, the bull among men, rising again, stood raising his discus to strike.
m.2.2.37.35: His exceedingly fierce discus, radiant like the sun at the time of doom, Vīrabhadra — undaunted in spirit, Śiva himself, the Lord — paralysed.
m.2.2.37.36: O sage, by the power of Śambhu, lord of Māyā, the great Lord, Hari's discus, held in his hand, did not move — it was surely paralysed.
m.2.2.37.37: Then Viṣṇu, paralysed by Vīrabhadra, lord of the gaṇas, who was speaking, stood motionless like a mountain.
m.2.2.37.38: Then Viṣṇu, paralysed by Vīrabhadra, O Nārada, began reciting the mantra of sacrificial invocation that removes paralysis.
m.2.2.37.39: Then, freed from the paralysis, the wielder of the Śārṅga bow, lord of Ramā, enraged, seized his own bow Śārṅga with its arrows, O sage.
m.2.2.37.40: Struck by three arrows from that Vīrabhadra, Hari's Śārṅga bow, dear one, broke into three pieces that very instant, O sage.
m.2.2.37.41: Then Viṣṇu, awakened to the truth by the great heavenly voice, knowing that great gaṇa to be of unbearable splendour, resolved to vanish.
m.2.2.37.42: And knowing that all this was destined to happen, brought about by Satī and unbearable for others, they went to their own worlds together with their attendants, remembering Śiva, the lord of all, the independent one.
m.2.2.37.43: And I, having gone to Satyaloka, afflicted by grief for my son and deeply distressed, thought: What indeed should I do now?
m.2.2.37.44: When Viṣṇu and I had gone, all the gods together with the sages—those who live on the sacrifice—were utterly defeated by the gaṇas.
m.2.2.37.45: Seeing that calamity and the great sacrifice destroyed, Yajña, though in great fear, took the form of a deer and fled.
m.2.2.37.46: Then Vīrabhadra seized him as he ran toward the sky in the form of a deer, and made him headless.
m.2.2.37.47: Then that hero seized Prajāpati, Dharma and Kaśyapa, and Ariṣṭanemi, the lord of sages with many sons,
m.2.2.37.48: and the sage Aṅgiras and Kṛśāśva, and Datta, the best of sages—the great gaṇa struck them on the head with his foot.
m.2.2.37.49: The mighty Vīrabhadra cut off the tip of the nose of Sarasvatī, and likewise of the mother of the gods, with the tip of his fingernail.
m.2.2.37.50: Then he, his eyes overcome with fury, tore apart other gods and the rest as well and threw them down on the ground.
m.2.2.37.51: Even after tearing apart the chief gods and the sages, Vīrabhadra, his anger flaring swiftly, did not become calm, like a hooded king of serpents, its adorned hood raised.
m.2.2.37.52: Vīrabhadra, having uprooted his enemies as a lion does forest elephants, looked around in all directions every moment, asking who was where.
m.2.2.37.53: Meanwhile the mighty Maṇibhadra struck down Bhṛgu, and then, pressing his chest with his foot, plucked out his beard.
m.2.2.37.54: And Caṇḍa violently knocked out the teeth of Pūṣan, who earlier, while Hara was being cursed, had laughed showing his teeth.
m.2.2.37.55: Nandī, in anger, tore out the eyes of Bhaga, who had been thrown to the ground—Bhaga who had encouraged Dakṣa with a wink of his eye while he was cursing Śiva.
m.2.2.37.56: There Svadhā, Svāhā and Dakṣiṇā, as well as the mantras, the tantras and the others present there, were mocked and maltreated by the gaṇa leaders.
m.2.2.37.57: In anger those gaṇas showered excrement into the sacrificial fire; the heroic gaṇas then reduced that sacrifice to a state beyond description.
m.2.2.37.58: Vīrabhadra, discovering the son of the Self-born (Dakṣa) hiding out of fear of him within the inner altar, dragged him out by force.
m.2.2.37.59: Seizing him by the cheeks, he struck at his head with a sword; but by the power of yoga that head of his proved impossible to cut.
m.2.2.37.60: Considering that head to be impervious to all weapons and missiles, he pressed on his chest with his feet and wrenched it off with his hand.
m.2.2.37.61: Vīrabhadra, foremost of the gaṇas, threw that head of the wicked Dakṣa, the enemy of Hara, into the fire-pit.
m.2.2.37.62: Then Vīrabhadra shone, whirling the trident in his hand; the gaṇas, enraged, mountain-like, like the fires of cosmic dissolution (saṃvarta) in battle, set everything ablaze.
m.2.2.37.63: Having killed them without effort, the wrathful Vīrabhadra then burned them with fire, as a blazing fire burns moths.
m.2.2.37.64: Then Vīrabhadra, seeing Dakṣa and the others headed by him burnt, let out a tremendous peal of laughter, filling the three worlds.
m.2.2.37.65: There, as Vīrabhadra stood surrounded by heroic glory and accompanied by the gaṇas, a divine shower of flowers from the Nandana garden fell upon him.
m.2.2.37.66: Cool, fragrant, pleasant breezes blew gently, and thereafter the drums of the gods sounded all together.
m.2.2.37.67: Thereafter that hero, his task accomplished, went swiftly to Kailāsa, like the sun that has dispelled dense darkness.
m.2.2.37.68: Seeing Vīrabhadra with his task accomplished, Śambhu, the supreme Lord, gladdened at heart, made him chief of the heroic gaṇas.
m.2.2.37.iti: Thus ends the thirty-seventh adhyāya, named The description of the destruction of the sacrifice, in the second khaṇḍa, the Satī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.2.38.1: Sūta said: Having heard these words of Vidhi (Brahmā), whose wisdom is immeasurable, Nārada, the best of the twice-born, was amazed and lovingly questioned him.
m.2.2.38.2: Nārada said: For what reason did Hari, leaving Śiva aside, go with the gods to Dakṣa's sacrifice, where the insult to Śiva then took place? Tell me that.
m.2.2.38.3: Does Hari not know Śambhu, whose might is that of cosmic dissolution? And how did he fight with his gaṇas like an ignorant one?
m.2.2.38.4: This is my great doubt; dispel it, O treasury of compassion. And tell me, O lord, the deeds of Śambhu, which bring zeal to the mind.
m.2.2.38.5: Brahmā said: O best of the twice-born, listen lovingly to the deeds of the moon-crested Śiva, which remove all doubts of one who asks and of one who acts upon them.
m.2.2.38.6: Long ago, owing to the curse of the sage Dadhīca, Hari lost his wisdom; and, having been the helper of Kṣuva, he went with the gods to Dakṣa's sacrifice.
m.2.2.38.7: Nārada said: Why did Dadhīca, the best of sages, curse Viṣṇu? What wrong was done to him by Hari, the helper of that Kṣuva?
m.2.2.38.8: Brahmā said: There arose a king of great splendour, known as Kṣuva. He became the friend of Dadhīca, the lord of sages, of great power.
m.2.2.38.9: Long ago, after a long time, in connection with austerity, a dispute arose between Kṣuva and Dadhīca, which caused great calamity and became famous in the three worlds.
m.2.2.38.10: Among the three classes, the brahmin alone is the highest; there is no doubt. So declared Dadhīca, the devotee of Śiva and knower of the Veda.
m.2.2.38.11: Hearing that statement of Dadhīca, O great sage, King Kṣuva, deluded by the intoxication of fortune, spoke thus:
m.2.2.38.12: Kṣuva said: The king bears the bodies of the eight guardians of the worlds. Therefore the king is indeed the highest, the master and lord of the classes and life-stages.
m.2.2.38.13: The Veda, intent on this, declares that the king is made of all the gods. That great deity of which it speaks—that am I myself; therefore, O sage,
m.2.2.38.14: therefore the king is superior to the brahmin—consider it, O son of Cyavana. Hence I must not be disrespected; I am to be honoured by you in every way.
m.2.2.38.15: Brahmā said: Hearing that view of Kṣuva, contrary to Śruti and Smṛti, the best of sages, the Bhārgava Dadhīca, became exceedingly angry.
m.2.2.38.16: Then, O sage, the enraged Dadhīca of great splendour, out of regard for his own dignity, struck Kṣuva on the head with his left fist.
m.2.2.38.17: Struck, Kṣuva—the evil-minded lord of the cosmic egg—greatly enraged, roared loudly and cut Dadhīca down with a thunderbolt.
m.2.2.38.18: Struck down by that thunderbolt, the Bhārgava fell to the ground. Wounded by Kṣuva, he, the upholder of the Bhārgava lineage, remembered Śukra.
m.2.2.38.19: Then Śukra, the yogin, quickly came to Dadhīca and joined together his body, which had been struck by Kṣuva.
m.2.2.38.20: Having restored Dadhīca's body as before, the Bhārgava Śukra, foremost of Śiva's devotees and promulgator of the death-conquering lore, spoke:
m.2.2.38.21: Śukra said: Dear Dadhīca, having worshipped Śiva, lord of all, the master, I shall tell you the supreme Vedic Mahāmṛtyuñjaya mantra.
m.2.2.38.22: We worship Tryambaka—the lord, father of the three worlds, father of the three spheres, great lord of the three guṇas;
m.2.2.38.23: lord of the three principles, of the three fires, of all that exists threefold everywhere, of the three heavens, of the three arms, of all that exists threefold everywhere;
m.2.2.38.24: Mahādeva is lord of the three gods. We worship him who is fragrant, increaser of nourishment—present in all beings everywhere, in the three guṇas, and in creation, just as
m.2.2.38.25: likewise in the senses, in other things, in the gods and in the gaṇas: like fragrance in a flower, the radiant lord of the immortals is the fragrance.
m.2.2.38.26: And since the nourishment of Prakṛti comes from that Puruṣa, O best of the twice-born, and also the differentiation from Mahat down to the particulars, O one of good vows,
m.2.2.38.27: and the nourishment of Viṣṇu, of the Grandsire, of the sages, O great sage, of the senses and of the gods—therefore he is the increaser of nourishment.
m.2.2.38.28: That god, the immortal Rudra, becomes manifest to one through ritual action or austerity, through Vedic study, yoga and meditation,
m.2.2.38.29: and through truth and other means; for Bhava himself, the lord, brings release from bondage—from the subtle-tipped noose of death—like a cucumber from its stalk.
m.2.2.38.30: This Mṛtasañjīvanī mantra is regarded by me as the highest of all. Thus, devoted to its repetition with love and discipline, remembering Śiva,
m.2.2.38.31: having repeated it, offered oblations and thus consecrated water with it, drink that water day and night. Meditating in Śiva's presence, there is no fear of death anywhere.
m.2.2.38.32: Having performed all the nyāsa and other rites, having duly worshipped Śiva and arranged this, undistracted, one should meditate on Śaṅkara, who is loving to his devotees.
m.2.2.38.33: I shall tell the meditation on him, having meditated in which way one should repeat the mantra; the wise one will then, by Śambhu's power, become perfected in the mantra.
m.2.2.38.34: I worship the three-eyed Mṛtyuñjaya together with Girijā: who, drawing water from the pair of pots held in one pair of lotus-hands, sprinkles his head with another pair of hands; who holds two hands with pots in his lap; whose other hands bear a rosary and a deer; who is seated on a lotus; and whose body is moist with nectar flowing from the moon on his head.
m.2.2.38.35: Brahmā said: Having thus instructed Dadhīci, the best of sages, Śukra went to his own abode, dear one, remembering Lord Śaṅkara.
m.2.2.38.36: Hearing his words, the great sage Dadhīca went to the forest for austerity, remembering Śiva with great love.
m.2.2.38.37: Going there, he duly and lovingly repeated that mantra called Mahāmṛtyuñjaya and performed austerity, remembering Śiva.
m.2.2.38.38: Having repeated that mantra for a very long time and propitiated Śaṅkara through austerity, he pleased Śiva, the Great Conqueror of Death.
m.2.2.38.39: Then Śambhu, loving to his devotees, pleased at heart by that repetition, lovingly appeared before him, O great sage.
m.2.2.38.40: Seeing Śambhu, his own lord, that lord of sages rejoiced; bowing duly with devotion, with palms well joined, he praised him.
m.2.2.38.41: Then, dear one, O sage, Śiva, pleased with affection, said to the son of Cyavana with a most gracious mind: Ask for a boon.
m.2.2.38.42: Hearing these words of Śambhu, Dadhīca, the best of devotees, with joined palms and bowing, spoke to Śaṅkara, who is affectionate to his devotees.
m.2.2.38.43: Dadhīca said: O God of gods, O Mahādeva, grant me three boons: bones like the thunderbolt, invulnerability, and freedom from abjectness everywhere.
m.2.2.38.44: Brahmā said: Hearing what he said, the Supreme Lord, pleased, granted those three boons to Dadhīca, saying, so be it.
m.2.2.38.45: Having obtained the three boons from Śiva, the great sage, joyful and established on the Vedic path, quickly went to the place of Kṣuva.
