m.2.2.38.46: Having obtained from the Fierce One (Ugra) invulnerability, bones of thunderbolt and freedom from abjectness, he struck the king of kings on the head with the sole of his foot.
m.2.2.38.47: Then King Kṣuva, greatly enraged and proud through the backing of Viṣṇu, struck Dadhīca on the chest with the thunderbolt.
m.2.2.38.48: That thunderbolt did not bring about the destruction of the great-souled Dadhīca, owing to the power of the Supreme Lord; the son of Brahmā (Kṣuva) was astonished.
m.2.2.38.49: Seeing the invulnerability and freedom from abjectness of Dadhīca, lord of sages, and the utterly superior power he had over the thunderbolt, Kṣuva, son of Brahmā, was astonished in his mind.
m.2.2.38.50: The protector of those seeking refuge (the king), defeated by Dadhīca, the servant of Mṛtyuñjaya, quickly went to the forest and worshipped Hari Mukunda, the younger brother of Indra.
m.2.2.38.51: Pleased by his worship, the blessed Madhusūdana, whose banner bears Garuḍa, granted him a divine vision of himself.
m.2.2.38.52: Seeing the god Janārdana with that divine sight, he bowed to the Garuḍa-bannered one and praised him with pleasing words.
m.2.2.38.53: Having thus worshipped and praised the unconquerable Lord, the god praised by Indra and the other gods, he looked at him with devotion, bowed with his head, and made his submission to Janārdana.
m.2.2.38.54: The king said: O Lord, a certain brahmin famed as Dadhīca, knower of dharma and of disciplined mind, was formerly my friend.
m.2.2.38.55: Having worshipped Mahādeva, the Conqueror of Death, free from all ill, he is by Śaṅkara's power always unslayable by anyone.
m.2.2.38.56: That Dadhīca of great austerity contemptuously and forcefully struck me on the head with his left foot, even in the assembly.
m.2.2.38.57: And he said to me arrogantly that he feared nothing from any quarter, having obtained an excellent boon from Mṛtyuñjaya, being proud beyond measure, O Hari.
m.2.2.38.58: Then, learning of the invulnerability of the great-souled Dadhīca, Hari called to mind the incomparable power of Maheśa.
m.2.2.38.59: Having thus remembered, Hari quickly said to Kṣuva, the son of Brahmā: O king of kings, brahmins have not the least fear anywhere.
m.2.2.38.60: Especially for devotees of Rudra there is no fear, O lord of the earth. One who causes distress to a brahmin brings on himself a curse — even were it I, a god.
m.2.2.38.61: By his curse, at Dakṣa's sacrifice, there will be my defeat at the hands of the Lord of gods (Śiva), O king of kings, and also my rising again.
m.2.2.38.62: Therefore, O king of kings, though success is not assured for me who am the whole sacrifice, having joined with you, O king of kings, I shall make an effort for your victory over Dadhīca.
m.2.2.38.63: Hearing Hari's words, King Kṣuva said, so be it, and remained right there, pleased by that, his mind eager for the fulfilment of his desire.
m.2.2.38.iti: Thus ends the thirty-eighth adhyāya, named The description of the dispute between Kṣuva and Dadhīca, in the second khaṇḍa, the Satī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.2.39.1: Brahmā said: For the purpose of benefiting Kṣuva, the Lord, who is affectionate to his devotees, then assumed the form of a brahmin and went to Dadhīca's hermitage.
m.2.2.39.2: The preceptor of the world, intent on accomplishing Kṣuva's task and resorting to deceit, saluted Dadhīca, the brahmin-sage and foremost of Śaivas, and spoke.
m.2.2.39.3: Viṣṇu said: O Dadhīca, O brahmin-sage, devoted to the worship of Bhava, O imperishable one, I ask one boon from you; you should grant it.
m.2.2.39.4: Brahmā said: Dadhīca, the best of Śaivas, being thus asked by the god of gods, who was seeking to accomplish Kṣuva's purpose, quickly spoke words to Hari.
m.2.2.39.5: Dadhīca said: Your wish is known to me, O brahmin; you have come for the sake of Kṣuva's task. You are indeed the Lord Hari, the master of illusion, in the form of a brahmin.
m.2.2.39.6: O lord of gods, O Janārdana, by the grace of Rudra I always have knowledge of the three times — the past, the future and the present.
m.2.2.39.7: I know you to be Hari, Viṣṇu; give up the guise of a brahmin, O you of good vows. You have been propitiated by the king Kṣuva of wicked mind.
m.2.2.39.8: I know your affection for devotees, O Lord Hari. Give up deceit, take on your own form, and remember Śaṅkara.
m.2.2.39.9: If I, devoted to the worship of Bhava, have fear of anyone, you should tell me carefully, holding to the truth.
m.2.2.39.10: My mind being attached to the remembrance of Śiva, I never speak falsely anywhere. I do not fear anyone in this world, not even gods, demons and the like.
m.2.2.39.11: Viṣṇu said: O Dadhīca, O you of good vows, your fear has vanished everywhere, since you are devoted to the worship of Bhava and are indeed all-knowing.
m.2.2.39.12: Salutations to you. At my request, you should say just once: I am afraid of Kṣuva, the lord of kings, my adversary.
m.2.2.39.13: Brahmā said: Even after hearing these words of Viṣṇu, the great sage Dadhīca, best of Śaivas, laughed and fearlessly spoke.
m.2.2.39.14: Dadhīca said: By the power of Śambhu, the god of gods, the very wielder of Pināka, I never fear anything from anyone anywhere.
m.2.2.39.15: Brahmā said: Then, hearing the sage's words, Hari grew angry and stood with his discus raised, wishing to burn the best of sages.
m.2.2.39.16: But there, against the brahmin, the most terrible discus became blunted by the power of the Lord, even in the presence of the king.
m.2.2.39.17: Seeing that discus with its edge blunted, Dadhīca smilingly spoke to Viṣṇu, the very cause of the manifestation of the existent and the non-existent.
m.2.2.39.18: Dadhīca said: O Lord, the extremely terrible discus famed as Sudarśana, which you, Viṣṇu, obtained long ago through great effort — that auspicious discus of Bhava does not wish to slay me here.
m.2.2.39.19: So now, Lord Hari, in your anger discharge all your weapons at me one after another; you should make the effort with arrows and missiles beginning with the Brahmāstra.
m.2.2.39.20: Brahmā said: Hearing his words and seeing him as a man without might, Hari then in anger discharged all his weapons at him one after another.
m.2.2.39.21: Then the gods, bereft of understanding, eagerly gave help to Viṣṇu, who had set out to fight a single brahmin.
m.2.2.39.22: Indra and the others on Hari's side swiftly hurled their own weapons and missiles with force from all sides upon Dadhīca.
m.2.2.39.23: Then Dadhīca, the self-controlled one with adamantine bones, taking a handful of kuśa grass and remembering Śiva, cast it on all sides at all the gods.
m.2.2.39.24: By the power of Śaṅkara, that handful of kuśa of the sage became a divine trident resembling the fire of universal destruction, O sage.
m.2.2.39.25: That Śaiva trident with its prongs, blazing on all sides with splendour surpassing the fire at the end of the age, set its mind on burning the gods along with their weapons.
m.2.2.39.26: And all the weapons that had been hurled by the gods headed by Nārāyaṇa and Indra bowed down to that three-pronged trident.
m.2.2.39.27: All the gods, the dwellers of heaven, their valour shattered, fled. Only Hari, the best of illusionists, remained there, frightened.
m.2.2.39.28: Lord Viṣṇu, the supreme person, created from his own body divine attendants resembling himself, in hundreds of thousands upon tens of thousands.
m.2.2.39.29: Then those heroic attendants of Viṣṇu also fought there with the lone sage Dadhīca, whose self was Śiva, O divine sage.
m.2.2.39.30: Then Dadhīca, best of Śaivas, having fought those attendants of Viṣṇu repeatedly in battle, suddenly burnt them all.
m.2.2.39.31: Then, to astonish the sage Dadhīca, Hari, expert in great illusion, quickly assumed the cosmic form.
m.2.2.39.32: In that very body of Hari, Dadhīca, best of brahmins, saw thousands of gods and other living beings,
m.2.2.39.33: and crores of beings, crores of attendants, and crores of cosmic eggs, then, in the body of the cosmic-formed one.
m.2.2.39.34: Having seen all this there, the son of Cyavana then spoke to Viṣṇu, the lord of the world, praised by the world, the unborn, the all-pervading.
m.2.2.39.35: Dadhīca said: Give up this illusion, O mighty-armed one; on reflection it is mere appearance. Thousands of things hard to know are known to me, O Mādhava.
m.2.2.39.36: Look attentively in me at the whole universe together with yourself, and also Brahmā and Rudra; I give you divine sight.
m.2.2.39.37: Brahmā said: Having said this, the sage, the son of Cyavana, whose body was filled with Śambhu's radiance, showed the entire cosmic egg within his own body.
m.2.2.39.38: Then Dadhīca, the best of Śaivas, the wise and fearless one, remembering Śaṅkara in his heart and laughing, spoke to Viṣṇu, the lord of gods.
m.2.2.39.39: Dadhīca said: What use is this illusion, or the power of mantras, O Hari? Making this a true resolve, you should fight with effort.
m.2.2.39.40: Brahmā said: Having heard these words of that sage, Viṣṇu, fearless then, became extremely angry with that sage, who was full of Śambhu's splendour.
m.2.2.39.41: And the gods again rushed forward, along with that god Nārāyaṇa, eager to fight with the mighty sage Dadhīca.
m.2.2.39.42: Meanwhile Kṣuva came there together with me, I the lotus-born, restraining Hari, who had been rendered powerless, and the gods.
m.2.2.39.43: Having heard my words that a brāhmaṇa cannot be conquered, Hari went near him and bowed to the sage.
m.2.2.39.44: Kṣuva, becoming most wretched, went there to Dadhīca, lord of sages, saluted him, and in distress entreated him.
m.2.2.39.45: Kṣuva said: Be gracious, O tiger among sages, crest-jewel of Śiva's devotees. Be gracious, O supreme lord, you who are ever hard for the wicked to perceive.
m.2.2.39.46: Brahmā said: Having heard these words of the king and of the host of gods, the brāhmaṇa Dadhīca, a treasury of austerities, showed favour to him.
m.2.2.39.47: Then, seeing Ramā's lord and the others, the sage, overcome with anger, remembering Śiva in his heart, cursed Viṣṇu and the gods as well.
m.2.2.39.48: Dadhīca said: O gods, together with Indra lord of gods, and O lords of sages, may you be destroyed by the fire of Rudra's wrath, along with the god Viṣṇu and your hosts.
m.2.2.39.49: Brahmā said: Having thus cursed the gods, the sage looked at Kṣuva and then said: O king of kings, the best of the twice-born is to be worshipped by the gods and by kings as well.
m.2.2.39.50: Brāhmaṇas alone, O king of kings, are strong and mighty. Having said this plainly, that brāhmaṇa entered his own hermitage.
m.2.2.39.51: Having saluted Dadhīca, Kṣuva went to his own home; Viṣṇu went with the gods to his own world, as he had come.
m.2.2.39.52: Thus that place became a sacred ford, remembered as Sthāneśvara; one who reaches Sthāneśvara would attain union with Śiva.
m.2.2.39.53: I have told you in brief, dear one, the dispute between Kṣuva and Dadhīca, and the story of Brahmā and Viṣṇu, who incurred a curse on the king's account, acting without Śiva.
m.2.2.39.54: Whoever recites daily this dispute between Kṣuva and Dadhīca, conquering untimely death, goes to Brahmaloka at the end of the body.
m.2.2.39.55: Whoever recites this and enters battle will never have fear of death, and he will be victorious.
m.2.2.39.iti: Thus ends the thirty-ninth adhyāya, named The description of the battle between Viṣṇu and Dadhīca, in the second khaṇḍa, the Satī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.2.40.1: Nārada said: O Vidhi, O Vidhi, most wise one, revealer of the Śaiva truth, you have let me hear Śiva's most wonderful sport, which is utterly delightful.
m.2.2.40.2: When the heroic Vīrabhadra had destroyed Dakṣa's sacrifice and gone back to Mount Kailāsa, what happened then, dear father? Tell me that now.
m.2.2.40.3: Brahmā said: Then all the hosts of gods and the sages, defeated, their limbs wounded by Rudra's troops, went to my world.
m.2.2.40.4: Bowing to me, the Self-born, and praising me profusely, they reported their own distress in full detail.
m.2.2.40.5: Hearing that, I, afflicted by grief for my son, pondered, greatly agitated, with a tormented mind.
m.2.2.40.6: What should I do quickly today that brings happiness to the gods, by which the god Dakṣa may live and the sacrifice be completed?
m.2.2.40.7: Reflecting thus in many ways, O sage, I found no peace. Then, remembering Viṣṇu with devotion, I obtained the understanding appropriate to that moment.
m.2.2.40.8: Then, with the gods and sages, I went to Viṣṇu's world; bowing and praising him with various hymns, I told him of our grief.
m.2.2.40.9: O God, act so that the sacrifice may be completed, and he, the performer of the sacrifice may live, and all the gods and the sages may be happy.
m.2.2.40.10: O God of gods, Lord of Ramā, Viṣṇu, bringer of happiness to the gods, we, together with the gods and sages, have surely come to you for refuge.
m.2.2.40.11: Brahmā said: Hearing these words of mine, Brahmā, that Lord of Ramā, whose self is Śiva, remembering Śiva, replied with a sorrowful mind.
m.2.2.40.12: Viṣṇu said: For those who wish to prosper, an offence against one more powerful does not lead to welfare; in such a case the offenders' wish to thrive is fulfilled in many ways only by appeasing him.
m.2.2.40.13: All the gods have sinned against Śiva, the supreme Lord, since, O Vidhi, they withheld the sacrificial share of that Śambhu.
m.2.2.40.14: All of you, with pure minds, propitiate that Śiva of unsurpassed grace, clasping his two feet.
m.2.2.40.15: He is the god at whose anger the whole world perishes; seek quickly, by his command, the restoration to life of the sacrifice together with the world-guardians.
m.2.2.40.16: Quickly seek forgiveness from that god, who is bereft of his beloved and whose heart has been pierced by harsh words from the very wicked Dakṣa.
m.2.2.40.17: This alone, O Vidhi, is the great means to pacify him and to please Śambhu, I believe; what I have said is the truth.
m.2.2.40.18: Neither I, nor you, nor the other gods, nor even the sages and embodied beings know his true nature or the measure of his strength and valour.
m.2.2.40.19: Who would try to devise a scheme against that self-dependent, transcendent Supreme Self? Only an utterly deluded adversary.
m.2.2.40.20: I too, O Brahmā, will go with everyone to Śiva's abode and will surely seek forgiveness from Giriśa, for I too have offended against Śiva.
m.2.2.40.21: Brahmā said: Having thus instructed me, Brahmā, along with the gods and others, Viṣṇu resolved, together with the gods, to go to that mountain.
m.2.2.40.22: Hari, accompanied by the gods, sages, Prajāpatis and others, went to Kailāsa, the auspicious best of mountains, the dwelling of Śiva's own abode,
m.2.2.40.23: ever most dear to the Lord, well frequented by Kinnaras and others, by non-human beings, Apsarases and those perfected in yoga, and very lofty,
m.2.2.40.24: shining on all sides with peaks made of various gems, variegated with various minerals, and crowded with various trees and creepers,
m.2.2.40.25: filled with herds of various animals, endowed with various birds, with various springs of water, with the immortal lovers of the Siddha women
m.2.2.40.26: who sport there with their lovers, with various caves and slopes and with other kinds of trees — resplendent, shining like silver,
m.2.2.40.27: resounding with tigers and other great beasts yet free from cruelty, endowed with every beauty, divine, causing great wonder,
m.2.2.40.28: encircled by the Gaṅgā, whose waters are made holier by Satī's bathing at that place, she who purifies all, born from Viṣṇu's foot — exceedingly pure.
m.2.2.40.29: Seeing such a mountain, named Kailāsa, dear to Śiva, the gods headed by Viṣṇu, along with the great sages, were filled with wonder.
m.2.2.40.30: Near it the immortals saw the lovely city named Alakā, most divine, belonging to Kubera, the friend of Rudra.
m.2.2.40.31: Near it they also saw the Saugandhika forest, divine and full of all kinds of trees, where there is that wondrous sound.
m.2.2.40.32: Outside it were its two divine and most purifying rivers, Nandā and Alakanandā, which remove sin by their mere sight.
m.2.2.40.33: Celestial women, coming secretly from their own world, always drink their water; plunging in, they sport there with men, wearied by love-play.
m.2.2.40.34: Leaving behind the city of the lord of Yakṣas and the Saugandhika forest, the gods, going on, saw nearby Śaṅkara's banyan tree,
m.2.2.40.35: which cast a steady shade all around, whose branches spread over seventy-five yojanas, a hundred yojanas high, without nests, free from heat,
m.2.2.40.36: visible only to those of great merit, very lovely and most purifying, the divine place of Śambhu's yoga, resorted to by yogins, supremely excellent.
m.2.2.40.37: Beneath that banyan, refuge of those seeking liberation and full of great yoga, all the gods headed by Viṣṇu saw Śiva seated,
m.2.2.40.38: joyfully worshipped by Brahmā's sons, great Siddhas ever devoted to Śiva, tranquil, with completely calm forms,
m.2.2.40.39: and likewise especially attended always by his friend Kubera, lord of the Guhyakas and Rākṣasas, and by his own attendants and kinsmen,
m.2.2.40.40: the supreme Lord, bearing the true form cherished by ascetics, out of affection the friend of the universe, gloriously adorned with ash and the like.
m.2.2.40.41: O sage, they saw him well seated on a seat of kuśa grass, expounding the supreme knowledge to you, who were asking, while all the virtuous ones listened.
m.2.2.40.42: Having placed his left foot on the right thigh and the other on the knee, with a rosary on his forearm, he sat in the gesture of true reasoning (tarka-mudrā).
m.2.2.40.43: Seeing Śiva in this form, the gods headed by Viṣṇu then all quickly bowed down, humbly joining their hands.
m.2.2.40.44: Rudra, the refuge of the virtuous, perceiving that Viṣṇu had come with me, rose, and the Lord even saluted him with his head.
m.2.2.40.45: Then Śiva, whose feet had been saluted by all the divine ones headed by Viṣṇu, bowed in turn, just as Viṣṇu, the true refuge of the worlds, bows to Kaśyapa.
m.2.2.40.46: Śiva respectfully addressed Viṣṇu, who is well revered by the gods, siddhas, lords of the gaṇas and great sages, and who, together with the gods, had made obeisance.
m.2.2.40.iti: Thus ends the fortieth adhyāya, named The description of the sight of Śiva, in the second khaṇḍa, the Satī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.2.41.1: Viṣṇu and the others said: O God of gods, Mahādeva, O Lord who follows worldly custom, by your grace we know you, Śambhu, the Lord, to be Brahman.
m.2.2.41.2: Why do you delude us, dear one, with your supreme māyā, which is always hard for men to understand and which bewilders them, O Supreme Lord?
m.2.2.41.3: You are the supreme Brahman, beyond Prakṛti and Puruṣa, the womb and the seed of the world, and beyond the reach of mind and speech.
m.2.2.41.4: You alone, by your own independent power, create, protect and devour the universe, sporting with Śiva-śakti, who is your own form, like a spider with its web.
m.2.2.41.5: You alone, O Īśāna, full of compassion, created the sacrifice, using Dakṣa as your instrument, O all-pervading one, for the constant upholding of the threefold Veda.
m.2.2.41.6: By you alone the boundaries of dharma have been set in the world, which brahmins firm in their vows and skilled in the Vedic path trust, knowing them to be pure.
m.2.2.41.7: For the doer of auspicious deeds you grant his own world or the highest in happiness, O Lord; and for the doers of inauspicious deeds, what is due — or a mixture, or the reverse.
m.2.2.41.8: You alone are always the giver of the fruits of all actions. All beings are declared to be paśus, and you are their lord, as heard in the Śruti.
m.2.2.41.9: Those of divisive minds, who see only ritual action, who wound others to the quick and are evil-hearted — these fools, filled with envy, torment others with harsh words.
m.2.2.41.10: O Lord, for those already struck down by fate, let there not be slaying by you as well. Blessed one, supreme Īśāna, show mercy, O highest Lord.
m.2.2.41.11: Salutation to Rudra, the peaceful, to Brahman, the supreme Self; salutation to the wearer of matted locks, to Maheśa, the radiant, the great.
m.2.2.41.12: You are the creator of the creators of the universe; you are the sustainer, the great-grandsire; you are of the three guṇas and also beyond the guṇas, higher than Prakṛti and Puruṣa.
m.2.2.41.13: Salutation to you, the blue-throated, the ordainer, the supreme Self, the universe, the seed of the universe, the cause of the world's joy.
m.2.2.41.14: You are the syllable Om and the call vaṣaṭ, the one who sets every undertaking in motion; the call hanta and the call svadhā, always the eater of offerings to the gods, to the ancestors, and of food.
m.2.2.41.15: How was the sacrifice destroyed by you, O one devoted to dharma? You are devoted to brahmins, O Mahādeva; how could you be the destroyer of the sacrifice, O Lord?
m.2.2.41.16: You are the protector of brahmins, of cows, and of dharma; you are the refuge, ever infinite, of all living beings, O Lord.
m.2.2.41.17: Salutation to you, Blessed Rudra, whose brilliance surpasses the sun's beyond measure. Salutation to you, Bhava, the god, who are taste (rasa), consisting of water.
m.2.2.41.18: Salutation to Śarva, whose form is the earth, ever fragrant. Salutation to Rudra, whose nature is fire, of great brilliance.
m.2.2.41.19: Salutation again and again to you, Īśa, the wind, who are touch. Salutation to you, lord of creatures, the sacrificer, the ordainer.
m.2.2.41.20: Salutation to you, Bhīma, whose form is space, who are sound alone. Salutation be to you, Mahādeva, Soma, the active one.
m.2.2.41.21: Salutation to you, Ugra, whose form is the sun, the yogin of action. Salutation to you, death of Death; salutation to you, wrath of Rudra.
m.2.2.41.22: Salutation to you, Śiva, Bhīma, Śaṅkara, Śiva. You are fierce, the controller of all beings, yet you are auspicious to us.
m.2.2.41.23: To the bestower of happiness, the universe, Brahman, the destroyer of affliction; salutation to you, lord of Ambikā, lord of Umā.
m.2.2.41.24: To Śarva, of all forms, the Puruṣa, the supreme Self, free of manifestation as being or non-being, the cause of Mahat — to you salutation.
m.2.2.41.25: Salutation again and again to the one born in many ways in the world, the abundant. To the Blue one, Nīlarudra, Kadrudra, the wise.
m.2.2.41.26: Salutation to you, the most bountiful, the god, Śipiviṣṭa. Salutation to you, the greatest, ever the slayer of the enemies of the gods.
m.2.2.41.27: Salutation again and again to Tāra and Sutāra, the youthful, of fine brilliance, to Harikeśa, the god, Maheśa.
m.2.2.41.28: To you, Śambhu of the gods, the all-pervading, the supreme Self; salutation to you, the supreme; salutation to you, the dark-throated.
m.2.2.41.29: Salutation to the golden one, the supreme Lord, golden-bodied; to the terrible one, of terrible form, delighting in terrible deeds.
m.2.2.41.30: To the one whose body is smeared with ash and who is adorned with rudrākṣa; salutation to the short, the tall; salutation be to you, the dwarf.
m.2.2.41.31: Salutation again and again to you, O god, who slay from afar and who slay in front. Salutation to you, bearer of the bow, the trident, the mace, the plough.
m.2.2.41.32: To the bearer of many weapons, destroyer of Daityas and Dānavas; salutation indeed to Sadya, of the form of Sadya, to Sadyojāta.
m.2.2.41.33: Salutation to you, Vāma, of beautiful form, of beautiful eyes. Salutation again and again to Aghora, the supreme Lord, the formidable.
m.2.2.41.34: To Tatpuruṣa, the Lord, and the ancient Puruṣa; to the giver of the aims of human life, the observer of vows, Parameṣṭhin.
m.2.2.41.35: Salutation to you, Īśāna; salutation again and again to Īśvara; salutation to Brahman, of the form of Brahman, the supreme Self in person.
m.2.2.41.36: You are fierce, the controller of all the wicked; you are auspicious to us. Salutation to you, the swallower of the Kālakūṭa poison, the protector of the gods and others.
m.2.2.41.37: Salutation to the hero, Vīrabhadra, protector of heroes, the trident-bearer; to Mahādeva, the great, the lord of creatures.
m.2.2.41.38: To the heroic-souled, the one of excellent knowledge, Śrīkaṇṭha, the bearer of Pināka; salutation to the endless, the subtle; salutation to you, the wrath that is death to death.
m.2.2.41.39: To the supreme, the supreme Lord, higher than the highest; salutation to you, the highest beyond the highest, the all-pervading, whose form is the universe.
m.2.2.41.40: Salutation to the one whose consort is Viṣṇu, whose field is Viṣṇu, the sun; to Bhairava, the refuge, Tryambaka, the one who sports.
m.2.2.41.41: To Mṛtyuñjaya (the conqueror of death), to the one who is grief to the wicked, to the one possessing the three guṇas, to the one whose self is the guṇas, to the one whose eyes are the moon, the sun and fire, to the bridge that is the ground of all causes — salutations.
m.2.2.41.42: For the whole world is pervaded by you through your own splendour. You are the supreme Brahman, changeless, consciousness and bliss, luminous.
m.2.2.41.43: All the gods, headed by Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Indra, Candra and others, and the other sages too, have been born from you, O Maheśvara.
m.2.2.41.44: Since you sustain everything by dividing your body eightfold, you are called Aṣṭamūrti; and you are the Lord, the primordial one, full of compassion.
m.2.2.41.45: From fear of you this wind blows; from fear of you fire burns; through fear of you the sun gives heat; and death runs about everywhere.
m.2.2.41.46: O ocean of compassion, O Maheśāna, be gracious, O supreme Lord. Protect, protect us always, since we are ruined and bewildered.
m.2.2.41.47: We have constantly been protected by you alone, O Lord, O treasure of compassion, from various calamities, O Śambhu; likewise protect us today.
m.2.2.41.48: O Lord, bestower of grace, quickly bring about the restoration of the unfinished sacrifice of Dakṣa the Prajāpati, O Durgeśa.
m.2.2.41.49: May Bhaga regain his eyes, and may the sacrificer live; may Pūṣan's teeth grow again, and Bhṛgu's beard be as before.
m.2.2.41.50: And, O Śaṅkara, may there be health for the gods and others, favoured by you, whose limbs have been entirely shattered by weapons and stones.
m.2.2.41.51: O Lord, let there be a full share for you in the remaining sacrificial rite. The sacrifice shall be arranged for you with Rudra's share, never otherwise anywhere.
m.2.2.41.52: Having spoken thus, that Lord of creatures (Brahmā) and the Lord of Ramā (Viṣṇu), with joined palms, fell prostrate on the ground like a staff, intent on seeking forgiveness.
m.2.2.41.iti: Thus ends the forty-first adhyāya, named The description of the praise by the gods, in the second khaṇḍa, the Satī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.2.42.1: Brahmā said: Entreated by the glorious Brahmā, lord of creatures, and constantly by the sage as well, Śambhu, the supreme Lord, became gracious.
m.2.2.42.2: Having reassured the gods headed by Viṣṇu, the supreme Lord, treasure of compassion, smiled and spoke, bestowing supreme grace.
m.2.2.42.3: Śrī Mahādeva said: Listen attentively to my words, O two best of gods. I tell you both the truth, dear ones: I have always borne your anger.
m.2.2.42.4: I neither speak of nor dwell upon the sin of those who are like children in their person; on those overcome by my māyā, the punishment there was inflicted by me.
m.2.2.42.5: This destruction of Dakṣa's sacrifice was in no way done by me. When one hates another, what one intends for others will befall oneself.
m.2.2.42.6: An act that harms others should never be done. When one hates another, what one intends for others will befall oneself.
m.2.2.42.7: Let Dakṣa, whose head was offered in the sacrifice, have a goat-faced head; let the god Bhaga see his share of the sacrifice through the eye of Mitra.
m.2.2.42.8: The god named Pūṣan, dear one, whose teeth were broken, shall eat ground flour with the teeth of the sacrificer; this I have declared truly.
m.2.2.42.9: Bhṛgu, who opposed me, shall indeed have a goat's beard. The gods who gave me the remnant of the offering shall have all their limbs restored to their natural state.
m.2.2.42.10: Let the other adhvaryu priests be provided with arms made from the arms of the Aśvins and the hands of Pūṣan; this I have spoken out of affection for you.
m.2.2.42.11: Brahmā said: Having spoken thus, the supreme Lord, full of compassion, fell silent — the god, lord of the moving and unmoving, the sovereign who acts in accordance with the Veda.
m.2.2.42.12: Then all the gods and the rest, together with Viṣṇu and Brahmā, hearing Śaṅkara's words, were fully satisfied and exclaimed, excellent, excellent.
m.2.2.42.13: Then, having invited Śambhu, Viṣṇu, with me and the gods and sages, went once more with great joy to that place of sacrifice.
m.2.2.42.14: Thus, at the request of the gods headed by Viṣṇu, Śambhu went to Kanakhala, to the sacrificial enclosure of the Prajāpati.
m.2.2.42.15: Then Rudra saw there the destruction of the sacrifice wrought by Vīrabhadra, especially that inflicted on the gods and sages.
m.2.2.42.16: Svāhā, Svadhā, Pūṣan, Tuṣṭi, Dhṛti, Sarasvatī, and likewise all the other sages, the Pitṛs and the Fires,
m.2.2.42.17: and the many others there — Yakṣas, Gandharvas and Rākṣasas — had been torn and plucked apart, and some had died on the battlefield.
m.2.2.42.18: Seeing the sacrifice in such a state, the Lord summoned the mighty Vīrabhadra, chief of the gaṇas, and spoke to him, laughing.
m.2.2.42.19: O mighty-armed Vīrabhadra, what is this deed you have done? Dear one, you have swiftly inflicted a great punishment on the gods, sages and others.
m.2.2.42.20: Bring Dakṣa quickly, by whom this sacrifice was performed in such a manner — a strange sacrifice indeed, dear one, whose fruit is such as this.
m.2.2.42.21: Brahmā said: Thus addressed by Śaṅkara, Vīrabhadra hastily brought the headless trunk and threw it down before Śambhu.
m.2.2.42.22: Seeing him headless, Śaṅkara, the benefactor of the worlds, smiling, spoke to Vīrabhadra before him, O best of sages.
m.2.2.42.23: When he asked where the head was, the lordly Vīrabhadra said: I offered the head into the fire at that very moment, O Śaṅkara.
m.2.2.42.24: Hearing these words of Vīrabhadra, Lord Śaṅkara kindly commanded the gods accordingly, as he had said before.
m.2.2.42.25: Having carried out completely what the blessed Bhava had said, Viṣṇu and all the others, with me, then quickly restored Bhṛgu and the rest.
m.2.2.42.26: Then, by Śambhu's gracious command, they swiftly joined to the body of that Prajāpati the head of the goat that was the animal for the soma-pressing.
m.2.2.42.27: As the head was being joined, the Prajāpati, looked upon by Śambhu's gracious glance, at once regained his life and rose up as if from sleep.
m.2.2.42.28: Having risen, Dakṣa saw before him Śambhu, the treasure of compassion; with a delighted heart and a mind fully serene, he stood there in affection.
m.2.2.42.29: Formerly his soul had been sullied by great hatred of Hara; at the sight of Śiva he at once became spotless like the autumn moon.
m.2.2.42.30: Then, though he wished to praise Bhava, he could not, because of his overwhelming love and his agitation from longing, as he remembered his departed daughter.
m.2.2.42.31: Then Dakṣa, his heart serene and filled with shame, bowed down and praised Śiva, Śaṅkara, the benefactor of the worlds.
m.2.2.42.32: Dakṣa said: I bow to the god, giver of boons, most worthy of choice, the great Lord, treasure of knowledge, eternal. I bow to Hara, lord over the sovereigns of the gods, ever full of bliss, the sole kinsman of the world.
m.2.2.42.33: O Lord of the universe, I bow to you whose form is the universe, the ancient one, whose own essential form is Brahman. I bow to Śarva, the source of existence and being; to Śaṅkara, higher than the highest, I am bowed down.
m.2.2.42.34: O God of gods, O Mahādeva, show mercy; salutation to you. Forgive my offence today, O Śambhu, treasure of compassion.
m.2.2.42.35: Indeed, O Śaṅkara, you have bestowed grace under the guise of punishment. I am wicked and dull-witted, O God; I did not know your true nature.
m.2.2.42.36: Today I have known the truth: you are held to be above all, the great Lord, to be served by Viṣṇu, Brahmā and others, knowable through the Vedas.
m.2.2.42.37: You are the wish-fulfilling tree for the good and ever the wielder of the rod for the wicked; you are independent, the supreme Self, granting the boons desired by devotees.
m.2.2.42.38: You, the supreme Lord, first created from your mouth the twice-born, bearers of learning, austerity and vows, so that they might fully know the truth of the Self.
m.2.2.42.39: You protect them from all calamities as a herdsman protects his cattle; rod in hand against those wicked ones, you are the guardian of the bounds of right conduct.
m.2.2.42.40: The supreme Lord, though pierced by me with the arrows of harsh words, is the bestower of grace upon me and upon the gods whose hopes were utterly wretched.
m.2.2.42.41: Such are you, the Lord, O Śambhu, friend of the afflicted, higher than the highest; O you who are affectionate to your devotees, you are pleased by your own most worthy deed.
m.2.2.42.42: Brahmā said: Having thus praised the great lord Śaṅkara, who brings welfare to the worlds, the Prajāpati Dakṣa, humble in spirit, fell silent before the great Lord.
m.2.2.42.43: Then Viṣṇu, gladdened in heart, having bowed deeply with joined palms, praised the bull-bannered Śiva in a voice choked with tears.
m.2.2.42.44: Viṣṇu said: O Mahādeva, great lord, bestower of grace on the worlds, you are the supreme Brahman, the supreme Self, O friend of the afflicted, O treasury of compassion.
m.2.2.42.45: O Lord, you are all-pervading, acting by your own will, whose glory is to be known through the Vedas. By this you have shown grace, and we have been made well-doers.
m.2.2.42.46: This Dakṣa is my devotee; that the wicked one formerly reviled you—that should be forgiven, O great lord, today, since you are free from all change.
m.2.2.42.47: I too committed an offence against you, O Śaṅkara, out of folly, in that I fought with your attendant Vīrabhadra by taking Dakṣa's side.
m.2.2.42.48: You are my master, the supreme Brahman; I am your servant, O Sadāśiva, and ever to be sustained by you, for you are the father of all.
m.2.2.42.49: Brahmā said: O God of gods, Mahādeva, ocean of compassion, Lord, you are independent, the supreme Self, the supreme lord, without a second, imperishable.
m.2.2.42.50: O God, O Īśvara, you have shown grace to my son. Disregarding the insult to yourself, restore Dakṣa's sacrifice.
m.2.2.42.51: Be gracious, O lord of the gods, and remove all curses. You, with knowledge, are my inspirer, and you alone are the one who restrains.
m.2.2.42.52: Having thus praised the supreme great lord, O great sage, I stood with palms joined in a cup and head bowed low.
m.2.2.42.53: Then the gods headed by Śakra, the guardians of the worlds, pure-minded, praised the god Śaṅkara, whose lotus face was gracious.
m.2.2.42.54: Then all the gods, glad at heart, and others as well—the Siddhas, the sages and the Prajāpatis—joyfully praised Śaṅkara.
m.2.2.42.55: Likewise the demigods and Nāgas, the members of the assembly and the brāhmaṇas, bowing with supreme devotion, praised him each separately.
m.2.2.42.iti: Thus ends the forty-second adhyāya, named The description of the removal of Dakṣa's suffering, in the second khaṇḍa, the Satī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.2.43.1: Brahmā said: Thus praised by Viṣṇu, the lord of Ramā, by me, by the divine sages, and likewise by others, Mahādeva became gracious.
m.2.2.43.2: Then Śambhu, having reassured with his compassionate glance all the sages, gods and others, as well as Brahmā and Viṣṇu, spoke this to Dakṣa.
m.2.2.43.3: Mahādeva said: Listen, Dakṣa, I shall speak; I am pleased, O Prajāpati. Though independent and lord of all, I am always subject to my devotees.
m.2.2.43.4: Four kinds of virtuous people always worship me, O Dakṣa, O Prajāpati; among them each succeeding one is superior to the one before.
m.2.2.43.5: The distressed, the seeker of knowledge, the seeker of wealth, and the knower as the fourth: the first three are ordinary, but the fourth is distinguished.
m.2.2.43.6: Of them the knower is dearest to me and is considered my very form. None is dearer than him; truly, truly I say this.
m.2.2.43.7: I, the knower of the Self, am to be reached through knowledge by those who have mastered the Vedānta scriptures; yet the dull-witted strive to attain me without knowledge.
m.2.2.43.8: Not by the Vedas, nor by sacrifices, nor by gifts, nor ever by austerity are deluded men bound by ritual action able to attain me.
m.2.2.43.9: You wished to cross worldly existence by ritual action alone; for that very reason I became angry and caused the destruction of the sacrifice.
m.2.2.43.10: From now on, O Dakṣa, regarding me as the supreme Lord, become devoted to knowledge through understanding and perform your actions with a collected mind.
m.2.2.43.11: Hear also another word of mine with a good mind, O Prajāpati: for the sake of dharma I tell you a secret, even about my aspect with attributes.
m.2.2.43.12: I, Brahmā and Viṣṇu are the supreme cause of the world; I am the Self, the Lord, the witness, self-seeing and without distinguishing attributes.
m.2.2.43.13: Entering my own Māyā, which consists of the guṇas, O sage, I, that very one, creating, protecting and withdrawing the universe, bear names suited to those functions.
m.2.2.43.14: In that supreme, non-dual, sole Brahman, the Self, the ignorant one sees beings, Brahmā and the Lord as separate.
m.2.2.43.15: Just as a person never thinks of his own limbs such as head and hands as belonging to another, so one devoted to me never regards beings as other.
m.2.2.43.16: He who sees no difference among the three gods, who are of one essence and are the selves of all beings, O Dakṣa, attains peace.
m.2.2.43.17: The vilest of men who conceives of difference among the three gods will surely dwell in hell as long as the moon and stars endure.
m.2.2.43.18: The discerning person devoted to me should worship all the gods too; he obtains the knowledge by which liberation becomes everlasting.
m.2.2.43.19: Without devotion to Brahmā, devotion to Viṣṇu does not arise at all; and without devotion to Viṣṇu, devotion to me never arises anywhere.
m.2.2.43.20: Having said this, Śaṅkara, the master and supreme Lord of all, the abode of compassion, spoke these words there while everyone listened.
m.2.2.43.21: If a devotee of Hari should revile me, or likewise a Śaiva should revile Hari, those curses would fall on both of them, and they would never attain the truth.
m.2.2.43.22: Brahmā said: Hearing these delightful words of Maheśa, all the gods, sages and others there rejoiced, O sage.
m.2.2.43.23: Then Dakṣa with his family, in great joy, became devoted to Śiva; and the gods and others, too, regarded Śiva as the lord of all.
m.2.2.43.24: In whatever way each one had praised Śambhu, the supreme Self, in that way Śambhu, pleased at heart, granted him a boon.
m.2.2.43.25: Permitted quickly by Śiva, Dakṣa, now a devotee of Śiva and serene in mind, completed the sacrifice through Śiva's grace, O sage.
m.2.2.43.26: He gave the gods their shares and the full share to Śiva; he also gave gifts to the brāhmaṇas, and Śambhu's grace was obtained.
m.2.2.43.27: Then Dakṣa the Prajāpati, together with the officiating priests, duly completed that very great rite for the god, performed according to the injunctions.
m.2.2.43.28: Thus Dakṣa's sacrifice was completed there, O lord of sages, through the grace of Śaṅkara, whose form is the supreme Brahman.
m.2.2.43.29: Then all the gods and sages, extolling Śaṅkara's glory, went contentedly to their own abodes, and the others too went happily.
m.2.2.43.30: Viṣṇu and I too, greatly pleased, went joyfully each to our own supreme abode, ever singing the fair glory of Śambhu, which bestows every auspiciousness.
m.2.2.43.31: Mahādeva too, the refuge of the good, honoured lovingly by Dakṣa, went, well pleased, with his gaṇas to his own mountain Kailāsa.
m.2.2.43.32: Having reached his own mountain, Śambhu remembered his beloved Satī and told her story to the gaṇas, especially the chief ones.
m.2.2.43.33: The all-knowing Lord passed much time recounting her deeds, adopting the way of the world and displaying the state of a lover.
m.2.2.43.34: The master, who never acts improperly, is the supreme Brahman, the goal of the good; where, then, is delusion for him, or grief, or any other change, O sage?
m.2.2.43.35: Viṣṇu and I never know his secret; what then of other sages, gods, humans and yogins?
m.2.2.43.36: Śaṅkara's greatness is infinite and hard for the wise to comprehend; it is known to devotees through true devotion, by his grace, without toil.
m.2.2.43.37: Śiva, the supreme Self, has not even a single change; he shows such a condition to the worlds by assuming it.
m.2.2.43.38: By reading and hearing this, O sage, any wise person among all people attains a divine, blessed destiny and supreme happiness even here.
m.2.2.43.39: Thus Satī, the daughter of Dakṣa, having given up her body, was born again of Menā, the wife of Himavat; so it is well known.
m.2.2.43.40: Performing austerities there once more, she chose Śiva as her husband; becoming Gaurī, the left half of his body, Śivā performed wondrous sports.
m.2.2.43.41: Thus the supremely wondrous story of Satī has been described to you — divine, bestowing worldly enjoyment and liberation, and granting all desires.
m.2.2.43.42: This narrative is sinless, pure, supremely purifying; it leads to heaven, brings fame and long life, and yields the fruit of sons and grandsons.
m.2.2.43.43: Whoever listens to this with devotion, or, being devoted, makes other people hear it, O dear one, attains the fruit of all rites and reaches the supreme state in the next world.
m.2.2.43.44: Whoever reads this auspicious narrative, or has it read, he too, having enjoyed all pleasures, would attain liberation at the end.
m.2.2.43.iti: Thus ends the forty-third adhyāya, named The description of the setting in order of Dakṣa's sacrifice, in the second khaṇḍa, the Satī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.3.1.1: Nārada said: O Brahmā, how did the goddess Satī, daughter of Dakṣa, who gave up her body at her father's sacrifice, become the daughter of the mountain, the Mother of the world?
m.2.3.1.2: And how, having performed extremely fierce austerity, did she obtain Śiva as her husband? Tell me, who am asking, this properly and in detail.
m.2.3.1.3: Brahmā said: Listen, O tiger among sages, to the excellent story of Śiva, purifying, supreme, divine, auspicious, and removing all sins.
m.2.3.1.4: When the goddess Dākṣāyaṇī, the supreme Goddess, joyfully sported playfully with Hara on the Himālaya,
m.2.3.1.5: Menā, the beloved of Himācala, full of all prosperity, thinking, this is my daughter, served her with a mother's affection.
m.2.3.1.6: When Dākṣāyaṇī, the supreme Goddess, having gone to that sacrifice and been disrespected by her father Dakṣa, became angry and abandoned her own body,
m.2.3.1.7: then indeed, O sage, that Menakā, the beloved of Himācala, desired to propitiate that goddess dwelling in Śiva's world.
m.2.3.1.8: Satī, having resolved in her heart that she would be her daughter, after abandoning her body set her mind on becoming the daughter of Himavat.
m.2.3.1.9: When the time came, that goddess Satī, praised by all the gods, who had abandoned her body, lovingly became again the daughter of Menakā.
m.2.3.1.10: That goddess, by name Pārvatī, having performed most unbearable austerity on the instruction of Nārada, again obtained Śiva as her husband.
m.2.3.1.11: Nārada said: O Brahmā, O Creator, O greatly wise one, best of speakers, tell me of Menakā's origin and likewise the story of her marriage.
m.2.3.1.12: Blessed indeed is the goddess Menakā, in whom Satī was born as daughter; therefore that faithful wife is honoured and blessed by all.
m.2.3.1.13: Brahmā said: Listen, O sage Nārada, to the origin of Pārvatī's mother, and to her marriage and story, which purify and increase devotion.
m.2.3.1.14: In the northern direction, O best of sages, there is the great lord of mountains, Himavat, a mountain of great splendour, possessed of prosperity.
m.2.3.1.15: His twofold form is well known, by the distinction of mobile and immobile. I shall describe briefly his subtle nature.
m.2.3.1.16: He stands having plunged into the eastern and western oceans, a delightful mine of various gems, like a measuring rod of the earth.
m.2.3.1.17: Covered with various trees, beautifully adorned with many peaks, always frequented by happy animals such as lions and tigers,
m.2.3.1.18: a store of snow, very formidable, variegated with many wonders, resorted to by gods, seers, Siddhas and sages, very dear to Śiva,
m.2.3.1.19: a place of austerity, very pure in nature, purifying for the great-souled, greatly bestowing success in austerity, an auspicious mine of various minerals.
m.2.3.1.20: He indeed has a divine form, delightful, beautiful in every limb, a portion of Viṣṇu, unchanging, king of the kings of mountains, dear to the good.
m.2.3.1.21: That mountain, for the continuance of his lineage and for the increase of dharma, wished to marry, desiring the welfare of the ancestors and gods.
m.2.3.1.22: At that time, O lord of sages, the gods, having fully considered their own interest, approached the divine Pitṛs and lovingly spoke.
m.2.3.1.23: The gods said: All of you Pitṛs, with pleased minds, listen to our words; if you desire the gods' task, it must be done quickly just so.
m.2.3.1.24: Your eldest daughter named Menā, of auspicious form — marry her with great affection to the mountain named Hima.
m.2.3.1.25: Thus there will be great gain in every way for all, for you and for the immortals, and removal of sorrow at every step.
m.2.3.1.26: Brahmā said: Having heard these words of the immortals, the Pitṛs reflected, and remembering the curse on their daughters, said Om (yes) to those words.
m.2.3.1.27: They gave their own daughter Menā with proper rites to the mountain Hima; there was a great festival at that most auspicious wedding.
m.2.3.1.28: Those gods headed by Hari, and all the other sages too, came there, remembering in their minds Bhava, Vāmadeva.
m.2.3.1.29: They had the festival celebrated, giving gifts in many ways; having highly praised the divine Pitṛs, they praised Himācala.
m.2.3.1.30: All those gods, together with the lords of sages, filled with great joy, went to their respective abodes, remembering Śiva and Śivā.
m.2.3.1.31: Having received abundant dowry and duly married his beloved, the lord of mountains came to his own home and rejoiced.
m.2.3.1.32: Brahmā said: O lord of sages, I have lovingly told you of the happy marriage of the mountain Hima with Menā, which gives joy. What more do you wish to hear?
m.2.3.1.iti: Thus ends the first adhyāya, named The description of the marriage of Himācala, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.3.2.1: Nārada said: O Vidhi (Brahmā), O wise one, now tell me with due care of the origin of Menā. Relate the curse as well, and dispel my doubt.
m.2.3.2.2: Brahmā said: Listen, Nārada, with great delight, to the origin of Menā, told with discernment. I shall tell it as discussed together with the sages, O best of sons, O greatly wise one.
m.2.3.2.3: My son named Dakṣa, who was spoken of earlier, O sage — to him were born daughters numbering sixty, the causes of creation.
m.2.3.2.4: He married them to excellent husbands such as Kaśyapa. All that is known to you; now hear what is relevant, Nārada.
m.2.3.2.5: Among them, he gave the daughter named Svadhā to the Pitṛs. To her were born three daughters, fortunate, embodiments of dharma.
m.2.3.2.6: Hear from me their purifying names, O lord of sages, which always remove obstacles and bestow great auspiciousness.
m.2.3.2.7: The eldest daughter was named Menā, the middle one Dhanyā, and the last Kalāvatī. All these daughters were mind-born of the Pitṛs.
m.2.3.2.8: They were not born from a womb; by common usage they are regarded as daughters of Svadhā. By uttering their auspicious names a person would obtain all desires.
m.2.3.2.9: They are worthy of the world's worship, ever mothers of the worlds, givers of supreme joy, supreme yoginīs, treasuries of knowledge, moving through the three worlds.
m.2.3.2.10: Once, O lord of sages, those three sisters went to Śvetadvīpa, the world of Viṣṇu, for the sake of seeing him.
m.2.3.2.11: Full of devotion, having bowed to Viṣṇu and praised him, they stayed there by his command. A great assembly had gathered there.
m.2.3.2.12: At that very time, O sage, the Siddhas Sanaka and the others, sons of Brahmā, went there; having bowed to Hari and praised him, they stayed by his command.
m.2.3.2.13: Seeing the sages Sanaka and the others, all those present quickly rose; and the sages bowed to those stationed there, the gods and others revered by the worlds.
m.2.3.2.14: But those three sisters did not rise there, O sage, deluded by the Māyā of Śaṅkara, the Supreme Self, helpless under fate.
m.2.3.2.15: Śiva's Māyā is mightiest, the deluder of all worlds. The whole universe depends on it; it is proclaimed as Śiva's will.
m.2.3.2.16: That same is called prārabdha (destiny already set in motion); it has many names. Everything happens by Śiva's will alone; there should be no deliberation on this.
m.2.3.2.17: Having come under its sway, they did not even bow to them; amazed, merely gazing, they just remained seated there.
m.2.3.2.18: Seeing their conduct thus, the lords of sages Sanaka and the others, though men of wisdom, became exceedingly and unbearably angry.
m.2.3.2.19: There, deluded by Śiva's will, the lord of yogins Sanatkumāra, full of anger, spoke to them, giving a punishing curse.
m.2.3.2.20: Sanatkumāra said: You three sisters are foolish, devoid of true understanding, ignorant of the essence of the Vedas, even though you are surely daughters of the Pitṛs.
m.2.3.2.21: Proud ones, you did not rise to greet us, nor even offer salutation. Deluded by this human-like disposition, may you be removed far from heaven.
m.2.3.2.22: May all three of you, deluded by ignorance, be born as human women. By the power of your own deed, receive such a fruit.
m.2.3.2.23: Brahmā said: Hearing this, those three virtuous women, greatly alarmed, fell at his feet and spoke with bowed heads.
m.2.3.2.24: The daughters of the Pitṛs said: O best of sages, ocean of compassion, be gracious now. We, deluded, did not make obeisance to you with true feeling.
m.2.3.2.25: We have received its fruit, O brahmin; the fault is not yours, great sage. Show us favour in this, so that we may regain our heavenly state.
m.2.3.2.26: Brahmā said: Hearing their words, dear son, the sage, now pleased at heart and prompted by Śiva's Māyā, then declared the release from the curse.
m.2.3.2.27: Sanatkumāra said: O three daughters of the Pitṛs, listen with glad hearts to my words, which destroy grief and always bring you happiness.
m.2.3.2.28: Let the eldest become the beloved wife of the mountain Himālaya, a portion of Viṣṇu; her daughter will be Pārvatī.
m.2.3.2.29: The second, Dhanyā, will be the yoginī wife of Janaka; her daughter, Mahālakṣmī, will be known by the name Sītā.
m.2.3.2.30: The youngest, Kalāvatī, will be the wife of the vaiśya Vṛṣabhāna; her daughter will be Rādhā, at the end of the Dvāpara age.
m.2.3.2.31: The yoginī Menakā, together with her husband and by the boon of Pārvatī, will go in that very body to Kailāsa, the supreme abode.
m.2.3.2.32: And Dhanyā, with Sītā, and Sīradhvaja of Janaka's line, liberated while living, a great yogin, will go to Vaikuṇṭha.
m.2.3.2.33: Kalāvatī, wife of Vṛṣabhāna, liberated while living, will joyfully go with her daughter to Goloka; there is no doubt.
m.2.3.2.34: Without adversity, whose greatness will arise, and where? When the sorrow of the virtuous has passed, rare happiness may arise.
m.2.3.2.35: You are all daughters of the Pitṛs, delighting in heaven; and by the sight of Viṣṇu your karma has been exhausted.
m.2.3.2.36: Having said this, the lord of sages, his anger gone, spoke again, remembering in his mind Śiva, the giver of knowledge, of enjoyment and liberation.
m.2.3.2.37: Hear lovingly further words of mine, ever bringing happiness. You are blessed, dear to Śiva, to be honoured and worshipped constantly.
m.2.3.2.38: Menā's daughter, the goddess Pārvatī, Mother of the universe, having performed extremely arduous austerity, will become the beloved of Śambhu.
m.2.3.2.39: Dhanyā's daughter, known as Sītā, will be Rāma's wife; adopting worldly conduct, she will sport with Rāma.
m.2.3.2.40: Kalāvatī's daughter Rādhā, herself a dweller of Goloka, bound by secret love, will be Kṛṣṇa's wife.
m.2.3.2.41: Brahmā said: Having spoken thus, the venerable sage Sanatkumāra, praised by them together with his brothers, vanished right there.
m.2.3.2.42: Those three sisters, dear one, the mind-born daughters of the Pitṛs, freed of sin and having obtained happiness, quickly went to their own abode.
m.2.3.2.iti: Thus ends the second adhyāya, named The description of the former history, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.3.3.1: Nārada said: O Vidhi (Brahmā), wise one of great intellect, best of speakers, tell me: what happened after that? Tell me the deeds of Śiva, the true guru of Viṣṇu.
m.2.3.3.2: This wondrous and auspicious story of Menā's earlier life has been told, and the marriage too has been fully heard. Now tell the supreme story that follows.
m.2.3.3.3: Having married Menā, what did that mountain do after that? How was Pārvatī, the Mother of the world, born of her?
m.2.3.3.4: Having performed a most unbearable austerity, how did she obtain Hara as husband? Relate all this, the glory of Śaṅkara, in detail.
m.2.3.3.5: Brahmā said: O sage, listen with great delight to the auspicious, excellent glory of Śaṅkara, by hearing which even a slayer of a brāhmaṇa is purified and obtains all his desires.
m.2.3.3.6: When the mountain, having celebrated the marriage with Menā, went home, then a great festival arose in the three worlds, O Nārada.
m.2.3.3.7: Himācala too, greatly delighted, held a supreme festival. With a good mind he honoured the brāhmaṇas, his kinsfolk, and others.
m.2.3.3.8: All the twice-born, satisfied, gave him excellent words of blessing and went to their own abodes; so too did the kinsfolk and the others.
m.2.3.3.9: Himācala too, much delighted, sported with Menā in his pleasant home, and elsewhere in fine places, even in Nandana and other groves.
m.2.3.3.10: At that time, O sage, all the gods headed by Viṣṇu, and the great-souled sages, came to the mountain's presence.
m.2.3.3.11: Seeing those gods arrive, the mountain bowed joyfully; the great one honoured them with devotion, praising his own good fortune.
m.2.3.3.12: With joined palms and bowed head he praised them with deep devotion. A great thrill arose on the mountain's body, and tears of love fell.
m.2.3.3.13: Then, having bowed, the Snow Mountain, delighted and serene of mind, humbly prostrate, spoke, O sage, to the gods headed by Viṣṇu.
m.2.3.3.14: Himavān said: Today my birth is fruitful, fruitful my very great austerity; today my knowledge is fruitful, today my rites are fruitful.
m.2.3.3.15: Today I have become blessed; blessed is my whole land; blessed my lineage and my wife; everything is blessed, without doubt.
m.2.3.3.16: since you have all come together at once. Regarding me as your own servant, kindly command me as is fitting.
m.2.3.3.17: Brahmā said: Having heard these words of the mountain, the gods headed by Hari were then pleased, considering their own purpose accomplished, and spoke.
m.2.3.3.18: The gods said: O Himācala, of great wisdom, hear our beneficial words. We shall gladly tell you why we have all come.
m.2.3.3.19: O mountain, Umā, the Mother of the world, who formerly was born as Dakṣa's daughter, became Rudra's wife and sported on earth for a very long time.
m.2.3.3.20: Receiving disrespect from her father, Satī, remembering her own vow, abandoned that body and then Ambikā went to her own abode.
m.2.3.3.21: That story is known in the world, and to you also, O Snow Mountain. If it comes about thus, that she is born to you, there would indeed be great gain for the host of gods,
m.2.3.3.22: for all, and for you as well; all those gods would be under your sway.
m.2.3.3.23: Brahmā said: Hearing these words of Hari and the others, the lord of mountains, pleased at heart, said with respect, so be it.
m.2.3.3.24: Then, having instructed him with great respect in the procedure for it, they themselves went for refuge to Umā, Śaṅkara's consort.
m.2.3.3.25: Staying in a pleasant place, the gods remembered the Mother of the world in their minds; bowing there many times, they praised her with faith.
m.2.3.3.26: The gods said: O Goddess Umā, Mother of the worlds, dweller in Śivaloka, beloved of Sadāśiva, O Durgā, O Maheśvarī, we bow to you.
m.2.3.3.27: With devotion we bow to you, the glorious Power, purifying, peaceful, nourishment itself, supremely purifying, whose form is the Great (mahat) and the Unmanifest.
m.2.3.3.28: We bow to you, Śivā, maker of auspiciousness, pure, gross and subtle, the supreme refuge, well pleased by inner knowledge and true knowledge.
m.2.3.3.29: You are faith, you are steadfastness, you are prosperity (śrī); you alone pervade all things. You are the radiance residing in the sun, illuminating your own manifest world.
m.2.3.3.30: She who abides in the structure of the cosmic egg and in the living beings of the world, she who nourishes the world from Brahmā down to a blade of grass — to her we bow.
m.2.3.3.31: You are Gāyatrī, the Mother of the Vedas; you are Sāvitrī and Sarasvatī; you are the livelihood (vārtā) of all the worlds; you are the threefold Veda, embodying dharma.
m.2.3.3.32: You are sleep in all beings, you alone are hunger and satisfaction; thirst, loveliness, lustre, contentment — ever the giver of all joy.
m.2.3.3.33: You are Lakṣmī for the doers of merit, you are ever Jyeṣṭhā (misfortune) for the sinful; you are peace for all the worlds, you are the nurse who sustains life.
m.2.3.3.34: You are the essential nature of the five elements, and the one who makes their essence; you are the policy of those who uphold policy, embodying resolute effort.
m.2.3.3.35: You are the chant of the Sāmaveda, the binding knot and oblation of the Yajus formulas, likewise the metre (mātrā) of the Ṛgveda, and the supreme goal of the Atharvaveda.
m.2.3.3.36: She who is the power of the entire host of gods, consisting of tamas, visible only through the qualities of the Creator, and through the expansion of rajas having the single form of existence — she, heard of by us as the bringer of welfare, is praised here.
m.2.3.3.37: We bow indeed to her who is the boat that carries one across the sorrows of embodied existence in the terrible ocean of saṃsāra, who is without the sacred thread, who is skilled in the sport of upholding eight-limbed yoga, and who delights in dwelling on the Vindhya mountain.
m.2.3.3.38: She who, by sustaining them, ever spreads comforts in the nose, eyes, mouth, arms, chest and mind of a creature, who, the gracious one, goes by the name of Sleep for the beings of the world — may she be gracious to us for the preservation of the world's continuance.
m.2.3.3.39: Brahmā said: Having thus praised Maheśānī, Umā the Mother of the world, Satī, all of them, their minds full of love, stood waiting, eager for her vision.
m.2.3.3.iti: Thus ends the third adhyāya, named The praise by the gods, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.3.4.1: Brahmā said: Thus praised by the gods, the Goddess Durgā, destroyer of the distress of hardships, the Mother of the world, appeared before the gods.
m.2.3.4.2: She was seated in a divine chariot made of jewels, supremely wondrous, fitted with networks of little bells, excellent, with a soft cushioned seat.
m.2.3.4.3: She shone with lovely limbs whose radiance surpassed that of ten million suns; she stood in the midst of a mass of her own splendour, of excellent form and of unequalled beauty.
m.2.3.4.4: She is incomparable, the Great Māyā, the consort who sports with Sadāśiva, possessed of the three guṇas yet beyond the guṇas, eternal, dwelling in Śivaloka.
m.2.3.4.5: She is the mother of the three gods, Caṇḍī, Śivā, destroyer of all distress, mother of all, the Great Sleep, the deliverer of all her own people.
m.2.3.4.6: But owing to the power of that mass of radiance, Śivā was scarcely seen by the gods; so those gods, longing for a sight of her, praised her again.
m.2.3.4.7: Then all the hosts of gods, headed by Viṣṇu, desirous of seeing her, having obtained her grace there, beheld that Mother of the world.
m.2.3.4.8: A flood of bliss arose for all the dwellers of heaven; again and again they bowed to her and praised her in particular.
m.2.3.4.9: The gods said: O Śivā, O Śarvāṇī, O auspicious one, O Mother of the world, O Maheśvarī, we gods bow to you in every way, you who destroy all distress.
m.2.3.4.10: O Mistress of the gods, the Vedas and the śāstras do not know you completely; your greatness and the meditation on you lie beyond speech and mind, O Śivā.
m.2.3.4.11: Even the Śruti, ever filled with awe, speaks of you only by excluding what you are not; what then to say of others?
m.2.3.4.12: Many devotees know you, having obtained your grace through devotion; for devotees who have taken refuge in you there is no fear or the like anywhere.
m.2.3.4.13: O Ambikā, being well pleased, hear the petition of those who are ever your servants; O Devī, O Mahādevī, we set it forth humbly.
m.2.3.4.14: Formerly, having become Dakṣa's daughter, you were born as the beloved of Hara, and you removed the great affliction of Brahmā and of others.
m.2.3.4.15: Having met with disrespect from your father, you gave up your body because of a vow and went to your own world; and Hara too suffered sorrow.
m.2.3.4.16: That task of the gods has not been fully accomplished, O Maheśvarī; distressed, we sages and gods have come to you for refuge.
m.2.3.4.17: O Maheśānī, fulfil the desire of the immortals, so that the word of Sanatkumāra may bear fruit, O Śivā.
m.2.3.4.18: Descending to the earth, O Devī, become Rudra's wife again; perform your sport as befits, so that the immortals may attain happiness.
m.2.3.4.19: May Rudra too, dwelling on Mount Kailāsa, be happy, O Devī; may all be happy; may sorrow perish completely.
m.2.3.4.20: Brahmā said: Having spoken thus, all the immortals headed by Viṣṇu, overflowing with love, fell silent and stood with their bodies bowed in devotion.
m.2.3.4.21: Śivā too became very pleased on hearing the praise of the immortals; then, considering its purpose and remembering her own lord Śiva,
m.2.3.4.22: the Goddess Umā, compassionate and loving to her devotees, then smiled and, addressing those gods headed by Viṣṇu, spoke.
m.2.3.4.23: Umā said: O Hari, O Vidhi, O gods and sages, be free of distress. All of you, listen to my words: I am pleased, there is no doubt.
m.2.3.4.24: My deeds everywhere bring happiness to the three worlds; all that — the delusion of Dakṣa and the rest — was done by me in this way.
m.2.3.4.25: I shall take a full incarnation on earth, there is no doubt. There are many reasons for this too; I shall tell them with great regard.
m.2.3.4.26: Formerly, O gods, Himācala and Menā, with very great devotion, served me, then in the body of Satī, like a father and mother.
m.2.3.4.27: Now too they serve me constantly with deep devotion — Menā especially, wishing me to be her daughter; there is no doubt of this.
m.2.3.4.28: Let Rudra go there, and you too take incarnation in Himavat's house; therefore I too shall descend, and there will be an end of sorrow.
m.2.3.4.29: All of you, go to your own abodes and enjoy happiness for long. Descending and becoming Menā's daughter, I shall bestow great happiness.
m.2.3.4.30: I shall become Hara's wife — this is my own closely guarded intention. For Śiva's sport is wondrous, deluding even the wise.
m.2.3.4.31: O gods, from the time when I, Dakṣa's daughter, having gone to his sacrifice and seen the disrespect shown by my father to my lord, abandoned my own body,
m.2.3.4.32: from then on that lord Rudra, called Kālāgni, quickly became sky-clad, wholly absorbed in thinking of me.
m.2.3.4.33: Reflecting thus: Seeing my anger at the sacrifice, Satī, who had gone there to her father's, gave up her body out of love, being a knower of dharma,
m.2.3.4.34: Maheśvara abandoned his fitting abode and assumed an unworldly guise; he could not bear separation from Satī, who was of my form.
m.2.3.4.35: On my account he became greatly grieved, wearing a wretched guise; from then on he renounced the highest pleasure born of desire.
m.2.3.4.36: Hear something more, O Viṣṇu, O Vidhi, O sages and gods: the sport of the great lord Maheśa, which protects the worlds.
m.2.3.4.37: Making a garland of my bones with great love, distraught by separation, he found peace nowhere; though awakened, he remained alone.
m.2.3.4.38: That lord wept aloud here and there as though helpless; wandering everywhere at all times, he did not discern the proper from the improper.
m.2.3.4.39: Thus the lord Hara performed his sport, showing the state of lovers; he spoke words like a lover, as if distraught by separation.
m.2.3.4.40: In reality the Supreme Lord is unchanging, never dejected, unconquered; Śiva the master is perfectly complete, the ruler of Māyā, the lord of all.
m.2.3.4.41: Otherwise, what purpose would he have with delusion, or with desire? That Lord is not quickly tainted by Māyā through any modification of mind whatsoever.
m.2.3.4.42: Rudra, the all-pervading one, greatly desires to take my hand in marriage. Therefore, O gods, I shall take an incarnation on earth, in the house of Menā and Himācala.
m.2.3.4.43: And therefore I shall descend, for the sake of pleasing Rudra, in Menā, the wife of the Himālaya mountain, adopting the worldly course of birth.
m.2.3.4.44: Becoming a devotee dear to Rudra and performing extremely hard austerity, I shall accomplish the task of the gods — truly, truly, there is no doubt.
m.2.3.4.45: Go, all of you, to your own homes and worship Bhava constantly. By his grace all sorrow perishes; there is no doubt.
m.2.3.4.46: By the grace of the compassionate one there will always be auspiciousness. And because I am his wife, I shall be worthy of salutation and worship in the three worlds.
m.2.3.4.47: Brahmā said: Having said this, that Mother of the world, Śivā, vanished then while the gods looked on, O dear one, and quickly reached her own world.
m.2.3.4.48: All the gods headed by Viṣṇu, and the sages, filled with joy, bowed in that direction and went to their respective abodes.
m.2.3.4.49: Thus the noble story of Durgā has been described to you, O lord of sages; it always gives happiness to men and bestows both enjoyment and liberation.
m.2.3.4.50: Whoever, with a concentrated mind, constantly listens to this or makes others listen, or reads it or has it read, would obtain all his desires.
m.2.3.4.iti: Thus ends the fourth adhyāya, named The consoling of the gods, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.3.5.1: Nārada said: When the goddess Durgā had vanished and the hosts of immortals had gone to their own homes, what happened after that?
m.2.3.5.2: How did Menā and the lord of mountains perform supreme austerity? And how was a daughter born to him in Menā? Tell me that, dear father.
m.2.3.5.3: Brahmā said: O best of brahmins, best of sons, listen to that great story. Having bowed to Śaṅkara with devotion, I shall narrate it, which increases devotion.
m.2.3.5.4: Dear son, when the host of gods headed by Hari had departed after giving instruction, the lord of mountains and Menakā too performed supreme austerity.
m.2.3.5.5: Meditating day and night on Śivā and Śambhu, the couple worshipped them properly and constantly with a mind filled with devotion.
m.2.3.5.6: She, the mountain's beloved, with great joy worshipped the goddess together with Śiva, and always gave gifts to brahmins for the sake of pleasing her.
m.2.3.5.7: Beginning in the month of Caitra, for twenty-seven years, desiring offspring, she devotedly worshipped Śivā every day.
m.2.3.5.8: Having fasted on the eighth lunar day, she made offerings on the ninth with sweet balls, rice-flour cakes for oblation, milk-rice, fragrances and flowers.
m.2.3.5.9: At the Gaṅgā in Oṣadhiprastha she made an earthen image of Umā and worshipped it with offerings of various articles.
m.2.3.5.10: Sometimes she went without food, sometimes she kept vows, sometimes she lived on air, sometimes she subsisted on water.
m.2.3.5.11: With her mind fixed on Śivā, Menakā, radiant with pure splendour, lovingly passed twenty-seven years.
m.2.3.5.12: At the end of twenty-seven years, Umā, the mother of the world, who pervades the world, beloved of Śaṅkara, became exceedingly pleased.
m.2.3.5.13: To show favour to Menā, that supreme goddess, delighted by her deep devotion, appeared before her.
m.2.3.5.14: Endowed with divine limbs, standing in the midst of a halo of light, she, having become visible, smilingly spoke to Menā.
m.2.3.5.15: The Goddess said: Ask for a boon, O great virtuous lady, whatever is in your mind. I am well pleased with your austerity, O beloved of the mountain.
m.2.3.5.16: Whatever you have prayed for, Menā, through austerity, vows and meditation, all that you desire, whenever it may be, I shall give you.
m.2.3.5.17: Then Menakā, seeing the goddess Kālikā visibly present, bowed down and spoke these words.
m.2.3.5.18: Menā said: O goddess, now I have seen your form directly. I wish to praise you; be pleased, O Kālikā.
m.2.3.5.19: Brahmā said: Then Kālikā, who enchants all, thus addressed by Menā, with a delighted heart embraced Menakā with both arms.
m.2.3.5.20: Then Menakā, having attained great knowledge, devotedly praised with pleasing words the auspicious Kālikā who had become visible.
m.2.3.5.21: Menā said: I bow to the great Māyā, the sustainer of the world, Caṇḍikā, upholder of the worlds, the great goddess who grants all desires and aims.
m.2.3.5.22: I always bow to her who causes eternal bliss, Māyā, Yoganidrā, mother of the world, the perfected one, garlanded with auspicious essence.
m.2.3.5.23: I bow to the grandmother, ever blissful, destroyer of devotees' grief, the adornment of women and the form of intelligence in living beings.
m.2.3.5.24: You are the cause of cutting the bonds of ascetics; how can your power be sung by women like me? You are the destructive power of the Atharvaveda; ever fulfil my cherished desire.
m.2.3.5.25: The group of elements is joined together by their respective subtle elements (tanmātras), eternal and non-eternal, devoid of states, transcendent. You are ever their power, of eternal form; in time you become a woman, endowed with yoga and all-capable.
m.2.3.5.26: You alone are the womb and supporter of the worlds; you alone are the eternal Prakṛti beyond; by whom even the form of Brahman is brought under control—you, the eternal one, be gracious to me today, O mother.
m.2.3.5.27: You are the fierce power residing in fire; you are the burning power of the sun's rays; you are the gladdening abundant moonlight—you, Caṇḍī, I praise and bow to.
m.2.3.5.28: You are the true beloved of women, and you are the eternal goal of celibates; you are the desire of all the worlds, and you are Māyā, as the Māyā of Hari.
m.2.3.5.29: The goddess who, assuming desired forms, is the maker consisting of creation, preservation and destruction, the cause of the bodies of Brahmā, Acyuta and Sthāṇu—you, be gracious today; again, salutation to you.
m.2.3.5.30: Brahmā said: Then, thus praised, Durgā Kālikā again said to the lady Menakā: Choose what you desire.
m.2.3.5.31: Umā said: You are as dear to me as my life, O delight of Himācala. Whatever you wish I shall surely give; there is nothing I cannot give.
m.2.3.5.32: Hearing these nectar-like words of Maheśānī, Menakā, the mountain's beloved, fully satisfied, spoke.
m.2.3.5.33: Menā said: O Śivā, victory, victory to you! O wise one, O Maheśvarī, O Bhavāmbikā, if I am worthy of a boon from you, I choose again an excellent boon.
m.2.3.5.34: First, O mother of the world, may I have a hundred sons, long-lived, valiant, endowed with prosperity and success.
m.2.3.5.35: Afterwards likewise one daughter, rich in beauty and virtues, bringing joy to both families, worshipped in the three worlds.
m.2.3.5.36: O Śivā, become my daughter for the sake of the gods' purpose; and become Rudra's wife, and so perform your divine play, O Bhavāmbikā.
m.2.3.5.37: Brahmā said: Hearing what Menakā said, the goddess, gracious-minded, spoke with a smile, fulfilling her wish.
m.2.3.5.38: The Goddess said: May a hundred valiant sons be born to you; among them one mighty chief will be born first.
m.2.3.5.39: Pleased by your devotion, I shall be born as your daughter; served by all the gods, I shall accomplish the gods' task.
m.2.3.5.40: Brahmā said: Having spoken thus, Kālikā, sustainer of the world, the supreme goddess Śivā, vanished right there while Menakā looked on.
m.2.3.5.41: Menakā too, having obtained from Maheśānī the boon she desired, attained boundless joy, O dear one, and the hardship of her austerity also vanished.
m.2.3.5.42: Bowing toward that direction, the virtuous lady, her mind greatly delighted, uttering the cry of victory, entered her own abode.
m.2.3.5.43: Then she told her husband of that excellent boon, in fine words repeated again, as though it were confirmed by its own signs.
m.2.3.5.44: Hearing that speech of Menā, the lord of mountains became delighted, and with affection he praised his beloved, who was devoted to devotion to Śivā.
m.2.3.5.45: Then, in the course of time, when their union had taken place, O sage, Menā conceived, and the embryo grew day by day.
m.2.3.5.46: She bore an excellent, wondrous son named Maināka, fit to be enjoyed by the nāga maidens, who formed a true friendship with the ocean.
m.2.3.5.47: He, who even when Vṛtra's foe Indra was enraged and cutting off the mountains' wings, O divine sage, remained winged and of excellent form, knowing the pain of those wounded by the thunderbolt.
m.2.3.5.48: He was the foremost of a hundred sons, of great strength and valour, the one alone established as lord of mountains among the mountains born of Himavat himself.
m.2.3.5.49: A wondrous great festival took place there in Himācala's city; the couple's joy overflowed and their hardships came to an end.
m.2.3.5.50: He gave gifts to the twice-born and bestowed wealth on others as well; the love of the two for the pair of feet of Śivā and Śiva grew greater.
m.2.3.5.iti: Thus ends the fifth adhyāya, named The description of Menā's obtaining a boon, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.3.6.1: Brahmā said: Then that couple, with devotion and reverence, called to mind Bhavāmbikā there, so that she might be born to them for the sake of accomplishing the gods' task.
m.2.3.6.2: Then that Caṇḍikā, who long ago had abandoned her body through yoga at the sacrifice of her father, wished by her own will to be born again from the mountain's wife.
m.2.3.6.3: To make her own word true, the gracious Maheśvarī, granter of all desires, then entered the mind of the mountain with her full portion.
m.2.3.6.4: Then he shone exceedingly, full of joy, with an unprecedented splendour, unassailable like fire, a mass of radiance, great-souled.
m.2.3.6.5: Then the mountain, by virtue of his concentrated meditation, at the proper time placed that complete portion of Śivā into his own most auspicious beloved.
m.2.3.6.6: Through the grace of the Goddess, the mine of compassion, who abode in his mind, the mountain's wife conceived an embryo that brought joy to the mountain.
m.2.3.6.7: Menā, the mountain's beloved, shone all the more brightly for being the refuge of her in whom all the worlds dwell, ever encircled by a halo of radiance.
m.2.3.6.8: And Menā bore the signs of pregnancy-craving, which gave rise to joy for her husband, the auspicious and longed-for cause of the gods' bliss.
m.2.3.6.9: Owing to the languor of her body she wore only some of her ornaments, and her face was pale as lodhra; she was like a night at the waning of the moon, of faint light, its few stars hard to make out.
m.2.3.6.10: O sage, the lord of mountains, smelling in private her face fragrant with the scent of earth, found no satiety; that became an excess of love.
m.2.3.6.11: For which things does Menā long? Out of shyness she tells me nothing she desires — so the mountain asked her friends again and again.
m.2.3.6.12: Whatever the mountain-queen, gripped by craving, asked for, she soon saw it brought; indeed nothing he desired was unattainable for him, even in heaven.
m.2.3.6.13: Her limbs growing fuller, having passed beyond the discomfort of craving, Menā shone like a young creeper abounding in freshly formed leaves.
m.2.3.6.14: The mountain regarded his pregnant queen as like the earth bearing treasure within, like the śamī tree with fire hidden inside.
m.2.3.6.15: The wise one performed the rites prescribed by scripture, befitting his love for his beloved, the loftiness of his mind, and his self-earned wealth.
m.2.3.6.16: In due time he, delighted, saw Menā about to give birth, in the birth-chamber attended by physicians, like the sky laden with clouds.
m.2.3.6.17: Seeing his beloved of auspicious limbs, who then bore in her womb the Mother of the World and was full of great radiance, the lord of mountains rejoiced greatly.
m.2.3.6.18: At that time, O sage, the gods, Viṣṇu and the others, and the sages assembled and praised Śivā, who was in the womb.
m.2.3.6.19: The gods said: O Durgā, victory, victory to you! O wise one, Mother of the World, Maheśvarī, O you of true vows, devoted to truth, threefold truth, embodiment of truth,
m.2.3.6.20: O you who abide in truth, who are well pleased by truth, source of truth, arisen from truth, whose mouth is truth and whose eye is truth — we have come to you for refuge.
m.2.3.6.21: O beloved of Śiva, Maheśānī, destroyer of the gods' sorrow, you are the Mother of the three worlds, Śarvāṇī, all-pervading, loving to your devotees.
m.2.3.6.22: Manifest yourself, O Ruler of the three worlds, and accomplish the gods' task; for by your grace, O Maheśvarī, all of us have a protector.
m.2.3.6.23: Through you all beings become happy and attain the highest happiness; without you nothing at all shines, even in the three worlds.
m.2.3.6.24: Brahmā said: Having thus offered abundant praise to Maheśānī abiding in the womb, the gods, glad at heart, then went each to his own abode.
m.2.3.6.25: When the ninth month had passed and the tenth month was complete, Kālikā, the Mother of the World, abiding in the womb, began to move toward birth.
