m.2.3.28.42: Assuming his charming form, exactly as she had meditated on Śiva, and showing it to Śivā, Śiva spoke to her as she stood with her face cast down.
m.2.3.28.43: Śiva said: Where will you go, leaving me? You shall never again be abandoned by me. I am pleased; ask for a boon. There is nothing that cannot be given to you.
m.2.3.28.44: From today on I am your servant, bought indeed by your austerities. I am bought by your beauty; a single moment apart from you is like an age.
m.2.3.28.45: Let shyness be cast off by you; you are my eternal wife. O Girijā, O Maheśvarī, consider this with sound understanding.
m.2.3.28.46: You have been tested by me in many ways, O firm-minded one. So forgive my offence, committed by me as one following the ways of worldly play.
m.2.3.28.47: Nowhere in the three worlds do I see a loving woman like you. In every way I am subject to you; let your desire be fulfilled, O Śivā.
m.2.3.28.48: Come near me, beloved; you are my wife and I am your bridegroom. With you I shall quickly go to my own home, the finest of mountains.
m.2.3.28.49: Brahmā said: When the god of gods had spoken thus, Pārvatī was filled with joy, and she cast off all the former hardship that had arisen from her austerity.
m.2.3.28.50: All the weariness of Satī vanished, O best of sages; for when the fruit has come, a creature's earlier toil comes to an end.
m.2.3.28.iti: Thus ends the twenty-eighth adhyāya, named Pārvatī's sight of the form of Śiva, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.3.29.1: Nārada said: O Brahmā, O Creator, O greatly fortunate one, what happened after that? I wish to hear all of it; narrate to me the glory of Śivā.
m.2.3.29.2: Brahmā said: O divine sage, listen well; I gladly narrate that story, which destroys great sins and increases devotion to Śiva.
m.2.3.29.3: Having heard the words of Hara, the Supreme Self, and having seen his bliss-giving form, Pārvatī rejoiced exceedingly, O brahmin.
m.2.3.29.4: The goddess Śivā, the great chaste lady, exceedingly happy, her face blossoming with love, replied to the Lord who stood near her.
m.2.3.29.5: Pārvatī said: You are my lord, O Lord of gods. What have you forgotten of the past—the destruction of Dakṣa's sacrifice, which you forcibly brought about for my sake?
m.2.3.29.6: You are that same one, and I, that same one, have been born of Menā to accomplish the task of the gods, O God of gods, who are afflicted by Tāraka.
m.2.3.29.7: If you are pleased, O Lord of gods, and if you show compassion, become my husband, O Īśāna; do as I ask, O Lord.
m.2.3.29.8: With your permission I shall duly go to my father's house; let that pure, supreme glory be made famous.
m.2.3.29.9: You should go, O lord, O master, to Himavat's side; then, becoming a mendicant, ask for me, you who are skilled in divine sport.
m.2.3.29.10: So should you act, proclaiming your glory in the worlds; in this way make my father's householder life wholly fruitful.
m.2.3.29.11: Lovingly instructed by the sages and surrounded by his kinsmen and retinue, my father will do as you ask; there is no doubt.
m.2.3.29.12: Formerly, when I, as Dakṣa's daughter, was given to you by my father, the marriage was not performed by you there according to the prescribed rite.
m.2.3.29.13: The planets were not worshipped by Dakṣa, my father; therefore this marriage became greatly flawed in respect of the planets.
m.2.3.29.14: Therefore, O Lord Mahādeva, you should perform the marriage with me according to the prescribed rite, for accomplishing the task of the gods.
m.2.3.29.15: As the custom of marriage is, so it must surely be carried out. Let Himavat fully know that his daughter has performed auspicious penance.
m.2.3.29.16: Brahmā said: Having heard these words, Sadāśiva, greatly pleased, spoke lovingly to Girijā, as if laughing.
m.2.3.29.17: Śiva said: Listen, O goddess, O Maheśānī, to my supreme words; do what is fitting, most auspicious and free from change.
m.2.3.29.18: The beings beginning with Brahmā are impermanent, O fair-faced one; know, O beautiful lady, that all this which is seen is perishable.
m.2.3.29.19: The One has become many; the attributeless has become endowed with attributes; he who shines by his own light has become endowed with another's light.
m.2.3.29.20: Independent as I am, I have been made dependent by you, O goddess; you alone are Prakṛti, the doer of all, Mahāmāyā.
m.2.3.29.21: This entire world, made of māyā, has been created and wholly sustained by your supreme intelligence; it is pervaded within the self by the virtuous, who are the selves of all and have the nature of the Supreme Self, and is enveloped by the guṇas.
m.2.3.29.22: What are planets, what are the groups of seasons, or what other planets are there for you? And what is it that you have now said for Śiva's sake, O goddess of fair complexion?
m.2.3.29.23: Through the distinction of guṇas and functions, we two have manifested in this world for the sake of devotees, out of love for devotees.
m.2.3.29.24: You indeed are the subtle Prakṛti, consisting of rajas, sattva and tamas, ever skilled in activity, with attributes and also without attributes.
m.2.3.29.25: I am the Self of all beings here, O slender-waisted one, changeless and desireless, assuming a form at the wish of devotees.
m.2.3.29.26: I would not go to Himālaya, your father, O mountain-born one; nor, becoming a mendicant, would I in any way beg for you.
m.2.3.29.27: Even one weighty with great virtues, even a great soul, O daughter of the mountain-king, at once falls into lightness by the word give.
m.2.3.29.28: Knowing this, O auspicious one, what do you now tell us? The task is by your command, O good lady; do as you wish.
m.2.3.29.29: Brahmā said: Though thus addressed by him, the great goddess, chaste and lotus-eyed, bowing again and again, spoke to Śaṅkara with devotion.
m.2.3.29.30: Pārvatī said: You are the Self and I am Prakṛti; there is no need for deliberation here. We two are independent yet subject to devotees, attributeless and also with attributes.
m.2.3.29.31: With effort, O Śambhu, my request must be fulfilled by you, O Lord. Ask Himagiri for me; grant me good fortune, O Śaṅkara.
m.2.3.29.32: Show compassion, O Maheśāna; I am ever your devotee. I am always your wife, O lord, birth after birth.
m.2.3.29.33: You are Brahman, the Supreme Self, attributeless, beyond Prakṛti, changeless and desireless, independent, the Supreme Lord.
m.2.3.29.34: Yet here you are also with attributes, devoted to uplifting your devotees, sporting, delighting in your own Self, skilled in manifold sports.
m.2.3.29.35: I know you in every way, O Mahādeva, O Maheśvara. What use is saying much, O all-knowing one? Show mercy.
m.2.3.29.36: Spread your glory in the world by performing a most wondrous sport, by singing of which people, O lord, easily cross the ocean of worldly existence.
m.2.3.29.37: Brahmā said: Having spoken thus to Maheśāna and bowed again and again, Girijā fell silent, with shoulders bent and palms joined.
m.2.3.29.38: Thus addressed by her, the great-souled Maheśvara, to imitate the ways of the world, thought, so be it, and laughing, became joyful, intent on doing just that.
m.2.3.29.39: Then Śambhu, greatly delighted, vanished and went to Kailāsa, his mind drawn by separation from Kālī.
m.2.3.29.40: Having gone there, Maheśāna, filled with supreme bliss, told Nandin and the others that whole account.
m.2.3.29.41: Hearing this, all the Gaṇas too, Bhairava and the rest, everywhere, became exceedingly happy and held a grand festival.
m.2.3.29.42: O Nārada, there was a great and exceedingly auspicious celebration there. The sorrow of all was destroyed, and Rudra too attained great joy.
m.2.3.29.iti: Thus ends the twenty-ninth adhyāya, named The description of the dialogue of Śivā and Śiva, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.3.30.1: Nārada said: O Vidhi (Brahmā), dear father, most fortunate one, you are blessed, a seer of the supreme truth. Through your grace I have heard this wondrous story.
m.2.3.30.2: When Hara had gone to his own mountain, what did Pārvatī, the all-auspicious one, do, and where did she go? Tell me that, O great-minded one.
m.2.3.30.3: Brahmā said: Listen with great delight, dear son, to what happened after that. When Hara had gone to his own abode — that I shall tell, remembering Śiva.
m.2.3.30.4: Pārvatī too, accompanied by her friends, having made her beauty fruitful, went to her father's house, repeating the name Mahādeva.
m.2.3.30.5: Hearing of Pārvatī's arrival, Menā and Himācala, overwhelmed with joy, mounted a divine vehicle and set out.
m.2.3.30.6: The family priest, the citizens, and her friends in great numbers, the relatives and others as well — all of them came together.
m.2.3.30.7: Then all her brothers, headed by Maināka, went, shouting cries of victory, filled with great joy.
m.2.3.30.8: Having set up an auspicious pot on the resplendent royal road, furnished with sandal, aguru, musk, fruits and branches,
m.2.3.30.9: the road adorned with excellent priests and brāhmaṇas, with sages who expound Brahman, with women and dancing girls, and beautified by lordly elephants and the like,
m.2.3.30.10: lined all around with rows of plantain stems, with groups of women who had husbands and sons, holding lamps in their hands,
m.2.3.30.11: joined by throngs of twice-born making auspicious sounds, and resounding with many kinds of instruments and the blare of conches —
m.2.3.30.12: Meanwhile Durgā came near her own city. Entering the city, the Goddess saw her parents again.
m.2.3.30.13: Seeing them, very pleased, running forward, their minds overwhelmed with joy, Kālī, greatly delighted, bowed to them together with her companions.
m.2.3.30.14: The two, giving her full blessings, pressed her to their bosoms, weeping and overwhelmed with love, saying, O dear child.
m.2.3.30.15: Then her own kinswomen, other women too, joyfully, and her brothers' wives with great affection, embraced her tightly.
m.2.3.30.16: You have properly accomplished a noble task that delivers the family; by your virtuous conduct we have all been purified.
m.2.3.30.17: Thus praising her highly, all of them, delighted, bowed to her, and joyfully worshipped Śivā with sandal paste and fine flowers.
m.2.3.30.18: At that moment the gods, standing in their aerial cars in the sky, joyfully showered auspicious flowers and, bowing to her, praised her with hymns.
m.2.3.30.19: Then all of them, the brāhmaṇas and the rest, placing her in an excellent, splendidly adorned chariot, joyfully led her into the city.
m.2.3.30.20: Then the brāhmaṇas, the priest, her friends and other women led the auspicious one Śivā into the house with great honour.
m.2.3.30.21: The women performed the waving of lamps, the brāhmaṇas bestowed blessings; Himavān and Menakā the mother rejoiced exceedingly, O lord of sages.
m.2.3.30.22: Himavān considered his household life fruitful — a daughter is better than a bad son — and he praised you, Nārada, saying, well done, well done.
m.2.3.30.23: The lord of mountains gave wealth to the brāhmaṇas and the bards, and had the twice-born recite auspicious texts — a great festival.
m.2.3.30.24: Thus, delighted by their daughter, the parents, the brothers, and the women of the family sat together in the courtyard with great affection, O sage.
m.2.3.30.25: Then Himavān, dear son, greatly delighted and serene of mind, having honoured everyone affectionately, went to the Gaṅgā to bathe.
m.2.3.30.26: Meanwhile Śambhu, delighting in sport and loving to his devotees, became a skilled dancer-actor and went into the presence of Menakā.
m.2.3.30.27: Holding a horn in his left hand and a ḍamaru drum in his right, a patched cloak on his back, clad in red, skilled in dance and song,
m.2.3.30.28: then he, in the form of a fine actor, joyfully performed in Menā's courtyard beautiful dances of many kinds and exceedingly charming songs.
m.2.3.30.29: There he played the horn and the ḍamaru with a sweet sound, and there he gave a great, varied and captivating performance.
m.2.3.30.30: To see it, all the townsfolk, men and women alike, came there at once — even children and the old, certainly.
m.2.3.30.31: Hearing that sweet song and seeing the charming dance, all were suddenly entranced, and Menā too then, O sage.
m.2.3.30.32: Durgā fell into a swoon, beholding Śaṅkara in her heart, bearing the trident and other emblems, exceedingly handsome,
m.2.3.30.33: adorned with sacred ash, delightful, wearing a garland of bones, his face radiant with three eyes, with a serpent as his sacred thread,
m.2.3.30.34: Maheśvara, fair of complexion, who was telling her to choose a boon, the friend of the afflicted, an ocean of compassion, utterly enchanting.
m.2.3.30.35: Seeing Hara thus dwelling in her heart, she bowed to him and chose a boon in her mind: Be my husband.
m.2.3.30.36: Having then lovingly granted Śivā such a boon in her heart, he vanished from it, and that mendicant again danced beautifully there.
m.2.3.30.37: Then Menā, her mind pleased by his splendour, lovingly went to give him fine jewels placed in a golden vessel.
m.2.3.30.38: He did not accept them, saying: I beg as alms that Śivā. And out of playfulness he was ready to dance and sing beautifully again.
m.2.3.30.39: Hearing his words, Menā, greatly astonished, became extremely angry; she rebuked the mendicant and wished to drive him out.
m.2.3.30.40: Meanwhile the Mountain king returned there from the Gaṅgā and saw before him the mendicant in human form standing in the courtyard.
m.2.3.30.41: Having heard that whole account from Menā's mouth, he became very angry and ordered his attendants to throw that dancer out.
m.2.3.30.42: But, O best of sages, no one was able to throw him out, for he was hard to touch like a great fire, blazing and full of splendour.
m.2.3.30.43: Then, dear one, that mendicant, skilled in many sports, showed the mountain his own infinite power.
m.2.3.30.44: There the mountain suddenly saw him bearing the form of Viṣṇu, crowned, wearing earrings, clad in yellow garments, four-armed.
m.2.3.30.45: Whatever flowers and other offerings he had given to the Mace-bearer at the time of worship, all of that he indeed saw on the mendicant's body and head.
m.2.3.30.46: Then the lord of mountains saw him as the four-faced creator of the worlds, red in colour, reciting Vedic hymns.
m.2.3.30.47: Then the king of mountains saw him for a moment in the form of the Sun, the eye of the world, causing wonder.
m.2.3.30.48: Then, dear one, he saw him in the most wondrous form of Rudra, together with Pārvatī, charming, smiling, full of splendour.
m.2.3.30.49: Then he saw him as a form of pure light, formless, stainless, free of limiting adjuncts, desireless, most wondrous and without shape.
m.2.3.30.50: Thus he saw many forms of him there; he at once became greatly astonished and filled with supreme bliss.
m.2.3.30.51: Then that best of mendicants begged from him and from her who had given birth to her for Durgā herself as alms, and accepted nothing else at all.
m.2.3.30.52: The lord of mountains, deluded by Śiva's māyā, did not agree. The mendicant took nothing and then vanished right there.
m.2.3.30.53: Then true understanding arose in Menā and the lord of mountains: The Lord Śiva has deceived us both and gone to his own abode.
m.2.3.30.54: As they reflected thus there, supreme devotion to Śiva arose in them—divine, bestowing great liberation and granting every bliss.
m.2.3.30.iti: Thus ends the thirtieth adhyāya, named The description of the great festival on the return of Pārvatī, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.3.31.1: Brahmā said: Knowing the supreme, unswerving devotion of those two, Himavat and Menā, to Śiva, all the gods led by Śakra reflected thus, O Nārada.
m.2.3.31.2: The gods said: If the mountain gives his daughter to him with single-minded devotion, he will surely attain liberation at once, here in Bhārata.
m.2.3.31.3: If he, the support of endless gems, leaves the earth and departs, the earth's name Ratnagarbhā (bearing gems in her womb) will surely become false.
m.2.3.31.4: Abandoning his immobile state and assuming a divine form, he will give his daughter to the Trident-bearer and go to Śiva's world.
m.2.3.31.5: He will gain likeness of form with Mahādeva, there is no doubt of this; having enjoyed excellent pleasures there, he will then attain liberation.
m.2.3.31.6: Brahmā said: Having thus deliberated and consulted among themselves, all the gods, greatly astonished, wished to send their preceptor there.
m.2.3.31.7: Then all the gods led by Śakra, intent on their own ends, went gladly and with humility to the preceptor's abode, O Nārada.
m.2.3.31.8: Going there and bowing to the preceptor, all the gods together with Vāsava respectfully reported the matter to that preceptor.
m.2.3.31.9: The gods said: O preceptor, go to Himālaya's house for the accomplishment of our purpose; having gone there, make an effort to speak ill of the Trident-bearer.
m.2.3.31.10: Durgā will choose no groom other than the Pināka-bearer. But if he gives his daughter unwillingly, he will quickly obtain only an ordinary fruit.
m.2.3.31.11: For the time being, let the mountain remain on the earth now; establish him, the support of many gems, on the earth, O preceptor.
m.2.3.31.12: Brahmā said: Hearing these words of the gods, the preceptor put his hands over his ears; he did not accept, and remembered the name Śiva.
m.2.3.31.13: Then, remembering Mahādeva, the noble-minded Bṛhaspati spoke to the foremost gods, reproaching them again and again.
m.2.3.31.14: Bṛhaspati said: All you gods are bent on your own interest and destroy the interests of others. Indeed, if I disparage Śaṅkara, I will surely go to hell.
m.2.3.31.15: O gods, let one among you go near the mountain and accomplish what you desire by persuading the lord of mountains.
m.2.3.31.16: Having given his daughter unwillingly, let him live happily in Bhārata; whereas having given his daughter to him with devotion, he would certainly attain liberation.
m.2.3.31.17: Afterwards all the seven sages will enlighten the mountain; Durgā will choose no groom other than the Pināka-bearer.
m.2.3.31.18: Or else, O gods, go with Vāsava to Brahmā's world and tell your story; he will do your work.
m.2.3.31.19: Brahmā said: Hearing that, the gods deliberated and came to my assembly; bowing, they all respectfully reported what had happened.
m.2.3.31.20: Hearing then those words of the gods, which amounted to disparaging Śiva, I, the speaker of the Vedas, lamented and said to those gods, O sage:
m.2.3.31.21: Brahmā said: My children, I am not able to commit disparagement of Śiva, which is utterly intolerable, which is destruction of prosperity itself and the very seed of calamities.
m.2.3.31.22: O gods, go to Kailāsa and please Śaṅkara; send him quickly towards Himālaya's house.
m.2.3.31.23: Let him go near the lord of mountains and indeed disparage himself. Disparaging others is held to lead to ruin, disparaging oneself to glory.
m.2.3.31.24: Brahmā said: Hearing these words of mine, the gods joyfully bowed to me and quickly went to Kailāsa, the mountain that is lord of mountains.
m.2.3.31.25: Going there and seeing Śiva, the gods bowed with heads lowered and, with palms well joined, all praised that Hara.
m.2.3.31.26: The gods said: O God of gods, Mahādeva, mine of compassion, Śaṅkara, we have come to you for refuge; show us grace; salutation to you.
m.2.3.31.27: O Lord, you are loving to your devotees, ever accomplishing the work of devotees, uplifter of the wretched, ocean of compassion, releaser of devotees from distress.
m.2.3.31.28: Brahmā said: Having thus praised Maheśāna, all the gods with Vāsava then respectfully reported that whole matter.
m.2.3.31.29: Hearing the gods' words, Maheśvara accepted; smiling and reassuring the gods, he sent them off.
m.2.3.31.30: All the gods rejoiced; quickly going to their own abodes, they praised Sadāśiva, considering their purpose accomplished.
m.2.3.31.31: Then the blessed Śambhu, Maheśa, loving to his devotees, the Lord of Māyā, ever free of change, went to the king of mountains.
m.2.3.31.32: When the mountain himself was seated joyfully in the midst of his assembly, surrounded by his kinsfolk and accompanied by Pārvatī,
m.2.3.31.33: at that moment Sadāśiva came there, carrying a staff and an umbrella, in divine garments, bearing a shining tilaka,
m.2.3.31.34: holding a crystal rosary in his hand and a śālagrāma at his neck, devoutly repeating the name of Hari—a brahmin wearing the garb of a holy man.
m.2.3.31.35: Seeing him, Himālaya with his retinue rose up and, with devotion, prostrated on the ground like a staff before the unprecedented guest.
m.2.3.31.36: Pārvatī devoutly bowed to the lord of her life in the form of a brahmin; recognising him in her mind, the goddess praised him with supreme joy.
m.2.3.31.37: The brahmin, Śiva, lovingly bestowed blessings on all, and on Śivā especially, granting from his heart what her mind desired, dear child.
m.2.3.31.38: The brahmin gladly accepted the madhuparka and all the other offerings given with great reverence by Himavat, the overlord of mountains.
m.2.3.31.39: Having duly worshipped that best of brahmins with great affection, Himādri, the best of mountains, asked after his welfare, O sage.
m.2.3.31.40: Then the lord of mountains asked him again, who are you? The foremost brahmin promptly addressed respectful words to the king of mountains.
m.2.3.31.41: The best of brahmins said: O best of mountains, I am a Brāhmaṇa, a Vaiṣṇava, foremost among the learned. Following the profession of a match-maker, I wander over the surface of the earth.
m.2.3.31.42: By the power of my guru I move with the speed of thought, I go everywhere, and I know everything. I am a benefactor of others, pure-souled, an ocean of compassion, a remover of afflictions.
m.2.3.31.43: I have come to know that you wish to give your own daughter to Hara — this girl, like a lotus, divine, of excellent beauty, endowed with auspicious marks —
m.2.3.31.44: — to one without support, without attachment, ugly in form and devoid of qualities, who dwells in the cremation ground, who has the appearance of a snake-catcher, a yogin,
m.2.3.31.45: to one clad in the directions (naked), of ugly body, wearing serpents as ornaments, whose family and name are unknown, of bad conduct, who takes no pleasure in household life,
m.2.3.31.46: whose body is smeared with ashes, who is wrathful and lacks discernment, whose age is utterly unknown, who always bears ugly matted locks,
m.2.3.31.47: who shelters with everyone, a wanderer, wearing snakes as a necklace, a beggar, devoted to wrong paths, and who has wilfully abandoned the path of the Veda.
m.2.3.31.48: O Mountain, this intention of yours is surely not auspicious. Understand this, O best of the wise, born of the lineage of Nārāyaṇa.
m.2.3.31.49: He is not a recipient befitting you in the act of giving Pārvatī. Eminent people will smile in mockery the moment they hear of it.
m.2.3.31.50: Look, O lord of mountains: he has not a single kinsman. You are a great mine of jewels, but he has no wealth at all.
m.2.3.31.51: O lord of mountains, quickly and carefully ask your kinsmen, Menakā, your sons, and all the learned — everyone except Pārvatī.
m.2.3.31.52: O best of mountains, medicine never pleases a sick man; unwholesome diet, which always causes great harm, constantly pleases him.
m.2.3.31.53: Brahmā said: Having spoken thus, that Brāhmaṇa — Śiva, the performer of many sports — having eaten, joyful and calm, quickly went to his own abode.
m.2.3.31.iti: Thus ends the thirty-first adhyāya, named Śiva's māyā, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.3.32.1: Brahmā said: Having heard the brāhmaṇa's words, Menā, her eyes filled with tears from grief and her heart burning, spoke to Himālaya.
m.2.3.32.2: Menā said: Listen, O lord of mountains, to my words, which will bring happiness in the end. Ask all the foremost devotees of Śiva what the brāhmaṇa has said.
m.2.3.32.3: This Vaiṣṇava brāhmaṇa has spoken ill of Śambhu. Having heard that censure, my mind has become utterly disheartened, O lord of mountains.
m.2.3.32.4: O lord of mountains, I will not give my own daughter, who is endowed with good marks, to that Rudra, whose form, conduct and name are all ill-favoured.
m.2.3.32.5: If you do not heed my words, I shall die, without doubt. I shall leave the house at once, or I shall swallow poison.
m.2.3.32.6: Binding Ambikā by the neck with a rope, I shall go into the dense forest; I shall drown her in the great ocean. I will not give my daughter to him.
m.2.3.32.7: Having said this, Menā went quickly, in grief, to the chamber of anger; casting off her necklace, weeping, she lay down on the ground.
m.2.3.32.8: Meanwhile, dear one, Śambhu, his mind agitated by separation, at once called to mind those seven sages.
m.2.3.32.9: When all those sages were remembered by Śambhu, they came at once of their own accord, like so many other wish-fulfilling trees.
m.2.3.32.10: Arundhatī too came, like another Siddhi (Accomplishment) incarnate. Seeing them, radiant as the sun, Hara left off his own japa.
m.2.3.32.11: Standing before him, those excellent sages, O sage, bowed to Śiva and praised him, and then those ascetics considered themselves fulfilled.
m.2.3.32.12: Then, filled with wonder, having bowed again they stood, and with joined palms they spoke to Śiva, who is saluted by the worlds.
m.2.3.32.13: The sages said: O Supreme over all, great King, Sovereign of the dwellers of heaven, our own good fortune is now being extolled by us—what more need be said? It is the highest of all.
m.2.3.32.14: Austerity was formerly practised in three ways, excellent Vedic study was done, fires were offered oblations to, and various sacred places visited.
m.2.3.32.15: Whatever merit arose from speech, mind and body, and from remembrance of you—all of that has come to fruition today through the grace of your remembering us.
m.2.3.32.16: The man who worships you constantly becomes one who has accomplished all. What merit can be described of those whom you remember?
m.2.3.32.17: We have become the most exalted of all through your remembrance, O Sadāśiva. You never in any way come within the path of mere wishes.
m.2.3.32.18: Like a fruit reached by a dwarf, like eyes for one born blind, like speech for the mute, like the sight of a treasure for a pauper,
m.2.3.32.19: like the climbing of a great mountain by a lame man, and the giving birth by a barren woman—so has the sight of you, hard to obtain, come to us, O Lord.
m.2.3.32.20: From today onward, we lords of sages have become honoured and worshipful in the worlds, merely by the sight of you, having attained our own lofty station.
m.2.3.32.21: What use is saying much here? We have become honoured in every way through the sight of you, O Lord of gods, who are indeed the Lord of all the gods.
m.2.3.32.22: What remains to be done by those who are fulfilled? Yet if there is your supreme grace, some auspicious task befitting your servants should be given by you.
m.2.3.32.23: Brahmā said: Hearing these words of theirs, Śambhu, the great Lord, adopting worldly custom, spoke delightful words.
m.2.3.32.24: Śiva said: Sages are always worthy of worship, and you especially. It is for a purpose concerning you, O brāhmaṇas, that I called you to mind.
m.2.3.32.25: You know that my state is one of benefiting others; it must especially be accomplished for the success of the worlds.
m.2.3.32.26: Distress has arisen for the gods from the utterly wicked Tāraka; and a boon was granted to him by Brahmā. He is hard to overcome—what am I to do?
m.2.3.32.27: The eight forms that are declared to be mine, O great sages, all exist for the benefit of others, not for my own sake—that is plain.
m.2.3.32.28: So I wish to marry Śivā. She has performed severe austerity, difficult even for the great sages.
m.2.3.32.29: To her must be given the supreme fruit she desires, bringing her welfare. Such is my pledge, which clearly gives joy to devotees.
m.2.3.32.30: At Pārvatī's word, I went to the mountain's house in the form of a mendicant and purified Kālī, for I am skilled in divine play.
m.2.3.32.31: Knowing me to be the supreme Brahman, that couple, out of supreme devotion, became desirous of giving their daughter to me according to Vedic rite.
m.2.3.32.32: At the prompting of the gods I then, in the guise of a Vaiṣṇava, made censure of myself, so as to destroy their devotion.
m.2.3.32.33: Hearing that, the two became deeply disheartened and bereft of that devotion; now, O sages, they do not wish to give their daughter to me.
m.2.3.32.34: Therefore you must surely go to Himācala's house. Having gone there, enlighten the great mountain and his wife.
m.2.3.32.35: Words in accord with the Veda should be spoken with effort; that must be done in every way so that the task turns out excellently.
m.2.3.32.36: I wish to marry his daughter, O best ones. I have accepted that marriage, and such a boon has been granted by me.
m.2.3.32.37: What use is saying much here? Himālaya must be enlightened, and likewise Menā must be made to understand, so that the gods' welfare may come about.
m.2.3.32.38: Whatever procedure you devise, let it be even greater than that; this task is yours, for you are sharers in the task.
m.2.3.32.39: Brahmā said: Hearing these words, all those sages of pure heart, favoured by the Lord, attained joy.
m.2.3.32.40: They said: We have become blessed and fulfilled in every way; we have become worthy of salutation by all and especially worthy of worship.
m.2.3.32.41: He who is indeed to be worshipped by Brahmā and Viṣṇu, the accomplisher of all aims, sends us, his messengers, on a task that brings happiness to the world.
m.2.3.32.42: He is the lord of the worlds and the father; she is regarded as the mother. This alliance is fitting; may it always grow like the waxing moon.
m.2.3.32.43: Brahmā said: Having said this, the divine sages then bowed to Śiva and went by the path of the sky to where Himavat's city stands.
m.2.3.32.44: Seeing that divine city, those sages were greatly astonished, and, extolling their own good fortune, they spoke to one another.
m.2.3.32.45: The sages said: We are meritorious and blessed, having seen this city of Himavat, since we have been appointed by Śiva himself to such a task.
m.2.3.32.46: This excellent city appears superior to Alakā, to Svarga, and again to Bhogavatī, and especially to Amarāvatī.
m.2.3.32.47: The fine houses are very charming, and the courtyards are built and adorned in variety with many excellent crystals or gems.
m.2.3.32.48: In every house there are sunstones and likewise moonstones, and wonderful trees born of heaven.
m.2.3.32.49: Likewise the splendour of arched gateways is seen in every house, varied and wonderful, with parrots, swans and little aerial cars as decorations.
m.2.3.32.50: There are wonderful canopies made of cloth together with gateways, many reservoirs of water, and various long ponds.
m.2.3.32.51: There are wonderful gardens, tended by delighted people; and all the men are gods, and the women likewise are celestial nymphs.
m.2.3.32.52: In the land of action, sacrificers and those versed in the Purāṇas perform rites out of desire for heaven; all of them do so in vain, passing over the city of Himavat.
m.2.3.32.53: As long as this has not been seen, so long are men devoted to heaven; but once this is seen, O brahmins, what need is there of heaven?
m.2.3.32.54: Brahmā said: Thus describing that city, all those foremost sages went to the house of Himālaya, rich in every prosperity.
m.2.3.32.55: Seeing from afar those seven very radiant sages, resplendent like the sun, standing on the path of the sky, Himavat, astonished, said:
m.2.3.32.56: Himavān said: These seven, resplendent like the sun, are coming near me. Worship of the sages must now be performed by me with care.
m.2.3.32.57: Blessed are we householders, givers of happiness to all, since to our house such great souls come.
m.2.3.32.58: Brahmā said: Meanwhile, seeing them come down from the sky and standing on the ground before him, Himavat went forward with reverence.
m.2.3.32.59: With joined palms and bowed shoulders, he bowed deeply to the seven sages and performed their worship with great honour.
m.2.3.32.60: Those benevolent seven sages, taking hold of Himavat, lord of mountains, spoke with cheerful faces words that were an abode of auspiciousness.
m.2.3.32.61: Placing them before him, he said, blessed is my householder's life. Having said this, he brought seats and offered them with devotion.
m.2.3.32.62: When they had sat down on the seats, he himself, permitted by them, took his place; then Himavat spoke there to the radiant sages.
m.2.3.32.63: Himavān said: I am blessed indeed and have fulfilled my purpose; my life is fruitful. I am worthy to be seen in the worlds and am regarded as equal to many holy places.
m.2.3.32.64: For you, who are forms of Viṣṇu, have come to my house. What business could you, who are complete, have in the houses of poor beings?
m.2.3.32.65: Even so, kindly tell me some task befitting me, your servant, so that my birth may become fruitful.
m.2.3.32.iti: Thus ends the thirty-second adhyāya, named The coming of the seven sages, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.3.33.1: The sages said: Śiva is declared the father of the world, and Śivā is regarded as the mother of the world. Therefore you should give your daughter to the great-souled Śaṅkara.
m.2.3.33.2: By doing so, O Himālaya, your birth will become fruitful. You will surely become the guru of the guru of the world; there is no doubt.
m.2.3.33.3: Brahmā said: Hearing these words of the seven sages, O lord of sages, the king of mountains bowed to them, folded his hands, and said this:
m.2.3.33.4: Himavān said: O greatly fortunate seven sages, what you have said had indeed been accepted by me as authoritative long ago, through the will of Giriśa.
m.2.3.33.5: But just now a certain brahmin, following the Vaiṣṇava dharma, came and, with great affection, spoke words contrary in praise concerning Śiva.
m.2.3.33.6: From then on, Śivā's mother has lost her good sense; she does not want her daughter's marriage with that yogin Rudra.
m.2.3.33.7: She has gone to the chamber of anger, greatly distressed, wearing soiled garments; having resolved on great obstinacy, O brahmins, she did not understand even when admonished.
m.2.3.33.8: And I too have lost my good sense — the truth is being told: I do not wish to give my daughter to Maheśa, who has the form of a beggar.
m.2.3.33.9: Brahmā said: Having said this, the king of mountains, deluded by Śiva's māyā, fell silent, remaining there in the midst of the sages, O sage.
m.2.3.33.10: All those seven sages, praising Śiva's māyā, then sent Arundhatī to Menakā.
m.2.3.33.11: Then, receiving her husband's instruction, Arundhatī, the giver of wisdom, went swiftly to where Menā and Pārvatī were.
m.2.3.33.12: Having gone, she saw Menā lying down, swooning with grief. The virtuous lady, attentive, spoke sweet and beneficial words.
m.2.3.33.13: Arundhatī said: Rise, O virtuous Menakā. I, Arundhatī, have come to your house, and the seven compassionate sages have come as well.
m.2.3.33.14: Brahmā said: Hearing Arundhatī's voice, Menakā rose quickly, bowed her head, and spoke to her, who was like Padmā (Lakṣmī) in radiance.
m.2.3.33.15: Menā said: Ah! What merit is this today for us who are of meritorious birth — that the daughter-in-law of the world's creator, the wife of Vasiṣṭha, has come here.
m.2.3.33.16: For what purpose have you come, O goddess? Tell me that in detail. I, together with my daughter, am like your maidservant; show compassion.
m.2.3.33.17: Brahmā said: When the virtuous Menakā had spoken thus, Arundhatī, having counselled her at length, came gladly with her to where those seven sages also were.
m.2.3.33.18: Then they, all skilled in speech, remembering the pair of Śiva's feet, respectfully counselled the lord of mountains.
m.2.3.33.19: The sages said: O lord of mountains, listen to our words, which are a cause of good. Give Pārvatī to Śiva; become the father-in-law of the Destroyer.
m.2.3.33.20: Brahmā earnestly entreated the Lord of all, who asks for nothing, to enter into this marital alliance for the destruction of Tāraka.
m.2.3.33.21: Śaṅkara, the best of yogins, is not eager for union with a wife; yet at the Creator's entreaty the god will accept your daughter.
m.2.3.33.22: Your daughter has performed austerities, and she has secured a promise; for these two reasons the lord of yogins will perform the marriage.
m.2.3.33.23: Brahmā said: Hearing the sages' words, Himālaya laughed, and, somewhat afraid, spoke with the utmost humility.
m.2.3.33.24: Himavān said: I see no royal possessions whatever of Śiva — no shelter, no wealth, nor any kinsman or relative.
m.2.3.33.25: I do not wish to give my daughter to an utterly detached yogin. You are the sons of the Creator of the Vedas; tell me decisively.
m.2.3.33.26: If a father gives his daughter to an unsuitable bridegroom out of desire, delusion, fear or greed, he is ruined and goes to hell.
m.2.3.33.27: I will not willingly give my daughter to the Trident-bearer. O sages, let whatever arrangement is proper be made.
m.2.3.33.28: Brahmā said: Hearing these words of Himālaya, O lord of sages, Vasiṣṭha, the most skilled in speech among them, replied to him.
m.2.3.33.29: Vasiṣṭha said: Listen, O lord of mountains, to my words, which are in every way beneficial to you, not opposed to dharma, true, and bringing joy here and hereafter.
m.2.3.33.30: Speech is of three kinds, O mountain, both in worldly and in Vedic usage; one who knows the śāstras understands it all with the eye of pure knowledge.
m.2.3.33.31: What is untrue and harmful in the end, yet pleasant to hear for the present — that a clever enemy speaks; he never speaks what is beneficial.
m.2.3.33.32: What is unpleasant at first but brings happiness in the end — that a compassionate, righteous kinsman always counsels.
m.2.3.33.33: Speech that is like nectar the moment it is heard, brings happiness at all times, has truth as its essence and is beneficial — that is the best and most desired.
m.2.3.33.34: Thus, O mountain, speech is of three kinds, as stated in the treatises on policy. Tell me: of the three, which kind of speech do you wish me to speak?
m.2.3.33.35: Śaṅkara, lord of the gods, is devoid of external wealth; his single mind is wholly immersed in the oceans of knowledge of reality.
m.2.3.33.36: What desire for external things can the Lord have, whose bliss is knowledge? Only a householder gives his daughter to one endowed with kingdom and riches.
m.2.3.33.37: A father who gives his daughter to a miserable man becomes a slayer of his daughter. But who can claim Śaṅkara is miserable, whose servant is Kubera?
m.2.3.33.38: He is able to create and destroy the universe by the mere play of a knitting of his brows. He is beyond the guṇas, the supreme Self, the highest Lord, beyond Prakṛti.
m.2.3.33.39: In the work of creation, he, the Ordainer, has a threefold form — named Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Hara — which brings about creation, preservation and dissolution.
m.2.3.33.40: Brahmā dwells in Brahmaloka, Viṣṇu resides in the Ocean of Milk, Hara has Kailāsa as his abode — all are manifestations of Śiva's glory.
m.2.3.33.41: And Prakṛti, born of Śiva, assumes three forms; in creation, through a portion of herself, playfully, and by a fraction of her power, she takes many forms as well.
m.2.3.33.42: From Brahmā's mouth arose Vāṇī herself, the deity presiding over speech; from Viṣṇu's chest arose Lakṣmī, the embodiment of all wealth.
m.2.3.33.43: That Śivā manifested herself from the radiant energies of the gods; having slain all the Dānavas, she gave prosperity to the gods.
m.2.3.33.44: In another kalpa she took birth in the womb of Dakṣa's wife; named Satī, she obtained Hara, and Dakṣa gave her to him.
m.2.3.33.45: Having heard her husband reviled, she abandoned her body through yoga. That same Śivā has now been born from you, out of the womb of Menā.
m.2.3.33.46: O mountain, this Śivā is Śiva's wife in birth after birth; in every kalpa she is the supreme mother of the wise, in the form of intelligence.
m.2.3.33.47: She, ever perfect, the giver of siddhi and the embodiment of siddhi, is born again and again. Hara himself devotedly bears Satī's bones and the ashes of her pyre.
m.2.3.33.48: Therefore give your auspicious daughter to Hara of your own will; otherwise, she herself will go to her beloved's abode, even if you do not give her.
m.2.3.33.49: Having made a promise, and having seen the countless hardships of your daughter, the Lord of the gods came to her place of penance in the form of a brahmin.
m.2.3.33.50: Having consoled her and granted a boon, he went to his own abode. Moved by her entreaty, Śambhu asked you for Śivā, O mountain.
m.2.3.33.51: That was accepted by you both, with minds devoted to Śiva. Tell us, O lord of mountains, why has your mind turned contrary?
m.2.3.33.52: Therefore we sages, and Arundhatī too, have been quickly sent to you by the Lord, who was entreated by the gods.
m.2.3.33.53: We indeed counsel you: give Pārvatī to Rudra. If this is done, O mountain, great joy will be yours.
m.2.3.33.54: O king of mountains, if you do not give Śivā to Śiva of your own will, their marriage will take place here anyway, by the force of destiny.
m.2.3.33.55: Dear one, that Śaṅkara granted a boon to Śivā while she was performing penance. What the Lord has promised can never turn out otherwise.
m.2.3.33.56: Ah! The promise of the virtuous who abide by the Lord is hard to transgress among all the worlds; how much more, O mountain, that of the Lord himself.
m.2.3.33.57: Mahendra alone playfully cut off the wings of the mountains, and Pārvatī playfully broke the peak of Meru.
m.2.3.33.58: O lord of mountains, all one's possessions should not be destroyed for the sake of one; one should give up one for the sake of the family — this is the eternal scriptural teaching.
m.2.3.33.59: King Anaraṇya, lord of kings, having fallen into fear of a brahmin, gave his own daughter to the brahmin and thus protected his own possessions.
m.2.3.33.60: Men versed in the science of polity, his preceptors and the best of his kinsmen, quickly counseled him, who was terrified of a brahmin's curse.
m.2.3.33.61: O king of mountains, you too in the same way give your daughter to Śiva, protect all your kinsfolk, and bring even the gods under your sway.
m.2.3.33.62: Brahmā said: Having heard these words of Vasiṣṭha, he smiled and, with an aching heart, asked about the story of the king.
m.2.3.33.63: Himavān said: O brahmin, in whose lineage was that king Anaraṇya born? And how did he, having given away his daughter, protect all his possessions?
m.2.3.33.64: Brahmā said: Having heard these words of the mountain, Vasiṣṭha, with a serene mind, told that mountain the pleasing story of the king.
m.2.3.33.iti: Thus ends the thirty-third adhyāya, named The consoling of the mountain, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.3.34.1: Vasiṣṭha said: King Anaraṇya, lord of kings, was born in the lineage of Manu, namely of the fourteenth Manu, called Indrasāvarṇi.
m.2.3.34.2: Anaraṇya, best of kings, ruler of the earth with its seven continents, was especially devoted to Śambhu; born of Maṅgalāraṇya, he was mighty.
m.2.3.34.3: Making Bhṛgu his priest, he performed a hundred sacrifices; yet he did not accept the status of Indra even when the gods offered it.
m.2.3.34.4: That king had a hundred sons, O Himālaya, and one daughter, beautiful, named Padmā, equal to Padmālayā (Lakṣmī).
m.2.3.34.5: Whatever affection the king had for his hundred sons, greater than that was his affection for the daughter, O best of mountains.
m.2.3.34.6: The king had five wives, queens dearer than life, most beloved, foremost among all women, all endowed with good fortune.
m.2.3.34.7: That girl reached youth in her father's house; he sent out letters to bring a fine bridegroom.
m.2.3.34.8: Once the sage Pippalāda, eager to go to his own hermitage, saw a Gandharva in a lonely place of austerity.
m.2.3.34.9: He saw him with a woman, his mind immersed in the ocean of the erotic sentiment, sporting with great love, skilled in the science of love.
m.2.3.34.10: Seeing him, that tiger among sages became filled with desire; his mind no longer given to austerities, he thought of taking a wife.
m.2.3.34.11: While that good sage Pippalāda was thus disposed, his mind churned by desire, some time passed there.
m.2.3.34.12: Once, going to bathe in the Puṣpabhadrā, the lord of sages saw the young Padmā, charming like Padmā (Lakṣmī).
m.2.3.34.13: Who is this girl? Thus the sage asked the people standing nearby. The people, bowing and held in check by fear of a curse, told him.
m.2.3.34.14: The people said: This is indeed Anaraṇya's daughter, named Padmā, a second Ramā, fair-hipped, an abode of virtues, sought after by the best of kings.
m.2.3.34.15: Brahmā said: Hearing those words of the truthful people, the sage was greatly agitated in mind and became eager to obtain her.
m.2.3.34.16: The sage, having bathed and duly worshipped Śiva, his chosen deity, went, full of desire, to Anaraṇya's court on the pretext of alms, O mountain.
m.2.3.34.17: The king, seeing the sage, quickly bowed down, anxious with fear, and offering madhuparka and the rest, worshipped him with devotion.
m.2.3.34.18: Having accepted everything, the sage out of desire asked for the girl. The king fell silent, unable to say anything.
m.2.3.34.19: The sage demanded the girl: Give her to me, O lord of kings; otherwise I shall reduce everything to ashes in an instant.
m.2.3.34.20: All the attendants were overwhelmed by his radiance, O sage. The king with his retinue wept, seeing the brahmin worn by old age.
m.2.3.34.21: All the queens wept, unable to decide what should be done; the chief queen, the girl's mother, overcome by grief, fainted.
m.2.3.34.22: All the sons became stricken with grief; everything connected with the king was plunged in sorrow, O lord of mountains.
m.2.3.34.23: Meanwhile the wise brahmin, his unsurpassed preceptor, and the intelligent family priest came into the king's presence.
m.2.3.34.24: The king bowed to them, worshipped them, and wept before the two; he told them everything and promptly asked what was proper.
m.2.3.34.25: Then the king's preceptor, a learned brahmin, and the priest, both knowers of scripture and of right conduct, counselled the king,
m.2.3.34.26: and the grief-stricken queens, the princes and the girl, relying on the highest counsel, beneficial to all.
m.2.3.34.27: The guru and the family priest said: Listen, O king of great wisdom, to our words that bring true welfare. Do not grieve, you and your family; set your mind rightly on scripture.
m.2.3.34.28: Whether today or at the end of a year, a daughter must be given away, O king, to a worthy recipient — especially a brahmin — or to someone else.
m.2.3.34.29: In the three worlds we see no worthier recipient than a brahmin. Give your daughter to the sage and protect all your prosperity.
m.2.3.34.30: O king, through a single cause all prosperity perishes; by giving up that one, one protects everything — unless that one has come seeking refuge.
m.2.3.34.31: Vasiṣṭha said: Hearing the words of the wise and lamenting again and again, the king adorned the girl and gave her to the lord of sages.
m.2.3.34.32: Taking the lovely Padmā, lotus-like, and marrying her with due rites, O mountain, the sage joyfully went to his abode.
m.2.3.34.33: The king, having given his daughter to the old man, renounced everyone and, with dejection settled in his heart, went to the forest for austerities.
m.2.3.34.34: When her lord of life had gone to the forest, O mountain, his beautiful wife gave up her life from grief for her husband and daughter.
m.2.3.34.35: The elders, the sons and the servants fainted without the king; all the other people, learning of it, grieved, sighing heavily.
m.2.3.34.36: Anaraṇya went to the forest, performed intense austerities, and having propitiated Śaṅkara with devotion, attained Śiva's world, free from affliction.
m.2.3.34.37: Then the king's eldest son, the righteous one named Kīrtimān, protected the subjects as if they were his sons and ruled the kingdom.
m.2.3.34.38: Thus I have told you, O mountain, the auspicious story of Anaraṇya — how by giving away his daughter he protected his lineage and all his wealth.
m.2.3.34.39: O king of mountains, you too, likewise giving your daughter to Śiva, protect your entire family, and bring all under your sway — even the gods.
m.2.3.34.iti: Thus ends the thirty-fourth adhyāya, named The story of Anaraṇya, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.3.35.1: Nārada said: Having heard the story of Anaraṇya together with the account of the giving of his daughter, what did the best of mountains do, dear one? Tell me that.
m.2.3.35.2: Brahmā said: Having heard the story of Anaraṇya together with the giving away of his daughter, the lord of mountains, with joined palms, questioned Vasiṣṭha again.
m.2.3.35.3: Himavān said: O Vasiṣṭha, tiger among sages, son of Brahmā, treasure of compassion, you have told the most wondrous story of Anaraṇya.
m.2.3.35.4: Since Anaraṇya's daughter obtained the sage Pippalāda as husband, what did she do? Tell me that delightful story.
m.2.3.35.5: Vasiṣṭha said: Pippalāda, the excellent sage, greatly worn with age, having gone to his own hermitage with that woman, the daughter of Anaraṇya,
m.2.3.35.6: dwelt there with great delight, an ascetic not excessively lustful; there in the forest on that excellent mountain he constantly performed his own dharma.
m.2.3.35.7: Then that daughter of Anaraṇya served the sage with devotion, in deed, mind and speech, as Lakṣmī serves Nārāyaṇa.
m.2.3.35.8: Once, as she, sweetly smiling, was going to bathe in the heavenly river, Dharma, having assumed the form of a king by illusion, saw her on the path.
m.2.3.35.9: Seated in a beautiful jewelled chariot, adorned with various ornaments, in fresh youth, splendid, his radiance equal to Kāmadeva's.
m.2.3.35.10: Seeing that beautiful Padmā, the mighty Vṛṣa (Dharma) spoke, in order to know the inner disposition of that sage's wife.
m.2.3.35.11: Dharma said: O beautiful one, truly a Lakṣmī, worthy of a king, charming, in the very prime of youth, O lovely woman of lasting youth,
m.2.3.35.12: I tell you the truth, slender one: beside the old sage Pippalāda, afflicted by age, you do not shine at all.
m.2.3.35.13: Abandoning that brahmin devoted to austerities, unfeeling, facing death, look at me, a lord of kings, a hero in love, tormented by desire.
m.2.3.35.14: A beautiful woman obtains her beauty from the merit of a former birth; all of that becomes fruitful through the embrace of a passionate lover.
m.2.3.35.15: Abandoning that husband, O beloved, make me your servant, me who am the lover of a thousand beauties and expert in the science of love.
m.2.3.35.16: In lonely, delightful forests, on mountain after mountain, on river banks, sport with me; make this birth fruitful.
m.2.3.35.17: Vasiṣṭha said: To him who had spoken thus and, descending from his chariot, was eager to seize her by the hand, the devoted wife said:
m.2.3.35.18: Padmā said: Go far away, go far away. You are most sinful, O king. If you look at me with lust, you will perish at once.
m.2.3.35.19: Abandoning Pippalāda, the best of sages, whose body is purified by austerity, how could I resort to you, conquered by women and greedy for pleasure?
m.2.3.35.20: By the mere touch of one conquered by women all merit perishes; one conquered by women is a great sinner, and even the sight of him brings sin.
m.2.3.35.21: Even if he performs good rites, that man who is conquered by a woman is always impure; the ancestors, the gods and all humans censure him.
m.2.3.35.22: What use to him are knowledge, good austerity, japa, oblations and worship? What use is learning or charity to one whose mind has been stolen by women?
m.2.3.35.23: Since you speak to me, who am like a mother, regarding me as a woman to be enjoyed, therefore, in time, decline will come upon you through my curse.
m.2.3.35.24: Vasiṣṭha said: Hearing the chaste woman's curse, Dharma, lord of gods, cast off the king's form, assumed his own form, and trembling, spoke.
m.2.3.35.25: Dharma said: O mother, know me to be Dharma, the teacher of the teacher of the wise, who always regards others' wives as mothers, O chaste one.
m.2.3.35.26: I came into your presence to know your inner nature. I know your mind, yet I was impelled by destiny.
m.2.3.35.27: The chastisement inflicted on me, O virtuous lady, is not wrong; it is fitting. Punishment for those on the wrong path has been ordained by the Lord.
m.2.3.35.28: Salutation to that Śiva who himself is able to bestow on all happiness, sorrow and boons, prosperity and adversity.
m.2.3.35.29: Salutation to that Śiva who is able to make foe and friend, love and strife, and to create and destroy the creation.
m.2.3.35.30: Salutation to that Śiva by whom of old milk was made white, coolness placed in water, and fire made burning.
m.2.3.35.31: Salutation to that Śiva by whom Prakṛti was created, the principles beginning with Mahat, and Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Maheśa and the rest.
m.2.3.35.32: Brahmā said: Having said this, Dharma, preceptor of the world, stood before her; astonished and pleased by her wifely fidelity, he said nothing more.
m.2.3.35.33: Then Padmā too, that king's daughter, beloved of Pippalāda, the virtuous one, recognising him as Dharma, spoke in amazement, O mountain.
m.2.3.35.34: Padmā said: You indeed, O Dharma, are the witness of all the deeds of all beings. Why, O lord, do you mock me to know my mind?
m.2.3.35.35: Whatever was done, O holy one, no fault was mine; yet you were cursed by me in ignorance, out of a woman's nature, needlessly, O Vṛṣa.
m.2.3.35.36: What remedy can there be for it? I am now pondering this. May that understanding flash in my mind by which I may obtain peace.
m.2.3.35.37: Even if this sky, all the directions and the winds should perish, still the curse of a chaste woman never fails.
m.2.3.35.38: In the Satya age you are complete with four feet, like the moon on the full-moon day; you shine, O king of gods, at all times, day and night.
m.2.3.35.39: If you were to perish, then creation would be destroyed. Bewildered about what ought to be done, I speak, even if in vain.
m.2.3.35.40: In the Tretā age there will be the loss of one foot, O best of gods; another foot in the Dvāpara, and the third also in the Kali, O lord.
m.2.3.35.41: At the end of the Kali age all your feet will be cut off. When the Satya age comes again, you will be whole once more.
m.2.3.35.42: In the Satya age you are all-pervading, and in the other ages only here and there; according to the order of the ages, you will be as each age requires.
m.2.3.35.43: Thus let this word of mine prove true and bring you happiness. I go to serve my husband; you go to your own home, O lord.
m.2.3.35.44: Brahmā said: Hearing her words, Dharma was indeed pleased. O son of Vidhi, he spoke to that chaste woman who had spoken thus.
m.2.3.35.45: Dharma said: You are blessed, you are devoted to your husband; may it be well with you, O faithful wife. Accept a boon. For the sake of your protection, your husband—
m.2.3.35.46: May your husband become young, valiant in love and righteous, handsome, virtuous, eloquent, with youth that is ever constant.
m.2.3.35.47: May he be long-lived, surpassing Mārkaṇḍeya, O auspicious one; richer than Kubera and more lordly than Śakra.
m.2.3.35.48: May he be a devotee of Śiva equal to Hari, a perfected one surpassing Kapila, equal to Bṛhaspati in intellect, and equal to Vidhi in equanimity.
m.2.3.35.49: May you be endowed with the good fortune of having your husband for as long as you live; and likewise, O fortunate lady, may you be of lasting youth.
m.2.3.35.50: You will be the mother of ten sons, virtuous, long-lived and surpassing their own father—there is no doubt.
m.2.3.35.51: O virtuous woman, may your houses be filled with every kind of wealth, ever radiant, surpassing the mansion of Kubera.
m.2.3.35.52: Vasiṣṭha said: Having spoken thus, that Dharma stood still, O best of mountains. She circumambulated him, bowed, and went to her own home.
m.2.3.35.53: Dharma, having thus given blessings, went to his own abode, and with affection praised that Padmā in assembly after assembly.
m.2.3.35.54: She delighted constantly in private with her young husband. Afterwards good sons were born, surpassing their father in virtues.
m.2.3.35.55: All prosperity came to the couple, increasing their happiness, bringing growth of every joy, for their welfare both here and hereafter.
m.2.3.35.56: O lord of mountains, this whole ancient history of that couple has been told, and you have heard it with love and the highest respect.
m.2.3.35.57: Having understood the truth, give your daughter Pārvatī to Īśvara; give up your ill resentment, O lord of mountains, together with your wife Menā.
m.2.3.35.58: When a week has passed, at a rare and most auspicious moment, when the lord of the ascendant stands in the ascendant and the Moon is joined with its own son Budha,
m.2.3.35.59: the Moon being joyful and conjoined with Rohiṇī, the Moon and stars being pure, in the month of Mārgaśīrṣa, on a Monday free from all defects,
m.2.3.35.60: the moment being associated with all benefic planets and free from the aspect of malefic planets, with Jupiter granting good progeny and the good fortune of a husband,
m.2.3.35.61: —having given the maiden Girijā, the Mother of the world, the primordial Prakṛti, the sovereign Goddess, to the Father of the world, become fulfilled, O mountain.
m.2.3.35.62: Brahmā said: Having said this, Vasiṣṭha, tiger among sages and best of the wise, fell silent, remembering Śiva, the Lord who performs many divine sports.
m.2.3.35.iti: Thus ends the thirty-fifth adhyāya, named The story of Padmā and Pippalāda, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.3.36.1: Brahmā said: Having heard Vasiṣṭha's words, Himālaya, the lord of mountains, astonished, together with his retinue and his wife, spoke to the mountains.
m.2.3.36.2: Himavān said: O Meru, king of mountains, Sahya, Gandhamādana, Mandara, Maināka, Vindhya, O lords of mountains, all of you, listen to my words.
m.2.3.36.3: Vasiṣṭha speaks thus; what should I do? Let it be considered. Having decided everything in your minds, tell me how matters stand.
m.2.3.36.4: Brahmā said: Hearing his words, those mountains headed by Sumeru, having carefully decided, spoke affectionately to Himālaya.
m.2.3.36.5: The mountains said: What need now of deliberation? The matter is already settled just so. O fortunate one, she has been born solely for the purpose of the gods' task.
m.2.3.36.6: She must be given to Śiva, for she has incarnated for Śiva's sake. Rudra has been propitiated by her, and Rudra himself has spoken to her.
m.2.3.36.7: Brahmā said: Hearing these words of Meru and the others, Himācala became exceedingly pleased, and Girijā laughed in her heart.
m.2.3.36.8: And Arundhatī enlightened that Menā about the reason, with many kinds of words and various ancient tales.
m.2.3.36.9: Then Menakā, the mountain's wife, having understood, with a cheerful mind fed the sages, Arundhatī and the mountain, and then ate herself.
m.2.3.36.10: Then the wise best of mountains, having served those sages well, spoke with joined palms, affectionately, his mind serene and his confusion gone.
m.2.3.36.11: Himavān said: O fortunate Seven Sages, hear my words. All my astonishment is gone, now that I have heard the story of Śiva and Śivā.
m.2.3.36.12: My body, my wife Menā, my daughter, my sons, prosperity, success and everything else belong to Śiva alone, not otherwise.
m.2.3.36.13: Brahmā said: Having said this, he then looked at his daughter, and respectfully adorning her limbs, seated her on the lap of the sages.
m.2.3.36.14: And the king of mountains again spoke affectionately to the sages then: This portion is to be given by me to him — this is decided.
m.2.3.36.15: The sages said: Śaṅkara is the mendicant coming to you; you yourself, O mountain, are the giver; and the alms is the goddess Pārvatī — what could be more excellent than this?
m.2.3.36.16: O Himavat, because of this your state is equal to the loftiness of your peaks. Blessed are you, lord of all mountains, excellent in every way.
m.2.3.36.17: Brahmā said: Having spoken thus, the pure-minded sages gave their blessing to the maiden: Be a giver of happiness to Śiva.
m.2.3.36.18: Touching her there with their hands they said: Welfare will be yours. As the moon in the bright fortnight, so may your virtues grow.
m.2.3.36.19: Having said this, all the sages joyfully gave the mountain flowers along with fruits, and thereby made the pledge of betrothal then.
m.2.3.36.20: Then there the fair-faced Arundhatī, that supreme chaste lady, joyfully enticed Menā with the description of Śiva's virtues.
m.2.3.36.21: Following worldly custom, he smeared the mountain's beard with turmeric and saffron, an excellent auspicious rite.
m.2.3.36.22: Then, having fixed an excellent auspicious moment on the fourth day, and being mutually satisfied, they went to Śiva's presence.
m.2.3.36.23: Going there, bowing to Śiva and praising him with various hymns, all the sages headed by Vasiṣṭha spoke to the Supreme Lord.
m.2.3.36.24: The sages said: O God of gods, Mahādeva, Supreme Lord, great master, hear graciously our account of what has been done by your servants.
m.2.3.36.25: The king of mountains and Menā have been instructed with various sayings and ancient tales, O Maheśāna; he is fully awakened, no doubt.
m.2.3.36.26: Pārvatī has been promised to you by the lord of mountains, it is not otherwise. Go forth for the marriage, accompanied by your gaṇas and the gods.
m.2.3.36.27: Go quickly, O Mahādeva, O Lord, to Himācala's house, and marry Pārvatī according to custom, for the birth of your own offspring.
m.2.3.36.28: Brahmā said: Hearing their words, Maheśāna, intent on worldly custom, delighted at heart, laughed and said this.
m.2.3.36.29: Maheśa said: O fortunate ones, a marriage has been neither seen nor heard of by me. Its procedure, as practised of old, should be explained by you in detail.
m.2.3.36.30: Brahmā said: Hearing that auspicious, worldly speech of Maheśa, they laughingly replied to Sadāśiva, the God of gods.
m.2.3.36.31: The sages said: Summon quickly Viṣṇu especially, together with his retinue, Brahmā with his sons, lovingly, and likewise the god Śatakratu (Indra);
m.2.3.36.32: likewise all the hosts of sages, the Yakṣas, Gandharvas and Kinnaras, the Siddhas and Vidyādharas, and also the hosts of Apsarases.
m.2.3.36.33: Bring all these and others here respectfully, O Lord; they will accomplish all your work, no doubt.
m.2.3.36.34: Brahmā said: Having said this, the Seven Sages, receiving his permission, joyfully all went to their own abode, praising Śaṅkara's ways.
m.2.3.36.iti: Thus ends the thirty-sixth adhyāya, named The words of the seven sages, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.3.37.1: Nārada said: Dear father, O wise one, tell me now: when the seven sages had gone, what did the Himālaya mountain do? Show me your grace, O lord, and tell me that.
m.2.3.37.2: Brahmā said: O lord of sages, when all seven of those sages, together with Arundhatī, had gone, I shall tell you what Himavān did.
m.2.3.37.3: Then, having consulted his brothers Meru and the others, the great-hearted Himavān, lord of mountains, rejoiced together with his sons and his wife.
m.2.3.37.4: Then, so instructed by them, Himavān lovingly and with great delight had the letter fixing the auspicious marriage time written by Garga, his own family priest.
m.2.3.37.5: Then he sent that letter to Śiva, along with articles of many kinds, through his own people, who were joyful at heart.
m.2.3.37.6: Those people went there to Kailāsa into Śiva's presence, applied the tilaka to him, and gave the letter to Śiva.
m.2.3.37.7: Specially honoured by the Lord, as was fitting, they all came back, glad at heart, into the presence of the mountain.
m.2.3.37.8: Seeing his people return, specially honoured by Maheśa and overjoyed, the mountain rejoiced exceedingly in his heart.
m.2.3.37.9: Then, delighted, he sent invitations, a source of happiness, to all his kinsmen dwelling in various lands.
m.2.3.37.10: Then he carefully had a store of fine food gathered, and materials of many kinds suited to performing the wedding.
m.2.3.37.11: He made many mountains of rice, and likewise of flattened rice, of jaggery, of sugar, and likewise of salt;
m.2.3.37.12: he made pools of milk, of ghee and of curd, and likewise heaps of flour of barley and other grains, and of laḍḍus;
m.2.3.37.13: and of śaṣkulī cakes, svastika sweets and likewise sugar; and there he made pools of nectar-like sugarcane juice.
m.2.3.37.14: He made many pools of fresh butter and likewise of fermented drinks, and heaps of various cooked foods, and likewise very tasty juices;
m.2.3.37.15: various savoury dishes beneficial to the gaṇas and gods, and priceless garments of many kinds, such as were purified by fire;
m.2.3.37.16: kinds of jewels and gems, gold and silver: having gathered these and other articles according to rule,
m.2.3.37.17: the mountain began to perform the auspicious rites on an auspicious day. The mountain-women had the purificatory rite of Pārvatī performed.
m.2.3.37.18: Adorned themselves with ornaments, they joyfully performed the auspicious rite; the delighted brāhmaṇa women of the city carried out the customary folk observances,
m.2.3.37.19: various rites there with festivity, preceded by great auspiciousness. Himālaya too, glad at heart, having performed the very auspicious customary rite,
m.2.3.37.20: was wholly delighted and eager for the arrival of his kinsfolk. Meanwhile his kinsmen, who had been invited,
m.2.3.37.21: came, delighted, with their wives, sons and retinues. Listen attentively, O divine sage, to that very arrival of the mountains.
m.2.3.37.22: I shall describe it briefly, for the increase of love for Śiva. The great mountain that is the abode of the gods Meru, bearing a divine form,
m.2.3.37.23: with his company shining with many gems, together with his retinue, having carefully brought the choicest of many jewels and great gems,
m.2.3.37.24: adorned with fine attire, the glorious one went to Himālaya. Mandara, the mountain rich in every splendour, with his wife and sons,
m.2.3.37.25: went, taking various fine gifts. Astācala too, divine-natured and noble-minded, bearing gifts,
m.2.3.37.26: came full of joy, endowed with great splendour. Udayācala, bringing fine gems and jewels too,
m.2.3.37.27: came most happy, with a most excellent retinue. Malaya, king of mountains, honoured, with his retinue,
m.2.3.37.28: came, adorned with very divine arrangements and with a large, fine army. And promptly the one named Dardura, joyful, with his wife,
m.2.3.37.29: full of great splendour, dear one, went to the house of the Himālaya mountain. Niṣada too, glad at heart, came with his retinue;
m.2.3.37.30: with his sons and womenfolk he lovingly went to the house of the Himālaya mountain. The greatly fortunate mountain Gandhamādana came,
m.2.3.37.31: and likewise Karavīra, endowed with great wealth. Mahendra, best of mountains, came to Himālaya,
m.2.3.37.32: with his attendants, sons and wife, endowed with great splendour. Pāriyātra, glad at heart, laden with mines of jewels and gems,
m.2.3.37.33: came to the Himālaya mountain with his attendants and retinue. Krauñca, king of mountains, with a retinue of great strength, the best of mountains, came respectfully with gifts.
m.2.3.37.34: The Puruṣottama mountain too, respectful, with his retinue, came to the Himālaya mountain bringing a great gift.
m.2.3.37.35: Nīla, playful, with his sons and wife, laden with goods, came full of joy to the house of the snow mountain.
m.2.3.37.36: Trikūṭa, Citrakūṭa too, Veṅkaṭa and likewise Śrīgiri, Gokāmukhī and Nārada came to Himālaya's home.
m.2.3.37.37: And Vindhya, best of mountains, endowed with manifold riches, auspicious, came glad at heart with his wife and sons.
m.2.3.37.38: Kālañjara, the great mountain, filled with great joy, lovingly came to the Himālaya mountain with many of his own attendants.
m.2.3.37.39: And Kailāsa, the great mountain, filled with great joy, the lord shining above all, came out of kindness.
m.2.3.37.40: O brāhmaṇa, the other mountains that are in other continents too, and all the mountains that are here as well, came to Himālaya.
m.2.3.37.41: O sage, the mountains whom he had joyfully invited there beforehand all came with affection, thinking, it is the wedding of Śiva and Śivā.
m.2.3.37.42: Then indeed all of them, Śoṇabhadra and the others, came, greatly splendid, with great affection, thinking, it is the wedding of Śiva and Śivā.
m.2.3.37.43: All the rivers came, adorned with various ornaments and bearing divine forms, with affection, thinking, it is the wedding of Śiva and Śivā.
m.2.3.37.44: Godāvarī and Yamunā, and likewise Brahmā's consort Sarasvatī and Veṇikā came to the Himālaya mountain, thinking, it is the wedding of Śiva and Śivā.
m.2.3.37.45: Gaṅgā, with very great joy, adorned with various ornaments and divine in form, came with affection, thinking, it is the wedding of Śiva and Śivā.
m.2.3.37.46: Narmadā, the daughter of Rudra and best of rivers, full of great delight, came quickly with great affection, thinking, it is the wedding of Śiva and Śivā.
m.2.3.37.47: Then, with all of them arriving from every side at the Himālaya mountain, the divine city, endowed with every splendour, became crowded.
m.2.3.37.48: It was full of great festivity, abounding in gleaming banners, flags and arched gateways; the sun was screened off by canopies, and it shone with manifold brilliance.
m.2.3.37.49: Himālaya too, with great affection and respect of many kinds, honoured them — the mountains and the rivers — each as was fitting.
m.2.3.37.50: He lodged them all separately in fine quarters and satisfied them completely with abundant provisions.
m.2.3.37.iti: Thus ends the thirty-seventh adhyāya, named The sending of the wedding letter, the gathering of provisions and the coming of the mountains, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.3.38.1: Brahmā said: Then, O best of sages, Himavān, the lord of mountains, pleased, adorned his own city wonderfully for a supreme festival.
m.2.3.38.2: Its roads were sprinkled with water, cleaned, and adorned with the highest splendours; and at every door there were auspicious decorations of plantains and the like, furnished with auspicious articles.
m.2.3.38.3: He arranged the courtyard with plantain-trunk pillars, bound together with silk cords and decorated with mango sprouts,
m.2.3.38.4: furnished with garlands of mālatī jasmine, resplendent with shining arches, and adorned with auspicious articles placed in the four directions.
m.2.3.38.5: In the same way, filled with supreme joy, the king of mountains did everything for the sake of his own daughter, placing the greatly powerful Garga at the front, doing all that was fitting for the occasion and highly auspicious.
m.2.3.38.6: Having summoned Viśvakarman, he respectfully had him build a very spacious pavilion, charming with altars and the like.
m.2.3.38.7: O celestial sage, it extended over ten thousand yojanas, possessed of many excellent features and filled with various wonders.
m.2.3.38.8: All things there, moving and unmoving, were charmingly made in the likeness of the real ones; it was on every side a treasury of marvels, astonishing with various objects.
m.2.3.38.9: There the moving was especially surpassed by the unmoving, and the unmoving too was surpassed by the moving.
m.2.3.38.10: There dry ground was outdone by water, and water not otherwise by ground; no experts at all could tell what was water and what was land.
m.2.3.38.11: In some places there were artificial lions, in some rows of cranes, and in some places charming artificial peacocks.
m.2.3.38.12: In some places artificial women were dancing with men, bewitching all people; and likewise artificial women were gazing on.
m.2.3.38.13: Likewise, in the same manner, there were charming doorkeepers holding bows raised in their hands, motionless yet seeming alive.
m.2.3.38.14: At the door stood a wondrous artificial Mahālakṣmī, possessed of all auspicious marks, as if she had come directly from the ocean of milk.
m.2.3.38.15: There were adorned artificial elephants, like real ones; likewise horses with their riders, and elephants with elephant-riders.
m.2.3.38.16: Chariots drawn by charioteers, full of great wonder; likewise other vehicles and foot-soldiers, all artificial.
m.2.3.38.17: Thus, O sage, all this was made by Viśvakarman with a delighted heart, for the purpose of enchanting the gods and the sages.
m.2.3.38.18: At the main gate, O sage, an artificial Nandin was made, resembling pure crystal; he was exactly like Nandin himself.
m.2.3.38.19: Above it was a very divine Puṣpaka aerial car, decked with jewels, gleaming with bright sprouts and beautifully adorned with chowries.
m.2.3.38.20: On the left side were two elephants, the colour of pure saffron, four-tusked, sixty years old, in rut, greatly resplendent.
m.2.3.38.21: Likewise he made two horses, radiant like the sun, greatly brilliant, divine, adorned with chowries and decked with divine ornaments.
m.2.3.38.22: Likewise the guardians of the worlds, armoured and rich in fine jewels, and all the gods, were made by Viśvakarman true to life.
m.2.3.38.23: So too all the sages, Bhṛgu and the others rich in austerity, and other demigods likewise, and other Siddhas too, were made.
m.2.3.38.24: Likewise an artificial Viṣṇu was fashioned, accompanied by all his attendants headed by Garuḍa, of supremely wondrous form.
m.2.3.38.25: In the same way, O Nārada, an artificial image of me was fashioned, surrounded by my sons, the Vedas and the Siddhas, reciting hymns.
m.2.3.38.26: Likewise an artificial Śakra was fashioned, mounted on the elephant Airāvata, accompanied by his retinue, resembling the full moon.
m.2.3.38.27: What need of saying much, O divine sage? The whole assembly of the gods was swiftly fashioned by Viśvakarman, urged on by the Snow Mountain.
m.2.3.38.28: Such was the pavilion made by him: of divine form, full of many wonders, vast, bewildering even to the gods.
m.2.3.38.29: Then, commanded by the lord of mountains, the highly intelligent Viśvakarman carefully built the respective worlds for the residence of the gods and others.
m.2.3.38.30: And right there great couches, very bright, supremely wondrous, comfortable and divine, were made for them by Viśvakarman.
m.2.3.38.31: Likewise, in a moment, he created a wondrous Satyaloka, endowed with supreme radiance, for the residence of the Self-born (Brahmā).
m.2.3.38.32: In the same way he created in a moment for Viṣṇu another abode called Vaikuṇṭha, greatly brilliant, divine, full of various wonders.
m.2.3.38.33: Likewise that Viśvakarman created the divine, wondrous and excellent mansion of the lord of the immortals (Indra), endowed with every splendour.
m.2.3.38.34: He likewise gladly created beautiful houses for the guardians of the worlds, divine, wondrous and great.
m.2.3.38.35: And likewise, in due order, wonderful dwellings were made by him for all the other immortals.
m.2.3.38.36: Viśvakarman of great intellect, who had obtained a great boon from Śambhu, created everything in a moment, solely for the satisfaction of Śiva.
m.2.3.38.37: Likewise he made Śambhu's mansion: supremely wonderful, greatly brilliant, very radiant, well worshipped by the foremost gods, bearing the emblems of the Mountain-Lord (Śiva), set as in Śivaloka, beautifully adorned.
m.2.3.38.38: Such was the construction made by Viśvakarman for Śiva's satisfaction: varied, supremely wondrous and greatly brilliant.
m.2.3.38.39: Having thus done all this, along with the worldly customs, Himācala joyfully awaited the arrival of Śambhu.
m.2.3.38.40: Thus, O divine sage, the delightful account of Himālaya has been told in full. What more do you wish to hear?
m.2.3.38.iti: Thus ends the thirty-eighth adhyāya, named The building of the pavilion and the rest, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.3.39.1: Nārada said: O Vidhi (Brahmā), dear father, greatly wise one, disciple of Viṣṇu, salutation to you. This wondrous story has been heard by us from you, O treasure of compassion.
m.2.3.39.2: Now I wish to hear the marriage-story of the moon-crested Śiva, most auspicious, destroying all floods of sin.
m.2.3.39.3: What did Mahādeva do on receiving the auspicious letter? Narrate to me that divine story of Śaṅkara, the Supreme Self.
m.2.3.39.4: Brahmā said: Listen, dear child, greatly wise one, to the supreme glory of Śaṅkara — what Mahādeva did on receiving the auspicious letter.
m.2.3.39.5: Then Śambhu, taking that auspicious letter with joy, laughed, delighted at heart; the all-pervading Lord showed honour to them the messengers.
m.2.3.39.6: Having had it read out properly, he accepted it according to rule; and, respectful, he sent those people off after honouring them greatly.
m.2.3.39.7: He said to those groups of sages: The task has been done well and auspiciously. You must come to my wedding; the marriage has been accepted by me.
m.2.3.39.8: Hearing these words of Śambhu, they, overjoyed, bowed to him, circumambulated him and went to their abodes, extolling their own supreme good fortune.
m.2.3.39.9: Then Śambhu, lord of the gods, the Lord who performs great sports, following worldly custom, quickly remembered you, O sage.
m.2.3.39.10: You came with great love, praising your supreme good fortune, bowing, with lowered shoulders, humble in spirit, with joined palms.
m.2.3.39.11: You praised him, uttering cries of victory again and again, requesting his command and extolling your good fortune, O sage.
m.2.3.39.12: Then Śambhu, delighted at heart, displaying the worldly way, spoke to you, O best of sages, gladdening you with auspicious words.
m.2.3.39.13: Śiva said: Listen with love, O best of sages; today I tell you from myself. I tell you this because you are dear to me, the crest-jewel among the kings of devotees.
m.2.3.39.14: Great austerity was performed by the goddess Pārvatī at your instruction. Pleased, I granted her the boon of having me as husband.
m.2.3.39.15: And I shall marry her, for I am subject to her through her devotion. The auspicious moment has been fixed by the seven sages and verified by them.
m.2.3.39.16: It will take place on the seventh day from today, O Nārada. Following the worldly way, I shall hold a great festival.
m.2.3.39.17: Brahmā said: Having heard these words of Śaṅkara, the Supreme Self, you, dear son, with a glad mind, bowed to the Lord and spoke these words.
