m.2.3.39.18: Nārada said: This indeed is your vow: you are regarded as subject to your devotees. And you have rightly fulfilled what Pārvatī desired in her heart.
m.2.3.39.19: Some task fit for me should be told by you, O Lord. Regarding me as your own servant, show me grace; salutation to you.
m.2.3.39.20: Brahmā said: Thus addressed by you, Śambhu Śaṅkara, loving to his devotees, glad at heart, replied to you respectfully, O lord of sages.
m.2.3.39.21: Śiva said: On my word, O sage, invite without fail the gods headed by Viṣṇu, the sages and the Siddhas, and others too, from everywhere.
m.2.3.39.22: Let all come eagerly, adorned with every splendour, with their wives, sons and retinues, out of love and out of regard for my command.
m.2.3.39.23: Those gods and others who do not come here to my wedding festival, O sage, shall surely not be regarded by me as my own.
m.2.3.39.24: Brahmā said: Then you, beloved of Śaṅkara, bearing the Lord's command, quickly went to each one and invited them all, O sage.
m.2.3.39.25: After that invitation, you, the best of sages, quickly came back to Śambhu's presence and, receiving his permission, remained there, O Nārada.
m.2.3.39.26: Śiva too waited eagerly, longing for their arrival, with all his Gaṇas festive and dancing in every direction.
m.2.3.39.27: At that very time Acyuta (Viṣṇu), having arrayed himself in his attire, quickly came to Kailāsa with his retinue.
m.2.3.39.28: Having joyfully bowed to Śiva with true devotion, together with his wife and his host, and receiving his permission, he stayed in a fine place, pleased at heart.
m.2.3.39.29: Likewise I quickly and joyfully went to Kailāsa with my attendants, and having bowed to the Lord, I stayed there, delighted, accompanied by my followers.
m.2.3.39.30: Indra and the other guardians of the worlds came with their retinues, all likewise adorned, festive, and with their wives.
m.2.3.39.31: In the same way the sages, Nāgas, Siddhas and Upasuras, and others too, duly invited, came here festively.
m.2.3.39.32: Then Maheśvara joyfully honoured each of all the gods and others who had come there, one by one.
m.2.3.39.33: Then there was a great, supremely wondrous festival on Kailāsa; the celestial women then performed dances and the like, as was fitting.
m.2.3.39.34: At this time all the gods headed by Viṣṇu who had assembled stayed there, O sage, in order to conduct Śambhu's wedding procession.
m.2.3.39.35: Then all of them, commanded by Śiva and bound by the thought, this is our own task, did all this work of Śiva as service to Śiva.
m.2.3.39.36: The Seven Mothers there, filled with joy, performed the supreme rite of adorning Śiva, again as was fitting.
m.2.3.39.37: Then, by the will of that Supreme Lord, the glorious master, O best of sages, his natural attire itself became his adornment.
m.2.3.39.38: The moon then took its place as the crown, and the beautiful third eye became an auspicious tilaka.
m.2.3.39.39: And the two serpents known as his ear-ornaments became his earrings, set with many kinds of gems, O sage.
m.2.3.39.40: The serpents on his other limbs became ornaments for those limbs, exceedingly lovely and made of many kinds of gems.
m.2.3.39.41: The sacred ash became a body-ointment made from sandal and the like, and the elephant hide and the rest became that beautiful divine silken garment.
m.2.3.39.42: Such a beautiful form came about, extremely hard to describe. The Lord himself, in person, attained majesty of his own accord.
m.2.3.39.43: Then all the gods and dānavas, the nāgas, birds, apsarases and great sages, all gathering at that time in Śiva's presence, in great festive mood and full of joy, exclaimed, Aho!
m.2.3.39.44: They all said: Go, go, Mahādeva, O Maheśvara, for your marriage with Girijā, the great goddess; together with us, show your grace.
m.2.3.39.45: Then Viṣṇu, his mind gladdened by understanding, bowed to Śaṅkara with devotion and spoke these words suited to the occasion.
m.2.3.39.46: Viṣṇu said: O God of gods, Mahādeva, loving to those who come for refuge, accomplisher of the tasks of your devotees, O Lord, hear my request.
m.2.3.39.47: O Śambhu, O Śaṅkara, you should perform here the rite of your own marriage with the goddess, daughter of the lord of mountains, according to the procedure laid down in the Gṛhya texts.
m.2.3.39.48: And when the marriage rite is being performed by you, O Hara, that very procedure will thereby gain full renown throughout the world.
m.2.3.39.49: O Lord, gladly have the erection of the pavilion and the Nāndīmukha rite performed according to that family custom, proclaiming your own glory in the world.
m.2.3.39.50: Brahmā said: Thus addressed by Viṣṇu, Śambhu, the supreme Lord, intent on worldly custom, then did that according to the rules.
m.2.3.39.51: Authorized by him, I, together with the sages, gladly and respectfully performed there everything fitting for the auspicious occasion, that whole rite.
m.2.3.39.52: Kaśyapa, Atri and Vasiṣṭha, Gautama, Bhāguri, the preceptor Bṛhaspati's kin? — rather: Gautama, Bhāguri, Guru, Kaṇva, Bṛhaspati, Śakti, Jamadagni, Parāśara,
m.2.3.39.53: Mārkaṇḍeya, Śilāpāka, Aruṇapāla, Akṛtaśrama, Agastya, Cyavana, Garga and Śilāda, O great sage,
m.2.3.39.54: Dadhīci and Upamanyu, Bharadvāja, Akṛtavraṇa, Pippalāda, Kuśika, Kautsa, and Vyāsa with his disciples—
m.2.3.39.55: These and many others came to Śiva's presence; well urged by me, they performed the rite there according to rule.
m.2.3.39.56: All of them, masters of the Vedas and Vedāṅgas, performed the protective rite for Maheśa by the Vedic procedure, after carrying out the auspicious kautuka wedding-thread ceremony.
m.2.3.39.57: With hymns of the Ṛg, Yajus and Sāman, and likewise with various other excellent ones, all the sages gladly performed many auspicious rites.
m.2.3.39.58: Together with Śambhu and me, they gladly performed the worship of the planets and of all the gods stationed in the maṇḍala, for the removal of obstacles.
m.2.3.39.59: Then Śiva, well pleased, having done everything properly—both worldly and Vedic rites—joyfully bowed to the brāhmaṇas.
m.2.3.39.60: Then the Lord of all, placing the brāhmaṇas and gods in front, joyfully set out from that Kailāsa, the best of mountains.
m.2.3.39.61: Outside the Kailāsa mountain Śambhu, the Lord, stood joyfully together with the gods and brāhmaṇas, accepting various honours.
m.2.3.39.62: Then a great festival took place there, held by the gods and others for Maheśa's delight, with singing, instrumental music and fine dancing.
m.2.3.39.iti: Thus ends the thirty-ninth adhyāya, named The invitation of the gods, the coming of the gods and Śiva's journey, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.3.40.1: Brahmā said: Then Śambhu, having summoned all the gaṇas headed by Nandin, joyfully commanded them to go there together with himself.
m.2.3.40.2: Śiva said: You too, come along with me to the mountain's city, leaving some gaṇas here, with great festivity.
m.2.3.40.3: Brahmā said: Then, thus permitted, the lords of the gaṇas set out joyfully, each taking his own force; I shall describe them in some measure.
m.2.3.40.4: Śaṅkhakarṇa, lord of gaṇas, went forth with a crore of gaṇas to proceed with Śiva toward the city of Himācala.
m.2.3.40.5: Kekarākṣa, full of great festive joy, went with ten crores of gaṇas, and Vikṛta, leader of gaṇas, with eight crores of gaṇas.
m.2.3.40.6: Viśākha, leader of gaṇas, went with four crores of gaṇas, and Pārijāta, foremost of gaṇas, with nine crores.
m.2.3.40.7: The glorious Sarvāntaka went with sixty crores, and likewise Vikṛtānana; Dundubha, leader of gaṇas, with eight crores of gaṇas.
m.2.3.40.8: Likewise the gaṇa-lord named Kapāla went with five crores, and the heroic Sandāraka with six crores of gaṇas, O sage.
m.2.3.40.9: Here Kanduka and likewise Kuṇḍaka went with crores upon crores, and Viṣṭambha, a gaṇa-chief, likewise with eight crores of gaṇas.
m.2.3.40.10: The gaṇa-chief Pippala went joyfully with a thousand crores, and so did the heroic gaṇa-lord Sanādaka, O best of sages.
m.2.3.40.11: Likewise Āveśana, leader of gaṇas, went with eight crores; the gaṇa-chief Mahākeśa went with a thousand crores.
m.2.3.40.12: Kuṇḍa went with twelve crores, and likewise Parvataka, O sage; the heroic Candratāpana went along with eight crores.
m.2.3.40.13: Kāla, Kālaka, and Mahākāla went with a hundred crores, and likewise the gaṇa-lord named Agnika.
m.2.3.40.14: Agnimukha, leader of gaṇas, went with a crore; and Ādityamūrdhan with a crore, and likewise Ghanāvaha.
m.2.3.40.15: Sannāha went with a hundred crores, and likewise the gaṇa-chief Kumuda; Amogha and Kokila, overlords of gaṇas, with a hundred crores.
m.2.3.40.16: Sumantra, leader of gaṇas, went with crores upon crores; Kākapādodara with sixty crores, and likewise Santānaka.
m.2.3.40.17: Mahābala with nine crores, and Madhupiṅga and Kokila; Nīla with ninety crores, and likewise Pūrṇabhadra.
m.2.3.40.18: Caturvaktra went with seven crores, Karaṇa with twenty crores, and the gaṇa-lord Ahiromaka went with ninety crores.
m.2.3.40.19: Yajvākṣa, Śatamanyu and Meghamanyu, O Nārada—all these gaṇa-lords went, each separately, with as many crores.
m.2.3.40.20: Kāṣṭhāṅguṣṭha, leader of gaṇas, went with sixty-four crores; also Virūpākṣa, Sukeśa, and the eternal Vṛṣabha,
m.2.3.40.21: Tālaketu, Ṣaḍāsya, the eternal Cañcvāsya, Saṃvartaka, likewise Caitra, Lakulīśa the self-ruling lord,
m.2.3.40.22: Lokāntaka, the radiant-souled Dīptātman, likewise Daityāntaka, O sage, the divine and glorious Bhṛṅgiriṭi, and likewise Devadevapriya,
m.2.3.40.23: Aśani and Bhānuka, each with sixty-four crores by thousands, went festively with Śiva for Śiva's wedding.
m.2.3.40.24: The Pramathas went with a thousand crores of bhūtas and three crores more; Vīrabhadra with sixty-four crores and three crores of the Romajas (born of his hair).
m.2.3.40.25: Surrounded by twenty hundreds of thousands of crores of crores, the gaṇa-chiefs headed by Nandin went there to Śaṅkara's festival.
m.2.3.40.26: Kṣetrapāla and Bhairava, accompanied by crores upon crores of gaṇas, came lovingly in great festivity, thinking, it is Śaṅkara's wedding.
m.2.3.40.27: These and other countless, mighty gaṇa-chiefs went there with great love and enthusiasm to Śaṅkara's festival.
m.2.3.40.28: All were thousand-handed, wearing crowns of matted hair, adorned with the crescent moon, blue-throated and three-eyed.
m.2.3.40.29: All wore rudrākṣa ornaments and holy ash, and were adorned with necklaces, earrings, armlets, crowns and the like.
m.2.3.40.30: Resembling Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Indra, endowed with powers such as aṇimā, and shining like crores of suns, the lords of gaṇas looked splendid there.
m.2.3.40.31: Some moved on the earth, some in the netherworld, some in the sky, and some in the seven heavens, O sage.
m.2.3.40.32: What need of saying more, O divine sage? Śambhu's own gaṇas, dwelling in all the worlds, came lovingly to Śaṅkara's festival.
m.2.3.40.33: Thus, accompanied by the gods, the gaṇas and others, Lord Śaṅkara went to the city of Himagiri for his own wedding.
m.2.3.40.34: When the Lord of all went for his wedding with the gods and others, what happened there—hear that, O lord of sages.
m.2.3.40.35: Becoming Rudra's sister, Caṇḍī, full of festive spirit, came there with great delight, bringing great terror to others.
m.2.3.40.36: Mounted on a corpse as her seat, adorned with serpent ornaments, carrying on her head a full golden pitcher of great brilliance,
m.2.3.40.37: accompanied by her own retinue, with blazing face and blazing eyes, playing about in sport, filled with joy, of mighty strength.
m.2.3.40.38: There, O sage, divine hosts of bhūtas, misshapen, by crores and of many kinds, then shone in great numbers.
m.2.3.40.39: Joined by them, Caṇḍī of distorted face went in front, full of playfulness, delighted, causing playful mischief out of affection.
m.2.3.40.40: Then all the gaṇas of Rudra, numbering eleven crores, fierce and dear to Rudra, were placed behind by Caṇḍī.
m.2.3.40.41: Then the three worlds were filled with the booming of ḍamaru drums, with the clanging sound of bherī drums, and with the blare of conches.
m.2.3.40.42: Likewise, with the thunder of dundubhi drums, a tumultuous sound arose, bringing auspiciousness to the world and dispelling whatever was inauspicious.
m.2.3.40.43: Following behind the gaṇas, all the gods, full of eagerness, went along, together with all the Siddhas and the guardians of the worlds and others, O sage.
m.2.3.40.44: Then the Lord of Ramā (Viṣṇu), moving in the middle, seated on Garuḍa, shone with a great parasol held over him, O sage.
m.2.3.40.45: He was being fanned with chowries, surrounded by his own attendants and by radiant companions, and adorned in the manner of his own ornaments.
m.2.3.40.46: So too I Brahmā shone forth, moving along the path, resplendent, accompanied by the embodied Vedas, the Śāstras, the Purāṇas and the Āgamas,
m.2.3.40.47: and by Sanaka and the other great Siddhas, and by my sons together with the Prajāpatis; joined with my retinue, I was intent on serving Śiva.
m.2.3.40.48: Śakra, lord of the gods, in the midst of his own army, mounted on the elephant Airāvata and exceedingly adorned with various ornaments, shone as he went.
m.2.3.40.49: Then those many sages, going along, shone forth, exceedingly eager for Śiva's wedding.
m.2.3.40.50: Śākinīs, Yātudhānas, Vetālas, Brahmarākṣasas, Bhūtas, Pretas and Piśācas, and likewise others, the Pramathas and the rest, went along.
m.2.3.40.51: Tumburu, Nārada, Hāhā and Hūhū and other excellent Gandharvas, and the Kinnaras, went joyfully, sounding their instruments.
m.2.3.40.52: All the Mothers of the world and the daughters of the gods from every side, Gāyatrī and Sāvitrī, Lakṣmī and other celestial women,
m.2.3.40.53: these and others—the wives of the gods, mothers of the world—all went filled with joy, thinking, it is Śaṅkara's wedding.
m.2.3.40.54: The bull, shining like pure crystal and beautiful in every way, who is called Dharma by the Vedas, the Śāstras, the Siddhas and the great sages—
m.2.3.40.55: mounted on that bull, Mahādeva, who loves Dharma, shone exceedingly as he went, attended by all the gods and sages.
m.2.3.40.56: Accompanied by these and by the great sages whose aims were fulfilled, Maheśa, richly adorned in many ways, shone as he proceeded to the abode of the mountain named Himālaya for the taking of Śivā's hand in marriage.
m.2.3.40.57: Thus has been told the story of Śambhu—his journey, a supreme festival. Now hear, O Nārada, the noble account of what took place in the city of Himālaya.
m.2.3.40.iti: Thus ends the fortieth adhyāya, named Śiva's journey, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.3.41.1: Brahmā said: Then, having consulted together and having received Śaṅkara's command, Hari, O sage, sent you first to the abode of the mountain.
m.2.3.41.2: Then, having bowed to the Lord of all, you, Nārada, urged affectionately by Hari, went ahead towards the house of Himācala.
m.2.3.41.3: Having gone there, O sage, you saw yourself—an artificial likeness fashioned there by Viśvakarman—and, astonished, you were filled with embarrassment.
m.2.3.41.4: O great sage, you were wearied by that artificial self of yours; you became intent on gazing at the handiwork of Viśvakarman.
m.2.3.41.5: You entered the pavilion of that Himādri, adorned with jewels, furnished with golden pitchers and greatly beautified with plantain trees and the like,
m.2.3.41.6: furnished with a thousand pillars, wonderful and supremely marvellous; and seeing the altar likewise, O sage, you fell into amazement.
m.2.3.41.7: Then, O sage Nārada, greatly astonished in mind, with your understanding lost and your intellect bewildered, you said to the lord of mountains:
m.2.3.41.8: Have the gods headed by Viṣṇu arrived now? And likewise all the great sages, the Siddhas and the demigods?
m.2.3.41.9: Has Mahādeva, mounted on the bull and surrounded by the Gaṇas, come for the wedding? Tell the truth, O lord of mountains.
m.2.3.41.10: Brahmā said: Hearing these words of yours, whose mind was astonished, O sage, that mountain Himavat spoke truthful words to you.
m.2.3.41.11: Himavān said: O Nārada, most wise one, Śiva has not yet come for the marriage of Pārvatī, with his Gaṇas and the wedding party.
m.2.3.41.12: Know with a clear mind, Nārada, that this is a marvel made by Viśvakarman. Give up your amazement, O divine sage; be at ease and remember Śiva.
m.2.3.41.13: Having eaten and rested, well pleased, show me kindness and go to Śaṅkara together with Maināka and the other mountains.
m.2.3.41.14: Accompanied by these mountains, O great-minded one, entreat Śiva and quickly bring him here, together with the gods and the hosts of great sages—he whose tender lotus-feet are worshipped by gods and demons.
m.2.3.41.15: Brahmā said: Saying, so be it, you, high-minded one, having duly finished your tasks there and having eaten, went quickly at once with those sons of the mountain and others to the presence of Śiva.
m.2.3.41.16: There the radiant Mahādeva, surrounded by the gods and others, was seen, and was saluted with devotion by you and by those mountains.
m.2.3.41.17: Then, together with me and Viṣṇu, all the gods with Vāsava, O sage, and likewise all the attendants of Rudra questioned you,
m.2.3.41.18: astonished and with minds troubled by doubt on seeing the mountains Maināka, Sahya, Meru and the rest, adorned with various ornaments.
m.2.3.41.19: The gods said: O Nārada, most wise, you appear astonished. Were you honoured by the Himālaya or not? Tell us in detail.
m.2.3.41.20: Why have these excellent mountains come here—Maināka, Sahya, Meru and the others—most majestic and finely adorned?
m.2.3.41.21: Will that mountain give his daughter to Śambhu or not, Nārada? What is happening today in Himālaya's house, dear one? Tell us that.
m.2.3.41.22: Speak to us gods, whose minds are thus in doubt and who are asking you; remove our doubt, O you of good vows.
m.2.3.41.23: Brahmā said: Having heard these words of the gods led by Viṣṇu, O sage, you, astonished by the magic of Tvaṣṭṛ, spoke to them.
m.2.3.41.24: Taking us aside, O sage, you spoke these words to me, to Viṣṇu, and to Śacī's lord, ruler of all the gods, the wing-cutter, the old enemy of the mountains.
m.2.3.41.25: Nārada said: That strange, wondrous display made by Tvaṣṭṛ is bewildering to all the gods; by it he wishes to bewilder all the gods, through a contrivance, out of sheer affection.
m.2.3.41.26: Formerly you dealt him a bewildering blow; you have entirely forgotten all that, O lord of Śacī. Therefore he surely wishes to get the better of you in the house of that great-souled mountain.
m.2.3.41.27: I was bewildered by him with a shining replica of myself; likewise Viṣṇu was made by him, and Brahmā and Śakra too in the same way.
m.2.3.41.28: What need of much talk, O lord of gods? All the hosts of gods have been made artificially as images; nothing has been left out.
m.2.3.41.29: To bewilder everyone, and the gods especially, an illusion made of images has been created, producing jest and mischief.
m.2.3.41.30: Brahmā said: Hearing his words, the lord of gods, his body shaken with fear, quickly spoke then to Viṣṇu, Hari:
m.2.3.41.31: Indra said: O God of gods, lord of Ramā, Tvaṣṭṛ will kill me. Burning with grief for his son, he will do it by this pretext, not otherwise.
m.2.3.41.32: Brahmā said: Hearing his words, Janārdana, the God of gods, laughing, spoke then, reassuring Śakra:
m.2.3.41.33: Viṣṇu said: Formerly, O lord of Śacī, you were bewildered by the Nivātakavacas, Dānavas and old enemies, through the power of great magic.
m.2.3.41.34: This mountain Himavat and all the other mountains were made wingless by you, O Vāsava, at my word.
m.2.3.41.35: These foolish mountains, remembering that and seeing you, wish to conquer you by illusion; but there is no need to fear even an enemy such as this.
m.2.3.41.36: Śaṅkara, kind to his devotees, is the Lord of us all; he will bring about well-being in every way, Śakra, without doubt.
m.2.3.41.37: Brahmā said: Śakra, his mind disturbed, was conversing thus, and Hari had spoken; then Giriśa, adopting the manner of the world, spoke.
m.2.3.41.38: Īśvara said: O Hari, O lord of gods, what are you two saying to each other now? Having said this to the two, Maheśāna then addressed you, O sage:
m.2.3.41.39: What does the great mountain say? Tell it truly, Nārada. Relate the whole account; you should not keep anything secret.
m.2.3.41.40: Does the mountain give his own daughter or not? Tell me that quickly. What did you see, and what was done when you went there? Tell all of it gladly and at once, dear one.
m.2.3.41.41: Brahmā said: Thus addressed there by Śambhu, O sage, you, who have vision of the divine, told the whole secret: what had been seen there in the pavilion.
m.2.3.41.42: Nārada said: O God of gods, Mahādeva, listen to my auspicious words. There is no fear of any obstacle at all in the marriage, O Lord.
m.2.3.41.43: The lord of mountains will certainly give you the maiden. These mountains have come to fetch you; there is no doubt.
m.2.3.41.44: But a wondrous illusion has been fashioned to bewilder the immortals, for amusement, O all-knowing one; there is no possibility of any obstacle.
m.2.3.41.45: At his command, O Lord, Viśvakarmā, the great master of illusion, made in his house a marvellous pavilion full of many wonders.
m.2.3.41.46: And a bewildering assembly of all the gods was fashioned there. Seeing it, I was struck with amazement, deluded by that illusion.
m.2.3.41.47: Brahmā said: Hearing those words, dear one, the Lord Śambhu, who acts according to worldly custom, laughingly addressed Hari and all the other gods.
m.2.3.41.48: Īśvara said: If the mountain Himācala is going to give me the maiden, what have I to do with illusion? Tell me truly, O Viṣṇu.
m.2.3.41.49: O Brahmā, Śakra, sages and gods, tell me truly: what have I to do with illusion, if the mountain is going to give the maiden?
m.2.3.41.50: The goal is to be achieved by some means or other—so say the learned who know sound reasoning. Therefore let all of you, seeking the aim, led by Viṣṇu, go quickly.
m.2.3.41.51: Brahmā said: Conversing thus with the gods, Śambhu, though self-controlled, then became as if brought under the sway of Smara, like an ordinary man.
m.2.3.41.52: Then, at Śambhu's command, all the immortals headed by Viṣṇu, and the great-souled sages, went to that place which brings delusion and bewilderment.
m.2.3.41.53: Placing you, O sage, and those mountains at the front, they, full of wonder, then went to the supremely marvellous mansion of Himādri.
m.2.3.41.54: Then Hara, joined by Viṣṇu and the others and accompanied by his own delighted hosts, came joyfully near the city of the Snowy Mountain.
m.2.3.41.iti: Thus ends the forty-first adhyāya, named The building of the pavilion, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.3.42.1: Brahmā said: Then Himālaya, lord of the mountains, hearing that the all-pervading Lord had arrived near his own city, rejoiced exceedingly.
m.2.3.42.2: Then, having gathered all the requisites, he sent out the mountains and also the brahmins, all of them, to greet and converse with the Lord.
m.2.3.42.3: The mountain himself went with true devotion to see the Lord, dear to him as life, his mind melting with devotion, joyfully praising his own good fortune.
m.2.3.42.4: Seeing then the army of the gods, Himavat was filled with wonder, and he went forward to meet it there, thinking, I am blessed.
m.2.3.42.5: The gods too, seeing his host, were struck with supreme wonder; and the gods as well as the mountains attained supreme joy.
m.2.3.42.6: O sage, the great host of the mountains and that of the gods, meeting together, shone like the eastern and western oceans joining.
m.2.3.42.7: Meeting one another, the gods and the mountains considered themselves fulfilled, with supreme joy.
m.2.3.42.8: Then, seeing the Lord before him, Himālaya bowed; all the mountains and the brahmins bowed to Sadāśiva —
m.2.3.42.9: — seated on the bull, with a gracious face, adorned with various ornaments, illuminating the regions of space with the loveliness of his divine limbs;
m.2.3.42.10: his body resplendent in very fine, new, excellent silk garments, his crown gleaming with fine jewels, smiling, of pure radiance;
m.2.3.42.11: his limbs bearing serpents that served as ornaments, with wondrous radiance of limbs, of divine lustre, attended by the lords of the gods with chowries in their hands;
m.2.3.42.12: the Lord with Acyuta standing on his left, Brahmā (Vidhi) on his right side, Hari behind him, and the gods and others behind and at his sides;
m.2.3.42.13: praised by gods and beings of many kinds, the benefactor of the worlds, who assumed a body by his own will, Brahman, lord of all, giver of boons;
m.2.3.42.14: with attributes and also without attributes, subject to his devotees, a mine of compassion, beyond both Prakṛti and Puruṣa, whose nature is being, consciousness and bliss.
m.2.3.42.15: On the Lord's right side he saw Hari Acyuta, mounted on the son of Vinatā (Garuḍa), adorned with various ornaments.
m.2.3.42.16: And on the Lord's left side, O sage, he saw me, the four-faced one, of great splendour, accompanied by my retinue.
m.2.3.42.17: Seeing these two lords of the gods, ever very dear to Śiva, the lord of mountains bowed with reverence along with his retinue.
m.2.3.42.18: Likewise, seeing the gods and others shining behind Śiva and at his two sides, that lord of the best of mountains bowed to them.
m.2.3.42.19: At Śiva's command the mountain went ahead to his own city; Śeṣa, Hari and the Self-born (Brahmā) followed quickly, with the sages, the gods and others.
m.2.3.42.20: O Nārada, all the sages, gods and others, going along with the Lord, delighted, praised the mountain's city greatly.
m.2.3.42.21: Having lodged the gods and others on a lovely, specially constructed peak, Himavat went to where the ritual altar stood.
m.2.3.42.22: Having had a square pavilion specially made, furnished with arches, and having performed bathing, gift-giving and the like, he then made an inspection of the preparations.
m.2.3.42.23: Likewise Hima, king of mountains, sent his own sons to the presence of Śiva, who was accompanied by the full company headed by Viṣṇu.
m.2.3.42.24: Full of great joy, the king of the snowy mountains, together with all his kinsmen, wished to perform the bridegroom's reception rite with a great festival.
m.2.3.42.25: Then those sons of the mountain went there, bowed to him together with his company, and conveyed the message of the lord of mountains, ending with his request.
m.2.3.42.26: Then, by his leave, the sons of the mountain returned to their home and joyfully told the king of mountains: They are coming.
m.2.3.42.27: Then, O sage, hearing the mountain's request, the gods, Viṣṇu and all the others, along with the Lord, were overjoyed and rejoiced exceedingly.
m.2.3.42.28: All the gods, sages, Gaṇas and others too, having dressed themselves finely, set out with the Lord for the house of the king of mountains.
m.2.3.42.29: At that moment Menā became eager to see Śiva, and, O sage, she summoned you, the best of sages, from the Lord's side.
m.2.3.42.30: You went there then, O sage, urged on by the Lord, who in his mind wished to fulfil that purpose dear to Śiva's heart.
m.2.3.42.31: Bowing to you, O sage, Menā, her mind full of wonder, spoke, wishing to see the form of Lord Śaṅkara, which dispels pride.
m.2.3.42.iti: Thus ends the forty-second adhyāya, named The meeting of the gods and the mountain, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.3.43.1: Menā said: O sage, I shall first look at that husband of Girijā. What kind of form does Śiva have, for whose sake she performed supreme penance?
m.2.3.43.2: Brahmā said: Thus, given over to ignorance, she came at once with you, O sage, to the upper terrace in order to see Śiva.
m.2.3.43.3: Then Śiva too, the Lord, knowing the pride in her, performed a wondrous sport and spoke to Viṣṇu and to me, dear son.
m.2.3.43.4: Śiva said: By my command, you two dear ones, together with the gods, go separately to the mountain's door; we shall come afterwards.
m.2.3.43.5: Brahmā said: Hearing this, Hari summoned everyone and told them; and all the gods, absorbed in him, eagerly set out quickly just as instructed.
m.2.3.43.6: O sage, the Lord of the universe, through you, showed Menā, who stood in the upper chamber, the procession in just such a way that her heart would be confounded.
m.2.3.43.7: At this time Menā, observing the supreme and auspicious army, O sage, was delighted on seeing it as a whole.
m.2.3.43.8: First of all the Gandharvas came then, handsome and charming, rich in fine garments and adorned with various ornaments,
m.2.3.43.9: furnished with various vehicles, intent on various musical instruments, with colourful banners, and accompanied by hosts of Apsarases.
m.2.3.43.10: Then, seeing Vasu there, their lord, of supreme majesty, Menā was overjoyed and said, this is Śiva.
m.2.3.43.11: These are Śiva's attendants; this is not Śiva, the husband of Śivā — thus you then told her, O best of sages.
m.2.3.43.12: Hearing this, Menā then became absorbed in thought: He who is even greater than this—what will he be like?
m.2.3.43.13: Meanwhile the Yakṣas, Maṇigrīva and the others—their army was seen by her, twice as splendid and so on.
m.2.3.43.14: And seeing their lord Maṇigrīva, full of splendour, Menā said in delight, this is Rudra, Śivā's lord.
m.2.3.43.15: This is not Rudra, Śivā's lord; he is a servant of Śiva—thus you told the mountain's wife. Meanwhile Agni arrived.
m.2.3.43.16: Seeing his splendour, twice even that, she said, this is Rudra, Girijā's lord; then you said, no.
m.2.3.43.17: Meanwhile Yama arrived, twice as radiant even as that; seeing him, Menā said in delight, this is Rudra.
m.2.3.43.18: You told her, no. Meanwhile Nirṛti arrived, the auspicious lord of the Puṇyajanas (Rākṣasas), bearing twice the splendour.
m.2.3.43.19: Seeing him, Menā said in delight, this is Rudra. You told her, no. Meanwhile Varuṇa arrived.
m.2.3.43.20: Seeing his splendour, twice even that, she said, this is Rudra, Girijā's lord; then you said, no.
m.2.3.43.21: Meanwhile Vāyu arrived, twice as radiant even as that; seeing him, Menā said in delight, this is Rudra.
m.2.3.43.22: You told her, no. Meanwhile Dhanada (Kubera), lord of the Guhyakas, arrived, bearing a splendour twice even that.
m.2.3.43.23: Seeing him, Menā said in delight, this is Rudra. You told her, no. Meanwhile Īśāna arrived.
m.2.3.43.24: Seeing his splendour, twice even that, she said, this is Rudra, Girijā's lord; then you said, no.
m.2.3.43.25: Meanwhile Indra arrived, twice as radiant even as that—the foremost of all immortals, shining with various divine lustres, lord of the threefold heaven.
m.2.3.43.26: Seeing him, Menakā said, this is that Śaṅkara. Then you said, this is Śakra, lord of the gods—not he.
m.2.3.43.27: Meanwhile the Moon arrived, bearing splendour twice that; seeing him she said, this is Rudra, but you told her, no.
m.2.3.43.28: Meanwhile the Sun arrived, bearing splendour twice that; seeing him she said, this is he, but you told her, no.
m.2.3.43.29: Meanwhile there arrived the lords of sages, Bhṛgu and the others, all masses of radiance, accompanied by their hosts of disciples.
m.2.3.43.30: Seeing Vāgīśa (Bṛhaspati) in their midst, Menakā said, this is Rudra, Girijā's lord; then you said, no.
m.2.3.43.31: Meanwhile Brahmā arrived, the supreme mass of radiance, together with his sons, the foremost sages, praised as if he were dharma itself embodied.
m.2.3.43.32: Seeing me then, O sage, Menā, full of great joy, said, this is he, the husband of Śivā, but you told her, no.
m.2.3.43.33: Meanwhile the god Viṣṇu arrived there, endowed with every splendour, glorious, dark as a rain-cloud, four-armed,
m.2.3.43.34: with the beauty of a crore of Kandarpas, wearing yellow garments, self-ruling, lotus-eyed, serene, whose excellent mount is the king of birds,
m.2.3.43.35: bearing the marks of the conch and the rest, adorned with a crown and other ornaments, with the Śrīvatsa on his chest, lord of Lakṣmī, endowed with immeasurable radiance.
m.2.3.43.36: Seeing him, her eyes grew wide with wonder, and in great joy she said, this is the husband of Śivā, Śiva himself—there is no doubt of it.
m.2.3.43.37: Then you, the helper, hearing Menakā's words, said, this is not the husband of Śivā; rather, this is Keśava, Hari.
m.2.3.43.38: He is in charge of all Śaṅkara's affairs and dear to him. The excellent one greater than him is to be known as Śiva, the lord of Pārvatī.
m.2.3.43.39: O Menā, his splendour cannot be described by me at all. He alone is the lord of the entire cosmos, lord of all, self-ruling.
m.2.3.43.40: Brahmā said: Hearing his words thus, Menā considered her daughter auspicious, greatly rich, fortunate, a bringer of happiness to three families.
m.2.3.43.41: And with a cheerful face and a heart full of affection she spoke, describing again and again her own great good fortune.
m.2.3.43.42: Menā said: Now I have become blessed in every way through the birth of Pārvatī. Blessed today is the lord of mountains too; everything of mine is most blessed.
m.2.3.43.43: Whichever gods I have seen, leaders endowed with great splendour—he who is the lord of all these will here be her husband.
m.2.3.43.44: What can be said of her fortune? Even in hundreds of years it could not be described, seeing that she has won that Lord.
m.2.3.43.45: Brahmā said: Thus spoke Menā, her mind overflowing with love. Meanwhile Rudra, the Lord, worker of wondrous deeds, arrived.
m.2.3.43.46: O dear one, he of wondrous nature came, and his gaṇas, removers of Menā's pride, displaying himself as untouched by māyā and free from change.
m.2.3.43.47: Then, O sage Nārada, perceiving that he had arrived, you spoke to Menā with great delight, pointing out to her that husband of Śivā.
m.2.3.43.48: Nārada said: This is Śaṅkara himself; behold him, O beautiful lady—he for whose sake Śivā performed exceedingly great austerity in the forest.
m.2.3.43.49: Brahmā said: When this was said, delighted Menā joyfully beheld that Lord, Īśāna, of wondrous form, with wondrous followers, himself wondrous.
m.2.3.43.50: Just then Rudra's most wondrous army arrived, joined by bhūtas, pretas and the like, accompanied by many kinds of gaṇas.
m.2.3.43.51: Some bore the form of whirlwinds, with sounds like the rustling of banners; some there had crooked snouts, and others likewise were misshapen.
m.2.3.43.52: Some were dreadful and bearded; some lame, and some eyeless; some carried staffs and nooses, some had clubs in their hands.
m.2.3.43.53: Some rode strange mounts, sounding with blasts of horns; some were playing ḍamarus, some were playing gomukha trumpets.
m.2.3.43.54: Some gaṇas were faceless, some had distorted faces, some had many faces; some were handless, some had deformed hands, some had many hands.
m.2.3.43.55: Eyeless and many-eyed, headless and ugly-headed, earless and many-eared—gaṇas wearing all kinds of guises.
m.2.3.43.56: Thus, O dear one, there were many mighty gaṇas of such deformed shapes, countless, great heroes and terrifying.
m.2.3.43.57: Then, O sage, pointing out Rudra's gaṇas to her with your finger, you said: Behold the servants of Hara, and Hara too, O fair-faced lady.
m.2.3.43.58: Seeing the countless gaṇas, bhūtas, pretas and the rest, O sage, Menakā was at that very moment overwhelmed with fear.
m.2.3.43.59: And in their midst she saw Śaṅkara—beyond attributes yet supremely endowed with qualities, seated on a bull, five-faced, three-eyed, adorned with ash,
m.2.3.43.60: with matted locks, the moon on his crest, ten-armed, bearing a skull, with a tiger-skin as upper garment, holding the excellent Pināka bow in his hand,
m.2.3.43.61: bearing a trident, odd-eyed, of deformed and wild appearance, clad in an elephant's hide—seeing him, Śivā's mother trembled with fear.
m.2.3.43.62: To her—startled, trembling, distraught, her mind reeling—you said, pointing with your finger: This is Śiva.
m.2.3.43.63: Hearing those words of yours, the virtuous Menā, laden with grief, quickly fell to the ground like a creeper struck by the wind.
m.2.3.43.64: What is this monstrosity? Seeing it, I have been deceived through this stubborn insistence. Having said this, Menakā fainted there in an instant.
m.2.3.43.65: Then, tended by her friends with various efforts, Menā, beloved of the mountain-lord, slowly regained consciousness.
m.2.3.43.iti: Thus ends the forty-third adhyāya, named Śiva's wondrous sport, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.3.44.1: Brahmā said: Then Menā, the chaste beloved of the Mountain, regained consciousness. Greatly agitated, she lamented and then began to hurl reproaches.
m.2.3.44.2: There, faltering again and again, she first reviled her own sons; then she spoke harsh words to her daughter.
m.2.3.44.3: Menā said: O sage, earlier you declared, Śivā will choose Śiva. Afterwards you set Himavat to the task of arranging worship of him.
m.2.3.44.4: Then the fruit was truly seen—perverse and worthless. O evil-minded sage, wretched I have been utterly deceived by you.
m.2.3.44.5: Moreover, she performed austerities that are hard even for sages; and this is the fruit she obtained from them—a source of grief to those who see it.
m.2.3.44.6: What shall I do? Where shall I go? Who will dispel my grief? My family and all else are ruined, and so has my life been dealt with.
m.2.3.44.7: Where have those divine seers gone? I will pluck out their beards. And that ascetic wife of Vasiṣṭha who came of her own accord—she is a cheat.
m.2.3.44.8: Through whose offence has everything of mine now been ruined? Having said this and looking at her daughter, she spoke bitter words.
m.2.3.44.9: O wicked daughter, what grievous deed have you done to me? Giving away gold, you, wicked one, have yourself brought home glass.
m.2.3.44.10: Abandoning sandal paste, you have instead smeared yourself with mud; letting the swan fly away, you have caught a crow in the cage of your hand.
m.2.3.44.11: Casting holy water far away, you have drunk well water; abandoning the sun, you have painstakingly grasped a firefly.
m.2.3.44.12: Likewise, abandoning rice grains, you have eaten husks; throwing away ghee, you have eagerly consumed kāraṇḍa oil.
m.2.3.44.13: Likewise, giving up service to a lion, you have served a jackal; giving up knowledge of Brahman, you have listened to a vile tale.
m.2.3.44.14: Casting far away the most auspicious sacrificial ash of the household, you, O daughter, have taken up the inauspicious ash of the funeral pyre.
m.2.3.44.15: Forsaking all the foremost gods, Viṣṇu and the other supreme lords, you, with your perverse mind, performed such austerity for Śiva's sake.
m.2.3.44.16: Fie on you and on your intellect! Fie on your beauty and your conduct! Fie on the one who instructed you, and fie likewise on your two friends!
m.2.3.44.17: Fie also on us two, O daughter, who brought about your birth! Fie on your intellect, O Nārada, and on the seven seers, givers of evil counsel!
m.2.3.44.18: Fie on the family! Fie on skill in rites! Fie on everything you have done! This house has been set on fire—this is nothing but my death.
m.2.3.44.19: Let this king of mountains not come near me; let the seven seers themselves never show me their faces.
m.2.3.44.20: What has been achieved? All of them together have destroyed the family. Why did I not become barren? Why was the embryo not miscarried?
m.2.3.44.21: Or why did I not die? Why did my daughter not die? Or why was she not devoured in the sky by rākṣasas and the like?
m.2.3.44.22: I will cut off your head today. What shall I do with these bodies? Abandoning you, where could I go? Alas, alas, my life is ruined!
m.2.3.44.23: Brahmā said: Having said this, Menā fell to the ground unconscious. Distraught with grief, anger and the like, she did not go into her husband's presence.
m.2.3.44.24: At that time, O lord of sages, there arose a great cry of lament. All the gods came there one after another into her presence.
m.2.3.44.25: Earlier, O divine sage, I myself had come there then; and seeing me, you, O best of seers, spoke these words to her:
m.2.3.44.26: Nārada said: You have not known Śiva's true, beautiful form. This form has been assumed by Śiva in play; it is not his true one.
m.2.3.44.27: Therefore, giving up anger, be composed, O faithful wife. Abandon obstinacy, do what must be done, and give Śivā to Śiva.
m.2.3.44.28: Brahmā said: Hearing your words, Menā said to you: Get up and go far from here. You are the foremost of the wicked and vile.
m.2.3.44.29: When she had said this, all the gods led by Indra, and the guardians of the quarters, came one after another and spoke these words.
m.2.3.44.30: The gods said: O Menā, daughter of the Pitṛs, listen gladly to our words. This is indeed the supreme Śiva himself, the bringer of highest bliss.
m.2.3.44.31: Seeing your daughter's most unbearable austerity, Śambhu, who is loving to his true devotees, out of compassion granted her his vision and a boon.
m.2.3.44.32: Brahmā said: Then Menā, lamenting bitterly again and again, said to the gods: My daughter shall not be given by me to Giriśa of fearsome form.
m.2.3.44.33: Why have all of you gods been led astray, and set yourselves to render her supreme beauty futile?
m.2.3.44.34: When she had said this, the seven seers, Vasiṣṭha and the others, came there and spoke, O lord of sages.
m.2.3.44.35: The seven sages said: We have come to accomplish this task, O daughter of the Pitṛs, beloved of the Mountain. How could we consider anything contrary in this fitting matter?
m.2.3.44.36: This indeed is the supreme gain—the sight of Śaṅkara. Becoming the recipient of your gift, he has come to your house.
m.2.3.44.37: Brahmā said: Addressed thus by them, Menā set the sages' words at naught; angry and weak in understanding, she replied to those seers.
m.2.3.44.38: Menā said: I will have her killed with weapons or the like, but I will not give her to Śaṅkara. Go far away, all of you; do not come near me.
m.2.3.44.39: Brahmā said: Having said this, she quickly fell silent, lamenting and utterly distraught. Because of that event, O sage, a great cry of lament arose there.
m.2.3.44.40: Then Himālaya came there, greatly perturbed, and, to bring her to understanding, spoke to her affectionately, revealing the truth.
m.2.3.44.41: Himavān said: Listen to my words today, Menā. Why are you so distressed, my dear? Who are these who have come to our house, and why do you revile them?
m.2.3.44.42: You know Śaṅkara, yet you are agitated on seeing his form — the fierce form of that Śambhu, who indeed has many forms and names.
m.2.3.44.43: That Śaṅkara is known to me as the protector of all. He is indeed the most worshipful among the worshipful, the one who bestows grace and punishment.
m.2.3.44.44: Do not be obstinate; give up your grief, O you dear as life, O sinless one. Get up quickly; you should do what has to be done, O lady of good vows.
m.2.3.44.45: Formerly Śambhu came to our door bearing a fierce form and performed various sports; I remind you of that very episode.
m.2.3.44.46: Having seen his supreme greatness, you and I then agreed to give him the girl, O goddess; make that agreement good, my dear.
m.2.3.44.47: Brahmā said: Having said this, the lord of mountains then fell silent, O sage. Hearing that, Menā, the mother of Śivā, spoke to Himālaya.
m.2.3.44.48: Menā said: Let my words be heard, lord; you should act thus: take this daughter Pārvatī and, tying a stone to her neck,
m.2.3.44.49: throw her down without hesitation; I will not give her to Hara. Or else, lord, go and throw this daughter into the ocean —
m.2.3.44.50: drown her, casting off pity, and then, lord of mountains, be happy; if you give the daughter to Rudra of hideous form, then, my lord, I will certainly give up my body.
m.2.3.44.51: Brahmā said: When these words had been spoken there by Menā out of obstinacy, Pārvatī came of her own accord and spoke charming words.
m.2.3.44.52: Pārvatī said: Mother, your mind has become perverse, bringing misfortune. Though you stand on dharma, how can you abandon dharma?
m.2.3.44.53: This Rudra is the unsurpassed Lord in person, the source of all, Śambhu, beautiful, giver of happiness, described in all the Vedas.
m.2.3.44.54: He is Maheśa and Śaṅkara, lord of all the gods, self-ruling, of many forms and names, O mother; he is Hari the remover, served by Brahmā and the others.
m.2.3.44.55: That Lord is the foundation of all, the creator and the destroyer, changeless, lord of the three gods, imperishable and eternal.
m.2.3.44.56: For his sake all the gods have come, made into servants, and are at your door today in festive mood — what greater happiness is there than this?
m.2.3.44.57: So rise with effort and make your life fruitful. Give me to this Śiva and make your household meaningful.
m.2.3.44.58: Give me to the supreme Lord Śaṅkara, O mother! Accept this humble plea of mine, mother; I am telling you.
m.2.3.44.59: If you do not give me to him, I will not choose any other groom. How could a deceitful jackal obtain the lion's share?
m.2.3.44.60: In mind, speech and deed, mother, Hara himself has been chosen by me — truly chosen. Do as you wish.
m.2.3.44.61: Brahmā said: Hearing Śivā's words, Menā, beloved of the lord of mountains, lamenting bitterly and greatly enraged, seized her body,
m.2.3.44.62: and, grinding her teeth, distraught and filled with extreme fury, she beat that daughter with fists and elbows.
m.2.3.44.63: The sages who were there, dear one — you and others, O sage — wrested her from Menā's hands and then took her far away.
m.2.3.44.64: Seeing them act thus, she scolded them again and again, and once more spoke harsh words, making them all hear.
m.2.3.44.65: Menā said: What shall I do with this wickedly obstinate Śivā? I will give her strong poison, or surely throw her into a well.
m.2.3.44.66: Or I will hack Kālī into many pieces with weapons and missiles, or indeed drown my own daughter Pārvatī in the sea.
m.2.3.44.67: Or else I will surely give up my own body at once. I will not give the girl Durgā to Śambhu of hideous form.
m.2.3.44.68: What kind of dreadful groom is this that this wicked girl has won? She has made me a laughing-stock, and the mountain and our family too.
m.2.3.44.69: He has no mother, no father, no brother, no kinsman, not even anyone of his lineage; no beauty, no skill, nor any house whatsoever.
m.2.3.44.70: No clothes, no ornaments, no companions at all has he; no fine vehicle, no youth, and no wealth either.
m.2.3.44.71: No purity, no learning — and what a body, causing distress. Seeing what in him should I give my daughter to him, that she may be truly blessed?
m.2.3.44.72: Brahmā said: Having lamented much in this and similar ways, Menakā then wept loudly, O sage, overwhelmed with grief and sorrow.
m.2.3.44.73: Then I came quickly and explained to that Menakā the supreme truth of Śiva, excellent and dispelling wrong understanding.
m.2.3.44.74: Brahmā said: O Menā, listen gladly to my auspicious words; by hearing them with love, your wrong thinking will be destroyed.
m.2.3.44.75: Śaṅkara is the creator, sustainer and destroyer of the world. You do not know his true form; why do you court grief?
m.2.3.44.76: The Lord has many forms and names and performs various sports; he is master of all, independent, ruler of Māyā, free of all dualistic notions.
m.2.3.44.77: Knowing this, Menā, give Śivā to Śiva. Give up this wrong obstinacy and wrong understanding, which ruins every undertaking.
m.2.3.44.78: Brahmā said: Thus addressed by me, Menā, lamenting again and again, slowly cast off a little of her shame, O sage, and spoke to me.
m.2.3.44.79: Menā said: Why, O Brahmā, do you make her surpassing beauty go to waste? Why should this Śivā not rather be killed outright?
m.2.3.44.80: And you should not say, let her be given to Śiva. I will not give this daughter of mine, dear to me as my life, to Śiva.
m.2.3.44.81: Brahmā said: When she had spoken thus, O great sage, the Siddhas, Sanaka and the others, came together and with great affection spoke these words.
m.2.3.44.82: The siddhas said: This is indeed the supreme Śiva himself, the bringer of highest bliss. Out of compassion the Lord has granted his sight to your daughter.
m.2.3.44.83: Brahmā said: Then Menā, lamenting again and again, said to them: She certainly shall not be given by me to Giriśa of terrible form.
m.2.3.44.84: Why are all of you Siddhas, crafty as you are, bent on rendering her supreme beauty futile?
m.2.3.44.85: When she had said this there, O sage, I was astonished; all — gods, Siddhas, seers and men — were filled with wonder.
m.2.3.44.86: At this time, hearing of her firm and great obstinacy, Viṣṇu, beloved of Śiva, quickly came and said this.
m.2.3.44.87: Viṣṇu said: You are the beloved mind-born daughter of the Pitṛs, endowed with virtues, the wife of Himavat himself; yours is the excellent lineage of Brahmā.
m.2.3.44.88: Such are your supporters in the world; you are blessed indeed — what more shall I say? You are the very foundation of dharma; how then can you abandon dharma?
m.2.3.44.89: Is anything contrary to the truth being spoken by the gods and the seers, by Brahmā or likewise by me? Let it be carefully considered by you yourself.
m.2.3.44.90: You do not know Śiva: he is both without attributes and with attributes; he is of misshapen form and also of beautiful form; he is to be served by all, the refuge of the good.
m.2.3.44.91: By him alone was created the goddess, the sovereign primordial Prakṛti; and then beside her he created the Supreme Person (Puruṣottama).
m.2.3.44.92: From those two came I and likewise Brahmā; and then Rudra himself, the benefactor of the worlds, descended in the form of a guṇa.
m.2.3.44.93: Then the Vedas and the gods, and whatever world is seen, moving and unmoving — all of that came forth from Śaṅkara.
m.2.3.44.94: By whom has his form been described, or by whom can it be known? Even by me and by Brahmā his end has never been found.
m.2.3.44.95: Whatever world is seen, from Brahmā down to a blade of grass, know all that to be Śiva; there should be no doubt about this.
m.2.3.44.96: He himself, having descended in such a form through his own sport, has come to your door by the power of Śivā's penance.
m.2.3.44.97: Therefore, O wife of Himavat, give up your grief and worship Śiva. There will be great joy, and your distress will come to an end.
m.2.3.44.98: Brahmā said: O sage, when Menakā had been thus admonished, her mind, awakened by Viṣṇu, became somewhat softened.
m.2.3.44.99: But she did not give up her great obstinacy; Menā, deluded by Śiva's māyā, did not then consent to give the maiden to Hara.
m.2.3.44.100: Having heard Viṣṇu's pleasing words, Menā, the beloved of the Mountain and mother of Girijā, somewhat awakened, spoke to Hari.
m.2.3.44.101: If he takes on a handsome body, then my daughter may be given by me — not otherwise, even with millions of efforts. I speak a true and firm word.
m.2.3.44.102: Brahmā said: Having spoken these words, Menā, firm in her resolve, fell silent — the blessed one, impelled by Śiva's will, which thus deludes all.
m.2.3.44.iti: Thus ends the forty-fourth adhyāya, named The enlightening of Menā, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.3.45.1: Brahmā said: Meanwhile, O sage, urged by Viṣṇu, you quickly went near Śambhu to make him favourable.
m.2.3.45.2: Having gone there, you praised that Rudra with hymns of many kinds and duly prompted him, wishing to accomplish the gods' task.
m.2.3.45.3: Hearing your words, Śambhu gladly assumed a wondrous, supreme, divine form, and displayed his compassion.
m.2.3.45.4: Seeing that beautiful Śambhu, whose form surpassed Manmatha's, the supreme abode of loveliness, you, O sage, were overjoyed.
m.2.3.45.5: Having praised him with hymns of many kinds, filled with supreme bliss, you came, O sage, to where Menā stood with everyone.
m.2.3.45.6: Arriving there, very pleased and overflowing with love, O sage, you spoke these words, delighting Menā, the mountain's wife.
m.2.3.45.7: Nārada said: O Menā, O wide-eyed one, behold Śiva's unsurpassed form. Śiva himself, compassionate by nature, has shown great grace.
m.2.3.45.8: Brahmā said: Hearing those words, Menā, the mountain's beloved, was astonished and beheld that form of Śiva which bestows supreme bliss.
m.2.3.45.9: It was radiant like ten million suns, beautiful in every limb, in wonderful garments, adorned with many ornaments,
m.2.3.45.10: very gracious, sweetly smiling, exceedingly lovely, captivating, fair-hued, shining, adorned with the crescent moon,
m.2.3.45.11: lovingly attended by all the hosts of gods headed by Viṣṇu, shaded on the head by the Sun as an umbrella, and made splendid by the Moon.
m.2.3.45.12: He was charming in every way; the great splendour of the vehicle of him, adorned with ornaments, simply cannot be described.
m.2.3.45.13: Gaṅgā and Yamunā held fine chowries, and the eight Siddhis danced beautifully before him.
m.2.3.45.14: Then I, Viṣṇu, and the immortals headed by Indra, each well adorned in his own attire, moved along together with Giriśa.
m.2.3.45.15: Likewise the Gaṇas of many forms, crying victory, well adorned and in great joy, moved ahead of Girīśa.
m.2.3.45.16: The Siddhas, all the demigods, and the sages in great happiness went along with Śiva, much delighted, and likewise all the others.
m.2.3.45.17: Thus all the gods and others, full of eager curiosity, adorned and accompanied by their wives, went extolling the supreme Brahman.
m.2.3.45.18: There the Gandharvas led by Viśvāvasu, together with the troupes of Apsarases, sang before him the supreme glory of Śaṅkara.
m.2.3.45.19: Thus, O best of sages, a great festival of many kinds took place there as Maheśa proceeded to the mountain's door.
m.2.3.45.20: Who, O lord of sages, can describe in detail the splendour of the Supreme Self there at that time?
m.2.3.45.21: Seeing him in such a form, Menā stood for a moment as if painted in a picture; then, O sage, she lovingly spoke these words.
m.2.3.45.22: Menā said: Blessed is my daughter, who performed great austerity, by whose power you, O great lord, have come here to my house.
m.2.3.45.23: The grievous censure of Śiva which I committed earlier, forgive it, O lord of Śivā; be well pleased now.
m.2.3.45.24: Brahmā said: Having spoken thus and praised the moon-browed one, Menā, the mountain's beloved, bowed with joined palms and became overcome with bashfulness.
m.2.3.45.25: Meanwhile the women of the city came in great numbers, abandoning their many pursuits, eager to see Śiva.
m.2.3.45.26: One who was bathing went off with the bath-powder still on her, full of curiosity to see Śaṅkara, Girijā's bridegroom.
m.2.3.45.27: Another, with her friend, left off serving her husband and gladly went, chowry in hand, to see Śambhu.
m.2.3.45.28: Another, leaving her child who was eagerly drinking at her breast and not yet satisfied, went, longing for the sight, to see Śaṅkara.
m.2.3.45.29: One who was tying her girdle went with it in her hand; another went off wearing her garment inside out.
m.2.3.45.30: A loving wife, leaving her husband seated for his meal, went gladly, thirsting and curious, to see Śivā's bridegroom.
m.2.3.45.31: Another lady, holding the collyrium stick in her hand, having applied collyrium to only one eye, went to see the mountain-daughter's bridegroom.
m.2.3.45.32: Another lovely woman, dyeing her feet with lac, heard the uproar, left that, and came to see.
m.2.3.45.33: Thus, abandoning various tasks and their homes, the women went; and seeing Śaṅkara's form, they were then overcome with infatuation.
m.2.3.45.34: Then, stirred with love and thrilled at seeing Śiva, they placed his image in their hearts and spoke these words.
m.2.3.45.35: The women of the city said: The eyes of the dwellers of Himavat's city have borne fruit; whoever saw this form, his birth is truly meaningful.
m.2.3.45.36: His alone is a fruitful birth, his alone are fruitful deeds, by whom Śiva, destroyer of all sins, has been seen face to face.
m.2.3.45.37: Pārvatī has accomplished everything through the austerity she performed for Śiva's sake; blessed is she, fulfilled is she, Śivā, having won Śiva as her husband.
m.2.3.45.38: If Brahmā had not joyfully united this pair, Śiva and Śivā, then all his labour would have been fruitless.
m.2.3.45.39: It has been done well, and this excellent pair has been united here; everyone's life has become meaningful, the source of all accomplishments.
m.2.3.45.40: Without austerity, the sight of Śambhu is hard for men to obtain; through the very sight of Śaṅkara all have attained fulfilment.
m.2.3.45.41: Just as Lakṣmī long ago obtained Nārāyaṇa as her lord, so this goddess Pārvatī, well adorned, shines having obtained Hara.
m.2.3.45.42: And just as Sarasvatī obtained Brahmā as her lord, so this goddess Pārvatī, well adorned, shines having obtained Hara.
m.2.3.45.43: Blessed are we all, the women, and all the excellent men — whoever behold Śaṅkara, the Lord of all, the husband of Girijā.
m.2.3.45.44: Brahmā said: Having spoken these words, they worshipped Śiva with sandal paste and unbroken rice grains, and showered parched grain on him with reverence.
m.2.3.45.45: All the women stood there eagerly with Menā, extolling the great good fortune of Menā and of the mountain Himavat too.
m.2.3.45.46: Hearing such auspicious words spoken by those women, the Lord, O sage, became delighted then, together with all, Viṣṇu and the others.
m.2.3.45.iti: Thus ends the forty-fifth adhyāya, named Śiva's beautiful form and the festivity of the townspeople, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.3.46.1: Brahmā said: Then Śambhu, delighted at heart, went eagerly to the mountain's abode together with the messenger, with his own gaṇas, the gods, and all the others.
m.2.3.46.2: Menā too, the beloved wife of the excellent Himācala, rising from there with those groups of women, went into the interior of her own house.
m.2.3.46.3: Holding a lamp-vessel in her hand for the waving of lights (nīrājana) before Śambhu, the virtuous lady went respectfully to the door together with the hosts of the wives of all the sages.
m.2.3.46.4: There Menā lovingly beheld the arrived Maheśāna, Śaṅkara, the bridegroom of Girijā, attended by all the gods.
m.2.3.46.5: He was radiant with the hue of a lovely campaka flower, five-faced, three-eyed, his face bright with a gentle smile, adorned with jewels, gold and the like;
m.2.3.46.6: wearing a garland of mālatī flowers, resplendent with a crown of fine gems, with a fine necklace, adorned with lovely bracelets and armlets;
m.2.3.46.7: greatly splendid in a pair of priceless, wondrous garments, fire-purified, matchless, extremely fine and beautiful;
m.2.3.46.8: adorned with sandal, aguru, musk and lovely saffron, holding a jewelled mirror in his hand, his eyes bright with collyrium;
m.2.3.46.9: enveloped in the radiance of his whole being, exceedingly charming, exceedingly youthful and delightful, and adorned with ornamented limbs;
m.2.3.46.10: beloved of women, composed, his lotus-face bright as a crore of moons, the lustre of his body surpassing a crore of Kāmas, beautiful in every limb.
m.2.3.46.11: Seeing that lord, the excellent god of such a kind, her son-in-law, standing before her, Menā, filled with joy, cast off her grief.
m.2.3.46.12: She praised her own good fortune, Girijā, the mountain her husband and the family; she considered herself fulfilled and rejoiced again and again.
m.2.3.46.13: With beaming face the virtuous Menā performed the nīrājana there, joyfully intent on gazing at her son-in-law.
m.2.3.46.14: Recalling what Girijā had said, Menā was struck with wonder, and, her lotus-face blooming with delight, said this within her mind:
m.2.3.46.15: Whatever Pārvatī told me earlier on that occasion, I now see the beauty of the Supreme Lord to be greater than that.
m.2.3.46.16: The exquisite loveliness of Maheśa is now beyond words. Thus overcome with wonder, Menā returned to her house.
m.2.3.46.17: The young women praised her: Blessed, blessed is the mountain's daughter! Some maidens said, she is Durgā, the Bhagavatī.
m.2.3.46.18: Such a bridegroom, worthy of the gift of a bride, has never been seen by us; truly blessed is Goddess Girijā, said some maidens.
m.2.3.46.19: The foremost Gandharvas sang and the hosts of Apsarases danced; and all the deities, seeing Śaṅkara's form, were delighted.
m.2.3.46.20: The musicians, with devotion, played various kinds of instruments sweetly, with manifold skill.
m.2.3.46.21: Himācala too, delighted, then performed the door-rite (dvārācāra); and Menā too, with all the women, amid great festivity,
m.2.3.46.22: performed the parapṛcchā (welcoming inquiry) rite and, joyful, went to her house. Śiva, with the gaṇas and gods, went to the place assigned to him.
m.2.3.46.23: Meanwhile the attendants of the mountain's inner apartments went outside, taking Durgā with them to worship the family deity.
m.2.3.46.24: There the gods, unblinking, joyfully beheld her, shining with the hue of deep-blue collyrium, adorned by her own limbs,
m.2.3.46.25: her eyes honoured fixed by the Three-eyed One, her gaze turned away from others, her face bright with a gentle smile, with side-long glances, enchanting;
m.2.3.46.26: with a very lovely mass of braided hair, beautified with charming leaf-designs on her face, adorned with a dot of vermilion along with dots of musk;
m.2.3.46.27: her bosom shining with a necklace of the finest jewels, wearing jewelled armlets and bracelets, decked with jewelled wristlets;
m.2.3.46.28: her lovely cheeks glowing with ear-rings of fine gems, resplendent with rows of teeth that rob the lustre of gems and jewels;
m.2.3.46.29: her lips sweet and red like bimba fruit, tinged with jewel-like lac, holding a jewelled mirror in her hand, adorned with a play-lotus;
m.2.3.46.30: richly anointed with sandal, aguru, musk and saffron, with tinkling anklets on her feet, and shining with reddened soles.
m.2.3.46.31: Seeing the Goddess, the primal one of the world and mother of the world, all the gods and others, full of devotion, bowed their heads to her along with Menakā.
m.2.3.46.32: The Three-eyed One, filled with joy, looked at her from the corner of his eye; seeing in her the form of Satī, Śiva cast off the fever of separation.
m.2.3.46.33: Śiva, his eyes fixed on Śivā, forgot everything; with all his limbs thrilling with horripilation, he gazed at Gaurī in delight.
m.2.3.46.34: Then Kālī, having gone outside the city and worshipped the family mother-goddess, entered the lovely mansion of her father along with the wives of the brāhmaṇas.
m.2.3.46.35: Śaṅkara too, with the gods, with Hari and likewise Brahmā, joyfully went to his own lodging assigned by Himācala.
m.2.3.46.36: There all stayed happily, serving Śaṅkara as befitting, honoured by the Lord of the Mountains with riches of many kinds.
m.2.3.46.iti: Thus ends the forty-sixth adhyāya, named The arrival of the bridegroom and the rest, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.3.47.1: Brahmā said: Then that best of mountains, with affection and enthusiasm, had the sacred-thread ceremony of Durgā performed with Vedic mantras, and that of Śiva as well.
m.2.3.47.2: Then the gods headed by Viṣṇu and the sages, full of eagerness, entered the inner apartments of the mountain at Himācala's request.
m.2.3.47.3: Having duly carried out the Vedic custom and the worldly custom, they adorned Śivā with the ornaments given by Śiva.
m.2.3.47.4: First they bathed her, then adorned her in every way; and she was waved with lights (nīrājana) by her friends and by the wives of the brahmins.
m.2.3.47.5: Adorned with a pair of new, unworn garments, the fair-complexioned daughter of the great mountain, beloved of Śaṅkara, shone forth.
m.2.3.47.6: O sage, a supreme, divine, wondrous bodice set with many jewels was worn by that goddess, and it gleamed exceedingly.
m.2.3.47.7: She likewise wore a necklace set with divine gems, and very precious bracelets of pure gold.
m.2.3.47.8: Staying right there, meditating on Śiva in her mind, the auspicious daughter of the great mountain, mother of the three worlds, shone exceedingly.
m.2.3.47.9: Then there was a great festival on both sides, bringing joy; various gifts were given to the brahmins.
m.2.3.47.10: And to others too there was a great and varied gift of wealth; and there was entertainment with song and instrumental music as part of the festival.
m.2.3.47.11: Then Viṣṇu, I the Creator, the immortals headed by Śakra, and all the sages, festive and joyful with great delight,
m.2.3.47.12: having bowed deeply to Śivā with devotion and remembering Śiva's lotus feet, obtained the permission of Himagiri and returned each to his own place.
m.2.3.47.13: Meanwhile Garga, expert in the science of astrology, spoke these words there to Himavat, that lord of mountains.
m.2.3.47.14: Garga said: O Himācala, lord of the earth, master, O lord, bring Śambhu, the husband of Kālī, to your own mansion for the taking of the hand.
m.2.3.47.15: Brahmā said: Then the mountain, knowing the time suitable for giving away the bride, as announced by Garga, rejoiced greatly in his heart.
m.2.3.47.16: Joyfully and with great affection, the mountain sent mountains, brahmins and others too, desiring to bring Śiva.
m.2.3.47.17: Those mountains and brahmins, holding all auspicious articles in their hands, went festively and gladly to where the god Maheśvara was.
m.2.3.47.18: Then, with the sound of instruments and abundant Vedic chanting, accompanied by song and dance, there was great jubilation there.
m.2.3.47.19: Hearing the resounding of the instruments, all the attendants of Śaṅkara, together with the hosts of gods and sages, rose up joyfully all at once.
m.2.3.47.20: With minds brimming with delight they said to one another: The mountains are coming here, wishing to take Śiva along.
m.2.3.47.21: Surely the time for the taking of the hand has now arrived. We think great good fortune has come to all here.
m.2.3.47.22: We are especially blessed: we shall certainly behold with supreme joy the wedding of Śiva and Śivā, the abode of auspiciousness for the worlds.
m.2.3.47.23: Brahmā said: While this conversation was taking place among them there with respect, all the ministers of the lord of mountains arrived.
m.2.3.47.24: Having come, they requested Śiva and also Viṣṇu and the others: The time suitable for giving away the bride is at hand; please come.
m.2.3.47.25: O sage, hearing that, all those gods, Viṣṇu and the rest, rejoiced exceedingly in their hearts and quickly said to the mountain: Victory!
m.2.3.47.26: Śiva too, longing to obtain Kālī, rejoiced greatly; he of wondrous form kept that sign of joy hidden within his mind.
m.2.3.47.27: Then a bath with auspicious substances was taken by the trident-bearer, highly pleased, who bestows grace upon the worlds.
m.2.3.47.28: Bathed and clad in fine garments, surrounded by all of them, he was placed on the bull's back and well attended by the guardians of the worlds.
m.2.3.47.29: Placing the Lord in front, all went to Himagiri's house, playing instruments and making merry.
m.2.3.47.30: The brahmins sent by Himavat and those best of mountains went ahead of Śambhu, full of eagerness.
m.2.3.47.31: Maheśvara shone with a great parasol held over his head, fanned with chowries, and with a canopy above.
m.2.3.47.32: I, Viṣṇu, Indra and likewise the guardians of the worlds, going in front, shone exceedingly, endowed with supreme splendour.
m.2.3.47.33: Then conches, kettledrums, paṭahas, ānakas, gomukhas and other instruments were sounded again and again at the great festival.
m.2.3.47.34: Likewise all the singers sang most auspicious songs, and all the dancing girls danced to various rhythms.
m.2.3.47.35: Accompanied by these, the sole kinsman of the world then proceeded with the radiance of the Supreme Lord, well served by all the lords of the gods and showered with flowers by the delighted beings.
m.2.3.47.36: Then Śambhu, the Supreme Lord, duly worshipped and praised with many hymns, entered the sacrificial pavilion.
m.2.3.47.37: The best of mountains helped Maheśa down from the bull and joyfully led him into the house amid great festivity.
m.2.3.47.38: Himālaya too, having bowed with devotion according to rule to the Lord who had arrived with the hosts of gods, then performed the waving of lights (nīrājana).
m.2.3.47.39: Having bowed to all the gods, the sages and the others amid great festivity, he honoured them, joyfully praising his own good fortune.
m.2.3.47.40: That mountain led Īśāna together with Acyuta and the group of chief gods into his own abode, preceded by fine water for the feet and arghya offerings.
m.2.3.47.41: He seated them all in the courtyard on jewelled thrones: Viṣṇu, me, the Lord Śiva, and the distinguished ones with special honour.
m.2.3.47.42: Menā, together with her friends, the brahmin women and other matrons, joyfully and lovingly performed the waving of lights (nīrājana).
m.2.3.47.43: By the priest, knower of rites, every rite such as the madhuparka that was to be done for the great-souled Śaṅkara was joyfully performed.
m.2.3.47.44: Urged by me there, the priest then performed the auspicious rite befitting the occasion, O sage.
m.2.3.47.45: Having entered with great joy, along with Himādri, into the inner altar area, where the maiden Pārvatī, adorned with all ornaments,
m.2.3.47.46: the slender-limbed one, was seated on the altar, shining splendidly—there Mahādeva was led by Viṣṇu and by me.
m.2.3.47.47: Those led by Vācaspati watched for the auspicious moment suitable for the giving of the bride; there great festivities took place.
m.2.3.47.48: Garga sat where the water-clock was; as long as a ghaṭī remained, the praṇava (Om) was recited.
m.2.3.47.49: Proclaiming puṇyāham (auspicious day), Garga joyfully joined Pārvatī's palms; and Pārvatī, her palms full of unbroken rice, showered it upon Śiva.
m.2.3.47.50: Rudra was worshipped there by her, the most noble Pārvatī of lovely face, with curd, unbroken rice, kuśa grass and water.
m.2.3.47.51: Gazing at that Śambhu for whose sake she had earlier performed supreme austerity with great love, Śivā shone exceedingly.
m.2.3.47.52: Then, O sage, told by me and by the sages beginning with Garga, Śambhu, devoted to worldly custom, worshipped Śivā in return.
m.2.3.47.53: Thus Pārvatī and the Supreme Lord, who pervade the world, worshipping each other at that time, shone forth.
m.2.3.47.54: Enveloped by the splendour of the three worlds and gazing at each other, they were then specially honoured with the waving of lights by Lakṣmī and other women.
m.2.3.47.55: Likewise other brahmin wives and the women of the city performed the waving of lights; and gazing at Śivā and Śambhu, all of them attained joy—a great festival.
m.2.3.47.iti: Thus ends the forty-seventh adhyāya, named The festivity of Śiva's going into the house of the Himālaya mountain, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.3.48.1: Brahmā said: Meanwhile, there, urged on by the preceptor Garga, Himavān, together with Menā, began to give away their daughter.
m.2.3.48.2: Taking a golden pitcher, the most fortunate Menā, adorned with garments and ornaments, took her place at Himādri's side.
m.2.3.48.3: Then the mountain, delighted, together with his family priest, honoured that bridegroom with water for the feet and the other offerings, and with garments, sandal paste and ornaments.
m.2.3.48.4: Then the brāhmaṇas were told by Himādri: Now that this moment has come, let the formula for proclaiming the lunar day and the rest be pronounced.
m.2.3.48.5: Being so addressed, all those excellent brāhmaṇas, knowers of auspicious time, said, so be it, and, supremely content, gladly performed the proclamation of the lunar day and the rest.
m.2.3.48.6: Then Himācala, prompted in his heart by Śambhu, the Supreme Lord who was directing everything, laughing, gladly spoke to Śambhu:
m.2.3.48.7: Let your gotra be stated, O Śambhu, and your pravara and family likewise, your name, your Veda and your śākhā. Do not let the auspicious time pass.
m.2.3.48.8: Brahmā said: Hearing these words of Himādri, Śaṅkara, though of gracious countenance, at once turned his face away; though not one to be pitied, he came into a pitiable state.
m.2.3.48.9: When the blessed Maheśa was seen in such a state, with no answer on his face, by the foremost gods, the sages, and likewise the hosts of Gandharvas, Yakṣas and Siddhas, then there, O Nārada, you burst into a hearty laugh.
m.2.3.48.10: Then, O Nārada, you, knower of Brahman, prompted there inwardly by Śiva, with your mind fixed on Śambhu, played the vīṇā.
m.2.3.48.11: Then you, wise one, were forcibly restrained by the lord of mountains, and by Viṣṇu, by me, by the gods and by all the sages as well.
m.2.3.48.12: When you, by Śaṅkara's will, did not stop, then the mountain told you: Do not play the vīṇā now.
m.2.3.48.13: When you, O wise divine sage, were firmly and forcibly forbidden by him, you, keeping Maheśvara well in mind, replied to that lord of the mountains:
m.2.3.48.14: Nārada said: You have fallen into delusion and know nothing at all. In what may be said about Maheśa, you are utterly turned away from the truth.
m.2.3.48.15: Hara himself has been questioned by you about stating his own gotra; at this moment such speech is utterly laughable.
m.2.3.48.16: O mountain, even Viṣṇu, Brahmā and the others here do not know his gotra, family or name; what then is to be said of others?
m.2.3.48.17: O mountain, he in a single day of whom a crore of Brahmās has gone to dissolution—that very Śaṅkara is seen by you today through the power of Kālī's austerity.
m.2.3.48.18: He is formless, the supreme Brahman, without attributes, beyond Prakṛti, shapeless, changeless, the master of Māyā, higher than the highest.
m.2.3.48.19: He is without gotra, family or name, independent, loving to his devotees; by his own will he becomes endowed with attributes, of fair body, bearing many names.
m.2.3.48.20: He has a noble gotra yet is without gotra; he is without family yet of noble family. Through Pārvatī's austerity he is today your son-in-law—there is no doubt.
m.2.3.48.21: By him who sports in play, the whole world, moving and unmoving, is deluded. No one, however wise, knows Śiva, O best of mountains.
m.2.3.48.22: Who has seen the top of Maheśa in the form of the liṅga? No one. Even Viṣṇu, going down to Pātāla, did not then reach him and was astonished.
m.2.3.48.23: What need of many words, O best of mountains? Śiva's Māyā is hard to cross; the three worlds are subject to it, and so are Hari, Brahmā and the others.
m.2.3.48.24: Therefore, O father of Śivā, having reflected carefully and with effort, you should not entertain the slightest doubt here about such a bridegroom.
m.2.3.48.25: Brahmā said: Having said this, O sage, you, the knowing one, the accomplisher of Śiva's will, spoke again to that lord of mountains, delighting him with your words:
m.2.3.48.26: Nārada said: Listen to my words, dear great mountain, father of Śivā; having heard them, give your daughter, the goddess, to Śaṅkara.
m.2.3.48.27: Know that the gotra and family of Maheśa with attributes, who assumes a form in play, is Nāda (primordial sound) alone.
m.2.3.48.28: Truly Śiva consists of Nāda, and Nāda likewise consists of Śiva; there is no difference between the two, Nāda and Śiva.
m.2.3.48.29: Because Nāda was the first-born in creation from Śiva, who assumes a form with attributes in play, therefore, O lord of mountains, it is the most excellent of all.
m.2.3.48.30: That is why, O Himālaya, the vīṇā was played by me today, prompted inwardly by Śaṅkara, the Lord of all.
m.2.3.48.31: Brahmā said: Hearing these words of yours, O sage, Himādri, the lord of mountains, became satisfied, his mind freed of perplexity.
m.2.3.48.32: Then Viṣṇu and the others, the gods and likewise the sages, all freed of perplexity, exclaimed: Well said, well said!
m.2.3.48.33: Understanding the profundity of Maheśvara, all the discerning ones, full of wonder and great joy, said to one another:
m.2.3.48.34: He by whose command this vast universe came into being, higher than the highest, whose form is his own awareness, Śarva, who moves by his own free will and is reached through supreme devotion—that very lord of the three worlds has today been clearly seen by us.
m.2.3.48.35: Then those foremost mountains, Meru and the others, agitated, spoke with one voice to Himavān, the lord of mountains:
m.2.3.48.36: The mountains said: Hold firm now to the giving of your daughter, O lord of mountains. Why ruin your own purpose through further talk? We speak the truth: no deliberation should be made here. Therefore let the daughter be given to the Lord.
m.2.3.48.37: Brahmā said: Hearing those words of his friends, Himālaya, impelled by Providence, performed the gift of his daughter to Śiva:
m.2.3.48.38: I give this maiden to you, O Supreme Lord. Accept her as your wife; be gracious, O Lord of all.
m.2.3.48.39: With this mantra Himācala gave his own daughter Pārvatī, mother of the three worlds, to that great Rudra.
m.2.3.48.40: Having thus placed Śivā's hand in Śiva's hand, the mountain rejoiced greatly in his mind, having crossed the great ocean of his desire.
m.2.3.48.41: With a Vedic mantra Giriśa, the Supreme Lord, well pleased, quickly took the lotus-hand of Girijā in his own hand.
m.2.3.48.42: O sage, touching the earth, Śaṅkara joyfully recited the mantra kāmasya ko'dāt (Who gave this? ... of Kāma), showing the worldly custom.
m.2.3.48.43: There was a great festival everywhere, bringing delight; shouts of victory arose in heaven, on earth and in the sky.
m.2.3.48.44: All, exceedingly delighted, cried well done and homage; the Gandharvas sang sweetly with joy and the hosts of Apsarases danced.
m.2.3.48.45: The citizens of Himācala rejoiced greatly in their hearts; there was indeed great auspiciousness, accompanied by a grand festival.
m.2.3.48.46: I, Viṣṇu, Śakra, the gods and all the sages became exceedingly delighted, our lotus-faces blooming.
m.2.3.48.47: Then Himācala, best of mountains, very pleased, gave to Śiva the accompaniments of the gift of the maiden, fully as was proper.
m.2.3.48.48: Then his kinsmen, having worshipped Śivā with devotion, gave excellent articles to Śiva according to various rites and procedures.
m.2.3.48.49: Himālaya, with a contented mind, gave there many kinds of articles for the pleasure of Pārvatī and Śiva, O lord of sages.
m.2.3.48.50: He gave him dowry gifts, various gems, and various vessels made of beautiful jewels.
m.2.3.48.51: He gave a hundred thousand cows, likewise a hundred caparisoned horses, and a hundred thousand devoted maidservants adorned with fine ornaments.
m.2.3.48.52: And, O sage, ten million elephants, and likewise chariots inlaid with gold, fashioned of the finest jewels.
m.2.3.48.53: Thus, having duly given his own daughter Girijā Śivā to Śiva, the Supreme Lord, Himālaya attained fulfilment.
