m.2.3.48.54: Then the best of mountains, with joined palms, joyfully praised the Supreme Lord in noble words with the hymn taught in the Mādhyandina recension.
m.2.3.48.55: Then, instructed by him who knew the Vedas, the hosts of sages, full of great festivity, performed the anointing of Śivā's head.
m.2.3.48.56: Pronouncing the name of the deity, they performed the rite of sprinkling around; and then, O sage, there was a great festival producing great bliss.
m.2.3.48.iti: Thus ends the forty-eighth adhyāya, named The giving away of the bride, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.3.49.1: Brahmā said: Then, at my instruction, the Lord had the fire installed by the brāhmaṇas and, seating Pārvatī on his lap, performed the homa there.
m.2.3.49.2: Śiva poured oblations into the fire with mantras of the Ṛg, Yajur and Sāma Vedas. Kālī's brother, named Maināka, offered the handful of parched grain.
m.2.3.49.3: Then Kālī and Śiva, both of them, joyfully and according to rule circumambulated the fire, dear son, also observing the customs of the world.
m.2.3.49.4: There the Lord of Girijā enacted a wondrous deed. Listen to just that, O divine sage; out of affection for you I shall tell it.
m.2.3.49.5: At that moment I, deluded by Śiva's māyā, saw the charming moon-like toenail on the Goddess's foot.
m.2.3.49.6: By the sight of it, O divine sage, I then became possessed by Madana, my mind greatly agitated.
m.2.3.49.7: Infatuated by Smara, I gazed again and again at her body; then, from that sight, my seed at once fell to the ground.
m.2.3.49.8: Ashamed at that oozing semen, I, the Grandsire, O sage, crushed what had fallen with my feet, trying to hide it.
m.2.3.49.9: Knowing this, Mahādeva became exceedingly angry, O Nārada, and at once wished to kill me, Vidhi, infatuated by lust.
m.2.3.49.10: A great cry of alarm arose there on every side, O Nārada; all the people trembled, and even the sustainer of the universe was struck with fear.
m.2.3.49.11: Then the immortals headed by Viṣṇu, O sage, praised that Śambhu, who was blazing with wrath and radiance and poised to kill.
m.2.3.49.12: The gods said: O God of gods, all-pervading one, Supreme Lord, Sadāśiva, Lord of the world, Master of the world, you who consist of the world, be gracious.
m.2.3.49.13: You are the self, the cause and the ruler of all beings; changeless, imperishable, eternal, beyond distinctions, undecaying, supreme.
m.2.3.49.14: That from which come the beginning and end of this world, its middle, this and the other, the I and the outside — being imperishable, he is none of these; that truth, Brahman, consciousness, is you.
m.2.3.49.15: Sages firm in their vows, longing for liberation, abandon attachment on both sides and worship only your lotus feet.
m.2.3.49.16: You are Brahman — full, immortal, free from sorrow, without qualities, supreme, pure bliss, unperturbed, changeless, without individual self.
m.2.3.49.17: You are indeed the cause of the arising, sustenance and withdrawal of the universe; in relation to it you are the lord of selves, yet the all-pervading one is ever independent.
m.2.3.49.18: You alone are the one, the existent and the non-existent, the dual and the non-dual; just as gold, whether worked or unworked, has no difference in substance.
m.2.3.49.19: Since distinction in you is perceived by people through ignorance, the remedy is only for the delusion; for you, who are free of limiting adjuncts, there is none in yourself.
m.2.3.49.20: We are blessed, O Maheśāna, merely by seeing you. O Śambhu, giver of bliss to your steadfast devotees, show compassion.
m.2.3.49.21: You are the beginning and you are beginningless; you are the Person beyond Prakṛti, Lord of the universe, Master of the world, changeless, higher than the highest.
m.2.3.49.22: This Brahmā, the Grandsire, who through rajas is the form of the universe, and Viṣṇu, the Supreme Person, through sattva, exist by your grace, O Lord.
m.2.3.49.23: Through tamas you are Kālāgnirudra; yet you are the Supreme Self beyond the guṇas, Sadāśiva, Maheśāna, all-pervading Maheśvara.
m.2.3.49.24: The manifest, Mahat, the source of elements (ahaṃkāra), the subtle elements and the senses are all presided over by you alone, O Maheśvara whose form is the universe.
m.2.3.49.25: O Mahādeva, Supreme Lord, mine of compassion, Śaṅkara, be gracious, O Lord of the gods of gods; be gracious, O Supreme Person.
m.2.3.49.26: The seven oceans are your garments, the directions your mighty arms; heaven is your head, O all-pervading one, the sky your navel, and the wind your nose.
m.2.3.49.27: Fire, sun and moon are your eyes, the clouds your hair, O Lord; the lunar mansions, stars and the rest, and the planets are your ornaments.
m.2.3.49.28: How shall I praise you, O Lord of gods, all-pervading Supreme Lord? You are beyond the reach of words, and of the mind too, O Śaṅkara.
m.2.3.49.29: Salutation to you, the five-faced Rudra, whose forms number five hundred million, lord of the three worlds, most excellent, the very essence of knowledge.
m.2.3.49.30: Salutations again and again to the indescribable, the eternal, the one with form like a lightning flame, fire-hued, the god Śaṅkara.
m.2.3.49.31: Salutations again and again to him who abides in this world, having assumed a most beautiful eight-cornered form shining like ten million lightnings.
m.2.3.49.32: Brahmā said: Hearing their words thus, the Supreme Lord, affectionate to his devotees, was pleased and quickly granted fearlessness to me, Brahmā.
m.2.3.49.33: Then all the gods there, headed by Viṣṇu, and the sages likewise, broke into smiles, dear son, and held a great celebration.
m.2.3.49.34: From that semen of mine, dear son, crushed again and again, there arose there a great many particles, exceedingly radiant.
m.2.3.49.35: From those particles of seed, blazing with their own radiance, many sages were born — the Bālakhilyas, by the thousands.
m.2.3.49.36: Then all those sages approached me, O sage, with great love, and said: Father, father.
m.2.3.49.37: Those Bālakhilyas were then addressed there by Nārada, prompted by the Lord's will, with an angry mind.
m.2.3.49.38: Nārada said: Go together, all of you, to Mount Gandhamādana. You must not stay here, for you have no purpose here.
m.2.3.49.39: Having performed intense austerity there, you will become lords among sages, disciples of the Sun. This I have told you at Śiva's own command.
m.2.3.49.40: Brahmā said: Thus addressed, all those Bālakhilyas then bowed to Śaṅkara and swiftly went to Mount Gandhamādana.
m.2.3.49.41: Then, O lord of sages, I was comforted by Viṣṇu and the others, those great-souled ones impelled by the Supreme Lord, and I became free of fear.
m.2.3.49.42: And I praised Śaṅkara, the Lord of all, affectionate to his devotees, knowing him to be the accomplisher of all deeds and the remover of the pride of the wicked.
m.2.3.49.43: O God of gods, O Mahādeva, O ocean of compassion, O Lord, you alone are in every way the creator, sustainer and destroyer of all.
m.2.3.49.44: By your will indeed the whole universe, moving and unmoving, is held in place, like bullocks tied to a rope; this I have come to know especially.
m.2.3.49.45: Having spoken thus, I, with joined palms, made obeisance; and all the others too, Viṣṇu and the rest, praised that Maheśvara.
m.2.3.49.46: Then, having heard the pure praise offered by me in humility, and that of Viṣṇu and all the others, Maheśvara became pleased.
m.2.3.49.47: With a delighted mind he granted me the supreme boon of fearlessness. All attained great happiness, and I, O sage, attained great joy.
m.2.3.49.iti: Thus ends the forty-ninth adhyāya, named The bewilderment of Vidhi, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.3.50.1: Brahmā said: Then, O Nārada, at Śiva's command, I, together with the hosts of sages, lovingly performed the remaining rites of the marriage of Śiva and Śivā.
m.2.3.50.2: Then the anointing of their heads took place with reverence; and the brahmins respectfully had them view the pole star (Dhruva).
m.2.3.50.3: After that came the rite of touching the heart, and, O best of brahmins, the recitation of blessings accompanied by great festivity.
m.2.3.50.4: At the brahmins' bidding Śambhu placed vermilion on Śivā's head; at that moment Girijā's splendour became wondrous and indescribable.
m.2.3.50.5: Then, at the brahmins' bidding, the two, seated together on one seat, attained supreme beauty that brought joy to the hearts of devotees.
m.2.3.50.6: Then, O sage, coming to their own place, the two performers of wondrous sport joyfully partook of the remnant of the oblation at my direction.
m.2.3.50.7: When the marriage sacrifice had thus been completed according to rule, Lord Śiva gave the full vessel (pūrṇapātra) to me, Brahmā, the maker of the worlds.
m.2.3.50.8: Then Śambhu duly gave a gift of cows to the officiating teacher, and lovingly gave the great gifts that bestow auspiciousness.
m.2.3.50.9: Then he gave a hundred gold pieces to each brahmin separately, and to many, crores of gems and various goods in abundance.
m.2.3.50.10: Then all the immortals and other beings, moving and unmoving, rejoiced greatly at heart, and a loud cry of victory arose.
m.2.3.50.11: Auspicious sounds and songs rose abundantly on all sides; and the delightful sound of musical instruments arose, increasing everyone's joy.
m.2.3.50.12: Then Hari, along with me, the gods, the sages and all the others, taking leave of the Mountain with great affection, quickly went to their own places.
m.2.3.50.13: Then in the Mountain's city the delighted women, bringing the excellent pair Śiva and Śivā, went to the bridal chamber (kuhavara).
m.2.3.50.14: There those honoured women carried out the worldly customs; then great festivity, bringing delight, spread everywhere.
m.2.3.50.15: Then those women, bringing the couple, the benefactors of people, to the very divine bed-chamber, joyfully performed the customary rites.
m.2.3.50.16: Then the women of the lord of mountains' city came near, completed the auspicious rite, and brought the couple into the house.
m.2.3.50.17: Raising cries of victory, they performed the untying of the knot and other rites, smiling, casting sidelong glances, their bodies thrilled with joy.
m.2.3.50.18: Entering the bed-chamber, those excellent ladies were entranced, praising their own good fortune as they gazed at the Supreme Lord—
m.2.3.50.19: —of exceedingly beautiful form and attire, endowed with all loveliness, in fresh youth, captivating the hearts of women,
m.2.3.50.20: his face bright with a gentle smile, casting sidelong glances, most handsome, wearing very fine garments and adorned with various jewels.
m.2.3.50.21: Then sixteen celestial women came near, with great eagerness, to see that couple.
m.2.3.50.22: Sarasvatī and Lakṣmī, Sāvitrī and likewise Jāhnavī, Aditi and Śacī, Lopāmudrā and Arundhatī,
m.2.3.50.23: Ahalyā, Tulasī, Svāhā, Rohiṇī and Vasundharā, Śatarūpā, Saṃjñā and Rati—these were the celestial women.
m.2.3.50.24: Charming daughters of gods, of Nāgas, of sages—who is able to count all those who were present there?
m.2.3.50.25: When they had offered him a jewelled seat, Śiva sat there joyfully; and the goddesses in turn spoke to him sweet words with lovely smiles.
m.2.3.50.26: Sarasvatī said: O Mahādeva, now you have joyfully obtained Satī, dearer than life. Seeing your beloved's moon-like face, O lover, give up your anguish.
m.2.3.50.27: O Lord of Time, pass your time in Satī's embrace; there will be no separation for you, for she has taken refuge in you for all time.
m.2.3.50.28: Lakṣmī said: O Lord of gods, abandon shyness and remain holding Satī to your bosom. What shyness toward her, without whom your life-breaths depart?
m.2.3.50.29: Sāvitrī said: O Śambhu, having fed Satī, eat quickly yourself; do not be weary. Then, after rinsing your mouth, lovingly give her betel with camphor.
m.2.3.50.30: Jāhnavī said: Holding her gold-lustred hand, comb the woman's hair; for a loving wife there can be no happiness of a husband's favour greater than this.
m.2.3.50.31: Aditi said: O Śivā, at the end of the meal, respectfully and with great love give Śambhu water for rinsing his mouth; the love of a married couple is hard to find.
m.2.3.50.32: Śacī said: You who, for her sake, lamenting and holding Śivā on your chest, wandered ceaselessly in delusion—what shyness can you have toward your beloved?
m.2.3.50.33: Lopāmudrā said: O Śiva, it is the women's custom: having eaten in the bed-chamber and given betel to Śivā, you should go to bed.
m.2.3.50.34: Arundhatī said: Satī was given to you through me, persuading Menā, who was unwilling to give her to you; having coaxed her in various ways, you should make delightful love.
m.2.3.50.35: Ahalyā said: Giving up the state of old age, become very youthful indeed, so that Menā, whose heart is devoted to her daughter, may approve of you.
m.2.3.50.36: Tulasī said: Satī was abandoned by you; Kāma was formerly burnt by you. How then, O Lord, was Vasiṣṭha now sent to ask for her?
m.2.3.50.37: Svāhā said: O Mahādeva, stay steady now under the women's words; at a wedding it is the custom for matrons to be bold.
m.2.3.50.38: Rohiṇī said: O expert in the science of love, fulfil Pārvatī's desire; being yourself a lover, carry her across the ocean of the beloved's longing.
m.2.3.50.39: The Earth said: O knower of feelings, you know the feelings of women afflicted by love; O Śambhu, such a woman does not always merely cherish her own husband as a lord.
m.2.3.50.40: Śatarūpā said: One tormented by hunger is not satisfied by eating without divine food; O Śambhu, it is proper to do that by which a woman's satisfaction arises.
m.2.3.50.41: Saṃjñā said: Quickly and lovingly send Śaṅkara off with Pārvatī, after preparing in a secluded place a jewelled lamp, betel, and a bed.
m.2.3.50.42: Brahmā said: Hearing those words of the women, Śiva himself, the Lord free from all perturbation, the preceptor of the preceptors of the lords of yogins, spoke to them.
m.2.3.50.43: Śaṅkara said: O goddesses, do not speak such words in my presence. You are mothers of the worlds and chaste ladies; how can there be such frivolity toward a son?
m.2.3.50.44: Brahmā said: Hearing Śaṅkara's words, the wives of the gods were ashamed and, out of embarrassment, fell silent like figures in a painting.
m.2.3.50.45: Having eaten the sweet food and rinsed his mouth, Maheśa, delighted at heart, partook of betel with camphor together with his wife.
m.2.3.50.iti: Thus ends the fiftieth adhyāya, named The jesting, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.3.51.1: Brahmā said: At that moment Rati, knowing the time to be favourable and greatly pleased, spoke to Śaṅkara, who is tender towards the afflicted.
m.2.3.51.2: Rati said: By taking Pārvatī as your wife you have obtained extremely rare good fortune. Why then was my lord of life reduced to ashes, though he sought nothing for himself?
m.2.3.51.3: Revive my husband here; let the working of desire be active in yourself, and remove my anguish caused by separation.
m.2.3.51.4: At this wedding festival all people are happy; I alone, O Maheśāna, am miserable without my husband.
m.2.3.51.5: Make me one who has a protector, O god; be gracious, O Śaṅkara. Make your own words come true, O friend of the afflicted, O supreme Lord.
m.2.3.51.6: Apart from you, who in the three worlds with their moving and unmoving beings is able to destroy my grief? Knowing this, show compassion.
m.2.3.51.7: In this festive wedding of yours, which bestows joy on all, make me too joyful, O Lord, O source of mercy to the afflicted.
m.2.3.51.8: When my lord is revived, your delightful sport with your beloved Pārvatī will indeed be complete; there is no doubt.
m.2.3.51.9: You are able to do everything, since you are the supreme Lord. What is the use of many words here, O Lord of all? Quickly revive my husband.
m.2.3.51.10: Brahmā said: Having said this, she gave him Kāma's ashes tied up in a knotted bundle, and wept before Śambhu, crying, O lord, O lord.
m.2.3.51.11: Hearing Rati's weeping, the women headed by Sarasvatī—all the goddesses—wept and spoke very piteous words.
m.2.3.51.12: The goddesses said: You bear the name loving to devotees; you are the friend of the afflicted, a treasure of compassion. Revive Kāma, make Rati joyful again; salutation to you.
m.2.3.51.13: Brahmā said: Hearing these words of theirs, Maheśvara became pleased; the Lord, an ocean of compassion, quickly cast a merciful glance.
m.2.3.51.14: By the nectar-like glance of the trident-bearer, Smara came forth from the ashes, with the same form, dress and marks as before, handsome and of wondrous appearance.
m.2.3.51.15: Seeing her husband of that same form and shape, smiling, with bow and arrows, Rati bowed to Maheśvara.
m.2.3.51.16: She became fulfilled, and with joined palms, together with her revived husband, she praised again and again the god Śiva, who had given back her lord of life.
m.2.3.51.17: Hearing the praise of Kāma together with his wife, Śaṅkara became exceedingly pleased and, his mind moist with compassion, spoke.
m.2.3.51.18: Śaṅkara said: I am pleased with your praise, O mind-born one, offered together with your wife. O self-born one, name a boon; whatever you wish, I shall give you.
m.2.3.51.19: Brahmā said: Hearing these words of Śambhu, Smara, filled with great joy, then spoke with joined palms, humbly, in a voice choked with emotion.
m.2.3.51.20: Kāma said: O God of gods, Mahādeva, ocean of compassion, O Lord, if you are pleased, O Lord of all, be the giver of joy to me.
m.2.3.51.21: Forgive the offence that I committed before, O Lord. Grant me supreme affection for your own people and devotion to your feet.
m.2.3.51.22: Brahmā said: Hearing Smara's words, the supreme Lord, a treasure of compassion, was pleased; saying Om, he smiled and spoke to him.
m.2.3.51.23: Īśvara said: O Kāma, I am pleased; abandon fear, O wise one. Go near Viṣṇu and stay in the place outside.
m.2.3.51.24: Brahmā said: Hearing that, he bowed his head, circumambulated the all-pervading Lord while praising him, went outside, saluted Hari and the gods, and attended upon them.
m.2.3.51.25: The gods, having conversed with Kāma, gave him auspicious blessings; Viṣṇu and the others, pleased, spoke while remembering Śiva in their hearts.
m.2.3.51.26: The gods said: Blessed are you, Smara: burnt by Śiva, yet favoured by him. The Lord of all has revived you with his compassionate glance born of his sattva portion.
m.2.3.51.27: There is no other giver of happiness and sorrow, since a person experiences the fruit of his own deeds. Protection, marriage and conception at their appointed time—by whom can they be prevented?
m.2.3.51.28: Brahmā said: Having said this and honoured him, the immortals, Viṣṇu and the rest, all with their wishes fulfilled, then remained there happily.
m.2.3.51.29: He too, delighted, dwelt there by Śiva's command. Cries of victory, salutation and excellent arose.
m.2.3.51.30: Then Śambhu, in the bridal chamber, seated Pārvatī on his left and fed her sweet food, and she, full of joy, fed him too.
m.2.3.51.31: Then Śambhu, following worldly custom, having performed the rites there, took leave of Menā and the Mountain and went to the lodging of the bridegroom's party.
m.2.3.51.32: Then there was a great festival and the sound of the Vedas arose, O sage; and people played the four kinds of musical instruments.
m.2.3.51.33: Śambhu, having come to his own place, then saluted the sages, Hari and me, according to worldly custom, and was saluted by the gods and others.
m.2.3.51.34: Then arose the cry of victory and likewise salutation, and the auspicious sound of the Vedas that shatters all obstacles.
m.2.3.51.35: Then Viṣṇu, I, Śakra, all the gods with the sages, the Siddhas, the Upasuras and the Nāgas praised him each separately.
m.2.3.51.36: The gods said: Victory to you, Śambhu, support of all! Victory indeed, Maheśvara! Victory, Rudra, Mahādeva! Victory, O Lord, sustainer of the universe!
m.2.3.51.37: Victory, O husband of Kālī, O master! Victory, O increaser of bliss! Victory, Tryambaka, Lord of all! Victory, O all-pervading Lord of Māyā!
m.2.3.51.38: Victory, O attributeless, desireless one, beyond causes, all-pervading! Victory, O support of all through your sport, who have assumed form; salutation to you.
m.2.3.51.39: Victory, O Lord who grants the good desires of your devotees, O source of compassion! Victory, O you whose form is being and bliss! Victory, O you who take form through the guṇas of Māyā!
m.2.3.51.40: Victory to you, O fierce one, O gracious one (Mṛḍa), O Self of all, O friend of the afflicted, O treasure-house of compassion! Victory to you, O changeless one, O lord of Māyā, whose form is beyond speech and mind!
m.2.3.51.41: Brahmā said: Having thus praised the great lord, the master, the consort of Girijā, Viṣṇu and the others served him with supreme affection, as was fitting.
m.2.3.51.42: Then Śambhu, the great lord, the Īśvara who had assumed a body in play, bestowed honour and boons upon all of them there, O Nārada.
m.2.3.51.43: All of them, Viṣṇu and the others, O dear one, having received the command of the supreme lord, greatly delighted, with cheerful faces and honoured, went to their own abodes.
m.2.3.51.iti: Thus ends the fifty-first adhyāya, named The revival of Kāma, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, in the dialogue between Brahmā and Nārada, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.3.52.1: Brahmā said: Then, dear child, Himavat, the best of mountains, most fortunate of all and wise, arranged the courtyard for the feast.
m.2.3.52.2: He had it properly swept and plastered, and he respectfully adorned it with fragrances and various articles.
m.2.3.52.3: Then the Mountain, through his sons and other mountains as well, invited all the gods, together with the Lord, and others too, to the feast.
m.2.3.52.4: Hearing the Mountain's invitation, O sage, the Lord, with Acyuta (Viṣṇu) and all the gods and others, joyfully went there for the meal.
m.2.3.52.5: The Mountain, having duly honoured the Lord and all of them according to rule, joyfully seated them on fine seats inside the house.
m.2.3.52.6: Having served many excellent dishes, he then, with folded hands, made a humble request that they begin the meal.
m.2.3.52.7: Then the gods, led by Viṣṇu, thus honoured there, placing Sadāśiva at their head, all ate.
m.2.3.52.8: Then all of them, gathered together at once in every way, sitting in rows, ate, laughing, each group separately.
m.2.3.52.9: Nandin, Bhṛṅgin, Vīrabhadra and Vīrabhadra's attendants ate separately — those illustrious ones, full of merriment.
m.2.3.52.10: The gods with Indra, and the guardians of the worlds, resplendent in many ways, those illustrious ones ate amid many kinds of humour.
m.2.3.52.11: All the sages, brahmins and seers headed by Bhṛgu likewise all ate with delight, seated then in separate rows.
m.2.3.52.12: Likewise all Caṇḍī's attendants ate and finished their meal, joyfully making merry and cracking many jokes.
m.2.3.52.13: Thus, having eaten and rinsed their mouths, all of them, Viṣṇu and the rest, full of joy, gladly went each to his own lodging to rest.
m.2.3.52.14: At Menā's bidding, the virtuous women devoutly entreated Śiva and lodged him in the house called the bridal chamber (vāsa), amid great festivity.
m.2.3.52.15: Śambhu, seated on the charming jewelled throne given by Menā, joyfully beheld the bridal chamber.
m.2.3.52.16: It was lit up splendidly by hundreds of blazing jewelled lamps, filled with jewelled vessels and jars, and gleaming with pearls and gems,
m.2.3.52.17: rich in the beauty of jewelled mirrors, adorned with white chowries, festooned with fine garlands of pearls and gems, supremely opulent,
m.2.3.52.18: incomparable, greatly divine, wondrous, most charming, delighting the mind, its spaces laid out in many designs,
m.2.3.52.19: displaying the unequalled, supreme power of the boon granted by Śiva, radiant, and bearing the name Śivaloka,
m.2.3.52.20: perfumed with many fragrant substances, brilliantly bright, furnished with sandal and aguru, and provided with a bed of flowers,
m.2.3.52.21: rich with many wondrous paintings, built by Viśvakarman, and studded with excellent ornaments made of the finest gems.
m.2.3.52.22: In one place was depicted the most charming Vaikuṇṭha, fashioned by the gods; in another, Brahmaloka; elsewhere, the city of the world-guardians;
m.2.3.52.23: in one place lovely Kailāsa, in another Śakra's (Indra's) palace, and in another Śivaloka, shining above all.
m.2.3.52.24: Seeing the whole house, such a marvel, Maheśvara praised the lord of the snowy mountains and was greatly pleased.
m.2.3.52.25: There, on a most delightful, excellent jewelled couch, the Supreme Lord joyfully lay down in sport.
m.2.3.52.26: Himācala fed all his own kinsmen completely, and all the others too with great affection, and attended to the remaining duties.
m.2.3.52.27: While the lord of mountains was thus occupied and the beloved Lord slept, the whole night passed and morning came.
m.2.3.52.28: Then at daybreak the people, full of resolve and enthusiasm, played many kinds of musical instruments.
m.2.3.52.29: All the gods, Viṣṇu and the rest, rose up in great joy; remembering their beloved Lord of the gods, they made themselves ready in haste.
m.2.3.52.30: Having readied their own vehicles, eager to go to Kailāsa, they sent Dharma to Śiva.
m.2.3.52.31: Then Dharma, the yogin, coming to the bridal chamber at Nārāyaṇa's command, spoke words fitting the occasion to Śaṅkara, the lord of yogins.
m.2.3.52.32: Dharma said: Arise, arise. May it be well with you, O Bhava, our lord of the Pramathas. Come to the guests' lodging and make them there fulfilled.
m.2.3.52.33: Brahmā said: Hearing Dharma's words, Maheśvara laughed, looked on him with a compassionate glance, and left his bed.
m.2.3.52.34: Laughing, he said to Dharma: You go ahead there; I too shall come very soon, no doubt.
m.2.3.52.35: Brahmā said: Thus addressed by Śaṅkara, he went to the guests' lodging; and Lord Śambhu himself also intended to go there.
m.2.3.52.36: Learning of this, the group of women came there in great festivity and sang auspicious songs, gazing at Śambhu's two feet.
m.2.3.52.37: Then Śambhu, following worldly custom, performed his morning rites, took leave of Menā and the Mountain, and went to the guests' lodging.
m.2.3.52.38: Then there was a great festival; the sound of the Vedas arose, O sage, and the people played instruments of the four kinds.
m.2.3.52.39: Śambhu, reaching his own quarters, then saluted the sages, and, following worldly custom, Hari and me; and he was saluted by the gods and others.
m.2.3.52.40: Then arose cries of victory and likewise cries of salutation; the auspicious sound of the Vedas too, and a great tumult arose.
m.2.3.52.iti: Thus ends the fifty-second adhyāya, named The feast of the bridegroom's party and Śiva's sleep, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.3.53.1: Brahmā said: Then the gods headed by Viṣṇu, and the sages rich in austerity, having performed their obligatory rites, made preparations for the departure from the mountain's city.
m.2.3.53.2: Then the best of mountains, having bathed and carefully worshipped his chosen deity, summoned the citizens and kinsmen and joyfully went to the guests' lodging.
m.2.3.53.3: There, having worshipped the Lord, he joyfully made an earnest request: Stay for some days in my house together with everyone.
m.2.3.53.4: O Śambhu, by the sight of you I am fulfilled, there is no doubt; and blessed am I, into whose house you have come with the gods.
m.2.3.53.5: Brahmā said: Having spoken much in this way, the lord of mountains, with joined palms and bowing, invited the Lord together with Viṣṇu, the gods and the others.
m.2.3.53.6: Then the sages and gods, having mentally consulted together with Śiva, delighted, replied respectfully, along with Viṣṇu, the gods and the rest.
m.2.3.53.7: The gods said: Blessed are you, O tiger among mountains; your fame is very great. In the three worlds there is no one equal to you, no person more meritorious.
m.2.3.53.8: At whose door Maheśāna, the supreme Brahman, the refuge of the good, loving to his devotees, has come out of compassion together with his attendants.
m.2.3.53.9: The lodging is very delightful, and varied honour has been shown; and the dishes are unprecedented, beyond description, O lord of mountains.
m.2.3.53.10: Surely there is nothing to wonder at where the goddess Śivā Ambikā dwells; everything is complete without remainder, and we are blessed that we have come.
m.2.3.53.11: Brahmā said: Thus there was excellent mutual praise there; a festival of many kinds arose, with sounds of Vedic chanting, well done and victory.
m.2.3.53.12: There was auspicious singing, and the troop of Apsarases danced; the bards (Māgadhas) and others sang praises, and gifts of wealth were given in abundance.
m.2.3.53.13: Then, having invited the lord of gods, the mountain went to his own house and began the festive feast according to various prescribed procedures.
m.2.3.53.14: For the meal he lovingly and fittingly brought the Lord, Īśvara, together with his retinue, amid great excitement.
m.2.3.53.15: Having washed with great reverence the feet of Śambhu, of Viṣṇu and of me, and duly those of all the immortals and the sages,
m.2.3.53.16: and of the others who had come, the lord of mountains, accompanied by his kinsmen, seated each of them with great affection inside the pavilion.
m.2.3.53.17: The mountain satisfied them with delicious and varied foods; all of them ate, together with Śambhu, Viṣṇu and me.
m.2.3.53.18: At that time the women of the city joyfully sang teasing abuse-songs, laughing with gentle voices and gazing intently at them.
m.2.3.53.19: Having eaten and duly rinsed their mouths, and taken leave of the mountain, O Nārada, they all went to their own quarters, delighted and fully satisfied.
m.2.3.53.20: Thus on the third day too, O sage, they were duly honoured by the lord of mountains with gifts, honours, respect and the like.
m.2.3.53.21: When the fourth day arrived, the Caturthī rite was duly performed with purity—without which that marriage remains incomplete.
m.2.3.53.22: There was a festival of many kinds with cries of well done and victory, abundant gifts, fine singing, and dancing of various kinds as well.
m.2.3.53.23: When the fifth day came, all the gods, full of joy, with great affection made a request to the mountain regarding their departure.
m.2.3.53.24: Hearing that, the lord of mountains, with joined palms, said to the gods: Let the gods stay some more days and show me grace.
m.2.3.53.25: Having said this, out of affection he made them—the Lord, Viṣṇu, me and the others—stay for many days, always with great respect.
m.2.3.53.26: Thus many days passed for them as they dwelt there; then the gods sent the seven sages to the lord of mountains.
m.2.3.53.27: They counselled him and Menā as befitted the occasion, and joyfully, duly praising, explained the supreme truth of Śiva.
m.2.3.53.28: Through their various counsels, O sage, it was accepted by the lord of mountains; and Śambhu, with the gods and others, went to the lord of mountains to take leave for the journey.
m.2.3.53.29: As Śiva, the lord of gods, accompanied by the gods, was setting out for his own mountain, Menā wept loudly and spoke to that treasure of compassion.
m.2.3.53.30: Menā said: O treasure of compassion, showing compassion, you will cherish Śivā; being easily pleased, you will forgive Pārvatī's thousand faults.
m.2.3.53.31: My child has been devoted to your lotus feet birth after birth; in dream or in waking awareness she has no remembrance of anything but the Lord Mahādeva.
m.2.3.53.32: Merely on hearing of devotion to you she is filled with tears of joy and thrilling of the hair; at slander of you she becomes silent, as if dead, O Mṛtyuñjaya.
m.2.3.53.33: Brahmā said: Having spoken thus, Menakā then entrusted her own daughter to him, and weeping very loudly, fainted before the two of them.
m.2.3.53.34: Then, having consoled Menā and taken leave of her and likewise of the mountain, Śiva set out on the journey with the gods, amid a great festival.
m.2.3.53.35: Then all the immortals, with the Lord and his own Gaṇas, silently set out on the journey toward the mountain, keeping Śiva in mind.
m.2.3.53.36: In a garden outside the city of Himācala the delighted gods, together with the Lord and in festive mood, halted and awaited the coming of Śivā.
m.2.3.53.37: Thus has been told Śiva's auspicious journey with the gods, O lord of sages; now hear of Śivā's journey, attended by the festivity mingled with separation.
m.2.3.53.iti: Thus ends the fifty-third adhyāya, named Śiva's journey, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.3.54.1: Brahmā said: Then those Seven Sages said to the lord of the Himālaya mountain: O mountain, have the departure of your daughter, the goddess, carried out today, as is fitting.
m.2.3.54.2: Hearing this, the lord of the mountains, realising the great separation from her that was coming, became dejected for some time out of his great love, O lord of sages.
m.2.3.54.3: After some time the king of mountains regained his composure; then, saying in words, so be it, he gave the message to Menā.
m.2.3.54.4: Hearing the mountain's message, O sage, Menā, overcome by joy and sorrow, made arrangements for the send-off and became ready to carry it out.
m.2.3.54.5: O sage, Menā, beloved of the mountain, duly performed the customs of the Vedas and of her own family, and held various festivities there.
m.2.3.54.6: She adorned Girijā with excellent garments set with various jewels, with the twelve ornaments, and with adornments befitting royalty.
m.2.3.54.7: Understanding Menā's wish, a certain virtuous brahmin lady instructed Girijā in the supreme vow of wifely devotion.
m.2.3.54.8: The brahmin's wife said: O Girijā, listen with good will to my words, which increase righteousness, bring joy here and hereafter, and give happiness to those who hear them.
m.2.3.54.9: Blessed is the woman devoted to her husband; no other is so especially worthy of honour. She purifies all the worlds and destroys the mass of all sins.
m.2.3.54.10: She who serves her husband with love as if he were the Supreme Lord, O Śivā, enjoys all pleasures here and at the end attains the auspicious goal together with her husband.
m.2.3.54.11: Devoted wives were Sāvitrī, Lopāmudrā, Arundhatī, Śāṇḍilyā, Śatarūpā, Anasūyā, Lakṣmī, Svadhā, Satī,
m.2.3.54.12: Saṃjñā, Sumati, Śraddhā, Menā and likewise Svāhā; and many other virtuous women too, who are not mentioned for fear of prolixity.
m.2.3.54.13: Through the virtue of wifely devotion alone they attained universal honour, and became revered even by Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Hara and the great sages.
m.2.3.54.14: Therefore your husband, Lord Śaṅkara, should always be served by you; he bestows grace on the afflicted, is to be served by all, and is the refuge of the good.
m.2.3.54.15: Great is the dharma of the devoted wife, enjoined in the Śrutis and Smṛtis. As this is described as the best, certainly no other is equal to it.
m.2.3.54.16: Intent on wifely devotion, she should eat after her beloved husband has eaten; O Śivā, O virtuous one, the woman should stand when he is standing, in every way.
m.2.3.54.17: She should always sleep when he sleeps, but the wise one should wake first. Guileless in conduct, the beloved should always do what is good for him.
m.2.3.54.18: O Śivā, she should never show herself to him unadorned; when he has gone abroad on business, she should remain without ornaments.
m.2.3.54.19: A devoted wife should never utter her husband's name; even when scolded she should not scold back, and even when struck she should remain gracious. She should say: Let me be struck, O master, but show me mercy.
m.2.3.54.20: When called, she should leave her household tasks and go quickly to him, with joined palms, lovingly; bowing deeply, she should say thus:
m.2.3.54.21: For what purpose have I been called, O lord? Let that favour be shown to me. Then, as instructed by him, she should do the task with a cheerful mind.
m.2.3.54.22: She should not stand long at the door, nor go to another's house; taking anything whatsoever of his, she should never give it to anyone.
m.2.3.54.23: Without being told, she should herself prepare all the requisites for worship, awaiting the occasion and doing what is beneficial and suited to the time.
m.2.3.54.24: She should never go on a pilgrimage without her husband's permission; she should keep far away from watching social gatherings and festivals.
m.2.3.54.25: A woman who desires the merit of holy places should drink the water of her husband's feet; in it are all the holy places and sacred sites, there is no doubt.
m.2.3.54.26: The devoted wife should eat her husband's leftovers, whatever food and the like is pleasing, given by her husband, calling it great prasāda.
m.2.3.54.27: She should not eat without sharing among gods, ancestors and guests, among the servants, cows and groups of mendicants.
m.2.3.54.28: With household goods well kept, skilful, cheerful, averse to extravagance, that lady should always be devoted to the vow of wifely loyalty.
m.2.3.54.29: Without her husband's permission she should not undertake fasts, vows and the like; otherwise they bear no fruit, and she goes to hell in the next world.
m.2.3.54.30: She should never rouse her husband when he is comfortably seated at ease or enjoying himself as he pleases, even for household matters.
m.2.3.54.31: Whether her husband is impotent, in bad circumstances, sick or old, happy or unhappy, she should not transgress her one husband.
m.2.3.54.32: During her menses, for three nights she should not show her face, nor let her voice be heard, until she is purified by bathing.
m.2.3.54.33: Having bathed well, she should look at her husband's face and never at another's; or else, meditating on her husband in her mind, she should look at the sun.
m.2.3.54.34: Turmeric, kuṅkuma, vermilion, collyrium and the like, the bodice, betel, the auspicious ornaments and so on,
m.2.3.54.35: the dressing of the hair, the braid, and ornaments of the hands, ears and so on—a devoted wife who desires long life for her husband should not set these aside.
m.2.3.54.36: She should never make friends with a washerwoman, an unchaste woman, a female ascetic, or an ill-fated woman.
m.2.3.54.37: She should never converse with a woman who hates her husband. She should never stay alone anywhere, nor ever bathe naked.
m.2.3.54.38: A chaste woman should never sit on a mortar, a pestle, a broom, a grinding stone, a mill, or the threshold.
m.2.3.54.39: Except at the time of intimacy she should never behave boldly; wherever her husband's liking lies, there she should be loving.
m.2.3.54.40: She should be joyful when he is joyful and dejected when her beloved's face is dejected. O Devī, the beloved wife should be devoted to her husband (pativratā), always seeking her husband's welfare.
m.2.3.54.41: The virtuous woman should remain the same in prosperity and in adversity. Holding firm to fortitude, she should never let herself be thrown out of balance.
m.2.3.54.42: Even when ghee, salt, oil and the like have run out, the devoted wife should not tell her husband there is none; she should not burden him with troubles.
m.2.3.54.43: For a devoted wife, her husband alone is held to be greater than Brahmā, Viṣṇu or even Hara. O Queen of the gods, her own husband is indeed Śiva.
m.2.3.54.44: She who undertakes vows, fasts and observances in disregard of her husband takes away her husband's lifespan, and after death goes to hell.
m.2.3.54.45: The woman who, when spoken to, answers back, given to anger, is reborn as a bitch in a village or a she-jackal in a desolate forest.
m.2.3.54.46: A woman should not occupy a high seat, nor go near wicked people, nor ever speak words of distress to her husband.
m.2.3.54.47: She should not speak slander; she should keep far away from quarrels. In the presence of elders she should never speak loudly nor laugh.
m.2.3.54.48: Seeing her husband coming from outside, with promptly offered food, water and refreshments, with betel, with garments, and with massaging of his feet and the like,
m.2.3.54.49: and likewise with sweet words and other excellent means of removing fatigue — she who, herself pleased, gladdens her beloved, by her the three worlds are gladdened.
m.2.3.54.50: A father gives in measure, a brother gives in measure, a son gives in measure; she should always honour her husband, who is the giver of the immeasurable.
m.2.3.54.51: The husband is her god, the husband is her guru, he is her dharma, holy places and vows. Therefore, abandoning all else, she should worship her husband alone.
m.2.3.54.52: The evil-minded woman who abandons her husband and roams about in secret is reborn as a cruel owl, dwelling in the hollow of a tree.
m.2.3.54.53: If, when struck, she wishes to strike back, she becomes a tigress or a she-cat; she who casts side-glances at another man becomes squint-eyed.
m.2.3.54.54: She who, leaving out her husband, eats sweet food by herself becomes a sow in the village, or else a bat that eats its own excrement.
m.2.3.54.55: She who addresses her beloved disrespectfully with tu (you) is surely born mute; she who is always jealous of a co-wife is ill-fated again and again.
m.2.3.54.56: She who, evading her husband's gaze, looks at some other man is born one-eyed, with a turned-away face, and ugly.
m.2.3.54.57: Just as a body devoid of life becomes impure in a moment, so a woman devoid of her husband is always impure, even when well bathed.
m.2.3.54.58: Blessed in the world is that mother, blessed is that father who begot her, and blessed is that husband in whose home there is a noble devoted wife.
m.2.3.54.59: Three generations each of the father's line, the mother's line and the husband's line enjoy happiness in heaven through the merit of a devoted wife.
m.2.3.54.60: Women of bad conduct, through breach of virtue, cause the three families — of father, mother and husband — to fall, and they suffer both here and hereafter.
m.2.3.54.61: Wherever the foot of a devoted wife touches the ground, there that ground becomes destructive of sin and highly purifying.
m.2.3.54.62: Even the mighty Sun makes contact with a devoted wife, as do the Moon and the Wind, for their own purification and for no other reason.
m.2.3.54.63: The waters always long for the touch of a devoted wife, thinking: Today the destruction of our coldness has come about; today we are purifiers of others.
m.2.3.54.64: The wife is the root of the householder; the wife is the root of happiness; the wife is for attaining the fruit of dharma; the wife is for the increase of progeny.
m.2.3.54.65: Are there not in every house women proud of their beauty and charm? But a devoted wife is obtained only through devotion to the Lord of the universe.
m.2.3.54.66: The other world and this world — both are won through a wife. A man without a wife is not entitled to rites such as worship of the gods, ancestors and guests.
m.2.3.54.67: He alone should be known as a true householder in whose home there is a devoted wife; others are devoured day by day, as if by the demoness Old Age.
m.2.3.54.68: Just as the body becomes pure by bathing in the Gaṅgā, so by seeing a devoted wife everything becomes pure.
m.2.3.54.69: There is no difference between the Gaṅgā and the woman for whom her husband is her deity. Such a couple are directly equal to Umā and Śiva; therefore the wise should worship them both.
m.2.3.54.70: The husband is the Praṇava (Om), the wife is the Veda; she is forbearance, he is austerity itself; the husband is the fruit, she is the good deed. Blessed, O Śivā, is such a couple.
m.2.3.54.71: Thus, O daughter of the king of mountains, the dharma of the devoted wife has been described to you. Now hear from me, with great delight and attention, its divisions.
m.2.3.54.72: O Devī, devoted wives are said to be of four kinds, distinguished as the best and so on; they remove the sins of those who remember them.
m.2.3.54.73: The best, the middling, the inferior and the very inferior — I shall tell their characteristics; listen attentively.
m.2.3.54.74: She whose mind, even in dreams, always sees only her own husband and never another man, O gentle one, is declared the best.
m.2.3.54.75: She who with a pure mind looks upon another man as a father, brother or son is called the middling devoted wife, O daughter of the mountain.
m.2.3.54.76: She who, understanding her own dharma in her mind, does not commit infidelity is called the inferior one, yet she is of good conduct, O Pārvatī.
m.2.3.54.77: She who refrains from infidelity out of fear of her husband and of the family is called the lowest devoted wife by the sages of old.
m.2.3.54.78: O Śivā, all four kinds of devoted wives destroy sin; they purify all the worlds and are joyful both here and hereafter.
m.2.3.54.79: Through the power of her wifely devotion, the wife of Atri, at the request of the three gods, brought back to life a certain brāhmaṇa who had died through the curse of Vārāha.
m.2.3.54.80: Knowing this, O Śivā, O daughter of the mountain, you should always serve your husband with love, for this service always bestows all desires.
m.2.3.54.81: You are the Mother of the world, the great Goddess, and Śiva himself is your husband. Indeed, by remembering you women become devoted to their husbands.
m.2.3.54.82: O Goddess, what purpose is there in telling this before you? Still, O Śivā, I have told it today in keeping with the custom of the world.
m.2.3.54.83: Brahmā said: Having said this and bowed deeply to Śivā, that Brahmin woman fell silent. Pārvatī, beloved of Śaṅkara, attained great joy.
m.2.3.54.iti: Thus ends the fifty-fourth adhyāya, named The dharma of a devoted wife, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.3.55.1: Brahmā said: Then that Brahmin woman, having taught the goddess that vow, addressed Menā and said: Arrange her departure.
m.2.3.55.2: Saying, so be it, she became overwhelmed by love. Gathering her composure, she called Kālī, distressed at the pain of separation.
m.2.3.55.3: Embracing her again and again, she wept very loudly. Pārvatī too wept loudly, uttering words of tenderness.
m.2.3.55.4: The mountain's beloved Menā and Śivā too, afflicted by grief, fell into a swoon; and at Pārvatī's weeping the wives of the gods also swooned.
m.2.3.55.5: All the women wept; everything became senseless. The lord of yogins himself wept as he was going — what other lord could be higher?
m.2.3.55.6: Meanwhile Himālaya quickly came there, with all his sons, his ministers and eminent Brahmins.
m.2.3.55.7: He himself wept out of affection, holding his darling child to his breast, crying again and again, where are you going, and feeling everything empty.
m.2.3.55.8: Then the family priest, most wise, together with the Brahmins, compassionately comforted everyone gently with spiritual knowledge.
m.2.3.55.9: Pārvatī bowed with devotion to her mother, father and preceptor; the Great Māyā, following worldly custom, wept loudly again and again.
m.2.3.55.10: At Pārvatī's very weeping all the women wept — above all her mother Menā, and likewise her female kin and brothers.
m.2.3.55.11: Again and again Śivā's mother, the kinswomen and other women, the brothers and the father, bound by affection, wept out of love.
m.2.3.55.12: Then the Brahmins came and respectfully consoled them, and announced the auspicious moment for the journey, supremely favourable.
m.2.3.55.13: Then Himālaya, having steadied Menā and himself with discernment, had a palanquin brought for Śivā to mount.
m.2.3.55.14: The Brahmin women seated Śivā in it; and all of them, the father, mother and the Brahmins likewise, gave her blessings.
m.2.3.55.15: Menā and the mountain gave her the requisites befitting a great queen, and a heap of various auspicious goods hard for others to obtain.
m.2.3.55.16: Śivā, having bowed to all her elders, to her father and mother, to the Brahmins, the family priest, the kinswomen and other women, departed, O sage.
m.2.3.55.17: The wise Himācala too, moved by affection, went along with his sons, and arrived where the Lord was with the gods, bearing delight.
m.2.3.55.18: All rejoiced lovingly amid a great festival; they bowed to the Lord with devotion and, praising him, entered the city.
m.2.3.55.19: Śiva said: I remind you, who remember your former births — if you remember, tell me. O queen of the gods, in my play you are ever dear to me as my life.
m.2.3.55.20: Brahmā said: Hearing this from Maheśa, her own lord, Pārvatī — the chaste one, ever dear to Śaṅkara — spoke with a smile.
m.2.3.55.21: Pārvatī said: I remember everything, O lord of my life; be silent about it. Now quickly do what befits the occasion. Salutation to you.
m.2.3.55.22: Brahmā said: Hearing his beloved's words, like a hundred streams of nectar, the Lord of the universe, intent on worldly custom, rejoiced greatly.
m.2.3.55.23: Śiva, having gathered provisions, fed the gods headed by Nārāyaṇa with many delightful things.
m.2.3.55.24: Likewise the Lord lovingly fed all the others who had come to his wedding with tasty food of many kinds.
m.2.3.55.25: Then, having eaten, all those gods, adorned with various jewels, with their wives and attendants, bowed to the moon-crested Śiva.
m.2.3.55.26: Having praised him with pleasing words and circumambulated him, full of joy and praising the wedding, they then went to their own abodes.
m.2.3.55.27: O sage, Śiva himself, adopting worldly custom, bowed to Nārāyaṇa and to me, just as Viṣṇu bows to Kaśyapa.
m.2.3.55.28: I embraced him and gave him my blessing; then, before Śiva, regarding him as the supreme Brahman, I offered an excellent hymn of praise.
m.2.3.55.29: Taking leave of him, Viṣṇu together with me, with folded hands before Śiva and Śivā, joyfully praising their wedding, went to his own supreme abode.
m.2.3.55.30: Śiva too stayed on his own mountain, sporting joyfully with Pārvatī; all the Gaṇas, worshipping the divine pair, attained great happiness.
m.2.3.55.31: Thus, dear one, has the most auspicious wedding of Śiva been narrated: it destroys grief, brings joy, prolongs life and increases wealth.
m.2.3.55.32: Whoever, pure and with mind fixed on it, listens to this regularly, or recites it to others with discipline, would attain Śiva's world.
m.2.3.55.33: This wondrous narrative that has been told is an abode of auspiciousness, allaying all obstacles and destroying all diseases.
m.2.3.55.34: It brings fame, heaven and long life, supremely grants sons and grandsons, bestows all desires here, and always gives enjoyment and liberation.
m.2.3.55.35: It averts untimely death, brings great peace, is auspicious, removes all bad dreams, and is a means to intelligence, wisdom and the like.
m.2.3.55.36: At all festivals of Śiva it should be recited with care and love by people desiring good, for it is a cause of Śiva's satisfaction.
m.2.3.55.37: One should recite it especially at the time of installing images of gods and others, and with great delight at the beginning of every undertaking connected with Śiva.
m.2.3.55.38: Or, having become pure, one should listen to the auspicious story of Śiva and Śivā; all undertakings succeed — truly, truly, without doubt.
m.2.3.55.iti: Thus ends the fifty-fifth adhyāya, named Śiva goes to Kailāsa, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, in the dialogue between Brahmā and Nārada, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.4.1.1: I bow to Śiva, whose mind is pleased by salutation, who holds intense love dear and bestows love; who is full and makes others full, the sole abode of all complete sovereign powers; who is Truth, made of truth, whose glory is true in the three times, who loves truth and grants truth; to Śaṅkara, praised by Viṣṇu and Brahmā, who has taken on a form out of his own grace.
m.2.4.1.2: Nārada said: After marrying Girijā, what did Śaṅkara, the benefactor of the worlds, do on going to his own mountain, O Brahmā? Tell me that.
m.2.4.1.3: How indeed was a son born to Śiva, the Supreme Self, for whose sake the Lord, though delighting in his own Self, married Śivā?
m.2.4.1.4: How, O Brahmā, did the slaying of Tāraka, which brought welfare to the gods, come about? Tell me all this completely, showing kindness to me.
m.2.4.1.5: Sūta said: Having heard these words of Nārada, Prajāpati, his mind well pleased, remembered Śaṅkara and replied.
m.2.4.1.6: Brahmā said: Listen, O Nārada: I shall tell the deeds of the moon-crested one, the divine story of Guha's birth and the righteous slaying of the demon Tāraka.
m.2.4.1.7: Let it be heard: today I narrate a story that destroys sin, hearing which a person is surely freed from all sins.
m.2.4.1.8: This narrative is pure, secret and supremely wonderful; it removes the torment of sin and destroys all obstacles.
m.2.4.1.9: It grants every auspiciousness, is the essence, delightful to all ears, gives happiness, is the seed of liberation, and cuts the root of karma.
m.2.4.1.10: Having come to Kailāsa after marrying Śivā, Śiva too attained great splendour; and he reflected on the task of the gods, and also on the suffering of people in carrying out the gods' task.
m.2.4.1.11: When that Lord Śiva himself went to Kailāsa, all the Gaṇas, overjoyed, made various festivities.
m.2.4.1.12: When Śiva had come to Kailāsa there was a great festival; the gods returned to their own domains, their minds brimming with joy.
m.2.4.1.13: Then Śambhu, the Great God, taking Girijā, Śivā, went to a solitary place, most divine and charming.
m.2.4.1.14: There he made a bed conducive to love, strewn with flowers and sandal paste, wonderful, supreme, auspicious, and furnished with articles of enjoyment.
m.2.4.1.15: There the Lord Śambhu, the giver of honour, sported with Girijā for a thousand years by the reckoning of the gods.
m.2.4.1.16: By the mere touch of Durgā's body Śiva playfully swooned; and she, swooning from Śiva's touch, did not know day from night.
m.2.4.1.17: While Hara was engaged in enjoyment, setting in motion the way of the world, a great span of time passed for the two of them like a moment, O sinless one.
m.2.4.1.18: Then once, dear son, all the gods led by Śakra gathered together, came to Meru and held counsel.
m.2.4.1.19: The gods said: The Lord Śambhu, lord of yogins, changeless, delighting in his own Self, stainless, married for the sake of our task.
m.2.4.1.20: No son has been born to him; we do not know the reason for this. Why is this delay being made by the lord of the gods?
m.2.4.1.21: Brahmā said: Meanwhile the gods learned from Nārada, who sees the divine, the extent of the enjoyment of the two as they made love.
m.2.4.1.22: Knowing the enjoyment of the two to be long-lasting, those gods became anxious and, putting me, Brahmā, at their head, went to Nārāyaṇa.
m.2.4.1.23: Bowing to him, I related the whole matter as desired; all the gods stood still like figures in a painting.
m.2.4.1.24: I said: For a thousand years by the gods' reckoning Śaṅkara, absorbed in love-play and motionless, the yogin, does not desist.
m.2.4.1.25: The Lord said: There is no cause for worry, O creator of the world; all will be well. O lord of gods, go for refuge to Śaṅkara, the great Lord.
m.2.4.1.26: Those people who with their mind and with joy have taken refuge in Maheśa — for those devotees, O lord of creatures, there is no fear from anywhere at any time.
m.2.4.1.27: The interruption of their love-play will happen in due time, not now, O Vidhi. A task prompted by time attains success, not otherwise.
m.2.4.1.28: Who here is able to break off Śambhu's cherished love-union? When a thousand years are complete, he will desist of his own accord.
m.2.4.1.29: Whoever by some device breaks off the love-making of a woman and a man suffers separation from wife and sons birth after birth.
m.2.4.1.30: Here he becomes bereft of knowledge, his fame lost, deprived of fortune; and at the end that sinner goes to the Kālasūtra hell for a hundred thousand years.
m.2.4.1.31: The great lord of sages Durvāsas made this Śakra, united with Rambhā, desist from love-play; as a result, his separation from his wife came about.
m.2.4.1.32: Again, having obtained and enjoyed another, fair-handed woman, after a thousand divine years he cast off the fever of separation.
m.2.4.1.33: Guru Bṛhaspati restrained Kāma while he was embracing Ghṛtācī; within six months Candra carried off his wife.
m.2.4.1.34: Then, having worshipped Śiva and fought the war over Tārā, he got Tārā back, pregnant, and cast off the fever of separation.
m.2.4.1.35: The great seer Gautama made Candra, who was with Mohinī, desist from love-play; as a result, his separation from his wife came about.
m.2.4.1.36: Hariścandra stopped a ploughman who lay motionless, united with a low-caste woman in a lonely place; hear the result of that.
m.2.4.1.37: He was deprived of wife, son and kingdom and was tormented by Viśvāmitra; then, having worshipped Śiva, he was freed from that misery.
m.2.4.1.38: Out of fear, the gods did not restrain Ajāmila, the best of brahmins, when he was united with a low-caste woman, nor did anyone restrain her.
m.2.4.1.39: Everything is accomplished through destiny (niṣeka), O Vidhi; destiny is powerful. It indeed gives its fruit; by whom can destiny be warded off?
m.2.4.1.40: That love-making of Śambhu lasts a thousand divine years; when the thousand years are complete, O lords of gods, go there…
m.2.4.1.41: You will certainly do that by which the semen falls upon the ground. And from that semen will be born the Lord's son, named Skanda.
m.2.4.1.42: Now go to your own abode, O Vidhi, together with the hosts of gods. Let Śambhu enjoy union with Pārvatī in solitude.
m.2.4.1.43: Brahmā said: Having said this, the beloved of Kamalā quickly went to his own inner palace. The gods, along with me, went to their own abodes, O lord of sages.
m.2.4.1.44: Then, through the intense love-play of Śakti and the Possessor of Śakti, the earth, overwhelmed by the weight, trembled, together with Śeṣa and the Tortoise.
m.2.4.1.45: Indeed, through the weight on the Tortoise, the wind, the support of all, was brought to a standstill; then the three worlds became distraught with fear.
m.2.4.1.46: Then all the gods, with me, went to Hari for refuge and, dejected in mind, reported that whole occurrence.
m.2.4.1.47: The gods said: O God of gods, Lord of Ramā, O Master who protects all, save us who have come to you for refuge, our minds agitated by fear.
m.2.4.1.48: The life-breath of the three worlds has been stilled, for what reason we do not know. The three worlds, with moving and unmoving beings, together with the sages and gods, are in distress.
m.2.4.1.49: Brahmā said: Having spoken thus, all the gods, with me, O lord of sages, stood dejected before Viṣṇu, fallen silent and deeply grieved.
m.2.4.1.50: Hearing that, Hari took all of us gods with him and quickly went to Mount Kailāsa, dear to Śiva.
m.2.4.1.51: Having gone there, Hari, dear to the gods, together with the gods and me, went to Śiva's excellent abode, desiring to see Śaṅkara.
m.2.4.1.52: Not seeing Śiva there, Viṣṇu along with the gods was astonished. Full of humility, he questioned Śiva's attendants (gaṇas) stationed there.
m.2.4.1.53: Viṣṇu said: O followers of Śaṅkara, O gaṇas, where has Śiva, the Lord of all, gone? Kindly tell us, who are distressed, O compassionate ones.
m.2.4.1.54: Brahmā said: Hearing these words of Hari, who was accompanied by the gods, those gaṇas of Śaṅkara spoke affectionately to the Lord of Ramā.
m.2.4.1.55: The attendants of Śiva said: O Hari, listen: out of love for Śiva we shall truly tell you, together with Brahmā and the gods, the whole account as it happened.
m.2.4.1.56: Mahādeva, the Lord of all, adept in many kinds of divine play, went to Girijā's dwelling, having lovingly stationed us here.
m.2.4.1.57: What Śambhu, the great Lord, is doing inside that cave we do not know, O Lord of Ramā; many years have passed.
m.2.4.1.58: Brahmā said: Hearing these words of theirs, that Viṣṇu, with the gods and me, greatly astonished, O best of sages, went to Śiva's door.
m.2.4.1.59: Having gone there with me and the gods, that Hari, dear to the gods, then called out in an anguished voice, in a loud tone, O sage.
m.2.4.1.60: Standing there, O best of sages, Hari, together with the gods and me, praised Śambhu with great love—Hara, Lord of all the worlds.
m.2.4.1.61: Viṣṇu said: What are you doing within, O Mahādeva, Supreme Lord? Protect all of us gods, tormented by Tāraka, who have come to you for refuge.
m.2.4.1.62: Praising Śambhu thus in many ways, Hari, together with me and the gods tormented by Tāraka, wept bitterly there, O lord of sages.
m.2.4.1.63: There arose there a tumult of grief from the heaven-dwellers, the afflicted gods, mingled with praise of Śiva, O lord of sages.
m.2.4.1.iti: Thus ends the first adhyāya, named Śiva's sport, in the fourth khaṇḍa, the Kumāra-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.4.2.1: Brahmā said: Having heard that, Mahādeva, expert in yoga and knowledge, though he had given up desire, did not break off his union with her for fear of Pārvatī.
m.2.4.2.2: Śiva came to the door of the house, near the gods who were oppressed by the demon — Śaṅkara, who is affectionate to his devotees.
m.2.4.2.3: Then all the gods, together with Hari and me, having seen the Lord Śiva, affectionate to devotees, became exceedingly happy.
m.2.4.2.4: Having thus heard the words of those gods, the blessed Bhava replied, dejected in spirit, with an aching heart.
m.2.4.2.5: Bowing with very great love, their shoulders bent, all the immortals, together with me and Hari, praised Śaṅkara, O sage.
m.2.4.2.6: The gods said: O God of gods, O Mahādeva, O ocean of compassion, O Lord, you are indeed the inner controller of all; you know everything, O Śaṅkara.
m.2.4.2.7: Accomplish the gods' task, O all-pervading one; protect the gods, O Maheśvara. Showing compassion, slay the demons headed by Tāraka, O great Lord.
m.2.4.2.8: Śiva said: O Viṣṇu, O Vidhi (Brahmā), O gods — the intent of all of you is known to me. What is to be, that indeed comes to pass; no one can prevent it.
m.2.4.2.9: What has happened has happened. Listen to the matter at hand, O immortals: who will now take my semen that has slipped forth from Śiva?
m.2.4.2.10: Saying, let him take it, he let it fall upon the ground. Then Agni, having become a dove, urged on by all the gods,
m.2.4.2.11: then swallowed the whole of Śambhu's semen with his beak. Meanwhile, O sage, Girijā came there.
m.2.4.2.12: And as Śiva's return was delayed, she saw the foremost of the gods; having learned that whole affair, Śivā was filled with great wrath.
m.2.4.2.13: Then she spoke to all the gods, headed by Hari.
m.2.4.2.14: The Goddess said: O you hosts of gods, all of you are especially wicked. Ever bent on achieving your own ends, you cause suffering to others for that purpose.
m.2.4.2.15: For your own sake you propitiated Maheśāna, the supreme Lord, and spoiled my love-sport; I have become barren, O gods.
m.2.4.2.16: By opposing me, O immortals, no one at all finds happiness; therefore suffering shall indeed befall you, wicked dwellers of heaven.
m.2.4.2.17: Brahmā said: Having said this, Śivā, the daughter of the king of mountains, blazing with fury, cursed all the gods headed by Viṣṇu.
m.2.4.2.18: Pārvatī said: From this day on, may the wives of the gods be barren; and may all the gods who oppose me be miserable.
m.2.4.2.19: Brahmā said: Having thus cursed all the gods headed by Viṣṇu, the Mistress of all, enraged, spoke to Pāvaka (Agni), the swallower of Śiva's semen.
m.2.4.2.20: Pārvatī said: Be an eater of everything, O Śuci, and ever tormented in yourself. You do not know the truth of Śiva; you are a fool, a mere doer of the gods' business.
m.2.4.2.21: O rogue, most wicked one, of wicked mind even among the wicked, in swallowing Śiva's semen you did not do what was proper and beneficial.
m.2.4.2.22: Brahmā said: Having thus cursed Fire, Śivā, the mountain's daughter, still dissatisfied, quickly went from there to her own abode with the Lord, O sage.
m.2.4.2.23: Having gone there, Śivā carefully and fully made Śiva understand, and she brought forth an excellent son named Gaṇeśa, O lord of sages.
m.2.4.2.24: I shall describe that whole account later, O sage. Now listen with great delight: I tell of the birth of Guha.
m.2.4.2.25: The immortals indeed eat the food and other offerings placed in the fire — so says the word of the Veda; hence all those gods became pregnant.
m.2.4.2.26: Then, unable to bear that semen, all the gods headed by Viṣṇu became greatly afflicted, their minds ruined by Śivā's command.
m.2.4.2.27: Then all the gods headed by Viṣṇu, bewildered and burning, quickly went for refuge to the Lord of Pārvatī.
m.2.4.2.28: Going to the door of Śiva's abode, all the gods, humbled, with joined palms, lovingly praised Śambhu together with Śivā.
m.2.4.2.29: The gods said: O God of gods, O Mahādeva, O Lord of Girijā, O great Lord, what has now happened, O master? Your māyā is hard to overcome.
m.2.4.2.30: We have become pregnant and are burning with your semen, O Śambhu. Show compassion; remove this condition.
m.2.4.2.31: Brahmā said: Having heard this praise of the immortals, the supreme Lord, husband of Śivā, swiftly came to the door where the gods stood, O sage.
m.2.4.2.32: All the gods together with Acyuta, bowing to Śaṅkara, affectionate to devotees, who had come to the door, lovingly praised him, dancing with joy.
m.2.4.2.33: The gods said: O Śambhu, O Śiva, O Maheśāna, we bow to you especially. Protect us, who have come for refuge and are burning with the semen.
m.2.4.2.34: Remove this suffering, O Hara. Surely we are dying. Without you, who today is able to remove the gods' suffering?
m.2.4.2.35: Brahmā said: Having heard these most piteous words, the Lord, king of the gods, affectionate to devotees, laughed and then replied to the gods.
m.2.4.2.36: Śiva said: O Hari, O Vidhi, O gods, all of you listen to my words: today you will have relief; be attentive.
m.2.4.2.37: All you gods, vomit out this semen of mine at once; by the command of me, your good Lord, you will then be especially happy.
m.2.4.2.38: Brahmā said: Placing this command on their heads, all the gods headed by Viṣṇu quickly vomited, remembering the imperishable Śiva.
m.2.4.2.39: That semen of Śambhu, gold-like in hue, wondrous, the shape of a mountain, fell upon the earth, very radiant, touching the very sky.
m.2.4.2.40: All the gods, Acyuta (Viṣṇu) and the rest, became happy, and they praised the supreme Lord Śaṅkara, who is affectionate to his devotees.
m.2.4.2.41: But Pāvaka (Agni) alone did not become happy there, O lord of sages. Śaṅkara, the supreme Lord, then gave him a command.
m.2.4.2.42: Then that Fire-god, distressed, with joined palms and bowing low, O sage, praised Śiva, not at ease in himself, and spoke these words.
m.2.4.2.43: Agni said: O God of gods, O great Lord, I, your servant, am a fool. Forgive my offence and remove my burning.
m.2.4.2.44: You, O master, are kind to the afflicted; you are Śaṅkara, the supreme Lord. Thus Pāvaka, with a gracious mind, replied to the one who is kind to the afflicted.
m.2.4.2.45: Brahmā said: Having heard these words of Śuci (Agni), that Śambhu, the supreme Lord, kind to the afflicted, replied to Pāvaka with a gracious mind.
m.2.4.2.46: Śiva said: You did an improper deed in that you swallowed my semen. Hence the burning came from the excess of sin; now by my command your burning has ceased.
m.2.4.2.47: Now, O Śuci, you have truly become happy, since you have sought refuge in me. Therefore I have become pleased; all your sorrow is perishing.
m.2.4.2.48: Carefully deposit my semen in the womb of some good woman; then you will become happy and especially free from burning.
m.2.4.2.49: Brahmā said: Having heard these words of Śambhu, Śuci, with joined palms and bowing, replied slowly and with affection to Śaṅkara, the benefactor of devotees.
m.2.4.2.50: O Lord, O Maheśvara, this energy of yours is unapproachable. Apart from Śakti, there is no woman in the three worlds able to hold it in her womb.
m.2.4.2.51: When the Fire-god spoke thus, then you, O best of sages, prompted by Śaṅkara and wishing to help, spoke to Agni with sincere heart.
m.2.4.2.52: Nārada said: Listen, O Fire, to my auspicious words which will take away your burning, which grant supreme bliss, are pleasing, and remove all distress.
m.2.4.2.53: Having carried out this remedy, O Fire, be happy and free of burning. By Śiva's will I have properly told you this with respect, dear one.
m.2.4.2.54: O Śuci, those women who perform the early-morning bath in the month of Tapas (Māgha) — in their bodies place this great semen of Śiva.
m.2.4.2.55: Brahmā said: At that moment the wives of the seven sages came there in the morning, observing their vows, wishing to bathe in the month of Tapas, O sage.
m.2.4.2.56: Having bathed, six of those women, afflicted by severe cold and wishing to leave, went near the flames of the fire, O sage.
m.2.4.2.57: Seeing them deluded by Giriśa's command, Arundhatī, of virtuous conduct and good understanding, firmly forbade them.
m.2.4.2.58: Those six sages' wives, deluded by Śiva's Māyā, went there forcibly out of infatuation, O sage, to rid themselves of their cold.
m.2.4.2.59: At once the particles of that semen entered their bodies, all of them through the pores of the hair, O sage, and the Fire-god became free of burning.
m.2.4.2.60: Vanishing quickly, the Fire-god in the form of flame went happily to his own world, remembering you and that Śaṅkara in his mind.
m.2.4.2.61: Those women, O virtuous one, became pregnant and were tormented by burning; they went to their own homes, dear one. Arundhatī was grieved on account of Agni.
m.2.4.2.62: Seeing the condition of their wives, dear one, the husbands, overcome with anger, quickly abandoned those women after consulting together, dear one.
m.2.4.2.63: Then all those six women, seeing their apparent unfaithfulness, were filled with great sorrow, dear one, and became troubled in mind.
m.2.4.2.64: The sages' wives cast off that semen of Śiva in the form of an embryo on the ridge of the Himālaya, and then became free of burning.
m.2.4.2.65: Unable to bear that semen of Śiva, the Himālaya began to tremble and, tormented by the burning, quickly threw the unbearable substance into the Gaṅgā.
m.2.4.2.66: And by the Gaṅgā too that unbearable seed of the Supreme Self was cast by her own waves into a clump of reeds, O lord of sages.
m.2.4.2.67: That semen, having fallen there, quickly became a boy — handsome, charming, glorious, radiant, increasing delight.
m.2.4.2.68: In the month of Mārgaśīrṣa, in the bright fortnight, on the sixth lunar day, O lord of sages, the manifestation of that son of Śiva took place on earth.
m.2.4.2.69: At that moment, O Brahman, the daughter of the snowy mountain (Pārvatī) and Giriśa too suddenly became joyful there on their own mountain.
m.2.4.2.70: Milk born of joy flowed from Śivā's breasts; and, having gone there, everyone felt great happiness, O sage.
m.2.4.2.71: Auspiciousness arose in the three worlds, dear one, bringing happiness to the good; for the wicked, and especially for the Daityas, obstacles arose.
m.2.4.2.72: Suddenly a great sound of kettledrums arose in the sky, and a shower of flowers quickly fell upon the boy, O Nārada.
m.2.4.2.73: For all the gods, Viṣṇu and the rest, O best of sages, there suddenly arose supreme joy and a great festival.
m.2.4.2.iti: Thus ends the second adhyāya, named The birth of Śiva's son, in the fourth khaṇḍa, the Kumāra-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.4.3.1: Nārada said: O god of gods, lord of creatures, O Brahmā, maker of creation, O lord, what happened there after that? Be gracious and tell me that now.
m.2.4.3.2: Brahmā said: At that time, dear son, the mighty Viśvāmitra, prompted by the Creator, came there by chance, pleased at heart.
m.2.4.3.3: Seeing the unearthly radiance of that very brilliant son, he had his desires fulfilled; deeply delighted, he bowed down.
m.2.4.3.4: With a delighted mind, and with words inspired by the Creator, Viśvāmitra, who knew the boy's power, offered him fine praise.
m.2.4.3.5: Then the son there, the doer of great sports, became very pleased; laughing heartily, he of wondrous splendour spoke to Viśvāmitra.
m.2.4.3.6: The son of Śiva said: O greatly wise one, by Śiva's will you have come here unexpectedly. Dear sir, perform my purificatory rite properly, in accordance with the Veda.
m.2.4.3.7: From today on, be my priest, bringing me delight. You will always be worthy of worship by all; there is no doubt of this.
m.2.4.3.8: Brahmā said: Hearing his words, the son of Gādhi was greatly pleased, and, much astonished, he replied to him in a low voice.
m.2.4.3.9: Viśvāmitra said: Listen, dear child: I am not a brāhmaṇa. I am the kṣatriya son of Gādhi, known as Viśvāmitra, a kṣatriya who serves brāhmaṇas.
m.2.4.3.10: Thus I have told you my own story, O excellent boy. Who are you? Tell me your whole story, for I am astonished.
m.2.4.3.11: Brahmā said: Hearing his words, the boy told him his own story. Then the doer of great sports spoke with great affection to that son of Gādhi.
m.2.4.3.12: The son of Śiva said: O Viśvāmitra, by my boon you are a brahmarṣi; there is no doubt of this. Vasiṣṭha and the others will always praise you with respect.
m.2.4.3.13: Therefore, at my command, you should perform the rite. All this is to be kept strictly secret by you; it must not be told anywhere.
m.2.4.3.14: Brahmā said: Then, O divine sage, he lovingly performed for Śiva's son the complete rite, in the proper way, by the excellent procedure prescribed in the Veda.
m.2.4.3.15: Śiva's child too, the lord who performs great sports, greatly pleased, gave supreme divine knowledge to the sage Viśvāmitra.
m.2.4.3.16: The son of Śuci Agni made Viśvāmitra his priest; from then on Viśvāmitra was the best of the twice-born, and the boy remained skilled in manifold sports.
m.2.4.3.17: Thus was a sport performed by him, and I have narrated it, O sage. Now, dear son, listen with delight to another sport of his; I shall tell it.
m.2.4.3.18: At that time, dear son, the one named Śveta Agni then saw there his own divine, supremely purifying son.
m.2.4.3.19: Then Pāvaka Agni went to him, saw him, embraced and kissed him; calling him my son, he gave him a weapon — the Śakti spear.
m.2.4.3.20: Guha took that spear and climbed the peak; he struck it with that spear, and the peak fell to the ground.
m.2.4.3.21: Heroic rākṣasas numbering ten padmas, who had come earlier to kill him, were swiftly destroyed by that blow.
m.2.4.3.22: A great cry of alarm arose; the earth with its mountains quaked, and the three worlds too. The lord of the gods Indra, together with the gods, came there.
m.2.4.3.23: He struck him on his right side with the thunderbolt; from that was born a single very powerful man named Śākha.
m.2.4.3.24: Again Śakra quickly struck him then on the left side with the thunderbolt; another man was born, a second powerful one called Viśākha.
m.2.4.3.25: Then Śakra struck his heart with the thunderbolt; another man arose, called Naigama, likewise very powerful.
m.2.4.3.26: Then the four — Skanda and the others — great heroes of great strength, rushed swiftly to kill Indra; and he Indra sought his refuge.
m.2.4.3.27: Śakra, with the host of immortals, seized by fear, then left that place and went to his own world, bewildered; he did not understand the secret, O sage.
m.2.4.3.28: But that boy, the lord who performs manifold sports, remained right there, full of joy and fearless as before, dear son.
m.2.4.3.29: At that time six women called the Kṛttikās came there to bathe and saw that boy, the great lord.
m.2.4.3.30: All those Kṛttikā women set their minds on taking him; a quarrel arose among them, each eager to take him, O sage.
m.2.4.3.31: To settle their quarrel he made himself six faces and drank the milk of all of them; and they were satisfied, O sage.
m.2.4.3.32: Understanding the inclination of his mind, all those Kṛttikās then took him and joyfully went to their own world, O sage.
m.2.4.3.33: Giving the breast to him who longed for it, they raised that boy called Kumāra, the son of the Lord, more radiant than the sun.
m.2.4.3.34: They never let the boy out of their sight; dearer than life itself is a little son to the one who nurtures him.
m.2.4.3.35: Whatever garments were rare in the three worlds, those they lovingly gave him, and excellent ornaments too.
m.2.4.3.36: Day by day they nourished that boy, the great lord, feeding him especially with delicious, much-praised foods.
m.2.4.3.37: Then one day, dear son, that boy, the son of the Kṛttikās, went to the divine assembly of the gods and performed a fine feat.
m.2.4.3.38: The boy who performs great sports displayed his own most wondrous splendour to all the gods, Viṣṇu included.
m.2.4.3.39: Seeing him, all those gods, together with Acyuta and the sages, were utterly astonished and questioned the boy.
m.2.4.3.40: Who are you? Hearing that, he said nothing at all; he quickly went to his own abode and remained hidden as before.
m.2.4.3.iti: Thus ends the third adhyāya, named The sport of Kārttikeya, in the fourth khaṇḍa, the Kumāra-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.4.4.1: Nārada said: O god of gods, lord of creatures, O Vidhi (Brahmā), what happened then? Out of compassion, tell me now the account filled with Śiva's divine play.
m.2.4.4.2: Brahmā said: O sage, after that son of Śambhu had been taken by the Kṛttikās, some time passed, and the daughter of the Himālaya did not know of it.
m.2.4.4.3: At that time Durgā, her lotus-face smiling, spoke to her husband Śambhu, the Lord, the master of the gods of gods.
m.2.4.4.4: Pārvatī said: O god of gods, Mahādeva, hear my auspicious words. Through the great weight of my former merit I obtained you, the Lord as husband.
m.2.4.4.5: Out of grace, though the foremost among yogins, you became intent on amorous sport. There the interruption of my love-play was brought about by the gods and by you, O Bhava.
m.2.4.4.6: Your semen, O all-pervading one, fell on the ground, not into my womb. Where did it go, O god, and by which god was it concealed?
m.2.4.4.7: How could the unfailing semen of you, my lord, O Maheśvara, have become futile? Or what has happened? Has a child been born somewhere?
m.2.4.4.8: Brahmā said: Having heard Pārvatī's words, the Lord of the world laughed, summoned the gods and the sages too, and spoke, O lord of sages.
m.2.4.4.9: Maheśvara said: O gods, hear my words; Pārvatī's words have been heard. Where has my unfailing semen gone, and by whom was it concealed?
m.2.4.4.10: If the one who hid it, out of fear, does not quickly produce it, does he not deserve punishment? A king who, though able, is not a punisher of wrongdoers is a devourer of his people and deserves to be harassed by his subjects.
