m.2.4.4.11: Brahmā said: Having heard those words of Śambhu and conferred among themselves, all of them, frightened, spoke one after another in the presence of the Lord.
m.2.4.4.12: Viṣṇu said: May those by whom your semen was concealed become, in Bhārata, liars, violators of the teacher's wife, ever devoted to reviling the teacher.
m.2.4.4.13: Brahmā said: He by whom your semen was concealed—may he never be blessed, there in the holy land of Bhārata, with your service and worship.
m.2.4.4.14: The guardians of the worlds said: The sinner who, under the delusion that it had merely fallen, concealed your semen—may he be utterly the recipient of that sin, its torment and its karma, perpetually.
m.2.4.4.15: The gods said: The fool who makes a vow and does not bring it to completion—may he by whom your semen was concealed be a vessel of that sin.
m.2.4.4.16: The wives of the gods said: May she by whom your semen was concealed be like the woman who reviles her own husband, goes to another man, and is bereft of mother and kin.
m.2.4.4.17: Brahmā said: Having heard the words of the gods, Hara, lord of the gods of gods, spoke awe-inspiring words to Dharma and the others, the witnesses of all deeds.
m.2.4.4.18: Śrī Śiva said: It was not concealed by the gods; then by whom was that semen surely concealed—that unfailing semen of me, the blessed Maheśa, the Lord?
m.2.4.4.19: You are all constantly the witnesses of all deeds. What is hidden from you? Or rather, what you know, you ought to tell.
m.2.4.4.20: Brahmā said: Having heard the Lord's words, they trembled in the assembly; looking at one another, they spoke in turn before the Lord.
m.2.4.4.21: Brahmā said: When you rose from love-play, the semen fell onto the surface of the earth. I knew it to be unfailing, having fallen because of Śaṅkara's agitation.
m.2.4.4.22: The Earth said: Unable to bear the semen, I formerly cast it into Fire. Hence, O Brahman, since it was hard to bear here, you should forgive me, a weak woman.
m.2.4.4.23: Agni said: Unable to bear your semen, O Śaṅkara, I, in the form of a dove, at once cast that most unbearable semen on Mount Kailāsa.
m.2.4.4.24: The mountain said: Unable to bear your semen, O Śaṅkara, protector of the worlds, I at once cast that unbearable semen into the Gaṅgā, O supreme Lord.
m.2.4.4.25: Gaṅgā said: Unable to bear your semen, O Śaṅkara, protector of the worlds, greatly distressed, O Lord, O master, I cast it into the forest of reeds.
m.2.4.4.26: Vāyu said: The semen that fell among the reeds at once became a child, exceedingly beautiful, O Śambhu, on the holy bank of the heavenly river.
m.2.4.4.27: Sūrya said: Having seen the crying child, O Lord, I went to the western mountain of setting, impelled by the wheel of time, unable to remain at night.
m.2.4.4.28: Candra said: The band of Kṛttikās, going to Badarikāśrama, came upon the crying child, took him, and went to their own abode, O Śambhu.
m.2.4.4.29: The water said: Having brought him, crying, they nourished with their breast-milk your son, O Lord, son of the Īśa, radiant as the sun.
m.2.4.4.30: Sandhyā said: Now, having fostered that little son in the forest, the Kṛttikās lovingly, out of delight, gave him the name Kārttika.
m.2.4.4.31: The night said: They never let the boy out of their sight. To whoever nourishes him, a little son is an object of love dearer even than life.
m.2.4.4.32: The day said: Whatever garments and excellent ornaments there were, they gave him, and they fed him with praiseworthy, tasty foods.
m.2.4.4.33: Brahmā said: Hearing those words of theirs, the destroyer of the cities (Śiva) was satisfied; filled with joy, he lovingly gave abundant gifts to the brāhmaṇas.
m.2.4.4.34: Receiving news of her son, Pārvatī, delighted at heart, gave to the brāhmaṇas millions of jewels and much wealth.
m.2.4.4.35: Lakṣmī, Sarasvatī, Menā, Sāvitrī, all the women, Viṣṇu, and all the gods gave wealth to the brāhmaṇas.
m.2.4.4.36: Then that Lord, urged by the gods, sages and mountains, sent messengers—those gaṇas—to where his son was.
m.2.4.4.37: Vīrabhadra, Viśālākṣa, Śaṅkukarṇa, Karākrama, Nandīśvara, Mahākāla, Vajradaṃṣṭra, Mahonmada,
m.2.4.4.38: Gokarṇāsya, Dadhimukha, who was like a blazing flame of fire, and a hundred thousand Kṣetrapālas and three hundred thousand bhūtas,
m.2.4.4.39: and Rudras and Bhairavas, equal to Śiva in prowess, and others of deformed shape, countless, O Nārada.
m.2.4.4.40: All those messengers of Śiva, bearing various weapons and missiles in their hands, fiercely surrounded the dwelling of the Kṛttikās.
m.2.4.4.41: Seeing them, all the Kṛttikās, their minds overwhelmed with fear, spoke to Kārttika, who was blazing with brahmic splendour.
m.2.4.4.42: The Kṛttikās said: Child, countless armies have surrounded our dwelling. What should be done? Where should we go? A great danger has arisen.
m.2.4.4.43: Kārttikeya said: Give up fear, O auspicious ladies. What fear can there be while I am here? Though a child, I am hard to withstand, O mothers; by whom can I be held back?
m.2.4.4.44: Brahmā said: Meanwhile, Nandikeśvara, the commander of the army, seated himself there in front of Kārtikeya and spoke.
m.2.4.4.45: Nandīśvara said: Brother, and you mothers, hear my auspicious news. I have been sent by Maheśa, by Śaṅkara the destroyer.
m.2.4.4.46: On Kailāsa all the gods, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva and the rest, were assembled in the hall, dear one, at a great festive celebration.
m.2.4.4.47: Then in the assembly Śivā addressed Śaṅkara, the benefactor of all, and spoke about the matter of searching for you.
m.2.4.4.48: Śiva questioned those gods one by one about finding you, and they each gave a fitting reply.
m.2.4.4.49: All of them—Dharma and the others, witnesses of righteous and unrighteous deeds—declared that you, the lord, were here in the abode of the Kṛttikās.
m.2.4.4.50: Formerly there was secret love-play between Pārvatī and Śiva; and when Śambhu was seen by the gods, his seed fell upon the ground.
m.2.4.4.51: The Earth cast it into Fire, Fire onto the mountain; that mountain cast it into the Gaṅgā, and by the force of her waves it reached the reed-forest.
m.2.4.4.52: There you became a child, the lord who accomplishes the gods' task. There you were found by the Kṛttikās. Now go forth to your rightful place.
m.2.4.4.53: Śambhu together with the gods will perform your consecration. You will obtain all weapons and you will slay the one called Tāraka.
m.2.4.4.54: You are the son of the destroyer of the universe, and these women are unable to keep you, just as a dry tree cannot hide fire within its own hollow.
m.2.4.4.55: You are radiant throughout the worlds; you do not shine fittingly in their houses, just as the moon, the king of the twice-born, fallen into a deep well, does not shine.
m.2.4.4.56: Since you give forth light, you are not hidden from us, because of your brilliance—just as the sun cannot be covered by a man's contrivance.
m.2.4.4.57: You are Viṣṇu, the pervader of the worlds; you are not born as anything other, O son of Śambhu—just as the all-pervading sky is pervaded by none.
m.2.4.4.58: You are the lord of yogins, untainted even if you partake in being nourished by them, just as the Self is never tainted by the activities of living beings.
m.2.4.4.59: You are the origin of the universe and its lord; your dwelling among these women is not fitting. You are a mass of virtues and radiance, as yogins know the Self to be.
m.2.4.4.60: Brother, men who do not know you are of ruined understanding, just as frogs, though living in the same place, do not value the lotuses.
m.2.4.4.61: Kārttikeya said: Brother, you know everything, including the knowledge of the three times. You are wise—what praise is enough for you, since you have taken refuge in Mṛtyuñjaya?
m.2.4.4.62: Whatever wombs beings are born in through their karmas, in those very ones, brother, they find contentment here and now.
m.2.4.4.63: The Kṛttikās are wise yoginīs, portions of Prakṛti. I have been nourished continually by their milk and kindness.
m.2.4.4.64: I am their foster-son, and these women are portions of me; they are portions of that Prakṛti, and so I am born of the seed of her lord.
m.2.4.4.65: My birth was not from the daughter of the lord of mountains, O Nandikeśvara; yet she is my mother by dharma, just as these are—as all agree.
m.2.4.4.66: You have been sent by Śambhu, and you are great, equal to a son of Śambhu. I shall come with you and see the assembly of gods.
m.2.4.4.67: Having spoken thus to him, Kārttikeya quickly took leave of the band of Kṛttikās and set out together with Śaṅkara's attendants.
m.2.4.4.iti: Thus ends the fourth adhyāya, named The search for Kārttikeya and the dialogue with Nandin, in the fourth khaṇḍa, the Kumāra-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.4.5.1: Brahmā said: Meanwhile, there he saw a superb chariot, wondrous and ever resplendent, built by Viśvakarman.
m.2.4.5.2: It had a hundred wheels, was very spacious, moved at the speed of thought and was charming; it had been sent by Pārvatī and was surrounded by excellent attendants.
m.2.4.5.3: Then the infinite Kārttika, supremely wise, born of the seed of the Supreme Lord, mounted it with a grieving heart.
m.2.4.5.4: At that very moment the Kṛttikās arrived, their hair loosened, stricken with grief, and there, as if maddened, they began to speak these words.
m.2.4.5.5: The Kṛttikās said: O ocean of compassion, you are going away, abandoning us — you are truly heartless. It is not right that a son who has been reared should forsake his mothers.
m.2.4.5.6: You were raised by us with love and are rightfully our son. What shall we do? Where shall we go? What indeed are we to do?
m.2.4.5.7: Having said this, all the Kṛttikās clasped Kārttika to their breasts and quickly fell into a swoon because of separation from their son.
m.2.4.5.8: Kumāra consoled them with words of spiritual wisdom, and then, O sage, he mounted the chariot together with them and the attendants.
m.2.4.5.9: Seeing and hearing many auspicious, delightful omens, Kumāra went with the attendants to his father's abode.
m.2.4.5.10: Accompanied by Nandin, in the swift chariot that moved like the mind, Kumāra reached Kailāsa, at the foot of the imperishable banyan tree.
m.2.4.5.11: There Kumāra, son of Śaṅkara, skilled in many kinds of play, stayed contentedly with the Kṛttikās and the chief attendants.
m.2.4.5.12: Then all the hosts of gods, the sages, the Siddhas and Cāraṇas, together with Viṣṇu and Brahmā, announced his arrival.
m.2.4.5.13: Then, to see Gāṅgeya, Śiva set out joyfully, accompanied by others, by Hari, by Brahmā and by the divine sages.
m.2.4.5.14: Many conches sounded, kettledrums and trumpets in great numbers; there was a very great festival for the gods, whose hearts were glad.
m.2.4.5.15: At that very moment all the gaṇas, Vīrabhadra and the rest, followed him closely, making merry, with voices keeping many rhythms.
m.2.4.5.16: The panegyrists, and those being praised as well, recited his virtues; with joyful minds they shouted victory and salutation.
m.2.4.5.17: They went to see that unsurpassed son of Śiva, born in the reeds.
m.2.4.5.18: Pārvatī made auspicious preparations: the charming royal road, adorned with rubies and other gems all around the city.
m.2.4.5.19: Placing in front the thirty goddesses beginning with Lakṣmī, accompanied by chaste women blessed with husbands and sons, she came forth.
m.2.4.5.20: At Śiva's command the divine Apsarases, Rambhā and others, smiling and finely attired, devoted themselves to song and dance.
m.2.4.5.21: Those who beheld Gāṅgeya, the equal of Śaṅkara, saw a great radiance that pervaded the three worlds.
m.2.4.5.22: All quickly bowed to the boy Kumāra, enveloped in that radiance, gleaming like molten gold, brilliant as the sun.
m.2.4.5.23: Then they rejoiced, shoulders bent, intent on uttering salutations; coming from left and right, they surrounded him and stood in attendance.
m.2.4.5.24: I, Viṣṇu, Śakra and likewise all the gods and others fell prostrate on the ground like sticks, surrounding the young Kumāra.
m.2.4.5.25: Meanwhile Śambhu and the joyful Girijā arrived at the great festival and beheld their son with delight.
m.2.4.5.26: Then, gazing at his son, the sole friend of the world — the Lord of all, the Supreme Lord himself, adorned with serpent coils and surrounded by the Pramathas — together with the supreme Bhavānī, was filled with the highest joy and affection.
m.2.4.5.27: Then Skanda, bearer of the spear, seeing Pārvatī and Śiva, swiftly got down from the chariot and bowed with his head.
m.2.4.5.28: Śiva Śaṅkara, the Supreme Lord, embracing Kumāra with love, gracious and full of affection, lovingly smelled kissed his head.
m.2.4.5.29: There Pārvatī, overcome with emotion and steeped in affection, embraced Guha and suckled him at her breast, which flowed with milk.
m.2.4.5.30: Then the joyful gods with their wives performed the āratī-waving for him; the vault of the sky was filled with a great cry of victory.
m.2.4.5.31: The sages with Vedic chanting, the singers with song, and many others with instruments waited upon young Kumāra there.
m.2.4.5.32: Then Maheśa, lord of Bhavānī, placing on his lap that young Kumāra blazing with radiance, shone in person, endowed with splendour, the foremost of those blessed with sons.
m.2.4.5.33: At Śiva's command Kumāra, overjoyed, came to Śiva's abode together with his gaṇas and the greatly enthusiastic gods.
m.2.4.5.34: Then the divine couple shone there side by side, being worshipped by the sages and surrounded by the best of gods.
m.2.4.5.35: Kumāra played joyfully on Śiva's lap and squeezed with both hands Vāsuki, who lay on Śiva's neck.
m.2.4.5.36: Laughing, the compassionate Lord Śambhu, looking with a gracious glance at the child's playful form, then pointed it out to Girijā.
m.2.4.5.37: Then the blessed Maheśa, together with Girijā, smiling with delight, attained supreme joy; his voice choked with love, the all-pervading sole friend of the world, sole sustainer of the worlds, said nothing at all.
m.2.4.5.38: Then Śambhu, lord of the world, delighted and following worldly custom, seated Kārttika on a lovely jewelled throne.
m.2.4.5.39: With joy he bathed him from hundreds of fine jewelled pitchers filled with the waters of all holy places and sanctified by Vedic mantras.
m.2.4.5.40: Hari gave him a diadem, crown and armlets made of the finest jewels, his own Vaijayantī garland, and a discus.
m.2.4.5.41: Śiva gave him the trident, the Pināka bow, the battle-axe, the spear, the Pāśupata arrow, the weapon of destruction, and the supreme knowledge.
m.2.4.5.42: I Brahmā gave the sacred thread, the Vedas and the Mother of the Vedas Gāyatrī, a water-pot, the Brahmā weapon, and the knowledge that crushes enemies.
m.2.4.5.43: The lord of the gods Indra gave him a lordly elephant and the thunderbolt; the lord of the waters Varuṇa gave a white parasol, a garland of jewels, and the noose.
m.2.4.5.44: The Sun gave a chariot moving at the speed of mind and armour of great solidity; Yama gave the staff of Yama, and the Moon, store of nectar, a pot of nectar.
m.2.4.5.45: Fire lovingly gave a great spear to his own son; Nirṛti gave his own weapon, and the Wind the Vāyavya weapon.
m.2.4.5.46: Kubera gave a mace, Īśa joyfully gave a trident, and all the gods joyfully gave various weapons and devices.
m.2.4.5.47: Then Kāmadeva, full of joy, gave him the weapon of love; and with supreme joy he gave him a mace and his own lore.
m.2.4.5.48: The Ocean of Milk gave priceless jewels and a special jewelled anklet; Himālaya gave divine ornaments and garments.
m.2.4.5.49: Garuḍa gave his own son named Citrabarhaṇa the peacock; Aruṇa gave the strong cock called Tāmracūḍa.
m.2.4.5.50: Pārvatī, smiling and delighted, with great love gave him supreme, excellent sovereignty and also long life.
m.2.4.5.51: Lakṣmī joyfully gave divine wealth and a great, charming necklace; Sāvitrī gave the entire knowledge of perfection.
m.2.4.5.52: And the other goddesses too, O sage, whoever had assembled there, gave gifts to him as to one of their own; so too did the nurses of the child.
m.2.4.5.53: O best of sages, a very great festival took place there; all attained joy, and especially Śiva and Śivā.
m.2.4.5.54: At that moment, O sage, the mighty Rudra Bharga, laughing joyfully, spoke to Brahmā and the other gods.
m.2.4.5.55: Śiva said: O Hari, O Vidhi Brahmā, O gods, all of you listen to my words: I am pleased in every way; choose the boons you desire.
m.2.4.5.56: Brahmā said: Hearing that speech of Śambhu, O sage, all the gods headed by Viṣṇu, with cheerful faces, spoke to the god Paśupati, the Lord.
m.2.4.5.57: O Lord, this Tāraka will indeed be slain by Kumāra; it is for that very purpose that this excellent deed has come about.
m.2.4.5.58: Therefore we shall go this very day, ready to kill Tāraka. Give the command to Kumāra, so that he may kill him for our happiness.
m.2.4.5.59: Thinking, so be it, the all-pervading Lord, moved by compassion, then gave his son to the gods to kill Tāraka.
m.2.4.5.60: Then, at Śiva's command, all the gods headed by Brahmā and Viṣṇu, placing Guha in front, together at once went out from the mountain.
m.2.4.5.61: Having come out from Kailāsa, Tvaṣṭṛ, at Hari's order, built a lovely, wondrous city near the mountain.
m.2.4.5.62: There Tvaṣṭṛ built for Guha a lovely, divine, wondrous, supremely radiant house, and in it an excellent throne.
m.2.4.5.63: Then wise Hari, with devotion, had the auspicious consecration of Kārttika performed by the gods with the waters of all sacred places.
m.2.4.5.64: Having adorned him fully, he installed him there with all his retinue, and lovingly had the rite and festival of Kārttika celebrated.
m.2.4.5.65: Hari joyfully gave him lordship over the cosmic egg; he marked his forehead with the tilaka and worshipped him together with the gods.
m.2.4.5.66: Bowing lovingly to Kārttika together with all the gods and sages, he praised with various hymns the eternal one who is the form of Śiva.
m.2.4.5.67: Seated on the excellent throne, Kārttika shone exceedingly, having attained the state of lordship, protector even of the cosmic egg.
m.2.4.5.iti: Thus ends the fifth adhyāya, named The consecration of Kumāra, in the fourth khaṇḍa, the Kumāra-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.4.6.1: Brahmā said: Then and there that son of Gaṅgā (Kārttikeya) displayed a marvel. Listen to it with great delight, O Nārada, for it grants devotion to him.
m.2.4.6.2: Just then a certain brahmin named Nārada, a glorious performer of sacrifices, came there to seek refuge with Guha.
m.2.4.6.3: That brahmin, with a gladdened mind, approached Kārttika, bowed deeply, and with auspicious hymns made known his purpose.
m.2.4.6.4: The brahmin said: Hear my words today, O lord, and ward off my trouble. You are the lord of all the universes; therefore I have come to you for refuge.
m.2.4.6.5: I had begun to perform a goat-sacrifice (ajamedha). That goat has left my house, having broken its tether.
m.2.4.6.6: I do not know where it has gone; much searching has been done for it. That strong goat has not been found; hence my sacrifice is being ruined.
m.2.4.6.7: While you are the protector, O mighty one, how can a sacrifice be ruined? Considering this, O lord of all, fulfil my wish completely.
m.2.4.6.8: Leaving you, to what refuge should I go, O son of Śiva, O lord — you who are the lord of all universes, well served by all the immortals?
m.2.4.6.9: You are the friend of the distressed, an ocean of compassion, easy to serve, affectionate to devotees, well praised by Hari, Brahmā and the other gods, the supreme lord;
m.2.4.6.10: Son of Pārvatī, Skanda, the one supreme, scorcher of foes, the supreme Self, giver of the Self, the lord of the good and of those seeking refuge.
m.2.4.6.11: O lord of the lowly, great lord, son of Śaṅkara, lord of the three worlds, master, O ruler of māyā, I have come for refuge; protect me, O lover of brahmins. You are lord of all, praised by Brahmā and the other all-knowing gods who bow to you; your form is made of māyā, you give happiness to your devotees, you are intent on protection, the wielder of māyā.
m.2.4.6.12: You are the life of devotees and a mine of virtues, distinct from the three guṇas, dear to Śambhu; you are Śambhu, Śambhu's son, giving joy when pleased, of the nature of being and consciousness, great; all-knowing, son of Śaṅkara the slayer of Tripura, ever won over by true love; six-faced, fond of the good, fond of those who bow, lord of all, bringer of welfare. O slayer of those who harm the good, O teacher of Śaṅkara, lord of the universe, master, whose feet are served by the immortals and all others — protect me, O you who love service.
m.2.4.6.13: O terror of enemies, O bringer of welfare, I salute your lotus feet — you who are the refuge of people and the cause of happiness. O Skanda, place my petition in your ear; ever establish devotion to yourself in people's hearts.
m.2.4.6.14: What can a mighty adversary do to him — even a skilful one guarded on both flanks by his allies? What can even Takṣaka or a flesh-eater do to one whose protector is you, with your able, watchful mind?
m.2.4.6.15: Even the preceptor of the gods would not be able to praise you; tell me, O most worshipful one, how could I, dull-witted, be able? Pure or impure, ignoble, whatever I may be, O Skanda, I pray for the pollen of your lotus feet.
m.2.4.6.16: O lord of all, affectionate to devotees, ocean of compassion, I am yours, your own servant; O good master, O lord of the gaṇas, do not count the hundred offences of your servant. O mighty one, remover of your servants' afflictions, you know devotion done anywhere, however little. There is no protector other than you, O Lord, and no man more wretched than I.
m.2.4.6.17: Maker of welfare, destroyer of the stains of the Kali age, friend of Kubera, with heart moist with compassion, eighteen-eyed, resplendent with six faces — O Guha, make my sacrifice complete.
m.2.4.6.18: You are the protector of the three worlds, affectionate to those who come for refuge, the performer and the sustainer of sacrifice; you destroy those who create obstacles.
m.2.4.6.19: O remover of the obstacles of the good, O cause of creation in every way, O lord, O son of Śiva, O embodiment of sacrifice, make my rite complete; salutation to you.
m.2.4.6.20: You, Skanda, are indeed the protector of all; you alone are the knower of all; you are the lord of all, the ruler, the guardian of every abode.
m.2.4.6.21: You alone are the knower of music, the knower of the Vedas, the supreme lord; you abide in all, you are the ordainer, the god of gods, the goal of the good.
m.2.4.6.22: You are the son of Bhavānī, the son of Śambhu, knowledge itself, self-ruling; the meditator and the object of meditation, the father even of the Pitṛs, the source of good souls.
m.2.4.6.23: Brahmā said: Having heard his words thus, Śiva's son, the sovereign of the gods, sent his attendant (gaṇa) named Vīrabāhu for that purpose.
m.2.4.6.24: At his command the great hero Vīrabāhu, having bowed to the lord with devotion, went swiftly to search for it.
m.2.4.6.25: He searched throughout the whole sphere of the universe. He did not find the goat anywhere, but heard of the havoc it was causing.
m.2.4.6.26: Then he went to Vaikuṇṭha and there saw that goat, very mighty, with the sacrificial post on its neck, causing havoc.
m.2.4.6.27: The hero seized it by the horns, overpowered it with great force, and brought it before the lord, while it bleated loudly.
m.2.4.6.28: Seeing it, Lord Kārttika, Guha, who bears the weight of the universe and works great wonders, quickly mounted it.
m.2.4.6.29: Within a mere muhūrta, O sage, that goat roamed the entire universe, and, merely wearied, quickly came back to that place.
m.2.4.6.30: Then the lord dismounted and sat on his seat. The goat stood right there, and Nārada spoke to him.
m.2.4.6.31: Nārada said: Salutation to you, O god, lord of gods; give me the goat, O treasury of compassion. Let me perform the sacrifice joyfully; ah, make me your friend!
m.2.4.6.32: Kārttikeya said: The goat is not fit to be slain, O brahmin; go to your home, Nārada. Let your entire sacrifice be complete, accomplished by my grace alone.
m.2.4.6.33: Brahmā said: Having heard thus the lord's words, the brahmin, pleased at heart, gave him an excellent blessing and went to his own home.
m.2.4.6.iti: Thus ends the sixth adhyāya, named The wonderful deeds of Kumāra, in the fourth khaṇḍa, the Kumāra-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.4.7.1: Brahmā said: And those gods, Hari and the others, having seen that deed of the Lord, became greatly pleased indeed, their minds settled in faith.
m.2.4.7.2: Leaping about and roaring, inspired by Śiva's splendour, they placed Kumāra at their head and came to kill Tāraka.
m.2.4.7.3: Hearing of the gods' preparation, the mighty Tāraka too at once went with a great army to fight against the gods.
m.2.4.7.4: The gods, seeing Tāraka's great army approaching, though roaring loud lion-roars with all their might, were astonished.
m.2.4.7.5: Then the celestial voice, the lady of the sky, urged by Śaṅkara, swiftly spoke from above at once to all the gods, Hari and the rest.
m.2.4.7.6: The heavenly voice said: O gods, you who stand ready with Kumāra placed at your head, having conquered the Daityas in battle, will then be victorious.
m.2.4.7.7: Brahmā said: Hearing that voice from the sky, all the gods, full of eagerness and shouting heroic cries, then became fearless.
m.2.4.7.8: With Kumāra at their head, all those gods, their fear gone and eager to fight, went to the place where the land meets the ocean.
m.2.4.7.9: That Tāraka quickly came to the place where the gods were, together with a great army, surrounded by many Asuras.
m.2.4.7.10: At his arrival the war-drums sounded, with a din like the clouds of the cosmic dissolution, and other harsh instruments too.
m.2.4.7.11: Then the Daityas, together with the Asura Tāraka, roared, making the earth tremble with their strides as they leapt about.
m.2.4.7.12: Hearing that most fierce uproar, all the gods, wholly fearless, rose up as one, eager to fight Tāraka.
m.2.4.7.13: The lord of the gods, having seated Kumāra on an elephant, went in front, surrounded by a great army of gods and by the guardians of the worlds.
m.2.4.7.14: Then drums sounded, kettledrums and trumpets in great number, lutes, flutes and mṛdaṅgas, as well as the singing of the Gandharvas.
m.2.4.7.15: Giving the elephant to great Indra, Kumāra mounted a vehicle made of many marvels and set with various jewels.
m.2.4.7.16: Having then mounted the aerial car, that greatly renowned son of Śaṅkara, endowed with all virtues and attended by supreme splendour, shone forth magnificently, being fanned with brilliantly gleaming chowries.
m.2.4.7.17: Then Varuṇa's umbrella, exceedingly radiant, adorned with jewels and resplendent with various gems, was held over Kumāra's head, gleaming with countless moon-like rays of great brilliance.
m.2.4.7.18: Then all those gods, led by Śakra, assembled, each surrounded by his own forces, mighty and eager for battle.
m.2.4.7.19: Thus the gods and the Daityas, eager to fight, stood on the earth, each side having arrayed its great army in a separate battle formation.
m.2.4.7.20: Those two armies of the gods and the Daityas shone facing each other, each eager to slay the other, and being praised by bards.
m.2.4.7.21: Then both their armies, like forests, roared, terrifying to the utterly unheroic, delightful to the others.
m.2.4.7.22: Meanwhile there the Daityas and gods, great heroes intoxicated with their strength and overwhelmed with rage, fought one another.
m.2.4.7.23: There was a most tumultuous battle crowded with gods and Daityas; in a moment everything became strewn with headless trunks and severed heads.
m.2.4.7.24: There, by hundreds and thousands, warriors esteemed as heroes fell on the ground, slain, their limbs cut off by mighty weapons.
m.2.4.7.25: In the battle, the arms of some proud heroes were cut off by terrible sword-strokes; the thighs of others were severed.
m.2.4.7.26: Some had all their limbs crushed by maces and hammers; some, their hearts pierced, were struck down by nooses and javelins.
m.2.4.7.27: Some were torn open in the back by lances, spears and goads; and severed heads too fell upon the ground.
m.2.4.7.28: And there many headless trunks were dancing, leaping by hundreds, with weapons raised in their hands.
m.2.4.7.29: Then hundreds of rivers flowing with blood were set in motion there, and bhūtas, pretas and the like gathered there in hundreds.
m.2.4.7.30: Jackals and she-jackals were there, devouring much flesh, and likewise vultures, vaṭa-birds, hawks and crows, eaters of flesh, feasted indeed on the abundant flesh of the fallen.
m.2.4.7.31: Meanwhile there the mighty one named Tāraka at once went with a great army to fight against the gods.
m.2.4.7.32: Seeing Tāraka, frenzied in battle, approaching eager to fight, the gods, Śakra and the others, then at once advanced; and a great roar arose from both armies.
m.2.4.7.33: Then indeed began a series of single combats, crushing gods and Asuras, at the sight of which heroes rejoiced and cowards were seized with fear.
m.2.4.7.34: The mighty son of Diti, Tāraka, fought in battle with Śakra; Saṃhrāda with Agni; and Yama himself with Jambha.
m.2.4.7.35: Mahāprabhu fought with Nairṛta; the noose-bearer Varuṇa with Bala; Suvīra with Vāyu; and the king of the Guhyakas Kubera with Pavamāna.
m.2.4.7.36: Śambhu, most skilled in battle, fought with Īśāna; Śumbha fought with Śeṣa, and the Dānava Kumbha with Candra.
m.2.4.7.37: Kuñjara, of great strength and valour and expert in many kinds of warfare, fought in battle with Mihira using supreme weapons.
m.2.4.7.38: Thus all the gods and Asuras fought in the conflict in great single combats, resolved on victory through their strength.
m.2.4.7.39: Vying with one another, those mighty immortals and Daityas proved invincible in that battle of gods and Asuras, O sage.
m.2.4.7.40: Then there arose a tumultuous battle between those gods and demons, all eager for victory — bringing delight to the heroic and high-spirited, but bringing terror to the others.
m.2.4.7.41: In that battle the earth then became exceedingly dreadful, impassable and most terrifying, with gods and demons fallen and destroyed in great numbers — yet it brought great joy to the high-spirited.
m.2.4.7.iti: Thus ends the seventh adhyāya, named The beginning of the battle, in the fourth khaṇḍa, the Kumāra-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.4.8.1: Brahmā said: Thus, dear son, the extremely tumultuous battle between the armies of the gods and the Dānavas has been described to you. Now hear, O Nārada, the fight of their two lords.
m.2.4.8.2: Thus, in that extremely tumultuous battle, destructive to gods and Dānavas, the lord of the gods was struck by Tāraka himself with a supreme spear (śakti).
m.2.4.8.3: At once he fell from his elephant to the ground and became unconscious; the wielder of the thunderbolt, lord of the gods, fell into deep stupor.
m.2.4.8.4: In the same way, dear son, all the guardians of the worlds were defeated in battle by the far stronger Asuras, skilled in great warfare.
m.2.4.8.5: Other gods too, fighting with the Daityas, were defeated; unable to bear their might, they were intent only on flight.
m.2.4.8.6: There the victorious Asuras, their efforts successful, roared, making lion-roars and given to uproar.
m.2.4.8.7: Meanwhile Vīrabhadra, filled with fury, came there with his heroic Gaṇas and confronted Tāraka, who prided himself on his valour.
m.2.4.8.8: Putting the gods behind him, the mighty one born of Śiva's wrath, foremost of the Gaṇas, then stood facing him, eager to fight.
m.2.4.8.9: Then all those Pramathas and the Daityas, in great elation, fought one another in the combat, locked together in the great battle.
m.2.4.8.10: With tridents, double-edged swords, nooses, swords, axes and spears, those skilled in war struck one another in the fight.
m.2.4.8.11: Tāraka, struck hard by Vīrabhadra with the trident, suddenly fell to the ground, overwhelmed by a swoon for a moment.
m.2.4.8.12: Rising quickly, the hero Tāraka, best of the Daityas, regaining consciousness, forcefully struck Vīrabhadra with his spear.
m.2.4.8.13: Likewise the hero Vīrabhadra, of great splendour, swiftly struck Tāraka with his terrible, sharp trident.
m.2.4.8.14: Then Tāraka too, lord of the sons of Diti, very powerful and esteemed by heroes, struck Vīrabhadra in the fight with his spear.
m.2.4.8.15: Thus fighting, the two, skilled in the science of war, struck each other in the combat with many kinds of missiles and weapons.
m.2.4.8.16: Then a single combat took place there between those two great beings, tumultuous and hair-raising, while all looked on.
m.2.4.8.17: Then kettledrums, mṛdaṅgas, paṭahas, ānakas and gomukhas, beaten by the warriors, resounded, most terrifying to those who heard.
m.2.4.8.18: Fully armoured, battered by blows, the two fought each other in great fury, like Budha and Aṅgāraka (Mercury and Mars).
m.2.4.8.19: Seeing then such a fight of Vīrabhadra with him, you, dear to Śiva, went there and spoke to Vīrabhadra.
m.2.4.8.20: Nārada said: O Vīrabhadra, great hero, you are the leader of the Gaṇas. Turn back from this battle; his slaying by you is not desired.
m.2.4.8.21: Hearing these words of yours, Vīrabhadra, leader of the Gaṇas, though filled with anger, then spoke to you with joined palms.
m.2.4.8.22: Vīrabhadra said: O best of sages, most wise one, hear my supreme words: I will slay Tāraka. Behold my valour today.
m.2.4.8.23: Those warriors who bring their master into the arena of battle are sinners and great cowards; having gone to battle, they perish.
m.2.4.8.24: They attain an evil destiny, and hell is certain for them. Know me to be Vīrabhadra; I should never be addressed thus by you.
m.2.4.8.25: Those who fight fearlessly, their limbs pierced by weapons and missiles, are praiseworthy here and hereafter and obtain wondrous happiness.
m.2.4.8.26: Let the gods headed by Hari hear my words: today, without the help of my master, I will make the earth free of Tāraka.
m.2.4.8.27: Having said this, Vīrabhadra, bearing the trident, together with the Pramathas, meditated on Śambhu in his mind and fought with Tāraka.
m.2.4.8.28: Joined in battle with many great heroes mounted on bulls, three-eyed and bearing excellent tridents, he shone forth.
m.2.4.8.29: Raising an uproar, the fearless Gaṇas in hundreds, placing Vīrabhadra at their head, fought with the Dānavas.
m.2.4.8.30: Those Asuras too, who lived by Tāraka, fierce in strength and great heroes, fought, crushing the Gaṇas in fury.
m.2.4.8.31: Again and again there was a fierce clash of the Gaṇas with the foremost Daityas. Then those Gaṇas, rejoicing and expert in supreme weapons, became victorious.
m.2.4.8.32: Defeated by the mighty Gaṇas, those Asuras turned away from battle and took to flight, distressed and agitated in mind.
m.2.4.8.33: Seeing his army thus routed, its protector, the Asura Tāraka, filled with rage, went forth to slay the hosts of the gods.
m.2.4.8.34: Assuming ten thousand arms and mounting a lion swiftly, he felled those gods and Gaṇas at the forefront of battle.
m.2.4.8.35: Seeing that deed of his, Vīrabhadra, the very mighty leader of the Gaṇas, became greatly enraged, resolved on his slaying.
m.2.4.8.36: Remembering the lotus feet of Śiva, he seized his supreme trident; by its splendour all the quarters and the sky blazed.
m.2.4.8.37: Meanwhile the Lord (Kumāra), a witness of great wonders, at once restrained him and those headed by Vīrabāhu from the battle.
m.2.4.8.38: By his command Vīrabhadra then withdrew from the battle. Thereupon the great hero Tāraka, leader of the Asuras, became enraged.
m.2.4.8.39: Then the Asura released a shower of arrows upon the gods; inflamed with wrath, skilled in battle with many weapons, he at once challenged the gods.
m.2.4.8.40: Having thus done a mighty deed, Tāraka, protector of the Asuras, best of the strong, was invincible to all the gods.
m.2.4.8.41: Seeing those gods, overwhelmed with fear, being struck down in this way, Acyuta grew angry and quickly made himself ready for battle.
m.2.4.8.42: Taking up the discus Sudarśana and the bow Śārṅga, the armed Lord Hari advanced against the great demon for battle.
m.2.4.8.43: Then there arose a great battle between Hari and Tāraka, hair-raising and exceedingly fierce, while all looked on, O sage.
m.2.4.8.44: Raising his mace, Hari struck the demon with force; the mighty demon split it in two with his trident.
m.2.4.8.45: Then the Lord, who grants fearlessness to the gods, enraged, struck the leader of the demons with volleys of arrows released from Śārṅga.
m.2.4.8.46: That demon Tāraka too, a great hero and slayer of enemy heroes, swiftly cut down all the arrows with his own sharp shafts.
m.2.4.8.47: Then the demon Tāraka quickly struck Murāri with his spear; stunned by that blow, Hari fell to the ground.
m.2.4.8.48: Rising up in a moment, Acyuta in fury seized his discus, ablaze with flaming fire, letting out a great lion's roar.
m.2.4.8.49: With it Hari struck that lord of the demons; pained by that mighty blow, he fell to the ground.
m.2.4.8.50: Rising again, Tāraka, king of the Daityas and leader of the demons, endowed with great strength, swiftly shattered the discus with his spear.
m.2.4.8.51: Again with that great spear he struck the beloved of the immortals; Acyuta too, the great hero, struck him with his sword Nandaka.
m.2.4.8.52: Thus the demon and Viṣṇu, both mighty, fought each other at length there in battle, their strength undiminished, O sage.
m.2.4.8.iti: Thus ends the eighth adhyāya, named The general battle of the gods and the Daityas, in the fourth khaṇḍa, the Kumāra-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.4.9.1: Brahmā said: O God of gods, Guha, lord, son of Śaṅkara, son of Pārvatī, this battle between Viṣṇu and the demon Tāraka is pointless and does not befit them.
m.2.4.9.2: That exceedingly mighty Tāraka cannot be slain by Viṣṇu, for he has received a boon from me. I tell you the truth, the truth.
m.2.4.9.3: O son of Pārvatī, there is no other slayer of this sinner except you. Therefore, O great lord, you must carry out my word.
m.2.4.9.4: O scorcher of foes, quickly make yourself ready to slay the demon. It was for his slaying that you were born from Śaṅkara, O son of Śivā.
m.2.4.9.5: Protect, protect, O great hero, the gods who are distressed in battle. You are not a child, nor even a youth, but the lord, the master of all.
m.2.4.9.6: See Śakra, and Viṣṇu too, in distress, and the gods and the gaṇas. Slay this great demon and make the three worlds happy.
m.2.4.9.7: Formerly Indra, together with the guardians of the worlds, was conquered by him, and even the great hero Viṣṇu was humiliated through the power of his austerity.
m.2.4.9.8: The entire three worlds were conquered by this wicked demon. Now, because of your presence, they the gods have waged battle once again.
m.2.4.9.9: Therefore Tāraka, that sinful being, must be slain by you. By virtue of my boon he cannot be killed by anyone else, O son of Śaṅkara.
m.2.4.9.10: Hearing these words of mine, Kumāra, the son of Śaṅkara, laughed with a pleased heart and said, so be it.
m.2.4.9.11: Having resolved upon slaying the demon, that great lord, the son of Śaṅkara, then descended from his aerial chariot and went on foot.
m.2.4.9.12: Then, running about on foot, that supremely heroic Kumāra, born of Śiva, shone brilliantly, holding in his hand that spear of great radiance, blazing with splendour like a great meteor.
m.2.4.9.13: Seeing him approach—exceedingly fierce, unperturbed, six-faced, immeasurable—the demon said to the foremost of the gods: Is this Kumāra the slayer of his enemies?
m.2.4.9.14: I, the peerless hero, shall fight with him, and I alone shall fight all the heroes. I shall slay all the gaṇas too, together with the world-guardians and those led by Hari.
m.2.4.9.15: Having spoken thus, that mighty one then set out to fight, aiming at Kumāra. Seizing a most wondrous spear, Tāraka addressed the foremost gods.
m.2.4.9.16: Tāraka said: How is it that you have put Kumāra before me today? You gods are shameless—especially Śakra and Keśava.
m.2.4.9.17: Formerly these two did deeds opposed to the path of the Veda. Listen to what I declare; I shall describe it in detail.
m.2.4.9.18: Of these, Viṣṇu is a deceiver, a wrongdoer, and especially lacking in discernment—he by whom Bali was formerly bound, sinfully resorting to trickery.
m.2.4.9.19: It was by him too that long ago the two demons Madhu and Kaiṭabha were deliberately beheaded through cunning, and the Vedic path was abandoned.
m.2.4.9.20: In the form of Mohinī he made a distinction between the rows of diners at the drinking of nectar by gods and demons, and so the Vedic path was violated.
m.2.4.9.21: Becoming Rāma, he killed a woman, and he struck down Vāli. Then he slew Vaiśravaṇa Rāvaṇa, a brāhmaṇa, and the ordinance of scripture was destroyed.
m.2.4.9.22: That his own wife, though sinless, was abandoned by him who delights in sin—there too the Vedic path was destroyed for the sake of his own interest.
m.2.4.9.23: In the incarnation so named (rasākhyaka) as Paraśurāma he cut off his own mother's head, and this wicked one also insulted the son of his preceptor.
m.2.4.9.24: Becoming Kṛṣṇa, he defiled other men's women against the law of family, and likewise contracted his own marriages abandoning the Vedic way.
m.2.4.9.25: And again, in his ninth birth, the Vedic path was reviled, and a heretical doctrine opposed to the Vedic path was established.
m.2.4.9.26: How can he who has committed such sin, forsaking the Vedic path, win in battle or be the foremost of the righteous?
m.2.4.9.27: And Śakra, who is his elder brother, is held to be a great sinner; many sins were committed by him for his own ends.
m.2.4.9.28: Diti's embryo was cut up by him, especially for his own interest; Gautama's wife was violated; and Vṛtra, born of a brāhmaṇa, was slain.
m.2.4.9.29: And the heads of the brāhmaṇa Viśvarūpa, a sister's son and a preceptor, were cut off—thereby the path of the Veda was destroyed.
m.2.4.9.30: Having committed many sins again and again, Hari and Śakra have had their splendour struck down and are especially bereft of valour.
m.2.4.9.31: Through their strength you will not gain victory in battle. Why, having fallen into folly, have you come here to lose your lives?
m.2.4.9.32: These two, their minds greedy for self-interest, do not know dharma. O immortals, without dharma every undertaking becomes fruitless.
m.2.4.9.33: These two most impudent ones have today placed a child in front of me. I shall kill the boy, and that sin too will be theirs.
m.2.4.9.34: But let the boy go far away from here if he wishes to save his life. Having said this, aiming at the two Haris, Viṣṇu and Indra, he spoke to Vīrabhadra.
m.2.4.9.35: Formerly at Dakṣa's sacrifice you killed many brāhmaṇas. Today, O sinless one, I shall show you the fruit of that deed.
m.2.4.9.36: Brahmā said: Having spoken thus, and having shaken off his own merit through that act of reviling them, Tāraka, the foremost of warriors, seized a most wondrous spear.
m.2.4.9.37: As the demon Tāraka came forcefully near the boy, Śakra, with Guha at his front, struck him with the thunderbolt.
m.2.4.9.38: Shattered by that blow of the thunderbolt, Tāraka, his strength sapped by his reviling, suddenly fell to the ground for a moment.
m.2.4.9.39: Though fallen, he rose up and in rage struck him with his spear, and threw Purandara, mounted on his elephant, down to the ground.
m.2.4.9.40: When Purandara fell, a great cry of lament arose, and seeing that, distress entered the army of the gods.
m.2.4.9.41: Hear from me what painful deed Tāraka also did right there, a deed contrary to dharma that became the cause of his own destruction.
m.2.4.9.42: Trampling with his foot on Indra, who had fallen, and seizing the thunderbolt from his hand, he struck Śakra hard again with a blow of the raised thunderbolt.
m.2.4.9.43: Seeing Śakra thus humiliated, the mighty Lord Viṣṇu raised his discus and struck Tāraka.
m.2.4.9.44: Struck by the blow of the discus, he fell to the ground; but rising again, the lord of the Daityas struck that Viṣṇu with his spear.
m.2.4.9.45: By that blow of the spear Acyuta fell to the earth; there was a great cry of alas, and the gods wailed greatly.
m.2.4.9.46: In the twinkling of an eye, even as Viṣṇu was rising again by himself, Vīrabhadra arrived at that very moment and faced the Asura.
m.2.4.9.47: Raising his trident, the mighty and powerful Vīrabhadra violently struck Tāraka, the overlord of the sons of Diti.
m.2.4.9.48: By that blow of the trident he then fell to the ground; yet though fallen, the greatly radiant Tāraka rose again.
m.2.4.9.49: Growing furious, the great hero, leader of all the Asuras, then struck Vīrabhadra on the chest with his supreme spear.
m.2.4.9.50: Vīrabhadra too, struck hard on the chest by that supreme spear hurled in anger, fell to the ground, unconscious for a moment.
m.2.4.9.51: The gods with the Gaṇas, and the Gandharvas, serpents and Rākṣasas, cried out again and again with a great wail of alas.
m.2.4.9.52: Within a mere instant, suddenly, that greatly vigourous Vīrabhadra, slayer of enemies, raising his trident gleaming like lightning, shone forth blazing with radiance.
m.2.4.9.53: That trident illumined the expanse of the directions with its own lustre; its disc was like the orbs of the sun, the moon and fire; it was of great brilliance, terrifying to heroes, supreme, called Kāla, utterly destructive, and intensely blazing.
m.2.4.9.54: Just as the mighty Vīrabhadra was then about to slay the Asura with the trident, he was restrained by Kumāra.
m.2.4.9.iti: Thus ends the ninth adhyāya, named The words of Tāraka and the battle of Śakra, Viṣṇu and Vīrabhadra, in the fourth khaṇḍa, the Kumāra-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.4.10.1: Brahmā said: Having restrained that Vīrabhadra, Kumāra, the slayer of enemy heroes, remembering the lotus feet of Śiva, resolved upon the killing of Tāraka.
m.2.4.10.2: Then the greatly radiant, mighty Kārttikeya roared; armed for battle and enraged, he stood surrounded by a great army.
m.2.4.10.3: Then all the hosts of gods cried victory, victory, and at that very moment he was praised with pleasing words by the divine sages.
m.2.4.10.4: Then arose a battle between Tāraka and Kumāra, exceedingly hard to endure, most dreadful, terrifying to all beings.
m.2.4.10.5: Those two heroes, spears in hand, fought each other there, O sage, while all looked on in great amazement.
m.2.4.10.6: Their bodies pierced by spears, the two, equipped with great means of war, kept deceiving each other like two mighty lions.
m.2.4.10.7: Adopting the Vaitālika mode, likewise the Khecaraka method, and adopting the Prāpata, they struck spear against spear.
m.2.4.10.8: With these techniques the two great heroes, of great strength and valour, each becoming a practitioner against the other, waged a wondrous battle.
m.2.4.10.9: Exerting great force, each seeking the other's death, the two experts in warfare struck in battle with torrents of spear-blows.
m.2.4.10.10: On the head, the neck, the thighs, the knees, the hips, the breast, the chest and the back, they cut into each other.
m.2.4.10.11: Then those two mighty ones, fighting and eager to kill, leaping about with heroic shouts, skilled in many kinds of combat—
m.2.4.10.12: All the gods, Gandharvas and Kinnaras became spectators; they said to one another there: Who will win in this battle?
m.2.4.10.13: Then a voice from the sky spoke, consoling the gods: This Kumāra will kill the demon Tāraka here.
m.2.4.10.14: Let all the gods not grieve; let them remain at ease. For Śaṅkara himself has taken his stand in the form of a son for your sake.
m.2.4.10.15: Hearing then that auspicious voice uttered in the sky, young Kumāra, surrounded by the Pramathas, became gladdened and quickly eager to slay Tāraka, lord of the Daityas.
m.2.4.10.16: Filled with wrath, the mighty-armed Kumāra forcefully struck the demon Tāraka between the breasts with that spear.
m.2.4.10.17: Disregarding that blow, Tāraka, chief of the Daityas, greatly enraged, in turn struck Kumāra with his own spear.
m.2.4.10.18: By that spear-blow Śiva's son fell unconscious; after a moment he regained consciousness, being praised by the great sages.
m.2.4.10.19: Like a lion maddened with rage, eager to kill, so the valiant Kumāra struck the demon Tāraka with his spear.
m.2.4.10.20: Thus the two, Kumāra and Tāraka, both skilled in spear-fighting, fought each other in extreme fury.
m.2.4.10.21: Each wishing to defeat the other, they were wholly intent on their practised skill, fighting on foot, wondrous in appearance and swift.
m.2.4.10.22: With volleys of various blows they struck each other, executing many manoeuvres, roaring, of excellent valour.
m.2.4.10.23: All the gods, Gandharvas and Kinnaras, intent on watching, were struck with supreme amazement; they said nothing there.
m.2.4.10.24: The wind did not blow, the sun became lustreless, and the whole earth with its mountains, woods and forests shook.
m.2.4.10.25: Meanwhile the mountains headed by Himālaya, distressed out of affection, came there, wishing to protect Kumāra.
m.2.4.10.26: Then Śiva's son, the son of Girijā, seeing all those mountains stricken with fear, spoke to them, reassuring them.
m.2.4.10.27: Kumāra said: Do not be troubled, O blessed ones; do not worry, O mountains. Today I shall slay this most wicked one while all of you look on.
m.2.4.10.28: Having thus comforted the mountains and the hosts of immortals, and having bowed to Girijā and Śambhu, he took up his brilliantly shining spear.
m.2.4.10.29: Resolved to kill that Tāraka, spear in hand, the great lord, the mighty hero Kumāra, child of Śambhu, shone forth.
m.2.4.10.30: Then Kumāra, rich with the radiance of Śaṅkara, struck with that spear the demon Tāraka, the tormentor of the worlds.
m.2.4.10.31: Instantly and suddenly the demon named Tāraka, the great hero, lord of all the hosts of Asuras, fell to the ground, his limbs shattered.
m.2.4.10.32: Slain by Kumāra, that exceedingly heroic Tāraka indeed perished right there, O sage, as all looked on.
m.2.4.10.33: Seeing the very powerful Tāraka thus fallen, the hero did not strike him again, since he had become lifeless in the battle.
m.2.4.10.34: When that mighty great Daitya named Tāraka was slain, many Asuras were then brought to destruction by the hosts of gods.
m.2.4.10.35: Some, frightened, stood with joined palms there in the battle; some Daityas, their limbs cut and pierced, died by thousands.
m.2.4.10.36: Some Daityas, seeking refuge, then took refuge with Kumāra, saying with joined palms, protect us, protect us.
m.2.4.10.37: Many were killed there and many fled; as they fled, distressed, they were beaten by the hosts of the immortals.
m.2.4.10.38: By thousands they entered Pātāla, wishing to save their lives; all of them fleeing, their hopes broken, sank into misery.
m.2.4.10.39: Thus the entire Daitya army was routed, O lord of sages; none remained there then, out of fear of the Gaṇas and the gods.
m.2.4.10.40: When that wicked one was slain, everything became free of thorns; then all those gods, Śakra and the rest, attained happiness.
m.2.4.10.41: When Kumāra had thus won victory, all the gods were delighted at once, and the three worlds were filled with great happiness.
m.2.4.10.42: Then Śiva too, learning of Kārttika's victory, came there joyfully with his attendants (gaṇas) and his beloved.
m.2.4.10.43: Placing his own son Kumāra, radiant as the sun, on his lap, he fondled him with great love; and Śivā, overflowing with affection, did so too.
m.2.4.10.44: Then Himālaya came, surrounded by his sons, with his kinsmen and followers, and praised Śambhu, Śivā and Guha.
m.2.4.10.45: Then all the hosts of gods, the sages, the Siddhas and Cāraṇas praised Śaṅkara's son, Śambhu, and Girijā, who was greatly pleased.
m.2.4.10.46: Then the demigods showered a very great rain of flowers; the lords of the Gandharvas sang and the troupes of Apsarases danced.
m.2.4.10.47: Likewise musical instruments sounded at that time especially, and cries of victory and obeisance rose loudly again and again.
m.2.4.10.48: Then I Brahmā and Acyuta too became especially delighted, and with great reverence praised Śiva, Śivā and Kumāra.
m.2.4.10.49: Placing Kumāra in front, the gods headed by Hari and Indra, and likewise other sages, lovingly performed the nīrājana (waving of lights).
m.2.4.10.50: With the sound of songs and instruments and abundant Vedic chanting, there was then a great festival, and especially much glorification.
m.2.4.10.51: O sage, the Lord of the world was praised by all the hosts of gods, delighted, with songs and instruments and with joined palms.
m.2.4.10.52: Then the blessed Rudra, praised by all, went with Bhavānī, the Mother of the world, to his own mountain, surrounded by his gaṇas.
m.2.4.10.iti: Thus ends the tenth adhyāya, named The slaying of the demon Tāraka and the festival of the gods, in the fourth khaṇḍa, the Kumāra-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.4.11.1: Brahmā said: Meanwhile, O sage, the mountain named Krauñca, tormented by Bāṇa, came there to Kumāra for refuge.
m.2.4.11.2: He Bāṇa, who had fled from the battle unable to bear the lordly splendour of Kumāra, and who was endowed with the strength of ten thousand crores, harassed Krauñca exceedingly.
m.2.4.11.3: Bowing with devotion at Kumāra's lotus feet, he reverently praised Guha with words full of love.
m.2.4.11.4: Krauñca said: O Kumāra, O Skanda, lord of the gods, destroyer of the demon Tāraka, protect me, who have come for refuge, sorely oppressed by the demon Bāṇa.
m.2.4.11.5: O Mahāsena, routed in battle with you, he fled, and coming to me he oppressed me. Alas, O lord, mine of compassion!
m.2.4.11.6: Tormented by him, I have come fleeing to your refuge in great distress. O lord of the gods, O reed-born one, show mercy.
m.2.4.11.7: O mighty one, destroy that demon called Bāṇa and make me happy. You especially are the slayer of demons, the protector of the gods, the self-ruling sovereign.
m.2.4.11.8: Brahmā said: Thus praised by Krauñca, Skanda, protector of devotees, was pleased; taking up his own incomparable spear, the auspicious one meditated on Śiva in his mind.
m.2.4.11.9: The son of Śaṅkara hurled it, aiming at Bāṇa. Then there arose a great sound, and the directions and the sky blazed.
m.2.4.11.10: Having reduced that demon together with his army to ashes in a mere instant, that supreme spear returned to Guha's side, O sage.
m.2.4.11.11: Then Lord Kumāra said to Krauñca, the best of mountains: Go to your home without fear; that demon has perished with his army.
m.2.4.11.12: Hearing those words of the lord, the king of mountains was then delighted; having praised Guha, the foe of that demon, he returned to his own abode.
m.2.4.11.13: Then, O sage, Skanda joyfully installed there, according to rite, three liṅgas of Maheśa that destroy sin.
m.2.4.11.14: First the one named Pratijñeśvara, then reverently Kapāleśvara, and then Kumāreśvara — the triad that grants every attainment.
m.2.4.11.15: Further, Guha, lord of all, joyfully installed there, near the pillar of victory, a liṅga named Stambheśvara.
m.2.4.11.16: Then all the gods there, Viṣṇu and the others, joyfully installed liṅgas of the trident-bearing god of gods.
m.2.4.11.17: Then the glory of all those Śiva-liṅgas became wondrous; it grants all desires and also bestows liberation on those who practise devotion.
m.2.4.11.18: Then all the gods headed by Viṣṇu, glad at heart, wished to go to the best of mountains Kailāsa, joyfully placing Guha at their head.
m.2.4.11.19: At that moment Śeṣa's son, named Kumuda, oppressed by a demon, came to Kumāra for refuge.
m.2.4.11.20: The demon called Pralamba, who had fled from this battle — that mighty follower of Tāraka was causing havoc there.
m.2.4.11.21: Then Kumuda, the great son of Śeṣa, lord of serpents, having come to Kumāra for refuge, praised the son of Girijā.
m.2.4.11.22: Kumuda said: O god of gods, great god, excellent dear one, great lord, I am tormented by Pralamba; I have come to you for refuge.
m.2.4.11.23: Protect me, who have sought refuge, oppressed by the demon Pralamba, O Kumāra, Skanda, lord of gods, foe of Tāraka, great lord.
m.2.4.11.24: You are the friend of the afflicted, an ocean of compassion, loving to those who bow down; you are indeed the punisher of the wicked, the giver of refuge and the goal of the good.
m.2.4.11.25: Thus praised by Kumuda and entreated for his Pralamba's slaying, he took up his own spear, remembering the lotus feet of Śiva.
m.2.4.11.26: The son of Girijā hurled it, aiming at Pralamba. Then there arose a great sound, and the directions and the sky blazed.
m.2.4.11.27: The spear, which acts without effort, swiftly reduced him with his ten thousand forces to ashes and suddenly returned to Guha's side.
m.2.4.11.28: Then Kumāra said to Kumuda, the serpent youth: Go to your home without fear; that demon has perished with his army.
m.2.4.11.29: Hearing Guha's words, Kumuda, son of the lord of serpents, praised Kumāra, bowed to him, and joyfully went to Pātāla.
m.2.4.11.30: Thus, O lord of sages, I have described to you Kumāra's victory, the deed of Tāraka's slaying, which causes supreme wonder.
m.2.4.11.31: It is divine, removes all sins, grants all desires to men; it is auspicious, bestows fame and long life, and gives enjoyment and liberation to the good.
m.2.4.11.32: Those men, endowed with boundless good fortune, who recite the glorious, divine story of Kumāra, go to Śiva's world.
m.2.4.11.33: And those people who, full of faith, listen with devotion to his glory will enjoy supreme happiness here and attain divine liberation.
m.2.4.11.iti: Thus ends the eleventh adhyāya, named The slaying of Bāṇa and Pralamba and the victory of Kumāra, in the fourth khaṇḍa, the Kumāra-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.4.12.1: Brahmā said: Seeing Tāraka slain, the gods headed by Viṣṇu, and all the others with joyful faces, praised Śaṅkara's son with devotion.
m.2.4.12.2: The gods said: Obeisance to you whose form is auspicious; obeisance to you, O auspiciousness of the universe. O friend of the universe, obeisance be to you; obeisance to you, O maker of the universe.
m.2.4.12.3: Obeisance be to you, slayer of the foremost of the Dānavas, taker of Bāṇāsura's life, O god; to the destroyer of Pralamba, whose form is pure, again and again obeisance to you, O child of Śaṅkara.
m.2.4.12.4: You alone are the creator and sustainer of the worlds; you alone are the destroyer, O son of Śuci (Agni) — be gracious. The image of the world is your manifest form; be gracious, O son of Śambhu, friend of the distressed.
m.2.4.12.5: O protector of the gods, O master, protect us always, O lord; O preserver of the gods' lives, be gracious, O mine of compassion.
m.2.4.12.6: By slaying the demon Tāraka together with his retinue, O all-pervading one, you have freed all the gods from calamities, O supreme lord.
m.2.4.12.7: Brahmā said: Thus praised by the gods headed by Viṣṇu, that lord Kumāra gave new boons to all of them in turn, O sage.
m.2.4.12.8: Then that son of Giriśa, seeing the mountains praising him, became exceedingly pleased and spoke, granting boons.
m.2.4.12.9: Skanda said: All of you mountains shall indeed be worthy of worship by ascetics, and shall be resorted to by men of ritual action and men of knowledge.
m.2.4.12.10: By my word, O mountains, you shall become distinguished forms of Śambhu and forms of the liṅga as well — there is no doubt.
m.2.4.12.11: This Himavat, best of mountains, who is now my maternal grandfather, most fortunate, shall indeed be the giver of fruits to ascetics.
m.2.4.12.12: The gods said: Having thus given boons and slain Tāraka, lord of the asuras, you have made all of us, moving and unmoving, happy.
m.2.4.12.13: Now indeed, with great love, you should go to Kailāsa, the abode of Giriśa, to see your mother and father, Śivā and Śambhu.
m.2.4.12.14: Brahmā said: Having said this, all the gods headed by Viṣṇu, having received his consent, held a great festival on a grand scale and went with Kumāra to the mountain.
m.2.4.12.15: As the lord Kumāra went to Kailāsa, the abode of Śaṅkara, a great auspicious tumult arose and there was the cry of victory.
m.2.4.12.16: That Kumāra mounted an aerial car of supreme splendour, adorned on every side, delightful, shining above all.
m.2.4.12.17: Then I and Viṣṇu, both joyful, held chowries over Guha's head with great love, O sage, and were tireless.
m.2.4.12.18: Indra and all the other immortals, rendering service to Guha as was fitting, went along then in the four directions, delighted.
m.2.4.12.19: Proclaiming Śambhu's victory, they reached Śambhu's mountain; joyfully they entered, and there an auspicious sound was raised.
m.2.4.12.20: Seeing Śiva and Śivā, all of them, Viṣṇu and the others, quickly bowed with devotion to Śaṅkara, joining their palms, humbly.
m.2.4.12.21: Kumāra too, humble in spirit, descended from the aerial car and joyfully bowed to Śambhu and to Śivā seated on the lion-throne.
m.2.4.12.22: Then, seeing that Kumāra, their son dear as life, the divine couple Śiva and Śivā rejoiced exceedingly, O Nārada.
m.2.4.12.23: The great lord lifted him up and seated him on his lap; out of affection he joyfully smelled his head and caressed him with his hand.
m.2.4.12.24: Filled with great bliss, Śambhu, out of great affection, kissed the face of Kumāra, the great lord, the enemy of Tāraka.
m.2.4.12.25: Śivā too lifted him up and seated him on her own lap; out of great affection, placing her hand on his head, she kissed his lotus-face.
m.2.4.12.26: Then the great joy of the two, the couple Śiva and Śivā, who were acting in worldly fashion, grew exceedingly, O Nārada, dear one.
m.2.4.12.27: Then there was a great festival, full of many wonders, in Śiva's abode; cries of victory and of obeisance rang out exceedingly on all sides.
m.2.4.12.28: Then all the hosts of gods headed by Viṣṇu, and likewise the sages, bowing reverently with joy to Śambhu, praised him together with Śivā, O sage.
m.2.4.12.29: The gods said: O god of gods, O Mahādeva, giver of fearlessness to devotees, obeisance, obeisance to you many times over, O mine of compassion, O Maheśvara.
m.2.4.12.30: Wondrous is your great divine play, O Mahādeva, bestowing happiness on all the virtuous, O Śaṅkara, friend of the distressed, great lord.
m.2.4.12.31: Being thus dull-minded and ignorant, we do not know the eternal mode of invocation in your worship, nor indeed your wondrous ways, O lord.
m.2.4.12.32: To the bearer of the stream of Gaṅgā's waters, to the support of all, to the one whose nature is the guṇas, obeisance to you, lord of the thirty gods; to Śaṅkara obeisance again and again.
m.2.4.12.33: Obeisance to the one bearing the bull emblem, to the great lord, to the lord of the gaṇas; obeisance to the lord of all, the god, the lord of the three worlds.
m.2.4.12.34: To the destroyer of all the worlds, O lord, obeisance, obeisance to you; to the sustainer and creator, O lord of gods, to the lord of the three guṇas, the eternal one.
m.2.4.12.35: To the unattached one, the supreme lord, to Śiva, the supreme Self, to the one beyond the manifest world, the pure, the supreme and the imperishable.
m.2.4.12.36: Obeisance to you, staff in hand, who are Kāla (Time), noose in hand; obeisance to you, foremost of the Vedic mantras, the hundred-tongued.
m.2.4.12.37: Whatever was, is, and will be, whatever is stationary and moving — all has arisen entirely from your body, O supreme lord.
m.2.4.12.38: Protect us always, O master; be gracious, O blessed lord. We have taken refuge in you completely, O supreme lord.
m.2.4.12.39: Obeisance to you, the dark-throated Rudra, who are the svāhā-utterance; obeisance to you, formless, with form, and of universal form.
m.2.4.12.40: To Śiva, the blue-throated, who bears pyre-ash on his limbs, to the one ever blue-crested, to Śrīkaṇṭha, obeisance again and again.
m.2.4.12.41: To him before whom all bodies bow, to him who is bowed to through self-restraint, to Mahādeva, to Śarva, and to him whose feet are worshipped by all — salutations.
m.2.4.12.42: Among all the gods you are Brahmā; among the Rudras, Nīlalohita; you are the Self of all beings, and by the Sāṅkhyas you are called Puruṣa.
m.2.4.12.43: Among mountains you are Sumeru, among the stars the moon; among the sages you are Vasiṣṭha, and likewise among the gods Vāsava (Indra).
m.2.4.12.44: You are the Oṃkāra of all the Vedas; be our protector, O Maheśvara. And for the welfare of the worlds you sprinkle (nourish) the beings.
m.2.4.12.45: O Maheśvara, O most fortunate one, observer of good and evil, O lord of gods, nourish us, who are indeed the doers of your word.
m.2.4.12.46: Among your thousands of crores of forms and hundreds of crores of forms, we are unable to reach the end; O god of gods, salutation be to you.
m.2.4.12.47: Brahmā said: Having thus praised him, all the gods headed by Viṣṇu, standing in front, bowed again and again, placing Skanda at their head.
m.2.4.12.48: Having heard the gods' hymn, Śiva, lord of all, the self-ruling one, became very pleased, and then, full of compassion, he smiled.
m.2.4.12.49: With a delighted mind, Śaṅkara, the supreme lord, friend of the afflicted and refuge of the good, spoke to Viṣṇu and the other best of gods.
m.2.4.12.50: Śiva said: O Hari, O Vidhi (Brahmā), O gods, listen to my words with attention. I am in every way the protector of the good, and for you gods, a treasure of compassion.
m.2.4.12.51: I am Śaṅkara, slayer of the wicked, lord of the three worlds, loving to devotees; creator, sustainer and destroyer of all, yet free from change.
m.2.4.12.52: Whenever distress befalls you, O best of gods, then you should worship me for the sake of your happiness.
m.2.4.12.53: Brahmā said: Thus commanded, the gods headed by Viṣṇu, together with the lords of sages, joyfully bowed to Śivā, to Śiva with her, and to Kumāra;
m.2.4.12.54: And recounting that delightful glory of Śiva and Śivā and of Śiva's son, having attained supreme bliss, they went to their own abodes, O sage.
m.2.4.12.55: Śiva too, the supreme lord, together with Śivā and his gaṇas, joined by Kumāra, dwelt joyfully and lovingly on that mountain.
m.2.4.12.56: Thus, O sage, the whole story of Kumāra has been told, which is Śaiva, bliss-giving and divine. What else do you wish to hear?
m.2.4.12.iti: Thus ends the twelfth adhyāya, named The deeds of Śiva and Śivā, containing the deeds of Lord Kārttika, in the fourth khaṇḍa, the Kumāra-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.4.13.1: Sūta said: Having heard this wonderful and excellent account of the enemy of Tāraka, Nārada was greatly pleased, and then he lovingly questioned Vidhi (Brahmā).
m.2.4.13.2: Nārada said: O god of gods, lord of creatures, treasury of the knowledge of Śiva, I have heard the noble story of Kārttika, which is finer even than nectar.
m.2.4.13.3: Now I wish to hear the excellent story of Gaṇeśa — the divine account of his birth, the most auspicious of all auspicious things.
m.2.4.13.4: Sūta said: Hearing these words of the great sage Nārada, Brahmā, pleased at heart, replied while remembering Śiva.
m.2.4.13.5: Brahmā said: Owing to the difference of kalpas, the birth of Gaṇeśa has been told in another way on higher authority: there his head, looked upon by Śani, was cut off, and an elephant's face was joined to him.
m.2.4.13.6: Now the origin of Gaṇeśa as told in the Śveta kalpa is narrated, in which his head was cut off by the compassionate Śiva.
m.2.4.13.7: No doubt should be entertained here, O sage: Śaṅkara is the maker of creation. That Śambhu is indeed the lord of all, without qualities and yet also with qualities.
m.2.4.13.8: By his play the whole universe is created, likewise sustained, and destroyed, O best of sages. Now listen attentively to the matter at hand.
m.2.4.13.9: After Śiva had been married and had gone to Kailāsa, within some time the birth of Gaṇapati took place.
m.2.4.13.10: At one time the friends Jayā and Vijayā, meeting together with Pārvatī, became engaged in deliberation.
m.2.4.13.11: They said: All the gaṇas belong to Rudra and are devoted to Śiva's command; all of them, headed by Nandin and Bhṛṅgin, are reckoned ours as well.
m.2.4.13.12: Those pramathas are countless, yet not one is our own. They all stand at the door, devoted to Śaṅkara's command.
m.2.4.13.13: Though all of them are ours too, still our mind does not accord with them. One who is truly our own should be created by you, O sinless one.
m.2.4.13.14: Brahmā said: When these beautiful words were spoken by her two friends, the goddess Pārvatī then considered them beneficial and resolved to carry them out.
m.2.4.13.15: Then once, while Pārvatī was bathing, Sadāśiva rebuked Nandin and came into the inner apartment.
m.2.4.13.16: Seeing Śaṅkara arriving at an untimely moment, the beautiful mother of the world, who was bathing, rose up then, embarrassed.
m.2.4.13.17: On that occasion the goddess, filled with eagerness, considered the words of her friends beneficial and conducive to happiness.
m.2.4.13.18: When things had happened thus, at some time Pārvatī Śivā, the supreme goddess possessing the highest māyā, reflected in her mind as follows:
m.2.4.13.19: Let there be some servant of my own, very auspicious and capable, who will not move even a line's breadth from my command.
m.2.4.13.20: Having reflected thus, the goddess created from the dirt of her body a person endowed with all auspicious marks,
m.2.4.13.21: flawless in all his limbs, beautiful in all his limbs, large, rich in every splendour, of great strength and valour.
m.2.4.13.22: Then she gave him various garments, many kinds of ornaments, and abundant, unsurpassed blessings.
m.2.4.13.23: You are my son, you are my own; I have no one else here. Thus addressed, that person bowed to Śivā and spoke.
m.2.4.13.24: Gaṇeśa said: What task do you have today? I shall do what you command. Thus addressed by him, Śivā then replied to her son.
m.2.4.13.25: Śivā said: O dear one, hear my word: be my doorkeeper today. You are my son, you are my own; I have no one else.
m.2.4.13.26: Without my permission, good son, no one at all, from anywhere, may force his way into my inner apartment, dear one. This I have spoken truly.
m.2.4.13.27: Brahmā said: Having said this, O sage, she gave him a very strong staff, and looking at his beautiful form she was filled with joy.
m.2.4.13.28: Kissing his face and embracing her son with great love and tenderness, she stationed the lord of gaṇas, staff in hand, at her door.
m.2.4.13.29: Then, dear one, the goddess's son, the gaṇa, a great hero, staff in hand, stood at the door of the house, wishing for Pārvatī's good.
m.2.4.13.30: Having stationed Gaṇeśa, her own son, at her door, Śivā herself remained bathing, accompanied by her friends.
m.2.4.13.31: At that very moment Śiva arrived at the door, playful, O tiger among sages, skilled in many sports.
m.2.4.13.32: Not recognising that lord Śiva, the lord of gaṇas said: O god, without my mother's permission you may not go in now.
m.2.4.13.33: My mother is engaged in bathing. Where are you going? Go away from here now. Saying this, he then seized his staff to block him.
m.2.4.13.34: Seeing him, Śiva said: Whom are you forbidding, foolish one? Do you not know me, wicked-minded one? I am Śiva, none other.
m.2.4.13.35: Struck with the staff by Gaṇeśa, Maheśvara, who delights in many sports, grew angry and replied to that son.
m.2.4.13.36: Śiva said: You are a fool, you do not know: I am Śiva, the husband of Girijā. I am going into my own house, boy — how can you stop me?
m.2.4.13.37: Brahmā said: As Maheśa, having said this, was entering, the leader of the gaṇas grew angry, O brahmin, and struck him again with the staff.
m.2.4.13.38: Then Śiva, enraged, commanded his own gaṇas: Who is this standing here, and what is he doing? Look into it, O gaṇas.
m.2.4.13.39: Having said this, Śiva stood there outside the house in anger — the Lord who delights in worldly conduct and performs many wondrous sports.
m.2.4.13.iti: Thus ends the thirteenth adhyāya, named The birth of Gaṇeśa, in the fourth khaṇḍa, the Kumāra-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.4.14.1: Brahmā said: Those gaṇas, filled with anger, went there at Śiva's command and then questioned that son of Girijā, the gatekeeper.
m.2.4.14.2: The attendants of Śiva said: Who are you? Where have you come from? And what do you intend to do? Go far away from here today, if you wish to live.
m.2.4.14.3: Brahmā said: Hearing those words of theirs, that son of Girijā, fearless and staff in hand, said this to the would-be gatekeepers.
m.2.4.14.4: Gaṇeśa said: Who are you, and where have you come from, you handsome ones here? Go far away. Why are you standing here as opponents?
m.2.4.14.5: Brahmā said: Hearing his words thus and laughing among themselves, all the gaṇas of Śiva, great heroes, now unabashed, spoke.
m.2.4.14.6: Having spoken thus to one another, all those attendants of Śiva, angry at heart, replied to that gatekeeper Gaṇeśa.
m.2.4.14.7: The attendants of Śiva said: Listen: we are indeed the gatekeepers, the foremost gaṇas of Śiva. We have come to stop you by the command of the Lord Śaṅkara.
m.2.4.14.8: Considering you too to be a gaṇa here, we do not kill you; otherwise you would be slain. Keep far away of your own accord—why do you seek death?
m.2.4.14.9: Brahmā said: Though addressed thus, Gaṇeśa, the fearless son of Girijā, rebuked Śaṅkara's gaṇas and did not then give up the door.
m.2.4.14.10: All those gaṇas of Śiva who were there, having heard his words, then went to Śiva and told him what had happened.
m.2.4.14.11: Then, hearing their report, Maheśvara of wondrous play, the goal of the worlds, rebuked his own gaṇas and spoke, O sage.
m.2.4.14.12: Maheśvara said: Who is this fellow, and what does he say, puffed up like an enemy? What will this ill-minded one do? Surely he desires his own death.
m.2.4.14.13: Let this new gatekeeper be driven far away. How is it that you stand there like eunuchs and report his doings to me?
m.2.4.14.14: Told thus by their master Śambhu of wondrous play, those gaṇas came back to that very spot and spoke to the gatekeeper.
m.2.4.14.15: The attendants of Śiva said: Hey, hey, door-guard, who are you, standing here? By whom were you posted? You take no account of us at all—how then do you wish to live?
m.2.4.14.16: We are all standing here as the gatekeepers; why do you bluster? A jackal that has seized a lion's seat merely hopes for its own safety.
m.2.4.14.17: You roar, fool, only so long as the might of the gaṇas has not been felt by you; once it is felt, you will fall right here.
m.2.4.14.18: Addressed thus by them, he grew very angry, and then, seizing his staff with both hands, he struck those gaṇas who were speaking insolently.
m.2.4.14.19: Then the son of Śivā, the fearless lord of gaṇas, rebuking those great heroes, the chief gaṇas of Śaṅkara, spoke.
m.2.4.14.20: The son of Śivā said: Go, go far away from here. If not, I will show you my own exceedingly fierce valour, and you will become utter laughing-stocks.
m.2.4.14.21: Hearing those words of Girijā's son, Śaṅkara's gaṇas then spoke among themselves.
m.2.4.14.22: The attendants of Śiva said: What should be done? Where should we go? Why is he not dealt with? We are keeping to propriety; otherwise what could he say?
m.2.4.14.23: Brahmā said: Then all Śambhu's gaṇas went to Śiva, who was staying at a distance, a mere krośa from Kailāsa, and told him likewise.
m.2.4.14.24: Śiva, the Supreme Lord, trident in hand and fierce of mind, laughed and spoke to all those gaṇas of his, who were esteemed as heroes.
m.2.4.14.25: Śiva said: Hey, hey, gaṇas, you have the minds of eunuchs; you are no heroes, only thinking yourselves heroes. You are not fit to speak before me. Rebuked by him, what more can one say?
m.2.4.14.26: Go, and let him be beaten, whoever he may be who holds sway here. What use is much talk on this? He must simply be removed.
m.2.4.14.27: Brahmā said: Thus rebuked by Maheśa, that god, all those best of gaṇas went there, O lord of sages, and spoke.
m.2.4.14.28: The attendants of Śiva said: Hey, you, listen, boy. Why do you talk so insolently, relying on force? Go far away from here; if not, death will be yours.
m.2.4.14.29: Brahmā said: Hearing these words of those who were surely carrying out Śiva's command, the son of Śivā became distressed then, thinking, what shall I do?
m.2.4.14.30: Meanwhile the Goddess, hearing again the quarrel at the door between them and him, said to her friend, go and see.
m.2.4.14.31: The friend came there and understood what had happened; having watched for a moment, she went back delighted to Śivā's presence.
m.2.4.14.32: Having gone there, O sage, that friend related in full before Girijā everything that had happened.
m.2.4.14.33: The friend said: O Great Goddess, that gaṇa of ours who stands at the door—Śaṅkara's heroic gaṇas are surely abusing him.
m.2.4.14.34: How can Śiva and all the gaṇas force their way into the house without your leave? This is not good for you.
m.2.4.14.35: He has acted rightly indeed, for no one has been let in, even though he has suffered pain here, as well as insult and the like.
m.2.4.14.36: From now on, a war of words is going on between them. Even when the dispute has taken place, let them not simply come in at their ease.
m.2.4.14.37: Since the dispute has been started here, let them all enter only by defeating him and winning; never otherwise, my dear.
m.2.4.14.38: In this very one of ours, all of us have been insulted. Therefore, O Goddess, O gracious one, you must not give up your high self-respect.
m.2.4.14.39: Śiva today always behaves toward you like a monkey, O virtuous lady. What arrogance will he show? He will become compliant.
m.2.4.14.40: Brahmā said: Ah! Satī remained there for a moment, under the sway of Śiva's will.
m.2.4.14.41: Then Pārvatī, becoming proud and resolute, spoke within her mind:
m.2.4.14.42: Śivā said: Ah! He (Śiva) did not wait even for a moment; how was this forcible entry made? And how should I act here now — with humility, or otherwise?
m.2.4.14.43: What is to happen will surely happen; what has been done cannot be otherwise. Having said this, the beloved Pārvatī then sent a female companion there.
m.2.4.14.44: She came and spoke what the beloved Pārvatī had told her; she then reported it to Gaṇeśa, the son of Girijā.
m.2.4.14.45: The friend said: You have done well, good one; let them not enter by force. How can these gaṇas, standing before you, conquer one such as you?
m.2.4.14.46: Whether it has been done or not done, you must do what is to be done. Whoever is defeated, again — there is surely no enmity in it.
m.2.4.14.47: Brahmā said: Hearing these words of her and of his mother, the lord of gaṇas attained supreme joy, abundant strength and great exaltation.
m.2.4.14.48: Girding his loins and tying on his turban, touching his shanks and thighs, he joyfully spoke fearless words to all those gaṇas.
