m.2.4.14.49: Gaṇeśa said: I am the son of Girijā, and you are Śiva's gaṇas; both of us stand on equal footing, so let what must be done be done.
m.2.4.14.50: You are doorkeepers; why am I not a doorkeeper too? You are stationed there, and I am stationed here — that is settled.
m.2.4.14.51: When it is settled that you are stationed here, then you should carry out Śiva's command.
m.2.4.14.52: But now, O heroes, it is I who am here truly carrying out Śivā's command; I have decided this as is fitting.
m.2.4.14.53: Therefore, all you gaṇas of Śiva, listen attentively to my word: neither by force nor by entreaty shall you go into the palace again.
m.2.4.14.54: Brahmā said: Thus addressed by the gaṇa Gaṇeśa, all those gaṇas, ashamed, went to Śiva; having bowed, they stood before him.
m.2.4.14.55: Standing there, they all reported that astonishing account; with joined palms and bowed shoulders, having praised Śiva, they stood before him.
m.2.4.14.56: Then, having heard all that account told by his own gaṇas, Śaṅkara, adopting worldly conduct, spoke these words.
m.2.4.14.57: Śaṅkara said: Listen, all you gaṇas: a fight would not be proper, for you here are mine, and he likewise is Gaurī's gaṇa.
m.2.4.14.58: Yet if humility is shown, the report will spread in the world that Śambhu is always under his wife's control; my gaṇas would surely be reproached.
m.2.4.14.59: When something has been done, one must respond in kind — this is the weightier policy. That gaṇa is a lone boy; what valour can he show?
m.2.4.14.60: You gaṇas are renowned in the world and highly skilled in battle. Being mine, how could you abandon the fight and go into disgrace?
m.2.4.14.61: How can a woman be obstinate, especially before her husband? Having done so, Girijā will surely reap its fruit.
m.2.4.14.62: Therefore, all my heroes, listen attentively to my word: you must fight by all means; let whatever is to be, be.
m.2.4.14.63: Brahmā said: Having spoken thus, O Brahmin, Śaṅkara, skilled in many sportive plays, fell silent, O best of sages, displaying the way of the world.
m.2.4.14.iti: Thus ends the fourteenth adhyāya, named The dispute of the gaṇas, in the fourth khaṇḍa, the Kumāra-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.4.15.1: Brahmā said: Thus addressed by that Lord, they came to a firm resolve; then, armed for battle, they went there to Śiva's abode.
m.2.4.15.2: Gaṇeśa too, seeing the excellent gaṇas thus arrived, and making a show of readiness for battle, said this to them as they stood there.
m.2.4.15.3: Gaṇeśa said: Let all the gaṇa-leaders come, who carry out Śiva's command. I am alone, and a boy, carrying out Śivā's (Pārvatī's) command.
m.2.4.15.4: Even so, let the goddess Pārvatī see the strength of her son, and let Śiva in turn see the strength of his own gaṇas.
m.2.4.15.5: This will be a battle between the mighty and a boy, between the sides of Bhavānī and Śiva. You, skilled in warfare, have fought battles before;
m.2.4.15.6: by me it was never done before; I am a boy, yet it is being done now. Even so, the shame here before Girijā and Śiva will be yours.
m.2.4.15.7: It will not be so for me; the reverse will happen. The shame here before Girijā and Śiva will be yours, not mine.
m.2.4.15.8: Knowing this, O lords of the gaṇas, the battle must be fought—by you with an eye to your master, and by me with an eye to my mother.
m.2.4.15.9: Whatever kind of battle is fought, let what must be, be. No one in the three worlds is able to prevent it.
m.2.4.15.10: Brahmā said: Thus rebuked, they, their arms adorned with staffs, took up various weapons and advanced together.
m.2.4.15.11: Grinding their teeth and roaring huṃ again and again, crying, look, look, those gaṇas drew near.
m.2.4.15.12: Nandī, coming first, seized a foot and pulled; Bhṛṅgī, running up, seized the gaṇa's other foot.
m.2.4.15.13: While the two were pulling at his feet, the gaṇa struck them on their hands with his hand, and himself freed his two feet from them.
m.2.4.15.14: Then the heroic son of the Goddess, Gaṇapati, standing at the door, seized a huge iron club and struck down all of them.
m.2.4.15.15: Of some the hands were broken, of some the backs, of some the heads, and of some the skulls.
m.2.4.15.16: Of some the knees there, of some the shoulders likewise were broken. All those who came face to face with him were struck in the chest.
m.2.4.15.17: Some fell to the ground, some fled to the intermediate quarters, of some both feet were severed, and some went to Śarva.
m.2.4.15.18: Among them not one stood facing him in the fight; just as deer, seeing a lion, flee in the ten directions,
m.2.4.15.19: so all those gaṇas fled by the thousands. And he too, turning back, took his stand at the fine doorway.
m.2.4.15.20: Just as Kāla (Time/Death) appears terrifying when bringing about the end of an aeon, so he appeared, as the bringer of dissolution to all.
m.2.4.15.21: At this very time all the gods, together with the lord of Ramā (Viṣṇu) and the lord of the gods (Indra), urged by Nārada, assembled here.
m.2.4.15.22: Then all of them, wishing Śiva's good, stood before him, bowed to Śiva and said: Give us your command, O Lord.
m.2.4.15.23: You are the supreme Brahman, the lord of all, and all are your servants; you are the creator of the world, ever its sustainer and destroyer, the supreme Lord.
m.2.4.15.24: Through sport you take the forms of rajas, sattva and tamas, while by nature you are beyond attributes. What sport have you devised today? Tell us that now, O Lord.
m.2.4.15.25: Brahmā said: Hearing their words, O best of sages, Maheśvara, seeing then his gaṇas shattered, related everything to them.
m.2.4.15.26: Then Śaṅkara, lord of all and lord of Girijā, O best of sages, laughed and spoke to me, Brahmā.
m.2.4.15.27: Śiva said: Listen, Brahmā: at my door stands a single boy, very mighty, staff in hand, barring entry into the house.
m.2.4.15.28: He deals mighty blows and strikes down my attendants; by force he has inflicted defeat on my gaṇas here.
m.2.4.15.29: Brahmā, you yourself must go; this mighty one must be pacified. O Vidhi, act so that conciliation may come about.
m.2.4.15.30: Brahmā said: Hearing the Lord's words, not understanding, deluded by ignorance, I went near him, dear one, with all the foremost sages.
m.2.4.15.31: Seeing me approach, that very mighty Gaṇeśa grew angry, rushed up, and plucked out my beard.
m.2.4.15.32: Forgive me, forgive me, O god. I have not come to fight. I am a brāhmaṇa, deserving favour, a maker of peace, harmless.
m.2.4.15.33: While I was speaking thus, O brāhmaṇa, that Gaṇeśa, the great hero, a boy of more than boyish valour, took up the iron club.
m.2.4.15.34: Seeing that mighty Gaṇeśa with the club in hand, I, bent on flight, then ran off very swiftly.
m.2.4.15.35: Crying, go, go, they were then struck by the club; some fell by themselves, and some were felled by him.
m.2.4.15.36: And some, reaching Śiva's presence in that very instant, reported the whole event to Śiva.
m.2.4.15.37: Seeing them in such a state and hearing that account, Hara, skilled in divine sport, conceived boundless anger.
m.2.4.15.38: He then commanded all the hosts of gods headed by Indra, the gaṇas led by Ṣaṇmukha, and the bhūtas, pretas and piśācas.
m.2.4.15.39: All of them, as befitted each, went forth from every direction, eager to kill that gaṇa, commanded by Śiva, with weapons raised.
m.2.4.15.40: Whatever weapon each one had, all of it in particular, rushing up with force, they hurled upon Gaṇeśa.
m.2.4.15.41: A great cry of distress arose in the three worlds with their moving and unmoving beings; all the people dwelling in the three worlds fell into the utmost anxiety.
m.2.4.15.42: They thought: Even Brahmā's lifespan has not run out, yet the cosmic egg is surely going to destruction — untimely indeed, by the force of Śiva's own will.
m.2.4.15.43: All those who had come there, and those again headed by Ṣaṇmukha — the gods, their weapons rendered futile, were struck with supreme amazement.
m.2.4.15.44: Meanwhile the goddess Jagadambā, the awakener of all, having learned of all that had been done, conceived boundless anger.
m.2.4.15.45: Then, O lord of sages, two Śaktis were created there by that goddess, for the purpose of giving every help to her own gaṇa.
m.2.4.15.46: One of them, O great sage, assuming a fierce form, stood there, opening wide her cave-like mouth, resembling a dark mountain.
m.2.4.15.47: The other had the form of lightning, was endowed with many arms — a terrifying great goddess, dealing punishment to the wicked.
m.2.4.15.48: All the weapons released by the gods and gaṇas, the two seized in their mouths and swiftly hurled back.
m.2.4.15.49: No weapon of the gods could be seen — only the iron club of Gaṇeśa all around again. Thus a most wondrous deed was performed there by the two.
m.2.4.15.50: A single boy churned up the entire invincible army, just as the ocean was churned of old by the best of mountains.
m.2.4.15.51: All the immortals headed by Śakra were struck down by him alone, and Śaṅkara's gaṇas too then became distraught.
m.2.4.15.52: Then all of them, gathering together and sighing again and again, distressed by his blows, spoke to one another.
m.2.4.15.53: The hosts of the gods said: What should be done? Where should we go? The ten directions cannot be made out. He whirls his club to the left and to the right.
m.2.4.15.54: Brahmā said: At this time the foremost apsarases, with flowers and sandal-paste in their hands, and the sages headed by you, who were exceedingly eager for a great battle —
m.2.4.15.55: — they all came together to witness the battle; and then, O best of sages, the fair pathway of the sky was filled with them.
m.2.4.15.56: Those apsarases and those sages, seeing that battle, were filled with great wonder, for such a supreme battle had never been seen even once.
m.2.4.15.57: Then the earth together with the oceans trembled there, and the mountains fell; all this upheaval was brought about by the battle.
m.2.4.15.58: The sky reeled with its hosts of planets and stars; all became agitated. All the gods then fled, and all the gaṇas as well.
m.2.4.15.59: Only the valiant Ṣaṇmukha did not flee there; the great hero, holding them all back, stood in front.
m.2.4.15.60: In that battle all were rendered fruitless by the two Śaktis; all the missiles hurled by the immortals and gaṇas were cut to pieces.
m.2.4.15.61: Those who remained all came into Śiva's presence — all the gods who had fled, and all the gaṇas too, then.
m.2.4.15.62: Gathered together, they bowed to Śiva again and again and quickly said: Who is this excellent gaṇa, O Lord?
m.2.4.15.63: Battles have been heard of before, and now again many are seen; but such a one was never heard of or seen at any time.
m.2.4.15.64: Let something be considered, O God; otherwise there will be no victory. You alone, O Master, are the protector of the universe — there is no doubt.
m.2.4.15.65: Brahmā said: Hearing these words of theirs, Rudra, who is fierce in wrath, grew angry and went right there with his own gaṇas.
m.2.4.15.66: And that whole army of the gods, together with Viṣṇu the discus-bearer, making a great festive display, followed Śiva.
m.2.4.15.67: Meanwhile, O Nārada, you bowed with devotion to Maheśvara and, with folded hands, addressed the God of gods.
m.2.4.15.68: Nārada said: O God of gods, Mahādeva, hear my words, O all-pervading one. You alone are the omnipresent Master, skilled in manifold sports.
m.2.4.15.69: By performing a great sport, you have removed the pride of the gaṇas, and, by granting abundant strength to this one, the pride of the gods as well, O Śaṅkara.
m.2.4.15.70: Your own wondrous strength has been displayed in the world, O Lord, by you, the independent one, the destroyer of all pride, O Śambhu.
m.2.4.15.71: Now, O Lord, loving to your devotees, do not prolong that sport; honour your own gaṇas and the immortals well and make them prosper.
m.2.4.15.72: Do not play with him any longer now; slay him, O bestower of the state of Brahman. Having said this, O Nārada, you then vanished.
m.2.4.15.iti: Thus ends the fifteenth adhyāya, named The battle of Gaṇeśa, in the fourth khaṇḍa, the Kumāra-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.4.16.1: Brahmā said: Having heard this, Maheśāna, who bestows grace on his devotees, became eager to fight that boy, O Nārada, at your word.
m.2.4.16.2: Having summoned Viṣṇu and taken counsel with him, the three-eyed god, accompanied by a great force and with the gods, came face to face with him.
m.2.4.16.3: And the gods fought with him, remembering Śiva's lotus feet — very strong, full of great zeal, beheld by Śiva's gracious glance.
m.2.4.16.4: Then Hari, of great strength and valour, fought with him — the hero bearing great divine weapons, devoted, himself a form of Śiva.
m.2.4.16.5: Then that lord of the gaṇas, the hero endowed with great strength granted by Śakti, suddenly struck the foremost of the gods and Hari with his staff.
m.2.4.16.6: All the hosts of gods there, O sage, had their strength blunted; struck by him with the staff, together with Viṣṇu, they turned their backs.
m.2.4.16.7: Śiva too, having fought for a long time with his army, O sage, and seeing him so formidable, was filled with the greatest astonishment.
m.2.4.16.8: He must be slain only by stratagem; otherwise he cannot be slain — settling on this thought, he took his stand in the midst of the army.
m.2.4.16.9: Then, when the god Śiva — attributeless yet taking form with attributes — was seen, and when Viṣṇu too had come to the battle, all the deities
m.2.4.16.10: and the gaṇas of Maheśa then attained great joy; all of them, meeting one another with affection, held a celebration.
m.2.4.16.11: Then the heroic son of Śakti, with a hero's stride, first honoured with his own staff Viṣṇu, the bringer of all happiness.
m.2.4.16.12: Viṣṇu said: I shall delude him, and let him be slain by you, O Lord. Without a stratagem he cannot be killed; he is of tāmasic nature and hard to overcome.
m.2.4.16.13: Having made up his mind thus and consulted thoroughly with Śambhu, Viṣṇu, receiving Śiva's command, set himself to deluding him.
m.2.4.16.14: The two Śaktis, seeing Hari engaged in this way, gave the power of Śakti to Gaṇeśa and merged into him, O sage.
m.2.4.16.15: Then, the two Śaktis having merged into him, Gaṇeśa, now even mightier, hurled his iron club to where Viṣṇu himself was standing.
m.2.4.16.16: Making some effort here, Viṣṇu evaded its course, remembering Śiva Maheśāna, his own lord, who is affectionate to devotees.
m.2.4.16.17: Seeing his face turned to one side, Śaṅkara too came, taking up his trident, greatly enraged, eager for battle.
m.2.4.16.18: The mighty hero, son of Śivā, saw Śambhu Maheśvara arrive, trident in hand, wishing to slay him.
m.2.4.16.19: Remembering his mother's lotus feet, that great hero Gaṇeśa, strengthened by Śiva's Śakti, struck him on the hand with a spear.
m.2.4.16.20: Seeing the trident fallen from his hand, Śiva, the Supreme Self, together with his attendants, took up the bow Pināka.
m.2.4.16.21: That too the lord of gaṇas knocked to the ground with his club. Thus five of Śiva's hands were struck; with the other five he took up the trident.
m.2.4.16.22: Alas, surely a more grievous trouble has now arisen for me! What could befall the gaṇas again? So spoke Bhava, following worldly ways.
m.2.4.16.23: Meanwhile the heroic lord of gaṇas, endowed with strength given by Śakti, struck the gods along with the gaṇas with his club.
m.2.4.16.24: The gods with the gaṇas, battered by the club, fled to the ten directions; none could stand in battle against that wondrous striker.
m.2.4.16.25: Viṣṇu, seeing that gaṇa, said: Blessed is he — of great strength, a great hero, very valiant, delighting in battle.
m.2.4.16.26: Many deities have I seen, and likewise many Dānavas, Daityas, Yakṣas, Gandharvas and Rākṣasas,
m.2.4.16.27: but none of them in all the three worlds attains equality with this lord of gaṇas in splendour, beauty, valour, virtues and the like.
m.2.4.16.28: As he was speaking thus, the son of Śakti, lord of gaṇas, whirling his club, hurled it there at Viṣṇu.
m.2.4.16.29: Hari took up his discus, remembering Śiva's lotus feet, and with that discus the club was quickly shattered to pieces.
m.2.4.16.30: The gaṇa hurled a fragment of the club at Hari; it was caught by the bird Garuḍa and rendered futile.
m.2.4.16.31: Thus for a long time both great heroes, Viṣṇu and the gaṇa, fought with each other.
m.2.4.16.32: Again the best of heroes, the mighty son of Śakti, remembering Śiva, took up his matchless staff and struck Viṣṇu with it.
m.2.4.16.33: Unable to bear that blow, he fell to the ground; rising quickly, he fought on with that son of Śivā.
m.2.4.16.34: Seizing this opportunity, the trident-bearer came from the north and cut off his head with the trident.
m.2.4.16.35: When the head of that lord of gaṇas was cut off, O Nārada, the army of the gaṇas and the army of the gods became utterly still.
m.2.4.16.36: You, Nārada, came and reported everything to the Goddess: O proud lady, listen — you must not give up your pride now.
m.2.4.16.37: Having said this, you, Nārada, lover of strife, vanished from there — you, the sage ever unchanging, who carry out the intent of Śambhu.
m.2.4.16.iti: Thus ends the sixteenth adhyāya, named The battle of Gaṇeśa and the cutting off of his head, in the fourth khaṇḍa, the Kumāra-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.4.17.1: Nārada said: O Brahmā, O greatly wise one, tell me: now that I have heard that whole account, what did the great Goddess do next? I wish to hear it truly.
m.2.4.17.2: Brahmā said: Listen, O tiger among sages; today I shall surely narrate the deeds of the Mother of the world that took place after that.
m.2.4.17.3: The Gaṇas then beat mṛdaṅga drums and kettle-drums, and held a great festival when that lord of the Gaṇas had been slain.
m.2.4.17.4: Even as Śiva, having cut off his head, was seized with grief, at that very time the goddess Girijā became exceedingly angry, O lord of sages.
m.2.4.17.5: She said: What shall I do? Where shall I go? Alas, alas, sorrow has befallen me! How can this sorrow be destroyed? Great is my anguish now.
m.2.4.17.6: My son has been destroyed today by all the gods and the Gaṇas. I shall destroy them all, or I shall bring about the dissolution of the world.
m.2.4.17.7: Grieving thus, she, the great Sovereign of all worlds, in her wrath instantly created Śaktis by hundreds of thousands.
m.2.4.17.8: Those Śaktis, once created, blazing with energy, bowed then to Śivā, the Mother of the world, and said: O Mother, command us.
m.2.4.17.9: Hearing that, she—Śambhu's Śakti, Prakṛti, Mahāmāyā—intent on wrath, replied to all of them, O lord of sages.
m.2.4.17.10: The Goddess said: O Śaktis, O goddesses, now by my command you must bring about dissolution here; there should be no hesitation in this.
m.2.4.17.11: O friends, forcibly devour the gods, the sages, the Yakṣas and Rākṣasas, both our own people and others.
m.2.4.17.12: Brahmā said: Thus commanded, all those Śaktis, intent on wrath, set about destroying the gods and all the rest.
m.2.4.17.13: Just as fire destroys grass, so all those Śaktis set about the destruction.
m.2.4.17.14: Whether it was a leader of the Gaṇas, or Viṣṇu, or Brahmā, or Śaṅkara, or Indra, or the king of the Yakṣas, or Skanda, or even Sūrya—
m.2.4.17.15: —the Śaktis went on ceaselessly destroying them all; wherever anyone was seen, there the Śaktis were too.
m.2.4.17.16: Many of them—fearsome, hunchbacked, lame, long-headed—seized the gods in their hands and then flung them into their mouths.
m.2.4.17.17: Seeing that destruction then, Hara, Brahmā and Hari, all the gods headed by Indra, the Gaṇas and the sages likewise—
m.2.4.17.18: —fell into doubt: What will this goddess do? Will she bring about an untimely dissolution? And their hope of life was lost.
m.2.4.17.19: All of them gathered together: Let it be considered what is to be done. Deliberating thus, they quickly spoke to one another.
m.2.4.17.20: Only when the goddess Girijā becomes gracious here will there be well-being; not otherwise, even with countless efforts.
m.2.4.17.21: Śiva too, expert in manifold divine play, fell into grief, adopting the ways of the world and deluding everyone there.
m.2.4.17.22: When the backs of all the gods had been broken, then no one dared to go before Śivā, who was wrath incarnate.
m.2.4.17.23: Whether one's own or another's, god or demon, Gaṇa or guardian of a quarter, Yakṣa, Kinnara or sage,
m.2.4.17.24: or Viṣṇu, or Brahmā, or the Lord Śaṅkara himself—no one was able to stand before Girijā, O sage.
m.2.4.17.25: Seeing that blazing radiance burning on all sides, they all became exceedingly afraid and stood very far away.
m.2.4.17.26: At that time, O sage, you, Nārada of divine vision, arrived there for the comfort of the hosts of gods.
m.2.4.17.27: He bowed to me, Brahmā, to Bhava, to Viṣṇu and to Śaṅkara, and coming together and meeting them, spoke, considering what was to be done.
m.2.4.17.28: All the gods consulted together with you, the great-souled one, on how the distress might be allayed; then they said together:
m.2.4.17.29: As long as the goddess Girijā does not show mercy, there will be no happiness at all; of this there is no doubt.
m.2.4.17.30: Then the sages, with you at their head, went to Śivā's presence, and all of them sought to propitiate Śivā to calm her wrath.
m.2.4.17.31: Again and again they bowed, praising her with many hymns; propitiating her with love, all of them spoke at the behest of the hosts of gods.
m.2.4.17.32: The divine sages said: O Mother of the world, salutation to you. Salutation be to you, Śivā. Salutation to you, Caṇḍikā; and salutation be to you, Kalyāṇī.
m.2.4.17.33: You alone, O Mother, are the primordial Śakti, ever the maker of all creation; you alone are the sustaining power, and you alone bring about dissolution.
m.2.4.17.34: Be gracious, O Sovereign of the gods; bring peace — salutation to you. For the whole of the three worlds is distressed by your anger, O Goddess.
m.2.4.17.35: Brahmā said: Though praised thus by the sages headed by you, the supreme Goddess Śivā, looking at them with an angry glance, said nothing at all.
m.2.4.17.36: Then all the sages, bowing at her lotus feet, again spoke softly to Śivā with devotion, their palms joined.
m.2.4.17.37: Forgive, forgive, O Goddess. Destruction is happening now. Your Lord is standing here—look, look at him, O Ambikā.
m.2.4.17.38: Who are we? And these gods, Viṣṇu, Brahmā and the rest, are your own subjects, standing with palms joined.
m.2.4.17.39: The offence of all must be forgiven, O Supreme Sovereign. All are distressed today; grant them peace, O Śivā.
m.2.4.17.40: Brahmā said: Having spoken thus, all the sages, utterly wretched and agitated, then stood before Caṇḍikā with palms joined.
m.2.4.17.41: Hearing their words in this way, Caṇḍikā became pleased, and with her mind filled with compassion she replied to those sages.
m.2.4.17.42: The Goddess said: If my son comes back to life, then there will be no destruction; and only if he becomes worthy of worship among you all —
m.2.4.17.43: and if he becomes the chief of all today — if you bring that about, then there will be peace in the world; otherwise you will not attain happiness.
m.2.4.17.44: Brahmā said: Thus addressed, all those sages, beginning with you, then came to those gods and reported everything that had happened.
m.2.4.17.45: And all those gods, Śakra and the rest, having heard this, bowed with joined palms and, dejected, reported it to Śaṅkara.
m.2.4.17.46: Having heard the gods, Śiva too spoke thus in turn: It must be done in that way, so that the well-being of all the worlds may come about here.
m.2.4.17.47: Go again towards the north; whoever is met first there, bring back his head and join it to the body.
m.2.4.17.48: Brahmā said: Then they, carrying out Śiva's command, did all that: they brought the body and washed it according to rule,
m.2.4.17.49: and having worshipped it, they then went facing northward. There an elephant with a single tusk was the first to be met.
m.2.4.17.50: Then, taking its head, they firmly joined it there. Having joined it, all the deities bowed then to Śiva, Viṣṇu and Brahmā,
m.2.4.17.51: and bowing, they spoke these words: What you commanded has been done by us. What remains of the task after this is to be done by you, O Bhava.
m.2.4.17.52: Then the attendants and the gods shone forth happily; and having heard that word spoken by Śiva, they carried it out.
m.2.4.17.53: Then Brahmā, Viṣṇu and the gods there, bowing to the Lord Śiva, their own master, who is beyond the guṇas, spoke:
m.2.4.17.54: Since all of us were born from the splendour of you, the great-souled one, may that splendour of yours enter this body through the application of Vedic mantras.
m.2.4.17.55: With this invocation they consecrated excellent water, and, together remembering Śiva, they sprinkled it on that body.
m.2.4.17.56: By the mere touch of that water, the boy, endowed with consciousness, quickly came to life; and by Śiva's will he rose up as if from sleep.
m.2.4.17.57: He was handsome, exceedingly beautiful, elephant-faced, of a fine red hue, with a very cheerful face, radiant, and of charming form.
m.2.4.17.58: O lord of sages, seeing that boy, the son of Śivā, alive, all there rejoiced, and all sorrow came to an end.
m.2.4.17.59: All of them, filled with joy, showed him to the Goddess; seeing her son alive, the Goddess became overjoyed.
m.2.4.17.iti: Thus ends the seventeenth adhyāya, named Gaṇeśa restored to life, in the fourth khaṇḍa, the Kumāra-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.4.18.1: Nārada said: O lord of creatures, when Girijā's son had been revived and seen by the Goddess, what happened there after that? Kindly tell me that now.
m.2.4.18.2: Brahmā said: O lord of sages, hear now what took place when Girijā's son had been revived and seen by the Goddess; I shall tell you of that great festival.
m.2.4.18.3: O sage, Śivā's son, revived, untroubled and transformed with an elephant's head, the elephant-faced one, was then consecrated by the gods and the leaders of the gaṇas.
m.2.4.18.4: Seeing her son, the goddess Śivā, filled with joy, took the boy in her arms and embraced him with delight.
m.2.4.18.5: Then the Mother joyfully and lovingly gave various garments and many ornaments to Gaṇeśa, her own son.
m.2.4.18.6: Having been worshipped by that Goddess and by the Siddhis in many ways, he was then touched by her hand, which removes all sorrow.
m.2.4.18.7: Having worshipped her son and kissed his face, the Goddess, Śaṅkara's consort, then lovingly granted boons, saying: You have been made to suffer just now.
m.2.4.18.8: You are blessed, you have fulfilled your purpose; now be the first to be worshipped among all the immortals, always free from sorrow.
m.2.4.18.9: Since vermilion is now seen on your face, you shall therefore always be worshipped by men with vermilion.
m.2.4.18.10: Whoever performs your worship with flowers or sandal paste, with auspicious fragrance, with delightful food-offerings, with the waving of lights according to rule,
m.2.4.18.11: with betel, with gifts, with circumambulations, and with the rite of prostration —
m.2.4.18.12: for him there will indeed be complete success, no doubt; obstacles of many forms will undoubtedly be destroyed.
m.2.4.18.13: Brahmā said: Having said this, the great goddess Maheśvarī then worshipped her son again with many excellent articles.
m.2.4.18.14: Then, O brahmin, by Girijā's grace, well-being came to the gods and especially to the gaṇas in a mere instant.
m.2.4.18.15: At that moment the devoted gods led by Vāsava (Indra), having joyfully praised Śiva and propitiated that god, brought Gaṇeśa near Śiva.
m.2.4.18.16: Having approached Giriśa, they then placed that boy of Maheśānī on his lap, for the happiness of the three worlds.
m.2.4.18.17: Śiva too, placing his lotus-hand on his head, spoke these words to the gods: This is another son of mine.
m.2.4.18.18: Gaṇeśa too then rose, bowed to Śiva, bowed to Pārvatī, and likewise to me and to Viṣṇu,
m.2.4.18.19: and standing before Nārada and all the sages, he said: My offence should be forgiven; such pride is natural to men.
m.2.4.18.20: I, Śaṅkara and Viṣṇu — we three gods — replied together lovingly, granting him an excellent boon:
m.2.4.18.21: Just as we three chief gods are worshipped in the three worlds, so let this lord of the gaṇas be worshipped by all.
m.2.4.18.22: We are primordial, and he too is primordial and indeed worthy of worship; for Gaṇeśa is the remover of obstacles and the giver of the fruits of all desires.
m.2.4.18.23: Having first performed his worship, men should worship us afterwards. When we all are worshipped but he is not worshipped —
m.2.4.18.24: O gods, if worship of others is performed while he remains unworshipped, then its fruit is lost; there need be no deliberation about this.
m.2.4.18.25: Brahmā said: Having said this, that lord of the gaṇas was reverently worshipped first by Śiva with various articles, and afterwards worshipped by Viṣṇu.
m.2.4.18.26: He was worshipped there by me, Brahmā, and by Pārvatī, and by all the hosts of gods with supreme joy.
m.2.4.18.27: All, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Hara and the rest, gathering together right there, proclaimed Gaṇeśa the chief of all, for the satisfaction of Śivā.
m.2.4.18.28: And again Śiva, with a well-pleased mind, granted him many boons that bring happiness in the world forever.
m.2.4.18.29: Śiva said: O son of the daughter of the lord of mountains, I am pleased, no doubt. When I am pleased the world is pleased; no one can be hostile.
m.2.4.18.30: Since, though in the form of a child, you performed great valour, being Śakti's son and very radiant, therefore be ever happy.
m.2.4.18.31: May your name be foremost in destroying obstacles. Now become the chief of all my gaṇas, worthy of worship.
m.2.4.18.32: Having spoken thus, Śaṅkara at once performed many rites of worship and bestowed many blessings upon him.
m.2.4.18.33: Then the hosts of gods joyfully had song, instrumental music and dance performed, and so too the troupes of apsarases.
m.2.4.18.34: Once more a boon was given to that lord of the gaṇas by the well-pleased Śambhu, the great-souled Śiva himself.
m.2.4.18.35: O lord of the gaṇas, you were born on the fourth lunar day in the month of Bhādra, in the dark fortnight, at the auspicious time of moonrise.
m.2.4.18.36: In the first watch of the night your form became manifest from the noble-minded Girijā; hence your vow is supreme.
m.2.4.18.37: Therefore, beginning from that day, on that very lunar day, the most splendid vow should be joyfully observed, especially for the attainment of all success.
m.2.4.18.38: Until the fourth day comes round again at the end of the year, your vow should be observed by my command.
m.2.4.18.39: Those who desire incomparable and manifold happiness in worldly life should worship you with devotion on the fourth day according to rule.
m.2.4.18.40: Likewise, on the lovely fourth day in the month of Mārgaśīrṣa, having bathed in the morning, one should then announce the vow to the brahmins.
m.2.4.18.41: Worship is to be done with dūrvā grass, and a fast of that kind is to be kept. When a watch (prahara) of the night has passed, a man should bathe and worship duly.
m.2.4.18.42: Having made an image of metal, or likewise one made of coral, or of white arka wood, or fashioned of clay,
m.2.4.18.43: having then installed it there, the man, self-restrained, should worship it here with various divine fragrances, sandal pastes and flowers.
m.2.4.18.44: The dūrvā should be a span long, three-jointed, and without root. With one hundred and one of such grass blades,
m.2.4.18.45: or with just twenty-one, he should worship the installed image, the leader of the gaṇas, with incense, lamps and various food offerings,
m.2.4.18.46: with betel and other fine articles of offering, prostrating and likewise with hymns. Having thus worshipped you there, he should also worship the crescent moon.
m.2.4.18.47: Afterwards, having honoured the brahmins, he should joyfully feed them with sweet foods; and then he himself should eat sweet food, without salt.
m.2.4.18.48: Then afterwards he should conclude all his own observances and remember Gaṇeśa; thus the auspicious vow becomes complete.
m.2.4.18.49: When a full year has thus passed with the vow, the man should then perform the rite of concluding (udyāpana) for the completion of the vow.
m.2.4.18.50: There, by my command, twelve brahmins are to be fed; and having set up a single pot, your image is to be worshipped.
m.2.4.18.51: Having then drawn an eight-petalled lotus on the altar according to Vedic rule, a homa is to be performed here by those free from stinginess with wealth.
m.2.4.18.52: Likewise here he should respectfully feed two women and two young boys, having worshipped them according to rule in front of the image.
m.2.4.18.53: A vigil is to be kept at night; in the morning he should worship again, and then perform the dismissal, praying for the deity's return.
m.2.4.18.54: Blessings are to be received from a boy, as well as the svastivācana; and he should offer a handful of flowers for the completion of the vow.
m.2.4.18.55: Then, having made obeisances, he should carry out the various remaining acts. Whoever performs the vow in this way obtains the fruit he desires.
m.2.4.18.56: Whoever daily, with faith and according to his own ability, performs your worship, O Lord of the gaṇas, for obtaining the fruit of all desires,
m.2.4.18.57: should worship you, the lord of the gaṇas, with vermilion, sandal paste, rice grains and ketaka flowers, and with many other services.
m.2.4.18.58: Those who worship you thus with devotion through various services will always have success, and obstacles will be destroyed here.
m.2.4.18.59: It should be performed by all classes, and especially by women; and by those seeking prosperity, and especially by kings.
m.2.4.18.60: Whatever one desires, that he surely obtains. Therefore you should always be served by one who has desires.
m.2.4.18.61: Brahmā said: Thus was it spoken then by Śiva to the great-souled Gaṇeśa. At that time, by the gods and by all the best of sages,
m.2.4.18.62: having said, so be it, by all of them and by the gaṇas dear to Śambhu, O sage, that lord of the gaṇas was worshipped with the supreme rite.
m.2.4.18.63: Then all those gaṇas bowed to the lord of the gaṇas and respectfully worshipped him especially with various objects.
m.2.4.18.64: O lord of sages, the joy that arose in Girijā is indescribable; how could I describe it even with my four mouths?
m.2.4.18.65: The drums of the gods resounded, the hosts of apsarases danced, the chief gandharvas sang, and a shower of flowers fell.
m.2.4.18.66: When the lord of the gaṇas was installed, the world then attained well-being; there was a great festival, and all sorrow came to an end.
m.2.4.18.67: Śivā and Śiva rejoiced exceedingly, O Nārada; there was abundant great auspiciousness everywhere, bestowing happiness.
m.2.4.18.68: Then all the hosts of gods and likewise the hosts of sages who had assembled there departed by Śiva's command,
m.2.4.18.69: praising Śivā and Gaṇeśa there again and again, and likewise having extolled Śiva, saying, what a battle that was.
m.2.4.18.70: When that goddess Girijā became free of anger, Śiva too, approaching Girijā there as before,
m.2.4.18.71: brought about various joys for the welfare of the worlds — he who, though supreme and delighting in his own Self, is ever ready to accomplish his devotees' purposes.
m.2.4.18.72: Viṣṇu, having taken leave of Śiva, and I, Brahmā, likewise — we two came to our own abodes after devoutly serving Śiva and Śivā.
m.2.4.18.73: And you, venerable Nārada, having sung the glory of Śiva and Śivā and taken leave of them, went to your own abode, O lord of sages.
m.2.4.18.74: All this glory of Śiva and Śivā, blended with the glory of Vighneśa, has been respectfully narrated to you by me, as you asked.
m.2.4.18.75: Whoever, well-restrained, listens to this most auspicious narrative becomes endowed with every auspiciousness, an abode of auspiciousness.
m.2.4.18.76: The sonless gains a son, the poor gains wealth, one seeking a wife gains a wife, one seeking offspring gains offspring.
m.2.4.18.77: The sick gains health, the unfortunate gains good fortune; one regains a lost son or lost wealth, and a woman whose husband is away regains her husband. One overcome by grief becomes free of grief — there is no doubt of this.
m.2.4.18.78: He in whose house this narrative of Gaṇeśa remains is ever endowed with auspiciousness — there is no doubt of this.
m.2.4.18.79: Whoever listens to it attentively at the time of setting out on a journey or on a holy day obtains all he desires by the grace of Śrī Gaṇeśa.
m.2.4.18.iti: Thus ends the eighteenth adhyāya, named Gaṇeśa attains the rank of lord of the gaṇas, in the fourth khaṇḍa, the Kumāra-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.4.19.1: Nārada said: O dear father, I have heard in full the unsurpassed birth of Gaṇeśa, and also his divine deeds, adorned with great valour.
m.2.4.19.2: What happened after that, dear father? Tell me the truth, O lord of the gods: the account rich in the glory of Śivā and Śiva, which gives great bliss.
m.2.4.19.3: Brahmā said: Well asked, O best of sages, by you who are compassionate by nature. Listen with attentive ears; I shall tell it, O best of seers.
m.2.4.19.4: O chief of brahmins, Śivā and Śiva, watching again and again the play of their two sons, felt the highest, great love for them.
m.2.4.19.5: As the parents fondled them there, their happiness grew exceedingly; and the two sons always played a great deal with affection and joy.
m.2.4.19.6: O lord of sages, those two sons, filled with great devotion, rendered service there to their mother and father.
m.2.4.19.7: And the parents' great affection for Ṣaṇmukha and Gaṇeśa grew ever more, like the moon in the bright fortnight.
m.2.4.19.8: Once, O divine seer, Śivā and Śiva were sitting there in private, full of love, absorbed in careful deliberation.
m.2.4.19.9: Śiva and Śivā said: Our two sons have become fit for marriage, so said both of them; how should the auspicious marriage of both our sons be performed?
m.2.4.19.10: Ṣaṇmukha is most dear, and Gaṇeśa just as much. Thus the two, who delight in play, became agitated with worry.
m.2.4.19.11: Learning their parents' intention, the two sons too became eager, by that wish, for marriage, O sage.
m.2.4.19.12: I shall marry first. No, I shall. Again and again, both were constantly engaged in dispute with each other.
m.2.4.19.13: Hearing their words, the divine couple, lords of the worlds, following worldly custom, were greatly astonished.
m.2.4.19.14: What should be done? How should the marriage rite of these two be carried out? Having deliberated thus, they devised a wonderful plan.
m.2.4.19.15: Once, at a suitable time, the parents sat down, called their two sons, and spoke to them there.
m.2.4.19.16: We have earlier made a rule, which will indeed be pleasing to you two; listen, good sons, we tell you with love exactly how it is.
m.2.4.19.17: You are both equal, good sons; no distinction is found here. Therefore a wager that brings good has been set for both sons.
m.2.4.19.18: Whoever goes round the whole earth and returns first, his auspicious marriage shall be performed first.
m.2.4.19.19: Brahmā said: Hearing these words of the two, the mighty reed-born Kārttikeya swiftly left the palace to go round the earth.
m.2.4.19.20: But Gaṇanātha, foremost in intellect, remained right there, reflecting thus again and again in his mind with keen intelligence:
m.2.4.19.21: What is to be done? Where shall I go? The earth cannot possibly be crossed. Having gone a mere krośa, I could go no further.
m.2.4.19.22: How much less could I traverse this earth and win happiness thereby? Having reflected thus — hear what Gaṇeśa did.
m.2.4.19.23: Having bathed in the proper manner and come home himself, he then spoke to his father and mother there.
m.2.4.19.24: Gaṇeśa said: Two seats have been set here for your worship. Please be seated, dear parents; let my wish be fulfilled.
m.2.4.19.25: Brahmā said: Hearing his words, Pārvatī and Parameśvara sat on the seats there to receive his worship.
m.2.4.19.26: Then he worshipped them both and circumambulated them again and again; thus he made seven circuits, and likewise seven prostrations.
m.2.4.19.27: Then Gaṇeśa, ocean of wisdom, with joined palms, having praised at length his parents who were overcome with love, spoke, dear one.
m.2.4.19.28: Gaṇeśa said: O mother, O father, hear my excellent words: my splendid marriage must be performed here quickly.
m.2.4.19.29: Brahmā said: Hearing these words of the great-souled Gaṇeśa, the parents then spoke to him, that treasury of great wisdom.
m.2.4.19.30: Śiva and Śivā said: You should duly go round the earth with its forests. Kumāra has gone; you too go, and come back first.
m.2.4.19.31: Brahmā said: Hearing these words of his parents, Gaṇapati, self-controlled yet stirred with anger, promptly spoke there.
m.2.4.19.32: Gaṇeśa said: O mother, O father, you are regarded as the embodiments of dharma and as wise. O most excellent ones, hear my words properly, in accordance with dharma.
m.2.4.19.33: I have gone round the earth seven times, again and again. How then can you, my parents, speak thus again here?
m.2.4.19.34: Brahmā said: Hearing his words then, the parents, performers of great divine play, adopting the worldly way, said to him there:
m.2.4.19.35: The parents said: When, son, did you traverse the vast earth with its seven continents, bounded by the oceans and filled with great forests?
m.2.4.19.36: Brahmā said: Hearing these words of Śivā and Śaṅkara, O sage, their son Gaṇeśa, treasury of great wisdom, spoke:
m.2.4.19.37: Gaṇeśa said: By worshipping you both, Śivā and Śaṅkara, I have, through my own intelligence, made the circuit of the earth bounded by the ocean.
m.2.4.19.38: Is there not such a statement in the Veda, in the śāstra, or in the compendia of dharma? Is that true, or is it not true?
m.2.4.19.39: Whoever, having worshipped his parents, performs circumambulation of them, for him the fruit arising from circumambulating the earth certainly comes about.
m.2.4.19.40: Whoever leaves his parents at home and goes off to a pilgrimage site, his sin is declared to be just like that of killing them.
m.2.4.19.41: For a son the great holy place is the lotus-feet of his parents; other holy places are attained only after going far away.
m.2.4.19.42: This holy place is near at hand, easily reached, a means of attaining dharma; for a son and for a wife the holy place at home is most excellent.
m.2.4.19.43: What the scriptures and Vedas thus declare constantly—would you two now make that false?
m.2.4.19.44: If this form of yours were to become false here, then the Veda too would become false—there is no doubt.
m.2.4.19.45: Let my auspicious marriage be performed quickly; or else let the Veda and scriptures be declared false.
m.2.4.19.46: Whichever of the two is the very best, having considered it properly, that should be done with effort, O parents, embodiments of dharma.
m.2.4.19.47: Brahmā said: Having spoken thus, Gaṇeśa, son of Pārvatī, of excellent intellect, greatly wise, best of the intelligent, then fell silent.
m.2.4.19.48: Then that couple, lords of the universe, Pārvatī and Śaṅkara, hearing his words thus, became supremely astonished.
m.2.4.19.49: Then Śivā and Śiva, praising their son, discerning in intellect and speaking the truth, the two spoke with affection.
m.2.4.19.50: Śiva and Śivā said: O son, a pure intellect has arisen in you, great-souled one, and the words you have spoken are just so, not otherwise.
m.2.4.19.51: When sorrow arises, he whose intellect excels—his sorrow perishes, as darkness when the sun is seen.
m.2.4.19.52: He who has intellect has strength; for the witless, whence strength? A lion maddened with pride was made to fall into a well by a hare.
m.2.4.19.53: What is declared for a child in the Vedas, scriptures and Purāṇas—all that you have done: the upholding of dharma.
m.2.4.19.54: What you have done rightly—who else here could do it? It is honoured by us both, and it will not now be done otherwise.
m.2.4.19.55: Brahmā said: Having spoken thus and reassured Gaṇeśa, the ocean of intellect, the two set their excellent resolve on performing his marriage.
m.2.4.19.iti: Thus ends the nineteenth adhyāya, named The beginning of the marriage of Gaṇeśa, in the fourth khaṇḍa, the Kumāra-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.4.20.1: Brahmā said: Meanwhile Prajāpati Viśvarūpa, having considered their undertaking there, felt happy and his mind was pleased.
m.2.4.20.2: Prajāpati Viśvarūpa had two daughters of divine form, known as Siddhi and Buddhi, auspicious and lovely in every limb.
m.2.4.20.3: With these two, the lords Girijā and Śaṅkara joyfully had Gaṇeśa's marriage performed as a great festival.
m.2.4.20.4: All the gods, delighted, came together at that wedding, just as Śiva and Girijā had wished.
m.2.4.20.5: And so that Viśvakarman performed the marriage accordingly, and the sages and gods obtained supreme joy.
m.2.4.20.6: Gaṇeśa too then obtained from those two a happiness most hard to attain; O sage, it cannot be described.
m.2.4.20.7: After some time, two divine sons were born to the great-souled Gaṇeśa from his two wives.
m.2.4.20.8: To Siddhi, Gaṇeśa's wife, a son named Kṣema was born; to Buddhi was born a most handsome son called Lābha.
m.2.4.20.9: While the lord of the Gaṇas was thus enjoying inconceivable happiness, the second son then returned, having circled the earth.
m.2.4.20.10: Just then he was met at home by the great-souled Nārada, who said: I speak what is true, not falsehood, neither with deceit nor out of envy.
m.2.4.20.11: What your parents, Śivā and Śaṅkara, have done to you, no other in the world would do; I tell you the truth, the truth.
m.2.4.20.12: Having sent you away, deliberately contriving the pretext of a wrongful circuit, they performed Gaṇeśa's excellent and most splendid marriage.
m.2.4.20.13: Gaṇeśa, his marriage performed, joyfully obtained two wives, the most excellent jewels among maidens, daughters of Prajāpati Viśvarūpa.
m.2.4.20.14: He obtained two sons from his two fair-limbed wives: Kṣema from Siddhi and Lābha from Buddhi, bestowers of every happiness.
m.2.4.20.15: That Gaṇeśa, having obtained two auspicious sons from his two wives, enjoys happiness unceasingly by the will of his mother and father.
m.2.4.20.16: You traversed the earth with its oceans and forests under the sway of that deceitful command, dear one; and this is the fruit that has come of it.
m.2.4.20.17: Consider, dear one, the deceit your parents have practised. When one's own masters do such a thing especially, what will others not do?
m.2.4.20.18: Improper indeed is the act done by those two, your parents. Consider it yourself here; in my mind it is not thought good.
m.2.4.20.19: If a mother gives poison, if a father sells his child, and the king seizes everything, to whom and what can one say?
m.2.4.20.20: A wise man who desires peace, dear one, should not look upon the face of one by whom such an extremely harmful deed has been done.
m.2.4.20.21: Such is the rule of conduct declared in Śruti, in Smṛti and in the śāstras everywhere. I have conveyed it to you today; do as you wish.
m.2.4.20.22: Brahmā said: Having spoken these words thus to the Kumāra, O Nārada, you, who knew the mind of Maheśvara, fell silent.
m.2.4.20.23: Skanda too, blazing with the fire of anger, bowed to his father and then went to Mount Krauñca, though restrained by his parents.
m.2.4.20.24: When we have forbidden you, how can you go today? Though thus prohibited, he said no and went.
m.2.4.20.25: O parents, I must not stay here even a moment, since such deceit has been practised on me, casting love aside.
m.2.4.20.26: Having said this he went there, O sage, and he dwells there even today, removing the sins of all people by the mere sight of him.
m.2.4.20.27: From that day onward, O divine sage, the bachelorhood (kumāratva) of Kārttikeya, Śiva's son, became established.
m.2.4.20.28: His name is auspicious in the world, renowned in the three worlds, holy, removing all sins, and supremely bestowing celibacy.
m.2.4.20.29: On the full moon of Kārttika the gods, the sages with the holy places, and the great ascetics always go to see the Kumāra.
m.2.4.20.30: Whoever has sight of the Lord (Svāmin) on the Kārttika full moon in conjunction with Kṛttikā, all his sin is burnt and he obtains the fruit his heart desires.
m.2.4.20.31: Umā too fell into grief at separation from Skanda, and wretched, she said to her lord: O lord, go there with me.
m.2.4.20.32: For her happiness Śambhu himself went to the mountain with a portion of himself; it became the happiness-bringing Jyotirliṅga named Mallikārjuna.
m.2.4.20.33: Even today Śiva is seen there together with Śivā, fulfiller of the desires of all his devotees, the refuge of the good.
m.2.4.20.34: The Kumāra, knowing that Śiva had come with Śivā, became averse and was eager to go elsewhere from there.
m.2.4.20.35: Entreated by the gods and sages, Kārttika moved away three yojanas and stayed at a place at a distance.
m.2.4.20.36: Śiva and Śivā, anxious with love for their son, go on every festival day to see that Kumāra, O Nārada.
m.2.4.20.37: On the new-moon day Śambhu himself goes there; on the full-moon day Pārvatī surely goes there.
m.2.4.20.38: Whatever account of Kārttika and Gaṇeśa you asked about, O lord of sages, I have narrated it in its excellence.
m.2.4.20.39: A wise man who hears this is freed from all sins and always obtains all his desired, auspicious wishes.
m.2.4.20.40: Whoever reads or has it read, hears or causes it to be heard, obtains all desires; there is no doubt about this.
m.2.4.20.41: A brāhmaṇa who hears this becomes endowed with spiritual splendour, a kṣatriya becomes victorious, a vaiśya becomes rich in wealth, and a śūdra attains excellence.
m.2.4.20.42: A sick man would be freed from disease, one stricken with fear would be freed from fear; a man would not be afflicted by the troubles caused by ghosts, spirits and the like.
m.2.4.20.43: This narrative is sinless, bestows fame, increases happiness, grants long life, leads to heaven, is incomparable, and brings sons, grandsons and the like.
m.2.4.20.44: It also bestows liberation and supreme knowledge of Śiva; it brings delight to Śiva and Śivā and increases devotion to Śiva.
m.2.4.20.45: It should always be listened to by devotees, by the desireless and by those seeking liberation; it grants non-duality with Śiva, is auspicious, and is pervaded by Sadāśiva.
m.2.4.20.iti: Thus ends the twentieth adhyāya, named The marriage of Gaṇeśa, in the fourth khaṇḍa, the Kumāra-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.5.1.1: Nārada said: We have heard the excellent, bliss-giving account of Śambhu as a householder, together with the good stories of the Gaṇas, Skanda and others.
m.2.5.1.2: Now, with great kindness, tell the excellent, supreme account of how Śaṅkara, as Rudra, slew the wicked while sporting.
m.2.5.1.3: How did the mighty Lord burn the three cities of the enemies of the gods simultaneously with a single arrow—with what arrow?
m.2.5.1.4: Narrate all this account of the moon-crested one, the Lord who ever sports through his māyā, which always gives delight to gods and sages.
m.2.5.1.5: Brahmā said: O best of sages, when this was asked in the same way long ago by Vyāsa, Sanatkumāra related it; that very account I now narrate.
m.2.5.1.6: Sanatkumāra said: Listen, O greatly wise Vyāsa, to the account of the moon-crested one—how the destroyer of the universe burned Tripura with a single arrow.
m.2.5.1.7: When the demon Tāraka had been slain by Skanda, Śiva's son, his three sons, the Daityas, were sorely grieved, O lord of sages.
m.2.5.1.8: Tārakākṣa was the eldest, Vidyunmālī the middle one, and Kamalākṣa the youngest; all were always equal in strength.
m.2.5.1.9: They had conquered their senses, were well prepared, self-restrained, truthful, firm-minded, great heroes—and yet hostile to the gods.
m.2.5.1.10: Those three went to a cave of Meru and, giving up all fine and most charming enjoyments, performed a most wondrous austerity.
m.2.5.1.11: In spring, abandoning all desires and the sound of song and instruments along with festivity, those three sons of Tāraka performed austerities.
m.2.5.1.12: In summer, overcoming the sun's glare, they kindled fires in the four directions and, standing in their midst, reverently offered oblations for the sake of success.
m.2.5.1.13: Struck down by the great heat, all of them became utterly faint; in the rains, free of fear, they bore the downpour on their heads.
m.2.5.1.14: In autumn, though hungry, they gave away abundant food—delightful, rich, wholesome, heart-pleasing, excellent fruits and roots—
m.2.5.1.15: —and conquering hunger and thirst through restraint, giving these and drinks of every kind to the hungry, they became like stones.
m.2.5.1.16: In winter those great-souled ones, taking refuge on a mountain, stood without support, facing the four directions, with supreme fortitude.
m.2.5.1.17: In the cold season, their bodies covered with frost, wrapping their bodies in water-soaked linen garments, they stood in the midst of water.
m.2.5.1.18: Then, undaunted, they all gradually increased their austerity; those three excellent sons of his practised penance directed towards Brahmā (Vidhi).
m.2.5.1.19: Undertaking fierce austerity and established in supreme discipline, those foremost Dānavas emaciated their own bodies by penance.
m.2.5.1.20: For a hundred years, placing one foot on the ground and standing there, those very mighty ones performed supreme austerity.
m.2.5.1.21: For a thousand years those most fierce, evil-minded ones lived on air and performed austerity, reaching extreme torment.
m.2.5.1.22: Likewise for a thousand years they stood on their heads, and for a hundred years they stood with arms raised up.
m.2.5.1.23: Thus these Daityas, bent on obstinate resolve, underwent extreme hardship; in this manner those Daityas remained, tireless day and night.
m.2.5.1.24: Thus a long time passed for those sons of Tāraka, who practised good austerity with minds fixed on Brahmā, in a righteous way—such is my view, O sage.
m.2.5.1.25: Then Brahmā, the great preceptor of gods and demons, of great fame, pleased by their austerity, appeared in order to grant a boon.
m.2.5.1.26: Then, together with sages, gods and demons, the grandsire of all beings addressed all of them with these soothing words:
m.2.5.1.27: Brahmā said: I am pleased with your austerity, O great Daityas —O sage. I will give you everything; state the boon you desire.
m.2.5.1.28: For what purpose has this great austerity been performed? Tell me, O enemies of the gods. I am always the giver of the fruit of everyone's austerity, the maker of all.
m.2.5.1.29: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing his words, all of them, with joined palms, bowed to the Grandsire and slowly spoke what was in their minds.
m.2.5.1.30: The demons said: If you are pleased, O lord of gods, and if a boon is to be given by you, grant us invulnerability for all of us from all beings.
m.2.5.1.31: Make us enduring, O lord of the world; may all adversaries such as old age and disease spare us, and may death never approach us anywhere.
m.2.5.1.32: May we all become free from old age and immortal—this is our wish. We shall make all others in the three worlds subject to death.
m.2.5.1.33: What use is vast wealth, what use are splendid cities, other abundant pleasures, or again position and sovereignty—
m.2.5.1.34: when one is surely seized by death within five days? For such a one everything is in vain, O Brahmā—this is indeed our firm conviction.
m.2.5.1.35: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing these words of the ascetic Daityas, Brahmā (Vidhi), remembering his own lord Śiva, Giriśa, replied.
m.2.5.1.36: Brahmā said: There is no complete immortality; therefore desist, O Asuras. Choose another boon, whatever kind pleases you.
m.2.5.1.37: Any creature that is born will surely be slain somewhere, O Asuras; none in the world, on the earth, will be free from old age and immortal—
m.2.5.1.38: except Khaṇḍaparaśu (Śiva), the Death of Death, and likewise Hari; those two are beyond dharma and adharma, unmanifest yet having manifest forms.
m.2.5.1.39: Even if austerity is performed for the oppression of the world, it should be known to have become fruitful; therefore your austerity has been well performed.
m.2.5.1.40: Considering this yourselves with your intellect—that which is impossible for gods and demons, rare or extremely hard to accomplish—evade death by some other means, O sinless ones.
m.2.5.1.41: Therefore, relying on your resolve, choose some cause for your death, through which death, though not directly chosen, may keep it away from each of you separately.
m.2.5.1.42: Sanatkumāra said: Having heard these words of Brahmā, they remained in meditation for a moment; then, having reflected, they spoke to the Grandsire of all the worlds.
m.2.5.1.43: The demons said: O Lord, though we are possessed of valour, we have no dwelling, unassailable by enemies, in which we may live happily.
m.2.5.1.44: Construct and give us three most wondrous cities, rich in every kind of wealth and unassailable by the gods.
m.2.5.1.45: Thus occupying the three cities, we shall roam over this earth, O Lord of the worlds, by your grace, O Teacher of the world.
m.2.5.1.46: Then Tārakākṣa said: Let Viśvakarman make for me a city of gold that is impenetrable even by the gods.
m.2.5.1.47: Kamalākṣa asked for a very great city of silver, and Vidyunmālī, delighted, asked for a great one of hard iron.
m.2.5.1.48: O Brahmā, when these cities stand at one place, at the midday hour of Abhijit, when the moon is positioned in Puṣya,
m.2.5.1.49: when, one above the other, they are invisible in the sky amid sportive clouds, and when the dark clouds named Puṣkarāvarta are raining,
m.2.5.1.50: thus at the end of a thousand years we shall meet one another; these cities will become one — not otherwise.
m.2.5.1.51: Then the god who embodies all the gods, as a marvel to all of us, standing on an impossible chariot furnished with all equipment,
m.2.5.1.52: may pierce our cities with a single inconceivable arrow. Kṛttivāsas, who is ever without enmity towards us,
m.2.5.1.53: and who is worthy of our homage, worship and salutation — how could he burn us? Keeping this in mind, we ask it; such a one is hard to find on earth.
m.2.5.1.54: Sanatkumāra said: Having heard their words, Brahmā, the Grandsire of the worlds and creator, remembering Śiva, said to them, so be it.
m.2.5.1.55: He also gave command to Maya: Make three cities — one of gold, one of silver and one of iron, O Maya.
m.2.5.1.56: Having thus instructed Maya, Brahmā visibly entered heaven, his own abode, while those sons of Tāraka looked on.
m.2.5.1.57: Then the steadfast Maya, by his austerity, made the cities: the golden one for Tārakākṣa, the silver one for Kamalākṣa,
m.2.5.1.58: and the iron one for Vidyunmālī — a threefold, excellent fortress. They are to be known as situated in heaven, in the sky and on earth respectively.
m.2.5.1.59: Having given the three cities to those asuras, Maya himself entered there, intent on their welfare.
m.2.5.1.60: Thus having obtained the three cities and entered them, the sons of Tāraka, of great strength and valour, enjoyed all pleasures.
m.2.5.1.61: The city was crowded with wish-fulfilling trees, thronged with elephants and horses, crowded with various palaces, and covered with networks of jewels;
m.2.5.1.62: adorned with aerial cars resembling the sun's disc, facing every direction, made of rubies and shining like the moon;
m.2.5.1.63: with palaces and divine gate-towers like the peaks of Kailāsa, crowded with celestial women, and with Gandharvas, Siddhas and Cāraṇas;
m.2.5.1.64: with shrines of Rudra in every house, with established fire-sacrifices, and with excellent twice-born versed in the scriptures, ever devoted to the worship of Śiva;
m.2.5.1.65: beautifully adorned with step-wells, wells, ponds and long lakes, and with gardens, groves and trees of the finest qualities, as if fallen from heaven;
m.2.5.1.66: ever adorned with rivers, streams and foremost lotus-lakes, and charming with many trees yielding the fruits of all desires;
m.2.5.1.67: decorated with herds of rutting elephants, splendid horses, chariots of various shapes and palanquins;
m.2.5.1.68: with separate pleasure-grounds set apart according to occasion, and with various separate halls for Vedic study;
m.2.5.1.69: It was never seen, even in mind or word, by sinful men; it is beheld by great souls of virtuous conduct, the meritorious.
m.2.5.1.70: That excellent place was purified everywhere by chaste wives devoted to serving their husbands and averse to wrongful conduct;
m.2.5.1.71: it was filled with heroic, highly fortunate Daityas together with their wives and sons, and with twice-born who knew the true meaning of Śruti and Smṛti and were devoted to their own duty;
m.2.5.1.72: with broad-chested, bull-shouldered warriors, ever skilled in conciliation and in war, some calm and some wrathful, some hunchbacked and some dwarfish;
m.2.5.1.73: resembling blue lotus petals, with dark curly hair, all protected by Maya, well trained and eager for battle.
m.2.5.1.74: That city was filled on all sides and well attended by warriors delighting in excellent battles, whose valour was purified by the worship of Brahmā and Śiva, who resembled the Sun, the Maruts and great Indra, crushers of the gods, exceedingly firm.
m.2.5.1.75: Whatever dharmas are proclaimed in the śāstras, Vedas and Purāṇas, ever dear to Śiva and the gods — those dharmas prevailed there everywhere.
m.2.5.1.76: Thus, having obtained their boons, those Daityas, the sons of Tāraka, dwelt there, relying on Maya, the devotee of Śiva.
m.2.5.1.77: Having driven out the inhabitants of all the three worlds and entered the cities, they ruled a great kingdom, ever devoted to the path of Śiva.
m.2.5.1.78: Then a long time passed, O sage, while they of meritorious deeds dwelt there, ruling a good kingdom as they pleased and to their contentment.
m.2.5.1.iti: Thus ends the first adhyāya, named Tripura described, in the account of the slaying of Tripura, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.5.2.1: Vyāsa said: O son of Brahmā, O greatly wise one, best of speakers, tell me: what happened after that? And how did the gods become happy?
m.2.5.2.2: Brahmā said: Having heard these words of Vyāsa, whose intellect is immeasurable, Sanatkumāra spoke, remembering the lotus-feet of Śiva.
m.2.5.2.3: Sanatkumāra said: Then the gods, Indra and the others, scorched by their (the demons') splendour, having consulted together, all went in distress to Brahmā for refuge.
m.2.5.2.4: All the gods, having bowed with affection to the Grandsire and gathered around him, then, seeing the right moment, made their misery known.
m.2.5.2.5: The gods said: O Creator, all of us dwellers of heaven have surely been tormented by Maya, the lord of Tripura, together with the sons of Tāraka.
m.2.5.2.6: Therefore, O Vidhi, we in distress have come to you for refuge. Devise the means of their destruction, so that we may be happy.
m.2.5.2.7: Sanatkumāra said: Thus addressed by the gods, Vidhi, the maker of the world, smiled and then replied to all of them, whose minds were afraid of Maya.
m.2.5.2.8: Brahmā said: O gods, you need not fear those Dānavas in particular. I shall tell you the means of their destruction; Śarva will bring about your welfare.
m.2.5.2.9: The Daitya was made to prosper by me, so he does not deserve death at my hands. Moreover, merit continues to grow in the city of Tripura.
m.2.5.2.10: So all of you gods, with Vāsava (Indra), entreat Śiva. If the Lord of all is pleased, he will accomplish your task.
m.2.5.2.11: Sanatkumāra said: Having heard Vidhi's words, all the gods with Vāsava, distressed, went to where the bull-bannered one (Śiva) dwells.
m.2.5.2.12: Having bowed with devotion to the Lord of gods, all of them then, with joined palms and bent shoulders, praised Śaṅkara, the benefactor of the worlds.
m.2.5.2.13: The gods said: Salutation to Hiraṇyagarbha, the ordainer of all creation; salutation to you, the maintainer, Viṣṇu, the mighty one.
m.2.5.2.14: Salutation to you in the form of Hara, who brings about the destruction of beings; salutation to you, the attributeless, Śiva of immeasurable radiance.
m.2.5.2.15: Salutation to the one free of states, changeless, pure effulgence, the very self of the great elements, untainted, the great soul.
m.2.5.2.16: Salutation to you, lord of beings, bearer of the great burden, remover of craving, whose form is free of enmity, of abundant radiance.
m.2.5.2.17: Salutation to you, the forest-fire that destroys the great forest of great Daityas, the axe for the trees that are the Daityas, the trident-bearer.
m.2.5.2.18: Salutation to you, O supreme Lord, destroyer of the great Dānavas; salutation to you, husband of Ambikā, O bearer of all weapons.
m.2.5.2.19: Salutation to you, O lord of Pārvatī, O supreme Self, O Maheśvara; salutation to you, the blue-throated Rudra, who has the form of Rudra.
m.2.5.2.20: Salutation to you, knowable through Vedānta; salutation to you, who are beyond all paths; salutation to you, whose nature is the guṇas, possessor of guṇas, yet devoid of guṇas.
m.2.5.2.21: O Mahādeva, salutation to you, the delight of the three worlds; salutation to you as Pradyumna, Aniruddha and Vāsudeva.
m.2.5.2.22: Salutation to you, the god Saṅkarṣaṇa, slayer of Kaṃsa; to you, crusher of Cāṇūra, O Dāmodara, swallower of poison.
m.2.5.2.23: O Hṛṣīkeśa, O Acyuta, O all-pervading one, O Mṛḍa, O Śaṅkara, salutation to you; O Adhokṣaja, O foe of the elephant demon, O enemy of Kāma, O drinker of poison.
m.2.5.2.24: Salutation to the god Nārāyaṇa, to the one devoted to Nārāyaṇa, to the one whose form is Nārāyaṇa, O you who arose from Nārāyaṇa's body.
m.2.5.2.25: Salutation to you, who have all forms, remover of great hells; salutation to you, destroyer of sin, O you whose mount is the bull.
m.2.5.2.26: Salutation to you who are Time in the form of moments and the rest, giver of strength to your devotees, of many forms, form itself, crusher of the host of Daityas.
m.2.5.2.27: Salutation to the god devoted to Brahmins, the benefactor of cows and Brahmins; to you of a thousand forms and a thousand limbs.
m.2.5.2.28: Salutation, O Hara, to you who are the form of dharma, sattva itself, whose self is sattva; salutation to you whose nature is knowable through the Vedas, who love the Vedas.
m.2.5.2.29: Salutation to the one whose form is the Veda; salutations again and again to the speaker of the Veda; to the one reached by the path of right conduct, who himself walks the path of right conduct.
m.2.5.2.30: Salutation to you, Viṣṭaraśravas, the embodiment of truth; salutation to you, lover of truth, truth itself, attainable through truth.
m.2.5.2.31: Salutation to you, the wielder of Māyā; salutation indeed to the lord of Māyā; salutation to you who abide in Brahman, who are Brahmā, and who are born of Brahmā.
m.2.5.2.32: Salutation to you, O Lord, who are austerity itself and who grant fruit through austerity; to the one ever worthy of praise, who is praise itself, whose heart is delighted by praise.
m.2.5.2.33: Salutation to the one pleased by conduct according to the Śruti, who loves the practice of praise, who has a fourfold form, who takes the form of beings born in water and on land.
m.2.5.2.34: O Lord, all the gods and others are your manifestations by virtue of their excellence. Among the gods you are Indra; among the planets you are considered the Sun.
m.2.5.2.35: Among the worlds you are Satyaloka; among rivers you are the celestial river (Gaṅgā); among colours you are white; among lakes you are Lake Mānasa.
m.2.5.2.36: Among mountains you are the father of Girijā (Himavat); among cows you are the wish-granting Kāmadhenu; among oceans the Ocean of Milk; among metals you are gold.
m.2.5.2.37: Among the classes you are the Brahmin; among men you are the king, O Śaṅkara; among the fields of liberation you are Kāśī; among sacred fords you are the king of tīrthas.
m.2.5.2.38: Among all stones you are crystal, O Maheśvara; among flowers you are the lotus; and likewise among mountains, the Himālaya.
m.2.5.2.39: You are the foremost in the dealings of speech; among poets you are Bhārgava (Śukra); among birds you are the Śarabha; among beasts of prey you are esteemed as the lion.
m.2.5.2.40: Among stones you are the Śālagrāma stone, O bull-bannered one; and among all forms worthy of worship, you are indeed the Narmadā liṅga.
m.2.5.2.41: You are Nandīśvara; among animals you are the bull, O Supreme Lord; among the Vedas you are in the form of the Upaniṣads; among sacrificers you are the moon, possessor of cool rays.
m.2.5.2.42: Among the blazing you are fire; among Śaivas you are Acyuta; you are the Bhārata among the Purāṇas, and you are the letter ma among syllables.
m.2.5.2.43: You are the praṇava (Om) among seed-mantras, poison among dreadful things; among the all-pervading you are indeed the sky, and among selves you are the Supreme Self.
m.2.5.2.44: Among the senses you are the mind; among gifts you are the gift of fearlessness; among purifiers you are water, and likewise among life-sustainers, nectar.
m.2.5.2.45: Among gains you are the gain of a son; you are the wind among the swift; among all daily rites you are held to be the sandhyā worship.
m.2.5.2.46: Among sacrifices you are the Aśvamedha; among the ages, the first age; you are Puṣya among all the lunar mansions; you are the new-moon day among lunar days.
m.2.5.2.47: Among all seasons you are spring; among all festivals, the saṅkrānti (sun's transit); you are kuśa among kinds of grass, and the banyan among great trees.
m.2.5.2.48: Among astral yogas you are Vyatīpāta, and among creepers the soma-creeper; among intellects you are the righteous intellect; among friends you are the wife.
m.2.5.2.49: Among pure spiritual practitioners you are prāṇāyāma, O Maheśvara; among all the Jyotirliṅgas you are held to be Viśveśvara.
m.2.5.2.50: Among all kinsmen you are dharma; among the life-stages you are the highest; among all aims you are liberation; among the Rudras, Nīlalohita.
m.2.5.2.51: Among the Ādityas you are Vāsudeva, and Hanumān among monkeys; among sacrifices you are the sacrifice of japa; you are Rāma among weapon-bearers.
m.2.5.2.52: Among the Gandharvas you are Citraratha; among the Vasus, surely Pāvaka; among months you are the intercalary month; among vows you are the fourteenth lunar day.
m.2.5.2.53: You are Airāvata among lordly elephants, held to be Kapila among the Siddhas; you are indeed Ananta among the Nāgas, and Aryaman among the ancestors.
m.2.5.2.54: And you are Time among those who reckon, and Bali among the Daityas. What use is saying more, O Lord of gods? Having pervaded the whole world,
m.2.5.2.55: you indeed stand with a single portion of yourself, both remaining outside and pervading it within.
m.2.5.2.56: Sanatkumāra said: Having thus praised Mahādeva, the bull-bannered, the trident-bearer, the Supreme Lord, with hymns of many kinds, divine, all the gods —
m.2.5.2.57: — distressed, shrewd in their own interest, led by Vāsava, with bowed shoulders and joined palms, spoke in reply of the matter at hand, their own purpose, O sage.
m.2.5.2.58: The gods said: O Mahādeva, O Lord, all the gods along with Vāsava have been defeated by the sons born of Tāraka — by the eldest together with his two brothers.
m.2.5.2.59: The three worlds have been brought under their control; likewise the best of sages and all the perfected ones have been crushed, and the whole world laid waste.
m.2.5.2.60: The dreadful one himself seizes all the sacrificial shares; unrighteousness has been set going by them, and the dharma of the sages has been obstructed.
m.2.5.2.61: The sons of Tāraka are certainly unslayable by any being; all creatures perform all their actions according to their will, O Śaṅkara.
m.2.5.2.62: Before the world is destroyed by the terrible Daityas dwelling in Tripura, let a plan be devised by which the world may be protected.
m.2.5.2.63: Sanatkumāra said: Having heard these words of the heaven-dwellers led by Indra as they spoke, Śiva gave his reply.
m.2.5.2.iti: Thus ends the second adhyāya, named The praise by the gods, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.5.3.1: Śiva said: This overlord of Tripura is indeed virtuous at present. Where merit prevails, such a one should never be killed by the wise.
m.2.5.3.2: O gods, I know the whole great distress of the gods. But those Daityas are very powerful and cannot be killed by gods and asuras.
m.2.5.3.3: All those sons of Tāraka, together with Maya, are meritorious; the slaying of them, of all the city-dwellers, is hard to accomplish.
m.2.5.3.4: How could I, though fierce in battle, knowingly commit treachery against a friend? Great sin in betraying a friend was declared long ago by Svayambhū.
m.2.5.3.5: For the slayer of a brahmin, for the drinker of liquor, for theft and likewise for one who has broken a vow, expiation has been prescribed by the good; for the ungrateful there is no expiation.
m.2.5.3.6: Those Daityas are my devotees; how can they be slain by me, O gods? Let this be considered by you, knowers of dharma, in accordance with dharma.
m.2.5.3.7: They should not be slain so long as they practise devotion to me. Nevertheless, O gods, this matter should be reported to Viṣṇu.
m.2.5.3.8: Sanatkumāra said: Having heard those words thus, all the gods led by Śakra quickly reported them first to Brahmā, O sage.
m.2.5.3.9: Then, placing Brahmā at their head, all the gods together with Vāsava quickly went to Vaikuṇṭha, which is full of splendour.
m.2.5.3.10: Having gone there and seen Hari, the gods, overcome with agitation, bowed and praised him with great devotion, their palms joined.
m.2.5.3.11: Thereafter, as before, they quickly reported the whole cause of their sorrow to that Viṣṇu, the mighty lord.
m.2.5.3.12: Then, having heard of the gods' distress inflicted by the dwellers of Tripura, and knowing their religious observance, Viṣṇu spoke these words.
m.2.5.3.13: Viṣṇu said: This statement is true indeed: where eternal dharma is, there sorrow does not arise, just as darkness does not when the sun is seen.
m.2.5.3.14: Sanatkumāra said: Having heard these words, the gods fell into sorrow and, their lotus-faces withered, spoke again to Viṣṇu.
m.2.5.3.15: The gods said: How then should it be done? How is sorrow to be removed? How may we become happy? How shall we survive?
m.2.5.3.16: How will the dharmas endure while Tripura remains alive? Surely all the dwellers of Tripura are givers of distress to the gods.
m.2.5.3.17: Either let the slaying of Tripura be arranged here by you, or else let an untimely destruction of the gods certainly be brought about.
m.2.5.3.18: Sanatkumāra said: Having spoken thus, those gods, grieving again and again, neither stayed at ease nor went away from the best of gods there.
m.2.5.3.19: Seeing them in such a state, dejected and full of humility, that glorious Nārāyaṇa too pondered thus in his mind:
m.2.5.3.20: What should be done by me, the helper of the gods, in the affairs of the gods? For those Daityas, the sons of Tāraka, are devotees of Śiva.
m.2.5.3.21: Having reflected thus at that time, the mighty Viṣṇu then called to mind the imperishable Yajñas for the sake of the gods' purpose.
m.2.5.3.22: By that mere remembrance of Viṣṇu, those Yajñas came quickly, that very instant, to where the lord of Śrī, Puruṣottama, dwells.
m.2.5.3.23: Then, bowing to Viṣṇu, the lord of sacrifice, the ancient Person, Hari, they praised him with palms joined.
m.2.5.3.24: The Lord, the eternal Acyuta, seeing them, the eternal Yajñas, and looking at the gods along with Indra, then spoke.
m.2.5.3.25: Viṣṇu said: O gods, with this very sacrifice constantly worship the Supreme Lord, for the destruction of the three cities and for the welfare of the three worlds.
m.2.5.3.26: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing the words of Acyuta, the wise god of gods, those gods lovingly bowed and praised the lord of sacrifice.
m.2.5.3.27: Having praised thus, the gods then worshipped the Sacrificial Person by the procedure prescribed for sacrifice, with all rites complete, O sage.
m.2.5.3.28: Then from that sacrificial fire-pit sprang up, by thousands, hosts of bhūtas, huge-bodied, bearing tridents, spears and maces as weapons.
m.2.5.3.29: The gods saw those hosts of bhūtas by thousands, with tridents, spears and maces in hand, armed with staffs, bows and stones,
m.2.5.3.30: furnished with various weapons and wearing various garbs, resembling Kālāgnirudra, like the sun at the time of dissolution.
m.2.5.3.31: Seeing those bhūtas standing before him, the glorious Viṣṇu, lord of sacrifice and upholder of Rudra's command, bowed and spoke to them.
m.2.5.3.32: Viṣṇu said: O bhūtas, ready for the gods' purpose, hear my words: let all of you go at once to Tripura, for you are exceedingly strong.
m.2.5.3.33: Having gone, burnt, split and shattered the three cities of the Daityas, O bhūtas, you should return as you came, for the welfare of the worlds.
m.2.5.3.34: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing the Lord's words, those hosts of bhūtas bowed to that god of gods and went to the three cities of the Daityas.
m.2.5.3.35: Having gone there and entering it, they were at once reduced to ashes in the splendour of Tripura's lord, like moths in fire.
m.2.5.3.36: Those few who survived, bent on flight, came out and quickly arrived, distressed, near Hari.
m.2.5.3.37: Seeing them and hearing that whole incident, the Lord Hari, Puruṣottama, pondered in his mind:
m.2.5.3.38: What is to be done now?—with anguished mind, having perceived that all the immortals, together with Vāsava, were distressed.
m.2.5.3.39: How, having destroyed by force the three cities of those Daityas, shall I accomplish the gods' work?—thus he was overwhelmed with anxiety.
m.2.5.3.40: There is no destruction of the most righteous through hostile magic rites, no doubt—so the Lord himself, who establishes the authority of Vedic conduct, has declared.
m.2.5.3.41: All those Daityas dwelling in Tripura are indeed most righteous; therefore those foremost of Asuras have attained invulnerability, and not otherwise.
m.2.5.3.42: Even having committed a very great sin, they worship Rudra; thereby they are freed from all sins, as a lotus leaf remains untouched by water.
m.2.5.3.43: O gods, through the worship of Rudra all desires are indeed fulfilled; the wealth of manifold enjoyments comes under one's control on earth.
m.2.5.3.44: Therefore the Daityas, devoted to the worship of the liṅga, are enjoyers of that—of manifold wealth here and of liberation too in the hereafter.
m.2.5.3.45: Therefore, having created an obstacle to the dharma of those very Daityas by my own māyā, for the sake of the gods' cause I shall destroy Tripura in a moment.
