m.2.5.3.46: Having reflected thus, the Lord, the Supreme Person, then set about creating an obstacle to the dharma of those enemies of the gods.
m.2.5.3.47: As long as the Vedic dharmas remain, as long as there is worship of Śaṅkara, and as long as there are pure observances, so long there can be no destruction of them.
m.2.5.3.48: Therefore it must be done thus: the Vedic dharma should then depart from them; the Daityas will abandon the worship of the liṅga—there is no doubt.
m.2.5.3.49: Having thus resolved, Viṣṇu then devised, for obstructing the dharma of those Daityas, a means: the refutation of the Veda (śruti).
m.2.5.3.50: Then Viṣṇu, the helper of the gods, commissioned by Śiva himself at Śiva's command for the protection of the three worlds, spoke to the gods.
m.2.5.3.51: Viṣṇu said: O gods, all of you go to your own abodes, surely. I shall accomplish the gods' task according to my understanding; there is no doubt.
m.2.5.3.52: With great effort I shall certainly make them averse to Rudra; and knowing them to be bereft of devotion to him, I shall reduce them to ashes.
m.2.5.3.53: Sanatkumāra said: O sage, those immortals, reassured, placing his command on their heads, went to their respective abodes, trusting and supremely delighted.
m.2.5.3.54: Then Viṣṇu did what was supremely beneficial for the gods' sake; let that very account, destroyer of all sins, be heard properly.
m.2.5.3.iti: Thus ends the third adhyāya, named The bhūtas and the dharma of Tripura, in the account of the slaying of Tripura, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.5.4.1: Sanatkumāra said: And Acyuta, of great splendour, created a man born from his own self, a single being made of illusion (māyā), for the purpose of obstructing their dharma.
m.2.5.4.2: He was shaven-headed, in soiled clothes, furnished with a bowl, holding a broom in his hand and moving it at every step;
m.2.5.4.3: likewise with a hand holding a cloth, always placed at his mouth, a sage uttering dharma in a faltering voice.
m.2.5.4.4: Having bowed to that Viṣṇu, he then stood before him, and there, with joined palms, he spoke these words to Hari.
m.2.5.4.5: O destroyer of foes, Acyuta, worshipful one, what shall I do? Command me that. What are my names, O God? And tell me also my abode, O Lord.
m.2.5.4.6: Having heard his auspicious words thus, Lord Viṣṇu, pleased at heart, spoke these words.
m.2.5.4.7: Viṣṇu said: Learn for what purpose you have been created; I shall tell you. O you born of my body, O greatly wise one, you are of my own form, no doubt.
m.2.5.4.8: Born from my body, you ought to do my work. You are mine and will always be worthy of worship, no doubt.
m.2.5.4.9: Your name shall be Arihan; other names are not auspicious. I shall tell you your abode later; now listen attentively to the matter at hand.
m.2.5.4.10: O illusionist, a treatise made of illusion, of sixteen thousand verses, opposed to śruti and smṛti, devoid of varṇa and āśrama,
m.2.5.4.11: a treatise in Apabhraṃśa, consisting likewise of the doctrine of karma — compose it with effort; its spread will come about.
m.2.5.4.12: I grant you the capacity for its composition; it will come about. And varied illusion will quickly be under your control.
m.2.5.4.13: Having heard those words of Hari, the Supreme Self, the illusionist bowed and replied to Janārdana.
m.2.5.4.14: The shaven-headed ascetic said: Whatever I must do, O God, command that quickly, O Lord. By your command all my work will be fruitful.
m.2.5.4.15: Sanatkumāra said: Having said this, Viṣṇu taught him the treatise made of illusion, which holds that the experience of heaven and hell is here alone and not otherwise.
m.2.5.4.16: Viṣṇu, remembering Śiva's lotus feet, spoke to him again: All these demons dwelling in Tripura are to be deluded.
m.2.5.4.17: They must surely be initiated and taught with effort. By my command no sin will attach to you, O great-minded one.
m.2.5.4.18: There the dharmas of śruti and smṛti shine forth, no doubt. By this lore they must all certainly be shattered, O ascetic.
m.2.5.4.19: O shaven one, you should go for the destruction of the dwellers of Tripura. Proclaiming the dharma of darkness (tamas), destroy the three cities.
m.2.5.4.20: And then, going again from there, you must remain in the desert region, O mighty one, according to your own dharma, until Kali arrives.
m.2.5.4.21: When that age has begun, let your own dharma be proclaimed; and it must be carried on by you again through disciples and disciples' disciples.
m.2.5.4.22: By my command your dharma will certainly spread. Ever intent on my permission, you will attain my state.
m.2.5.4.23: Thus the command was then given by the mighty Viṣṇu; and Hari, following at heart the command of the God of gods, vanished.
m.2.5.4.24: Then that shaven one, obeying Hari's command, created four disciples resembling his own form, and then himself taught them the treatise made of illusion.
m.2.5.4.25: As he himself was, so were those four splendid shaven ones; having bowed to Hari, the Supreme Self, they stood there.
m.2.5.4.26: And Hari too, supremely pleased, the upholder of Śiva's command, then himself spoke there to those four sages.
m.2.5.4.27: As your teacher is, so shall you be by my command. You are blessed; you will attain a good state here, no doubt.
m.2.5.4.28: Then those four shaven ones, adopting a heretical dharma, holding bowls in their hands and wearing cloths over their mouths,
m.2.5.4.29: wearing only soiled garments, sparing of speech, and saying with great delight, may you have the gain of dharma (dharmo lābhaḥ), the supreme truth,
m.2.5.4.30: carrying brooms made of strips of cloth, and moving very slowly out of fear of harming living beings, indeed;
m.2.5.4.31: all of them then, full of joy, bowed again to the divine Lord there, O sage, and stood before him.
m.2.5.4.32: Then Hari took them by the hand and entrusted them to the teacher, and with great affection declared their names specifically:
m.2.5.4.33: As you are, so too these are mine, no doubt. And your name, of the primal form — because you are worshipful, you are called Pūjya.
m.2.5.4.34: Ṛṣi, Yati, Ākīrya and Upādhyāya — let these names too become well known for you.
m.2.5.4.35: And my auspicious name too should be taken up by you: Arihan — that name, destroyer of sin, is to be meditated upon.
m.2.5.4.36: And you must do work that brings happiness to the world; for those who act in accord with the world there will be the highest state.
m.2.5.4.37: Sanatkumāra said: Then the illusionist, with his disciples, bowed to him, the doer of Śiva's will, and at once went himself to Tripura, O sage.
m.2.5.4.38: Having swiftly entered that city, the self-controlled sage, urged on by that great master of illusion Viṣṇu, then worked his illusion.
m.2.5.4.39: Taking up residence with his disciples in a grove near the city, he then set in motion an illusion that could delude even the masters of illusion.
m.2.5.4.40: But because of the power of their worship of Śiva, O sage, his illusion did not quickly take effect in Tripura, and the ascetic then became dejected.
m.2.5.4.41: Then he remembered Viṣṇu and praised him much in his heart, his enthusiasm lost, his mind confused, with a heart that was distressed.
m.2.5.4.42: Remembered by him, Viṣṇu quickly remembered Śaṅkara in his heart; having received his command mentally, he swiftly called Nārada to mind.
m.2.5.4.43: As soon as Viṣṇu remembered him, Nārada appeared; having bowed and praised, he then stood before him with joined palms.
m.2.5.4.44: Then Viṣṇu, foremost of the wise, ever devoted to the welfare of the worlds and accomplishing the gods' work, spoke to Nārada.
m.2.5.4.45: By Śiva's command it is said, dear one: go quickly to Tripura. The sage has gone there with his disciples to delude its inhabitants.
m.2.5.4.46: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing his words, Nārada, best of sages, went quickly to where that sage, foremost of illusionists, was.
m.2.5.4.47: Nārada too, likewise wielding illusion by the command of the lord of illusion, entered that city and was initiated by that illusionist.
m.2.5.4.48: Then Nārada went into the presence of the lord of Tripura and, after inquiring about his welfare and so forth, reported everything to the king.
m.2.5.4.49: Nārada said: A certain ascetic has come here, devoted to dharma, truly excelling in all knowledge and endowed with supreme Vedic learning.
m.2.5.4.50: Though we have seen many dharmas, none is equal to this. Having seen this eternal dharma here, we have been duly initiated.
m.2.5.4.51: If you have a desire for that dharma, O best of Daityas, then, great king, you too should take initiation into that dharma.
m.2.5.4.52: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing his words, pregnant with great meaning, the lord of the Daityas was amazed at heart and, deluded, spoke there.
m.2.5.4.53: Since Nārada has been initiated, we too shall receive initiation. Knowing this, he went there himself.
m.2.5.4.54: Then, seeing his form and thus deluded by illusion, he bowed to that great soul and spoke these words to him.
m.2.5.4.55: The lord of Tripura said: You must give me initiation, O sage of pure intent. I shall become your disciple—truly, truly, without doubt.
m.2.5.4.56: Hearing these sincere words of the Daitya king, that ancient sage replied with great care.
m.2.5.4.57: If my command is to be carried out, O best of Daityas, then I shall give initiation—not otherwise, even with countless efforts.
m.2.5.4.58: Hearing these words, the king became wholly possessed by illusion and, with joined palms, quickly spoke to that ascetic.
m.2.5.4.59: The demon said: Whatever command you give, it shall be done just so and not otherwise. I will not transgress your command—truly, truly, without doubt.
m.2.5.4.60: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing then these words of the lord of Tripura, the best of sages removed the cloth from his mouth and spoke.
m.2.5.4.61: Take this initiation, O lord of Daityas, the very highest among all dharmas, by the rite of which you will attain fulfilment.
m.2.5.4.62: Having said this, that illusionist swiftly gave the Daitya king the initiation prescribed by his own dharma, according to rule.
m.2.5.4.63: When the Daitya king had been initiated together with his brothers, O sage, all the inhabitants of Tripura there became initiated.
m.2.5.4.64: Then, O sage, the whole of Tripura was quickly pervaded by the disciples and disciples' disciples of that great illusionist sage.
m.2.5.4.iti: Thus ends the fourth adhyāya, named The rite of initiation in Tripura, in the dialogue of Sanatkumāra and Pārāśarya, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.5.5.1: Vyāsa said: When the king of the Daityas had been initiated and deluded by that deceiver, what did the deceiver say then, and what did that lord of the Daityas do?
m.2.5.5.2: Sanatkumāra said: Having given initiation to him, the ascetic Arihan, whose lotus feet were served by disciples such as Nārada, spoke to the king of the Daityas.
m.2.5.5.3: Arihan said: Listen, O lord of the Daityas, to my words, filled with true knowledge, the whole essence of Vedānta, a secret supreme and most excellent.
m.2.5.5.4: Worldly existence is beginningless and self-established, devoid of a creator and of action; it arises of itself and dissolves of itself.
m.2.5.5.5: From Brahmā down to a blade of grass, whatever is bound to a body—there the self alone is the one lord; there is no second ruler over it.
m.2.5.5.6: As for the names Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Rudra, these names belong to embodied beings, just as for us the name Arihan and the like is spoken.
m.2.5.5.7: Just as the body of us and others dissolves in its own time, so too the body of all from Brahmā down to the mosquito dissolves in its own time.
m.2.5.5.8: When this body is examined, nothing is greater anywhere in one than another; food, sexual union, sleep and fear are the same everywhere.
m.2.5.5.9: Every embodied being, when hungry and obtaining its measure of food, attains the same satisfaction, neither greater nor otherwise.
m.2.5.5.10: Just as we, when thirsty, become free of thirst on joyfully drinking a drink, so too do others who are thirsty; there is no difference, lesser or greater.
m.2.5.5.11: Let there be thousands of women, abodes of form and loveliness; yet at the time of love-making only one is enjoyed here.
m.2.5.5.12: Let there be hundreds of excellent horses, let there be many of many kinds; yet for riding only one serves a person, not a second.
m.2.5.5.13: The happiness that arises in sleep for those who lie on couches—that same happiness comes through sleep to beings who lie on the ground.
m.2.5.5.14: Just as embodied beings like us fear death, so do all from Brahmā down to the worm fear death.
m.2.5.5.15: If it is considered with the intellect, all embodied beings are equal. Having determined this, no one should harm anyone anywhere.
m.2.5.5.16: Nowhere on the face of the earth is there a dharma equal to compassion for living beings; therefore people should practise compassion for living beings with every effort.
m.2.5.5.17: When one living being is protected, the three worlds are protected; when one is killed, they are likewise killed. Therefore one should protect and not kill.
m.2.5.5.18: Non-violence is the highest dharma; sin is the tormenting of oneself; liberation is independence from others; heaven is eating what one desires.
m.2.5.5.19: This has been declared with certainty by earlier sages as true authority; therefore men who fear hell should not commit violence.
m.2.5.5.20: In the three worlds with their moving and unmoving beings there is no sin like violence. The violent man goes to hell; the non-violent goes to heaven.
m.2.5.5.21: There are many gifts—what use are they, yielding trifling fruit? Here there is not even one supreme gift equal to granting freedom from fear.
m.2.5.5.22: Here four gifts have been declared by the great sages, after considering various scriptures, for welfare in this world and the next.
m.2.5.5.23: Freedom from fear should be given to the frightened, medicine likewise to the sick; knowledge should be given to seekers of knowledge, and food to one afflicted by hunger.
m.2.5.5.24: Whatever many gifts have been spoken of here by the sages, they are not worth a sixteenth part of the gift of fearlessness to living beings.
m.2.5.5.25: Indeed the power of gems, mantras and herbs is of inconceivable efficacy; it should be practised with effort for acquiring fame and wealth.
m.2.5.5.26: Having acquired wealth abundantly, the twelve āyatanas should be worshipped all around; what is the use of worshipping others here?
m.2.5.5.27: The group of five organs of action, the five organs of perception, mind and intellect—these are here declared to be the auspicious twelve āyatanas.
m.2.5.5.28: Heaven and hell for living beings are right here, not anywhere else. Happiness is called heaven, and suffering is indeed hell.
m.2.5.5.29: The giving up of the body while pleasures are being enjoyed—this alone should be known by thinkers on reality as the supreme liberation.
m.2.5.5.30: When the afflictions together with their latent impressions are certainly uprooted, the cessation of ignorance—this should be known by thinkers on reality as liberation.
m.2.5.5.31: This scriptural text is declared authoritative by those who expound the Veda: One should not harm any beings. No other text that promotes violence is authoritative.
m.2.5.5.32: The text agniṣṭomīyam, prescribing the victim, is misleading, upheld by the wicked here; for the wise it is no authority, since it causes the slaughter of animals.
m.2.5.5.33: Having cut down trees, killed animals, made a mire of blood, and burnt sesame, ghee and the like in the fire—how strange that heaven is desired thereby.
m.2.5.5.34: Having thus declared his own doctrine to the lord of Tripura and made all the citizens hear it, the ascetic spoke again with earnestness—
m.2.5.5.35: —then he taught dharmas laid down in the Buddhist scriptures, outside the Veda, which produce conviction through visible results and serve solely to accomplish bodily pleasure.
m.2.5.5.36: What is declared by śruti thus—'bliss is the form of Brahman'—should be understood here exactly so; the notion of multiplicity is false.
m.2.5.5.37: As long as this body is healthy, as long as the senses are not impaired, as long as old age is far off, so long should one secure pleasure.
m.2.5.5.38: In ill health, in impairment of the senses, and in old age, whence can there be pleasure? Therefore those who seek happiness should give even their body to supplicants.
m.2.5.5.39: He whose life is not spent in gratifying the wishes of those who beg—by him this earth is burdened, not by oceans, mountains and trees.
m.2.5.5.40: The body passes away swiftly; accumulations end in decline. Knowing this, the wise one should secure bodily pleasure.
m.2.5.5.41: This body is a morning meal for dogs, crows and worms, and that body ends in ashes: this truth is recited in the Veda.
m.2.5.5.42: This distinction of caste is imagined in the worlds for nothing. Since humanity is common to all, who is low and who is high?
m.2.5.5.43: This is the creation beginning with Brahmā, so the elders declare. Two sons were born to him, renowned as Dakṣa and Marīci.
m.2.5.5.44: By Kaśyapa, son of Marīci, thirteen fair-eyed daughters of Dakṣa were married, indeed by the lawful path.
m.2.5.5.45: And now, by present-day mortals of little intellect and strength, this deliberation — this woman may be approached, that one may not — is made in vain.
m.2.5.5.46: The four classes, born from the mouth, arms and thighs of the Creator, arose together; this notion devised by the ancients does not hold up on examination.
m.2.5.5.47: If ever four sons were born in a single body, or from a single father, how could they obtain different classes?
m.2.5.5.48: Therefore this division into class and non-class does not appear true. Hence no one should anywhere consider distinction among human beings.
m.2.5.5.49: Sanatkumāra said: Having spoken thus to the lord of the Daityas and to the citizens, O sage, that ascetic, with his disciples, zealously destroyed the Vedic dharmas.
m.2.5.5.50: He undermined the great dharma of women, centred on devotion to the husband, and likewise the self-control of all men.
m.2.5.5.51: He undermined especially the duties toward the gods, and likewise the rites of śrāddha, the duties of sacrifice, vows and the like, and particularly śrāddha at sacred fords;
m.2.5.5.52: especially the worship of Śiva preceded by the adoration of the liṅga, and the worship of Viṣṇu, Sūrya, Gaṇeśa and others performed according to rule;
m.2.5.5.53: and all bathing, giving and the like, particularly at the time of the festival days — all this that ascetic, the deluder, foremost of illusionists, demolished.
m.2.5.5.54: What need of saying much, O best of brahmins? In Tripura, by that deluder, whatever Vedic dharmas there were — all of them were driven far away.
m.2.5.5.55: All the women of Tripura, deluded and taking refuge in the ascetic's doctrine, abandoned the excellent disposition of serving their husbands.
m.2.5.5.56: Having practised the art of attraction and also that consisting of subjugation, the men, deluded, made them fruitful with others' wives.
m.2.5.5.57: The women moving in the inner apartments, likewise the young princes, the citizens and the city's women too — all were deluded by them.
m.2.5.5.58: Thus, when all the citizens had become wholly averse to their own dharmas, adharma flourished exceedingly.
m.2.5.5.59: And, O lord, the Māyā of Viṣṇu, god of gods, by his command — and Alakṣmī herself by his order — went to Tripura.
m.2.5.5.60: The Lakṣmī whom they had obtained through austerity as a boon from the lord of gods abandoned them and went out, at the order of lord Brahmā.
m.2.5.5.61: Having given them such delusion of mind, fashioned by the Māyā of Viṣṇu, that Nārada at once became one whose purpose was accomplished.
m.2.5.5.62: Nārada too had taken the same form as the deluder; even so he was not perverted, owing to the grace of the Supreme Lord.
m.2.5.5.63: The king of the Daityas too, O sage, together with his two brothers and with Maya, had his power blunted there, by the will of Śiva.
m.2.5.5.iti: Thus ends the fifth adhyāya, named The deluding of Tripura, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.5.6.1: Vyāsa said: When that lord of the Daityas, together with the citizens and his brothers, had been thus deluded, what happened then, O Sanatkumāra? Tell it all, O lord.
m.2.5.6.2: Sanatkumāra said: When Tripura had become like this, the Daitya having abandoned the worship of Śiva, the entire dharma of women destroyed, and wicked conduct established,
m.2.5.6.3: Hari, the lord of Lakṣmī, as though his purpose were accomplished, went with the gods to Kailāsa to report that conduct to the lord of Umā.
m.2.5.6.4: Having stationed himself near it with the gods, that lord of Ramā, and then Brahmā too, with supreme and intense concentration—
m.2.5.6.5: having reached the Omniscient One with the mind, then Hari, the Supreme Person, together with Brahmā, praised Śaṅkara with pleasing words.
m.2.5.6.6: Viṣṇu said: Salutation to you, the god Maheśvara, the Supreme Self, Nārāyaṇa, Rudra, Brahman, whose form is Brahman.
m.2.5.6.7: Having done so and prostrated like a staff before Mahādeva, he recited the Rudra mantra that originates from Dakṣiṇāmūrti.
m.2.5.6.8: Standing in water, the lord, with his mind absorbed in him, recited it one and a half crore times, remembering in his mind Śambhu, his own lord, the Supreme Lord.
m.2.5.6.9: Meanwhile, then, all the gods, with their minds fixed on him, praised Maheśvara.
m.2.5.6.10: The gods said: Salutation to you, the Self of all, Śaṅkara, remover of affliction, Rudra, the blue-throated one, whose form is consciousness, the wise one.
m.2.5.6.11: You indeed are always our refuge, the remover of all calamities; you alone are always to be worshipped by all souls, O slayer of the gods' enemies.
m.2.5.6.12: You are the beginning and you are beginningless, self-blissful, the imperishable lord, the direct creator of Prakṛti and of Puruṣa too, the lord of the world.
m.2.5.6.13: You alone are the maker of the worlds, the sustainer, and you alone the destroyer, becoming Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Hara through the guṇas of rajas, sattva and tamas.
m.2.5.6.14: You are the deliverer in this world, the imperishable ruler of all, the giver of boons, consisting of speech, the one to be expressed, yet free from the distinction of expressed and expresser.
m.2.5.6.15: You, the Lord, are to be entreated for liberation by yogins who are the best knowers of yoga; you indeed dwell in the cavity of the heart-lotus of yogins.
m.2.5.6.16: The Vedas and the virtuous declare you to be of the nature of the Supreme Brahman; they now call you the Reality, the mass of radiance, higher than the highest.
m.2.5.6.17: That which they call the Supreme Self in this world, O lord, is you alone, O Śarva, O Self of all, O lord of the three worlds, O Bhava.
m.2.5.6.18: All that is seen, heard, praised and known is you, O guru of the world; they call you smaller than the atom and greater even than the great.
m.2.5.6.19: That which has hands and feet everywhere, eyes, heads and faces everywhere, ears and noses everywhere—you I salute on every side.
m.2.5.6.20: O all-pervading one, you the omniscient, lord of all, unveiled, of universal form, the odd-eyed one—you I salute on every side.
m.2.5.6.21: You, the lord of all, overseer of worldly existence, the Truth, the auspicious, the unsurpassed, radiant like ten million suns—you I salute on every side.
m.2.5.6.22: You, the god of the universe, without beginning or end, comprising the thirty-six principles, having no lord above you, and the impeller of all—you I salute on every side.
m.2.5.6.23: You, the impeller of Prakṛti, the great-grandsire of all, the Lord whose body is everything—you I salute on every side.
m.2.5.6.24: Thus do the Śrutis, and those who know the essence of the Śrutis, describe you—the boon-giver, the abode of all, the self-born, the knower of the essence of the Śrutis.
m.2.5.6.25: Whatever, invisible to us and manifold, has been made by you in the world is you; the gods, Asuras, Brāhmaṇas and others too, the stationary and the moving, resort to you alone.
m.2.5.6.26: Protect us gods, who have no other refuge, O Śambhu, beloved of the gods, who are nearly ruined because of Tripura, by slaying the Asuras in an instant.
m.2.5.6.27: They are now deluded by your māyā, O Supreme Lord; by the device declared by Viṣṇu they have been made to forsake dharma, O lord.
m.2.5.6.28: Those Daityas, having wholly abandoned all dharma and taken refuge in the Buddhist scriptures, have become so by the power of our good fortune, O you who love your devotees.
m.2.5.6.29: You are always the accomplisher of the gods' tasks, O giver of refuge; we have taken refuge in you—do as you wish.
m.2.5.6.30: Sanatkumāra said: Having thus praised Maheśāna, the gods stood before him, with palms joined, dejected, their bodies bowed down.
m.2.5.6.31: Thus praised by Indra and the other gods, and by Viṣṇu's japa, the Lord of all came there, delighted, mounted on his bull.
m.2.5.6.32: Having descended from Nandin and embraced Viṣṇu, with a gracious mind, his hand supported by Nandin, he looked there upon all with a kindly glance.
m.2.5.6.33: Then Hara, the lord of Pārvatī, pleased, looking upon the gods and Hari with a compassionate gaze, spoke in a deep voice.
m.2.5.6.34: Śiva said: I have now understood this task of the gods, O lord of the gods, and also the power of Viṣṇu's māyā and of the wise Nārada.
m.2.5.6.35: I shall bring about the destruction of the three cities of those Daityas devoted to adharma, O best of gods; there is no doubt.
m.2.5.6.36: But those great Daityas are my devotees, firm of mind. Should they then be slain by me myself, when they have abandoned the highest dharma only through a ruse?
m.2.5.6.37: Let Viṣṇu or someone else slay them, since all the Daityas dwelling in Tripura have been made to abandon dharma and are devoid of devotion to me.
m.2.5.6.38: Hearing these words of Śambhu, all the heaven-dwellers became downcast, and Hari too, O lord of sages.
m.2.5.6.39: Seeing the gods and Viṣṇu dispirited, Brahmā the ordainer, maker of the world, with joined palms before Śambhu, spoke these words.
m.2.5.6.40: Brahmā said: There is no sin whatsoever for you, since you are the foremost knower of yoga, the Supreme Lord, the Supreme Brahman, ever the protector of gods and sages.
m.2.5.6.41: By your command alone they are deluded; you are the one who impels them. Though they have abandoned their own dharma and your worship, still they cannot be slain by others.
m.2.5.6.42: Therefore, O Mahādeva, protector of the lives of gods and sages, the barbarian (mleccha) races must be slain by you for the protection of the good.
m.2.5.6.43: For a king who does this, that sin does not exist according to dharma, and so for you too. Therefore a king should protect the twice-born and the good, and should clear away the thorns.
m.2.5.6.44: Thus should a king act, here and elsewhere, if he desires his own kingdom. Yours is the lordship of all worlds; therefore protect us without delay.
m.2.5.6.45: The chief sages and lords, likewise the sacrifices, the Vedas, the scriptures and all the rest, are your subjects, O lord of the gods of gods; and I and Viṣṇu too, certainly.
m.2.5.6.46: You are the sovereign over the gods, the emperor, the lord of all, O Lord. This entire world, beginning with Hari, is your retinue alone.
m.2.5.6.47: Hari is your crown prince, O Unborn One; I, Brahmā, am your royal priest; Śakra is the executor of royal affairs, the guardian of your command.
m.2.5.6.48: The other gods too, O lord of all, governed by your command, always perform their respective duties. This is true, true; there is no doubt.
m.2.5.6.49: Sanatkumāra said: Having heard this speech of Brahmā, the Supreme Lord Śaṅkara, protector of the gods, pleased at heart, replied to Vidhi (Brahmā).
m.2.5.6.50: Śiva said: O Brahmā, if I am proclaimed king of the gods and emperor, I have none of the corresponding equipment which I, as lord, might take up here.
m.2.5.6.51: There is no great divine chariot of that sort, together with a charioteer, nor bow, arrows and the like that bring victory in battle,
m.2.5.6.52: mounting which, taking up bow and arrows and fixing my mind, I would slay the demons in battle, however powerful they may be.
m.2.5.6.53: Sanatkumāra said: Now the gods, with Brahmā, with Indra and Upendra, overjoyed on hearing the Lord's words, bowed and spoke to Maheśvara.
m.2.5.6.54: The gods said: O lord of the gods, O Maheśvara, we shall become that equipment of yours—the chariot and the rest—ready for battle, O Master.
m.2.5.6.55: Having said this, all the gods together, understanding Śiva's wish, pleased and with joined palms, spoke individually.
m.2.5.6.iti: Thus ends the sixth adhyāya, named The praise of Śiva, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.5.7.1: Sanatkumāra said: Having heard these words of all the gods and the others, Hara, the refuge of all and loving to his devotees, accepted them with great delight.
m.2.5.7.2: Meanwhile, O sage, the goddess Śivā, accompanied by her two sons, came to the place where Hara was, attended by the gods.
m.2.5.7.3: Then, seeing Śivā arrived, all of them, Viṣṇu and the others, quickly bowed down, very humble, astonished, their agitation gone.
m.2.5.7.4: O sage, all of them uttered the good and auspicious word, victory, and then remained silent, not knowing the reason for her coming.
m.2.5.7.5: Then the goddess, praised by all the gods and full of wondrous playfulness, spoke lovingly to her lord, who is skilled in manifold sports.
m.2.5.7.6: The Goddess said: O mighty one, best among those who have sons, look at your son, the six-faced one, playing, shining like the sun, adorned with excellent ornaments.
m.2.5.7.7: Sanatkumāra said: Thus addressed with these words by the Mother of the worlds, Śiva, the Lord, could not be sated as he drank the nectar of Skanda's face.
m.2.5.7.8: Maheśvara did not remember the gods who had come, oppressed by his own splendour; embracing Skanda and smelling his head, he rejoiced greatly.
m.2.5.7.9: Then the Mother of the world, skilled in many sports, having conferred with the Lord right there and stayed a little while, rose up.
m.2.5.7.10: Then Śambhu, with Nandin, together with the six-faced one and with her, the daughter of the king of mountains, playfully entered the palace, being saluted by all the gods.
m.2.5.7.11: Then all those gods, O sage, greatly perturbed and dejected, stood beside the door of the wise God of gods.
m.2.5.7.12: What is to be done? Where shall we go? Who will give us happiness? What now, what now? Thus it came about, and they cried, alas, we are ruined!
m.2.5.7.13: Looking at one another, Śakra and the others became extremely distressed; cursing their own fate, they spoke broken words.
m.2.5.7.14: Some gods said, we here are sinners; others, we are unfortunate; and still others, those lords of the Daityas are fortunate.
m.2.5.7.15: Just then, hearing their many cries, the greatly powerful Kumbhodara struck the gods with his staff.
m.2.5.7.16: Seized with fear, the gods fled crying alas, alas; others, the sages, fell down, and there was utter distress.
m.2.5.7.17: Indra, extremely shaken, sank to the ground on his knees; other divine sages, greatly distressed, fell on the earth.
m.2.5.7.18: All the sages and gods, equally agitated, came together and gathered near Vidhi (Brahmā) and Hari, whose minds were friendly to them.
m.2.5.7.19: Ah, this is the power of fate! So then all the sages, Kaśyapa and the others, said to Hari, the remover of the world's fear.
m.2.5.7.20: Other Brahmins said, through misfortune the task has not been accomplished; others, greatly astonished, said, why has this obstacle arisen?
m.2.5.7.21: Hearing these words spoken by Kaśyapa and the others, O sage, Hari, comforting the sages and gods, took up speech.
m.2.5.7.22: Viṣṇu said: O gods and all sages, listen attentively to my words. Why have you fallen into sorrow? Give up all sorrow.
m.2.5.7.23: O gods, consider that the worship of the Great One is not easy to accomplish; it is heard that in worshipping the Great One sorrow comes first, and, O gods, knowing your firmness, he surely becomes pleased —
m.2.5.7.24: — Śiva, the supreme Lord, the ruler of all the gaṇas, becomes pleased quickly. Let all of you consider in your hearts how he may be won over.
m.2.5.7.25: First uttering the praṇava (Om), one should then say namaḥ, then śivāya, and after that śubha twice;
m.2.5.7.26: then kuru twice is prescribed, then again śivāya, and namaḥ and the praṇava — this mantra, O wise ones, repeat always.
m.2.5.7.27: If you repeat it again for Śambhu's sake, then, having thus done one crore (ten million) of japa, Śiva will accomplish the task.
m.2.5.7.28: When this had been said then by the mighty Hari, the gods again performed the worship of Hara accordingly, O sage.
m.2.5.7.29: Hari too, together with Vidhi (Brahmā), his mind fixed on Śiva, performed japa for the accomplishment of the gods' purpose and especially that of the sages.
m.2.5.7.30: Repeatedly saying Śiva, the gods, endowed with fortitude, completed a count of a crore and then remained waiting, O best of sages.
m.2.5.7.31: Meanwhile Śiva himself appeared in person, in the form described, and spoke these words:
m.2.5.7.32: Śrī Śiva said: O Hari, O Vidhi, O gods and sages of auspicious vows, I am pleased with this japa; ask for the boon you desire.
m.2.5.7.33: The gods said: If you are pleased, O lord of gods, lord of the world, Śaṅkara, then, knowing the gods to be distressed, let the three cities be destroyed.
m.2.5.7.34: Protect us, O supreme Lord, friend of the afflicted, source of compassion; by you alone have the gods always been protected from calamities again and again.
m.2.5.7.35: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing these words spoken by them along with Hari and Vedhas (Brahmā), Maheśa then laughed inwardly, O Brahmin, and spoke again.
m.2.5.7.36: Maheśa said: O Hari, O Vidhi, O gods and all sages, listen attentively to my words, considering the three cities as already destroyed.
m.2.5.7.37: The chariot, a divine charioteer, the bow and the excellent arrow — all that was previously agreed upon, provide without delay.
m.2.5.7.38: O Viṣṇu, O Vidhi, you are surely the lord of the three worlds; you should carefully make for me all the arrangements befitting a supreme sovereign.
m.2.5.7.39: Considering the three cities as destroyed, you two, entrusted with creation and preservation, will with effort render help to the gods.
m.2.5.7.40: This mantra is greatly meritorious, producing my pleasure, auspicious, bestowing enjoyment and liberation, granting all desires, and bringing one to the Śaiva state.
m.2.5.7.41: It is blessed, bringing fame and long life to men who seek heaven and desires; for the desireless it is final emancipation, and for the liberated it grants enjoyment and liberation.
m.2.5.7.42: The man who, having become pure, always recites this mantra, or hears it, or causes others to hear it, would obtain all desires.
m.2.5.7.43: Sanatkumāra said: Having heard these words of Śiva, the Supreme Self, all the gods attained joy, and likewise Hari and Brahmā rejoiced even more.
m.2.5.7.44: By his command, Viśvakarmā fashioned, for the sake of the world, a divine, supremely beautiful chariot composed of all the gods.
m.2.5.7.iti: Thus ends the seventh adhyāya, named The praise by the gods, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.5.8.1: Vyāsa said: O Sanatkumāra, all-knowing, foremost of Śaivas, of noble mind, dear one, this wondrous story of the Supreme Lord has been narrated to me.
m.2.5.8.2: Now tell me about the building of the supreme chariot made of the gods, the divine chariot that was made for Śiva by the wise Viśvakarman.
m.2.5.8.3: Sūta said: Having heard these words of Vyāsa, that lord of sages Sanatkumāra spoke, remembering the lotus feet of Śiva.
m.2.5.8.4: Sanatkumāra said: Listen, O Vyāsa of great wisdom, O sage, to the making of the chariot and the rest. I shall tell it as far as I understand, remembering the lotus feet of Śiva.
m.2.5.8.5: Then for the god Rudra, Viśvakarman built with effort and reverence a divine chariot made of all the worlds,
m.2.5.8.6: made of all beings, golden, approved by all. Its right wheel was the Sun, and its left the Moon.
m.2.5.8.7: The right wheel had twelve spokes and the left sixteen. In those spokes of the right wheel, O best of Brahmins, were the twelve Ādityas.
m.2.5.8.8: The sixteen spokes of the left wheel were the digits of the Moon, O you of good vows; and likewise the constellations were the ornament of that same left wheel.
m.2.5.8.9: The six seasons were the rims of those two wheels, O bull among Brahmins; the mid-space was the puṣkara front body, and Mandara was the chariot's seat.
m.2.5.8.10: The Setting Mountain and the Rising Mountain, those two are known as the shafts; the great Meru was the base, and the Keśara mountains the supports.
m.2.5.8.11: The years were its speed; the two solar courses (ayanas) the junctions of the wheels; the muhūrtas were its frame-pieces, and the kalās are known as its yoke-pins.
m.2.5.8.12: Its kāṣṭhās are known as the nose-points, the kṣaṇas as the axle-rods, the nimeṣas as the bottom-boards, and the lavas as the poles.
m.2.5.8.13: Heaven was the protective cover of this chariot; heaven (svarga) and liberation (mokṣa) its two banners; Bhramā and Kāmadughā are known as the two tips at the ends of its yoke.
m.2.5.8.14: Likewise the manifest principle was the pole-shaft, and growth (vṛddhi) its naḍvala reed-frame; ego (ahaṅkāra) its corners, and the elements are known as its strength.
m.2.5.8.15: The senses were its ornaments all around, and faith was the motion of this chariot, O best of sages.
m.2.5.8.16: Then the six Vedāṅgas were its ornaments, and the Purāṇas, Nyāya, Mīmāṃsā and the Dharmaśāstras its secondary ornaments, O you of good vows.
m.2.5.8.17: The excellent ones, endowed with all auspicious marks, were the supports of its strength; the mantras are known as its bells, the varṇas as their feet, and likewise the āśramas.
m.2.5.8.18: Then the binding was Ananta, adorned with a thousand hoods; the directions were the feet of this chariot, and also the intermediate directions.
m.2.5.8.19: Puṣkara and the others were the banners, golden and adorned with gems; the four oceans are known as its chariot-blankets.
m.2.5.8.20: The Gaṅgā and the other foremost rivers, adorned with all ornaments, with chowries held at their fingertips, all shining in women's forms,
m.2.5.8.21: taking their places here and there, beautified the chariot. Likewise the seven winds Āvaha and the rest were the excellent golden stairway.
m.2.5.8.22: The Lokāloka mountain formed its side-steps all around; and likewise the outer region and the splendid Mānasa lake and the rest were part of it.
m.2.5.8.23: All the boundary mountains of the varṣas are known as its cords all around; and all the dwellers of the nether regions were the floors of that chariot.
m.2.5.8.24: The charioteer was Lord Brahmā, and the gods are known as the holders of the reins; the goad of that Brahmā was the praṇava, whose deity is Brahmā.
m.2.5.8.25: The syllable a was the great umbrella, Mandara the bearer of the side-staff; the lord of mountains was his bow, and the bowstring the king of serpents himself.
m.2.5.8.26: The bell of the bow was the goddess Sarasvatī in the form of the Veda; the arrow was Viṣṇu of great splendour, and Agni is declared the arrowhead.
m.2.5.8.27: Its horses, likewise, are said to be the four Vedas, O sage; the remaining luminaries beyond these were their ornaments.
m.2.5.8.28: The army was born of poison; the winds are known as the musicians; and the sages headed by Vyāsa became the drivers of the steeds.
m.2.5.8.29: I tell it in few syllables—what use is much speech, O lord of sages? Whatever thing exists in the cosmic egg, that is held to be in the chariot.
m.2.5.8.30: Thus the auspicious arrangement of the chariot and the rest was properly made by the wise Viśvakarman at the command of Brahmā and Viṣṇu.
m.2.5.8.iti: Thus ends the eighth adhyāya, named The chariot and the other arrangements for the battle, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.5.9.1: Sanatkumāra said: Brahmā harnessed the Vedas as horses to that chariot, so made, supremely divine and full of many wonders, and offered it to Śiva.
m.2.5.9.2: Having presented it to Śambhu and having entreated many times the lord of gods, honoured by Viṣṇu and the other gods, he made the trident-bearer mount it.
m.2.5.9.3: Then Śambhu, the great Lord, who embodies all the gods, mounted that divine chariot fitted with its protective rampart.
m.2.5.9.4: And he was praised by the sages, by gods, gandharvas and serpents, by Viṣṇu and Brahmā, and by the guardians of the worlds.
m.2.5.9.5: Surrounded by troops of apsarases skilled in song, the boon-giving Śambhu shone; and he looked at the charioteer.
m.2.5.9.6: As he was mounting the chariot fashioned and assembled from the worlds, the horses born of the Vedas fell headlong to the ground.
m.2.5.9.7: The earth shook, all the mountains trembled, and Śeṣa suddenly quaked, distressed, unable to bear that weight.
m.2.5.9.8: Then the blessed Lord, the upholder of the earth, taking the form of a great bull, rose from beneath this chariot and held it steady for a moment.
m.2.5.9.9: In another moment the great bull too sank to the earth on his knees, unable to bear the intense splendour of Maheśa mounted on the chariot.
m.2.5.9.10: Then the blessed Brahmā, reins in hand, lifted up the horses and, at the god's command, set the excellent chariot steady.
m.2.5.9.11: Then Brahmā, standing on the excellent chariot, urged on the harnessed horses made of the Vedas, swift as mind and wind,
m.2.5.9.12: toward the three cities of the mighty Dānavas, which stood in the sky, once Maheśa had taken his seat.
m.2.5.9.13: Then the blessed Rudra Śaṅkara, looking at the gods, said: Grant me lordship over the paśus (bound beings); then I will slay the asuras.
m.2.5.9.14: O best of gods, only after assigning the state of paśu separately to the gods and likewise to the others can those chief Daityas be slain, not otherwise.
m.2.5.9.15: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing these words of the wise god of gods, all fell into dejection, apprehensive about becoming paśus.
m.2.5.9.16: Then, knowing their feeling, Śambhu, god of gods and husband of Ambikā, smiled and out of compassion spoke thus to those gods.
m.2.5.9.17: Śambhu said: O best of gods, let there be no fall for you even in the state of paśu. Hear the release from paśu-hood, and let it be practised.
m.2.5.9.18: Whoever practises the divine Pāśupata vow will be released from paśu-hood—this I truly promise you; listen attentively.
m.2.5.9.19: And any others who perform my Pāśupata vow will also be released from paśu-hood, O best of gods; there is no doubt.
m.2.5.9.20: Whoever performs this service lifelong, or for twelve years, or half that, or for three years, is freed from paśu-hood.
m.2.5.9.21: Therefore, O best of gods, you will practise this supreme divine vow; then you will be released from paśu-hood—of this there is no doubt.
m.2.5.9.22: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing these words of Maheśa, the supreme Self, the gods, Hari, Brahmā and the rest, said, so be it.
m.2.5.9.23: Therefore all the foremost gods and asuras are the paśus of the Lord, and Rudra is Paśupati, the releaser from the bonds of the paśus.
m.2.5.9.24: Then this name of the great Lord, Paśupati, truly became renowned in all the worlds, bestowing welfare.
m.2.5.9.25: Then all the gods and sages, joyfully crying victory, rejoiced exceedingly—the lord of gods, Brahmā, Viṣṇu and others too.
m.2.5.9.26: The form that the great-souled one assumed at that time cannot be described even in hundreds of years.
m.2.5.9.27: Thus Maheśāna, lord of Maheśānī and of all, the giver of happiness to all, went forth to destroy Tripura.
m.2.5.9.28: Then, following that god of gods as he went to destroy Tripura, all of them, radiant as the sun, led by the king of immortals, went on elephants, horses, excellent lions, chariots and bulls.
m.2.5.9.29: With ploughs, trees, maces and bhuśuṇḍīs, weapons like great mountains, themselves mountain-like, their arms bearing various weapons, the lords of gods then went forth delighted.
m.2.5.9.30: Rich in various weapons, supremely radiant, in great festivity, proclaiming Śambhu's victory, those led by Indra, the lotus-born Brahmā and Viṣṇu then went before that Maheśvara.
m.2.5.9.31: All the sages, staff in hand and wearing matted locks, rejoiced; the sky-goers, siddhas and cāraṇas showered rains of flowers.
m.2.5.9.32: And all the lords of the gaṇas went to the three cities, O chief of brahmins. Who can count them? I shall name some.
m.2.5.9.33: Bhṛṅgī, foremost of all gaṇa-chiefs, surrounded by gaṇa-lords and hosts of gods, mounted an aerial car like great Indra and went with his forces to destroy Tripura.
m.2.5.9.34: Keśa, Vigatavāsa, Mahākeśa, Mahājvara, Somavallīsavarṇa, Somapa and Sanaka;
m.2.5.9.35: Somadhṛk, Sūryavarcas, Sūryapreṣaṇaka, Sūryākṣa, Sūrināman, Sura and Sundara;
m.2.5.9.36: Praskanda, Kundara, Caṇḍa, Kampana and Atikampana, Indra and Indrajava, Yantā and Himakara;
m.2.5.9.37: Śatākṣa, Pañcākṣa, Sahasrākṣa, Mahodara, Satījuha, Śatāsya, Raṅka and Karpūrapūtana;
m.2.5.9.38: Dviśikha and Triśikha, likewise Ahaṅkārakāraka, Ajavaktra, Aṣṭavaktra, Hayavaktra and Ardhavaktraka—
m.2.5.9.39: these and many other heroic, immeasurable gaṇa-leaders, beyond all definable marks, went forth surrounding the Lord.
m.2.5.9.40: Surrounding Mahādeva, they then attended the Pināka-bearer—they who could burn the universe with all its moving and unmoving beings in a moment by mere thought.
m.2.5.9.41: His gaṇas are capable of burning this entire world; so why would Pinākī himself need to go here to burn Tripura? And what need does Śambhu have here of a chariot, of his arrow, of gaṇas, or of the hosts of gods?
m.2.5.9.42: Yet he himself, the Pināka-wielder, O Vyāsa, went there together with his own gaṇas to burn those three cities of the enemies of the gods — he who is the wondrous helper even of the gods.
m.2.5.9.43: What other reason was there for that? I tell you, O best of sages: it was indeed to proclaim in the worlds his glory, which removes the supreme impurity.
m.2.5.9.44: And this is another reason: indeed, to convince the wicked, since among all the gods no other surpasses him.
m.2.5.9.iti: Thus ends the ninth adhyāya, named The description of Śiva's march, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.5.10.1: Sanatkumāra said: Then Śambhu, the great god, standing on the chariot and fully equipped, became ready to burn the entire Tripura of the enemies of the gods.
m.2.5.10.2: Taking up the foremost stance, the most wondrous pratyālīḍha posture, fitting the finest arrow, and making that bow ready,
m.2.5.10.3: and setting the arrow in his firm grip and fixing his gaze upon the target, he stood there motionless for a hundred thousand years.
m.2.5.10.4: Then the lord of the Gaṇas, stationed on his thumb, kept pricking it incessantly, and those cities did not come within the aim of the trident-bearer.
m.2.5.10.5: Then Hara, holding bow and arrow, with hair of muñja grass and odd eyes, heard from the sky a most auspicious voice:
m.2.5.10.6: O, O Lord, lord of the lords of the world, so long as that Vināyaka has not been worshipped, you will not now destroy the cities.
m.2.5.10.7: Hearing these words, the slayer of Andhaka then summoned Bhadrakālī and worshipped the elephant-faced one.
m.2.5.10.8: When Vināyaka, the foremost, had been duly worshipped and was fully pleased with joy, then Lord Hara saw in the sky
m.2.5.10.9: the three cities of the Daityas, the mighty sons of Tāraka, joined together just as they should be. Some indeed speak thus:
m.2.5.10.10: that in the case of Maheśvara, the Supreme Brahman, lord of gods, worshipped by all, success in an undertaking through the grace of another does not apply.
m.2.5.10.11: He is independent, the Supreme Brahman, with attributes and also without attributes, imperceptible to all, the Lord, the Supreme Self, stainless.
m.2.5.10.12: He embodies the five deities, is worshipped by the five deities, the supreme Lord. There is none whom he must worship; he alone is to be worshipped, the abode of all.
m.2.5.10.13: Or else, O sage, everything comes about through his play — the conduct of the god of gods, the great Lord, the giver of boons.
m.2.5.10.14: While Mahādeva remained there, having worshipped the lord of the Gaṇas, the cities there quickly came into union in due time.
m.2.5.10.15: When Tripura had come into union there, O sage, a tumultuous joy arose among the gods and other great beings.
m.2.5.10.16: Then all the hosts of gods, the Siddhas and the great sages uttered cries of victory, praising the eight-formed Śiva.
m.2.5.10.17: Then Brahmā and Viṣṇu, lord of the worlds, said thus: The time has come for the act of slaying the Daityas.
m.2.5.10.18: O Maheśvara, the three cities of those sons of Tāraka have come into union; O all-pervading one, accomplish the task of the gods.
m.2.5.10.19: O lord of gods, before the cities separate, release the arrow and reduce Tripura to ashes.
m.2.5.10.20: Then Śarva, stringing the bow and fitting that arrow, meditated on the venerable Pāśupata weapon and on Tripura.
m.2.5.10.21: Then the god Mahādeva, skilled in the play of granting boons, for some reason looked at it here with disdain.
m.2.5.10.22: The gods said: Virūpākṣa, the supreme Lord, refuge of the virtuous, is able to turn the three cities to ashes in an instant — let this be known.
m.2.5.10.23: The lord of gods is able to burn the three worlds with a glance; yet for the increase of our glory you should release the arrow here.
m.2.5.10.24: Thus praised then by all the immortals, Viṣṇu, Brahmā and the rest, Maheśvara wished to burn the three cities with the arrow.
m.2.5.10.25: In the auspicious hour called Abhijit, drawing the wondrous bow and making the bowstring twang with an utterly unbearable sound,
m.2.5.10.26: proclaiming his own name and addressing the great Asuras, the fierce one released the shaft, whose form was like ten million suns.
m.2.5.10.27: That swift arrow, pure and destructive, made of Viṣṇu, with fire as its tip, blazing mightily, burned those three Daityas dwelling in Tripura.
m.2.5.10.28: Then the cities, burned, fell together to the earth girdled by the four oceans — all three burned to ashes.
m.2.5.10.29: The Daityas were burned in hundreds by the fire in his arrow, crying out in anguish, because of their transgression of Śiva's worship.
m.2.5.10.30: Tārakākṣa, being burned along with his two brothers, remembered his own lord, the god Śaṅkara, who loves his devotees.
m.2.5.10.31: Filled with supreme devotion, uttering various words, he gazed at Mahādeva and spoke to him in his mind.
m.2.5.10.32: Tārakākṣa said: O Bhava, you are known to us. If you are pleased with us along with our kinsmen, then by that truth, whenever you burn us again, let it be so.
m.2.5.10.33: We have obtained what is rare, unattainable even by gods and Asuras. May our minds be imbued with devotion to you in every birth.
m.2.5.10.34: Speaking thus, those Dānavas, burned wondrously by that fire at Śiva's command, were reduced to ashes, O sage.
m.2.5.10.35: Other Dānavas too, children and old men, were quickly burned by that fire at Śiva's command and reduced to ashes, O Vyāsa.
m.2.5.10.36: Women or men, and the vehicles that were there — all were burned by that fire, as the world is at the end of an aeon.
m.2.5.10.37: Some fine women were burned letting go of husbands clinging to their necks; some women were asleep, some intoxicated, some wearied from lovemaking.
m.2.5.10.38: Half-burned and awakened, they wandered about, stupefied by delusion. By that terrible fire of Tripura not even the tiniest thing
m.2.5.10.39: was left unburned or spared, whether stationary or moving — except the Daitya Maya, the imperishable craftsman (Viśvakarman),
m.2.5.10.40: who was not hostile to the gods, a true devotee who had taken refuge in Maheśa even in time of calamity, and was protected by Śambhu's power.
m.2.5.10.41: For we are those for whom there exists no destructive coming-together with the Daityas or other beings, whether in existence or non-existence, in what is done or not done.
m.2.5.10.42: Therefore a well-considered effort must indeed be made by the good. Through censure a person declines; one should not perform such an act.
m.2.5.10.43: It should be arranged so that there may be no contact with those dwellers of Tripura—this indeed is the view of all—should it by fate arise from any quarter.
m.2.5.10.44: Those Daityas there who, with their kinsmen, were worshipping Rudra even then all attained the rank of gaṇa-chiefs by the power of the rite of Śiva-worship.
m.2.5.10.iti: Thus ends the tenth adhyāya, named The description of the burning of Tripura, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.5.11.1: Vyāsa said: O son of Brahmā, O greatly wise one, blessed are you, O best of Śaiva devotees. What did all the gods do then, after Tripura had been burnt?
m.2.5.11.2: Where did Maya, who was not burnt, go? Where did those ascetics go? Tell me all that fully, if it pertains to the story of Śambhu.
m.2.5.11.3: Sūta said: Having heard Vyāsa's words, the blessed Sanatkumāra, son of the creator of the world (Brahmā), spoke, remembering the pair of Śiva's feet.
m.2.5.11.4: Sanatkumāra said: Listen, O Vyāsa of great intellect, O son of Parāśara, to the deeds of the great Lord, which destroy all sins — the Lord who conforms to worldly play.
m.2.5.11.5: When the whole of Tripura, crowded with Daityas, had been burnt by Maheśvara, the gods there became exceedingly astonished.
m.2.5.11.6: The gods, Indra, Upendra (Viṣṇu) and the rest, said nothing then; all were agitated on seeing Rudra of great splendour —
m.2.5.11.7: — greatly terrifying, fierce, blazing in the ten directions, shining like ten million suns, resembling the fire of cosmic dissolution.
m.2.5.11.8: Merely on beholding the God and the Goddess, daughter of Himavat, all the leading gods were afraid out of fear and stood bowed down.
m.2.5.11.9: Seeing then the host of gods frightened, the foremost sages said nothing; they stood still and bowed on all sides.
m.2.5.11.10: Then Brahmā too, very frightened on seeing Śaṅkara's form, yet glad at heart, praised him attentively together with the gods,
m.2.5.11.11: and with the frightened Viṣṇu, he praised the God of gods, Bhava, Hara, the enemy of Tripura, together with Girijā, subject to his devotees, Maheśvara.
m.2.5.11.12: Brahmā said: O God of gods, O Mahādeva, bestower of grace on devotees, be gracious, O supreme Lord, giver of welfare to all the gods.
m.2.5.11.13: Be gracious, O Lord of the worlds; be gracious, O giver of bliss; be gracious, O Śaṅkara, O master; be gracious, O supreme Lord.
m.2.5.11.14: Salutation to you, the Oṃkāra, O you who carry beings across beyond form; be gracious, O Lord of all gods, O destroyer of Tripura, O Maheśvara.
m.2.5.11.15: Salutation to the God denoted by many names, O Śaṅkara, lover of those who bow; salutation to you, the attributeless, O you who are beyond Prakṛti and Puruṣa.
m.2.5.11.16: Salutation to you, the changeless, the eternal, the ever-content, the radiant, the stainless, the divine, the possessor of the three guṇas.
m.2.5.11.17: Salutation to you with attributes; salutation to you, lord of heaven; to Sadāśiva, the tranquil, Maheśa, the wielder of the Pināka bow.
m.2.5.11.18: Salutation to you, the omniscient, the refuge, Sadyojāta; to Vāmadeva, Rudra, and also to Tatpuruṣa.
m.2.5.11.19: Salutation to you, Aghora, well worthy of service, subject to devotees; to Īśāna, the most excellent, bestower of bliss on devotees.
m.2.5.11.20: Protect, protect, O Mahādeva, all of us frightened immortals. By burning Tripura you have made all the immortals fulfilled in their purpose.
m.2.5.11.21: Having praised thus, all the deities, Brahmā and the rest, supremely pleased, made obeisance to Sadāśiva each separately.
m.2.5.11.22: Then Brahmā himself, bowing, with shoulders lowered and palms joined, praised the God Maheśvara, enemy of Tripura.
m.2.5.11.23: Brahmā said: O Lord, Lord of the God of gods, destroyer of Tripura, Śaṅkara, O Mahādeva, may I have supreme, unfailing devotion to you.
m.2.5.11.24: May the charioteership of you always be mine, O Lord of gods, Śaṅkara. Be always favourable, O all-pervading one, O supreme Lord.
m.2.5.11.25: Sanatkumāra said: Having thus praised Śambhu, loving to his devotees, Vidhi (Brahmā) of noble mind, bowing, with lowered shoulders and joined palms, fell silent.
m.2.5.11.26: The blessed Janārdana too, having bowed to Maheśvara and joined his palms in cupped reverence, praised Maheśvara.
m.2.5.11.27: Viṣṇu said: O overlord of gods, great Lord, friend of the afflicted, source of compassion, be gracious, O supreme Lord; show compassion, O lover of those who bow.
m.2.5.11.28: Salutation to you, the attributeless, and again to you with attributes; again to you in the form of Prakṛti, and again to you as Puruṣa.
m.2.5.11.29: Then, bowing, I offer salutation to you whose nature is the guṇas, the soul of the universe; to the lover of devotion, the tranquil, Śiva, the supreme Self.
m.2.5.11.30: Salutation to Sadāśiva, Rudra, lord of the worlds. May my devotion to you be firm and ever-increasing from today.
m.2.5.11.31: Sanatkumāra said: Having spoken thus, he, the best among the foremost Śaivas, fell silent. Then all the gods, bowing, spoke to that supreme Lord.
m.2.5.11.32: The gods said: O Lord of gods, Mahādeva, source of compassion, Śaṅkara, be gracious, O Lord of the worlds; be gracious, O supreme Lord.
m.2.5.11.33: Be gracious; you are the maker of all. We bow to you with joy. May our devotion to you be firm, constant and unfailing.
m.2.5.11.34: Sanatkumāra said: Thus praised by Brahmā, Hari and the immortals, the Lord of gods, Śaṅkara, benefactor of the world, replied with a pleased heart.
m.2.5.11.35: Śaṅkara said: O Vidhi, O Hari, O gods, I am especially pleased. All of you, after reflection, ask for the boon your mind desires.
m.2.5.11.36: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing these words spoken by Hara, O best of sages, all the gods replied with pleased inner hearts.
m.2.5.11.37: All the gods said: If you are pleased, O Lord, and if a boon is to be given by you to us, O Lord of the God of gods, knowing us gods to be your servants —
m.2.5.11.38: — whenever distress arises for the gods, O best of gods, then always become manifest and destroy that distress.
m.2.5.11.39: Sanatkumāra said: Thus addressed by Brahmā, Hari and the immortals all at once, the blessed Rudra, pleased at heart, said: So be it, ever.
m.2.5.11.40: I am pleased with these hymns too, O gods; I shall surely always grant whatever is most desired in the world to those who recite or hear them.
m.2.5.11.41: Having spoken thus, Śaṅkara, pleased, who is ever the remover of the gods' sorrow, bestowed everything that was indeed dear to all the gods.
m.2.5.11.iti: Thus ends the eleventh adhyāya, named The description of the gods' hymn of praise, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.5.12.1: Sanatkumāra said: Meanwhile, seeing Śambhu pleased, the Dānava Maya, who had not been burnt thanks to the power of Śiva's grace, came there, greatly delighted.
m.2.5.12.2: He lovingly bowed to Hara and indeed to the other gods as well; with joined palms and bent shoulders, he bowed again to Śiva.
m.2.5.12.3: Then, rising and looking at Śiva, Maya, the best of Dānavas, his heart full of devotion and his sweet voice choked with love, praised him.
m.2.5.12.4: Maya said: O God of gods, O Mahādeva, O Śaṅkara, loving to devotees, you are the very form of the wish-fulfilling tree, free of all partiality.
m.2.5.12.5: You whose form is light, salutation be to you; O universal form, salutation be to you. Salutation to you, the pure-souled; to the purifier, salutations again and again.
m.2.5.12.6: Salutation to you of wondrous form, the eternal, beyond form; salutation to the one of divine form, the divine, of supremely divine shape.
m.2.5.12.7: Salutation to the auspicious-souled one who destroys all the afflictions of those who bow down; salutations again and again to the creator, sustainer and destroyer of the three worlds.
m.2.5.12.8: Salutation to you, attainable by devotion, compassionate to devotees, granter of the true fruit of austerity, O beloved of Śivā, O Lord Śiva.
m.2.5.12.9: I do not know how to offer praise, O supreme Lord fond of praise. Be pleased, O Lord of all; protect me, who have come to you for refuge.
m.2.5.12.10: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing this hymn spoken by Maya, the supreme Lord became pleased, O best of twice-born, and spoke respectfully to Maya.
m.2.5.12.11: Śiva said: Ask for a boon, O Maya, best of Dānavas; I am pleased. Whatever your mind desires, that I shall give; there is no doubt.
m.2.5.12.12: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing Śambhu's auspicious words, Maya, the bull among Dānavas, bowed to the Lord and, with bent shoulders and joined palms, replied.
m.2.5.12.13: Maya said: O God of gods, O Mahādeva, if you are pleased with me, and if I am worthy of a boon, then grant me everlasting devotion to you.
m.2.5.12.14: Grant me constant friendship with your devotees, constant compassion for the afflicted, and indifference towards other beings who are wicked, O supreme Lord.
m.2.5.12.15: May a demonic disposition never arise in me, O Maheśvara. May I always be fearless, O Lord, absorbed in your auspicious worship.
m.2.5.12.16: Sanatkumāra said: Being thus entreated, Śaṅkara, the supreme Lord, the master, pleased and loving to devotees, replied to Maya.
m.2.5.12.17: Maheśvara said: O bull among Dānavas, you are blessed, my devotee, free from perversion. All the boons that you now desire are granted to you.
m.2.5.12.18: By my command, go with your own retinue to the world Vitala, which is more delightful even than heaven.
m.2.5.12.19: Dwell there fearless, joyful and always devoted. By my command, a demonic disposition will never arise in you.
m.2.5.12.20: Sanatkumāra said: Thus, placing the command of the great-souled Śaṅkara on his head, and bowing to him and to the gods as well, he went to Vitala.
m.2.5.12.21: Meanwhile the shaven-headed ones also arrived, and bowing, they spoke to all those gods, Viṣṇu, Brahmā and the rest.
m.2.5.12.22: Where shall we go, O gods? What work shall we do? Command us quickly, for we carry out your orders.
m.2.5.12.23: A wicked deed has been done by us, O Hari, O Vidhi, O gods: the devotion to Śiva of the Daityas, who were Śiva's devotees, has been destroyed.
m.2.5.12.24: Our dwelling in hell will be for ten million kalpas; surely there will be no deliverance for those who oppose Śiva's devotees.
m.2.5.12.25: Yet this wicked deed was done by us at your wish. Out of compassion, tell us its expiation; we have come to you for refuge.
m.2.5.12.26: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing their words, those gods, Viṣṇu, Brahmā and the rest, spoke to the shaven-headed ones standing before them with joined palms.
m.2.5.12.27: Viṣṇu and the others said: You need never be afraid, O shaven-headed ones; this whole excellent episode came about by Śiva's command.
m.2.5.12.28: No painful evil destiny will ever be yours, since you are servants of Śiva who act for the good of gods and sages.
m.2.5.12.29: Śambhu works for the good of gods and sages, and one who works for the good of gods and sages is dear to him; for men who work for the good of gods and sages there is never an evil destiny.
m.2.5.12.30: From today on, for men who enter this doctrine in the Kali age, there will be an evil destiny; we speak the truth, there is no doubt in this.
m.2.5.12.31: O steadfast shaven-headed ones, by my command you should dwell in the desert land in concealment until the Kali age arrives.
m.2.5.12.32: And when Kali has come, you will establish your own doctrine; in Kali, deluded fools will adopt your doctrine.
m.2.5.12.33: Thus commanded by the lords of the gods, O lord of sages, those shaven-headed ones paid homage and went to their own hermitage as directed.
m.2.5.12.34: Then the blessed Rudra, the great yogin, having burnt the inhabitants of Tripura, his task accomplished, was worshipped by Brahmā and the others.
m.2.5.12.35: Then the Lord, accompanied by all his Gaṇas, by the goddess Śivā and by his sons, having accomplished the great task of the immortals, disappeared.
m.2.5.12.36: When the god Śiva with his retinue had vanished, the bow, together with the arrow, the chariot and the rest, and the enclosure also disappeared.
m.2.5.12.37: Then Brahmā, Hari, the gods, sages, Gandharvas, Kinnaras, Nāgas, serpents, Apsarases and humans, all delighted,
m.2.5.12.38: went joyfully each to his own place, extolling Śaṅkara's glory; and having reached their own places, they attained supreme bliss.
m.2.5.12.39: Thus I have told you the whole great story of the moon-crested Śiva, which narrates the destruction of Tripura and is full of supreme divine play.
m.2.5.12.40: It is blessed, conferring fame and long life, increasing wealth and grain, granting heaven and liberation too. What more do you wish to hear?
m.2.5.12.41: Whoever always reads or listens to this supreme narrative, having enjoyed all desires here in this world, would attain liberation at the end.
m.2.5.12.iti: Thus ends the twelfth adhyāya, named The description of the gods' hymn after the slaying of Tripura, Maya's hymn, the settling of the shaven-headed ones and the gods' return to their own places, in the dialogue of Sanatkumāra and Pārāśarya, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.5.13.1: Vyāsa said: O Brahman, O venerable one, O son of Brahmā, I have heard before that the Lord Śaṅkara slew the great demon Jalandhara.
m.2.5.13.2: Therefore, O greatly wise one, tell me in detail the deeds of the moon-crested Śiva. Who, hearing his spotless glory, could ever be satiated?
m.2.5.13.3: Sūta said: Thus questioned by Vyāsa, the great sage, the son of Brahmā, skilled in speech, spoke words full of meaning, without agitation.
m.2.5.13.4: Sanatkumāra said: Once, O sage, Jīva Bṛhaspati and Śakra Indra, with supreme devotion, eagerly went to Kailāsa to have the sight of the Lord.
m.2.5.13.5: Then the Lord Śaṅkara, knowing of the coming of the Guru Bṛhaspati and Indra, wished to test the understanding of those two, whose minds were intent on seeing him.
m.2.5.13.6: Then, naked, he who is the true refuge of the good blocked their path and stood there with his head bound in matted locks, his face radiant.
m.2.5.13.7: Then those two, the Guru and Śakra, travelling joyfully, saw in the middle of the path a fearsome man of wondrous form,
m.2.5.13.8: greatly radiant, calm, his head bound with matted locks, mighty-armed, broad-chested, fair, with terrifying eyes.
m.2.5.13.9: Then Purandara Indra, arrogant because of his authority, questioned that man standing in his path, not recognising him as Śaṅkara.
m.2.5.13.10: Purandara said: Hey, who are you? Where have you come from? What is your name? Tell me truly. Is Śambhu, the Lord, staying in his own abode, or has he gone elsewhere?
m.2.5.13.11: Sanatkumāra said: Though questioned thus by Śakra, the ascetic said nothing. Śakra asked again, but the naked one did not speak.
m.2.5.13.12: Again Purandara, the supreme ruler of the worlds, asked; the great yogin, the Lord who had assumed a form in play, remained silent.
m.2.5.13.13: Thus questioned again and again by Śakra, the naked Lord said nothing, in order to test Śakra's understanding.
m.2.5.13.14: Then the lord of the gods, proud of his sovereignty over the three worlds, became angry, and rebuking that wearer of matted locks, he spoke these words.
m.2.5.13.15: Indra said: Hey, even though I am questioning you, you have given no answer. Therefore I will strike you with my thunderbolt. Who is there to protect you, O fool?
m.2.5.13.16: Sanatkumāra said: Having said this, the wielder of the thunderbolt glared at him in anger and raised his thunderbolt to strike the naked one.
m.2.5.13.17: Seeing Purandara with the thunderbolt in hand, the god Sadāśiva, Śaṅkara, paralysed the fall of his thunderbolt.
m.2.5.13.18: Then Rudra, filled with anger, with fierce eyes and terrifying, at once blazed up with radiance as if he would burn everything.
m.2.5.13.19: The lord of Śacī burned within with rage born of the paralysis of his arm, like a serpent whose power has been checked by a spell.
m.2.5.13.20: Seeing that man blazing with his own radiance, Bṛhaspati quickly recognised him by his insight as Hara, and bowed to the Lord.
m.2.5.13.21: Then the noble-minded Guru, with joined palms, bowing down to the ground like a staff, began to praise the Lord.
m.2.5.13.22: The guru said: Salutation to the God of gods, to Mahādeva, to the Self, to Maheśvara, the Lord, the three-eyed one, the wearer of matted hair.
m.2.5.13.23: Salutation to the protector of the wretched, the all-pervading one, the slayer of Andhaka, the destroyer of Tripura, to Śarva, to Brahman, the supreme one.
m.2.5.13.24: Salutation to you, the odd-eyed one, Rudra, the many-formed, Śambhu; to the misshapen one, the one of surpassing form, the one beyond all form.
m.2.5.13.25: Salutation to you, destroyer of the sacrifice and giver of the fruits of sacrifices, whose form is the sacrifice, who sets in motion the actions of others.
m.2.5.13.26: Salutation to you, the ender of Kāla, who are Time itself, who wear the serpents of Time; salutation to the supreme Lord, the all-pervading one.
m.2.5.13.27: Salutation to the cutter of Brahmā's head, to the one praised by Brahmā and the Moon; salutation be to you, friend of brāhmaṇas; salutation to you, the supreme Self.
m.2.5.13.28: You are fire, wind, and sky; you alone are water and earth; you are the sun, the moon, the stars; you indeed are the circle of luminaries.
m.2.5.13.29: You alone are Viṣṇu, you are Brahmā; praised by them, you are the supreme Lord. You are the sages beginning with Sanaka; you are Nārada, rich in austerity.
m.2.5.13.30: You alone are the lord of all worlds; you alone are the soul of the universe; connected with all, yet distinct from all, you alone are beyond Prakṛti.
m.2.5.13.31: Through rajas, bearing the name Vidhi Brahmā, you create the worlds; through sattva, in the form of Hari, you sustain the whole universe.
m.2.5.13.32: You alone, O Mahādeva, through tamas, assuming the form of Hara, dissolve in play the entire world made of the five elements.
m.2.5.13.33: By the power of meditation on you, O creator of the universe, the sun shines, the moon pours down nectar upon the world, and the wind blows.
m.2.5.13.34: By the power of meditation on you, O Śaṅkara, the clouds rain water; by the power of meditation on you Śakra protects the three worlds like a son.
m.2.5.13.35: By the power of meditation on you, the clouds, all the gods, and the lords of sages perform their own duties, trembling from fear of you.
m.2.5.13.36: Through service of your lotus feet alone, O Rudra, men on earth disregard the gods and enjoy sovereignty over the worlds.
m.2.5.13.37: Through service of your lotus feet alone, devotees have reached the supreme state, unattainable even by those rich in yoga and hard for all to gain.
m.2.5.13.38: Sanatkumāra said: Having thus praised Śaṅkara, the benefactor of the worlds, Bṛhaspati made Purandara fall at the feet of that Lord.
m.2.5.13.39: Having made Indra, lord of the gods, fall down with bowed neck, Bṛhaspati, bent low in humility, said this to Śiva:
m.2.5.13.40: Bṛhaspati said: O protector of the helpless, O Mahādeva, raise up Indra who is bowed at your feet, and make calm your own anger born from your eye.
m.2.5.13.41: Be pleased, O Mahādeva; protect Indra, who has come to you for refuge. May this fire, born from the eye on your forehead, be quenched.
m.2.5.13.42: Sanatkumāra said: Having heard these words of the preceptor, Maheśvara, the god of gods, the ocean of compassion, spoke in a voice deep as the rumbling of clouds.
m.2.5.13.43: Maheśvara said: O Bṛhaspati, how can I hold back the wrath that has already issued from my eye? How indeed does a snake put on again the slough it has cast off?
m.2.5.13.44: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing these words of Śaṅkara, Bṛhaspati, distressed in appearance, his mind agitated with fear, spoke.
m.2.5.13.45: Bṛhaspati said: O god, O Lord, devotees are ever to be shown compassion. O Śaṅkara, make true your name Bhaktavatsala (affectionate to devotees).
m.2.5.13.46: O lord of gods, you should cast your extremely fierce energy elsewhere. O deliverer of all devotees, deliver Purandara (Indra).
m.2.5.13.47: Sanatkumāra said: Thus addressed by the preceptor, Rudra, who bears the name affectionate to devotees and removes the distress of those who bow to him, replied with a gracious heart to the priest of the gods.
m.2.5.13.48: Śiva said: Pleased by this hymn, dear one, I grant you an excellent boon: since you have obtained life for Indra, become famed as Jīva.
m.2.5.13.49: This fire which has arisen from my forehead eye, the slayer of the lord of gods—I shall cast it far away, so that it may not afflict Indra.
m.2.5.13.50: Sanatkumāra said: Having said this, taking in his hand that wondrous fire of his own energy, born from his forehead eye, he hurled it into the salt ocean.
m.2.5.13.51: Then Rudra, the Lord, performer of great sports, vanished. The preceptor and Śakra, freed from fear, attained supreme happiness.
m.2.5.13.52: Having obtained the sight of him for whose sake they had set out, the preceptor and Śakra, their purpose fulfilled, joyfully returned to their own abodes.
m.2.5.13.iti: Thus ends the thirteenth adhyāya, named The saving of Śakra's life, in the account of the slaying of Jalandhara, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.5.14.1: Vyāsa said: O Sanatkumāra, all-knowing son of Brahmā, salutation to you. Today I have heard this wondrous story of the great-souled Śambhu.
m.2.5.14.2: O Brahman, when his own fiery energy, born from the eye on his forehead, was cast into the salt ocean, what happened there, dear one? Tell me that quickly.
m.2.5.14.3: Sanatkumāra said: Listen, dear one of great wisdom, to Śiva's most wondrous sport, hearing which with faith a devotee would attain the goal of yogins.
m.2.5.14.4: Then that energy of Śiva, born of his forehead-eye, once thrown into the salt ocean, at once took the form of a child.
m.2.5.14.5: There, at the confluence of the Gaṅgā river with the ocean, that child, terrifying to all the worlds, cried out loudly.
m.2.5.14.6: By the sound of his crying the earth shook again and again, and heaven and Satyaloka were deafened by that noise.
m.2.5.14.7: By the child's crying alone all the worlds were terrified, and the guardians of the worlds everywhere had their minds thrown into agitation.
m.2.5.14.8: What need of saying more, O best of brahmins? The whole universe, with its moving and unmoving beings, shook, dear one, O lord, from the crying of that infant.
m.2.5.14.9: Then all the gods, distressed, together with the sages, quickly went for refuge to Brahmā, the Grandsire, the preceptor of the worlds.
m.2.5.14.10: Having gone there, those gods and sages along with Vāsava (Indra) bowed, praised him well, and spoke to that Supreme One (Parameṣṭhin).
m.2.5.14.11: The gods said: O lord of the worlds, lord of the gods, a danger has come upon us. Destroy it, O great yogin, for this wondrous roar has arisen.
m.2.5.14.12: Sanatkumāra said: Having heard their words thus, Brahmā, the Grandsire of the worlds, then wished to go there, astonished, thinking, what is this?
m.2.5.14.13: Then, dear one, Brahmā with the gods descended from Satyaloka to the earth, and wishing to learn about that, he went to the ocean.
m.2.5.14.14: As soon as Brahmā, the Grandsire of all worlds, arrived there, he saw that child in the lap of the ocean.
m.2.5.14.15: Seeing Vidhi (Brahmā) arrived, the Ocean, taking a divine form, bowed his head and placed the child in his (Brahmā's) lap.
m.2.5.14.16: Then Brahmā, filled with wonder, said to the Ocean: O mass of waters, tell me quickly, whose is this wondrous infant?
m.2.5.14.17: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing Brahmā's words, the Ocean, delighted, bowed, praised the lord of creatures, and with joined palms replied.
m.2.5.14.18: The Ocean said: O Brahmā, O protector of all worlds, I suddenly found this child in the Gaṅgā river, without knowing his origin.
m.2.5.14.19: O preceptor of the world, perform for him the rites beginning with the birth ceremony (jātakarman). O Creator, please tell all the results foretold by his horoscope.
m.2.5.14.20: Sanatkumāra said: While the Ocean was speaking thus, that child, son of the Ocean, seized Brahmā by the neck as he kept shaking again and again.
m.2.5.14.21: Because of this shaking of Vidhi, the maker of all worlds, and his being pained, water came from his eyes, O Kāleya (Vyāsa).
m.2.5.14.22: Having somehow freed his neck from the hands of that mighty son born of the ocean, Brahmā spoke respectfully.
m.2.5.14.23: Brahmā said: Listen, O Ocean: with my mind concentrated, I shall tell you all the results foretold in the horoscope of this son of yours.
m.2.5.14.24: Since water was held (dhṛta) from my eyes by him, therefore let him be known here by the name Jalandhara.
m.2.5.14.25: Even now he is a youth, master of the meaning of all scriptures, of great valour, steadfast, a warrior, and fierce in battle.
m.2.5.14.26: He will be profound like you and, in war, like Guha (Skanda); a conqueror of all in battle, resplendent with every kind of prosperity.
m.2.5.14.27: This child will become the overlord of all the Daityas. He will be a conqueror even of Viṣṇu; there will be no defeat for him from any quarter.
m.2.5.14.28: He will be unslayable by all beings except Rudra. He will now return there whence he arose.
m.2.5.14.29: His wife will be devoted to her husband, increasing his good fortune, beautiful in every limb, charming, an ocean of sweet speech and good conduct.
m.2.5.14.30: Sanatkumāra said: Having said this, Brahmā summoned Śukra and had him (Jalandhara) consecrated to kingship; then, taking leave of the lord of rivers, he vanished.
m.2.5.14.31: Then the Ocean, his eyes wide with joy at seeing him, took up that son of his and went joyfully to his own home.
m.2.5.14.32: Delighted at heart, he nourished with great efforts his own child, beautiful in every limb, charming, and of most wondrous splendour.
m.2.5.14.33: Then the Ocean summoned the great asura Kālanemi and asked for his daughter named Vṛndā to be his son's wife.
m.2.5.14.34: The asura Kālanemi, heroic, foremost of asuras, wise and skilled in his own duties, approved the Ocean's request, O sage.
m.2.5.14.35: To the heroic Jalandhara, born of the Ocean, he gave his own daughter, dear as life, according to the Brāhma rite.
