m.2.5.24.40: Even Garuḍa, together with Viṣṇu, was bound by me with a serpent-noose; Urvaśī and the other women were brought by me into prison.
m.2.5.24.41: O Rudra, you do not know me, the conqueror of the three worlds, Jalandhara, the great demon, the son of the Ocean, of great strength.
m.2.5.24.42: Sanatkumāra said: Having said this to Mahādeva, the son of the Ocean then neither wavered nor remembered the Dānavas slain in battle.
m.2.5.24.43: By that arrogant, ill-mannered one, slapping his two arms in the pride of his arm-strength, Mahādeva was insulted with words of harsh syllables.
m.2.5.24.44: Hearing those inauspicious words uttered by the demon, Mahādeva laughed and took on supreme anger.
m.2.5.24.45: Rudra took in his hand the discus called Sudarśana, which had been fashioned by the drawing of his big toe, and with it he made ready to kill Jalandhara.
m.2.5.24.46: Lord Hara hurled that discus called Sudarśana, which shone like ten million suns and resembled the fire of the cosmic dissolution.
m.2.5.24.47: Burning heaven and earth with its speed, it reached Jalandhara and swiftly cut off his head with its large, wide eyes.
m.2.5.24.48: The body fell from the chariot to the ground, making the surface of the earth resound, and so did the head of the Ocean's son; a great cry of lament arose.
m.2.5.24.49: His body fell in two, like the immovable Añjana mountain, just as a great mountain split in two by the thunderbolt falls into the ocean.
m.2.5.24.50: With his terrible blood the world became filled; then the whole earth became disfigured, O lord of sages.
m.2.5.24.51: By Rudra's command all that blood, and the flesh too, reached Mahāraurava and became the pool of blood (Raktakuṇḍa) there.
m.2.5.24.52: His radiance, issuing from the body, merged into Rudra, just as that which arose from Vṛndā's body had dissolved into Gaurī.
m.2.5.24.53: Seeing Jalandhara slain, the gods, Gandharvas and serpents became greatly delighted and said, well done, O God!
m.2.5.24.54: All the gods, Siddhas and great sages became joyful; showering flowers, they loudly sang his glory.
m.2.5.24.55: The celestial women, overcome with love, danced in great delight; sweet-voiced, they sang melodious songs together with the Kinnaras.
m.2.5.24.56: When Vṛndā's husband was slain, O sage, all the quarters became clear, and the winds of all three kinds blew pure and pleasant to the touch.
m.2.5.24.57: The moon became cool, the sun shone with fine brilliance, the fires blazed calmly, and the sky became undisturbed.
m.2.5.24.58: Thus, O sage, the entire three worlds attained greater well-being when that son of the Ocean was slain by Hara of infinite forms.
m.2.5.24.iti: Thus ends the twenty-fourth adhyāya, named The description of Jalandhara, in the account of the slaying of Jalandhara, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.5.25.1: Sanatkumāra said: Then the gods headed by Brahmā, and likewise all the sages, bowing low, praised the Lord of the god of gods with pleasing words.
m.2.5.25.2: The gods said: O God of gods, O Mahādeva, loving to those who seek refuge, you indeed always grant happiness to the good and destroy the sorrow of your devotees.
m.2.5.25.3: You perform great and wondrous noble sports; you are reached through devotion, hard to approach, and hard for the wicked to propitiate. O Lord, be ever gracious.
m.2.5.25.4: Even the Veda does not truly know your greatness; all great souls sing your true glory according to their understanding.
m.2.5.25.5: Sahasravadana (the thousand-mouthed Śeṣa) and others always sing with great love your deeply hidden majesty; thereby they purify their own speech.
m.2.5.25.6: By your grace, O Lord of gods, even a dull person can become a knower of Brahman. You are always reached through devotion — so indeed the Vedas declare.
m.2.5.25.7: You are indeed compassionate to the afflicted and ever all-pervading. Changeless, the refuge of the good, you manifest yourself through true devotion.
m.2.5.25.8: Through devotion to you alone, O Maheśāna, many who were afflicted, having enjoyed every happiness here, attained perfection through steadfastness.
m.2.5.25.9: Formerly the devotee Dāśārha, lord of the Yadus, attained perfection, and so did his wife Kalāvatī, attaining the supreme state through devotion alone, O Lord.
m.2.5.25.10: Likewise King Mitrasaha and his beloved Madayantī attained supreme liberation (kaivalya) through devotion to you alone, O Lord of gods.
m.2.5.25.11: So too the daughter named Saumini of the foremost Kaikeya king, through devotion to you, attained supreme happiness, hard to gain even for true yogins.
m.2.5.25.12: King Vimarṣaṇa, best of kings, having enjoyed various pleasures over seven births, O Lord, attained the good state through devotion to you.
m.2.5.25.13: Candrasena, best of kings, enjoying all pleasures through devotion to you, freed from sorrow, attained supreme happiness here and hereafter.
m.2.5.25.14: Śrīkara, the son of a cowherdess and disciple of the great hero, through devotion to you, having enjoyed life here, attained the good state and supreme happiness in the hereafter.
m.2.5.25.15: You removed the sorrow of King Satyaratha and granted him the good goal; and you rescued Prince Dharmagupta and made him happy here.
m.2.5.25.16: Likewise, O great Lord, out of compassion you made the brahmin Śucivrata, who followed devotion to you along with his mother, free from poverty and endowed with wisdom.
m.2.5.25.17: Citravarmā, best of kings, having constantly enjoyed in this world pleasures hard even for the immortals to obtain, attained the good state through devotion to you.
m.2.5.25.18: Prince Candrāṅgada, together with his wife Sīmantinī, casting off all sorrow, became happy and attained the great state.
m.2.5.25.19: Even the brahmin named Mandara, a wicked and vile frequenter of prostitutes, becoming your devotee and worshipping you, O Śiva, attained the good state together with her.
m.2.5.25.20: Bhadrāyu, the prince, your devotee, freed from distress, gained happiness, and through the grace of devotion to you, together with his mother, the supreme state, O Lord.
m.2.5.25.21: A wicked man addicted to enjoying all women, who constantly ate forbidden food, also became liberated through service to you, O Maheśvara.
m.2.5.25.22: Śambara, devoted to Śaṅkara and always wearing ashes from the funeral pyre, went to your city with his wife, O Śambhu, through the observance of wearing ash.
m.2.5.25.23: Likewise, O Lord, the son of Bhadrasena and the minister's son, Sudharma and Śubhakarma, always wore rudrākṣa beads.
m.2.5.25.24: By your grace those two, who in a former birth were a monkey and a cock adorned with Rudra's ornament rudrākṣa, having enjoyed true happiness here, became liberated.
m.2.5.25.25: Piṅgalā and Mahānandā, the two courtesans, attained the good state through devotion to you, O Lord intent on uplifting devotees.
m.2.5.25.26: Śāradā, a brahmin's daughter widowed in childhood, by the power of devotion to you became blessed with sons and marital good fortune.
m.2.5.25.27: Binduga, a brahmin in name only and a consorter with prostitutes, and his beloved Vañcukā, having heard your glory, attained the supreme state.
m.2.5.25.28: Thus and in other ways, many beings have attained perfection through the feeling of devotion to you, O Lord, O Maheśāna, friend of the afflicted, abode of compassion.
m.2.5.25.29: You are Brahman, beyond Prakṛti and beyond Puruṣa, O Supreme Lord; attributeless, the support of the three guṇas, having the nature of Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Hara.
m.2.5.25.30: You ever perform manifold works, yet are changeless, the Lord of all. We all, Brahmā and the rest, are your servants, O Maheśvara.
m.2.5.25.31: Be gracious, O Lord of gods; protect us always, O Śiva. We are your subjects, O Lord, and have ever taken refuge in you.
m.2.5.25.32: Sanatkumāra said: Having thus praised him, those gods headed by Brahmā, together with the chief sages, then fell silent, their minds fixed on Śiva's two feet.
m.2.5.25.33: Then Śambhu, the great Lord, having heard the auspicious hymn of the gods and granted excellent boons at once, vanished right there.
m.2.5.25.34: All the gods, headed by Brahmā, their enemy slain, joyful and pleased, went each to his own abode, singing Śiva's true glory.
m.2.5.25.35: This supreme narrative of the crushing of Jalandhara is a holy account of Maheśa's deeds, destroying great floods of sin.
m.2.5.25.36: This holy hymn of the gods destroys all sins, always grants every happiness, and gives delight to Maheśa.
m.2.5.25.37: Whoever reads or causes to be read this twofold narrative, having enjoyed supreme happiness here, will attain the status of a leader of Śiva's gaṇas.
m.2.5.25.iti: Thus ends the twenty-fifth adhyāya, named The description of the gods' hymn of praise, in the account of the slaying of Jalandhara, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.5.26.1: Vyāsa said: O son of Brahmā, salutations to you. You are blessed, O best of Śaiva devotees, for you have made me hear this most divine and auspicious story of Śaṅkara.
m.2.5.26.2: Now, O sage, kindly tell me the story of Viṣṇu: having deluded Vṛndā, what did he do, and where did he go?
m.2.5.26.3: Sanatkumāra said: Listen, O Vyāsa of great wisdom, foremost among Śaivas, most excellent one, to the very pure story of Viṣṇu, rich with the deeds of Śambhu.
m.2.5.26.4: When the gods headed by Brahmā had fallen silent, Maheśvara Śambhu, very pleased and loving towards those who seek refuge, spoke.
m.2.5.26.5: Śambhu said: O Brahmā and all you best of gods, for your sake I have slain Jalandhara, though he was a portion of myself — I speak the truth, the truth.
m.2.5.26.6: Dear ones, have you attained happiness or not? Tell me truly, O immortals. For it is for your sake that I, ever free from change, perform my sport.
m.2.5.26.7: Sanatkumāra said: Then the gods headed by Brahmā, their eyes wide with joy, bowed their heads to Rudra and reported what Viṣṇu had done.
m.2.5.26.8: The gods said: O Mahādeva, O god, you have protected us from the fear arising from the enemy. But something else has come up; what shall we do about it?
m.2.5.26.9: O Lord, Vṛndā was deliberately deluded by Viṣṇu; she quickly turned to ashes in the fire and attained the supreme state.
m.2.5.26.10: Infatuated by Vṛndā's beauty, Viṣṇu remains deluded, bearing the ashes of her pyre, bewildered by your māyā.
m.2.5.26.11: Though we, along with the hosts of Siddhas and sages, have earnestly tried to awaken him, Hari does not come to his senses, deluded as he is by your māyā.
m.2.5.26.12: Show compassion, O Maheśāna; awaken Viṣṇu, awaken him. All this material world, with its moving and unmoving beings, is subject to you.
m.2.5.26.13: Sanatkumāra said: Having heard these words of the heaven-dwellers, Maheśa, whose sport is great and who acts at his own will, replied to them as they stood with joined palms.
m.2.5.26.14: Maheśa said: O Brahmā, O all you gods, listen attentively to my words: my māyā, which deludes all the worlds, is hard to overcome.
m.2.5.26.15: The whole world — gods, demons and humans — is under her control. By her alone was Viṣṇu deluded; Hari became a slave to desire.
m.2.5.26.16: She is the great goddess called Umā, the supreme mother of the three gods, renowned as Primordial Nature (mūlaprakṛti), most lovely, embodied as Girijā.
m.2.5.26.17: Go, O gods, for the removal of Viṣṇu's delusion, and take refuge with the māyā called Śivā, the refuge-giving enchantress who grants all desires.
m.2.5.26.18: Offer to her, my Śakti, a hymn that will please her. If she is well pleased, she will accomplish the whole task.
m.2.5.26.19: Sanatkumāra said: Having said this to the gods, the five-faced lord Śambhu, Hara, quickly vanished, O Vyāsa, together with all his attendants.
m.2.5.26.20: And by Śambhu's command the gods headed by Brahmā, along with Indra, praised in their minds Primordial Nature, who is loving to her devotees.
m.2.5.26.21: The gods said: We bow to that Primordial Nature from whom arise the guṇas sattva, rajas and tamas, which bring about creation, preservation and destruction, and by whose will this universe unfolds its existence and dissolution.
m.2.5.26.22: Protect the twenty-three well-named principles, O Supreme one who presides over the entire world. We bow to that Primordial Nature whose forms and deeds even the three worlds do not know.
m.2.5.26.23: We bow ever to that Primordial Nature, loving to her devotees, through devotion to whom people never meet poverty, delusion, death, birth and the like.
m.2.5.26.24: Accomplish the task of us gods, O Mahādevī, O supreme Mistress. Remove Viṣṇu's delusion, O Śivā, O Durgā; O Devī, salutations to you.
m.2.5.26.25: O Śivā, when the battle had begun between Jalandhara and Śambhu, the dweller of Kailāsa, for the purpose of killing him, by Gaurī's command…
m.2.5.26.26: …Vṛndā was deliberately deluded by Viṣṇu, O Devī, and made to abandon her own virtue; she turned to ashes in the fire and attained her goal.
m.2.5.26.27: Jalandhara was slain in battle, and we were freed from fear of him by Giriśa, who showed compassion and bestows grace on his devotees.
m.2.5.26.28: By his command we have all come to you for refuge. For you and Śambhu — you two, O Devī, are devoted to uplifting your devotees.
m.2.5.26.29: Infatuated by Vṛndā's beauty, Viṣṇu remains there, bearing the ashes of her pyre, bereft of wisdom and deluded.
m.2.5.26.30: Though admonished by the hosts of perfected beings and gods, O Maheśvarī, Hari does not come to his senses, deluded by your māyā.
m.2.5.26.31: Show compassion, O Mahādevī; awaken Hari, awaken him, so that, his mind restored, he may protect his own world and accomplish the gods' work.
m.2.5.26.32: As the gods were praising thus, they saw there in the sky a sphere of light whose flames pervaded the space of the quarters.
m.2.5.26.33: From its midst, O Vyāsa, all the immortals headed by Brahmā, along with Indra, heard a wish-granting voice moving in the sky.
m.2.5.26.34: The heavenly voice said: It is I alone who, divided threefold by the three guṇas — rajas, sattva and tamas — abide as Gaurī, Lakṣmī and Surā, the Radiance.
m.2.5.26.35: Go there, all of you, respectfully into their presence. By my command, they, being pleased, will accomplish what you desire.
m.2.5.26.36: Sanatkumāra said: While the gods, their eyes wide with wonder, were hearing this speech, that radiance then vanished, O sage.
m.2.5.26.37: Then all those gods, having respectfully heard that utterance and urged on by it, bowed to Gaurī, Lakṣmī and Surā.
m.2.5.26.38: And all the gods headed by Brahmā, with heads bowed, praised those goddesses with great devotion in words of many kinds.
m.2.5.26.39: Then at once, O Vyāsa, those goddesses appeared before them, illuminating the expanse of the quarters with their own most wondrous radiance.
m.2.5.26.40: Then the immortals, seeing them, with hearts full of joy, bowed, praised them with devotion, and made known their own purpose.
m.2.5.26.41: Then these goddesses, affectionate to their devotees, seeing the gods bowed down, gave them seeds and spoke words to them respectfully.
m.2.5.26.42: The goddesses said: Sow these seeds there where Viṣṇu is staying; then your purpose will attain success.
m.2.5.26.43: Sanatkumāra said: Having said this, those goddesses then vanished, O sage — they were indeed the powers of Rudra, Viṣṇu and Brahmā, constituted of the three guṇas.
m.2.5.26.44: Then all the gods, Brahmā and the rest together with Indra, delighted, took those seeds and went to where Hari was staying.
m.2.5.26.45: Those gods scattered them on the ground of Vṛndā's funeral pyre, remembering those goddesses, portions of Śiva's śakti, who were present there, O sage.
m.2.5.26.46: From the seeds that were sown arose three plants: Dhātrī, Mālatī and Tulasī, O lord of sages.
m.2.5.26.47: Dhātrī is held to have arisen from Dhātrī Brahmā's śakti, Mālatī from Mā Lakṣmī, and Tulasī from Gaurī; they are the guṇas tamas, sattva and rajas.
m.2.5.26.48: Then, O sage, when Viṣṇu saw the plants in the form of women, an agitation of excessive passion for them arose in him.
m.2.5.26.49: Seeing them, he, out of delusion, with a mind attached to desire, solicited them; and Tulasī and Dhātrī too looked upon him with passion.
m.2.5.26.50: And the seed that had earlier been offered by Lakṣmī with mere illusion — the woman born from it became filled with jealousy toward him.
m.2.5.26.51: Hence she received the name Barbarī, which is greatly despised. Dhātrī and Tulasī, because of their love, are always pleasing to him.
m.2.5.26.52: Then that Viṣṇu, his grief forgotten, went together with the two of them to Vaikuṇṭha, pleased, saluted by all the gods.
m.2.5.26.53: In the month of Kārttika, O best of brahmins, Dhātrī and Tulasī should always be known as dear to all the gods, and especially to Viṣṇu.
m.2.5.26.54: Even among these, Tulasī is blessed and supremely excellent, O great sage; except for Gaṇeśa, she gives delight to all and grants all desires.
m.2.5.26.55: Seeing Hari established in Vaikuṇṭha, those immortals, Brahmā, Indra and the rest, bowed to and praised the great Viṣṇu and went each to his own abode.
m.2.5.26.56: Vaikuṇṭha Viṣṇu too, dwelling in his own world, his delusion gone and possessed of clear understanding, became happy, O best of sages, remembering Śiva as before.
m.2.5.26.57: Thus this narrative destroys masses of sin, grants all desires to men, removes all perturbations of desire, and increases all knowledge.
m.2.5.26.58: Whoever, devoted, recites this daily or has it recited, or hears it or causes it to be heard, attains the supreme state.
m.2.5.26.59: The wise hero who, having recited this most excellent narrative, enters battle will be victorious; there is no doubt.
m.2.5.26.60: This gives knowledge of Brahman to brahmins, victory to kṣatriyas, all wealth to vaiśyas, and happiness to śūdras.
m.2.5.26.61: O Vyāsa, it grants devotion to Śambhu, destroys the sins of all, and always bestows a good destiny in this world and the next.
m.2.5.26.iti: Thus ends the twenty-sixth adhyāya, named The description of the hymn to the Goddess after the slaying of Jalandhara and the dispelling of Viṣṇu's delusion, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.5.27.1: Sanatkumāra said: Now, O sage, listen with love to another account of Śambhu, by the mere hearing of which devotion to Śiva becomes firm.
m.2.5.27.2: It tells how the heroic Dānava named Śaṅkhacūḍa, a thorn to the gods, was slain by Śiva with the trident at the forefront of battle.
m.2.5.27.3: Listen, O Vyāsa, with great delight to that divine, purifying, sin-destroying account of Śambhu; I tell it to you out of deep affection.
m.2.5.27.4: The sage Kaśyapa, son of Marīci who was the son of the Creator, was most righteous, a maker of creation, instructed in sacred knowledge, a Prajāpati.
m.2.5.27.5: Dakṣa lovingly gave him thirteen of his own daughters. Their progeny, being very extensive, cannot be fully told.
m.2.5.27.6: From them the whole world, moving and unmoving, beginning with the gods, came into being. Who in the three worlds is able to relate that in detail?
m.2.5.27.7: Hear the account at hand, which is bound up with Śambhu's divine play; that alone I narrate today. Listen to it, for it increases devotion.
m.2.5.27.8: Among those wives of Kaśyapa, one was Danu, an excellent lady, extremely beautiful, virtuous, and blessed with her husband's favour.
m.2.5.27.9: That Danu had many exceedingly mighty sons; their names are not told, O sage, for fear of prolixity.
m.2.5.27.10: Among them was one, Vipracitti, of great strength and valour. His son was Dambha, righteous, a devotee of Viṣṇu, with senses subdued.
m.2.5.27.11: He had no heroic son, and so he became absorbed in anxiety. Making Śukrācārya his guru and obtaining the Kṛṣṇa mantra,
m.2.5.27.12: he performed supreme austerity at Puṣkara for a hundred thousand years; firmly fixing his posture, he repeated the Kṛṣṇa mantra for a long time.
m.2.5.27.13: As he performed austerity, a blazing radiance issued from his head and spread everywhere; that radiance was utterly unbearable.
m.2.5.27.14: Scorched by it, all the gods, the sages and likewise the Manus, placing Indra at their head, went to Brahmā for refuge.
m.2.5.27.15: Bowing to the Ordainer, giver of all riches, they praised him and, distressed, told him their situation in detail.
m.2.5.27.16: Hearing that, the Ordainer too went with them to Vaikuṇṭha to report it fully to Viṣṇu.
m.2.5.27.17: Having gone there, all of them, humbly, with joined palms, bowed to Viṣṇu, lord of the three worlds, the supreme protector, and praised him.
m.2.5.27.18: The gods said: O God of gods, we do not know what cause has arisen here. We have all become scorched; by whose radiance? Tell us that.
m.2.5.27.19: O friend of the afflicted, you are the protector of your dependents whose hearts are scorched. Protect, protect us, O Lord of Ramā; you are the refuge of those who seek shelter.
m.2.5.27.20: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing these words of the heaven-dwellers led by Brahmā, Viṣṇu, loving to those who seek refuge, smiled and spoke affectionately.
m.2.5.27.21: Viṣṇu said: Be at ease and untroubled; do not be afraid, O immortals. No calamities will occur; it is not the time of dissolution.
m.2.5.27.22: A Dānava named Dambha, my devotee, is performing austerity, desiring a son. I shall pacify him by granting a boon.
m.2.5.27.23: Sanatkumāra said: Thus addressed, O sage, all the gods led by Brahmā took courage and, reassured, went each to his own abode.
m.2.5.27.24: Acyuta too went to Puṣkara to grant the boon, where that Dānava named Dambha was performing austerity.
m.2.5.27.25: Having gone there, Hari, consoling with kind and pleasant words his devotee who was repeating his mantra, said: Ask for a boon.
m.2.5.27.26: Hearing Viṣṇu's words and seeing him standing before him, Dambha bowed with great devotion and praised him again and again.
m.2.5.27.27: Dambha said: O God of gods, lotus-eyed one, salutation to you. O Lord of Ramā, Lord of the three worlds, show me your grace.
m.2.5.27.28: Grant me a son devoted to you, of great strength and valour, a hero who conquers the three worlds and is invincible to the gods.
m.2.5.27.29: Sanatkumāra said: Thus addressed by the lord of Dānavas, Hari granted him that boon and, having made him desist from his fierce austerity, then vanished, O sage.
m.2.5.27.30: When Hari had gone, the lord of Dānavas bowed toward that direction and, his austerity fulfilled and his desire accomplished, went to his own home.
m.2.5.27.31: In a short time his fortunate wife became pregnant. She shone exceedingly with radiance, illuminating the interior of the house.
m.2.5.27.32: The cowherd named Sudāmā, foremost of Kṛṣṇa's attendants, entered her womb, because, O sage, he had been cursed by Rādhā.
m.2.5.27.33: Then in due time the virtuous lady bore a radiant son. The father, summoning many sages, duly performed the birth rite.
m.2.5.27.34: When he was born, O best of the twice-born, there was a very great festival. On an auspicious day his father named him Śaṅkhacūḍa.
m.2.5.27.35: He grew up in his father's house like the moon in the bright fortnight. Having mastered learning in childhood, he became very brilliant.
m.2.5.27.36: With his childish play he constantly spread joy to his parents, and he became dear to all, especially to the members of his family.
m.2.5.27.iti: Thus ends the twenty-seventh adhyāya, named The description of the birth of Śaṅkhacūḍa, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.5.28.1: Sanatkumāra said: Then that Śaṅkhacūḍa, following the instruction of Jaigīṣavya, performed austerities with great delight for a long time at Brahmā's Puṣkara.
m.2.5.28.2: With senses controlled, he repeated the Brahma-knowledge given by his guru, becoming single-minded and restraining his faculties.
m.2.5.28.3: To that Dānava Śaṅkhacūḍa, practising austerity at Puṣkara, Brahmā, the all-pervading teacher of the worlds, quickly went to grant a boon.
m.2.5.28.4: Then the Creator said to the lord of Dānavas, ask for a boon. Seeing him, Śaṅkhacūḍa bowed very humbly and praised him with fine words.
m.2.5.28.5: He asked Brahmā for the boon of being unconquerable by the gods. The Creator, with a well-pleased mind, said to him, so be it.
m.2.5.28.6: He gave Śaṅkhacūḍa the divine armour of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the most auspicious of auspicious things for the world, which grants victory everywhere.
m.2.5.28.7: Go to Badarī; there marry Tulasī. She is performing austerities there out of desire for a husband.
m.2.5.28.8: She is the daughter of Dharmadhvaja, so the Creator instructed him; and at that very moment he quickly vanished as Śaṅkhacūḍa looked on.
m.2.5.28.9: Then Śaṅkhacūḍa, perfected by austerity in the excellent Puṣkara, tied around his neck the armour, most auspicious for the world.
m.2.5.28.10: At Brahmā's command he too, his wish fulfilled through austerity, came swiftly with a joyful face to the Badarikā hermitage.
m.2.5.28.11: The Dānava Śaṅkhacūḍa came, as if by chance, to the place where Tulasī, daughter of Dharmadhvaja, was performing austerities.
m.2.5.28.12: Beautiful, sweetly smiling, slender, adorned with fine ornaments, she looked with sidelong glances at that very excellent man.
m.2.5.28.13: Seeing her, graceful, charming, well-mannered, beautiful and chaste, he stayed near her and spoke to her sweetly.
m.2.5.28.14: Śaṅkhacūḍa said: Who are you? Whose daughter are you? What are you doing, staying here? Why are you silent? You should honour me, your servant, here with a reply.
m.2.5.28.15: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing these words, she spoke to him, who was full of desire.
m.2.5.28.16: Tulasī said: I am the daughter of Dharmadhvaja, an ascetic woman performing austerities, and I dwell in this penance-grove. Who are you? Go as you please.
m.2.5.28.17: Womankind is bewitching, like poison even to Brahmā and the others; blameworthy, a cause of faults, an illusion, and indeed a fetter for those attached to them.
m.2.5.28.18: Sanatkumāra said: Having spoken thus charmingly to him, Tulasī fell silent. Seeing her smiling, he too began to speak.
m.2.5.28.19: Śaṅkhacūḍa said: O goddess, what you have said is not all false; some is true and some false. Hear the rest from me.
m.2.5.28.20: Among women devoted to their husbands, you are the foremost. I am not a lustful man with sinful gaze, and neither are you sinful—such is my view.
m.2.5.28.21: I come to you now at Brahmā's command. O lovely one, I shall take you by the Gāndharva form of marriage.
m.2.5.28.22: I am Śaṅkhacūḍa himself, the one who puts the gods to flight. Do you not know me, good lady? Have you never heard of me?
m.2.5.28.23: I am a Dānava of Danu's lineage, specifically the son of Dambha. Formerly I was the cowherd named Sudāmā, an attendant of Hari.
m.2.5.28.24: Now, through Rādhikā's curse, I am the lord of the Dānavas. I remember my former birth and know everything by Kṛṣṇa's power.
m.2.5.28.25: Sanatkumāra said: Having spoken thus, Śaṅkhacūḍa fell silent before her. Addressed by the Dānava lord with these true words respectfully, Tulasī, pleased, began to speak with a smile.
m.2.5.28.26: Tulasī said: Now I have been defeated by you through your judgement of truth. Blessed in the world is the man who is not conquered by a woman.
m.2.5.28.27: The man who is conquered by a woman is ever impure, even if he performs good rites; the ancestors, the gods and all humans censure him.
m.2.5.28.28: A brāhmaṇa becomes pure in ten days after birth- or death-impurity, a kṣatriya in twelve days, a vaiśya in fifteen days.
m.2.5.28.29: A śūdra becomes pure in a month—such is the Vedic injunction. But a man conquered by a woman is never pure anywhere, except by burning on the funeral pyre.
m.2.5.28.30: Therefore the ancestors do not willingly accept his rice-ball offerings and libations, nor do the gods accept flowers, fruits and the like given by him.
m.2.5.28.31: What use to him are knowledge, good austerity, japa, fire-offerings and worship? What use are learning or charity to one whose mind has been stolen by women?
m.2.5.28.32: I tested you to know the power of your learning. A woman should choose her husband only after testing her beloved.
m.2.5.28.33: Sanatkumāra said: While Tulasī was speaking thus, at that moment Brahmā, the Creator, came there and then spoke these words.
m.2.5.28.34: Brahmā said: O Śaṅkhacūḍa, why are you conversing with her? Take her by the Gāndharva form of marriage.
m.2.5.28.35: You are a jewel among men, and this chaste lady is a jewel among women. The union of a clever woman with a clever man is surely virtuous.
m.2.5.28.36: O king, who would give up unobstructed happiness that is hard to obtain? He who renounces happiness free from conflict is a beast—no doubt about it.
m.2.5.28.37: O chaste one, why do you test such a virtuous beloved, the crusher of gods, asuras and Dānavas?
m.2.5.28.38: O beautiful one, sport with him for a very long time, always, in place after place as you wish, throughout all the worlds.
m.2.5.28.39: In the end he will again attain Śrī Kṛṣṇa in Goloka; and when he has died, you will attain the four-armed Viṣṇu in Vaikuṇṭha.
m.2.5.28.40: Sanatkumāra said: Having given this blessing, Brahmā went to his own abode, and the Dānava took her as wife by the Gāndharva form of marriage.
m.2.5.28.41: Having thus married Tulasī, he went to his father's place. He delighted there together with her, beautiful as Ramā, in a charming dwelling-house.
m.2.5.28.iti: Thus ends the twenty-eighth adhyāya, named The description of Śaṅkhacūḍa's austerities and marriage, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.5.29.1: Sanatkumāra said: When that Śaṅkhacūḍa, having performed penance and obtained a boon, had married and returned to his own home, the Dānavas and the others rejoiced.
m.2.5.29.2: Quickly setting out from their own world, accompanied by their preceptor, all the Asuras gathered together and came to his presence.
m.2.5.29.3: Having bowed to him humbly and praised him with manifold respect, they remained right there with great affection, regarding him as a radiant, mighty lord.
m.2.5.29.4: He too, the son of Dambha, seeing that family preceptor arrived, bowed to him with great devotion, prostrating with all eight limbs, with the highest reverence.
m.2.5.29.5: Then Śukra, the family preceptor, having looked upon him, bestowed an unsurpassed blessing and then narrated the history of the gods and the Dānavas.
m.2.5.29.6: He told of that natural enmity, the defeat of the Asuras, the victory of the gods, and the help given by Jīva (Bṛhaspati).
m.2.5.29.7: Then the preceptor, having obtained the consent of all the Asuras, with a grand festival made him the overlord of the Dānavas and other Asuras.
m.2.5.29.8: Then there was a great celebration among the joyful Asuras, and all of them gladly gave him presents.
m.2.5.29.9: Then the heroic and valourous Śaṅkhacūḍa, son of Dambha, having received the royal consecration, shone forth as king of the Asuras.
m.2.5.29.10: Leading a vast army of Daityas, Dānavas and Rākṣasas, he mounted his chariot and went swiftly to conquer Indra's city.
m.2.5.29.11: As he went, that lord of the Dānavas shone amid those attending on him like the moon among the stars, like the king of planets among the planets.
m.2.5.29.12: Hearing that Śaṅkhacūḍa was approaching, Ākhaṇḍala (Indra), king of heaven, along with all the immortals, made ready to fight him.
m.2.5.29.13: Then a tumultuous battle took place between the Asuras and the gods, delighting the heroes, frightening the cowards, making the hair stand on end.
m.2.5.29.14: A great uproar arose from the heroes roaring in battle, and there was also the sound of musical instruments, increasing heroism.
m.2.5.29.15: The gods, enraged and being the stronger, fought with the Asuras; the Asuras suffered defeat and fled in fear.
m.2.5.29.16: Seeing them fleeing, lord Śaṅkhacūḍa himself fought with the gods, roaring a lion's roar.
m.2.5.29.17: Swiftly and suddenly he made a slaughter of the heaven-dwellers; all the gods fled, unable to bear his great splendour.
m.2.5.29.18: Wretched, they stayed here and there, even in mountain caves, subject to him and not independent, lustreless like stilled oceans.
m.2.5.29.19: That valiant, mighty son of Dambha, lord of the Dānavas, having conquered all the worlds, seized the offices of the gods.
m.2.5.29.20: He brought the three worlds under his control, and the sacrificial shares in their entirety; he himself even became Indra, and the whole world was ruled by him.
m.2.5.29.21: By his own power he exercised the offices of Kubera, the Moon, the Sun, Agni, Yama and Vāyu.
m.2.5.29.22: Of the gods, Asuras, Dānavas and Rākṣasas, of the Gandharvas, Nāgas, Kinnaras and the dwellers of Rasātala —
m.2.5.29.23: — of the three worlds and of all others, that great hero Śaṅkhacūḍa of immense strength became the supreme lord.
m.2.5.29.24: Thus the great Śaṅkhacūḍa, emperor over kings, enjoyed sovereignty over all the worlds for many years.
m.2.5.29.25: In his kingdom there was no famine, no plague, no inauspicious planets, no mental or bodily ailments at all, and the people were always happy.
m.2.5.29.26: The earth, yielding crops without tilling, gave grain in abundance; and the various herbs were always fruitful and full of sap.
m.2.5.29.27: The mines abounded in gems, the oceans were mines of jewels, the trees always bore flowers and fruits, and the rivers carried excellent water.
m.2.5.29.28: Except for the gods, all beings were happy and free from affliction; all others, people of the four varṇas and āśramas, abided in their respective dharma.
m.2.5.29.29: While he ruled the three worlds, no one was unhappy; only the immortals were distressed, owing to their fraternal enmity.
m.2.5.29.30: That mighty Śaṅkhacūḍa was the supreme friend of Kṛṣṇa, the dweller in Goloka — a virtuous one, ever devoted to Kṛṣṇa.
m.2.5.29.31: Through the force of a former curse he had taken birth in a Dānava womb; yet, O sage, even as a Dānava he did not have a Dānava's mind.
m.2.5.29.32: Then all the hosts of gods, defeated and robbed of their kingdom, having taken counsel together with the sages, went, dear one, to Brahmā's assembly.
m.2.5.29.33: There, seeing the Creator, they bowed and praised him especially, and in distress told Brahmā the whole account.
m.2.5.29.34: Then Brahmā, having consoled all the gods and the sages, went with them to the world of Vaikuṇṭha, which gives happiness to the good.
m.2.5.29.35: There Brahmā, with the hosts of gods, saw the Lord of Lakṣmī, wearing a crown and earrings, adorned with a garland of forest flowers,
m.2.5.29.36: the four-armed god holding conch, discus, mace and lotus, clad in yellow garments, attended by Sanandana and other Siddhas.
m.2.5.29.37: Seeing Viṣṇu, all the gods headed by Brahmā, together with the chief sages, bowed and, with joined palms, praised the Lord with devotion.
m.2.5.29.38: O God of gods, Lord of the universe, ruler of Vaikuṇṭha, O master, protect us who have come to you for refuge, O Śrī Hari, preceptor of the three worlds.
m.2.5.29.39: You alone are the protector of the worlds, O Lord of the three worlds, O Acyuta, O master; O abode of Lakṣmī, Govinda, life of your devotees — salutations to you.
m.2.5.29.40: Having praised thus, all the gods wept before Hari. Hearing that, Lord Viṣṇu said this to Brahmā.
m.2.5.29.41: Viṣṇu said: Why have you come to Vaikuṇṭha, which is hard even for yogins to reach? What trouble has arisen for you? Tell me that, here before me.
m.2.5.29.42: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing these words of Hari, Brahmā bowed again and again, joined his palms together, and with his neck bent in humility,
m.2.5.29.43: he then narrated, before Viṣṇu the Supreme Self, the account of what Śaṅkhacūḍa had done, a full telling of the gods' distress.
m.2.5.29.44: Having heard his words, the Lord Hari, who knows the nature of all things in every respect, smiled and spoke that secret to Vidhi (Brahmā).
m.2.5.29.45: The Lord said: O lotus-born one, I know the whole story of Śaṅkhacūḍa, who formerly was a cowherd, my devotee, of great splendour.
m.2.5.29.46: Listen to that whole account, an ancient history. No doubt should be entertained: Śaṅkara will bring about well-being.
m.2.5.29.47: Above all is his Śivaloka, higher than the highest, where Śambhu shines, the Supreme Brahman, the Supreme Lord,
m.2.5.29.48: who is the presiding ruler of Prakṛti and of Puruṣa as well, bearer of the three powers; he is both without attributes and with attributes, the supreme light possessing form.
m.2.5.29.49: O Brahmā, from his body were born the three who bring about creation and the rest, endowed with the qualities sattva and the others, named Viṣṇu, Brahmā and Hara.
m.2.5.29.50: That very Supreme Self sports there together with Umā, free from Māyā, the creator of the eternal and the non-eternal.
m.2.5.29.51: Near it is Goloka, the cow-pen of Śaṅkara. By his will Kṛṣṇa, who is of my form, dwells there.
m.2.5.29.52: Commanded by him to protect his cows, he is ever happy; having obtained happiness from that, he too, skilled in pastimes, sports there.
m.2.5.29.53: His consort is renowned as Rādhā, mother of the world, the supreme embodiment of Prakṛti, the fifth form, delighting in pastimes.
m.2.5.29.54: Many cowherds and cowherdesses live there, born from their bodies, ever devoted to delightful pastimes, followers of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa.
m.2.5.29.55: That very one cowherd, deluded now by this Māyā through Śambhu's play, has needlessly, because of a curse, obtained a demonic birth that brings him sorrow.
m.2.5.29.56: His death by Rudra's trident was ordained long ago by Kṛṣṇa. Then, abandoning his body, he will become an attendant of Śiva.
m.2.5.29.57: Knowing this, O lord of the gods, you should not be afraid. Go to Śaṅkara for refuge; he will at once bring about well-being.
m.2.5.29.58: I, you, and all the gods — let us remain here free from fear.
m.2.5.29.59: Sanatkumāra said: Having said this, Viṣṇu, together with Vidhi, went to Śivaloka, remembering in his mind Śambhu, the Lord of all, loving to his devotees.
m.2.5.29.iti: Thus ends the twenty-ninth adhyāya, named The description of Śaṅkhacūḍa's rule of the kingdom, followed by the description of the story of what happened in his previous birth, in the account of the slaying of Śaṅkhacūḍa, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.5.30.1: Sanatkumāra said: Then, O Vyāsa, Rameśvara (Viṣṇu), together with Vidhi (Brahmā), going at once to Śivaloka, which is supremely divine, needs no support and is not made of material elements,
m.2.5.30.2: Viṣṇu, full of joy and with a delighted face, went inside that world, which was set all around with many kinds of gems, glittering and intensely radiant.
m.2.5.30.3: Reaching the first gate, wondrous, attended by the gaṇas, adorned with supreme splendour, very lofty and exceedingly beautiful,
m.2.5.30.4: he saw the gatekeepers seated on jewelled thrones, resplendent in white garments and adorned with jewelled ornaments,
m.2.5.30.5: five-faced and three-eyed, with fair and handsome bodies, heroes bearing tridents and other weapons, shining with sacred ash and rudrākṣa beads.
m.2.5.30.6: Brahmā and Rameśa (Viṣṇu), humbly bowing to them, explained the matter, namely their purpose of seeing the Lord.
m.2.5.30.7: They gave him permission, and by their permission he entered the next gate, very delightful, wondrous and supremely radiant.
m.2.5.30.8: To that gatekeeper he reported the matter, with the aim of going into the Lord's presence; and permitted by him, he entered another gate.
m.2.5.30.9: Having thus passed through fifteen gates, the lotus-born (Brahmā) came to the great gate, and there he saw Nandin.
m.2.5.30.10: Having duly bowed to him and praised him, and being permitted, as before, by that Nandin, Viṣṇu slowly and joyfully went inside.
m.2.5.30.11: Going there, he saw the lofty assembly-hall of Śambhu, brilliantly radiant, surrounded by attendants with shining bodies and well adorned,
m.2.5.30.12: attendants having the very form of Maheśvara: ten-armed, of auspicious lustre, five-faced, three-eyed, blue-throated, greatly radiant,
m.2.5.30.13: adorned with ornaments of rudrākṣa set with fine gems and with sacred ash. The hall was shaped like the orb of the new moon, square and charming,
m.2.5.30.14: beautified with necklaces made of the finest gems and with choice diamonds, built of priceless jewels and adorned with lotus petals,
m.2.5.30.15: variegated with festoons of ruby lattices and many kinds of decorations, fashioned of the finest rubies, wondrous by Śaṅkara's will,
m.2.5.30.16: furnished with hundreds of steps made of Syamantaka gems, and with lovely sandal sprays tied with knots of golden thread,
m.2.5.30.17: encircled by pillars of sapphire, most charming, well arranged everywhere and perfumed by fragrant breezes,
m.2.5.30.18: a thousand yojanas in extent and filled with many servants. There Viṣṇu, lord of the gods, saw Śaṅkara together with Ambā,
m.2.5.30.19: dwelling in the centre like the moon surrounded by stars, seated on a wondrous throne made of priceless jewels,
m.2.5.30.20: wearing a crown and earrings, adorned with a jewelled garland, his whole body smeared with ash, holding a lotus for play,
m.2.5.30.21: watching with a smile and with delight the singing and dancing before him,
m.2.5.30.22: tranquil, of serene mind, the beloved of Umā, greatly exultant, chewing betel given by the Goddess, fragrantly perfumed,
m.2.5.30.23: served with supreme devotion by the gaṇas with white fly-whisks, and being praised by the Siddhas whose necks were bowed in devotion,
m.2.5.30.24: Śiva, beyond the guṇas, the supreme lord, father of the three gods, all-pervading, free of mental constructs, formless, yet taking form by his own will,
m.2.5.30.25: free of māyā, unborn, primordial, master of māyā, higher than the highest, beyond both Prakṛti and Puruṣa, ever his own lord.
m.2.5.30.26: Seeing him thus distinguished, most perfectly complete and impartial, Viṣṇu and Brahmā bowed with joined palms and praised him.
m.2.5.30.27: Viṣṇu and Brahmā said: O God of gods, O Mahādeva, O supreme Brahman, O lord of all, O you who are beyond the three guṇas, untroubled, father of the three gods, O Lord,
m.2.5.30.28: we have come to you for refuge. Protect us, O all-pervading one, who are distressed, tormented and afflicted by Śaṅkhacūḍa, yet have you as our protector, O supreme Lord.
m.2.5.30.29: This world that is presided over by you is known as Goloka. Its ruler, the mighty Kṛṣṇa here, is himself under your authority.
m.2.5.30.30: His foremost attendant Sudāmā, impelled by fate and cursed by Rādhā, then became the Dānava Śaṅkhacūḍa.
m.2.5.30.31: Driven out by him, O Śambhu, oppressed on all sides and stripped of their offices, the gods wander on the earth.
m.2.5.30.32: Without you he cannot be slain by any of the dwellers of heaven. Slay him, O Maheśāna, and bring happiness to the worlds.
m.2.5.30.33: You alone are without qualities, the truth, infinite, of infinite valour; you are also with qualities and the abode of all, beyond Prakṛti and Puruṣa.
m.2.5.30.34: Through rajas, at the time of creation, you are Brahmā the creator, O Lord; through sattva, in preservation, you are Viṣṇu, the protector of the three worlds;
m.2.5.30.35: through tamas, at dissolution, you are Rudra, the destroyer of the world; in the state beyond the three guṇas you are called Śiva, the Fourth, whose nature is light.
m.2.5.30.36: By your ordinance in Goloka you are the protector of the cows, and Kṛṣṇa, dwelling amid your cowsheds, plays day and night.
m.2.5.30.37: You are the cause of all, the master, the supreme lord of Vidhi (Brahmā) and Viṣṇu, changeless, the eternal witness, the supreme Self, the highest lord.
m.2.5.30.38: You are the helper of the wretched and the helpless, the protector of the afflicted, the friend of the distressed, lord of the three worlds, loving toward those who seek refuge.
m.2.5.30.39: Rescue us, O lord of Gaurī; be gracious, O supreme Lord. We depend on you, O Master; do as you wish.
m.2.5.30.40: Sanatkumāra said: O Vyāsa, having spoken thus, those two gods, Hari and Brahmā, then fell silent, having bowed to Śiva with joined palms, humble as they were.
m.2.5.30.iti: Thus ends the thirtieth adhyāya, named The hymn to the God of gods, in the slaying of Śaṅkhacūḍa, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.5.31.1: Sanatkumāra said: Then, having heard the words of the deeply distressed Hari and Brahmā, Śambhu, laughing, spoke in a voice as deep as the rumbling of clouds.
m.2.5.31.2: Śiva said: O Hari, dear child, O Brahmā, give up entirely the fear arising from Śaṅkhacūḍa. Good will come about, without doubt.
m.2.5.31.3: I know in truth the whole story of Śaṅkhacūḍa, who formerly was the cowherd Sudāman, a devotee of Kṛṣṇa, O lord.
m.2.5.31.4: By my command Hṛṣīkeśa, having assumed the form of Kṛṣṇa, dwelt in the cowshed in lovely Goloka, which is presided over by me.
m.2.5.31.5: Formerly, thinking of himself, I am independent, he fell into delusion; deluded, he performed many sports as if acting at his own will.
m.2.5.31.6: Seeing him thus, I deluded him intensely by my own māyā; withdrawing their good sense, I caused a curse to be pronounced, indeed.
m.2.5.31.7: Having thus performed my sport, I withdrew that māyā. Then they became endowed with knowledge, freed from delusion, of sound understanding.
m.2.5.31.8: They came near me, humbled, bowed to me, and, meek with joined palms, offered fine praise with devotion.
m.2.5.31.9: With minds agitated by shame they told the whole story; wretched, before me they spoke the words, protect, protect.
m.2.5.31.10: Then I, Bhava, being pleased, spoke these words to them: O Kṛṣṇa, give up fear, all of you, by my command.
m.2.5.31.11: I am ever your protector out of love; great good will be yours. All this has happened by my will, there is no doubt.
m.2.5.31.12: Go to your own abode together with Rādhā and the attendant. But this one will become a Dānava here in Bhārata, no doubt.
m.2.5.31.13: I shall surely bring about the release from the curse for you two in due time. Holding my words thus on his head, together with Rādhā,
m.2.5.31.14: the wise Śrī Kṛṣṇa rejoiced greatly and went to his own abode. The two remained there with fear, intent on worshipping me,
m.2.5.31.15: considering everything as dependent on me and themselves as not independent. That Sudāman, through Rādhā's curse, became the lord of the Dānavas,
m.2.5.31.16: named Śaṅkhacūḍa, an enemy of the gods, though versed in dharma. That evil-minded one constantly oppresses the entire host of gods with great force.
m.2.5.31.17: Deluded by my māyā, he has very wicked ministers as his helpers. Therefore give up that fear quickly, since I am the chastiser.
m.2.5.31.18: Sanatkumāra said: While Śiva was thus telling the story before Hari and Brahmā, meanwhile another event took place; hear that, O sage.
m.2.5.31.19: At that very moment Kṛṣṇa came with Rādhā, his attendants and good cowherds, to propitiate the lord Śambhu.
m.2.5.31.20: Having bowed to the Lord with true devotion and having respectfully met Hari, and being welcomed with affection by Brahmā, he stood there at Śiva's command.
m.2.5.31.21: Then, bowing again to Śambhu with joined palms, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, freed from delusion and having understood Śiva's true nature, praised him.
m.2.5.31.22: Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: O God of gods, Mahādeva, Supreme Brahman, refuge of the good, forgive my offence; be gracious, O Supreme Lord.
m.2.5.31.23: From you, O Śarva, is everything, and everything is in you, O Maheśvara; you are everything, O lord of all; be gracious, O Supreme Lord.
m.2.5.31.24: You are manifestly the supreme light, all-pervading, eternal. With you as our master, O lord of Gaurī, all of us are protected.
m.2.5.31.25: Thinking myself above all, I sported and fell into delusion. I have reaped its fruit: I received a curse, together with my beloved.
m.2.5.31.26: My foremost attendant, the cowherd named Sudāman, has, through Rādhā's curse, O master, entered a Dānava birth.
m.2.5.31.27: Uplift us, O lord of Durgā; be gracious, O Supreme Lord. Bring about the release from the curse today; protect us who have come for refuge.
m.2.5.31.28: Having said this, Śrī Kṛṣṇa fell silent together with Rādhā. Then Śiva, kind to those who seek refuge, became pleased.
m.2.5.31.29: Śrī Śiva said: O Kṛṣṇa, lord of the gopīs, give up fear and be happy. All this, dear one, was done by me in order to show favour.
m.2.5.31.30: Good will come to you; go to your excellent abode. You should always remain attentive in your own office.
m.2.5.31.31: Sport as you wish, knowing me to be higher than the highest. Do your own work undisturbed, together with Rādhā and your attendants.
m.2.5.31.32: In the excellent Vārāha kalpa, he, together with young Rādhā, having undergone the effect of the curse, will return to his own abode.
m.2.5.31.33: Sudāman, your attendant, O Kṛṣṇa, dearest of the dear, having entered a Dānava birth, now torments the world.
m.2.5.31.34: Through the power of Rādhā's curse he is an enemy of the gods, a Dānava named Śaṅkhacūḍa, a strong partisan of the Daityas, hostile to the gods.
m.2.5.31.35: By him the gods, including Indra, have been driven out and constantly oppressed; stripped of their offices and miserable, they have all gone off in the ten directions.
m.2.5.31.36: For that very reason Brahmā and Acyuta have come here to me for refuge. I shall free them from their distress; there is no doubt about this.
m.2.5.31.37: Sanatkumāra said: Having said this to Kṛṣṇa, Śaṅkara again respectfully addressed Hari and Brahmā and spoke words that destroy distress.
m.2.5.31.38: Śiva said: O Hari, O Brahmā, listen with love to these words of mine. Go quickly, dear ones, without fear, for the joy of the gods,
m.2.5.31.39: to Rudra who dwells on Kailāsa, who is my own form, complete and supreme, manifested for the gods' purpose and bearing a separate shape.
m.2.5.31.40: For this very purpose the Lord, my own form, most perfect, abides on Mount Kailāsa, under the sway of his devotees, O Hari.
m.2.5.31.41: There is no difference between me and you; he alone is to be served by you both, and always by all moving and unmoving beings and by the gods and others.
m.2.5.31.42: Whoever makes a distinction between us two, that man goes to hell; even here he suffers hardship, deprived of sons and grandsons.
m.2.5.31.43: Having bowed again and again to the lord of Durgā who had spoken thus, Kṛṣṇa, together with Rādhā and with his attendants, went to his own abode.
m.2.5.31.44: O Vyāsa, Hari and Brahmā, both joyful and freed from fear, bowed again and again to the Lord and quickly went to Vaikuṇṭha.
m.2.5.31.45: Having arrived there and reported the whole event to the gods, those two, Brahmā and Viṣṇu, taking them along, went to Mount Kailāsa.
m.2.5.31.46: There, having seen Maheśāna, the Lord, beloved of Pārvatī, who had assumed a body to protect the distressed, endowed with attributes, the leader of the gods,
m.2.5.31.47: they all praised him as before with devotion, in a voice choked with emotion, with joined palms, bowed shoulders, and full of humility.
m.2.5.31.48: The gods said: O God of gods, Mahādeva, lord of Girijā, Śaṅkara, we have come to you for refuge; protect the gods who are distraught with fear.
m.2.5.31.49: Slay Śaṅkhacūḍa, lord of the Dānavas, the destroyer of the gods; by him the gods have been tormented and defeated in battle.
m.2.5.31.50: Deprived of their positions, they wander on the earth like men; indeed, out of fear of him, the world of the gods has become hard for them even to behold.
m.2.5.31.51: O uplifter of the distressed, ocean of compassion, O Maheśāna, rescue the gods from this crisis, and Śakra from fear, by slaying that lord of the Dānavas.
m.2.5.31.52: Having heard these words of the gods, Śambhu, affectionate to his devotees, smiling, spoke in a voice deep as the rumble of clouds.
m.2.5.31.53: Śrī Śaṅkara said: O Hari, O Vidhi, O gods, go to your own abodes without worry; I shall slay Śaṅkhacūḍa together with his followers—there is no doubt of this.
m.2.5.31.54: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing these nectar-like words of Maheśa, they all became joyful, regarding the Dānava as already destroyed.
m.2.5.31.55: Then Hari went to Vaikuṇṭha and Vidhi to Satyaloka; and having bowed to Maheśa, the gods and others went to their own stations.
m.2.5.31.iti: Thus ends the thirty-first adhyāya, named Śiva's instruction, in the slaying of Śaṅkhacūḍa, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.5.32.1: Sanatkumāra said: Then Īśāna, the great Rudra, who is death to the wicked and the refuge of the good, resolved in his mind on the slaying of Śaṅkhacūḍa, in accordance with the wish of the gods.
m.2.5.32.2: Making Citraratha, the esteemed lord of the Gandharvas, his messenger, he gladly and swiftly dispatched him to Śaṅkhacūḍa.
m.2.5.32.3: At the command of the Lord of all, that messenger went to his city, which surpassed the city of great Indra and excelled the abode of Kubera.
m.2.5.32.4: Having gone there, he saw in its midst the splendid palace of Śaṅkhacūḍa, adorned with twelve gates and furnished with gatekeepers.
m.2.5.32.5: Having seen it, Puṣpadanta saw the principal gate and fearlessly told the gatekeeper the purpose of his coming.
m.2.5.32.6: Passing through that gate, he gladly went inside, into a place exceedingly beautiful, delightful, spacious and well adorned.
m.2.5.32.7: Going on, he saw that Śaṅkhacūḍa, lord of the Dānavas, seated on a jewelled throne in the midst of a circle of heroes.
m.2.5.32.8: He was surrounded by Dānava chiefs and attended by three crores of them, and by a hundred crores of others moving about with weapons in hand.
m.2.5.32.9: Seeing him thus, Puṣpadanta, filled with wonder, related the message about battle that Śaṅkara had spoken.
m.2.5.32.10: Puṣpadanta said: O king of kings, I am Śiva's messenger named Puṣpadanta, O lord. Listen to what Śaṅkara himself has said; I tell it to you.
m.2.5.32.11: Śiva said: Give back now the kingdom and the rightful offices of the gods; if not, then fight a battle with me, the Supreme Lord of the good.
m.2.5.32.12: The gods have sought refuge in me, Śaṅkara, lord of the gods and of the good. Angered, I, the great Rudra, shall slay you without doubt.
m.2.5.32.13: I am Hara; I have granted freedom from fear to all the gods. I am indeed the bearer of the rod of punishment for the wicked, and loving to those who come for refuge.
m.2.5.32.14: Will you give back the kingdom, or will you wage battle? Consider well, O lord of the Dānavas, and tell me truly which one of the two.
m.2.5.32.15: Puṣpadanta said: What Maheśa said thus to you, I have conveyed. Śambhu's word is never false, O lord of the Dānavas.
m.2.5.32.16: I wish to return quickly to my own master Hara. Tell me here what I should say to Śambhu when I go.
m.2.5.32.17: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing these words of Puṣpadanta, the messenger of Śiva, lord of the good, the king laughed and spoke to him.
m.2.5.32.18: Śaṅkhacūḍa said: I will not give the kingdom to the gods; the earth is to be enjoyed by heroes. I shall give you battle, O Rudra, partisan of the gods.
m.2.5.32.19: The hero against whom another marches first is the lowest in the world. Therefore, O Rudra, I shall march against you first, without doubt.
m.2.5.32.20: Considering the heroes' march, I shall come at dawn. Go, and tell Rudra these words of mine.
m.2.5.32.21: Hearing these words of Śaṅkhacūḍa, Śambhu's messenger laughed heartily and spoke to the proud lord of the Dānavas.
m.2.5.32.22: Puṣpadanta said: O king of kings, you are not fit to stand even before the other attendants (gaṇas) of Śaṅkara—how much less before him.
m.2.5.32.23: So give back to the gods all their offices entirely, and go quickly to Pātāla if you wish to live.
m.2.5.32.24: Do not regard him as an ordinary god, O best of Dānavas. Śaṅkara is indeed the Supreme Self, the Lord of the lords of all.
m.2.5.32.25: All the gods headed by Indra always abide by his command, as do the Prajāpatis, the Siddhas, the sages and the lords of serpents.
m.2.5.32.26: He is the master of Hari and of Brahmā; he is both without attributes and with attributes. By the mere knitting of his brow the dissolution of all would occur.
m.2.5.32.27: He is the full form of Śiva, the bringer of the world's destruction, the refuge of the good, the slayer of the wicked, changeless, higher than the highest.
m.2.5.32.28: He is the overlord of Brahmā and the great lord of Hari as well. His command, O bull among Dānavas, must never be disregarded.
m.2.5.32.29: What use is saying much, O king of kings? Reflecting well in your mind, know Rudra, Maheśāna, to be the supreme Brahman, whose nature is consciousness.
m.2.5.32.30: Give back the kingdom and all the offices of the gods entirely. Thus it will be well with you, dear friend; otherwise there will be danger.
m.2.5.32.31: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing this, the mighty Śaṅkhacūḍa, lord of the Dānavas, deluded by what was destined to be, spoke to that messenger of Śiva.
m.2.5.32.32: Śaṅkhacūḍa said: Of my own accord I will not give up the kingdom, nor the offices—this is my firm resolve—without a battle with Maheśa. This I tell you truly.
m.2.5.32.33: The whole world, with its moving and unmoving beings, should be understood as subject to Time. Everything comes into being from Time and perishes through Time.
m.2.5.32.34: Go to Śaṅkara, Rudra, and tell him faithfully what I have said. Let him then do what is fitting; do not prolong the talk.
m.2.5.32.35: Sanatkumāra said: Thus addressed, that messenger of Śiva, Puṣpadanta, went to his own master and reported everything exactly as it was, O good sage.
m.2.5.32.iti: Thus ends the thirty-second adhyāya, named The going of the messenger, in the slaying of Śaṅkhacūḍa, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.5.33.1: Sanatkumāra said: Then, having heard those words of the messenger, Giriśa, the sovereign of the gods, spoke in anger to Vīrabhadra and the other gaṇas.
m.2.5.33.2: Rudra said: O Vīrabhadra, O Nandin, O Kṣetrapālas and eight Bhairavas, all you gaṇas, armed, bearing weapons and endowed with strength,
m.2.5.33.3: let them go forth today by my command, together with the two Kumāras; and let Bhadrakālī go forth for battle with her own army. I myself am setting out swiftly today for the slaying of Śaṅkhacūḍa.
m.2.5.33.4: Sanatkumāra said: Having thus given the command, the great Lord set out accompanied by the army; all the heroic gaṇas, greatly delighted, followed him.
m.2.5.33.5: Meanwhile Skanda and Gaṇeśa, leaders of the whole army, joyful, armored and bearing weapons, went to Śiva's side.
m.2.5.33.6: Vīrabhadra and Nandī, Mahākāla, Subhadraka, Viśālākṣa and Bāṇa, Piṅgalākṣa, Vikampana,
m.2.5.33.7: Virūpa and Vikṛti, Maṇibhadra and Bāṣkala, the one named Kapila, Dīrghadaṃṣṭra, Vikara, Tāmralocana,
m.2.5.33.8: Kālaṅkara, Balībhadra, Kālajihva, Kuṭīcara, Balonmatta, Raṇaślāghya, Durjaya and likewise Durgama —
m.2.5.33.9: These and others were the lords of the gaṇas, excellent commanders of the armies. I shall tell their count; listen attentively.
m.2.5.33.10: Śaṅkhakarṇa, crusher of foes, was accompanied by a crore of gaṇas; Kekarākṣa by ten crores, and Vikṛta by eight.
m.2.5.33.11: Viśākha with sixty-four, Pāriyātrika with nine, the glorious Sarvāntaka with six, and likewise Vikṛtānana.
m.2.5.33.12: Jālaka, the foremost of gaṇas, with twelve crores; the glorious Samada with seven, and Dundubha with eight.
m.2.5.33.13: Karālākṣa with five, the excellent Sandāraka with six; and here Kanduka and likewise Kuṇḍaka with crores upon crores.
m.2.5.33.14: Viṣṭambha, a gaṇa-leader best of all, with eight; Pippala with a thousand, and Sannāda likewise.
m.2.5.33.15: Āveśana likewise with eight, Candratāpana with eight, and the gaṇa-leader Mahākeśa surrounded by a thousand crores.
m.2.5.33.16: Kuṇḍī with twelve heroes, and likewise the auspicious Parvataka; Kāla and Kālaka, and Mahākāla with a hundred.
m.2.5.33.17: Agnika with a hundred crores, Agnimukha with a crore, Āditya with half a crore, and likewise Ghanāvaha.
m.2.5.33.18: Sannāha with a hundred, Kumuda likewise with crores; Amogha, Kokila, and Sumantraka with a hundred crores.
m.2.5.33.19: Kākapāda with sixty crores, Santānaka likewise with sixty, Mahābala with nine, and Madhupiṅgala with five.
m.2.5.33.20: Nīla, a lord among gods, with ninety, and likewise Pūrṇabhadra; and the mighty Caturvaktra with seven crores.
m.2.5.33.21: Likewise, with hundreds and twenties of thousands of crores of crores, all those heroes came there to the festival of battle.
m.2.5.33.22: Vīrabhadra came with a thousand crores of bhūtas, three crores of pramathas, sixty-four crores, and three crores of the Lomajas.
m.2.5.33.23: Kāṣṭhārūḍha with sixty-four, Sukeśa and Vṛṣabha likewise, and the blessed, eternal Virūpākṣa with sixty-four.
m.2.5.33.24: Tālaketu, Ṣaḍāsya, the valiant Pañcāsya, Saṃvartaka, likewise Caitra, and Laṅkulīśa, the lord himself;
m.2.5.33.25: Lokāntaka of blazing self, and likewise the lord Daityāntaka; the glorious god Bhṛṅgīriṭi, beloved of the God of gods,
m.2.5.33.26: Aśani and Bhānuka with sixty-four thousands; Kaṅkāla, Kālaka, Kāla, Nandī, and likewise Sarvāntaka.
m.2.5.33.27: These and other innumerable, mighty gaṇa-leaders went forth gladly and fearlessly to fight with Śaṅkhacūḍa.
m.2.5.33.28: All were thousand-handed, wearing crowns of matted hair, adorned with the crescent moon, blue-throated and three-eyed.
m.2.5.33.29: All were adorned with rudrākṣa ornaments and wore sacred ash, decorated with necklaces, earrings, armlets, crowns and the like.
m.2.5.33.30: Resembling Brahmā, Indra and Viṣṇu, endowed with powers such as aṇimā, radiant like a crore of suns, skilled in the work of war.
m.2.5.33.31: Some moved on the earth, some in the netherworld, some in the sky, and some in the seven heavens, O sage.
m.2.5.33.32: What need of saying more, O divine sage? All Śiva's gaṇas, dwelling in all the worlds, went to fight with the Dānavas.
m.2.5.33.33: The eight fierce Bhairavas and the eleven Rudras swiftly, the eight Vasus, Vāsava (Indra), and the twelve Ādityas quickly went.
m.2.5.33.34: Hutāśana (Agni) and Candra, Viśvakarmā and the two Aśvins, Kubera and Yama, Nirṛti and Nalakūbara,
m.2.5.33.35: Vāyu and Varuṇa, Budha and Maṅgala, and the other planets, along with Maheśa, and the valiant Kāmadeva,
m.2.5.33.36: Ugradaṃṣṭra and Ugradaṇḍa, Koraṭa and likewise Koṭabha; and the hundred-armed goddess Bhadrakālī herself, the great sovereign,
m.2.5.33.37: seated upon a celestial chariot made of the finest gems, clad in red garments, with red garlands and red unguents,
m.2.5.33.38: dancing, laughing, and singing sweetly with joy, she gave fearlessness to her own and fear to the enemies,
m.2.5.33.39: bearing a dreadful, playfully moving tongue a yojana long, and conch, discus, mace, lotus, sword, shield, bow and arrows,
m.2.5.33.40: She bore a skull-bowl, round in shape, deep and a yojana wide; a trident touching the sky, and a spear a yojana long;
m.2.5.33.41: a hammer, a pestle-club, a thunderbolt, a sword, a formidable shield, the Vaiṣṇava missile, the Vāruṇa missile, the Vāyavya missile, the serpent-noose,
m.2.5.33.42: the Nārāyaṇa missile, the Gāndharva, the Brahmā missile and likewise the Gāruḍa, the Pārjanya and the Pāśupata, the Jṛmbhaṇa missile and the Pārvata,
m.2.5.33.43: the Mahāvīra and the Saura, the Kālakāla, the Mahānala, the Māheśvara missile and the Yāmya, the Daṇḍa and likewise the Sammohana,
m.2.5.33.44: and the potent divine missile, and a hundred other supreme divine missiles — bearing these and others as well in all her hands, she then
m.2.5.33.45: came and stood there with three crores of yoginīs, together with three crores of fearsome ḍākinīs.
m.2.5.33.46: Bhūtas, pretas and piśācas, kūṣmāṇḍas, brahmarākṣasas, vetālas and rākṣasas, and yakṣas along with kinnaras also came.
m.2.5.33.47: Surrounded by them, Skanda, having bowed to the moon-crested Śiva, stayed at his father's side as his helper, by his command.
m.2.5.33.48: Then Śambhu, Rudra, having gathered his entire army, fearlessly went forth to battle with Śaṅkhacūḍa.
m.2.5.33.49: On the bank of the river Candrabhāgā, at the foot of a charming banyan tree, there Mahādeva stationed himself for the deliverance of the gods.
m.2.5.33.iti: Thus ends the thirty-third adhyāya, named The description of Mahādeva's march to battle, in the slaying of Śaṅkhacūḍa, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.5.34.1: Vyāsa said: O dear son of Brahmā, O sage of great intellect, may you live for many years. You have narrated the very great and wonderful story of the moon-crested Śiva.
m.2.5.34.2: When Śiva's messenger had gone from there, what did that mighty Dānava Śaṅkhacūḍa do? Tell me this truly and in full detail.
m.2.5.34.3: Sanatkumāra said: Then, when the messenger had gone, the mighty Śaṅkhacūḍa went into the inner apartment and told Tulasī that news.
m.2.5.34.4: Śaṅkhacūḍa said: O goddess, having heard from the mouth of Śambhu's messenger, I am ready for battle. Therefore I am going to fight; surely give me your leave.
m.2.5.34.5: Having spoken thus and consoled his beloved with many kinds of counsel, that wise one sported joyfully with her, disregarding Śaṅkara.
m.2.5.34.6: That couple sported through the night, immersed in an ocean of bliss, with various arts of love and with hundreds of endearing words.
m.2.5.34.7: Rising at the Brāhma-muhūrta, he performed the morning rites, and having first done his daily duties, he gave limitless gifts.
m.2.5.34.8: He made his son the sovereign king over all the Dānavas, and entrusted to his son his wife, the kingdom and all its wealth.
m.2.5.34.9: The king again comforted his beloved, who was weeping and trying to prevent his departure, telling her many things.
m.2.5.34.10: Summoning his own heroic commander-in-chief, he, honoured by all, armed and eager to wage war, gave him orders.
m.2.5.34.11: Śaṅkhacūḍa said: O commander, today let all the heroes skilled in war, fully equipped for every action, march out to battle.
m.2.5.34.12: Let the valiant Daityas and Dānavas, eighty-six clans with weapons raised, and the armies of the mighty Kaṅkas quickly march out, fearless.
m.2.5.34.13: Let fifty clans of Asuras, of immense valour (koṭi-vīrya), march out indeed to fight with Śambhu, the partisan of the gods.
m.2.5.34.14: And let a hundred clans of the Dhaumras, armed, quickly march out by my command to battle with Śambhu.
m.2.5.34.15: Let the Kālakeyas, Mauryas, Daurhṛdas and likewise the Kālakas, ready for war, march out by my command to fight with Rudra.
m.2.5.34.16: Sanatkumāra said: Having given these orders, the very mighty lord of the Asuras, king of the Dānavas, marched out with a great army, surrounded by many thousands.
m.2.5.34.17: His commander too was expert in the science of war, a great chariot-warrior, a great hero, the foremost of chariot-fighters in battle.
m.2.5.34.18: Accompanied by three lakh akṣauhiṇīs, he arranged the troops in a circular array, and, terrifying to heroes in battle, he came out of the camp.
m.2.5.34.19: Mounting an aerial chariot made of the finest jewels and placing his elders in front, he set out for battle, it is said.
m.2.5.34.20: On the bank of the river Puṣpabhadrā, where stands the auspicious undecaying banyan, at the Siddhāśrama—the field of attainment of the Siddhas, bestowing great success—
m.2.5.34.21: which is the abode of Kapila, in the holy land of Bhārata, east of the western ocean and west of Malaya,
m.2.5.34.22: in the region north of Śrīśaila and south of Gandhamādana, five yojanas in breadth and a hundred times that in length.
m.2.5.34.23: There flows the lovely river Puṣpabhadrā, resembling pure crystal, bestowing great merit in Bhārata, full of water, a form of Sarasvatī,
m.2.5.34.24: the beloved wife of the salt ocean, ever endowed with good fortune, joined with the Sarasvatī; she issues from the Himālaya.
m.2.5.34.25: Keeping Gomanta on her left, she enters the western ocean. Having gone there, Śaṅkhacūḍa saw the army of Śiva.
m.2.5.34.iti: Thus ends the thirty-fourth adhyāya, named The description of Śaṅkhacūḍa's march, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.5.35.1: Sanatkumāra said: Staying there, the lord of the Dānavas made a great and very wise Dānava chief his messenger and sent him to Śaṅkara.
m.2.5.35.2: The messenger went there and saw the moon-browed Lord seated at the foot of a banyan tree, shining like ten million suns.
m.2.5.35.3: He was seated in a yogic posture, with a gesture (mudrā) of the gaze, smiling, resembling pure crystal, blazing with the splendour of Brahman.
m.2.5.35.4: Holding a trident and a paṭṭiśa, clad in a tiger-skin garment, remover of death for his devotees, tranquil, the beloved of Gaurī, the three-eyed one;
m.2.5.35.5: the giver of the fruits of austerities, the bestower of all riches, quickly pleased, of gracious face, granting favour to his devotees;
m.2.5.35.6: the lord of the universe, its seed, having the universe as his form, the source of the universe, the ruler of the universe, its maker, and the cause of its dissolution;
m.2.5.35.7: the cause of causes, the one who carries beings across the ocean of hell, the giver of knowledge, the seed of knowledge, the bliss of knowledge, the eternal one.
m.2.5.35.8: Seeing him, the messenger, that Dānava chief, got down from his chariot and bowed his head to Śaṅkara together with Kumāra.
m.2.5.35.9: He bowed also to Bhadrakālī on the left and to Skanda standing in front of him. Kālī, Skanda and Śaṅkara gave him the customary blessings.
m.2.5.35.10: Then that messenger of Śaṅkhacūḍa, a supreme knower of the scriptures, bowing to Śaṅkara with joined hands, spoke auspicious words.
m.2.5.35.11: The messenger said: I am Śaṅkhacūḍa's messenger, come here into your presence. What is your wish now? Tell me that, O Maheśvara.
m.2.5.35.12: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing these words of Śaṅkhacūḍa's envoy, Śaṅkara, the blessed Mahādeva, with a gracious mind, spoke to him.
m.2.5.35.13: Mahādeva said: Listen, O very wise messenger, to my words, which bring happiness. Having reflected, this should be told to him without dispute.
m.2.5.35.14: Brahmā, the creator of the worlds, is the father of Dharma and the knower of dharma. Marīci is his son, and Kaśyapa is known as Marīci's son.
m.2.5.35.15: Dakṣa lovingly gave him thirteen of his own daughters. Among them one was the virtuous Danu, who increased his good fortune.
m.2.5.35.16: Danu had four sons, the Dānavas, mighty in splendour. Among them one, Vipracitti, was of great strength and valour.
m.2.5.35.17: His son was the righteous Dambha, a Dānava lord of great intellect. You are his excellent son, a righteous-souled lord of the Dānavas.
m.2.5.35.18: Formerly you were an attendant, a cowherd, righteous among the cowherds. Now, through Rādhikā's curse, you have been born as the lord of the Dānavas.
m.2.5.35.19: You have come into a Dānava birth, but in truth you are not a Dānava. Knowing your own former history, give up enmity with the gods now.
m.2.5.35.20: Do not act with hostility towards them; enjoy your own position respectfully. Having reflected, do not make your rule excessive or disorderly.
m.2.5.35.21: Give the kingdom of the gods back, O Dānava, and preserve my goodwill. Remain happily in your own kingdom, and let the gods remain in their own places.
m.2.5.35.22: Enough of hostility towards beings—how much more towards the gods. All of you born in Kaśyapa's line are noble and pure in deeds.
m.2.5.35.23: Whatever sins there are, such as killing a brahmin, they are not equal to a sixteenth part of the sin born of hostility towards one's kinsmen.
m.2.5.35.24: Sanatkumāra said: Śaṅkara spoke to him these and many other auspicious words grounded in Śruti and Smṛti, imparting supreme knowledge.
m.2.5.35.25: That messenger, instructed by Śaṅkhacūḍa, foremost of logicians, bewildered by what was destined, spoke humbly.
m.2.5.35.26: The messenger said: O god, what you have said is not otherwise; that speech is so. Yet hear my submission, which is somewhat true and to the point.
m.2.5.35.27: The great sin in hostility towards kinsmen which you have just spoken of—is it, O Lord, only for the asuras and not for the gods? Tell me, O master.
m.2.5.35.28: If you say it applies to all, then I will speak after reflection. Give your verdict on that today and dispel my doubt.
m.2.5.35.29: Why, O Maheśvara, did the discus-bearer Viṣṇu cut off the heads of Madhu and Kaiṭabha, the foremost of Daityas, in the ocean of dissolution?
m.2.5.35.30: Why did you, O Giriśa, wage battle with the Tripuras and reduce them to ashes? It is well known that you are a partisan of the gods.
m.2.5.35.31: Why was Bali, after all his possessions were taken, sent off to Sutala and the other nether worlds, with the mace-bearer Viṣṇu at his door to raise him up?
m.2.5.35.32: How was Hiraṇyākṣa, together with his brother, slain by the gods? And how were Śumbha and the other asuras struck down by the gods?
m.2.5.35.33: Formerly, at the churning of the ocean, the nectar was consumed by the gods. We had our share of the toil there, but they all enjoyed the fruit.
m.2.5.35.34: This universe is the plaything of Time, the Supreme Self. When he grants it to someone, then sovereignty becomes his.
m.2.5.35.35: The enmity between gods and Dānavas is perpetual and ever occasioned by circumstance. Their defeat and victory depend on Time, in due succession.
m.2.5.35.36: Your going to intervene in the conflict of these two would be fruitless. That befits those who are related equally to both, not you, the Lord.
m.2.5.35.37: For you, the great-souled Lord of all gods and asuras, this present rivalry with us is devoid of shame.
m.2.5.35.38: For for us there is greater glory in victory and loss in defeat; for you it is the reverse. Let this be considered carefully in your mind.
m.2.5.35.39: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing these words, the three-eyed one laughed heartily and spoke fittingly and sweetly to the Dānava chief.
m.2.5.35.40: Maheśa said: We are dependent on our devotees and never independent. Acting by their wish, we take no one's side.
m.2.5.35.41: Long ago, at the request of Vidhi (Brahmā), even Hari first fought a battle with Madhu and Kaiṭabha, the foremost of the Daityas, in the ocean of cosmic dissolution.
m.2.5.35.42: Long ago, at the request of the gods, the slaying of Hiraṇyakaśipu was carried out by him, the benefactor of devotees, for Prahlāda's sake.
m.2.5.35.43: At the request of the gods, I too long ago waged battle with the Tripuras and then reduced them to ashes; this has been heard by all.
m.2.5.35.44: Long ago, at the request of the gods, there was a battle of the all-sovereign Mother of all with Śumbha and the others, and their slaying was accomplished by her.
m.2.5.35.45: Even now all the thirty gods went to Brahmā for refuge; and he, with the gods and the god Hari, came to me for refuge.
m.2.5.35.46: And so, O messenger, compelled by the entreaty of Hari, Brahmā and the others, I, the lord of the gods, have indeed come for battle.
m.2.5.35.47: For you are the foremost attendant of the great-souled Kṛṣṇa; of all the Daityas who have been slain, none at all were your equal.
m.2.5.35.48: What great shame is there for me, O king, in a battle with you? I, the Lord, have been sent humbly for the sake of the gods' cause.
m.2.5.35.49: Go to Śaṅkhacūḍa, and my words are to be told to him. Let him do here what is fitting; I shall do the gods' work.
m.2.5.35.50: Having spoken thus, Śaṅkara, the great Lord, fell silent there. The messenger of Śaṅkhacūḍa rose and went into his master's presence.
m.2.5.35.iti: Thus ends the thirty-fifth adhyāya, named The dialogue of Śiva's messenger, in the slaying of Śaṅkhacūḍa, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.5.36.1: Sanatkumāra said: That messenger went there and delivered Śiva's message in full and accurately, conveying his resolve exactly as it was.
m.2.5.36.2: Hearing that, Śaṅkhacūḍa, the mighty lord of the Dānavas, gladly accepted nothing but battle.
m.2.5.36.3: Swiftly he mounted his chariot together with his ministers, and ordered his own army to battle with Śaṅkara.
m.2.5.36.4: Śiva swiftly urged on his own army and the gods; and he himself, the Lord of all, playfully made ready for battle.
m.2.5.36.5: The battle began at once; musical instruments sounded in great numbers; an uproar arose, and likewise the cries of heroes.
m.2.5.36.6: O sage, a battle broke out between the gods and the Dānavas; there the hosts of gods and Dānavas fought according to the rules of righteous combat.
m.2.5.36.7: Mahendra himself fought with Vṛṣaparvan; Bhāskara (the Sun) fought righteously with Vipracitti.
m.2.5.36.8: Viṣṇu waged a supreme battle with Dambha; Kāla with Kālāsura, and Hutāśana (Fire) with Gokarṇa.
m.2.5.36.9: Kubera fought with Kālakeya, Viśvakarman with Maya, Mṛtyu with Bhayaṅkara, and likewise Yama with Saṃhāra.
m.2.5.36.10: Varuṇa fought with Kālambika, Samīraṇa (Wind) with Cañcala, Budha with Ghaṭapṛṣṭha, and Śanaiścara (Saturn) with Raktākṣa.
m.2.5.36.11: Jayanta fought with Ratnasāra, the Vasus with the hosts of Varcas, the two Aśvins with the two Dīptimats, and Nalakūbara with Dhūmra.
m.2.5.36.12: Dharma fought with Dhurandhara, Maṅgala (Mars) with Gaṇakākṣa, Vaiśvāna with Śobhākara, and Manmatha with Pipiṭa.
m.2.5.36.13: With Gokāmukha, with Cūrṇa, with the asura named Khaḍga, with Dhūmra, with Saṃhala, and with the mighty Viśva—
m.2.5.36.14: —and with Palāśa, the twelve Ādityas fought righteously. Other immortals, endowed with Śiva's support, fought with the asuras.
m.2.5.36.15: The eleven great Rudras fought with eleven fearsome heroic asuras of great strength and valour.
m.2.5.36.16: Mahāmaṇi fought with Ugracaṇḍa and others; Candra (the Moon) with Rāhu, and Jīva (Jupiter) righteously with Śukra.
m.2.5.36.17: Nandīśvara and all the others fought in the great battle with the foremost Dānavas; they are not described separately in detail.
m.2.5.36.18: Then Śambhu stayed at the foot of a banyan tree with Kālī's son, and all the masses of troops fought ceaselessly, O sage.
m.2.5.36.19: And Śaṅkhacūḍa, adorned with jewelled ornaments, sat on a lovely jewelled throne, surrounded by millions of Dānavas.
m.2.5.36.20: Then a great battle took place, crushing gods and asuras; various divine weapons flew about in that great fight.
m.2.5.36.21: Maces, double-edged swords, spears, discuses, bhuśuṇḍis, lances, hammers, swords, arrows, iron bars, śaktis, unmukhas and battle-axes—
m.2.5.36.22: arrows, javelins and swords, śataghnīs by the thousands, bhindipālas and others besides shone in the hands of the heroes.
m.2.5.36.23: With these the heroes there, in great exultation, cut off the heads of the roaring warriors of both armies in the battle.
m.2.5.36.24: Many elephants, horses, chariots and foot-soldiers, of various kinds, together with riders and mounts, lay there cut to pieces.
