m.2.5.55.6: Then, with his horses held by Kumbhāṇḍa as charioteer and bearing many kinds of weapons and missiles, the mighty son of Bali waged an incomparable battle.
m.2.5.55.7: Seeing his own army destroyed, that lord of the Daityas, exceedingly enraged — the mighty son of Bali — waged an incomparable battle.
m.2.5.55.8: Śrī Kṛṣṇa too, the great hero, whose great strength was obtained from Giriśa, roared loudly there in the battle, regarding Bāṇa as a mere blade of grass.
m.2.5.55.9: He twanged his own wonderful bow named Śārṅga, terrifying what remained of Bāṇa's army, O lord of sages.
m.2.5.55.10: By that great sound born of the twang of the bow, the space between heaven and earth was at once completely filled.
m.2.5.55.11: Enraged, Hari then drew the bow to his ear and hurled at Bāṇa various sharp arrows resembling venomous serpents.
m.2.5.55.12: Seeing them coming, Bāṇa, the son of Bali, cut them down before they reached him, with his own arrows released from his bow.
m.2.5.55.13: Again that mighty Bāṇa, crusher of hosts of enemies, roared; all the Vṛṣṇis, devoted to Kṛṣṇa, trembled, bewildered.
m.2.5.55.14: Remembering the lotus feet of Śiva, the very proud son of Bali hurled his own arrows at the exceedingly valiant Kṛṣṇa.
m.2.5.55.15: Kṛṣṇa too, the mighty one, swiftly cut them down with his own arrows before they reached him, remembering the lotus feet of Śiva.
m.2.5.55.16: Rāma and the other mighty Vṛṣṇis, all aroused and filled with anger, struck down each his own opponent in the battle.
m.2.5.55.17: Thus for a very long time there took place there a tumultuous battle between the two mighty ones, astonishing to those who hear of it.
m.2.5.55.18: At that moment the king of birds Garuḍa, becoming exceedingly angry, crushed the entire army of the asura Bāṇa with blows of his wings.
m.2.5.55.19: Seeing his army crushed and him crushing it, the mighty son of Bali, foremost of Śaivas and lord of the sons of Diti, became extremely enraged.
m.2.5.55.20: Remembering the lotus feet of Śiva, he, possessed of a thousand arms, swiftly displayed great prowess, unbearable to his enemies.
m.2.5.55.21: That slayer of heroes simultaneously hurled countless arrows there, separately at each of the Yadus beginning with Kṛṣṇa, and at Garuḍa.
m.2.5.55.22: With one arrow the mighty one struck Garuḍa, with one Kṛṣṇa, with one Bala Balarāma, O sage, and likewise the others too.
m.2.5.55.23: Then Kṛṣṇa, of great valour, a form of Viṣṇu and slayer of the gods' enemies, became exceedingly angry in that battle, and the great lord roared.
m.2.5.55.24: Remembering Śaṅkara, he forcefully struck Bāṇa with excellent arrows shot from the Śārṅga, and at the same time his extremely fierce army.
m.2.5.55.25: Unperturbed, Hari quickly cut his bow, his parasol and the rest, and, killing his horses with his own arrows, felled them.
m.2.5.55.26: Bāṇa too, the great hero, roared, greatly enraged, and struck Kṛṣṇa with his mace; he fell to the ground.
m.2.5.55.27: Then Kṛṣṇa, quickly rising, fought with that enemy, the devotee of Śiva, O divine sage, in keeping with worldly play.
m.2.5.55.28: Thus for a long time there was a very great battle between the two: Hari-Kṛṣṇa, a form of Śiva, and he Bāṇa, the mighty, foremost of Śaivas.
m.2.5.55.29: Then the valiant Kṛṣṇa, having fought with Bāṇa for a long time and having gained strength by Śiva's command, became exceedingly angry, O lord of sages.
m.2.5.55.30: Then the blessed Kṛṣṇa, slayer of enemy heroes, swiftly cut off Bāṇa's many arms with the Sudarśana, at the command of Śambhu.
m.2.5.55.31: Four of his arms remained, exceedingly beautiful; and by the grace of Śaṅkara he quickly became free of pain.
m.2.5.55.32: When Bāṇa had lost consciousness and Kṛṣṇa, filled with heroic fervour, was ready to cut off his head, then Rudra arose.
m.2.5.55.33: Rudra said: O blessed son of Devakī, what I commanded earlier has been done by you, O Viṣṇu, who always carry out my command.
m.2.5.55.34: Do not cut off Bāṇa's head; withdraw the Sudarśana. By my command, withdraw this unfailing discus; it is always to be held back in regard to my devotee.
m.2.5.55.35: Formerly I gave you the discus, irresistible in your battles, and victory too, O Govinda; therefore withdraw from the battle.
m.2.5.55.36: Against Dadhīci, against the hero Rāvaṇa, and against Tāraka and the three cities too, O lord of Lakṣmī, you did not formerly release the discus without my command.
m.2.5.55.37: You indeed are the lord of yogis, the Supreme Self in person, O Janārdana, devoted to the welfare of all beings; consider this in your own mind.
m.2.5.55.38: I gave him a boon that he would have no fear of death; that word of mine is ever true. I am fully pleased with you.
m.2.5.55.39: Formerly this one, proud and intoxicated with arrogance, said to me, give me battle, scratching his itching arms and forgetful of his own true state, O Hari.
m.2.5.55.40: Then I cursed him: One who will cut off your arms will come; before long you will be stripped of your pride.
m.2.5.55.41: By my command Hari came here as the severer of your arms. Now, therefore, withdraw from the battle; go to your own home with the bride and bridegroom.
m.2.5.55.42: Having spoken thus, Maheśvara brought about friendship between the two, and, taking leave of him, went to his own abode with his attendants and his sons.
m.2.5.55.43: Sanatkumāra said: Having heard these words of Śambhu and having withdrawn the Sudarśana discus, Kṛṣṇa, victorious and with body unhurt, then went to the inner apartments.
m.2.5.55.44: Having comforted Aniruddha, who was again united with his wife, he accepted the many heaps of jewels given by Bāṇa.
m.2.5.55.45: Taking also her friend Citralekhā, the supreme yoginī, Kṛṣṇa then became pleased, his task accomplished by Śiva's command.
m.2.5.55.46: Bowing in his heart to Giriśa and bidding farewell to the son of Bali, Hari, accompanied by his retinue, went to his own city.
m.2.5.55.47: On the way, having conquered Varuṇa, who opposed him in many ways, he reached the city of Dvārakā, amid great festivity.
m.2.5.55.48: Having dismissed Garuḍa, and having looked upon his friends and laughed with them, he then, going into Dvārakā, roamed about as he pleased.
m.2.5.55.iti: Thus ends the fifty-fifth adhyāya, named The cutting off of Bāṇa's arms and the removal of his pride, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.5.56.1: Nārada said: When Kṛṣṇa had gone to Dvārakā with Aniruddha and his wife, what did Bāṇa do after that? Tell me the truth, O great sage.
m.2.5.56.2: Sanatkumāra said: When Kṛṣṇa had gone to Dvārakā with Aniruddha and his wife, Bāṇa then became grief-stricken, recalling in his heart his own ignorance.
m.2.5.56.3: Then Nandī, Śiva's attendant, spoke to the grieving demon Bāṇa, whose limbs were smeared with blood and who was filled with remorse.
m.2.5.56.4: Nandīśvara said: O Bāṇa, true devotee of Śaṅkara, do not grieve with remorse, sir. Śambhu is indeed compassionate to devotees and bears the name Affectionate to Devotees.
m.2.5.56.5: Whatever has happened, it happened by his will—consider it so in your mind, O tiger among devotees, and remember Śiva again and again.
m.2.5.56.6: Fixing your mind on the Primal One, celebrate a great festival constantly; for this Śaṅkara is compassionate to devotees again and again.
m.2.5.56.7: Then, at Nandī's words, Bāṇa—reduced by the enemy almost to his head alone—gathered his courage and, great-minded, quickly went to Śiva's abode.
m.2.5.56.8: Having gone there and bowed to the Lord, Bāṇa, all his pride gone, his mind overwhelmed with love, wept, greatly agitated.
m.2.5.56.9: Praising him with various hymns, bowing down with praises likewise, stamping his feet as was fitting and flinging out his arms,
m.2.5.56.10: he danced the principal Tāṇḍava, adorned with the pratyālīḍha and other postures, and with stances of various forms headed by the ālīḍha.
m.2.5.56.11: He made thousands of mouth-sounds together with movements of the brows, and thousands of shakings of the head, displaying arrays of gestures by the thousands.
m.2.5.56.12: Displaying slowly, step by step, dance movements of various kinds, and likewise drenching the ground with streams of blood,
m.2.5.56.13: the asura Bāṇa, the great devotee, bowing and forgetful of his own state, propitiated Rudra, the trident-bearer, the moon-crested.
m.2.5.56.14: Then, the great dance having been performed, the Lord Hara, affectionate to devotees and fond of dance and song, delighted, spoke to Bāṇa.
m.2.5.56.15: Rudra said: O Bāṇa, dear son of Bali, I am pleased with your dancing. Choose a boon, O lord of demons, whatever is in your mind.
m.2.5.56.16: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing these words of Śambhu, O sage, the demon-lord Bāṇa then chose as a boon the healing of his wounds,
m.2.5.56.17: and prowess in arm-to-arm combat, and then imperishable leadership of the gaṇas, and kingship for Uṣā's son in that city called Śoṇitaka;
m.2.5.56.18: freedom from enmity with the gods, and especially with Viṣṇu; and never again the wicked demon-nature joined with rajas and tamas;
m.2.5.56.19: especially, devotion to Śambhu, ever unchanging, O sage; affection for Śiva's devotees, and compassion toward all creatures.
m.2.5.56.20: Having thus obtained these boons from Śambhu, the great asura, son of Bali, his eyes filled with tears of love, palms reverently joined, praised Rudra.
m.2.5.56.21: Bāṇa said: O God of gods, Mahādeva, loving to those who seek refuge, I bow to you, O great Lord, friend of the lowly, ocean of compassion.
m.2.5.56.22: Great mercy has been shown to me, O Śaṅkara, ocean of mercy; all my pride has been taken away by you, being gracious, O Lord.
m.2.5.56.23: You are indeed Brahman, the Supreme Self, all-pervading, Lord of all; your body is the cosmic egg, O fierce Lord; you are Virāṭ, containing all, the Supreme.
m.2.5.56.24: The sky is your navel, fire your mouth, water your semen, the quarters your ears; heaven is your head, the earth your feet, and the moon is your mind, O Lord.
m.2.5.56.25: The sun is your eye, the ocean your belly, Indra your arms, Vidhi (Brahmā) Your intellect, Prajāpati your organ of procreation, and Dharma indeed is your heart.
m.2.5.56.26: The plants are your body-hairs, O Lord, the clouds your hair; the three guṇas are your three eyes; you are the Person, the Self of all.
m.2.5.56.27: They call the brāhmaṇa your mouth and the kṣatriya your arm; they call the vaiśya born of your thighs and the śūdra born of your feet.
m.2.5.56.28: You alone are always to be worshipped by all beings, O Maheśvara; worshipping you, a person surely attains supreme liberation.
m.2.5.56.29: The mortal who abandons you—the beloved Self and Lord—for the sake of perverse sense-objects, drinks poison, rejecting nectar.
m.2.5.56.30: Viṣṇu, Brahmā, the gods, and the sages of pure heart have taken refuge with their whole being in you, Śaṅkara, the beloved Lord.
m.2.5.56.31: Sanatkumāra said: Having spoken thus, the son of Bali, the asura Śara (Bāṇa), his limbs thrilling with love, bowed to Maheśvara and fell silent.
m.2.5.56.32: Hearing this from his devotee Bāṇa, Lord Bhava said, you shall obtain everything, and vanished right there.
m.2.5.56.33: Then, by Śambhu's grace, Bāṇa attained the status of Mahākāla; as Rudra's attendant he became exceedingly joyful.
m.2.5.56.34: Thus indeed has been told here, in words pleasing to the ear, this most excellent account of the one named Śara (Bāṇa) together with Śaṅkara—the trident-bearer, the true guru of all gurus, who eternally sports in the midst of all the worlds.
m.2.5.56.iti: Thus ends the fifty-sixth adhyāya, named Bāṇāsura attains the rank of a lord of the gaṇas, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.5.57.1: Sanatkumāra said: Listen, O Vyāsa, with great love, to the deed of the moon-crested Śiva: how he slew with his trident Gajāsura, the lord of the Dānavas.
m.2.5.57.2: Formerly, when the Dānava Mahiṣāsura had been slain in battle by the Goddess for the welfare of the gods, the gods attained happiness.
m.2.5.57.3: His son, O lord of sages, was the great hero Gajāsura; he remembered the slaying of his father, carried out by the Goddess at the request of the gods.
m.2.5.57.4: Recalling that enmity, he went to the forest for austerity, and, with Brahmā (Vidhi) as his aim, he performed supreme austerity with devotion.
m.2.5.57.5: I shall be unslayable by men and women who are conquered by desire — having thus reflected in his mind, he became one whose mind was absorbed in austerity.
m.2.5.57.6: He performed most terrible austerity in a valley of the Himālaya, arms raised upward, gaze fixed on the sky, touching the earth only with his big toes.
m.2.5.57.7: With his masses of matted locks he shone like the sun at the dissolution with its rays — this noble-minded Gajāsura, son of Mahiṣāsura.
m.2.5.57.8: From his head arose a smoky fire born of austerity, which, spreading in all directions, scorched the worlds across, above and below.
m.2.5.57.9: Because of the fire arising from his head, the rivers and oceans were agitated, the stars fell along with the planets, and the ten directions blazed.
m.2.5.57.10: Scorched by it, all the gods together with Indra (Vāsava) left heaven and went to Brahmaloka and reported: The earth is shaking.
m.2.5.57.11: The gods said: O Vidhi, scorched by Gajāsura's austerity we are distressed; we cannot remain in heaven, therefore we have come to you for refuge.
m.2.5.57.12: O Vidhi, bring about his pacification so that the others may live; otherwise the worlds will perish — truly, truly we say this.
m.2.5.57.13: Thus petitioned by the gods headed by Indra, the self-born Brahmā, with Bhṛgu, Dakṣa and others, went to the hermitage of the foremost Daitya.
m.2.5.57.14: Seeing him scorching the worlds with austerity, like the sun veiled by clouds in the sky, the Creator, amazed, spoke smiling.
m.2.5.57.15: Brahmā said: Rise, rise, O lord of Daityas, son of Mahiṣa; you are perfected in austerity. I, the giver of boons, have come, dear one; choose a boon as you wish.
m.2.5.57.16: Sanatkumāra said: Rising up again and again, the Daitya lord, son of Mahiṣa, gazing at the Lord with his eyes, delighted, addressed the god in a voice choked with emotion.
m.2.5.57.17: Gajāsura said: Salutation to you, O lord of the gods of gods. If you will give me a boon, may I be unslayable by men and women overcome by desire.
m.2.5.57.18: May I be of great strength and great valour, ever unconquerable by the gods and others, and, O Lord, the full enjoyer of all the riches of all the guardians of the worlds.
m.2.5.57.19: Sanatkumāra said: Thus requested by that Dānava, Brahmā (Śatadhṛti), pleased by his austerity, granted him that boon, so very hard to obtain.
m.2.5.57.20: Having thus obtained the boon, the Daitya Gajāsura, son of Mahiṣa, with a greatly gladdened mind, then returned to his own abode.
m.2.5.57.21: That great Asura conquered all the directions and the three worlds, and the lords of gods, Asuras and men, the Gandharvas, Garuḍas and serpents—
m.2.5.57.22: —having conquered all these and others and brought them under his control, the world-conqueror seized the positions of the world-guardians along with their splendour.
m.2.5.57.23: He occupied heaven (Triviṣṭapa), graced with the beauty of the divine gardens — the very palace of the great Indra built by Viśvakarman himself.
m.2.5.57.24: In that house of the great Indra, the mighty, high-spirited sole sovereign, who had conquered the worlds, enjoyed himself, his pair of feet worshipped by the gods and others whom he had oppressed, his fierce rule firmly established.
m.2.5.57.25: Thus, sole sovereign having conquered the quarters, enjoying pleasing sense-objects to his heart's content, he, with senses unconquered, was never satisfied.
m.2.5.57.26: Thus, as he was intoxicated with lordship, arrogant and acting contrary to scripture, after a long time had passed, an evil intent arose in him.
m.2.5.57.27: That son of Mahiṣāsura, the Dānava who crushed the gods, greatly tormented the excellent brahmins and ascetics on earth.
m.2.5.57.28: The evil-minded one tormented gods, men and Pramathas — all of them, and especially those devoted to dharma, remembering his former enmity.
m.2.5.57.29: Once, dear one, that mighty Dānava Gajāsura went to the capital of Śaṅkara.
m.2.5.57.30: When the Asura lord arrived, O sage, a great uproar of save us, save us arose there among the dwellers of Ānandavana.
m.2.5.57.31: When that son of Mahiṣāsura came to the city, crushing all the Pramathas, puffed up with pride in his own might—
m.2.5.57.32: —at that time the gods headed by Śakra, defeated by him, went to Śiva for refuge, bowed and praised him with reverence.
m.2.5.57.33: They reported the arrival of that Dānava in Kāśī and the excessive distress of the people there, especially of their leaders.
m.2.5.57.34: The gods said: O god of gods, Mahādeva, the Asura has come to your city and is causing suffering to your people; slay him, O treasure of compassion.
m.2.5.57.35: Wherever on earth he sets his foot, there by his weight he makes the immovable earth move.
m.2.5.57.36: By the speed of his thighs trees fall along with mountain peaks; by the blows of his staff-like arms the rocky heights are pulverised.
m.2.5.57.37: Because of friction with the hair of his head, the clouds even abandon the sky, and even today they have not lost the dark-blue hue born of contact with his hair.
m.2.5.57.38: By the force of his breaths the great oceans swell with high waves, and the rivers too, with their whales, become wildly billowing.
m.2.5.57.39: His height is nine thousand yojanas, and the breadth of this magician's body is just as much.
m.2.5.57.40: The tawny hue and the restless flicker of whose eyes the lightnings have not given up even today — he is coming swiftly.
m.2.5.57.41: Whichever direction this unbearable demon approaches, he declares, I am unslayable by men and women who are conquered by desire.
m.2.5.57.42: Thus the conduct of that demon has been reported to you. Protect your devotees, O Lord of the gods, you who are intent on protecting Kāśī.
m.2.5.57.43: Sanatkumāra said: Thus entreated by the gods, Hara, intent on protecting his devotees, came there swiftly with the desire to slay him.
m.2.5.57.44: Seeing that Śaṅkara, affectionate to his devotees, arrived, trident in hand and roaring, Gajāsura roared back.
m.2.5.57.45: Then there was a great battle between the two, terrible and wondrous, as they raised heroic cries amid showers of various missiles and weapons.
m.2.5.57.46: Gajāsura, exceedingly brilliant, of great strength and valour, pierced Giriśa, the slayer of demons, with sharp arrows.
m.2.5.57.47: Then Rudra, of fierce form, with his own exceedingly terrible arrows swiftly cut his arrows into pieces as small as sesame seeds before they reached him, O sage.
m.2.5.57.48: Then Gajāsura, enraged, rushed at Maheśvara, sword in hand, roaring loudly, today you are surely slain by me.
m.2.5.57.49: Then he whose weapon is the trident, knowing that the chief of demons who was coming at him could not be slain by anyone else, struck him with the trident.
m.2.5.57.50: Pierced through by that trident, the demon Gajāsura, regarding himself as made into a parasol held aloft over Śiva, addressed Hara.
m.2.5.57.51: Gajāsura said: O God of gods, Mahādeva, I am your devotee in every way. I know you as the lord of heaven, O trident-bearer, destroyer of Smara.
m.2.5.57.52: Death at your hand is deemed most auspicious for me, O Maheśāna, enemy of Andhaka, destroyer of Tripura, all-pervading one.
m.2.5.57.53: I wish to submit something; hear it, O mine of compassion. I speak the truth, not falsehood; consider it, O Mṛtyuñjaya.
m.2.5.57.54: You alone are to be revered by the worlds, established above the universe. In time all must die; such a death as this is for my highest good.
m.2.5.57.55: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing his words, Śaṅkara, the treasury of compassion, the Lord, smiled and replied to Gajāsura, the son of Mahiṣa.
m.2.5.57.56: Īśvara said: O treasury of great valour, best of demons, noble-minded Gajāsura, I am pleased; choose a boon to your liking.
m.2.5.57.57: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing these words of Maheśa, the giver of boons, Gajāsura, lord of demons, replied with a pleased heart.
m.2.5.57.58: Gajāsura said: If you are pleased, O sky-clad one, then always wear this hide of mine, O Maheśāna, purified by the fire of your trident,
m.2.5.57.59: a hide fitted to your size, pleasant to the touch, won as the stake on the battlefield, beautiful, greatly divine, ever bringing comfort.
m.2.5.57.60: May it always be fragrant, always exceedingly soft, always spotless, and always a splendid adornment.
m.2.5.57.61: Even though it endured the blazing fire of great austerity for a very long time, O Lord, this hide of mine — I being a store of holy fragrance — was not burnt; therefore let it be yours.
m.2.5.57.62: If this hide of mine were not meritorious, O Digambara, how then could it have come into contact with your body on the battlefield?
m.2.5.57.63: And grant me another boon, if you are pleased, Śaṅkara: from this day onward may your name be Kṛttivāsas.
m.2.5.57.64: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing these words of his, Śaṅkara, affectionate to his devotees, greatly pleased, said so be it to him, the son of Mahiṣāsura.
m.2.5.57.65: Again the pleased Maheśāna, who loves his devotees, spoke to the demon Gajāsura, whose mind was made pure by devotion.
m.2.5.57.66: Īśvara said: This holy body of yours, in this sacred field that is the means of liberation — let my liṅga be here, bestowing liberation on all.
m.2.5.57.67: named Kṛttivāseśvara, destroyer of great sins, the crown of all liṅgas, granting liberation.
m.2.5.57.68: Having said this, the Lord of gods, Digambara, took the huge hide of Gajāsura and wore it.
m.2.5.57.69: A great festival took place on that day, O lord of sages; all the people dwelling in Kāśī, and the Pramathas too, rejoiced.
m.2.5.57.70: Then the gods headed by Hari and Brahmā, their minds filled with joy, bowed with joined palms and praised Maheśāna.
m.2.5.57.71: When that lord of demons, Gajāsura son of Mahiṣa, was slain, the gods returned to their own abodes and the world regained its well-being.
m.2.5.57.72: Thus has been told the deed of Śambhu which reveals his affection for devotees; it leads to heaven, brings fame and long life, and increases wealth and grain.
m.2.5.57.73: Whoever, observing pure vows, listens to this with love or causes it to be heard, having enjoyed great happiness, obtains supreme bliss at the end.
m.2.5.57.iti: Thus ends the fifty-seventh adhyāya, named The slaying of Gajāsura, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.5.58.1: Sanatkumāra said: Listen, O Vyāsa, I shall narrate the deed of the moon-crested Śiva: how Hara slew Dundubhinirhrāda, the son of Diti.
m.2.5.58.2: When the mighty demon Hiraṇyākṣa, son of Diti, had been slain by the god Viṣṇu, Diti in course of time fell into great sorrow.
m.2.5.58.3: The wicked demon Dundubhinirhrāda, maternal uncle of Prahlāda and a giver of distress to the gods, consoled the grieving Diti with words.
m.2.5.58.4: Then that deceitful demon, king of the daityas, having comforted Diti, pondered a means: How might the gods be easily conquered?
m.2.5.58.5: He thought: The heroic great asura Hiraṇyākṣa, together with his brother, was slain through the gods, those deceitful enemies of the daityas, and through Viṣṇu.
m.2.5.58.6: What is the strength of the immortals, what their food, what their support? How could they be easily conquered by me? Thus he pondered a means.
m.2.5.58.7: Having reflected many times, the demon ascertained the truth with certainty: On consideration, the brāhmaṇas are surely the cause in this matter.
m.2.5.58.8: Thereupon the demon Dundubhinirhrāda, enemy of the gods and a great villain, repeatedly ran after brāhmaṇas to kill them.
m.2.5.58.9: Since the gods feed on sacrifices, and sacrifices arise from the Vedas, and those Vedas rest on brāhmaṇas, therefore the twice-born are the strength of the gods.
m.2.5.58.10: Certainly all the Vedas rest on brāhmaṇas; the gods, along with Vāsava (Indra), have brāhmaṇas as their strength. No deliberation is needed here.
m.2.5.58.11: If the brāhmaṇas were destroyed, the Vedas would then perish of themselves; hence, when they have perished, the gods are ruined for good.
m.2.5.58.12: When the sacrifices go to ruin, the gods, deprived of their food, become powerless and easy to conquer; and then, the gods being conquered—
m.2.5.58.13: I alone shall become the honoured lord of the three worlds; I shall seize all the imperishable riches of the gods.
m.2.5.58.14: I shall enjoy only pleasures in a kingdom whose thorns have been removed. Having resolved thus, the evil-minded villain reflected again.
m.2.5.58.15: Where are the twice-born found in greatest numbers, greatly swelled with brahmanic splendour, accomplished in Vedic study and endowed with the power of austerity?
m.2.5.58.16: Vārāṇasī is surely the abode of the greatest number of brāhmaṇas. Having first destroyed it, I shall then go on to another holy place.
m.2.5.58.17: Wherever, in whatever holy places and in whatever hermitages, brāhmaṇas are found, all of them everywhere are to be devoured by me.
m.2.5.58.18: Thus having formed an intention befitting his race, the wicked, deceitful Dundubhinirhrāda reached Kāśī and killed the twice-born.
m.2.5.58.19: Into whatever forest the best of the twice-born went to gather sacrificial fuel and kuśa grass, there that evil-minded one would devour them all.
m.2.5.58.20: So that no one would know it, he kept himself concealed, becoming a forest creature in the forest and an aquatic creature in a lake.
m.2.5.58.21: Of invisible form, the deceiver, imperceptible even to the gods, would by day remain intent on meditation like a sage, in the midst of the sages.
m.2.5.58.22: Watching the entering and leaving of the huts, at night he devoured many brāhmaṇas in the form of a tiger.
m.2.5.58.23: Thus he devoured them fearlessly, not leaving even a bone; in this way many brāhmaṇas were struck down by that wicked one.
m.2.5.58.24: Once, on Śivarātri, a devotee in his own hut, having performed worship of the God of gods, remained absorbed in meditation.
m.2.5.58.25: And that Dundubhinirhrāda, lord of the daityas, proud of his strength, assumed the form of a tiger and set his mind on seizing him.
m.2.5.58.26: But he could not overpower that devotee, who was immersed in meditation, firm of mind in beholding Śiva, and who had performed the protective placement of the astra-mantra.
m.2.5.58.27: Then the all-pervading Śambhu, Hara, knowing his intention, resolved upon the killing of that demon of wicked form.
m.2.5.58.28: Just as the tiger was about to seize him, Hara appeared—the three-eyed one, the protecting jewel of the world, whose mind is skilled in guarding devotees.
m.2.5.58.29: Seeing Rudra coming forth from the liṅga worshipped by that devotee, the demon, in that very tiger form, swelled up like a mountain.
m.2.5.58.30: Then, even as the dānava looked contemptuously at the all-knowing one, Śiva seized him as he came on and crushed him in the vice of his armpit.
m.2.5.58.31: Then the five-faced one, he who bears the name Fond of Devotees, struck the five-faced beast on the head with his fist, harder even than a thunderbolt.
m.2.5.58.32: By that blow of the fist and the crushing in the armpit, the tiger roared in extreme agony, filling heaven and earth, and died.
m.2.5.58.33: Their minds trembling at that great roar, the ascetics gathered there in the night, following the sound.
m.2.5.58.34: Seeing there the Lord holding the king of beasts under his arm, they all bowed down and praised Śarva with cries of victory, victory.
m.2.5.58.35: The brahmins said: Protect, protect us, O God, from this terrible calamity. Show us grace, O Lord; remain right here, O Teacher of the world.
m.2.5.58.36: In this very form, under the name Vyāghreśa, O Mahādeva, always guard the Jyeṣṭhasthāna.
m.2.5.58.37: Protect us, the dwellers of this holy place, from other calamities as well; driving away the wicked, O Lord of Gaurī, grant fearlessness to your devotees.
m.2.5.58.38: Sanatkumāra said: Having heard these words of the devotees, the moon-crested one, loving to his devotees, said so be it and spoke again to the devotees.
m.2.5.58.39: Maheśvara said: Whoever beholds me here in this form with faith, I shall without doubt cast down the onset of calamities upon him.
m.2.5.58.40: A mortal who hears this story of mine and remembers this liṅga in his heart, when entering battle, attains victory without doubt.
m.2.5.58.41: Meanwhile the gods, together with Indra (Vāsava), arrived, shouting victory and leading a great festive celebration.
m.2.5.58.42: All the gods bowed to Śaṅkara with love, with joined palms and bent shoulders, and praised with fine words the Lord who is loving to his devotees.
m.2.5.58.43: The gods said: Victory to you, Śaṅkara, lord of the gods, remover of the distress of those who bow to you, O Lord! By the slaying of this Dundubhinirhrāda we gods have been protected.
m.2.5.58.44: O you who love your devotees, you should always protect your devotees; and the wicked should be slain by you, O lord of the gods, lord of all, O Master.
m.2.5.58.45: Having heard these words of the gods, the Supreme Lord, pleased at heart, said so be it and merged into that liṅga.
m.2.5.58.46: Then the gods, filled with wonder, joyfully went each to his own abode; and those brāhmaṇas too, in great delight, returned as they had come.
m.2.5.58.47: Whoever hears this supreme account of the origin of Vyāghreśvara, or causes it to be heard, or reads it, or likewise causes it to be read —
m.2.5.58.48: that man obtains all the desires wished for in his own mind, and hereafter attains liberation, free from all sorrow.
m.2.5.58.49: This incomparable narrative, whose syllables are the nectar of Śiva's divine play, leads to heaven, brings fame and long life, and increases sons and grandsons.
m.2.5.58.50: It is supreme, bestows devotion, is blessed, pleases Śiva, and is auspicious; it grants the highest knowledge, is delightful, and is the supreme remover of mental disturbances.
m.2.5.58.iti: Thus ends the fifty-eighth adhyāya, named The slaying of the daitya Dundubhinirhrāda, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.2.5.59.1: Sanatkumāra said: Listen, O Vyāsa, with great delight, to the deed of the Supreme Lord: how he slew the demons through his own beloved, by a signal directed at the demon.
m.2.5.59.2: Formerly there were two great demons named Vidala and Utpala, who could not be slain by a male, great heroes, extremely arrogant because of a boon from Brahmā (Vidhi).
m.2.5.59.3: By those two men who, through the strength of their own arms, treated the three worlds like straw—by those two demons, O brahmin, all the gods were defeated in battle.
m.2.5.59.4: Defeated by those two, the gods went to Vidhi for refuge; bowing to him duly, they all reported the matter respectfully.
m.2.5.59.5: Then Brahmā said to them: Those two are certainly to be slain by the Goddess. Take courage, reverently remembering Śiva together with Śivā.
m.2.5.59.6: He who bears the name Affectionate to Devotees, the auspicious Śaṅkara together with Śivā, the Supreme Lord, will bring about your welfare before long.
m.2.5.59.7: Sanatkumāra said: Having said this to them, Brahmā then fell silent, remembering Śiva. And the gods too, having gained joy, then went each to his own abode.
m.2.5.59.8: Then the divine sage Nārada, at Śiva's prompting, went to their dwelling and loudly extolled the beauty of Śivā.
m.2.5.59.9: Hearing his words, the two demons became deluded by illusion; tormented by the god of love (the odd-arrowed one), they longed to carry off the Goddess.
m.2.5.59.10: Those two pondered: When and where will that Śivā be ours, through the favour of fate that has dawned for us?
m.2.5.59.11: At one time Śambhu was sporting gracefully, and Śivā, out of playfulness, was playing a game of ball,
m.2.5.59.12: with her friends, joyfully, for fun, in Śiva's presence.
m.2.5.59.13: Leaping up, displaying the nimbleness of her bending limbs, her eyes troubled by bees delighted by the fragrance of her breath,
m.2.5.59.14: the ground before her strewn with fine garlands slipping from her braided hair, shining with drops of moisture trickling from the leaf-designs on her perspiring cheeks,
m.2.5.59.15: enveloped by the radiance of her limbs streaming out through her bursting bodice, her lotus-hands deeply reddened from striking the bouncing ball,
m.2.5.59.16: the tips of her creeper-like brows dancing with her lovely gaze that followed the ball—thus Mṛḍānī, the Mother of the world, was seen at play.
m.2.5.59.17: And she was eyed sidelong by the two sons of Diti roaming in the sky, who were as if already taken onto the lap of Death that had drawn near—
m.2.5.59.18: by those named Vidala and Utpala, arrogant through Brahmā's boon, who by the strength of their own arms regarded the beings of the three worlds as straw.
m.2.5.59.19: Desiring to carry off that Goddess, tormented by the god of love, the two swiftly came down from the sky, having adopted the magic of Śambara.
m.2.5.59.20: Assuming by illusion the guise of Śiva's attendants, those two, utterly wicked and of very restless minds, came near Ambikā.
m.2.5.59.21: Then, by Hara, the slayer of the wicked, regarding them with contempt, the two were recognised in an instant, because of the restlessness showing in their eyes.
m.2.5.59.22: Then Durgā, destroyer of misfortune, was given a sidelong glance by the god who is the form of all, meaning: These two are demons, not gaṇas.
m.2.5.59.23: Then she understood that eye-signal of her own lord, O dear one—of Śaṅkara, the Supreme Lord, who delights in great sport.
m.2.5.59.24: Then, having understood that signal, she who is half the body of the Omniscient One struck down both of them at once with that very ball.
m.2.5.59.25: Struck by the great Goddess with the ball, those two mighty wicked ones, whirling round and round, fell down,
m.2.5.59.26: like two ripe fruits falling from their stalk on a palm tree shaken by the wind, or like two peaks of a great mountain struck by the thunderbolt.
m.2.5.59.27: Having felled those two great demons who were bent on doing what should not be done, the ball then transformed into the form of a liṅga.
m.2.5.59.28: That liṅga then became known as Kandukeśvara, near Jyeṣṭheśvara, warding off all evil ones.
m.2.5.59.29: At that very time the gods headed by Hari and Brahmā, and the sages, learning of the manifestation of Śiva (śiva-āvirbhāva), assembled there.
m.2.5.59.30: Then all the gods, having received boons from Śambhu, went by his command to their own abodes, delighted; and so too the residents of Kāśī.
m.2.5.59.31: Seeing Śaṅkara together with Ambikā, they joined their palms, bowed, and praised him with devotion and reverence in pleasing words.
m.2.5.59.32: And Śiva, together with Ambikā, O Vyāsa, the knower of fine sport, affectionate to devotees, having played, went delighted to his own abode with his gaṇas.
m.2.5.59.33: And the Kandukeśvara liṅga in Kāśī destroys the wicked, and always grants enjoyment and liberation and all desires to the good.
m.2.5.59.34: Whoever listens to this incomparable narrative with joy, or causes it to be heard, or reads it—whence could he have the fear of sorrow?
m.2.5.59.35: Having enjoyed here every kind of happiness, manifold and unsurpassed, he attains in the hereafter a divine state, hard to reach even for the gods.
m.2.5.59.36: Thus, O dear one, I have described to you this most wondrous deed, which shows the affection of Śiva and Śivā for their devotees and brings good to the virtuous.
m.2.5.59.37: Brahmā said: Having spoken thus and taken leave of Vyāsa, praised by him, my excellent son went through the sky to Kāśī, contemplating the deeds of the moon-crested one.
m.2.5.59.38: This Yuddhakhaṇḍa within the Rudrasaṃhitā, which yields the fruit of all desires, has been narrated by me to you, O best of sages.
m.2.5.59.39: This Rudrasaṃhitā has been described by me in full; it is most dear to Sadāśiva and yields the fruits of enjoyment and liberation.
m.2.5.59.40: Whoever reads this daily—which removes the harassment of enemies—obtains all desires, and then that man attains liberation.
m.2.5.59.41: Sūta said: Thus the son of Brahmā Nārada, having heard from his father the supreme glory of Śiva and having received the hundred names of Śambhu, became fulfilled, a follower of Śiva.
m.2.5.59.42: The dialogue of Brahmā and Nārada has been narrated by me in full. Śiva indeed is foremost of all; what more do you wish to hear?
m.2.5.59.iti: Thus ends the fifty-ninth adhyāya, named The slaying of the daityas Vidala and Utpala, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.3.1.0: I bow to Maheśvara, who is great bliss, whose play is endless, the all-pervading Lord of all, the Great One, beloved of Gaurī, the source from whom Kārttika and the King of Obstacles Gaṇeśa arose: Śaṅkara, the primal God.
m.3.1.1: Śaunaka said: O disciple of Vyāsa, most fortunate Sūta, treasury of knowledge and compassion, tell us of the incarnations of Śambhu, through which he brought about the welfare of the good.
m.3.1.2: Sūta said: O sage Śaunaka, I shall tell you, the sage, the incarnations of Śiva; listen with true devotion, with attentive mind and senses subdued.
m.3.1.3: Long ago, O sage, Nandī, who is a form of Śiva and the refuge of the good, was asked this by Sanatkumāra; remembering Śiva, he spoke to him.
m.3.1.4: Nandīśvara said: Countless indeed are the incarnations of the all-pervading Lord of all across the kalpas; even so, I shall tell of them here as far as my understanding goes.
m.3.1.5: The nineteenth kalpa is to be known as Śvetalohita; in it the incarnation Sadyojāta is proclaimed as the first.
m.3.1.6: In that kalpa, as Brahmā was meditating on the supreme Brahman, a boy with a topknot, white and red in colour, came forth.
m.3.1.7: Seeing that Person, the Lord whose form is Brahman, Brahmā recognised him, meditated on him in his heart, and bowed with folded hands.
m.3.1.8: Knowing him to be Śiva Sadyojāta, the Lord of the worlds rejoiced, and again and again with a pure mind he contemplated that Supreme One.
m.3.1.9: Then, as he meditated, there appeared glorious white youths, embodiments of supreme knowledge and the supreme Brahman.
m.3.1.10: Sunanda, Nandana, Viśvananda and Upanandana—these great-souled ones were his disciples, by whom that Brahman was encompassed.
m.3.1.11: And Śambhu as Sadyojāta, the Supreme Lord, being pleased, lovingly gave knowledge to Brahmā (Vedhas), and also the power of creation.
m.3.1.12: Then came the twentieth kalpa, called Rakta (Red), in which the greatly radiant Brahmā assumed a red colour.
m.3.1.13: As Brahmā (Vidhi), desiring a son, meditated, a son appeared to him, wearing red garlands and garments, red-eyed, with red ornaments.
m.3.1.14: Seeing that great-souled boy, Brahmā, absorbed in meditation, recognised him as Śiva Vāmadeva and bowed with folded hands.
m.3.1.15: Then he had four sons clad in red: Viraja, Vivāha, Viśoka and Viśvabhāvana.
m.3.1.16: That Śambhu as Vāmadeva, the Supreme Lord, being pleased, lovingly gave knowledge to Brahmā, and also the power of creation.
m.3.1.17: The twenty-first kalpa is known as Pītavāsas, in which the illustrious Brahmā became clad in yellow.
m.3.1.18: As Brahmā, desiring a son, meditated, a boy was born to him, splendid in yellow garments and the like, greatly radiant and mighty-armed.
m.3.1.19: Seeing him absorbed in meditation and knowing him to be Śiva Tatpuruṣa, Brahmā (Vidhi) bowed; then, with understanding, he recited the Śaiva Gāyatrī—
m.3.1.20: —having recited that great goddess the Gāyatrī, revered by all the worlds, with a mind absorbed in meditation, Mahādeva was pleased.
m.3.1.21: Then at his side appeared divine boys, all clad in yellow, promoters of the path of yoga.
m.3.1.22: Then, when that yellow kalpa of the Self-born Brahmā had passed, another kalpa began again, and it was named Śiva.
m.3.1.23: When the single ocean of dissolution had lasted a thousand divine years, Brahmā, wishing to create beings, pondered in distress.
m.3.1.24: Then the greatly radiant Brahmā saw a boy appear, black in colour, of great might, blazing with his own splendour,
m.3.1.25: wearing black garments and a black turban, with a black sacred thread, adorned with a black crown, with black bathing-unguents.
m.3.1.26: Seeing that great-souled Aghora of terrible valour, the wondrous lord of the god of gods, black and tawny, he bowed to him.
m.3.1.27: Then Brahmā meditated on Aghora, whose form is Brahman, and praised with pleasing words the imperishable one, tender to his devotees.
m.3.1.28: Then at his side four great-souled boys came into being, black, with black bathing-unguents.
m.3.1.29: Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇaśikha, Kṛṣṇāsya and Kṛṣṇakaṇṭhadhṛk—these were they, of mysterious names, Śiva-formed and very radiant.
m.3.1.30: Being such, these great souls, for the sake of Brahmā's creation, set in motion the great and wondrous yoga called Ghora.
m.3.1.31: Then, O lords of sages, another kalpa of Brahmā began, supremely wondrous, known by the name Viśvarūpa.
m.3.1.32: As Brahmā, desiring a son, meditated on Śiva in his mind, Sarasvatī appeared, of mighty sound and universal form.
m.3.1.33: Likewise appeared the blessed Īśāna, the Supreme Lord, resembling pure crystal, adorned with every ornament.
m.3.1.34: Seeing him, Brahmā bowed to Īśāna, the unborn, all-pervading, omnipresent giver of all, who is all, beautiful in form yet devoid of form.
m.3.1.35: Īśāna, the all-pervading, having thus taught the true path to Brahmā, together with his Śakti created four auspicious boys.
m.3.1.36: Jaṭī, Muṇḍī, Śikhaṇḍī and Ardhamuṇḍa were born; having taught the true dharma through yoga and accomplished their task, they attained the goal of yoga.
m.3.1.37: Thus, O omniscient Sanatkumāra, the origin of Sadyojāta and the others has been told in brief, out of desire for the welfare of the worlds.
m.3.1.38: Now, O greatly wise one, hear their activity in due order, all of which, established throughout the cosmic egg, brings about the welfare of the three worlds.
m.3.1.39: Īśāna, Tatpuruṣa, Aghora, the one called Vāmadeva, and likewise the one called Brahma Sadyojāta—these are the five renowned forms of Maheśa.
m.3.1.40: Īśāna, of the form of Śiva, is remembered as the first and the weightiest. He directly presides over the kṣetrajña, the enjoyer of prakṛti.
m.3.1.41: The second form of Śiva, called Tatpuruṣa, presides over the object of enjoyment, whose nature is to be the substratum of the guṇas, and which is all-knowing.
m.3.1.42: The third, the form of the Pināka-bearer called Aghora, abides within the principle of intellect (buddhi-tattva), joined with its own limbs, for the sake of dharma.
m.3.1.43: The fourth form of Śaṅkara, called Vāmadeva, is the presiding principle of ego (ahaṅkāra), ever performing many works.
m.3.1.44: The form of Śaṅkara named Īśāna is ever the lord of hearing, of speech, and likewise of the all-pervading ether.
m.3.1.45: The wise who are skilled in discernment declare the lordly form named Tatpuruṣa to be the lord of skin, hand, touch and air.
m.3.1.46: The wise call the form named Aghora the presiding principle of the body, of form (sight) and likewise of fire.
m.3.1.47: The form of Śaṅkara named Vāmadeva is regarded as the lord of the tongue, of the anus, of taste and likewise of the waters.
m.3.1.48: They know the form of Śaṅkara named Sadyojāta as the lord of the nose, of the genital organ, of smell and likewise of the earth.
m.3.1.49: These forms of Śambhu, the sole causes of all welfare, should always be worshipped with effort by men who seek welfare.
m.3.1.50: Whoever reads or hears of the origin of Sadyojāta and the others, having enjoyed all desires, attains the supreme goal.
m.3.1.iti: Thus ends the first adhyāya, named The five Brahmā incarnations of Śiva, in the third saṃhitā, the Śatarudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.3.2.1: Nandīśvara said: Listen, dear one, O lord, O sage, to the supreme incarnations of Maheśa, which accomplish every purpose in the world and give happiness to all.
m.3.2.2: This world consists of the eight forms of that Śambhu, the supreme Lord; the universe abides pervaded in him, like clusters of gems on a thread.
m.3.2.3: Śarva, Bhava, Rudra, Ugra, Bhīma, Paśupati, Īśāna and Mahādeva—these are the eight renowned forms.
m.3.2.4: Earth, water, fire, wind, space, the knower of the field (the soul), the sun and the moon are presided over by Śiva's eight forms beginning with Śarva.
m.3.2.5: The form of Śaṅkara, Maheśa, that is all-sustaining (earth) bears the moving and unmoving universe; such is the settled conclusion of scripture.
m.3.2.6: The form of the Supreme Self Bhava that consists of water, the life-giver of the entire world, is called Bhava.
m.3.2.7: The form of the good lord Ugra that sustains the whole world outside and within and itself moves (wind) is called Ugra by the wise.
m.3.2.8: The form of Bhīma consisting of the sky, which gives room to all and pervades all, is called Bhīma; it breaks the hosts of wicked kings.
m.3.2.9: The form of Paśupati should be known as the support of all souls, dwelling in all fields (bodies), cutting the bonds of the bound souls.
m.3.2.10: Illuminating the whole world, the form of Maheśa named Īśāna, called the sun (Divākara), moves across the sky.
m.3.2.11: The nectar-rayed moon that nourishes the universe is the form of Mahādeva, and it bears the name Mahādeva.
m.3.2.12: The self is the eighth form of that Śiva, the Supreme Self, pervading the other forms; therefore the universe is of the nature of Śiva.
m.3.2.13: The branches of a tree flourish by watering the tree's root; likewise the universe, his body, flourishes through the worship of Śiva.
m.3.2.14: Just as here a father is pleased by the happiness of his sons, grandsons and others, so Śaṅkara is pleased by the happiness of the universe.
m.3.2.15: If harm is done to any embodied being whatsoever, that is surely an offence done to the Eight-formed One; there is no doubt.
m.3.2.16: Worship with your whole being Śiva, Rudra, the supreme cause, who abides presiding over the universe in his eightfold form.
m.3.2.17: Thus have been described to you, O son of Brahmā, his eight renowned forms, devoted to the welfare of all; they should be served by men seeking the highest good.
m.3.2.iti: Thus ends the second adhyāya, named The eight forms of Śiva, in the third saṃhitā, the Śatarudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.3.3.1: Nandīśvara said: Listen, dear one of great wisdom, to the unsurpassed form of Śiva called Ardhanārīnara (half-woman, half-man), which fulfilled the desire of Vidhi (Brahmā).
m.3.3.2: When all the creatures created by the Creator did not multiply, he became troubled with anxiety, distressed by that grief.
m.3.3.3: Then a voice arose from the sky: Make a creation born of couples. Hearing that, Brahmā resolved to produce sexual creation.
m.3.3.4: But since the race of women had not previously come forth from Īśāna, the lotus-born one was unable to make a creation born of union.
m.3.3.5: Without the power of Śambhu these creatures cannot be born — reflecting thus, Brahmā began to perform austerity.
m.3.3.6: Meditating lovingly in his heart on the Supreme Lord united with Śivā, the supreme Śakti, he performed supreme austerity.
m.3.3.7: By the intense austerity of that Self-born one, so absorbed, Śiva was quickly pleased in a very short time.
m.3.3.8: Then Hara, entering the wish-granting form of the Lord who is perfect consciousness, became half-woman, half-man, and came near Brahmā.
m.3.3.9: Seeing the god Śaṅkara accompanied by the supreme Śakti, Brahmā prostrated like a staff and, with joined palms, praised him.
m.3.3.10: Then the god Mahādeva, Maheśvara the maker of the universe, greatly pleased, spoke with a voice deep as a thundercloud, for the sake of creation's increase.
m.3.3.11: Īśvara said: Child, child, most fortunate one, my son, Grandsire, I have truly understood your entire wish.
m.3.3.12: You have now performed austerity solely for the increase of creatures. I am pleased with that austerity and I grant what you desire.
m.3.3.13: Having spoken these most generous, naturally sweet words, Śiva separated the goddess Śivā from a portion of his body.
m.3.3.14: Seeing that supreme Śakti, separated and come forth from Śiva, Vidhi bowed down humbly and entreated her.
m.3.3.15: Brahmā said: O Śivā, I was created in the beginning by the God of gods, your husband, and all creatures were appointed to me by Śambhu, the Supreme Self.
m.3.3.16: O Śivā, all the gods and others were fashioned by me with the mind; though created again and again, they do not increase.
m.3.3.17: Henceforth, by making creation arise from couples, I wish to make all my creatures increase.
m.3.3.18: The imperishable race of women has not previously come forth from you; therefore I do not have the power to create the race of women.
m.3.3.19: Surely all powers originate from you; therefore I entreat you, the supreme Śakti, Mistress of all.
m.3.3.20: O Śivā, give me the power to create the race of women; salutation to you, O Mother, beloved of Śiva, for the sake of the increase of the moving and unmoving world.
m.3.3.21: And I ask another boon of you, O sovereign of boon-givers; grant it to me out of compassion, O Mother of the world; salutation to you.
m.3.3.22: O all-pervading one, for the increase of the moving and unmoving, united with the one Lord, become the daughter of my son Dakṣa, O Bhavāmbikā.
m.3.3.23: Thus entreated by Brahmā, the goddess, the Supreme Mistress, said so be it and gave that power to Vidhi.
m.3.3.24: Therefore that goddess Śivā, the Śakti of Śiva who pervades the world, created from between her brows a single Śakti radiant like herself.
m.3.3.25: Looking at that Śakti, Bhavāmbikā, Hara the best of gods, the ocean of compassion, the great Lord who acts in play, smiling, said to her:
m.3.3.26: Śiva said: O Goddess, you have been worshipped with austerity by Brahmā Parameṣṭhin; be gracious with great love and fulfil all his wishes.
m.3.3.27: Receiving that command of the Supreme Lord with her head bowed, the goddess, at Brahmā's request, became the daughter of Dakṣa.
m.3.3.28: Having thus given incomparable power to Brahmā, O sage, that Śivā entered the body of Śambhu, and the Lord Śambhu vanished.
m.3.3.29: From then on in this world a share was assigned to woman; Vidhi attained joy, and creation through union came about.
m.3.3.30: Thus I have told you, dear one, this most excellent form of Śiva, half-woman and half-man, which bestows great auspiciousness on the good.
m.3.3.31: Whoever reads or even hears this sinless narrative enjoys all pleasures and attains the supreme goal.
m.3.3.iti: Thus ends the third adhyāya, named Śiva's incarnation as Ardhanārīśvara, in the third saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.3.4.1: Nandīśvara said: O all-knowing Sanatkumāra, hear gladly the story of Śaṅkara, ever bestowing happiness, which Rudra lovingly narrated to Brahmā.
m.3.4.2: Śiva said: In the seventh, Vārāha kalpa, in the period called manvantara, then the blessed lord of the kalpa, who illumines all the worlds,
m.3.4.3: he, the son of Manu Vaivasvata, will be your great-grandson. Then, O Vidhi, in that manvantara, the four yugas will come,
m.3.4.4: For the grace of the worlds and for the welfare of brāhmaṇas, I shall be born, O Vidhi, O Brahmā, near the end of the age called Dvāpara.
m.3.4.5: And then, by the course of the yugas, in that first yuga — in the first Dvāpara, O Brahmā, when the Vyāsa is Svayamprabhu (the self-luminous lord),
m.3.4.6: then, for the sake of the brāhmaṇas, at the end of that age in the Kali, I shall become, united with Śivā, a great sage named Śveta,
m.3.4.7: on the lovely Himalayan peak Chāgala, the best of mountains. Then, O Vidhi, I shall have disciples wearing tufts of hair:
m.3.4.8: Śveta, Śvetaśikha, Śvetāśva and Śvetalohita — these four, through the yoga of meditation, will go to my city.
m.3.4.9: Then, having known me in truth as the imperishable, they will become devotees, free from birth, death and old age, absorbed in the supreme Brahman.
m.3.4.10: I cannot be seen by men except through meditation, O Grandsire, not, dear son, by means such as charity and dharma, which are rooted in action.
m.3.4.11: In the second Dvāpara, when the Vyāsa is the Prajāpati named Satya, then in the Kali I shall be the sage named Sutāra.
m.3.4.12: There too I shall have disciples, twice-born knowers of the Veda: Dundubhi, Śatarūpa, Hṛṣīka and Ketumān.
m.3.4.13: These four, through the yoga of meditation, will go to my city; then, having known me in truth as the imperishable, they will be liberated.
m.3.4.14: And in the third Dvāpara, when the Vyāsa is Bhārgava, then too, at the end of the age, I shall be Damana.
m.3.4.15: There too I shall have four sons: Viśoka, Viśeṣa, Vipāpa and Pāpanāśana.
m.3.4.16: With my disciples I shall render help to the Vyāsa, O four-faced one, and here in the Kali I shall firmly establish the path of renunciation.
m.3.4.17: And in the fourth Dvāpara, when Aṅgiras is remembered as the Vyāsa, then too I shall be the one named Suhotra.
m.3.4.18: There too I shall have four sons, great-souled practitioners of yoga; I tell you their names, O Vidhi:
m.3.4.19: Sumukha, Durmukha, Durdama and Duratikrama. With these disciples I shall then help the Vyāsa, O Vidhi.
m.3.4.20: And in the fifth Dvāpara, Savitṛ is known as the Vyāsa; then I shall be a yogin named Kaṅka, of great austerity.
m.3.4.21: There too I shall have four sons, great-souled practitioners of yoga; hear their names from me:
m.3.4.22: Sanaka, Sanātana, the lord Sanandana, and the mighty Sanatkumāra — pure and free of egoism.
m.3.4.23: There too, I, named Kaṅka, O Vidhi, shall give help to Savitṛ the Vyāsa, furthering the path of renunciation.
m.3.4.24: Again, in the sixth cycle, in the Dvāpara, Mṛtyu, maker of the worlds, will be the Vyāsa, the divider of the Veda.
m.3.4.25: Then too I shall be the one named Lokākṣi, for the good assistance of the Vyāsa, furthering the path of renunciation.
m.3.4.26: There too I shall have four disciples, firm in their vows: Sudhāmā, Virajā, Sañjaya and Vijaya.
m.3.4.27: In the seventh cycle, when Śatakratu is the Vyāsa, then too, O Vidhi, I shall be the mighty Jaigīṣavya.
m.3.4.28: Skilled in the great yoga, I shall make yoga firm, dwelling in a cave in Kāśī, a divine place, lying on a bed of kuśa grass.
m.3.4.29: And I shall help Śatakratu the Vyāsa, and I shall lift the devotees out of the fear of saṃsāra, O Vidhi.
m.3.4.30: In that age too I shall have four sons: Sārasvata, Yogīśa, Meghavāha and Suvāhana.
m.3.4.31: In the eighth cycle, Vasiṣṭha, the best of sages, will be the Veda-Vyāsa, the divider of the Veda.
m.3.4.32: There too I shall be the one named Dadhivāhana, and I shall indeed help the Vyāsa, O best of yoga-knowers.
m.3.4.33: Kapila, Āsuri, Pañcaśikha and Śālvala — four yogin sons equal to me will be born.
m.3.4.34: In the ninth cycle, in that same age, O Vidhi, the best of sages called Sārasvata will be the Vyāsa.
m.3.4.35: For the growth of the path of renunciation of that meditating Vyāsa, I too shall then be born, known by the name Ṛṣabha.
m.3.4.36: Parāśara, Garga, Bhārgava and Giriśa — these four excellent yogins will be my disciples there.
m.3.4.37: Together with them I shall make firm the path of yoga, O Prajāpati, and I shall indeed give help to Veda-Vyāsa, the good sage.
m.3.4.38: In that form, O Vidhi, I, the compassionate one, shall indeed bring about the deliverance of many suffering devotees from worldly existence.
m.3.4.39: That incarnation of mine, O Vidhi, called Ṛṣabha, accomplisher of true yoga, will shape the mind of the Vyāsa Sārasvata and perform manifold acts of help.
m.3.4.40: By which incarnation of mine Bhadrāyu, the king's young son, who had died from the effect of poison and was abandoned by his father, was restored to life.
m.3.4.41: Then, when that royal child reached his sixteenth year, that Ṛṣabha, who is Śiva's own self, suddenly went to his house again.
m.3.4.42: Honoured by him, that sage, of true form and a treasury of compassion, taught him the duties of kings and the royal yogas, O Prajāpati.
m.3.4.43: Then he, pleased at heart, gave him a divine armour, a conch, and a shining sword, destroyer of all enemies.
m.3.4.44: Touching his body with sacred ash out of compassion, he who is kind to the afflicted gave him the strength of twelve thousand elephants.
m.3.4.45: Having thus fully reassured Bhadrāyu together with his mother, the lord Ṛṣabha, honoured by the two of them, departed, moving as he willed.
m.3.4.46: Bhadrāyu too, the royal sage, having conquered the hosts of his enemies, O Vidhi, married Kīrtimālinī and ruled the kingdom righteously.
m.3.4.47: Thus I have told you of the Ṛṣabha incarnation of mine, Śaṅkara, of such power—the ninth, the refuge of the good and friend of the afflicted.
m.3.4.48: The story of Ṛṣabha is indeed supremely purifying and great; it bestows heaven, fame and long life, and should be listened to with diligence.
m.3.4.iti: Thus ends the fourth adhyāya, named The story of Ṛṣabha, in the third saṃhitā, the Śatarudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.3.5.1: Śiva said: In the tenth Dvāpara the Vyāsa will be the sage named Tridhāmā; I shall then appear on the lovely peak of Himavat, on Bhṛgutuṅga, the best of mountains.
m.3.5.2: There too will be my sons, headed by Bhṛgu, in accord with the Veda: Balabandhu, Narāmitra, and Ketuśṛṅga, rich in austerity.
m.3.5.3: In the eleventh Dvāpara, when Trivṛta is the Vyāsa, then in the Kali phase at Gaṅgādvāra I shall be born by the name Tapas.
m.3.5.4: Lambodara, Lambākṣa, Keśalamba, and Pralambaka—there too four sons of firm vows will be born.
m.3.5.5: In the twelfth cycle Śatatejas will be the compiler of the Veda; there too I shall be born, here in the Kali at the end of the Dvāpara.
m.3.5.6: Having reached Hemakañcuka, I shall be named Atri, steeped in yoga, to assist that very Vyāsa, establishing the path of renunciation.
m.3.5.7: Sarvajña, Samabuddhi, Sādhya, and Śarva, excellent yogins—these four will be my sons there, O great sage.
m.3.5.8: In that thirteenth age, when Dharma Nārāyaṇa is the Vyāsa, then I shall be the great sage named Bali.
m.3.5.9: I shall dwell in the hermitage of the Vālakhilyas on Gandhamādana, the best of mountains; my sons will be Sudhāmā, Kāśyapa, Vasiṣṭha, and Virajas, auspicious ones.
m.3.5.10: When, in the fourteenth turn, the Vyāsa is the one called Rakṣa, then there in the lineage of Aṅgiras I shall be Gautama.
m.3.5.11: There too, in that Kali, those sons of mine will be: Atri, Davaśada, Śravaṇa, and Śraviṣkaṭa.
m.3.5.12: When in the fifteenth Dvāpara the Vyāsa is Trayyāruṇi, then I shall be Vedaśiras, and likewise there will be Vedaśiras—
m.3.5.13: —that weapon of great power, and the mountain Vedaśīrṣa, I having reached the slope of Himavat, likewise to the north of the Sarasvatī.
m.3.5.14: There too four steadfast sons of mine will be: Kuṇi, Kuṇibāhu, Kuśarīra, and Kunetraka.
m.3.5.15: In the sixteenth age, when Deva will be the Vyāsa, then I shall indeed be Gokarṇa, for bestowing yoga.
m.3.5.16: And right there is that most holy forest named Gokarṇa. There too my sons, yogins, will be born, equal in number to the four oceans.
m.3.5.17: Kāśyapa, Uśanas, Cyavana, and Bṛhaspati—they too, by that very path, will go to Śiva's abode.
m.3.5.18: In the seventeenth cycle the Vyāsa is Devakṛtañjaya; I shall be by name Guhāvāsin, on the auspicious peak of Himavat,
m.3.5.19: in the great abode, very lofty, the Himālaya, a field of Śiva; my sons will be Utathya, Vāmadeva, Mahāyoga, and Mahābala.
m.3.5.20: In the eighteenth cycle, when Ṛtañjaya is the Vyāsa, then I shall be by name Śikhaṇḍin, on the auspicious peak of Himavat,
m.3.5.21: in the most holy Siddhakṣetra, where there is the mountain named Śikhaṇḍin, or the forest of Śikhaṇḍin, frequented by siddhas.
m.3.5.22: Vācaḥśravas, Rucīka, Śyāvāsya, and Yatīśvara—these sons, rich in austerity, will be there too.
m.3.5.23: In the nineteenth cycle the Vyāsa will be the great sage Bharadvāja; then too I shall be born, named Jaṭī Mālī.
m.3.5.24: There on the peak of Himavat will be my sons, numbering as the oceans four: Hiraṇyanāmā, Kauśalya, Lokākṣī, and Pradhimi.
m.3.5.25: In the twentieth cycle Gautama will be the Vyāsa; there I shall be named Aṭṭahāsa, and men will be fond of loud laughter.
m.3.5.26: Right there on the slope of Himavat is the great mountain Aṭṭahāsa, frequented by gods, humans, lords of yakṣas, siddhas, and cāraṇas.
m.3.5.27: There too those sons of mine, excellent yogins, will be: Sumantu, the learned Barbari, Kabandha, and Kuśikandhara.
m.3.5.28: In that twenty-first age, when Vācaḥśravas is the Vyāsa, then I shall be named Dāruka; from that comes the name of the auspicious Dāruvana.
m.3.5.29: There too those sons of mine, excellent yogins, will be: Plakṣa, Dārbhāyaṇi, Ketumān, and Gautama.
m.3.5.30: In the twenty-second cycle, when Śuṣmāyaṇa is the Vyāsa, then too I shall be a great sage at Vārāṇasī,
m.3.5.31: named Lāṅgalī Bhīma, where the gods together with Vāsava (Indra) will see me in that Kali as Bhava bearing the plough as weapon.
m.3.5.32: There too those sons of mine, very righteous, will be: Bhallavī, Madhupiṅga, and likewise Śvetaketu.
m.3.5.33: In the twenty-third cycle, when the sage Tṛṇabindu is the Vyāsa, then I shall be named Śveta, on the auspicious mountain Kālañjara.
m.3.5.34: There too those sons of mine, ascetics, will be: Uśika, Bṛhadaśva, Devala, and Kavi.
m.3.5.35: In the twenty-fourth cycle, when the mighty Yakṣa is the Vyāsa, then in that age I shall be the great yogin named Śūlī, in Naimiṣa.
m.3.5.36: There too those disciples of mine, ascetics, will be: Śālihotra, Agniveśa, Yuvanāśva, and Śaradvasu.
m.3.5.37: In the twenty-fifth, when the Vyāsa will be named Śakti, then too I shall be the great yogin, the lord Daṇḍī Muṇḍīśvara.
m.3.5.38: There too those disciples of mine, ascetics, will be: Chagala, Kuṇḍakarṇa, Kumbhāṇḍa, and Pravāhaka.
m.3.5.39: When Parāśara is the Vyāsa in the twenty-sixth, I too shall be born, having reached the city of Bhadravaṭa, called by name Sahiṣṇu.
m.3.5.40: There too those disciples of mine, ascetics, will be: Ulūka, Vidyuta, Śambūka, and Āśvalāyana.
m.3.5.41: In the twenty-seventh Dvāpara, when Jātūkarṇya will be the Vyāsa, then too I shall be Somaśarmā, having resorted to the Prabhāsa pilgrimage site.
m.3.5.42: There too those disciples of mine will be ascetics: Akṣapāda, Kumāra, Ulūka, and likewise Vatsa.
m.3.5.43: But in the twenty-eighth Dvāpara, when Hari, the son of Parāśara, the lord, will be the Vyāsa named Dvaipāyana,
m.3.5.44: then, with a sixth portion of Viṣṇu, Kṛṣṇa, the best of beings, the excellent son of Vasudeva, will be born as Vāsudeva.
m.3.5.45: Then too I shall appear, as the Self of yoga, through yogic māyā, in the body of a celibate student, to astonish the world.
m.3.5.46: Seeing a dead body abandoned in a cremation ground, yet free of defect, I shall enter it by yogic māyā for the welfare of the brāhmaṇas,
m.3.5.47: and entering the divine, holy cave of Meru together with you and Viṣṇu, I shall then, O Brahmā, be known by the name Laṅkulī.
m.3.5.48: Then the supreme siddha-field called Kāyāvatāra will be very famous as long as the earth endures.
m.3.5.49: There too those disciples of mine will be ascetics: Kuśika, Garga, Mitra and Kauruṣya.
m.3.5.50: These yogin brāhmaṇas, masters of the Vedas, celibate, having attained Maheśvara's yoga, will go to the city of Śiva.
m.3.5.51: Thus in the Vaivasvata Manvantara the incarnations of the Lord of Yoga in all the cycles have been properly declared by the Supreme Self, O you of good vows.
m.3.5.52: And the twenty-eight Vyāsas, in each Dvāpara, O lord, and the incarnations of the Lord of Yoga at the beginning of each Kali age.
m.3.5.53: Of the incarnations of the Lord of Yoga, each has four imperishable disciples, great Śaivas, promoters of the path of yoga.
m.3.5.54: These Pāśupata disciples have bodies smeared with ash, are adorned with rudrākṣa garlands, and their foreheads are marked with the tripuṇḍra.
m.3.5.55: All the disciples are devoted to dharma, masters of the Vedas and Vedāṅgas, ever devoted to the worship of the liṅga, established in it outwardly and inwardly,
m.3.5.56: steadfast in meditation on me through devotion and yoga, with senses conquered; in number they are counted by the wise as one hundred and twelve.
m.3.5.57: Thus I have declared the characteristics of the incarnations, from Manu up to Kṛṣṇa, in the sequence of twenty-eight yugas.
m.3.5.58: There, in that kalpa, when Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana appears, the arrangement of the collections of śruti, bearing the mark of Brahman, will take place.
m.3.5.59: Having spoken thus and blessed Brahmā, Maheśvara, the lord of the gods, looked at him once more and vanished right there.
m.3.5.iti: Thus ends the fifth adhyāya, named The nineteen incarnations of Śiva, in the account of Śiva's incarnations, in the third saṃhitā, the Śatarudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.3.6.1: Sanatkumāra said: How did you, born of a portion of Mahādeva, attain Śiva? I wish to hear all of that; please tell it to me, O lord.
m.3.6.2: Nandīśvara said: O all-knowing Sanatkumāra, listen attentively to how I, born of a portion of Mahādeva, attained Śiva, O sage.
m.3.6.3: Śilāda became desirous of offspring, having been respectfully told by his ancestors, who longed for deliverance, to beget a son; and he, with devotion, set his mind on delivering them.
m.3.6.4: The mighty one named Śilāda, with downcast eyes and righteous soul, had his way of life among the sages, and later he went to Śiva's world.
m.3.6.5: Directing it towards Śakra, that sage named Śilāda, steady of mind and firm in his vow, performed a most unbearable austerity for a long time.
m.3.6.6: Śatakratu was pleased by the austerity of him as he practised it; and then the lord of all gods went to grant a boon.
m.3.6.7: Śakra said to Śilāda with great affection: I am pleased with you, O sinless one; therefore, O tiger among sages, choose boons.
m.3.6.8: Then, bowing to the lord of gods and reverently praising him with hymns, Śilāda, the tiger among sages, with hands folded, said to him:
m.3.6.9: Śilāda said: O Śatakratu, lord of the gods, if you are pleased with me, O lord, I desire a son not born of a womb, free from death, and of good vows.
m.3.6.10: Śakra said: I will give you a son, O seeker of a son, born of a womb and subject to death. Otherwise I will not give one to you; for there are indeed none free from death.
m.3.6.11: I will not give you a son free from death and not born of a womb. Not even Hari and the blessed Vidhi can—what then of anyone else, O great sage?
m.3.6.12: Even those two, born from the body of the enemy of Tripura, are subject to death; the measure of their lifespans too is stated separately in the Veda.
m.3.6.13: Therefore, O best of brahmins, earnestly give up hope for a son not born of a womb and free from death; accept a son befitting yourself.
m.3.6.14: But if Rudra, lord of the gods, Maheśvara, is gracious, then a most rare son, free from death and not born of a womb, may be yours.
m.3.6.15: I, the blessed Viṣṇu, and Druhiṇa, O great sage, are unable to give a son not born of a womb and free from death.
m.3.6.16: Worship Mahādeva with the desire for such a son; he, lord of all and supremely powerful, will grant you a son.
m.3.6.17: Nandīśvara said: Having spoken thus to the best of brahmins and having favoured him, the compassionate lord of the gods, surrounded by the gods, went to his own world, O sage.
m.3.6.18: When that boon-giving thousand-eyed one had gone, Śilāśana (Śilāda), worshipping Mahādeva, pleased Bhava through austerity.
m.3.6.19: Then for that brahmin, thus ceaselessly absorbed in it, a thousand divine years passed, wondrously, like a moment.
m.3.6.20: The sage's body was covered by an anthill and on all sides by hosts of hundreds of thousands of insects, and by other blood-sucking creatures with mouths like diamond needles.
m.3.6.21: Remaining in that hollow, without flesh, blood or skin, Śilāda, best of sages, at length became nothing but bones.
m.3.6.22: Then the Lord, pleased, showed him his own form—divine, endowed with divine qualities, unattainable by the perverse-minded.
m.3.6.23: To him who had been practising austerity for a thousand divine years, the trident-bearer, overlord of all gods, said: I am the giver of boons.
m.3.6.24: Absorbed in deep samādhi, that great sage Śilāda did not hear those words of Śambhu, who is so wholly subject to devotion.
m.3.6.25: When the sage was touched with his hand by the enemy of Tripura, at that very moment the tiger among sages gave up the course of his austerity.
m.3.6.26: Then the sage opened his eyes and, beholding Śambhu together with Umā, quickly bowed with joy and fell at his feet, O sage.
m.3.6.27: With a voice choked with joy, shoulders bowed and hands folded, Śilāda, his heart gladdened, praised the Supreme Lord.
m.3.6.28: Then the blessed god of gods, the three-eyed one, being pleased, said to Śilāda, the bull among sages: I am the giver of boons.
m.3.6.29: What need have you of this austerity, O great-minded one? I give you a son, all-knowing, who has mastered the meaning of all scriptures.
m.3.6.30: Then, having heard that and bowed to the lord of gods, Śilāśana spoke, with a voice choked with joy, to the moon-adorned one.
m.3.6.31: Śilāda said: O Maheśa, if you are pleased, or if you are indeed granting me a boon, I desire a son equal to you, free from death and not born of a womb.
m.3.6.32: Nandīśvara said: Thus addressed by him, the god Tryambaka Śaṅkara, pleased at heart, replied to Śilāda, best of sages.
m.3.6.33: Śiva said: Formerly, O brahmin rich in austerity, I was propitiated through austerity by Brahmā, and by the sages and the best of gods, for the sake of my incarnation.
m.3.6.34: I shall become your son, named Nandī, not born of a womb; and you, O sage, shall be the father of me, the father of the worlds.
m.3.6.35: Nandīśvara said: Having spoken thus and looked upon the sage, who stood after prostrating, the compassionate Hara, together with Umā, quickly gave him instruction and vanished right there.
m.3.6.36: When that Mahādeva had gone, the great sage Śilāda went to his own hermitage and then told the sages what had happened.
m.3.6.37: And after some time, that father of mine, foremost among knowers of sacrifice, quickly ploughed the sacrificial ground for a sacrifice.
m.3.6.38: Then in an instant, by Śambhu's command, I—born of his body—was born even at the outset of the ploughing, radiant like the fire at the end of an age.
m.3.6.39: Then the Puṣkara, Āvartaka and other clouds poured rain; the sky-dwellers, Kinnaras, Siddhas and Sādhyas sang; and when I had become the son of Śilāda, the chief sages showered flowers all around.
m.3.6.40: Then the gods headed by Brahmā and all the wives of the gods came there with great joy, and Hari too, and Śiva and Ambikā.
m.3.6.41: Then there was a great festival, and the troops of Apsarases danced. Having honoured me and embraced me, they, delighted, praised me.
m.3.6.42: Having highly commended that Śilāda and having praised Śiva and Śivā with fine hymns, all went to their abodes; Śiva and Śivā, the lords of all, also departed.
m.3.6.43: Śilāda too, seeing me—radiant like the fire of the sun at the time of dissolution, three-eyed, four-armed, a child, wearing a crown of matted locks—
m.3.6.44: bearing weapons such as the trident, blazing, in every way having the form of Rudra—he, filled with great bliss, lovingly bowed to me, who was worthy of obeisance.
m.3.6.45: Śilāda said: Since I have been gladdened by you, O lord of the gods, you are Nandī by name. Therefore I bow to you, the god who is bliss, the lord of the world.
m.3.6.46: Nandīśvara said: My father, joyful, having bowed deeply to Maheśvara, quickly went with me to his own hut, like a pauper who has found a treasure.
m.3.6.47: When I had gone to Śilāda's hut, O great sage, then I abandoned that form and assumed a human state.
m.3.6.48: Seeing me in human form, my father, honoured by the world, lamented, deeply afflicted with grief, surrounded by his kinsmen.
m.3.6.49: Śilāda, son of Śālaṅkāyana, loving towards his son, performed for me all the rites beginning with the birth ceremony (jātakarma).
m.3.6.50: In my fifth year my father taught me the Vedas completely, together with their auxiliaries and subsidiary branches, and other scriptures as well.
m.3.6.51: When my seventh year was complete, two sages named Mitra and Varuṇa came to his hermitage to see me, at the command of the Lord.
m.3.6.52: Honoured by that sage and comfortably seated, the two great-souled great sages, gazing at me again and again, spoke.
m.3.6.53: Mitra and Varuṇa said: Dear one, your Nandī, though he has mastered the meaning of all scriptures, is short-lived. Indeed, no life beyond one year from now is seen; we have not seen it.
m.3.6.54: When the two brahmins had spoken thus, Śilāda, loving his son, embraced him and, stricken with grief, wept loudly in a broken voice.
m.3.6.55: Seeing my father and grandfather fallen as if dead, I, serene in mind, remembering the lotus feet of Śiva, replied:
m.3.6.56: From what sorrow, dear father, do you weep, trembling? Whence has your sorrow arisen? I wish to know it truly.
m.3.6.57: The father said: I am exceedingly grieved by the sorrow of your early death, my little son. Who will remove my sorrow? To him I go for refuge.
m.3.6.58: The son said: Whether a god or a demon, or Yama or Kāla—even if these, and other beings too, should rise against me,
m.3.6.59: even so, early death will not befall me; do not torment yourself. I speak the truth, father; I swear it to you.
m.3.6.60: The father said: What austerity, what knowledge, what yoga, and who is your lord, by which you will evade this dreadful sorrow, my son?
m.3.6.61: The son said: Not by austerity, father, nor by learning shall I evade death; by the worship of Mahādeva I shall conquer death, not otherwise.
m.3.6.62: Nandīśvara said: Having said this, O sage, I bowed my head at my father's feet, circumambulated him, and went to an excellent forest.
m.3.6.iti: Thus ends the sixth adhyāya, named The incarnation as Nandikeśa, in the third saṃhitā, the Śatarudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.3.7.1: Nandīśvara said: Having gone there, O sage, I, wise as I was, stayed in a secluded spot and performed fierce austerity, hard to do even for the best of sages.
m.3.7.2: Meditating in the cavity of the lotus of my heart on the god Tryambaka, the three-eyed, ten-armed, peaceful, five-faced Sadāśiva,
m.3.7.3: I performed the japa of the Rudra hymn, established in supreme meditation, on the holy northern bank of the river, single-minded and composed.
m.3.7.4: Then, pleased with that japa, the Supreme Lord Mahādeva, together with Umā, adorned with the half-moon, satisfied, spoke to me as I stood there.
m.3.7.5: Śiva said: O son of Śilāda, I am pleased by this austerity and will grant you a boon. Well have you performed austerity, O wise one; tell me what is in your mind.
m.3.7.6: Thus addressed by the god, I bowed my head at his feet and praised the Supreme Lord, the destroyer of old age and sorrow.
m.3.7.7: Then Śambhu, seeing me, Nandin, full of supreme devotion, eyes filled with tears, bowed properly with my head at his feet,
m.3.7.8: the Supreme Lord, remover of the greatest affliction, bull-bannered, raised me up, took hold of me with both hands facing me, and touched me.
m.3.7.9: Looking at the gaṇa leaders and at the goddess, daughter of Himavat, the Lord of the worlds, gazing on me with a compassionate look, spoke to me:
m.3.7.10: Dear child Nandin, greatly wise one, whence your fear of death? It was I who sent the two brahmins. You are equal to me, no doubt.
m.3.7.11: You will be immortal, free from old age, without sorrow, ever a lord of gaṇas, imperishable, undecaying, beloved, together with your father and your friends.
m.3.7.12: Having my strength, always at my side, you will be dear to me forever. By my grace there will be no old age, birth or death for you.
m.3.7.13: Nandīśvara said: Having said this, the treasure of compassion took off his own head-garland made of lotuses and quickly tied it around my neck.
m.3.7.14: By that auspicious garland clinging to my neck, O brahmin, I became three-eyed and ten-armed, like a second Śaṅkara.
m.3.7.15: Then, taking me by the hand, the Supreme Lord said: Tell me, what excellent boon shall I give you today?
m.3.7.16: Then the bull-bannered one took water held in his matted locks, pure as a pearl necklace, and saying, become a river here, released it.
m.3.7.17: Then five rivers began to flow, bringing auspiciousness, with good water, of great speed, divine in form and beautiful.
m.3.7.18: Jaṭodakā, Trisrotā, Vṛṣadhvani, Svarṇodakā and Jambunadī: thus are the five rivers celebrated.
m.3.7.19: This is called Pañcanada, auspicious and most closely connected with Śiva; near Japeśvara it is supremely purifying, O sage.
m.3.7.20: Whoever reaches Pañcanada, bathes, does japa and worships the Lord of lords, surely attains union with Śiva; there is no doubt.
m.3.7.21: Then Śambhu said to Umā: I shall consecrate Nandin; I shall proclaim him lord of the gaṇas. What do you think, O imperishable one?
m.3.7.22: Umā said: You should grant it to Nandin, O lord of gods, O Supreme Lord. The son of Śilāda is my most dearly beloved son, O master.
m.3.7.23: Nandīśvara said: Then that Śaṅkara, the independent Supreme Lord, giver of all, affectionate to devotees, called to mind his own excellent gaṇa leaders.
m.3.7.24: At Rudra's mere remembrance the lords of gaṇas arrived, countless, greatly joyful, all of them in Śaṅkara's form.
m.3.7.25: Those gaṇa lords, bowing to Śiva and the Goddess, spoke auspicious words; bowing, with joined hands and lowered shoulders, those mighty ones said:
m.3.7.26: The chiefs of the attendants said: For what purpose have we been remembered, O god? Command us, great lord, your servants who have come, O destroyer of Tripura, granter of desires.
m.3.7.27: Shall we dry up the oceans, or slay Yama along with his servants, Death, the Great Death, or especially the aged lotus-born Brahmā?
m.3.7.28: Shall we bind and bring Indra with the gods, or Viṣṇu with his attendants, or the furious Daityas together with the Dānavas?
m.3.7.29: On whom shall we bring dreadful calamity today at your command? Or for whom shall there be a festival today, O god, for the fulfilment of all desires?
m.3.7.30: Nandīśvara said: Hearing these words of the heroically speaking gaṇas, the Supreme Lord praised those gaṇa lords and spoke to them.
m.3.7.31: Śiva said: This Nandīśvara is my son, lord of lords over all, dear, foremost of the gaṇas. Let my word be carried out by all.
m.3.7.32: All of you, with love, consecrate him as the refuge and lord of my gaṇas. From today this Nandīśvara is your master.
m.3.7.33: Nandīśvara said: Thus addressed by Śaṅkara, all those gaṇa leaders said so be it and then brought the requisites.
m.3.7.34: Then the gods with Indra, those headed by Nārāyaṇa, the sages and the worlds came from all sides with joyful faces.
