m.3.7.35: The Grandsire too, O venerable one, at Śaṅkara's command, attentively performed the entire consecration of Nandin.
m.3.7.36: Then Viṣṇu, then Śakra, and likewise the guardians of the worlds and the sages, headed by the Grandsire, offered praise.
m.3.7.37: While they were praising, Viṣṇu, lord of all worlds, placing joined palms on his head, also praised attentively.
m.3.7.38: With joined palms and bowing, he raised the cry of victory; then all the gaṇa chiefs, then the gods, then the asuras did so.
m.3.7.39: Thus was I, Nandīśvara, O best of brahmins, praised and consecrated then by the gods together with Brahmā, at the command of the Supreme Lord.
m.3.7.40: And there, at the command of the Supreme One, my marriage was performed with love by Viṣṇu, Brahmā and the others, accompanied by a great festival.
m.3.7.41: And the daughter of the Maruts, the charming goddess Suyaśā, divine and a delight to mind and eyes, became my wife.
m.3.7.42: There, a parasol radiant as the moon was obtained, adorned by her, accompanied by chowries and by groups of women whose fingertips held the chowries.
m.3.7.43: And the supreme lion-throne was occupied by me together with her; I was adorned by Mahālakṣmī with fine ornaments, a crown and the rest.
m.3.7.44: Likewise I obtained a supreme necklace that had been on the Goddess's neck, and a lordly bull, a white elephant, a lion, and a lion-banner too.
m.3.7.45: and a chariot, and an auspicious golden necklace like the disc of the moon; other things too were obtained by me, O sage.
m.3.7.46: Thus, having been married to that wife, O great sage, I bowed at the feet of Śambhu, of Śivā, of Brahmā and of Hari.
m.3.7.47: To me, in that state and together with my wife, the Lord of the three worlds, the master Śiva, affectionate to devotees, spoke with supreme love.
m.3.7.48: Īśvara said: Listen, good son: you are dear, and this Suyaśā is your beloved. With love I grant you the boon that is desired in your mind.
m.3.7.49: I am always pleased with you, O Nandīśa, lord of the gaṇas, together with the Goddess; dear child, hear my supreme word.
m.3.7.50: You shall be ever dear and distinguished, endowed with supreme lordship, a great yogin, a great archer, together with your father and grandfather;
m.3.7.51: invincible, all-conquering, ever worthy of worship, of great strength. Where I am, there you are; and where you are, there too am I.
m.3.7.52: And this father of yours, son, endowed with supreme lordship, will be a chief of the gaṇas, my devotee, of great strength.
m.3.7.53: Your grandfather too, dear child—let it be so; these are the decrees. Likewise, having received boons from me, they will come to my presence.
m.3.7.54: Nandīśvara said: Then the most fortunate Goddess, the giver of boons, said to Nandin: Tell me a boon, son—all desires as you wish.
m.3.7.55: Hearing that speech of the Goddess, he then spoke with joined palms: May I always have excellent devotion to your feet, O Goddess.
m.3.7.56: Hearing my words, the Goddess said, so be it, and with great affection spoke to that auspicious Suyaśā, the most beloved of Nandin.
m.3.7.57: The Goddess said: Dear daughter, receive a boon as you desire: be three-eyed and free from birth; and may there be devotion to me through your sons and grandsons, and likewise to your husband.
m.3.7.58: Nandīśvara said: Then Brahmā and Viṣṇu and all the hosts of gods, greatly pleased, lovingly gave boons to the two of them at Śiva's command.
m.3.7.59: Then the Lord Īśāna, taking me with my lineage, along with relatives and kinsmen, mounted the bull and went with the Goddess to his own abode.
m.3.7.60: Then all those gods headed by Viṣṇu, praising this, went joyfully to their own abodes, extolling the auspicious Śiva.
m.3.7.61: Thus, dear child, O great sage, my own incarnation has been told to you—ever bringing joy to people and increasing devotion to Śiva.
m.3.7.62: Whoever would hear, or cause to be heard, this account of Nandin's birth, likewise the bestowal of boons on me, the consecration and the marriage,
m.3.7.63: or would read it or have it read, full of faith and devotion, enjoys all happiness here and attains the supreme goal hereafter.
m.3.7.iti: Thus ends the seventh adhyāya, named The consecration and marriage of the incarnation Nandikeśvara, in the third saṃhitā, the Śatarudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.3.8.1: Nandīśvara said: O Sanatkumāra, all-knowing one, listen to the story of Bhairava, by merely hearing which devotion to Śiva becomes firm.
m.3.8.2: Bhairava is indeed the complete form of Śaṅkara, the Supreme Self. Fools, deluded by Śiva's māyā, do not know him.
m.3.8.3: O Sanatkumāra, even four-armed Viṣṇu, even four-faced Brahmā does not know the greatness of the Great Lord.
m.3.8.4: There is nothing surprising in this: Śambhu's māyā is truly hard to comprehend. Deluded by it, all fail even to worship him, the Supreme.
m.3.8.5: If the Supreme Lord himself makes himself known, then they all know him; no one knows him by his own will.
m.3.8.6: Though all-pervading, Maheśāna is not seen by the dull-minded. He who transcends minds and words is regarded in the world as just a god.
m.3.8.7: On this I shall relate an ancient account, O great sage. Listen to it with faith, dear one; it is a supreme cause of knowledge.
m.3.8.8: All the divine sages went to Lord Brahmā, who was seated on a wondrous, lovely peak of Meru, wishing to know the true reality.
m.3.8.9: Arriving there and bowing to Brahmā, all those chief sages, with joined palms and bent shoulders, questioned him with great reverence.
m.3.8.10: The divine sages said: O God of gods, lord of creatures, creator, leader of the worlds, tell us truly: what is the one imperishable reality?
m.3.8.11: Nandīśvara said: The lotus-born Brahmā, deluded by Maheśa's māyā, not knowing the supreme truth, replied out of self-esteem.
m.3.8.12: Brahmā said: O gods and sages, all of you, listen attentively with a good mind: I shall tell you truly the supreme, imperishable reality.
m.3.8.13: I am the womb of the world, the Creator, self-born, unborn, the Lord; I am without beginning, Brahman, the one stainless Self.
m.3.8.14: I alone set the worlds in motion, I withdraw them and dissolve them; there is no one else greater than me, O best of gods.
m.3.8.15: Nandīśvara said: As the Creator spoke thus, Viṣṇu, who was present there, O sage, angered and deluded by the unborn māyā, laughingly said these words:
m.3.8.16: O Brahmā, this foolishness does not befit one endowed with yoga. Not knowing the supreme reality, you speak this in vain.
m.3.8.17: I am the maker of all the worlds, the Supreme Self, the highest Person, the Sacrifice, the god Nārāyaṇa, lord of māyā, the supreme goal.
m.3.8.18: O Brahmā, it is by my command that this creation is carried out by you; and there is no life for the worlds if I, the Lord, am disregarded.
m.3.8.19: Thus quarrelling out of delusion, each desiring victory over the other, they called upon the Vedas, present here in bodily form, as the authority in every respect.
m.3.8.20: They should especially be asked, for they stand here bearing forms. Having said this, the two questioned all four of them, the knowers of authority.
m.3.8.21: Brahmā and Viṣṇu said: O Vedas, you are the authority everywhere and have attained the highest standing. Tell us confidently: what is the one imperishable reality?
m.3.8.22: Nandīśvara said: Hearing their words, the Ṛg and the other Vedas, all remembering the Supreme Lord, spoke truthfully again.
m.3.8.23: If we are respected by you, O two mighty gods who bring about creation and preservation, then we shall state the authority that dispels your doubt.
m.3.8.24: Nandīśvara said: Hearing the condition stated by the Śrutis, the two gods said to them: What you say is authority for us; let the reality be properly stated.
m.3.8.25: The Ṛgveda said: That within which all beings abide, from which everything proceeds, which they call the supreme reality — that is Rudra alone, the One.
m.3.8.26: The Yajurveda said: The Lord who is worshipped by all sacrifices and by yoga, through whom we are indeed authoritative — he is the one all-seeing Śiva.
m.3.8.27: The Sāmaveda said: He by whom this universe is set revolving, who is contemplated by yogins, by whose light the universe shines — he is the one supreme Tryambaka.
m.3.8.28: The Atharvaṇaveda said: The Lord of gods whom people favoured through devotion behold — him they call the One, Kaivalya liberation itself, Śaṅkara, beyond sorrow.
m.3.8.29: Nandīśvara said: Hearing this declared by the Śrutis, Brahmā and Hari, utterly deluded by māyā and bereft of sense, smiled and said to those Vedas:
m.3.8.30: Brahmā and Hari said: O Vedas, what is this you say, as if you had lost your senses? What has happened to you today? All your excellent, supreme knowledge is lost.
m.3.8.31: How can that lord of the Pramathas — who sports ceaselessly with Śivā, naked, yellowish in hue, grey with dust,
m.3.8.32: of hideous attire, matted-haired, riding a bull, adorned with snakes — have attained the state of the supreme Brahman? And where is that Brahman which is free of attachment?
m.3.8.33: Hearing what they had said, the all-pervading Praṇava, formless yet assuming form, manifesting with goodwill, spoke to the two.
m.3.8.34: The Praṇava said: The Lord, the blessed Rudra, Hara, who takes on forms in play, never sports with a Śakti separate from himself.
m.3.8.35: He is the Supreme Lord, self-luminous, eternal; and this Śakti of his, Śivā, whose nature is bliss, is not something adventitious.
m.3.8.36: Nandīśvara said: Though thus addressed, the ignorance of Brahmā and Viṣṇu was not then destroyed, owing to the māyā of Śrīkaṇṭha alone.
m.3.8.37: Then a great light appeared between the two, filling with its own radiance the space between heaven and earth.
m.3.8.38: There, in the middle of the circle of light, O sage, a figure in human form with a most wondrous body was seen by Brahmā and Viṣṇu.
m.3.8.39: Then Brahmā's fifth head blazed with anger: Who is this who bears a human form between the two of us?
m.3.8.40: Even as Brahmā was pondering thus, in an instant that three-eyed Great Person, blue and red Nīlalohita, was seen.
m.3.8.41: He appeared trident in hand, with an eye on his forehead, adorned with serpents and the moon. Seeing him, Hiraṇyagarbha, deluded, laughed and said:
m.3.8.42: Brahmā said: O Nīlalohita, I know you; do not be afraid, O Candraśekhara. Long ago you came forth from my forehead as Rudra.
m.3.8.43: Because of your weeping, I also gave you the name Rudra long ago. Take refuge in me alone, son; I will protect you.
m.3.8.44: Nandīśvara said: Then the Lord, hearing the arrogant words of the lotus-born one, became exceedingly angry at that moment, as if about to bring about dissolution, O sage.
m.3.8.45: The Supreme Lord, out of anger, brought forth a certain being, Bhairava, blazing with great splendour, and with affection spoke to him:
m.3.8.46: Īśvara said: First, this lotus-born one is to be punished by you, O Kālabhairava. You shine like Kāla (Time) himself; therefore you are Kālarāja.
m.3.8.47: You are able to sustain the universe; because you are terrifying you are called Bhairava. Even Kāla will fear you; therefore you are Kālabhairava.
m.3.8.48: Since you, when angered, will crush the wicked-souled, you will gain fame everywhere as Āmardaka (the Crusher).
m.3.8.49: Since you will devour the sins of devotees at that very instant, your name will be Pāpabhakṣaṇa (Devourer of Sins).
m.3.8.50: Kāśī, my city of liberation, greater than all cities — sovereignty over it is yours forever, O Kālarāja.
m.3.8.51: Of the sinful men there, you alone are the punisher; and Citragupta will record their deeds, good and bad.
m.3.8.52: Nandīśvara said: Having received these boons, Kālabhairava then, at that very moment, cut off Vidhi's head with the tip of the nail of his left finger.
m.3.8.53: Whichever limb offends, that alone should be punished. Therefore the fifth head, by which the censure was uttered, was cut off.
m.3.8.54: Then, seeing Vidhi's head severed, Hari, greatly frightened, praised Śaṅkara with devotion using the Śatarudriya mantras.
m.3.8.55: Hiraṇyagarbha too, frightened, recited the Śatarudriya. Thus those two became free of pride at that very moment, O sage.
m.3.8.56: They attained the knowledge that Śiva is directly the Supreme Brahman, characterized by being, consciousness and bliss, the Supreme Self, beyond the guṇas.
m.3.8.57: O omniscient Sanatkumāra, hear from me this supremely auspicious truth: as long as there is pride, so long is knowledge especially concealed.
m.3.8.58: Having given up self-conceit, a person comes to know the Supreme Lord. The Lord of the universe destroys the proud, having become the remover of pride.
m.3.8.59: Then the Supreme Lord, knowing Viṣṇu and Vidhi to be free of pride, became pleased; the Lord Mahādeva made them both fearless.
m.3.8.60: Having reassured the two, Mahādeva, pleased and affectionate to those who bow to him, spoke to his other form, that matted-haired Bhairava.
m.3.8.61: Mahādeva said: This Viṣṇu is to be honoured by you, and likewise Śatadhṛti (Brahmā) himself. And carry Vedhas's skull, O Nīlalohita.
m.3.8.62: For the removal of the sin of brahmin-slaying, show the world this vow: having adopted the skull-vow, wander constantly for alms.
m.3.8.63: Having said this, Śiva, whose form is radiance, brought forth, while he (Bhairava) looked on, a maiden renowned as Brahmahatyā, and spoke to her:
m.3.8.64: Until this one reaches the divine city of Vārāṇasī, until then you follow this terrible Kāla of fierce form.
m.3.8.65: You may enter everywhere except the city of Vārāṇasī. When he goes to Vārāṇasī, at that very instant be released from him.
m.3.8.66: Nandīśvara said: Having thus appointed that Brahmahatyā, the Lord Śiva, greatly wondrous, then vanished from there.
m.3.8.iti: Thus ends the eighth adhyāya, named The incarnation as Bhairava, in the third saṃhitā, the Śatarudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.3.9.1: Nandīśvara said: O omniscient Sanatkumāra, listen with delight to another story of Bhairava, which destroys great sins and increases devotion.
m.3.9.2: Bhairava too, Kāla, who brings even Time to its end, was accompanied by her Brahmahatyā; at the word of the God of gods he bore the Kāpālika vow,
m.3.9.3: and, skull in hand, the Self of the universe wandered through the three worlds; yet the dreadful Brahmahatyā did not leave that god.
m.3.9.4: Though wandering to every sacred ford, he was not freed from Brahmahatyā. From this let the whole greatness of the foe of Kāma be understood.
m.3.9.5: Once Hara, though attended by the Pramathas, roaming freely as a Kāpālika, went to the abode of Nārāyaṇa.
m.3.9.6: Then, seeing Bhairava approaching—Mahākāla, three-eyed, with serpents for earrings, born of a portion of Mahādeva, yet of complete form—
m.3.9.7: having seen him, the Garuḍa-bannered Viṣṇu fell flat on the ground like a stick, and so did the gods, the sages and the celestial women all around.
m.3.9.8: Then Viṣṇu, the lord of Kamalā, having bowed to him, came forward and, placing his joined palms on his head, praised him with various hymns.
m.3.9.9: Then, O great sage, Hari, joyful and serene at heart, gladly spoke to Padmā, who dwells in the lotus and arose from the churning of the milk-ocean.
m.3.9.10: Viṣṇu said: Beloved, look, O lotus-eyed one. You are blessed, O fortunate and sinless one; and I am blessed, O goddess of lovely hips, since we two behold the Lord of the world.
m.3.9.11: He is the sustainer and the ordainer of the worlds, their master and Lord; beginningless, the refuge, the tranquil one, the twenty-sixth principle, standing before us.
m.3.9.12: He is omniscient, lord of all yogins, the sole leader of all beings, the inner Self of all beings, ever the giver of everything to all.
m.3.9.13: He whom the sleepless, those who have stilled their breath, the tranquil ones devoted to meditation, see with their intellect in the heart—behold him here, O Padmā.
m.3.9.14: He whom knowers of the essence of the Veda and yogins with controlled minds know—he, the formless, having taken form, is coming here, the all-pervading one.
m.3.9.15: Ah, how wondrous is the conduct of the supreme God! For one who constantly utters his name there is no further body, yet he himself bears a body.
m.3.9.16: Having seen him, men on earth do not obtain rebirth. He, the blessed Tryambaka adorned with the moon, is coming here.
m.3.9.17: Blessed today are my two eyes, long as lotus petals, O Lakṣmī, since Mahādeva, the great Lord, is seen by them.
m.3.9.18: Fie, fie on the status of the gods, where, even after seeing the supreme Śaṅkara, nirvāṇa, which puts an end to all sorrow, is not attained!
m.3.9.19: In the world of the gods there is nothing more inauspicious than godhood, since all of us, even having seen the Lord of gods, do not obtain liberation.
m.3.9.20: Nandīśvara said: Having spoken thus, Hṛṣīkeśa, his hair bristling with delight, bowed down to Mahādeva, the bull-bannered one, and said this:
m.3.9.21: Viṣṇu said: What is this being done by you, O all-pervading one, God of gods, omniscient sustainer of the worlds, O imperishable remover of all sins?
m.3.9.22: This is your play, O Lord of gods, three-eyed, great-minded one. What is the reason for this conduct of yours, O Virūpākṣa, tormentor of Smara?
m.3.9.23: For what purpose, O blessed Śambhu, lord of Śakti, do you go about begging alms? This is my doubt, O Lord of the world, giver of sovereignty over the three worlds.
m.3.9.24: Nandīśvara said: Thus addressed by Viṣṇu, Śambhu—Hara as Bhairava, the lord of wondrous deeds—then replied to Viṣṇu, laughing.
m.3.9.25: Bhairava said: Brahmā's head was cut off by the tip of the nail of my finger; to destroy that sin I am observing this auspicious vow.
m.3.9.26: Nandīśvara said: Thus addressed by Maheśa as Bhairava, the lord of Ramā reflected for a moment, and with head slightly bowed, again submitted thus:
m.3.9.27: Viṣṇu said: Sport as you wish, O remover of all obstacles; but, Mahādeva, you should not cover me with your illusion.
m.3.9.28: From the cup of the lotus of my navel, in age after age of old, lotus-seated Brahmās arose by the millions, through the power of your command, O all-pervading one.
m.3.9.29: Give up this illusion, O God, hard to cross for those of unperfected self; Brahmā and the others, O Mahādeva, are deluded by your illusion.
m.3.9.30: I understand your conduct as it truly is, O lord of Śivā, only by your grace, O Śambhu, Lord of all, goal of the good.
m.3.9.31: When the time of dissolution arrives and you, O Hara, withdraw all the sages together with the gods, and the worlds with their classes and stages of life—
m.3.9.32: then, O Mahādeva, though sin such as the slaying of Brahmā is committed, there is no subjection to it for you, O Śambhu; therefore you sport freely.
m.3.9.33: A garland of the bones of past Brahmās shines on your neck; even so, O sinless Śambhu, Brahmahatyā follows you.
m.3.9.34: Even having committed a very great sin, the man who remembers you, O Lord, the support of the worlds—his sin dissolves away.
m.3.9.35: Just as darkness cannot remain in the presence of the sun, so the sin of one who is your devotee goes to destruction.
m.3.9.36: The virtuous soul who meditates on your two lotus feet—even his sin of brahmin-slaying goes to destruction.
m.3.9.37: O Lord of the world, the man whose speech is devoted to your name—sin, even if equal to a mountain peak, does not afflict him.
m.3.9.38: O Supreme Self, supreme abode, who assume a form by your own will, O Lord, this subjection like that of a wretched one is merely your playful whim, O Īśvara.
m.3.9.39: Today I am blessed, O Lord of gods, since I see him whom the yogins do not see—the supreme, imperishable Lord whose form is the universe.
m.3.9.40: Today is my supreme gain, today my supreme blessing; having seen you, for me, sated with nectar, heaven and liberation are mere straw.
m.3.9.41: While Govinda was speaking thus, that pure Padmā Lakṣmī placed in the bowl alms named Manorathavatī ('wish-fulfilling').
m.3.9.42: The god then went forth on his alms-round with supreme joy; Mahādeva as Bhairava, having taken on a bodily form, went to other places as well.
m.3.9.43: Seeing her following him, Janārdana called Brahmahatyā to him and entreated her: Release the trident-bearer.
m.3.9.44: Brahmahatyā said: Under this very pretext I shall serve this bull-bannered one, whose sight frees one from rebirth, and so purify myself.
m.3.9.45: Nandīśvara said: Though addressed by Murāri, she did not leave his side. Then Śambhu, as Bhairava, with a smiling face, spoke these words to Hari.
m.3.9.46: Bhairava said: By drinking the nectar of your words I am satisfied, O giver of great honour. What you say, O lord of Mā, is indeed the very nature of the good.
m.3.9.47: Choose a boon, Govinda; I am ready to grant you a boon, O sinless one. You, O Hari, free from all change, are the foremost of my devotees.
m.3.9.48: Mendicants are not delighted even by finely prepared alms so much as those feverish from the begging round are by drinking the nectar of respect.
m.3.9.49: Nandīśvara said: Having heard these words of Śambhu Bhairava, the supreme Self, Viṣṇu became exceedingly pleased and spoke to Maheśvara.
m.3.9.50: Viṣṇu said: This alone is the praiseworthy boon: that I behold you, the lord of the deities, O God of gods, who lie beyond the path of mind and speech.
m.3.9.51: This nectar-like glance is abundant; through it I have a great festival. This sight of you, O Hara, is for the good the gaining of a treasure without effort.
m.3.9.52: May there be no separation for me, O God, from your pair of feet. This alone is the boon, Śambhu; I choose no other boon.
m.3.9.53: Śrī Bhairava said: Let it be for you just as you have said, dear one, O great-minded one. You will also be the giver of boons to all the gods.
m.3.9.54: Nandīśvara said: Having thus favoured the enemy of the Daityas, and wandering through regions, mountains and worlds, he reached the city Avimukta, the city named Vārāṇasī.
m.3.9.55: Then, the moment Bhairava of terrifying form entered the sacred field, Brahmahatyā cried alas and at once entered the netherworld (Pātāla).
m.3.9.56: Brahmā's skull at once fell from Bhairava's lotus-hand to the ground; that place became the tīrtha Kapālamocana ('release of the skull').
m.3.9.57: Seeing Brahmā's skull falling from his hand while all looked on, Rudra danced with supreme joy.
m.3.9.58: The skull of Vidhi (Brahmā), utterly unbearable, did not leave the hand of the Supreme as he wandered anywhere else; in Kāśī it fell away in an instant.
m.3.9.59: The sin of slaying Brahmā, which did not leave the trident-bearer anywhere, perished in Kāśī in an instant; therefore Kāśikā should indeed be resorted to.
m.3.9.60: Whoever remembers Kapālamocana, the supreme tīrtha in Kāśī — whatever sin he has done here or elsewhere quickly perishes.
m.3.9.61: Coming to this best of tīrthas, bathing according to rule, and offering libations to the ancestors and gods, one is freed from the sin of brahmin-slaying.
m.3.9.62: Placing the tīrtha Kapālamocana before him, Bhairava stayed right there, devouring the continuous stream of his devotees' sins.
m.3.9.63: On the eighth day of the dark fortnight of the month Mārgaśīrṣa, the Supreme Lord, engaged in noble sport and dear to the good, manifested in the form of Bhairava.
m.3.9.64: On the dark eighth of Mārgaśīrṣa, one who fasts and keeps vigil in the presence of Kālabhairava is freed from great sins.
m.3.9.65: Even elsewhere, the man who performs that vow with devotion, together with the vigil, will be freed from great sins and go to a good destiny.
m.3.9.66: Whatever sin has been committed by living beings over many myriads of births — all of it dissolves through the sight of Kālabhairava.
m.3.9.67: Whoever commits offences against the devotees of Kālabhairava, that fool becomes wretched and again falls into an evil state.
m.3.9.68: Those who are devoted to Viśveśvara but not devoted to Kālabhairava obtain great suffering, and especially in Kāśī.
m.3.9.69: The man who lives in Vārāṇasī yet does not worship Bhairava — his sins grow like the moon in the bright fortnight.
m.3.9.70: Whoever in Kāśī does not worship Kālarāja on every fourteenth (bhūta), eighth and Tuesday — his merit wanes like the moon in the dark fortnight.
m.3.9.71: Having heard this sacred narrative, called The Origin of Bhairava, which removes the sin of brahmin-slaying, one is freed from all sins.
m.3.9.72: Even one confined in prison, even one who has met the gravest calamity, would be freed from distress by hearing of Bhairava's manifestation.
m.3.9.iti: Thus ends the ninth adhyāya, named The sport of the Bhairava incarnation, in the third saṃhitā, the Śatarudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.3.10.1: Nandīśvara said: The destroyer of Dakṣa's sacrifice, named Vīrabhadra, should be known as an incarnation of the Lord Śiva, the Supreme Self.
m.3.10.2: His story has been told in full in the account of Satī; you too have heard it many times, so it is not narrated here at great length.
m.3.10.3: Next, O best of sages, out of affection for you I shall tell it: hear of the incarnation called Śārdūla of the Lord Śaṅkara.
m.3.10.4: For the welfare of the gods, Sadāśiva assumed a wondrous, divine Śarabha form, radiant like blazing flames.
m.3.10.5: Śiva's incarnations are countless, bringing good to true devotees; O best of sages, it is impossible to count them.
m.3.10.6: The stars of the sky, the dust particles of the earth, and the drops of rain may perhaps at some time be counted by one grown old over many kalpas—
m.3.10.7: —counting them is possible for the very wise over many births, but not of Śiva's incarnations; know my word to be true.
m.3.10.8: Even so, according to my understanding and as I have heard, I shall tell the divine Śarabha story, which reveals his supreme lordship.
m.3.10.9: When Jaya and Vijaya were cursed by you sages, then, O sage, the two were born as sons of Diti from Kaśyapa.
m.3.10.10: Hiraṇyakaśipu was the elder, and the mighty Hiraṇyākṣa the younger; those two attendants of Viṣṇu were born as the sons of Diti.
m.3.10.11: Formerly, entreated by the Creator for the uplifting of the earth, the Lord Viṣṇu, assuming the form of a boar, slew Hiraṇyākṣa.
m.3.10.12: Hearing that his heroic brother, dear as his own life, had been slain, Hiraṇyakaśipu became extremely angry with Hari, O sage.
m.3.10.13: After performing austerities for ten thousand years, he obtained a boon from the pleased Brahmā: May no one in your creation kill me.
m.3.10.14: Going to the city called Śoṇita, summoning the gods from all sides, and bringing the three worlds under his control, he ruled a kingdom free of foes.
m.3.10.15: The sinful Hiraṇyakaśipu, O sage, destroyer of all dharma and tormentor of the twice-born, oppressed the gods and sages.
m.3.10.16: When the king of the Daityas, an enemy of Hari above all, showed hatred toward his own son Prahlāda, a devotee of Hari,
m.3.10.17: then, O sage, Viṣṇu swiftly appeared from a pillar of the assembly hall at twilight, filled with wrath, in the form of Nṛsiṃha.
m.3.10.18: O tiger among sages, the terrible body of the Man-Lion blazed forth, utterly frightening, terrifying the foremost Daityas.
m.3.10.19: Then the Daityas were slain by Nṛsiṃha in that very instant, and Hiraṇyakaśipu then waged a most dreadful battle.
m.3.10.20: A great battle took place between the two for a muhūrta, O best of sages—fierce, fearsome, and hair-raising for all.
m.3.10.21: At dusk, Nṛsiṃha, the lord of the gods and lord of Ramā, dragged the chief of Daityas to the threshold, while the gods watched from the sky.
m.3.10.22: Then, placing him on his lap, he swiftly tore open his belly with his nails and killed him as the dwellers of heaven looked on.
m.3.10.23: When Hiraṇyakaśipu was slain by Viṣṇu as Nṛsiṃha, the world then regained its well-being, but the gods in particular did not.
m.3.10.24: The gods' kettledrums sounded; Prahlāda was astonished, and Lakṣmī too was amazed on seeing the wondrous form of Hari.
m.3.10.25: Although the lord of Daityas was slain, the gods did not attain complete happiness, for that blaze of Nṛsiṃha did not subside.
m.3.10.26: By it the whole world was again thrown into turmoil, and the gods fell into distress, thinking: What will happen now?
m.3.10.27: Speaking thus, the gods headed by the Lotus-born Brahmā, tormented by the blaze born of Nṛsiṃha's wrath, stood far off out of fear.
m.3.10.28: They sent Prahlāda near Hari to pacify it; entreated by all of them together, Prahlāda then went.
m.3.10.29: Nṛsiṃha, the treasury of compassion, embraced him to his chest; his heart grew cool, yet the blaze of wrath did not subside.
m.3.10.30: When even so the Man-Lion's blaze of wrath did not subside, the gods, distressed, sought refuge with Śaṅkara.
m.3.10.31: Going there, all the gods headed by Brahmā, and the sages too, praised Śaṅkara for the happiness of the worlds.
m.3.10.32: The gods said: O God of gods, Mahādeva, loving to those who come for refuge, protect us, all the gods who have sought refuge, and the worlds.
m.3.10.33: Salutations to you, salutations to you, salutations to you, O Sadāśiva. Whenever distress arose before, we were protected by you.
m.3.10.34: When the ocean was churned and the gods divided the jewels, then, O Śambhu, the poison was taken by you.
m.3.10.35: Then we were protected, O Lord, and you became known as Nīlakaṇṭha; had you not drunk the poison, all would then have been reduced to ashes.
m.3.10.36: It is well known, O Lord, that whenever anyone has distress, then by your name alone all distress dissolves.
m.3.10.37: Now, O Sadāśiva, protect us who are tormented by the Man-Lion's blaze; you, O God, are surely able to quell it.
m.3.10.38: Nandīśvara said: Thus praised by the gods, Śaṅkara, the supreme Lord, loving to his devotees, gracious at heart, granted fearlessness and replied.
m.3.10.39: Śaṅkara said: Go to your own abodes, all you gods headed by Brahmā, free from fear. I shall quell this distress entirely; that indeed is my vow.
m.3.10.40: Whoever has come to me for refuge, his distress has come to an end. One who has sought refuge in me is dearer to me than life itself; there is no doubt.
m.3.10.41: Nandīśvara said: Having heard this, the gods then attained supreme joy, and they went back the way they had come, joyfully remembering Śaṅkara.
m.3.10.iti: Thus ends the tenth adhyāya, named The story of Nṛsiṃha, in the Śārdūla incarnation, in the third saṃhitā, the Śatarudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.3.11.1: Nandīśvara said: Thus entreated by the gods, the Supreme Lord, abode of compassion, resolved to withdraw the great fiery energy called Nṛsiṃha.
m.3.11.2: Thereupon Rudra called to mind the mighty Vīrabhadra, whom he declared to be his own terrible (Bhairava) form, the bringer of dissolution.
m.3.11.3: Then at once there came, laughing, the foremost of the gaṇas, with excellent gaṇas laughing loudly and leaping here and there,
m.3.11.4: surrounded by crores of exceedingly fierce beings in the form of Nṛsiṃha, and on all sides by heroes who were frenzied, dancing and filled with joy,
m.3.11.5: and by great heroes playing with Brahmā and the others as if with balls, and by other beings never seen before—thus encircled, honoured by heroes,
m.3.11.6: blazing like the fire at the end of the aeon, with three shining eyes, weaponless, with matted locks, adorned with the radiant crescent moon,
m.3.11.7: with a pair of sharp budding tusks shaped like the curve of the crescent moon, with creeper-like brows resembling a segment of Indra's bow (the rainbow),
m.3.11.8: deafening the quarters with his tremendously fierce huṃ roar, dark as a blue cloud or collyrium, terrifying, bearded, wondrous,
m.3.11.9: whirling again and again with his two unbroken arms the three-pointed trident like a drumstick—the blessed Vīrabhadra too, swelling with heroic power,
m.3.11.10: himself submitted: What is the reason for calling me to mind here? Command me, O Lord of the world; let your grace be shown to me.
m.3.11.11: Nandīśvara said: Having heard these words spoken by Vīrabhadra with respect, and regarding him with affection, Maheśāna, who wields the rod against the wicked, spoke.
m.3.11.12: Śaṅkara said: An untimely, dreadful fear has arisen even among the gods. That fire of Nṛsiṃha is blazing; pacify it, hard to approach as it is.
m.3.11.13: First, consoling him, bring him to understanding. If by that he is not calmed, then reveal my supreme terrible form.
m.3.11.14: Withdrawing the subtle by the subtle and the gross by gross energy, bring that fire under control, O Vīrabhadra, by my command.
m.3.11.15: Nandīśvara said: Thus commanded, the chief of the gaṇas assumed a calm form and went swiftly to where the Man-Lion was.
m.3.11.16: Then Vīrabhadra, a form of Hara, addressed Hari; the Lord spoke words as a father to his own son.
m.3.11.17: Vīrabhadra said: O Lord Mādhava, you have descended for the happiness of the world. You, a supreme lord, have been appointed by the Supreme Being for its preservation.
m.3.11.18: Long ago, in the single ocean, you, the Lord in the form of a fish, bound the hidden host of creatures with your tail alone and moved about carrying them.
m.3.11.19: In the form of a tortoise you bear the earth; by the Boar the earth was lifted up; by this lion form Hiraṇyakaśipu has been slain.
m.3.11.20: Again, as Vāmana striding forth, you bound Bali. You alone are the origin of all beings, the imperishable Lord.
m.3.11.21: Whenever any sorrow arises for the world, then you descend and will make it free of affliction.
m.3.11.22: O Hari, there is none greater than you, nor even equal to you, in devotion to Śiva. By you the Vedas and the dharmas are established on the auspicious path.
m.3.11.23: That demon for whose sake this incarnation took place, Hiraṇyakaśipu, has indeed been slain, and Prahlāda too is well protected.
m.3.11.24: O Lord, your Man-Lion body is exceedingly terrible. O Soul of the universe, withdraw it yourself in my presence.
m.3.11.25: Nandīśvara said: Addressed thus by Vīrabhadra in gentle speech, Nṛsiṃha, greatly arrogant, became even more terribly enraged.
m.3.11.26: And then, O sage, terrifying the great hero Vīrabhadra with his fangs, he spoke very dreadful, harsh words.
m.3.11.27: Nṛsiṃha said: Go back to where you came from; do not speak to me of my good. Now I shall destroy this world of moving and unmoving beings.
m.3.11.28: For the destroyer there is no destruction, either from himself or from another. My rule extends everywhere; there is no ruler over me at all.
m.3.11.29: By my grace everything proceeds free from fear. I indeed am the one who sets in motion and withdraws all powers.
m.3.11.30: Whatever being is glorious, splendid or mighty, know that, O chief of the gaṇas, to be an expansion of my splendour.
m.3.11.31: The deities know me alone as the Supreme, the knower of ultimate truth. Brahmā, Śakra and the other gods, endowed with power, are portions of me.
m.3.11.32: Long ago Brahmā, maker of the world, was born from the lotus of my navel. I am supreme over all, independent, the creator, the destroyer, lord of all.
m.3.11.33: This is my supreme splendour; what more do you wish to hear? Therefore, taking refuge in me, go, free from anxiety.
m.3.11.34: Know, O lord of the gaṇas, this supreme state that has come into being: the entire universe, with gods, demons and humans, is mine.
m.3.11.35: I am Time, the cause of the world's destruction; I have set out to withdraw the worlds. Know me, O Vīrabhadra, as the death of Death; these gods live by my grace.
m.3.11.36: Nandīśvara said: Hearing Hari's arrogant words, Vīrabhadra of immeasurable prowess laughed and then spoke contemptuously, his lip quivering.
m.3.11.37: Vīrabhadra said: Do you not know Pinākin, the Lord of the universe, the destroyer? False talk and quarrel lead to nothing but destruction for you.
m.3.11.38: Which of your various incarnations now remain? They were brought about by someone or other; you will remain only as a tale.
m.3.11.39: Name that fault through which you have come to such a state. By that One skilled in destruction you will be brought to a mere remnant, like Dakṣa's sacrifice.
m.3.11.40: You are Prakṛti; Rudra is the Person (Puruṣa); his seed is deposited in you. From the lotus of your navel was born the five-faced Grandsire Brahmā.
m.3.11.41: For the creation of the three worlds, he Brahmā, established in fierce austerity, meditated in his forehead on Śaṅkara, the blue-red one (Nīlalohita).
m.3.11.42: From his forehead Śambhu arose for the sake of creation; by him Brahmā was adorned. Therefore I, of that god of gods who has the form of Bhairava, —
m.3.11.43: — am appointed for your destruction, with both restraint and force, by Rudra, the god of gods, the lord of all, O Hari.
m.3.11.44: Having merely torn apart a single demon, while endowed with a fraction of his power, you roar tirelessly in the arrogance of your ego.
m.3.11.45: A kindness done to the good is indeed held to lead to happiness; but a kindness done to the wicked leads only to harm.
m.3.11.46: If, O Nṛsiṃha, you regard the great lord as one who has been born again, then you are ignorant, greatly conceited, and wholly subject to distortion.
m.3.11.47: You are not the creator, not the destroyer, nor even the sustainer, O little Nṛsiṃha; you are dependent, deluded in mind, and never independent anywhere.
m.3.11.48: Like a potter's wheel you are set in motion by the power of Pinākin; you, the maker of various incarnations, are always dependent on him, O Hari.
m.3.11.49: Even today the skull of you, when you were in the form of a tortoise, lies set, burnt, in the middle of Hara's necklace-string — yet is no one restrained by this?
m.3.11.50: Have you forgotten how, by his portion, you in the boar form were tormented by the uprooting of your tusk, crying out today in the hand of the obstacle-remover, by the foe of Tāraka?
m.3.11.51: See: you were burnt by the fire of the trident, under the guise of Viṣvaksena; at Dakṣa's sacrifice your head was cut off by me, embodied as splendour.
m.3.11.52: Even today the fifth head of Brahmā, your son, once cut off, has not been restored again; O Hari, have you forgotten that?
m.3.11.53: You, together with the hosts of Maruts, were defeated by Dadhīca in battle; how, as you scratch your head, have you forgotten that?
m.3.11.54: The discus dear to you, O Cakrapāṇi — from whose prowess was it obtained, by whom was it made? That too you have forgotten.
m.3.11.55: When all the worlds are seized in dissolution by me, you lie in the ocean overpowered by sleep; how then are you called sāttvika?
m.3.11.56: From you down to a blade of grass, everything is the unfolding of Rudra's power; and though you appear endowed with power all around, you are deluded by his fire.
m.3.11.57: No person is able to behold the greatness of that splendour; only those who are not gross perceive that supreme abode of Viṣṇu.
m.3.11.58: Of heaven and earth, of Indra and Agni, of Yama and of Varuṇa, within the belly of darkness and in the moon, the Supreme Lord is the generator.
m.3.11.59: You are Time; Maheśvara is the Great Time, the Time of Time. Therefore, by his fierce portion, you will meet the death of death.
m.3.11.60: He is steady, imperishable, the hero, the hero, the protector of all, the lord, the destroyer of fever, the terrible one — beast, bird, golden.
m.3.11.61: The ruler of the entire world is not you, nor the four-faced Brahmā, nor others; Śambhu alone is the ruler of all — there is no doubt.
m.3.11.62: Having thus considered everything — him whose very self is destruction — do not, by your own doing, bring yourself to ruin, O foolish man-lion.
m.3.11.63: Otherwise, now death from the wrath of the one in the form of Mahābhairava will fall upon you, like a thunderbolt upon a tree-trunk.
m.3.11.64: Nandīśvara said: Having spoken thus, Vīrabhadra, who feared nothing from any quarter — he, the embodiment of Śiva's wrath — fell silent, having observed Nṛsiṃha's intention.
m.3.11.iti: Thus ends the eleventh adhyāya, named The incarnation as Śarabha, in the third saṃhitā, the Śatarudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.3.12.1: Sanatkumāra said: O Nandīśvara, most wise one, you know what happened after that. Show me kindness and, out of affection, tell it to me now.
m.3.12.2: Nandīśvara said: Addressed thus by Vīrabhadra, Nṛsiṃha, overwhelmed with anger, roared and rushed forward to seize him.
m.3.12.3: Meanwhile a radiance of Śiva arose: exceedingly terrible, a visible cause of fear, pervading the sky, and irresistible.
m.3.12.4: Then in a moment that form of Vīrabhadra became invisible. That radiance was golden and gentle, neither of the sun nor born of fire,
m.3.12.5: not like lightning or the moon, incomparable, belonging to Maheśvara. Then all radiances merged into that Śaṅkara.
m.3.12.6: Then the sky was no longer to be seen. That great radiance became manifest within it, marked with the emblems common to Rudra, and of a monstrous shape.
m.3.12.7: Then, as all the gods looked on, amid auspicious sounds such as cries of victory, the Supreme Lord became clearly manifest in the form of destruction:
m.3.12.8: thousand-armed, with matted hair, with the half-moon as his crest; a bird with a mighty, fierce body, two wings and a beak;
m.3.12.9: exceedingly sharp, with huge fangs, with claws like thunderbolts for weapons, black at the throat, mighty-armed, four-footed, blazing like fire;
m.3.12.10: with a dreadful, deep roar like storm clouds risen at the end of an age, his three eyes rolling like the fire of a furious kṛtyā;
m.3.12.11: with fangs and lips plainly visible, accompanied by roars of huṃ. In such a form the fierce Hara appeared.
m.3.12.12: At the very sight of him Hari lost his strength and valour, looking like a firefly beneath the brilliance of the sun.
m.3.12.13: Then, wheeling about with his wings and tearing at his navel and feet, he bound his feet with his tail and the ring of his arms with his arms.
m.3.12.14: Piercing him in the chest with his arms, Hara seized Hari. Then he went up into the sky together with the gods and great sages.
m.3.12.15: Fearlessly and suddenly he carried Viṣṇu off as a hawk carries a snake, tossing him up again and again, catching him, and dashing him down again and again.
m.3.12.16: Flying up again and again, the blessed Hara, the infinite Lord, bore that Hari, the foremost of gods, stunned by the blows of his wings, and entered the sky.
m.3.12.17: All the gods, following him, praised him with words of homage, and Brahmā and the others and the chief sages bowed with reverence and love.
m.3.12.18: Being carried off, helpless, with a downcast face and folded hands, Hari praised that Supreme Lord in graceful words.
m.3.12.19: Having praised that Mṛḍa with a hundred and eight names, Nṛsiṃha then entreated the Lord Śarabha:
m.3.12.20: Whenever this ignorant mind of mine becomes tainted by pride, then, O Supreme Lord, it must be removed by you alone.
m.3.12.21: Nandīśvara said: Thus lovingly entreating Śaṅkara, Viṣṇu the man-lion bowed and became powerless, vanquished to the end of his life.
m.3.12.22: Then in a moment Vīrabhadra took his face, severed where the rest of the body ended, making it his whole embodiment, and his limb (skin) endowed with power.
m.3.12.23: Nandīśvara said: Then Brahmā and the other gods praised the god Śaṅkara, who had assumed the Śarabha form, the sole benefactor of all the worlds.
m.3.12.24: The gods said: O Maheśvara, all the gods such as Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Indra and Candra, all the great sages, and the sons of Diti and others are born from you.
m.3.12.25: You create, protect and devour Brahmā, Viṣṇu, great Indra, the Sun and the others, the asuras and the gods; you alone are the Lord of all.
m.3.12.26: Because you take away saṃsāra, you are called Hara by the wise; because Hari was subdued by you, you are called Hara by the wise.
m.3.12.27: Since you sustain everything by dividing your body eightfold, therefore, O Lord, protect us gods with the gifts we desire.
m.3.12.28: You are the Great Person, Śambhu, Lord of all, leader of the gods, whose self owns nothing, whose self is changeless, the supreme Brahman, the refuge of the good.
m.3.12.29: You are the friend of the afflicted, an ocean of compassion, of wondrous protection, the seer of the supreme Self, the wise one, Virāṭ, all-pervading, the true, characterised by being, consciousness and bliss.
m.3.12.30: Nandīśvara said: Having heard these words of the gods, Śambhu, the Supreme Lord, spoke to those gods and to the ancient great sages.
m.3.12.31: As water poured into water, milk into milk, ghee into ghee becomes one, so Viṣṇu has then merged into Śiva as one, and not otherwise.
m.3.12.32: Viṣṇu alone, in the form of Nṛsiṃha, proud and mighty, the man-lion, had set about destroying the world.
m.3.12.33: He is to be entreated by my devotees who seek success; homage to him. He is foremost among my devotees and grants boons to my devotees.
m.3.12.34: Nandīśvara said: Having said this much, the blessed, mighty king of birds vanished right there as all the gods looked on.
m.3.12.35: The blessed Vīrabhadra too, the mighty chief of the gaṇas, stripped off Nṛsiṃha's hide, took it and went to the mountain.
m.3.12.36: From then on Śaṅkara wears the hide of Nṛsiṃha as his garment, and that face was set as the central jewel in his garland of skulls.
m.3.12.37: Then the gods, freed from fear, recounting this story, their eyes wide with wonder, all went back as they had come.
m.3.12.38: Whoever reads or hears this supreme, holy narrative, filled with the essence of the Vedas, will obtain all his desires.
m.3.12.39: It is blessed, conferring fame, long life and health, increasing prosperity, allaying all obstacles, destroying all diseases,
m.3.12.40: allaying sorrow, granting fulfilment of wishes, an abode of auspiciousness, removing untimely death, bestowing intelligence, and destroying enemies.
m.3.12.41: This supreme form of Pināka-bearer Śaṅkara in the shape of a Śarabha should be revealed only to his devotees, those who follow (walk in the path of) Śaṅkara.
m.3.12.42: It should be read and heard only by them, whose very self is devoted to Śiva; it is divine, it grants the ninefold devotion, and it bestows purity of the inner faculty and understanding.
m.3.12.43: One should recite it at all festivals of Śiva, on the fourteenth and eighth lunar days, and at the time of an image's installation, for it brings about the presence of Śiva;
m.3.12.44: and in fears arising from thieves, tigers, lions, from oneself, or from the king; and in other calamities such as portents, earthquakes, bandits and the like, and showers of dust;
m.3.12.45: in the fall of meteors, in great gales, in drought and in excessive rain — in all these the learned devotee of Śiva, self-controlled and firm in his vows, should recite it.
m.3.12.46: Whoever, free from desire, reads or even listens to this observance relating to the Lord (Īśvara), attains the world of Rudra and becomes an attendant of Rudra.
m.3.12.47: Having reached the world of Rudra, he rejoices together with Rudra; then, O sage, by Śiva's grace he attains union (sāyujya) with him.
m.3.12.iti: Thus ends the twelfth adhyāya, named The incarnation as Śarabha, in the third saṃhitā, the Śatarudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.3.13.1: Nandīśvara said: Listen with affection, O son of Brahmā, to the story of the moon-crested Lord: how Śiva, out of love, became incarnate in the house of Viśvānara.
m.3.13.2: He was named Gṛhapati, O sage, the lord of the world of Agni, fire-formed and radiant, the Self of all, the supreme Lord.
m.3.13.3: Long ago, in the city of Narmapura on the lovely bank of the Narmadā, there lived a sage Viśvānara, a devotee of the Enemy of the Cities (Śiva), pure of soul.
m.3.13.4: He was steadfast in the stage of celibate studenthood, always devoted to the Brahma-yajña (Vedic recitation), of the Śāṇḍilya lineage, pure, a treasure-house of brahmanical splendour, and self-controlled.
m.3.13.5: He knew the meaning of all the scriptures, was ever devoted to right conduct, highly skilled in Śaiva observance, and excellent in knowledge of worldly custom.
m.3.13.6: Having weighed in his mind the auspicious qualities desirable in a wife, Viśvānara married, according to rite, a maiden of good family suited to himself.
m.3.13.7: He was devoted to tending the sacred fire, intent on the five sacrifices, constantly engaged in the six duties, and fond of gods, ancestors and guests.
m.3.13.8: When a long time had thus passed, the wife of that brāhmaṇa, named Śuciṣmatī, faithful to her vows, spoke to her husband.
m.3.13.9: Lord, through your grace, having come to you, I have enjoyed all the pleasures that are fitting for women and that bring delight.
m.3.13.10: Yet, lord, there is a wish of mine that has long dwelt in my heart, fitting for householders; you should grant it.
m.3.13.11: Viśvānara said: What indeed cannot be given to you, O fair-hipped one, you who seek my dear welfare? Ask for it, O fortunate one; I will grant it without delay.
m.3.13.12: By the grace of the Great Lord, the bringer of all welfare, nothing is hard for me to obtain, here or hereafter, O auspicious one.
m.3.13.13: Nandīśvara said: Hearing these words of her husband, she, to whom her husband was a deity, with a joyful face and folded hands, humbly spoke.
m.3.13.14: Śuciṣmatī said: If I am worthy of a boon, lord, if a boon is to be given to me, give me a son like Maheśa; I choose no other boon.
m.3.13.15: Nandīśvara said: Hearing her words, that brāhmaṇa of pure vows entered meditation for a moment and pondered this in his heart:
m.3.13.16: Ah, what an extremely rare thing that slender woman has asked of me! It lies far beyond the path of desire—yet he indeed accomplishes all.
m.3.13.17: It was uttered by that very Śambhu, dwelling in her mouth in the form of speech; who could dare to make it otherwise? This shall come to pass.
m.3.13.18: Having reflected thus, that noble-minded sage Viśvānara, steadfast in the vow of having one wife, then spoke to his wife.
m.3.13.19: Nandīśvara said: Having thus consoled his wife, the sage went for austerity to where Viśveśvara, the Lord of Kāśī, dwells in person.
m.3.13.20: Quickly reaching Vārāṇasī and beholding Maṇikarṇikā, he cast off the threefold affliction, even that accumulated over a hundred births.
m.3.13.21: Having seen all the liṅgas headed by Viśveśa, and having bathed in all the pools, step-wells, wells and lakes,
m.3.13.22: having bowed to all the Vināyakas, saluted Gaurī the consort of Śarva, and worshipped Kālarāja Bhairava, the devourer of sins,
m.3.13.23: having diligently praised the gaṇas headed by Daṇḍanāyaka, and propitiated Keśava in his forms headed by Ādikeśava,
m.3.13.24: having bowed again and again to the Suns headed by Lolārka, and tirelessly made piṇḍa offerings at all the tīrthas,
m.3.13.25: having gratified sages and brāhmaṇas with feasts for thousands and the like, and devoutly worshipped the liṅgas with the offerings of great worship,
m.3.13.26: he pondered repeatedly: Which liṅga grants success quickly, where austerity undertaken in desire of a son attains steadfastness?
m.3.13.27: Having reflected thus for a moment, the wise sage Viśvānara extolled the liṅga Vīreśa as the swift bestower of a son:
m.3.13.28: Countless thousands of siddhas have attained perfection from it; therefore the supreme Vīreśvara is renowned as the Siddhaliṅga.
m.3.13.29: By worshipping the great liṅga Vīreśvara with devotion for a year, people obtain long life, every wish, sons and the like, in many ways.
m.3.13.30: I too, worshipping Vīreśa here at the three times of day, shall quickly obtain a son such as my wife desires.
m.3.13.31: Nandīśvara said: Having thus made up his mind, the steadfast and accomplished brāhmaṇa Viśvānara bathed in the water of Candrakūpa and, keeping vows, undertook a discipline.
m.3.13.32: For a month he ate once a day; for a month he ate only at night; for a month he ate only what came unasked; and for a month again he gave up food altogether.
m.3.13.33: For a month he lived on milk; for a month on vegetables and fruits; for a month on a fistful of sesame; for a month on water alone.
m.3.13.34: For a month he took the five products of the cow; for a month he kept the Cāndrāyaṇa vow; for a month he drank only water from the tips of kuśa grass; for a month he lived on air.
m.3.13.35: Thus for a period of a year he performed wondrous austerity, and three times a day he devoutly worshipped the excellent liṅga Vīreśa.
m.3.13.36: Then in the thirteenth month, having bathed in the waters of the Gaṅgā (the river of three paths), just as that brāhmaṇa was coming to Vīreśa at dawn,
m.3.13.37: at that very moment the ascetic beheld in the middle of the liṅga a child adorned with sacred ash, a boy with the appearance of eight years,
m.3.13.38: with eyes stretching to his ears, deep-red lips, a lovely crown of tawny matted hair, naked, with a smiling face,
m.3.13.39: wearing attire befitting childhood, bearing the ash of the pyre, reciting Vedic hymns, and laughing in his own play.
m.3.13.40: Seeing him, the sage was filled with joy, his hair bristling like a garment, and from his heart he cried out again and again, salutation be to you.
m.3.13.41: With eight verses that grant one's desires, the accomplished Viśvānara praised Śambhu, the supreme bliss, who had taken the form of a child.
m.3.13.42: Viśvānara said: Brahman alone is one, without a second, and it is everything — this is truth, truth; here there is no diversity whatsoever. Rudra alone is one; no second stood beside him. Therefore I take refuge in you, the one Great Lord.
m.3.13.43: O Śambhu, you indeed are the creator and destroyer of all; among many forms you are of a single form, and yet formless. Just as the inner Self is one and yet many, so are you; therefore I take refuge in no lord other than you.
m.3.13.44: Like a snake seen in a rope, silver in mother-of-pearl, and a flood of water in the sun's rays called a mirage — whatever thus appears as real, so is this whole world all around seen through when he is known; in that Great Lord I take refuge.
m.3.13.45: Coolness in water, the power of burning in fire, heat in the sun, serene light in the moon, fragrance in the flower, and ghee even within milk — whatever that is, O Śambhu, that is you; therefore I take refuge in you.
m.3.13.46: Without ears you grasp sound; without a nose you smell; without feet you come from afar; without eyes you see; without a tongue you know taste. Who can rightly know you? Therefore I take refuge in you.
m.3.13.47: O Lord, not even the Veda knows you directly, nor Viṣṇu, nor the Ordainer of all Brahmā, nor the lords of yogis, nor the gods led by Indra; only the devotee knows you. Therefore I take refuge in you.
m.3.13.48: O Lord, you have no lineage, no birth, no name, no form, no character, and no place; yet, being such, you are the Lord of the three worlds and fulfil all desires. I worship you.
m.3.13.49: From you comes everything; you indeed are everything, O foe of Smara. You are the lord of Gaurī, and you are the naked one, supremely tranquil. You are the old man, you the youth, and you the child. What reality is there that is not you? Hence, turning from all else, I bow to you.
m.3.13.50: Nandīśvara said: Having praised thus, the Brahmin fell to the ground; while he remained there with joined palms, that child — the eldest of all elders — greatly delighted, spoke to the Brahmin.
m.3.13.51: The boy said: O Viśvānara, best of sages, O Brahmin, today I have been pleased by you and am thoroughly gracious at heart; choose a supreme boon.
m.3.13.52: Then, rising up, the accomplished sage Viśvānara, best of sages, joyful at heart, replied to Śaṅkara who had the form of a child.
m.3.13.53: Viśvānara said: O Maheśvara, O Lord, what is unknown to you, the all-knowing? You are the inner Self of all, the blessed Śarva, the giver of everything.
m.3.13.54: Why do you urge me toward begging, which brings humiliation? Knowing this, O Maheśāna, do as you yourself wish.
m.3.13.55: Nandīśvara said: Having heard these words of Viśvānara of pure vows, the pure god in the form of a child then smiled a pure smile and spoke.
m.3.13.56: O pure one, the desire you have cherished in your heart concerning Śuciṣmatī will without doubt be fulfilled in a very short time.
m.3.13.57: O great-minded one, I shall become your son through Śuciṣmatī, renowned by the name Gṛhapati, pure and dear to all the immortals.
m.3.13.58: This holy hymn, the Abhilāṣāṣṭaka, uttered by you, grants desires when recited three times a day for a year in the presence of Śiva.
m.3.13.59: Reciting this hymn grants sons, grandsons and wealth; it also brings complete peace and destroys all calamities.
m.3.13.60: It brings about heaven, liberation and prosperity — there is no doubt of this. Indeed it equals all hymns and always grants every desire.
m.3.13.61: Rising at dawn, well bathed, having worshipped Śambhu's liṅga, one without a son who recites this hymn for a year will obtain a son.
m.3.13.62: This Abhilāṣāṣṭaka should not be given to just anyone; it must be carefully guarded, for it brings childbirth even to a woman who is utterly barren.
m.3.13.63: Whether by a woman or by a man, this hymn recited with discipline for a year near a liṅga grants a son; there is no doubt of this.
m.3.13.64: Nandīśvara said: Having said this, Śambhu in the form of a child, the refuge of the good, vanished; and the Brahmin Viśvānara, joyful at heart, went to his own home.
m.3.13.iti: Thus ends the thirteenth adhyāya, named The incarnation as Gṛhapati, in the third saṃhitā, the Śatarudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.3.14.1: Nandīśvara said: That Brahmin came home, filled with great joy, and told his beloved wife the whole account of what had happened.
m.3.14.2: Hearing that, the Brahmin's wife Śuciṣmatī was delighted; full of deep love, she praised her own destiny.
m.3.14.3: Then, in due time, after he had duly performed the rite called garbhādhāna (conception), that woman became pregnant.
m.3.14.4: Then, before the foetus began to stir, that learned man duly performed the puṃsavana rite according to the procedure taught in the Gṛhya sūtras, for the increase of male qualities.
m.3.14.5: Then in the eighth month that knower of rites performed the sīmanta (hair-parting) rite, which enriches the form of the embryo, and for the accomplishment of an easy delivery.
m.3.14.6: Then, under auspicious stars, with Jupiter in a kendra (angular house), in an auspicious ascendant, with benefic planets in favourable conjunctions, a son whose face was lovely like the lord of stars (the moon) —
m.3.14.7: — outshining the lamps of the lying-in chamber and destroying all misfortunes, a son was born to her, Śuciṣmatī.
m.3.14.8: He was Śarva himself, giver of every happiness to the dwellers of Bhūḥ, Bhuvaḥ and Svaḥ. And the clouds, borne by the winds, became perfumes for the faces of the maidens of the quarters;
m.3.14.9: those dense clouds rained showers of flowers with delightful fragrance. The drums of the gods resounded, and all the directions became serene.
m.3.14.10: Everywhere the rivers became clear, together with the minds of beings; darkness (tamas) utterly faded, and even rajas (dust/passion) became free of rajas.
m.3.14.11: Creatures were filled with sattva (goodness); a rain of nectar fell; and the speech of every living being became wholly auspicious and pleasing.
m.3.14.12: Apsarases led by Rambhā, with auspicious articles in their hands, Vidyādharīs, Kinnarīs and celestial women by the thousands,
m.3.14.13: and the honoured women of the Gandharvas, serpents and Yakṣas, sweet-voiced, singing auspicious songs, came there in great numbers.
m.3.14.14: Marīci, Atri, Pulaha, Pulastya, Kratu, Aṅgiras, Vasiṣṭha, Kaśyapa, Agastya, Vibhāṇḍa, the son of Māṇḍavī,
m.3.14.15: Lomaśa, Romacaraṇa, Bharadvāja, then Gautama, Bhṛgu, Gālava, Garga, Jātūkarṇya, Parāśara,
m.3.14.16: Āpastamba, Yājñavalkya, Dakṣa, Vālmīki and Mudgala, Śātātapa, Likhita, Śilāda, Śaṅkha, Uñchabhuk,
m.3.14.17: Jamadagni, Saṃvarta, Mataṅga, Bharata, Aṃśumān, Vyāsa, Kātyāyana, Kutsa, Śaunaka, Suśruta, Śuka,
m.3.14.18: Ṛṣyaśṛṅga, then Durvāsas, Śuci, Nārada and Tumburu, Uttaṅka, Vāmadeva, Pavana, Asita and Devala,
m.3.14.19: Sālaṅkāyana and Hārīta, Viśvāmitra, then Bhārgava, Mṛkaṇḍa together with his son, Parvata and also Dāruka,
m.3.14.20: Dhaumya, Upamanyu, Vatsa and other sages, along with the sages' daughters, came together to the blessed hermitage of Viśvānara to perform rites for his well-being.
m.3.14.21: Brahmā accompanied by Bṛhaspati, the god whose mount is Garuḍa (Viṣṇu), and the bull-bannered Śiva together with Gaurī, attended by Nandin and Bhṛṅgin,
m.3.14.22: the gods headed by the great Indra, the Nāgas dwelling in Pātāla, and the great oceans with their rivers, bringing jewels in abundance,
m.3.14.23: and the immobile beings, assuming moving forms, came in thousands. At that great festival there was a moonlit radiance out of season.
m.3.14.24: Brahmā (Vidhi) himself, reverently, performed his birth rite (jātakarma). Having considered the Veda and his form, he declared: This one by name is Gṛhapati.
m.3.14.25: Thus he gave him the name, which is to be given on the eleventh day, following the procedure of the naming rite and reciting the Vedic text for that purpose.
m.3.14.26: And having greeted him with blessings spoken in the mantras of the four Vedas, the Grandsire of all, at the proper time, mounted his swan and departed.
m.3.14.27: Hara too, having performed the protective rite suited to a child, following worldly custom, mounted his vehicle and went with Hari to his own abode.
m.3.14.28: Oh, what beauty! Oh, what radiance! Oh, the marks on all his limbs! Oh, the good fortune of Śuciṣmatī — Hara himself has appeared as her son!
m.3.14.29: Or rather, what is so wonderful in this, among the devotees of Śarva? Rudra himself has appeared, because Rudra was worshipped by him.
m.3.14.30: Praising thus to one another, their hair bristling with joy, they all took leave of Viśvānara and went back as they had come.
m.3.14.31: Therefore those living in the householder stage long for a son: Through a son one conquers the worlds — this is the eternal Vedic teaching.
m.3.14.32: The house of a sonless man is empty; the earning of a sonless man is in vain; the austerity of a sonless man is cut off; one does not become purified while sonless.
m.3.14.33: There is no gain higher than a son, no happiness higher than a son, no friend higher than a son, anywhere, in the next world or here.
m.3.14.34: Then in his fourth month his father performed the niṣkramaṇa (first going out) from the house; the first feeding with grain at half a year, and the tonsure (cūḍā) at one year, were duly performed.
m.3.14.35: Then, having performed the ear-piercing under the asterism Śravaṇa, that knower of rites gave him the vow of initiation in the fifth year, for the increase of Brahmic splendour.
m.3.14.36: Then, after performing the upākarma, the wise one taught him the Vedas; within three years he duly studied the Vedas together with their limbs and their pada and krama recitations.
m.3.14.37: Capable as he was, displaying humility and other virtues, he acquired the entire body of knowledge from his teacher's mouth, the teacher being a mere witness.
m.3.14.38: Then, in his ninth year, Nārada came to see Gṛhapati, son of Viśvānara, who was devoted to serving his parents.
m.3.14.39: Reaching Viśvānara's hut, the curious divine sage, having duly received the guest-water and a seat, asked him there about his welfare.
m.3.14.40: Then, remembering the lotus-feet of Śiva, he told Viśvānara to his face all about his good fortune and about the destiny of the son.
m.3.14.41: Nandīśvara said: Addressed thus by the sage, that glorious boy, having obtained his parents' permission, bowed to Nārada with devotion and, humbly bending, sat down near him.
m.3.14.42: Nārada said: O Vaiśvānara, come here; sit on my lap, dear child. I shall examine your marks; show me your right hand.
m.3.14.43: Then the wise Nārada, having examined everything—the palate, tongue and the rest—spoke to Viśvānara, prompted by Śiva.
m.3.14.44: Nārada said: O sage Viśvānara, I tell you; listen attentively about your son's marks. This son bears auspicious marks on all his limbs; he is endowed with great characteristics.
m.3.14.45: But he who is endowed with all virtues, marked with all auspicious signs, with all his digits full and spotless — may Fate protect him, as it protects the moon.
m.3.14.46: Therefore this child must be protected with every effort; even a virtue turns into a fault when the Creator becomes adverse.
m.3.14.47: I fear that in his twelfth year there will be a danger from lightning and fire. Having said this, Nārada went back to the world of the gods as he had come.
m.3.14.iti: Thus ends the fourteenth adhyāya, named The incarnation as Gṛhapati, in the account of the Gṛhapati incarnation, in the third saṃhitā, the Śatarudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.3.15.1: Nandīśvara said: Viśvānara and his wife, having heard what Nārada had said, took it to be a most dreadful stroke of a thunderbolt.
m.3.15.2: Crying out, alas, I am ruined, he beat his chest, and overwhelmed with grief for his son he fell into a deep swoon.
m.3.15.3: Śuciṣmatī too, stricken with sorrow, wept unbearably, with loud wails of alas, her senses utterly distraught.
m.3.15.4: Hearing this cry of anguish, Viśvānara too shook off his swoon and rose, crying aloud: What? What is it? What, what is this? Where is my Gṛhapati, my life-breath walking outside me, dwelling in my inner self, the lord of all my senses?
m.3.15.5: Then the boy Gṛhapati, born of a portion of Śaṅkara, seeing his parents overcome with great grief, smiled and spoke.
m.3.15.6: Gṛhapati said: O mother, O father, what has happened? Tell me the cause now. Why this excessive weeping? Whence such fear has come to you two?
m.3.15.7: Time itself cannot seize me, whose body is armoured by the dust of your feet — what then of the wretched, fickle, puny lightning?
m.3.15.8: Hear my vow, dear parents: if I am truly your son, I shall act in such a way that Death itself will be terrified.
m.3.15.9: Having worshipped Mṛtyuñjaya, the all-knowing giver of all to the good, I shall practise japa to Mahākāla — I tell you the truth, dear parents.
m.3.15.10: Nandīśvara said: Hearing his words, the afflicted brahmin couple, their anguish dispelled as if by floods of unseasonable showers of nectar, then said:
m.3.15.11: The brahmin couple said: Say it again, say it again. How was it, how? Tell us again: Time is not able to seize me — what is this wretched lightning?
m.3.15.12: You have spoken of a great means to end our anguish, namely the worship of the god called Mṛtyuñjaya.
m.3.15.13: And likewise taking refuge in Śambhu — there is nothing higher than that — who accomplishes what lies beyond the path of wishes, and who removes sins.
m.3.15.14: Have you not heard, dear son, how of old the destroyer of Tripura protected Śvetaketu when he was bound by the noose of Death?
m.3.15.15: Śiva made Śilāda's son Nandin, a mere eight years old and seized by death, his own attendant, a delight to the whole world.
m.3.15.16: Drinking the dreadful Hālāhala poison, born from the churning of the milk-ocean and like the fire of cosmic dissolution, he saved the three worlds.
m.3.15.17: He who slew the arrogant Jalandhara, who had seized the wealth of the three worlds, with the discus that arose from a line drawn by his beautiful toe.
m.3.15.18: He who of old, with the flames sprung from the fall of a single arrow, withered Tripura, deluded by its lordship over the three worlds, as the sun withers things.
m.3.15.19: With a mere glance he sent Kāma, mighty from conquering the three worlds, to the state of the bodiless, while Brahmā and the others looked on.
m.3.15.20: Go, son, for refuge to that Śiva, the sole creator of Brahmā and the rest, whose vehicle is the cloud, the imperishable, the protecting jewel of the universe.
m.3.15.21: Nandīśvara said: Having thus obtained his parents' permission, he bowed at their feet, circumambulated them, comforted them much, and set out.
m.3.15.22: He reached Kāśī, hard to attain even for Brahmā, Nārāyaṇa and others, which destroys the torment of the great cosmic dissolution and is protected by Viśveśa,
m.3.15.23: adorned at its neck-regions by the heavenly river Gaṅgā as by a necklace-string, and made resplendent by Hara's consort endowed with wondrous qualities.
m.3.15.24: Having arrived there, that best of brahmins first went to Maṇikarṇikā; bathing there according to rule, and seeing Lord Viśveśvara,
m.3.15.25: the wise boy, filled with great bliss, with joined palms and bowed head, prostrated before him who saves the life of the three worlds.
m.3.15.26: Gazing again and again at that liṅga, he rejoiced repeatedly in his heart: This is clearly rich with the very root of supreme bliss, there is no doubt.
m.3.15.27: Ah, there is none more blessed than I in the three worlds with their moving and unmoving beings, since today I have seen the glorious all-pervading Viśveśvara.
m.3.15.28: It was only for the dawning of my good fortune that the great sage Nārada came earlier and spoke as he did; therefore I have fulfilled my purpose.
m.3.15.29: Nandīśvara said: Having thus broken his fast with the nectar-juices of bliss, he then, on an auspicious day, installed a liṅga bestowing welfare on all,
m.3.15.30: and undertook severe observances, hard to perform for those of undisciplined mind. With a hundred and eight auspicious pots filled with Gaṅgā water,
m.3.15.31: purified by straining through cloth, he, pure in soul, bathed Śiva every day, and daily offered him a garland made of blue lotuses,
m.3.15.32: fashioned of one thousand and eight flowers. Once a fortnight, or once a month, he ate bulbs, roots and fruits.
m.3.15.33: For six months the steadfast one lived on withered leaves; for six months he subsisted on air; for six months he lived on drops of water.
m.3.15.34: Thus, O brahmins, O Nārada, two years passed for that great soul as he performed austerities with his mind fixed solely on Śiva.
m.3.15.35: In the twelfth year from his birth, as if to make true the words spoken by Nārada, the wielder of the thunderbolt (Indra) approached him,
m.3.15.36: and said: Ask a boon; I will give whatever is in your mind. I am Śatakratu, O brahmin; I am pleased with your auspicious vows.
m.3.15.37: Nandīśvara said: Hearing these words of the great Indra, the steadfast young son of the sage spoke sweetly, uttering sweet syllables:
m.3.15.38: Gṛhapati said: O Maghavan, enemy of Vṛtra, I know you as the bearer of the thunderbolt. I do not choose a boon from you; Śaṅkara is my giver of boons.
m.3.15.39: Indra said: Śaṅkara is not other than I; I am the god of gods, child. Give up your childishness and ask for a boon without delay.
m.3.15.40: Gṛhapati said: Go away, lover of Ahalyā, you wicked one, foe of the mountains, chastiser of Pāka. Plainly, I seek no god other than Paśupati.
m.3.15.41: Nandīśvara said: Having heard his words thus, Indra, his eyes reddened with anger, raised his terrible thunderbolt and frightened the boy.
m.3.15.42: Seeing the thunderbolt, covered with flashes of lightning, and remembering Nārada's words, the boy, overwhelmed with fear, fainted.
m.3.15.43: Then Śambhu, the lord of Gaurī, dispeller of darkness, appeared, saying, rise, rise, may good befall you, as though reviving him with his touches.
m.3.15.44: Opening his lotus-eyes, which had been as if closed like lotuses at the close of day, and rising, he saw before him Śambhu, more brilliant than a hundred suns.
m.3.15.45: Beholding the eye on his forehead, he saw him dark-throated, bearing the bull on his banner, with the Mountain's daughter seated on his left side, and the moon on his crest,
m.3.15.46: shining with matted locks, bearing the trident and the Ajagava bow as weapons, his body gleaming white like camphor, wrapped in an elephant's hide,
m.3.15.47: recognising Mahādeva from his guru's words and from scripture, his throat choked with tears of joy, his body clad as in a garment of bristling hair,
m.3.15.48: for a moment he stood still like a mountain, like a painted or artificial doll, utterly so, forgetting even himself.
m.3.15.49: When he was unable either to praise, or to bow, or to say anything at all, then Śaṅkara smiled and spoke.
m.3.15.50: Īśvara said: O child, O Gṛhapati. Ah, I know you are frightened of Śakra with the thunderbolt raised in his hand. Do not fear; I made a test of you.
m.3.15.51: Neither Śakra, nor the thunderbolt, nor even Death has power over my devotee. It was I myself, in the form of Indra, who frightened you.
m.3.15.52: I grant you a boon, good one: become the holder of Agni's position. You will be the giver of boons to all the gods.
m.3.15.53: O Agni, be the one who moves within all beings. As lord of a quarter, between Dharmarāja (Yama) and Indra, obtain your realm.
m.3.15.54: This liṅga established by you shall bear your name; known as Agnīśvara, it will increase all radiance.
m.3.15.55: For the devotees of Agnīśvara there is no fear from lightning or fire, no fear of weakness of digestion, and never untimely death.
m.3.15.56: Having worshipped in Kāśī Agnīśvara, the giver of all prosperity, one who by fate dies even elsewhere is honoured in the world of Fire.
m.3.15.57: Nandīśvara said: Having said this, and having brought his kinsmen, Śiva, while his parents looked on, consecrated Agni to the lordship of a quarter and entered into that liṅga.
m.3.15.58: Thus, dear one, I have described to you the incarnation as Agni, named Gṛhapati, of Śaṅkara, the supreme Self, the remover of people's afflictions.
m.3.15.59: The city of Agni (Citrahotra), Arciṣmatī, is delightful, bestowing happiness and excellent; those who are devoted to Jātavedas indeed dwell there.
m.3.15.60: Those of firm resolve and controlled senses who enter fire, or women endowed with courage — all of them become radiant as fire.
m.3.15.61: Brahmins devoted to the agnihotra, celibate students who have established the sacred fire, and likewise those who practise the five-fire austerity, dwell in the world of Agni, radiant as fire.
m.3.15.62: He who in the cold gives loads of firewood to dispel the cold, or who makes a fire-place for warmth, shall dwell near Agni.
m.3.15.63: He who, full of faith, performs the cremation rite for one without protector, or, if unable, urges another to do it, is honoured in the world of Agni.
m.3.15.64: Fire alone is the supreme bestower of the highest good for the twice-born. Guru, deity, vow, sacred ford — all is determined to be Fire.
m.3.15.65: All impure things become pure in an instant through contact with fire; therefore it is known as Pāvaka (the Purifier).
m.3.15.66: This Fire (Āśuśukṣaṇi) is indeed directly the inner Self, certainly; it digests morsels of flesh in the belly, but not the lump of flesh (embryo) in women's wombs.
m.3.15.67: This fiery form of Śambhu, visible and of the nature of burning, is creator, destroyer and protector; without it, what can be seen?
m.3.15.68: This Citrabhānu is directly the eye of the Lord of the three worlds. In a world blind and full of darkness, who but he is the illuminator?
m.3.15.69: Incense, lamps, food offerings, milk, curd, ghee and sugarcane products — this, when consumed by Fire, all the dwellers of heaven enjoy in heaven.
m.3.15.iti: Thus ends the fifteenth adhyāya, named The incarnation as Gṛhapati, in the third saṃhitā, the Śatarudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.3.16.1: Nandīśvara said: O lord of sages, hear also of Śambhu's incarnation as Yakṣeśvara, which destroys the pride of the proud and increases the devotion of the good.
m.3.16.2: Long ago the mighty gods and Daityas churned the Ocean of Milk for the sake of nectar, joined together in an alliance for their own good purpose.
m.3.16.3: While the Ocean of Milk was first being churned for nectar by the gods and Dānavas, there arose from it a poison blazing like the fire of universal destruction.
m.3.16.4: Seeing it, all the gods and Daityas, overwhelmed with fear, fled swiftly, dear one, and went to Śambhu for refuge.
m.3.16.5: Seeing Śaṅkara, the crest-jewel of all gods, they all, together with Acyuta, bowed with heads lowered and praised him with devotion.
m.3.16.6: Then the blessed Śaṅkara, loving to his devotees, being pleased, drank the most terrible poison that tormented the hosts of gods and demons.
m.3.16.7: That terrible, virulent poison, once drunk, he held in his throat; the all-pervading Lord shone exceedingly by it and became Nīlakaṇṭha (the Blue-throated).
m.3.16.8: Then the hosts of gods and demons, all freed from the burning of the poison by Śiva's grace, churned it again.
m.3.16.9: Then, O sage, many jewels came forth from it, and also the nectar, the very object sought by gods and Dānavas, O sage.
m.3.16.10: By Hari's grace only the gods drank it, not the asuras. Then a very great conflict arose among them mutually.
m.3.16.11: Then, O sage, a hand-to-hand battle took place between the gods and Dānavas. There the Moon, afflicted by fear of Rāhu, fled.
m.3.16.12: Overwhelmed with fear, he went to Śambhu's abode for refuge, and bowing deeply, praised him, saying, protect me, protect me.
m.3.16.13: Then Śaṅkara, giver of fearlessness to the good and loving to his devotees, the Lord, bore upon his head the Moon who had come for refuge.
m.3.16.14: Then Rāhu arrived and, bowing deeply, reverently praised Śaṅkara, lord of all, with pleasing words.
m.3.16.15: Śambhu, understanding his wish, placed on his neck Rāhu's heads, called Ketu, which had earlier been severed by Acyuta.
m.3.16.16: Then in the battle all the asuras were defeated by the gods; all the gods, having drunk the nectar, became mighty and gained victory.
m.3.16.17: All of them, led by Viṣṇu, became exceedingly proud, deluded by Śiva's māyā, inwardly vaunting their own strength.
m.3.16.18: Then the god Śaṅkara, lord of all and destroyer of pride, becoming a Yakṣa, quickly went to where the gods were, O sage.
m.3.16.19: Seeing all the gods headed by Acyuta, with minds full of great pride, Maheśa, the lord of Yakṣas and destroyer of pride, spoke.
m.3.16.20: The lord of the yakṣas said: Why are you all, O gods, gathered here together? What is the whole matter? Tell me the reason, since I am asking.
m.3.16.21: The gods said: O great god, a great and most dreadful battle took place here. The asuras were destroyed, all of them; the survivors have fled away.
m.3.16.22: We are all great heroes, slayers of Daityas, exceedingly strong. What are those Daityas before us—always of petty strength?
m.3.16.23: Nandīśvara said: Hearing these words of the gods, full of pride, Mahādeva, destroyer of pride, in the form of a Yakṣa, spoke.
m.3.16.24: The lord of the yakṣas said: O all you gods, listen attentively to my words. I speak the truth, not falsehood—words that remove all pride.
m.3.16.25: Do not indulge in this pride; the creator and destroyer is another, the Lord. Having forgotten Maheśāna, you boast in vain of your strength.
m.3.16.26: If you have such pride, believing your own strength to be great, then cut this blade of grass set down by me with those weapons of yours, O gods.
m.3.16.27: Nandīśvara said: Having said this, he cast a single blade of grass before them. Then the Lord in Yakṣa form, refuge of the good, took away all their pride.
