m.3.28.29: And the Bhilla will be the great son of Vīrasena, named Nala, in the excellent city of Niṣadha; there is no doubt.
m.3.28.30: You, O sinless one, will be the daughter of King Bhīma in the city of Vidarbha, renowned as Damayantī and endowed with virtues.
m.3.28.31: You two, having been united and having enjoyed abundant royal pleasures, will surely attain liberation, which is hard to attain even for the foremost yogins.
m.3.28.32: Nandīśvara said: Having said this, Śambhu himself then took the form of a liṅga. Because he did not swerve from dharma, he is remembered as Acaleśa.
m.3.28.33: That Bhilla Āhuka became the son of Vīrasena in the city of Niṣadha, dear one, the great king named Nala.
m.3.28.34: That great Bhilla woman Āhukā became the daughter of King Bhīma in the city of Vidarbha, famed as Damayantī.
m.3.28.35: And Śiva, who was called Yatinātha, became the swan and brought about the marriage of Damayantī with Nala.
m.3.28.36: Owing to the great merit of their former hospitality, Lord Śaṅkara, assuming the form of a swan, gave happiness to the two.
m.3.28.37: Śiva, the swan incarnation, skilled in various kinds of talk, bestowed supreme bliss on Damayantī and Nala.
m.3.28.38: This account of Śiva's incarnation of pure fame, named Yatīśa, and also of the one called Haṃsa, is supreme, purifying, most wonderful, and grants liberation.
m.3.28.39: Whoever hears or recites to others this auspicious account of the incarnations called Yatīśa and Brahmahaṃsa attains the supreme goal.
m.3.28.40: This faultless narrative grants the fruit of all desires; it leads to heaven, brings fame and long life, increases devotion, and is excellent.
m.3.28.41: Having heard this account of Śambhu in his two forms as the ascetic (yati) and the swan (haṃsa), one enjoys every happiness here in this world and at the end goes to Śiva's city.
m.3.28.iti: Thus ends the twenty-eighth adhyāya, named The deeds of the incarnations of Śiva called Yatinātha and Brahmahaṃsa, in the third saṃhitā, the Śatarudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.3.29.1: Nandīśvara said: O Sanatkumāra, hear of Śambhu's supreme and excellent incarnation called Kṛṣṇadarśana, which granted knowledge to Nabhaga.
m.3.29.2: There were the sons of Śrāddhadeva, headed by Ikṣvāku; among them Nabhaga was the ninth, and Nābhāga is remembered as his son.
m.3.29.3: His son was Ambarīṣa; he became a devotee of Viṣṇu, upon whom Durvāsas became pleased because of his devotion to the brahmins.
m.3.29.4: Hear, O sage, the story of Nabhaga, who is declared to be Ambarīṣa's grandfather, to whom Śiva gave knowledge.
m.3.29.5: Nabhaga, the son of Manu, very intelligent and self-controlled, lived for a long time in the teacher's house for the sake of study.
m.3.29.6: At this time those sons headed by Ikṣvāku, without allotting any share to him, took their own shares in order.
m.3.29.7: Each taking his own share, those fortunate and wise ones enjoyed the excellent kingdom without distress, by their father's command.
m.3.29.8: Afterwards Nabhaga, the celibate student, having studied in order all the Vedas with their aṅgas and upāṅgas, came there from the teacher's place.
m.3.29.9: Seeing all his brothers had divided the property, Nabhaga, seeking his inheritance, spoke affectionately to them, headed by Ikṣvāku, O sage.
m.3.29.10: Nabhaga said: Brothers, leaving my inheritance unallotted, as things stood, you have all divided the property with great pleasure; give a share to me too, who have come for my own inheritance.
m.3.29.11: The brothers said: At that time you were forgotten by us; now we allot your father as your share. Take him, without doubt.
m.3.29.12: Hearing his brothers' words, Nabhaga, greatly astonished, then came near his father and spoke to him.
m.3.29.13: Nabhaga said: O father, all my brothers divided the property, leaving me out, while I had gone as a celibate student to the teacher's house for study.
m.3.29.14: Then, when I came and respectfully asked them to give me my inheritance, they named you as my share; for that reason I have come.
m.3.29.15: Nandīśvara said: Hearing his words, his father Śrāddhadeva, astonished, consoled him, who was devoted to truth and dharma, and spoke to him, O sage.
m.3.29.16: Manu said: Do not heed what they said, dear son, for it is deceitful. I am by no means a fine inheritance, a means of enjoyment.
m.3.29.17: Even so, I have been given by those deceivers as your inheritance. I will tell you a means of livelihood; listen truly.
m.3.29.18: The wise Āṅgirasa brahmins are performing a sattra today; in that rite they become confused on every sixth day.
m.3.29.19: Go there, Nabhaga, O great poet, and recite to them the two Vaiśvadeva hymns; then that sattra will become pure.
m.3.29.20: When that rite is completed, those brahmins, going to heaven, will be pleased and give you the wealth remaining from their sattra.
m.3.29.21: Nandīśvara said: Hearing his father's words, Nabhaga, steadfast in truth, went with great joy to where that excellent sattra was.
m.3.29.22: Then, O sage, in the rite of that day in the sattra, the wise son of Manu clearly recited the two Vaiśvadeva hymns.
m.3.29.23: When the rite was completed, those Āṅgirasa brahmins gave him each his own remainder of the sattra and went to heaven.
m.3.29.24: Then, knowing that he was about to accept that remainder of the excellent sattra, Giriśa, the bestower of good favour, at once appeared.
m.3.29.25: He appeared as a glorious man, beautiful in every limb, dark in appearance (Kṛṣṇadarśana), to test his disposition, to give him a share, and that supreme knowledge.
m.3.29.26: Then that Śaṅkara, Śambhu, the Lord who tests, approached from the north and spoke to Nabhaga, the son of Manu.
m.3.29.27: Īśvara said: Who are you, man, taking this wealth of mine left at the sacrificial site? By whom were you sent? Tell all of it truly before me.
m.3.29.28: Nandīśvara said: Hearing those words, dear one, Nabhaga, the wise son of Manu, humbly replied to the dark-looking man.
m.3.29.29: Nabhaga said: This wealth from the sacrifice was surely given to me by the sages. How can you, the dark-looking one, stop me as I take it?
m.3.29.30: Nandīśvara said: Hearing these truthful words spoken by Nabhaga, the dark-looking man, pleased at heart, replied.
m.3.29.31: The dark-looking man said: In this dispute between us, dear boy, your father is the authority. Go and ask him; he will truthfully state what is right.
m.3.29.32: Nandīśvara said: Hearing his words, Nabhaga, the wise son of Manu, went gladly to his father and asked him about what had been said, O sage.
m.3.29.33: Hearing what his son said, Manu Śrāddhadeva remembered Śiva's lotus feet, regained his recollection, and spoke to him.
m.3.29.34: Manu said: O son, hear my words: that man is the god Śiva. Everything belongs to him alone, especially what is obtained from a sacrifice.
m.3.29.35: What remains of a sacrifice is declared to be Rudra's share — this teaching of the wise arose somewhere by his will.
m.3.29.36: That god, the Lord, is entitled to everything, no doubt — how much more the remnant of the sacrifice. Others receive only by the will of that all-pervading one.
m.3.29.37: The Lord has come in that form to show you grace. Go there, Nabhaga, and sincerely make him pleased.
m.3.29.38: Beg forgiveness for your offence, bow deeply and offer praise. He alone is the Lord, master of all, lord of sacrifice, ruler of everything.
m.3.29.39: The gods headed by Viṣṇu and Brahmā, the Siddhas, and all the sages too, dear son, are capable in every act only by his grace.
m.3.29.40: Why say more, best of sons? Go there quickly, without delay, and in every way propitiate Mahādeva, the Lord of all.
m.3.29.41: Nandīśvara said: Having said this, Manu Śrāddhadeva quickly sent his son to Śambhu; and he too, approaching him,
m.3.29.42: Nabhaga, having quickly bowed, with joined palms and bowed head, the greatly wise one, very serene in mind, spoke with humility:
m.3.29.43: Nabhaga said: O Lord, everything that exists in the three worlds is indeed yours—so my father has surely said; how much more, then, what is left over from the sacrifice.
m.3.29.44: O Lord, the words I spoke out of ignorance were said in error. Please forgive my offence; I propitiate you with bowed head.
m.3.29.45: Having said this, Nabhaga, very humble in mind, with joined palms and bowing, praised that Great Lord Kṛṣṇadarśana.
m.3.29.46: Śrāddhadeva too, pure-souled and wise, bowing with joined palms, praised that Lord after saluting him, seeking forgiveness for his own offence.
m.3.29.47: Meanwhile, the gods headed by Viṣṇu and Brahmā, those headed by Vāsava (Indra), the Siddhas and the sages also assembled there.
m.3.29.48: Holding a great festival, all of them with palms well joined, bowing, praised him with devotion, each separately after prostrating deeply.
m.3.29.49: Then Rudra Kṛṣṇadarśana, pleased at heart, looking upon them with a compassionate glance, spoke lovingly and with a smile to Nabhaga.
m.3.29.50: The dark-looking man said: The righteous words your father spoke are indeed just so; and what you said was also true. You are virtuous; there is no doubt in this.
m.3.29.51: Therefore I am entirely well pleased with your good conduct; out of grace I give you knowledge, the eternal Brahman.
m.3.29.52: Become a great knower, together with the brahmins. O Nabhaga, quickly take all this wealth, given by me out of grace, now.
m.3.29.53: Enjoy here every happiness, untroubled, O great-minded one; and by my grace you, together with the brahmins, shall attain a good destiny.
m.3.29.54: Nandīśvara said: Having said this, dear one, the blessed Rudra Hara, lover of truth, vanished right there while they all looked on.
m.3.29.55: Viṣṇu, Brahmā, and all the gods and others, O best of sages, went happily each to his own abode, after joyfully bowing to that direction.
m.3.29.56: Śrāddhadeva too, with his son, went joyfully to his own place; having enjoyed abundant pleasures, at the end he went to Śiva's city.
m.3.29.57: Thus, O brahmin, I have narrated to you the incarnation of Śiva named Kṛṣṇadarśana, the giver of joy to Nabhaga.
m.3.29.58: This sinless narrative grants enjoyment and liberation to the good, and bestows the fruit of all desires on those who read or hear it.
m.3.29.59: The wise person who remembers this story morning and evening becomes a poet and knower of mantras, and at the end attains the supreme goal.
m.3.29.iti: Thus ends the twenty-ninth adhyāya, named The incarnation of Śiva called Kṛṣṇadarśana, in the dialogue of Nandīśvara and Sanatkumāra, in the third saṃhitā, the Śatarudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.3.30.1: Nandīśvara said: O son of Brahmā, now listen to the incarnation of the Supreme Lord called Avadhūteśvara, which took away Śakra's pride.
m.3.30.2: Long ago, O sage, Śakra, together with his preceptor and accompanied by all the gods, went to Kailāsa to have the sight (darśana) of the Lord.
m.3.30.3: Then Śaṅkara, knowing of the coming of the two, the preceptor and Indra, and wishing to test the disposition of those two whose minds were devoted to seeing him,
m.3.30.4: the Lord, performer of many sports (līlā), took the form of an Avadhūta—naked, very terrifying, with a radiance like blazing fire.
m.3.30.5: Śambhu, the true refuge, in that Avadhūta form, stood blocking the path, with a hanging cloth, his form shining.
m.3.30.6: Then the two, the preceptor and Śakra, going toward Śiva's presence, saw in the middle of the path a terrifying man of wondrous form.
m.3.30.7: Then, O sage, Śakra, arrogant because of his authority, not recognising that man standing in his path as Śaṅkara, questioned him.
m.3.30.8: Śakra said: Who are you, naked Avadhūta? Where have you come from? What is your well-known name? Tell me truly, without delay.
m.3.30.9: Is Śambhu staying in his own abode, or has he now gone elsewhere? For I am going, with my preceptor and the gods, to see him.
m.3.30.10: Nandīśvara said: Questioned thus by Śakra, that man said nothing—he was Śaṅkara, the Lord, destroyer of pride, who had assumed a body in sport.
m.3.30.11: Śakra asked him again; that naked one did not speak—Śambhu, whose ways are unknown, the maker of great wonders.
m.3.30.12: Again Purandara, the overlord of the three worlds, the self-ruling king, asked; but that great yogin, the performer of great sport, remained silent.
m.3.30.13: Thus questioned again and again by Śakra, that naked Lord said nothing, wishing to destroy Śakra's arrogance.
m.3.30.14: Then the lord of the gods, proud of his sovereignty over the three worlds, became angry, and rebuking that bearer of matted locks, spoke these words out of anger.
m.3.30.15: Indra said: Fool, though being asked, you have given no answer. Therefore I will strike you with my thunderbolt. Who is there to protect you, wicked-minded one?
m.3.30.16: Having said this, the wielder of the thunderbolt, glaring at him in anger, raised his thunderbolt to slay that naked one.
m.3.30.17: Seeing Śakra with the thunderbolt in his hand, Sadāśiva Śaṅkara swiftly paralysed the fall of his thunderbolt.
m.3.30.18: Then that man, enraged, with dreadful eyes, terrifying, at once blazed up with his splendour as if burning everything.
m.3.30.19: The lord of Śacī, his might checked like a serpent held by a spell, burned inwardly with rage arising from the paralysis of his arm.
m.3.30.20: But Bṛhaspati, seeing that man blazing with his own splendour, recognised him in his mind and quickly bowed to Hara.
m.3.30.21: Then the noble-minded preceptor, with joined palms, bowing again on the ground like a staff, praised the Lord with devotion.
m.3.30.22: The guru said: O God of gods, Mahādeva, loving to those who seek refuge, be gracious, O lord of Gaurī, O lord of all; salutation to you.
m.3.30.23: All, even Brahmā, Viṣṇu and the others, deluded by your māyā, do not know you in truth; they know you only through your grace.
m.3.30.24: Nandīśvara said: Having thus praised Lord Śaṅkara, Bṛhaspati then made Purandara fall at the feet of that Lord.
m.3.30.25: Then, dear one, Bṛhaspati, the preceptor of the gods, noble-minded and wise, with joined palms, bowed in humility, said this:
m.3.30.26: Bṛhaspati said: O protector of the wretched, Mahādeva, lift up this one bowed at your feet, and me as well; therefore, do not show anger—show kindness.
m.3.30.27: Be pleased, Mahādeva, protect Indra who has sought refuge. This fire born from your forehead-eye is coming forth.
m.3.30.28: Nandīśvara said: Hearing these words of the preceptor, the Lord in the Avadhūta form, the ocean of compassion, the bestower of true protection, spoke, laughing.
m.3.30.29: The avadhūta said: How can I hold back the fiery energy that has come out of my eye in anger? How indeed does a snake put back on the slough it has cast off?
m.3.30.30: Nandīśvara said: Hearing these words of Śaṅkara, Bṛhaspati, his mind troubled with fear, spoke again with joined palms.
m.3.30.31: Bṛhaspati said: O God, O Lord, devotees are always to be shown compassion. O Śaṅkara, make true your own name Bhaktavatsala (loving to devotees).
m.3.30.32: O lord of gods, you should cast your extremely fierce energy elsewhere. Rescuer of all devotees, rescue Purandara.
m.3.30.33: Nandīśvara said: Thus addressed by the preceptor, Rudra, who bears the name Bhaktavatsala, the remover of the distress of those who bow, replied, pleased at heart, to the priest of the gods.
m.3.30.34: Rudra said: I am pleased with you, O preceptor of the gods; I grant you an excellent boon. Because you have given life to Indra, become renowned as Jīva.
m.3.30.35: This fire that has arisen from my forehead-eye, unbearable to the gods, I shall cast far away, so that it may not harm Indra.
m.3.30.36: Nandīśvara said: Having said this, he took in his hand that wondrous fire of his own energy, born from his forehead-eye, and hurled it into the salt ocean.
m.3.30.37: Then that energy of Śiva, born from his forehead-eye, cast into the salt ocean, immediately became a boy.
m.3.30.38: He became the lord of the asuras named Jalandhara, son of the Ocean. The Lord Maheśāna slew him at the request of the gods.
m.3.30.39: Having thus performed this noble deed in the form of the Avadhūta, Śaṅkara, the benefactor of the worlds, then vanished.
m.3.30.40: All the gods became happy and wholly free from fear; the preceptor and Śakra, released from fear, attained supreme happiness.
m.3.30.41: Having obtained the sight of him for whose sake they had set out, the two, Guru Bṛhaspati and Śakra Indra, their purpose fulfilled, went joyfully to their own abodes.
m.3.30.42: I have narrated to you the incarnation of the Supreme Lord named Avadhūteśvara, which bestows supreme bliss and metes out punishment to the wicked.
m.3.30.43: This narrative is sinless, conferring fame and heaven, divine, bestowing enjoyment and liberation, and granting the fruit of all desires.
m.3.30.44: Whoever listens to this daily, or with a composed mind causes it to be heard, enjoys every happiness here and at the end attains the state of Śiva.
m.3.30.iti: Thus ends the thirtieth adhyāya, named The deeds of the incarnation of Śiva called Avadhūteśvara, in the dialogue of Nandīśvara and Sanatkumāra, in the third saṃhitā, the Śatarudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.3.31.1: Nandīśvara said: Now, O best of sages, I shall tell you of an incarnation of Śambhu; listen, O brahmin. Out of compassion for his devotee, it dispelled a woman's doubt.
m.3.31.2: In the land of Vidarbha there was a king named Satyaratha. He was righteous at heart, devoted to truth, and dear to the great devotees of Śiva.
m.3.31.3: O sage, while that king ruled the earth with good dharma, a long time passed happily for him through his practice of Śiva's dharma.
m.3.31.4: Then once a great battle took place between that king and the Śālvas, who besieged his city with many troops, arrogant in their strength.
m.3.31.5: That king of Vidarbha fought a fierce battle with them; his great army was destroyed, and by the working of fate he was slain by the Śālvas.
m.3.31.6: When that king was killed in battle by the Śālvas, the surviving soldiers, overwhelmed with fear, fled along with the ministers.
m.3.31.7: Then, O sage, his chief queen, who was pregnant, escaped with great effort at night from her own city, which was besieged by the enemies.
m.3.31.8: Having left, that queen, burning with grief, slowly went far toward the eastern direction, remembering the lotus feet of the Lord.
m.3.31.9: Then at dawn, having travelled a long way through Śaṅkara's compassion, the queen saw a clear lake.
m.3.31.10: Arriving there, the king's beloved, delicate and distressed, took shelter under a shady tree on the lakeshore in order to rest.
m.3.31.11: There, by the power of destiny, at an auspicious hour endowed with good qualities, the queen gave birth to a divine son marked with all the auspicious signs.
m.3.31.12: Then, by fate, his mother, the king's wife, being very thirsty, went down into the lake to drink and was seized in the water by a crocodile.
m.3.31.13: That son, just born, sorely afflicted by hunger and thirst, wept on the lakeshore, having lost both father and mother.
m.3.31.14: O sage, as the newborn son was crying in that forest, Maheśa, the indwelling controller and protector, was filled with compassion.
m.3.31.15: Prompted in her mind by the Lord, the remover of fear, a certain woman who lived by begging, wandering about, suddenly arrived there.
m.3.31.16: That widow, carrying her own one-year-old child, saw there a lone, helpless infant crying.
m.3.31.17: O sage, seeing that child there in the deserted forest, the brahmin woman was greatly astonished and pondered much in her heart.
m.3.31.18: Ah, what a great wonder I have now seen—altogether inconceivable by the mind and indescribable in words!
m.3.31.19: This infant, with his navel cord still uncut, lies alone on the ground, motherless and crying—the best of the radiant ones.
m.3.31.20: None of his relatives, father or others, are here to help. What could have been the cause? Ah, great is the power of fate!
m.3.31.21: I do not know whose son he is, and no one here knows him, from whom I might ask about his birth. Yet compassion has arisen in me.
m.3.31.22: I wish to raise this child like a son of my own body, but I dare not touch him without knowing his family, birth, and so on.
m.3.31.23: Nandīśvara said: While that excellent brahmin woman was reflecting thus, Śaṅkara, who loves his devotees, showed great compassion.
m.3.31.24: Maheśvara of great sport assumed the form of a mendicant—he who always grants happiness to his devotees in every way, and is himself ever free of limiting attributes.
m.3.31.25: That mendicant, the Supreme Lord, suddenly came to where the doubting brahmin woman was, wishing to know the truth.
m.3.31.26: That Lord in the form of an excellent mendicant, whose ways are unknowable, the treasure of compassion, smiled and spoke to the brahmin woman.
m.3.31.27: The best of mendicants said: Do not harbour doubt in your mind, O brahmin lady; do not be troubled. Protect this very pure child lovingly as your own little son.
m.3.31.28: Through this infant you will before long attain the highest good. Nourish this greatly radiant child in every way.
m.3.31.29: Nandīśvara said: When he, Śambhu, the treasure of compassion in the form of a mendicant, had spoken thus, the brahmin woman questioned him lovingly and respectfully.
m.3.31.30: The brahmin woman said: By your command I will protect this child like my own son and nourish him—there is no doubt about this. Through my good fortune you have come here.
m.3.31.31: Even so, I wish to know in particular and truly: who is he, whose son is he, and who are you who have come here?
m.3.31.32: O lord, best of mendicants, again and again an insight comes to me: you are Śiva, the ocean of compassion, and this infant was formerly your devotee.
m.3.31.33: Through some fault in his past actions he has come to this state. Having undergone it, he will attain the highest good by your grace.
m.3.31.34: It is by your māyā alone that I, having strayed from my path and been bewildered, have come here—sent by you for the sake of protecting him.
m.3.31.35: Nandīśvara said: To the brahmin woman, who had gained understanding through seeing him and who wished to know in detail, Śiva in the body of a mendicant spoke.
m.3.31.36: The best of mendicants said: Listen gladly, O brahmin's wife, to the past doings of this child. All of it, including what concerns his other life, will be told truly and with great affection, O sinless one.
m.3.31.37: This is the son of the wise king of Vidarbha, Satyaratha, a devotee of Śiva, devoted to his own dharma.
m.3.31.38: Listen: King Satyaratha was slain by enemies in battle with the Śālvas. His wife, greatly distressed, quickly left her home at night.
m.3.31.39: Arriving here at dawn, she gave birth to this son; then, going down into the lake out of thirst, she was by fate seized by a crocodile.
m.3.31.40: Nandīśvara said: Thus he related to her everything: the child's birth, his father's death in battle, and his mother's death by the crocodile.
m.3.31.41: Then that Brahmin woman, greatly astonished, O lord of sages, again questioned that mendicant, the wise one who had the form of a perfected being.
m.3.31.42: The brahmin woman said: O mendicant, why was that king, this child's father, slain in the very midst of his excellent enjoyments by the Śālvas, his own enemies, with but little effort?
m.3.31.43: Why was this infant's mother swiftly devoured by a crocodile, so that he has become helpless and kinless from his very birth?
m.3.31.44: Why is my own son here also so very poor, a beggar? How may happiness come to these two sons? Tell me, O mendicant.
m.3.31.45: Nandīśvara said: Having heard these words of the Brahmin's wife, that mendicant, the Supreme Lord, pleased at heart and smiling, spoke to her.
m.3.31.46: The best of mendicants said: O wife of the Brahmin, I shall answer all your questions in detail. Listen attentively to this excellent account.
m.3.31.47: That king of Vidarbha, father of this boy, was in his former birth a Pāṇḍya, the best of kings.
m.3.31.48: That Śaiva king, protecting the whole earth righteously, delighted his subjects and destroyed all calamities.
m.3.31.49: Once, on the thirteenth lunar day, fasting and observing the day-and-night vow, he was worshipping Śiva, the Lord of all, at the pradoṣa twilight hour.
m.3.31.50: While he, absorbed, was worshipping Śambhu Giriśa at pradoṣa, a great and terrible noise arose throughout the city.
m.3.31.51: Hearing that sound, the king abandoned the worship of Śiva and, fearing an enemy attack, went out of the palace.
m.3.31.52: At that very moment his very mighty minister, having captured an enemy feudal lord, came to the king.
m.3.31.53: Seeing that enemy lord, the king, overwhelmed by great anger, without considering righteousness, had his head cut off.
m.3.31.54: Without completing that worship of the Lord, the king, impure, his judgement lost, ate his meal at night with great relish, his auspiciousness destroyed.
m.3.31.55: In this birth he became king in Vidarbha, a keeper of Śiva's vow; but because of the interruption of Śiva's worship he was slain by enemies in the midst of his enjoyments.
m.3.31.56: He who was his father in the former life is, in this birth, his son—this very one, deprived of sovereignty because of the breach in Śiva's worship.
m.3.31.57: His mother, in her former life, did away with her co-wife by deceit; because of that sin she was devoured by a crocodile in this life.
m.3.31.58: This history of theirs has been told to you. Those who do not worship Śiva with devotion fall into poverty.
m.3.31.59: This son of yours was, in his former birth, an excellent Brahmin; he spent his life accepting gifts, not in sacrifices and other good deeds.
m.3.31.60: Therefore your son has fallen into poverty, O Brahmin lady. To remove that fault, go to Śaṅkara for refuge.
m.3.31.61: Let these two boys perform the worship of Śiva; after their investiture with the sacred thread, Śiva will surely bring about their welfare.
m.3.31.62: Nandīśvara said: Having thus instructed her, Śiva, who had taken the body of the excellent mendicant and who is loving to his devotees, revealed his supreme true form.
m.3.31.63: Then that Brahmin woman, recognising him as Lord Śaṅkara, bowed down deeply and praised him with love, in a voice choked with emotion.
m.3.31.64: Then Lord Śambhu, who had assumed the mendicant's body, swiftly vanished right there as the Brahmin's wife looked on.
m.3.31.65: When that mendicant had gone, the Brahmin woman, reassured, took that infant and went home together with her own son.
m.3.31.66: Making her dwelling in the charming village called Ekacakra, she raised her own son and the prince with good food.
m.3.31.67: The two, having had their sacraments and sacred-thread ceremony performed by Brahmins, grew up in their home, devoted to the worship of Śiva.
m.3.31.68: Dear one, by the instruction of the sage Śāṇḍilya, the two, steadfast in their observances, kept the auspicious vow and worshipped Śambhu at pradoṣa.
m.3.31.69: Once the prince, having gone to bathe in the river without the Brahmin's son, found an excellent pot of treasure.
m.3.31.70: Thus, as the prince and the Brahmin boy worshipped Śambhu, four months passed for them in happiness.
m.3.31.71: As they continued to worship Śambhu with supreme joy, a year passed for them in that very home.
m.3.31.72: When the year had passed, O sage, the prince, having gone to the edge of the forest with the Brahmin boy, by the grace of the all-pervading Śiva—
m.3.31.73: —married the Gandharva's daughter who had unexpectedly come there and was given to him by her father, and ruled a kingdom free of enemies.
m.3.31.74: The Brahmin woman who had earlier nourished him like her own son became his mother, and the Brahmin's son his brother.
m.3.31.75: Having thus worshipped the Lord of gods, he, named Dharmagupta, enjoyed royal pleasures with that queen in the land of Vidarbha.
m.3.31.76: Thus I have now described to you Śiva's incarnation as the excellent mendicant, which bestowed happiness on the boy-king named Dharmagupta.
m.3.31.77: This narrative is sinless, holy, purifying and great; it is a means to dharma, wealth, desire and liberation, and grants all wishes.
m.3.31.78: Whoever with a focused mind constantly hears this or causes it to be heard, enjoys all desires here and at the end goes to the city of Śiva.
m.3.31.iti: Thus ends the thirty-first adhyāya, named The deeds of the incarnation of Śiva called Bhikṣuvarya, in the third saṃhitā, the Śatarudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.3.32.1: Listen, dear one; I shall tell you of the Sureśvara incarnation of Śiva, the Supreme Self, which brought welfare to Dhaumya's elder brother.
m.3.32.2: The wise Upamanyu, son of Vyāghrapāda, dear to the virtuous, already perfected through a former birth, had attained the state of a sage's boy.
m.3.32.3: While still a mere child he lived with his mother in his maternal uncle's house; Upamanyu, son of Vyāghrapāda, was poor by the will of fate.
m.3.32.4: Once, at his uncle's hermitage, he drank a very little milk; then, longing for milk, he lovingly begged his mother again and again.
m.3.32.5: Hearing her son's words, his mother, an ascetic woman, went inside and then devised a good expedient.
m.3.32.6: Grinding seeds gathered by gleaning and stirring them with water, she coaxed her son and gave him artificial milk.
m.3.32.7: Having drunk the artificial milk given by his mother, the boy said to her, this is not milk, and wept again.
m.3.32.8: Hearing her son's weeping, she, lovely as a lotus, grieved, wiped her son's eyes with her hands and spoke to him.
m.3.32.9: The mother said: Where could milk come from for us, who always dwell in the forest? Without Śambhu's grace there can be no obtaining of milk.
m.3.32.10: Whatever was done in a former birth with Śiva as its aim, O son, that alone is surely obtained; there is no need for doubt here.
m.3.32.11: Hearing these words of his mother, that boy, son of Vyāghrapāda, loving to his mother and free of sorrow, replied to her.
m.3.32.12: Enough of this grief, mother. If Śambhu, Śaṅkara, exists, give up your sorrow, O fortunate one; all will be well.
m.3.32.13: Hear my words today, mother: if Mahādeva exists anywhere, then sooner or later I will obtain an ocean of milk.
m.3.32.14: Nandīśvara said: Having said this, the child joyfully declared, may Śiva be mine, took leave of her, bowed deeply, and set about performing austerity.
m.3.32.15: Going to the Himālaya mountain, living on air, concentrated, he made a shrine of eight bricks and a liṅga of clay.
m.3.32.16: Invoking there Śiva together with Ambā with devotion through the five-syllable mantra, the child worshipped him with forest leaves, flowers and the like.
m.3.32.17: Meditating on that Śiva with Ambā, repeating the five-syllable mantra and worshipping for a long time, he practised supreme austerity.
m.3.32.18: By the austerity of that boy, the great-souled Upamanyu, the world of moving and unmoving beings was set ablaze, O sage.
m.3.32.19: Meanwhile the Lord Śambhu, entreated by Viṣṇu and the others, took the form of Śakra (Indra) to test his devotion.
m.3.32.20: Śivā took the form of Śacī, all the gaṇas became gods, Nandī became the elephant Airāvata, and everything else was transformed accordingly.
m.3.32.21: Then Śiva with Ambā, in the form of Śakra and with his gaṇas, went swiftly to Upamanyu's hermitage to bestow grace.
m.3.32.22: To test his devotion, Hara, bearing Śakra's form, spoke to that boy in a deep voice, O lord of sages.
m.3.32.23: The lord of the gods said: I am pleased with you by this austerity, O you of good vows; ask a boon. I will grant all the desires you wish; there is no doubt about this.
m.3.32.24: Thus addressed by Śambhu in Śakra's form, he said with joined palms: I choose devotion to Śiva.
m.3.32.25: Hearing that, Hari (Indra) said: Do you not know me, the lord of the gods, Śakra, ruler of the three worlds, saluted by all the gods?
m.3.32.26: Become my devotee, O brahmin sage; worship me alone always. I will give you every good thing; and abandon Rudra, who is without attributes.
m.3.32.27: Enough of the attributeless Rudra. What purpose of yours will he serve—he who is outside the race of gods and has become a piśāca?
m.3.32.28: Nandīśvara said: Hearing that, the sage's son, repeating the five-syllable mantra and regarding him as one come to obstruct his dharma, spoke to him.
m.3.32.29: Upamanyu said: All this has been said by you, intent on reviling Bhava; incidentally you have spoken of the attributelessness and the piśāca-nature of the God of gods.
m.3.32.30: You do not know Rudra, the lord of the lords of all gods, the begetter of Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Maheśa, beyond Prakṛti.
m.3.32.31: He whom the knowers of Brahman call being and non-being, manifest and unmanifest, eternal, one and many—from him I choose a boon.
m.3.32.32: He whom the knowers of truth declare to be supreme, free from mere argumentation, bestower of the goal of Sāṅkhya and Yoga—from him I choose a boon.
m.3.32.33: There is no reality higher than Śambhu, the cause of all causes, the all-pervading one beyond the guṇas, who is foremost among the gods Brahmā, Viṣṇu and the rest.
m.3.32.34: I do not choose a boon from you, nor from Viṣṇu or Brahmā, nor from any other immortal; may Śaṅkara be my boon-giver.
m.3.32.35: What use is saying much here? I state the truth, my own conviction: I plainly ask of no god or other being apart from Paśupati.
m.3.32.36: Hear my conviction, O foe of the mountains (Indra); this I have inferred today: if I have heard reviling of Bhava, it is due to sin committed in another birth.
m.3.32.37: Having heard reviling of Bhava, one should at that very moment give up one's own body; having quickly slain that reviler, he goes to Śiva's world.
m.3.32.38: Let this desire of mine for milk rest for now, O vilest of gods; having slain you with Śiva's weapon, I shall abandon this body.
m.3.32.39: Nandīśvara said: Having spoken thus, Upamanyu, himself resolved to die and giving up even his desire for milk, made ready to slay Śakra.
m.3.32.40: Then, taking ash from its receptacle, consecrated with the Aghora-weapon mantra, and hurling it at Śakra, the sage roared.
m.3.32.41: Remembering the two feet of his beloved deity and ready to burn his own body, Upamanyu stood holding the fiery (āgneyī) yogic concentration (dhāraṇā).
m.3.32.42: When the brahmin had thus resolved, the Lord, who had taken Indra's form, restrained that yogin's concentration with a gentle (saumya) one.
m.3.32.43: At the command of Śiva, Nandī's lord, Nandī, dear to Śaṅkara, caught in mid-course the Aghora weapon released and hurled by him.
m.3.32.44: Assuming his own form, the Lord, the Supreme Ruler, showed the brahmin his form crowned with the crescent moon.
m.3.32.45: And that Lord showed him a thousand oceans of milk, likewise an ocean of curd and the rest, and an ocean of foods to chew and to eat.
m.3.32.46: Thus Śambhu was seen with the Goddess upon the bull, surrounded by the lords of the gaṇas and by divine weapons, the trident and others.
m.3.32.47: Drums sounded in heaven, a shower of flowers fell, and the ten directions were filled with gods headed by Viṣṇu, Brahmā and Indra.
m.3.32.48: Then Upamanyu, engulfed by the waves of an ocean of bliss, fell flat on the ground like a staff, with a mind bowed in devotion.
m.3.32.49: At that moment Lord Bhava, smiling, called him, saying, come, come, kissed him on the head and granted boons.
m.3.32.50: Śiva said: Dear Upamanyu, I am pleased by your excellent conduct. You are a steadfast devotee, O brahmin sage; you have just been tested by me.
m.3.32.51: Enjoy foods and pleasures as you wish with your kinsmen at all times. Be happy, ever free from sorrow, devoted to me.
m.3.32.52: O greatly fortunate Upamanyu, this Pārvatī is indeed your mother. Today you have been made our son by me, and granted eternal youth.
m.3.32.53: Oceans of milk, curd, ghee and honey by the thousands, and likewise all the oceans of foods and other things—
m.3.32.54: —are given to you by me with love; accept them, O great sage. Immortality too is granted, and eternal leadership of the gaṇas.
m.3.32.55: I, Mahādeva, am your father; your mother is Jagadambikā. Choose, with great joy, other boons that your heart desires.
m.3.32.56: Be ageless and deathless, free from sorrow, famous, of excellent splendour, endowed with divine knowledge, a great master.
m.3.32.57: Then Śambhu, gracious at heart, remembering his great austerity, gave ten more divine boons to the sage Upamanyu:
m.3.32.58: He gave him the Pāśupata vow, knowledge, the yoga of the vow in its true essence, eloquence in exposition, skill, and his own state.
m.3.32.59: Having given thus, Mahādeva took him in both hands, kissed him on the head, and told the Goddess: This is your son.
m.3.32.60: And the Goddess, hearing this with love, placed her lotus hand upon his head and bestowed on him the imperishable state of Kumāra.
m.3.32.61: She also gave him the Milk Ocean in embodied form—the ocean that yields the sweetness of milk—bringing it near, solidified and imperishable.
m.3.32.62: With a fully satisfied mind she gave him yogic sovereignty, constant contentment, imperishable knowledge of Brahman, and supreme prosperity.
m.3.32.63: He too, having obtained divine boons and perpetual youth from that Śiva and from Śivā, was overjoyed.
m.3.32.64: Then, glad at heart, bowing low with folded hands, he lovingly asked a boon of Maheśvara, the God of gods.
m.3.32.65: Upamanyu said: Be gracious, O Lord of the God of gods; be gracious, O Supreme Lord. Grant me supreme, divine, unwavering devotion to you.
m.3.32.66: O Mahādeva, grant me always faith in those connected with you, supreme servitude to you, love, and your presence at all times.
m.3.32.67: Nandīśvara said: Having spoken thus, Upamanyu, best of the twice-born, glad at heart, praised Mahādeva in a voice choked with joy.
m.3.32.68: Thus addressed by him, Śiva, the Lord, the ruler of all, pleased at heart, replied to Upamanyu while everyone listened.
m.3.32.69: Śiva said: Dear Upamanyu, you are blessed, and especially my devotee. Everything you have chosen has been granted to you by me, O sinless one.
m.3.32.70: Be ageless and deathless, ever free from sorrow, worshipped by all, unchanging, the foremost of devotees.
m.3.32.71: Your kinsmen, family and lineage will always be imperishable, O best of the twice-born, and your devotion to me eternal.
m.3.32.72: And I shall always be present in your hermitage, O sage. Stay as you please, dear child; you will feel no longing.
m.3.32.73: Nandīśvara said: Having spoken thus and given him excellent boons, the blessed Lord, together with Ambā and his gaṇas, vanished at once right there.
m.3.32.74: Upamanyu, glad at heart, having obtained excellent boons from Śambhu, went to his mother's dwelling and related everything to his mother.
m.3.32.75: Hearing that, his mother attained great joy. He too became worshipped by all and always enjoyed abundant happiness.
m.3.32.76: Thus, dear one, I have described to you the Sureśvara incarnation of Śiva, the Supreme Self, which ever gives happiness to the good.
m.3.32.77: This pure narrative grants the fruit of all desires; it leads to heaven, fame and long life, and bestows enjoyment and liberation on the good.
m.3.32.78: Whoever listens to this with devotion, or with a collected mind causes it to be heard, having enjoyed every happiness here, attains in the end the goal of Śiva.
m.3.32.iti: Thus ends the thirty-second adhyāya, named The deeds of the incarnation of Śiva called Sureśvara, in the third saṃhitā, the Śatarudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.3.33.1: Nandīśvara said: O Sanatkumāra, listen with great delight to the most purifying incarnation, named Jaṭila, of Śiva, the Supreme Self, the all-pervading Lord.
m.3.33.2: Formerly Satī, the daughter of Dakṣa, disrespected by her own father, gave up her body at her father's sacrifice and was born of Menā from Himālaya, the mountain.
m.3.33.3: Going into a dense forest, Śivā, accompanied by her two female friends, performed very pure austerity, desiring Śaṅkara as her husband.
m.3.33.4: To test that austerity thoroughly, Śiva, skilled in many sports, sent the seven sages to Pārvatī's place of austerity.
m.3.33.5: Those sages went there and carefully put her to the test, but despite great effort they were not able to shake her.
m.3.33.6: Coming there to Śiva, they bowed to him, reported that account, and, having received his permission, respectfully went to heaven.
m.3.33.7: When those sages had gone to their own abode, Śaṅkara himself, the Lord, the cause of creation, wished to test Śivā's conduct.
m.3.33.8: Greatly pleased, this Lord, in order to fulfil the desire of the ascetic maiden, then took the most wondrous form of a celibate student.
m.3.33.9: Very old, bearing the body of a brahmin, blazing with his own splendour, delighted in mind, carrying a staff and an umbrella, he was exceedingly radiant.
m.3.33.10: Having thus assumed the matted-haired form, Śambhu, Śaṅkara, affectionate to his devotees, full of great love, went to Girijā's forest.
m.3.33.11: There he saw the goddess seated on an altar, surrounded by her friends, pure within, auspicious like a digit of the moon.
m.3.33.12: Having looked at that goddess, Śambhu, bearing the form of a celibate student, affectionate to his devotees and eager, approached her lovingly.
m.3.33.13: Then, seeing the brahmin who had arrived, wondrous in splendour, hairy on his limbs, calm, furnished with a staff and a hide,
m.3.33.14: observing celibacy, old, matted-haired, carrying a water-pot, she worshipped him with supreme love, with all the articles of worship.
m.3.33.15: Then the goddess Pārvatī, with supreme joy, respectfully asked that celibate student, whom she had worshipped, about his welfare.
m.3.33.16: Who indeed are you, in the form of a celibate student, and from where have you come? You illumine this forest. Tell me, O best of the knowers of the Veda.
m.3.33.17: Nandīśvara said: Thus asked by Pārvatī, that twice-born celibate student replied quickly and affectionately, in order to test Śivā's disposition.
m.3.33.18: The brahmacārī said: I am a twice-born celibate student who goes wherever he wishes; an ascetic, a giver of happiness to others, a benefactor, no doubt.
m.3.33.19: Nandīśvara said: Having said this, that celibate student, Śaṅkara, affectionate to his devotees, stood nearby, concealing his own form.
m.3.33.20: The brahmacārī said: What shall I say, O great goddess? There is nothing fit to be said. A great and perverse affair, causing great harm, is to be seen.
m.3.33.21: In fresh youth, which is the means of fine enjoyments and the cause of happiness, you are practising austerity in vain, forgoing great comforts and fine pleasures.
m.3.33.22: Who are you? Whose daughter are you? Why do you perform, in a lonely forest, austerity hard to undertake even for sages of controlled mind?
m.3.33.23: Nandīśvara said: Hearing his words, the Supreme Goddess laughed and lovingly spoke to the excellent celibate student.
m.3.33.24: Pārvatī said: Listen, O brahmin, O celibate student, O sage, to my whole story. My present birth is in Bhārata-varṣa, in the house of Himavat.
m.3.33.25: Formerly I was born in Dakṣa's house as Satī, the beloved of Śaṅkara; I gave up my body through yoga because of my father, who reviled my husband.
m.3.33.26: In this birth, O brahmin, Śiva was obtained through great merit; but he abandoned me, reduced Manmatha to ashes, and went away.
m.3.33.27: When Śaṅkara had departed, ashamed out of distress, I came here from my father's house to practise austerity, bound by the words of my preceptor.
m.3.33.28: With mind, speech and action, directly, in the sense of a husband, Śaṅkara has been chosen by me; I speak the truth, not falsehood.
m.3.33.29: I know it is a thing hard to obtain—how could it be attained by me? Even so, out of my mind's longing, I am now performing austerity.
m.3.33.30: Setting aside the gods headed by Indra, and even Viṣṇu and Brahmā, I truly wish to obtain the Pināka-bearer as my husband.
m.3.33.31: Nandīśvara said: Having heard these resolute words of Pārvatī, O sage, that Jaṭila, Rudra, laughing, spoke.
m.3.33.32: The matted-haired ascetic said: O goddess, daughter of Himācala, what notion have you adopted, that for Rudra's sake, abandoning the gods, you perform such vast austerity?
m.3.33.33: I know that Rudra; listen, I shall tell you. That Rudra has a bull on his banner, is of deformed nature, and wears matted locks.
m.3.33.34: He is always solitary, perpetually so, and above all dispassionate. Therefore you ought not to join your mind to that Rudra.
m.3.33.35: Everything—form and the rest—of yours and Hara's is opposed, O goddess. This does not please me; but do as you wish.
m.3.33.36: Nandīśvara said: Having said this, Rudra, in the form of a celibate student, again reviled himself in many ways in her presence, in order to test her.
m.3.33.37: Hearing that unbearable speech of the brahmin, the goddess Pārvatī, greatly enraged, replied to him who was bent on reviling Śiva.
m.3.33.38: So far I had thought that someone blessed had come; but now everything is known: you appear merely as one who must not be slain.
m.3.33.39: You are some rogue who has come in the guise of a celibate student. You have reviled Śiva, you fool, and my wrath has arisen.
m.3.33.40: You do not know Śiva; indeed you are turned away from Śiva. Since I have worshipped you, I am therefore filled with remorse.
m.3.33.41: The man who here reviles Śiva without knowing the truth: the merit he has accumulated since birth turns to ashes.
m.3.33.42: Having touched one hostile to Śiva, one should perform expiation.
m.3.33.43: O you wicked one, you said that you know Śaṅkara. Certainly you have not understood him: Śiva alone is the supreme Lord.
m.3.33.44: However Rudra may be, assuming many forms through māyā, to me he is the giver of what I desire most, changeless, and dear to the good.
m.3.33.45: Nandīśvara said: Having said this to him, the goddess Śivā expounded the truth of Śiva, in which Rudra is declared, as Brahman, to be beyond attributes and imperishable.
m.3.33.46: Hearing those words of the goddess, that brahmin, the brahmacārin, had just begun to speak again,
m.3.33.47: when Girijā, whose mind was devoted to Śiva and who was averse to the reviling of Śiva, quickly spoke to her friend Vijayā.
m.3.33.48: Girijā said: O friend, this vilest of brahmins must be stopped with effort; he is intent on speaking again and will revile Śiva.
m.3.33.49: Sin falls not only on the one who reviles Śiva; whoever hears that reviling also becomes a sharer in sin here.
m.3.33.50: One who reviles Śiva is by all means to be slain by Śiva's servants; if he is a brahmin, he is to be shunned, and one should leave that place quickly.
m.3.33.51: This wicked one will revile Śiva again. Being a brahmin he cannot be slain, so he must be shunned and by all means not be looked upon.
m.3.33.52: Leaving this place quickly, we shall go elsewhere without delay, so that there may be no further conversation with this ignorant man.
m.3.33.53: Nandīśvara said: Just as Umā, having said this, lifted her foot to go, O sage, at that very moment Śiva himself, in person, caught hold of her garment.
m.3.33.54: Assuming his divine form exactly as Śivā meditated on it, and revealing it to Śivā, Śiva spoke to her as she stood with face cast down.
m.3.33.55: Śiva said: Where are you going, leaving me? You are not to be abandoned by me, O Śivā. You have been tested by me; you are my firm devotee, O sinless one.
m.3.33.56: Wishing to know your disposition, I came near you in the form of a brahmacārin and spoke words of various kinds.
m.3.33.57: I am deeply pleased, O Śivā, especially by your devotion. Name the boon your heart desires; there is nothing that cannot be given to you.
m.3.33.58: From today, O you full of love, I have been made your servant by your austerities. Because of your beauty a single moment seems like an age.
m.3.33.59: Let shyness be abandoned by you; you are my eternal wife. Come, beloved; with you I go quickly to my own mountain.
m.3.33.60: When the Lord of gods had spoken thus, Śivā attained great joy, and at once cast off all the suffering of her austerities.
m.3.33.61: Then, delighted at seeing that divine form of Śiva, Śivā, her face lowered in shyness, lovingly replied to the Lord.
m.3.33.62: Śivā said: If you are pleased, O Lord of gods, and show grace to me, become my husband, O Lord of gods. Thus was Śiva addressed by Śivā.
m.3.33.63: Nandīśvara said: Taking her hand according to rite, he went with her to Kailāsa; and Girijā, having gained him as husband, accomplished the task of the gods.
m.3.33.64: Thus, dear one, I have told you of Śiva's incarnation in the form of a brahmacārin, the tester of Śivā's devotion.
m.3.33.65: This pure and supreme narrative has been told by me. Whoever listens to it with love becomes happy and attains the highest goal.
m.3.33.iti: Thus ends the thirty-third adhyāya, named The incarnation of Śiva as the celibate student, in the third saṃhitā, the Śatarudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.3.34.1: Nandīśvara said: O omniscient Sanatkumāra, hear of the incarnation of the all-pervading Śiva, the supreme Self, called Sunartaka-naṭa (the excellent dancer-actor).
m.3.34.2: When the goddess Kālikā, Pārvatī the daughter of Himavat, went to the forest and performed very pure austerities to attain Śiva,
m.3.34.3: then, O sage, Śiva became pleased with her fine austerity; to test her conduct thoroughly and to grant a boon, he went joyfully to her.
m.3.34.4: With a delighted heart he revealed his own form to her, and Śaṅkara said to that Śivā, O sage: Ask for a boon.
m.3.34.5: Hearing Śambhu's words and seeing his supreme form, Śivā rejoiced exceedingly; bowing deeply to him, she spoke.
m.3.34.6: Pārvatī said: If you are pleased, O lord of gods, and if a boon is to be given to me, then become my husband, O Īśāna; show compassion towards me.
m.3.34.7: With your permission I shall go properly to my father's house; you, O lord, O master, should then come to my father's presence.
m.3.34.8: Then, as a mendicant, ask for me, proclaiming my father's auspicious fame; and lovingly make his whole householder's life fruitful.
m.3.34.9: Then, O lord, O Maheśāna, you should perform the marriage according to the prescribed rite, for the accomplishment of the gods' purpose.
m.3.34.10: Fulfil my desire, O all-pervading one; you are ever free from change, and you are indeed named the one loving to devotees; I am always your devotee.
m.3.34.11: Nandīśvara said: Thus addressed by her, Śambhu, the great lord loving to devotees, said, so be it, vanished, and went to his own mountain.
m.3.34.12: Pārvatī too then, with delight, accompanied by her two friends, went to her father's house, having made her beauty fruitful.
m.3.34.13: Hearing of Pārvatī's arrival, that Himācala, with Menā and accompanied by his household, joyfully went to see his daughter.
m.3.34.14: Seeing her with a radiant face, the two brought her home and, overjoyed, lovingly had a great festival held.
m.3.34.15: Menā and likewise the best of mountains gave wealth to brāhmaṇas and others, and respectfully had auspicious rites performed with the sound of the Vedas.
m.3.34.16: Then Menā joyfully stayed in the courtyard with her daughter, while Himavat, the mountain, went to bathe in the Gaṅgā.
m.3.34.17: Meanwhile Śambhu, fond of sport and loving to devotees, became an excellent dancer-actor and came into Menakā's presence.
m.3.34.18: Holding a horn in his left hand and a ḍamaru in his right, with a patched cloak on his back, wearing red garments, skilled in dance and song,
m.3.34.19: then he, in the form of an actor, joyfully performed in Menakā's courtyard various dances and very charming songs.
m.3.34.20: There he sounded the horn and the ḍamaru with a fine tone, and lovingly performed various charming grand displays.
m.3.34.21: All the townspeople, men and women alike, even children and the old, certainly came there at once to see him.
m.3.34.22: Hearing that fine song and seeing the charming dance, all were suddenly entranced, and Menā too then, O sage.
m.3.34.23: Then Menā, her heart delighted by his performance, quickly went with love to give him jewels placed in golden vessels.
m.3.34.24: He did not accept them, saying, I desire as alms that Śivā; and, out of playfulness, he set about dancing and singing again.
m.3.34.25: Hearing his words, Menā, greatly astonished, became very angry; she rebuked the mendicant and wished to drive him out.
m.3.34.26: Meanwhile the king of mountains came there from the Gaṅgā and saw before him the mendicant in human form standing in the courtyard.
m.3.34.27: Hearing all that had happened from Menā's mouth, he became very angry and ordered his attendants to throw the mendicant out.
m.3.34.28: But no one could put him out, O best of sages, for he was blazing with great radiance and untouchable like a mighty fire.
m.3.34.29: Then, dear one, that mendicant, skilled in many sports, showed the mountain his own infinite power.
m.3.34.30: The mountain saw him there at once bearing the form of Viṣṇu, then the form of Brahmā, and then in a moment the form of the Sun.
m.3.34.31: Then, dear one, he saw him in the most wondrous form of Rudra, with Pārvatī, lovely, smiling, and radiant.
m.3.34.32: Thus he saw there his very many forms; at once he became greatly astonished and was flooded with supreme bliss.
m.3.34.33: Then that best of mendicants, the creator of all, begged from him and from her (Menā) that Durgā as alms, and accepted nothing else.
m.3.34.34: Then the Supreme Lord in the guise of a mendicant vanished and, prompted by Durgā's words, quickly went to his own abode.
m.3.34.35: Then true understanding arose in Menā and the lord of mountains as well: The all-pervading Śiva has deceived us and gone to his abode.
m.3.34.36: To him this our daughter Pārvatī, the great ascetic, should be given. Reflecting thus, supreme devotion to Śiva arose in the two of them.
m.3.34.37: Thereafter Rudra, having performed great sports that bring joy to devotees, lovingly married Pārvatī according to the prescribed rite.
m.3.34.38: Thus, dear one, I have told you of Śiva's incarnation named Sunartaka-naṭa, which fulfilled Śivā's words.
m.3.34.39: This sinless, supreme narrative has been told by me. Whoever listens to it with devotion becomes happy and attains the highest goal.
m.3.34.iti: Thus ends the thirty-fourth adhyāya, named The incarnation of Śiva called Sunartaka Naṭa, in the third saṃhitā, the Śatarudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.3.35.1: Nandīśvara said: O all-knowing Sanatkumāra, hear of the incarnation of Śiva, the Supreme Self and all-pervading Lord, that is called the Brahmin in the guise of a holy man (sādhu-veṣa-dvija).
m.3.35.2: Knowing the supremely great devotion of Menā and Himālaya to Śiva, all the gods became anxious, and they consulted together earnestly.
m.3.35.3: If the mountain, with single-minded devotion, gives his daughter to Śambhu, he will surely attain at once the state of liberation (nirvāṇa) in Śiva.
m.3.35.4: If he, the repository of endless gems, goes to liberation, then the earth's name Ratnagarbhā (womb of gems) will surely become false.
m.3.35.5: Abandoning his immobile state and assuming a divine form, he, having given his daughter to the Trident-bearer, will go to Śiva's world.
m.3.35.6: Attaining likeness of form with Mahādeva by Śambhu's grace, and enjoying great pleasures there, he will then attain liberation.
m.3.35.7: Having thus considered, O sage, all the gods, intent on securing their own interest, went to the house of their preceptor (Bṛhaspati), and on arriving made their petition to him.
m.3.35.8: The gods said: O preceptor, go to Himālaya's house to accomplish our purpose; by speaking ill of Maheśa, turn the mountain away from his devotion.
m.3.35.9: O preceptor, by giving his daughter to Śiva with his own faith, that mountain would gain liberation; rather let him remain right here on the earth.
m.3.35.10: Hearing these words of the gods, and after reflecting, he spoke to them.
m.3.35.11: The guru said: O gods, let someone among you go to the mountain and accomplish what you desire; I am unable to do it.
m.3.35.12: Or else, O gods, go with Vāsava (Indra) to Brahmā's world; tell him your situation, and he will do your task.
m.3.35.13: Nandīśvara said: Hearing that, the gods deliberated and went to Brahmā's (Vidhi's) assembly, and laid the whole matter before Brahmā.
m.3.35.14: Having heard their words and pondered them well, Brahmā said to them: I will not utter censure of him, which always brings sorrow and destroys happiness.
m.3.35.15: O gods, go to Kailāsa and please Śaṅkara; send that god himself to Himālaya's house.
m.3.35.16: Let him go to the lord of mountains and censure himself; for censuring another is held to lead to ruin, while self-censure leads to glory.
m.3.35.17: Nandīśvara said: Then all the gods went quickly to Kailāsa, bowed devoutly to Śiva, and together recounted the whole matter.
m.3.35.18: Hearing the gods' words, Maheśvara accepted their request; smiling and reassuring them, he sent the gods off.
m.3.35.19: Then the blessed Śambhu, Maheśa, loving to his devotees, the lord of Māyā who is free of change, wished to go to the mountain's abode.
m.3.35.20: Carrying a staff and an umbrella, clad in splendid garments, bearing a bright tilaka mark, with a crystal rosary in his hand and a śālagrāma stone at his neck,
m.3.35.21: devoutly repeating the name of Hari, the Brahmin in the guise of a holy man went swiftly to Himācala, who was surrounded by his kinsfolk.
m.3.35.22: Seeing him, Himālaya rose up together with his attendants, and bowed down on the ground like a staff, with all eight limbs, according to rule.
m.3.35.23: Then the lord of mountains asked that Brahmin: Who are you? That foremost of Brahmins, the yogī, at once replied to the mountain with great courtesy.
m.3.35.24: Sādhudvija said: O mountain, I am called Sādhudvija; I am a Vaiṣṇava who sees the highest truth, devoted to helping others, all-knowing, and able to go everywhere through the power of my guru.
m.3.35.25: O best of mountains, I came to know your intention by my own insight while in my own place. Hear it: out of affection, I speak to you, casting aside deceit.
m.3.35.26: You wish to give your own daughter, this lovely girl equal to Padmā (Lakṣmī), to Śaṅkara, whose family and conduct are unknown.
m.3.35.27: This intention of yours, O king of mountains, is neither proper nor auspicious. Understand this, O best of the wise, born of Nārāyaṇa's line.
m.3.35.28: Consider your status as lord of mountains: he has not a single kinsman. Ask your own relatives carefully, and Menā, your beloved wife.
m.3.35.29: Ask all of them carefully, Menā and the rest, except Pārvatī; for, O mountain, to a sick man medicine is never pleasing—unwholesome food always is.
m.3.35.30: He is not a recipient suited to you in the act of giving Pārvatī; people of standing will smile merely on hearing of it.
m.3.35.31: He has no shelter, is ever unattached, ill-formed, without qualities, changeless; he dwells in cremation grounds, is frightful, handles snakes, and is naked (sky-clad).
m.3.35.32: His ornament is ash; his head is encircled by great serpents; he has fallen away from every stage of life (āśrama), and his ways are always unknown.
m.3.35.33: Brahmā said: Having spoken these and similar words—true, yet intent on censuring Śiva—Śiva, the performer of many sports, quickly returned to his own abode.
m.3.35.34: Hearing the Brahmin's words, the minds of the two, Himālaya and Menā, became contrary and inclined to mischief: What indeed shall we do?
m.3.35.35: Then Rudra, bestowing a great favour that brought joy to his devotees, married Girijā and accomplished the gods' purpose.
m.3.35.36: Thus, dear one, O lord, I have told you of Śiva's incarnation named the Brahmin in the guise of a holy man, who accomplished the gods' task.
m.3.35.37: This narrative is sinless, leads to heaven, grants long life, and is excellent; whoever reads or hears it becomes happy and attains the highest goal.
m.3.35.iti: Thus ends the thirty-fifth adhyāya, named The incarnation of Śiva as Sādhudvija, in the third saṃhitā, the Śatarudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.3.36.1: Nandīśvara said: O Sanatkumāra, all-knowing one, hear of the supreme incarnation, named Aśvatthāman, of Śiva, the all-pervading Lord and Supreme Self.
m.3.36.2: O sage, from a portion of Bṛhaspati, the divine sage of great intellect, Droṇa, self-possessed and not born from a womb, was born of Bharadvāja.
m.3.36.3: He was the best of bowmen, a hero, a brahmin seer, knower of all the scriptures, of great fame and great splendour, foremost among those who know all weapons.
m.3.36.4: The wise know Droṇa as expert in the science of archery and in the Veda, the most excellent, of wondrous deeds, the one who increased the glory of his own family.
m.3.36.5: O brahmin, by his own strength he became the preceptor of the Kauravas, famed among the six great chariot-warriors in the Kaurava camp.
m.3.36.6: To aid the Kauravas, Droṇācārya, best of brahmins, performed extensive austerity directed to Śiva, for the sake of a son.
m.3.36.7: Then, pleased, the blessed Śaṅkara, loving to his devotees, appeared before Droṇa, O best of sages.
m.3.36.8: Seeing him, the brahmin Droṇa quickly bowed to him and praised him, his heart greatly delighted, bending low with palms joined.
m.3.36.9: Pleased by his praise and austerity, the Lord Śaṅkara, loving to devotees, said to Droṇa: Ask for a boon.
m.3.36.10: Hearing Śambhu's words, Droṇa, bowing deeply, then said: Grant me a son born of a portion of yourself, invincible to all, of great strength.
m.3.36.11: Hearing Droṇa's words, Śambhu said, so be it, and, dear one, the playful bestower of happiness vanished, O sage.
m.3.36.12: Droṇa went to his own abode, greatly delighted and free of anxiety, and joyfully told his wife all that had happened.
m.3.36.13: Then, at the proper time, Rudra, the Lord who ends all, was born through a portion of himself as Droṇa's son, mighty in strength.
m.3.36.14: He became famous on earth as Aśvatthāman, O sage — a great hero with lotus-petal eyes, the destroyer of the enemy's side.
m.3.36.15: Renowned in the Bhārata war, that mighty one, having received his father's command, became a helper of the Kauravas.
m.3.36.16: Relying on that great hero, the very mighty Kauravas, Bhīṣma and the others, became invincible even to the gods.
m.3.36.17: Out of fear of him, all the Pāṇḍavas, though great heroes and all skilled, were unable to conquer the Kauravas and were dispirited.
m.3.36.18: On Kṛṣṇa's advice Arjuna performed a most severe austerity to Śambhu, and having obtained a weapon through Śambhu's boon, he then conquered them.
m.3.36.19: Aśvatthāman, the great hero born of a portion of Mahādeva, O sage, nevertheless, under the sway of devotion to him, displayed his own prowess.
m.3.36.20: He, whose strength could not be checked by the enemy, the great heroes Kṛṣṇa and others, destroyed the sons of the Pāṇḍavas, even though they had been carefully trained.
m.3.36.21: Seeing that Arjuna, distraught with grief for his sons, rushing at him in a chariot with Acyuta, he fled.
m.3.36.22: He released at him the weapon called Brahmaśiras; then a fierce blaze arose in every direction.
m.3.36.23: Perceiving danger to his life, Arjuna, afflicted, exhausted, his vigour gone and in great fear, spoke to Kṛṣṇa.
m.3.36.24: Arjuna said: O Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa, I do not know what this is or from where it comes; this utterly unbearable blaze advances facing every side.
m.3.36.25: Nandīśvara said: Hearing these words of Arjuna, Kṛṣṇa, the best of Śaivas, meditated on Śiva together with his consort and respectfully replied to Arjuna.
m.3.36.26: Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: Know this to be the most dreadful Brahmā-weapon of Droṇa's son. There is no other weapon whatever that can counter it.
m.3.36.27: Quickly remember Śiva, Śambhu, your own Lord, protector of devotees, by whom his own supreme weapon, accomplishing every purpose, was given to you.
m.3.36.28: With the blaze of that Śaiva weapon, destroy this surging blaze of the weapon. Having said this, Kṛṣṇa himself meditated on Śiva for that purpose.
m.3.36.29: Hearing Kṛṣṇa's words, Pārtha remembered Śiva in his heart, touched water, bowed to him, and quickly discharged the weapon, O sage.
m.3.36.30: Although the Brahmaśiras weapon is unfailing and cannot be countered, it was instantly pacified by the blaze of the Śaiva weapon, O great sage.
m.3.36.31: Do not think this a marvel in the case of Śiva, who is full of every wonder — the Unborn who by his own power creates, protects and destroys the entire universe.
m.3.36.32: Then Aśvatthāman, born of Śiva's portion, knowing this event to be Śiva's doing, was not in the least distressed, his mind content with Śiva's will, O sage.
m.3.36.33: Then Drauṇi set his mind on destroying the child in Uttarā's womb, so as to make this whole world bereft of Pāṇḍavas.
m.3.36.34: That great lord hurled, aiming at Uttarā's womb, the Brahmā-weapon of great radiance, which other weapons could not check.
m.3.36.35: Then Uttarā, daughter-in-law of Jiṣṇu (Arjuna), her mind distraught, being burned by that weapon, praised Kṛṣṇa, the lord of Lakṣmī.
m.3.36.36: Then Kṛṣṇa, having meditated on Śiva, praised him in his heart and bowed, understood that Drauṇi's weapon was meant to make this world free of Pāṇḍavas.
m.3.36.37: By Śiva's command he made her protection with that radiant weapon Sudarśana, which had been given to him by the lord for his own protection.
m.3.36.38: Knowing the true nature of the deed performed by Kṛṣṇa, the foremost of Śaivas, at Śaṅkara's command, Aśvatthāman gradually became downcast.
m.3.36.39: Then Kṛṣṇa, king among Śaivas, pleased at heart, made all the Pāṇḍavas fall at his feet to gratify him.
m.3.36.40: Then Drauṇi Aśvatthāman, gracious at heart, showed them favour and lovingly gave various boons to the Pāṇḍavas and to Kṛṣṇa as well.
m.3.36.41: Thus, dear one, O best of sages, the Lord Maheśvara performed a supreme divine play, having descended upon the earth in the form of Drauṇi, the son of Droṇa.
m.3.36.42: Aśvatthāmā, the incarnation of Śiva, of great strength and valour, the giver of happiness to the three worlds, still dwells even today on the bank of the Jāhnavī Gaṅgā.
m.3.36.43: Thus the Aśvatthāmā incarnation of Lord Śaṅkara has been described to you; it brings about all accomplishments and also grants devotees the fruits they desire.
m.3.36.44: Whoever listens to this with devotion, or recites it with a concentrated mind, would attain the accomplishment he desires, and at the end would go to Śiva's city.
m.3.36.iti: Thus ends the thirty-sixth adhyāya, named The incarnation of Śiva as Aśvatthāman, in the third saṃhitā, the Śatarudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.3.37.1: Nandīśvara said: Listen, O wise one, to the incarnation of the Pināka-bearer Śiva called Kirāta, in which he killed the demon Mūka and, being pleased, gave a boon to Arjuna.
m.3.37.2: Those excellent Pāṇḍavas, defeated by Suyodhana, went with that virtuous Draupadī to the forest called Dvaita.
m.3.37.3: There, relying on the vessel given by Sūrya, the Pāṇḍavas then passed their time in comfort, it is said.
m.3.37.4: O chief of brahmins, Durvāsas, foremost of sages, was sent by that Suyodhana with a deceitful purpose, respectfully, to the presence of the Pāṇḍavas.
m.3.37.5: Having arrived there with his own disciples, numbering ten thousand, he gladly asked them for food as his heart desired.
m.3.37.6: Having agreed, those Pāṇḍavas then sent the ascetic sages headed by Durvāsas off to bathe.
m.3.37.7: Then, O lord of sages, all those Pāṇḍavas, distressed for lack of food, resolved in their minds to give up their lives.
m.3.37.8: Remembered by Draupadī, Kṛṣṇa came at that very moment; and by eating a leaf of vegetable he brought about their satisfaction.
m.3.37.9: Then Durvāsas, knowing his disciples to be satiated, went away again; and the Pāṇḍavas were then freed from hardship by the grace of Kṛṣṇa.
m.3.37.10: Then those Pāṇḍavas asked Kṛṣṇa: What will happen? A powerful enemy has arisen. Tell us what should be done, O lord.
m.3.37.11: Nandīśvara said: Thus asked then by those Pāṇḍavas, O sage, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, remembering the lotus feet of Śiva, said this to the Pāṇḍavas.
m.3.37.12: Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: Listen, excellent Pāṇḍavas, to my story, especially as it concerns the service of Śiva; having heard it, you must act accordingly.
m.3.37.13: Having gone to Dvārakā with the desire to conquer my enemies, and having reflected on the teachings of the great-souled Upamanyu,
m.3.37.14: I worshipped Śambhu, the supreme Lord, well served for seven months on Baṭuka, the best of mountains, and he became pleased.
m.3.37.15: The Lord of the universe, standing before me in person, granted me my desired wishes; by his power I obtained supreme capability in all things.
m.3.37.16: Even now that god, giver of the fruits of enjoyment and liberation, is served by me. You too should serve that Śambhu, who brings all happiness.
m.3.37.17: Nandīśvara said: Having said this and consoled the Pāṇḍavas, Kṛṣṇa vanished and quickly went to Dvārakā, remembering the lotus feet of Śiva.
m.3.37.18: Then the Pāṇḍavas promptly sent a Bhilla as spy to examine the qualities of that Duryodhana.
m.3.37.19: He too, having learned all that was there—the flourishing of Duryodhana's qualities—and that it was sound, returned to his masters.
m.3.37.20: Hearing what he said, O lord of sages, they became sorrowful; and the Pāṇḍavas, deeply distressed, spoke to one another:
m.3.37.21: What should we do now, where should we go regarding war? Though all capable, we are bound by the noose of truth, our promise.
m.3.37.22: Nandīśvara said: At that time Vyāsa came, his forehead adorned with ash, wearing rudrākṣa ornaments, and adorned with matted locks.
m.3.37.23: Muttering the five-syllable mantra, overflowing with love for Śiva, himself a mass of radiance, like another Dharma incarnate.
m.3.37.24: Seeing him, they were delighted, rose and stood before him, and then offered him a seat beautified with kuśa grass and deerskin.
m.3.37.25: Joyful, they worshipped Vyāsa seated there, and having offered various praises, said: We are blessed.
m.3.37.26: The austerities well performed and the various gifts—all that has borne fruit; we are satisfied by the sight of you, O lord.
m.3.37.27: By your sight, O grandfather, sorrow has gone far away—great sorrow that was inflicted on us by the wicked, whose deeds are cruel.
m.3.37.28: When the sight of the illustrious occurs, sorrow will surely depart. If at any time it does not depart in such a case, this conclusion has been reached:
m.3.37.29: When the hermitage of the great, who are capable in every undertaking, has been reached, if sorrow still does not go, then fate alone is the cause here.
m.3.37.30: Poverty, the cause of sorrow, will certainly go. This nature of the great is held to be like the wish-fulfilling tree.
m.3.37.31: Counting only their qualities, by the very nature of the great one, it is solely through the power of one's refuge that, for a man, O lord, arise
m.3.37.32: smallness and greatness; no deliberation is needed on this. This is the nature of the noblest, that they protect the wretched.
m.3.37.33: The mark of a poor man is considered in the world most conducive to welfare: before him lies supreme effort and the service of good people.
m.3.37.34: Beyond this lies fortune; let no blame be assigned. For this reason, O master, when you have been seen, auspiciousness comes then.
m.3.37.35: By your mere arrival our minds are gladdened. Give us instruction by which our sorrow may quickly be destroyed.
m.3.37.36: Nandīśvara said: Hearing these words of the Pāṇḍavas, the great sage Vyāsa, his mind pleased, said this:
m.3.37.37: O Pāṇḍavas, you ought not to grieve. You are blessed, you have fulfilled your duty; truth has not been violated by you.
m.3.37.38: This is the most beautiful nature of good people: even at the end of life they never abandon dharma. Here, truth is the vessel of fruitful reward.
m.3.37.39: To us, you and they are alike; nevertheless, partiality toward the most righteous is approved by the wise.
m.3.37.40: First of all, by the wicked and blind Dhṛtarāṣṭra dharma was himself abandoned out of greed, and your kingdom was seized.
m.3.37.41: You, and they too, are indeed his sons; there is no doubt. Since your father has passed away, you children are to be treated with compassion by that great-souled one.
m.3.37.42: But afterwards his son was never restrained by him. Had he been restrained, no calamity would have arisen, nor what was then done in this way.
m.3.37.43: What has happened after that has happened; it could not be otherwise. This one is wicked, while you are most righteous and truthful.
m.3.37.44: Therefore, in the end, misfortune will surely come to him alone; whatever seed is sown, its sprout appears here.
m.3.37.45: Therefore you should by no means grieve. Good will surely come to you; there need be no doubt about this.
m.3.37.46: Nandīśvara said: When he had spoken thus, all the Pāṇḍavas, gladdened by Vyāsa, led by Yudhiṣṭhira, spoke these words again.
m.3.37.47: The Pāṇḍavas said: You have spoken the truth, O lord. The wicked, evil-souled ones inflict sorrow on us incessantly, again and again, even in the forest.
m.3.37.48: So destroy our misfortune today; grant us something auspicious, O mighty one. Kṛṣṇa told us before that Śaṅkara is always to be worshipped.
m.3.37.49: But we were negligent, and that advice was neglected. Let that divine path now be taught to us again.
m.3.37.50: Nandīśvara said: Hearing these words, Vyāsa, filled with joy, spoke lovingly to the Pāṇḍavas, having remembered the lotus-feet of Śiva.
m.3.37.51: Vyāsa said: Listen to my words today, O Pāṇḍavas of righteous mind. Kṛṣṇa indeed spoke the truth; Śiva is served by me as well.
m.3.37.52: Let him be served by you with love; there will always be incomparable happiness. All sorrow arises precisely from not serving Śiva.
m.3.37.53: Nandīśvara said: Then, having considered among those five who was suited for the worship of Śiva, Vyāsa, the best of sages, named Arjuna as the fit one;
m.3.37.54: and having thus considered a place for austerity, that most excellent sage then spoke this again to the Pāṇḍavas, who were firmly devoted to dharma.
m.3.37.55: Vyāsa said: Listen, all you Pāṇḍavas; I shall tell you what is always beneficial: seeing Śiva as everything, the Supreme, the supreme Brahman, the goal of the virtuous.
m.3.37.56: Whatever world is seen, from Brahmā up to the end of the triple parārdha, all that is Śiva's form; and that again is to be worshipped and meditated upon.
m.3.37.57: This Śaṅkara, destroyer of all sorrows, is to be served by all. Śiva becomes fully pleased in a short time through devotion.
m.3.37.58: For Maheśa, when well pleased, grants everything to his devotees; he bestows enjoyment and liberation, here and hereafter—this is firmly established.
m.3.37.59: Therefore Śambhu should always be served by those who desire the fruits of enjoyment and liberation. Śaṅkara is the Supreme Person himself, destroyer of the wicked, the goal of the virtuous.
m.3.37.60: But first one should, with a firm mind, recite the Śakra-vidyā (lore of Indra). For an eminent kṣatriya this alone is prescribed.
m.3.37.61: Therefore Arjuna, steadfast, should first recite the Śakra-vidyā. Indra will first test him, and then he will be satisfied.
m.3.37.62: Well pleased, he will always remove obstacles, and further he will bestow the excellent mantra of Śiva himself.
m.3.37.63: Nandīśvara said: Having said this, he summoned Arjuna and taught him the Upendra-vidyā. Having bathed and faced east, Arjuna of intense mind received it.
m.3.37.64: The best of sages also gave him the procedure for worshipping the earthen liṅga; and Vyāsa, of noble mind, spoke to Dhanañjaya in turn.
m.3.37.65: Vyāsa said: Go now from here, Pārtha, to the beautiful Indrakīla, and staying near the Jāhnavī (Gaṅgā), perform austerity properly.
m.3.37.66: And may this invisible lore always be beneficial to you. Thus he gave him a blessing; then the sage spoke to the others.
m.3.37.67: Let all of you, best of kings, remain steadfast in dharma. The highest success will come in every way; there need be no doubt about this.
m.3.37.68: Nandīśvara said: Having thus given his blessing to the Pāṇḍavas, Vyāsa, lord of sages, remembered Śiva's lotus-feet and vanished in an instant.
m.3.37.iti: Thus ends the thirty-seventh adhyāya, named Vyāsa's instruction to Arjuna, in the course of the account of the Kirāta incarnation, in the third saṃhitā, the Śatarudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.3.38.1: Nandīśvara said: Then Arjuna too was seen there, shining, bearing incomparable radiance through the mantra, which has the form of Śiva.
m.3.38.2: All the Pāṇḍavas, seeing Arjuna, reached certainty: Victory is surely ours, since his radiance is so great.
m.3.38.3: This task is to be accomplished by you and never by anyone else; so it appears from Vyāsa's words. Make your life fruitful.
m.3.38.4: Having said this to Arjuna, they, distressed by the anxiety of separation, though unwilling, respectfully sent him off from that very place.
m.3.38.5: Draupadī, the devoted wife, filled with grief, holding back the tears in her eyes, then spoke auspicious words as she sent him off.
m.3.38.6: Draupadī said: O prince, what Vyāsa has instructed must be done by you with effort. May your path bring auspiciousness; may Śaṅkara grant you well-being.
m.3.38.7: Having respectfully sent Arjuna off, they all stayed there, overcome by extreme sorrow, the five of them together.
m.3.38.8: Staying there, they said—listen, O best of sages—even in sorrow, the company of a dear one does not lead to sorrow.
m.3.38.9: In separation from him, one's sorrow becomes constantly twofold; then how could even one who holds firm have fortitude here?
m.3.38.10: Nandīśvara said: While the Pāṇḍavas were thus grieving, the lord of sages, Vyāsa, the ocean of compassion and best of seers, arrived.
m.3.38.11: Then the Pāṇḍavas, filled with sorrow, bowed to him, worshipped him respectfully, offered him a seat, and with joined palms spoke these words.
m.3.38.12: The Pāṇḍavas said: Listen, O most excellent one; we are burned by sorrow, O lord. Having obtained your sight today, O sage, we attain joy.
m.3.38.13: Stay right here for some time to destroy our sorrow, O lord; through seeing you, O brahmin seer, all sorrow dissolves.
m.3.38.14: Nandīśvara said: Thus addressed, that best of sages stayed for their comfort, and then with various stories he drove away their sorrow.
m.3.38.15: While the conversation was being carried on by Vyāsa, O good sage, Dharmarāja, humble in spirit, bowed deeply and said this:
m.3.38.16: Yama said: Listen, O best of sages: I regard your presence as the pacification of my sorrow. I ask you, O greatly wise one; please tell me, O lord.
m.3.38.17: Has anyone in the past met with such sorrow? We alone have met with supreme sorrow, no one else.
m.3.38.18: Vyāsa said: Formerly, to the king named Nala, lord of Niṣadha, that great soul, there came sorrow greater than your sorrow.
m.3.38.19: King Hariścandra met with even greater sorrow; it is especially indescribable, and likewise brings grief to others who hear it.
