m.3.38.20: Likewise, O Pāṇḍava, know the sorrow of Rāma too, hearing which women and men would fall into still greater bewilderment.
m.3.38.21: Therefore I cannot describe it again. Regarding the body as a heap of sorrow, you should now give up attachment to it.
m.3.38.22: Whoever has taken on this body is pervaded by sorrow, no doubt. First, birth in the mother's womb is a cause of sorrow.
m.3.38.23: In childhood too there is great sorrow, which follows from childish play; and after that, in youth, one enjoys pleasures that are sorrow in form.
m.3.38.24: With the coming and going of days and the many burdens of duties, life wastes away constantly, yet one does not realise it.
m.3.38.25: And at the end comes death, the greatest sorrow beyond this; and then the torments of various hells are suffered by ignorant men.
m.3.38.26: Therefore this world is unreal; you, however, practise what is true. A man should act in such a way that Śambhu is pleased.
m.3.38.27: Nandīśvara said: Thus, with various conversations and along the paths of their hopes, all the brothers then passed the time.
m.3.38.28: Arjuna too, firm in his vow, went on himself through difficult mountains, and, having obtained a Yakṣa as guide, with his help slaying robbers many times,
m.3.38.29: joyful in mind, went to the excellent mountain. Having gone there, near the Gaṅgā, he came to a beautiful spot,
m.3.38.30: an Aśoka grove, where it was as if the highest heaven stood. There he stayed, having bathed and bowed to his excellent teacher.
m.3.38.31: He himself adopted the dress and the rest just as he had been instructed. First withdrawing his senses, he became settled in mind.
m.3.38.32: Then, having made a beautiful, well-proportioned earthen liṅga, he meditated before it on the supreme mass of radiance.
m.3.38.33: Bathing well at the three times of day, he then performed various worship and repeatedly adored Hara there.
m.3.38.34: A radiance issued from his very head. Seeing that, the spies of Indra were seized with fear: When did this one enter here?
m.3.38.35: Then, having reflected thus, they said, this must be told to Indra (Viḍaujas), and went swiftly to Śakra's presence.
m.3.38.36: The spies said: Whether a god, or a sage, or the Sun, or Fire—someone is practising austerity in the forest, O lord of gods; we do not know who he is.
m.3.38.37: Scorched by his radiance, we have come into your presence. This account has been reported; let whatever is proper be done.
m.3.38.38: Nandīśvara said: Thus addressed by the spies, and understanding fully what his son intended, he dismissed the mountain-guardians and resolved to go there.
m.3.38.39: The lord of Śacī, becoming an old brahmin celibate, went there, O chief of brahmins, to test him.
m.3.38.40: Seeing him arrived, the Pāṇḍava then worshipped him, and standing before him, having praised him, said: Tell me now, from where have you come?
m.3.38.41: Addressed thus by him, the lord of the gods, out of affection and to test his steadfastness, then spoke to the Pāṇḍava words that concealed a test.
m.3.38.42: The brahmin said: Dear one, why are you now performing austerity at so young an age? Is this austerity of yours wholly for liberation or for victory?
m.3.38.43: Nandīśvara said: Questioned thus by him, Arjuna then again related everything. Hearing that, the brahmin then spoke again.
m.3.38.44: The brahmin said: O hero, austerity that is performed in accordance with kṣatriya duty to obtain happiness is not fitting; austerity is performed for liberation, O best of the Kurus.
m.3.38.45: Indra indeed is a giver of happiness, but he cannot be a giver of liberation. Therefore, O excellent one, you should by all means perform true austerity.
m.3.38.46: Nandīśvara said: Hearing these words, Arjuna then became angry; yet, humble of spirit and firm in his vows, he disregarded it and replied.
m.3.38.47: Arjuna said: It is for the kingdom and not for liberation — why do you say this? Such austerity is being performed solely at the word of Vyāsa.
m.3.38.48: Go away from here, celibate student. You wish to make me fall. What purpose do you, a celibate, have here?
m.3.38.49: Nandīśvara said: Addressed thus, he was pleased and revealed his own beautiful, wondrous form, endowed with his own insignia.
m.3.38.50: Seeing the form of Śakra, Arjuna then felt ashamed; Indra, having comforted him, spoke words again.
m.3.38.51: Indra said: Choose a boon, O dear Dhanañjaya of great intellect, whatever your heart desires; nothing exists that cannot be given to you.
m.3.38.52: Hearing Śakra's words, Arjuna then replied: Grant me victory in every way, dear one, for I am afflicted by enemies.
m.3.38.53: Śakra said: Your enemies, led by Duryodhana, are very mighty; Droṇa, Bhīṣma and Karṇa — all of them are surely hard to conquer.
m.3.38.54: Aśvatthāmā, Droṇa's son, a portion of Rudra, is extremely invincible. They would be wholly beyond my power; hear what is for your own good.
m.3.38.55: O hero, no one now is able to bring about this victory. Śiva, the most excellent, is there; therefore now undertake the japa of Śambhu.
m.3.38.56: Śaṅkara is the lord of all worlds, master of the moving and the unmoving, self-ruling; he is able to do everything and bestows the fruits of enjoyment and liberation.
m.3.38.57: I believe that I, Brahmā and the others, Viṣṇu the bestower of all boons, and all others who seek victory — all of them are worshippers of Śiva.
m.3.38.58: From today, abandoning that mantra, worship Śiva with devotion, by the rite of the earthen liṅga and by meditation on Śiva,
m.3.38.59: and with many offerings, with your whole being, O Bhārata; then your success will be unshakable today — there need be no deliberation about this.
m.3.38.60: Nandīśvara said: Having said this, he summoned all his attendants and said: You must always remain vigilant in protecting him.
m.3.38.61: Having instructed his attendants about Arjuna's protection and so on, Indra, his heart full of affection, again spoke to the one with the monkey banner.
m.3.38.62: Indra said: You must never rule the kingdom carelessly. May this knowledge be for your welfare, good one, O scorcher of foes.
m.3.38.63: Steadfastness must be maintained by the practitioner; Śiva is the protector in every way. He will give you prosperity and the fruit you seek; there is no doubt of this.
m.3.38.64: Nandīśvara said: Having thus given the boon to the Bhārata, the lord of the gods, remembering the lotus feet of Śiva, went to his own abode.
m.3.38.65: Arjuna too, the great hero, having bowed deeply to the lord of the gods, with self-control performed austerity of that kind directed toward Śiva.
m.3.38.iti: Thus ends the thirty-eighth adhyāya, named Arjuna's austerity, in the course of the account of the Kirāta incarnation, in the third saṃhitā, the Śatarudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.3.39.1: Nandīśvara said: Having bathed according to rule, and likewise performed nyāsa and the rest according to rule, he performed with true devotion the meditation on Śiva exactly as Vyāsa had taught it.
m.3.39.2: Standing on the sole of one foot like an eminent sage, fixing his single-pointed gaze on the sun, he remained repeating the mantra.
m.3.39.3: He performed austerity with great delight, remembering Śiva in his mind and repeating Śambhu's five-syllabled mantra, the highest of all.
m.3.39.4: Such was the radiance of his austerity that the gods were amazed. They went again to Śiva and, composed, spoke to him.
m.3.39.5: The gods said: O Lord of all, a single man has undertaken austerity for your sake. Whatever this man desires, why do you not grant it, O Lord?
m.3.39.6: Nandīśvara said: Having said this, the gods then offered various hymns of praise, and fixing their eyes on his feet they stood there with steady minds.
m.3.39.7: Śiva, the great Lord of noble mind, hearing their words, laughed heartily and, pleased at heart, spoke to the gods.
m.3.39.8: Śiva said: Go to your own abodes, all you gods; this is true, without doubt. I shall accomplish your purpose in every way; there is no doubt about it.
m.3.39.9: Nandīśvara said: Hearing Śambhu's words, the gods attained supreme certainty, and all of them turned back and went to their own abodes.
m.3.39.10: Meanwhile a demon named Mūka arrived, having assumed the form of a boar, sent by the wicked one—
m.3.39.11: by the deceitful Duryodhana, O best of brahmins, against Arjuna; he came then by the path where Arjuna was staying,
m.3.39.12: breaking the peaks of the mountain and many trees, making various noises, rushing with great speed.
m.3.39.13: Arjuna too, seeing that demon named Mūka, remembered the lotus feet of Śiva and became intent on reflection.
m.3.39.14: Arjuna said: Who is this, and from where does he come? He appears to be of cruel deeds. Surely he is coming to do me harm, without doubt.
m.3.39.15: So my mind tells me: he is surely an enemy, no doubt. Many Daityas and Dānavas were slain by me before.
m.3.39.16: Someone of theirs is coming to take revenge again; or else some friend devoted to Duryodhana's welfare.
m.3.39.17: He at whose sight one's own mind becomes serene is surely a well-wisher; he at whose sight that same mind becomes agitated is surely an enemy.
m.3.39.18: Conduct reveals one's family, the body reveals one's food, speech reveals one's learning, and the eye reveals affection.
m.3.39.19: By appearance, gait, gesture and speech, and by changes in the eyes and face, the hidden mind is known.
m.3.39.20: The wise have declared the eye to be of four kinds—bright, tender, oblique and reddish—each with its own distinct meaning.
m.3.39.21: Bright on meeting a friend, tender on seeing a son, oblique in union with a beloved woman, and red on seeing an enemy.
m.3.39.22: In his presence all my senses are disturbed. This must be an enemy; he is to be killed, no doubt.
m.3.39.23: And my guru's instruction stands for me today: One who causes pain is to be killed by you by all means, O king; no hesitation should be had here.
m.3.39.24: And my weapons are for this very purpose, no doubt. Reflecting thus, he stood right there, fitting an arrow to his bow.
m.3.39.25: Meanwhile, to protect Arjuna and to test his devotion, Śaṅkara, who is affectionate to his devotees,
m.3.39.26: assumed the most wondrous form of a skilled Bhilla hunter together with his gaṇas, and quickly arrived there to destroy that demon.
m.3.39.27: Hara then, with his garment girded up and his hair tied with creepers, with white stripes on his body, himself bearing bow and arrows,
m.3.39.28: carrying a quiver of arrows on his back, went forth. His gaṇas too became hunters likewise, and Śiva became the king of the Bhillas.
m.3.39.29: Making various cries, the leader of the host set out; then the sound pursued the boar in all ten directions.
m.3.39.30: Arjuna was then disturbed by the sound of the forest-dweller, and by those sounds the mountains and everything else were all shaken.
m.3.39.31: Arjuna thought: Ah, what could this be? Yet Śiva is the bestower of good here. I have heard this before, and Kṛṣṇa too has told it again,
m.3.39.32: and Vyāsa told it as well; and the gods too, remembering, have said again: Śiva is declared the bestower of good, and Śiva likewise the giver of happiness.
m.3.39.33: He himself is called the giver of liberation because he grants liberation, no doubt. By remembering his name, welfare surely arises for people.
m.3.39.34: For those who worship him with their whole being, sorrow does not arise even in a dream; if it ever does arise, then it springs from past karma.
m.3.39.35: What is destined, even if great, should be known as surely small, no doubt; or else it should be understood especially as the fault of prārabdha karma.
m.3.39.36: Or else Śaṅkara, having carried the devotee through what must be experienced, whether much or little, may at times remove it by his will, no doubt.
m.3.39.37: He can turn poison into nectar, or nectar into poison. Whatever he wishes, he does; he is all-powerful—what can restrain him?
m.3.39.38: Even as this is pondered thus, it is understood by other devotees of old and by devotees yet to come: having always brought the mind here to Śiva, one should keep it steady.
m.3.39.39: Whether fortune departs or remains, whether death is near and before one, whether people blame or praise—and likewise the ending of sorrow—
m.3.39.40: all this arises from merit and sin. Śaṅkara is always the giver of happiness; and sometimes Śiva gives sorrow in order to test his devotee.
m.3.39.41: And in the end he is declared to be the giver of happiness, because of his compassion; there is no doubt. Just as gold, when refined, attains purity, so too does the devotee through hardship.
m.3.39.42: Thus indeed I heard it formerly from the mouth of the sage. Therefore, by worshipping him alone, I shall obtain supreme happiness.
m.3.39.43: While he was reflecting in this way, just then the boar arrived within range of an arrow's release.
m.3.39.44: Śiva too came, following closely behind the boar. Then, between the two of them, that boar appeared like a wondrous peak.
m.3.39.45: His greatness has been proclaimed: Śiva, Śaṅkara who is affectionate to his devotees, moved even more swiftly for the protection of Arjuna.
m.3.39.46: At that moment the two of them released their arrows: Śiva's arrow struck at the tail, and Arjuna's at the mouth.
m.3.39.47: Śiva's arrow, having entered through the tail and swiftly emerged from the mouth, vanished into the ground; Arjuna's went out through its tail.
m.3.39.48: And Arjuna's arrow fell to the side. At that instant the boar-demon fell dead upon the ground.
m.3.39.49: The gods attained supreme joy and showered flowers; crying victory, they offered praises, bowing again and again.
m.3.39.50: Śiva was pleased at heart and Arjuna attained happiness; then the two of them saw the cruel form of the demon.
m.3.39.51: Arjuna in particular spoke with a joyful heart: Ah! This is a mighty demon, and his form is most wondrous.
m.3.39.52: Having assumed this form, he came to kill me; I have been well protected by Śiva. The Lord has granted me understanding this very day; there is no doubt.
m.3.39.53: Having reflected thus, Arjuna there chanted Śiva, Śiva, bowed once more to Śiva, and praised him again and again.
m.3.39.iti: Thus ends the thirty-ninth adhyāya, named The slaying of the demon Mūka, in the account of the Kirāta incarnation, in the third saṃhitā, the Śatarudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.3.40.1: Nandīśvara said: O Sanatkumāra, knower of all, hear the sport (līlā) of the Supreme Self, filled with affection for his devotees and interwoven with the testing of Arjuna's firmness.
m.3.40.2: Then Śiva too quickly sent his own servant for the arrow; and at that time Arjuna also came there for it.
m.3.40.3: At one and the same moment both his attendant (gaṇa) and Arjuna arrived for the arrow; Arjuna, rebuking him, then took up his own arrow.
m.3.40.4: The attendant said to him there: Why is the arrow being taken? The arrow is ours indeed; let it go, O best of sages.
m.3.40.5: O best of sages, thus addressed by that attendant of the Bhilla, Arjuna remembered Śaṅkara and spoke these words to him.
m.3.40.6: Arjuna said: What are you saying without knowing? You are a fool, forest-dweller. The arrow was released by me today; how then is it yours?
m.3.40.7: Its lined shape and feathers, and it is marked with my very name—how has it become yours? Your nature is hard to give up.
m.3.40.8: Nandīśvara said: Having heard these words of his, that lord of attendants, in the form of a Bhilla, laughed and addressed Arjuna, who was in the guise of a sage.
m.3.40.9: Listen, you ascetic. No austerity is being performed by you. You are an ascetic only by your garb, not in truth; you act deceitfully.
m.3.40.10: How can a man who is an ascetic speak falsely? And know that I am not alone: I serve the lord of an army.
m.3.40.11: That master of mine dwells accompanied by many forest Bhillas, and he is fully able to bestow both hostility and favour.
m.3.40.12: This arrow, which has just now been taken by you, is his; this arrow will never remain by your side.
m.3.40.13: Why, O ascetic, do you wish to throw away the fruit of your austerity? Through theft, deceit, harassing others, arrogance and breaking the truth—
m.3.40.14: —austerity wanes; this is what I have heard. Therefore, how will there be any fruit of your austerity today?
m.3.40.15: Therefore, if you do not let go of the arrow, you will be ungrateful; for surely it was my own master who released the arrow for your sake.
m.3.40.16: The enemy was slain by him, and your life was protected by the arrow; so you are utterly ungrateful, and likewise one who makes his austerity inauspicious.
m.3.40.17: You do not speak the truth; how then do you hope for success? If you need the arrow, let my master be asked for it.
m.3.40.18: He himself is able then to give many such arrows. My king is present here today; why then is he not asked by you in this way?
m.3.40.19: Casting aside the favour done to you, you seek to do harm. What you are doing right now is not proper; give up this rashness.
m.3.40.20: Nandīśvara said: Having heard these words of his, Arjuna, son of Pṛthā, grew angry, yet remembering Śiva he then spoke measured words.
m.3.40.21: Arjuna said: Listen, Bhilla, I shall speak: your speech is not true. As your birth is, so do I know you to be, forest-dweller.
m.3.40.22: I am a king; you are a thief. How can there be fighting between us? I must fight with the mighty, never with the base.
m.3.40.23: So too your master will be just like you. We are called givers; you forest-dwellers are thieves.
m.3.40.24: How should the Bhilla king be begged by me now in this way? Why do you yourself not ask me for the arrow, forest-dweller?
m.3.40.25: If asked, I would give you arrows, for surely I have many; but a king will not yield to seizure—so it must be.
m.3.40.26: Why indeed should I hand over arrows thus, forest-dweller? If your lord has any design against me, why does he not come now?
m.3.40.27: Let your master rather come; why does he merely talk now? Having come and fought with me, and having defeated me in battle,
m.3.40.28: let your Bhilla master, the lord of the army, take this arrow and go happily to his own abode. Why is there delay?
m.3.40.29: Nandīśvara said: Having heard these words of Arjuna, who had obtained true strength through the grace of Maheśvara, the Bhilla then spoke.
m.3.40.30: The Bhilla said: You are ignorant; you are no sage. Why do you seek death? Give up the arrow and remain at ease; otherwise you will suffer distress.
m.3.40.31: Nandīśvara said: Thus addressed by that Bhilla attendant, who shone with the true power of Śiva, the Pāṇḍava remembered Śaṅkara and spoke to him.
m.3.40.32: Arjuna said: Listen truly to my words, Bhilla, forest-dweller: when your master comes, then I shall show him the result.
m.3.40.33: Fighting with you is not fitting; I shall fight with your master. A fight between a lion and a jackal is to be known as laughable.
m.3.40.34: You have heard my words today; you will see great might. Go to your master, Bhilla, and do as you wish.
m.3.40.35: Nandīśvara said: Thus addressed by Pārtha, O sage, the Bhilla went to where the Kirāta, the lord of the army, the incarnation of Śiva, was staying.
m.3.40.36: Then he reported all of Arjuna's words in detail to the lord of the Bhillas, that Supreme Self in the form of a Bhilla.
m.3.40.37: Hearing those words, that lord of the Kirātas, Śaṅkara bearing the form of a Bhilla, was delighted and came with his own army.
m.3.40.38: Then Arjuna the Pāṇḍava, seeing the Kirāta's army, took up his bow with arrows and came forward to face it.
m.3.40.39: Then the Kirāta again sent that messenger, and through his mouth spoke these words to the great-souled Bhārata.
m.3.40.40: The Kirāta said: Look at the army, O ascetic. Release the arrow and go now. Why do you wish for death at this moment for so trifling a matter?
m.3.40.41: Your brothers will be stricken with grief, and after that your wife as well; and the earth will today slip from your hand. This is my view.
m.3.40.42: Nandīśvara said: Thus spoke the supreme Lord Śambhu, who had assumed a form in order to test Pārtha's firmness and, in every way, for the protection of Arjuna.
m.3.40.43: Thus addressed, that attendant of Śaṅkara then came and reported to Arjuna the whole matter in detail.
m.3.40.44: Hearing that, Pārtha spoke again to the messenger who had come: Tell the commander of the army that the opposite will happen.
m.3.40.45: If I give you my arrow, I shall become a disgrace to my lineage; there is no doubt.
m.3.40.46: Then my brothers would surely be stricken with grief, and my learning would be fruitless. Therefore come to fight, certainly.
m.3.40.47: Never have I heard of a lion afraid of a jackal; likewise a king never fears a forest-dweller.
m.3.40.48: Nandīśvara said: Thus addressed by the Pāṇḍava, he went back to his master and reported everything, especially what Arjuna had said.
m.3.40.49: Then Mahādeva too, called the Kirāta, with his host, having heard that, came at that time against Arjuna accompanied by his army.
m.3.40.iti: Thus ends the fortieth adhyāya, named The dialogue of the Bhilla and Arjuna, in the account of the Kirāta incarnation, in the third saṃhitā, the Śatarudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.3.41.1: Then, seeing him arrive, Arjuna meditated on Śiva, went there, and fought a very fierce battle with him.
m.3.41.2: With the gaṇas he harassed him with various sharp weapons. Then Pārtha, afflicted by them, remembered his lord Śiva.
m.3.41.3: Then Arjuna cut down their volley of arrows; and whatever weapon was hurled by them, he cut that too, and then he contemplated Śarva.
m.3.41.4: Afflicted by him, those gaṇas fled in the ten directions; and the gaṇa-chiefs, being held back, did not come back to their master.
m.3.41.5: Śiva and Arjuna fought each other with many kinds of weapons, both possessed of great strength and valour.
m.3.41.6: Śiva too, surely feeling compassion in his mind, approached Arjuna; and Arjuna then dealt a firm blow there.
m.3.41.7: Then Śiva cut off Arjuna's weapons and all his armour; only his body remained.
m.3.41.8: Then Arjuna, remembering Śiva, engaged in wrestling with that commander of the host; though distressed by fear, he remained steadfast.
m.3.41.9: By that fight the whole earth with its oceans trembled. The gods fell into distress, wondering: What will happen now?
m.3.41.10: Meanwhile the god Śiva rose into the sky and fought from there; and Arjuna did likewise.
m.3.41.11: Leaping up again and again, the two, the god and the prince, fought; and the gods were struck with wonder on seeing that marvellous combat.
m.3.41.12: Then Arjuna, perceiving his chance and remembering the lotus-feet of Śiva, having gained true strength through that meditation, seized him by the feet.
m.3.41.13: Holding his feet, Arjuna then whirled him round; and Mahādeva, loving to his devotees and their helper, laughed.
m.3.41.14: O sage, this deed was done by Śiva alone, out of his submission to his devotees, in order to grant him the status of his own servant; it could not be otherwise.
m.3.41.15: Afterwards, laughing, Śaṅkara, out of submission to his devotee, suddenly revealed there his wondrous, auspicious form,
m.3.41.16: as described in the Vedas, the śāstras and the Purāṇa, O best of persons, the form taught by Vyāsa for meditation upon him, which bestows all accomplishments.
m.3.41.17: Seeing that beautiful form of Śiva, attained before in meditation, Arjuna was exceedingly amazed and was himself ashamed.
m.3.41.18: Ah! This is Śiva, Śiva himself, whom I chose as my lord — the Lord of the three worlds in person. Alas, what have I now done!
m.3.41.19: Powerful is the Lord's māyā, deluding even the masters of illusion. What has the Lord done, concealing his form? I have truly been deceived.
m.3.41.20: Having reflected thus in his mind, with joined palms and bowed head, he lovingly bowed to the Lord; then, dejected in mind, he spoke.
m.3.41.21: Arjuna said: O God of gods, Mahādeva, mine of compassion, Śaṅkara, Lord of all — please forgive my offence.
m.3.41.22: What have you done, concealing your form? I have now been deceived by you. Shame on me, who fought with you, my master, O Lord!
m.3.41.23: Nandīśvara said: Speaking thus, the Pāṇḍava was filled with remorse and quickly fell at the feet of Śaṅkara, the great Lord.
m.3.41.24: Then the Lord, pleased at heart, Maheśa, loving to his devotees, consoled Arjuna again and again and replied to him thus.
m.3.41.25: Śaṅkara said: Do not grieve, Pārtha; you are my devotee in a special way. I did this today to test you; cast off your sorrow.
m.3.41.26: Nandīśvara said: Having said this, the Lord raised Arjuna with his own hands and, with the gaṇas extolling the master's virtues, freed him from his shame.
m.3.41.27: Again Śiva, Śaṅkara, loving to his devotees, spoke to Arjuna the Pāṇḍava, esteemed by heroes, delighting him in every way with affection.
m.3.41.28: Śiva said: O Pārtha, best of the Pāṇḍavas, I am pleased; choose a boon. Your blows and strikes today I have honoured as worship.
m.3.41.29: It was done today by my own will; there is no offence on your part now. There is nothing that cannot be given to you; whatever you desire, choose that.
m.3.41.30: This has been done for your good, to establish your fame and kingdom over your enemies. Do not grieve over this; give up all your despondency.
m.3.41.31: Nandīśvara said: Thus addressed by the Lord Śaṅkara, Arjuna, standing attentively, spoke to Śaṅkara with devotion.
m.3.41.32: Arjuna said: O good Lord, what more is to be desired from you, Śambhu, who love your devotees? Your glory is what I should describe, O God; you are compassionate, O Sadāśiva.
m.3.41.33: Having said this, the Pāṇḍava then offered to Śaṅkara, the great Lord, a hymn of praise, true devotion in accord with the Veda.
m.3.41.34: Arjuna said: Salutation to you, God of gods; salutation to the dweller on Kailāsa. O Sadāśiva, salutation to you; salutation to you, the five-faced one.
m.3.41.35: Salutation to you, wearer of matted locks; salutation be to you, the three-eyed. Salutation to the one of gracious form and to the thousand-faced.
m.3.41.36: O blue-throated one, salutation be to you; salutation indeed to Sadyojāta. O bull-bannered one, salutation be to you, who have Girijā on your left side.
m.3.41.37: O ten-armed one, salutation to you; salutation to you, the Supreme Self. Salutation to you who hold the ḍamaru and the skull in your hands, who wear a garland of skulls.
m.3.41.38: To you whose body is like pure crystal and pure camphor, who hold Pināka in hand, bearer of the excellent trident — salutation.
m.3.41.39: Salutation to you who wear a tiger-skin as upper garment and an elephant-hide as clothing, whose limbs are adorned with serpents; O bearer of the Gaṅgā, salutation be to you.
m.3.41.40: Salutation be to you of beautiful feet, of reddish soles, to be served by Nandin and the other gaṇas, and lord of the gaṇas — salutation to you.
m.3.41.41: Salutation to you who have the form of Gaṇeśa and who are attended by Kārttikeya; to you who give devotion to the devotees and who give liberation, salutation, salutation.
m.3.41.42: Salutation be to you who are without attributes; salutation, salutation to you who have attributes; to the formless and to the one with form, to the one with parts and to the partless.
m.3.41.43: Salutation to you who took the form of a Kirāta (hunter), who bestow grace on me, who are fond of battle with heroes, and who enact many kinds of divine play.
m.3.41.44: Whatever form is seen is regarded as your own radiance. You, whose nature is consciousness, delight in the three worlds through both immanence and distinction.
m.3.41.45: There is no counting your qualities, just as there is none here for the particles of earth's dust, for the stars in the sky, or for the drops of rain-water.
m.3.41.46: Even the Vedas are not able to count your qualities; how then, O Lord, can I, of dull intellect, describe them?
m.3.41.47: You are that which you are; salutation be to you. Please show me compassion here. I am your servant, O Maheśāna; you are my master, O Maheśvara.
m.3.41.48: Nandīśvara said: Hearing these words of his, the Lord Śaṅkara, becoming even more pleased, smiling, spoke again to Arjuna.
m.3.41.49: Śaṅkara said: What is the use of saying much? Listen to my word: quickly choose a boon, son, and I shall give you all of it.
m.3.41.50: Nandīśvara said: Thus addressed by him, Arjuna prostrated before Sadāśiva and, with joined palms, bowing, spoke with love in a voice choked with emotion.
m.3.41.51: Arjuna said: What shall I say? You abide as the inner controller of all. Nevertheless, O all-pervading one, may what I describe today be heard by you.
m.3.41.52: The distress caused by enemies is gone through the sight of you. Act so that I may attain success both in this world and the supreme one.
m.3.41.53: Nandīśvara said: Having said this and bowed to Śaṅkara, who is affectionate to his devotees, Arjuna stood there with bent shoulders and joined palms.
m.3.41.54: Śiva, the master, knowing the Pāṇḍava Arjuna to be thus, the best of his own devotees, became greatly pleased.
m.3.41.55: Maheśāna gave him his own Pāśupata missile, ever invincible by all, and spoke these words.
m.3.41.56: Śiva said: My own great missile has been given by me; you will be invincible. With it, achieve the task of conquering all your enemies.
m.3.41.57: I shall also tell Kṛṣṇa; he will give you help. He is indeed my very self, my devotee, who accomplishes my work.
m.3.41.58: Through my power, O Bhārata, make your kingdom free of thorns (enemies), and always, together with your brother, have the various kinds of dharma performed.
m.3.41.59: Nandīśvara said: Having said this and placed his own hand on his head, Śaṅkara, worshipped by Arjuna, quickly vanished.
m.3.41.60: Then Arjuna, delighted at heart, having obtained the missile and the boon from the Lord, went to his principal hermitage, remembering with devotion Śiva, his guru.
m.3.41.61: All his brothers were delighted, like bodies to which the life-breath has returned; meeting him, they attained happiness, and so did Draupadī of excellent vows.
m.3.41.62: All the Pāṇḍavas, hearing the whole account and that the supreme Śiva was pleased, were filled with joy and could not have enough of hearing it.
m.3.41.63: In the hermitage a shower of flowers mixed with sandal paste fell, for the welfare of those great-souled ones.
m.3.41.64: Joyfully bowing to the blessed Śaṅkara, Śiva, they rejoiced, knowing that the end of the term of exile had arrived and that victory would surely follow.
m.3.41.65: Meanwhile Kṛṣṇa, hearing that Arjuna had returned, came to meet him, and on hearing everything he was filled with happiness.
m.3.41.66: Therefore I have proclaimed Śaṅkara as the remover of all sorrows. He is constantly served by me; let him be served by you too.
m.3.41.67: Thus has the incarnation of Śaṅkara called Kirāta been told to you. Whoever hears it, or causes others to hear it, will attain all desires.
m.3.41.iti: Thus ends the forty-first adhyāya, named The incarnation as Kirāteśvara, in the third saṃhitā, the Śatarudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.3.42.1: Nandīśvara said: Hear, O sage, about the supreme incarnations of the all-pervading Lord, twelve in number, which have the form of jyotirliṅgas and bring manifold blessings.
m.3.42.2: Somanātha in Saurāṣṭra, Mallikārjuna on Śrīśaila, Mahākāla in Ujjayinī, and Amareśvara at Oṅkāra;
m.3.42.3: Kedāra on the ridge of the Himālaya, Bhīmaśaṅkara in Ḍākinī, Viśveśa in Vārāṇasī, and Tryambaka on the bank of the Gautamī;
m.3.42.4: Vaidyanātha at Citābhūmi, Nāgeśa in Dārukāvana, Rāmeśa at Setubandha, and Ghuśmeśa at Śivālaya.
m.3.42.5: This set of twelve incarnations of Śambhu, the Supreme Self, brings every joy to people through seeing and touching them, O sage.
m.3.42.6: Among them the first is Somanātha, who ended the Moon's suffering; through his worship, O sage, he destroys diseases such as consumption and leprosy.
m.3.42.7: Someśa, an incarnation of Śiva, abides in the form of a liṅga in Saurāṣṭra, an auspicious land, and was worshipped long ago by the Moon.
m.3.42.8: There too is the Candrakuṇḍa, which destroys all sins; a wise man who bathes there is freed from all diseases.
m.3.42.9: Having seen Someśvara, the great liṅga of Śiva, the very embodiment of the Supreme Self, one is freed from sin and obtains both enjoyment and liberation.
m.3.42.10: The second incarnation of Śaṅkara, named Mallikārjuna, is on Śrīgiri, dear one; he grants devotees the fruits they desire.
m.3.42.11: That Śiva, who went there from his own mountain with great love in order to see his son, O sage, is praised there in the form of a liṅga.
m.3.42.12: That second jyotirliṅga, O sage, through seeing and worshipping it, brings great happiness and at the end grants liberation; there is no doubt about this.
m.3.42.13: Dear one, the incarnation of Śaṅkara named Mahākāla arose in the city of Ujjayinī as the protector of his own people.
m.3.42.14: He who destroyed the demon named Dūṣaṇa, crusher of Vedic dharma, hater of brahmins, destroyer of all, who had come to Ujjayinī—
m.3.42.15: —meditated upon by the sons of the brahmin Vedapriya, he swiftly reduced to ashes with a mere huṃ that demon who dwelt on Ratnamāla.
m.3.42.16: Having slain him, that Mahākāla, entreated by the gods, remained in the form of a jyotirliṅga as the protector of his devotees.
m.3.42.17: Having seen and diligently worshipped the liṅga called Mahākāla, one attains all desires and afterwards gains the supreme goal.
m.3.42.18: Oṅkāra and Parameśāna, assumed by Śambhu the Supreme Self, is indeed the fourth incarnation, granting devotees the fruits they desire.
m.3.42.19: Installed with devotion according to rite, O sage, Mahādeva appeared from his own earthen liṅga, fulfilling the desire of Vindhya.
m.3.42.20: Entreated there by the gods, he abides in a twofold form; in the form of the liṅga, he who loves his devotees grants enjoyment and liberation.
m.3.42.21: In the praṇava form the excellent liṅga was named Oṅkāra, and the earthen one was named Parameśvara, O lord of sages.
m.3.42.22: Whichever of them is seen and worshipped, O sage, should be known to grant devotees their desires. Thus the two most divine jyotirliṅgas have been described to you, O great sage.
m.3.42.23: The fifth incarnation is Kedāreśa, the supreme Śiva; he abides at Kedāra in the form of a jyotirliṅga.
m.3.42.24: Entreated by the two incarnations of Hari named Nara and Nārāyaṇa, O sage, who dwelt there, Śiva stays at Kedāra on the snowy mountain.
m.3.42.25: Worshipped daily by those two and called Kedāreśvara, Śambhu grants devotees their desires through being seen and worshipped.
m.3.42.26: Though lord of all, he is especially the master of this region; that incarnation of Śiva, dear one, grants all desires.
m.3.42.27: The sixth incarnation of Śambhu, the great Lord, is called Bhīmaśaṅkara, of great sport, the destroyer of the demon Bhīma.
m.3.42.28: He protected his devotee Sudakṣiṇa, king and lord of Kāmarūpa, having slain that wondrous demon who tormented the devotees.
m.3.42.29: Entreated by him, Śaṅkara himself, named Bhīmaśaṅkara, abides in Ḍākinī in the form of a jyotirliṅga.
m.3.42.30: The seventh, the incarnation Viśveśvara, arose in Kāśī; he has the form of the entire cosmos and grants enjoyment and liberation, O sage.
m.3.42.31: He is always worshipped with devotion by all the gods led by Viṣṇu, and constantly also by the lord of Kailāsa and by Bhairava.
m.3.42.32: The Lord, giver of liberation, abides there in the form of a jyotirliṅga; being himself of self-accomplished nature, he dwells thus in his own city.
m.3.42.33: Those who, with devotion to Kāśī and Viśveśa, repeat their names remain ever untainted by actions and share in the state of liberation (kaivalya).
m.3.42.34: The incarnation called Tryambaka is the eighth, on the bank of the Gautamī; entreated by Gautama, this form of the moon-crested one manifested.
m.3.42.35: At Gautama's request, out of love and wishing to please that sage, he stays there immovably in the form of a jyotirliṅga.
m.3.42.36: Through seeing, touching, and worshipping that great Lord, all desires are fulfilled, and then, ah, liberation follows.
m.3.42.37: By Śiva's grace, the Gaṅgā, named Gautamī, purifying and dear to Śaṅkara, abides there out of love for Gautama.
m.3.42.38: The Vaidyanātha incarnation is declared the ninth among them; the Lord, performer of many sports, manifested for Rāvaṇa's sake.
m.3.42.39: Making a pretext of being carried by Rāvaṇa, Maheśvara established himself at Citābhūmi in the form of a jyotirliṅga.
m.3.42.40: He became famed in the three worlds by the name Vaidyanātheśvara; through being seen and worshipped with devotion, he indeed grants enjoyment and liberation.
m.3.42.41: O sage, this teaching on the greatness of Śiva as Vaidyanātheśvara grants worldly enjoyment and liberation to those who read it and also to those who hear it.
m.3.42.42: The Nāgeśvara incarnation is declared to be the tenth. He manifested for the sake of his devotees and always punishes the wicked.
m.3.42.43: Having slain the demon named Dāruka, the destroyer of dharma, he protected his devotee, the chief of merchants named Supriya.
m.3.42.44: For the benefit of the worlds, Śambhu, the Supreme, the performer of many sports, together with Ambikā, remained there assuming the form of a jyotirliṅga.
m.3.42.45: O sage, by seeing that Śiva-liṅga named Nāgeśvara and worshipping it, heaps of great sins are swiftly destroyed.
m.3.42.46: The Rāmeśvara incarnation is remembered as Śiva's eleventh; O sage, he did what was dear to Rāmacandra and was installed by Rāma.
m.3.42.47: Śaṅkara, affectionate to devotees, who, being well pleased, lovingly gave Rāma the boon of victory, manifested as the liṅga.
m.3.42.48: Earnestly entreated by Rāma, O sage, he remained at Setubandha in the form of a jyotirliṅga, worshipped by Rāma.
m.3.42.49: The glory of Rāmeśvara became wondrous and unequalled on earth; it grants enjoyment and liberation and always fulfils the desires of devotees.
m.3.42.50: The man who, with true devotion, bathes that Rāmeśvara with Gaṅgā water is indeed liberated while living.
m.3.42.51: Having enjoyed here all pleasures, even those hard for the gods to obtain, he then attains supreme knowledge and reaches kaivalya, liberation.
m.3.42.52: The Ghuśmeśvara incarnation is indeed Śaṅkara's twelfth; he performs various sports, gives joy to Ghuśmā, and is affectionate to devotees.
m.3.42.53: O sage, in the southern direction, near Devaśaila, the Lord who did what was dear to Ghuśmā manifested in a lake.
m.3.42.54: O sage, Śambhu, affectionate to devotees, pleased by her devotion, fully restored and protected Ghuśmā's son who had been killed by Sudehā.
m.3.42.55: Entreated by her, that Śambhu, the granter of desires, remained there in the lake in the form of a jyotirliṅga, named Ghuśmeśvara.
m.3.42.56: Having seen that Śiva-liṅga and worshipped it with devotion, one enjoys every happiness here and then attains liberation.
m.3.42.57: Thus I have narrated to you the divine series of jyotirliṅgas, twelve in number, which grants enjoyment and liberation.
m.3.42.58: Whoever reads or even hears this account of the jyotirliṅgas is freed from all sins and attains enjoyment and liberation.
m.3.42.59: And this saṃhitā named Śatarudra has been described by me; it celebrates the hundred incarnations and grants the fruit of all desires.
m.3.42.60: Whoever reads this daily, or listens to it with a concentrated mind, obtains all desires and then surely attains liberation.
m.3.42.iti: Thus ends the forty-second adhyāya, named The incarnations as the twelve jyotirliṅgas, in the dialogue of Sanatkumāra and Nandīśvara, in the third saṃhitā, the Śatarudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.4.1.1: Eternal salutation to that Radiance whose half-body is graced by the Daughter of the Mountain: who, though free from all change, takes on the form of the universe through his own māyā alone; whose two splendours of a compassionate side-glance are called heaven and liberation; and whom yogins always behold in the heart as the non-dual bliss of inner awareness.
m.4.1.2: May that indescribable Radiance bring about auspiciousness: whose glance is gentle with compassion, whose lotus-face is lovely with a smile, which shines with the digit of the moon, which has quelled the terrible threefold affliction, whose form is being-and-consciousness glowing with supreme bliss, and which is encircled by the arms of the Daughter of the Mountain.
m.4.1.3: The sages said: You have rightly told, O Sūta, out of a wish for the welfare of the worlds, the greatness of Śiva's incarnations, together with many narratives.
m.4.1.4: And again, dear one, please narrate with great affection the supreme greatness of Śiva connected with the liṅga. You are blessed, O best of Śaivas.
m.4.1.5: Listening from your lotus-mouth, O lord, we are not satiated. Let that delightful nectar of Śiva's glory be told once more.
m.4.1.6: The auspicious liṅgas that exist on earth at each and every tīrtha, or the famous ones that stand in other places,
m.4.1.7: all those divine liṅgas of the Supreme Lord, O disciple of Vyāsa, describe to us for the welfare of the worlds.
m.4.1.8: Sūta said: Well asked, O best of sages, for the welfare of the worlds. Out of affection for you, O twice-born ones, I shall tell of them briefly.
m.4.1.9: O sage, there is no counting all the Śiva-liṅgas. The whole earth is full of liṅgas; the whole world consists of liṅgas.
m.4.1.10: The tīrthas are endowed with liṅgas; everything is established in the liṅga. There is no count of them; I shall tell of a few of them.
m.4.1.11: Whatever visible thing is seen, whatever is described or remembered, all that is indeed the form of Śiva; there is nothing else whatsoever.
m.4.1.12: Nevertheless, listen with love: I shall tell, as I have heard, O best of sages, of those liṅgas that are on the earth.
m.4.1.13: They exist in Pātāla, in heaven, and likewise on earth. Everywhere Śambhu is worshipped by gods, asuras and humans.
m.4.1.14: The three worlds, with their gods, asuras and humans, are pervaded by Śambhu in the form of the liṅga, for the grace of the worlds, O most excellent ones.
m.4.1.15: For the grace of the worlds, Maheśvara assumes various liṅgas here, at tīrthas and likewise in other places.
m.4.1.16: Wherever and whenever Śambhu was remembered with devotion by his devotees, there he descended, accomplished the task, and then remained.
m.4.1.17: For the benefit of the worlds he also established his own liṅga. By worshipping that liṅga one attains perfection.
m.4.1.18: There is no count of the liṅgas on earth; nevertheless, O twice-born ones, the principal ones are being told by me.
m.4.1.19: Among the principal ones, I shall declare here those that are foremost, hearing which a person is freed from all sins in an instant.
m.4.1.20: The jyotirliṅgas here, which are the most foremost of all, O excellent one, I shall tell today; hearing of them one dispels sin.
m.4.1.21: Somanātha in Saurāṣṭra, Mallikārjuna on Śrīśaila, Mahākāla in Ujjayinī, Parameśvara at Oṅkāra,
m.4.1.22: Kedāra on the slope of the Himālaya, Bhīmaśaṅkara in Ḍākinī, Viśveśa in Vārāṇasī, Tryambaka on the bank of the Gautamī,
m.4.1.23: Vaidyanātha in Citābhūmi, Nāgeśa in the Dārukā forest, Rāmeśa at Setubandha, and Ghuśmeśa at Śivālaya.
m.4.1.24: Whoever, rising at dawn, recites these twelve names is freed from all sins and obtains the fruit of all accomplishments.
m.4.1.25: Whatever desire the best of men recite them with in view, that very desire they will obtain, here and in the hereafter, O lords of sages.
m.4.1.26: Those of pure intent who recite them without desire will never again dwell in a mother's womb.
m.4.1.27: Through the worship of these alone, the sorrows of all the varṇas are destroyed; in this world and the next, liberation certainly comes about.
m.4.1.28: Their food-offering should be accepted and eaten with care; all the sins of the one who does so are reduced to ashes in an instant.
m.4.1.29: The fruit of the jyotirliṅgas, O twice-born ones, cannot be fully described in detail even by Brahmā and the others, nor likewise by anyone else.
m.4.1.30: For one by whom even one of them has been worshipped without interruption for six months, the suffering arising from birth in a mother's womb will not occur.
m.4.1.31: If one born in a low birth sees a jyotirliṅga, his next birth will be in a pure and noble family.
m.4.1.32: Having obtained birth in a noble family, wealthy and a master of the Vedas, he then performs auspicious deeds and attains imperishable liberation.
m.4.1.33: Whether a mleccha, an outcaste, or a eunuch, O lords of sages, he becomes twice-born and is liberated; therefore one should undertake the sight of it.
m.4.1.34: I have told a little of the fruit of the jyotirliṅgas. Now hear of the upaliṅgas of the jyotirliṅgas, O best of sages.
m.4.1.35: The liṅga arising from Someśvara is declared to be Antakeśa; at the confluence of the Mahī with the sea, that liṅga is the upaliṅga.
m.4.1.36: The upaliṅga arising from Mallikārjuna is declared to be the one famed as Rudreśvara, at Bhṛgukakṣa, bestowing happiness.
m.4.1.37: The liṅga born of Mahākāla is renowned as Dugdheśa; it is famous on the Narmadā and is held to remove all sins.
m.4.1.38: The liṅga born of Oṃkāra is known as Kardameśa; famous at Bindusaras, it grants the fruit of all desires.
m.4.1.39: Born of Kedāreśvara is Bhūteśa on the bank of the Yamunā, declared to remove great sins for those who see and likewise worship it.
m.4.1.40: Arising from Bhīmaśaṅkara is the one known as Bhīmeśvara; famous on the Sahya mountain, it greatly increases strength.
m.4.1.41: That upaliṅga which arose from Viśveśvara is renowned as Śaraṇyeśvara; and that which is declared as arising from Tryambaka is known as Siddheśvara.
m.4.1.42: That which arose from Vaidyanātha is remembered as Vaijanātha; that which sprang from Nāgeśvara is called Bhūteśvara.
m.4.1.43: It stands on the bank of the Mallikā-Sarasvatī and removes sin by being seen. And that which arose from Rāmeśvara is remembered as Gupteśvara.
m.4.1.44: And that which arose from Ghuśmeśa is remembered as Vyāghreśvara. Thus the upaliṅgas of the jyotirliṅgas have been declared here by me, O brāhmaṇas.
m.4.1.45: They remove sins by being seen and grant all desires. These are the most eminent and have indeed attained pre-eminence; now let other principal ones also be heard, O best of sages.
m.4.1.iti: Thus ends the first adhyāya, named The greatness of the jyotirliṅgas and their upaliṅgas, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.4.2.1: Sūta said: On the bank of the Gaṅgā, the renowned Kāśī indeed grants liberation. It should be known as made up of liṅgas, and it is remembered as Śiva's dwelling-place.
m.4.2.2: There itself the chief liṅga is declared to be Avimuktaka; Kṛttivāseśvara is Śiva directly, and equal to it is Vṛddhakālaka.
m.4.2.3: And Tilabhāṇḍeśvara, and Daśāśvamedha too; at the confluence of the Gaṅgā with the ocean, the liṅga is remembered as Saṅgameśa.
m.4.2.4: The one declared as Bhūteśvara always grants every aim to devotees. The one famed as Nārīśvara is near the Kauśikī.
m.4.2.5: On the bank of the Gaṇḍakī stands Baṭukeśvara. Famed as Pūreśvara, a liṅga on the bank of the Phalgu grants happiness.
m.4.2.6: And Siddhanātheśvara, who by being seen grants success to men; and likewise the one famed as Dūreśvara in the northern town.
m.4.2.7: And one named Śṛṅgeśvara, and likewise Vaidyanātha; and the one famed as Japyeśvara, which is at the battle-site of Dadhīci.
m.4.2.8: Gopeśvara is well known, another is remembered as Raṅgeśvara; also Vāmeśvara, Nāgeśa, Kāmeśa and Vimaleśvara.
m.4.2.9: Vyāseśvara is famed, and Sukeśa likewise; Bhāṇḍeśvara is famed, and Huṅkāreśa likewise.
m.4.2.10: Surocana is famed, and Bhūteśvara itself; likewise Saṅgameśa is declared, the destroyer of great sins.
m.4.2.11: Then on the bank of the Taptakā is Kumāreśvara; Siddheśvara is famed, and Seneśa is likewise remembered.
m.4.2.12: One is declared as Rāmeśvara, and Kumbheśa is held to be supreme; also Nandīśvara and Puñjeśa, and likewise Pūrṇaka on the Pūrṇā.
m.4.2.13: And at Prayāga is Brahmeśvara, installed long ago by Brahmā at the Daśāśvamedha tīrtha, granting the fruit of the four aims of life.
m.4.2.14: Likewise there is Someśvara, who wards off all calamities, and Bhāradvājeśvara, who increases brahmic splendour.
m.4.2.15: Śūlaṭaṅkeśvara is declared to be directly the granter of desires, and right there Mādhaveśa, who effects the protection of devotees.
m.4.2.16: The one called Nāgeśa is famous in the city of Sāketa, O brāhmaṇas; he grants happiness especially to those born in the Solar dynasty.
m.4.2.17: In the city of Puruṣottama is Bhuvaneśa, granting great success, and Lokeśa, a great liṅga bestowing all bliss.
m.4.2.18: Kāmeśvara, the liṅga of Śambhu; Gaṅgeśa, who brings supreme purity; and Śukreśvara, established by Śukra out of desire for the welfare of the worlds.
m.4.2.19: Likewise Vaṭeśvara is famed, granting the fruit of all desires; on the bank of the Sindhu is Kapāleśa, and Vaktreśa, destroyer of all sins.
m.4.2.20: Dhautapāpeśvara is directly the Supreme Lord present by a portion; others are declared as Bhīmeśvara and remembered as Sūryeśvara.
m.4.2.21: Nandīśvara should be known as the giver of knowledge, worshipped by the world; Nākeśvara is greatly meritorious, and likewise Rāmeśvara is remembered.
m.4.2.22: One named Vimaleśvara, and Kaṇṭakeśvara; and likewise, at the confluence with the eastern ocean, Dhartukeśa.
m.4.2.23: Candreśvara should be known as granting the fruit of moon-like radiance; and the granter of all desires is remembered as Siddheśvara.
m.4.2.24: Bilveśvara is famed, and likewise Andhakeśa, where the demon Andhaka was slain long ago by Śaṅkara.
m.4.2.25: Śambhu, having taken on this form by a portion, remained there again; famed as Śaraṇeśvara, he always grants happiness to the worlds.
m.4.2.26: Kardameśa is declared supreme, and Koṭīśa is on Mount Arbuda; Acaleśa is famed, always granting happiness to the worlds.
m.4.2.27: Nāgeśvara abides perpetually on the bank of the Kauśikī; and the one called Anantēśvara is a vessel of welfare and auspiciousness.
m.4.2.28: Yogeśvara is famed, and likewise Vaidyanātheśvara; Koṭīśvara should be known, and one is remembered as Sapteśvara.
m.4.2.29: Bhadreśvara is famed — Hara himself, named Bhadra; likewise Caṇḍīśvara is declared, and Saṅgameśvara too.
m.4.2.30: The Śiva-liṅgas that arose in the eastern direction, and others too that are ordinary — these have been told to you here.
m.4.2.31: Likewise, the Śiva-liṅgas that arose in the southern direction, O best of sages — those I shall now tell you.
m.4.2.iti: Thus ends the second adhyāya, named The greatness of the Śiva-liṅga, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.4.3.1: Sūta said: In Brahmapurī at Citrakūṭa there is the liṅga called Mattagajendraka, installed long ago by Brahmā, which grants the fulfilment of all desires.
m.4.3.2: To its east is the liṅga Koṭīśa, bestower of all boons; to the west of the Godāvarī is the liṅga named Paśupati.
m.4.3.3: In the southern direction there is one called Atrīśvara, the god himself, for the benefit of the worlds and for the happiness of Anasūyā—
m.4.3.4: the god manifested himself and, during a drought, kept beings alive. He is indeed Śaṅkara himself, directly, present by a portion of himself.
m.4.3.5: The sages said: O Sūta, O Sūta, most fortunate one, how did Hara, supreme and divine, arise as Atrīśvara? Tell us the truth, O you of good vows.
m.4.3.6: Sūta said: Well asked, O best of sages. I shall tell the auspicious story, by constantly hearing which one is surely freed from sins.
m.4.3.7: In the southern direction, near Citrakūṭa, there is a great forest named Kāmada, beneficial for the austerities of the virtuous.
m.4.3.8: There Brahmā's son, the sage named Atri himself, accompanied by Anasūyā, performed extremely severe austerity.
m.4.3.9: Once, long ago, in that very place, O sage, by fate there occurred a terrible drought lasting a hundred years, bringing misery to living beings.
m.4.3.10: Then all the trees dried up, and the leaves and fruits too; nowhere was water seen for daily needs, O lords of sages.
m.4.3.11: No moisture could be found; harsh winds blew in the ten directions; a great and very painful cry of woe arose on earth.
m.4.3.12: Seeing the destruction of beings, Atri's beloved wife, the virtuous one, said to Atri: I cannot bear this suffering.
m.4.3.13: Then the best of sages, seated himself on his seat, having performed breath-control three times, became absorbed in samādhi.
m.4.3.14: He, Atri, the wise and foremost sage, meditated by his self upon the supreme light abiding in the self—Śaṅkara, the changeless.
m.4.3.15: While the master was absorbed in meditation, his disciples went far away; lacking food, they then abandoned their own guru, the sage.
m.4.3.16: Then that devoted wife Anasūyā was left alone, and she constantly served that best of sages with joy.
m.4.3.17: Having made a beautiful earthen liṅga with mantra according to the rules, she worshipped Śaṅkara, also with mental offerings.
m.4.3.18: She praised Śaṅkara with devotion, having served him again and again; with palms joined, having circumambulated her lord Śiva,
m.4.3.19: then Anasūyā, of good conduct, the sage's beloved, made the return circuit with prostrations like a staff.
m.4.3.20: All the Daityas and Dānavas, seeing the beautiful woman then, became agitated there and stayed far off because of her radiance.
m.4.3.21: Just as creatures keep far away on seeing fire, so, seeing her then, they did not come near here.
m.4.3.22: O foremost of brāhmaṇas, Anasūyā's service to Śiva, refined by mind, speech and body, surpassed even Atri's austerity.
m.4.3.23: For as long as the best of sages was intent on breath-control, for that long the lady performed her service.
m.4.3.24: That couple then remained there, each intent on his or her own task, O tiger among sages; no one else stayed there.
m.4.3.25: As time passed thus, Atri, the best of seers, absorbed in supreme meditation, was aware of nothing at all.
m.4.3.26: Anasūyā too, that virtuous woman, worshipped her husband and likewise Śiva; that chaste one knew nothing else higher.
m.4.3.27: Through his austerity and her worship, all the gods and seers, and likewise the rivers headed by the Gaṅgā,
m.4.3.28: all came together with great affection to see the two; and seeing that austerity and service, they were filled with supreme wonder.
m.4.3.29: Seeing that marvel of the two, they declared worship to be superior: Of the two, which is more excellent—austerity or worship?
m.4.3.30: Having observed all of it in both—what is called Atri's austerity and Anasūyā's devoted service—they declared worship to be superior.
m.4.3.31: Difficult austerity was performed by earlier seers too, but where has anyone ever done such as this? Thus they said.
m.4.3.32: Blessed is this sage, and blessed likewise is this Anasūyā, since by these two such excellent austerity is performed again with supreme love.
m.4.3.33: Who in the three worlds now performs such auspicious, difficult and excellent austerity as this? None is known.
m.4.3.34: Having praised the two, they all then went back as they had come—except Gaṅgā and Giriśa Śiva.
m.4.3.35: Gaṅgā, the virtuous one, pleased by her devotion to me and captivated by her dharma, said: Having done her a favour, I shall go.
m.4.3.36: Śiva too, bound by the meditation of the sage Atri, O lords of sages, remained there with his full portion and did not go to Kailāsa.
m.4.3.37: Thus fifty-four years had passed here, O best of seers, and still no rain fell then.
m.4.3.38: As long as Atri thus remained in meditation through austerity, Anasūyā then made the resolve: I will not take anything.
m.4.3.39: While this was being done, with the sage remaining in austerity, hear now what happened in the course of Anasūyā's excellent worship.
m.4.3.iti: Thus ends the third adhyāya, named The austerity of Anasūyā and Atri, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.4.4.1: Sūta said: Once that best of sages, Atri, foremost among the knowers of Brahman, on waking said to his beloved: Give me water.
m.4.4.2: She too, the virtuous one, taking the water-pot without fail, went into the forest there thinking: From where can water be brought by me?
m.4.4.3: What shall I do? Where shall I go? From where indeed can water be brought? Overcome with bewilderment thus, she saw that Gaṅgā.
m.4.4.4: As she was following her, Gaṅgā—the goddess, best of rivers, bearing a beautiful form—then spoke to her:
m.4.4.5: Gaṅgā said: I am pleased with you, O lady. Tell me now, where are you going? You are blessed, O fortunate one; truly I will carry out your command.
m.4.4.6: Sūta said: Hearing those words then, the ascetic wife of the sage, herself much astonished, replied lovingly, O Brahmins:
m.4.4.7: Anasūyā said: Who are you, O lotus-petal-eyed one, and from where have you come? Be kind and tell me the truth; so said the virtuous, well-spoken, chaste lady.
m.4.4.8: Sūta said: When the sage's wife had spoken thus there, O lords of sages, Gaṅgā, best of rivers, of divine form, then spoke these words:
m.4.4.9: Gaṅgā said: Having seen your service to your husband and to Śiva, the Supreme Self, and having seen your righteousness, O virtuous one, I have stayed near you.
m.4.4.10: I am Gaṅgā, come here because of your devotion, O sweetly smiling one. I have become subject to you; choose whatever you desire.
m.4.4.11: Sūta said: When Gaṅgā had said this, the virtuous lady bowed, stood before her and said: If you are pleased with me now, give me water.
m.4.4.12: Hearing these words, she Gaṅgā said: Make a pit. Anasūyā quickly came, made it, and stood there in that very moment.
m.4.4.13: She Gaṅgā entered there and then took the form of water. Filled with the greatest wonder, she Anasūyā took up the water.
m.4.4.14: Anasūyā, the sage's wife, then spoke these words to the divine-formed best of rivers, for the happiness of the worlds:
m.4.4.15: Anasūyā said: If you are well pleased with me and have compassion for me, you should stay here until my husband comes.
m.4.4.16: Sūta said: Hearing these words of Anasūyā, which bring joy to the good, Gaṅgā said: I am greatly pleased; I will stay if you give me the merit of your service to Atri, O sinless one.
m.4.4.17: When she Gaṅgā had said this there, she Anasūyā did accordingly; giving that divine water to her husband, she stood before him.
m.4.4.18: The sage, too, with great delight, having duly sipped water for purification according to rule, drank that divine water, and having drunk it attained bliss.
m.4.4.19: Ah! This is not the water that is drunk every day. Reflecting thus, he quickly looked all around.
m.4.4.20: Seeing the trees withered and the quarters very parched, the best of sages said to her: Has rain not fallen again?
m.4.4.21: Hearing what he said, she answered, no, no. Then he again said to his beloved: From where was the water brought by you?
m.4.4.22: When he said this, Anasūyā fell into great bewilderment and became anxious in her mind, O lords of sages.
m.4.4.23: If I tell it, there will be self-exaltation on my part; if I do not tell it, there will be a breach of my vow.
m.4.4.24: It should be told by me in such a way that neither fault arises. While she was reflecting thus, she was asked again and again.
m.4.4.25: Then the devoted wife, having gained understanding through the grace of Śambhu, said: Listen, my lord; I shall tell you what happened.
m.4.4.26: Anasūyā said: By the might of Śaṅkara and by your own good deeds, Gaṅgā has come right here; this water is hers.
m.4.4.27: Sūta said: Hearing these words then, the sage, his mind filled with wonder, spoke lovingly to his beloved, remembering Śaṅkara in his mind:
m.4.4.28: Atri said: O beloved, beautiful one, do you speak the truth or false words? Even if you speak truly, I do not believe it, for this is rare indeed.
m.4.4.29: O auspicious one, how has that come about today which is always impossible even for yogins and gods? My astonishment is supreme.
m.4.4.30: If it is seen to be so, then I will believe it, not otherwise. Hearing these words, his beloved replied to her husband:
m.4.4.31: Anasūyā said: Come with me, O lord, great sage, if you wish to see Gaṅgā, the best of rivers.
m.4.4.32: Sūta said: Having said this, the devoted wife took her husband along and, remembering Śiva, went quickly to where Gaṅgā, the best of rivers, was.
m.4.4.33: There the devoted wife showed her husband that Gaṅgā, abiding in the pit, herself of divine form.
m.4.4.34: Having gone there and seen the beautiful pit filled with water up to the brim, the best of sages said: Blessed is she!
m.4.4.35: What is my penance compared to this, and what then of others' penance? Having said this, the tiger among sages then praised her with devotion.
m.4.4.36: Then the sage bathed well there in the blessed water, sipped it for purification, and again and again offered praise there.
m.4.4.37: Anasūyā too then bathed in that beautiful water. The sage performed his daily rites, and so did Anasūyā, firm in her vows.
m.4.4.38: Then Gaṅgā said to her: I am going to my own place. When this was said, the virtuous lady again spoke to the best of rivers:
m.4.4.39: Anasūyā said: O sovereign goddess, if you are pleased and if you have compassion for me, you should remain steadfastly in this penance-grove, O goddess.
m.4.4.40: It is the nature of the great that, having accepted someone, they do not abandon them. Having said this, she joined her palms and praised her again and again.
m.4.4.41: The sage too spoke likewise: You must stay here, O best of rivers. Be favourable, O goddess, and make us feel protected.
m.4.4.42: Hearing those pleasing words of his, Gaṅgā, the best of rivers, with a gladdened mind, spoke these words to Anasūyā.
m.4.4.43: Gaṅgā said: If you give me the fruit arising from one year's worship of Śaṅkara and of service to your husband, then I shall stay, for the sake of helping the gods.
m.4.4.44: I am not so pleased by gifts, nor by baths at sacred places, nor by sacrifices or yogic practices, as by a wife's devotion to her husband.
m.4.4.45: The delight of mind that arises from seeing a chaste, devoted wife does not come from any other means. I have spoken the truth, O virtuous lady.
m.4.4.46: By seeing a woman devoted to her husband, my sins are destroyed. A devoted wife becomes especially pure, equal to Gaurī.
m.4.4.47: Therefore, if you give that merit for the welfare of the world, then I shall become steadfast here, if you desire its well-being.
m.4.4.48: Sūta said: Hearing these words, that devoted wife Anasūyā gave to Gaṅgā all the merit born of that year.
m.4.4.49: For it is the nature of the great to bring about the welfare of others; gold, sandalwood and sugarcane juice are examples of this.
m.4.4.50: Seeing this great act of wifely devotion by Anasūyā, Mahādeva was pleased and swiftly manifested from the earthen liṅga.
m.4.4.51: Śambhu said: Seeing this deed of yours, O virtuous one, I am pleased, O devoted wife. Ask a boon of me, dear one, for you are most dear to me.
m.4.4.52: Then that couple, beholding Śambhu Hara of beautiful form, endowed with five faces and other features, became greatly astonished.
m.4.4.53: Bowing, praising, joining their palms, filled with great devotion, the two worshipped Śaṅkara, the benefactor of the worlds, and spoke.
m.4.4.54: The couple said: If you are pleased, O Lord of the gods, and the Mother of the universe is pleased, stay in this penance-grove and be the giver of happiness to the worlds.
m.4.4.55: Then Gaṅgā was pleased, and Śiva too was pleased; and both of them remained there where the best of sages was.
m.4.4.56: The Lord, remover of others' sorrow, became known by the name Atrīśvara; and Gaṅgā too then remained there in a pit, by her divine power (māyā).
m.4.4.57: From that day onward there has always been inexhaustible water there; in that pit, a mere hand's span in size, Gaṅgā became the Mandākinī.
m.4.4.58: To that very place the divine sages came together with their wives — all those twice-born who had earlier departed, coming back from one holy place after another.
m.4.4.59: Barley and rice grew again; and those people, devoted to sacrifices and rites, joined with those excellent sages, performed oblations (homa).
m.4.4.60: Satisfied by those rites, the clouds then sent rain, and supreme joy arose in the world, O lords of sages.
m.4.4.61: Thus has the glory of Atrīśvara been told to you, bringing happiness, granting enjoyment and liberation, fulfilling all desires and increasing devotion.
m.4.4.iti: Thus ends the fourth adhyāya, named The greatness of Atrīśvara, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.4.5.1: Sūta said: On the divine mountain Kālañjara dwells Nīlakaṇṭha, the Great Lord, ever in the form of a liṅga and ever granting bliss to his devotees.
m.4.5.2: His greatness is divine, proclaimed in Śruti and Smṛti. There is a tīrtha there by that name; bathing in it destroys sins.
m.4.5.3: O you of good vows, the Śiva-liṅgas that exist on the bank of the Revā, bestowing all happiness here—their number is not known.
m.4.5.4: And she the Revā is indeed of the very form of Rudra, removing sin by mere sight; whatever stones lie in her are of Śiva's form.
m.4.5.5: Even so, O lords of sages, I shall tell of other principal Śiva-liṅgas, which grant both enjoyment and liberation.
m.4.5.6: There is one well named Ārteśvara, remover of sin; one renowned as Parameśvara; and one remembered as Siṃheśvara.
m.4.5.7: Likewise here are Śarmeśa and Kumāreśvara, the renowned Puṇḍarīkeśvara, and Maṇḍapeśvara.
m.4.5.8: There was one named Tīkṣṇeśa, removing sin by sight; and on the bank of the Narmadā one named Dhundhureśvara, destroyer of sin.
m.4.5.9: One is renowned as Śūleśvara, likewise Kumbheśvara is remembered; one named Kubereśvara, and likewise Someśvara is remembered.
m.4.5.10: Nīlakaṇṭha, Maṅgaleśa, the great Maṅgalāyatana, and the god Mahākapīśvara, who was installed by Hanumān.
m.4.5.11: Then there is the god Nandika, who wards off the sin of crores of killings, and is proclaimed the giver of all desires and aims, and the giver of liberation.
m.4.5.12: Whoever worships Nandīkeśa daily with supreme joy—all success will be his; there is no doubt.
m.4.5.13: O best of sages, whoever bathes in the Revā there at that bank—his desires are fulfilled and all his sin perishes.
m.4.5.14: The sages said: How did such greatness of his arise there, O great-minded one? By the grace of Nandikeśa, may it now be told by you.
m.4.5.15: Sūta said: You have asked well; I shall tell it as I heard it. O Śaunaka and the other sages, all of you listen attentively.
m.4.5.16: Formerly the best of sages was asked in this way by Yudhiṣṭhira; as he spoke, so I tell it, in keeping with my affection for you.
m.4.5.17: On the western bank of the Revā there shines a city named Karṇikī, rich in great beauty and crowded with people of the four varṇas.
m.4.5.18: There a certain excellent brahmin, born in the lineage of Utathya, went to Kāśī after entrusting his wife to his two sons.
m.4.5.19: That brahmin died right there, and the two sons then heard of it; the two young sons performed his funeral rites.
m.4.5.20: And the wife, wishing her sons' welfare, raised the two sons; and, keeping aside a little, she divided the wealth.
m.4.5.21: A little wealth was kept as her own for the sake of the rites at her death. Then, after some time had passed, that brahmin's wife—
m.4.5.22: —once, when on the point of death, she performed various meritorious acts; yet, O brahmins, by the working of fate that brahmin's wife did not die.
m.4.5.23: When their mother, by fate, did not give up her life-breaths, the two sons, seeing that suffering of their mother, then spoke.
m.4.5.24: The two sons said: What is lacking, mother, that there is such great suffering? Express it quickly and gladly; then we two shall do it.
m.4.5.25: Sūta said: Hearing that, she said there: Much is lacking for me; if that indeed is done, death would come easily.
m.4.5.26: Her eldest son said: Let it be told by you; I shall do it. Then it was told by her.
m.4.5.27: The brahmin's wife said: Listen lovingly to my words, son. Formerly I had a heartfelt wish to go to Kāśī; it did not come about, and now I am dying.
m.4.5.28: My bones, son, must be cast by you diligently into the water of the Gaṅgā; then good will come to you today, no doubt.
m.4.5.29: Sūta said: When the mother had spoken thus, that eldest son, devoted to his mother, spoke to his mother of good vows, who was facing death.
m.4.5.30: The son said: Mother, you may give up your life-breaths in peace, no doubt. Having first done your task, afterwards I shall do my own.
m.4.5.31: Having thus placed water in her hand as a pledge, no sooner had the son gone into the house than she died there, intent on remembering Hara.
m.4.5.32: Having arranged all the rites due to her, and having performed the monthly ceremony, he set out to go.
m.4.5.33: The elder of the two, known by the name Suvāda, taking her bones, went forth with the wish to reach the tīrtha.
m.4.5.34: Taking along a certain servant and accompanied by him, he then consoled his wife and sons, wishing to do what was dear to his mother.
m.4.5.35: Having performed the śrāddha, gifts and the like, the feeding of brahmins, and the excellent rite, and having made auspicious invocations, the brahmin departed from his house.
m.4.5.36: That day, having travelled twenty yojanas, when the sun had set he stayed in a pleasant village, in the house of a certain brahmin.
m.4.5.37: That brahmin performed the sandhyā and other good rites according to rule, and there he offered hymns and the like to Śambhu of wondrous deeds.
m.4.5.38: Then the brahmin remained there with his servant, and two muhūrtas of the night passed there.
m.4.5.39: Meanwhile a wonder occurred there. Listen to it attentively, O sages; I shall tell it to you.
m.4.5.iti: Thus ends the fifth adhyāya, named The death of the brahmin woman, in the Nandikeśvara Māhātmya, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.4.6.1: Sūta said: And there was one auspicious cow tied up there in the courtyard. Just then, at night, the brahmin householder, who had gone out, came home.
m.4.6.2: Seeing the cow standing unmilked in the courtyard, he, wearied with vexation and wishing to milk her, spoke to his own wife, O lords of sages.
m.4.6.3: Dear, the cow has not been milked by you. Told thus, she brought the calf; then, having very quickly called the woman for the milking, ...
m.4.6.4: then that brahmin, the master of the house, eager for milk, himself made an effort to tie the calf to the peg, O sages.
m.4.6.5: The calf, pulling away, struck him on the foot, and the brahmin suffered pain, O you of good vows.
m.4.6.6: Because of that blow to his foot, the twice-born, stupefied with anger, then beat the calf very hard with blows.
m.4.6.7: The calf, hurt by him, then became exhausted. The cow was milked, but out of anger the twice-born did not release the calf.
m.4.6.8: The cow, who had given herself to be milked with great affection, then wept; and seeing her weeping, the calf then spoke these words.
m.4.6.9: The calf said: Why are you weeping, mother? What sorrow has come upon you? Tell me that, out of love. Hearing that, the cow spoke.
m.4.6.10: Hear my sorrow, son—indeed I cannot even speak it. You were beaten by that wicked one, and by that sorrow came to me as well.
m.4.6.11: Sūta said: Hearing his mother's words, that calf enlightened her; firmly grounded in the truth of prārabdha karma, he replied to his mother.
m.4.6.12: What is to be done? Where is one to go? For we are bound by karma. As deeds were done before, so they are experienced now.
m.4.6.13: A deed is done laughing; it is reaped weeping. There is no one who gives sorrow, and no one who gives happiness.
m.4.6.14: Joy and sorrow are given by another—this is held to be wrong understanding. I myself am the doer here—that too is called false knowledge.
m.4.6.15: Sorrow comes from one's own karma, and happiness from that same karma. Therefore karma is revered; everything rests in karma.
m.4.6.16: You and I, mother, and these living beings and the rest—all are bound by karma; they should never be grieved over by you.
m.4.6.17: Sūta said: Having heard thus her son's words full of wisdom, the cow, wretched and filled with grief for her son, said this.
m.4.6.18: The cow said: Child, you know everything—that creatures are subject to karma. Yet, seized by māyā, I fall into sorrow again.
m.4.6.19: Much weeping has been done, yet no relief from sorrow comes. Hearing these words, the calf said this to his mother.
m.4.6.20: The calf said: If you understand this, why weep again? Is anything achieved by doing so? Therefore give up your sorrow now.
m.4.6.21: Sūta said: Hearing her son's words thus, his mother, the cow, full of sorrow, then sighed deeply and spoke words to the calf.
m.4.6.22: The cow said: My sorrow will go only when a like sorrow befalls the brahmin too; I tell you this truly.
m.4.6.23: In the morning, son, he will be struck by me with my two horns, and once struck, his life will depart at once—there is no doubt.
m.4.6.24: The calf said: The fruit of the karma done earlier is being reaped now. And what fruit, mother, will you obtain from this killing of a brahmin?
m.4.6.25: Through merit and sin in equal measure, birth occurs in Bhārata; and when both are exhausted by experiencing their fruits, mother, liberation is attained.
m.4.6.26: Sometimes karma is destroyed, sometimes its experiencing arises. Therefore do not again set yourself to do such a deed.
m.4.6.27: How am I your son today, and how indeed are you my mother? The pride in sonship and motherhood is vain—let this be considered.
m.4.6.28: Know this: where is a mother, where a father, where a husband, where a wife? No one here belongs to anyone; all reap the fruits of their own deeds.
m.4.6.29: Knowing this, mother, you should give up sorrow with great effort, and practise virtuous conduct out of desire for happiness in the other world.
m.4.6.30: The cow said: I know this, son, but this māyā does not leave me. I shall give him a sorrow equal to your sorrow; that indeed I shall do.
m.4.6.31: And moreover, I have seen the place here where the sin of brahmin-slaying is destroyed; so my sin of killing will surely go away.
m.4.6.32: Sūta said: Hearing these words of his mother, the cow, O best of the twice-born, the calf fell silent there; nothing more was said by him.
m.4.6.33: Hearing that wondrous exchange between the two, the travelling brahmin then pondered in his heart, astonished, O lords of sages.
m.4.6.34: Only after seeing this most wondrous event in the morning should I go; and then from here I must go on to that place.
m.4.6.35: Sūta said: Having thus reflected in his heart, O twice-born ones, that brahmin, devoted to his mother and supremely amazed, slept there together with his servant.
m.4.6.36: Then, when morning came, the master of the house rose, woke that traveller, and said these words.
m.4.6.37: The brahmin said: Why are you still sleeping? It is fully morning. Set out on your journey to the country where you wish to go.
m.4.6.38: He replied: Listen, brahmin: there is pain in my servant's body. We will stay a little while and then go.
m.4.6.39: Sūta said: Having made this pretext, the man then slept on, in order to learn the whole of that wondrous, astonishing affair.
m.4.6.40: Then, at milking time, the brahmin, wishing to go somewhere on business, spoke to his own son.
m.4.6.41: The father said: Son, I am going off again somewhere on some business. Dear child, you must milk this cow of ours carefully.
m.4.6.42: Sūta said: Having said this, that excellent brahmin went off somewhere. The son then got up there and released the calf.
m.4.6.43: His mother herself then came for the milking. Then the brahmin's son, the calf—distressed, being struck with a peg—
m.4.6.44: —led to the cow's side to tie it up, eager for the milk. Then the cow, enraged, struck him with her horn.
m.4.6.45: Struck in a vital spot, he fell down unconscious. People gathered there saying, the boy has been gored by the cow.
m.4.6.46: Crying, water, water, they ran to where his father and others were. While efforts were being made, the boy died then.
m.4.6.47: When the boy died there, a great cry of lament arose. His mother was stricken with grief and wept again and again.
m.4.6.48: What shall I do? Where shall I go? Who can take away my sorrow? Weeping thus, she then beat the cow and let it loose.
m.4.6.49: That cow, white in colour, was then at once seen to have turned dark. Oh, look! the people cried out to one another.
m.4.6.50: Then the travelling brahmin, having seen this wonder, set out; wherever the cow went, there the brahmin followed her.
m.4.6.51: Raising her tail, the cow quickly ran toward the Narmadā, and coming near this Nandika tīrtha, into the Narmadā's water—
m.4.6.52: —having plunged in three times, she became white. She went back the way she came, and the brahmin was filled with amazement.
m.4.6.53: Oh, this is a most blessed tīrtha, removing the sin of slaying a brahmin! The brahmin himself bathed there, and likewise his servant.
m.4.6.54: Having bathed, the two went on, praising that river. On the way a certain beautiful woman, adorned with ornaments, met them.
m.4.6.55: She said to him: O traveller, from where are you going, so greatly astonished? Abandon deceit and tell the truth before me, O best of brahmins.
m.4.6.56: Sūta said: Hearing these words, the brahmin told everything exactly as it was. Then the woman again said to the brahmin there, stay here.
m.4.6.57: Hearing what she said, the brahmin stopped, and humble-minded he replied: What is it to be told? Speak.
m.4.6.58: She said: Here, at the very spot you saw, cast your mother's bones now. Why go elsewhere?
m.4.6.59: Your mother, O best of travellers, assuming a truly excellent divine body, will quickly attain the blessed state of Śambhu himself.
m.4.6.60: When the month of Vaiśākha arrives, on the auspicious seventh day of the bright fortnight, Gaṅgā always comes here, O best of brahmins.
m.4.6.61: Today itself is that seventh day. I am Gaṅgā, and I am going there. Having said this, the goddess Gaṅgā vanished, O best of sages.
m.4.6.62: The brahmin turned back, and as soon as he cast half of his mother's bones from his cloth into that tīrtha, a marvel took place.
m.4.6.63: His own mother was seen, having attained a divine body: You are blessed, you have fulfilled your duty, and the family has been purified by you.
m.4.6.64: May your wealth, grain, lifespan and lineage increase. Having repeatedly given this blessing to her son, she went to heaven.
m.4.6.65: There, having enjoyed abundant and supreme happiness for a long time, she attained the highest state by the grace of Śaṅkara.
m.4.6.66: And her son the brahmin, having then cast the remaining bones there as well, became joyful in mind and, purified in soul, went to his own home.
m.4.6.iti: Thus ends the sixth adhyāya, named The brahmin woman goes to heaven, in the account of the greatness of the Nandikeśvara liṅga, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
