m.4.7.1: The sages said: How did Gaṅgā come, especially to the Narmadā, on the seventh day of the month of Vaiśākha? O Sūta, O lord, describe this.
m.4.7.2: And how did the Lord come to be known by the name Nandikeśa? Tell us that story too, with great kindness, O wise one.
m.4.7.3: Sūta said: Well asked, O best of sages, is this question concerning Nandikeśa. I shall now tell it today; hearing it increases merit.
m.4.7.4: A Brāhmaṇa woman named Ṛṣikā, daughter of a certain twice-born, was married according to rule to a certain Brāhmaṇa.
m.4.7.5: By the power of past deeds, that wife of the Brāhmaṇa, though of good vows, O chief Brāhmaṇas, became a widow while still a girl.
m.4.7.6: Then that Brāhmaṇa's wife, observing the vow of celibacy, performed very severe austerity, preceded by worship of an earthen liṅga.
m.4.7.7: At that time a wicked, powerful asura named Mūḍha, a great sorcerer, went there, struck by the arrow of desire.
m.4.7.8: Seeing her performing austerity, beautiful and exceedingly desirable, he begged her for enjoyment, displaying various enticements.
m.4.7.9: But that woman of good vows, devoted to meditation on Śiva, did not cast even a glance of desire on him, O lords of sages.
m.4.7.10: That Brāhmaṇa woman, devoted to austerity, did not respect him; she was exceedingly steadfast in austerity, resorting to meditation on Śiva.
m.4.7.11: Then that demon-king Mūḍha, scorned by that slender woman, became angry and afterwards showed her a terrible form.
m.4.7.12: Then the evil-souled one spoke harsh, frightening words and terrified that wife of the Brāhmaṇa again and again.
m.4.7.13: Then that slender Brāhmaṇa's wife, whose refuge was Śiva, stricken with fear, lovingly uttered the name Śiva many times.
m.4.7.14: Extremely distressed, that woman, uttering Śiva's name, took refuge in Śambhu for the protection of her own dharma.
m.4.7.15: To protect one who had sought refuge, to uphold good conduct, and for her joy, Śiva indeed appeared.
m.4.7.16: Then Śaṅkara, affectionate to his devotees, instantly reduced to ashes that demon-king named Mūḍha, overcome by lust.
m.4.7.17: Then the Supreme Lord, whose mind is skilled in protecting devotees, looking at her with a compassionate glance, said, ask for a boon.
m.4.7.18: Hearing Maheśa's words, that chaste Brāhmaṇa lady beheld Śaṅkara's auspicious form, which produces bliss.
m.4.7.19: Then bowing to Śambhu, the Supreme Lord who brings happiness, the chaste one of pure intent, with joined palms and bowed shoulders, praised him.
m.4.7.20: Ṛṣikā said: O God of gods, O Mahādeva, affectionate to those who seek refuge, you are the friend of the afflicted, the Lord, ever the protector of devotees.
m.4.7.21: Here you have protected my dharma from the asura named Mūḍha; since this wicked one has been slain, the world has been protected by you.
m.4.7.22: Grant me supreme, unfailing devotion to your feet. This alone is the boon, O Lord; what could be greater than this?
m.4.7.23: Hear another request of mine, O all-pervading one, O Maheśvara: for the benefit of the worlds, remain established here.
m.4.7.24: Sūta said: Having thus praised Mahādeva, that Ṛṣikā of auspicious vows fell silent; then Giriśa, the mine of compassion, spoke.
m.4.7.25: Giriśa said: O Ṛṣikā, you are of good conduct and especially my devotee. All the boons that you have asked for have been granted to you.
m.4.7.26: Meanwhile the gods, Hari, Brahmā and others, learning of Śiva's manifestation, came there filled with joy.
m.4.7.27: Bowing to Śiva with great love, they all worshipped him; and, O Brāhmaṇas, bowed down, pure-minded, with joined hands, they praised him.
m.4.7.28: At this time Gaṅgā, the heavenly river, with a very gracious heart, spoke to that chaste Ṛṣikā, praising her observance.
m.4.7.29: Gaṅgā said: For my sake, give me your word: in the month of Vaiśākha, for one day, you must grant me nearness so that I may stay here.
m.4.7.30: Sūta said: Hearing Gaṅgā's words, that chaste woman of good vows lovingly said, so be it, for the welfare of the worlds.
m.4.7.31: For her joy, Śiva Hara, well pleased, merged with his full portion into that earthen liṅga worshipped by her.
m.4.7.32: All the gods, very pleased, praised Śiva and her; Viṣṇu, Brahmā and the others, and also the heavenly river, went each to their own abode.
m.4.7.33: From that day it became such an excellent purifying tīrtha, and Śiva became renowned as Nandikeśa, destroyer of all sins.
m.4.7.34: Gaṅgā too goes there every year on that day with good intent, to wash away her own sin, which she has taken on from men, O Brāhmaṇas.
m.4.7.35: A man who bathes there properly and worships Nandikeśa is freed from all sins, even brahmin-slaying and the like.
m.4.7.iti: Thus ends the seventh adhyāya, named The greatness of the Nandikeśvara Śiva-liṅga, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.4.8.1: Sūta said: O twice-born ones, listen with true devotion as I describe those Śiva-liṅgas that are famed on earth in the western direction.
m.4.8.2: In the city of Kapilā there is the supremely divine Śiva-liṅga named Kālarāmeśvara, which takes away sin merely by being seen.
m.4.8.3: And at the western ocean Mahāsiddheśvara is celebrated; he grants dharma, wealth and desires, and likewise bestows liberation too.
m.4.8.4: Situated on the shore of the western ocean is Gokarṇa, the most excellent holy place, which destroys sins such as the killing of a brahmin and grants the fruit of all desires.
m.4.8.5: In Gokarṇa there are Śiva-liṅgas by crores upon crores, and countless tīrthas stand at every step.
m.4.8.6: What is the use of saying much here? Everything situated in Gokarṇa, in every way, is a visibly manifest liṅga of Śiva, and all its waters are tīrthas.
m.4.8.7: Dear one, the greatness of the Śiva-liṅgas and of all the tīrthas in Gokarṇa is described in the Purāṇas by the great sages.
m.4.8.8: In the Kṛta age he Mahābala is white, in the Tretā deep red, in the Dvāpara yellow-coloured, and in the Kali age he will be dark.
m.4.8.9: Though Mahābala pervades the hollows of the seven netherworlds, when the terrible Kali age arrives he will become soft.
m.4.8.10: Even great sinners, having worshipped here the Śiva-liṅga Mahābala in Gokarṇa, have gone to the abode of Śaṅkara.
m.4.8.11: O sages, those who go there to Gokarṇa on a day of an auspicious constellation and worship him with devotion become Rudras; there is no doubt.
m.4.8.12: Whatever man, whoever he may be, worships that Śiva-liṅga in Gokarṇa at any time whatever, he goes to the abode of Brahmā.
m.4.8.13: Out of the wish for the welfare of the gods, Brahmā, Viṣṇu and the rest, the god Śaṅkara is ever present there under the name Mahābala.
m.4.8.14: That liṅga, obtained through severe austerity by the demon named Rāvaṇa, was installed in Gokarṇa by the Leader of the Gaṇas Gaṇeśa.
m.4.8.15: Viṣṇu, Brahmā, the great Indra, the Viśvedevas, the hosts of Maruts, the Ādityas, the Vasus, the two Aśvins, and the Moon together with the stars—
m.4.8.16: These gods, travelling in aerial cars, together with their attendants, attend upon his eastern gate for the sake of pleasing him.
m.4.8.17: Yama, Death himself in person, Citragupta and Agni, together with the Pitṛs and the Rudras, have resorted to the southern gate.
m.4.8.18: Varuṇa, lord of rivers, with the hosts of rivers beginning with the Gaṅgā, resorting to the western gate, serve Mahābala.
m.4.8.19: Likewise Vāyu, Kubera and the sovereign goddess Bhadrakālikā, with the Mothers headed by Caṇḍikā, have resorted to the northern gate.
m.4.8.20: All the gods with the Gandharvas, the Pitṛs, the Siddhas and Cāraṇas, the Vidyādharas, Kimpuruṣas, Kinnaras, Guhyakas and birds—
m.4.8.21: Various Piśācas, Vetālas and mighty Daityas, all the Nāgas beginning with Śeṣa, the Siddhas and all the sages—
m.4.8.22: —praise that god and bow down to Mahābala; they obtain their desired wishes and enjoy themselves as they please.
m.4.8.23: Many have performed fine austerity there and, having worshipped that all-pervading Lord, have attained the supreme accomplishment, which gives happiness here and hereafter.
m.4.8.24: The Śiva-liṅga in Gokarṇa is declared to be the gate of liberation; O twice-born ones, he who is named Mahābala is worshipped and praised there.
m.4.8.25: The worship of Mahābala on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight of Māgha especially bestows liberation on all, even on sinners.
m.4.8.26: On this holy day of Śiva, great multitudes of all four varṇas, eager to see the grand festival, come from every land.
m.4.8.27: Women, the old, children and those living in the four āśramas, having come there and seen the Lord of gods, attained fulfilment of their purpose.
m.4.8.28: They attained this through the power of Mahābala; and once a certain Cāṇḍāla woman, having worshipped that liṅga of Śiva, quickly went to Śiva's world.
m.4.8.iti: Thus ends the eighth adhyāya, named The greatness of Mahābala, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.4.9.1: The sages said: O Sūta, O Sūta, most fortunate one, you are blessed, the best of Śaivas. Who is the cāṇḍāla woman who was mentioned? Tell us her story, O lord.
m.4.9.2: Sūta said: O twice-born ones, listen with true devotion to that most wondrous story, interwoven with Śiva's power, which increases the devotion of those who hear it.
m.4.9.3: That cāṇḍāla woman, in a former birth, was a brahmin's daughter named Saumini, moon-faced and endowed with every auspicious mark.
m.4.9.4: Then, O twice-born ones, when the maiden Saumini had come of age and was a young woman, her father duly gave her in marriage to a certain brahmin's son.
m.4.9.5: Having obtained a husband, she of good vows, radiant with fresh youth, enjoyed herself with him for some time, O best of the twice-born.
m.4.9.6: Then Saumini's husband, the young brahmin, afflicted by a severe illness, met his death through the course of time, O twice-born ones.
m.4.9.7: When her husband died, that woman, grieved and deeply dejected in mind, lived in the house for some time, of good conduct and virtuous character.
m.4.9.8: Then, her heart possessed by desire, though a widow, owing to the peculiar force of youth she became unchaste.
m.4.9.9: Learning of her evil deed that defiled the family, her kinsmen assembled, dragged her far away by the hair, and abandoned her.
m.4.9.10: A certain prominent śūdra, seeing her wandering at her own will in the forest, made her his woman and then took her to his own house.
m.4.9.11: Then she, eating meat and constantly drinking liquor, fond of sexual pleasure, bore a daughter by that śūdra.
m.4.9.12: Once, when her husband had gone somewhere, the unchaste Saumini, having drunk liquor, craved a meal of meat.
m.4.9.13: Then, with the rams tethered together with the cows in the pen outside, at nightfall, when it was blind with darkness, she took a sword and went.
m.4.9.14: Without reflecting, owing to her drunken state, that most wretched meat-lover killed a single bleating calf, thinking it a ram.
m.4.9.15: Having brought the slain animal home and realising it was a calf, the woman in fear said, Śiva, Śiva, owing to some meritorious deed of the past.
m.4.9.16: Having meditated on Śiva for a moment, she, eager to eat meat, cut up that very calf and made the meal she desired.
m.4.9.17: Thus, after much time had passed, O twice-born ones, Saumini fell under the sway of Death and went to Yama's abode.
m.4.9.18: Yama, too, considering her merit and her former deeds, turned her back from residence in hell and made her of cāṇḍāla birth.
m.4.9.19: Then, fallen from Yama's city, she entered the womb of a cāṇḍāla woman, and was born blind, dark as an extinguished coal.
m.4.9.20: Blind from birth, she lost father and mother even in childhood; being wretched and afflicted by severe leprosy, she was married by no one.
m.4.9.21: Then, tormented by hunger, miserable, staff in hand and sightless, she appeased the fire of her belly with the leftover morsels of cāṇḍālas.
m.4.9.22: Thus, having passed her long life in great hardship, her whole body seized by old age, she suffered insurmountable misery.
m.4.9.23: Once, as Śiva's holy day was approaching, that cāṇḍāla woman learned that crowds of travellers were going to that shrine of Gokarṇa.
m.4.9.24: Then that cāṇḍāla woman too, longing for clothing and food, set out very slowly to beg from the crowds.
m.4.9.25: Having gone there, the cāṇḍāla woman wandered here and there, beseeching the crowds with piteous words and outstretched cupped hands.
m.4.9.26: As the cāṇḍāla woman was thus begging, a most virtuous traveller cast a sprig of bilva into her outstretched cupped hands.
m.4.9.27: Feeling it again and again as it fell into her hands, and judging it inedible, the distressed woman threw it far away.
m.4.9.28: Released from her hand in the night, that bilva sprig by good fortune fell on the top of a certain Śiva-liṅga.
m.4.9.29: Thus, on the night of Śiva's fourteenth, though she begged the travellers again and again, by the turn of fate she obtained nothing at all.
m.4.9.30: Thus, unknowingly, the pure vow of Śiva's fourteenth came about, along with the vigil that bestows supreme bliss.
m.4.9.31: Then at dawn that woman, overwhelmed by great sorrow, miserable, slowly turned back alone toward her own place.
m.4.9.32: Exhausted by her long fast, stumbling at every step, having crossed only that much ground, she fell down unconscious.
m.4.9.33: Then, by Śambhu's grace, she went to the supreme abode, mounting a splendid aerial chariot brought swiftly by Śiva's attendants.
m.4.9.34: Because earlier this woman, though unchaste, uttered Śiva's name even by accident, by that merit, augmented here, O brahmins, she attained the divine abode of Mahābala.
m.4.9.35: For at holy Gokarṇa, on Śiva's day, having fasted and kept vigil, she performed at night the worship with bilva on Śiva's head.
m.4.9.36: Even today, by the grace of Mahābala, she enjoys the fruit of this merit performed without intention.
m.4.9.37: Such is Śaṅkara's great liṅga Mahābala, which instantly removes all sins and bestows supreme bliss.
m.4.9.38: Thus, O brahmins, I have told you the supreme greatness of the excellent Śiva-liṅga called Mahābala.
m.4.9.39: Now I shall tell another wondrous account of its greatness, by merely hearing which devotion to Śiva quickly arises.
m.4.9.iti: Thus ends the ninth adhyāya, named The attainment of a good end by the Cāṇḍāla woman, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.4.10.1: Sūta said: In the illustrious Ikṣvāku dynasty there was a supremely righteous king named Mitrasaha, the foremost of all archers.
m.4.10.2: That king's beloved, Madayantī, was most devoted to dharma and auspicious; she was renowned as a chaste wife, like Damayantī the wife of Nala.
m.4.10.3: Once King Mitrasaha, who was fond of hunting, went into a dense forest accompanied by a great army.
m.4.10.4: Roaming there, the king slew a night-prowler named Kamaṭha, a very wicked villain who tormented the virtuous.
m.4.10.5: Then his sinful younger brother, a deceiver, thinking, I shall overcome him by trickery alone, went to the king's presence.
m.4.10.6: Seeing him of humble appearance, come to take up service, the king out of ignorance made him superintendent of the kitchen.
m.4.10.7: Then, having sported in that forest for some time, the king turned back, gave up the hunt, and joyfully returned to his own city.
m.4.10.8: When the anniversary of his father's death arrived, the king invited his own preceptor Vasiṣṭha, brought him to his house, and fed him with devotion.
m.4.10.9: Seeing placed before him a dish of vegetables and meat mixed with human flesh by the demon in the guise of a cook, the preceptor then spoke.
m.4.10.10: The guru said: Fie on you, O king! Since human flesh has been offered to me by you, a deceiver and villain, you shall therefore become a demon.
m.4.10.11: Then, realising that it had been done by the demon, the preceptor reconsidered and made that curse last twelve years.
m.4.10.12: The king, knowing the curse to be undeserved, was overcome with anger; taking water in his cupped hands, he made ready to curse the preceptor.
m.4.10.13: Then his beloved, the chaste and righteous Madayantī, falling at his feet, restrained him from that curse.
m.4.10.14: Then, desisting from the curse out of regard for her words, he let the water fall on his own feet; his feet became stained.
m.4.10.15: From then on, O lords of sages, that king became known in this world as Kalmaṣāṅghri ('stained-foot'), indeed through the power of that water.
m.4.10.16: Through the curse of his preceptor, the best of sages, King Mitrasaha became a terrible, violent demon roaming the forest.
m.4.10.17: Bearing a demonic form like Kāla, Antaka and Yama, he roamed the forest and devoured various creatures, humans and others.
m.4.10.18: Once, somewhere in the forest, he, looking like Death, saw a young newly-married sage couple sporting together.
m.4.10.19: That man-eating demon, afflicted by the curse, seized the young son of the sage in order to eat him, as a tiger seizes a fawn.
m.4.10.20: Seeing her husband seized under his arm, his frightened beloved pleaded with him, speaking piteous words.
m.4.10.21: Though entreated many times, that pitiless, evil-minded man-eater cut off the brahmin boy's head and devoured it.
m.4.10.22: Then that wretched chaste woman, greatly grieved, lamented, gathered her husband's bones, and made a fierce blazing pyre.
m.4.10.23: Following her husband and entering the fire, that brahmin woman cursed the king in his demon form:
m.4.10.24: From today, whenever you unite with women, then shall be your death. Having said this, the chaste woman entered the fire.
m.4.10.25: That king too, having undergone his preceptor's curse for its fixed term, regained his own form and joyfully went to his home.
m.4.10.26: Knowing of the curse of the brahmin's chaste wife, Madayantī, greatly fearing widowhood, restrained her husband who desired love-making.
m.4.10.27: Childless and disgusted with royal pleasures, the king gave up all his wealth and went to the forest.
m.4.10.28: He saw the sin of brahmin-slaying, very painful and hideous in form, following behind him and threatening him again and again.
m.4.10.29: Seeking release from her, the king, dejected in mind, employed various means such as japa, vows, and sacrifices.
m.4.10.30: O brahmins, when the king's brahmin-slaying did not cease by various means such as bathing at holy places, he then went to Mithilā.
m.4.10.31: Having reached an outer garden, tormented by intense anxiety about her, the king saw the sage Gautama approaching.
m.4.10.32: Approaching Gautama of pure heart, that great king, having gained some relief from seeing him, bowed again and again.
m.4.10.33: Then, asked by him about his welfare, sighing long and hot, and having gained comfort from his compassionate glance, the king spoke to him.
m.4.10.34: The king said: O sage, this insurmountable brahmin-slaying torments me; unseen by others, dear sir, she threatens me at every step.
m.4.10.35: Since a brahmin's son was devoured by me while I was burnt by the curse, there is no expiation of that sin even by thousands of penances.
m.4.10.36: Wandering about, O sage, I tried various means to quell it; yet the brahmin-slaying of sinful me has not ceased—what more can I do?
m.4.10.37: Today I feel as though my birth has borne fruit, for by the mere sight of you a flood of joy has arisen in me.
m.4.10.38: Today, O fortunate one, grant peace to me, a sinner who has taken refuge at your lotus-feet, so that I may attain happiness.
m.4.10.39: Sūta said: Thus addressed by the king, Gautama, his mind moist with compassion, properly prescribed the expiation for terrible sins.
m.4.10.40: Gautama said: Well done, O great king, you are blessed; give up fear of great sins. When Śiva is the ruler, where is fear for devotees who seek refuge?
m.4.10.41: Listen, O king, O greatly fortunate one: there is another established sacred site, the abode of Śiva called Gokarṇa, which destroys even the great sins.
m.4.10.42: There sins cannot remain, not even the greatest of the great; Śiva himself is present there under the name Mahābala.
m.4.10.43: Among all Śiva-liṅgas, Mahābala is the sovereign; in the four ages he takes four colours, and he removes all sins.
m.4.10.44: Gokarṇa, an excellent tīrtha, lies on the shore of the western ocean; there is that Śiva-liṅga which destroys great sins.
m.4.10.45: Great sinners, having gone there, bathed abundantly in the tīrthas and worshipped Mahābala, have attained the abode of Śaṅkara.
m.4.10.46: So you too, O lord of kings, should go to Gokarṇa, the abode of Giriśa, worship that liṅga, and attain fulfilment.
m.4.10.47: Having bathed there in all the tīrthas and worshipped Mahābala, freed from all sins, you will attain Śiva's world.
m.4.10.48: Sūta said: Thus instructed by the great-souled sage Gautama, the king, his mind overjoyed, went to Gokarṇa.
m.4.10.49: Having bathed well there in the tīrthas and duly worshipped Mahābala, his entire mass of sins shaken off, he attained the supreme abode of Śambhu.
m.4.10.50: Whoever regularly listens to this beloved story of Mahābala goes to Śiva's world together with twenty-one generations of his family.
m.4.10.51: Thus I have narrated to you the supremely wondrous greatness of Mahābala, the liṅga of Giriśa, which removes all sins.
m.4.10.iti: Thus ends the tenth adhyāya, named The greatness of the Śiva-liṅga called Mahābala, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.4.11.1: The sages said: O Sūta, O Sūta, most fortunate one, blessed are you, whose mind is devoted to Śiva! This wondrous story of the Mahābala liṅga has been narrated to us by you.
m.4.11.2: And whatever Śiva-liṅgas there are in the northern direction, tell us their pure glory, which destroys sin.
m.4.11.3: Sūta said: Listen attentively, O Brāhmaṇas: I shall relate in brief the glory of the Śiva-liṅgas, particularly of the northern ones.
m.4.11.4: Gokarṇa is another holy region, destroying the great sins; and there is a great forest there, holy and very extensive.
m.4.11.5: There stands the supreme Śiva-liṅga named Candrabhāla, brought by Rāvaṇa out of true devotion, granting all accomplishments.
m.4.11.6: O lords of sages, his abiding there, like that of Vaidyanātha, is for the welfare of all the worlds, he being an ocean of compassion.
m.4.11.7: Having bathed at Gokarṇa and worshipped Candrabhāla, one attains the world of Śiva — truly, truly, there is no doubt.
m.4.11.8: The glory of the Candrabhāla liṅga is supremely wondrous; it cannot be described fully, even by Vyāsa, who delights in devotion and love.
m.4.11.9: The great glory of the Candrabhāla Mahādeva liṅga has been told somehow; now listen to that of another liṅga.
m.4.11.10: The Dādhīca Śiva-liṅga, at the tīrtha of the Miśra sages, was installed with great love by Dadhīci, lord of sages.
m.4.11.11: Going there and bathing in that tīrtha properly according to rule, one should reverently worship the Śiva-liṅga Dādhīceśvara.
m.4.11.12: Right there, the image of Dadhīci should be worshipped according to rule, promptly, for Śiva's pleasure, by those seeking the fruit of pilgrimage.
m.4.11.13: When this is done, O best of sages, a man becomes fulfilled; having enjoyed every happiness here, he attains the highest goal hereafter.
m.4.11.14: At the Naimiṣāraṇya tīrtha there is a Śiva-liṅga, installed by all the sages, famed as Ṛṣīśvara, bestowing happiness.
m.4.11.15: By seeing and worshipping it, even sinful people obtain enjoyment and liberation, here and hereafter, O lords of sages.
m.4.11.16: At the Hatyāharaṇa tīrtha, the sin-removing Śiva-liṅga should be especially worshipped; it destroys crores of the sins of killing.
m.4.11.17: At the Devaprayāga tīrtha, the Śiva-liṅga named Laliteśvara, destroyer of all sins, should always be worshipped by men.
m.4.11.18: In the city called Nayapāla, renowned on earth, is the liṅga named Paśupatīśa, granting the fruit of all desires.
m.4.11.19: That Śiva-liṅga indeed exists in the form of the head portion; I shall narrate its story in the description of Kedāreśvara.
m.4.11.20: Near it is the most wondrous Śiva-liṅga named Muktinātha; by seeing and worshipping it, enjoyment and liberation are obtained.
m.4.11.21: Thus the excellent description of the liṅgas in the four directions has been told to you, O best of sages. What else do you wish to hear?
m.4.11.iti: Thus ends the eleventh adhyāya, named The greatness of the Candrabhāla and Paśupatinātha liṅgas, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.4.12.1: The sages said: O Sūta, by the grace of Vyāsa you know every matter; nothing is unknown to you. Therefore we ask you.
m.4.12.2: The liṅga is worshipped in the world, and what you have told about it is just so; but is there not some other reason for it here?
m.4.12.3: Pārvatī, the beloved of Śiva, is heard in the world to have the form of the bāṇa pedestal. What is the reason for this, O Sūta? Tell it as you have heard it.
m.4.12.4: Sūta said: O twice-born, I heard from Vyāsa the story of the different kalpas; that very story I tell now. Let it be heard, O best of sages.
m.4.12.5: Let that very event which happened long ago to the twice-born in the Dāru forest be heard properly; I shall narrate it as I heard it.
m.4.12.6: There was an excellent forest named Dāru; there lived the best of sages, devotees of Śiva, ever and always intent on meditation on Śiva.
m.4.12.7: They performed the worship of Śiva at the three times of day without interruption; those lords of sages praised him with divine hymns of many kinds.
m.4.12.8: Once they all went into the forest to gather sacrificial fuel—all those bulls among the twice-born, Śaivas intent on meditation on Śiva.
m.4.12.9: Meanwhile Śaṅkara himself, the Blue-red One, assuming a deformed appearance, came there in order to test them.
m.4.12.10: Naked, exceedingly radiant, adorned with ash as his ornament, he behaved in an indecent way, holding his liṅga in his hand.
m.4.12.11: With the intention in his mind of doing what was dear to those forest-dwellers, Hara himself, pleased with his devotees, went lovingly to that forest.
m.4.12.12: Seeing him, those wives of the sages fell into great fear; others, agitated and amazed, likewise came together again to him.
m.4.12.13: Some embraced him, and others took hold of his hand; then those women, jostling one another, were wholly immersed in him.
m.4.12.14: At that very time the eminent sages arrived; seeing him acting improperly, they were distressed and overcome with anger.
m.4.12.15: Then, stricken with distress, all those sages, deluded by Śiva's māyā, said: Who is this? Who is this?
m.4.12.16: When that naked ascetic said nothing at all, then those great sages spoke to that fearsome person.
m.4.12.17: Since you are doing what is improper, destructive of the Vedic path, therefore let that liṅga of yours fall to the surface of the earth.
m.4.12.18: Sūta said: When they had said this, the liṅga of that avadhūta, Śiva of wondrous form, fell instantly.
m.4.12.19: That liṅga, like fire, burned everything that stood before it; wherever it went, there it burned again.
m.4.12.20: It went into Pātāla, and likewise into heaven; it went everywhere on earth, and nowhere did it stay still.
m.4.12.21: The worlds became agitated, and those sages were greatly distressed; none found peace—neither the gods nor the sages.
m.4.12.22: All those gods and sages by whom Śiva had not been recognised, distressed, assembled quickly and went to Brahmā for refuge.
m.4.12.23: Going there, all those twice-born bowed to and praised Vidhi, and told the whole event to Brahmā, the maker of creation.
m.4.12.24: Brahmā, hearing their words and knowing them to be deluded by Śiva's māyā, bowed to Śaṅkara and spoke to those best of sages.
m.4.12.25: Brahmā said: O twice-born, you, though men of knowledge, do what is blameworthy; if the ignorant were to do so, what more need be said?
m.4.12.26: Having thus opposed the god Śiva, who can hope for welfare? Whoever at midday does not attend to a guest—
m.4.12.27: the guest goes away taking that person's merit and leaving behind his own sin; how much more so in the case of Śiva himself?
m.4.12.28: As long as the liṅga is not stable, nothing auspicious will arise anywhere in the three worlds; this I tell you truly.
m.4.12.29: You must act in such a way that the Śiva-liṅga may become steady here, O sages; let it be carefully considered in your minds.
m.4.12.30: Sūta said: Thus addressed, the sages bowed and said to Brahmā: O Vidhi, what should we do? Instruct us what is to be done.
m.4.12.31: Thus addressed by those lords of sages, Brahmā, grandfather of all worlds, then himself spoke to them.
m.4.12.32: Brahmā said: Let the gods worship the goddess Girijā and entreat Śivā; if she takes the form of the yoni, then it will attain stability.
m.4.12.33: I shall now explain the procedure for it; listen, all of you, O excellent ones. Perform it with love, and she will be pleased.
m.4.12.34: Having set up a pot and drawn an excellent eight-petalled lotus, one should then fill it with sacred water, along with dūrvā grass and barley sprouts.
m.4.12.35: Then one should consecrate that pot with Vedic mantras, having performed its worship by the method taught in śruti, while remembering Śiva.
m.4.12.36: O great sages, one should bathe that liṅga with that water; sprinkled with the Śatarudriya mantras, it will attain peace.
m.4.12.37: Then, having installed the auspicious bāṇa in the form of Girijā's yoni, that liṅga should be installed upon it, and one should again consecrate it with mantras.
m.4.12.38: With fragrances and sandal-paste, with flowers, incense and the like, and with worship such as food-offerings, one should please the Supreme Lord.
m.4.12.39: Likewise with prostrations, holy hymns, instrumental music and songs; then, having performed the svastyayana benediction rite, one should proclaim, Victory!
m.4.12.40: Be gracious, O Lord of gods, bringer of joy to the world. You are the creator and the preserver, you are the destroyer, beyond all words.
m.4.12.41: You are the origin of the world, the womb of the world, and also the one who dwells within the world. Be calm, O Maheśāna, and protect all the worlds.
m.4.12.42: When this rite has been performed, well-being will come about, there is no doubt. There will be no disturbance in these three worlds; there will always be happiness.
m.4.12.43: Sūta said: Thus addressed, those Brāhmaṇas and gods bowed to the Grandfather Brahmā and went for refuge to that Śiva, desiring the happiness of all the worlds.
m.4.12.44: Then Śaṅkara, worshipped with supreme devotion and entreated, became very pleased, and the Great Lord spoke to them.
m.4.12.45: Maheśvara said: O gods and all you sages, listen to my words with respect. If my liṅga is held in the form of a yoni, then there will be well-being.
m.4.12.46: Apart from Pārvatī, no other is able to hold the liṅga. Held by her, my liṅga will quickly become calm.
m.4.12.47: Sūta said: Hearing that, O lords of sages, the sages and gods, greatly delighted, taking Brahmā along, then entreated Girijā.
m.4.12.48: Having pleased Girijā and the bull-bannered one Śiva too, and having performed the rite described earlier, the excellent liṅga was installed.
m.4.12.49: By the procedure prescribed in the mantras, the gods and the sages likewise pleased Girijā and Śiva, for the sake of dharma.
m.4.12.50: All the gods and sages especially worshipped Śiva — Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and others too, and the three worlds with their moving and unmoving beings.
m.4.12.51: Śiva became very pleased, and so did Śivā, the Mother of the world; and then she held that liṅga in that form.
m.4.12.52: When the liṅga was installed, there was then welfare for the worlds, and that liṅga became famous in the three worlds, O Brāhmaṇas.
m.4.12.53: It is known as Hāṭakeśa and also as Śivāśiva. By worshipping it, happiness arises for people in every way.
m.4.12.54: Here there will be abundant prosperity of every kind, bringing many joys; and hereafter supreme liberation — no doubt need be entertained about this.
m.4.12.iti: Thus ends the twelfth adhyāya, named The cause of the form of the liṅga, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.4.13.1: Sūta said: O brāhmaṇas, I have lovingly told you how Śiva came to take the form of the liṅga, worthy of worship in the three worlds. What else do you wish to hear?
m.4.13.2: The sages said: O lord, tell us the greatness of the Andhakeśvara liṅga, and here you should also kindly tell us about other Śiva-liṅgas.
m.4.13.3: Sūta said: Long ago the demon Andhakāsura, tormentor of the gods, dwelling in a pit in the ocean, brought the three worlds under his control.
m.4.13.4: Coming out of that pit and oppressing the people, the very mighty demon would then enter that pit again.
m.4.13.5: All the gods, distressed, entreated Śiva again and again and reported everything, their own suffering, O chief sages.
m.4.13.6: Sūta said: Hearing those words of the gods, the Supreme Lord, slayer of the wicked and refuge of the good, replied with a gracious mind.
m.4.13.7: Śiva said: I shall have that demon Andhaka, tormentor of the gods, slain. Lead out the army, O gods; I am coming with my gaṇas.
m.4.13.8: Then, when that terrifying Andhaka, enemy of gods and sages, had come out of the pit, the gods occupied the pit.
m.4.13.9: The demons and the gods fought a most terrible battle, and then, by Śiva's grace, the gods became very strong.
m.4.13.10: Hard pressed by the gods, he made for the pit, but just as he reached it he was transfixed with the trident by Śiva, the Supreme Self.
m.4.13.11: Lying there, he then meditated on Śambhu and prayed: One who sees you at the time of death becomes like you in an instant.
m.4.13.12: Praised in this way, Śaṅkara was pleased and spoke there: Name a boon; I shall grant it to you.
m.4.13.13: Hearing these words, the demon, now endowed with a sāttvic disposition, bowed deeply to Śiva, praised him, and spoke again.
m.4.13.14: Andhaka said: O Lord of the gods, if you are pleased, grant me auspicious devotion to you, and showing special grace, remain established here.
m.4.13.15: Sūta said: Thus addressed by him, Hara cast that demon into that pit, and he himself remained there in the form of a liṅga, out of desire for the good of the world.
m.4.13.16: The man who worships that liṅga, Andhakeśa, daily attains the fulfilment of his wishes within six months; there is no doubt.
m.4.13.17: But the brāhmaṇa who worships for six months this liṅga, which benefits the world, for the sake of livelihood, is known as a devalaka.
m.4.13.18: He then becomes, here, just like a devalaka; and for one who is called a devalaka there is no entitlement as a twice-born.
m.4.13.19: The sages said: Who is called a devalaka, and what is his duty? O most wise one, tell us the truth for the welfare of the worlds.
m.4.13.20: Sūta said: There was a brāhmaṇa named Dadhīci, most righteous, master of the Vedas, ever delighting in devotion to Śiva and devoted to the Śaiva scriptures.
m.4.13.21: He had a son known by the name Sudarśana; and Sudarśana's wife was named Dukūlā, born of a wicked family.
m.4.13.22: The husband was under her control; he had four sons. He too always performed the worship of Śiva alone.
m.4.13.23: At that time Dadhīci had to stay in another village; because of ties with his kinsmen, he was not released by them.
m.4.13.24: Having told his son, remain devoted to Śiva, and having said this, Dadhīci, best of Śaivas, being let go, departed.
m.4.13.25: His son Sudarśana too performed the worship of Śiva. In this way a very long time passed, O chief sages.
m.4.13.26: Then once Śivarātri arrived, and on it all observed the fast, each of their own accord, as the occasion came.
m.4.13.27: He who was known as Sudarśana, having performed the worship, went away; but having had union with a woman on Śivarātri, he came here again.
m.4.13.28: He did not bathe, yet performed Śiva's worship that night. Because of the fruition of that deed, Śaṅkara, angered, spoke.
m.4.13.29: Maheśvara said: O wicked one, on Śivarātri you have had intercourse with a woman, and without bathing, thoughtlessly, you have performed my worship.
m.4.13.30: Since you did this knowingly, therefore become dull-witted. Become untouchable to me, and behold me only from afar.
m.4.13.31: Sūta said: Thus cursed by Maheśa, Sudarśana, son of Dadhīci, deluded by Śiva's māyā, at once became dull-witted.
m.4.13.32: At that moment, O brāhmaṇas, Dadhīci, best of Śaivas, returned from the other village and heard what had happened.
m.4.13.33: He too, as if rebuked by Śiva, became exceedingly grieved, and, in sorrow over his son's deed, wept: Alas, I am ruined!
m.4.13.34: Dadhīci, esteemed by the good, said again and again: By this wicked son my excellent family has been ruined.
m.4.13.35: The son too, stricken, and rebuked by his own father, was seized by remorse and at once denounced his wife as a wanton woman.
m.4.13.36: There his father worshipped Girijā with excellent rites, with great effort and great devotion, for the sake of his son's well-being.
m.4.13.37: Sudarśana too himself worshipped Girijā, following the method of Caṇḍī worship, with great devotion and auspicious hymns.
m.4.13.38: Thus father and son, through various means and with deep devotion, made the goddess Girijā, who loves her devotees, pleased.
m.4.13.39: Pleased by the power of their service, Caṇḍikā Girijā then adopted Sudarśana as her son, O sage.
m.4.13.40: Caṇḍikā herself propitiated Śiva for the sake of her son; Caṇḍī, angry and then no longer angry, again had a gracious mind toward that son.
m.4.13.41: Then, knowing that Maheśa, the bull-bannered one, was pleased, and having bowed to him, she herself placed Sudarśana on his lap.
m.4.13.42: Then Girijā herself performed the ghee-bath of her son; and a sacred thread of three twists, joined with a single knot,
m.4.13.43: Ambikā then gave with affection to her son Sudarśana, imparting the Śiva-Gāyatrī consisting of sixteen syllables,
m.4.13.44: namely Om namaḥ śivāya preceded by the word śrī. She said: This boy (baṭu) should perform the saṅkalpa-worship sixteen times,
m.4.13.45: worshipping the bull-bannered one from bathing up to prostration, with mantras, musical instruments and offerings, in the presence of the sages.
m.4.13.46: She then made him recite many name-mantras. And then Caṇḍikā, with a well-pleased heart, and likewise Śiva said:
m.4.13.47: Whatever wealth, grain and the like is offered to me, all that is to be accepted by you; it will not lead to any fault.
m.4.13.48: In my rites you are the foremost, and especially in the Devī's rites; ghee, oil and all else offered to me is to be taken by you.
m.4.13.49: When a prājāpatya feast takes place, then you alone should be the one fed; then the worship is complete, otherwise it is all fruitless.
m.4.13.50: A round tilaka is to be made by you, and bathing always done; the Śiva-sandhyā is to be performed, and its Gāyatrī.
m.4.13.51: Having first done my service, other duty befitting your family should be done. When everything is done thus, there will be well-being; your faults are forgiven by me.
m.4.13.52: Sūta said: Having said this, his four sons were then consecrated as baṭukas in the four directions by Śiva, the supreme Self.
m.4.13.53: And Caṇḍī, placing her son Sudarśana near herself, directed his sons, having given boons in many ways.
m.4.13.54: The Goddess said: Whoever is my baṭuka, between two opposing battle-arrays his victory shall always be; no doubt should be entertained in this.
m.4.13.55: By whom you are worshipped, by him alone am I truly worshipped. And your own duty must always be done by you all, O son.
m.4.13.56: Sūta said: Thus boons were given out of compassion to the great-souled Sudarśana together with his sons by Śiva and Śivā, for the sake of the worlds.
m.4.13.57: Because they were established by Śiva and Śivā, they are called baṭukas; because they were born of one fallen from austerity, they are called tapo'dhamas (lowly in austerity).
m.4.13.58: By the grace of Śiva and Śivā they all spread out in many ways. And theirs is the first worship, the great worship of the great-souled Lord.
m.4.13.59: As long as the worship of Śaṅkara has not been done by him the baṭuka, so long others' worship should not be done; if it is done, it is not auspicious.
m.4.13.60: Whether good or bad, one should not abandon the baṭuka; in the prājāpatya and in feeding, a single baṭu is preeminent.
m.4.13.61: Likewise in the rites of Śiva and Śivā a special distinction is seen here; hear that, O very wise one, as I tell it to you, O sinless one.
m.4.13.62: In the city of that same king Bhadra, during the daily feeding, in the observance of the prājāpatya, near the liṅga Andhakeśa,
m.4.13.63: the wondrous event that took place through Śiva's grace — let it be heard with great delight; I narrate it as I have heard it.
m.4.13.64: A banner was given to that king by the pleased Śambhu, and the king was told graciously by that God of gods:
m.4.13.65: Let the banner be tied up in the morning, O king; it will fall at night when my prājāpatya is thus completed, and so again each day.
m.4.13.66: Otherwise this banner of mine will stay fixed even at night. Having said this, Śambhu, the treasure of compassion, pleased with the king, vanished.
m.4.13.67: With the words so be it, this became the rule of that king, O great sage: the prājāpatya was performed daily according to the procedure of Śiva-worship.
m.4.13.68: The banner would rise of itself in the morning and fall in the evening, if the rite here had been completed.
m.4.13.69: Once, here, the rite of the baṭu was done first, and that banner fell even without the feeding of the brāhmaṇas.
m.4.13.70: Seeing that, the king then asked the learned men there: The brāhmaṇas are still eating here, yet the banner has not stayed up —
m.4.13.71: how has it fallen here? O brāhmaṇas, tell truthfully. Thus asked, the brāhmaṇas, best of the learned, then spoke:
m.4.13.72: O great king, at the brāhmaṇa-feast a baṭuka, Caṇḍī's son, was fed first; Śiva was pleased, and therefore the banner fell.
m.4.13.73: Hearing that, the king and all the other people there were amazed, and then they gave praise.
m.4.13.74: Thus their glory was increased by Śaṅkara; hence the baṭukas are proclaimed the best by those who know ancient lore.
m.4.13.75: The Śiva-worship should first be concluded (removed) by them, not otherwise; others have no entitlement here, by Śiva's command.
m.4.13.76: The concluding removal (uttāraṇa) must be done with the words, may the worship be complete; this alone is their task, and nothing else.
m.4.13.77: All this which was asked has been narrated, O lords of sages; hearing it, a man indeed obtains the fruit of Śiva-worship.
m.4.13.iti: Thus ends the thirteenth adhyāya, named The origin of the baṭukas, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.4.14.1: The sages said: Now tell us the greatness of the Jyotirliṅgas, and likewise their origin; tell everything just as you have heard it.
m.4.14.2: Sūta said: Listen, O brahmins; I shall tell their greatness and likewise their origin, briefly and according to my understanding, as I heard it from my true teacher.
m.4.14.3: The greatness of these cannot be told even in hundreds of years, O best of sages; nevertheless I shall tell it to you.
m.4.14.4: Among them Somanātha is proclaimed the first. Listen attentively first to its greatness, O sage.
m.4.14.5: Twenty-seven daughters, beginning with Aśvinī, were given to the Moon by the great-souled Dakṣa, O lords of sages.
m.4.14.6: Having obtained the Moon as their husband they shone especially; and the Moon too, having obtained them, shone constantly.
m.4.14.7: A gem shines through gold, and gold through a gem. Now hear what happened at that time.
m.4.14.8: Among all the wives, the one called Rohiṇī was dear to him as no other ever was.
m.4.14.9: The others, falling into sorrow, went to their father for refuge; having gone, they told him their grief as it was.
m.4.14.10: Hearing this, Dakṣa too was then grieved; O brahmins, coming to the Moon he then spoke words calmly.
m.4.14.11: Dakṣa said: O treasure of digits (kalānidhi), you were born in a spotless family; why then is there partiality, more and less, in you toward all who depend on you?
m.4.14.12: If it has been done, it is done; but it should not be done by you again. Conduct marked by unevenness is declared to lead to hell.
m.4.14.13: Sūta said: Having thus personally entreated the Moon, his son-in-law, Dakṣa went to his own home, fully resolved.
m.4.14.14: But the Moon, deluded, did not act on his word, through the power of Śiva's Māyā, by which the world is deluded.
m.4.14.15: When good is destined for someone, good indeed comes to him; and when ill is destined, how can good come to him?
m.4.14.16: The Moon, under the sway of powerful destiny, did not heed that word; attached to Rohiṇī, he never regarded any other.
m.4.14.17: Hearing that, Dakṣa, skilled as his name says, came again himself, full of grief, and entreated the Moon with good counsel.
m.4.14.18: Dakṣa said: Listen, O Moon: since you did not honour what I asked of you earlier in many ways, therefore become subject to waning.
m.4.14.19: Sūta said: When he had said this, the Moon at once became wasting; and as the Moon dwindled, there arose a great cry of distress.
m.4.14.20: Then all the gods and sages, thinking, what is to be done? Alas, how will it be? fell into grief and became distraught, O sage.
m.4.14.21: Informed by the Moon, all the gods headed by Indra and the sages headed by Vasiṣṭha went to Brahmā for refuge.
m.4.14.22: Having gone there, the sages and gods, greatly distressed, bowed to Brahmā, praised him, and told him the whole affair, O sage.
m.4.14.23: Brahmā too, hearing their words, was greatly amazed; extolling Śiva's Māyā, he spoke to them, making them hear.
m.4.14.24: Brahmā said: Alas, a great calamity has occurred, bringing sorrow to the whole world. The Moon was always wicked, and Dakṣa has cursed him.
m.4.14.25: All kinds of deeds have been done many times by the wicked Moon. Hear, O sages and gods, the Moon's former doing.
m.4.14.26: Going to Bṛhaspati's house, the wicked one carried off Tārā, his wife; and then he betook himself to the Daityas.
m.4.14.27: Taking refuge with the Daityas, he then waged war with the gods. Restrained by me and by Atri, the Moon (śaśin) gave Tārā back to him.
m.4.14.28: Seeing her pregnant, he (Bṛhaspati) said, I will not take her. Dissuaded by us, Jīva then reluctantly took her back.
m.4.14.29: He said again, if she gives up the embryo here, I will take her. Then, when I had made her give up the embryo there, O best of sages—
m.4.14.30: —when asked whose this embryo was, she said, Soma's. Afterwards she was taken back by him, Bṛhaspati, dissuaded by me.
m.4.14.31: Many such misdeeds of the Moon are told; why recount them again? How is it that he still acts so even today?
m.4.14.32: What has happened has rightly happened; it surely cannot be otherwise. Now I shall tell you a remedy; listen with attention.
m.4.14.33: Let the Moon go with the gods to the auspicious holy field of Prabhāsa, and there worship Śiva according to the Mṛtyuñjaya rite.
m.4.14.34: Placing the Lord before him there, let the Moon perform austerities constantly; then Śiva, pleased, will make him free from waning.
m.4.14.35: Sūta said: Hearing these words of Brahmā, all those gods and sages returned and then came to where Dakṣa and the Moon were.
m.4.14.36: Then the gods, taking the Moon and reassuring Dakṣa, and all the sages, went to Prabhāsa and there performed—
m.4.14.37: —having invoked the best of sacred waters, Sarasvatī and the rest, worship with an earthen liṅga according to the Mṛtyuñjaya rite.
m.4.14.38: Then all those gods and the pure-minded sages, having established the Moon at Prabhāsa, joyfully went each to his own abode.
m.4.14.39: The Moon performed austerities continuously for six months, and the bull-bannered Śiva was worshipped with the Mṛtyuñjaya mantra.
m.4.14.40: Having repeated that mantra ten crore times and meditating on the Mṛtyuñjaya mantra, the Moon remained with an unwavering mind.
m.4.14.41: Having seen him, the god Śaṅkara, the Lord, became pleased. Then, appearing before him, the one who is affectionate to his devotees spoke to the Moon, his own devotee.
m.4.14.42: Śaṅkara said: Choose a boon — may good be with you — whatever is desired by your mind. I am pleased, O Moon; I will grant everything, a boon unsurpassed.
m.4.14.43: Candra said: If you are pleased, O Lord of the gods, what could be unattainable for me? Even so, O Śaṅkara, ward off the waning of my body.
m.4.14.44: And may my offence be forgiven; do me good always. When this had been said by him, Śiva then spoke these words.
m.4.14.45: Śiva said: In one fortnight, O Candra, let your digit wane day by day; and in the other fortnight let that digit grow again continuously.
m.4.14.46: Sūta said: When it was so, the gods, their minds overflowing with joy, and likewise all the sages, came together quickly, O brahmins.
m.4.14.47: Having come, they all then pronounced blessings upon Candra; bowing to Śiva and joining their palms, they prayed to him with reverence.
m.4.14.48: The gods said: O God of gods, Mahādeva, Supreme Lord, salutations to you. Together with Umā, O Śambhu, O Master, remain here firmly.
m.4.14.49: Sūta said: Then Śaṅkara, who had earlier been praised by Candra with true devotion, the Lord who is formless, became endowed with form once more.
m.4.14.50: And being pleased, for the sake of the glory of the holy site for the gods and for Candra's fame, Śaṅkara there, by the name of Candra,
m.4.14.51: became renowned in the three worlds by the name Someśvara, the destroyer, through his worship, of diseases such as consumption and leprosy, O brahmins.
m.4.14.52: Blessed is he, fulfilled is he Candra, by whose name Śaṅkara himself, the Lord of the worlds, abides there, purifying the surface of the earth.
m.4.14.53: That pool was established right there by all those gods; and there, moreover, it remains never separated from Śiva and Brahmā.
m.4.14.54: It is famed on earth as Candrakuṇḍa, the destroyer of sins. The man who bathes there is freed from all sins.
m.4.14.55: All diseases, beginning with consumption, which are indeed incurable — they all go to destruction merely by bathing there for six months.
m.4.14.56: And having circumambulated Prabhāsa, the pure-souled one obtains the merit that comes from going around the whole earth; when he dies he is honoured in heaven.
m.4.14.57: Having seen the Soma-liṅga, a man is freed from all sin; having obtained the fruit his mind desires, when he dies he attains heaven.
m.4.14.58: Whatever fruit one aims at when performing the pilgrimage to this excellent tīrtha, that very fruit he obtains in every way; there is no doubt about this.
m.4.14.59: Thus those sages and gods, having seen such a fruit, joyfully bowed to Śiva and, taking with them the Moon, now free from waning,
m.4.14.60: and having circumambulated that tīrtha, they departed, praising it. And Candra too took up again his own ancient task.
m.4.14.61: Thus the whole origin of Someśa has been related. In this way the Someśvara liṅga came into being, O lords of sages.
m.4.14.62: The man who hears of its origin, or causes others to hear it, obtains all his desires and is freed from all sins.
m.4.14.iti: Thus ends the fourteenth adhyāya, named The origin of the Somanātha jyotirliṅga, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.4.15.1: Sūta said: After this I shall relate the origin of Mallikārjuna, on hearing which a devoted and wise person is freed from all sins.
m.4.15.2: What was told before, that I tell again: the divine story of Kumāra, which destroys all sins.
m.4.15.3: When Kumāra, the son of Śivā, the mighty foe of Tāraka, having gone round the earth, came back to Kailāsa,
m.4.15.4: then the divine sage Nārada came and told him the whole affair—the marriage of the lord of the gaṇas Gaṇeśa and the rest—misleading him by his own cunning.
m.4.15.5: Hearing that, Kumāra bowed to his two parents and went to the Krauñca mountain, even though restrained by them.
m.4.15.6: When his mother Girijā was grieved by separation from Kumāra, then Śambhu, who gives good understanding, spoke to her:
m.4.15.7: Why are you sad, beloved? Do not grieve, Pārvatī. Your son will come back, O fair-browed one; let this intense sorrow be abandoned.
m.4.15.8: When Pārvatī, deeply grieved, did not accept that, then Śaṅkara sent the divine sages there.
m.4.15.9: All the gods and sages, together with the gaṇas, joyful and wise, went there to bring back Kumāra.
m.4.15.10: Going there, they all bowed deeply to Kumāra and, having appealed to him in many ways, made their request with respect.
m.4.15.11: But Kumāra, the venerable one, overcome by great pride, did not accept that request of the gods and others, though it was filled with Śiva's command.
m.4.15.12: Then they all returned to Śiva, bowed, and having received Śaṅkara's command, went each to his own abode.
m.4.15.13: Then, as he did not come, the goddess Girijā felt the pain of separation from her son, and Śambhu too fell into great sorrow.
m.4.15.14: Then the two, very grieved and dejected, following worldly custom, went out of great affection to where their son was staying.
m.4.15.15: That son, called Kumāra, learning of his parents' arrival at the mountain, went far away—three yojanas—out of lack of affection.
m.4.15.16: When their son had gone far from the Krauñca mountain, the two settled there, assuming the form of light.
m.4.15.17: Afflicted by love for their son, Śiva and Śivā go on each parva day to see their own son Kumāra.
m.4.15.18: On the new-moon day Śambhu himself goes there; on the full-moon day Pārvatī certainly goes there.
m.4.15.19: From that day onward, the unique liṅga of Śiva called Mallikārjuna became famous in the three worlds.
m.4.15.20: Whoever beholds that liṅga is freed even from all sins—there is no doubt of this—and would obtain all his desires.
m.4.15.21: Sorrow departs far away and he gains supreme bliss; he never again undergoes the suffering born of a mother's womb.
m.4.15.22: Abundance of wealth and grain, renown and health, and the attainment of desired fruits arise—there is no doubt of this.
m.4.15.23: Thus has been told the second jyotirliṅga, named Mallika, which by its sight bestows every happiness; it was narrated for the good of the world.
m.4.15.iti: Thus ends the fifteenth adhyāya, named The second jyotirliṅga, named Mallikārjuna, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivapurāṇa.
m.4.16.1: The sages said: O Sūta, through the grace of Vyāsa you know every matter. Having heard the story of the Jyotis the jyotirliṅgas, we do not feel satisfied at all.
m.4.16.2: Therefore, O lord, showing us incomparable kindness in particular, tell us now about the third jyotirliṅga.
m.4.16.3: Sūta said: I am blessed, I have fulfilled my purpose, since I have come into the company of you illustrious ones, O brahmins. Blessed indeed is the company of the good.
m.4.16.4: Therefore, considering it my good fortune, I shall tell the purifying, divine story that destroys sins; listen with reverence.
m.4.16.5: There is the lovely city of Avantī, which grants liberation to all embodied beings; dear to Śiva, supremely holy, it purifies the world.
m.4.16.6: There lived an excellent brahmin, devoted to auspicious rites, a student of the Vedas, always engaged in Vedic rituals.
m.4.16.7: Having established the sacred fires and ever devoted to Śiva's worship, the brahmin worshipped an earthen image of Śiva every day.
m.4.16.8: Having obtained the fruit of all his rites, the brahmin Vedapriya, ever devoted to true knowledge, attained the goal of the good.
m.4.16.9: His four sons were like him, excellent sages, always devoted to Śiva's worship and never inferior to their parents.
m.4.16.10: Devapriya was the eldest of them, Priyamedhas came next, the third was named Sukṛta, and the fourth Dharmavāhī, of good vows.
m.4.16.11: Through the power of their merit, happiness grew on earth, just as the moon waxes continually in the bright fortnight.
m.4.16.12: So too their virtues, bringing happiness, kept increasing there, and that city then became filled with brahminical splendour.
m.4.16.13: Meanwhile, hear, O best of brahmins, the excellent event that happened there; I shall tell it as I have heard it.
m.4.16.14: On the mountain Ratnamāla there was a great asura named Dūṣaṇa, a mighty king of the Daityas, ceaselessly hostile to dharma.
m.4.16.15: By the boon granted by Brahmā he treated the world as worthless; the gods were defeated by him and likewise driven from their abodes.
m.4.16.16: On earth the Vedic and Smṛti duties were entirely shattered by that wicked one, just as hares are by a lion.
m.4.16.17: As many Vedic observances as there were, all were driven far away; at every sacred ford and holy site dharma was likewise taken far away.
m.4.16.18: Only the lovely city of Avantī is still seen there with dharma intact; having reflected thus, hear what he then did.
m.4.16.19: That great asura Dūṣaṇa, accompanied by a large army, came there, aiming at all the brahmins living there.
m.4.16.20: Having arrived there, that lord of the Daityas, the great villain and enemy of brahmins, summoned four excellent Daityas and spoke these words.
m.4.16.21: The demon said: Why do these wicked brahmins not obey my command? Devoted as they are to Vedic dharma, all of them deserve punishment in my view.
m.4.16.22: All the gods and kings in the world have been defeated by me; can the brahmins not be brought under control, O best of Daityas?
m.4.16.23: If they wish to live, then let them abandon the dharma of Śiva and the supreme dharma of the Vedas and become partakers of happiness.
m.4.16.24: Otherwise their lives will be in danger. This I have spoken truly; carry it out without hesitation.
m.4.16.25: Sūta said: Having resolved thus, those four Daityas then appeared in the four directions like fires, as at the dissolution of old.
m.4.16.26: Then those brahmins, hearing of the Daityas' undertaking, felt no distress there, being absorbed in meditation on Śiva.
m.4.16.27: Resorting to firmness, those brahmins did not move even a hair's breadth from their supreme meditation. What are those wretches before Śiva?
m.4.16.28: Meanwhile the fair city was overrun by them, and the people, tormented by them, came to the brahmins.
m.4.16.29: The people said: O masters, what should be done? The wicked ones have arrived; many people have been harmed, and they have come near.
m.4.16.30: Sūta said: Hearing these words of theirs, those sons of Vedapriya, ever trusting in Śaṅkara, spoke to those brahmins.
m.4.16.31: The brahmins said: Listen: we have no strength to frighten the wicked, nor are there weapons by which they might be turned back.
m.4.16.32: Here our humiliation would be the humiliation of even an ordinary protector; how much more, then, will it be that of the all-powerful Śiva?
m.4.16.33: May the Lord Śiva protect us today from fear of the asuras; there is no other refuge in the world than Śiva, loving to his devotees.
m.4.16.34: Sūta said: Thus resolving on firmness, and having duly worshipped the earthen liṅga, those brahmins remained absorbed in meditation. Just then those brahmins were seen by the Daitya with his army.
m.4.16.35: Dūṣaṇa uttered the words, let them be killed, let them be slain. But those words spoken by the Daitya were not heard at all by the brahmins, the sons of Vedapriya, intent on the path of meditation on Śambhu.
m.4.16.36: Then, just as that evil-minded one wished to kill those brahmins, at that very moment a pit opened with a loud sound at the place of the earthen liṅga.
m.4.16.37: From that pit arose Śiva, bearing a fearsome form, renowned as Mahākāla, slayer of the wicked and refuge of the good.
m.4.16.38: I, Mahākāla, have arisen for the destruction of wicked ones like you. You villain, go far away from the presence of the brahmins.
m.4.16.39: Having said this, Mahākāla Śaṅkara then swiftly reduced Dūṣaṇa together with his army to ashes with a mere roar of huṃ.
m.4.16.40: Part of the army was slain by him, part of the army fled; and Dūṣaṇa was killed here by Śiva, the Supreme Self.
m.4.16.41: Just as darkness goes to destruction everywhere on seeing the sun, so too, on seeing Śiva, that army of the demon perished.
m.4.16.42: The drums of the gods resounded and a shower of flowers fell. All the gods, Hari, Brahmā and the others, likewise assembled.
m.4.16.43: Having bowed with devotion to that god Śaṅkara, who brings welfare to the world, the Brahmins, with palms joined, praised him with various hymns.
m.4.16.44: Having comforted the Brahmins, Śiva himself, Mahākāla, the great Lord, being very pleased, said: Ask for a boon.
m.4.16.45: Hearing that, all those Brahmins then, with palms joined, bowing deeply to Śiva with devotion, spoke with heads bent low.
m.4.16.46: The brahmins said: O Mahākāla, O Mahādeva, O Lord who punishes the wicked, O Śambhu, O Śiva, grant us liberation from the ocean of worldly existence.
m.4.16.47: O Śiva, you must remain right here for the protection of the world. O Śambhu, O Lord, always deliver the people who behold you.
m.4.16.48: Sūta said: Thus addressed by them, Śiva remained there in that very beautiful pit, for the protection of his devotees, having granted them the good destination.
m.4.16.49: Those Brahmins attained liberation; and then the abode of Śiva, who is in the form of the liṅga, extended for a krośa in the four directions.
m.4.16.50: Śiva became famous on earth by the name Mahākāleśvara. O Brahmins, one who has seen him will not suffer even the slightest sorrow, even in a dream.
m.4.16.51: Whoever worships that liṅga with whatever desire in mind obtains that very desire, and also gains liberation in the hereafter.
m.4.16.52: O you of good vows, all this has been related: the origin and the glory of Mahākāla. What else do you wish to hear?
m.4.16.iti: Thus ends the sixteenth adhyāya, named The greatness of the Mahākāla jyotirliṅga, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.4.17.1: The sages said: O greatly wise one, tell us again the greatness of the jyotirliṅga bearing the name Mahākāla, the protector of its devotees.
m.4.17.2: Sūta said: O Brāhmaṇas, listen attentively to the greatness of the Mahākāla liṅga, which brings about the protection of devotees and increases devotion.
m.4.17.3: In Ujjayinī there was a great king named Candrasena, who knew the true meaning of all the scriptures, a devotee of Śiva, with senses subdued.
m.4.17.4: O twice-born ones, that king had a friend, the gaṇa Maṇibhadra, a chief among the gaṇas of Girīśa, honoured by all the worlds.
m.4.17.5: Once that lord of gaṇas, the generous-minded Maṇibhadra, with a pleased face, gave him a great jewel, the Cintāmaṇi.
m.4.17.6: That jewel, shining like the Kaustubha and resembling the sun, surely bestows auspiciousness whether it is meditated upon, seen, or even heard of.
m.4.17.7: Bronze, copper, iron, tin, stone and the like, or anything else touched by the surface of its radiance, quickly becomes gold.
m.4.17.8: Wearing the Cintāmaṇi on his neck, King Candrasena, who had taken refuge in Śiva, shone exceedingly, like the sun in the midst of the gods.
m.4.17.9: Hearing that Candrasena, the best of kings, wore the Cintāmaṇi on his neck, all the kings of the earth became agitated at heart with greed.
m.4.17.10: All the jealous, foolish kings begged Candrasena by various means for that jewel obtained from a divine being.
m.4.17.11: O Brāhmaṇas, the request of all the kings was rendered futile by that Candrasena, a firm devotee of Mahākāla.
m.4.17.12: Thus slighted by King Candrasena, all those kings of all the lands then became enraged.
m.4.17.13: Then all those kings, equipped with fourfold armies, became ready, it is said, to conquer Candrasena in battle.
m.4.17.14: All of them, having assembled and made a mutual agreement on signals, with many soldiers besieged the four gates of Ujjayinī.
m.4.17.15: Seeing his own city being besieged by all the kings, the king went for refuge to that very Mahākāleśvara.
m.4.17.16: Free of doubt, fasting, firm in resolve, with mind fixed on nothing else, that king worshipped Mahākāla day and night.
m.4.17.17: Then the blessed Śambhu Mahākāla, pleased in mind, devised a means to protect him; hear it attentively.
m.4.17.18: At that very time, O Brāhmaṇas, a certain cowherd woman wandering in that best of cities came with her child near Mahākāla.
m.4.17.19: Carrying a boy five years of age, she, a widow, watched with reverence the worship of Mahākāla performed by the king.
m.4.17.20: Having seen that most wondrous worship of Śiva performed by him, she bowed down and returned again to her own camp.
m.4.17.21: The cowherdess's son, having seen all this completely, out of curiosity set his mind on performing that worship of Śiva.
m.4.17.22: Bringing a pleasing stone, he with devotion set it up as a Śiva-liṅga in an empty spot within the camp, not far from his own dwelling.
m.4.17.23: Having established it, he worshipped it with fragrances, ornaments and garments, with incense, lamps, unbroken rice and the like, and also prepared a food offering with make-believe substances.
m.4.17.24: Worshipping again and again with lovely leaves and flowers, and performing various dances, he bowed down repeatedly.
m.4.17.25: At this time, that cowherd woman affectionately called her son, whose good mind was absorbed in Śiva, to have his meal.
m.4.17.26: When the boy, his mind steeped in Śiva's worship, did not want food even though called many times, then the mother went there.
m.4.17.27: Seeing him seated before Śiva with eyes closed, she seized his hand, dragged him, and struck him in anger.
m.4.17.28: When her son, though dragged and beaten, still did not come, she destroyed that worship, throwing the liṅga far away.
m.4.17.29: Scolding her son, who was crying out alas, alas in distress, the cowherd woman, filled with anger, went back into her house.
m.4.17.30: Seeing the worship of the trident-bearing god destroyed by his mother, the boy cried out, O God of gods, and fell down.
m.4.17.31: Overwhelmed by grief, he suddenly lost consciousness; regaining consciousness after a moment, he opened his eyes.
m.4.17.32: At that very moment, by Śiva's grace, the child soon saw there a beautiful shrine of Mahākāla that had come into being.
m.4.17.33: It had a large golden door, an excellent arched gateway with doors, and was resplendent with a platform of precious, flawless blue diamonds.
m.4.17.34: It was furnished with many wonderful pitchers of refined gold, with brilliantly shining jewelled pillars and floors inlaid with crystal.
m.4.17.35: In its midst the cowherdess's son saw the jewelled liṅga of Śaṅkara, the treasury of compassion, along with the worship he himself had offered.
m.4.17.36: Seeing it, the child rose up at once, amazed in mind, and was as though immersed in an ocean of supreme bliss.
m.4.17.37: Then, having praised Giriśa and bowed again and again, the boy left the temple of Śiva when the sun had set.
m.4.17.38: Then he saw his own dwelling, resembling the city of Purandara (Indra), instantly turned to gold, wonderful and supremely radiant.
m.4.17.39: Rejoicing, at nightfall he entered the house, endowed with every splendour and strewn with masses of jewels and gold.
m.4.17.40: There he saw his mother sleeping, bearing divine marks, her limbs shining with jewelled ornaments, like a very celestial maiden.
m.4.17.41: Then, O brahmins, that son, a recipient of Śiva's grace, overwhelmed with joy, quickly raised his mother up.
m.4.17.42: Having risen and beheld the marvel, she found everything as though never seen before; deeply immersed in great bliss, she embraced that son of hers.
m.4.17.43: Having heard from her son's mouth all about the grace of Girijā's lord, she informed the king, who worships Śiva unceasingly.
m.4.17.44: That king, having completed his observance, came at once in the night and saw the power of the cowherdess's son, which had pleased Śiva.
m.4.17.45: Having seen all that, the king, together with his ministers and priest, was plunged, beside himself, into an ocean of supreme bliss.
m.4.17.46: That king Candrasena, shedding tears out of love and joyfully uttering Śiva's name, embraced that boy.
m.4.17.47: O twice-born ones, a wondrous great festival arose there, and all, overwhelmed with joy, sang the praises of Maheśa.
m.4.17.48: Thus, owing to the most wondrous happenings, the sight of Śiva's greatness, and the excitement of the citizens, that night passed like a moment.
m.4.17.49: Then at dawn the kings, who were stationed besieging the city for battle, heard of that event from the mouths of their spies.
m.4.17.50: Hearing that, all those kings who had come there, having assembled and being greatly astonished, spoke thus to one another.
m.4.17.51: The kings said: This king Candrasena is a devotee of Śiva, very hard to conquer, the unperturbed lord of Ujjayinī, the city of Mahākāla.
m.4.17.52: He in whose city even such children are devoted to Śiva's vows — that king Candrasena is truly a great servant of Śaṅkara.
m.4.17.53: Surely, by opposing him, Śiva will become angry, and from that anger we shall all be destroyed.
m.4.17.54: Therefore peace must certainly be made with this king; when that is done, Maheśāna will show supreme compassion.
m.4.17.55: Sūta said: Having resolved thus, those kings gave up their enmity and became well-intentioned; all of them were well pleased and laid down the weapons and missiles in their hands.
m.4.17.56: Those kings entered the lovely city of Mahākāla and, with Candrasena's approval, worshipped Mahākāla.
m.4.17.57: Then those kings went to the house of the cowherd woman, all praising her good fortune and divine exaltation.
m.4.17.58: There they were received and honoured by Candrasena, who came forward to meet them; seated on very costly seats, greatly amazed, they rejoiced in return.
m.4.17.59: Seeing the Śiva temple that had appeared through the grace of the cowherd's son, and the Śiva-liṅga, they fixed their minds supremely on Śiva.
m.4.17.60: Then all those kings, pleased and seeking Śiva's grace, gave many things to that cowherd boy.
m.4.17.61: All the kings made him alone the king of all the cowherds who dwell in great numbers in every land.
m.4.17.62: Meanwhile, the radiant Hanumān, lord of the monkeys, worshipped by all the gods, appeared.
m.4.17.63: At his very arrival those kings, filled with excitement, rose up and bowed, their bodies bent low in devotion.
m.4.17.64: Seated among them and honoured, the lord of the monkeys embraced the cowherd's son and, looking at the kings, said this.
m.4.17.65: Hanumān said: Let all of you listen — blessings upon you — you kings and all embodied beings: apart from Śiva there is no other refuge for embodied beings.
m.4.17.66: Thus, by good fortune, this cowherd's son, having watched the worship of Śiva and having worshipped Śiva even without mantras, has attained Śiva.
m.4.17.67: This foremost devotee of Śambhu, who enhances the fame of the cowherds, will enjoy all pleasures here and in the end attain liberation.
m.4.17.68: In his lineage, the eighth descendant will be the greatly renowned one named Nanda; Kṛṣṇa, Nārāyaṇa himself, will become his son.
m.4.17.69: From today onward in this world, this cowherd boy will attain great worldwide fame under the name Śrīkara.
m.4.17.70: Sūta said: Having spoken thus, Añjanī's son, the lord of monkeys, a form of Śiva, looked upon all the kings and Candrasena with a compassionate gaze.
m.4.17.71: Then, with great affection, he taught that wise cowherd's son Śrīkara the Śaiva discipline dear to Śiva.
m.4.17.72: Then, O brahmins, Hanumān, well pleased, having blessed Candrasena and Śrīkara, vanished right there while all looked on.
m.4.17.73: And all the kings, delighted and honoured in return, took leave of him and of Candrasena and went back as they had come.
m.4.17.74: Śrīkara too, of great splendour, instructed by Hanumān, performed the worship of Śambhu together with brahmins versed in dharma.
m.4.17.75: The great king Candrasena and the cowherd boy Śrīkara both worshipped Mahākāla with supreme love.
m.4.17.76: In time, that Śrīkara and King Candrasena, having fully worshipped Mahākāla, attained the supreme state.
m.4.17.77: Such is the Mahākāla Śiva-liṅga, the refuge of the good; Śaṅkara, ever the slayer of the wicked, is loving towards his devotees.
m.4.17.78: This narrative has been told — purifying, supremely secret, bestowing all happiness, leading to heaven, and increasing devotion to Śiva.
m.4.17.iti: Thus ends the seventeenth adhyāya, named The greatness of the Mahākāla jyotirliṅga, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.4.18.1: The sages said: O Sūta, O Sūta, most fortunate one, you have indeed narrated to us the wondrous story of the liṅga called Mahākāla, the protector of his own devotees.
m.4.18.2: And now, O best of the learned, kindly tell us about the fourth jyotirliṅga, that of the Supreme Lord at Oṃkāra, the remover of all sins.
m.4.18.3: Sūta said: O twice-born ones, I shall gladly tell you how the liṅga named Parameśa came to be at Oṃkāra. Listen, O great sages.
m.4.18.4: Once, at a certain time, the venerable sage Nārada, full of supreme devotion, went to Śiva named Gokarṇa and worshipped him there.
m.4.18.5: Then that best of sages came to Vindhya, lord of mountains; there he was worshipped by him with great honour.
m.4.18.6: Adopting the attitude, everything exists in me; nothing is ever lacking, he stood before Nārada.
m.4.18.7: Then Nārada, the destroyer of pride, having heard that pride of his, sighed and stood there. Hearing the sigh, Vindhya said this:
m.4.18.8: Vindhya said: What deficiency have you seen in me, the cause of your sighing? Hearing that, the great sage Nārada spoke these words:
m.4.18.9: Nārada said: Everything indeed exists in you, yet Meru is higher. He has a share even among the gods; you never have that.
m.4.18.10: Sūta said: Having said this, Nārada left that place as he had come. And Vindhya was deeply distressed: Fie upon my life and all else!
m.4.18.11: I shall worship Śambhu, the Lord of the universe, and perform austerities. Resolving thus in his mind, he took refuge in Śaṅkara.
m.4.18.12: Joyfully he went to the place where Oṅkāra himself is, and there he made an earthen image of Śiva.
m.4.18.13: Then, worshipping Śambhu continuously for six months, intent on meditation upon Śiva, he did not move from the place of his austerity.
m.4.18.14: Seeing Vindhya's austerity thus, the Lord of Pārvatī was pleased and revealed his own form, which is hard to attain even for yogins.
m.4.18.15: Pleased, he then said: Tell me what your mind desires. I am pleased with your austerity; I am the giver of what devotees desire.
m.4.18.16: Vindhya said: If you are pleased, O Lord of gods, grant me the understanding I desire, one that accomplishes my own purpose, O Śambhu; you are ever affectionate to your devotees.
m.4.18.17: Sūta said: Hearing that, the blessed Śambhu pondered long in his heart: This dull-witted Vindhya wants a boon that will cause distress to others.
m.4.18.18: What shall I do so that this gift of a boon to him becomes auspicious, so that a boon given by me does not bring suffering to others?
m.4.18.19: Sūta said: Nevertheless Śambhu granted him that excellent boon: O Vindhya, king of mountains, do as you wish.
m.4.18.20: At that time the gods and the pure-minded sages, having worshipped Śaṅkara, said: You must remain here.
m.4.18.21: Hearing the words of the gods, the Supreme Lord was pleased and gladly did just so, for the happiness of the worlds.
m.4.18.22: The single liṅga that was Oṅkāra became twofold: in the praṇava form that Sadāśiva came to be named Oṅkāra,
m.4.18.23: and that which arose in the earthen image became Parameśvara. O twice-born ones, both grant devotees their desires and bestow enjoyment and liberation.
m.4.18.24: Then the gods and likewise the sages performed their worship, and, having pleased the bull-bannered Śiva, they obtained many boons.
m.4.18.25: The gods went each to his own abode, and Vindhya too, greatly delighted, accomplished his own purpose and gave up his distress, O twice-born ones.
m.4.18.26: Whoever worships Śambhu thus will not dwell again in a mother's womb, and will obtain whatever fruit he desires; there is no doubt about this.
m.4.18.27: Sūta said: I have told you all this, the fruit connected with the origin of Oṅkāra. Next I shall describe the excellent liṅga Kedāra.
m.4.18.iti: Thus ends the eighteenth adhyāya, named The greatness of the Oṅkāreśvara jyotirliṅga, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.4.19.1: Sūta said: O twice-born ones, the two incarnations of Hari known as Nara and Nārāyaṇa performed austerities in the Bhārata region, at the Badarī hermitage itself.
m.4.19.2: Entreated by those two to be present for worship in an earthen liṅga, Śambhu, Śiva, comes every day into that liṅga, because he is subject to his devotees.
m.4.19.3: While those two incarnations of Viṣṇu, the Śaiva sons of Dharma, were thus worshipping Śambhu, a long time passed.
m.4.19.4: At one time there, the Supreme Lord, pleased, replied: I am pleased; let a boon be chosen from me.
m.4.19.5: When he had said this, Nara and Nārāyaṇa themselves then spoke there, desiring the welfare of the worlds.
m.4.19.6: Nara and Nārāyaṇa said: O Lord of gods, if you are pleased, if a boon is to be given by you, then, O Śaṅkara, remain here yourself in your own form for the sake of worship.
m.4.19.7: Sūta said: Thus addressed by the two, Śaṅkara, the Great Lord, himself then took his stand at Kedāra in the Himālaya, in the form of light.
m.4.19.8: And worshipped by those two, he who removes all sorrow and fear remained there for the benefit of the worlds and so that devotees might see him.
m.4.19.9: Śambhu then stood there himself, bearing the name Kedāreśvara, ever granting the desires of devotees through being seen and worshipped.
m.4.19.10: The gods and the ancient sages worship him here; each of them obtains the fruit desired by the mind from the well-pleased Maheśvara.
m.4.19.11: Those dwelling at the Badarī hermitage obtain it by constantly worshipping Bhava, since he always grants the desires of devotees.
m.4.19.12: From that day onward, for one by whom Kedāreśvara has been worshipped with devotion, sorrow is hard to find even in a dream.
m.4.19.13: He who, on seeing the Pāṇḍavas, assumed the form of a buffalo and, resorting to his māyā, set about fleeing right there,
m.4.19.14: and was caught there by the Pāṇḍavas, remaining with face turned downward; his tail was held by them, and he was entreated again and again.
m.4.19.15: He, bearing the name affectionate to devotees, remained there in that form; the head portion went to Nepal and abides there in that form.
m.4.19.16: Likewise he gave the command for daily worship; and Śambhu himself, being worshipped, remained there and bestowed boons.
m.4.19.17: Having worshipped him, the Pāṇḍavas then departed joyfully, having obtained all that their hearts desired, freed from all sorrow.
m.4.19.18: There, in the sacred field called Kedāra, Hara is directly present always, and is likewise worshipped by the people of Bhārata.
