m.4.19.19: He who, dear to Hara, offers a bracelet there near the form of Hara — that bracelet endowed with Hara's form —
m.4.19.20: and likewise, having seen the form, is released from all sins. He too who has gone to the Badarī forest becomes liberated while living.
m.4.19.21: Having seen the form of Nara, and likewise of Nārāyaṇa, and of Śambhu as Kedāreśvara, one becomes a partaker of liberation; there is no doubt.
m.4.19.22: Those devotees of Kedāreśa who die while on the road to him — they too certainly become liberated; no deliberation is needed on this.
m.4.19.23: Having gone there full of love, having worshipped Kedāreśa and drunk the water there, one does not obtain rebirth.
m.4.19.24: O Brahmins, in this Bhārata region Kedāreśa, the Lord of Nara and Nārāyaṇa, is to be worshipped by all beings with great devotion.
m.4.19.25: Though he is the Lord of all, he is especially the master of this region — Śambhu named Kedāra, the granter of all desires; there is no doubt.
m.4.19.26: O best of sages, this account which you asked about has been narrated; on hearing it one would remove all sin; no deliberation is needed on this.
m.4.19.iti: Thus ends the nineteenth adhyāya, named The greatness of the Kedāreśvara jyotirliṅga, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.4.20.1: Sūta said: After this I shall relate the greatness of Bhaimaśaṅkara (Bhīmaśaṅkara), by merely hearing which a man obtains everything he desires.
m.4.20.2: In the land called Kāmarūpa, Śaṅkara, out of desire for the welfare of the world, descended himself in person — he who is the vessel of auspiciousness and happiness.
m.4.20.3: Listen attentively, O lords of sages; I shall tell you why that Śaṅkara, the benefactor of the worlds, descended.
m.4.20.4: Long ago, O brahmins, there was a rākṣasa named Bhīma, of great valour, who caused suffering to all beings and was always destroying dharma.
m.4.20.5: Very mighty, he was born of Kumbhakarṇa in Karkaṭī, and he lived with his mother on the Sahya mountain.
m.4.20.6: When Kumbhakarṇa, the terror of the worlds, had been slain by Rāma, the rākṣasī remained by herself on the Sahya with her son.
m.4.20.7: One day, O brahmins, that boy Bhīma — wicked, a tormentor of the world, of fearsome prowess — questioned his mother Karkaṭī.
m.4.20.8: Bhīma said: Mother, who is my father, and where is he? Why do you live alone? I wish to know all this; tell me truly now.
m.4.20.9: Sūta said: Asked thus by her son, that wicked rākṣasī said to him: Listen, I shall tell you.
m.4.20.10: Karkaṭī said: Your father was Kumbhakarṇa, the younger brother of Rāvaṇa. That mighty one was killed by Rāma together with his brother.
m.4.20.11: Once, dear son, that rākṣasa Kumbhakarṇa came here and, being strong, enjoyed me by force long ago.
m.4.20.12: That mighty one went to Laṅkā, leaving me right here. I have never seen that Laṅkā; I live here alone.
m.4.20.13: My father was named Karkaṭa, and my mother is known as Puṣkasī. My husband was Virādha, who was slain by Rāma earlier.
m.4.20.14: When my dear husband was slain, I stayed by my parents' side; and my parents died here, burnt to ashes by a sage.
m.4.20.15: They had gone there to devour him, and were burnt then by the enraged, great-souled Sutīkṣṇa, rich in austerity, the disciple of Agastya.
m.4.20.16: So I became alone and grief-stricken, and I lived on the mountain, afflicted with sorrow, without support or shelter.
m.4.20.17: At that time the rākṣasa, Rāvaṇa's younger brother, came here and united with me; then he left me and went away.
m.4.20.18: Then you were born, of great strength and valour; and relying on you, I pass my time.
m.4.20.19: Sūta said: Hearing these words of hers, Bhīma of terrible prowess grew angry and reflected: What shall I do against Hari?
m.4.20.20: By him my father was slain, and likewise my maternal grandparents; Virādha too was killed by him — great sorrow has he caused.
m.4.20.21: If I am truly his son, I shall torment that Hari. Having so resolved, Bhīma went off to perform great austerity.
m.4.20.22: Directing himself to Brahmā, resorting to meditation with his mind, he then performed great austerity for a thousand years.
m.4.20.23: With arms raised, standing on one foot, fixing his gaze on the sun, Bhīma, the rākṣasa's son, remained thus.
m.4.20.24: From his head arose an extremely fierce radiance; scorched by it, the gods then went to Brahmā for refuge.
m.4.20.25: Bowing to the Creator with devotion, they praised him with various hymns; and they, along with Vāsava (Indra), made known their distress to Brahmā.
m.4.20.26: The gods said: O Brahmā, the radiance of the rākṣasa is set to torment the worlds. Whatever boon the wicked one asks for, grant it, O Ordainer.
m.4.20.27: Otherwise, burnt today by his intense radiance, we shall all go to destruction; therefore grant him what he asks.
m.4.20.28: Sūta said: Hearing their words, Brahmā, grandsire of the worlds, went to grant the boon and spoke these words:
m.4.20.29: Brahmā said: I am pleased; ask for the boon that is in your mind. Hearing this speech of the Ordainer, that rākṣasa spoke.
m.4.20.30: Bhīma said: If you are pleased, O lord of gods, and if a boon is to be given by you, then grant me today incomparable strength, O lotus-seated one.
m.4.20.31: Sūta said: Having said this, that rākṣasa bowed to Brahmā; and Brahmā, having granted him the boon, then returned to his abode.
m.4.20.32: The rākṣasa Bhīma, having obtained immense strength from Brahmā, came home, quickly bowed to his mother, and arrogantly said:
m.4.20.33: Bhīma said: Behold my strength now, mother. I shall bring great destruction upon the gods headed by Śakra, and upon Hari, their helper.
m.4.20.34: Sūta said: Having said this, Bhīma of terrible prowess first conquered the gods along with Vāsava, and drove them out of their respective abodes.
m.4.20.35: Then he defeated in battle Hari, who had been entreated for help by the gods; thereafter the daitya gleefully began to conquer the earth.
m.4.20.36: First he went there to conquer Sudakṣiṇa, the mighty lord of Kāmarūpa; then a fearful battle took place with him.
m.4.20.37: Then the asura Bhīma, by Brahmā's power — by the potency of the boon — defeated that great king, a mighty hero who had taken refuge in Śiva.
m.4.20.38: Having then conquered that mighty lord of Kāmarūpa, Bhīma of terrible prowess bound and beat him.
m.4.20.39: O brahmins, all the possessions of that king, the servant of Śiva — his kingdom with all its equipment — were seized by that wicked Bhīma.
m.4.20.40: And the king — most righteous, a lover of dharma, dear to Hara — was seized by him in fetters and placed in a solitary place.
m.4.20.41: There, at that time, having made an excellent earthen image of Śiva, he began the worship of Śiva alone, out of desire to please him.
m.4.20.42: Then he praised the Gaṅgā in many ways; and having performed mental bathing and the other rites, he performed the worship of Śaṅkara.
m.4.20.43: The best of kings performed it by the procedure for the earthen liṅga; and having duly done the meditation on him as it should be,
m.4.20.44: and having done all that with prostrations and hymns, preceded by mudrās and postures, he worshipped Śaṅkara with joy.
m.4.20.45: He repeated the five-syllabled mantra joined with the Praṇava (Om); he then found no opportunity to do any other work.
m.4.20.46: His wife too, the chaste lady renowned by the name Dakṣiṇā, the king's beloved, lovingly performed the earthen liṅga rite.
m.4.20.47: The couple, with one mind, constantly worshipped there Śaṅkara, who brings welfare to devotees, both devoted to the adoration of Śiva.
m.4.20.48: The demon, deluded by pride in his boon, abolished all sacrificial rites and the like, saying, let it be given to me.
m.4.20.49: Accompanied by a great army of wicked demons, he brought the whole earth under his control, O best of sages.
m.4.20.50: Abolishing all the dharma of the Vedas, of the śāstras, of the smṛtis and that born of the Purāṇas, the mighty one enjoyed everything himself.
m.4.20.51: The gods with Śakra (Indra) and likewise the sages were oppressed by him; they fell into extreme misery, and the Brahmins were driven out of the world.
m.4.20.52: Then all of them, distressed, gods and sages together with Vāsava, placing Brahmā and Viṣṇu at their head, went to Śaṅkara for refuge.
m.4.20.53: Praising with many hymns Śaṅkara, the benefactor of the worlds, they pleased him on the auspicious bank of the Mahākośī.
m.4.20.54: Having made an earthen image and worshipped it according to rule, they praised him in due order with various hymns, salutations and so on.
m.4.20.55: Thus praised then by the gods' hymns and the like, Śambhu became exceedingly pleased and said this to those gods.
m.4.20.56: Śiva said: O Hari, O Vidhi (Brahmā), O gods and all you sages, I am pleased. Ask for a boon: what task shall I do for you?
m.4.20.57: Sūta said: When these words had been spoken thus by Śiva, O Brahmins, the gods bowed deeply, joined their palms, and then spoke to Śiva.
m.4.20.58: The gods said: O Lord of gods, you know everything that lies in the minds of all; you are the inner controller of all; nothing is unknown to you.
m.4.20.59: Nevertheless, O Lord, let it be heard: at your command we tell our own sorrow. O Mahādeva, look on us with a compassionate glance.
m.4.20.60: The mighty demon, son of Karkaṭī, born of Kumbhakarṇa, empowered by the boon given by Brahmā, oppresses the gods incessantly.
m.4.20.61: Slay this demon named Bhīma, the giver of sorrow. Show mercy, O Maheśāna; do not delay, O Lord.
m.4.20.62: Sūta said: Thus addressed by all the gods, Śambhu, affectionate to his devotees, said, I shall bring about his death, and then spoke to the gods.
m.4.20.63: Śambhu said: The king, lord of Kāmarūpa, is my excellent devotee. Tell him this, O gods: the task will soon be accomplished.
m.4.20.64: Say: O Sudakṣiṇa, great king, lord of Kāmarūpa, master, you are especially my devotee; perform my worship with love.
m.4.20.65: I shall slay the wicked Daitya named Bhīma, empowered by the boon obtained from Brahmā, who has insulted you; there is no doubt.
m.4.20.66: Sūta said: Then all those immortals, filled with joy, went there and told that great king what Śambhu had said.
m.4.20.67: Having spoken thus to him, the gods attained supreme bliss, and all those great sages quickly went to their own hermitages.
m.4.20.iti: Thus ends the twentieth adhyāya, named The troubles caused by the demon Bhīma, in the Bhīmeśvara Jyotirliṅga Māhātmya, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.4.21.1: Sūta said: Śiva too, together with his gaṇas, went there out of a wish for his devotee's welfare; hidden, he stood near his own devotee, attentively, in order to protect him.
m.4.21.2: Meanwhile, there, the lord of Kāmarūpa then began an intense meditation in front of the earthen liṅga.
m.4.21.3: Someone went there and reported to the rākṣasa: The king is doing something like this — a hostile rite (ābhicārika) aimed at you.
m.4.21.4: Sūta said: Hearing that, the rākṣasa grew angry and, wishing to kill him, seized a sword and went toward the king.
m.4.21.5: Seeing there what was set up — the earthen liṅga and the rest — and observing its form and its purpose, the rākṣasa thought: This man is up to something.
m.4.21.6: Therefore I shall kill this king today by force, together with his ritual implements. Having reflected thus, the rākṣasa, furious, spoke to the king.
m.4.21.7: Bhīma said: Hey, hey, king, wicked soul, what are you doing now? Tell the truth and I will not kill you; otherwise I will certainly kill you.
m.4.21.8: Sūta said: Hearing his words, the lord of Kāmarūpa, filled with faith in Śiva, quickly reflected thus in his mind:
m.4.21.9: What is destined will surely happen; there is nothing to turn it back. Here everything depends on prārabdha (destiny already set in motion), and that prārabdha is declared to be Śiva himself.
m.4.21.10: The compassionate Śaṅkara is surely present here in the earthen liṅga. Will he not act here for my sake? Who then is this rākṣasa, and from where could he harm me?
m.4.21.11: He will surely make true his own promise, befitting himself; for it is heard in the Veda that the Lord Śiva is true to his vow.
m.4.21.12: His vow is: Whenever someone exceedingly cruel torments my devotee, I then kill that wicked one to protect the devotee; there is no doubt.
m.4.21.13: Thus taking hold of courage and meditating on the god Śaṅkara, the lord of the earth prayed with true devotion, in his mind alone:
m.4.21.14: I am yours, O great king; do as you wish. I am about to speak the truth here — do what is good for me.
m.4.21.15: Having meditated thus in his mind, the king, bound by the noose of truth, spoke truthful words, scorning the rākṣasa.
m.4.21.16: The king said: I worship the god Śaṅkara, protector of his devotees, lord of all moving and unmoving beings, the changeless one.
m.4.21.17: Sūta said: Hearing these words of the lord of Kāmarūpa, Bhīma, his limbs trembling with rage, spoke:
m.4.21.18: Bhīma said: I know your Śaṅkara. What will he do to me — he who was installed by my own paternal uncle like a servant?
m.4.21.19: Relying on his strength you hope to conquer me? Then you have conquered everything — no need to think about it.
m.4.21.20: As long as Śaṅkara, your protector, has not been seen by me, only so long do you serve him, deeming him your master — not otherwise at all.
m.4.21.21: Once I have seen him, O king, all that will become entirely clear. So keep this form of Śiva far away.
m.4.21.22: Otherwise, there will be danger for you today, no doubt. I, of terrible valour, will deal your master a sharp blow (lit. hand).
m.4.21.23: Sūta said: Hearing those words, King Kāmarūpeśvara, firm in his faith in Śaṅkara, quickly replied to him:
m.4.21.24: The king said: Lowly and faulty though I am, I will never abandon Śaṅkara; and my master, supreme above all, never abandons me.
m.4.21.25: Sūta said: Hearing these words of that king devoted to Śiva, the rākṣasa Bhīma laughed at him and quickly said to the king:
m.4.21.26: Bhīma said: He is an intoxicated one who constantly goes begging — does he even know his own form? And what commitment do yogins have to protecting devotees?
m.4.21.27: Make up your mind to this and stand completely aside; I and that master of yours will fight it out.
m.4.21.28: Sūta said: Addressed thus, that best of kings, a devotee of Śambhu firm in his vow, fearlessly replied to Bhīma, who was ever a source of misery to the worlds:
m.4.21.29: The king said: Listen, wicked rākṣasa: I cannot do what you ask. If anything is to be changed, let it be done by you — though whence do you have such power?
m.4.21.30: Sūta said: Addressed thus, he gathered his army, reviled the king, and then hurled his dreadful sword at the earthen liṅga.
m.4.21.31: Now behold this very day your master's might that brings joy to his devotees; so the mighty one said, laughing, together with the rākṣasas.
m.4.21.32: O brāhmaṇas, even before the sword touched the earthen liṅga, Hara himself manifested from that earthen liṅga.
m.4.21.33: Śiva said: Behold, I am Bhīmeśvara, manifested for protection. This is my vow of old: my devotee is always to be protected by me.
m.4.21.34: Therefore behold quickly my might that brings joy to devotees. Having said this, he split the sword in two with his Pināka.
m.4.21.35: Then the rākṣasa hurled his own trident; that trident of the wicked one too was shattered into a hundred pieces by Śambhu.
m.4.21.36: Again, O brāhmaṇas, he hurled a spear (śakti) at Śambhu; that too Śambhu swiftly cut into a hundred thousand pieces with his arrows.
m.4.21.37: Then he hurled a paṭṭiśa (sharp-edged spear) at Śiva; Śiva with his trident instantly cut it into pieces as small as sesame seeds.
m.4.21.38: Then a terrible battle took place between Śiva's gaṇas and the rākṣasas, bringing distress to those who watched.
m.4.21.39: Then in an instant the whole earth was thrown into turmoil, and all the oceans, together with the mountains, were agitated.
m.4.21.40: All the gods and sages became greatly distressed and said to one another: Śiva has been entreated in vain.
m.4.21.41: Nārada also came up to Śaṅkara, the consumer of sorrow, and right there, with joined palms and bowed head, entreated him.
m.4.21.42: Nārada said: Forgive, forgive, O Lord, O causer of bewilderment. What need is there of an axe for grass? Let them be slain quickly indeed.
m.4.21.43: Thus entreated, Lord Śambhu then reduced all the hosts of demons to ashes with the mere weapon of his roar huṃ.
m.4.21.44: O sage, all those demons were burnt up by Śaṅkara in a moment, swiftly, there, while all the gods looked on.
m.4.21.45: Just as fire turned into a forest blaze would burn up a forest, so the enraged Śiva burnt up the army of the demons in an instant.
m.4.21.46: And as for Bhīma himself, what became of his ashes was not known to anyone then. Burnt along with his retinue, his very name is heard nowhere.
m.4.21.47: Then, by Śiva's grace, the lords of sages attained peace, as did all the gods headed by Śakra, and the whole world regained well-being.
m.4.21.48: The flame of Maheśa's wrath spread forth from forest to forest, and those ashes of the demons pervaded the entire forest.
m.4.21.49: Then herbs sprang up that accomplish various purposes; through them men may attain a different form and likewise a different appearance.
m.4.21.50: Bhūtas, pretas, piśācas and the like would flee far away from them. There is no task, O brāhmaṇas, that is not accomplished through them.
m.4.21.51: Śambhu was entreated by those gods, and especially by the sages: The Lord should remain here for the happiness of the worlds.
m.4.21.52: This region is indeed a vile one, causing distress to the people of Ayodhyā; but now, by seeing you, welfare will come about.
m.4.21.53: You shall be known by the name Bhīmaśaṅkara, the accomplisher of all. This liṅga is ever to be worshipped, the warder-off of all calamities.
m.4.21.54: Sūta said: Thus entreated, Śambhu, the benefactor of the worlds, independent and loving toward his devotees, gladly remained right there.
m.4.21.iti: Thus ends the twenty-first adhyāya, named The origin of the Bhīmeśvara jyotirliṅga and its greatness, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.4.22.1: Sūta said: Next I shall tell you — listen, O best of sages — the greatness of Viśveśvara, which destroys the great sins.
m.4.22.2: Whatever is seen here in the world, as a mere object, is in truth of the nature of consciousness and bliss, changeless and eternal.
m.4.22.3: In him alone, who delights in absolute oneness, there then arose the desire for a second. He himself became endowed with attributes and is called Śiva.
m.4.22.4: He indeed became twofold, through the distinction of male and female forms. The male is known as Śiva; the female is called Śakti.
m.4.22.5: By those two, whose nature is consciousness and bliss, two persons were also created —
m.4.22.6: — by those two who were then unseen, spontaneously, O best of sages. Then those two, not seeing their own mother and father, O brahmins,
m.4.22.7: — those two, Prakṛti and Puruṣa, fell into great doubt. Then a voice arose from the attributeless Supreme Self: Austerity must be performed; from it will come the most excellent creation.
m.4.22.8: Prakṛti and Puruṣa said: But there is no place for austerity. Where now, O Lord, should we two stay and perform austerity at your command, O Śiva?
m.4.22.9: Then, the essence of radiance, auspicious, measuring five krośas, a beautiful city furnished with all requisites —
m.4.22.10: — having been fashioned, was sent as his own by the attributeless Śiva; and it stood in the sky near the Puruṣa.
m.4.22.11: Then, occupying it, Hari, with the desire for creation, performed austerity for a long time, resorting to meditation on him.
m.4.22.12: From the exertion, various streams of water then arose; that void was pervaded by them, and nothing else was seen.
m.4.22.13: Then Viṣṇu looked: What is this wonder that is seen? Seeing this marvel, he shook his head.
m.4.22.14: Then a jewel fell from his ear in front of the Lord; that became the great tīrtha named Maṇikarṇikā.
m.4.22.15: When that Pañcakrośī was being swept away in the flood of waters, it was then swiftly held up by the attributeless Śiva on his trident.
m.4.22.16: Viṣṇu slept right there with Prakṛti, his consort. From his navel-lotus Brahmā was born at Śaṅkara's command.
m.4.22.17: Having received Śiva's command, he then made a wondrous creation, in which fourteen worlds were fashioned within the cosmic egg.
m.4.22.18: The extent of the cosmic egg has been declared by the sages to measure fifty crores of yojanas.
m.4.22.19: How will beings in the cosmic egg, bound by karma, attain me again? Reflecting thus, Śiva kept the Pañcakrośī separate.
m.4.22.20: And this is held to be the bestower of auspiciousness in the world, the destroyer of karma. Kāśī reveals liberation, grants knowledge, and is very dear to me.
m.4.22.21: The Avimukta liṅga has been installed by the Supreme Self himself. This holy field must never be abandoned by you, O portion of mine.
m.4.22.22: Having said this, Hara himself took Kāśikā down from his trident and released it into the world, into the realm of mortals.
m.4.22.23: Even at the end of Brahmā's day it certainly does not perish; then, O sages, Śiva holds it up on his trident.
m.4.22.24: And when creation is made again by Brahmā, it is set back in place, O brahmins. Because it drags away (karṣaṇa) karmas, it is called Kāśī.
m.4.22.25: The Avimukteśvara liṅga abides in Kāśī always, granting liberation to people, even to great sinners.
m.4.22.26: Elsewhere liberation such as sārūpya is attained, O lords of sages; here alone souls attain the supreme liberation of sāyujya.
m.4.22.27: For those who have no refuge anywhere, the city of Vārāṇasī is the refuge: the Pañcakrośī, most holy, destroyer of crores of killings.
m.4.22.28: All the immortals long for death here — what then of others? This city, ever dear to Śaṅkara, grants both enjoyment and liberation.
m.4.22.29: Brahmā praises it, and Viṣṇu, the Siddhas and yogins, the sages likewise, and other people dwelling in the three worlds, always.
m.4.22.30: I cannot describe the whole glory of Kāśī even in hundreds of years; therefore I speak as far as I am able.
m.4.22.31: He who is the lord of Kailāsa — sattva within, tamas without, renowned by the name Kālāgni, Bhava, attributeless yet possessed of attributes — with many prostrations spoke these words:
m.4.22.32: Rudra said: O Viśveśvara, O Maheśāna, I am yours, no doubt. Show grace, O Mahādeva, you who are with Ambā, to me, your son.
m.4.22.33: You should always remain right here, out of desire for the welfare of the worlds. Deliver them, O Lord of the world — I pray, O Master of the universe.
m.4.22.34: Sūta said: Avimukta too, self-controlled, having entreated him again and again and shedding tears, joyfully spoke to Śaṅkara.
m.4.22.35: Avimukta said: O God of gods, O Mahādeva, excellent remedy for the disease of time (death), you are truly the lord of the three worlds, to be served by Brahmā, Acyuta and others.
m.4.22.36: O God, let your capital be established by you in the city of Kāśī. I, absorbed in meditation, shall dwell here for the sake of inconceivable bliss.
m.4.22.37: You alone here are the giver of liberation and the granter of desires, no other. Therefore, for the world's benefit, remain here always together with Umā.
m.4.22.38: Carry all souls across the ocean of worldly existence, O Sadāśiva. Accomplish the purpose of your devotees, O Hara — I pray again and again.
m.4.22.39: Sūta said: Thus entreated by that Viśvanātha, Śaṅkara, the sovereign of all, stayed there too for the benefit of the worlds.
m.4.22.40: From the very day Hara came to Kāśī, from then on Kāśī became the most excellent of all.
m.4.22.iti: Thus ends the twenty-second adhyāya, named Rudra's coming to Kāśī, in the Viśveśvara Māhātmya, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.4.23.1: The sages said: O Sūta, if the great city Vārāṇasī is so holy, then tell us its power, and also that of Avimukta, O lord.
m.4.23.2: Sūta said: I shall tell you properly, in brief, the most splendid greatness of Vārāṇasī and of Viśveśvara; listen, O lords of sages.
m.4.23.3: Once the goddess Pārvatī, with supreme joy and out of concern for the world, asked Śaṅkara about the greatness of the two Avimuktas, the sacred field and its liṅga.
m.4.23.4: Pārvatī said: Please tell the greatness of this sacred field in full, showing kindness to me, out of a wish for the welfare of the worlds.
m.4.23.5: Sūta said: Hearing those words of the goddess, the god of gods, lord of the world, replied to Bhavānī for the good of living beings.
m.4.23.6: The Supreme Lord said: Well asked by you, O gracious one — a question auspicious and bringing happiness to the worlds. I shall truly tell you, as it is, the greatness of the two Avimuktas.
m.4.23.7: This Vārāṇasī is ever my most secret sacred field, in every way the cause of liberation for all beings.
m.4.23.8: In this field siddhas always dwell, having taken up my vow, bearing various emblems, constantly longing for my world.
m.4.23.9: Self-controlled and with senses subdued, they practise the great yoga, the supreme Vedic Pāśupata discipline, which yields the fruits of enjoyment and liberation.
m.4.23.10: Dwelling in Vārāṇasī always pleases me, O Maheśvarī, leaving all other places; hear for certain the reason why.
m.4.23.11: He who is my devotee and he who has true knowledge — both of them share in liberation. They have no need of holy places; for them what is enjoined and what is not enjoined are alike.
m.4.23.12: Those two should be known as liberated while living; wherever they die, they attain liberation at once — this is a definite word spoken by me.
m.4.23.13: There is something special about this supreme holy place called Avimukta; listen to it attentively, O goddess, O supreme Śakti.
m.4.23.14: All castes and all stages of life, the young, the youthful and the old — if they die in this city, they are liberated; there is no doubt.
m.4.23.15: Whether impure or pure, a maiden or a married woman, a widow or a barren woman, or one afflicted with menstrual impurity,
m.4.23.16: one who has just given birth, one without the sacraments — whatever kind she may be, O brahmins — if she dies in this field she partakes of liberation; there is no doubt here.
m.4.23.17: Whether sweat-born, egg-born, sprout-born or womb-born, a being that dies here attains liberation as nowhere else.
m.4.23.18: Here there is no need of knowledge, nor again of devotion; here, O goddess, there is no need of ritual action, nor indeed of charity.
m.4.23.19: Here there is no need of sacraments at all, never any need of meditation; likewise here there is no need of the divine name, of worship, or of noble birth.
m.4.23.20: Whatever man dwells in my liberation-giving field, if he dies in whatever way, he certainly attains liberation.
m.4.23.21: This divine city of mine, O beloved, is more secret than the secret; even Brahmā and the others do not know its greatness, O Pārvatī.
m.4.23.22: Therefore this great field is known as Avimukta; superior to all holy places such as Naimiṣa, it grants liberation upon death.
m.4.23.23: Truth is the secret essence of dharma, equanimity the secret essence of liberation; the wise know Avimukta as the secret essence of sacred fields and holy places.
m.4.23.24: Even while eating as he pleases, sleeping, playing and doing various acts, a being who gives up his life in Avimukta becomes fit for liberation.
m.4.23.25: For men, even having committed thousands of sins, the state of a piśāca in Kāśī is better — but not the fruit of a thousand sacrifices in heaven away from the city of Kāśī.
m.4.23.26: Therefore the city of Kāśī is resorted to with every effort, and Sadāśiva, the unmanifest liṅga, is meditated upon by the sages.
m.4.23.27: Whatever fruit men aim at when they perform austerities here, O beloved, that very fruit I surely grant them fully.
m.4.23.28: And afterwards I grant union with myself and the desired abode; for those who give up the body here there is no bondage of karma from any source.
m.4.23.29: Brahmā with the divine sages, Viṣṇu, and the Sun too, and all other great souls worship me here.
m.4.23.30: Even a man whose mind is attached to sense objects and who has lost his taste for dharma — if he dies in this field, he does not enter saṃsāra again.
m.4.23.31: How much more, then, those who are free of possessiveness, steadfast, established in sattva, free from hypocrisy, accomplished and without worldly undertakings — all of them are absorbed in me.
m.4.23.32: What a yogī might attain only after thousands of births, that supreme liberation he attains right here through death.
m.4.23.33: Here many liṅgas have been installed by devotees; here they grant all desires and liberation as well, O Pārvatī.
m.4.23.34: This field is declared to extend five krośas in the four directions; all around, likewise, it bestows immortality on a being at the time of death.
m.4.23.35: One who dies sinless attains liberation immediately; one who dies with sins undergoes a series of bodies.
m.4.23.36: Only after experiencing torment would he then attain liberation. He who commits a sin in this field called Avimukta, certainly,
m.4.23.37: undergoes the torment of Bhairava for ten thousand years, and then, having exhausted his sin, attains liberation, O beautiful one.
m.4.23.38: Thus I have described to you the destiny of those of sinful conduct. Knowing this, a man should properly serve Avimukta.
m.4.23.39: There is no destruction of deeds done, even in hundreds of crores of kalpas; karma done, good or bad, must inevitably be experienced.
m.4.23.40: Purely bad karma here leads to hell; good karma leads to heaven; from both together human birth is said to result.
m.4.23.41: Here in this world, birth is favourable or unfavourable according to the deficiency or excess of merit and demerit; and the destruction of both is liberation. This is truly so, O Pārvatī.
m.4.23.42: Karma is declared in the section on ritual action to be threefold, O Maheśvarī: the accumulated (sañcita), that being done (kriyamāṇa), and that which has begun to bear fruit (prārabdha); all cause bondage.
m.4.23.43: That which has arisen from previous births is called sañcita; that which is being experienced through the body is called prārabdha.
m.4.23.44: And the karma, auspicious or inauspicious, that is being done now in this birth, O Queen of the gods, the wise know as kriyamāṇa.
m.4.23.45: Prārabdha karma is destroyed only through being experienced, not otherwise; the destruction of the other two karmas comes by means such as worship.
m.4.23.46: There is no destruction of all karmas without the city of Kāśī. Every other holy place is easy to reach; the city of Kāśikā is hard to attain.
m.4.23.47: If the sight of Kāśī was obtained with reverence in a previous birth, then, having reached Kāśī, one attains death there, and not otherwise.
m.4.23.48: The man who, having reached Kāśī, bathes in the Gaṅgā—then there is destruction of his kriyamāṇa and also his sañcita karma.
m.4.23.49: It is firmly established that prārabdha does not perish without being experienced; when his death has occurred, then its destruction takes place.
m.4.23.50: If Kāśī has been visited earlier and afterwards one commits sin, then by that powerful seed he is led to Kāśī again.
m.4.23.51: Then all sins indeed turn to ashes. Therefore a man should resort to Kāśī, which surely uproots karma.
m.4.23.52: He by whom even a single brahmin has been settled to live in Kāśī, O beloved, himself obtains residence in Kāśī and thereby attains liberation.
m.4.23.53: He who dies in Kāśī has no birth again. And for one who dies at Prayāga with a specific intention, there is the fruit of that desire.
m.4.23.54: If there should be a conflict of the two, the fruit born of Kāśī non-rebirth would be in vain; and if that desired rebirth is not obtained, the fruit of the king of holy places Prayāga would be in vain.
m.4.23.55: Therefore, by my command, Viṣṇu directly fashions a new creation and surely grants the fulfilment of what was intended in the mind.
m.4.23.56: Sūta said: Such and more, O best of sages, is the great glory of Kāśī, and likewise of Viśveśvara, granting enjoyment and liberation to the good.
m.4.23.57: Next I shall relate the glory of Tryambaka, hearing which a man is freed from all sins in an instant.
m.4.23.iti: Thus ends the twenty-third adhyāya, named The greatness of the Kāśī Viśveśvara jyotirliṅga, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.4.24.1: Sūta said: Listen, O excellent sages, to a story that destroys sin; I shall tell it as I heard it from Vyāsa, my true teacher.
m.4.24.2: Long ago there was a renowned excellent sage named Gautama; his wife was named Ahalyā, supremely righteous.
m.4.24.3: In the southern direction is the mountain called Brahma giri; there he performed austerity for ten thousand years.
m.4.24.4: Once, O you of good vows, a terrible drought occurred there for a hundred years, and the people fell into misery.
m.4.24.5: Not even a moist leaf was seen on the face of the earth; how then could water, which sustains the life of beings, be seen?
m.4.24.6: Then the sages, men, cattle, birds and wild animals there went away in the ten directions.
m.4.24.7: Seeing that drought, some sages and brahmins, devoted to breath-control, passed that very terrible time in meditation.
m.4.24.8: Gautama himself also, devoted to breath-control, performed an auspicious austerity there for six months for the sake of Varuṇa.
m.4.24.9: Then Varuṇa came to grant him a boon and spoke these words: I am pleased; ask a boon and I shall give it.
m.4.24.10: Then Gautama asked him for rain; and then Varuṇa replied to the sage, O brahmins.
m.4.24.11: Varuṇa said: How could I, transgressing the command of God, bring that rain? Ask something else that I may do for you; you are wise.
m.4.24.12: Sūta said: Having heard these words of the great-souled Varuṇa, Gautama, benefactor of others, spoke.
m.4.24.13: Gautama said: If you are pleased, O lord of gods, if a boon is to be given to me, then what I ask today must be done by you accordingly.
m.4.24.14: Since you are the lord of the waters, give me water, O lord of all gods — inexhaustible, divine, and bestowing perpetual fruit.
m.4.24.15: Sūta said: Thus entreated by Gautama, Varuṇa said to him: Let a pit be dug by you.
m.4.24.16: When this was said, he dug a pit a hand's measure deep, and Varuṇa filled it with divine water.
m.4.24.17: Then the god Varuṇa, lord of waters, spoke to the sage Gautama, tiger among sages, rich in helping others.
m.4.24.18: Varuṇa said: May your water be inexhaustible and become a holy place (tīrtha), O great sage; it will be renowned on earth by your name.
m.4.24.19: Whatever is given here, offered in fire, performed as austerity, sacrifice made to the gods, and śrāddha done for the ancestors — all will become inexhaustible.
m.4.24.20: Sūta said: Having said this, the god, praised by that great seer, vanished; and the sage Gautama too attained happiness, having done a service to others.
m.4.24.21: Taking refuge with the great leads to greatness for men; the great perceive the true nature of that, not the other, inauspicious ones.
m.4.24.22: As is the man one serves, such is the fruit one reaps: by serving the great comes loftiness, and by serving the petty, pettiness.
m.4.24.23: Service in a lion's den is held to yield pearls; service in a jackal's den is known to yield bones.
m.4.24.24: This is the nature of the noble: inability to bear others' suffering. They consider it as their own suffering, and the other's suffering is warded off.
m.4.24.25: Trees, gold, sandalwood and sugarcane — these on earth are thus fit for others' benefit; no others are so.
m.4.24.26: The compassionate, one untouched by pride, the benefactor, and one who has conquered the senses — by these four pillars of merit the earth is upheld.
m.4.24.27: Then Gautama, having obtained that very rare water there, duly performed his daily and occasional rites.
m.4.24.28: Then the lord of sages had rice, barley and wild rice of many kinds sown right there for the fire-offerings.
m.4.24.29: Various grains, and likewise various trees, flowers and fruits, came to be there in abundance.
m.4.24.30: Hearing of that, other sages came there in thousands; cattle, birds and many other creatures also came.
m.4.24.31: That forest became supremely beautiful in the whole sphere of the earth; through the presence of that inexhaustible water, the drought caused no distress.
m.4.24.32: Many sages too, devoted to auspicious deeds, took up residence in that forest, accompanied by their disciples, wives and sons.
m.4.24.33: They had grains sown to pass the time; and there was joy in that forest through the power of Gautama.
m.4.24.iti: Thus ends the twenty-fourth adhyāya, named The power of Gautama, in the Tryambakeśvara Māhātmya, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.4.25.1: Sūta said: Once, his own disciples, Brahmins with water-pots in their hands, were sent by Gautama for water, and they went there devotedly.
m.4.25.2: Seeing the disciples who had come near the water, the sages' wives, who had also come there in great numbers for water, stopped them.
m.4.25.3: We are the sages' wives; we shall draw water first. Keep away. The water is to be taken by you afterwards; thus they scolded them.
m.4.25.4: Turning back, they reported it to the sage's wife Ahalyā. She, taking them along and reassuring them, herself together with them—
m.4.25.5: the ascetic woman fetched the water and gave it to Gautama. With that water the best of sages carried out his daily rites.
m.4.25.6: Those sages' wives, angered, rebuked her in this way; then all of them, crooked-minded, turned back and went to their huts.
m.4.25.7: Then the whole incident was reported in a distorted way before their husbands by those evil-minded women.
m.4.25.8: Then, hearing their words, by the power of destined karma, those great sages became furious with Gautama.
m.4.25.9: In order to create an obstacle for Gautama, those enraged, ill-minded ones worshipped Gaṇeśa with various offerings of worship.
m.4.25.10: Then Gaṇeśvara, pleased, appeared, and there he who is subject to his devotees, the giver of fruits, spoke these words.
m.4.25.11: Gaṇeśa said: I am pleased. Tell me a boon — what shall I do for you? Hearing those words of his, the sages then said:
m.4.25.12: The sages said: If a boon is to be granted by you, then bring it about that Gautama, after being rebuked, is driven out of his own hermitage by the sages.
m.4.25.13: Sūta said: Thus entreated by them, the elephant-faced one, the refuge of the good, smiled and spoke again with affection, trying to enlighten them.
m.4.25.14: Gaṇeśa said: Listen, all you sages: what you are now doing is not proper. For those who are angry with him though he has committed no offence, there is only harm.
m.4.25.15: Causing pain to those who formerly rendered help is surely not beneficial; when pain is inflicted on them, ruin results here.
m.4.25.16: By performing such austerity a supreme fruit is attained; having yourselves cast away the auspicious fruit, one should not again pursue what is harmful.
m.4.25.17: Sūta said: Hearing these words of his, those best of sages, overcome then by delusion of mind, said only this:
m.4.25.18: The sages said: O lord, you must do exactly this and nothing else. Thus addressed, Lord Gaṇeśa then spoke these words:
m.4.25.19: Gaṇeśa said: The wicked never attains goodness, nor the good wickedness — this is declared by Brahmā and is certain.
m.4.25.20: When formerly you suffered distress from starvation, then happiness was given to you by the great sage Gautama.
m.4.25.21: Now pain is being given to him by you. This is by no means proper in the world; consider it carefully.
m.4.25.22: Deluded by the influence of your women, you will not heed my words. Yet this will turn out to be most beneficial for him, no doubt.
m.4.25.23: Again this best of sages will surely give you happiness. Driving him out would not be proper; choose another boon.
m.4.25.24: Sūta said: Although these words were spoken thus to the sages by the great-souled Gaṇeśa, they still did not accept them.
m.4.25.25: Then, out of his dependence on his devotees, Śiva's son spoke with an indifferent mind to those sages of wicked intellect.
m.4.25.26: Gaṇeśa said: What you request, I shall certainly do accordingly. What is to follow will surely happen. Having said this, he vanished again.
m.4.25.27: Gautama did not know the evil intent of the sages; with a joyful mind he continually performed his rites together with his wife.
m.4.25.28: O lords of sages, listen to the episode that occurred in the meantime through the effect of the boon, owing to the influence of those wicked sages.
m.4.25.29: In Gautama's field there were rice and barley. Gaṇeśa, becoming a feeble cow, went there, it is said.
m.4.25.30: Trembling, she went there and, by the force of that boon, devoured the rice and barley, O best of sages.
m.4.25.31: Meanwhile, by fate, Gautama arrived there; the compassionate one then tried to drive her away with a tuft of grass.
m.4.25.32: Touched by the tuft of grass, she fell to the ground and died at that very moment, as the sage looked on.
m.4.25.33: Those sages, in disguise, and likewise the inauspicious sages' wives, all said there then: What has Gautama done?
m.4.25.34: Gautama too, greatly astonished, called Ahalyā and, O Brahmins, spoke in sorrow with an anguished heart:
m.4.25.35: Gautama said: What has happened, O goddess, and how has the Supreme Lord become angry? What is to be done, where should we go? The sin of killing has befallen us.
m.4.25.36: Sūta said: Meanwhile the Brahmins reviled Gautama, and likewise the Brahmins' wives caused Ahalyā distress with harsh words.
m.4.25.37: Their evil-minded disciples and their sons likewise, reviling Gautama, repeatedly shouted words of reproach:
m.4.25.38: The sages said: Your face is not fit to be seen; go away, go away. On seeing the face of a cow-killer, one must at once bathe with one's clothes on.
m.4.25.39: As long as you remain in the hermitage, neither the gods who consume oblations nor the ancestors will accept anything offered by us.
m.4.25.40: Therefore go elsewhere with your household; make no delay, you cow-slayer, you sinner.
m.4.25.41: Sūta said: Having said this, they all struck him with stones, and they caused him great distress, and tormented Ahalyā too with harsh words.
m.4.25.42: Struck and reviled by the wicked ones, Gautama spoke these words: O sages, I am going away from here; I shall dwell elsewhere.
m.4.25.43: Having said this, Gautama then left that place, and having gone the distance of a krośa, he then made a hermitage there with their permission.
m.4.25.44: As long as the curse remains, so long nothing is to be done; there is no entitlement to any rite — divine, ancestral, or Vedic.
m.4.25.45: Then, having passed half a month, that excellent sage Gautama, afflicted by that sorrow, earnestly entreated the sages.
m.4.25.46: Gautama said: I am to be pitied by you; let it be told to me — it will be done by me. Let it be made known how my sin may go away.
m.4.25.47: Sūta said: Thus addressed, those Brāhmaṇas did not then speak to him; but being asked with great deference, they assembled and stood together in one place.
m.4.25.48: Gautama, standing at a distance and bowing to those best of sages, full of humility, asked: What indeed should be done by me now?
m.4.25.49: When this had been said by that great-souled sage Gautama, all those sages, assembled together, spoke these words.
m.4.25.50: The sages said: Without expiation, purity never arises. Therefore, for the purification of your body, perform an atonement.
m.4.25.51: Go around the whole earth three times, proclaiming your sin; and coming back right here, observe a month-long vow likewise.
m.4.25.52: And having likewise performed one hundred and one circumambulations of this Brahma mountain, your purification will come about.
m.4.25.53: Or else, having brought Gaṅgā here, perform a bath in the Gaṅgā; and likewise, having made a crore of earthen liṅgas, worship the god.
m.4.25.54: Then, having bathed in the Gaṅgā, you will be purified. But first perform ten and one (eleven) circumambulations of the mountain.
m.4.25.55: And having likewise bathed the earthen liṅga with a hundred pots of water, expiation would come about. Thus addressed by those sages, Gautama accepted their word and said, so be it, Om.
m.4.25.56: O best of sages, by the command of your honoured selves, I shall perform here the worship of the earthen liṅgas and likewise the circumambulation of the mountain.
m.4.25.57: Having said this, that best of seers, the most excellent sage, performed the circumambulation of the mountain and, having fashioned earthen liṅgas, worshipped them.
m.4.25.58: Then the virtuous Ahalyā too did all that; and the disciples and the disciples' disciples then rendered service to the two of them.
m.4.25.iti: Thus ends the twenty-fifth adhyāya, named The ruling given to Gautama, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.4.26.1: Sūta said: O brahmins, when the sage together with his wife had done this, Śiva, pleased, then appeared together with Śivā and with his attendants (gaṇas).
m.4.26.2: Then the pleased one, with Śivā, the treasure-house of compassion, said: O great sage, ask for a boon; I am pleased with your fine devotion.
m.4.26.3: Then, having seen that beautiful form of the great-souled Śambhu, he bowed to Śaṅkara with devotion and, filled with joy, offered a hymn of praise.
m.4.26.4: Having praised him much and bowed to the Lord, he stood with joined palms; that Gautama said: O God, make me free of sin.
m.4.26.5: Sūta said: Having heard these words of the great-souled Gautama, Śiva became even more pleased and began to speak.
m.4.26.6: Śiva said: You are blessed, you have fulfilled your purpose, you are ever free of sin, O sage. You have indeed been deceived by these wicked, evil-minded men.
m.4.26.7: By the sight of you people indeed become free of sin; how then could you, ever devoted to me, be sinful?
m.4.26.8: O sage, those evil-souled ones by whom this harm was done to you—they themselves are sinful, of wicked conduct, and guilty of killing.
m.4.26.9: By seeing them, may others become most sinful. They have likewise become ungrateful; for them there is no atonement anywhere.
m.4.26.10: Sūta said: Having said this, O brahmins, Lord Śaṅkara—giver of good to the good and of punishment to the wicked—then told him at length of their misdeeds.
m.4.26.11: Having heard what Śarva said, the sage, his mind greatly astonished, bowed deeply to Śiva with devotion and, with joined palms, spoke again.
m.4.26.12: Gautama said: O Maheśāna, those sages have done me a great favour; had they not acted thus, how could I have gained the sight of you?
m.4.26.13: Blessed are those sages, by whom something most auspicious has been done for me; through their very misconduct a great good of my own has come about.
m.4.26.14: Sūta said: Hearing these words of his, Maheśvara, greatly pleased, looked at Gautama with a compassionate gaze and quickly replied.
m.4.26.15: Śiva said: O best of brahmins, you are a blessed sage, truly the most excellent of sages. Knowing me to be well pleased, choose an excellent boon.
m.4.26.16: Sūta said: Gautama too reflected thus: it is well known in the world that what has been decided cannot turn out otherwise; therefore one should act according to what has been declared.
m.4.26.17: Having resolved thus, Gautama, best of sages and devoted to Śiva, with joined palms and bowed head, spoke these words to Śaṅkara.
m.4.26.18: Gautama said: O Lord, you speak the truth; nevertheless, what has been determined by five people does not turn out otherwise. So here, let what has happened remain as it is.
m.4.26.19: If you are pleased, O Lord of gods, let Gaṅgā be given to me; do this good for the world. Salutations to you, salutations to you.
m.4.26.20: Sūta said: Having spoken these words, Gautama, desiring the good of the world, clasped the lotus feet of the Lord of gods and bowed to him.
m.4.26.21: Then Lord Śaṅkara drew forth the essence of earth and heaven which had been preserved from before—
m.4.26.22: —that little which had remained of what Brahmā had given at the wedding; Śambhu, loving to his devotees, gave it to the sage.
m.4.26.23: Then and there the Gaṅgā water took on a supreme female form; and the best of sages praised her and bowed to her.
m.4.26.24: Gautama said: You are blessed, you have fulfilled your purpose; the world has been purified by you. O Gaṅgā, purify me too, who am surely falling into hell.
m.4.26.25: Then Śambhu too, the benefactor of all, said: listen, O Gaṅgā: by my command, purify this Gautama.
m.4.26.26: Having heard these words of Śambhu and of Gautama, Gaṅgā—the purifying power of Śiva—spoke to Śiva.
m.4.26.27: Gaṅgā said: O Lord, having purified the sage together with his family, I shall go to my own abode; I speak the truth.
m.4.26.28: Sūta said: When Gaṅgā had said this there, Maheśa, loving to his devotees, for the benefit of the world spoke again to Gaṅgā.
m.4.26.29: Śiva said: You must stay right here until the Kali age arrives, the Kali age of the twenty-eighth cycle of Vaivasvata Manu, O goddess.
m.4.26.30: Sūta said: Having heard these words of her lord Śaṅkara, Gaṅgā, that purifying best of rivers, replied again.
m.4.26.31: Gaṅgā said: O lord Maheśvara, O destroyer of Tripura, if my glory is to be greater than that of all others, then I shall remain on earth.
m.4.26.32: And hear something more, O lord: you too, O Master, remain near me in a beautiful form, with your attendants and with Ambikā.
m.4.26.33: Sūta said: Having heard her words thus, Śaṅkara, loving to his devotees, for the benefit of the world spoke again to Gaṅgā.
m.4.26.34: Śiva said: You are blessed; listen, O Gaṅgā: I am not separate from you. Even so, I shall stay here, and you too should stay.
m.4.26.35: Sūta said: Having heard these words of the Supreme Lord, her master, Gaṅgā became glad at heart and worshipped him in return.
m.4.26.36: Meanwhile the gods, the ancient sages, and many holy tīrthas and various sacred sites—
m.4.26.37: —all came, crying Victory, victory! and reverently worshipped Gautama, Gaṅgā and Giriśa.
m.4.26.38: Then all those immortals, headed by Hari and Brahmā, with joined hands and bowed shoulders, joyfully offered praise to them.
m.4.26.39: Then the pleased Gaṅgā and Giriśa said to them: ask for a boon, O best of gods; we two will grant it out of desire to please you.
m.4.26.40: The gods said: If you are pleased, O Lord of gods, and you, O best of rivers, are pleased, then please stay here out of compassion, for our sake and likewise for the good of humankind.
m.4.26.41: Gaṅgā said: Why should you all not also stay here, for the sake of what is dear to everyone? Otherwise, after purifying Gautama, I shall go back the way I came.
m.4.26.42: O gods, how is my special distinction among you here to be known? If that is proven, then I shall stay without doubt.
m.4.26.43: They all said: When Jupiter (Guru), the best friend of all, is in the sign of Leo, then all of us will come here; there is no doubt.
m.4.26.44: For eleven years the sin of people here is washed off by us; in this way we become impure, O best of rivers.
m.4.26.45: To wash away that very impurity, O dear one, we shall certainly come into your presence, O great goddess; this truth is spoken with respect.
m.4.26.46: For the favour of the worlds and out of the wish to please us, Śaṅkara too, and you as well, should remain here, O best of rivers.
m.4.26.47: As long as Jupiter is in Leo, just so long shall we stay; bathing in you three times a day and beholding Śaṅkara,
m.4.26.48: having done these, we shall cast off all our sin, no doubt; and we shall go to our own regions by your command.
m.4.26.49: Sūta said: Thus entreated by them and by the great sage Gautama, Śaṅkara remained there with pleasure, and that best of rivers also remained.
m.4.26.50: That Gaṅgā became known by the name Gautamī, and the liṅga was called Tryambaka; it then became most renowned, the destroyer of great sins.
m.4.26.51: From that day onward, whenever Jupiter is in Leo, all the sacred fords, holy fields and deities come there.
m.4.26.52: Lakes such as Puṣkara, likewise rivers such as Gaṅgā, and gods such as Vāsudeva are present on the bank of the Gautamī.
m.4.26.53: As long as they remain there, for that long there is no fruit from them in their own places; only when they have returned to their own regions does their fruit arise.
m.4.26.54: This is declared the Jyotirliṅga renowned by the name Tryambaka, standing on the bank of the Gautamī, the destroyer of great sins.
m.4.26.55: Whoever with devotion beholds the Jyotirliṅga named Tryambaka, worships it, praises it and bows to it, is freed from all sins.
m.4.26.56: The Jyotirliṅga Tryambaka, worshipped by Gautama, grants all desires here and bestows supreme liberation in the hereafter.
m.4.26.57: Thus I have narrated to you what I was asked, O lords among sages. What else do you wish to hear? That I shall tell you, without doubt.
m.4.26.iti: Thus ends the twenty-sixth adhyāya, named The description of the glory of Tryambakeśvara, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.4.27.1: The sages said: How did Gaṅgā come into being in the form of water? Tell us, O lord. And from where did her greatness especially arise? Tell us, O lord.
m.4.27.2: And what then happened to those wicked brahmins by whom suffering was given to Gautama? Let it be told, O you who have Vyāsa as your true teacher.
m.4.27.3: Sūta said: Thus entreated by Gautama at that time, Gaṅgā herself, O brahmins, quickly descended from that mountain of Brahmā.
m.4.27.4: Her stream issued forth from a branch of an udumbara tree. There the renowned sage Gautama joyfully bathed.
m.4.27.5: Gautama's disciples and other great sages too gathered there and bathed full of joy.
m.4.27.6: Then that place became famous by the name Gaṅgādvāra, delightful and removing all sins by its mere sight, O best of sages.
m.4.27.7: Those sages who were Gautama's rivals also came there to bathe; seeing them, she quickly vanished.
m.4.27.8: Do not, do not, Gautama quickly cried out there, praising Gaṅgā again and again with folded hands and bowed head.
m.4.27.9: Gautama said: These men are blinded by the intoxication of prosperity; whether they are good or wicked, by the power of this merit of mine let your sight be granted to them by you.
m.4.27.10: Sūta said: Then a voice of Gaṅgā arose from the vault of the sky. Hear that excellent speech of Gaṅgā, O best of sages.
m.4.27.11: Gaṅgā said: These are most wicked, ungrateful, traitors to their master, base and heretical; they are always to be avoided from seeing me.
m.4.27.12: Gautama said: O Mother, let this be heard — these are indeed the words of the great. Therefore the Lord's word must be made true by you.
m.4.27.13: He in this world who does good to those who harm him, by him I am purified here: this is the word of the Lord.
m.4.27.14: Sūta said: Having heard these words of the great-souled sage Gautama, again a voice of Gaṅgā arose from the vault of the sky.
m.4.27.15: True and auspicious words are indeed spoken by you, O sage Gautama; even so, for the sake of their acceptance, let them perform expiation.
m.4.27.16: Here a hundred and one circumambulations of the mountain must be performed by these men, at your command, being especially subject to you.
m.4.27.17: And then the evil-doers will gain eligibility, especially for seeing me. I have spoken the truth, O sage.
m.4.27.18: Hearing her words, they all did so, humbly entreating Gautama: our offence should be forgiven.
m.4.27.19: When this was done, Gautama then, at her command, made a pool named Kuśāvarta, situated below Gaṅgādvāra.
m.4.27.20: Then she appeared there again for his pleasure, and Kuśāvarta became a famous, unsurpassed holy place (tīrtha).
m.4.27.21: Whoever bathes there becomes fit for liberation, at once casting off all sins and attaining rare knowledge.
m.4.27.22: Gautama and the other sages met with one another; and those who had formerly been ungrateful were then ashamed.
m.4.27.23: The sages said: O Sūta, we have heard it otherwise, and we relate that: let it be understood that Gautama, in anger, cursed those brahmins.
m.4.27.24: Sūta said: O brahmins, that too is true, owing to the difference of aeons (kalpa). I shall narrate that story too in detail, O you of good vows.
m.4.27.25: Gautama, seeing the sages then afflicted by famine, performed very great austerity directed to the great-souled Varuṇa.
m.4.27.26: By Varuṇa's gift he produced inexhaustible water; then he had rice and barley sown in abundance.
m.4.27.27: Thus Gautama, the best of sages, devoted to helping others, provided food for them by the power of his own austerity.
m.4.27.28: Once their wicked wives, feeling slighted over fetching water, angrily spoke to their husbands words that stirred up jealousy against Gautama.
m.4.27.29: Then those brahmins, of perverted minds and crooked intent, fashioned an artificial cow and set it to eating his grain.
m.4.27.30: Seeing the cow eating his grain, Gautama then struck it with a blade of grass, gently driving it away.
m.4.27.31: By the mere touch of the grass that cow fell to the ground and instantly died, O brahmins, by the force of destined karma.
m.4.27.32: A cow has been killed by Gautama: so then all the sages living there, of crooked intent, gathered together and declared.
m.4.27.33: Then Gautama became afraid, thinking, a cow has been killed; that follower of Śiva, together with his wife Ahalyā and disciples, was astonished.
m.4.27.34: Then Gautama, the best of sages, understanding the truth about that cow and filled with anger, cursed all those sages.
m.4.27.35: Gautama said: You are all wicked, especially causing grief to me, a constant devotee of Śiva; may you be ever averse to the Veda.
m.4.27.36: From today onward may you have no faith in the good rites taught in the Veda, and especially not in the Śaiva path that grants liberation.
m.4.27.37: From today onward may your faith be in an evil path, one devoid of the way to liberation and ever turned away from the Veda.
m.4.27.38: From today onward may your foreheads be smeared with clay; fall into hell, you brahmins with clay-smeared foreheads.
m.4.27.39: May you not be those for whom Śiva alone is the supreme deity; may you regard the non-dual Śiva as merely equal to other gods.
m.4.27.40: May you never have love for the worship of Śiva and related rites, for devotees steadfast in Śiva, or for the festivals of Śiva.
m.4.27.41: However many sorrow-giving curses I have pronounced today, may that many befall your descendants too, always.
m.4.27.42: O brahmins, may your sons, grandsons and the rest be non-Śaivas; and may you, together with your sons, surely dwell in hell.
m.4.27.43: Then may you all become caṇḍālas, afflicted by sorrow and poverty, deceitful, slanderers, ever marked with heated brands.
m.4.27.44: Sūta said: Having thus cursed all the sages, Gautama went to his own hermitage. He practised intense devotion to Śiva and became exceedingly pure.
m.4.27.45: Then all those brahmin sages, sick at heart because of those curses, took up residence in Kāñcī, excluded from the Śaiva dharma.
m.4.27.46: Their sons too all became excluded from the Śaiva dharma; likewise in the future, in the Kali age, many people will be wicked.
m.4.27.47: Thus, O best of sages, that account has been told in full; and, O wise ones, the earlier account too has been heard by you all with reverence.
m.4.27.48: Thus the origin of the Gautamī has been narrated to you, and also its supreme, excellent glory that removes all sins.
m.4.27.49: And the glory of the Tryambaka jyotirliṅga has been proclaimed; hearing it one is freed from all sins—there is no doubt about this.
m.4.27.50: After this I shall tell the glory of the Vaidyanātheśvara jyotirliṅga, which removes sin; let it be heard.
m.4.27.iti: Thus ends the twenty-seventh adhyāya, named The description of the glory of the Tryambakeśvara jyotirliṅga, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.4.28.1: Sūta said: Rāvaṇa, the foremost of the rākṣasas, proud and wholly given to pride, worshipped Hara with devotion on Kailāsa, the best of mountains.
m.4.28.2: When Hara, though worshipped for some time, was not pleased, he then undertook another austerity to win Śiva's favour.
m.4.28.3: Then this glorious Rāvaṇa, the descendant of Pulastya, went to a grove of trees to the south of the Himavat mountain, the place of spiritual attainment,
m.4.28.4: There, O brahmins, having made an excellent pit in the ground and set up the fire in it, and having installed Śiva near it, he performed fire-offerings.
m.4.28.5: In summer he stood amid five fires, in the rains he lay on the bare ground, and in winter he stayed within water; thus he performed austerity in three ways.
m.4.28.6: Thus he performed much austerity, yet even then the Supreme Self, Maheśāna, hard to propitiate by the wicked, was not pleased.
m.4.28.7: Then the great-spirited Rāvaṇa, lord of the demons, began the worship of Śaṅkara by cutting off his heads.
m.4.28.8: One head after another was cut off according to rule in the worship of Śiva; when in this proper sequence nine had been cut off by him,
m.4.28.9: then, when only one remained, Śaṅkara, affectionate to his devotees, became pleased and, satisfied, appeared right there.
m.4.28.10: The Lord restored the heads as before, free from injury, and granted him his desire, incomparable and supreme strength.
m.4.28.11: Having obtained his favour, Rāvaṇa the rākṣasa, with bowed shoulders and joined palms, replied to Śiva Śambhu:
m.4.28.12: Rāvaṇa said: Be gracious, O Lord of gods; I shall take you to Laṅkā. Make my wish fruitful; I have come to you for refuge.
m.4.28.13: Sūta said: Thus addressed then by Rāvaṇa, Śambhu, perplexed and having fallen into great difficulty, replied:
m.4.28.14: Śiva said: Listen, O best of rākṣasas, to my words in their essence: take my excellent liṅga to your home with true devotion.
m.4.28.15: Wherever you place the liṅga on the ground, there it will remain, no doubt. Do as you wish.
m.4.28.16: Sūta said: Thus addressed by Śambhu, Rāvaṇa, lord of the rākṣasas, said, so be it, took it up and went toward his own abode.
m.4.28.17: On the way, by Śiva's māyā, he felt the urge to pass urine; the mighty Rāvaṇa, descendant of Pulastya, was unable to restrain it.
m.4.28.18: Seeing a cowherd there, he requested him and gave him the liṅga. When a short while had passed, the cowherd became distressed.
m.4.28.19: Greatly oppressed by its weight, he set it down on the ground. Right there that liṅga, born of the essence of diamond, remained — granting all desires and removing sins by its very sight.
m.4.28.20: That liṅga, O sage, became known by the name Vaidyanātheśvara, famed in the three worlds, granting enjoyment and liberation to the good.
m.4.28.21: This excellent jyotirliṅga, by sight and by worship, removes all sins; it is divine, supreme, and increases liberation.
m.4.28.22: When that liṅga had become established there for the welfare of all worlds, Rāvaṇa, having gone home with the supreme boon obtained, the great demon joyfully told everything to his beloved.
m.4.28.23: Hearing that, all the gods led by Śakra, and likewise the sages, pure and with minds fixed on Śiva, consulted one another.
m.4.28.24: At that time, O sage, all the gods headed by Hari and Brahmā came there with great joy and performed worship in a special manner.
m.4.28.25: Then, seeing him manifest, those gods consecrated him, named him Vaidyanātha, bowed and praised, and went to heaven.
m.4.28.26: The sages said: When that liṅga was established there and Rāvaṇa had gone home, what happened then, dear one? Tell that in detail.
m.4.28.27: Sūta said: Rāvaṇa, having gone home with the supreme boon obtained, told everything to his beloved, and the great demon rejoiced exceedingly.
m.4.28.28: Hearing all that, the gods led by Śakra and likewise the sages, those lords of sages, deeply alarmed, spoke to one another:
m.4.28.29: The gods and the others said: This Rāvaṇa is wicked-souled, hostile to the gods, vile and evil-minded; having obtained a boon from Śiva, he will cause us great suffering.
m.4.28.30: What shall we do, where shall we go, and what will happen next? The wicked one has gained power; what all will he not accomplish against us?
m.4.28.31: Thus fallen into distress, the gods and sages led by Śakra, agitated, summoned Nārada and then questioned him.
m.4.28.32: The gods said: You are able to accomplish every task, O best of sages. Devise a means, O divine sage, for destroying the gods' distress.
m.4.28.33: This Rāvaṇa is extremely wicked; what will he not do? Where shall we go? We here are oppressed by the wicked one.
m.4.28.34: Nārada said: Give up your distress, O gods; having devised a plan, I go. By Śaṅkara's grace I shall accomplish the gods' task.
m.4.28.35: Sūta said: Having said this, the divine sage went to Rāvaṇa's abode, and having received hospitality, spoke all this with affection:
m.4.28.36: Nārada said: O best of rākṣasas, you are blessed, foremost of Śaiva devotees, rich in austerity. Seeing you today, O Rāvaṇa, my mind is greatly delighted.
m.4.28.37: Tell me fully your story arising from the worship of Śiva. Thus questioned by him, Rāvaṇa then spoke these words:
m.4.28.38: Rāvaṇa said: Having gone to Kailāsa for austerity, O great sage, I performed there a very severe austerity for a long time.
m.4.28.39: When Śaṅkara was not pleased, I then changed course; coming to a grove of trees, O sage, I again performed austerity.
m.4.28.40: In summer I stood amid five fires, in the rains I lay on the bare ground, and in winter I stayed within water; thus was austerity performed in three ways.
m.4.28.41: O lord of sages, I performed extremely severe austerity there in this way; yet Śaṅkara did not become even slightly pleased with me.
m.4.28.42: Then, angered, I dug a pit in the ground, set up a fire there, and fashioned an earthen liṅga.
m.4.28.43: Then Śambhu was worshipped with fragrances, sandal-paste, various incenses and food-offerings, following the rite of āratī (waving of lamps).
m.4.28.44: Śaṅkara was propitiated by me with prostrations and holy hymns, with songs, dances and instrumental music, and with offerings made by mouth and fingers.
m.4.28.45: With these and many other various means, O sage, the blessed Hara was worshipped according to the procedure laid down in the scriptures.
m.4.28.46: When the blessed Hara was not pleased and did not appear before me, I became sorrowful, not having obtained the true fruit of my austerity.
m.4.28.47: Fie on my body and my strength! Fie on my practice of austerity! Saying this, I made many oblations into the fire established there.
m.4.28.48: And again, resolving, I shall give up my own body in the fire, I cut off my heads to offer in that blazing, pure fire.
m.4.28.49: Cutting them off one by one and purifying them thoroughly, I offered nine of them to Śaṅkara.
m.4.28.50: And just as I began to cut off the tenth, O best of sages, Hara himself appeared there in the form of light.
m.4.28.51: Lovingly and swiftly the one tender to his devotees cried, don't, don't, and, being pleased, said: ask a boon; I shall give what your mind desires.
m.4.28.52: When he had said this, I beheld Maheśvara, bowed to him and praised him, joining my palms with deep devotion.
m.4.28.53: Then I chose this: give me incomparable strength. If you are pleased, O lord of gods, what could be difficult for me to obtain?
m.4.28.54: The compassionate Śiva, fully pleased, saying aloud, so be it, gave me everything my mind desired.
m.4.28.55: With his unfailing, gracious glance the Supreme Self, like a physician, rejoined my heads; having set them together, he looked upon them.
m.4.28.56: When this was done there, my body became as before, and by his grace I obtained every fruit.
m.4.28.57: Then, entreated by me, that bull-bannered god stayed there, and became famous in the three worlds by the name Vaidyanātheśvara.
m.4.28.58: Maheśvara in the form of the jyotirliṅga, by being seen and worshipped, bestows enjoyment and liberation in the world and brings welfare to all.
m.4.28.59: Having specially worshipped that jyotirliṅga and bowed to it, I have come here to conquer the three worlds.
m.4.28.60: Sūta said: Hearing those words of his, the divine sage Nārada was agitated, and laughing inwardly, he spoke to Rāvaṇa.
m.4.28.61: Nārada said: Listen, O best of Rākṣasas, I shall tell you what is good for you. You must do exactly what I say, never otherwise.
m.4.28.62: What you said, that Śiva himself has now granted you what is good, you should never take all that as true.
m.4.28.63: He has become deranged; what does he not say? That may well not be true — how can it be known? You are dear to me, so I tell you.
m.4.28.64: So go back and do the deed again — he said this, in truth, for your harm: you must again make an effort to lift up Kailāsa.
m.4.28.65: If this Kailāsa is lifted up, then indeed everything will be fruitful; there is no doubt.
m.4.28.66: Set it back as before and then return happily. Having reached complete certainty, do as you wish.
m.4.28.67: Sūta said: Thus addressed, Rāvaṇa, deluded by fate, thought it beneficial; taking the sage's words as true, he then went to Kailāsa.
m.4.28.68: Going there, he lifted up that mountain, and everything situated on it was thrown into confusion, one thing upon another.
m.4.28.69: Seeing this, Girīśa said, what has happened? Then Girijā, laughing, replied to Śambhu.
m.4.28.70: Girijā said: The fruit of having a good disciple has come about; it has turned out properly from the disciple — the incomparable strength that was given to that tranquil-souled, most heroic one.
m.4.28.71: Sūta said: Hearing Girijā's pointed words, Maheśvara, regarding Rāvaṇa as ungrateful and proud of his strength, cursed him.
m.4.28.72: Mahādeva said: Ho, Rāvaṇa, wicked devotee, evil-minded one, do not carry such pride. Soon there shall arise here one who crushes the pride of your arms.
m.4.28.73: Nārada then heard what had happened there; and Rāvaṇa, pleased at heart, went back to his own abode as he had come.
m.4.28.74: Having made a firm resolve, the mighty Rāvaṇa, deluded by his strength and destroyer of others' pride, brought the world under his control.
m.4.28.75: With the greatly powerful divine weapon obtained by Śiva's command, no opponent was then able to match Rāvaṇa.
m.4.28.76: Thus has the greatness of Vaidyanātheśvara been narrated; the sin of men who hear it is reduced to ashes.
m.4.28.iti: Thus ends the twenty-eighth adhyāya, named The description of the glory of the Vaidyanātheśvara jyotirliṅga, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.4.29.1: Sūta said: Now, therefore, I shall narrate how the supreme and most excellent liṅga of the Supreme Self, called Nāgeśa, in the form of light, came into being.
m.4.29.2: There was a certain rākṣasī named Dārukā, made arrogant by a boon from Pārvatī; and her husband was Dāruka, exceedingly mighty.
m.4.29.3: With many rākṣasas he wrought slaughter of the virtuous there; he then destroyed the sacrifices and the dharma of the people.
m.4.29.4: On the western sea he had a forest rich in every abundance, extending sixteen yojanas in every direction.
m.4.29.5: That forest, where Dārukā goes for her own pleasure, was furnished there with land, trees and all requisites.
m.4.29.6: The Goddess granted Dārukā the power of overseeing that forest; indeed she would go to that forest with her husband at will.
m.4.29.7: Staying there, the rākṣasa Dāruka, together with his wife Dārukā, then struck fear into everyone.
m.4.29.8: All those afflicted people went for refuge to Aurva; bowing with great devotion, with heads bent, they spoke to him.
m.4.29.9: The people said: O great sage, grant us refuge; otherwise we are killed by the wicked. You are able to do everything; you are radiant with spiritual power.
m.4.29.10: On earth there is no one but you as our refuge, to whose presence we may go and, staying there, find happiness.
m.4.29.11: On seeing you, all the rākṣasas flee far away; in you the radiance of Śiva ever shines like fire.
m.4.29.12: Sūta said: Thus entreated by the people, Aurva, best of sages, grieving and a giver of refuge, spoke words for their protection.
m.4.29.13: Aurva said: If the rākṣasas harm living beings on earth, then those mighty rākṣasas shall themselves be separated from their lives.
m.4.29.14: When sacrifices are destroyed by them, then let all the rākṣasas be deprived of life. This truth is spoken by me.
m.4.29.15: Sūta said: Having spoken these words to them and comforted the people again, Aurva, bringer of happiness to the world, performed various austerities.
m.4.29.16: Then the gods, knowing that this was the reason given by the curse, made preparations for war with the enemies of the gods.
m.4.29.17: With every effort, all the gods led by Śakra, bearing various weapons, arrived there for battle.
m.4.29.18: Seeing them, all the wicked rākṣasas there, wherever they were stationed, again became intent on deliberating among themselves.
m.4.29.19: The demons said: What is to be done? Where shall we go? We have fallen into a crisis. If we fight, we die; and if we fight, the foe is not slain.
m.4.29.20: If we just remain as we are, what is to be eaten—each other? Misery has come upon us in every way; who could avert it?
m.4.29.21: Sūta said: Having deliberated thus, the rākṣasas there, Dāruka and the rest, not finding a remedy, fell into constant misery.
m.4.29.22: The rākṣasī Dārukā too, knowing the misery that had come, then told them of that boon of Bhavānī.
m.4.29.23: Dārukā said: Formerly the consort of Bhava, worshipped by me, granted a boon: go with your own people to the forest, wherever you wish to go.
m.4.29.24: Since that boon was obtained by me, why should misery be endured? Taking the forest into the water, the rākṣasas may live happily.
m.4.29.25: Sūta said: Hearing those words of the rākṣasī, all the rākṣasas became joyful and, now fearless, spoke among themselves.
m.4.29.26: Blessed is she, she has fulfilled her purpose; by the queen herself we are saved. Bowing to her, they respectfully told her all that.
m.4.29.27: If there is power to go, let us go; why deliberate? Going there into the water, O lady, we shall live happily forever.
m.4.29.28: Meanwhile the people, formerly afflicted by the rākṣasas with various miseries, arrived together with the gods for battle.
m.4.29.29: Then, the rākṣasas being hard pressed, she, relying on the power of that Bhavānī, carried off the entire city together with its water and land,
m.4.29.30: the rākṣasī, uttering the praise of the Goddess, Victory, victory! then flew up like a winged king of mountains.
m.4.29.31: She then settled fearlessly in the middle of the ocean; with all her retinue, that follower of Śivā rejoiced.
m.4.29.32: Living there in the ocean and in the city, the pleasure-loving rākṣasas attained happiness and sported fearlessly.
m.4.29.33: The rākṣasas never came onto the earth; out of fear of the sage's curse alone, they then roamed about on the water.
m.4.29.34: Seizing people who were in boats, they then carried them to that city and threw them into prison; some of them they killed.
m.4.29.35: Again and again those rākṣasas then caused affliction, dwelling there fearless because of Bhavānī's granting of the boon.
m.4.29.36: Just as formerly there was incessant fear among people on land, so now, O lords of sages, there was constant fear of them on the water.
m.4.29.37: Once that rākṣasī came out of the city onto the water and stood blocking the route, near the shore, in order to harass the people.
m.4.29.38: Meanwhile, very many fine boats arrived there from all sides in various ways, crowded with people.
m.4.29.39: Seeing those boats, the wicked rākṣasas were delighted; going there quickly, they forcibly seized those aboard.
m.4.29.40: Taking them, those mighty ones came to the city and, binding them with strong fetters, threw them into prison.
m.4.29.41: Those people, bound with fetters, remained in the prison; threatened again and again, they fell into extreme misery.
m.4.29.42: Among them, the one who was the chief was a vaiśya named Supriya; dear to Śiva, of virtuous conduct, he was always a devotee of Śiva.
m.4.29.43: He would never remain without the worship of Śiva; he was wholly devoted to Śiva's dharma, adorned with sacred ash and rudrākṣa beads.
m.4.29.44: If the worship had not been done, then he would not eat; therefore even there that vaiśya performed the worship of Śiva.
m.4.29.45: Though confined in the prison, he then taught many others the Śiva mantra and the worship of the earthen liṅga, O best of sages.
m.4.29.46: Then all of them there performed, according to rule, the worship of Śiva that grants one's desires, as they had seen and as they had heard.
m.4.29.47: Some there, having assumed an excellent posture, remained in meditation, and some, filled with joy, performed mental worship of Śiva.
m.4.29.48: Then, right there, the chief performed the visible worship of Śiva by the very rite of the earthen liṅga, O lords of sages.
m.4.29.49: And others, who did not know the rite, practised the supreme remembrance: they remained meditating on Śaṅkara with the mantra namaḥ śivāya.
m.4.29.50: And the one named Supriya, the best of vaiśyas, dear to Śiva, meditating in his mind there, performed the worship of Śiva.
m.4.29.51: And Śambhu, in the form as described in meditation, visibly accepted everything; yet he himself did not know that it was being accepted by Śiva.
m.4.29.52: While the vaiśya was thus performing the worship of Śiva, six months passed there without obstacle, O lords of sages.
m.4.29.53: Hear now, O best of sages, with an attentive mind, the deed of the moon-crested Śiva that took place after this.
m.4.29.iti: Thus ends the twenty-ninth adhyāya, named The description of the harassment by the rākṣasas of the Dāruka forest, in the Māhātmya of the Nāgeśvara jyotirliṅga, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.4.30.1: Sūta said: Once a servant of that evil-minded Rākṣasa saw, in front of him the merchant, the beautiful form of Śaṅkara.
m.4.30.2: Then he reported to that king of the Rākṣasas, exactly as it was, that whole event, wondrous and astonishing.
m.4.30.3: That king of the Rākṣasas, Dāruka, coming there quickly with his forces, agitated, questioned that devotee of Śiva.
m.4.30.4: Dāruka said: What are you meditating on, O Vaiśya? Speak the truth before me. If so, there will be no death for you—and my word is not otherwise.
m.4.30.5: Sūta said: He replied, I do not know. Hearing that, Dāruka became angry and urged the Rākṣasas: O Rākṣasas, let this one be killed.
m.4.30.6: Thus ordered by him, they, bearing various weapons, went swiftly to kill that tiger among Vaiśyas, whose mind was fixed on Śaṅkara.
m.4.30.7: Seeing them arrive, his eyes trembling with fear, he remembered Śiva with great love and sang his names again and again.
