m.4.30.8: The merchant lord said: Protect me, O Śaṅkara, Lord of gods; protect me, O Śambhu, O Śiva. Save me from this wicked one, O Lord of the three worlds, slayer of the wicked, lover of devotees.
m.4.30.9: You alone, O God, are my all today. I am dependent on you, I am yours, you are my life always, O Lord.
m.4.30.10: Sūta said: Thus entreated, Śambhu then emerged from a cleft in the earth, with an excellent shrine having four doors.
m.4.30.11: Seeing in its midst that wondrous form of Śiva, of the nature of light, accompanied by his retinue, he worshipped him.
m.4.30.12: Worshipped thus, Śambhu himself became pleased; giving him the weapon called Pāśupata, he struck the chief Rākṣasas.
m.4.30.13: He quickly slew all of them along with their equipment and their hosts; and that Śaṅkara, the destroyer of the wicked, protected his own devotee.
m.4.30.14: Having then slain them all, Śambhu, doer of utter wonders, who assumes a fine body through his own play, granted a boon to the forest as well.
m.4.30.15: In this forest may the duties of the varṇas always prevail—of Brāhmaṇas, Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas, and likewise of Śūdras.
m.4.30.16: May there be here excellent sages, never tāmasic ones—expounders and promoters of Śiva's dharma.
m.4.30.17: Sūta said: At this time the Rākṣasī named Dārukā, dejected in mind, offered praise to the Goddess Pārvatī.
m.4.30.18: Then the Goddess, pleased, said, what shall I do? She in turn said there, let my lineage be protected by you.
m.4.30.19: I will protect your lineage; truly this is said by me. Having said this, Pārvatī entered into a dispute with Śiva himself.
m.4.30.20: Śiva too, the Lord, seeing the Goddess angry and being bound by her boon, replied with great affection: do as you wish.
m.4.30.21: Sūta said: Hearing these words of her own husband Śaṅkara, Pārvatī, much pleased, laughed and quickly spoke.
m.4.30.22: Pārvatī said: Your word will come true at the end of the yuga; until then, let there be a tāmasic creation—this is my view.
m.4.30.23: Otherwise there would be dissolution. What I have said is true, O Śiva; let it be made valid, O Lord—I am yours, I take refuge in you.
m.4.30.24: And this Rākṣasī, the goddess Dārukā, is a śakti of mine, the strongest of Rākṣasīs; let her rule the kingdom of the Rākṣasas.
m.4.30.25: These wives of the Rākṣasas will give birth to sons; all of them together are approved by me to dwell in the forest.
m.4.30.26: Sūta said: Hearing these words of Pārvatī, his own wife, the Lord Śaṅkara, pleased at heart, spoke.
m.4.30.27: Śaṅkara said: If you say so, then hear my word, beloved: I shall gladly abide in this forest for the protection of devotees.
m.4.30.28: Whoever, abiding in the duties of his varṇa, beholds me here with love, he will become a universal emperor.
m.4.30.29: Further, at the turn of the Kali age, at the start of the Satya age, there will be a lord of kings, son of Mahāsena, renowned as Vīrasena.
m.4.30.30: He, most valiant through devotion to me, will behold me; having beheld me, he will become a universal emperor.
m.4.30.31: Sūta said: Thus that divine couple, having jested with each other, remained there themselves in person, O Brāhmaṇas, as bestowers of great aid.
m.4.30.32: Śiva, in the form of a jyotirliṅga, became by name Nāgeśvara, and the Goddess Śivā became Nāgeśvarī—both dear to the virtuous.
m.4.30.33: The sages said: How will Vīrasena go there to the Dārukā forest? How will he worship Śiva? Tell us that, O wise one.
m.4.30.34: Sūta said: In the beautiful land of Niṣadha, in a family of Kṣatriyas, was Vīrasena, son of Mahāsena, dear to Śiva.
m.4.30.35: Worshipping the Lord in an earthen liṅga, Vīrasena performed extremely difficult austerity for a period of twelve years.
m.4.30.36: Then Śaṅkara, Lord of gods, pleased, appeared before him and said: having made a fish of wood, coated with tin,
m.4.30.37: and having endowed it with yogic power, I shall give it to you, O dear Vīrasena. Taking it, entering this water, go now along with boats.
m.4.30.38: Then, going there and entering the cleft made by me, and worshipping Nāgeśvara,
m.4.30.39: then obtaining the Pāśupata weapon and slaying the chief Rākṣasīs—once I have been seen, nothing will then be lacking for you.
m.4.30.40: And the strength of Pārvatī too will be complete; and others who will be in the forest in the form of Mlecchas will be auspicious.
m.4.30.41: Having spoken thus to Vīrasena there, Śaṅkara, the Lord, the remover of sorrow, showed great compassion and vanished right there.
m.4.30.42: Thus granted a boon by Śiva, the Supreme Self, he too then became able to accomplish everything; there is no doubt.
m.4.30.43: Thus the god Nāgeśvara, lord of the luminous ones (jyotis), arose in the form of a liṅga, ever granting all desires to the three worlds.
m.4.30.44: The wise one who listens daily and with reverence to this account of the manifestation of Nāgeśa attains all desires, and the account is destructive of great sins.
m.4.30.iti: Thus ends the thirtieth adhyāya, named The description of the glory of the manifestation of the Nāgeśvara jyotirliṅga, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.4.31.1: Sūta said: Next I shall describe the liṅga named Rāmeśvara and how it arose in former times. O sages, listen with attention.
m.4.31.2: Long ago Viṣṇu, dear to the virtuous, descended upon the earth.
m.4.31.3: There, O brahmins, Sītā was abducted by Rāvaṇa, a master of great deception; the daughter of Janaka was taken to his own house in Laṅkā.
m.4.31.4: Intent on searching for her, he went to the city called Kiṣkindhā; becoming the benefactor of Sugrīva, he slew Vālin.
m.4.31.5: Staying there for some time, devoted to searching for her, he deliberated with Sugrīva and the others and with Lakṣmaṇa.
m.4.31.6: Rāma, the king's son, sent forth the monkeys headed by Hanumat in the four directions for the purpose of finding her.
m.4.31.7: Then, learning from the mouth of the foremost monkey that Sītā had been taken to Laṅkā, and receiving Sītā's crest-jewel, Rāghava rejoiced greatly.
m.4.31.8: Then, O twice-born, Rāma, with the monkey-lord and accompanied by Lakṣmaṇa, together with the virtuous and very mighty monkeys headed by Sugrīva,
m.4.31.9: and with troops numbering eighteen padmas, went to the shore of the ocean — the salt-mine that is seen in the southern sea.
m.4.31.10: Having come there, Rāma himself, beloved of Śiva, stood on the shore, attended by the monkeys and by Lakṣmaṇa.
m.4.31.11: Alas, Jānakī! Where has she gone, and when will she be united with me? The ocean is fathomless, and the monkey army cannot cross it.
m.4.31.12: The rākṣasa is a lifter of mountains, of great strength and valour; his fortress called Laṅkā is hard to reach; and Indrajit is his son.
m.4.31.13: Thus reflecting, he stood on the shore with Lakṣmaṇa and was consoled by the forest-dwellers led by Aṅgada and others.
m.4.31.14: Meanwhile Rāghava, the best of Śaivas, wanting water, affectionately spoke to his brother named Lakṣmaṇa.
m.4.31.15: Śrī Rāma said: Brother Lakṣmaṇa, lord of heroes, I am thirsty and want water. So bring water quickly by means of some monkeys.
m.4.31.16: Sūta said: Hearing that, the monkeys there ran in the ten directions; bringing water, they bowed, stood before him and said:
m.4.31.17: The monkeys said: Master, please take the water brought at your command — most excellent, very sweet, cool and refreshing to life.
m.4.31.18: Sūta said: Hearing that, Rāmacandra, greatly pleased, looked at them with a compassionate gaze and himself took that water.
m.4.31.19: When that Śaiva took the water and began to drink, then, by Śiva's will, this recollection arose in him:
m.4.31.20: I have not had the sight (darśana) of Śambhu, my own master, the supreme lord, the giver of all bliss; how can water be taken?
m.4.31.21: Saying this, the best of the Raghus set the water aside; and afterwards the joy of the Raghus performed worship of Śiva with an earthen liṅga.
m.4.31.22: Arranging the services beginning with invocation (āvāhana), he lovingly worshipped Lord Śaṅkara according to rule with the sixteenfold offerings.
m.4.31.23: Having diligently pleased Śiva with prostrations and divine hymns, Rāma joyfully entreated Śaṅkara with true devotion.
m.4.31.24: Śrī Rāma said: O master, Śambhu, Mahādeva, ever affectionate to devotees, protect me, your devotee, who has come for refuge and is dejected in mind.
m.4.31.25: O you who carry beings across worldly existence, this water of the ocean is fathomless; and the rākṣasa named Rāvaṇa is a great hero, exceedingly powerful.
m.4.31.26: This force of monkeys, my means of war, is fickle. How will my task of recovering my beloved be accomplished?
m.4.31.27: In that, O god of good vows, you must give me help; without your help, O lord, my task is hard to achieve.
m.4.31.28: Rāvaṇa too is yours, your devotee; here he is in every way unconquerable by all; proud of the boon given by you, he is a great hero, conqueror of the three worlds.
m.4.31.29: Yet I too am your servant and wholly dependent on you. Considering this, O Sadāśiva, you should take my side.
m.4.31.30: Sūta said: Having entreated thus and bowed again and again, he then cried aloud with loud shouts, Victory, victory, O Śaṅkara!
m.4.31.31: Having thus praised Śiva there, devoted to mantra and meditation, and having again performed worship, he danced before the Lord.
m.4.31.32: When, his heart melting with love, he made the cheek-sound (gallanāda), then Lord Śaṅkara became exceedingly pleased.
m.4.31.33: Maheśvara, in the form of light, with his limbs and his retinue, assuming the spotless form as described in scripture, quickly became manifest.
m.4.31.34: Then Maheśvara, his heart gratified by Rāma's devotion, said: may there be good fortune. Choose a boon, Rāma.
m.4.31.35: Seeing that form then, all became purified. Thereupon Rāghava, devoted to the dharma of Śiva, himself performed worship.
m.4.31.36: Having offered various praises and joyfully bowed to Śiva, he then asked for his own victory in the battle with Rāvaṇa.
m.4.31.37: Then Maheśvara, his heart pleased by Rāma's devotion, lovingly said again: may victory be yours, great king.
m.4.31.38: Having obtained the victory granted by Śiva and received his permission, he entreated again with joined palms and bowed head.
m.4.31.39: Śrī Rāma said: O master, if you are pleased, O Śaṅkara, you should remain here for the purification of the worlds and for the benefit of others.
m.4.31.40: Sūta said: Thus addressed, Śiva then took the form of a liṅga there, and became renowned on the face of the earth by the name Rāmeśvara.
m.4.31.41: Rāma, by its power, swiftly crossed the ocean, quickly slew Rāvaṇa and the other Rākṣasas, and regained his beloved.
m.4.31.42: The glory of Rāmeśvara became wondrous and unequalled on earth; it grants enjoyment and liberation, and always fulfils the desires of devotees.
m.4.31.43: Whoever, with true devotion, bathes Śiva as Rāmeśvara with the divine water of the Gaṅgā is indeed liberated while living.
m.4.31.44: Having enjoyed here all pleasures, even those hard for the gods to obtain, at the end, attaining supreme knowledge, he would surely attain kaivalya (final liberation).
m.4.31.45: Thus has been narrated to you the divine jyotirliṅga of Śiva named Rāmeśvara, which removes the sins of those who hear of it.
m.4.31.iti: Thus ends the thirty-first adhyāya, named The description of the glory of Rāmeśvara, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.4.32.1: Sūta said: After this, the jyotirliṅga Ghuśmeśa is declared. O best of sages, listen to its great glory.
m.4.32.2: In the southern direction there is an excellent mountain named Deva Devagiri. Wondrous to behold and endowed with great beauty, it always shines.
m.4.32.3: Near it lived a brahmin named Sudharmā, born in the lineage of Bharadvāja, foremost among knowers of Brahman.
m.4.32.4: His beloved wife Sudehā was devoted to the dharma of Śiva, always intent on serving her husband, and skilled in household work.
m.4.32.5: And Sudharmā, the best of the twice-born, worshipped the gods and guests, was always devoted to the Vedic path, and intent on tending the sacred fire.
m.4.32.6: He performed the sandhyā rites at the three junctures of the day, had radiance equal to the sun's form, taught students, and was learned in the Vedas and śāstras.
m.4.32.7: He was wealthy, a supreme giver, a vessel of the virtue of kindliness, always delighting in Śiva's rites, a Śaiva, and fond of Śaiva people.
m.4.32.8: Much of his life passed as he practised dharma, yet no son was born to him; the fertile season of his wife proved fruitless.
m.4.32.9: Devoted as he was to knowledge of reality, he did not grieve, thinking: the self is the saviour of the self, and it is the purifier of the self.
m.4.32.10: Holding such a thought in mind, he did not grieve then; but Sudehā grieved over having no son.
m.4.32.11: Every day she entreated her husband, expert in all branches of learning, to make efforts for begetting a son.
m.4.32.12: He too then rebuked his wife: what will a son do? Who is mother, who father, who son? Who is kinsman, and who is dear?
m.4.32.13: O lady, everything in the three worlds is bent on its own interest; there is no doubt of this. Understand this well with your intellect and do not grieve.
m.4.32.14: Therefore, O lady, you must surely give up your grief. O you of auspicious vows, you should not speak of this to me again and again.
m.4.32.15: Having thus restrained her, he, intent on the dharma of the Lord, remained supremely content and abandoned the sorrow of the pairs of opposites.
m.4.32.16: Once Sudehā went to a neighbour's house for friendly conversation, and a quarrel arose there.
m.4.32.17: His wife, out of a woman's nature, then reviled her; Sudehā, the brahmin's beloved, was addressed by her with harsh words thus:
m.4.32.18: The neighbour's wife said: O sonless woman, how can you be proud? I am the one with a son. My son will enjoy my wealth; who will enjoy yours?
m.4.32.19: Surely the king will seize your wealth; there is no doubt of this. Shame, shame on you! Shame on your wealth, and shame on your pride, O barren woman!
m.4.32.20: Sūta said: Reviled thus by those women, she came home distressed and respectfully told her husband all that had been said.
m.4.32.21: The wise brahmin did not grieve then either: let what has been said be said; whatever is to be will be, my dear.
m.4.32.22: Though consoled by him again and again in this way, she did not give up her grief then; she persisted in her insistence.
m.4.32.23: Sudehā said: By whatever means, you must beget a son; you are dear to me. Otherwise, O best of the embodied, I shall give up my body.
m.4.32.24: Sūta said: Hearing what she said, Sudharmā, the best of brahmins, distressed by her insistence, then remembered Śiva in his mind.
m.4.32.25: The brahmin, alert, placed two flowers before the fire, and in his mind regarded the right-hand flower as the one granting the wish for a son.
m.4.32.26: Having made this wager, the brahmin said to his wife: for the fruit of a son, you must pick one of these two flowers.
m.4.32.27: She resolved in her mind: may I have a son, and may the flower my husband has fixed upon come to me.
m.4.32.28: Having said this, she bowed there to Śiva, bowed to the fire, prayed again, and took a single flower.
m.4.32.29: But Sudehā did not take the one her husband had thought of, owing to a delusion arising from Śiva's will.
m.4.32.30: Seeing that, the man heaved a sigh, and remembering the lotus feet of Śiva, said to his wife:
m.4.32.31: Sudharmā said: It has been ordained by the Lord; how could it be otherwise? Give up hope, my dear, and serve the Lord.
m.4.32.32: Having said this, the brahmin himself gave up hope and became engaged in dharmic duties, intent on meditation on Śaṅkara.
m.4.32.33: But Sudehā, out of desire for a child, did not give up her insistence. With folded hands and bowed head, she lovingly replied to her husband:
m.4.32.34: Sudehā said: Let there be no son from me; take another wife at my bidding. Through her a son will surely be born; there is no doubt.
m.4.32.35: Sūta said: Thus entreated, that brahmin, the best of Śaivas, intent on dharma, then spoke to his beloved Sudehā:
m.4.32.36: Sudharmā said: All your sorrow and mine has surely gone. Therefore, my dear, do not now create an obstacle to dharma.
m.4.32.37: Sūta said: Though restrained thus, she then brought her own mother's daughter, her sister, to the house and said this to her husband: take her as wife.
m.4.32.38: Sudharmā said: Now you say, she is dear to me, but later, when she becomes the mother of a son, you will feel rivalry with her.
m.4.32.39: Sūta said: Addressed thus by her husband, Sudehā, his beloved, again spoke with joined hands to her husband Sudharmā, O brahmins:
m.4.32.40: I will not feel rivalry with my sister, O best of the twice-born. Marry her for the sake of a son; this is my bidding.
m.4.32.41: Thus entreated by that beloved wife of his, the brāhmaṇa Sudharmā married that Ghuśmā according to the rite of marriage.
m.4.32.42: Then, having married her, the brāhmaṇa entreated her, Sudehā: this younger one is truly yours; she should always be cared for, O sinless beloved.
m.4.32.43: Having spoken thus, the righteous-souled Sudharmā, foremost among Śaiva devotees, quickly undertook his own observance of dharma as was fitting.
m.4.32.44: And she, the beloved Sudehā, behaved toward that daughter of her mother like a friend; giving up hostility, she cared for her day and night.
m.4.32.45: And the younger wife, having obtained her sister's permission, promptly made one hundred and one earthen liṅgas every day.
m.4.32.46: Ghuśmā, having worshipped them according to the prescribed rite together with the offerings, cast them into the pond situated nearby.
m.4.32.47: Thus every day she performed the worship of Śiva that grants one's desires, dismissing the deity and invoking him again according to the rules of that worship.
m.4.32.48: As she thus performed the worship of Śaṅkara daily, the count of a hundred thousand was completed, bestowing the fruit of all desires.
m.4.32.49: By the grace of Śaṅkara alone, a son was born to her—handsome, fortunate, and a vessel of auspicious qualities.
m.4.32.50: Seeing him, that brāhmaṇa, the foremost knower of dharma, was supremely delighted; yet, unattached and devoted to knowledge and dharma, he enjoyed happiness.
m.4.32.51: Meanwhile Sudehā developed a fierce rivalry toward her; her heart, at first cool, then became like a sword.
m.4.32.52: What vile, sorrow-giving deed took place after that—listen to it with attentive mind, O lords of sages.
m.4.32.iti: Thus ends the thirty-second adhyāya, named The description of the doings of Sudehā and Sudharmā, in the Māhātmya of Ghuśmeśvara, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.4.33.1: Sūta said: Seeing the son of the younger wife, the elder fell into sorrow. Unable to bear that happiness, she quickly turned hostile.
m.4.33.2: Everyone constantly praised her for bearing a son; she could not bear that, nor likewise the child's beauty and other qualities.
m.4.33.3: Seeing that dearly loved son, the vessel of good qualities, beloved of his parents, her heart then burned like fire.
m.4.33.4: Meanwhile brāhmaṇas came to give their daughter in marriage, and he performed his son's marriage right there according to rule.
m.4.33.5: Sudharmā, together with Ghuśmā, attained supreme joy; all the relatives showed honour to that Ghuśmā.
m.4.33.6: Seeing that, Sudehā then burned in her mind; falling into extreme sorrow, she kept saying, Alas, I am ruined!
m.4.33.7: Sudharmā, coming home, presented the bride and his married son to his two dear wives, showing his joy as if to delight them.
m.4.33.8: Ghuśmā was delighted, but Sudehā fell into grief; unable to bear that happiness, she, in her distress, fell to the ground.
m.4.33.9: Ghuśmā said, the bride and son are yours, not mine. And the bride and son affectionately regarded her as mother and mother-in-law.
m.4.33.10: The husband too regarded the elder as dear, not so the younger; even so, the elder then remained impure within her heart.
m.4.33.11: One day the elder, the sorrowful Sudehā, pondered thus in her heart: how may my sorrow be quelled?
m.4.33.12: Sudehā said: The fire in my heart will surely be quenched only by the water of Ghuśmā's eyes, tears born of grief—not otherwise.
m.4.33.13: Therefore today I shall kill her sweet-spoken son; whatever is to come hereafter, let it be. This is my firm resolve.
m.4.33.14: Sūta said: The wicked have no discrimination between what should and should not be done. O brāhmaṇas, the feeling of co-wife rivalry is generally harsh and self-destructive.
m.4.33.15: One day, at night, the elder took a knife and cut at the limbs of the son sleeping with his bride.
m.4.33.16: That night she hacked every limb of Ghuśmā's son into pieces; and, arrogant and very strong, she carried them and threw them into the lake right there.
m.4.33.17: Where Ghuśmā daily cast her liṅgas, there she threw them, came back, and slept at ease, content.
m.4.33.18: Rising at dawn, Ghuśmā did her daily rite as usual, and the excellent Sudharmā himself performed his daily duties.
m.4.33.19: Meanwhile the elder went about the household work, full of joy, the fire in her heart now well quenched.
m.4.33.20: The bride, rising at daybreak, saw the bed wet with blood and strewn with pieces of the body, and fell into grief.
m.4.33.21: She told her mother-in-law: where has your son gone? The bed is wet with blood, and pieces of a body are seen.
m.4.33.22: Alas, I am ruined! Who has done this wicked deed, O you of pure vows? Uttering this, his beloved wept bitterly in many ways.
m.4.33.23: The elder then feigned grief, crying, Alas, I am ruined indeed! She made a show of sorrow outwardly while full of joy in her mind.
m.4.33.24: Ghuśmā too, hearing then the grief of her daughter-in-law, did not swerve from that vow of hers, the daily worship of earthen liṅgas.
m.4.33.25: Her mind did not become agitated in the least; and her husband too remained the same until the vow's rite was completed.
m.4.33.26: At midday, at the end of the worship, though she saw the dreadful bed, even then Ghuśmā showed no grief at all.
m.4.33.27: She thought: he by whom this son was given will surely protect him. He is renowned as fond of his devotees, the Death of Death, the refuge of the good.
m.4.33.28: If Śambhu, the Lord, the sole master, is our protector, what is there to fear? Like a garland-maker, those whom he joins he also separates.
m.4.33.29: What good will my worrying do now? Reflecting on this truth, she did not grieve then, having attained steadfastness in Śiva.
m.4.33.30: Taking the earthen liṅgas, calm-minded as before, she went to the bank of the lake, reciting the names of Śambhu.
m.4.33.31: When, having cast the earthen liṅgas there, she turned back, then she saw her son, risen from the pond, standing on the bank.
m.4.33.32: The son said: Mother, come, let me embrace you. I was dead and am now alive, through the power of your merit and by the grace of Śaṅkara.
m.4.33.33: Sūta said: Seeing her son alive, Ghuśmā, his mother, O brāhmaṇas, did not become elated there, just as earlier she had not been grieved.
m.4.33.34: At that moment Śiva swiftly manifested himself there in the form of light, and Maheśa, well pleased, spoke.
m.4.33.35: Śiva said: I am pleased; ask a boon. This son was killed by the wicked woman; and I shall kill her with my trident, O lovely-faced one.
m.4.33.36: Sūta said: Then Ghuśmā, bowing deeply to Śiva, humbly asked a boon: O Lord, this Sudehā, my sister, should be protected by you.
m.4.33.37: Śiva said: Harm was done by her; how can you do good to her? Sudehā, the evildoer, deserves to be slain.
m.4.33.38: Ghuśmā said: By the mere sight of you no sin remains. Now that she has seen you, that sin of hers would be reduced to ashes.
m.4.33.39: He who does good in return for wrongs—by the mere sight of him, sin goes far away.
m.4.33.40: This wondrous saying of the Lord I have heard, O God. Therefore, O Sadāśiva, let kindness be shown to her by whom this was done.
m.4.33.41: Sūta said: Thus addressed by her there, Maheśvara, the ocean of compassion, affectionate to his devotees, became exceedingly pleased once again and spoke to her.
m.4.33.42: Śiva said: O Ghuśmā, ask for another boon, and I shall grant what is beneficial to you. I am well pleased with your devotion and with you, by your nature free from perturbation.
m.4.33.43: Having heard his words, she said: O Lord, if a boon is to be given by you, then for the protection of the worlds you should dwell here under a name derived from mine.
m.4.33.44: Then Śiva, the Great Lord, well pleased, said there: I shall dwell here by your name, called Ghuśmeśa, the giver of happiness.
m.4.33.45: May my auspicious liṅga, named Ghuśmeśa, become well renowned. May this lake always become the abode of liṅgas.
m.4.33.46: Therefore it will be famed in the three worlds by the name Śivālaya. This lake will always grant all desires through its mere sight.
m.4.33.47: O lady of good vows, in your lineage, up to a hundred and one generations, such excellent sons will be born; there is no doubt.
m.4.33.48: They will have good wives and good wealth, long life, discernment, learning and generosity, for attaining the fruits of enjoyment and liberation.
m.4.33.49: A hundred and one sons abounding in virtues will be born; such a very splendid extension of the lineage will come about.
m.4.33.50: Sūta said: Having said this, Śiva then took the form of a liṅga there, renowned by the name Ghuśmeśa, and the lake became known as Śivālaya.
m.4.33.51: Sudharmā, Ghuśmā and Sudehā came together and quickly performed a hundred and one circumambulations of Śiva.
m.4.33.52: Having worshipped Maheśa and embraced one another, and having cast off the impurity within, they attained supreme happiness there.
m.4.33.53: Seeing the son alive, Sudehā became ashamed. Having sought forgiveness from the two, O brahmins, she performed a vow that removes her own sins.
m.4.33.54: Thus, O lords of sages, did this liṅga named Ghuśmeśa come into being. By seeing it and worshipping it, happiness ever increases.
m.4.33.55: Thus I have narrated to you the series of Jyotirliṅgas, twelve in number, which grant all desires and bestow enjoyment and liberation.
m.4.33.56: Whoever reads or even hears this story of the Jyotirliṅgas is freed from all sins and obtains enjoyment and liberation.
m.4.33.iti: Thus ends the thirty-third adhyāya, named The description of the glory of the origin of the Ghuśmeśa jyotirliṅga, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.4.34.1: Vyāsa said: Having heard these words of that Sūta, the lords among sages praised him highly and spoke to him, out of a wish for the welfare of the worlds.
m.4.34.2: The sages said: O Sūta, you know everything; therefore we ask you. O lord, tell us the greatness of the Harīśvara liṅga.
m.4.34.3: We have heard before that the discus Sudarśana was obtained by Viṣṇu through worship of him; O dear one, tell us that story too in detail.
m.4.34.4: Sūta said: Listen, O best of sages, to the auspicious story of Harīśvara, from which Viṣṇu formerly obtained Sudarśana from Śaṅkara.
m.4.34.5: At a certain time the Daityas became exceedingly powerful; they oppressed the worlds and brought about the destruction of dharma.
m.4.34.6: Those gods, oppressed by the Daityas of great strength and valour, told their sorrow to Viṣṇu, the protector of the immortals.
m.4.34.7: The gods said: O lord, show compassion; we are sorely oppressed by the Daityas. Where shall we go and what shall we do? We have taken refuge in you, the giver of shelter.
m.4.34.8: Sūta said: Having heard these words of the gods, distressed in heart, Viṣṇu remembered the lotus feet of Śiva and spoke.
m.4.34.9: Viṣṇu said: O gods, I shall accomplish your task by worshipping Giriśa. These enemies are very strong indeed and must be conquered with great effort.
m.4.34.10: Sūta said: Thus addressed by the mighty Viṣṇu, all those gods, considering the wicked Daityas as already slain, went each to his own abode.
m.4.34.11: Viṣṇu, for the victory of the immortals, worshipped Śiva, the overlord of all the immortals, the witness of all, the imperishable.
m.4.34.12: Going near Kailāsa, Hari himself performed austerities, having made a fire-pit and installed the fire in front.
m.4.34.13: With the rite of the earthen liṅga, with mantras of many kinds and with numerous hymns, he joyfully worshipped Giriśa.
m.4.34.14: O lords of sages, worshipping with lotuses born from the lake called Mānasa, Hari himself, having fixed his posture there, did not move.
m.4.34.15: Until his grace is granted, I must by all means remain here. Having made this resolve, Hari worshipped Śiva.
m.4.34.16: O brahmins, when Hara did not become pleased with Hari, then the blessed Viṣṇu became absorbed in reflection.
m.4.34.17: He reflected thus in his own mind: service has been rendered in many ways, yet Hara, the grace-bestowing lord, has not become pleased.
m.4.34.18: Then Viṣṇu, greatly astonished and filled with supreme devotion, lovingly praised the Supreme Lord with a thousand names.
m.4.34.19: Uttering a name-mantra for each, he offered him a lotus, and so worshipped Śambhu, who is tender toward those who come to him for refuge.
m.4.34.20: Then, to test Viṣṇu's devotion, Śaṅkara took away one lotus from the thousand lotuses.
m.4.34.21: Viṣṇu did not perceive that wondrous act caused by Śiva's māyā; but realising that the number was short, he became intent on searching for it.
m.4.34.22: Firm in his vow, he wandered the whole earth to please him; not finding it, he of pure soul offered one of his eyes.
m.4.34.23: Seeing that, Śaṅkara, the remover of all sorrows, became pleased; he appeared right there and spoke words to Hari.
m.4.34.24: Śiva said: O Hari, I am pleased with you; ask for whatever boon you desire. I grant what your heart longs for; there is nothing that cannot be given to you.
m.4.34.25: Sūta said: Hearing those words of Śambhu, Keśava, delighted in mind and filled with great joy, spoke to Śiva with folded hands.
m.4.34.26: Viṣṇu said: What need I say before you, for you abide as the inner controller? Still, O Lord, it is spoken out of respect for your command.
m.4.34.27: The universe is oppressed by the Daityas; there is no happiness for us, O Sadāśiva. O master, my own weapon does not prevail in slaying the Daityas.
m.4.34.28: What shall I do? Where shall I go? I have no other supreme protector. Therefore, O Supreme Lord, I have come to you for refuge.
m.4.34.29: Sūta said: Having said this and bowed to Śiva, the Supreme Self, he himself, greatly afflicted, stood before Śambhu.
m.4.34.30: Sūta said: Hearing these words of Viṣṇu, Maheśvara, God of gods, gave him his own discus Sudarśana, a mass of radiance.
m.4.34.31: Obtaining it, the blessed Viṣṇu swiftly slew with that discus all those very powerful Daityas, without effort.
m.4.34.32: The world attained supreme well-being, the gods became happy, and Hari, much pleased at obtaining his weapon, was supremely joyful.
m.4.34.33: The sages said: What is that thousand-name hymn of Śaṅkara? Tell us, by which Maheśvara, being pleased, gave the discus to Hari.
m.4.34.34: Tell me its glory, together with the dialogue with Śiva, and Śambhu's compassion toward Viṣṇu, exactly as it was.
m.4.34.35: Vyāsa said: Hearing these words of those sages of purified minds, Sūta remembered the lotus feet of Śiva and spoke.
m.4.34.iti: Thus ends the thirty-fourth adhyāya, named The description of Viṣṇu's obtaining the Sudarśana discus, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.4.35.1: Sūta said: Listen, O best of sages: today I shall recite the thousand names of Śiva, by which Maheśvara was pleased.
m.4.35.2: Śrī Viṣṇu said: Śiva, Hara, Mṛḍa, Rudra, Puṣkara, the Lotus-eyed, he who is reached by those who seek, he of good conduct, Śarva, Śambhu, Maheśvara;
m.4.35.3: Moon-crested, Moon-diademed, the Universe, the Lord of the all-sustaining earth, the gathered essence of Vedānta, the Skull-bearer, the Blue-red One;
m.4.35.4: The support of meditation, the Unlimited, the husband of Gaurī, the lord of the gaṇas, of eight forms, whose form is the universe, the means to the three aims of life and to heaven;
m.4.35.5: Attainable through knowledge, of firm wisdom, God of gods, Three-eyed, Vāmadeva, Mahādeva, the Skilful, the Master, the Firm;
m.4.35.6: Of universal form, the Odd-eyed, Lord of speech, the purest of the pure, in accord with all means of valid knowledge, bull-bannered, riding the bull;
m.4.35.7: The Lord, bearer of Pināka, bearer of the khaṭvāṅga, of wondrous attire, the Ancient, dispeller of darkness, the great Yogin, the Protector, Brahmā, and Dhūrjaṭi;
m.4.35.8: Death of Death, clad in a hide, the Fortunate, whose nature is Om, the Unbound, the Person, worthy of worship, Durvāsas, chastiser of the triple city;
m.4.35.9: Bearing divine weapons, preceptor of Skanda, the Supreme Abider, higher than the highest, without beginning, middle or end, Lord of the mountain, husband of the mountain's daughter;
m.4.35.10: Friend of Kubera, Śrīkaṇṭha, the best among the world's classes, the Gentle, knowable in samādhi, bow-bearer, Blue-throated, axe-bearer;
m.4.35.11: Large-eyed, hunter of the deer, Lord of the gods, heater of the sun, abode of dharma, field of forbearance, the Blessed One, piercer of Bhaga's eyes;
m.4.35.12: The Fierce, Lord of creatures, Tārkṣya, fond of devotees, scorcher of foes, the Giver, mine of compassion, the Able, wearer of matted hair, chastiser of Kāma;
m.4.35.13: Dwelling in the cremation ground, the Subtle, abiding in the cremation ground, the Great Lord, maker of the worlds, lord of beasts, the great Maker, the great Remedy;
m.4.35.14: The Higher, lord of cows, the Protector, reachable by knowledge, the Primeval, Policy, good Policy, pure-souled, Soma, delighting in Soma, the Happy One;
m.4.35.15: Drinker of Soma, drinker of nectar, the Gentle, of great vigour, of great splendour, full of radiance, full of nectar, consisting of food, and lord of ambrosia;
m.4.35.16: Having no born enemy, the Light, worthy of honour, bearer of oblations, maker of the worlds, maker of the Vedas, author of the sūtras, the Eternal;
m.4.35.17: The great sage Kapila as teacher, the light of the universe, Three-eyed, Pināka in hand, god on earth, giver of well-being, doer of well-being, the Wise;
m.4.35.18: The abode of the Creator, maker of abodes, all-pervading, perceptible in all, creator of Brahmā, creator of the universe, Creation itself, fond of karṇikāra flowers, the Poet;
m.4.35.19: Śākha, Viśākha, Gośākha, Śiva, the unsurpassed physician, he whose waters are the flow of the Gaṅgā, the Auspicious, the Abundant, the Architect, the Steady;
m.4.35.20: Self-conquered, of disciplined self, charioteer whose vehicle is the elements, accompanied by the gaṇas, whose body is the gaṇas, of fine fame, the dispeller of doubts;
m.4.35.21: Kāmadeva, protector of desires, whose body is smeared with ash, fond of ash, lying in ash, the Desiring, the Lovely, author of the scriptures;
m.4.35.22: The Return of cycles, of unreturning self, a mass of dharma, Sadāśiva, the Stainless, four-armed, hard to dwell with, hard to approach;
m.4.35.23: Hard to obtain, hard to reach, the Fortress, skilled in all weapons, abiding in the yoga of the self, the fine thread, increaser of the lineage;
m.4.35.24: Of auspicious limbs, the essence of the world, Lord of the universe, Janārdana, purifier through ash, Meru, the Vigourous, of pure form;
m.4.35.25: Unattainable, yet attainable by the good, assuming the form of a monkey-servant, golden-seeded, the Ancient, taker of the life of foes, the Mighty;
m.4.35.26: The great lake, the great abyss, praised by hosts of siddhas and gods, wearing a tiger-skin garment, adorned with serpents, the great Being, the great Treasure;
m.4.35.27: Eater of nectar, nectar-bodied, Pāñcajanya, the Shatterer, abiding in the twenty-five principles, the Pārijāta, the higher and the lower;
m.4.35.28: Easy to attain, of good vows, the Hero, treasury of the Veda of Brahman, the Treasure, guru of the varṇas and āśramas, the student, conqueror of foes, tormentor of foes;
m.4.35.29: The Āśrama, the ascetic mendicant, the Lean, possessed of knowledge, lord of the immovable mountains, the very standard of truth, hard to know, the fair-winged, borne by the wind;
m.4.35.30: Bow-wielder, the science of archery, a heap of virtues, mine of virtues, the True, devoted to truth, the Undejected, whose limbs are dharma, the means of dharma;
m.4.35.31: Of endless vision, Bliss, the Rod of chastisement, the Tamer, Restraint itself, worthy of salutation, of great māyā, skilled in fashioning the universe;
m.4.35.32: Free from passion, of humble self, the Ascetic, sustainer of beings, in the guise of a madman, the Hidden, conqueror of desire, dear to the Unconquered Viṣṇu;
m.4.35.33: Of auspicious nature, the Capable, Prajāpati of all worlds, the Swift, the Deliverer, the Wise, the Chief, the Lord, the Imperishable;
m.4.35.34: Guardian of the world, whose self is hidden, the beginning of the kalpa, lotus-eyed, knower of the true meaning of Vedas and śāstras, beyond rules, the refuge of the disciplined;
m.4.35.35: The Moon, the Sun, Saturn, Ketu, of excellent limbs, coral-hued, won over by devotion, the supreme Brahman, who loosed the arrow at the deer, the Sinless;
m.4.35.36: The Mountain, dwelling on the mountain, the Beloved, the supreme Self, the world's guru, abode of all actions, the Content, the Auspicious, surrounded by auspiciousness;
m.4.35.37: Of great austerity, of long austerity, the most massive, the Old, the Fixed, the Day, the Year, Pervasion, the Measure, the supreme Austerity;
m.4.35.38: Maker of the year, the conviction of mantras, all-seeing, the Unborn, Lord of all, the Perfected, of great seed, of great strength;
m.4.35.39: The Yogin, the Fitting, of great radiance, Accomplishment, the origin of all, the Ungraspable, Vasu, of generous mind, the True, remover of all sins, Hara;
m.4.35.40: Shining with fair fame, the Glorious, whose limbs are the Vedas, knower of the Veda, the Sage, the Radiant, the Food, the Enjoyer, Lord of the world, hard to withstand.
m.4.35.41: He is the Immortal, the Eternal, the Tranquil, the one with arrows in hand, the Majestic, the bearer of the water-pot, the Archer, the one beyond the reach of speech and mind.
m.4.35.42: Beyond the senses, the possessor of great Māyā, the abode of all, the Crossroads of four paths, the yogin of Time, the one of great sound, of great zeal, of great strength.
m.4.35.43: Of great intellect, of great valour, the one who roams with the bhūtas, the destroyer of cities (Purandara), the night-wanderer, the one who moves among the pretas, of great power, of great radiance.
m.4.35.44: Whose form cannot be described, the Glorious, the teacher of all, the one whose movement is swift as the mind, the greatly learned, the one free of great illusion, the self-controlled, the Fixed and the Unfixed.
m.4.35.45: The bearer of vigour, brilliance and radiance, the Progenitor, the ruler of all, fond of dance, ever-dancing, whose self is light, the Illuminator.
m.4.35.46: Of clear syllables, the Wise, the Mantra, the Equal, the flood of essence, the maker of the beginning of the yugas, the revolver of the yugas, the Profound, the one whose mount is the bull.
m.4.35.47: The Beloved, the Undifferentiated, dear to the cultured, easily attained, the purifier of essence, whose form is the tīrtha, whose name is a tīrtha, who is seen at the tīrthas, and the giver of tīrthas.
m.4.35.48: The treasury of the waters, the Substratum, the hard-to-conquer, the knower of the time for victory, the Established, the knower of the means of valid knowledge, the one with golden armour, Hari.
m.4.35.49: The Liberator, the host of gods, the lord of knowledge, the one abiding in the bindu, of childlike form, not maddened by strength, the Changeless agent, the Unfathomable, the Hidden One.
m.4.35.50: The Instrument, the Cause, the Doer, the releaser from all bonds, Resolve, the Orderer, the giver of abode, the one born at the beginning of the world.
m.4.35.51: The giver of the guru, the Charming, the Undivided, whose self is being, established in the Self, the lord of heroes, Vīrabhadra, the ordainer of the hero's posture, Virāṭ.
m.4.35.52: The crest-jewel of heroes, the Knower, consciousness-bliss, the bearer of the river, the upholder of command, the trident-bearer, Śipiviṣṭa, the abode of auspiciousness.
m.4.35.53: The Vālakhilya, the one with the great bow, the sharp-rayed sun, the Deaf one, the sky-mover, the Delightful, the good refuge, Subrahmaṇya, the lord of nectar.
m.4.35.54: Maghavān, Kauśika, rich in cows, Cessation, the means of all, the one with an eye on the forehead, whose body is the universe, the Essence, the bearer of the wheel of saṃsāra.
m.4.35.55: Whose rod of punishment never fails, the Impartial, the Golden, endowed with Brahmic splendour, the Supreme Reality, the Highest, the wielder of Māyā, Śambara, the tiger-eyed.
m.4.35.56: Lustre, Viriñci, the kinsman of heaven, the lord of speech, the lord of day, Ravi, Virocana, Skanda, the Ruler, the son of Vivasvat, Yama.
m.4.35.57: Reasoning, and the one of exalted fame, the affectionate, the conqueror of foes, the lord of Kailāsa, the Beloved, Savitṛ, the one whose eye is the sun.
m.4.35.58: The most learned, free from fear, the sustainer of the universe, the unobstructed, the Eternal, of fixed auspiciousness, the one whose hearing and praise are meritorious.
m.4.35.59: The far-hearing, the all-enduring, the one to be meditated upon, the destroyer of bad dreams, the one who carries across, the slayer of evil deeds, the one to be known, the unbearable, the Unborn.
m.4.35.60: The Beginningless, Bhūḥ, Bhuvaḥ, Lakṣmī, the diademed, the lord of the gods, the protector of the universe, the maker of the universe, the great hero, the one with splendid armlets.
m.4.35.61: The Begetter, the origin of the birth of beings, the affectionate, the wise in conduct, the Husband, Vasiṣṭha, Kaśyapa, the Sun, the Terrible, the one of terrible valour.
m.4.35.62: The Praṇava, the one who walks the true path, the great treasury, of great wealth, the lord of birth, Mahādeva, the one who has crossed to the far shore of all the Āgamas.
m.4.35.63: Reality, the knower of reality, the one Self, the all-pervading, the ornament of the universe, the Ṛṣi, the Brāhmaṇa, the one who transcends lordship, birth, death and old age.
m.4.35.64: The source of the five sacrifices, the lord of the universe, of spotless rising, self-born, without beginning or end, the affectionate, the sustainer of the world of devotees.
m.4.35.65: The beloved of Gāyatrī, the Tall, the abode of the universe, the maker of light, the Child, the one delighting in the mountain, the Emperor, Suṣeṇa, the slayer of the gods' enemies.
m.4.35.66: The Unfailing, and Ariṣṭanemi, Kumuda, free from fever, self-luminous, the light of the body, the light of the Self, the Unwavering.
m.4.35.67: The Tawny, the one with a reddish-brown beard, the forehead-eyed, whose body is the triple Veda, the mass of knowledge, of great statecraft, the origin of the universe, the Deluge.
m.4.35.68: Bhaga, Vivasvat, Āditya, the one who has gone beyond yoga, the lord of heaven, whose names are of auspicious qualities, the destroyer of sin, whose sight is meritorious.
m.4.35.69: Of noble fame, the Energetic, the true yogin, consisting of being and non-being, garlanded with stars, the lord of heaven, the one whose seat is the Svādhiṣṭhāna.
m.4.35.70: The Pure, the remover of sin, Maṇipūra, the one moving in the sky, seated in the lotus of the heart, Śakra, the Tranquil, Vṛṣākapi.
m.4.35.71: The Hot, the lord of the house, the Dark, the Capable, the destroyer of misfortune, the enemy of adharma, the Unknowable, the much-invoked, the much-renowned.
m.4.35.72: The womb of Brahman, the vast womb, the cow of dharma, the source of wealth, the one who desires the welfare of the world, the Well-gone, the Youth, the source of welfare.
m.4.35.73: Golden-hued, the Luminous, delighting in various beings, Sound, free from passion, the overseer of the eyes, Viśvāmitra, the lord of wealth.
m.4.35.74: The light of Brahman, the abode of riches, the great light, the Unsurpassed, the maternal grandfather, Mātariśvan, the Wind, the wearer of a garland of serpents.
m.4.35.75: Pulastya, Pulaha, Agastya, Jātūkarṇya, Parāśara, the unveiled and unobstructed, the son of Viriñci, Viṣṭaraśravas.
m.4.35.76: Self-born, Aniruddha, Atri, the embodiment of knowledge, of great fame, the foremost of the world's heroes, the Hero, the Fierce, of true valour.
m.4.35.77: Serpent-like, the great kalpa, the wish-fulfilling tree, the bearer of the moon's digit, the adorner, the Immovable, the Radiant, exalted in prowess.
m.4.35.78: The lord of life and of sound, the Swift, the Leaper, the one whose charioteer is the peacock-rider, the Unattached, the Guest, the subduer of Śakra, the one seated on trees.
m.4.35.79: The one famed for wealth, the bearer of oblations, the Glowing, the consumer of all, the one to be recited, the queller of old age and the rest, of red essence, Tanūnapāt.
m.4.35.80: The one with great horses, the source of the sky, of fair form, the destroyer of darkness, the summer heat, the Burner, the Cloud, the fair-eyed, the conqueror of enemy cities.
m.4.35.81: He is the pleasant breeze, the well-perfected, the fragrant, the one whose nature is the cool season; spring, Mādhava, summer, Nabhasya, the bearer of seeds.
m.4.35.82: He is Aṅgiras, the preceptor, Ātreya, the stainless, the bearer of the universe, the purifier, the right-minded, the learned, the master of the three Vedas, the one with an excellent mount.
m.4.35.83: He is mind, intellect and ego-sense, the knower of the field, the guardian of the field, Jamadagni, the treasury of strength, Vigāla, the universal Gālava.
m.4.35.84: He is Aghora, the unsurpassed, the sacrifice, the best, the giver of final beatitude, the mountain, the one lustrous like jasmine against the sky, the foe of the Dānavas, the subduer of enemies.
m.4.35.85: He is the creator of night, the lovely, the one free of thorns, the one who bears away the thorns of the world, the one of the four Vedas, of the four states, the clever, the one dear to the clever.
m.4.35.86: He is the sacred tradition and the collected tradition, the one whose abodes are sacred fords, deities and auspicious shrines; the many-formed, the great-formed, the all-formed, the moving and the unmoving.
m.4.35.87: He is the maker of right order, the just, the one reached through reasoning, the stainless, the thousand-headed, the lord of the gods, the shatterer of all weapons.
m.4.35.88: He is the shaven-headed, the strange-formed, the valiant, the staff-bearer, the self-controlled, the highest in virtues, the tawny-eyed, the overseer of beings, the blue-necked, the one free of affliction.
m.4.35.89: He is the thousand-armed, the lord of all, the refuge, the upholder of all worlds, the one seated on the lotus, the supreme light, the giver of the fruit handed down through succession.
m.4.35.90: He is the lotus-wombed, the great womb, the womb of the universe, the discerning, the knower of the higher and the lower, the boon-giver, the most excellent, and the one of mighty sound.
m.4.35.91: He is the preceptor of gods and asuras, the god, the one saluted by gods and asuras, the great friend of gods and asuras, the great lord of gods and asuras.
m.4.35.92: He is the ruler of gods and asuras, the divine, the great refuge of gods and asuras, the one composed of the god of gods, the inconceivable, the self-born god of gods.
m.4.35.93: He is the one of true origin, the tiger against the asuras, the lion among gods, the sun, the best of those who move at the head of the gods, the highest of the highest of all gods.
m.4.35.94: He is the one delighting in the knowledge of Śiva, the glorious, the one fond of Śikhi and Śrīparvata, the thunderbolt-handed, the one with the perfected sword, the one who struck down Narasiṃha.
m.4.35.95: He is the celibate, the wanderer through the worlds, the practiser of dharma, the lord of wealth, Nandī, Nandīśvara, the endless, the bearer of the vow of nakedness, the pure.
m.4.35.96: He is the presiding lord of the liṅga, the overseer of the gods, the master of yoga, the bringer of the ages, the one of his own dharma, the one dwelling in heaven, the one of heavenly voice, the one whose sound is made of musical notes.
m.4.35.97: He is the lord of Bāṇa, the maker of seeds, the doer of dharma, the source of dharma, pretence, greed, the knower of wealth, Śambhu, the great lord of all beings.
m.4.35.98: He is the one dwelling in the cremation ground, the three-eyed, the bridge, the one of incomparable form, the one whose clear light transcends the world, Tryambaka, the one adorned with serpents.
m.4.35.99: He is the foe of Andhaka, the enemy of the sacrifice of Dakṣa, the one who struck down Viṣṇu's neck, the faultless, the one of imperishable virtues, the enemy of Dakṣa, the breaker of Pūṣan's teeth.
m.4.35.100: He is Dhūrjaṭi, the one with the broken axe, the one with parts and the partless, the sinless, the timeless, the support of all, the one of pale lustre, Mṛḍa, the dancer.
m.4.35.101: He is the full, the fulfiller, the holy, the tender-youthful, the fair-eyed, the one fond of Sāman chants, the gentle, the one of holy fame, the one free of ailment.
m.4.35.102: He is swift as thought, the maker of sacred fords, the one with matted hair, the lord of life, the one who ends life, the eternal, the one whose seed is wealth, the giver of wealth.
m.4.35.103: He is the good goal, the good deed, accomplishment, the noble-born, the thorn to the wicked, the bearer of the moon's digit, the one who has become Mahākāla, the one devoted to truth.
m.4.35.104: He is the maker of the world's welfare, and the abode of bliss beyond the world, the reviver of the moon, the ruler, the one hidden from the world, the great overlord.
m.4.35.105: He is the kinsman of the world, the lord of the world, the grateful, the one adorned with fame, the undecaying, the imperishable, the beloved, the best of all weapon-bearers.
m.4.35.106: He is the radiant, the bearer of splendour, the leader of the worlds, the atom, the one of pure smile, the serene-souled, the hard to conquer, the hard to transgress.
m.4.35.107: He is the luminous, the lord of the world, the formless, the lord of the waters, the one with the gourd-lute, the one of great wrath, the sorrowless, the destroyer of sorrow.
m.4.35.108: He is the protector of the three worlds, the lord of the three worlds, the purity of all, Adhokṣaja, the god of unmanifest marks, the manifest and unmanifest, the lord of the people.
m.4.35.109: He is the one of excellent conduct, of excellent qualities, the essence, the one whose wealth is honour, Maya, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, the protector of creatures, the swan, the one moving like a swan, the bird.
m.4.35.110: He is the ordainer, the disposer and the sustainer, the creator, the destroyer, the four-faced, the dweller on the peak of Kailāsa, the dweller in all, the ever-moving.
m.4.35.111: He is Hiraṇyagarbha, Druhiṇa, the protector of beings and the lord of the earth, the true yogin, the knower of yoga, the yogin, the boon-giver, the one dear to brāhmaṇas.
m.4.35.112: He is dear to the gods, lord of the gods, knower of the gods, the one who cares for the gods, the odd-eyed, the wide-eyed, the giver of dharma, the increaser of dharma.
m.4.35.113: He is free of possessiveness, free of ego, free of delusion, free of calamity, the slayer of pride, the giver of pride, the proud, the one who turns all the seasons.
m.4.35.114: He is the conqueror of thousands, the thousand-rayed, the gentle-natured and gracious, the lord of past, future and present, the origin, the destroyer of worldly prosperity.
m.4.35.115: He is the purpose and the purposeless, the great treasury, the one solely skilled in others' affairs, the thornless, the one who has attained bliss, the guileless, the crusher of deceit.
m.4.35.116: He is the strong-spirited, the sāttvic, the one of true fame, the one who made the scriptures out of love, the unshaken, the appreciator of virtues, the many-selved, the doer of many deeds.
m.4.35.117: He is the well-pleased, the fair-faced, the subtle, the easy of access, the southern breeze, the one carried on Nandī's shoulder, the burden-bearer, the manifest, the increaser of love.
m.4.35.118: He is the unconquered, the essence of all beings, Govinda, the one whose vehicle is sattva, the unsupported, the self-supported, the perfected, the one of pure form, the one whose wealth is fame.
m.4.35.119: He is the bearer of the boar's tusk, the horned one, the mighty, the sole leader, the illuminator of the Veda, the one possessed of the Veda, the sole kinsman, the doer of many deeds.
m.4.35.120: He is the one fond of Śrī whose undertakings are auspicious, the calm and blessed, the impartial, fame, the one lying on the ground, the ornament, prosperity, the maker of beings, the sustainer of beings.
m.4.35.121: He is the Unshakable, the one whose body is devotion, the Slayer of Time, the Blue-and-Red one; the great renouncer whose vow is truth, wholly devoted to eternal peace.
m.4.35.122: He whose activity is for the sake of others, the Giver of boons, the Dispassionate, the Skilled; the Giver of good, the Doer of good, whose name is auspicious, who is himself the Auspicious.
m.4.35.123: He who asks for nothing, the Attributeless, the Witness, indeed the Non-doer, golden in splendour; good by his very nature, the Impartial one standing in the middle, the Slayer of enemies, the Destroyer of obstacles.
m.4.35.124: The one with a crest, the armoured one, the Trident-bearer, the one with matted locks, the shaven one, and the one with earrings; the Deathless, the All-seeing, the Lion, the Mass of radiance, the Great Jewel.
m.4.35.125: The Innumerable, whose self is immeasurable, the Mighty, the Knower of valour; the one to be known, whose nature is detachment, the Lord of sages both high and low.
m.4.35.126: The Unsurpassed, the Invincible, sweet and pleasing to behold; the Lord of the gods, the Refuge, the All, Brahman as sound (the Word), the goal of the good.
m.4.35.127: The one on the side of Time, the Death of Death, who has made Vāsuki into a bracelet; the great archer, the Sustainer of the earth, the Stainless, the Unfettered.
m.4.35.128: The Jewel of the sky (the sun), the Saviour, the Blessed, the Giver of accomplishments, the Means of accomplishment; enveloping on every side, the Praiseworthy, the broad-chested, the mighty-armed.
m.4.35.129: The Source of all, the Fearless, dear to Nara and Nārāyaṇa; the Untainted, whose self is beyond the manifold world, the Flawless, the Remover of defects.
m.4.35.130: The one to be praised, fond of praise, the Praiser himself, embodied as Vyāsa, the Unrestrained; whose means are faultless, the Treasury of knowledge, fond of rasa (essence/delight).
m.4.35.131: Of tranquil intellect, the Unimpaired, the Gatherer of all, ever beautiful; foremost among those clad in tiger-skin, Lord of the earth, Śākalya, Lord of the night (the moon).
m.4.35.132: The Teacher of the highest truth, Datta (the Given), the Wise one, affectionate to those who take refuge in him; Soma (united with Umā), the Knower of rasa, the Giver of rasa, the Support of all beings.
m.4.35.133: Thus with a thousand names Hari praised Hara; he entreated Śambhu and worshipped him with lotuses.
m.4.35.134: Then that playful Śambhu performed a deed, O Brahmins, most wonderful and delightful; listen to that very deed with reverence.
m.4.35.iti: Thus ends the thirty-fifth adhyāya, named The description of the thousand names of Śiva, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.4.36.1: Sūta said: Having heard the divine hymn of his own thousand names composed by Viṣṇu, adorned with supreme names, Maheśvara became pleased.
m.4.36.2: To test Hari, the Lord Maheśvara, ruler of the worlds, then hid one lotus among the lotuses.
m.4.36.3: Then, among those thousand lotuses, one was found missing; and then Viṣṇu became distressed in his worship of Śiva.
m.4.36.4: He reflected in his heart: where indeed has the lotus gone? Let what has gone be gone, gladly; is my eye not a lotus?
m.4.36.5: Resolving thus, he plucked out his eye, relying on all his fortitude, and worshipped Śiva with devotion, and praised him with it.
m.4.36.6: Then Hara, the guru of the world, seeing Hari who had praised him and was in such a state, appeared, crying out, don't, don't.
m.4.36.7: Maheśvara swiftly descended from the maṇḍala of his own earthen liṅga that had been installed by Hari.
m.4.36.8: Bowing to Śambhu, who bore the form as described and had arisen from a mass of radiance, and standing before him, he praised him in a special way.
m.4.36.9: Then Mahādeva, pleased and as if smiling, looking with compassion at Viṣṇu who stood with joined palms, spoke.
m.4.36.10: Śaṅkara said: O Hari, all this that your mind desires is known to me — especially the task of the gods, since your self is devoted to the gods' task.
m.4.36.11: For the accomplishment of the gods' task and for the destruction of the Daityas, I give you a refuge and the splendid discus named Sudarśana.
m.4.36.12: The form you have seen, which brings happiness to all the worlds and was assumed for your good, O lord of the gods — meditate on it steadfastly.
m.4.36.13: When remembered on the battlefield, it destroys the sorrows of the gods. This discus, this form, this hymn of a thousand names —
m.4.36.14: those who always listen to them with devotion will have unfailing fulfilment of all desires through my grace, O you of good vows.
m.4.36.15: Sūta said: Having said this, he gave the discus Sudarśana, brilliant as ten thousand suns, arisen from his own foot, destroyer of all enemies.
m.4.36.16: Viṣṇu too, after duly consecrating it, received it then facing north; and having bowed to Mahādeva, Viṣṇu spoke these words.
m.4.36.17: Viṣṇu said: Listen, O God: what should I meditate on and what should I recite, O Lord, for the destruction of sorrows? Tell me, O Śaṅkara, benefactor of the world.
m.4.36.18: Sūta said: Thus asked by him, Śiva, satisfied and with a pleased mind, then spoke to Viṣṇu, the helper of the gods.
m.4.36.19: Śiva said: O Hari, my form is to be meditated on for the calming of all misfortunes; for the destruction of many sorrows, recite the thousand names.
m.4.36.20: My discus is always to be borne by you with care, O Viṣṇu, for the attainment of all you desire; this indeed is the best of all discuses.
m.4.36.21: And others who will recite it or have it recited daily — sorrow does not arise for them even in a dream; there is no doubt of this.
m.4.36.22: When a crisis arising from kings has come, if a man performs a hundred recitations, complete with their accessory rites and according to rule, he obtains well-being.
m.4.36.23: This indeed destroys disease, is supreme in granting learning and wealth, bestows all desires, is holy, and always grants devotion to Śiva.
m.4.36.24: Whatever excellent fruit men here recite it with in view, they will obtain that fruit truly and in the highest degree; there is no doubt of this.
m.4.36.25: And whoever, rising early in the morning and performing my worship, recites it daily in my presence — success is not far from him.
m.4.36.26: He obtains complete worldly success fulfilling all desires, and at the end he attains liberation in the form of union (sāyujya); there is no doubt here.
m.4.36.27: Sūta said: Having thus spoken to Viṣṇu, Śaṅkara, with a delighted mind, touched him with both hands, and Giriśa spoke to him again.
m.4.36.28: Śiva said: I am the giver of boons, O best of gods; choose boons as you wish. Surely I have been won over by your devotion and by this hymn, O you of good vows.
m.4.36.29: Sūta said: Thus addressed by the God of gods, Viṣṇu, greatly delighted, bowed to that God of gods and with joined palms spoke these words.
m.4.36.30: Viṣṇu said: Just as grace is being shown now, O Lord, so too hereafter supreme grace should be shown by you, especially, out of your compassion, O master.
m.4.36.31: Devotion to you, O Mahādeva — be gracious — is the highest boon; I desire no other, since for your devotees there are no afflictions at all, O Lord.
m.4.36.32: Sūta said: Hearing those words of his, Bhava, exceedingly compassionate, touched his body, and the moon-crested one spoke.
m.4.36.33: Śiva said: O Hari, may your devotion to me always be unfailing; and be ever worthy of salutation and worship in the world, even by the gods.
m.4.36.34: Your name Viśvambhara will be supreme and remove all sins, by my grace, O best of gods; there is no doubt.
m.4.36.35: Sūta said: Having said this, Rudra, the Lord, master of all gods, vanished right there while Viṣṇu looked on, O great sages.
m.4.36.36: The blessed Janārdana too, having obtained that auspicious discus by Śaṅkara's word, rejoiced greatly in his heart.
m.4.36.37: Meditating on that form of Śambhu, he recited this hymn continually, taught it, and imparted it to devotees.
m.4.36.38: What you asked I have thus narrated, which removes the sins of those who hear it. What more, O excellent ones, do you wish to ask again?
m.4.36.iti: Thus ends the thirty-sixth adhyāya, named The description of the fruit of the hymn of the thousand names of Śiva, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.4.37.1: The sages said: O Sūta, O Sūta, most fortunate one, you are full of knowledge, O you of good vows. Tell us once more, in detail, the deeds of Śiva alone.
m.4.37.2: Tell how the ancient kings, sages and gods too performed the worship of him alone, the best of gods.
m.4.37.3: Sūta said: Well asked, O best of sages. Listen; I shall tell you the delightful story of Śaṅkara, which grants enjoyment and liberation to those who hear it.
m.4.37.4: Long ago, the Grandfather Brahmā, asked this very thing by Nārada, replied with a pleased mind to Nārada, the best of sages.
m.4.37.5: Brahmā said: Listen with great delight, O Nārada, to the excellent story of Śaṅkara, which destroys great sins; out of affection for you I shall narrate it.
m.4.37.6: Viṣṇu, together with Ramā, performed the worship of Śiva, and by the grace of the Supreme Lord he obtained all his desires.
m.4.37.7: I too, the Grandfather, am a worshipper of Śiva; by his grace alone, dear son, I am ever the creator of the universe.
m.4.37.8: My sons, the supreme sages, constantly worship Śiva; and the other sages too are worshippers of Śiva.
m.4.37.9: You, Nārada, are especially a worshipper of Śiva; the seven sages, Vasiṣṭha and the rest, are worshippers of Śiva.
m.4.37.10: Arundhatī, the great chaste lady, likewise Lopāmudrā, and Ahalyā, the wife of Gautama, are worshippers of Śiva.
m.4.37.11: Durvāsas, Kauśika, Śakti, Dadhīca and Gautama, Kaṇāda, Bhārgava, Jīva (Bṛhaspati) and Vaiśampāyana too—
m.4.37.12: all these sages are regarded as worshippers of Śiva; likewise Parāśara and Vyāsa are ever devoted to Śiva's worship.
m.4.37.13: Upamanyu is a great devotee of Śiva, the Supreme Self; Yājñavalkya is a great Śaiva, and so are Jaimini and Garga.
m.4.37.14: Śuka and Śaunaka and the others are ardent worshippers of Śaṅkara; there are many other sages too, O best of sages.
m.4.37.15: Aditi, the mother of the gods, together with her daughters-in-law, intent on love, constantly and gladly performed the worship of Śiva in an earthen liṅga.
m.4.37.16: Śakra (Indra) and the other guardians of the worlds, the Vasus and the gods, the Mahārājika gods and the Sādhyas are worshippers of Śiva.
m.4.37.17: The Gandharvas, Kinnaras and other demigods are worshippers of Śiva; likewise the great-souled asuras are regarded as worshippers of Śiva.
m.4.37.18: The Daitya Hiraṇyakaśipu, with his younger brother and his sons, O sage, constantly worshipped Śiva; so did Virocana and Bali.
m.4.37.19: Bāṇa is remembered as a great Śaiva, and likewise the sons of Hiraṇyākṣa; Vṛṣaparvan, Danu, dear son, and the Dānavas are worshippers of Śiva.
m.4.37.20: Śeṣa, Vāsuki, Takṣaka and other great serpents are devotees of Śiva, as are the birds headed by Garuḍa.
m.4.37.21: The two gods Sun and Moon, founders of dynasties on earth, are ever devoted to the service of Śiva together with their descendants, O lord of sages.
m.4.37.22: Likewise the Manus, headed by Svāyambhuva, performed the worship of Śiva in particular, wearing the garb of Śiva, O sage.
m.4.37.23: Priyavrata and his sons, and likewise the son of Uttānapāda, and the kings of their lineages were worshippers of Śiva.
m.4.37.24: Dhruva, Ṛṣabha, Bharata, the nine Yogins, their brothers and others too were worshippers of Śiva.
m.4.37.25: The sons of Vaivasvata, O Tārkṣya, the kings headed by Ikṣvāku, with minds devoted to Śiva's worship, always enjoyed happiness.
m.4.37.26: Kakutstha too, Māndhātṛ, Sagara the best of Śaivas, Mucukunda, Hariścandra and likewise Kalmāṣāṅghri—
m.4.37.27: the rulers headed by Bhagīratha, and many excellent kings, should be known as worshippers of Śiva, adopting the garb of Śiva.
m.4.37.28: The great king Khaṭvāṅga, who gave help to the gods, always worshipped an earthen image of Śiva according to the rules.
m.4.37.29: His son Dilīpa always performed the worship of Śiva; his son Raghu, a Śaiva, worshipped Śiva with great delight.
m.4.37.30: Aja was a worshipper of Śiva; his son, who fought righteous battles, was Daśaratha, born as an especially great king.
m.4.37.31: That Daśaratha, for the sake of a son, specially worshipped an earthen image of Śiva at the command of the sage Vasiṣṭha.
m.4.37.32: And that king, devoted to Bhava, the best of kings, having received the command of the sage Ṛṣyaśṛṅga, performed the sacrifice for a son (putreṣṭi).
m.4.37.33: His beloved Kausalyā, instructed by Ṛṣyaśṛṅga, joyfully worshipped an earthen image of Śaṅkara to obtain a son.
m.4.37.34: Sumitrā, and Kaikeyī the king's beloved, lovingly worshipped Śiva to obtain good sons, O best of sages.
m.4.37.35: By Śiva's grace they obtained sons who brought auspiciousness, of great valour, heroic, devoted to the righteous path, O sage.
m.4.37.36: Then, by Śiva's command, Hari himself became manifest in four forms in them the queens from that king, as the king's sons.
m.4.37.37: Kausalyā's son was Rāma, Sumitrā's Lakṣmaṇa and Śatrughna, and Kaikeyī's Bharata—all of good vows.
m.4.37.38: That Rāma, together with his brothers, constantly worshipped the earthen liṅga, wearing ash and rudrākṣa and following the Virajā rite.
m.4.37.39: The kings born in his lineage, with their followers, O sage, all worshipped the earthen liṅga of Śiva.
m.4.37.40: The great king Sudyumna, a Śaiva and son of Manu, O sage, became a woman together with his attendants through Śiva's curse, on account of Śiva's beloved.
m.4.37.41: Through worship of the Lord in the earthen liṅga (pārthiveśa), he again became an excellent man: a woman for a month and a man for a month; in this way his womanhood was partly removed.
m.4.37.42: Then, giving up the kingdom, devoted to Śiva's dharma and wearing the garb of a Śaiva, he attained through devotion the liberation that is hard to obtain.
m.4.37.43: And Purūravas, his son, a great king, was a fine worshipper of Śiva, the god of gods; his son too was a worshipper of Śiva.
m.4.37.44: Bharata always performed great worship of Śiva alone; and Nahuṣa was a great Śaiva, devoted to the worship of Śiva.
m.4.37.45: Yayāti, through worship of Śiva, obtained all his desires; he begot five sons devoted to Śiva's dharma.
m.4.37.46: His sons, headed by Yadu, all five of them, were worshippers of Śiva, and by the power of Śiva's worship they obtained all their desires.
m.4.37.47: Other highly fortunate ones too, both of their lineage and of other lineages, worshipped Śiva, the giver of enjoyment and liberation, O sage.
m.4.37.48: And Kṛṣṇa himself performed daily worship of Śiva alone on Badarī, the best of mountains, for a period of seven months.
m.4.37.49: Having obtained many divine boons from that gracious Śaṅkara, the Lord Kṛṣṇa brought the whole world under his control.
m.4.37.50: His son Pradyumna, dear one, always performed Śiva's worship; and other eminent sons of Kṛṣṇa, Sāmba and the rest, were worshippers of Śiva.
m.4.37.51: Jarāsandha was a great Śaiva, and so were the kings of his line; Nimi was a Śaiva, and Janaka and his sons were worshippers of Śiva.
m.4.37.52: And worship of Śiva was performed by Nala, the son of Vīrasena, who in a former birth was a Bhilla hunter in the forest, a protector of travellers.
m.4.37.53: Formerly he protected an ascetic near a shrine of Hara; he himself was devoured at night by tigers and other beasts and died for the sake of dharma.
m.4.37.54: By the power of that merit, that Bhilla became Nala, a great emperor, beloved of Damayantī.
m.4.37.55: Thus, dear one, sinless one, I have told you what you asked: the divine deeds of Śaṅkara. What else do you wish to ask?
m.4.37.iti: Thus ends the thirty-seventh adhyāya, named The description of the Śaiva faith of gods, sages and kings, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.4.38.1: The sages said: You are blessed, you have fulfilled your purpose, your life is fruitful, since, dear one, you make us hear the auspicious story of Maheśvara.
m.4.38.2: O Sūta, although the true matter has been heard by many sages, our doubt has not gone; therefore I put this to you.
m.4.38.3: By which vow is Śiva pleased and grants true happiness? You are skilled in matters concerning Śiva; therefore we ask you.
m.4.38.4: By which vow may devotees attain both enjoyment and liberation? Tell that in particular, O disciple of Vyāsa; salutation to you.
m.4.38.5: Sūta said: O best of sages, you compassionate ones have asked well. Remembering the lotus feet of Śiva, I shall narrate as I have heard.
m.4.38.6: Just as it is asked by you, so indeed was it asked of Śaṅkara by Brahmā, by Hari and by Śivā.
m.4.38.7: At some time it was asked by them of the Supreme Self: pleased by which vow do you grant enjoyment and liberation?
m.4.38.8: Thus was he asked then by them, by that Hari; that reply, which removes the sins of those who listen, I now narrate.
m.4.38.9: Śiva said: I have many vows that grant enjoyment and liberation; among them the principal ones should be known to be ten in number.
m.4.38.10: Those versed in the Jābāla Śruti speak of ten Śaiva vows; those vows should always be performed with effort by the twice-born.
m.4.38.11: On every eighth lunar day, eating only at night should be carefully observed; on Kālāṣṭamī especially, O Hari, eating by day is to be given up.
m.4.38.12: On the bright eleventh, O Viṣṇu, eating by day is to be given up; on the dark eleventh, O Hari, one should eat at night after worshipping me.
m.4.38.13: On the bright thirteenth, eating should be done at night; but on the dark fourteenth (bhūtā), that should not be done by observers of Śiva's vow.
m.4.38.14: On Monday, O Viṣṇu, in both fortnights, in every week, those devoted to Śiva should carefully eat at night.
m.4.38.15: In all these vows, excellent twice-born Śaivas should be fed with care, according to one's capacity, for the completion of the vow.
m.4.38.16: These vows must be observed regularly by the twice-born; twice-born who abandon these vows become thieves.
m.4.38.17: They should be performed regularly also by those skilled in the path of liberation. A set of four has been declared as that which leads to liberation:
m.4.38.18: Worship of Śiva, japa of Rudra's mantras, fasting, and death in Vārāṇasī, the abode of Śiva: this is the eternal way to liberation.
m.4.38.19: The eighth day, Monday, and the fourteenth of the dark fortnight: this pleases Śiva; there need be no deliberation about it.
m.4.38.20: Among even the four, O Hari, the Śivarātri vow is the most powerful; therefore that alone should be performed by those desiring the fruits of enjoyment and liberation.
m.4.38.21: There is nothing other than this vow that brings benefit to men; this vow is the supreme means of dharma for all.
m.4.38.22: For the desireless and the desirous, for all men likewise, for the classes and the life-stages, and for women and children, O Hari,
m.4.38.23: for male and female servants, and likewise for gods and others, for all embodied beings, this excellent vow is beneficial.
m.4.38.24: In the dark fortnight of Māgha, that fourteenth is proclaimed as especially distinguished; the one extending through midnight should be adopted; it destroys crores of sins of killing.
m.4.38.25: Hear, O Keśava, with attention, what is to be done on that day beginning from morning; I tell it to you with great affection.
m.4.38.26: Rising in the morning, the wise one, filled with supreme bliss, should diligently perform the daily duties such as bathing.
m.4.38.27: Then, going to a Śiva temple and worshipping according to rule, and bowing to Śiva, he should afterwards properly make the resolve.
m.4.38.28: O God of gods, Mahādeva, Nīlakaṇṭha, salutation to you. O Lord, I wish to perform your Śivarātri vow.
m.4.38.29: By your power, O Lord of gods, may it be without obstacles; may the enemies, desire and the rest, cause me no affliction at all.
m.4.38.30: Having made the resolve thus, he should gather the articles of worship. And the liṅga that is in an excellent place and renowned in the Āgamas —
m.4.38.31: going there himself at night and carrying out the excellent procedure, on the southern side of Śiva, or on the western, in an auspicious spot,
m.4.38.32: and placing those articles for worship near Śiva, the excellent man should then bathe again there according to rule.
m.4.38.33: Wearing a clean garment and likewise a clean undergarment, and sipping water three times, he should begin the worship.
m.4.38.34: Whatever article belongs to a given mantra, with that mantra he should perform the worship; the worship of Hara should not be done without mantras.
m.4.38.35: Having performed worship in the first watch with songs, instrumental music and dances imbued with devotion, the wise one should repeat the mantra.
m.4.38.36: If he knows the mantras, he should then make an excellent earthen liṅga; having completed his daily rites, he should afterwards worship the earthen liṅga.
m.4.38.37: First making the earthen liṅga, he should afterwards perform its installation, and please the bull-bannered God with hymns of various kinds.
m.4.38.38: The glorification arising from the vow should be recited by the wise one and listened to by the excellent devotee, desiring the completion of the vow.
m.4.38.39: And in all four watches, worshipping the set of four forms in order, beginning with invocation and ending with dismissal,
m.4.38.40: A night vigil should be kept with love, accompanied by a great festival. In the morning, having bathed, he should again install Śiva there and worship him.
m.4.38.41: Then, with bowed shoulders and joined palms, having completed the vow and bowing to him again and again, he should earnestly pray to Śambhu:
m.4.38.42: O Mahādeva, the observance that was undertaken at your command is now released by me, O Lord; the vow has been accomplished, unsurpassed.
m.4.38.43: By this vow, O Lord of gods, performed according to my ability, be pleased today, O Śarva, and show compassion upon me.
m.4.38.44: Having offered a handful of flowers to Śiva, he should give gifts according to rule; and having bowed to Śiva, he should conclude that observance.
m.4.38.45: According to his ability, having fed Śaiva brahmins and especially ascetics and having fully satisfied them, he himself should then take food.
m.4.38.46: How worship is to be performed by the best devotees in each watch of the night, O Hari, especially on Śivarātri — that I shall tell you.
m.4.38.47: In the first watch, O Hari, he should worship the installed earthen liṅga with supreme devotion and with many excellent offerings.
m.4.38.48: Hara is always to be worshipped first with the five substances; he should offer each substance separately with its own mantra.
m.4.38.49: Having offered that substance, he should pour a stream of water; and afterwards the wise one should wash off the substances with streams of water.
m.4.38.50: Having recited the mantra one hundred and eight times with a stream of water, he should worship Śiva there, who is without attributes yet takes the form of attributes.
m.4.38.51: He should worship the bull-bannered god with the mantra given by his guru; otherwise he should worship Sadāśiva with the name-mantra.
m.4.38.52: Worship of Śambhu, the supreme Self, should be done with variegated sandal-paste, with unbroken rice grains, and with black sesame seeds.
m.4.38.53: With flowers — hundred-petalled lotuses and also oleanders — he should offer the flowers to Śaṅkara with eight name-mantras.
m.4.38.54: Bhava, Śarva, Rudra, then Paśupati, Ugra, Mahān, Bhīma and Īśāna — these indeed are they.
m.4.38.55: He should worship Śiva with these names preceded by Śrī and ending in the dative; afterwards offer incense and lamp, and after that the food-offering.
m.4.38.56: In the first watch the wise one should have cooked food prepared as the food-offering; having given arghya and a bilva fruit, he should offer betel.
m.4.38.57: Then prostration, then meditation; japa of the guru's mantra is prescribed; otherwise he should please Śaṅkara with the five-syllabled mantra.
m.4.38.58: Then, having shown the cow-gesture (dhenu-mudrā), he should perform a libation with pure water, and arrange the feeding of five brahmins according to his means.
m.4.38.59: A great festival should be held here as long as the watch lasts; then, having offered the fruit of the worship to him, he should conclude it.
m.4.38.60: Again, in the second watch he should duly make the resolve (saṅkalpa); or, having made the resolve only once, he should perform worship of that same kind.
m.4.38.61: Having likewise worshipped with the previous substances, he should offer the stream of water; reciting the mantra twice as many times as before, he should worship Śiva.
m.4.38.62: Then he should worship Śiva with the previous items, sesame and barley, and with lotuses; especially with bilva leaves should he worship the Supreme Lord.
m.4.38.63: The arghya is to be made with a citron, and the food-offering likewise with milk-rice; and the repetition of the mantra twice that of before, O Janārdana.
m.4.38.64: Then he should make the resolve to feed brahmins, and do everything else likewise up to the end of the second watch.
m.4.38.65: When the third watch has come, he should perform worship as before; but in place of barley, wheat, and flowers of the arka plant.
m.4.38.66: He should worship there with various incenses and lamps of many kinds, O Viṣṇu, with food-offerings of cakes and with vegetables of many kinds.
m.4.38.67: Having done thus, he should then perform the rite of āratī with camphor; he should give arghya with a pomegranate and perform double the japa.
m.4.38.68: Then he should make the resolve for feeding brahmins, with gifts of fees (dakṣiṇā), and hold a festival as before until the limit of the watch is reached.
m.4.38.69: When the fourth watch has arrived, he should perform its concluding rite; and having again performed the preliminary procedure and the rest, he should carry out the worship according to rule.
