m.4.38.70: With black gram, foxtail millet and green gram, or else with the seven grains, with śaṅkhī flowers and bilva leaves, he should worship the Supreme Lord.
m.4.38.71: There he should give the food-offering with various sweets; or else he should please Sadāśiva with dishes of black gram.
m.4.38.72: He should give arghya with the fruit of the plantain, O Hari, or else give arghya to Śiva with various fruits.
m.4.38.73: The best of men should perform mantra-japa double that of before; the wise one should make the resolve for feeding brahmins according to his ability.
m.4.38.74: With songs, instrumental music and dances he should pass the time devoutly, with great festivities and with devotees, until dawn breaks.
m.4.38.75: When sunrise has come, having bathed again, he should worship Śiva, and then perform an excellent ablution of the deity with various offerings of worship.
m.4.38.76: Various kinds of gifts and various kinds of food should be given to brahmins and ascetics in accordance with the number of watches.
m.4.38.77: Having bowed to Śaṅkara, he should then offer a handful of flowers; and the discerning one, having uttered fine praises, should pray with these mantras:
m.4.38.78: I am yours; my life-breath rests in you; my mind is always on you, O Mṛḍa. O treasure of compassion, knowing this, do as is fitting.
m.4.38.79: Whatever japa, worship and the like I have done, whether in ignorance or with knowledge — since you are a treasure of compassion, take it as known, O Lord of beings, and be gracious to me.
m.4.38.80: Whatever fruit has arisen from this very fast, by that may the god Śaṅkara, the giver of happiness, be pleased.
m.4.38.81: O Mahādeva, may there always be worship of you in my family. May there be no birth in the family of one where you are not the deity worshipped.
m.4.38.82: Having thus offered a handful of flowers, one should receive the tilaka mark and blessings from the brāhmaṇas, and then one should ceremonially dismiss Śambhu.
m.4.38.83: Hara is certainly not far from the one by whom the vow has been performed in this way. Its fruit cannot be described; there is nothing that I would not give to him.
m.4.38.84: Even if this supreme vow is performed effortlessly, without deliberate intent, the seed of liberation is surely produced for that person; there is no doubt about this.
m.4.38.85: The vow should also be performed every month by people with devotion; afterwards, having carried out the rite of concluding the vow (udyāpana), one obtains the complete fruit.
m.4.38.86: Certainly, because of the performance of the vow, I, Śiva, the destroyer of all sorrows, give enjoyment and liberation, and every desired fruit.
m.4.38.87: Sūta said: Having heard these words of Śiva, most beneficial and wonderful, Viṣṇu went to his abode. Thereafter he practised this excellent vow and made this very vow known among people devoted to their own welfare.
m.4.38.88: Then, on one occasion, Keśava narrated to Nārada this divine Śivarātri vow, which grants enjoyment and liberation.
m.4.38.iti: Thus ends the thirty-eighth adhyāya, named The exposition of the greatness of the Śivarātri vow, in the Māhātmya of Vyādheśvara, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.4.39.1: The sages said: Tell us also the procedure for the concluding rite (udyāpana) of the Śivarātri vow, by performing which Śaṅkara himself surely becomes pleased.
m.4.39.2: Sūta said: Listen, O sages, with devotion and respect, to that concluding rite, by whose performance the vow surely becomes complete.
m.4.39.3: The auspicious Śivarātri vow should be observed for fourteen years: a single meal on the thirteenth lunar day and fasting on the fourteenth.
m.4.39.4: When the day of Śivarātri arrives, having completed the daily rites, then going to the Śiva temple and performing worship according to rule,
m.4.39.5: and then he should carefully have a divine maṇḍala made there, renowned in the three worlds by the name Gaurītilaka.
m.4.39.6: In its middle he should have the divine Liṅgatobhadra maṇḍala drawn, or else he should arrange a Sarvatobhadra maṇḍala inside the pavilion.
m.4.39.7: There pitchers should be prepared, as designated for the Prājāpatya rite, auspicious, with cloths, with fruits, and accompanied by fees (dakṣiṇā).
m.4.39.8: They should be carefully placed beside the maṇḍala, and in the middle one more pitcher, golden or otherwise, should be set up.
m.4.39.9: There the observer of the vow should make a golden image of Śambhu together with Umā, of one pala of gold, or half that, or according to his means.
m.4.39.10: Placing the image of Śivā on the left side and mine, the image of Śiva, on the right side, he should diligently worship at night.
m.4.39.11: There he should choose a pure ācārya together with officiating priests (ṛtvij), and, permitted by them, he should perform Śiva's worship with devotion.
m.4.39.12: He should keep vigil at night, performing the worship proper to each watch (yāma); the observer should pass the whole night with singing, dancing and the like.
m.4.39.13: Having thus worshipped duly and gratified the Lord, in the morning he should again perform worship and then perform the fire-offering (homa) according to rule.
m.4.39.14: According to his ability he should perform the Prājāpatya observance; he should feed brāhmaṇas with affection and give gifts with devotion.
m.4.39.15: Having adorned the officiating priests together with their wives with clothes, ornaments and decorations according to rule, he should give gifts to each separately.
m.4.39.16: He should give to the ācārya, according to rule, a cow with her calf, furnished with the proper accessories, saying: may Śiva be pleased with me.
m.4.39.17: Then he should offer to the ācārya that image together with the pitcher, clothed, set upon a bull, with all ornaments.
m.4.39.18: Then, with joined palms and bowed shoulders, with great love and a voice choked with emotion, he should pray to the god Maheśāna, the great Lord:
m.4.39.19: O God of gods, O Mahādeva, affectionate to those who seek refuge, O Lord of gods, through this vow show compassion upon me.
m.4.39.20: O Śiva, I have performed this vow according to the measure of my devotion; whatever is deficient, may it attain completeness by your grace, O Śaṅkara.
m.4.39.21: Whether out of ignorance or with knowledge, whatever japa, worship and so on I have done, may that by your compassion be fruitful, O Śaṅkara.
m.4.39.22: Having thus offered a handful of flowers to Śiva, the supreme Self, he should then make obeisance and pray once again.
m.4.39.23: For one who has performed the vow in this way, there is no deficiency; he then obtains the accomplishment desired by his mind—there is no doubt about this.
m.4.39.iti: Thus ends the thirty-ninth adhyāya, named The concluding rite of the Śivarātri vow, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.4.40.1: The sages said: O Sūta, having heard your words we have attained supreme bliss. Kindly narrate in detail that same excellent vow.
m.4.40.2: O Sūta, by whom was this excellent vow performed here in former times? And having performed it even unknowingly, what excellent fruit was obtained?
m.4.40.3: Sūta said: Listen, all you sages: I shall narrate the ancient history of a Niṣāda, which destroys all sins.
m.4.40.4: Formerly in a forest there was a certain Bhilla named Gurudruha—a householder with a family, strong, cruel, and devoted to cruel deeds.
m.4.40.5: Going constantly into the forest, he used to kill deer every day; and living in the forest, he committed various kinds of theft there.
m.4.40.6: From childhood onward he never did anything auspicious here. A long time passed for that wicked one in the forest.
m.4.40.7: Once the auspicious Śivarātri arrived there, but the wicked one, dwelling in the great forest, did not know of it.
m.4.40.8: At this time the Bhilla was implored by his mother, father and wife, overcome with hunger: give us food, O forest-dweller.
m.4.40.9: Thus implored, he too quickly took up his bow and went off to kill deer, and roamed the whole forest.
m.4.40.10: By the turn of fate, he then obtained nothing at all. Then the sun set, and he became distressed.
m.4.40.11: What should I do? Where should I go? I have obtained nothing today. And the children who are at home—what will become of them, and of my parents?
m.4.40.12: And my wife—something bad will happen to her. I must go home only after getting something; it cannot be otherwise.
m.4.40.13: Having reflected thus, the hunter went near a lake, to the spot where animals descend to the water, and stationed himself there.
m.4.40.14: Surely some creature will come here. Having killed it, I will go home happily, my task accomplished.
m.4.40.15: Thinking thus, the Bhilla took some water, climbed a tree called bilva, and stayed there.
m.4.40.16: When will something come? When shall I kill it? Fixing his mind thus, he stayed there, afflicted by hunger and thirst.
m.4.40.17: That night, in the first watch, a doe came, tormented by thirst and frightened, leaping about.
m.4.40.18: Seeing her, he, delighted, then quickly fitted an arrow onto his own bow in order to kill her.
m.4.40.19: As he was doing this, water and bilva leaves fell down there; below was a Śiva-liṅga.
m.4.40.20: Thus the worship of Śiva for the first watch took place, and by its greatness his sin then melted away.
m.4.40.21: Hearing that sound there, the doe, in fear, saw the hunter and, agitated, spoke these words.
m.4.40.22: The doe said: What do you wish to do, hunter? Tell the truth before me. Hearing the doe's words, the hunter spoke.
m.4.40.23: The hunter said: My family is hungry today; by killing you I shall satisfy them. Hearing those cruel words and seeing that relentless wretch,
m.4.40.24: she thought: what shall I do? Where shall I go? I must devise a plan. Having reflected thus, she spoke these words there.
m.4.40.25: The doe said: May there be gratification for you through my flesh, the flesh of a body that is otherwise useless. What merit could be greater? I am blessed, there is no doubt of it.
m.4.40.26: The merit that arises here for one who does a kindness to others cannot be described even in hundreds of years.
m.4.40.27: But my children are all in my own dwelling today. After entrusting them to my sister or else to my husband, I shall come.
m.4.40.28: Know that my word is not false, O forest-dweller. I shall come back here again near you; there is no doubt.
m.4.40.29: By truth the earth stands firm, by truth the ocean, by truth the streams of water; on truth everything is established.
m.4.40.30: Sūta said: When, though addressed thus by her, the hunter did not accept her words, then she, greatly astonished and afraid, spoke again.
m.4.40.31: The doe said: Listen, hunter, I shall declare it; I swear an oath: if, having gone to my home, I do not come back to you,
m.4.40.32: the sin of a brāhmaṇa who sells the Veda, of one who omits the sandhyā rites at the three times of day, of women who perform rites in transgression of their husband's command,
m.4.40.33: the sin that lies in an ingrate, the sin in one averse to Hari, the sin of a traitor, the sin in violating dharma,
m.4.40.34: and that in a betrayer of trust, and likewise in a deceiver—with that sin may I be smeared if I do not come back.
m.4.40.35: When the doe, having sworn these and many other oaths, stood there, then the hunter, trusting her, said, go home.
m.4.40.36: The doe, delighted, drank water and went to her own dwelling place. Meanwhile the first watch passed for him without sleep.
m.4.40.37: Then her sister, also a doe, anxious about her, came searching for her path and seeking water.
m.4.40.38: Seeing her, the Bhilla himself drew back the arrow, and again water and leaves fell upon Śiva.
m.4.40.39: Thereby, incidentally, the worship of the great-souled Śambhu for the second watch took place, bringing happiness to the hunter.
m.4.40.40: Seeing him, that doe said, what are you doing, forest-dweller? He told her as before, and hearing that, the doe spoke again.
m.4.40.41: The doe said: I am blessed; listen, O hunter: my bearing of a body is fruitful, for through this impermanent body a benefit to another will come about.
m.4.40.42: But my young ones, my little children, are staying at home. Having entrusted them to my husband, I will surely come back again.
m.4.40.43: The hunter said: I do not believe what you have said; I will kill you, there is no doubt about it. Hearing that, the doe spoke, swearing an oath by Hari.
m.4.40.44: The doe said: Listen, O hunter, I shall declare: if I do not come back again, may I incur this: whoever wavers from his spoken word loses by that his merit.
m.4.40.45: The man who abandons his wedded wife and goes to another woman; and he who, transgressing the Vedic dharma, proceeds by a self-invented path;
m.4.40.46: he who, endowed with devotion to Viṣṇu, reviles Śiva; and he who, reaching the death-anniversary of his parents, lets it pass empty of rites here;
m.4.40.47: and he who, having caused distress, again makes false promises — with that sin may I be smeared, if I do not come back again.
m.4.40.48: Sūta said: Thus addressed by her, the hunter said to the doe, go. And the doe, having drunk water, went joyfully to her own dwelling.
m.4.40.49: Meanwhile the second watch of the night passed for him without sleep. At this time, when the third watch had arrived there,
m.4.40.50: realising the delay, alarmed, and intent on searching for her, in that watch he then saw a stag that had come along the path to the water.
m.4.40.51: Seeing that well-fed stag, the forest-dweller was delighted; fixing an arrow on his bow, he set about killing it.
m.4.40.52: Then, as he was doing so, O brahmins, by the force of his destiny some bilva leaves fell upon Śiva.
m.4.40.53: Thereby, that night, through his good fortune, the worship of Śiva for the third watch took place; Śiva's compassion was shown.
m.4.40.54: Hearing that sound there, the stag said, what are you doing? He replied, I am a hunter, and I will kill you for the sake of my family.
m.4.40.55: Hearing the hunter's words, the stag, glad at heart, quickly spoke these words to that hunter:
m.4.40.56: The deer said: I am blessed, being well-fed today; your satisfaction will come about. He whose body is not for the benefit of others — all of his life has passed in vain.
m.4.40.57: He who, though possessed of ability, does not do good to others — that ability of his becomes useless, and in the hereafter he goes to hell.
m.4.40.58: But having entrusted my own young ones to their mother and having comforted all those little ones, I will come back again.
m.4.40.59: Thus addressed by him, the hunter, greatly astonished in mind, his mind a little purified and his mass of sins destroyed, spoke these words:
m.4.40.60: The hunter said: Whoever came here, all of them, speaking just as you do, went away from here — and the deceivers have not come back even now.
m.4.40.61: You too, caught in a predicament, will go off with a falsehood. How, O deer, will my livelihood come about today?
m.4.40.62: The stag said: listen, O hunter, I shall declare: there is no untruth in me. By truth the whole universe, moving and unmoving, stands firm.
m.4.40.63: He whose speech is false — his merit drains away in a moment. Even so, O Bhil, hear my true vow:
m.4.40.64: the sin in sexual union at twilight or by day, in eating on Śivarātri, in false testimony, in seizing a deposit, and likewise that of a twice-born devoid of the sandhyā rites;
m.4.40.65: of one whose mouth is devoid of Śiva's name; of one who, though able, is no benefactor; in plucking bilva fruit on a festival day; in eating forbidden food;
m.4.40.66: and he who, without worshipping Śiva and without wearing sacred ash, eats food — may the sin of all these be mine, if I do not come back again.
m.4.40.67: Sūta said: Hearing his words thus, the hunter said, go, and come back quickly. Thus addressed by the hunter, the stag drank water and went away.
m.4.40.68: They all, having made firm pledges, met there in their own dwelling, and heard that whole account from one another properly.
m.4.40.69: Bound by the noose of truth, resolving, we must certainly go, they comforted the young ones there and then became eager to go.
m.4.40.70: The elder doe there spoke to her lord: without you, O stag, how will the young ones remain here?
m.4.40.71: It was I who first made the vow there, O lord; therefore I must go. Let you two stay here.
m.4.40.72: Hearing her words, the younger one said: I am your servant; I will go today. Let you stay.
m.4.40.73: Hearing that, the stag said: I will go there. You two should stay here, for the protection of the young comes from the mother.
m.4.40.74: Hearing their lord's words, the two did not consider it in accord with dharma; lovingly they said to their husband: Fie on living in widowhood!
m.4.40.75: Having comforted the young ones there and entrusted them to their fellow dwellers, they all went swiftly to where the excellent hunter was.
m.4.40.76: Those young ones too, all of them, seeing this, followed after, thinking: whatever fate befalls these, let that be ours too.
m.4.40.77: Seeing them, the hunter, delighted, fixed an arrow on his bow; and again water and leaves fell upon Śiva.
m.4.40.78: Thereby the auspicious worship of the fourth watch took place, and then all his sin was reduced to ashes in a moment.
m.4.40.79: The doe, the other doe, and the stag said: quickly, O best of hunters, make our bodies meaningful; show us this kindness.
m.4.40.80: Hearing their words, the hunter was filled with wonder; through the power of the worship of Śiva he attained rare knowledge.
m.4.40.81: Blessed indeed are these deer, though devoid of knowledge, and worthy of high esteem: they are devoted to helping others with their very own bodies.
m.4.40.82: Having obtained birth as a human, what have I accomplished now? By tormenting the bodies of others I have nourished my own body.
m.4.40.83: I have always sustained my family by committing sins in many ways. Alas, having committed sins thus, what will be my fate?
m.4.40.84: Or to what destination shall I go, having committed sin since birth? Now I reflect thus: fie, fie upon my life!
m.4.40.85: Having thus attained knowledge, he then withdrew his arrow and said, go, O best of deer; you are blessed.
m.4.40.86: When he had spoken thus, Śaṅkara, pleased, then revealed his revered form, the very one that had been worshipped.
m.4.40.87: Touching the hunter out of compassion, Śambhu said to him lovingly: ask for a boon; I am pleased with this vow, O Bhilla.
m.4.40.88: The hunter, seeing Śiva's form, became liberated in an instant and fell at Śiva's feet, saying, I have obtained everything.
m.4.40.89: Śiva too, very pleased at heart, gave him the name Guha, and, looking at him with a compassionate glance, bestowed divine boons upon him.
m.4.40.90: Śiva said: Listen, O hunter: from today enjoy divine pleasures as you wish, residing in the excellent royal capital at Śṛṅgaverapura.
m.4.40.91: Your lineage will grow without decline, and you will be praiseworthy even to the gods. Rāma will certainly come to your house, O hunter.
m.4.40.92: He, who shows affection to my devotees, will make friendship with you. With your mind devoted to my service, you will attain liberation, hard to obtain.
m.4.40.93: Sūta said: Meanwhile, those deer, having had the vision of Śaṅkara, all bowed and attained true liberation from the deer-birth.
m.4.40.94: Mounting an aerial chariot, they departed then with divine bodies; freed from the curse by the mere sight of Śiva, they went to heaven.
m.4.40.95: Śiva became Vyādheśvara on the mountain Arbudācala, who by being seen and worshipped immediately grants enjoyment and liberation.
m.4.40.96: And the hunter too, O best of brāhmaṇas, from that day on surely enjoyed pleasures, obtained Rāma's grace, and attained union with Śiva (śiva-sāyujya).
m.4.40.97: He attained union with Śiva by performing this vow unknowingly; how much more, then, do those endowed with devotion attain auspicious identity with him.
m.4.40.98: Having examined all the scriptures and the many forms of dharma, this Śivarātri vow has been declared the most excellent of all.
m.4.40.99: Various vows here, various holy places, wondrous gifts, and various sacrifices likewise,
m.4.40.100: various austerities and many recitations of mantras—these do not attain equality with this Śivarātri vow.
m.4.40.101: Therefore this most auspicious, divine Śivarātri vow, ever granting enjoyment and liberation, should be performed by those who desire their welfare.
m.4.40.102: All this has been narrated: the auspicious Śivarātri vow, renowned as the king of vows. What else do you wish to hear?
m.4.40.iti: Thus ends the fortieth adhyāya, named The description of the glory of the Śivarātri vow, in the Māhātmya of Vyādheśvara, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.4.41.1: The sages said: You have spoken of what is called liberation (mukti). What indeed happens in it here? And what kind of state would there be in it? Tell us this.
m.4.41.2: Sūta said: Liberation is declared to be of four kinds; listen, I shall tell you. It removes the afflictions of worldly existence and bestows supreme bliss.
m.4.41.3: They are Sārūpya and Sālokya, and likewise Sānnidhya, the next; and the fourth is Sāyujya — the one that would come about through this vow.
m.4.41.4: O best of sages, Śiva alone is said to be the giver of liberation. Brahmā and the others are not to be known as such; they are only givers of the three aims of life.
m.4.41.5: Brahmā and the others are lords of the three guṇas; Śiva is beyond the three guṇas. He is changeless, the supreme Brahman, the Fourth (turya), beyond Prakṛti.
m.4.41.6: He is of the form of knowledge, imperishable, the witness, reachable through knowledge, non-dual by himself. Here he is the giver of liberation as kaivalya, and indeed also the bestower of the three aims.
m.4.41.7: And the fifth, called Kaivalya, is in every way difficult for men to attain. I shall describe its characteristics; listen, O best of seers.
m.4.41.8: That from which everything arises, by which this world is sustained, into which it dissolves, and by which all this is pervaded —
m.4.41.9: that alone is declared to be the form of Śiva, O lords of sages. It is described in the Vedas as twofold: with parts (sakala) and without parts (niṣkala).
m.4.41.10: It was not known by Viṣṇu, nor likewise by Brahmā; it was not known by Kumāra and the others, nor indeed was it known by Nārada;
m.4.41.11: nor by Śuka the son of Vyāsa, nor by Vyāsa, nor by the lords of sages, nor by all the gods before them, nor by the Vedas and the śāstras.
m.4.41.12: It is Truth, Knowledge, and Infinite, designated as Being-Consciousness-Bliss. He is without qualities, without limiting adjuncts, imperishable, pure, and stainless.
m.4.41.13: He is not red, nor yellow, not white nor blue; not short nor long, not gross nor subtle.
m.4.41.14: That from which words turn back, together with the mind, without reaching it — that alone is declared the supreme, the Brahman itself, which is called Śiva.
m.4.41.15: Just as space is all-pervading, so too is this all-pervading: beyond Māyā, the supreme Self, beyond the pairs of opposites, free from envy.
m.4.41.16: Its attainment surely comes about here through the dawning of the knowledge of Śiva, or else, O twice-born, through worship of Śiva alone with the subtle understanding of the virtuous.
m.4.41.17: Knowledge is difficult in the world, while worship is considered easy. Therefore, O best ones, worship Śiva, even for the sake of liberation.
m.4.41.18: For Śiva, whose very self is knowledge, the supreme giver of liberation, is subject to worship. Through devotion alone many perfected ones have joyfully attained the supreme liberation.
m.4.41.19: Devotion to Śambhu is the mother of knowledge, ever bestowing liberation and enjoyment. It becomes easy to attain through his grace, and is marked by the sprouting of true love.
m.4.41.20: That devotion should be known as of various kinds, O twice-born: with qualities (saguṇa) and without qualities (nirguṇa); prescribed (vaidhī) and natural (svābhāvikī). Whichever is the better, that is regarded as the higher.
m.4.41.21: It is declared twofold by the division into steadfast (naiṣṭhikī) and non-steadfast (anaiṣṭhikī). The steadfast should be known as sixfold; the second is held to be of one kind.
m.4.41.22: The wise know it to be manifold through the division into enjoined and not enjoined; and because both of these are of many kinds, their full extent is not described here.
m.4.41.23: Both of these should be known as having nine limbs, by the divisions beginning with hearing (śravaṇa). They are very difficult without his grace, and easy through it.
m.4.41.24: Devotion and knowledge have been described by Śambhu as not different, O twice-born. Therefore no distinction should be made between them; for one who practises it there is always happiness.
m.4.41.25: O twice-born, true knowledge never arises for one opposed to devotion. For one who practises devotion to Śambhu, the dawning of knowledge comes swiftly.
m.4.41.26: Therefore, O lords of sages, devotion to Maheśa should be cultivated. Through it alone everything will be accomplished; there is no doubt.
m.4.41.27: Thus what you asked, that very thing I have told. Hearing it, one is freed from all sins; there is no doubt about this.
m.4.41.iti: Thus ends the forty-first adhyāya, named The exposition of liberation, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.4.42.1: The sages said: Who is Śiva, who is Hari, who is Rudra, and who is Vidhi (Brahmā)? Among these, who is the one without attributes? Cut away this doubt of ours.
m.4.42.2: Sūta said: That which arose in the very beginning from the attributeless Supreme Self — that alone, the knowers of the Veda and Vedānta know, bears the name Śiva.
m.4.42.3: From that arose Prakṛti, joined with Puruṣa. By those two austerity was performed there, in the primordial water, O wise one.
m.4.42.4: That place is Kāśī, renowned as Pañcakrośī, dearest above all; and that water, spreading in every direction, pervaded this whole universe.
m.4.42.5: Having come into being, Hari, united with Māyā, slept there; he is renowned as Nārāyaṇa, and Māyā is regarded as Nārāyaṇī.
m.4.42.6: He who was born in the lotus of his navel is the Grandfather (Brahmā). The one seen by him through that very austerity is called Viṣṇu.
m.4.42.7: O wise ones, the form shown by the attributeless Śiva to settle the dispute of those two is renowned as Mahādeva.
m.4.42.8: By him it was declared: I, Śambhu, shall come forth from the forehead of Brahmā. He is renowned by the name Rudra, the bestower of grace upon the worlds.
m.4.42.9: For the sake of meditation by all, the formless one became endowed with form; he is Śiva himself, who shows tender love to his devotees.
m.4.42.10: Between Śiva, who stands apart from the three guṇas, and Rudra, the abode of the guṇas, there is in reality no difference, just as between gold and an ornament made of it.
m.4.42.11: The two are alike in form and deeds, alike grant the goal to devotees, are alike worthy of service by all, and sport in many divine plays.
m.4.42.12: Rudra, of fierce valour, is in every way of the very form of Śiva; he arose for the sake of the devotees' tasks, giving help to Hari and Brahmā.
m.4.42.13: The others who have arisen go to dissolution in due order; Rudra does not do so — Rudra merges into Śiva.
m.4.42.14: These created beings, on uniting with Rudra, pass into him; but Rudra, on meeting them, does not pass into them — such is the teaching of the Śruti.
m.4.42.15: All indeed worship Rudra; Rudra worships no one. Yet out of love for his devotees he sometimes, of his own accord, does worship them.
m.4.42.16: Those who constantly worship another deity attain absorption into him; through that very deity they reach Rudra after a long time, O wise ones.
m.4.42.17: But whoever are devotees of Rudra attain Śiva-hood at that very moment; they have no dependence on anyone else — this is the eternal Śruti.
m.4.42.18: Ignorance is manifold; true knowledge is not manifold. I shall explain its nature; listen attentively, O twice-born ones.
m.4.42.19: Whatever is seen here, from Brahmā down to a blade of grass — all that is Śiva alone; the notion of multiplicity is false.
m.4.42.20: Before creation Śiva is declared to exist; in the midst of creation likewise Śiva; at the end of creation Śiva is declared; when all is void, there is Sadāśiva.
m.4.42.21: Therefore, O lords of sages, Śiva alone is called fourfold; he alone is to be known as possessing attributes; and because he possesses Śakti, he is also twofold.
m.4.42.22: It was he who gave to Viṣṇu all the eternal Vedas, the many letters and prosodic measures, the meditation on himself, and his worship.
m.4.42.23: He is the Lord of all branches of knowledge — this is the eternal Śruti. Therefore Śambhu is called the maker of the Veda and the lord of the Veda.
m.4.42.24: He himself is Śaṅkara, the bestower of grace on all; creator, sustainer and destroyer, the witness — he is indeed without attributes.
m.4.42.25: For others there is a measure of time, but for Time itself there is no reckoning. He himself is Mahākāla, in direct union with Mahākālī.
m.4.42.26: And thus the Brāhmaṇas speak of Rudra, and likewise of Kālī. From those two, then, everything has come forth through their will, in their true divine play.
m.4.42.27: There is none who brings him into being, nor any sustainer or destroyer of him. He himself is the cause of all; Acyuta and the others are effects.
m.4.42.28: He himself is the cause, and never an effect of himself. Though one, he has become many; and though many, he returns to oneness.
m.4.42.29: A single seed, having gone forth outwardly as a plant, again becomes seed; so too, in multiplicity, Maheśvara, having the form of Śiva, is himself everything.
m.4.42.30: This is the supreme knowledge of Śiva, declared as it truly is. Only one who possesses knowledge knows it, no one else, O lords of seers.
m.4.42.31: The sages said: Tell us that knowledge together with its characteristics, knowing which one attains Śiva-hood. How is Śiva all that, or how is everything Śiva alone?
m.4.42.32: Vyāsa said: Having heard these words, Sūta, the foremost of Purāṇa narrators, remembering the lotus feet of Śiva, spoke these words to those sages.
m.4.42.iti: Thus ends the forty-second adhyāya, named The description of the distinction between the saguṇa and the nirguṇa, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.4.43.1: Sūta said: Listen, all you sages: I shall relate the knowledge of Śiva just as I heard it, a great secret whose very nature is supreme liberation.
m.4.43.2: In the assembly of Brahmā (Ka), Nārada, the Kumāras, Vyāsa and Kapila, it was determined and declared by them.
m.4.43.3: This knowledge should always be understood: the entire world is made of Śiva. Śiva should be known as constituting everything by the wise one who knows all.
m.4.43.4: Whatever world is seen, from Brahmā down to a blade of grass, all that is Śiva alone; that god is called Śiva.
m.4.43.5: When the desire arises in him, then this world is made. He alone knows everything; no one knows him.
m.4.43.6: Having himself created it and entered it, he remains far off; he has not truly entered there, being untainted and of the nature of consciousness.
m.4.43.7: Just as a luminary is reflected in water and the like, yet in reality does not enter it, so too is Śiva himself.
m.4.43.8: In reality he himself is everything; the graded sequence merely appears fair. Difference of view is ignorance; there is nothing else, and again no duality.
m.4.43.9: In all the philosophical systems a difference of views is set forth; but the Vedāntins always proclaim non-duality.
m.4.43.10: The individual soul, a portion of his own portion, deluded by nescience and helpless, thinks, I am another; freed from that nescience, it becomes Śiva.
m.4.43.11: Pervading all, Śiva is directly the pervader in all creatures; Śaṅkara himself, lord of the sentient and insentient, is everywhere.
m.4.43.12: The discerning one who undertakes a means for seeing him, resorting to the path of Vedānta, obtains the fruit of that vision.
m.4.43.13: Just as fire is pervasive and abides in every piece of wood, he who churns that wood surely sees it without doubt.
m.4.43.14: The discerning one who here practises the means beginning with devotion surely sees that Śiva; there is no doubt of this.
m.4.43.15: Śiva, Śiva, and Śiva alone; there is nothing else whatsoever. Through delusion Śaṅkara always appears as having manifold forms.
m.4.43.16: Just as the ocean, clay, or again gold acquires multiplicity through limiting adjuncts, so does Śaṅkara.
m.4.43.17: The difference between effect and cause does not really exist; it is only through deluded understanding, and when that is absent, it perishes.
m.4.43.18: When a sprout from a seed displays multiplicity, in the end there is only the seed, and that sprout perishes.
m.4.43.19: The knower is the seed itself; the sprout is considered the modification. When that ceases, he is again the knower; there need be no deliberation about this.
m.4.43.20: All is Śiva, Śiva is all; there is no difference whatsoever. How then does one see variety, and how again unity?
m.4.43.21: Just as the single light called the sun is seen by people in manifold ways, especially in water and the like, so too is he.
m.4.43.22: Just as space, though pervading everywhere, is not bound by contact, so the all-pervading god is never bound anywhere.
m.4.43.23: The individual soul is thus with ego; freed from that, it is Śaṅkara himself. The soul is petty, an experiencer of karma; Śaṅkara is great and untainted.
m.4.43.24: Just as a single metal such as gold, mixed with silver and the like, becomes of little value, so too is the soul joined with ego.
m.4.43.25: Just as gold and the like, purified by alkali and such, becomes fine and regains its former value, so too the soul through purification.
m.4.43.26: First, having found a true guru, endowed with the sentiment of devotion, one fervently performs worship, remembrance and the like, regarding him as Śiva.
m.4.43.27: Through that understanding, the impurity consisting of all sins and the like departs from the body; then ignorance perishes, when one becomes possessed of knowledge.
m.4.43.28: Then the soul, freed from ego and of pure intellect, attains Śaṅkara-hood again by the grace of Śaṅkara.
m.4.43.29: Just as one's own form is seen in a mirror, so he sees Śambhu present everywhere; this is well ascertained.
m.4.43.30: He alone is liberated while living; when the body has decayed, he merges in Śiva. The body is under the sway of prārabdha karma; the knower is considered distinct from it.
m.4.43.31: Obtaining good, he should not rejoice; obtaining evil, he should not be angry. He who has equanimity amid the pairs of opposites is called a knower.
m.4.43.32: By yoga of the self or by discrimination of the principles (tattvas), one desiring liberation should act so that he departs from the body, never to return to a body.
m.4.43.33: The liberated one would dissolve into Sadāśiva and attain separation from the body. Spiritual inquiry is the root of knowledge, and of that the root is devotion to Śiva.
m.4.43.34: Of devotion, love is declared the root; of love, likewise, hearing the sacred lore; of hearing, the company of the good; and from the company of the good comes a wise guru.
m.4.43.35: And when knowledge is thus perfected, one certainly becomes liberated. If this is so, whoever is a knower should always worship Śambhu alone.
m.4.43.36: Endowed with undivided devotion, he should worship Śambhu again and again; at the end he attains liberation. There need be no deliberation about this.
m.4.43.37: Therefore, for attaining liberation there is no god greater than Śaṅkara, by taking refuge in whom one turns back from saṃsāra.
m.4.43.38: Thus, O brahmins, I have told you this manifold teaching, determined by the assembled sages; it should be held in mind with effort.
m.4.43.39: First it was given by Śambhu to Viṣṇu before the liṅga; by Viṣṇu it was given to Brahmā, and by Brahmā to Sanaka and the others.
m.4.43.40: Then that knowledge was told by Sanaka and the others to Nārada; it was told by Nārada to Vyāsa, and by him, the compassionate one, to me.
m.4.43.41: It was imparted by me to you, and by you, for the good of the world, it should be carefully established, for it brings the attainment of Śiva.
m.4.43.42: Thus I have explained to you what I was asked, O lords among sages. It should be carefully guarded. What else do you wish to hear?
m.4.43.43: Vyāsa said: Having heard this, the sages attained supreme bliss; bowing, they praised him again and again with voices choked with joy.
m.4.43.44: The sages said: O disciple of Vyāsa, salutation to you. You are blessed, O best of Śaivas. You have made us hear the supreme reality, the unsurpassed Śaiva knowledge.
m.4.43.45: By your grace the confusion of our minds is indeed gone. We are content, having received from you the true knowledge of Śiva that grants liberation.
m.4.43.46: Sūta said: It should not be told to an unbeliever, to one without faith, or to a deceitful person, nor to one not devoted to Maheśa, nor to one unwilling to listen, O brāhmaṇas.
m.4.43.47: Having repeatedly examined the Itihāsas and Purāṇas, the Vedas and the śāstras, and having extracted their essence, Vyāsa told it to me.
m.4.43.48: By hearing this even once, sin is reduced to ashes. The non-devotee gains devotion, and the devotee's devotion increases.
m.4.43.49: When heard again, true devotion arises; and by hearing it yet again, liberation would come. Therefore it should be heard again and again by those who seek the fruits of enjoyment and liberation.
m.4.43.50: Five recitations should be done with the supreme fruit in view; one obtains it, there is no doubt—this is the word of Vyāsa.
m.4.43.51: Nothing is hard to attain for one by whom this excellent knowledge has been heard; by hearing it five times, the vision of Śiva is obtained.
m.4.43.52: Ancient kings, brāhmaṇas and excellent vaiśyas, having heard this five times with attentive mind, attained the supreme accomplishment.
m.4.43.53: Even today, whatever man, intent on devotion, hears this knowledge called Śaiva will obtain both enjoyment and liberation.
m.4.43.54: Vyāsa said: Having heard these words of his, they attained supreme bliss and reverently worshipped Sūta with various offerings.
m.4.43.55: With salutations and hymns, preceded by the recitation of auspicious blessings, they honoured him with benedictions, content, their doubts dispelled.
m.4.43.56: Sūta and those wise sages, mutually content, regarding Śambhu as the supreme god, bowed to and worshipped him.
m.4.43.57: This excellent knowledge of Śiva is great and very dear to Śiva; it is divine, grants enjoyment and liberation, and increases devotion to Śiva.
m.4.43.58: This sacred and supreme saṃhitā named Koṭirudra, the fourth of the Śiva Purāṇa, bringing joy, has been narrated by me.
m.4.43.59: Whoever, with concentrated mind, hears this with devotion or causes it to be heard, having enjoyed all pleasures here, attains the supreme state in the end.
m.4.43.iti: Thus ends the forty-third adhyāya, named The exposition of knowledge, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.5.1.1: We meditate on Śiva, the Full, who, endowed with the quality of sattva, sustains the worlds; who, resorting to rajas, is the creator; who, joined with tamas, is the destroyer; who abides beyond Māyā, which possesses the guṇas; who is truth and bliss, of infinite awareness, stainless, the ground of names such as Brahmā, eternal, and realised through union with sattva.
m.5.1.2: The sages said: O Sūta, O Sūta, greatly wise disciple of Vyāsa, salutation to you. You have recited to us the fourth compilation, called the Koṭirudra Saṃhitā.
m.5.1.3: Now tell us the story of Śambhu, the Supreme Self, together with Ambā, endowed with the various narratives contained within the Umā Saṃhitā.
m.5.1.4: Sūta said: O great sages headed by Śaunaka, listen with love to the auspicious, divine, supreme story of Śaṅkara, which grants both enjoyment and liberation.
m.5.1.5: When Vyāsa, the best of sages, had asked Sanatkumāra such a holy question, Sanatkumāra sang the excellent story of Śiva.
m.5.1.6: Sanatkumāra said: O Vyāsa, I shall now tell that story of the Great Lord which the great sage Upamanyu related to Vāsudeva.
m.5.1.7: Long ago Kṛṣṇa, son of Vasudeva, went to Kailāsa, the abode of Śaṅkara, to perform austerities to Śiva for the sake of a son.
m.5.1.8: There, seeing Upamanyu performing austerities on the highest peak, he bowed to the sage with devotion and, with joined palms, questioned him.
m.5.1.9: Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: O Upamanyu, greatly wise, foremost of Śaivas, noble-minded one, I have come here for the sake of a son, to perform austerities to Giriśa.
m.5.1.10: O sage, tell me the greatness of Śaṅkara, which brings constant bliss, hearing which I may with devotion perform the supreme austerity directed to the Lord.
m.5.1.11: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing these words of the wise Vāsudeva, Upamanyu, serene in mind, replied, remembering Śiva.
m.5.1.12: Upamanyu said: Listen, O Kṛṣṇa, great Śaiva, to the glory of the Great Lord Śambhu, which I beheld — supreme, and increasing devotion.
m.5.1.13: While engaged in austerity I beheld Śaṅkara and his weapons, and his entire retinue, the immortals headed by Viṣṇu and others.
m.5.1.14: I saw his weapon, shining with three parts, of unceasing bliss, imperishable, one-footed, great-tusked, with mouths devouring flames as mouthfuls;
m.5.1.15: blazing exceedingly with the light of two thousand rays, the foremost of all weapons, irresistible, many-eyed, thousand-footed;
m.5.1.16: which at the end of the kalpa surely destroys the universe, and for which nothing in the three worlds, moving or unmoving, would be unslayable.
m.5.1.17: Released from Maheśvara's arm, it burned up swiftly the entire three worlds, moving and unmoving, within half a blink — there is no doubt.
m.5.1.18: Engaged in austerity, I saw his imperishable, secret, supreme weapon standing at Rudra's side, to which nothing anywhere is equal or superior.
m.5.1.19: I saw that weapon of the Trident-bearer, famed in all worlds as the Śūla, named Vijaya, exceedingly fierce, destroyer of all weapons and missiles,
m.5.1.20: which could split the whole earth, which could dry up the great ocean, which could bring down the entire circle of the luminaries — there is no doubt of this;
m.5.1.21: by which, long ago, Māndhātṛ, son of Yuvanāśva, was slain together with his army — the universal emperor of great splendour, the king who had conquered the three worlds;
m.5.1.22: and the Haihaya, filled with pride; and the demon Lavaṇa was cast down, having challenged King Śatrughna to battle on every side.
m.5.1.23: That which, when that demon perished, returned to Rudra's hand — that is the trident, sharp-pointed, great, producing terror,
m.5.1.24: standing as if threatening, having formed a three-lined frown; like a smokeless fire, like the newly risen morning sun.
m.5.1.25: I saw the indescribable one with a serpent in hand, like Death with noose in hand; and the sharp-edged axe, adorned with serpents and other things,
m.5.1.26: resembling the fire at the end of the kalpa and having the form of a person — that axe of Bhārgava Rāma which made an end of the kṣatriyas in battle;
m.5.1.27: relying on whose power — it having been given by Śiva — the sage Rāma, exultant, long ago burned the kṣatriya race thrice seven times.
m.5.1.28: Likewise I beheld the discus Sudarśana, mighty, thousand-faced, two-thousand-armed, divine, having the form of a person,
m.5.1.29: two-thousand-eyed, blazing, crowded with a thousand feet, resplendent like ten million suns, able to burn the three worlds.
m.5.1.30: I saw the thunderbolt, greatly blazing, sharp, hundred-jointed, unsurpassed; and the great bow Pināka with its quiver, of great brilliance;
m.5.1.31: I saw the spear, the sword, and the noose, greatly blazing, together with the goad; and the great divine mace, and other weapons.
m.5.1.32: And likewise whatever weapons belong to the guardians of the worlds — all of them I beheld beside the blessed Rudra.
m.5.1.33: On the god's right side stood Brahmā, grandsire of the worlds, mounted on a divine aerial chariot yoked with swans and swift as thought.
m.5.1.34: And on his left side stood Nārāyaṇa, bearer of conch, discus and mace, likewise mounted on Vainateya (Garuḍa).
m.5.1.35: The Manus headed by Svāyambhuva, the sages headed by Bhṛgu, and the gods headed by Śakra — all came together.
m.5.1.36: Skanda, holding his spear, seated on a peacock and bearing a bell, stood near the Goddess like a second fire.
m.5.1.37: Nandī, holding a trident, stood before Bhava; and all the hosts of beings and the various Mothers were stationed there.
m.5.1.38: Then those gods, having saluted Maheśāna and surrounded him on all sides, praised Mahādeva with various hymns.
m.5.1.39: Whatever is seen or heard in this world — beholding all of it beside the Lord, I was utterly amazed;
m.5.1.40: then, summoning very great composure, with joined palms praising him with various hymns, I became immersed in supreme bliss in that worship, O Kṛṣṇa.
m.5.1.41: Seeing Śaṅkara before me, I, filled with faith, worshipped him properly according to rule, with a voice choked with tears.
m.5.1.42: Then the Lord Śaṅkara, the Supreme Lord, greatly pleased, spoke to me affectionately in a sweet voice, as if smiling.
m.5.1.43: O brahmin, you could not be shaken by me, though tested again and again. Good fortune to you. You are firm and endowed with devotion.
m.5.1.44: Therefore I am fully pleased with you; choose a boon, O you of good vows. Even what is hard to obtain among all the gods—nothing is withheld from you.
m.5.1.45: Hearing those words of Śambhu, full of true love, I, with joined palms, spoke to that god who is compassionate to his devotees.
m.5.1.46: Upamanyu said: O Lord, if you are pleased, if my devotion is steady, then by that truth may I have knowledge encompassing the three times.
m.5.1.47: Grant me abundant, unwavering devotion to you; and may there always be plenty of milk and rice for me together with my lineage.
m.5.1.48: May your presence always be in my hermitage, O all-pervading one; may there be friendship with your devotees, and may it always be mutual.
m.5.1.49: Thus addressed by me, Śambhu, the Supreme Lord, laughing, looked at me at once with a compassionate glance and spoke, O best of the Yadus.
m.5.1.50: Śrī Śiva said: O Upamanyu, O sage, dear child, you will be free from the defects born of old age and death; be endowed with all desires.
m.5.1.51: You will be worthy of worship by sages, endowed with fame and wealth; by my grace you will have virtue, beauty, good qualities and lordship at every step.
m.5.1.52: The presence of the Ocean of Milk itself, the treasury of waters, will always be with you wherever you wish, O sage.
m.5.1.53: That milk will be of the nature of nectar; as long as it is sustained, you will thereby behold this Vaivasvata kalpa together with your kinsmen.
m.5.1.54: And may your lineage be imperishable forever by my grace; I will make my presence in your hermitage, O great sage.
m.5.1.55: May your devotion to me be very steady; I will always grant you my sight when remembered by you, dear child. You are in every way dear to me.
m.5.1.56: Dwell in happiness as you desire; you should not feel anxious longing. May all that you have thought of come to complete fulfilment—there is no doubt of this.
m.5.1.57: Upamanyu said: Having spoken thus and granted the boons, the Lord Maheśāna, radiant like ten million suns, vanished right there.
m.5.1.58: Thus, O Kṛṣṇa, was Śaṅkara, the Supreme Lord, giver of enjoyment and liberation, seen by me together with his retinue.
m.5.1.59: Whatever was spoken by that wise Śambhu, the Supreme Lord, all of it I have attained through meditative absorption, O god of gods.
m.5.1.60: See before your very eyes the Gandharvas and Apsarases who have appeared, and likewise the sages, Vidyādharas and Siddhas stationed here.
m.5.1.61: See the delightful trees, with glossy leaves and sweet fragrance, laden with the flowers of all seasons, ever bearing blossoms and fruits.
m.5.1.62: All this, O mighty-armed one, the whole world filled with its being, exists by the grace of the great-souled Śaṅkara, the god of gods.
m.5.1.63: By the grace of the trident-bearer I possess all knowledge; I truly know everything—past, present and future.
m.5.1.64: I have seen that god whom even the gods, lords of the celestials, do not see without worshipping him. Who else is more blessed than I?
m.5.1.65: The supreme, eternal principle known as the twenty-sixth—thus do the wise meditate on the great, supreme, imperishable one.
m.5.1.66: He who knows the whole ordering of the principles, who beholds the meaning of all principles—he alone is the blessed god, the Lord of Pradhāna and Puruṣa.
m.5.1.67: It is the Lord who from his own right side created Brahmā, the cause of the worlds, and from his left side created Viṣṇu for the protection of the worlds.
m.5.1.68: And when the end of the kalpa arrived, the Lord created Rudra from his heart; then he withdrew the whole world, moving and unmoving.
m.5.1.69: At the end of the age, Mahādeva, having become Time, remains devouring all beings like the Saṃvartaka fire.
m.5.1.70: The all-knowing god, the Self of all beings, the source of the origin of all beings, abides all-pervading, to be seen by all the deities.
m.5.1.71: Therefore, worship Śaṅkara well for the sake of obtaining a son; Śiva, who loves his devotees, will quickly become gracious to you.
m.5.1.iti: Thus ends the first adhyāya, named The description of his own attainment, in the dialogue of Kṛṣṇa and Upamanyu, in the fifth saṃhitā, the Umā-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.5.2.1: Sanatkumāra said: Having heard these words of the great-souled sage Upamanyu, Kṛṣṇa, in whom devotion to Mahādeva had arisen, spoke to that sage.
m.5.2.2: Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: O Upamanyu, O sage, dear one, show me your kindness: tell me of those who, having worshipped Śiva, obtained their desires.
m.5.2.3: Sanatkumāra said: Having heard this, the sage Upamanyu, great and foremost among Śaivas, a treasury of compassion, highly praised Kṛṣṇa's words and replied.
m.5.2.4: Upamanyu said: I shall tell you of those devotees by whom, through the worship of Bhava, the heart's desire was indeed obtained; listen, O best of the Yadus.
m.5.2.5: Long ago Hiraṇyakaśipu obtained from Śarva, the moon-crested one, lordship over all the immortals for ten lakhs of years.
m.5.2.6: Then his foremost son, renowned by the name Nandana, by a boon of Śarva fought Indra for ten thousand years.
m.5.2.7: And Viṣṇu's terrible discus and the thunderbolt of Ākhaṇḍala (Indra) were shattered against his limbs in that great battle long ago, O Kṛṣṇa.
m.5.2.8: Owing to his merit, no weapons—not even the discus, thunderbolt and the rest—made any impression on the body of that wise and exceedingly mighty seizer (graha) in battle.
m.5.2.9: The gods, oppressed by that very powerful seizer, later, having received boons from the God, struck down the lords of the asuras fiercely.
m.5.2.10: Pleased, Bhava, lord of all worlds, granted to Vidyutprabha too lordship over the three worlds for a hundred thousand years.
m.5.2.11: Likewise Śiva gave him ten thousand thousands of sons, and said: you shall always be my attendant.
m.5.2.12: The blessed Bhava, Śaṅkara, with delighted mind, lovingly gave him an auspicious kingdom in Kuśadvīpa, O Vāsudeva.
m.5.2.13: Long ago the daitya Śatamakha, created by Dhātṛ, performed austerities for a hundred years and obtained a thousand sons from Bhava.
m.5.2.14: The sage famed as Yājñavalkya, celebrated in the Vedas, obtained supreme knowledge by worshipping Mahādeva.
m.5.2.15: He who by name is Vedavyāsa and gained incomparable fame—he too, by worshipping Śaṅkara, obtained knowledge of the three times.
m.5.2.16: Those Vālakhilyas, humiliated by Indra, obtained from Śaṅkara Garuḍa, the stealer of Soma, invincible to all.
m.5.2.17: All the waters had vanished through the former wrath of Kapardin; the gods, having worshipped Śarva with the samakapāla offering, set them flowing again.
m.5.2.18: And Anasūyā, wife of Atri, fasting for three hundred years and lying upon pestles, then obtained sons from Śarva—
m.5.2.19: —she obtained the sage Dattātreya, Candra and likewise Durvāsas; and that devoted wife brought the Gaṅgā to flow at Citrakūṭa.
m.5.2.20: Vikarṇa too, having propitiated Mahādeva, the bringer of happiness to devotees, attained great perfection, O Madhusūdana.
m.5.2.21: King Citrasena, firm in devotion, having propitiated Śambhu, obtained fearlessness from the dread of all kings, and incomparable happiness.
m.5.2.22: Śrīkara, son of a cowherd woman, devotion to Mahādeva having arisen in him from watching a king's worship, attained the highest perfection.
m.5.2.23: Citrāṅgada, a king's son and husband of Sīmantinī, though submerged in the Yamunā, did not die, through Śiva's grace, O Hari.
m.5.2.24: And he, of good vows, went to the abode of Takṣaka, gained his friendship, and returned happily to his own home, endowed with manifold riches.
m.5.2.25: Sīmantinī, his beloved, devoted to the Monday vow, obtained supreme marital fortune through Śiva's grace, O Kṛṣṇa.
m.5.2.26: By the power of that vow, long ago a certain brahmin's son, who out of greed had deceitfully assumed the guise of a wife, actually became a woman.
m.5.2.27: Cañcukā, a wicked unchaste woman, long ago at Gokarṇa heard from a brahmin the sacred story of Śambhu and with devotion attained the highest state.
m.5.2.28: The sinner Binduga, Cañcukā's husband, through the grace of his own wife heard the Śiva Purāṇa and attained the good state belonging to Śaṅkara.
m.5.2.29: The famed courtesan Piṅgalā and the vile brahmin named Madara, having worshipped the Śaiva Ṛṣabha, both obtained a good state.
m.5.2.30: A certain courtesan named Mahānandā, devoted to Śiva's feet, having fully propitiated Śiva through her firm pledge, obtained a good state.
m.5.2.31: Kaikeyī, a brahmin girl also called Sādarā, devoted to Śiva's vow, attained supreme happiness by observing the vow of Śiva the Lord.
m.5.2.32: King Vimarṣaṇa too, having practised devotion to Śiva, attained the highest state long ago through Śiva's grace, O Kṛṣṇa.
m.5.2.33: King Durjana, a sinful villain lusting after many women, reached Śiva through devotion to Śiva, untainted in all his actions.
m.5.2.34: One named Śambara, together with his wife, a votary of Śiva's vow and devoted to Śaṅkara, delighting in pyre-ash, through devotion obtained his supreme state.
m.5.2.35: A cāṇḍāla woman named Saumini, having worshipped Śiva even unknowingly, obtained the Śaiva state through the supreme grace of Śaṅkara, O Kṛṣṇa.
m.5.2.36: A hunter named Mahākāla, a Kirāta who harmed others, having worshipped Śiva with devotion, obtained the supreme good state.
m.5.2.37: Durvāsas, tiger among sages, through Śiva's grace long ago spread in the world his own doctrine—devotion to Śiva, the giver of liberation.
m.5.2.38: And Kauśika, a kṣatriya, having worshipped Śaṅkara, benefactor of the world, became a brahmin, like a second lotus-born (Brahmā).
m.5.2.39: Having worshipped Śiva with true devotion, Virañci (Brahmā), best of Śaivas, became the creator and grandsire of all worlds, O Kṛṣṇa.
m.5.2.40: Mārkaṇḍeya, best of sages, glorious, foremost among Śiva's devotees, became long-lived and a great master through Śiva's grace, O Hari.
m.5.2.41: Indeed, O Kṛṣṇa, the king of the gods, a great devotee of Śiva, once enjoyed rule over the three worlds through Śiva's grace, as the mighty overlord of all the gods.
m.5.2.42: Bāṇa, the son of Bali, a great devotee of Śiva and self-controlled, through Śiva's grace became ruler of the cosmic egg and lord of all.
m.5.2.43: Hari, Śakti and Dadhīca, through true devotion and Śiva's grace, became great lords; likewise Rāma too was a devotee of Śaṅkara.
m.5.2.44: Kaṇāda, Bhārgava, the preceptor Bṛhaspati and Gautama too — through devotion to Śiva they became lords of great power.
m.5.2.45: Śākalya, of disciplined mind, worshipped Bhava with a mental sacrifice for as long as nine hundred years, O Mādhava.
m.5.2.46: The Lord was pleased and said: you will be an author of treatises; dear child, your fame will be undying and will prevail in the three worlds.
m.5.2.47: May your lineage be imperishable, adorned with great sages. O best of sages, you will be a composer of sūtras, and thereafter so will your son.
m.5.2.48: In this way that best of sages obtained a boon from Śaṅkara, and he became renowned throughout the three worlds and worthy of worship, O delight of the Yadus.
m.5.2.49: There was a sage renowned as Sāvarṇi in the Kṛta age; here he performed austerities for six thousand years.
m.5.2.50: Lord Rudra, appearing in person, said to him: I am pleased with you, O sinless one. You will be an author of treatises, renowned in the world, free from old age and death.
m.5.2.51: Such is Mahādeva; worshipped by those rich in prior merit, he then grants auspicious desires just as they wish.
m.5.2.52: With only one mouth I cannot tell the qualities of the Lord that exist, not even in hundreds of years.
m.5.2.iti: Thus ends the second adhyāya, named The instruction of Upamanyu, in the dialogue of Sanatkumāra and Vyāsa, in the fifth saṃhitā, the Umā-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.5.3.1: Sanatkumāra said: Having heard these words of his, he (Kṛṣṇa), struck with the greatest wonder, spoke to that great sage Upamanyu, whose mind was at peace.
m.5.3.2: Vāsudeva said: You are blessed, O best of brāhmaṇas! What accomplished person is able to praise you, in whose hermitage the God of the first gods himself makes his presence felt?
m.5.3.3: O tiger among sages, may that blessed Śiva grant me his sight; may he likewise bestow his grace upon me too.
m.5.3.4: Upamanyu said: In a very short time, without doubt, you will surely see Mahādeva by his grace alone, O Puruṣottama.
m.5.3.5: In the sixteenth month you will obtain excellent boons from Maheśvara. How would the god, together with his consort, not grant you boons, O Hari?
m.5.3.6: You are worthy of worship by all the deities and ever praiseworthy for your virtues. I shall tell you, who have faith, the mantra to be repeated, O Acyuta.
m.5.3.7: By the power of that repetition you will truly see Śaṅkara, and from Maheśvara you will obtain a son equal to yourself in strength.
m.5.3.8: The repetition is namaḥ śivāya — this king of mantras, O Hari, divine, granting all desires and bestowing both enjoyment and liberation.
m.5.3.9: Sanatkumāra said: While he was thus narrating stories concerning Mahādeva, eight days passed like a single moment, O ascetic.
m.5.3.10: When the ninth day arrived, he was initiated by the sage and taught the great Śaiva mantra of the Atharvaśiras.
m.5.3.11: At once he became a staff-bearer with shaven head, well concentrated, and he performed austerities, his body raised on the tip of his big toe and his arms held aloft.
m.5.3.12: When the sixteenth month arrived, the Supreme Lord Śambhu, pleased, together with Pārvatī, granted Kṛṣṇa his sight.
m.5.3.13: He saw the god accompanied by Pārvatī, three-eyed, moon-crested, being praised by Brahmā and others and worshipped by millions of siddhas;
m.5.3.14: wearing divine garlands and garments, especially bowed to by gods and demons humble with devotion, adorned with various ornaments;
m.5.3.15: full of every wonder, lovely, the great Lord, unborn and imperishable, attended by various gaṇas, pleased, the Master accompanied by his two sons.
m.5.3.16: Seeing Śaṅkara thus, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, his eyes wide with wonder, with joined palms, delighted and full of great joy, bowed down.
m.5.3.17: Then he worshipped him with words, with many kinds of hymns, and with bowed neck he praised the Lord of gods with the Thousand Names.
m.5.3.18: Then the gods, with the gandharvas, vidyādharas and great serpents, released a shower of flowers and words of applause pleasing to the mind.
m.5.3.19: And looking at Pārvatī's face, the blessed Lord, loving to his devotees, Rudra the great Lord, pleased, then spoke to Keśava.
m.5.3.20: Śrī Mahādeva said: Kṛṣṇa, I know you to be my devotee, ever firm in your vow towards me. Choose from me holy boons, hard to obtain in the three worlds.
m.5.3.21: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing these words of his, Kṛṣṇa, with joined palms and reverence, bowing again and again, spoke to Śambhu, Lord of all.
m.5.3.22: Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: O God of gods, Mahādeva, I indeed ask of you excellent boons, eight in number, O Lord, as offered by you, O Maheśvara.
m.5.3.23: May my mind ever be in your dharma; may I have great and unshakable fame, nearness to you, and steady devotion to you always — thus I ask.
m.5.3.24: O Śambhu, may my wives indeed have sons, ten and more each; and may all enemies proud of their strength be slain in battle.
m.5.3.25: May I never suffer humiliation anywhere from an enemy, O Lord; and may I be exceedingly dear even to all yogins.
m.5.3.26: Grant these eight excellent boons, O God of gods; salutation to you. You alone are Lord of all, and especially my own Lord.
m.5.3.27: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing these words of his, the blessed Bhava said to him, all this shall be; then the trident-bearer spoke to him again.
m.5.3.28: A mighty son named Sāmba, of great valour, will be born to you. The terrible Saṃvartaka Āditya was cursed by the sages,
m.5.3.29: You shall become a human — he will be your son. And whatever you have asked for, obtain all of it.
m.5.3.30: Sanatkumāra said: Having thus obtained all the boons from the Supreme Lord, Śrī Kṛṣṇa gratified him with many hymns of various kinds.
m.5.3.31: Then Śivā Pārvatī, pleased and loving to her devotees, spoke to the great-souled Vāsudeva, the ascetic devoted to Śambhu.
m.5.3.32: Pārvatī said: O Vāsudeva of great intellect, O sinless Kṛṣṇa, I am pleased with you. Accept from me too boons that are delightful and rare on earth.
m.5.3.33: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing these words of Pārvatī, that scion of the Yadus, his heart deeply gladdened, spoke with a mind full of devotion.
m.5.3.34: Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: O Goddess, if you are fully pleased and are giving me boons, then by this true austerity may there never arise towards brāhmaṇas
m.5.3.35: hatred at any time; rather, may I always honour the twice-born. And may my mother and father be ever pleased with me.
m.5.3.36: Wherever I go, may I enjoy goodwill among all beings; and by your sight, may I have fitting offspring in my family.
m.5.3.37: May I gratify the gods, Indra and the rest, with a hundred sacrifices; and may I always feed thousands of ascetics and guests—
m.5.3.38: may I always feed them in my home with food purified by faith. And may there be constant affection with my kinsmen, and perfect contentment.
m.5.3.39: O Goddess, may I be dear as life to thousands of wives, and by your grace, O consort of Śaṅkara, may my desirability to them never wane.
m.5.3.40: And may their fathers in the world be truthful. Let these and other excellent boons be granted through your grace, O Pārvatī.
m.5.3.41: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing those words of his, the goddess, astonished, said to him: so be it; blessings to you—she, the eternal one, the giver of all desires.
m.5.3.42: Having given those boons to him, Pārvatī and the Supreme Lord, having bestowed true grace on Kṛṣṇa, vanished right there.
m.5.3.43: Kṛṣṇa considered himself fulfilled, O lord of sages. He quickly reached the incomparable hermitage of the sage Upamanyu.
m.5.3.44: Then the slayer of Keśin, having bowed his head there to that sage, related to Upamanyu all that had happened.
m.5.3.45: And he said to him: who else could there be, other than the god Śarva, O Janārdana, who is the lord of great gifts in the world, or so exceedingly unbearable in anger,
m.5.3.46: or in knowledge, in austerity, in valour, in steadfastness, or in rank? Listen, O Govinda, O illustrious one, to the divine sovereignty of Śambhu.
m.5.3.47: Hearing that, he became filled with faith and devoted to Śambhu; he asked about Śiva's greatness, and the lord of sages spoke to him.
m.5.3.48: Upamanyu said: Formerly, in the world of Brahmā, the blessed Śaṅkara was praised with a thousand names by the great-souled Taṇḍi, a yogin of Brahman.
m.5.3.49: The Sāṅkhyas recite that hymn, extensive like a lexicon. That hymn is hard for humans to understand, yet it grants all desires.
m.5.3.50: Remembering Śaṅkara constantly, go home happy, O Kṛṣṇa. You will always be, dear one, the foremost among the hosts of Śiva's devotees.
m.5.3.51: Thus addressed, Vāsudeva bowed to the lord of sages, and Keśava, recollecting Śambhu in his mind, went to Dvārakā.
m.5.3.52: Sanatkumāra said: Thus Kṛṣṇa, having worshipped Śaṅkara, the benefactor of the world, became fulfilled, O best of sages, and likewise became invincible to all.
m.5.3.53: Likewise Rāma, son of Daśaratha, having worshipped Śiva with devotion, became fulfilled, O best of sages, and was victorious everywhere.
m.5.3.54: Formerly, O sage, Rāma, having performed extremely vast austerity on a mountain, obtained from Śiva a bow, arrows, a further bow, and indeed supreme, excellent knowledge.
m.5.3.55: Having slain Rāvaṇa with his hosts, having built a bridge over the ocean, and having regained Sītā, he went home and enjoyed rule over the entire earth.
m.5.3.56: Likewise Rāma the Bhārgava, grieved on seeing his father killed by kṣatriyas, worshipped the all-pervading Lord with austerity, and from Śarva—
m.5.3.57: —from the pleased Supreme Lord he obtained a sharp axe, and with it he burned up those kṣatriyas thrice seven times.
m.5.3.58: Invincible and immortal, that treasury of austerities, ever devoted to the worship of the liṅga, is seen even today by Siddhas and Cāraṇas.
m.5.3.59: Rāma, dwelling on Mount Mahendra, remains in austerity; at the end of the kalpa he will again attain the station of a ṛṣi.
m.5.3.60: Formerly the younger brother of Asita, the ascetic named Devala, in affliction performed austerity, holding fast to the root of the universe Śiva.
m.5.3.61: That ascetic, who had been cursed by Purandara, by worshipping the wish-granting liṅga firmly obtained a dharma untouched by adharma.
m.5.3.62: Gṛtsamada, son of Cākṣuṣa Manu, became a deer in a desert region through Vasiṣṭha's curse; alone in the Daṇḍaka forest,
m.5.3.63: remembering with devotion in his heart Śiva united with the praṇava, he thereby became a deer-faced gaṇa, having the appearance of the mouth of death.
m.5.3.64: Having crossed beyond the curse, he was again brought to freedom from old age and death, and out of affection Śaṅkara made him a permanent follower of Lambodara.
m.5.3.65: Śarva granted Gārgya liberation, rare on earth, the power of moving at will, a great domain, and knowledge of time endowed with great prosperity,
m.5.3.66: and eternal mastery of the four-footed Sarasvatī speech; and Śiva gave him a thousand unequalled sons.
m.5.3.67: The wielder of Pināka, pleased, gave to Parāśara a son, Vedavyāsa, lord of yogins, free from old age and death.
m.5.3.68: Māṇḍavya, taken down from the point of the stake after ten hundred thousand years, was released by Śaṅkara himself, who gave him life.
m.5.3.69: A certain poor brahmin, who had formerly been a householder, placed his son Gālava in his teacher's house.
m.5.3.70: Hiding in the sages' hall, he said to his wife—since he was utterly penniless—whatever mendicant comes to this house,
m.5.3.71: he should be told by you,
m.5.3.72: Once a certain guest, emaciated and parched with hunger and thirst, said to her, where has your husband gone? And she to him
m.5.3.73: said, my husband is not to be seen at present. That seer, knowing the truth by his divine sight, said this to her:
m.5.3.74: Thus cursed, that brahmin, staying hidden in the house, died right there. Then his son Gālava, permitted by Viśvāmitra,
m.5.3.75: came home and, hearing from his mother of the most dreadful curse, worshipped the god Śaṅkara, performing the worship of Śambhu.
m.5.3.76: He the father came forth from the house, remembering Śaṅkara in his heart. Then, seeing his son, the father, with joined palms, said to him:
m.5.3.77: By Mahādeva's grace, through your deed I am fulfilled; I am wealthy and blessed with a son; I was dead and am alive again.
m.5.3.78: Thus I have told you everything; I am not able to describe Śambhu's virtues either briefly or in detail—even Śeṣa would not have enough mouths.
m.5.3.iti: Thus ends the third adhyāya, named The description of the glory of Śiva in uplifting Kṛṣṇa and other devotees of Śiva, in the fifth saṃhitā, the Umā-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.5.4.1: The sages said: Dear sir, dear sir, O greatly fortunate one, you are truly blessed, O wise one! This wondrous story of Śambhu, which bestows supreme devotion, has been narrated to us.
m.5.4.2: Tell again the story of Śambhu, following the questions of Vyāsa. You are all-knowing, the disciple of Vyāsa, skilled in the truth of Śiva.
m.5.4.3: Sūta said: In just this way my teacher Vyāsa questioned Sanatkumāra, born of the Unborn Brahmā, the all-knowing devotee of Śiva, lord among sages.
m.5.4.4: Vyāsa said: O all-knowing Sanatkumāra, this auspicious story of Śaṅkara, the great Lord who sports in various divine plays, has been narrated to me.
m.5.4.5: Tell again, in particular, of the greatness of Mahādeva; for, dear sir, my great eagerness to hear keeps growing.
m.5.4.6: Tell by what greatness of Śambhu, who sports in various plays, all those in the world were deluded, he having taken away their knowledge through his māyā.
m.5.4.7: Sanatkumāra said: Listen, O Vyāsa of great intellect, to the delightful story of Śaṅkara, by the mere hearing of which devotion to Śiva arises.
m.5.4.8: Śiva is the god, lord of all, the Self of all, the all-seeing; by his greatness this whole entire world is pervaded.
m.5.4.9: The supreme form of Śiva alone is made up of Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Īśvara; it is called the self of all beings, and has the form of the three liṅgas and of the liṅga-less.
m.5.4.10: There are eight orders of birth of the gods, the human one which is the ninth, and five orders of animals; thus there are fourteen.
m.5.4.11: Whether past, present or future, all beings everywhere come forth from Śiva, and, having reached their growth, dissolve into him.
m.5.4.12: Of Brahmā, Indra, Upendra and Candra, of gods, Dānavas and serpents, of Gandharvas, of humans, and of all others as well —
m.5.4.13: — Śiva is regarded as kinsman, friend, preceptor, protector, leader, benefactor, teacher, wish-fulfilling tree, or brother, father and mother.
m.5.4.14: Śiva, who comprises everything, is to be known by men through himself; he is higher than the highest; he cannot be described, and he is that which is both the higher and the lower.
m.5.4.15: His supreme divine māyā pervades everywhere, O sage; the whole world, with gods, asuras and humans, is subject to it.
m.5.4.16: By Kāma, its own helper, the mighty Mind-born one, every hero has been overpowered — even the mighty ones beginning with Viṣṇu.
m.5.4.17: Through the power of Śiva's māyā, Hari became infatuated by desire and violated others' wives many times, O lord of sages.
m.5.4.18: Indra, though lord of the gods, became infatuated with Gautama's wife; the wicked one committed sin and then received the sage's curse.
m.5.4.19: Even Fire, the foremost in the world, deluded by Śiva's māyā, was made subject to desire because of his pride; and afterwards he was rescued by that very Śiva.
m.5.4.20: Even the Wind, the life-breath of the world, deluded through pride by Śiva's māyā and conquered by desire, O Vyāsa, once took pleasure with another's wife.
m.5.4.21: The fierce-rayed Sun, Mārtaṇḍa, deluded by Śiva's māyā, quickly became overwhelmed with desire on seeing a mare, and assumed the form of a horse.
m.5.4.22: And the Moon, deluded by Śambhu's māyā and filled with desire, carried off his teacher's wife; then, united with her, he was rescued by that very Śiva.
m.5.4.23: Long ago Mitra and Varuṇa were engaged in severe austerity; yet even those two sages were deluded, bewildered by Śiva's māyā.
m.5.4.24: Seeing the young Urvaśī, both became lustful; Mitra discharged his semen into a jar, and Varuṇa likewise into water.
m.5.4.25: Then from the jar arose Vasiṣṭha, born of Mitra; and from Varuṇa was born Agastya, radiant like the submarine fire.
m.5.4.26: And Dakṣa, the son of Brahmā, deluded by Śambhu's māyā, once together with his brothers desired to enjoy their sister.
m.5.4.27: And Brahmā too, deluded many times by Śiva's māyā, became desirous of enjoying his own daughter and other women.
m.5.4.28: Even Cyavana, the great yogin, deluded by Śiva's māyā, sported with Sukanyā; he became attached to desire.
m.5.4.29: Kaśyapa, deluded through Śiva's māyā and filled with desire, once out of infatuation begged King Dhanvan for his daughter.
m.5.4.30: Garuḍa, utterly infatuated, wished to carry off the maiden Śāṇḍilī; but being found out by her, he at once had his wings burnt.
m.5.4.31: The sage Vibhāṇḍaka, on seeing a woman, fell under the sway of desire; his son Ṛṣyaśṛṅga was born of a doe by Śiva's command.
m.5.4.32: And the sage Gautama, his mind deluded by Śambhu's māyā, seeing Śāradvatī naked, was agitated by her and took pleasure.
m.5.4.33: That ascetic held his own spilled semen in a wooden vessel; and from that pot was born Droṇa, the best of weapon-bearers.
m.5.4.34: Parāśara, the great yogin, deluded by Śiva's māyā, sported with the maiden Matsyodarī, the fisherman's daughter.
m.5.4.35: Then Viśvāmitra, deluded by Śiva's māyā and fallen under the sway of desire, O Vyāsa, took pleasure with Menakā in the forest.
m.5.4.36: Bereft of sense, he entered into hostility with Vasiṣṭha; yet by Śiva's grace that same man again became a brāhmaṇa.
m.5.4.37: Rāvaṇa, son of Viśravas, became lustful through Śiva's māyā; the evil-minded one, deluded, carried off Sītā and met his death.
m.5.4.38: Bṛhaspati, best of sages, though self-controlled, deluded by Śiva's māyā, took pleasure with his brother's wife; from that Bharadvāja was born.
m.5.4.39: Thus, O Vyāsa, I have described to you the power of the māyā of the great-souled Śaṅkara. What else do you wish to hear?
m.5.4.iti: Thus ends the fourth adhyāya, named The description of the power of Śiva's māyā, in the fifth saṃhitā, the Umā-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.5.5.1: Vyāsa said: O Lord, describe to me those beings who are given to sin and who are the causes of falling into great hells. O son of Brahmā, salutations to you.
m.5.5.2: Sanatkumāra said: Those beings who are given to sin and who are the causes of falling into great hells are described here in brief; listen attentively.
m.5.5.3: Setting one's intent on another's wife or wealth, thinking of harm in the mind, and obsession with what ought not to be done: mental action of sin is of four kinds.
m.5.5.4: Incoherent babbling, whatever is untrue and unpleasant, and slander behind a person's back: verbal action of sin is of four kinds.
m.5.5.5: Eating what should not be eaten, violence, engaging in false deeds, and taking the property of others: bodily action of sin is of four kinds.
m.5.5.6: Thus this twelvefold action, performed through three means, has been declared. Now I shall further tell its subdivisions, whose fruit is endless.
m.5.5.7: Those who hate Mahādeva, who ferries beings across the ocean of saṃsāra, commit a very great sin; they go into the ocean of hell.
m.5.5.8: Those deluded ones who revile one who expounds the knowledge of Śiva, an ascetic, gurus, and fathers go to the ocean of hell.
m.5.5.9: Reviling Śiva, reviling the guru, defaming the knowledge of Śiva, stealing the property of the gods, destroying the property of brahmins,
m.5.5.10: and the act of those deluded ones who steal a book of Śiva-knowledge: these six they call great sins, yielding endless evil fruit.
m.5.5.11: Those who, seeing worship of Śiva being performed, do not rejoice in it; who, seeing a worshipped Śiva-liṅga, do not bow and do not praise it;
m.5.5.12: who, acting as they please and without fear, stand about and amuse themselves before Śiva and in the presence of the guru, devoid of proper courtesies;
m.5.5.13: those who, though established in the path of ritual action, do not on festival days perform consecration of the sacred place and worship, or honour the gurus according to rule;
m.5.5.14: those who abandon Śaiva conduct and hate Śiva's devotees; those who, without first worshipping the Śiva-knowledge scripture, study and copy it;
m.5.5.15: who impart it, hear it, and recite it improperly; who make sport of it out of greed and according to the rules of false knowledge;
m.5.5.16: and who lay it down as they please in unconsecrated places; he who, interrupting a discourse on Śiva-knowledge, speaks of something else;
m.5.5.17: he who does not speak the truth and does not give gifts; he who, being impure or in an impure place, expounds or listens to it;
m.5.5.18: he who wishes to hear scripture without first worshipping the guru, and who does not render service or obey his command with devotion;
m.5.5.19: who does not welcome his words but answers back, and who neglects whatever in the guru's work is hard to accomplish;
m.5.5.20: the evildoer who abandons his guru when he is afflicted, powerless, setting out for a foreign land, or humiliated by enemies;
m.5.5.21: and he who shows contempt toward his wife, sons, and friends — and likewise toward those of a good expounder who reveals dharma, even though he be not one's own guru:
m.5.5.22: All these deeds, O best of sages, they declare to be very great sins, equal to reviling Śiva.
m.5.5.23: The slayer of a brahmin, the drinker of liquor, the thief, and the violator of the guru's bed — these are the great sinners, and the fifth is one who associates with them.
m.5.5.24: He who, out of anger, greed, fear, or hatred, aiming at a brahmin's ruin, alleges a grave fault that cuts to the quick, becomes a brahmin-slayer.
m.5.5.25: He who invites a brahmin and then gives nothing, he who having given takes back, and he who defames a faultless one — that man becomes a brahmin-slayer.
m.5.5.26: He who, out of pride in his learning, puts to shame a good brahmin who is indifferent to dispute in the midst of an assembly is declared a brahmin-slayer.
m.5.5.27: He who by false merits forcibly raises himself to eminence, setting aside others' true merits, he too becomes a brahmin-slayer.
m.5.5.28: He who creates obstruction for cows being covered by bulls, and for brahmins, gurus foremost — him they call a brahmin-slayer.
m.5.5.29: He who seizes land given to gods, brahmins, or cows, even if it has been lost to them over time — him they call a brahmin-slayer.
m.5.5.30: The seizing of the property of gods and brahmins, and whatever is acquired unjustly, should be known as a sin equal to killing a brahmin; there is no doubt about this.
m.5.5.31: If a twice-born, having studied the Veda and the knowledge of Brahman that is of the nature of Śiva, foolishly abandons it, that is equal to drinking liquor.
m.5.5.32: Having undertaken any vow, observance, or sacrifice and then abandoning it, and the abandonment of the five daily sacrifices — that is equal to drinking liquor.
