m.5.26.51: By the sound of the conch, O Queen of the gods, one attains the power of taking any form at will; by the sound of thunder-clouds, the yogin meets with no calamity.
m.5.26.52: He who with one-pointed mind constantly meditates on the tuṅkāra, which has the form of Brahman—what is there that he cannot accomplish as he wishes, O fair-faced one?
m.5.26.53: He becomes all-knowing and all-seeing, and goes about taking forms at will; he is not touched by changes—he is Śiva himself, without doubt.
m.5.26.54: Thus, O Supreme Lady, I have told you all about the nature of Śabdabrahman in its ninefold form. What more do you wish to hear?
m.5.26.iti: Thus ends the twenty-sixth adhyāya, named The description of cheating Time, in the fifth saṃhitā, the Umā-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.5.27.1: The Goddess said: The yogin attains the state of Vāyu, which arises from the ether of yoga. Tell me all of that, O Lord, if you are pleased with me.
m.5.27.2: Śaṅkara said: Earlier, wishing for the welfare of yogins, I explained everything: how one has properly conquered Time, and what the sign of Vāyu is.
m.5.27.3: Knowing by that sign the day of death, the yogin who remains devoted to prāṇāyāma conquers the Time that has come within just half a month, O beautiful one.
m.5.27.4: The wind dwelling in the heart always kindles the fire; it is the companion of fire. That wind, both outer and inner, is pervasive, all-reaching and great.
m.5.27.5: Knowledge, understanding, energy — everything proceeds from the wind. He by whom the wind is conquered here has conquered this whole world.
m.5.27.6: Desiring to destroy old age and death, the yogin, delighting in yoga and wholly intent on concentration and meditation, should always remain in dhāraṇā.
m.5.27.7: Just as a blacksmith, O sage, fills the bellows through the mouth and accomplishes his work by means of air, so should the yogin practise.
m.5.27.8: The God is thousandfold, having a thousand eyes, feet and hands; covering the entire earth, he stands beyond it by ten fingers' breadth; on him one should meditate.
m.5.27.9: One should mutter the Gāyatrī together with its head (śiras), preceded by the vyāhṛtis, three times with breath restrained; that is called prāṇāyāma.
m.5.27.10: The planets such as the Moon and the Sun go and come back; but those devoted to yoga and meditation do not return even now.
m.5.27.11: The fruit a twice-born gains by performing austerity for a hundred years, drinking only water from the tip of kuśa grass — that fruit, O Devī, he obtains by a single retention of the breaths.
m.5.27.12: The twice-born who, rising at dawn, performs even a single prāṇāyāma quickly destroys all sin and goes to Brahmā's world.
m.5.27.13: He who, untiring, is always devoted to prāṇāyāma in solitude, having conquered old age and death, moves with the wind and becomes a sky-goer (khecarī).
m.5.27.14: He acquires the form of a siddha, radiance, intelligence, prowess and valour; he equals the wind in speed, and gains praiseworthy well-being and supreme happiness.
m.5.27.15: I have told in full the perfection of Vāyu which the yogin attains. What he obtains from the practice of light (tejas) too, I shall now tell you, O Queen of the gods.
m.5.27.16: Sitting in a comfortable posture in his own place, resting where there is no sound of people's talk, he should make the light shine in the middle region by the breath joined with moon and sun.
m.5.27.17: The vigilant yogin in whom the light residing in fire shines between the eyebrows sees without doubt even what is minute in the world, in darkness devoid of lamps.
m.5.27.18: Pressing the eyes slightly and carefully with the fingers, the yogin, looking at the star of light, should meditate on it with one-pointed mind for half a muhūrta.
m.5.27.19: Then, meditating in darkness, he sees the divine light of the Lord — white, red, yellow, black, with the lustre of the rainbow.
m.5.27.20: It is between the brows, situated on the forehead, with radiance like the rising sun. Knowing it, he, with a body as he wishes, sports assuming any form at will.
m.5.27.21: There arise absorption in the quieting of causes, entry into another's body, attainment of the powers beginning with aṇimā, and seeing by the mind;
m.5.27.22: hearing and knowing from afar, invisibility, assuming many forms — and through constant practice, the power of moving in the sky arises.
m.5.27.23: Even the wise, endowed with learning and study and skilled in many śāstras, are deluded when they follow the power of past karma.
m.5.27.24: Though seeing, they do not see; though hearing, they are like the deaf — like blind men in the world, foolish, deluded by sin.
m.5.27.25: I know this great Person, of the colour of the sun, beyond darkness. Only by knowing him does one pass beyond death; there is no other path for going there.
m.5.27.26: Thus I have properly told you the excellent method of the light, by which the yogin, conquering Time, attains immortality.
m.5.27.27: Again I shall tell something still higher, by which death does not occur. Listen attentively, O Devī, with one-pointed mind.
m.5.27.28: O Devī, this is the fourth (turīya) state for beings, for yogins and meditators alike. The yogin, with mind controlled, seated in a comfortable posture in a suitable place,
m.5.27.29: keeping his body erect and joining his hands into a cup, drinking the air slowly, slowly with the mouth shaped like a beak,
m.5.27.30: then in a moment the life-giving waters situated in the palate flow forth. He should draw them in, taking up with the breath that cool water, the nectar.
m.5.27.31: Drinking it every day, the yogin does not fall under the power of death; he has a divine body, great splendour, and is free from thirst and hunger.
m.5.27.32: In strength he is an elephant, in speed a horse, in sight Suparṇa (Garuḍa), with keen hearing even from afar; his black hair is curled and wavy, his complexion equal to that of Gandharvas and Vidyādharas.
m.5.27.33: Such a man would live a hundred years of the gods and attain equality with the wise Vākpati (Bṛhaspati). Living thus he attains the state of a sky-goer, moving as he pleases, ever happy.
m.5.27.34: Again I shall tell another method, which is guarded with effort even by the gods; listen to it, O fair-faced one.
m.5.27.35: Curling back the tongue towards the palate, the yogin should practise; within a short time he gradually reaches the lambikā (the uvula region).
m.5.27.36: Then, when touched, it releases cool nectar; drinking it constantly, that yogin attains immortality.
m.5.27.37: The tip of the tongue (the ra-point), the tip of the lambikā, the contact as of a palm, reaching the bindu of the white lotus — drawn by that, this nectar falls in the supreme abode, delighting the deities. It is the essence, the deliverer from saṃsāra, that which carries one across committed sins, the deliverer from Time, joined with Tāra (Om). He whose body is flooded by it does not die and is freed from hunger and thirst.
m.5.27.38: O daughter of the mountain, this earth is indeed sustained by these four kinds of yogins; through their constancy, how could there be an end to the whole world, which exists for the attainment of happiness? In a dream the embodied one always creates everything, regarding as real even what is sorrow; so too in heaven; and from the earth, or from that, something of the four comes forth.
m.5.27.39: Therefore the earth, joined with yoga, is protected in due order by men endowed with prudence and modesty, knowers of dharma, through mantras, austerities, and herbs together with vows and observances. The primal God of beings, united with the four, does not waver. Therefore I shall now set forth the method handed down, concerning the shadow, which is called Śiva's.
m.5.27.iti: Thus ends the twenty-seventh adhyāya, named The description of cheating Time and attaining Śiva, in the fifth saṃhitā, the Umā-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.5.28.1: The Goddess said: O God of gods, Mahādeva, you have told me the cheating of death, the nature of Śabdabrahman, and the excellent marks of yoga.
m.5.28.2: You have told in brief the excellent knowledge concerning the shadow; explain it in detail, out of desire for the welfare of yogins.
m.5.28.3: Śaṅkara said: Listen, O Devī, I shall describe the marks of the shadow-person, knowing which properly a man is freed from all sins.
m.5.28.4: Placing the sun, or the moon, behind oneself, O fair-complexioned one, wearing white garments, garlanded, perfumed with scents, incense and the like,
m.5.28.5: one should call to mind my great mantra, which grants the fruit of all desires, nine-fold and condensed into a seed (piṇḍa), and should gaze intently at one's own shadow.
m.5.28.6: Having seen it again in the sky, white in form, he, single-minded, sees Śiva, the supreme cause.
m.5.28.7: He attains Brahman — so it is declared by the knowers of time; he is freed from sins such as the killing of a brahmin; there is no doubt in this.
m.5.28.8: When he sees it headless, death will come within six months; for that yogin all this that has been said holds exactly so.
m.5.28.9: If the shadow is white, one should know it signifies dharma; if black, one should declare sin; if red, one should know bondage; if yellow, one should foretell enmity.
m.5.28.10: If it appears without a nose, there will be destruction of kinsmen; if with two mouths, fear of hunger; if without hips, the wife perishes; if without shanks, wealth indeed is lost.
m.5.28.11: If the feet are absent, there will be going to a foreign land. This has been told by me; it should be carefully examined by a man, O Maheśvarī.
m.5.28.12: Having properly seen that figure and settling it by oneself within oneself, one should repeat the nine-fold mantra, my heart mantra, O Maheśvarī.
m.5.28.13: When a year has passed, there is nothing the mantra-practitioner cannot accomplish; he attains the eight qualities beginning with aṇimā and the power of moving through the sky.
m.5.28.14: Again I shall tell something else: how to know the Śakti, hard to approach, who is seen directly in the world, standing before the wise.
m.5.28.15: She who is unknowable, who in the world is depicted as Kuṇḍalī coiled like a serpent — that mātrā, though dwelling in the vehicle of the body, is seen, yet is not recited.
m.5.28.16: She who abides at the crown of the cosmic egg, who is ever praised by the Vedas, the mother of all knowledges, is celebrated as the Secret Knowledge.
m.5.28.17: She is declared to be Khecarā, abiding in all living beings, visible and invisible, immovable, eternal, manifest and unmanifest, everlasting.
m.5.28.18: Without letters yet joined with letters, she is called Bindumālinī; the yogin who always beholds her becomes one who has accomplished all that is to be done.
m.5.28.19: Whatever fruit of charity would arise from bathing at all tīrthas, and whatever fruit of all sacrifices there is — that, then, from the sight of Mālinī,
m.5.28.20: he obtains here; there is no doubt — this has truly been told by me. Whatever fruit comes from bathing at all tīrthas and giving gifts in every way,
m.5.28.21: and whatever fruit there is of all sacrifices, O Devī — that fruit a man would obtain. Why say more, O Maheśānī? He attains all desires.
m.5.28.22: Therefore the wise one should constantly practise this knowledge in accordance with yoga. From practice arises accomplishment; through practice yoga grows.
m.5.28.23: Through practice understanding is gained; through practice one attains liberation. Practice, the cause of liberation, should be constantly undertaken by the intelligent.
m.5.28.24: Thus this has been told, O Devī, granting the fruits of enjoyment and liberation. What other truth is asked? Speak; I tell you the truth.
m.5.28.25: Sūta said: Having heard thus the words of Brahmā's son, which bestow the highest goal, Vyāsa, the son of Parāśara, became extremely pleased, O lords of sages.
m.5.28.26: Vyāsa, supremely satisfied, bowed again and again to Sanatkumāra, the all-knowing son of Brahmā, treasure of compassion.
m.5.28.27: Then Vyāsa, that lord of sages, son of Kālī, praised him, Sanatkumāra, the ocean of divine knowledge, O sages.
m.5.28.28: Vyāsa said: I am fulfilled, O best of sages; Brahmanhood has been bestowed on me by you. Salutation to you, salutation to you. You are blessed, the foremost knower of Brahman!
m.5.28.29: Sūta said: Having thus praised the great sage, Brahmā's son, Vyāsa the son of Kālī fell silent, well pleased and filled with supreme bliss.
m.5.28.30: Brahmā's son, honoured by him, took leave of him and went, well pleased, to his own abode, O Śaunaka; Vyāsa too was delighted at heart.
m.5.28.31: Thus, O brahmins, I have described to you the dialogue of Sanatkumāra and the son of Kālī, which gives happiness, is joined with the highest truth, and increases knowledge.
m.5.28.iti: Thus ends the twenty-eighth adhyāya, named The description of seeing the shadow-person, in the fifth saṃhitā, the Umā-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.5.29.1: Śaunaka said: I have heard the great narrative you recounted, the dialogue between Sanatkumāra and Kāleya Vyāsa, which bestows the highest truth.
m.5.29.2: Therefore I wish to hear how Brahmā's creation came about. Tell me, just as you heard it from Vyāsa.
m.5.29.3: Sūta said: O sage, listen to the divine story, destroyer of all sins, which I am narrating: wondrous, rich in meaning, and expansive as it has been heard in tradition.
m.5.29.4: Whoever has it recited, or hears it repeatedly, sustains his own lineage and is honoured in the heavenly world.
m.5.29.5: That which is Pradhāna and Puruṣa, eternal, whose nature is both being and non-being — having become Pradhāna-Puruṣa, the fashioner of the worlds created all.
m.5.29.6: Know him, O best of sages, to be Brahmā of immeasurable power, the creator of all beings, devoted wholly to Nārāyaṇa.
m.5.29.7: Since he devised them, from whom all the pure kalpas come into being, O tiger among sages — salutation to that Self-born one.
m.5.29.8: Having bowed to that Hiraṇyagarbha, the Puruṣa and Lord, I shall again relate the unsurpassed creation.
m.5.29.9: Brahmā is the creator, Hari the protector, and Maheśvara the destroyer; for that creation there is no other agent, as it proceeds thus age after age.
m.5.29.10: That Self-born Lord, wishing to create various beings, first created the waters alone, and released his seed into them.
m.5.29.11: The waters are called nārā, for the waters are the offspring of Nara. Since they were formerly his abode (ayana), he is therefore known as Nārāyaṇa.
m.5.29.12: That egg lying in the water became golden in colour; in it Brahmā himself was born, renowned as Svayambhū.
m.5.29.13: Lord Hiraṇyagarbha, having dwelt there for a year, split the egg in two and fashioned heaven and earth.
m.5.29.14: The fourteen worlds were arranged below and above; between those two halves the Lord created the sky (ākāśa).
m.5.29.15: He set the earth floating on the waters and established the ten directions. At that time he created mind, speech, desire and anger, and also delight.
m.5.29.16: That greatly radiant one created the seven mind-born sons: Marīci, Atri and Aṅgiras, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu and Vasiṣṭha.
m.5.29.17: These are determined in the Purāṇa to be the seven Brahmās. Then Brahmā again created the Rudras, born of anger,
m.5.29.18: and the sage Sanatkumāra, the eldest of all. These seven are born first, and afterwards the Rudras on all sides.
m.5.29.19: Hence Sanatkumāra remains with his radiance withdrawn. Of those seven, seven great divine lineages, honoured by the divine sages,
m.5.29.20: come forth, active in rites and adorned with great sages. He created lightnings, thunderbolts and clouds, and red rainbows (Indra's bows),
m.5.29.21: and in the beginning he created the waters, and he created Parjanya the rain-god. For the accomplishment of sacrifice he fashioned the Ṛk verses, the Yajus formulas and the Sāman chants.
m.5.29.22: With these they worshipped the venerable gods — so we have heard. From his mouth he produced the gods, and from his chest the Pitṛs; from his organ of generation he made humans, and from his loins he fashioned the Asuras.
m.5.29.23: Beings high and low were born from the limbs of that Prajāpati Āpava as he brought forth the creation of beings.
m.5.29.24: When the beings being created did not multiply, then, dividing his own body in two, he became woman and man.
m.5.29.25: Then he created all beings, pervading everything by his greatness. Viṣṇu created Virāj; that Virāj, once created, brought forth the Puruṣa.
m.5.29.26: Know him to be the second Manu, and the beginning of the Manu-period as well. That Vairāja Puruṣa, the lord, created all beings.
m.5.29.27: These are the progeny of that emanation of Nārāyaṇa, he too being not born of a womb. From that knowledge one becomes long-lived, famous, fortunate and rich in offspring.
m.5.29.28: Thus the primal creation has been described to you, O best of sages. Knowing the primal creation in this way, one would attain whatever destiny one desires.
m.5.29.iti: Thus ends the twenty-ninth adhyāya, named The description of the first creation, in the fifth saṃhitā, the Umā-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.5.30.1: Sūta said: When the creatures had been created, then the Prajāpati Āpava, the Puruṣa, obtained as his wife Śatarūpā, who was not born from a womb.
m.5.30.2: Through the greatness of Āpava, who stood pervading heaven, and through dharma alone, that great-souled Śatarūpā too was born.
m.5.30.3: She, having practised for a hundred years austerity most difficult to perform, obtained as husband the Puruṣa of blazing austerity.
m.5.30.4: That Puruṣa was born as Svāyambhuva and is called Manu; his Manvantara is said here to be of seventy-one yugas.
m.5.30.5: From the Vairāja Puruṣa the heroic Śatarūpā bore offspring; Priyavrata and Uttānapāda were born of Vīrakā Śatarūpā.
m.5.30.6: The highly fortunate one named Kāmyā was the daughter of Prajāpati Kardama; Kāmyā had three sons: Saṃrāṭ, Sākṣi and Raviṭ, each mighty.
m.5.30.7: The lord Uttānapāda begot sons equal to Śakra, and the divine son Dhruva, radiant with the bliss of the Self.
m.5.30.8: The daughter of Dharma, fair-hipped, renowned by the name Sunīti, born of Dharma, was the mother of Dhruva.
m.5.30.9: Dhruva, though a boy, performed austerity in the forest for three thousand divine years, praying for an imperishable abode.
m.5.30.10: Pleased, the lord Brahmā, the Prajāpati, gave him an abode equal to his own, immovable, in front of the seven sages.
m.5.30.11: From that Dhruva two sons were born, Puṣṭi and Dhānya. Puṣṭi likewise begot from Samutthā five sinless sons:
m.5.30.12: Ripu, Ripuñjaya, Vipra, Vṛkala and Vṛṣatejas. And thus Ripu's queen bore Cākṣuṣa, renowned in all directions.
m.5.30.13: Cākṣuṣa Manu begot Varuṇa in Puṣkariṇī. From Manu, in Naḍvalā, ten sons of great vigour were born,
m.5.30.14: in the daughter of Prajāpati Vairāja, O best of sages: Puru, Māsa, Śatadyumna, Tapasvin, Satyavit, Kavi,
m.5.30.15: Agniṣṭoma, Atirātra, Atimanyu and Suyaśas — these ten. Āgneyī bore to Pūru six sons of great splendour:
m.5.30.16: Aṅga, Sumanas, Khyāti, Sṛti, Aṅgiras and Gaya. Sunīthā, the wife of Aṅga, bore from Aṅga a single son, Vena.
m.5.30.17: Because of Vena's misconduct, great wrath arose in them; the sages devoted to dharma slew him with a mere hum.
m.5.30.18: Then, entreated by Sunīthā for the sake of progeny, the Sārasvata sages churned his right hand.
m.5.30.19: When Vena's hand was churned, Pṛthu came forth from it; he was born with bow and armour, resembling the sun in splendour.
m.5.30.20: He was indeed an incarnation of Viṣṇu, for the protection of the people, for the safeguarding of dharma, and for the punishment of the wicked.
m.5.30.21: Then Pṛthu, son of Vena, the forefather of the kṣatriyas, protected the earth; that lord of the earth was the first of those consecrated by the Rājasūya.
m.5.30.22: From him too arose the skilful Sūta and Māgadha. By him, O best of sages, this earth-cow was milked for the welfare of all.
m.5.30.23: The king, performer of a hundred sacrifices, became the giver of livelihood to all — gods, sages, suras and rākṣasas — and especially to humans.
m.5.30.24: To Pṛthu were born two sons, kings on earth who knew dharma: Vijitāśva and Haryakṣa, great heroes, well renowned.
m.5.30.25: Śikhaṇḍinī bore a son, Prācīnabarhis; his kuśa grass, with tips pointing east, spread over the surface of the earth.
m.5.30.26: The daughter of the Ocean was duly married by him according to dharma; having taken a wife, the king, a great lord, shone all the more.
m.5.30.27: From the daughter of the Ocean, ten divine sons were born to Prācīnabarhis, the performer of many sacrifices.
m.5.30.28: All of them, called the Prācetasas, masters of the science of archery, following one common dharma, performed great austerity,
m.5.30.29: for ten thousand years, lying in the waters of the ocean, chanting the Rudra-song and intent on meditation upon Śiva.
m.5.30.30: While they were practising austerity, trees grew over the earth; and the earth being unprotected, destruction of the people ensued.
m.5.30.31: Having returned from austerity with excellent boons obtained, they saw those trees, O tiger among sages, and grew angry, wishing to burn them, mighty through austerity.
m.5.30.32: Those Prācetasas emitted fire and wind from their mouths; the wind uprooted the trees and the fire burned them.
m.5.30.33: Then, seeing the destruction of the trees, when only a few trees remained, the powerful King Soma approached them and said:
m.5.30.34: Soma said: Restrain your anger, O kings, all you sons of Prācīnabarhis. This fair-complexioned maiden has come into being as the daughter of the trees.
m.5.30.35: Knowing the future, I have nurtured her from the embryo. Let her be your wife, O highly fortunate ones, she who will increase the lunar race.
m.5.30.36: In her will be born the learned Prajāpati named Dakṣa, the maker of creation, of great splendour, the ancient son of Brahmā.
m.5.30.37: With half of your splendour and with this splendour of mine, that king, full of Brahmā's splendour, will increase the creatures.
m.5.30.38: Then, at Soma's word, the Pracetases lovingly took as wife, according to dharma, that fair-complexioned maiden born of the trees.
m.5.30.39: From them, in her, the Prajāpati named Dakṣa was born; and he, of great splendour, was born with a portion of Soma, O sage.
m.5.30.40: Having created by mind the immobile and mobile beings, the two-footed and the four-footed, Dakṣa began creation through sexual union.
m.5.30.41: He married, with proper rites and in accordance with right dharma, the daughter of Prajāpati Vīraṇa, Vīraṇī by name, a woman devoted to her husband.
m.5.30.42: In her he begot ten thousand virtuous sons, the Haryaśvas; and they became detached from worldly life through the instruction of Nārada.
m.5.30.43: Hearing that, Dakṣa again begot in her sons named the Subalāśvas, numbering a thousand.
m.5.30.44: They too, through that sage's instruction, went the way of their brothers; detached and following the path of mendicants, they did not return to their father's presence.
m.5.30.45: Hearing that, enraged, he gave the sage an unbearable curse: O lover of strife, may you find no stable abode anywhere.
m.5.30.46: Then, pacified by the Creator (Brahmā), he afterwards created daughters, of the nature of great radiance and endowed with virtues, O lord of sages.
m.5.30.47: He gave ten to Dharma, thirteen to Kaśyapa, two likewise to the son of Brahmā, and two then to Aṅgiras.
m.5.30.48: Two he gave to the learned sage Kṛśāśva, O best of sages; and the remaining ones, called the Nakṣatras, lord Dakṣa gave to Soma.
m.5.30.49: From those daughters of Dakṣa were born the gods, the asuras and others—many renowned sons; by all of them the world was filled.
m.5.30.50: From then on, O chief of brahmins, creatures have been born of sexual union; the creation of earlier beings is said to have been through will, sight and touch.
m.5.30.51: Śaunaka said: Dakṣa was born from Brahmā's thumb, as you told earlier. How then did that great ascetic again obtain the status of being son of the Pracetases?
m.5.30.52: O Sūta, you should resolve this doubt of mine. This is a wonder: how did he become Soma's father-in-law?
m.5.30.53: Sūta said: Origin and dissolution always take place among beings; in every kalpa all these—Dakṣa and the others—come into being anew, O sage.
m.5.30.54: Whoever knows this creation of Dakṣa, with all its moving and unmoving beings, is blessed with offspring, full of life-span, and is honoured in the heavenly world.
m.5.30.iti: Thus ends the thirtieth adhyāya, named The description of creation, in the fifth saṃhitā, the Umā-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.5.31.1: Śaunaka said: O son of Sūta, quickly tell me in detail this creation of the gods and the Dānavas, and of the Gandharvas, serpents and Rākṣasas.
m.5.31.2: Sūta said: When that creation did not increase, the Prajāpati summoned the daughter of Vīraṇa, endowed with excellent austerity, for the purpose of creation.
m.5.31.3: He created various beings by the law of sexual union. Hear of them, O very wise one; I shall tell you briefly.
m.5.31.4: Uniting with that Vīriṇī, the mighty Prajāpati Dakṣa himself begot five thousand sons.
m.5.31.5: Seeing these sons who had been created, the sage Nārada spoke to them — that Nārada who was born at the sacrificial session of Parameṣṭhin (Brahmā).
m.5.31.6: Or rather, having heard from Kaśyapa that the creation of beings would take place in the daughters of Dakṣa alone, he therefore spoke to them.
m.5.31.7: Not knowing the world, how will you, foolish ones, carry out creation, ignorant as you are of any direction? Therefore, first learn the extent of that earth.
m.5.31.8: Thus addressed, they all set out vigourously to learn the regions; and not reaching their end, they did not return to their father's house.
m.5.31.9: Knowing that, he again begot five hundred sons; and to them too the all-seeing Nārada spoke once more.
m.5.31.10: Nārada said: Not knowing the measure of the earth, how will you carry out creation? You are all fools indeed; why are you eager to perform creation?
m.5.31.11: Sūta said: They too, the Subalāśvas, sons of Dakṣa, hearing his words, went forth in every direction, just as the Haryaśvas had done before.
m.5.31.12: Reaching the endless expanse (puṣkara), they too met their ruin; even today they do not return, like rivers that do not return from the oceans.
m.5.31.13: From that time on, O sage, a brother who sets out intent on searching for a brother perishes; therefore a wise man should not do so.
m.5.31.14: Learning that these sons too were lost, Prajāpati Dakṣa in anger pronounced a curse upon the great-souled Nārada:
m.5.31.15: O lover of strife, may you not find a settled abode anywhere; and wherever you are present in the world, may there always be strife.
m.5.31.16: Then, pacified by the Creator (Brahmā), Prajāpati Dakṣa afterwards created sixty daughters in Vīriṇī — so we have heard.
m.5.31.17: He gave ten to Dharma, thirteen to Kaśyapa, twenty-seven to Soma, and four to Ariṣṭanemi.
m.5.31.18: Likewise two to the son of Brahmā, two to Aṅgiras, and two to the learned Kṛśāśva. Hear from me their names.
m.5.31.19: Arundhatī, Vasu, Yāmi, Lambā, Bhānu, Marutvatī, Saṅkalpā, Muhūrtā, Sandhyā and Viśvā, O sage —
m.5.31.20: these, O sage, are the wives of Dharma. Hear from me their offspring: the Viśvedevas were born of Viśvā, and Sādhyā gave birth to the Sādhyas.
m.5.31.21: From Marutvatī were born the Marutvats, from Vasu the Vasus, from Bhānu all the Bhānus, and from Muhūrtā the Muhūrtas.
m.5.31.22: From Lambā was born Ghoṣa; Nāgavīthī was born of Yāmi; and from Arundhatī was born Pṛthivīviṣama (the earthly realm).
m.5.31.23: From Saṅkalpā was born Saṅkalpa, whose nature is truth. The sons of Vasu are eight, Aya and the rest; hear of them, O Śaunaka.
m.5.31.24: Aya, Dhruva, Soma, Dhara, Anila, Anala, Pratyūṣa and Prabhāsa — these by name are the eight Vasus.
m.5.31.25: The sons of Aya were Vaitaṇḍa, Śrama, Śānta and Muni. The son of Dhruva was the blessed Kāla, who sustains the worlds.
m.5.31.26: The son of Soma was the blessed Varcas, through whom one becomes radiant. The son of Dhara was Draviṇa, and likewise Hutahavyavaha.
m.5.31.27: From Manoharā were born Śiśira, Prāṇa and Ramaṇa. The wife of Anila was Śivā, whose sons were Purojava
m.5.31.28: and Avijñātagati — these two were the sons of Anila. The son of Agni was Kumāra, born in a clump of reeds enveloped in splendour.
m.5.31.29: After him were born Śākha, Viśākha and Naigameya. Being the offspring of the Kṛttikās, he is known as Kārttikeya.
m.5.31.30: To Pratyūṣa was born a son, a seer named Devala. Devala too had two wise sons, who had progeny.
m.5.31.31: The sister of Bṛhaspati, an excellent woman devoted to celibacy and perfected in yoga, then roamed all over the entire world.
m.5.31.32: She became the wife of Prabhāsa, the eighth of the Vasus; and from him, O highly fortunate one, was born Prajāpati Viśvakarman,
m.5.31.33: the maker of thousands of crafts, the carpenter of the gods, the maker of all ornaments, the foremost of craftsmen,
m.5.31.34: who made the aerial chariots of all the deities, and by whose craft, that great-souled one's, human beings make their living.
m.5.31.35: Raivata, Aja, Bhava, Bhīma, Vāma, Ugra, Vṛṣākapi, Ajaikapād, Ahirbudhnya, Bahurūpa and Mahān —
m.5.31.36: Rudras were born by the crore of the woman Sarūpā; among them eleven are chief. Hear their names, O sage.
m.5.31.37: Ajaikapād, Ahirbudhnya, Tvaṣṭṛ, the mighty Rudra, Hara, Bahurūpa, Tryambaka, Aparājita,
m.5.31.38: Vṛṣākapi, Śambhu, Kapardin and Raivata — these are declared the eleven Rudras, lords of the three worlds.
m.5.31.39: Thus a hundred Rudras of immeasurable might have been described. Now hear the names of Kaśyapa's wives, O best of sages.
m.5.31.iti: Thus ends the thirty-first adhyāya, named The description of creation, in the fifth saṃhitā, the Umā-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.5.32.1: Sūta said: Aditi, Diti, Surasā, Ariṣṭā, Ilā and Danu; Surabhi, Vinatā, Tāmrā, Krodhavaśā and Khaśā,
m.5.32.2: and Kadrū and Muni, O best of brahmins — hear from me the offspring born of them. In the excellent former manvantara there were twelve foremost gods,
m.5.32.3: named the Tuṣitas. They spoke to one another, when the Vaivasvata period was approaching, in the period of the illustrious Manu Cākṣuṣa:
m.5.32.4: For the welfare of all the worlds, having gathered together, come quickly, O gods, and having entered into Aditi,
m.5.32.5: let us be born in the coming manvantara; there will be good for the virtuous. Thus addressed, all of them, in the period of Manu Cākṣuṣa,
m.5.32.6: were born of Kaśyapa, son of Marīci, in Aditi, the daughter of Dakṣa. There Viṣṇu and Śakra were born once again.
m.5.32.7: And Aryaman, Dhātṛ, Tvaṣṭṛ and Pūṣan likewise, Vivasvat, Savitṛ, and Mitra and Varuṇa,
m.5.32.8: Aṃśa and Bhaga of surpassing splendour — these are remembered as the twelve Ādityas. Those who were formerly the Tuṣita gods in the period of Cākṣuṣa,
m.5.32.9: they, long ago in that period, are remembered as the twelve Ādityas. Thus the offspring of Aditi have been told in order, O Śaunaka.
m.5.32.10: The twenty-seven of good vows who were declared to be the wives of Soma — of them were born offspring, radiant ones of immeasurable splendour.
m.5.32.11: Of the wives of Ariṣṭanemi there were here sixteen offspring. Of the learned Bahuputra, four Lightnings are remembered as offspring.
m.5.32.12: Of Kṛśāśva, O divine sage, the divine weapons are remembered as offspring; and likewise, O sage, Dhūmrakeśa was born in his wife Arcis.
m.5.32.13: Svadhā and Satī were two wives: Svadhā the elder, Satī the younger. Svadhā bore the Pitṛs; Satī bore the Atharvāṅgirasa Veda.
m.5.32.14: These are born again at the end of a thousand yugas; and all the hosts of gods, the thirty-three, are born at will.
m.5.32.15: Just as the sun constantly rises and sets here, so those hosts of gods come into being age after age.
m.5.32.16: In Diti two sons were born of Kaśyapa — so we have heard: Hiraṇyakaśipu and the mighty Hiraṇyākṣa.
m.5.32.17: A daughter, Siṃhikā, was born, who became the wife of Vipracitti. Hiraṇyakaśipu had four sons of renowned vigour:
m.5.32.18: Anuhrāda, Hrāda and the mighty Saṃhrāda, and the youngest among them, Prahrāda, whose mind was set on contemplating devotion to Viṣṇu.
m.5.32.19: Of Anuhrāda, in Sūryā, were born Pulomā and Mahiṣa; Hrāda's wife Dhamani bore Vātāpi and Ilvala.
m.5.32.20: Saṃhrāda's wife Kṛti then bore Pañcajana. Virocana was the son of Prahrāda; of him, in Devī, Bali was born.
m.5.32.21: Bali had a hundred sons in Aśanā, O lord of sages. Bali was a great Śaiva, wholly devoted to devotion to Śiva,
m.5.32.22: generous by nature and noble, remembered as one whose fame and austerity were holy. His son named Bāṇa was also an eminent, wise Śaiva, who, having fully pleased Śiva, obtained the leadership of the Gaṇas.
m.5.32.23: That story of the great-souled Bāṇa you have heard before — the hero who in battle made Kṛṣṇa well pleased.
m.5.32.24: The sons of Hiraṇyākṣa were five, learned and exceedingly mighty: Kukura, Śakuni, and Bhūtasantāpana,
m.5.32.25: the valiant Mahānāda, and likewise Kālanābha. Thus the sons of Diti have been told; now hear, O sage, of the sons of Danu.
m.5.32.26: The sons of Danu were a hundred, of fierce valour: Ayomukha, Śambara, Kapola and Vāmana,
m.5.32.27: Vaiśvānara and Pulomā, Vidrāvaṇa and Mahāśiras, Svarbhānu, Vṛṣaparvan and the mighty Vipracitti.
m.5.32.28: All these sons of Danu were born of Kaśyapa. Hear of their daughters, O sage; I tell you incidentally, O sinless one.
m.5.32.29: Of Svarbhānu the daughter was Prabhā; of Pulomā the daughter was Śacī; Upadānavī, Hayaśirā and Śarmiṣṭhā were the daughters of Vṛṣaparvan.
m.5.32.30: Pulomikā and Pulomā, both daughters of Vaiśvānara, of many offspring and great might, became the wives of Mārīci (Kaśyapa).
m.5.32.31: In those two, Marīci('s son) begot sixty thousand sons, delights of the Dānavas, endowed with great austerity.
m.5.32.32: The Paulomas and Kālakhañjas, the mightiest of the Dānavas, dwellers in Hiraṇyapura, who could not be slain by the gods,
m.5.32.33: invulnerable by the grace of the Grandfather, were slain by Savyasācin (Arjuna). Then, born in Siṃhikā, were likewise the sons of Vipracitti,
m.5.32.34: born of the union of Daitya and Dānava, of fierce valour — thirteen very mighty ones, known as the Saiṃhikeyas:
m.5.32.35: Rāhu, Śalya — very powerful ones — and Bala of great strength, Vātāpi, Namuci, then Ilvala, and Svasṛpa,
m.5.32.36: Ajika, Naraka, and likewise Kālanābha, Śaramāṇa, Śara and Kalpa — these were the increasers of the lineage.
m.5.32.37: Their sons and grandsons, who increased the lineage of Danu, arose in great numbers; because of their extent they are not described.
m.5.32.38: In the family of Saṃhrāda were born the Daitya Nivātakavacas; in it also arose the Maruts, whose selves were refined by austerity.
m.5.32.39: The six principal ones, of great strength, are proclaimed as daughters of Tāmrā: Kākī, Śyenī, Bhāsī, Sugrīvī, and likewise Śukī,
m.5.32.40: Gṛdhrikā, Aśvī and Ulūkī — these are proclaimed as the daughters of Tāmrā. Kākī gave birth to crows, Ulūkī to owls.
m.5.32.41: Śyenī bore hawks, Bhāsī bore bhāsa-birds, Gṛdhrī bore vultures, Śukī bore parrots, and Sugrīvī bore auspicious birds.
m.5.32.42: Tāmrā, the beloved of Kaśyapa, also gave birth to horses, camels and donkeys. Thus the lineage of Tāmrā has been declared.
m.5.32.43: Vinatā had two sons, Aruṇa and Garuḍa; Suparṇa Garuḍa was the best of flying creatures, fearsome by his own deeds.
m.5.32.44: Of Surasā were born a thousand serpents of immeasurable might, many-headed, moving through the sky, great-souled.
m.5.32.45: Their chief kings were Śeṣa, Vāsuki and Takṣaka, Airāvata, Mahāpadma, and both Kambala and Aśvatara,
m.5.32.46: Elāpatra and Padma, Karkoṭaka and Dhanañjaya, Mahānīla and Mahākarṇa, Dhṛtarāṣṭra and Balāhaka,
m.5.32.47: Kuhara and Puṣpadanta, Durmukha and Sumukha, Bahuśa and Khararoman, and Pāṇi — these and others.
m.5.32.48: Then come the hosts of Krodhavaśā, and all of her offspring are fanged creatures; egg-born birds and water-born creatures are also counted, and the beasts are held to be of Varāhī.
m.5.32.49: Of Anāyuṣā fifty sons of great strength were born: Bala and Vṛkṣa, then Vikṣara, and likewise Bṛhan.
m.5.32.50: Surabhi gave birth to hares and likewise buffaloes; Ilā gave birth to trees, creepers, vines and all species of grasses.
m.5.32.51: Khaśā bore the Yakṣas and Rākṣasas, and Muni likewise the Apsarases; Ariṣṭā gave birth to serpents, and Prabhā indeed to the best of men.
m.5.32.52: These descendants of Kaśyapa have been described to you, O lord of sages, whose sons and grandsons number in the hundreds and thousands.
m.5.32.iti: Thus ends the thirty-second adhyāya, named The description of the lineage of Kaśyapa, in the fifth saṃhitā, the Umā-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.5.33.1: Sūta said: This, dear one, is known as the creation in the Svārociṣa Manvantara. But in the Vaivasvata Manvantara, at the great, extended sacrifice of Varuṇa,
m.5.33.2: the creation of beings by Brahmā as he offered oblations is told here. Those seven mind-born brahmarṣis who had been born earlier,
m.5.33.3: the Grandfather himself made them his sons. Among them arose the conflict of the gods and the Dānavas, O great sage.
m.5.33.4: Diti, whose sons had been destroyed, approached Kaśyapa. That Kaśyapa, pleased at heart, having been duly propitiated by her,
m.5.33.5: offered her a boon; and she then chose a boon: a son capable of slaying Indra, of immeasurable might.
m.5.33.6: And he, of very great austerity, granted her the boon she asked, and also prescribed the observance of celibacy and other rules for a hundred years.
m.5.33.7: That pure, fair-complexioned lady carried the embryo; Diti likewise kept the rule of celibacy and the rest.
m.5.33.8: Then, having placed that embryo in Diti, Kaśyapa of praiseworthy vows went off to perform austerity, delighted in mind.
m.5.33.9: And Pākaśāsana (Indra) became eager to find a lapse in her; when the hundred years were short by one, he saw just such a lapse in her.
m.5.33.10: Without washing her feet, Diti then lay down to sleep with her head turned downward, owing to the weight of what was destined to happen.
m.5.33.11: At that moment Śakra, the thunderbolt-wielder, entering her womb, cut that embryo into seven parts.
m.5.33.12: That embryo, being split by the thunderbolt, then cried loudly. Saying, do not weep, the thunderbolt-wielder again cut each of the seven that were weeping; yet even so they did not die.
m.5.33.13: Being cut, all of them, with joined palms, said to him, O sage: Why do you wish to kill us, Śakra? We are your brothers, the Maruts.
m.5.33.14: All of them were accepted by Indra into brotherhood, and they abandoned their Daitya nature, O brahmin-seer, by the will of Śaṅkara.
m.5.33.15: Those gods, named the Maruts, became very mighty—forty-nine sky-rovers, companions of the thunderbolt-wielder.
m.5.33.16: To those beings, once they had multiplied, Hari, the Prajāpati, gave kingdoms in due order, beginning with Pṛthu; hear about that.
m.5.33.17: He is Ariṣṭa, the Puruṣa, the hero, Kṛṣṇa, Jiṣṇu, Prajāpati, Parjanya and the lord of wealth; this whole world is his.
m.5.33.18: I have properly told you this creation of beings, O great sage. Hear the division of the kingdoms; I shall now tell it to you in order.
m.5.33.19: Having consecrated Pṛthu, son of Vena, to supreme sovereignty, the Grandfather then began to assign the kingdoms in order.
m.5.33.20: He consecrated Soma to the rule of the twice-born, the plants, the stars and planets, the sacrifices and the austerities.
m.5.33.21: He installed Varuṇa in the rule of the waters, the lord Vaiśravaṇa over kings, Viṣṇu likewise over the Ādityas, and Pāvaka over the Vasus.
m.5.33.22: Dakṣa over the Prajāpatis, Vāsava over the Maruts, and Prahlāda of immeasurable might over the Daityas and Dānavas.
m.5.33.23: He consecrated Yama Vaivasvata to the rule of the ancestors. Over the Mothers, the vows, the mantras, and likewise the cows,
m.5.33.24: over the Yakṣas, the Rākṣasas and likewise the kings, and over all beings and Piśācas, he installed Giriśa, the trident-holder.
m.5.33.25: Himavat over the mountains, the ocean over the rivers, the tiger over the wild beasts, and the bull over the cattle.
m.5.33.26: He consecrated the banyan to the rule of the forest-lords and trees. Thus kingship everywhere was bestowed in order by the Lord of creatures.
m.5.33.27: In the eastern quarter the all-souled, pervading lord of the universe installed in kingship the son of Prajāpati Vairāja.
m.5.33.28: Likewise, O tiger among sages, in the southern quarter he appointed Sudhanvan, the son of Prajāpati Kardama.
m.5.33.29: In the western quarter likewise the lord appointed as king the great-souled, unfailing Ketumant, son of Rajas.
m.5.33.30: Likewise he consecrated as king in the northern quarter the invincible Hiraṇyaroman, son of Prajāpati Parjanya.
m.5.33.31: Its extent has been told, O Śaunaka, together with the account of Pṛthu, son of Vena; that foundation is proclaimed as the Purāṇa, for great prosperity.
m.5.33.iti: Thus ends the thirty-third adhyāya, named The description of the lineage of Kaśyapa, in the fifth saṃhitā, the Umā-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.5.34.1: Śaunaka said: Recount all the Manvantaras in detail. And however many Manus there are, I wish to hear about them.
m.5.34.2: Sūta said: Svāyambhuva Manu, then Svārociṣa, likewise Uttama, Tāmasa, Raivata and Cākṣuṣa.
m.5.34.3: These six Manus have been declared to you, O foremost of sages. Vaivasvata, O best of sages, is said to be the present Manu.
m.5.34.4: And Sāvarṇi Manu, then Raucya as the next, and likewise Brahmasāvarṇi: these are four Manus.
m.5.34.5: Likewise Dharmasāvarṇi and Rudrasāvarṇi; Devasāvarṇi is named, and also Indrasāvarṇi.
m.5.34.6: Those Manus who are past, present and likewise yet to come have all been recounted by me, just as I heard them.
m.5.34.7: O sage, these fourteen Manvantaras, spanning the three times, have been told to you. A kalpa is constituted as a cycle of a thousand yugas.
m.5.34.8: I shall tell you of their sages, their sons and likewise their groups of gods. Listen, Śaunaka, with great delight, to those illustrious ones in order.
m.5.34.9: Marīci, Atri, the revered Aṅgiras, Pulaha, Kratu, Pulastya and Vasiṣṭha: these seven are the sons of Brahmā.
m.5.34.10: They are likewise the Seven Sages in the northern quarter, O sage; and in the Svāyambhuva period the gods were those named Yāmas.
m.5.34.11: Āgnīdhra, Agnibāhu, Medhā, Medhātithi, Vasu, Jyotiṣmān, Dhṛtimān, Havya, Savana and Śubhra —
m.5.34.12: these are declared to be the ten sons of the great-souled Manu Svāyambhuva, O tiger among sages. In that period the Indra is said to be Yajña.
m.5.34.13: Thus, dear one, the first divine Manvantara has been told. I shall tell you the second; understand it exactly as it is.
m.5.34.14: Ūrjastambha, Parastambha, Ṛṣabha, Vasumān, Jyotiṣmān, Dyutimān, and Rociṣmān as the seventh —
m.5.34.15: these are to be known as the great sages; the Indra there was Rocana, and the gods in the Svārociṣa period are remembered as those named Tuṣitas.
m.5.34.16: Harighna, Sukṛti, Jyoti, Ayomūrti, Ayasmaya, Prathita, Manasyu, Nabha and likewise Sūrya —
m.5.34.17: these are declared, O tiger among sages, as the ten sons of the great-souled Manu Svārociṣa, of great vigour and valour.
m.5.34.18: This second Manvantara has been told by me, O sage. I shall tell you the third; understand it exactly as it is.
m.5.34.19: There were seven sons of Vasiṣṭha, famed as the Vāsiṣṭhas, sons of Hiraṇyagarbha, of great vigour, named the Ūrjas.
m.5.34.20: These are declared as the sages here. Now learn from me those being recounted: O best of sages, the ten sons of Manu Uttama are remembered as the Auttameyas:
m.5.34.21: Iṣa, Ūrjita, Ūrja, Madhu, Mādhava, Śuci, Śukravaha, Nabhasa and Nabha —
m.5.34.22: and Ṛṣabha. The gods there were Satya, Veda, Śruta and others; and the Indra there, lord of the three worlds, was named Satyajit, O sage.
m.5.34.23: This excellent third Manvantara has been related. I shall tell you the fourth Manvantara, O sage; listen.
m.5.34.24: Gārgya, Pṛthu, likewise Vāgmī, Jaya, Dhātā, Kapīnaka and Kapīvān are the seven sages; and the Satyas are the groups of gods.
m.5.34.25: The Indra there is to be known as Triśikha. Hear, O sage, of the sons of Manu: Dyūtipota, Sautapasya, Tapas, Śūla and Tāpana,
m.5.34.26: Taporati, Akalmāṣa, Dhanvī, Khaḍgī, and the great sage Mahān — these are remembered as the ten sons of Tāmasa, of great vows.
m.5.34.27: The fourth period, that of Manu Tāmasa, has been told to you by me. Now hear, dear one, the next, the fifth Manvantara.
m.5.34.28: Devabāhu, Jaya, the sage Vedaśiras, Hiraṇyaromā, Parjanya, Ūrdhvabāhu and Somapa,
m.5.34.29: and others such as Satyanetra and Rata — these are the other Seven Sages; and the gods were the Bhūtarajasas and likewise the Tapaḥprakṛtis.
m.5.34.30: The Indra there, lord of the three worlds, was named Vibhu; and the Manu there is to be known as the one called Raivata, the uterine brother of Tāmasa.
m.5.34.31: Arjuna, Paṅkti, Vindhya and others are the sons of Dayā, O sage; endowed with great austerity, they dwell on the ridge of Meru.
m.5.34.32: The son of the Prajāpati Ruci is remembered as the Manu named Raucya; and the son begotten by Ruci in the goddess Bhūti became the one named Bhautya.
m.5.34.33: These seven Manus are remembered as those yet to come in this kalpa; and likewise seven great sages in heaven are remembered as those yet to come.
m.5.34.34: Kaśyapa, Atri, Vasiṣṭha, Viśvāmitra, then Gautama, Jamadagni and Bharadvāja — these are remembered as the seven sages of the present period.
m.5.34.35: Rāma, Vyāsa, likewise Ātreya the radiant and very learned, Bharadvāja, and likewise Drauṇi Aśvatthāmā of great splendour,
m.5.34.36: and the son of Gautama, Kṛpa Gautama son of Śaradvān; Gālava the Kauśika, Ruru and Kaśyapa —
m.5.34.37: these seven great-souled ones will be the future best of sages. And there, three groups of future gods have been declared by Svayambhū.
m.5.34.38: They are the sons of the great-souled Kaśyapa, son of Marīci. Among them, Bali, the son of Virocana, will be Indra.
m.5.34.39: Viṣāṅga, Avanīvān, Sumanta, Dhṛtimān, Vasu, Sūri, Surākhya, Viṣṇu, and King Sumati —
m.5.34.40: these will be the ten sons of Manu Sāvarṇi, O Śaunaka. Here the eighth period has been told; now hear the ninth period.
m.5.34.41: First I shall describe the Manu Dakṣasāvarṇi; listen. Medhātithi of Pulastya's line, Vasu of Kaśyapa's line,
m.5.34.42: Jyotiṣmān of Bhṛgu's line, Dhṛtimān of Aṅgiras' line, Savana of Vasiṣṭha's line, and Havya of Atri's line,
m.5.34.43: and Pulaha — these are the seven sages in the Rauhita interval. There, O great sage, the groups of gods are three.
m.5.34.44: They are the sons of Rohita the Prajāpati, the son of Dakṣa. Dhṛṣṭaketu, Dīptaketu, Pañcahasta, Nirākṛti,
m.5.34.45: Pṛthuśravas, Bhūridyumna, Ṛcīka, Bṛhata and Gaya — these are the nine mighty sons of the first Sāvarṇi.
m.5.34.46: Then in the tenth cycle, in the interval of the second Sāvarṇa Manu: Haviṣmān of Pulaha's line, and Prakṛti of Bhṛgu's line,
m.5.34.47: Āpomukti of Atri's line likewise, Avyaya of Vasiṣṭha's line is recorded, Prayati of Pulastya's line, and Bhāmāra of Kaśyapa's line,
m.5.34.48: and the truthful Anenas of Aṅgiras' line — these are the seven supreme sages. And the groups of gods are those known as the Dviṣimants.
m.5.34.49: Their Indra is said to be Śambhu, this very Maheśvara. Akṣatvān, Uttamaujas, and the valiant Bhūriṣeṇa,
m.5.34.50: Śatānīka, Nirāmitra, Vṛṣasena, Jayadratha, Bhūridyumna, Suvarcas and Arcis — these are the ten sons of the Manu.
m.5.34.51: In the eleventh cycle, in the interval of the third Sāvarṇa Manu, learn from me his seven sages too as they are named.
m.5.34.52: Haviṣmān of Kaśyapa's line, Vapuṣmān of Varuṇa's line, then the Ātreya and the Vasiṣṭha, and Anaya of Aṅgiras' line,
m.5.34.53: Cārudhṛṣya of Pulastya's line, and Niḥsvara, the fiery Agni — these seven are declared the sages; three groups of gods are recorded.
m.5.34.54: They are the sons of Brahmā; these are known as the Vaidhṛtas. Sarvaga, Suśarman, Devānīka, Kṣemaka,
m.5.34.55: Dṛḍheṣu, Khaṇḍaka, Darśa, Kuhu and Bāhu are recorded as sons of the Manu; these nine are known as the sons of the third Sāvarṇa.
m.5.34.56: Learn from me the seven sages of the fourth Sāvarṇi: Dyuti the son of Vasiṣṭha, and Sutapas of Atri's line,
m.5.34.57: Tapomūrti of Aṅgiras' line, Tapasvin of Kaśyapa's line likewise, Tapodhana of Pulastya's line, and Taporati of Pulaha's line;
m.5.34.58: the seventh of them should be known as Taponidhi of Bhṛgu's line. Five groups of gods are declared, the mind-born sons of Brahmā.
m.5.34.59: Ṛtadhāman is their Indra, happily ruling the three worlds. And in the twelfth cycle, in the future interval of Raucya, O sage,
m.5.34.60: Dhṛtimān of Aṅgiras' line, Havyavān who is of Pulastya's line, Tattvadarśin of Pulaha's line, Nirutsava of Bhṛgu's line,
m.5.34.61: Niṣprapañca of Atri's line likewise, Nirdeha of Kaśyapa's line, and Sutapas of Vasiṣṭha's line — these are the seven great sages.
m.5.34.62: Three groups of gods are declared by the Self-born; their Indra is Divaspati. Vicitra and Citra,
m.5.34.63: Naya, Dharma, Dhṛta, Andhra, Sunetra, Kṣatravṛddhaka, Nirbhaya, Sutapas and Droṇa — these are the sons of the Manu Raucya.
m.5.34.64: The thirteenth Manu to come will be the self-possessed Devasāvarṇi; Citrasena, Vicitra and others will be the sons born of Devasāvarṇi's body.
m.5.34.65: The gods will be those called Sukarmans and Sutrāmans, the Indra Divaspati; Nirmoka, Tattvadarśa and others will then be the seers.
m.5.34.66: In the fourteenth cycle, in the interval of the Manu Bhautya: Āgnīdhra of Kaśyapa's line, and Māgadha who is of Pulastya's line,
m.5.34.67: Ativāhya of Bhṛgu's line, Śuci of Aṅgiras' line likewise, Yukta of Atri's line, and Śukra of Vasiṣṭha's line,
m.5.34.68: and Ajita of Pulaha's line — these are the last seven sages. The gods will be the Pavitras and Cākṣuṣas, and Śuci will be Indra.
m.5.34.69: By people always rising at dawn and reciting the names of these great sages, past and future, happiness increases.
m.5.34.70: The groups of gods have been declared as five; hear, O great sage the sons: Turaṅgabhīru, Budhna, Tanugra and Anugra,
m.5.34.71: Atimānin, Pravīṇa, Viṣṇu, Saṅkrandana likewise, Tejasvin and Sabala — these are the sons of the Manu Bhautya.
m.5.34.72: When the reign of Bhauma is complete, the kalpa is completed. Thus have I described these Manus, future and past.
m.5.34.73: They were told by Sanatkumāra to Vyāsa of boundless splendour. At the close of a full thousand yugas, having ruled according to their own dharma,
m.5.34.74: they, together with their subjects and endowed with austerity, go to Brahmā's world. Seventy-one yugas, with something over, is called an interval (manvantara).
m.5.34.75: These fourteen Manus, increasers of fame, have been described. In all the manvantaras there is rebirth at the end of dissolution.
m.5.34.76: Their intervals cannot be told even in hundreds of years. When a full hundred thousand is complete, the kalpa is said to be ended.
m.5.34.77: Then all beings, burnt by the rays of the sun, placing Brahmā at their head, together with the hosts of Ādityas, O sage,
m.5.34.78: enter, O best of gods, Hari Nārāyaṇa the supreme, the creator of all beings, again and again at the ends of kalpas.
m.5.34.79: And further, the Lord Rudra is the destroyer, Time itself, at the end of the kalpa. I shall describe that concerning the Manu Vaivasvata.
m.5.34.80: Thus I have told you everything arising from the manvantaras — the secondary creation, a meritorious, auspicious narrative that increases one's lineage.
m.5.34.iti: Thus ends the thirty-fourth adhyāya, named The recounting of all the manvantaras, in the fifth saṃhitā, the Umā-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.5.35.1: Sūta said: Vivasvān was born from Kaśyapa, the great sage, in Dākṣāyaṇī. His wife was Saṃjñā, the goddess, daughter of Tvaṣṭṛ, also called Sureṇukā.
m.5.35.2: O sage, she, endowed with beauty and youth, was not pleased with her husband's form, with that fierce and unbearable brilliance.
m.5.35.3: Unable to bear that form of Āditya, so intensely brilliant, the fair-complexioned lady, being scorched, then became deeply distressed.
m.5.35.4: O sage, Bhāskara begot three children in her, in Saṃjñā: first Manu Śrāddhadeva, the Prajāpati;
m.5.35.5: and Yama and Yamunā were born as twins. Thus three children were born in her from the Sun.
m.5.35.6: Seeing that spherical form of Vivasvat and being unable to bear it, Saṃjñā then created a lovely shadow (Chāyā) of herself.
m.5.35.7: That illusory Chāyā spoke devotedly to Saṃjñā: O fair one, what task of yours shall I do here? Tell me, O bright-smiling one.
m.5.35.8: Saṃjñā said: I shall go to my own father's house—blessings on you. You must truly dwell in this house without any change of conduct.
m.5.35.9: These two good boys of mine and this slender-waisted girl are to be cared for with all comfort, if you wish to do what pleases me.
m.5.35.10: Chāyā said: O goddess, up to the point of being seized by the hair I shall bear even grave ill-treatment; I will not disclose your plan. Go as you please, O goddess.
m.5.35.11: Sūta said: Thus addressed, the goddess went, abashed, into her father's presence. There, rebuked by her father, she was enjoined again and again to return.
m.5.35.12: Then, concealing her own form and becoming a mare, she went away; reaching the Northern Kurus, she grazed there on grass.
m.5.35.13: Thinking her to be Saṃjñā, Ravi, the Savitṛ, then begot in Chāyā a fine son, Manu Sāvarṇi, so it is said.
m.5.35.14: Though requested by Saṃjñā, that Chāyā constantly showed greater affection for her own son, not so for the elder-born sons.
m.5.35.15: Manu tolerated that of hers, but Yama did not tolerate it; he, angered, both out of childishness and because of the weight of what was destined to be,
m.5.35.16: Yama, son of Vivasvat, threatened Chāyā with his foot. Then Chāyā, sullied by anger, cursed him in wrath:
m.5.35.17: May this foot of yours fall off — so she said in great fury. Then Yama, with joined palms, reported everything to his father.
m.5.35.18: Greatly troubled by fear of the curse and agitated by the words of the false Saṃjñā, he said: A mother should behave with affection towards all her sons.
m.5.35.19: Withdrawing her affection from us, she cherishes the younger one. Therefore I raised my foot; please be pleased to forgive that.
m.5.35.20: I have been cursed by my mother, O lord of gods, O best of those who shine. By your grace, O lord of rays, may my foot not fall.
m.5.35.21: Savitā said: Without doubt, son, there must be a great cause here, by which anger entered you, who know dharma and speak the truth.
m.5.35.22: That word of your mother cannot be made false. Worms will take flesh from your foot and go to the earth.
m.5.35.23: Thus her word will come true, and you will be saved. Have no doubt, dear son; console your own mind, O lord.
m.5.35.24: Sūta said: O lord of sages, having said this to his son named Yama, Sūrya, the Āditya, filled with anger, spoke to that Chāyā:
m.5.35.25: Sūrya said: O dear one, ill-minded, fierce woman, what is this you have done? And why this excessive affection for one son? You should explain this to me.
m.5.35.26: Sūta said: Hearing Ravi's words, she told him the truth exactly as it was; and, scorched by fear of the impassioned Sun, she then appeased him.
m.5.35.27: Hearing her words, Sūrya went to Tvaṣṭṛ and asked him: Where is Saṃjñā? Then Tvaṣṭṛ said to Sūrya:
m.5.35.28: Tvaṣṭā said: Scorched by your excessive brilliance—this form of yours is not pleasing—and unable to bear it, Saṃjñā lives in a grassy forest.
m.5.35.29: Praiseworthy and endowed with yogic power, she has taken to yoga, O lord of rays. If you are agreeable, O lord of gods, having given your own consent,
m.5.35.30: I shall alter your form today and make it lovely. Sūta said: Hearing that, the anger of Mārtaṇḍa Vivasvat subsided.
m.5.35.31: Setting him upon a lathe, the sage pared down that brilliance. Then the form shone forth, with its brilliance contained.
m.5.35.32: The form, made more lovely by Tvaṣṭṛ, then shone beautifully. Then, resorting to deep yoga, he saw his own wife,
m.5.35.33: unassailable by all beings through her brilliance and self-discipline. Taking the form of a horse, he went to her with desire for union,
m.5.35.34: and as she resisted the union out of suspicion of a strange male, O sage, he deposited that seed through her mouth into her nostrils.
m.5.35.35: From that were born the two gods, the Aśvins, best of physicians. Those two Aśvins are also known as Nāsatya and Dasra.
m.5.35.36: Bhāskara then revealed himself to her in his lovely form; seeing him, her husband, she rejoiced and received him with respect.
m.5.35.37: The virtuous lady, with a joyful face, went with her husband to her own home. Then the couple rejoiced in love more than before.
m.5.35.38: Yama, his mind greatly pained by that deed, as Dharmarāja delighted these creatures through dharma.
m.5.35.39: By that deed the greatly radiant Dharmarāja obtained sovereignty over the Pitṛs and the status of a Lokapāla.
m.5.35.40: Manu Sāvarṇi, rich in austerity, became a Prajāpati; by that deed he is to be the Manu in the future Sāvarṇika manvantara.
m.5.35.41: On the summit of Meru the lord performs severe austerity even today. And the younger of those two, the glorious maiden Yamī,
m.5.35.42: she became the best of rivers, the Yamunā, purifier of the worlds. He is called Manu in the world, and is also called Sāvarṇi.
m.5.35.43: Whoever hears this account of the birth of the gods, or retains it in memory, would be freed when he meets with calamity and would attain very great fame.
m.5.35.iti: Thus ends the thirty-fifth adhyāya, named The description of Vaivasvata, in the recounting of the manvantaras, in the fifth saṃhitā, the Umā-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.5.36.1: Sūta said: Vaivasvata Manu had nine sons equal to him; later they became greatly eminent, steadfast, and devoted to the dharma of the kṣatriyas.
m.5.36.2: They were Ikṣvāku, Śibi and Nābhāga, Dhṛṣṭa, and Śaryāti, then Nariṣyanta, Nābhāga, Karūṣa and Priyavrata.
m.5.36.3: Desiring a son, Manu the Prajāpati performed a sacrifice (iṣṭi) when sons had not yet been born; in that sacrifice, O foremost of sages—
m.5.36.4: —she, wearing divine garments, adorned with divine ornaments, and of divine form, the renowned Ilā, was born.
m.5.36.5: Manu, the bearer of the rod of rule, addressed her as Iḍā and said, follow me. Iḍā then replied to him—
m.5.36.6: with these righteous words to the Prajāpati who desired a son. Iḍā said: I was born from portions of Mitra and Varuṇa, O best of speakers.
m.5.36.7: I shall go to their presence; let my inclination not be towards adharma. Having spoken thus, that virtuous one then went to Mitra and Varuṇa—
m.5.36.8: having gone near them, the fair-hipped one, with folded hands, spoke these words: Born from portions of you two at Manu's sacrifice, O great sages,
m.5.36.9: I have come into your presence; tell me, what shall I do for you two? She had told Manu: Create other sons, O lord; through them your lineage will continue.
m.5.36.10: Sūta said: To that virtuous Iḍā, born of Manu's sacrifice, who spoke thus, the two sages named Mitra and Varuṇa spoke with respect.
m.5.36.11: Mitra and Varuṇa said: O knower of dharma, O fair-hipped one, O lovely one, we two are pleased with this modesty, self-restraint and truthfulness of yours.
m.5.36.12: O greatly fortunate one, you will attain fame as ours, and you yourself will become a son who perpetuates Manu's lineage,
m.5.36.13: renowned as Sudyumna, famed in the three worlds, dear to the world, righteous in conduct, and the increaser of Manu's lineage.
m.5.36.14: Sūta said: Having heard that, she turned back; as she was going to her father, Budha, finding an opportunity, invited her to union.
m.5.36.15: Then from Soma's son was born in her King Purūravas—a very handsome, wise, exalted son, the husband of Urvaśī.
m.5.36.16: Having lovingly borne the son Purūravas there, she, by Śiva's grace, again became Sudyumna.
m.5.36.17: Sudyumna had three heirs, supremely righteous: Utkala, Gaya, and the valiant Vinatāśva.
m.5.36.18: To Utkala belonged the Utkalas, O brahmins; to Vinatāśva the western region; and the eastern quarter, O tiger among sages, is remembered as Gayā, belonging to Gaya.
m.5.36.19: When Manu, dear one, then entered the body of the Sun, he divided this earth there into ten realms.
m.5.36.20: Ikṣvāku, the eldest heir, obtained the Middle Country; by Vasiṣṭha's word, Pratiṣṭhāna belonged to the great-souled Sudyumna.
m.5.36.21: Then Sudyumna, of great fame, having obtained the kingdom, established the righteous rule and later gave that kingdom to Purūravas.
m.5.36.22: He was the son of Manu, O best of sages, the lord who bore the marks of both woman and man. From Nariṣyanta came the Śakas as sons; to Nabhaga a son was born—
m.5.36.23: Ambarīṣa; and Bāhleya obtained the Bāhlaka region. Śaryāti had twins: a renowned one named Ānarta,
m.5.36.24: a son, and a daughter Sukanyā, who became the wife of Cyavana. Ānarta's heir was named Raibhya; he was called Raivata,
m.5.36.25: whose city in the land of Ānarta was named Kuśasthalī, most divine, which is regarded as the seventh among the seven sacred cities.
m.5.36.26: He had a hundred sons; Kakudmī was the eldest and best—radiant, very strong, accomplished, most righteous, a protector of brahmins.
m.5.36.27: To Kakudmī was born a maiden named Revatī, endowed with great loveliness, like a second divine Lakṣmī.
m.5.36.28: To ask about a husband for the maiden, King Kakudmī, lord of all, went duly with his daughter to Brahmā's world, to the Creator.
m.5.36.29: While the Gāndharva performance was going on, he waited for a moment to get an opportunity, and there, near Brahmā, he listened to the Gāndharva music during the dancing.
m.5.36.30: Then, in that time, many yugas passed as if a mere muhūrta, but King Kakudmī, O sages, noticed nothing.
m.5.36.31: Then, bowing to the Creator with folded hands, he of humble mind made known his intention to Brahmā, the Supreme Self.
m.5.36.32: Having heard his intention, Prajāpati laughed, addressed the great king Kakudmī, and said:
m.5.36.33: Brahmā said: Listen, O king, son of Raibhya, Kakudmī, lord of the earth: out of affection I shall tell you my words truly and in detail.
m.5.36.34: Those suitors whom you had in mind have been carried away by Time; their lineage no longer exists there—Time devours all.
m.5.36.35: Even your city, O king, was destroyed by the Puṇyajana rākṣasas; now, in the twenty-eighth Dvāpara, it has been rebuilt by Kṛṣṇa,
m.5.36.36: made into a city named Dvārāvatī, many-gated and charming, guarded by the Bhojas, Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas led by Vāsudeva.
m.5.36.37: So go there with a glad heart, O king, and give this maiden, your own daughter, to Baladeva, the son of Vasudeva.
m.5.36.38: Sūta said: Thus instructed, the king bowed to him and went to that city with his daughter, amazed on learning that many yugas had passed.
m.5.36.39: Then there he promptly gave that young maiden, his own Revatī, with due rites, to Bala, the brother of Kṛṣṇa.
m.5.36.40: Then the great lord went to the divine peak of Meru; there that king, established in austerity, worshipped Śiva.
m.5.36.41: The sages said: That Revata stayed there in Brahmaloka for many yugas, yet he came back to the mortal world still young. This is our great doubt.
m.5.36.42: Sūta said: There, indeed, there is no old age, hunger or thirst, nor any changes of the body. Near Brahmā, O sages, there is no untimely death for anyone.
m.5.36.43: Therefore the king did not undergo old age or death, nor did that daughter. Having taken counsel there about the best groom, he came back still young.
m.5.36.44: Having gone to the divine city Dvārāvatī, built by Kṛṣṇa, he had his daughter married to Balarāma.
m.5.36.45: That righteous great lord Balarāma had a hundred sons; and to Kṛṣṇa too countless sons were born from his many wives.
m.5.36.46: There the lineage of both great souls became vast; the kṣatriyas of it, joyful and very righteous, spread into all directions.
m.5.36.47: Thus the lineage of Śaryāti has been told. Now I shall speak briefly of the other descendants of Manu; listen attentively, O twice-born.
m.5.36.48: Nābhāga was the son of Diṣṭa; but he attained brahminhood, having established his own kṣatriya lineage and devoted himself to brahminical rites.
m.5.36.49: From Dhṛṣṭa arose the Dhārṣṭa kṣatriya clan, which attained brahminhood on earth. From Karūṣa came the Kārūṣas, kṣatriyas fierce in battle.
m.5.36.50: Nṛga, who was a son of Manu, was an especially great giver, gladly bestowing various riches and also cows upon brahmins.
m.5.36.51: Because of an error in a gift of cows, through his own poor judgment and his own sin, he fell into the state of a lizard, and was rescued by Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
m.5.36.52: He had one excellent son, Prayāti, a knower of dharma. Thus have I heard from Vyāsa, and it has been told briefly.
m.5.36.53: Vṛṣaghna, a son of Manu, was made a cowherd by his preceptor; he guarded the cows vigilantly, keeping at night the vow of the hero's posture (vīrāsana).
m.5.36.54: Once, hearing the cows crying out, the strong one, awake, perceived that a tiger had come into the cowpen to kill the cows, and went, sword in hand, to slay it.
m.5.36.55: Unknowingly, suspecting it to be the tiger, he struck off the head of a tawny cow. The tiger, frightened at seeing that lord with his sword, ran out.
m.5.36.56: Believing the tiger slain, he went back to his own place, confused in that night, his judgment ruined by the rain and wind.
m.5.36.57: When the night had dawned, he rose early and went there; he saw the tawny cow slain, not the tiger, and was grieved.
m.5.36.58: Hearing of that incident and understanding it, the preceptor, though considering that it was unintentional, cursed the offender: Become a śūdra, not a kṣatriya.
m.5.36.59: Thus cursed in anger by his preceptor, the family teacher, Pṛṣadhra departed and went into the great forest.
m.5.36.60: Despondent through hardship, he became detached and devoted to yoga; his body burnt in a forest fire, he reached the supreme goal.
m.5.36.61: Kavi, the wise son of Manu, by the grace of Śiva enjoyed divine happiness here and attained liberation, which is very hard to obtain.
m.5.36.iti: Thus ends the thirty-sixth adhyāya, named The description of the lineages of the nine sons of Manu, in the fifth saṃhitā, the Umā-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.5.37.1: Sūta said: From Manu, long ago, was born a son, Ikṣvāku, from his nostril. That Ikṣvāku had a hundred sons, all givers of abundant sacrificial fees.
m.5.37.2: Of them, some became kings in the east in Āryāvarta, O twice-born ones. Among them Vikukṣi was the eldest; he became king in Ayodhyā.
m.5.37.3: Hear with interest that deed of his which took place in the lineage sprung from Vidhi (Brahmā). Having been assigned to fetch meat for the śrāddha rite, while the śrāddha rite had not yet been performed,
m.5.37.4: he hastily ate a hare, and hence came to be called Śaśāda ('hare-eater'). Abandoned by Ikṣvāku, Śaśāda entered the forest.
m.5.37.5: When Ikṣvāku had passed away, he became king by Vasiṣṭha's word. His sons, headed by Śakuni, are remembered as fifteen,
m.5.37.6: kings who were protectors of the northern region. The heir of Ayodha was the valiant one named Kakutstha.
m.5.37.7: Kakutstha's son was Arinābha; his son was Pṛthu. Pṛthu's son was Viṣṭarāśva, and from him came Indra, a lord of the people.
m.5.37.8: Indra's son was Yuvanāśva; his son was Śrāva, a lord of the people. From him was born the wise Śrāvastaka, by whom Śrāvastī was built. The heir of Śrāvasta was the greatly renowned Bṛhadaśva.
m.5.37.9: His son was Yuvanāśva, and Kuvalāśva was his son. He, the best of kings, became known as Dhundhumāra from slaying Dhundhu.
m.5.37.10: Kuvalāśva had a hundred sons, excellent archers. Then the father appointed Kuvalāśva to the kingship.
m.5.37.11: The king, having transferred his royal fortune to his son, set out for the forest. Then Uttaṅka stopped that royal sage as he was departing.
m.5.37.12: Uttaṅka said: Listen: the protection of the earth according to dharma is to be carried out by you. For, O king, the earth, being protected by you, the great-souled one,
m.5.37.13: will be free from distress; you should not go to the forest. Near my hermitage, in the level desert lands,
m.5.37.14: in a place filled with sea-sand, there is a Dānava proud of his strength, huge-bodied and mighty, who cannot be slain by the gods.
m.5.37.15: Having gone beneath the ground, he lies there hidden within the sand — the son of the Rākṣasa Madhu, named Dhundhu, exceedingly terrible.
m.5.37.16: He lies there for the destruction of the worlds, having undertaken fierce austerity. At the end of each year he releases his breath.
m.5.37.17: Whenever he does so, the earth shakes with its mountains, woods and forests; his breath is full of sparks, embers and smoke, exceedingly dreadful.
m.5.37.18: Because of that, O king, I cannot stay in that hermitage of mine. Kill him, O mighty-armed one, out of desire for the welfare of the worlds.
m.5.37.19: Let the worlds be at ease today, once he is slain by you. For you alone, O lord of the earth, are capable of killing him.
m.5.37.20: And a boon was granted to me by Viṣṇu in a former age, O sinless one: Viṣṇu will augment your energy with his own energy.
m.5.37.21: For great dharma is seen here in protecting the people; it is not seen in the same way in the forest. Do not let such an idea be yours.
m.5.37.22: For nowhere, O king of kings, is there dharma such as that which was practised of old by royal sages in protecting the people.
m.5.37.23: The royal sage, thus addressed by the great-souled Uttaṅka, gave him his son Kuvalāśva for the subduing of Dhundhu,
m.5.37.24: saying: O revered one, I have laid down my weapons; but this son of mine, O best of brahmins, will be the slayer of Dhundhu, no doubt.
m.5.37.25: Having said this and instructed his son, the king went off for austerity; and Kuvalāśva, together with Uttaṅka, went to subdue Dhundhu.
m.5.37.26: Then the lord, the blessed Viṣṇu, entered him with his energy, at Uttaṅka's behest, out of desire for the welfare of the worlds.
m.5.37.27: When that invincible one set out, a great voice arose in heaven: This glorious prince will be Dhundhumāra.
m.5.37.28: The gods covered him all around with heavenly garlands, and praised him, crying, Victory! Long life!
m.5.37.29: Having gone there, that king, best of victors, together with his sons had the sand-ocean dug up from its middle.
m.5.37.30: Invigorated by the energy of Nārāyaṇa and of the brahmin sage, he became exceedingly brilliant and still more endowed with strength.
m.5.37.31: As his sons dug, O brahmin, Dhundhu, who lay within the sand, was reached, resting toward the western direction.
m.5.37.32: In his rage, as if consuming the worlds with the fire born from his mouth, he poured forth water with force, like the ocean at the rising of the moon.
m.5.37.33: Then that group of a hundred sons, struck by the fires, was burnt; only three among them remained, O lord of sages.
m.5.37.34: Then, O chief of brahmins, that greatly brilliant king attacked that mighty Rākṣasa Dhundhu, the destroyer of brahmins.
m.5.37.35: Drinking up his watery torrent, that ruler of men struck with a fire-arrow, and quenched the fire with water.
m.5.37.36: Having slain by his might that huge-bodied water-Rākṣasa, the ruler of men showed Uttaṅka the deed accomplished.
m.5.37.37: Uttaṅka then granted a boon to that king, O great sage: he gave him inexhaustible wealth and invincibility by enemies,
m.5.37.38: a mind ever set on dharma, and likewise an imperishable dwelling in heaven; and an imperishable world for his sons who had been slain by the Rākṣasa.
m.5.37.39: Of his three surviving sons, Dṛḍhāśva is called the eldest; and Haṃsāśva and Kapilāśva were the two princes younger than him.
m.5.37.40: Dṛḍhāśva, the son of Dhundhumāra — his son was Haryaśva; and Haryaśva's son was Nikumbha, ever devoted to dharma.
m.5.37.41: Saṃhatāśva, skilled in battle, was the son of Nikumbha. Akṣāśva and Kṛtāśva were the two sons of Saṃhatāśva, O brahmins.
m.5.37.42: His wife was Haimavatī, Dṛṣadvatī, honoured by the virtuous and famed in the three worlds; her son was Prasenajit.
m.5.37.43: Prasenajit obtained a devoted wife named Gaurī; but she, cursed by her husband, was turned into the river Bāhudā.
m.5.37.44: His son was the great king Yuvanāśva. Yuvanāśva's son was Māndhātā, renowned in the three worlds.
m.5.37.45: His wife was Caitrarathī, daughter of Śaśabindu; she was devoted to her husband and the eldest among ten thousand brothers.
m.5.37.46: Then Māndhātā begot on her two sons: Purukutsa, knower of dharma, and the righteous Mucukunda.
m.5.37.47: Purukutsa's son was the learned and wise Trayyāruṇi. His son was a very mighty prince named Satyavrata.
m.5.37.48: He obstructed the marriage mantras being recited by noble persons, he by whom formerly the bride of another was carried off while his wedding was being performed.
m.5.37.49: When, out of force, lust, delusion and intense excitement, he carried off, from desire, the maiden of a certain citizen,
m.5.37.50: King Trayyāruṇi, filled with anger, renouncing him who clung to unrighteousness, said again and again, begone.
m.5.37.51: Then the wicked one said to his father: Where shall I go? The king then told him: Live near the dog-eaters (śvapākas).
m.5.37.52: So that hero Satyavrata, abandoned by his father, the dharma-protecting king, lived near the dwellings of the dog-eaters.
m.5.37.53: Then King Trayyāruṇi, disgusted by his son's deed, abandoned everything and went to the forest to perform austerities to Śaṅkara.
m.5.37.54: Then, because of that unrighteousness, Indra (Pākaśāsana) did not rain in his realm for twelve years, O brahmin sage.
m.5.37.55: In his realm, the great ascetic Viśvāmitra, leaving his wife behind, practised vast austerity in the marshy land by the sea.
m.5.37.56: His wife, binding a rope round the neck of her middle son, born of her own husband, sold him for a hundred cows to sustain the rest.
m.5.37.57: Seeing her selling her own son, bound at the neck, the righteous one then had that son of the great sage released.
m.5.37.58: The mighty-armed Satyavrata maintained him, to please Viśvāmitra and out of compassion.
m.5.37.59: From then on, that son of the sage Viśvāmitra became known as Gālava, a great ascetic, because of the binding of his neck (gala-bandha).
m.5.37.iti: Thus ends the thirty-seventh adhyāya, named The description of the lineage of Manu, in the fifth saṃhitā, the Umā-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.5.38.1: Sūta said: Satyavrata, out of devotion to him (Viśvāmitra), out of compassion, and because of his vow, then indeed supported Viśvāmitra's wife and family.
m.5.38.2: Having killed deer, boars, buffaloes and other forest-roaming animals, he would throw their meat near Viśvāmitra's hermitage, O sage.
m.5.38.3: The sage Vasiṣṭha, owing to the bond between sacrificer and family priest, protected the sacred places, the cows, the king's person and likewise the inner palace.
m.5.38.4: Whether because of Satyavrata's words or by the force of what was destined to be, Vasiṣṭha constantly held ever greater anger towards him.
m.5.38.5: When he, the king's own son, was then banished from the kingdom by his father, the sage Vasiṣṭha did not prevent it, and for a reason.
m.5.38.6: The completion of the marriage mantras takes place at the seventh step; and Satyavrata did not understand that secret intention of his.
m.5.38.7: In that matter he, Vasiṣṭha, acted for the satisfaction of the great-souled father, thinking, this would be an atonement made for the family, O brahmin.
m.5.38.8: The blessed Vasiṣṭha did not restrain him when he was abandoned by his father; nor did the sage say, I shall consecrate his son.
m.5.38.9: That strong one kept that vow for twelve years. Once, when there was no meat to be had, ...
m.5.38.10: ... that prince saw the milch cow of the great-souled Vasiṣṭha that yields all desires. Then, out of anger, greed and weariness, and overcome by hunger, ...
m.5.38.11: ... the king, following the conduct of the Dāśas, killed her, O sage. He himself ate that meat and gave it to Viśvāmitra's son ...
m.5.38.12: ... he fed. Hearing that, Vasiṣṭha became angry with him, and the best of sages, filled with wrath, then said to him:
m.5.38.13: Vasiṣṭha said: O cruel one, I would without doubt bring down a spike (śaṅku) upon you, if these two spikes had not already been made by you before.
m.5.38.14: By your father's displeasure, by killing your preceptor's milch cow, and by using meat not consecrated with sprinkling — threefold is your transgression.
m.5.38.15: He called him Triśaṅku, and thus he is remembered as Triśaṅku. Viśvāmitra, for his part, returned after the maintenance of his wife and family had been accomplished.
m.5.38.16: For that reason the sage, pleased, granted a boon to Triśaṅku; and being offered a boon, the prince chose his boon.
m.5.38.17: When this fear of a twelve-year drought had arisen, the sage installed him in his father's kingdom and had him perform a sacrifice.
m.5.38.18: Then, while the gods and Vasiṣṭha looked on, the mighty Kauśika raised him to heaven in his body.
m.5.38.19: His wife, named Satyarathā, born of the Kekaya lineage, bore a son, the sinless Hariścandra.
m.5.38.20: That king Hariścandra is remembered as Traiśaṅkava (son of Triśaṅku); as the performer of the Rājasūya he is famed as an emperor.
m.5.38.21: Hariścandra's son was the famous one named Rohita; Rohita's son was Vṛka, and from Vṛka Bāhu was born.
m.5.38.22: The Haihayas and Tālajaṅghas drove out that king. He was not very righteous, O brahmins, though he lived in the age of dharma.
m.5.38.23: Bāhu begot a son, Sagara, who was born together with poison (gara), after his mother reached Aurva's hermitage and was protected by the Bhārgava.
m.5.38.24: Having obtained the fire-missile (āgneya) from the Bhārgava, King Sagara conquered the earth, slaying the Tālajaṅghas and the Haihayas.
m.5.38.25: Subduing the Śakas, the Bahūdakas, the Pāradas with their hosts, and the Khaśas, he established true dharma and ruled the earth righteously.
m.5.38.26: Śaunaka said: How was he born of a kṣatriya together with poison, and how did he conquer? Tell this in detail, O son of Sūta.
m.5.38.27: Sūta said: What Vaiśampāyana related when asked by Pārīkṣita (Janamejaya) — that I shall tell; listen with an undivided mind, O sage.
m.5.38.28: The son of Parīkṣit said: O sage, how was that King Sagara born together with poison, and how did he slay the kings? You should relate this.
m.5.38.29: Vaiśampāyana said: The kingdom of Bāhu, who was given to vices, was seized, it is said, my dear, by the Haihayas and Tālajaṅghas together with the Śakas, O lord of the people.
m.5.38.30: The Yavanas, the Pāradas, the Kāmbojas, the Pāhlavas and the Bahūdakas — these five are declared to be the hosts of the rākṣasas.
m.5.38.31: These five hosts of the rākṣasas, O king, displaying their valour on behalf of the Haihayas, forcibly gave them the kingdom taken from Bāhu.
