m.6.6.36: and placing on its stand a copper vessel wide enough to hold a prastha of water, filling it with pure water scented with flowers and the like,
m.6.6.37: and worshipping it with sandal, flowers and the like, kneeling on the ground, he should take up the arghya vessel and raise it up to between the eyebrows.
m.6.6.38: Then he should recite this Sāvitra mantra, which grants all accomplishments. Hear it, O Great Goddess; it ever bestows enjoyment and liberation.
m.6.6.39: Salutation be to you, vermilion-hued, of beautiful orb, adorned with diamond ornaments, with lotus-like eyes, holding a lotus, the cause of Brahmā, Indra and Nārāyaṇa.
m.6.6.40: Accepting this excellent arghya offered to you, with red powder, with golden water, rich with garlands and saffron, with kuśa grass and flowers, together with the golden vessel—O Lord, be gracious.
m.6.6.41: Having said this, and then having offered that arghya to Śiva in the form of the Sun, he should bow down, fully collected, reciting this mantra:
m.6.6.42: Salutation to you, Śiva, accompanied by Ambā, accompanied by your gaṇas, the first cause; to you who are Rudra, Viṣṇu and Brahmā, the threefold form.
m.6.6.43: Having said this and bowed, seated firmly on his own seat, having again performed the assignment of the ṛṣi and the rest, and having purified his hand with water,
m.6.6.44: and again having applied ash in the very manner described before, he should perform the whole set of nyāsas for the increase of the Śiva-state within himself.
m.6.6.45: Having worshipped the revered guru on the head with the five offerings, the wise one should then bow, uttering the praṇava, śrīguru in the dative, ending with namaḥ.
m.6.6.46: He should extract the seed-syllable of the five-natured letter joined with the bindu and with the fifth vowel; then that same letter with the bindu but without the fifth vowel;
m.6.6.47: then the lord-of-mantras letter joined with the fifth vowel and the bindu; having extracted these, he should then extract the saṃvartaka letter with the bindu.
m.6.6.48: With these seed-syllables thus extracted, in order, the wise one should bow to the guru and Gaṇapati on the two arms, and likewise on the pair of thighs
m.6.6.49: to Durgā and to Kṣetrapāla, standing with joined, cupped palms. Saying Om astrāya phaṭ, having purified the two hands six times in sequence,
m.6.6.50: having said apasarpantu (may they depart), then the praṇava, then saying astrāya phaṭ, with three strikes of the heel
m.6.6.51: having driven away the numerous obstacles on the ground, and with three hand-claps those present in the mid-air, and having cast a glance at those dwelling in the sky,
m.6.6.52: seated with breath restrained, remembering the haṃsa mantra, he should lead the living consciousness abiding in the heart upward through the brahma-nāḍī
m.6.6.53: into the clear great thousand-petalled lotus located at the dvādaśānta, to the Supreme Lord whose form is consciousness, abiding within the moon-disc of consciousness.
m.6.6.54: He should perform the drying, burning and flooding of the body in the order of exhalation (recaka) and the rest, with counts of sixteen, sixty-four and thirty-two,
m.6.6.55: using those seed-letters of air, fire and water, each with its own syllables beginning with the Vedic Om, in sequence. Having restrained the breaths, he should raise Kuṇḍalinī, seated at the root, as she goes to the brahmarandhra,
m.6.6.56: having brought her into the interior of the thousand-petalled lotus situated at the dvādaśānta, with the stream of supreme nectar arising from the moon-disc of consciousness
m.6.6.57: the body being thus drenched again, he, pure in body and rightly contemplating, then, saying so'ham (I am he), descending, places his own self in the heart-lotus,
m.6.6.58: and having made the self, nectar-like, enter into the Self by the flowing stream, he should here, concentrated, perform the installation of life (prāṇa-pratiṣṭhā) according to rule.
m.6.6.59: The yogī, with one-pointed mind, should contemplate that inner mātṛkā; then he should also place the mātṛkā externally, enclosed by the praṇava.
m.6.6.60: And again, with breath controlled, the wise one should perform the rites beginning with the gaze; remembering Śaṅkara in his mind, free of envy, he should perform the placing.
m.6.6.61: O Devī, the seer of the praṇava is Brahmā, its metre is declared to be Gāyatrī, and its deity here is I myself, the Supreme Self, Sadāśiva.
m.6.6.62: The letter A is declared to be the seed (bīja), the letter U is called the power (śakti), the letter M is said to be the pin (kīlaka); it is applied for the purpose of liberation.
m.6.6.63: Beginning from the two thumbs, he should wipe the hands down to the palms; then, O Queen of gods, saying Om, he should begin the hand-nyāsa.
m.6.6.64: Beginning with the thumb of the right hand, in due order, he should place the syllables up to the little finger of the left hand, in sequence as before.
m.6.6.65: Then, uttering A, U and M joined with the bindu, each ending with namaḥ, he should place them everywhere, beginning with the heart.
m.6.6.66: First extracting the letter A, he should then join the name Brahmātman in the dative, ending with namaḥ, and apply it to the heart; and likewise again:
m.6.6.67: he should place the letter U together with Viṣṇu on the region of the head, and the letter M together with Rudra on the topknot.
m.6.6.68: Having spoken thus, the sage who knows the mantras should place the kavaca and netra limb-mantras on the eyes and head, O Queen of the god of gods, with an attentive mind.
m.6.6.69: He should place the five Brahma-mantras according to the divisions of limbs, faces and kalās; he should place them on the head, face, heart, private parts and feet.
m.6.6.70: The five kalās of Īśāna are to be placed in order on these five places; then the kalās of Tatpuruṣa too, on the four faces,
m.6.6.71: the four are to be placed in order beginning with the east. On the heart, throat, shoulders, navel, belly, back and chest
m.6.6.72: the eight kalās of Aghora are to be worshipped in due order. Afterwards, the thirteen kalās, on the anus, penis, thighs, knees,
m.6.6.73: shanks, buttocks, hips and sides, he should contemplate as those of Vāmadeva. The eight kalās of Sadyojāta too, beginning on the eyes, in due order,
m.6.6.74: those kalās that have been declared, the best knower of ritual should thus arrange also on the two feet, the two hands, the nose, the head and the two arms.
m.6.6.75: Having thus completely performed the nyāsa of the thirty-eight kalās, the wise one who knows the praṇava should afterwards perform the praṇava-nyāsa:
m.6.6.76: on the two arms, on the elbows and likewise on the wrists, on the sides, belly and shanks, on the feet, and likewise on the back.
m.6.6.77: Having thus performed the placing of the praṇava, the one skilled in nyāsa should perform the haṃsa-nyāsa, O You who awaken one to the Supreme Self.
m.6.6.iti: Thus ends the sixth adhyāya, named The description of nyāsa, in the procedure of saṃnyāsa, in the sixth saṃhitā, the Kailāsa-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.6.7.1: Īśvara said: On his own left he should prepare a square maṇḍala. Having worshipped it with Om, he should set in it a conch purified by the astra mantra,
m.6.7.2: having placed it together with its stand, he should then worship it with the praṇava, filling it with pure water made fragrant with sandal and the like.
m.6.7.3: Having worshipped it with fragrance, flowers and the rest, and having consecrated it seven times with the praṇava, he should then display over it the dhenu-mudrā
m.6.7.4: and the conch-mudrā. In front he should design a square, within it a half-moon, and within that a triangle,
m.6.7.5: then a hexagon and a circle — thus he should prepare this maṇḍala. Having worshipped it with fragrance, flowers and the rest with the praṇava, then in its centre
m.6.7.6: having placed the arghya vessel with its stand, he should worship it with fragrance and the rest. Having filled it with pure water, he should put into that vessel
m.6.7.7: tips of kuśa grass, unbroken rice grains, barley, paddy and sesame, ghee, white mustard and flowers, and sacred ash, O fair-faced one.
m.6.7.8: Having worshipped it with fragrance, flowers and the rest using the mantras beginning with Sadyojāta, the six limb-mantras and the praṇava, and having consecrated it with the armour (kavaca) mantra,
m.6.7.9: and having veiled it, he should display the astra gesture with the astra mantra for protection, and the dhenu-mudrā; with that same water he should sprinkle, using the astra mantra,
m.6.7.10: himself and also the articles of worship such as fragrance and flowers. On the petal of the lotus in the north-east (Īśāna) direction, preceded by uttering the praṇava,
m.6.7.11: he should set up a seat with gurvāsanāya namaḥ (salutation to the guru's seat), and there he should fashion the image of the guru as instructed.
m.6.7.12: Uttering the praṇava, guṃ, gurubhyaḥ and at the end namaḥ, and having invoked the preceptor, he should then meditate on him as seated facing south:
m.6.7.13: with a very serene face, gentle, spotless like pure crystal, with hands showing the boon-giving and fear-dispelling gestures, two-eyed, the very embodiment of Śiva.
m.6.7.14: Having meditated thus, he should worship him in due order with fragrance, flowers and the rest. On the south-west petal of the lotus, upon the seat of Gaṇapati,
m.6.7.15: having fashioned the image right there and invoked him with the mantra gaṇānāṃ tvā, he should then meditate on the god with a one-pointed mind:
m.6.7.16: red in colour, of huge body, adorned with all ornaments, holding in his lotus-hands the noose, the goad, the rosary and the gesture granting desires,
m.6.7.17: the elephant-faced lord who destroys all the hosts of obstacles of the worshipper. Having meditated thus, he should worship with fragrance, flowers and other offerings,
m.6.7.18: and then, having offered food (naivedya) consisting of plantains, coconuts, mangoes, other fruits and laḍḍus, he should bow to the elephant-faced one.
m.6.7.19: On the north-west (Vāyu's) petal of the lotus, having conceived the seat of Skanda and fashioned Skanda's image, the wise one should invoke Skanda.
m.6.7.20: Having recited the Skanda-Gāyatrī, he should then meditate on Kumāra, resembling the rising sun, whose mount is the excellent peacock,
m.6.7.21: four-armed, of noble limbs, adorned with a crown and other ornaments, with hands in the boon-giving and fear-dispelling gestures, holding the spear (śakti) and the cock.
m.6.7.22: Having thus meditated and then worshipped him in due order with fragrance and other offerings, he should worship the one stationed at the right door-post of the eastern gate,
m.6.7.23: Nandin himself, lord of the inner palace, he should properly worship — him who is like a mountain of gold, adorned with all ornaments,
m.6.7.24: crowned with the crescent moon, gentle, three-eyed and four-armed, the mighty one holding a blazing trident, a deer, a chisel-axe (ṭaṅka) and a golden staff,
m.6.7.25: with a face shining like the orb of the moon, or else monkey-faced. Likewise to his north he should worship his wife, the daughter of the Maruts,
m.6.7.26: Suyaśā, of good vows, devoted to adorning the feet of the Mother — having worshipped her duly with fragrance, flowers and other offerings,
m.6.7.27: he should then sprinkle the lotus with drops of the conch-water consecrated with the astra mantra, and afterwards arrange the seat, beginning with the Support (ādhāra), in proper order.
m.6.7.28: He should meditate below, on the ground, on the auspicious, dark Ādhāraśakti (Power of Support); in front of her, on Ananta with uplifted neck, coiled in form,
m.6.7.29: white, five-hooded, as though licking the sky; above him an auspicious seat with lions as its four legs.
m.6.7.30: Dharma, knowledge, dispassion and sovereignty are its legs, placed from the south-east onward, white, yellow, red and dark in colour respectively.
m.6.7.31: Adharma and the rest, from the east up to the north in order, he should visualize as its body-parts, resembling the rājāvarta gem (lapis lazuli).
m.6.7.32: Then, having visualized the lower and upper coverings, the bulb, the stalk and the thorns, the petals and so on, and the pericarp, he should worship them in order.
m.6.7.33: On the petals are the eight siddhis, and on the filaments the śaktis; the eight Rudras, Vāma and the rest, are placed all around in order beginning from the east.
m.6.7.34: On the pericarp is dispassion; on the seeds the nine śaktis, Vāmā and the rest, from the east onward, and at their end Manonmanī.
m.6.7.35: In the bulb is dharma, of the nature of Śiva; in the stalk knowledge resting on Śiva; above the pericarp the circles of fire, sun and moon,
m.6.7.36: and beyond that the triad of principles: ātman, vidyā and the one called Śiva. Above all the seats, a comfortable seat, brilliant with variegated flowers,
m.6.7.37: exceedingly radiant through the Vidyā called the space of the supreme ether — having arranged this seat for the image, preceded by the placing of flowers,
m.6.7.38: from the Ādhāraśakti up to the seat of Śuddhavidyā, each with its name-mantra beginning with Om, ending in the dative case and concluding with namaḥ —
m.6.7.39: having uttered these, the learned one should worship; this is the order of the rite everywhere. As before, distinguishing them by limbs, faces and kalās, the five Brahmans
m.6.7.40: he should place in order upon the image, skilled in their respective mudrās. Then, standing with joined palms holding flowers, he should invoke the god.
m.6.7.41: Reciting the mantra that begins with sadyojātaṃ prapadyāmi and ends with Om, and raising the sound (nāda) that rises from the ādhāra centre by piercing the twelve knots,
m.6.7.42: having uttered it up to the brahmarandhra, one should meditate on the God who is the object of the Oṃkāra, resembling pure crystal, partless and imperishable,
m.6.7.43: the cause of all the worlds, consisting of all the worlds, the Supreme, abiding within and without having pervaded all, smaller than the atom and greatest of all,
m.6.7.44: the imperishable Lord, seen without effort by devotees, yet beyond the reach even of gods such as Brahmā, Indra, Viṣṇu and Rudra,
m.6.7.45: the essence of the Vedas, declared in scripture to be beyond the reach of the learned, without beginning, middle or end, the medicine for those afflicted by the disease of worldly existence.
m.6.7.46: Having thus meditated on the Supreme Lord with a concentrated mind, one should perform invocation, installation, confinement, gazing,
m.6.7.47: and obeisance, forming the mudrās one by one. One should meditate on Sadāśiva, the God himself, who is both with parts and without parts:
m.6.7.48: resembling pure crystal, serene, of cool radiance, like a ring of lightning, adorned with a crown of matted locks,
m.6.7.49: clothed in a tiger skin, his lotus face gently smiling, his palms, soles and lips resembling red lotus petals,
m.6.7.50: endowed with all auspicious marks, adorned with all ornaments, his hands holding divine weapons, anointed with divine fragrances,
m.6.7.51: five-faced, ten-armed, with a digit of the moon as his crest-jewel. His eastern face is gentle, with a radiance like the rising sun,
m.6.7.52: rich with three lotus eyes, crested with the young moon. The southern face has a lovely radiance like a dark rain cloud,
m.6.7.53: crooked with frowning brows, terrible, with three red round eyes, fearsome with fangs, hard to behold, with quivering, sprout-like lips;
m.6.7.54: the northern face resembles coral, is adorned with dark curls, full of grace, three-eyed, crested with the half-moon;
m.6.7.55: the western face shines like the full moon, radiant with three eyes, bearing the crescent, gentle, charming with a soft smile;
m.6.7.56: the fifth face resembles crystal, shines brightly with the streak of the moon, is exceedingly gentle and radiant with three wide-open eyes.
m.6.7.57: On the right his hands shine with the trident, axe, thunderbolt, sword and fire;
m.6.7.58: on the left they shine with the Pināka bow, the iron arrow, the bell, the noose and the goad. He is pervaded by Nivṛtti kalā up to the knees, and by Pratiṣṭhā up to the navel,
m.6.7.59: likewise by Vidyā up to the throat, by Śāntā up to the forehead, and above that by the supreme kalā called Śāntyatītā.
m.6.7.60: Hence he is pervading the five paths (adhvans), his body made of the five kalās; the ancient God, with Īśāna as his crown and Tatpuruṣa as his face,
m.6.7.61: likewise the Great Lord with Aghora as his heart, Vāmadeva as his private part and Sadyojāta as his feet; his form consists of the thirty-eight kalās,
m.6.7.62: the Lord consisting of the mātṛkā letters, consisting of the five Brahman mantras, consisting of what is called the Oṃkāra, and consisting of the haṃsa-nyāsa,
m.6.7.63: the God consisting of the five-syllabled mantra and likewise of the six-syllabled, consisting of the six limbs (aṅgas) and endowed with the six jātis.
m.6.7.64: Having thus meditated, then one should invoke you, Manonmanī Gaurī, on my left side, with devotion, using the mantra gaurīr mimāya preceded by the praṇava;
m.6.7.65: having invoked you, O Īśvarī, one should perform the rites as before, up to the obeisance. Then, O Queen of gods, the sage with concentrated mind should meditate on you:
m.6.7.66: shining like the petal of a full-blown lotus, with wide, long eyes, a face like the full moon, and dark curly hair,
m.6.7.67: resembling a blue lotus petal, crested with the half-moon, with very round, firm, high, smooth and full breasts,
m.6.7.68: slender-waisted, broad-hipped, wearing a very fine yellow garment, endowed with all ornaments, bright with a tilaka mark on the forehead,
m.6.7.69: beautified by tresses strewn with many-coloured flowers, of a form pleasing in every respect, her face slightly bent with modesty,
m.6.7.70: holding a shining golden lotus in her right hand, having placed the other hand firmly upon a chowrie, seated on a comfortable seat.
m.6.7.71: Having thus meditated on me and on you, O Queen of gods, with a restrained mind, one should bathe us with water from the conch, following the order of sprinkling with the praṇava.
m.6.7.72: With bhave bhave nātibhave one should offer water for the feet; saying vāmāya namaḥ one should give water for sipping.
m.6.7.73: Saying jyeṣṭhāya namaḥ one should offer a white cloth; saying śreṣṭhāya namaḥ one should give the sacred thread.
m.6.7.74: Saying rudrāya namaḥ, one should give water for sipping again; saying kālāya namaḥ one should give well-prepared sandal paste.
m.6.7.75: With kalavikaraṇāya namaḥ one should offer unbroken rice; with balavikaraṇāya namaḥ one should offer flowers.
m.6.7.76: Saying balāya namaḥ one should carefully offer incense; with balapramathanāya one should offer a fine lamp.
m.6.7.77: With the Brahman mantras and the six aṅga mantras, then with the mātṛkā, with the praṇava, and with the Śiva mantra joined with Śakti, in due order,
m.6.7.78: one should display the mudrās to me and to you, O fair-complexioned one. One should offer the services first to me and then to you.
m.6.7.79: When performing them for you, one should then use the feminine gender. This alone is the difference, O Pārvatī; there is no other.
m.6.7.80: Having thus performed meditation and worship properly according to the rule, the wise one should begin the worship of my surrounding retinue (āvaraṇa).
m.6.7.iti: Thus ends the seventh adhyāya, named The description of meditation on Śiva and his worship, in the sixth saṃhitā, the Kailāsa-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.6.8.1: Īśvara said: Here, O Mahādevī, there is indeed a set of five enclosures (āvaraṇa). One should begin the worship of the five enclosures in due order.
m.6.8.2: Right where the two were first worshipped, the wise one should first worship in order, with fragrance and the rest, the two gods Heramba and Ṣaṇmukha.
m.6.8.3: He should then worship in order the five Brahman mantras around the circle: in the north-east, in the east, in the south, likewise in the north,
m.6.8.4: and in the west. Then, in that same circle, he should worship the six limbs (aṅga): in the south-east, likewise in the north-east, in the south-west, in the north-west region,
m.6.8.5: the eye in the middle, and likewise the weapon all around in order beginning from the east. The first enclosure has been described; now hear the second enclosure.
m.6.8.6: He should worship Ananta on the eastern petal, likewise Sūkṣma on the south, Śivottama on the west, and Ekanetra on the north,
m.6.8.7: likewise Ekarudra in the north-east, Trimūrti on the petal of the south-east, Śrīkaṇṭha in the south-west, and in the north-west he should worship Śikhaṇḍīśa.
m.6.8.8: In the second enclosure those sovereigns (cakravartin) are to be worshipped. In the middle of the eastern gate he should worship Vṛṣeśāna.
m.6.8.9: Nandin to its south and Mahākāla to its north; Bhṛṅgīśa he should worship to the west of the southern gate.
m.6.8.10: Having worshipped Vināyaka with fragrance and the rest in the compartment east of it, he should worship Vṛṣabha in the north-western compartment and Guha in the south.
m.6.8.11: To the east of the northern gate, following the clockwise procedure, he should worship by the method of the eight names; that is now stated.
m.6.8.12: Bhava, Śarva, likewise Īśāna, Rudra, then Paśupati, Ugra, Bhīma and Mahādeva: this is the third enclosure.
m.6.8.13: Having invoked Maheśvara with the mantra yo vedādau svaraḥ, he should worship him in the eastern part, on the pericarp of the lotus.
m.6.8.14: He should worship Īśvara on the eastern petal, then Viśveśa in the south, Parameśāna in the north and Sarveśa in the west.
m.6.8.15: In the south he should worship Rudra, having invoked him with the verse ā vo rājānam, with fragrance, flowers and the rest, on the pericarp and on the petals:
m.6.8.16: Śiva in the east, Hara in the south, Mṛḍa in the north and Bhava on the western petal: these are to be worshipped in due order.
m.6.8.17: In the north, having invoked Viṣṇu by reciting pra tad viṣṇuḥ, he should worship him with fragrance, flowers and the rest on the pericarp and on the petals:
m.6.8.18: He should worship Vāsudeva in the eastern part, Aniruddha in the south, Saṅkarṣaṇa in the north and Pradyumna in the west.
m.6.8.19: The knower of mantras should invoke and worship Brahmā on the western lotus with the mantra hiraṇyagarbhaḥ samavartata.
m.6.8.20: He should worship Hiraṇyagarbha in the east, then Virāj in the south, Puṣkara in the north and Kāla in the west.
m.6.8.21: In the outermost row, following the clockwise order beginning from the east, having worshipped the world-guardians (lokapāla) in succession in their respective places—
m.6.8.22: the syllables ending in ra, ending in ma, likewise ending in kṣa, ending in la, ending in va, the one not preceded by another, ending in sa, ending in ha, the first syllable of the Veda (Om) and the seed of Śrī: ten in order—
m.6.8.23: are the seed syllables of the world-guardians; with these he should worship them. In the south-west, likewise in the north, and to the south of Īśāna,
m.6.8.24: he should duly worship Brahmā and Viṣṇu with offerings. On the outer lines, O Queen of the gods, he should worship in the fifth enclosure:
m.6.8.25: he should worship the glorious trident in the north-east, the thunderbolt in the direction of great Indra (east), the axe in the region of Fire (south-east), and the arrow in Yama's quarter (south).
m.6.8.26: In the south-west he should worship the sword, the noose in Varuṇa's domain (west), the goad in the region of the Wind (north-west), and in the north he should worship the Pināka bow.
m.6.8.27: The one who knows the procedure should duly worship the fierce Kṣetrapāla facing west, solely for the pleasure of Śiva.
m.6.8.28: All of them are to be contemplated with palms joined in reverence, with lotus-faces smiling, and ever gazing respectfully at the god and the goddess.
m.6.8.29: Having thus performed the worship of the enclosures, in order to calm distractions he should worship the Lord of gods again and utter the praṇava and the name Śiva.
m.6.8.30: Having thus duly worshipped and served him with fragrance and other offerings, he should then offer food (naivedya) prepared according to rule.
m.6.8.31: Again he should give water for sipping (ācamana) and the arghya as before; then, as instructed, offer drinking water and betel.
m.6.8.32: Having performed the waving of lights (nīrājana) and the like, he should complete the remainder of the worship; meditating on the god and the goddess, he should repeat the mantra one hundred and eight times.
m.6.8.33: Then rising and standing with palms cupped holding flowers, meditating on Mahādeva, he should recite in order the hymn beginning yo devānām
m.6.8.34: up to the words yo vedādau svaraḥ proktaḥ, O Supreme Goddess. Then, having offered the handful of flowers, he should circumambulate three times.
m.6.8.35: Filled with supreme devotion, he should bow to him with the eight limbs touching the ground; having again circumambulated, he should once more bow a single time.
m.6.8.36: Seated on his seat, having worshipped the god with the eight names, he should say: Whatever act, good or bad, has been performed by me—
m.6.8.37: all that, O Lord Śambhu, is supreme worship of you. With these words he should offer it with conch-water together with a flower.
m.6.8.38: Having worshipped the Adorable One again, he should recite the eight names together with their meanings. Hear that very set, O Queen of the gods; I shall tell it to you because of your devotion.
m.6.8.iti: Thus ends the eighth adhyāya, named The description of the worship of the enclosures, in the sixth saṃhitā, the Kailāsa-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.6.9.1: Īśvara said: Śiva, Maheśvara, Rudra, Viṣṇu, Pitāmaha, Saṃsāravaidya (Physician of Worldly Existence), Sarvajña (All-knowing), and Paramātman (Supreme Self): these are the principal names.
m.6.9.2: This set of eight names always denotes Śiva. Of these, the first five correspond in order to Śāntyatītā and the rest.
m.6.9.3: They are the designations of Sadāśiva and the others, owing to the assumption of five limiting adjuncts (upādhi); but when the adjunct ceases, each designation ceases accordingly.
m.6.9.4: The office (pada) alone is eternal; those who hold the office are held to be non-eternal. There is a change of office-holders, since the holders become liberated.
m.6.9.5: Thus, in another cycle of change, again through his adjunct, the name would designate another soul; such is the first group of five names.
m.6.9.6: The other triad of names, however, arises from the distinction of material cause and the like; through the arrangement of the threefold adjunct it is Śiva alone who abides in them.
m.6.9.7: Because there is from the outset no contact with beginningless impurity, he is by nature a self utterly pure; hence he is called Śiva.
m.6.9.8: Or else, the Lord, being a single dense mass of all auspicious qualities, is called Śiva by the virtuous who know the meaning of the Śiva-principle.
m.6.9.9: Prakṛti is said to be beyond the twenty-three principles (tattva); beyond Prakṛti they declare the Puruṣa, the twenty-fifth.
m.6.9.10: It is that which they call the syllable (svara) at the beginning of the Veda, by the relation of denoted and denoter; knowable through the Veda alone in its true nature, and established in the Vedānta.
m.6.9.11: That very Puruṣa, merged in Prakṛti, is the enjoyer, since he enjoys Prakṛti; the one who is beyond him who is merged in Prakṛti, he is Maheśvara.
m.6.9.12: He is so called because the activity of Prakṛti and Puruṣa depends on him. Or else, this imperishable principle of three guṇas is māyā.
m.6.9.13: One should know Prakṛti as māyā and Maheśvara as the wielder of māyā. The Infinite one who releases from māyā is so through connection with Maheśvara.
m.6.9.14: Rud is sorrow, or the cause of sorrow; the Lord who drives that away is called Rudra. Hence Śiva is the supreme cause.
m.6.9.15: Śiva pervades and presides over everything from the Śiva-principle down to earth, bodies and the like, and pots and the like; hence he is called Viṣṇu.
m.6.9.16: Because Śiva is the father of all, even of those embodied beings who are the fathers of the world, he is declared Pitāmaha.
m.6.9.17: Just as a physician who knows the root cause removes a disease by remedies and medicines, so Śiva, the controller of dissolution, enjoyment and authority,
m.6.9.18: the Lord of saṃsāra, ever the remover of gross existence, is called Saṃsāravaidya by the knowers of the meaning of all principles.
m.6.9.19: Even though the sense organs exist for accomplishing the fivefold knowledge, the bound souls do not know the things of the three times, gross and subtle, in their entirety.
m.6.9.20: the bound souls (aṇu), covered by the impurity of the ocean of māyā, do not know. But even when all these senses are absent, Sadāśiva, knower of all things that are established,
m.6.9.21: Sadāśiva knows effortlessly every object exactly as it stands; therefore he is called Sarvajña.
m.6.9.22: Being the Self of all through eternal union with these supreme qualities, and since there is no self higher than himself, Śiva himself is Paramātman.
m.6.9.23: Having thus praised Mahādeva, the imperishable one whose self is the praṇava, and having offered arghya and pādya before him, then on the head of Īśāna,
m.6.9.24: having again worshipped the Lord of gods with the praṇava, concentrated, and taking the worship-flower with hands joined in añjali,
m.6.9.25: having led Śiva up to the Unmanī state by way of the left nostril, and then having dismissed the Goddess by way of the right nostril,
m.6.9.26: and having experienced oneness with him in the thought, I am Śiva alone, he should again dismiss all the deities of the enclosures (āvaraṇa) into the heart.
m.6.9.27: Having performed the worship of Vidyā and the worship of the guru, he should afterwards place in the heart, in due sequence, the mantras of the conch and the arghya vessel.
m.6.9.28: Then, having offered the used offerings (nirmālya) to Caṇḍīśa in the north-east (Īśa's quarter), and again with breath restrained, he should then recite the ṛṣi and the rest.
m.6.9.29: This maṇḍala, named Kailāsaprastara, has been described. One should worship it daily, or every fortnight, or every month,
m.6.9.30: or every six months, or yearly, or on festival occasions such as Cāturmāsya; but the believer must without fail worship my liṅga regularly.
m.6.9.31: In that procedure, O Great Goddess, a certain special point is told: on the day of initiation, the liṅga worshipped together with the guru
m.6.9.32: he should receive, saying, I shall worship Śiva until the end of my life, uttering this oath three times in the presence of the guru.
m.6.9.33: Then he should worship daily by the procedure stated earlier, O beloved, and offer arghya on the top of the liṅga with arghya water.
m.6.9.34: Having worshipped with the praṇava, he should offer incense and lamp; having worshipped Caṇḍa in the north-east, he should present the nirmālya to him.
m.6.9.35: Then, having washed the liṅga and the altar with water filtered through cloth, and having placed a flower on the top of the liṅga with the praṇava,
m.6.9.36: and having mentally contemplated everything from the Ādhāraśakti up to the seat of Śuddhavidyā, he should install the Supreme Lord.
m.6.9.37: With substances such as pañcagavya, gathered according to one's means, or with pure water alone scented with fragrant substances,
m.6.9.38: with the Pāvamāna, the Rudra, the Nīla and the Tvarita hymns, with Ṛk or Sāman verses, and with the five Brahma-mantras,
m.6.9.39: he should bathe the Lord of the gods of gods with the praṇava and the Śiva mantra; and he should also anoint him with the special arghya water, using the praṇava.
m.6.9.40: Having wiped it with a cloth, he should place a flower on the top of the liṅga; having set the liṅga on the pedestal, he should perform the worship of Sūrya and the others.
m.6.9.41: Below the seat (pīṭha) one should worship the two, Ādhāraśakti and Ananta; and above that, having worshipped the lion-throne in due order,
m.6.9.42: then one should worship the upper covering; at the foot of the seat one should worship Skanda. Having conceived my form in the liṅga, one should worship me together with you,
m.6.9.43: properly, with devotion and according to the rule — the ascetic intent on meditation on me. Thus I have told you this most secret teaching, O beloved.
m.6.9.44: It must be guarded with effort and not given to just anyone. It should be given to my devotee, to an ascetic free from passion,
m.6.9.45: devoted to the guru, tranquil, a partaker of yoga for my sake. Whoever, deluded in mind, transgresses my command and gives this to others,
m.6.9.46: he will go to hell and be my enemy; there is no doubt. But by giving it to my devotee, O Queen of the gods, one surely becomes dear to me; having enjoyed all pleasures here, he attains my presence.
m.6.9.47: Vyāsa said: Having heard this spoken by Mahādeva, the great Goddess praised the god with various hymns imbued with the meaning of the Vedas,
m.6.9.48: and the Supreme Goddess, bowing at the glorious lotus-feet of her husband, rejoiced with a heart overflowing with delight, O best of sages.
m.6.9.49: This, O brahmins, is most secret, revealing the meaning of the Praṇava; it is supreme in the knowledge of Śiva and destroys your afflictions.
m.6.9.50: Sūta said: Having spoken thus, the tiger among sages, Pārāśarya of great austerity, honoured with supreme devotion by the sages who expound the Veda,
m.6.9.51: recalling Mount Kailāsa, departed from that penance-grove. They too, with delighted hearts, at the end of the sacrificial session worshipped the Supreme Lord,
m.6.9.52: having worshipped with supreme devotion Soma (Śiva with Umā), who bears the half-moon as crest, they became devoted to yoga beginning with yama and intent on meditation on Śiva.
m.6.9.53: This was told by the Goddess to Guha, and by him to Nandin; and that blessed one declared it to the sage Sanatkumāra.
m.6.9.54: From him it was received by my guru Vyāsa of immeasurable splendour; and from him, O foremost sages, I too received this holy teaching.
m.6.9.55: I have made you hear this supreme teaching, more secret than the secret, dear to Giriśa, knowing you through your devotion to be dear to Śiva.
m.6.9.56: You too should give this secret, dear to Śiva, to ascetics of tranquil mind who are devoted to Śiva's feet.
m.6.9.57: Having said this, the greatly fortunate Sūta, best of Purāṇa-narrators, wandered over this earth on a pilgrimage to holy places.
m.6.9.58: Having received this supreme secret from Sūta, the lords among sages, dwelling in Kāśī itself, were liberated and went to the abode of Śiva.
m.6.9.iti: Thus ends the ninth adhyāya, named The description of the procedure concerning the meaning of the praṇava, in the sixth saṃhitā, the Kailāsa-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.6.10.1: Vyāsa said: Then, after Sūta had gone, the sages, greatly astonished, reflected among themselves: This has been forgotten: the doctrine of Vāmadeva that was set forth by the lord of sages. That is truly a hardship for us today.
m.6.10.2: When might we experience the sight of that excellent sage, which is supreme and removes the flood of sorrows of the ocean of worldly existence? Through the merit of worshipping Maheśvara, may the lord of sages now quickly appear before us.
m.6.10.3: Thus filled with anxious thought, the sages worshipped Vyāsa, the foremost of sages, in the lotus of their hearts, and remained eager to see him Sūta.
m.6.10.4: At the end of a year that great sage again reached Kāśī, devoted to Śiva-bhakti, wise, the illuminator of the meaning of the Purāṇas.
m.6.10.5: Seeing that Sūta approaching, the sages, delighted at heart, honoured him with the customary worship of rising to greet him, offering a seat, arghya water and so on.
m.6.10.6: He too, having smilingly greeted those tigers among sages, joyfully bathed in the supremely purifying water of the Jāhnavī (Gaṅgā),
m.6.10.7: and having satisfied the sages, the gods and the ancestors with sesame and rice, he came to the bank, sprinkled himself, and put on two garments.
m.6.10.8: Having sipped water twice, having taken the ashes with the Sadyojāta and other mantras, and having applied them in the prescribed order beginning with smearing, the lord of sages then
m.6.10.9: adorned with a rudrākṣa garland, having performed his daily rites, the wise one drew the tripuṇḍra on the prescribed parts of the body according to rule.
m.6.10.10: He worshipped Viśveśvara, the beloved of Umā, together with his son and with the lord of the gaṇas, with true devotion, and praised him, bowing again and again.
m.6.10.11: Then, having worshipped Lord Kālabhairava according to rule, he circumambulated him, and again bowed three times and five times.
m.6.10.12: Again circumambulating and prostrating on the ground like a staff, he praised him with a supreme hymn, remembering his lotus feet.
m.6.10.13: Having recited the glorious five-syllable vidyā one thousand and eight times, standing before him, and having begged forgiveness of Maheśvara,
m.6.10.14: and then having worshipped Caṇḍīśa, he took the seat in the middle of the Mukti-maṇḍapa that was indicated to him by the sages who had mastered the Vedas.
m.6.10.15: When all were thus seated, having bowed with mantras, he then spoke words that increased the devotion of the chief sages.
m.6.10.16: Sūta said: Blessed are you, very wise sages of laudable vows. For your sake I have come here; hear this account of it.
m.6.10.17: After I had instructed you in the meaning of the Praṇava and went off on a pilgrimage to the sacred places, I now tell you that story.
m.6.10.18: Setting out from here, I reached the shore of the southern ocean, bathed, and duly worshipped the goddess Śivā in the form of a maiden (Kanyā); then, O chief brahmins, coming back to the bank of the Suvarṇamukharī,
m.6.10.19: in the most wonderful city named after the Śrī Kālahasti mountain, having bathed in the water of the Suvarṇamukharī, and offering libations to the gods and also the sages,
m.6.10.20: having duly satisfied them with devotion, remembering the ocean and Giriśa, I worshipped Kālahastīśa, whose radiance equals that of the moonstone,
m.6.10.21: facing west, five-headed, most wonderful, who by a single sight alone is the cause of the destruction of all sins,
m.6.10.22: bestower of all siddhis, giver of enjoyment and liberation, lord of the three guṇas. And then with supreme devotion, I worshipped his Śivā standing at his right side,
m.6.10.23: having worshipped Jñānaprasūnakalikā, the mother of the world, and the glorious five-syllable vidyā one thousand and eight times
m.6.10.24: having recited, I circumambulated, praised and bowed again and again.
m.6.10.25: Then, circumambulating the mountain every day with reverence, firm in my observances day after day, I rejoiced greatly, as it were, in my mind.
m.6.10.26: Thus, O lords of sages, I spent four months there by the grace of the great goddess Jñānaprasūnakalikā.
m.6.10.27: Once, having spread an excellent seat of cloth, deerskin and kuśa grass laid one upon another, the sage I, seated on it with senses restrained,
m.6.10.28: entering samādhi, a dense mass of supreme bliss and consciousness, with the conviction I am Śiva, perfectly full, I became one whose heart was wholly untroubled.
m.6.10.29: At that very moment my guru, an ocean of compassion, resembling a dark rain-cloud, bearing matted locks tawny as lightning,
m.6.10.30: tall, himself carrying a water-pot, a staff and a black deerskin, all his limbs white with ash, marked with every auspicious sign,
m.6.10.31: his forehead shining with the tripuṇḍra, his form adorned with rudrākṣas, his two eyes long and wide and reddish like lotus petals,
m.6.10.32: appeared swiftly in the lotus of my heart at that very moment. I was then bewildered — such was this marvel, O faithful ones.
m.6.10.33: Then, opening my eyes, I lamented, and my tears poured down like a mountain waterfall.
m.6.10.34: At that very moment a bodiless voice, most wondrous, was heard from the sky, O brahmins; listen to it attentively.
m.6.10.35: O son of Sūta, highly fortunate one, go to the city of Vārāṇasī. There are the sages whom you instructed before; now
m.6.10.36: they intensely long, helpless, for the blessing of your arrival; they remain without food. Having said this, it fell silent.
m.6.10.37: Then, rising quickly, I devoutly circumambulated the god and the goddess, and again prostrated on the ground like a staff
m.6.10.38: twelve times; then, understanding the command of my guru and of Śiva and Śivā, I left the sacred place quickly, and within forty days
m.6.10.39: I have arrived, O best of sages; may you favour me here. What should I speak about today? Tell me that.
m.6.10.40: Hearing these words of Sūta, the sages, delighted in mind, bowing again and again to Vyāsa, spoke to that tiger among sages.
m.6.10.iti: Thus ends the tenth adhyāya, named The teaching of Sūta, in the sixth saṃhitā, the Kailāsa-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.6.11.1: The sages said: O Sūta, O Sūta, most fortunate one, you are our supreme teacher. Therefore we question you, if we have your favour.
m.6.11.2: That teachers like you are always affectionate toward faithful disciples — this you have now shown us.
m.6.11.3: Formerly, at the time of the Virajā fire-offering, you alluded to the teaching of Vāmadeva, but we did not hear it in detail, O sage.
m.6.11.4: Now all of us wish to hear it with faith and the greatest reverence; O ocean of compassion, please relate it with kindness.
m.6.11.5: Hearing these words of theirs, Sūta, his hair bristling with joy, bowed to Mahādeva, the teacher higher than every teacher,
m.6.11.6: and to Mahādevī, mother of the three worlds, and devotedly to his teacher Vyāsa; then, in a deep voice, delighting the sages, he spoke this.
m.6.11.7: Sūta said: May all be well with you, O sages; may you always be happy — devotees of Śiva, steadfast in mind, promoters of devotion to Śiva.
m.6.11.8: That account, most wonderful indeed, I heard from the lotus-mouth of my teacher; I did not tell it before now, fearing to reveal a secret.
m.6.11.9: You are indeed most fortunate, devotees of Śiva, firm in your vows; having ascertained this, I shall tell you — listen with joy.
m.6.11.10: Long ago, in the Rathantara kalpa, the great sage Vāmadeva, liberated already in the womb, was himself the foremost teacher among the knowers of Śiva-knowledge.
m.6.11.11: He knew the true import of all scriptures — Vedas, Āgamas, Purāṇas and the rest — and knew the births and deeds of beings such as gods, demons and humans.
m.6.11.12: His whole body white with ash, adorned with a circle of matted locks, without shelter, free of desire, beyond the pairs of opposites, free of ego,
m.6.11.13: sky-clad, possessed of great wisdom, like a second Maheśvara, surrounded by eminent sages like himself who had become his disciples,
m.6.11.14: wandering over this earth, purifying it by the merit of the touch of his feet, his heart immersed day by day in the supreme abode,
m.6.11.15: joyfully entered Kumāra's Peak, south of Meru, where dwells the Lord, the son of Īśa, who rides the peacock,
m.6.11.16: the hero who bears the spear of knowledge, crusher of all asuras, accompanied by Gajāvallī, saluted by all the gods.
m.6.11.17: There is a lake named Skanda-saras, like an ocean, with cool, sweet water to drink, clear, deep and abundant,
m.6.11.18: endowed with every wondrous quality, lying near the Lord. Having bathed there with his disciples, the great sage Vāmadeva,
m.6.11.19: saw Kumāra seated on the peak, attended by hosts of sages, resplendent like the rising sun, having the excellent peacock as his mount,
m.6.11.20: four-armed, noble of form, adorned with a crown and other ornaments, worshipped by his two jewel-like consorts, holding the spear and the cock,
m.6.11.21: with hands in the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness — having seen Skanda, the lord of sages worshipped him with supreme devotion and began to praise him.
m.6.11.22: Vāmadeva said: Om, salutation to the meaning of the Praṇava, to the one who establishes the Praṇava's meaning, to the seed of the Praṇava syllable, to the Praṇava — salutation again and again.
m.6.11.23: Salutation again and again to the one whose form is the meaning of Vedānta, who expounds the meaning of Vedānta, who knows the meaning of Vedānta, and who is eternally known.
m.6.11.24: Salutation to Guha, who is hidden in the caves of the hearts of beings; to the secret one, whose form is secret, who knows the secret Āgamas.
m.6.11.25: Salutation to you, subtler than the subtle, greater even than the great, knower of the higher and the lower, whose nature is the Supreme Self.
m.6.11.26: Salutation always to Skanda, whose form is Skanda, whose splendour is ruddy like the sun, who wears a crown and other ornaments shining with mandāra garlands.
m.6.11.27: Salutation to the disciple of Śiva, the son of Śiva, the giver of auspiciousness, the beloved of Śiva, the treasure of bliss for Śiva and Śivā.
m.6.11.28: Salutation to you, son of Gaṅgā, Kārttikeya, the wise, the great son of Umā, who lay in the forest of reeds.
m.6.11.29: Salutation again and again to the six-faced one, whose body is the six-syllabled mantra, who establishes the sixfold meaning, whose form transcends the six paths.
m.6.11.30: To you with twelve wide eyes, with twelve raised arms, bearing twelve weapons — O twelvefold Self, salutation be to you.
m.6.11.31: Salutation to the four-armed, the peaceful, bearer of spear and cock, whose hands grant boons and fearlessness, the destroyer of asuras.
m.6.11.32: Salutation to him whose chest is marked with saffron smeared from Gajāvallī's breasts, whose self is gladdened by the joy and glory of Gajānana.
m.6.11.33: To you, abode of glory contemplated in purity through special songs sung by Brahmā and other gods, sages and Kinnaras; O you whose charming lotus-feet are worshipped with garlands adorning the spotless crowns of the gods — salutation be to you.
m.6.11.34: Whoever recites or even hears this divine hymn to Skanda spoken by Vāmadeva attains the supreme goal.
m.6.11.35: This indeed produces great wisdom, increases devotion to Śiva, brings long life, health and wealth, and always grants all desires.
m.6.11.36: Having thus praised the god, the Lord, the commander of the army, Vāmadeva circumambulated him three times and prostrated on the ground like a staff,
m.6.11.37: and again performing the eight-limbed prostration with circumambulation and salutation, he stood at his side, bowed in humility, O brahmins.
m.6.11.38: Hearing the hymn composed by Vāmadeva, unfolding the highest truth, the Lord, son of Maheśvara, became pleased.
m.6.11.39: Mahāsena said to him: I am pleased with your worship, devotion and praise. Blessings to you. What shall I do for you today?
m.6.11.40: O sage, you are the foremost of yogins, wholly fulfilled and free of desire; for such as you there is indeed nothing in this world to be sought.
m.6.11.41: Even so, for the protection of dharma and out of a wish to favour the worlds, good and holy men like you wander over the earth.
m.6.11.42: If there is something you wish to hear, O brahmin, you should state it now; then I shall now explain it for the sake of favouring the worlds.
m.6.11.43: Having heard these words of Skanda, the great sage Vāmadeva, bowed down in humility, spoke in a voice deep as a rain-cloud.
m.6.11.44: Vāmadeva said: O Lord, you are the supreme ruler, the bestower of both higher and lower glories, omniscient, the maker of all, the bearer of all powers, the master.
m.6.11.45: We are mere embodied souls, unfit to speak in the presence of you, the supreme ruler; yet it is your grace that you speak to me.
m.6.11.46: O greatly wise one, I am fulfilled by even a mere particle of your knowledge. Urged on, I ask further; my transgression should be forgiven.
m.6.11.47: The praṇava is indeed supreme, directly the word that denotes the Supreme Lord; what it denotes is the god Paśupati, who releases the bound souls (paśu) from their fetter.
m.6.11.48: Invoked by the denoting word, he frees the bound souls in an instant; therefore the praṇava is established as the word denoting Śiva.
m.6.11.49: Om — all this is Om, says the eternal Veda; and it declared, Om is Brahman; all this indeed is Brahman.
m.6.11.50: Salutation to you, commander of the gods' army, lord of the gods; salutation to the lord of ascetics; salutation to you, the all-complete.
m.6.11.51: This being so, in this world nothing exists other than Śiva; the master who bears all forms is Śiva, the all-pervading Maheśvara.
m.6.11.52: I have heard the meaning of the praṇava in terms of its collective and individual aspects; but never, O Mahāsena, have I found a teacher like you.
m.6.11.53: Therefore, showing compassion, you should explain that meaning by the method of formal instruction and in accordance with the order of right conduct.
m.6.11.54: You are the sole master of all beings, the teacher who cuts their fetters; therefore, O teacher, that meaning must be heard by me through your grace.
m.6.11.55: Thus questioned by the sage, Skanda bowed to Sadāśiva, whose body is the praṇava, marked by the excellent thirty-eight kalās, with Umā ever at his side and attended by the foremost sages, and began to expound the supreme good, hidden even in the Vedas.
m.6.11.iti: Thus ends the eleventh adhyāya, named The description of Brahman to Vāmadeva, in the sixth saṃhitā, the Kailāsa-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.6.12.1: Śrī Brahmaṇya said: Excellent, excellent, O greatly fortunate Vāmadeva, lord of sages! You are exceedingly devoted to Śiva and the best among those who possess knowledge of Śiva.
m.6.12.2: There is nothing anywhere in the worlds that is unknown to you; even so, I shall speak to you, who work for the benefit of the worlds.
m.6.12.3: In this world all bound souls (paśus) are deluded by various scriptures, deceived by the exceedingly wondrous māyā of the Supreme Lord.
m.6.12.4: They do not know Maheśvara, the Supreme, who is directly the meaning of the Praṇava — Brahman with and without attributes, the supreme progenitor of the three gods.
m.6.12.5: Raising my right arm, I declare an oath to you: it is true, true, again true; true, true, again and again.
m.6.12.6: Śiva himself is proclaimed as principally the meaning of the Praṇava in the Śrutis, in the Smṛti treatises, in the Purāṇas and in the Āgamas.
m.6.12.7: He from whom words turn back, together with the mind, without reaching him; knowing whose bliss the wise one fears nothing from anywhere.
m.6.12.8: From whom this entire universe, beginning with Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Indra, together with the groups of elements and senses, is first brought forth;
m.6.12.9: Who indeed is never born from anything at any time; in whom neither lightning shines, nor the sun, nor the moon;
m.6.12.10: By whose light this whole universe shines on all sides; endowed with all lordship, he himself is by name Sarveśvara (Lord of all).
m.6.12.11: Śambhu, who is to be meditated upon by those seeking liberation, abiding in the midst of the inner space, all-pervading, self-luminous, of the form of radiance, consisting of consciousness;
m.6.12.12: Of which Person the supreme Śakti is attainable through devotion, enchanting, without attributes, concealed by her own qualities, partless and auspicious (Śivā).
m.6.12.13: His form is threefold: gross, subtle, and then the supreme. O sage, it is to be meditated upon constantly and in sequence by yogins seeking liberation.
m.6.12.14: He who is partless, the eternal primal god of all gods, whose nature is knowledge and action, is sung of as the Supreme Self.
m.6.12.15: The embodied form of that God of gods is Sadāśiva himself, the god whose body is the five mantras and whose figure is the set of five kalās.
m.6.12.16: Resembling pure crystal, serene, of cool radiance, the Lord has five faces, ten arms and fifteen eyes.
m.6.12.17: The ancient one has Īśāna as his crown, Tatpuruṣa as his face, Aghora as his heart, and Vāmadeva as his secret parts;
m.6.12.18: and Sadyojāta as his feet. That form is directly both with parts and partless; his body is made of six limbs consisting of the six powers beginning with omniscience.
m.6.12.19: He is resplendent with a heart-lotus pulsing with the powers beginning with sound, and adorned on his left side by his own Śakti, Manonmanī.
m.6.12.20: By way of setting forth the meanings of the six kinds of meaning beginning with the mantra, I shall explain the sense of the collective and individual aspects, which is of the nature of the Praṇava.
m.6.12.21: First, the order of instruction must be stated; listen to it. O sage, the four-class order is well known in this human world.
m.6.12.22: Here, conformity to Vedic practice belongs only to the three twice-born classes; the Śūdras, whose essential duty is service alone, are excluded from the Veda.
m.6.12.23: For all members of the three classes, devoted to their respective stages of life, the dharma declared in Śruti and Smṛti is to be practised, and never any other.
m.6.12.24: Performing the action enjoined by Śruti and Smṛti, one will attain perfection — so declared the Supreme Lord, who reveals the Vedic path.
m.6.12.25: Having worshipped the Supreme Lord through the merits of the conduct of their class and stage of life, many excellent sages have all attained union (sāyujya) with him.
m.6.12.26: The sages are satisfied by celibate study, the gods by the path of sacrificial rites, the ancestors by progeny — so indeed the Śruti has said.
m.6.12.27: Thus freed from the three debts, having entered the forest-dweller stage, enduring cold and heat, pleasure and pain and the like, with senses subdued,
m.6.12.28: an ascetic with controlled diet should practise yoga beginning with yama, so that his understanding becomes very firm and unshakable.
m.6.12.29: Thus, purified in self by stages, he should lay aside all actions; having renounced all actions, he should become devoted to the worship of knowledge.
m.6.12.30: For that worship directly grants the fruit of liberation-in-life through oneness with Śiva; it should be known as the highest of all, changeless, for the self-controlled.
m.6.12.31: I shall describe its procedure out of desire to benefit the world and out of affection for you, O greatly wise one; listen attentively.
m.6.12.32: That ascetic should approach a preceptor who knows the essence of the meaning of all scriptures, who has mastered the knowledge of Vedānta, the best among the wise.
m.6.12.33: Going near him according to rule, the discerning, wise one should diligently please him with full-length prostrations and the like.
m.6.12.34: He who is the guru is declared to be Śiva; he who is Śiva is held to be the guru — having resolved this in his mind, he should make known his intention.
m.6.12.35: Having obtained permission from the guru, he should observe a milk-only vow for twelve days, and then, according to rule, on the fourth or the tenth day of the bright fortnight,
m.6.12.36: having bathed at dawn, pure in self, having performed his daily rites, the wise one should invite the guru and begin the Nāndī-śrāddha according to rule.
m.6.12.37: The Viśvedevas are declared to be those named Satya and Vasu; in the Deva-śrāddha, the three — Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Maheśa — are mentioned.
m.6.12.38: In the Ṛṣi-śrāddha, the sages born among the gods, of the holy fields and among men are declared; and in the Deva-śrāddha, the Vasus, Rudras and Ādityas are proclaimed.
m.6.12.39: In the human śrāddha, the four lords of sages beginning with Sanaka; in the Bhūta-śrāddha, the five great elements, and after that,
m.6.12.40: the group of senses beginning with the eye, and the fourfold class of beings; in the Pitṛ-śrāddha, the three: the father, his father, and his father.
m.6.12.41: In the śrāddha for the mothers, the recipients are the mother, the paternal grandmother and the great-grandmother. In the śrāddha for oneself there are four: oneself, the father and the grandfather,
m.6.12.42: and the one called the great-grandfather; these are declared to be honoured together with their wives. In the śrāddha for the maternal grandfathers there are three: the maternal grandfather and the others.
m.6.12.43: For each śrāddha, having arranged the invited brāhmaṇas in pairs, having called them, washed their feet, and having himself carefully sipped water,
m.6.12.44: May the dust of the brāhmaṇas' feet purify me — dust that is the cause of attaining all prosperity, a comet of destruction to the host of calamities that have arisen, a bridge across the shoreless ocean of saṃsāra.
m.6.12.45: May the dust of the brāhmaṇas' feet protect me — dust that is a thousand-rayed sun to the darkness of the dense cloud of calamity, a wish-granting cow bestowing desired objects, whose form is pure like the waters of all the holy places.
m.6.12.46: Having muttered this and bowed with all eight limbs on the ground like a staff, standing facing east, remembering the pair of lotus-feet of Śambhu,
m.6.12.47: with the kuśa-ring in his hand, pure, wearing the sacred thread, firm in his seat, he should perform three breath-controls, having again heard the statement of the lunar day and so on, and resolve:
m.6.12.48: That which is a component of my saṃnyāsa — the eightfold śrāddha beginning with the Viśvedevas and ending with the maternal grandfathers — by the pārvaṇa method,
m.6.12.49: I shall perform according to rule, with your permission preceding. Having made the resolve thus, he should cast away the darbha grass to the north.
m.6.12.50: Having touched water and risen, he should begin the sequence of choosing the brāhmaṇas. With the kuśa-ring in hand, touching the hands of the two brāhmaṇas, he should say:
m.6.12.51: For the sake of the Viśvedevas, and so on, and also, the occasion be granted by you two,
m.6.12.52: ending with, is to be graciously granted. This is the order of procedure in every case. Having thus completed the choosing, he should prepare the maṇḍalas,
m.6.12.53: ten of them, beginning from the north, and having worshipped them with unbroken rice, having seated the brāhmaṇas in them in order, again at their feet
m.6.12.54: he should utter the names of the Viśvedevas and the rest in the vocative, saying, This is water for your feet, with water containing kuśa, flowers and unbroken rice.
m.6.12.55: Having offered the foot-water, himself also with feet washed, facing north, having sipped water, and having seated those brāhmaṇas arranged in pairs on their seats,
m.6.12.56: having given a seat of darbha, saying, This is the seat for the brāhmaṇa who is in the form of the Viśvedevas, he himself, standing with darbha in hand,
m.6.12.57: having said, In this Nāndīmukha śrāddha, for the sake of the Viśvedevas, the occasion is to be granted by you two, should say, let it be done.
m.6.12.58: Having declared, may it obtain, he should say, you two, so that it runs, may you two obtain; and those two eminent brāhmaṇas should reply, may we two obtain.
m.6.12.59: Saying to them, May it be complete, may there be fulfilment of the resolve, he should entreat the eminent twice-born: May you favour me.
m.6.12.60: Then, in clean, washed vessels of plantain-leaf and the like, having served rice and other edibles, and separately with darbha,
m.6.12.61: having himself spread them around there and sprinkled water around, then respectfully holding each vessel with both hands,
m.6.12.62: having recited, The earth is your vessel, and so on, and naming in the dative the deities and others stationed there, together with unbroken rice,
m.6.12.63: taking water towards the north, he should then offer the food for the deity with svāhā; at the end he should say, not mine. This is the order of procedure everywhere.
m.6.12.64: I salute that Lord accompanied by Ambā, by remembering whose lotus-feet and even by muttering whose name a deficient rite becomes complete.
m.6.12.65: Having muttered this, he should then say: This Nāndīmukha śrāddha has been performed by me, and thereafter say as prescribed.
m.6.12.66: and, Please say, so be it; having propitiated those eminent twice-born, releasing the water held in his hand, and prostrating on the ground like a staff,
m.6.12.67: and having risen, he should then say to the brāhmaṇas, May it be nectar, and, noble-minded, with joined palms, he should entreat them with great affection.
m.6.12.68: Meditating on Sadāśiva in his mind, he should recite according to rule the Śrī Rudra, the Camaka, the Puruṣa Sūkta, and the five Brahman mantras.
m.6.12.69: At the end of the meal he should recite the Rudra Sūkta and again ask pardon of the brāhmaṇas; then with its mantra he should offer before them the concluding sip of water (uttarāpośana).
m.6.12.70: With feet washed, having sipped water, he should then go to the place of the piṇḍas; seated facing east, silent, he should perform three breath-controls,
m.6.12.71: resolving: I shall perform the offering of piṇḍas, a component of the śrāddha called Nāndīmukha. Having made this resolve, beginning from the south up to the north,
m.6.12.72: having drawn nine lines, and having spread twelve darbha blades in order with tips to the east, he should prepare the five places of the deities and others beginning from the south.
m.6.12.73: Silently he should offer water with unbroken rice in three places in order; in the other places, for the mothers, with the words mārjayantām thereafter.
m.6.12.74: Afterwards, with Here, O Fathers (atra pitaraḥ), having worshipped with water and unbroken rice, he should then offer in order in the five places of the deities and others,
m.6.12.75: and, uttering the names of the respective deities and others with the dative ending, he should then offer three piṇḍas in each of the five places.
m.6.12.76: He should offer the piṇḍas separately by the method stated in his own Gṛhyasūtra, and he should offer this with unbroken rice for the sake of the ancestors' fulfilment.
m.6.12.77: He should meditate on the god Sadāśiva in the centre of the lotus of the heart, again reciting the verse beginning By remembering whose lotus-feet.
m.6.12.78: Having bowed to the brāhmaṇas and given them a fee according to his means, having asked their pardon and dismissed them, then in due order,
m.6.12.79: having removed the piṇḍas, he should give them as a mouthful for a cow, or else cast them into water. Having performed the puṇyāhavācana, he should eat together with his kinsmen.
m.6.12.80: On the next day, rising at dawn, the wise man, having performed his daily rites and having fasted, should undergo shaving and the rest, excluding the armpits and the private parts.
m.6.12.81: Having removed the hair of the head, the beard and the nails, as the limit of the rite requires, and having had all the hair shaved properly, in accordance with the prescribed rule,
m.6.12.82: having bathed, wearing a washed cloth, pure, having sipped water twice, then restraining his speech, having applied holy ash according to rule and having performed the puṇyāha-vācana, the proclamation of the auspicious day,
m.6.12.83: having sprinkled himself with that water and thereby attained the natural state of a purified body, and having set aside what is needed for the materials of the fire-offering and for the preceptor's fee,
m.6.12.84: having then given away the rest of his possessions to Maheśa, and especially to the twice-born and to devotees, and to Śiva in the form of the guru,
m.6.12.85: having given a fee of clothes and the like, and bowed down on the ground like a staff, then taking the waist-string, loincloth, garment, staff and the rest, washed, placed on the ground,
m.6.12.86: and taking in due order the materials for the fire-offering, the fuel-sticks and the rest, — on a seashore, by a river, on a mountain, or in a temple of Śiva,
m.6.12.87: or in a forest, or in a cow-pen — having chosen an excellent spot, standing there and sipping water, then first performing the mental offering (mānasa-mañjarī),
m.6.12.88: having muttered three times the brāhma mantra together with Oṃkāra, and also namo brahmaṇe, salutation to Brahman, he should then recite agnim īḷe purohitam, the opening of the Ṛgveda,
m.6.12.89: then atha mahāvratam, and agnir vai devānām, and likewise the corpus of this Veda, iṣe tvorje tvā, the opening of the Yajurveda,
m.6.12.90: agna āyāhi vītaye, the opening of the Sāmaveda, śaṃ no devīr abhiṣṭaye, the opening of the Atharvaveda; afterwards he should recite the prosody formula with ma, ya, ra, sa, ta, ja, bha, na, la and ga,
m.6.12.91: then sammitam, then pañcasaṃvatsaramayam, the Jyotiṣa, then samāmnāyaḥ samāmnātaḥ, the Nirukta; then again he should recite the Śikṣā, uttering pravakṣyāmi (I shall expound), and then recite vṛddhir ādaic, Pāṇini's grammar.
m.6.12.92: Having uttered athāto dharmajijñāsā, the opening of the Mīmāṃsā-sūtra, and again promptly athāto brahmajijñāsā, the opening of the Brahma-sūtra, he should also mutter the beginnings of the Vedas and the rest.
m.6.12.93: Then the names Brahmā, Indra, Sūrya, Soma and Prajāpati, the Self, the inner Self, the knowledge-Self, and beyond that
m.6.12.94: and also the Supreme Self — having muttered each name in the dative case, beginning with Praṇava and ending with namaḥ, he should then take a handful of barley-meal
m.6.12.95: and having eaten it with the Praṇava alone, and having sipped water twice, he should touch his navel while reciting the mantras about to be stated, beginning with Praṇava and ending with namaḥ:
m.6.12.96: having uttered the Self, the inner Self, the knowledge-Self, again the supreme, and the Self, and after that Prajāpati,
m.6.12.97: he should then mutter these mantras ending with svāhā. Afterwards, having partaken of milk, curd and ghee separately, three times each with the Praṇava alone, he should again sip water twice.
m.6.12.98: Then, sitting down facing east, with a firm mind and a steady posture, he should properly perform three breath-controls according to the rule already stated.
m.6.12.iti: Thus ends the twelfth adhyāya, named The description of the rite of saṃnyāsa, in the sixth saṃhitā, the Kailāsa-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.6.13.1: Subrahmaṇya said: Then at midday, having bathed, with a controlled mind, one should bring the articles of worship: sandal paste, flowers, unbroken rice and the rest.
m.6.13.2: In the south-west one should worship the god Vighneśa, who is worshipped by the gods; one should invoke him with the mantra gaṇānāṃ tvā according to proper rule.
m.6.13.3: He is red in colour, huge in body, adorned with all ornaments, holding in his lotus-hands the noose, the goad, the rosary and the boon-granting gesture.
m.6.13.4: Having thus invoked and meditated upon the elephant-faced son of Śambhu, and having worshipped him with milk-rice, cakes, coconut, jaggery and the like,
m.6.13.5: one should offer excellent food-offering, and then betel and other things; having pleased him and bowed, one should then pray for freedom from obstacles.
m.6.13.6: In the aupāsana fire, according to the procedure stated in one's own Gṛhya-sūtra, the fire-rite up to the ājyabhāga offerings should be performed, and after this the main procedure of the sacrifice.
m.6.13.7: Having offered the full oblation with the three verses beginning bhūḥ svāhā and having concluded, one should, untiring, repeat the Gāyatrī until the afternoon.
m.6.13.8: Then, having performed the evening twilight worship preceded by a bath, and having offered the evening aupāsana, remaining silent, one should inform the guru.
m.6.13.9: Having cooked the caru in that fire, one should offer, with fuel-sticks, food and ghee separately, with the Raudra Sūkta and the five mantras beginning with Sadyojāta,
m.6.13.10: and with the Brahma-mantras; one should contemplate Mahādeva together with Ambā in the fire. Having offered with the mantra gaurīr mimāya, remembering Gaurī,
m.6.13.11: then one should offer once with agnaye sviṣṭakṛte svāhā. Having performed the concluding procedure, the wise one, then, to the north of the fire,
m.6.13.12: seated on a seat overspread with cloth, deerskin and kuśa grass, silent and firm of mind, should repeat the Gāyatrī until the Brāhma muhūrta.
m.6.13.13: Then, having bathed, or if unable, bathing with ash according to rule, having cooked the caru in that same fire, sprinkled with ghee,
m.6.13.14: having removed it to the north, placed it on the sacred grass and then sprinkled the caru with ghee, he should recite the vyāhṛtis, the Raudra Sūkta and the five
m.6.13.15: Brahma-mantras, fixing the mind on the lotus-feet of Śiva. Then Prajāpati, then Indra, and after that the Viśvedevas,
m.6.13.16: and Brahmā — in the dative, ending with svāhā and beginning with praṇava — having recited these and then having had the puṇyāha benediction recited, thereafter,
m.6.13.17: having completed the subsequent procedure from agnaye svāhā up to the agnimukha, afterwards, beginning with prāṇāya svāhā, with the five,
m.6.13.18: with caru mixed with ghee; afterwards he should offer to Agni Sviṣṭakṛt. And again he should recite the Raudra Sūkta and the five Brahma-mantras.
m.6.13.19: And again he should recite the mantras of the fourfold manifestation beginning with Maheśa. Having performed the concluding procedure by the method stated in one's own Vedic branch,
m.6.13.20: the discerning one should perform it with its subsidiary parts, directing it to the respective deities. Thus is the ritual procedure, beginning with the agnimukha, which has been set forth.
m.6.13.21: After this he should offer the Virajā homa for himself, for the purification of the self merged in this body consisting of the twenty-six tattvas,
m.6.13.22: remembering, May these tattvas in my body be purified. There, for the purification of the ātma-tattva, with the mantras of the Āruṇaketuka section,
m.6.13.23: being recited, in order from earth up to puruṣa, O sage, with caru mixed with ghee, silent, remembering the lotus-feet of Śiva.
m.6.13.24: Earth and the rest, sound and the rest, again the pentad beginning with speech, the pentad beginning with the ear, and the group of four — head, sides, back and belly —
m.6.13.25: and the shanks one should add; then the seven bodily constituents beginning with skin; then the pentad beginning with prāṇa; then the five sheaths beginning with the food-sheath;
m.6.13.26: mind, citta, intellect, ego, khyāti and saṅkalpa; then the guṇas, then prakṛti, and then puruṣa.
m.6.13.27: For the puruṣa, who has attained the state of enjoyer in the act of enjoyment, a pentad of tattvas is declared as the inner instrument.
m.6.13.28: Niyati, kāla, rāga, then vidyā, and kalā — this pentad, O lord of sages, has arisen from Māyā.
m.6.13.29: One should know Māyā to be Prakṛti — thus Māyā is spoken of in the śruti. These tattvas born of her are stated in the śruti; there is no doubt.
m.6.13.30: Time, inherent nature, niyati — so too the śruti declared. This very pentad is called his five sheaths (kañcukas).
m.6.13.31: Not knowing these five tattvas, even a learned man is deluded in mind. This puruṣa, placed below these five and above prakṛti,
m.6.13.32: resorting to the maxim of the crow's eye, abides daily at the side of both. This is called the vidyā-tattva. Śuddhavidyā, Maheśvara,
m.6.13.33: Sadāśiva, Śakti and Śiva — this pentad is the Śiva-tattva, O Brahman; it is prajñānaṃ brahma, meditated upon by one restrained in speech.
m.6.13.34: The whole group of tattvas from earth up to Śiva, O lord of sages — let its purification be effected through dissolution into its own cause.
m.6.13.35: For the eleven mantras, preceded by the word parasmai, one should then utter this word śivajyotiṣe in the dative.
m.6.13.36: Afterwards he should say na mama (not mine); this is called the renunciation of the dedicated offering. After this, for the two mantras viviḍḍhi and kaṣotkāya,
m.6.13.37: at the end of the word vyāpakāya he should add also paramātmane, śivajyotiṣe in the dative, and again the word viśvabhūta,
m.6.13.38: and then he should say the word ghasanotsuka in the dative; having uttered parasmai, he should utter the word devāya.
m.6.13.39: For the mantra uttiṣṭhasva, after the word viśvarūpāya he should say the word puruṣāya, and for it he should pronounce oṃ svāhā.
m.6.13.40: After the word loka-traya (the three worlds), he should then say the words: To the all-pervading Supreme Self, to Śiva, this is offered, not mine.
m.6.13.41: Having completed the preliminary rites in the manner prescribed by his own Vedic branch, and having eaten the caru mixed with ghee, to the priest
m.6.13.42: he should give to him a fee augmented with gold and other things. Then, having dismissed the Brahmā priest, he should perform the morning aupāsana oblation.
m.6.13.43: The man should recite the mantra saṃ mā siñcantu marutaḥ; and with the mantra yā te agne, having warmed his hand in the fire,
m.6.13.44: having placed his hand over the fire and taken the fire up into his own self, the abode of non-duality; then having performed the morning twilight worship, and then also worshipping the sun,
m.6.13.45: having attended upon the sun, entering the water and immersing himself up to the navel, he should recite those mantras with devotion, with steady mind and eager.
m.6.13.46: But one who maintains the sacred fires should properly perform the Prājāpatya sacrifice in the established śrauta Vaiśvānara fire, with a fee of all his possessions.
m.6.13.47: Then, having taken the fire into himself, the brāhmaṇa should go forth from home. Having uttered the first pāda of the Sāvitrī and the word sāvitrīm,
m.6.13.48: he should say bhūḥ om after the word praveśayāmi (I make enter). Having uttered the second pāda and sāvitrīm as before,
m.6.13.49: he should say bhūḥ om after the word praveśayāmi. Having uttered the third pāda, and after that sāvitrīm,
m.6.13.50: he should utter suvaḥ om after the word praveśayāmi. First he should utter the three pādas together, and after that sāvitrīm,
m.6.13.51: and after the word praveśayāmi he should then utter bhūr bhuvaḥ suvar om with devotion, with a steady mind, O lord of sages.
m.6.13.52: This Goddess is in very truth the one who forms half of Śaṅkara's body; she has five faces, ten arms, and shines with fifteen eyes.
m.6.13.53: She wears as crest-ornament the crescent moon rising on a crown of nine gems; she resembles pure crystal, bears ten weapons, and is auspicious.
m.6.13.54: Her limbs are adorned with necklaces, armlets, bracelets, girdle-bells, anklets and the like; she wears divine garments and jewelled ornaments.
m.6.13.55: She is always to be served by Viṣṇu, by Brahmā, by gods, sages, Gandharvas, Dānavas and men; she is Śivā, who pervades the selves of all.
m.6.13.56: She is the charming lawful wife of the god Sadāśiva, Mother of the world, Mother of the three worlds/deities, possessing the three guṇas yet free of guṇas, and unborn.
m.6.13.57: Having reflected thus, the wise one should then recite the Gāyatrī, the primordial Goddess, three-footed, unborn, who bestows brāhmaṇahood and the rest.
m.6.13.58: The sinner who recites the Gāyatrī, whose form is Śiva, otherwise than thus is cooked in a most terrible hell for a period of kalpas.
m.6.13.59: She arose from the vyāhṛtis and dissolves into them alone; and they arose from the Praṇava and dissolve into the Praṇava.
m.6.13.60: The Praṇava is the beginning of all the Vedas; the Praṇava denotes Śiva. It is the king of the kings of mantras, the great seed, the supreme mantra.
m.6.13.61: Śiva indeed is this Praṇava, or the Praṇava is declared to be Śiva, since there is no absolute difference between the denoted and that which denotes.
m.6.13.62: By causing beings who are leaving the body at death in Kāśī to hear this very great mantra, Śiva grants them supreme liberation.
m.6.13.63: Therefore the best of ascetics worship the one-syllabled god Śiva, the supreme cause, abiding in the middle of the heart-lotus.
m.6.13.64: Other steadfast seekers of liberation, and worldly men who have become dispassionate, having understood sense-objects with the mind, worship the supreme Śiva.
m.6.13.65: Having thus dissolved the Gāyatrī into the Praṇava, which denotes Śiva, he should then recite the anuvāka ahaṃ vṛkṣasya rerivā.
m.6.13.66: Reciting the anuvāka yaś chandasām ṛṣabhaḥ from its beginning up to its end with gopāya, he should afterwards say utthito'ham (I have arisen).
m.6.13.67: He should say and recite it three times, in low, middle and high tone in succession, O sage, first uttering the Praṇava, in the order of creation, maintenance and dissolution.
m.6.13.68: Then in order among them: bhūḥ saṃnyastam, likewise bhuvaḥ saṃnyastam, and having said suvaḥ saṃnyastam, uttering the word saṃnyastam,
m.6.13.69: at the end of all the mantras he should say the word mayā (by me). First uttering the Praṇava, he should say the vyāhṛtis together,
m.6.13.70: after that he should say samastam and mayā — so it has been declared — having meditated on Sadāśiva in the heart, then in the order of low tone and so on, O sage.
m.6.13.71: Having thus recited the praiṣa mantras with an attentive mind, reciting, Freedom from fear to all beings from me, svāhā,
m.6.13.72: taking up water toward the eastern direction, he should then cast out a handful. Then, pulling out the topknot and the sacred thread with his hand,
m.6.13.73: and holding them, he should say, Om bhūḥ, go to the ocean, uttering svāhā (Agni's wife); then with a handful of water
m.6.13.74: he should offer them into the water. Then, having consecrated water three times with the praiṣa mantras and sipped it, he should come to the bank and leave his clothes and other things on the ground.
m.6.13.75: Facing north or east, he should walk more than seven steps, some distance; then the teacher should say, Stop, stop.
m.6.13.76: For the sake of worldly conduct, he should give with his own hand a loincloth and a staff, saying, Revered one, accept these.
m.6.13.77: Having given the loincloth with a good string and then the ochre garment, and the disciple having covered himself and sipped water twice, he should address that disciple thus:
m.6.13.78: Then he should pronounce the mantra indrasya vajro'si (you are Indra's thunderbolt). Having made the request, the disciple should take the staff, reciting sakhāyaḥ.
m.6.13.79: Then, going to the side of the guru and remembering Śiva's lotus feet, he should prostrate on the ground like a staff three times, with self-restraint.
m.6.13.80: And rising again slowly, gazing with love at his own guru, he should stand near the guru's feet with his palms joined in reverence.
m.6.13.81: Even before the rite begins, he should take auspicious cow-dung, make it into balls the size of a large āmalaka fruit, and dry them,
m.6.13.82: by the rays of the sun alone. Placing them in the midst of the fire at the start of the homa, at the completion of the homa he should collect the ash and keep it safe.
m.6.13.83: Then the guru, taking the white ash produced from the Virajā fire, with that very ash, in due order, with the mantras beginning agniḥ,
m.6.13.84: touching the disciple's limbs with these mantras from the head down to the feet, and then with the five mantras beginning with Īśāna, starting from the head, all over the body,
m.6.13.85: having smeared the ash according to rule, he should then make him wear the tripuṇḍra, with the tryāyuṣa and tryambaka mantras, beginning from the head in due order.
