m.6.13.86: Then the excellent disciple, with a mind filled with true devotion, should meditate on Śiva, the companion of Umā, seated in the lotus of his heart.
m.6.13.87: Placing his hand on the disciple's head, the guru should utter the praṇava three times into his right ear, together with its ṛṣi and the rest.
m.6.13.88: Then, showing compassion, the best of gurus should teach the meaning of the praṇava, together with full knowledge of its six kinds of meaning.
m.6.13.89: He the disciple should prostrate to the guru on the ground like a staff in twelve ways. He should always remain dependent on him and should perform no other rite.
m.6.13.90: Then, by his command, the disciple should become devoted to the knowledge of Śiva in accordance with the meaning of the Vedānta, according to the distinction of Śiva with and without attributes.
m.6.13.91: Then the guru should have that very disciple perform the morning and other observances, preceded by the components beginning with hearing (śravaṇa), at the end of the japa.
m.6.13.92: And the worship, in that maṇḍala called Kailāsaprastara — the disciple should perform worship right there, by the method taught by Śiva.
m.6.13.93: If he is unable to worship the deity there daily, he should receive from the guru an auspicious crystal liṅga of the Lord, furnished with a pedestal.
m.6.13.94: He vows: Better for me the giving up of life, even the cutting off of my head, but I shall not eat without having worshipped the blessed three-eyed Lord.
m.6.13.95: Uttering this oath three times in the presence of the guru, the disciple, firm of mind and bearing devotion to Śiva, should take it.
m.6.13.96: From then on, with a mind ever zealous, he should worship Mahādeva daily with supreme devotion according to the method of the five enclosures (pañcāvaraṇa).
m.6.13.iti: Thus ends the thirteenth adhyāya in the sixth saṃhitā, the Kailāsa-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.6.14.1: Vāmadeva said: O Lord, six-faced one, ocean of the nectar of complete knowledge, son of the lord of all the gods, destroyer of the distress of those who bow down to you,
m.6.14.2: What is this knowledge of the sixfold meaning that has been declared to grant what is desired? What are the six kinds of meaning there, and what is that knowledge, O Lord?
m.6.14.3: And who is the one it sets forth, and what is the fruit of knowing it? Explain all this, everything that I have asked, O Guha.
m.6.14.4: Not knowing this meaning, deluded by the teachings meant for bound souls (paśu-śāstra), I am even now confused by Śiva's māyā, O Mahāsena.
m.6.14.5: So that I, having drunk the elixir of the nectar of knowledge of Śiva's pair of feet, may become free from delusion—
m.6.14.6: —in that way, looking upon me for a long time with a glance moist with the nectar of compassion, grace should be shown to me, who have taken refuge at your glorious lotus-feet.
m.6.14.7: Having heard these words spoken by the lord of sages, the all-pervading one who holds the power of knowledge spoke words that cause great terror to other doctrines.
m.6.14.8: Subrahmaṇya said: Listen, O tiger among sages, to what you have asked with reverence: the knowledge of the Great Lord in terms of the collective and the individual.
m.6.14.9: That knowledge, which consists in understanding the meaning of the praṇava, I shall explain in detail through understanding the unity of the six kinds of meaning, O you of good vows.
m.6.14.10: The first meaning is the form of the mantra; the second is what is conceived through the mantra the yantra; the third meaning is the deity; after that comes the meaning as the manifest world—
m.6.14.11: —that is the fourth; the fifth meaning reveals the form of the guru; the sixth meaning is the form of the disciple's self. These are proclaimed as the six kinds of meaning.
m.6.14.12: Among these, I shall tell you the nature of the mantra, O best of sages, by merely knowing which a man becomes a great knower.
m.6.14.13: The first vowel a, the fifth u, and after that the last of the fifth consonant group, m, together with bindu and nāda—these five letters are declared by the Vedas, and not otherwise.
m.6.14.14: Their combined form is indeed declared to be the beginning of the Veda Om. Nāda is the aggregate of all; the group of four accompanied by bindu—
m.6.14.15: —is established in individual form in the praṇava that denotes Śiva. Now hear the yantra form, O wise one: that indeed is the Śiva-liṅga.
m.6.14.16: At the very bottom one should draw the pedestal; above it the first vowel a; above that the letter u; and above that the last of the pa-group m.
m.6.14.17: One should draw the bindu on its top and the nāda above that. When the yantra is complete, every desire is fulfilled.
m.6.14.18: Having thus drawn the yantra, one should encircle it with nine praṇavas; and by the nāda arising from it one should know it as ending in nāda.
m.6.14.19: I shall explain the meaning as deity, which is hidden everywhere, O sage, out of affection for you, O Vāmadeva, just as Śaṅkara spoke it.
m.6.14.20: Beginning with sadyojātaṃ prapadyāmi and ending with sadāśivom, the Śruti has thus declared the tāra, the Praṇava, as denoting the five Brahmans.
m.6.14.21: The five subtle deities having the form of Brahman are to be known; these very ones are amplified as the embodied forms of Śiva too.
m.6.14.22: The mantra that denotes Śiva also denotes Śiva's form, since there is no absolute difference between the form and the one who has the form.
m.6.14.23: Śiva's body was described earlier, beginning with the words endowed with the crown of Īśāna; now hear about the five faces.
m.6.14.24: Beginning with the fifth, in order starting with Sadyojāta and ending with the upper one, Īśāna, the group of five faces is declared.
m.6.14.25: The fourfold Brahman-form, beginning with Puruṣa and ending with Sadyojāta, stands in the position of the fourfold emanation (catur-vyūha) of the god Īśāna himself.
m.6.14.26: Īśāna, renowned as Brahman, is the aggregate of the five Brahmans; and the four beginning with Puruṣa and ending with Sadyojāta are its individual forms, O sage.
m.6.14.27: This circle, consisting of grace, is the cause of the five purposes; it is of the nature of the Supreme Brahman, subtle, changeless and free from affliction.
m.6.14.28: Grace too is twofold: one pertains to concealment and the like; the other is that by which the Lord grants souls higher and lower liberation.
m.6.14.29: This pair of functions is declared to belong to Sadāśiva alone; and within grace too lies the Lord's set of five functions, creation and the rest.
m.6.14.30: There too, O sage, the deities beginning with Sadyojāta are proclaimed; those five, of the nature of the Supreme Brahman, always bestow welfare.
m.6.14.31: The circle of grace, consisting of the kalā beyond peace (śāntyatītā) and presided over by Sadāśiva, is called the supreme state.
m.6.14.32: This very state is to be attained by ascetics of purified selves, worshippers of Sadāśiva, whose minds are devoted to the praṇava.
m.6.14.33: Having attained this very state, the lords of sages, after enjoying very abundant pleasures together with him, the god in the form of Brahman,
m.6.14.34: at the occurrence of the great dissolution attain equality with Śiva; and those people never fall again anywhere into the ocean of saṃsāra.
m.6.14.35: They are in the Brahma-world—so the eternal Śruti says. And this indeed is the aggregate of Śiva's sovereignty as well.
m.6.14.36: Endowed with all sovereignty—so says the Atharva-śikhā; and they declare that the bestowing of all sovereignty belongs to him alone.
m.6.14.37: No state higher than the state of Camaka exists. The world is indeed seen as the unfolding of the expansion of the five Brahmans.
m.6.14.38: Thus the kalās beginning with Nivṛtti are held to have arisen from the Brahmans; they have the nature of the subtle elements and are renowned as causes.
m.6.14.39: That which exists in fivefold form within this world of gross nature, O you of good vows, is held to be the group of five Brahmans.
m.6.14.40: The pentad of Puruṣa, ear and speech, sound and space is pervaded by Brahman in the form of Īśāna, O best of sages.
m.6.14.41: The pentad of Prakṛti, skin and hand, touch and air is pervaded by Brahman in the form of Puruṣa, O lord of sages.
m.6.14.42: Ego (ahaṅkāra), the eye, the foot, form, and fire: this splendid group of five is pervaded by the Aghora-Brahman.
m.6.14.43: Intellect (buddhi), the tongue, the anus, taste, and water: this group of five is always pervaded by the Vāmadeva-Brahman.
m.6.14.44: Mind, the nose, the generative organ, smell, and earth: this group of five is pervaded by the Sadyojāta-Brahman. Thus the world consists of the five Brahmans.
m.6.14.45: The Praṇava, which denotes Śiva, is taught in the form of a yantra: it is the aggregate of the five letters, together with the group of four beginning with the bindu.
m.6.14.46: By the path taught by Śiva one should contemplate the Praṇava in the form of a yantra—the supreme king of mantras, whose form is Śiva.
m.6.14.iti: Thus ends the fourteenth adhyāya, named The description of the Praṇava as the form of Śiva, in the sixth saṃhitā, the Kailāsa-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.6.15.1: Īśvara said: Next I shall explain the excellent course of creation of the group of four beginning with Maheśa, as it arises from Sadāśiva, O fair-faced one.
m.6.15.2: Sadāśiva is the collective whole, the Lord, ruler of ether. The tetrad beginning with Maheśa is that very Sadāśiva having become individuated.
m.6.15.3: From a thousandth portion of Sadāśiva arose Maheśa; and since he has the form of Tatpuruṣa and is endless, he is the lord of air.
m.6.15.4: He is joined on his left with the Māyā-śakti, is with parts (sakala), and predominant in action. The tetrad beginning with Īśvara is his individuated form.
m.6.15.5: Īśa, then Viśveśvara, after that Parameśa, and next Sarveśvara — this is the excellent wheel of concealment (tirodhā).
m.6.15.6: Concealment is divided in two: one pertains to Rudra and the others; the other operates through embodiment for the continuing line of the class of bound souls (paśu),
m.6.15.7: intent on making them delight in enjoyments, lasting until the moment of the equipoise of karma. When karma is balanced, that same all-pervading one becomes full of grace.
m.6.15.8: There, the deities proclaimed with Sarveśvara as chief are directly of the nature of the supreme Brahman, free from distinctions and free from affliction.
m.6.15.9: The wheel consisting of concealment is made of the Śānti-kalā; presided over by Maheśvara, this abode is unsurpassed.
m.6.15.10: This very abode is to be attained by those who serve Maheśa's feet; for the Māheśvaras it grants liberation through the stages beginning with sālokya.
m.6.15.11: From a thousandth portion of Maheśvara was born the form of Rudra; he has the shape of the Aghora face and is ruler of the principle of fire (tejas).
m.6.15.12: Joined on his left with the Gaurī-śakti, the Lord is the destroyer of all. His individuated form is the tetrad beginning with Śiva.
m.6.15.13: Śiva, Hara, Mṛḍa and Bhava — this is known as the wondrous wheel called dissolution, greatly divine and supreme indeed, O lord of sages.
m.6.15.14: That dissolution is declared threefold by the wise, by the division beginning with the daily: the daily one is called the deep sleep of beings; the occasional one is considered to be that of Vidhi (Brahmā's night).
m.6.15.15: And his (Brahmā's) own dissolution is the great one — so the Veda shows. For beings exhausted by the sufferings of birth and the like, who have long dwelt in embodiment,
m.6.15.16: for their rest, O best of sages, and for the ripening of their karmas, dissolution was devised threefold by Rudra of immeasurable splendour.
m.6.15.17: This triad is declared to be among Rudra's own functions; yet even in dissolution the all-pervading Lord has the fivefold functions beginning with creation.
m.6.15.18: O sage, there the deities beginning with Bhava are proclaimed; they are of the nature of the supreme Brahman and bestow grace on the worlds.
m.6.15.19: This wheel called dissolution is made of the Vidyā-kalā; presided over by Rudra, this abode is free from affliction.
m.6.15.20: This very abode is to be attained by those who long to worship Rudra; for the Rudra-devotees it grants sāyujya (union) through the sequence of sālokya, O sage.
m.6.15.21: From a thousandth portion of the form of Rudra came the birth of Viṣṇu; he is the soul of the Vāmadeva wheel and the sole leader of the water principle.
m.6.15.22: Joined on his left with the Ramā-śakti, the great one is protector of all; four-armed, lotus-eyed, dark, bearing the conch and other emblems.
m.6.15.23: The group of four beginning with Vāsudeva is his individuated form; it grants liberation to the Vaiṣṇavas devoted to worship.
m.6.15.24: Vāsudeva, Aniruddha, then the supreme Saṅkarṣaṇa, and Pradyumna — thus is the renowned unsurpassed wheel of preservation.
m.6.15.25: Preservation is the protection of the created world together with its creator, until the end of the experiencing of the commenced (prārabdha) karma of beings who enjoy its fruits.
m.6.15.26: This function is declared to belong to Viṣṇu, the ordainer of protection; yet even in preservation the Lord has the fivefold functions beginning with creation.
m.6.15.27: There the deities headed by Pradyumna are proclaimed; they are free from distinctions, free from fear, and ever bestow the bliss of the liberated.
m.6.15.28: O Brahman, this wheel of preservation, excellent, has the form of the Pratiṣṭhā-kalā; presided over by Janārdana, it is called the supreme abode.
m.6.15.29: This very abode is to be attained by those who serve Viṣṇu's lotus feet; for the Vaiṣṇavas this wheel grants the states beginning with sālokya.
m.6.15.30: From a thousandth portion of Viṣṇu arose the Grandsire (Brahmā), who is the soul of the Sadyojāta face and leader of the earth principle.
m.6.15.31: Accompanied on his left by the goddess of speech, he is the creator and lord of the world, four-faced, red in colour, having the nature of rajas.
m.6.15.32: His individuated form is the tetrad beginning with Hiraṇyagarbha: Hiraṇyagarbha, then Virāṭ, Puruṣa, and Kāla.
m.6.15.33: This wheel of creation is served by the seers, the sons of Brahmā and others; O Brahman, it grants all desires and aims and bestows the happiness of family.
m.6.15.34: Creation, however, is bringing out this withdrawn soul, lying in Prakṛti, outward for the experience of karma, together with the means, the limbs, and the fruits,
m.6.15.35: and joining it with them — this function those who know the act of world-creation understand as the Grandsire's, extending throughout the happy array of creation.
m.6.15.36: Even in world-creation, O sage, the Lord has the fivefold functions. There the deities, Kāla and the others, are proclaimed.
m.6.15.37: This wheel of creation is declared by the wise to have the form of the Nivṛtti-kalā; presided over by the Grandsire, this abode is indeed beautiful.
m.6.15.38: This very abode is to be attained by men whose minds are offered to Brahmā; for the Paitāmahas (Brahmā's devotees) it grants liberation beginning with sālokya.
m.6.15.39: In this group of four wheels too the Praṇava is present; in the order beginning with Maheśa, it is their designator by secondary signification.
m.6.15.40: This, indeed, is the wheel of the world, whose glory is renowned in the Śruti; the Śruti praises it as the five-spoked wheel, O sage.
m.6.15.41: The wheel of the world, which is the unfolding of Śambhu's power, is one alone; having five members—creation and the rest—it is called five-spoked.
m.6.15.42: Because it revolves all around with uninterrupted dissolution and arising, like the whirling of a firebrand-circle, therefore it is called a wheel.
m.6.15.43: Because of the vast production of creation and the rest, it appears as vast—this wheel of the golden god Śambhu of immeasurable splendour.
m.6.15.44: This wheel, the effect of his power, rests on the golden light. It is enveloped by water; the water is enveloped by fire.
m.6.15.45: Fire is enveloped by wind, and the wind by space—that great one; likewise space by the bhūtādi (elemental ego), and the bhūtādi is enveloped by the Mahat.
m.6.15.46: Likewise the Mahat is enveloped by the Unmanifest. Thus, O best of sages, it has been declared by believing teachers to be the Cosmic Egg (brahmāṇḍa).
m.6.15.47: Seven sheaths are spoken of for the protection of this universe. The water is ordained to exceed the wheel tenfold.
m.6.15.48: And so, each one above the other, each is tenfold greater; that, O leader of sages, is to be understood by the wise as the Cosmic Egg.
m.6.15.49: Accepting this meaning, because the water lies near the wheel, the Veda itself declares, in the midst of the water.
m.6.15.50: Through grace, concealment, destruction, maintenance and creation, Śiva alone, united with Śakti, ceaselessly performs his play.
m.6.15.51: What use is saying much here, O sage? I tell you the essence: it is certain that all this is Śiva alone, the possessor of Śakti.
m.6.15.iti: Thus ends the fifteenth adhyāya, named The description of the forms for worship, in the sixth saṃhitā, the Kailāsa-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.6.16.1: Sūta said: Having heard the meaning of the Veda taught by the guru, the foremost of sages respectfully asked about what remained doubtful concerning the Supreme Self.
m.6.16.2: Vāmadeva said: O Lord, bearer of the power of knowledge, whose form is supreme bliss, the nectar of the meaning of the Praṇava, flowing from your blessed lotus-mouth, has been drunk by me.
m.6.16.3: I have become firm in understanding, and my doubt is gone. O Mahāsena, I ask you something else; listen, O Lord.
m.6.16.4: The existence of the world, whose forms range from Sadāśiva down to the worm, is seen everywhere in the form of female and male; there is no doubt of this.
m.6.16.5: The eternal cause of the world that has such a form — is it of female form, or is it male, or neuter?
m.6.16.6: Or is it mixed, or something else? No decision has arisen on this. The learned, bewildered by the scriptures, dispute here in many ways.
m.6.16.7: The Śrutis that ordain the creation of the world, together with the world itself, the gods beginning with Viṣṇu and Brahmā, and the Siddhas indeed do not know this.
m.6.16.8: Explain this, and something else as well, so that they may arrive at agreement. The usage I know, I do, is commonly seen.
m.6.16.9: That usage is indeed established in all beings; no one disputes it. But does it arise from the body, senses, mind, intellect and ego of all —
m.6.16.10: or is it the very form of the Self? Here too there is great doubt. These two indeed are a wondrous ground of dispute for everyone.
m.6.16.11: Uprooting the poison-tree called doubt, born of ignorance, so that my mind may become the soil for the great wish-fulfilling tree of Śiva-nondualism —
m.6.16.12: — so that my mind may become so, O god, I am to be instructed through your compassion. By your grace, O lord of gods, I shall become one of firm knowledge.
m.6.16.13: Sūta said: Having heard the words thus asked by the sage, steeped in Vedānta, the Lord, with a slightly smiling face, spoke this secret.
m.6.16.14: Subrahmaṇya said: O sage Vāmadeva, this very secret was expounded by Śiva to the Mother Goddess, while I too was listening.
m.6.16.15: Having then drunk her breast-milk, I was satisfied again and again; I heard it attentively, and it was ascertained and reflected upon by me.
m.6.16.16: Out of compassion I tell it to you, O Vāmadeva, great sage. Listen now, dear son, to this great and supreme secret.
m.6.16.17: Beginning from the view that karma exists and from the tattvas, the discourse of the śāstras is very extensive; O sage, what gives knowledge should be heard by the wise according to discernment.
m.6.16.18: Among the disciples you have taught, who indeed is equal to you? Those lowly ones still wander even today among the systems of Kapila and others.
m.6.16.19: Devoted to reviling Śiva, they were cursed long ago by six sages. Their talk should not be heard, since they speak contrary to the truth.
m.6.16.20: Here there is no need for scope even for applying a five-membered inference; yet, from the sight of smoke,
m.6.16.21: they declare that the mountain possesses fire; here too, O you of good vows, it rests on the perception of the visible world. Therefore —
m.6.16.22: — the Supreme Lord, the Supreme Self, is to be known; there is no doubt. The universe consisting of female and male forms is seen by direct perception itself.
m.6.16.23: The body has the form of six sheaths; among them the first three are born of the mother's portion, and the others of the father's portion — so says the Śruti.
m.6.16.24: Thus people know the female-male nature in all bodies; and the wise, O sage, know the female-male nature in the Supreme Self as well.
m.6.16.25: The Śruti declares Brahman to have the nature of existence-consciousness-bliss. The word sat, which removes non-existence, is said to be the Self.
m.6.16.26: The removal of insentience is effected by the word cit. The word sat, which occurs in all three genders, should here be taken as masculine.
m.6.16.27: It denotes light; clearly, sat means light. The word cit, a synonym of the word jñāna (knowledge), has taken the feminine gender.
m.6.16.28: Light and consciousness, as a couple, have become the cause of the world. Likewise, in the Self that is existence-consciousness, which has become the cause of the world,
m.6.16.29: the notion Śiva and Śakti is established in one single place. Even light has impurity, owing to oil, wick and the like;
m.6.16.30: impurity and inauspiciousness are seen in the fire of the funeral pyre and the like. Thus, as the remover of these, auspiciousness (Śivatva) is enjoined by the Śruti.
m.6.16.31: The power of consciousness resting in the individual soul always has weakness; to remove that, here, Śakti-hood is eternal.
m.6.16.32: The usage strong and powerful is constantly seen in the world and in the Veda, O Vāmadeva, great sage.
m.6.16.33: Thus Śiva-hood and Śakti-hood are shown in the Supreme Self; from the union of Śiva and Śakti, bliss constantly arises.
m.6.16.34: Therefore, O sage, aiming at that bliss, sages whose sins were destroyed fixed their minds on Śiva and attained Śiva, the untroubled.
m.6.16.35: Thus the all-pervading selfhood of those two is sung in the Upaniṣads as Brahman, by the word brahman, which falls within the sense of the root bṛṃh (to expand).
m.6.16.36: Expanding and greatness reside in the form called Śambhu, consisting of the five Brahmans; the manifestation of the universe therein is denoted by the word brahman.
m.6.16.37: Out of affection for you, O Vāmadeva, I shall tell of the origin of the Praṇava from the Haṃsa mantra in reverse order; listen attentively.
m.6.16.38: By dropping the consonants s and h, there remains only Om, the gross designator of the Supreme Self.
m.6.16.39: It should be known as the great mantra by sages who see the truth. Within it is the subtle great mantra; I shall tell you its extraction.
m.6.16.40: In the first vowel, in the one of the form three-times-five (the fifteenth), and in the sixteenth vowel — in these three — when it is joined with s at the beginning, the great mantra arises.
m.6.16.41: The reverse of haṃsa would be so'ham; the meaning of the letter sa is held to be Śiva. The one consisting of Śakti is what the great mantra denotes; this is the conclusion.
m.6.16.42: But at the time of the guru's instruction, it means, I am he, Śiva consisting of Śakti; thus the great mantra should refer to the individual soul. Then the bound soul (paśu),
m.6.16.43: consisting of Śakti and being a portion of Śiva, through oneness with Śiva comes to share equality with Śiva. In the Brahman-statement prajñānam brahma, the meaning of prajñāna is seen.
m.6.16.44: The word prajñāna is a synonym of consciousness (caitanya); there is no doubt. O sage, the Śiva-sūtra, Consciousness is the Self, was set forth.
m.6.16.45: Consciousness means the freedom over the universe consisting of all knowledge and action; he whose own nature is that is declared to be the Self.
m.6.16.46: I have given the commentary (vārttika) on the Śiva-sūtras beginning thus. Knowledge is bondage is the Lord's second sūtra.
m.6.16.47: Knowledge here is that of the self consisting of limited knowledge and action; thus by the first word the Lord stated the characteristic of the class of bound souls.
m.6.16.48: This pair, knowledge and action, is the first stirring (spanda) of the Supreme Śakti. This very Supreme Śakti the followers of the Śvetāśvatara branch
m.6.16.49: joyfully praised as natural to him is the action of knowledge and strength. Indeed they know Śambhu's threefold vision as having the form of knowledge, action and will.
m.6.16.50: This triad, being located within the mind, the bound soul, having entered the sphere of sense-knowledge, always knows and acts through it.
m.6.16.51: Therefore it is settled that this is the very form of the Self. I shall now expound the meaning of the manifest world, showing its oneness with the Praṇava.
m.6.16.52: The eternal Śruti says, Om is all this. Beginning with From that Self, verily, the creation of the world is declared.
m.6.16.53: Out of affection for you, O Vāmadeva, I shall tell the purport of that Śruti, unfolded for the sake of discernment; let this be heard.
m.6.16.54: The union of Śiva and Śakti is settled to be the Supreme Self. From the Supreme Śakti arose Cit-śakti, born of it;
m.6.16.55: from that was born Ānanda-śakti; from that arose Icchā-śakti; from that was born Jñāna-śakti; and Kriyā-śakti is the fifth. From these alone, O sage, arose the kalās beginning with Nivṛtti.
m.6.16.56: Nāda and Bindu are declared to have arisen from Cit and Ānanda. From Icchā-śakti comes the letter ma, and from Jñāna-śakti the fifth
m.6.16.57: vowel u; and the letter a is born of Kriyā-śakti, O lord of sages. Thus the origin of the Praṇava has been told; now hear the origin of the five Brahmans.
m.6.16.58: From Śiva arose Īśāna; from that the origin of Tatpuruṣa; then Aghora; then Vāmadeva; and then the origin of Sadyojāta.
m.6.16.59: From this mātṛkā arose the thirty-eight mātṛs (kalās). From Īśāna was born the kalā called Śāntyatītā; then from Tatpuruṣa arises the Śānti kalā; Vidyā is born of Aghora;
m.6.16.60: Pratiṣṭhā and Nivṛtti are held to arise from Vāma and Sadyojāta. From Īśa, headed by Cit-śakti, comes the fivefold pair of the all-pervading Lord.
m.6.16.61: This pentad is regarded as the cause of the functions beginning with grace, by wise sages who know it and reveal the highest truth.
m.6.16.62: In this pentad, which has become paired through the relation of denoted and denoter and has the nature of kalās and letters, the pentad of elements
m.6.16.63: came forth in order beginning with space, O best of sages, starting from the first pair up to the fifth, of which each element is known to consist.
m.6.16.64: Space has sound as its sole quality; air has the qualities of sound and touch; fire is said to be predominant in the qualities of sound, touch and form.
m.6.16.65: Water is held to have the qualities of sound, touch, form and taste; earth is held to be rich in sound, touch, form, taste and smell.
m.6.16.66: This very order is declared as the pervasiveness of the elements; their being pervaded is in reverse, in the order beginning with smell.
m.6.16.67: This manifest world, consisting of the five elements, is declared to be Virāṭ, the self of the totality of all, and clearly the cosmic egg (brahmāṇḍa).
m.6.16.68: Beginning from the earth-principle up to the Śiva-principle in order, the individual soul, merging into the mass of principles, is itself dissolved.
m.6.16.69: Again at creation, together with Śakti, he emerges through Śakti and remains happily in the form of the gross world until dissolution.
m.6.16.70: The first stirring of the great Lord, when he is intent on creating the world by his own will, is called the Śiva-principle.
m.6.16.71: This very will is the Śakti-principle, since it accompanies all functions. In the pair of knowledge- and action-powers, when knowledge predominates, it is Sadāśiva.
m.6.16.72: Know, O lord of sages, that when action predominates it is the Maheśvara principle. The equality of the knowledge- and action-powers is held to be the pure principle of the nature of Vidyā.
m.6.16.73: The notion of difference with regard to entities which are his own limbs is the Māyā-principle. When Śiva, his own form preceded by supreme lordship
m.6.16.74: concealing by Māyā, becomes the perceiver of all objects, then he bears the name Puruṣa; the Śruti, having created it, he entered into it, arose about this.
m.6.16.75: This very one is the transmigrating bound soul, deluded by Māyā, devoid of the knowledge of Śiva, his mind bewildered by various actions.
m.6.16.76: Delusion arises only for this bound soul, who knows the world as not non-different from Śiva and himself as different from him; not for the Lord,
m.6.16.77: just as there is no illusion for the magician or the yogin. One whose lordship is made known by the guru becomes Śiva, a mass of consciousness.
m.6.16.78: Having the form of all-doership, of the nature of omniscience, having the form of fullness, of the nature of eternity and pervasiveness —
m.6.16.79: these are the five powers of Śiva, which shine forth in contracted form,
m.6.16.80: always appearing even in the form of contraction. For the bound soul they become kalā, vidyā, rāga, kāla and niyati; in the form of this pentad of principles, here that first is called kalā.
m.6.16.81: Kalā would be the cause of limited agency; that which is the sole means of limited knowing (tattva) is vidyā; and rāga is that which makes one attached to sense-objects.
m.6.16.82: Kāla (time), whose nature is to make manifest the appearances of existent and non-existent things, becoming the delimiter of sequence, is spoken of as past and so on.
m.6.16.83: The power of the all-pervading Lord that regulates thus: This is to be done by me, this is not—that is niyati; by its impulsion the bound soul (paśu) falls.
m.6.16.84: This very group of five, because it veils his true nature, is declared to be the five sheaths (pañca-kañcuka), and the inner instrument of bondage.
m.6.16.iti: Thus ends the sixteenth adhyāya, named The description of the principle of Śiva, in the sixth saṃhitā, the Kailāsa-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.6.17.1: Vāmadeva said: Earlier you said that the Puruṣa is situated below Niyati and above Prakṛti; how is it now stated otherwise—
m.6.17.2: that, his form contracted by Māyā, he is then below it, O Lord? This doubt of mine, O master, you should cut away in truth.
m.6.17.3: Śrī Subrahmaṇya said: This is the doctrine of non-dual Śaivism; it nowhere tolerates duality. Duality is perishable; the non-dual Brahman is supreme and imperishable.
m.6.17.4: Śiva is omniscient, the maker of all, the lord of all, beyond the guṇas; he is Brahman, the begetter of the three gods, whose form is being, consciousness and bliss.
m.6.17.5: That very god Śaṅkara, by his own will and his own Māyā, became the Puruṣa, being as if of contracted form.
m.6.17.6: Constituted as experiencer by the group of five beginning with Kalā, this Puruṣa, abiding in Prakṛti, enjoys the guṇas born of Prakṛti.
m.6.17.7: Thus the Puruṣa, standing within both positions, is not contradictory; contracting, he possesses the aggregate of his own forms such as knowledge.
m.6.17.8: The citta, to be effected by the guṇas sattva and the rest, and threefold as intellect and the rest—that was the Prakṛti-principle, owing to sattva and the others as cause.
m.6.17.9: The guṇas arising from Prakṛti are distinguished as sāttvika and the rest; from the guṇas arose the intellect, which determines things.
m.6.17.10: Then came the great ego, and from it the sense organs of knowledge were born; the form of the mind is that which conceives and doubts.
m.6.17.11: The organs of knowledge are ear, skin, eye, tongue and nose; sound, touch, form, taste and smell are their objects—
m.6.17.12: —declared as belonging to the organs of knowledge in order, beginning with the ear. Then from the vaikārika ego the subtle elements (tanmātras) arose in sequence.
m.6.17.13: These are called subtle by sages who see the truth. The organs of action, together with their functions, should be known:
m.6.17.14: O brahmin sage, speech, the two hands, the two feet, the anus and the genital; their actions are called speaking, grasping, going, excretion and pleasure.
m.6.17.15: From the bhūtādi ego the subtle elements arose in sequence; they are the subtle forms of sound and the rest—so is the established view.
m.6.17.16: And from them, O tiger among sages, the birth of space, air, fire, water and earth in order should be understood; this is called the five elements.
m.6.17.17: Giving room, conveying, cooking, cohesion and supporting are declared to be their functions.
m.6.17.18: Vāmadeva said: Earlier the creation of the elements was said to be from Kalā and the rest; how is it again stated otherwise, O Skanda? Great is my doubt here.
m.6.17.19: You said: The Ātma-principle is the letter A; Vidyā is U, beyond that; the Śiva-principle is M—let this be contemplated, O Vāmadeva.
m.6.17.20: Bindu and Nāda should both be known as conveying the meaning of all principles. Now hear, O sage, the deities residing there:
m.6.17.21: Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Rudra, Maheśvara and Sadāśiva—they are directly the forms of Śiva himself, renowned in the Veda.
m.6.17.22: So you said earlier; now it is said otherwise, that the elements arise from the subtle elements. Great is my doubt here.
m.6.17.23: Showing that compassion, O Skanda, you should cut away the doubt. Hearing these words of the sage, Kumāra replied.
m.6.17.24: Śrī Subrahmaṇya said: Beginning from the Vedic passage tasmād vā, in the order of the creation of the elements, O sage, hear them, O most wise one, attentively and with respect.
m.6.17.25: It is settled that the five elements were born from the Kalās; they, forming the gross world, are the body of the Lord of beings.
m.6.17.26: In the order of the emergence of principles, from the Śiva-principle down to earth, the elements are to be described in sequence as arising from the subtle elements, O sage.
m.6.17.27: The union of the subtle elements and the Kalās is the cause of the elements; know that there is no contradiction here, O best of knowers of Brahman.
m.6.17.28: In the universe, gross and subtle, the planets such as moon and sun, along with the constellations, came into being, and likewise other hosts of luminaries;
m.6.17.29: the deities Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Maheśa and others, the classes of beings, the guardians of the quarters such as Indra, the gods, the ancestors, the asuras,
m.6.17.30: rākṣasas, humans and other mobile beings, beasts, birds, insects, and the various kinds such as serpents,
m.6.17.31: trees, shrubs, creepers and herbs, the eight famed mountains, the seven rivers beginning with the Gaṅgā, and the oceans of great wealth—
m.6.17.32: whatever collection of things there is, all that is established here in Śiva; it should be reflected upon with right understanding, not as outside, O best of sages.
m.6.17.33: This universe, of female and male form, whose nature is Śiva and Śakti, should be worshipped by the wise like you, skilled in the knowledge of Śiva.
m.6.17.34: One should worship all as Brahman, and also, All indeed is Rudra—so says the Veda, O sage; therefore Sadāśiva is the self of the world.
m.6.17.35: Through the power of the placement of the thirty-eight Kalās and through non-dual contemplation, the guru whose self is cultivated as I am Sadāśiva alone is Śiva.
m.6.17.36: A true disciple who reflects thus becomes a guru; he is Śiva himself, whose self is the world, the deities, yantras and mantras—there is no doubt.
m.6.17.37: By the grace of the teacher, O brahmin, the disciple, all his bonds cut away and devoted to Śiva's state, surely becomes one with the guru.
m.6.17.38: Whatever thing exists, all of it—taken collectively or severally, according to the predominance of its guṇas—they declare to be the meaning of the Praṇava.
m.6.17.39: Free from faults such as passion, the essence of the Veda, spoken by Śiva—this non-dual knowledge dear to Śiva has been told to you by me with affection.
m.6.17.40: Whoever, puffed up with pride, considers this word of mine otherwise—be he a god, a dānava, a siddha, a gandharva, or even a human—
m.6.17.41: With this unequalled true power (śakti), which is like the fire of universal destruction to enemies, you would surely cut off the head of that wicked-souled one; there is no doubt.
m.6.17.42: You alone, O sage, are manifestly the foremost among the knowers of Śiva's non-duality; indeed, in teaching the knowledge of Śiva, you are the one who demonstrates Śiva's conduct.
m.6.17.43: By contact with the ash of your body, an impure great piśāca, his mass of sins cut away, attained through your grace the goal of the virtuous.
m.6.17.44: You are one whose glory is renowned throughout the three worlds by the name Śivayogī; by contact with your glance a bound soul (paśu) would become Paśupati.
m.6.17.45: Your questioning of me about that is out of earnest care for the instruction of the world; the virtuous wander here for the sake of benefiting the world.
m.6.17.46: Therefore this supreme secret is established in you. You too, with faith, devotion and respect, teaching those devoted to the praṇava—
m.6.17.47: —having seated them all and united them with the Supreme Lord, make them adopt Śiva's conduct, together with sacred ash and rudrākṣa.
m.6.17.48: You are indeed Śiva, a follower of Śiva's conduct, through the non-dual state you have attained; wandering for the protection of the world, attain imperishable bliss.
m.6.17.49: Sūta said: Having heard this wondrous doctrine spoken by the six-faced one, grounded in Vedānta, the sage became humble in form, and bowing many times on the ground like a staff, attained the state of a bee roaming at his lotus feet.
m.6.17.iti: Thus ends the seventeenth adhyāya, named The account of creation, beginning with the teaching of the knowledge of non-duality with Śiva, in the sixth saṃhitā, the Kailāsa-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.6.18.1: Śaunaka said: Having heard that essence of Vedānta, a secret most wonderful, what did Vāmadeva then ask the son of Maheśvara?
m.6.18.2: Blessed is the yogī Vāmadeva, ever devoted to the knowledge of Śiva, through whose connection this divine, supremely purifying narrative arose.
m.6.18.3: Having heard these words of the sages, full of love, the wise Sūta, his mind attached to Śiva, being pleased, spoke to them.
m.6.18.4: Sūta said: Blessed are you, devotees of Mahādeva, benefactors of the world. Listen, all you sages, once more to the dialogue of those two.
m.6.18.5: Having heard the words of Maheśa's son, which destroy duality and give rise to non-dual knowledge, the great sage became satisfied.
m.6.18.6: Bowing to Kārtikeya, son of Śiva, and praising him in various ways, the great sage again humbly asked about the truth.
m.6.18.7: Vāmadeva said: O Lord, knower of all truths, O six-faced one, ocean of nectar, how does the status of guru arise for these renunciants whose selves are purified—
m.6.18.8: by whose power beings attain the accomplishment of enjoyment, liberation and the rest? Without a line of succession they have no authority to give instruction.
m.6.18.9: Likewise, how is the shaving rite, as a component, and such a bath performed? Please explain this, O master; you are able to cut away my doubt.
m.6.18.10: Having heard this, Kārtikeya, keeping Vāmadeva's words in mind and remembering Śiva and Śivā in his heart, began to explain.
m.6.18.11: Śrī Subrahmaṇya said: Out of affection for you, O Vāmadeva, I shall declare the Yogapaṭṭa rite, through which guruhood arises—a great secret that grants liberation.
m.6.18.12: In the month of Vaiśākha, Śrāvaṇa, likewise Āśvayuja, Kārtika, Mārgaśīrṣa or Māgha, in the bright fortnight, on an auspicious day,
m.6.18.13: on the fifth lunar day or the full-moon day, having performed the morning rites and received permission from the guru, the disciple should bathe, with a controlled mind.
m.6.18.14: Having performed full bodily cleansing and wiped the body with a cloth, having tied on a doubled cord and put on two garments,
m.6.18.15: with feet washed, having sipped water twice, he should take ash and apply it with the Sadyojāta and other mantras, in the manner of full smearing.
m.6.18.16: Then, O sage, his hand held by the kindly guru, that disciple, with joined palms of his own two hands, facing east,
m.6.18.17: being thus seated, should remain in the well-decorated pavilion, on a pure, excellent seat of the guru, covered with cloth, deerskin and kuśa grass.
m.6.18.18: Then the preceptor, taking the conch together with its stand and purifying it with the Astra mantra, should kindly place it in front of him.
m.6.18.19: Having worshipped the conch with its stand with flowers and the like, he should pour into it good water purified with the Astra and Kavaca mantras.
m.6.18.20: Having filled it and worshipped it as before, following the order prescribed for the six limbs, he should again consecrate it seven times with the Praṇava.
m.6.18.21: Having worshipped it with fragrance, flowers and so on, and shown incense and lamp, having protected that conch with the Astra, he should then veil it with the Kavaca.
m.6.18.22: Then the preceptor should display the gestures called Dhenu and Śaṅkha. Again, placing the conch before himself on an excellent spot to the right,
m.6.18.23: he should make a beautiful, auspicious maṇḍala according to the procedure prescribed for the worship-arghya, and worship it with fragrant flowers and the like.
m.6.18.24: A pot with its stand, cleansed and pure, adorned with thread, fumigated with incense, set in place, and filled with pure scented water—
m.6.18.25: that pot, O lord of sages, he should smear with the five barks, the five leaves and the five clays, mixed with fragrant substance.
m.6.18.26: Then he should make that pot well adorned with cloth, mango leaves, tips of dūrvā grass, a coconut, flowers and other articles.
m.6.18.27: He should place the five gems in that pot, O lord of sages; or, in their absence, he should devoutly place gold.
m.6.18.28: The gem called sapphire, likewise the two gems ruby and gold, and coral and gomedaka (zircon)—this is known as the set of five gems.
m.6.18.29: Then the preceptor, uttering nṛmluska and then glūṃ at the end, should, kindly disposed, worship properly and lovingly according to the rule.
m.6.18.30: Beginning with the Ādhāraśakti, according to the procedure stated for worship, he should invoke the deity and worship him by way of the five enclosures (āvaraṇas).
m.6.18.31: Having offered rice-pudding, betel and the rest as before, and having completed the worship ending with the eight names, he should consecrate it the pot with mantras:
m.6.18.32: with the Praṇava one hundred and eight times, then with the five Brahma-mantras in order, from Sadyojāta up to Īśāna, and also with the Astra; then, protected again with the Kavaca,
m.6.18.33: having veiled it, and having devoutly shown incense and lamp, he should then properly display there the gestures called Dhenu and Yoni.
m.6.18.34: Then the preceptor, covering its top with darbha grass, should prepare a square in the north-eastern (Īśāna) quarter of the maṇḍala.
m.6.18.35: Having arranged a pleasing seat upon it according to rule, he should kindly seat the disciple, that novice, there.
m.6.18.36: Then, lifting the pot, preceded by the recitation of auspicious blessings (svastivācana), the guru should sprinkle the disciple on the head, moving clockwise.
m.6.18.37: First uttering the Praṇava seven times, then the five Brahma-mantras, at the end of the ablution he should encircle him with the water of the conch.
m.6.18.38: Then, having shown a beautiful lamp and wiped him with a cloth, he should make him wear a new cord, loincloth and two garments.
m.6.18.39: With feet washed and having sipped water twice, the guru, himself wearing ash, holding the novice's two hands with his own hands in the middle of the pavilion,
m.6.18.40: the guru, having duly smeared that ash on his limbs, should then lead him to the prepared seat and seat him comfortably.
m.6.18.41: To him the disciple who faces east and longs for knowledge of the principle of his own self, the guru, seated on his own seat, should say: Be of pure self.
m.6.18.42: And the guru, firmly established in the conviction, I am Śiva, the all-full, should properly enter samādhi for a muhūrta, with his mind withdrawn inward.
m.6.18.43: Afterwards, opening his eyes, with a favourable mind and undisturbed, he should look upon the pure disciple standing with folded hands.
m.6.18.44: Placing his own hand, smeared with sacred ash, on the disciple's head, he should clearly impart into his right ear: Haṃsaḥ so'ham.
m.6.18.45: There, the meaning of the first word aham is the one whose nature is Śakti; saḥ is Śiva himself. He alone am I; I am Śiva — thus contemplate your own self.
m.6.18.46: Having thus taught the essential meaning of ya (the relative who) with respect to the individual soul (aṇu), he should then carefully explain the meaning and purport of the intermediate statements.
m.6.18.47: He should say clearly: I shall tell you the statements, O Brahman; listen with an attentive mind, and hold them firmly in your heart.
m.6.18.iti: Thus ends the eighteenth adhyāya, named The rite of making a disciple, in the procedure of saṃnyāsa, in the sixth saṃhitā, the Kailāsa-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.6.19.0: Subrahmaṇya said: Now the great sayings: (1) Consciousness is Brahman. (2) I am Brahman. (3) That you are. (4) This Self is Brahman. (5) All this is to be pervaded by the Lord. (6) I am prāṇa. (7) The Self is consciousness. (8) What is here, that is there; what is there, that is here too. (9) That is other than the known, and also beyond the unknown. (10) This is our Self, the inner controller, the immortal. (11) He who is in the person and he who is in the sun, he is one. (12) I am the supreme Brahman, beyond the higher and the lower, higher than the highest. (13) Through the Vedas, the śāstras and the guru, it is known as itself marked by bliss. (14) The Brahman abiding in all beings, that indeed am I; there is no doubt. (15) I am the prāṇa of the tattva; I am the prāṇa of earth. (16) I am the prāṇa of the waters, and I am the prāṇa of fire. (17) I am the prāṇa of air; I am the prāṇa of ether. (18) I am the prāṇa of the three guṇas. (19) I am all, I am the self of all, the one in saṃsāra; whatever has been, whatever will be, whatever is present, because I am the self of all, I am without a second. (20) All this indeed is Brahman. (21) I am all, I am liberated. (22) He who is that one, I am he; haṃsa: I am he.
m.6.19.1: The meaning of the saying Consciousness is Brahman has already been explained before. What the word aham (I) refers to is the Supreme Lord, whose self is Śakti.
m.6.19.2: The letter a, foremost of all letters, is light, the supreme Śiva. The letter ha has the form of space; it is declared to be of the nature of Śakti.
m.6.19.3: From the union of Śiva and Śakti arises bliss, ever manifest. The word Brahman denotes the all-selfhood of Śiva and Śakti; this is clear.
m.6.19.4: That was taught earlier; one should contemplate, I am he. In tat tvam, the meaning of the word tat has been explained.
m.6.19.5: Otherwise, in so 'ham there would be a contemplation of a contrary meaning. The word aham is masculine, while tat would be neuter; thus, owing to their mutual contradiction, there could be no grammatical connection between the two.
m.6.19.6: And otherwise the cause of the world, which has the form of female and male, would be something different. Thus sa tvam asi (he you are) is the contemplation of the meaning of the teaching.
m.6.19.7: And in the saying ayam ātmā, the pair of words is masculine in form. Because it is to be protected by the Lord (īśa), this world is īśāvāsya.
m.6.19.8: One should contemplate prajñānātmā and, what is here, that is there. He who is here is that very one — so it is stated here by learned adherents of the established doctrine.
m.6.19.9: And in the saying stated above, he who is there abides here; thus, as before, the meaning is the Puruṣa, according to the view of the wise.
m.6.19.10: That is other than the known, and also than the unknown — in this saying too there arises a notion of reversal even of the result.
m.6.19.11: How that may be, just so I shall explain here; listen, O sage. The word aviditāt is to be taken as before, like viditāt;
m.6.19.12: it would be employed thus: that is other than the known, and likewise beyond the unknown. It is certain that what is other would not serve for attainment in any other sense.
m.6.19.13: This is your Self, the inner controller, who is immortal and Śiva himself; the Śambhu who is in the person and who abides in the sun.
m.6.19.14: He and that one suggest separateness; yet he is not one place alone — he is declared to be all. The meaning here involves two limiting adjuncts; it is spoken thus figuratively.
m.6.19.15: The Śrutis indeed call that Lord Śambhu golden; the phrase to the golden-armed is an indication of all his limbs.
m.6.19.16: Otherwise his lordship over that would not hold; this is to be understood carefully. He who is within — so Śambhu, Śiva, is heard of in the Chāndogya.
m.6.19.17: Having a golden beard, and likewise golden hair; from the nails to the tips of the hair, he is golden everywhere.
m.6.19.18: I am the supreme Brahman, beyond higher and lower, higher than the highest — I shall tell the purport of this saying; listen to this.
m.6.19.19: The referent of the word aham is declared to be Śiva, whose self is Śakti. I am he alone — such is certainly the construal of the meaning of the saying.
m.6.19.20: He, most excellent of all and the self of all, is declared to be the supreme Brahman. Para, apara, and parātpara — thus it is threefold.
m.6.19.21: Rudra, Brahmā and Viṣṇu are so declared by Śruti itself, not otherwise; and the supreme God beyond them is indicated by the word para.
m.6.19.22: Through the force of repeated study of the sayings of the Vedas, śāstras and gurus, Śambhu, full of perfect bliss, becomes manifest in the heart of the disciple.
m.6.19.23: Śambhu abides in all beings; he indeed am I, there is no doubt. I am the prāṇa of the whole multitude of tattvas; I am Śiva.
m.6.19.24: Having said this, Śiva spoke again of being the prāṇa of the three tattvas. In the words I am prāṇa, O sage, from the inclusion of everything from earth up to the guṇas,
m.6.19.25: understand that all the ātma-tattvas are included. And again, the inclusion of all refers to the vidyā-tattva and the Śiva-tattva.
m.6.19.26: And of these two tattvas I am the prāṇas; I am all, indeed the self of all. And because I am the inner controller of the jīva, I am always its very life.
m.6.19.27: Whatever has been, whatever is to be, whatever will be — all of it; because it consists of me, I am all. All indeed is Rudra —
m.6.19.28: so the Śruti says, O sage, for it issued directly from Śiva's mouth. He is the self of all because of his eternal association with these supreme qualities.
m.6.19.29: Since there is no supreme self other than myself, I alone am without a second. The meaning of the saying All this indeed is Brahman was stated earlier.
m.6.19.30: I am full, being of the nature of pure being; I alone am eternally liberated. The paśus (bound souls), through my grace, are liberated, having taken refuge in my state.
m.6.19.31: That Śambhu who is the self of all — he am I; haṃsa — I am Śiva. Such indeed, O Vāmadeva, is the meaning of all the sayings, as declared by Śiva.
m.6.19.32: Thus the guru should carefully teach the disciple the meaning taught through the sayings of the Lord and of Śruti, which directly grants men oneness with Śiva.
m.6.19.33: Taking a conch together with its stand, purifying it with ash by means of the astra-mantra, and placing it before him on a worshipped square,
m.6.19.34: having worshipped the astra with Om using perfumes and the rest, adorned with cloth, filling it with scented water and worshipping it with the mantra Om,
m.6.19.35: then consecrating it again sevenfold with the praṇava he says: Whoever makes even the slightest distinction becomes subject to great fear —
m.6.19.36: thus speaks the true principle of Śruti; be firm of soul and free of fear. Having thus addressed the disciple himself, meditating on the God, he should worship.
m.6.19.37: Having worshipped the disciple's seat by the method of the six upliftings, and having conceived it as the seat of Śiva, he should form the image of Śiva upon it.
m.6.19.38: Placing the five Brahman-mantras from the head down to the feet, and also the kalās of the praṇava, according to the divisions of head, face and kalās,
m.6.19.39: the thirty-eight in the form of mantras, on the disciple's body and then on the head; having invoked Śiva, he should display the mudrās of establishing.
m.6.19.40: Then, having placed the limbs of the mantra in order, beginning with sarvajña (the omniscient), he should arrange the sixteen services of worship, starting with the offering of a seat.
m.6.19.41: Having offered rice cooked in milk as the food-offering with Om and the word for Agni's wife (svāhā), he should offer in order water for rinsing the mouth, sipping water, arghya and the rest, and incense, lamp and the rest.
m.6.19.42: Having worshipped Śiva with the eight names, he should then recite, together with brāhmaṇas who have mastered the Vedas, the passages brahmavid āpnoti and bhṛgur vai vāruṇiḥ.
m.6.19.43: He should recite starting from yo devānām up to yaḥ paraḥ sa maheśvaraḥ. Then, in front of him, a garland made of kahlāra lilies and other flowers —
m.6.19.44: — taking up the garland and standing up, he should softly recite the Siddhi-skandha in the five-faced form of the text within the scripture composed by Śrī Virūpākṣa,
m.6.19.45: from khyātiḥ up to pūrṇo'ham (I am full); then the preceptor, with a favourable mind, should place the garland on the neck of that disciple.
m.6.19.46: Then he should have a tilaka mark made with sandal paste, and again the anointing of all the limbs, in keeping with his own tradition, according to rule.
m.6.19.47: Then the preceptor, with affection, should give him a name bearing the title Śrīpāda, an umbrella and sandals, and the right of performing the dūrvā rites,
m.6.19.48: and the office of expounder, the ritual duties and so on, and the acceptance of the guru's seat — the guru, having bestowed these as grace upon that disciple who has the form of Śiva,
m.6.19.49: and having told him, Always remain established in samādhi, thinking, I am Śiva, should then himself make a prostration to him.
m.6.19.50: Likewise the others should bow to him in accordance with the tradition. Then the disciple, rising, should likewise bow to the guru, to his guru's guru, and to the disciples of his own guru as well.
m.6.19.51: To the disciple who has thus made his prostrations, of good conduct, restrained in speech, standing bowed in humility, the guru himself should give this instruction:
m.6.19.52: From today onward be devoted to the welfare of the people. Having tested a disciple for a year, accept him according to the rule.
m.6.19.53: Having abandoned faults such as passion, be devoted to meditation on Śiva. Keep company with those perfected in a true tradition, and not with others.
m.6.19.54: Never eat without first worshipping Śiva, as long as life lasts. Firmly holding to devotion to the guru, be happy, be happy.
m.6.19.55: Thus, in due order, the excellent guru, compassionate, an ocean of knowledge, should treat the disciple as his equal with a kindly mind.
m.6.19.56: Out of affection for you, O Vāmadeva, lord of sages, I have told you this procedure of the yogapaṭṭa, though it is very secret.
m.6.19.57: Having said this, the six-faced Skanda, with affection and out of compassion for ascetics, began to explain to him the auspicious sequence of the rite of shaving and bathing.
m.6.19.iti: Thus ends the nineteenth adhyāya, named The description of the rite of the yogapaṭṭa, in the sixth saṃhitā, the Kailāsa-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.6.20.1: Subrahmaṇya said: O Vāmadeva, great sage, I shall describe the procedure for shaving and bathing, by whose performance the ascetic at once attains supreme purity.
m.6.20.2: O lord of sages, once the disciple has received the rite of the yogapaṭṭa, he becomes a complete observer of vows; he should then make ready for the act of shaving.
m.6.20.3: Having bowed to the guru with special reverence and then obtained the guru's permission, he should wash his head, sip water, and, still wearing his garment, undergo the shaving.
m.6.20.4: Afterwards he should wash the cloth and the razor and other tools with clay and water; and having smeared the barber's hands with clay, he should give him clay, saying, Wash.
m.6.20.5: The tools having been set down and sprinkled with water while he utters Śiva, Śiva, and his own eyes having been closed and charged with mantra by the ring finger and thumb,
m.6.20.6: opening them with the Astra mantra, he should look at the shaving implements, the razor and the rest; then, having charged them twelve times, he should sprinkle them with the Astra mantra.
m.6.20.7: Taking the razor with the Tāra (Om), he should cut on the right side; and having himself shaved some hairs at the tips, he should have all the rest shaved.
m.6.20.8: Placing a leaf on the ground, he should cast the hair onto it, not onto the bare surface of the earth. He should also have the beard and the nails of hands and feet cut.
m.6.20.9: Gathering clay from the spot of a bilva, aśvattha, tulasī or similar plant, and having plunged twelve times into the water, going to the bank and sitting down,
m.6.20.10: placing the clay on a clean spot and dividing it into three, and again dividing each into three in the same way, he should sprinkle it and consecrate it with the Astra mantra.
m.6.20.11: Taking one portion of clay there and having it passed by the other hand, he should smear both hands twelve times and wash each one with water.
m.6.20.12: Again, taking in the hand in due order one portion for the feet and another for the face, having smeared and washed them with water, he should enter the water once more.
m.6.20.13: Dividing another portion of clay, smearing it in order twelve times on the head down to the face, and plunging again and again,
m.6.20.14: going to the bank, he should take sixteen mouthfuls of water for rinsing, sip water twice, and again restrain the breath with the praṇava sixteen times.
m.6.20.15: Again dividing another portion of clay into three, and with one of them cleansing the hips and the feet, sipping water twice,
m.6.20.16: then, restrained in speech, restraining the breath sixteen times with the praṇava, and again placing another portion on his thigh in three parts with Om,
m.6.20.17: he should sprinkle it and consecrate it seven times; then, having smeared the palms of his hands with one part three times, he should gaze upon the purifying form of the Sun.
m.6.20.18: Then, with another portion of clay, the wise and firm-minded disciple should smear both his armpits with his hands crossed over,
m.6.20.19: and likewise, devoted to his guru, taking another pure portion of clay, he should smear himself from head to feet, with his gaze fixed on the Sun.
m.6.20.20: Then, rising and taking up his staff from the ground, he should with devotion and steadfastness in knowledge remember his own guru, the giver of the mantra.
m.6.20.21: Then the disciple should devoutly remember Śiva together with Ambā — Maheśāna, Śaṅkara, the moon-crested one, lord of all sovereignty.
m.6.20.22: He should lovingly prostrate three times with all eight limbs to the guru and to Śiva, and once with five limbs; then, rising, he should offer salutation.
m.6.20.23: Entering the sacred water, plunging and emerging in its midst, and placing that clay on his shoulder, he should smear himself in the manner described before.
m.6.20.24: Gathering what remains there and going into the midst of the water, stirring it thoroughly there and smearing it on all his limbs,
m.6.20.25: uttering Om three times and remembering Śiva's lotus feet, which carry one across the ocean of worldly existence — for he always acts according to the rule —
m.6.20.26: having sprinkled himself with Om using water mixed with Virajā ash, and having wiped his body, he should then bathe thoroughly with ash.
m.6.20.27: Then, O sage, having applied the auspicious tripuṇḍra attentively by the prescribed method on all the prescribed limbs,
m.6.20.28: then, becoming pure in mind, he should perform the midday rites, bowing to Maheśvara, to the gurus, and to the sacred waters and the like.
m.6.20.29: O sage, he should worship with supreme devotion Maheśāna together with Ambikā, the giver of knowledge and protector of the three worlds.
m.6.20.30: Then that firm-minded ascetic, established in his own dharma and pure, should go out for alms among good communities of brāhmaṇas.
m.6.20.31: And there, pure in self, he should collect alms in the fivefold manner as is proper, and should avoid defiled food.
m.6.20.32: Purification, bathing, alms-seeking, and constant resort to solitude — these are the four duties of a mendicant; there is no fifth.
m.6.20.33: A gourd, a bamboo vessel, a wooden one and an earthen one — these are the four vessels of a mendicant; there is no fifth.
m.6.20.34: Betel, a metal vessel, emission of semen, white clothing, sleeping by day, and food at night — these six are forbidden to ascetics.
m.6.20.35: Those who are sākṣara (learned) yet perverse are known as rākṣasas (sākṣarā read in reverse). Therefore an ascetic should never do any contrary deed.
m.6.20.36: An ascetic should diligently perform the shaving and bathing for the sake of purity, remembering in his mind the pure supreme Brahman, Sadāśiva.
m.6.20.37: Thus, O tiger among sages, out of affection for you I have told the entire procedure of shaving and bathing. What more do you wish to hear?
m.6.20.iti: Thus ends the twentieth adhyāya, named The description of the rite of shaving and bathing, in the sixth saṃhitā, the Kailāsa-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.6.21.1: Vāmadeva said: For those ascetics who are liberated there is no cremation rite; I have heard that when the body has died, that body is buried.
m.6.21.2: O Kārttikeya, my teacher, kindly explain that rite to me with great affection, for there is no one other than you in the three worlds who can expound it.
m.6.21.3: Those who, resting in the sense of complete I-ness, are freed from the cage of the body, and those who, freed from the body by the path of worship, have gone to the Supreme —
m.6.21.4: O blessed son of Śaṅkara, considering me your own disciple, please kindly tell me the particular destiny of these.
m.6.21.5: Sūta said: Hearing the sage's request, the son of Śakti, slayer of the enemies of the gods, spoke that utmost secret which Bhṛgu had heard from the Lord.
m.6.21.6: Subrahmaṇya said: O sage, this very secret was told directly to Bhṛgu, the Śiva-yogin, by the omniscient Lord, the bearer of the Pināka.
m.6.21.7: I shall tell it to you today, O brahmin; it must not be given to just anyone. It should be given only to a disciple who is tranquil and endowed with devotion to Śiva.
m.6.21.8: If there is some ascetic who, established in samādhi, gives up the body in the awareness of being Śiva, that greatly steadfast one becomes the all-full Śiva.
m.6.21.9: But whoever is unsteady in mind and does not attain samādhi — I shall tell the means for him; listen attentively.
m.6.21.10: Having heard from the guru's mouth the full knowledge of the three categories, born of the words of the Vedānta and the Āgamas, he should practise yoga, beginning with yama.
m.6.21.11: Doing that properly, the ascetic should be intent on meditation on Śiva, O sage, always, with discipline, his mind attached to the praṇava.
m.6.21.12: If, owing to weakness of the body, the ascetic lacks steadiness, then, free of desire and remembering Śiva, he should give up his worn-out body.
m.6.21.13: O sage, by the grace of Sadāśiva, impelled by Nandin, there are five renowned deities in the form of conductors (ātivāhika) of the departed.
m.6.21.14: One has the form of the identity of fire, with a body that is a mass of light; one presides over the day; one presides over the bright fortnight;
m.6.21.15: and one in the form of the northern course of the sun — these five are intent on grace. The other five are smoke, the dark night, the one presiding over the dark fortnight,
m.6.21.16: and the one in the form of the southern course — these are known as the other five deities. Now hear their function, O Vāmadeva, great sage.
m.6.21.17: Those five deities take the souls devoted to performing ritual works and go to heaven by virtue of their merit, O sage.
m.6.21.18: Having enjoyed the pleasures as described, when that merit is exhausted they again reach the human world and take birth as before.
m.6.21.19: Those first five, in turn, dividing the path into five stages beginning from the earth and taking him in the order beginning with fire, lead the ascetic to the abode of Sadāśiva —
m.6.21.20: having led him to the adorable feet of the God of gods, they stand behind him, embodiments of grace, employed in this very task.
m.6.21.21: Seeing him arrived, Sadāśiva, the God of gods — if he is dispassionate — teaches him the inner meaning of the great mantra,
m.6.21.22: and gives him a body equal to his own, and consecrating him to the leadership of the gaṇas, Śaṅkara, Lord of all, leader of all, bestows grace on him.
m.6.21.23: That body is adorned with the deer, the axe, the excellent trident and the boon-granting gesture, three-eyed, bearing the crescent moon, and wearing matted locks gleaming with the Gaṅgā.
m.6.21.24: and seated on the finest aerial car, all-pervading, granting all desires. Thus, for one whose dispassion is partial, he grants an aerial car surrounded by maidens of Rudra,
m.6.21.25: charming with the sound of dance, song, mṛdaṅga drums and other instruments, and adorned with divine garments, garlands, unguents and ornaments,
m.6.21.26: full of jars of divine nectar, filled with divine waters, shining like millions of suns, cool as millions of moons,
m.6.21.27: swift as thought and going everywhere — granting such an aerial car; and when that one, having enjoyed the pleasures, loses his curiosity for enjoyment,
m.6.21.28: the Lord, causing to descend on him the most intense Śakti, by nature extremely hard to attain, eager to burn the wilderness of bondage, radiant as the fire of dissolution,
m.6.21.29: the Supreme Lord, granting the inner meaning of the great mantra — the unwavering conviction, I am the full Śambhu, in the form of pure awareness —
m.6.21.30: and granting samādhi, along with unobstructed powers (siddhi) which are the pulsation of his own service and consist in the capacity for the functions of the sun and others,
m.6.21.31: at the end of the lifespan of the lotus-born Brahmā, the Guru of the world bestows upon him supreme liberation, free from return.
m.6.21.32: Therefore this very state is endowed with all lordship and is all-comprehensive, and is the highway to liberation — such is the conclusion of the Vedāntas.
m.6.21.33: Then, around that weak, dying ascetic who belongs to the true tradition, ascetics should stand, out of goodwill.
m.6.21.34: Then all of them there, concentrated, should impart in due order the sayings beginning with the praṇava and their purport,
m.6.21.35: and should describe them clearly and lovingly, constantly causing him to remember Śiva, the attributeless supreme Light, bowing to him until his dissolution.
m.6.21.36: Here the sequence of rites for these ascetics is stated as the same for all. For those whose bodies have not received cremation rites, no evil destiny arises.
m.6.21.37: Since they, having renounced all actions, are wholly devoted to taking refuge in Śiva, the kingdom of a king who defiles their body perishes.
m.6.21.38: The inhabitants of that village too would become greatly afflicted. For removing that fault, the procedure is stated as follows.
m.6.21.39: With a humble mind, he should at that time recite the mantra beginning with nama iriṇyāya ca and ending with nama āmīvatkebhyaḥ.
m.6.21.40: Reciting Om at the end, he should then fill up the sacred pit; then indeed, O lord of sages, that fault is pacified.
m.6.21.41: Sons and others should perform the excellent rite for the dead ascetic in proper order. Out of kindness I shall describe it, O brāhmaṇa; listen attentively.
m.6.21.42: Having worshipped the body, bathed it with pure water, and worshipped it with flowers and the like, with the Śrī Rudra and Camaka and with the Rudra-sūkta in due order,
m.6.21.43: and having placed a conch in front and sprinkled the body with its water, placing a flower on the head, he should wipe it with the Praṇava.
m.6.21.44: Removing the loincloth and other garments, he should put others on it again. Then he should smear its whole body with ash according to rule.
m.6.21.45: Having made the tripuṇḍra three lines according to rule and a tilaka with sandal paste, he should adorn the body with flowers and garlands.
m.6.21.46: On the chest, throat, head, arms, forearms and ears in order, he should adorn it with rudrākṣa garlands and ornaments, with mantras.
m.6.21.47: Having fumigated it well with incense, lifting it up and placing it on a sling, he should set the body on a beautiful chariot consisting of the five Brahma mantras.
m.6.21.48: With the five Brahma mantras beginning with Om, Sadyojāta and the rest in order, he should adorn that chariot with fragrant flowers and garlands.
m.6.21.49: With dance and music and the chanting of the Vedas by brāhmaṇas on all sides, carrying that dead body, he should go around the village keeping it to the right.
m.6.21.50: Then all those ascetics, in the east or else in the north, in a holy place near a sacred tree,
m.6.21.51: having dug a sacrificial pit to the measure of a staff, should sprinkle it with the Praṇava and the Vyāhṛtis and strew it in order,
m.6.21.52: with śamī leaves and flowers; above that, spreading darbha grass with tips to the north, he should make a seat covered with cloth, deerskin and kuśa.
m.6.21.53: Sprinkling that body with the Praṇava, the Brahma mantras and the pañcagavya, and bathing it with the Rudra-sūkta and the Praṇava,
m.6.21.54: and bathing it with conch water, he should place a flower on the head. He the performer, intent on remembering Śiva, acts in accordance with the departed one.
m.6.21.55: Then, lifting the body with Om, preceded by the svastivācana, he should set it in the pit in a yogic posture so that it faces east.
m.6.21.56: Having adorned it with scents and flowers, then with incense of guggulu, saying Viṣṇo havyam and uttering rakṣasva, he should offer it.
m.6.21.57: He should place the staff in the right hand and the water-pot in the left, with water, with the mantra Prajāpate na tvad etāny anyo.
m.6.21.58: Touching the head with the mantra Brahma jajñānaṃ prathamam, and having recited the Rudra-sūkta, he should recite while touching the space between the brows,
m.6.21.59: then with the four verses beginning Mā no mahāntam. Then he should break open the head with a coconut, and then fill the pit.
m.6.21.60: Touching the spot with the five Brahma mantras, with undivided mind he should recite: He who, preceding the gods, he who is supreme, he is Maheśvara —
m.6.21.61: having thus recited and meditated on Mahādeva together with Ambā, the remedy for saṃsāra, omniscient, dependent on none, the bestower of grace on all,
m.6.21.62: he should then make with clay a platform one cubit high and two cubits wide, and smear it with cow-dung.
m.6.21.63: And drawing a square in its middle, he should worship with sandal and unbroken rice, fragrant flowers, bilva leaves and tulasī.
m.6.21.64: Then with the Praṇava he should offer incense and lamp, milk and food-offering; having offered, circumambulated, he should bow down five times.
m.6.21.65: Having recited the Praṇava twelve times, he should then bow, and with the Praṇava offer the brahmārghya in the order of the directions and intermediate directions.
m.6.21.66: Thus the procedure for ascetics up to the tenth day has been told to you; now, O best of sages, hear the procedure of the eleventh day.
m.6.21.iti: Thus ends the twenty-first adhyāya, named The description of the rites for ascetics from death up to the tenth day, in the sixth saṃhitā, the Kailāsa-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.6.22.1: Subrahmaṇya said: When the eleventh day has arrived, I shall tell you, O tiger among sages, out of affection for you, the rite that has been prescribed for ascetics.
m.6.22.2: Having swept the altar, smeared it, performed the puṇyāhavācana, the declaration of the auspicious day, and sprinkled it, he should draw five diagrams in order, beginning from the west and ending in the east,
m.6.22.3: he himself, seated facing north, should make the diagrams, each conceived as a span in size, with a square in the middle,
m.6.22.4: and, in order, shaped as a dot, a triangle, a hexagon and a circle. Placing a conch in front, following the sequence stated for worship,
m.6.22.5: having restrained the breath, made the resolve, and worshipped the sovereign goddesses — the five deities mentioned earlier, who take the form of conveyors (ātivāhika) of the departed,
m.6.22.6: he should then cast away the darbha grass to the north and touch water. Beginning from the west, by the method of the sixfold seat,
m.6.22.7: he should treat the diagrams as seats, placing flowers within them as on a pedestal. Saying Om hrīṃ, he should invoke that conveying deity in the form of fire,
m.6.22.8: with the words, I invoke … namaḥ, at the end; he should contemplate this everywhere, and should reverently show to each deity the mudrās beginning with the installation mudrā.
m.6.22.9: With hrāṃ hrīṃ and so on he should perform, in order, the consecration of their limbs. He should meditate on them as holding in their hands noose, goad, and the gestures of fearlessness and boon, radiant like moonstone,
m.6.22.10: colouring all the quarters with the lustre of their red finger-rings, wearing red garments, adorned with lotus-like hands and feet,
m.6.22.11: charming with full-moon faces shining with three eyes, decorated with the crescent moon gleaming on ruby crowns,
m.6.22.12: their cheeks brushed by earrings, with full and high breasts, lovely with necklaces, armlets, bracelets and girdle-strings,
m.6.22.13: slender-waisted, broad-hipped, clothed in red divine garments, with lotus feet tinkling with ruby anklets, graceful and exceedingly charming with toe-rings and adorned hips.
m.6.22.14: What indeed cannot be accomplished by grace embodied, as by Śiva? Therefore, by grace embodied as Śakti, everything can be accomplished, as by Maheśa.
m.6.22.15: These five forms have been adopted by the very Bestower of grace to all; they are divine, accomplishing every task, intent on bestowing supreme grace.
m.6.22.16: Having thus meditated on all of them, auspicious and devoted to grace, he should offer water for washing their feet with drops of water from the conch.
m.6.22.17: He should offer water for sipping into their hands and arghya onto their heads, and with drops of conch water he should conceive the rite of their bathing.
m.6.22.18: He should offer divine red garments with upper cloths, and give priceless ornaments beginning with crowns.
m.6.22.19: He should offer fragrant sandal paste, very beautiful unbroken rice grains, and sweet-smelling, lovely flowers.
m.6.22.20: He should offer incense of supreme fragrance and a lamp with a ghee-soaked wick, saying, I offer all, beginning with the praṇava and hrīṃ
m.6.22.21: and ending with namaḥ. Then he should offer milk-rice drenched in honey, mixed with ghee and sugar, and filled out with cakes, bananas and jaggery,
m.6.22.22: filled and fragrant, on a banana leaf for each one. Uttering bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ, he should perform the sprinkling and the other purifications.
m.6.22.23: Uttering Om hrīṃ, he should offer the food offering with svāhā (the wife of Fire), and saying, this drinking water, namaḥ, he should offer it with supreme love.
m.6.22.24: Then, O best of sages, he should lovingly remove the offerings, starting from the east, and having cleaned the place, he should offer mouth-rinsing water, sipping water and arghya.
m.6.22.25: Having offered betel, incense and lamp, and performed circumambulation and prostration, he should pray to them, placing his joined palms on his head:
m.6.22.26: May the auspicious Mothers, well pleased, commend this ascetic, who seeks the state of Śiva, as one to be protected at the lotus feet of the Supreme Lord.
m.6.22.27: Having thus prayed to them all and dismissed them to return as they came, he should take up their prasāda and give it to young girls,
m.6.22.28: or give it to cows, or cast it into water — never otherwise. Here itself he should perform the pārvaṇa śrāddha; never the ekoddiṣṭa śrāddha for an ascetic.
m.6.22.29: Here I declare the rule for the pārvaṇa śrāddha; listen to it, O best of sages, through which welfare will follow.
m.6.22.30: The performer, having bathed, having restrained his breath, wearing the sacred thread, composed, with the pavitra ring on his hand, saying, On this holy lunar day,
m.6.22.31: and resolving, I shall perform the pārvaṇa śrāddha, should place excellent darbha grass to the north for seats, and touch water.
m.6.22.32: Having invited four brāhmaṇas, devotees of Śiva, firm in their vows, who have been anointed with oil and have bathed, he should devoutly seat them there,
m.6.22.33: saying, May you do the favour of representing the Viśvedevas, then, you, for the Self, and also, for the Inner Self,
m.6.22.34: and, for the Supreme Self — having spoken and requested them thus, the ascetic's performer should reverently and with faith make the formal choosing of them, as is proper.
m.6.22.35: Having washed their feet and seated them facing east, having adorned them with sandal and the rest, he should feed them in front of Śiva.
m.6.22.36: Having smeared the ground here with cow-dung and spread darbha grass arranged with tips to the east, with breath restrained, resolving the offering of the piṇḍas,
m.6.22.37: resolving, I shall perform it, and having worshipped the three diagrams, then naming the Self, the Inner Self and the Supreme Self,
m.6.22.38: pronouncing each name in the dative case and then saying, this piṇḍa, and uttering, I give, he should offer the piṇḍas with his own devotion.
m.6.22.39: Then he should offer kuśa-water according to rule and procedure. Then, rising, he should perform circumambulation and prostration.
m.6.22.40: Then, having given the fee to the brāhmaṇas according to rule, he should perform the Nārāyaṇa-bali at that very place on the same day.
m.6.22.41: The rite of worshipping Viṣṇu is prescribed everywhere for the sake of protection alone. Therefore one should perform a great worship of Viṣṇu and offer rice cooked in milk (pāyasa).
