m.7.2.15.21: As is Śiva, so is knowledge; as is knowledge, so is the guru. The fruit from worship of Śiva, knowledge and the gurus is the same.
m.7.2.15.22: This guru embodies all the gods and consists of all mantras; therefore with every effort one should bear his command upon one's head.
m.7.2.15.23: If one seeks the highest good, one should not transgress the guru's command even in thought, since one who obeys the guru's command attains the wealth of knowledge.
m.7.2.15.24: Whether walking, standing, sleeping or eating, one should not undertake any other act; if one does anything in his presence, let it all be with the guru's permission.
m.7.2.15.25: In the guru's house or in his presence one should not sit as one pleases, since the guru is God in person and his house is a temple.
m.7.2.15.26: Just as through association with sinners one becomes fallen by their sin, and just as here gold gives up its impurity through contact with fire, so too a man gives up sin through contact with the guru.
m.7.2.15.27: Just as a pot of ghee placed near a fire melts, so sin melts away in the presence of the teacher.
m.7.2.15.28: Just as a blazing fire burns both dry and wet, so this guru too, when pleased, burns away sin in an instant.
m.7.2.15.29: By mind, deed or speech one should not provoke the guru's anger.
m.7.2.15.30: By his anger, life, prosperity, knowledge and good deeds are burnt up; for those who provoke his anger, even their sacrifices are fruitless,
m.7.2.15.31: and so too their restraints and observances—there need be no doubt about this. A man should never utter any word contrary to the guru.
m.7.2.15.32: If out of great delusion he should speak so, he goes to the Raurava hell. Carefully, in mind, deed and speech with regard to the guru,
m.7.2.15.33: a wise man who seeks the highest good should not behave falsely. He should always do what is beneficial and pleasing to the guru, whether instructed or not.
m.7.2.15.34: Whether in his absence or in his presence, he should carry out the guru's work. A devotee of such conduct, with mind ever diligent,
m.7.2.15.35: a disciple who does what pleases the guru then becomes worthy of the Śaiva dharmas. If the guru is virtuous, wise, a revealer of supreme bliss,
m.7.2.15.36: a knower of reality and devoted to Śiva, then he is a giver of liberation—but not another. Reality is what produces awareness and gives rise to supreme bliss.
m.7.2.15.37: He by whom that reality is known is alone the revealer of bliss—not one who is a guru in name only and devoid of awareness.
m.7.2.15.38: Boats may carry one another across; can a stone carry a stone across? Through one who is a guru in name only, liberation too is in name only.
m.7.2.15.39: But those by whom reality is known are themselves liberated and also liberate others. In one devoid of reality, how can there be awakening? How indeed can there be grasp of the Self?
m.7.2.15.40: One devoid of such grasp is called a paśu (bound soul); and one directed by paśus does not pass beyond the state of being a paśu.
m.7.2.15.41: Therefore only one who knows the reality (tattva), being himself liberated, is accepted here as a liberator. Even if this teacher is endowed with all the auspicious marks and knows all the scriptures,
m.7.2.15.42: and even if he knows the procedures of all the means, yet if he lacks realisation of the reality, he is fruitless. He whose intellect engages in the reality right up to direct experience—
m.7.2.15.43: from his glance and the like supreme bliss arises. Therefore, the one through whose very contact awakening and bliss arise—
m.7.2.15.44: a wise man should choose him alone as guru, not another. That guru, approved by disciples skilled in humility and good conduct,
m.7.2.15.45: should be served by seekers of liberation until he is fully known. When he is known, there should be steady devotion until one has taken refuge in the reality.
m.7.2.15.46: But one should never abandon the reality nor neglect it in any way. A guru in whom not even a little bliss or awakening is found—
m.7.2.15.47: even after a year, the disciple should leave him and resort to another guru. Even having taken refuge in another guru, he should not disrespect the former one, nor the guru's brothers, sons, instructors and inspirers.
m.7.2.15.48: In that matter, first approaching a brāhmaṇa who has mastered the Vedas, one should worship the guru who is wise, auspicious and pleasing to behold,
m.7.2.15.49: the giver of all fearlessness, whose mind is filled with compassion. One should please him with effort, by mind, deed and speech.
m.7.2.15.50: The disciple should worship him until he becomes pleased. When he is pleased, the disciple's sins are destroyed at once.
m.7.2.15.51: Therefore wealth, gems, fields and houses, ornaments and garments, vehicles, beds and seats—
m.7.2.15.52: these one should give to the guru with devotion, according to one's means. One should not be deceitful about wealth if one desires the supreme goal.
m.7.2.15.53: Since he alone is father, mother, husband, kinsman, wealth, happiness, companion and friend, therefore one should offer everything to him.
m.7.2.15.54: Having offered these, afterwards, dedicating to him one's own self together with one's lineage and possessions, with a libation of water, one should always remain under his control.
m.7.2.15.55: When an embodied being has given his own self to Śiva in the form of the preceptor, then he becomes a Śaiva; for him there is no rebirth thereafter.
m.7.2.15.56: The guru should test a disciple who has resorted to him for one year if a brāhmaṇa, two years if a kṣatriya, and three years if a vaiśya,
m.7.2.15.57: by commands, fitting and unfitting, such as demanding the giving of life and wealth, putting superior ones to low work and low ones to superior work.
m.7.2.15.58: Those who, even when reviled or beaten, do not fall into dejection—they are fit, self-controlled and pure for the rite of Śaiva consecration.
m.7.2.15.59: Non-violent, compassionate, always of diligent mind, free of pride, intelligent, having given up rivalry, sweet-spoken,
m.7.2.15.60: upright, gentle, pure, humble, steady-minded, endowed with purity and good conduct, devotees of Śiva, twice-born—
m.7.2.15.61: those thus endowed with good conduct in speech, mind, body and action are to be purified and instructed according to rule—this is the settled view in the scriptures.
m.7.2.15.62: A woman has no eligibility of her own for the rite of Śaiva consecration; but by her husband's authorization she certainly has it, if she is endowed with devotion to the Lord.
m.7.2.15.63: Likewise a widow certainly has eligibility with the permission of her son or others, and a maiden by her father's command. For śūdras, low-born castes, and especially the fallen,
m.7.2.15.64: and likewise for mixed castes, the purification of the paths (adhvan) is not prescribed. If they too have unfeigned devotion to Śiva, the supreme cause,
m.7.2.15.65: they should effect the purification of their sins by the giving of the guru's foot-water and the like. Here, those born in anuloma order are indeed counted among the twice-born;
m.7.2.15.66: for them one should perform the purification of the paths and the rest as befits their mother's lineage. But a maiden who has been appointed to Śiva's dharma by her father and others—
m.7.2.15.67: she should be given in marriage to a devotee, not to another who is hostile. If through negligence she has been given to an adverse man, she should enlighten her husband.
m.7.2.15.68: If unable, abandoning him in mind, she should practise dharma—just as the devoted wife Anasūyā, leaving her husband Atri, the best of sages,
m.7.2.15.69: long ago attained fulfilment by worshipping Śaṅkara with austerity; and just as Draupadī, having worshipped the god Nārāyaṇa with austerity, the Pāṇḍavas
m.7.2.15.70: obtained as husbands, though not appointed to that dharma by her elders. In truth, the fault arising from lack of independence does not apply here
m.7.2.15.71: for a woman engaged in Śiva's dharma, because of the weight of Śiva's command. What use is saying much here? Whoever it may be that takes refuge in Śiva—
m.7.2.15.72: he is fit to be consecrated if he is subject to the guru; the rite does not differ for him. Merely by the guru's glance, by touch, or by conversation,
m.7.2.15.73: for one in whom wisdom arises there is no defeat. The consecration that is performed mentally by the path of yoga—
m.7.2.15.74: that secret one, accessible only through the guru's mouth, is not described here. But the ritual consecration preceded by the fire-pit and pavilion will be told in brief; its full extent cannot be told.
m.7.2.15.iti: Thus ends the fifteenth adhyāya, named The greatness of the guru in the rite of initiation, in the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.7.2.16.1: Upamanyu said: On an auspicious day, in a pure place free from many defects, the preceptor should first perform the rite called Samaya.
m.7.2.16.2: Having examined the ground according to rule by its smell, colour, taste and so on, he should construct a pavilion there in the manner taught in the treatises of the builders.
m.7.2.16.3: Having made an altar in its middle, he should arrange fire-pits in the eight directions, or likewise in the four directions; then, in due order, in the northeast...
m.7.2.16.4: ...he should make the principal pit, or else on the western side. Or, having made only the one principal pit, he should arrange the decoration,
m.7.2.16.5: with canopies, banners and garlands of many kinds in abundance. Then in the middle of the altar he should make a maṇḍala with auspicious marks,
m.7.2.16.6: with red, golden and other powders, fit for invoking the Lord; but a poor man should make it with powders of vermilion, rice and wild rice only.
m.7.2.16.7: It may be one cubit or two cubits wide, white or red. For a lotus of one cubit the pericarp is held to be eight finger-breadths.
m.7.2.16.8: The filaments are half of that, and the remainder is the eight petals and so on. For a lotus of two cubits, the pericarp and the rest are double.
m.7.2.16.9: Having made it rich in ornaments and secondary ornaments, he should again prepare, on the altar to its northeast, a maṇḍala of one cubit or half of that,
m.7.2.16.10: spread with paddy, husked rice, white mustard, sesame, flowers and kuśa grass. There he should set up the Śiva-pot endowed with the proper marks,
m.7.2.16.11: made of gold, silver, copper or clay, strewn with sandal, flowers and unbroken rice, covered with kuśa and sprouts of dūrvā grass,
m.7.2.16.12: its neck wound with white thread, wrapped in a pair of new cloths, filled with pure water, with a tuft of kuśa on top, containing precious substances and having a lid.
m.7.2.16.13: He should also prepare a spouted pitcher and a vardhanī vessel, a conch or a discus, all without the thread and so on, or even a lotus leaf.
m.7.2.16.14: He should place the pot on the northern petal of its seat-lotus, and in front, with sandal-water, the vardhanī of the king of weapons (the Astra).
m.7.2.16.15: Then, to the east of the maṇḍala, having likewise prepared the mantra-pot as before, he should perform the great worship of the Lord according to rule.
m.7.2.16.16: Or else on the shore of the ocean, by a river, in a cowpen or on a mountain, in a temple or a house, or in any other charming place,
m.7.2.16.17: having done all that was described before, or doing it without the pavilion and the rest, having made the maṇḍala as before and the fire-ground (sthaṇḍila) for the fire,
m.7.2.16.18: the guru, with a joyful face, endowed with all auspicious things and having completed his daily rites, enters the hall of worship.
m.7.2.16.19: Having performed the great worship of Maheśa in the centre of the maṇḍala, he should again invoke Śiva in the Śiva-pot and worship him.
m.7.2.16.20: Having meditated on the Lord, protector of the sacrifice, as facing west, he should worship the Lord's Astra in the Astra-vardhanī on the south.
m.7.2.16.21: Having installed the mantra in the mantra-pot, the one skilled in mantras, having performed the mudrās and everything else, should carry out the mantra-worship.
m.7.2.16.22: Then the best of preceptors should perform the fire-offering in the Śiva-fire in the principal pit, and other brahmins should make offerings in the pits all around.
m.7.2.16.23: Their offering is prescribed as a quarter or a half of the ācārya's. Or else the best of preceptors alone may offer in the principal pit.
m.7.2.16.24: Others should recite the Veda, hymns and auspicious benedictions, and others, devoted to Śiva, should perform japa according to rule.
m.7.2.16.25: Having had dance, song, instrumental music and other auspicious things performed, and having properly honoured the assembled members according to rule,
m.7.2.16.26: and then having had the puṇyāha declaration recited and again worshipped Śaṅkara, the preceptor should pray to the god, desiring grace for the disciple:
m.7.2.16.27: Be gracious, O Lord of the gods of gods. Entering my body, O Lord of the universe, release this one out of compassion, O treasure of compassion.
m.7.2.16.28: Then, having received permission, as if the Lord said, I will do so, the preceptor should bring the disciple, who has fasted or has eaten only sacrificial food,
m.7.2.16.29: or who has eaten once a day, self-restrained, bathed, having done his morning rites, repeating the praṇava, meditating on the god, and having performed auspicious acts,
m.7.2.16.30: and, in the area in front of the western door or of the southern door, having seated the young disciple on a seat of darbha grass facing north,
m.7.2.16.31: the guru, himself standing and facing east, having sprinkled the disciple, who holds his body erect with joined palms, with water from the sprinkling vessel, on the head with the Astra mantra and mudrā,
m.7.2.16.32: and having struck him by tossing a flower, the guru should bind his eyes with a new, consecrated cloth, half of a fine silk garment.
m.7.2.16.33: Then the guru should lead the disciple into the maṇḍala through the door; and he, directed by him, should circumambulate Śambhu three times.
m.7.2.16.34: Then, having offered to the Lord a handful of flowers mixed with gold, facing east or north, he should prostrate on the ground like a staff.
m.7.2.16.35: Then the preceptor, having sprinkled him with the root mantra and struck him on the head with the Astra as before, should remove his blindfold.
m.7.2.16.36: Having seen the maṇḍala, he should again bow with joined palms to the Lord. Then the Śaiva preceptor, seated on the south of the maṇḍala,
m.7.2.16.37: the guru, having seated the disciple on a darbha seat on his own left, and having worshipped Mahādeva, should place the Śiva-hand,
m.7.2.16.38: Regarding his hand as full of Śiva's radiance, he should utter the Śiva-mantra and, filled with the conviction of being Śiva, place it on the disciple's head.
m.7.2.16.39: With that same hand the preceptor should touch all the limbs; and the disciple too should bow on the ground to the Lord in the form of the preceptor.
m.7.2.16.40: Then, having duly worshipped the god in the Śiva-fire and offered three oblations, and having seated the disciple as before,
m.7.2.16.41: Touching him with the tips of darbha grass, he should enter him with his own self by means of the vidyā mantra. Having bowed to Mahādeva, he should perform the joining of the channels (nāḍī).
m.7.2.16.42: By the method stated in the Śiva scriptures, having effected the going-out of the vital breath and contemplating its entry into the disciple's body, he should then satiate the mantras with oblations.
m.7.2.16.43: For satiating the root mantra, ten oblations are to be offered with that very mantra; likewise three for the limbs, with the limb-mantras themselves, in due order.
m.7.2.16.44: Then, having offered the full oblation, the preceptor who knows the mantras should, for expiation, again make ten oblations with the root mantra.
m.7.2.16.45: Again worshipping the Lord of gods and sipping water properly, and having offered oblations as prescribed, the preceptor should raise the disciple from his own birth-class to vaiśya status.
m.7.2.16.46: In the same way he should produce kṣatriya status for him; and then, again making the elevation in the same manner, the preceptor should produce brāhmaṇa-hood for him.
m.7.2.16.47: Having thus raised the kṣatriya and made him a brāhmaṇa, he should then produce Rudra-hood for both; for a born brāhmaṇa he should accomplish just the name Rudra.
m.7.2.16.48: Having performed sprinkling and striking (tāḍana) of the disciple, the guru, contemplating his own self within himself as of the nature of Śiva, flashing like a spark—
m.7.2.16.49: —the guru should expel the breath with the mantra through the channel as described; having gone out, he should likewise enter through the channel into the disciple's heart.
m.7.2.16.50: Having entered, recalling his consciousness as resembling a blue dot, he should contemplate it as blazing, its impurity dispelled by his own radiance.
m.7.2.16.51: Taking it through that channel with the withdrawal gesture (saṃhāra-mudrā), the mantra-adept, placing it within by inhalation (pūraka) for the sake of oneness with himself—
m.7.2.16.52: —holding it with retention (kumbhaka), and then with exhalation (recaka) through the channel as before, should take it from there and place it in the disciple's heart.
m.7.2.16.53: Touching him and giving him the sacred thread received from Śiva, he should offer three oblations and afterwards give the full oblation.
m.7.2.16.54: Seating the disciple to the right of the deity on an excellent seat strewn with kuśa grass and flowers, with joined palms, facing north,
m.7.2.16.55: making him sit in the svastika posture, the preceptor himself, facing east and seated on an excellent seat, with mantras and sounds of great auspiciousness,
m.7.2.16.56: taking up the full pot, fully prepared, the preceptor, meditating on Śiva, should consecrate the disciple by sprinkling (abhiṣeka).
m.7.2.16.57: Then, wiping off the bath water and putting on a white garment, the disciple, having sipped water and being adorned, should go to the pavilion with joined palms.
m.7.2.16.58: Seating him as before on a seat of darbha grass, the guru, having worshipped the deity in the maṇḍala, should perform hand-placement (karanyāsa).
m.7.2.16.59: Then the preceptor should meditate on the Lord in his mind and, with ash, touch the disciple with both hands, uttering Śiva.
m.7.2.16.60: Then the Śiva-preceptor, having performed for him the burning, flooding and so on, and the sakalīkaraṇa by way of the placement of the mātṛkā letters,
m.7.2.16.61: then the preceptor, contemplating Śiva's seat on the disciple's head, should invoke Śiva there as prescribed and worship him mentally.
m.7.2.16.62: With joined palms he should entreat the Lord: Remain here always. Having thus made the request, he should contemplate the disciple as shining with Śambhu's radiance.
m.7.2.16.63: Then, having worshipped Śiva and obtained Śiva's command, which is of Śiva's very nature, he should softly utter the Śiva mantra into the disciple's ear.
m.7.2.16.64: The disciple, with joined palms, having heard the mantra with his mind absorbed in it, should slowly repeat it at the Śiva-preceptor's instruction.
m.7.2.16.65: Then the one skilled in mantras, having imparted the Śakti mantra too and having had it pronounced comfortably, should pronounce a blessing upon him.
m.7.2.16.66: Then he should briefly explain the meaning of the mantra through the relation of the signified and the signifier, teach the form of the Lord, and instruct in yoga and posture.
m.7.2.16.67: Then, by the guru's command, in the presence of Śiva, the fire and the guru, the disciple, resolving thus with devotion, should utter the initiation vow:
m.7.2.16.68: Better the giving up of life, or even the cutting off of the head, than that I should eat without having worshipped the blessed three-eyed Lord.
m.7.2.16.69: He himself, self-restrained, should offer worship until delusion is overturned; until then he should propitiate the Lord, devoted to him and having him as his highest refuge.
m.7.2.16.70: Then he will be called a samaya initiate in the Śaiva order; having gained eligibility, he should keep the guru's command and remain under his control.
m.7.2.16.71: After this, the guru, having performed placement on his hands, should take ash with his own hand and give it to the disciple with the root mantra, and also a rudrākṣa consecrated by mantra,
m.7.2.16.72: or an image of the Lord, or else a concealed form of him, and, where possible, the means for worship, fire-offering, recitation and meditation.
m.7.2.16.73: The disciple, too, should accept with great reverence what he receives from the Śiva-preceptor, by that preceptor's command and not otherwise.
m.7.2.16.74: Placing on his head with devotion all that he received from the teacher, he should guard it and worship Śambhu, whether in a monastery or at home.
m.7.2.16.75: After this the preceptor should teach him the Śaiva code of conduct, in accordance with his devotion and faith and in accordance with his understanding.
m.7.2.16.76: Whatever is spoken, whatever is commanded, and whatever else is declared by the Śiva-preceptor at the samaya rite—all that he should bear on his head.
m.7.2.16.77: Taking up, reading aloud and hearing the Śaiva scriptures he should do at the preceptor's direction, not by his own wish nor from anyone else.
m.7.2.16.78: Thus has been briefly described the sacrament called samaya, the supreme means for men to attain Śiva's city directly.
m.7.2.16.iti: Thus ends the sixteenth adhyāya, named The consecration of the disciple, in the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.7.2.17.1: Upamanyu said: After this, the guru, having carefully examined the disciple's fitness, should perform the purification of the six paths (ṣaḍ-adhva) so that the disciple is released from all bonds.
m.7.2.17.2: Kalā, tattva, bhuvana, varṇa, then pada, and mantra — thus, in brief, the sixfold path is enumerated.
m.7.2.17.3: The five kalās beginning with Nivṛtti are called by the wise the path of kalā; the other five paths are pervaded by the five kalās.
m.7.2.17.4: From the Śiva-tattva down to earth is declared the path of tattvas; it comprises twenty-six in number and is of pure, impure and mixed nature.
m.7.2.17.5: The path of worlds is proclaimed as extending from Ādhāra up to Unmanā; without counting their divisions and subdivisions, it comprises sixty in number.
m.7.2.17.6: The fifty letters, which are forms of Rudra, are called the path of letters; the path of words is declared to have many varieties.
m.7.2.17.7: The path of mantras, together with all the subsidiary mantras, is pervaded by the supreme Vidyā. Just as Śiva, the lord of the tattvas, is not counted among the tattvas,
m.7.2.17.8: so he, the lord of mantras, is not to be counted in the path of mantras. The pervasiveness of the kalā-path and the pervadedness of the other paths —
m.7.2.17.9: he who does not truly know this is not at all fit for the purification of the paths. He by whom the form of the sixfold path is not known —
m.7.2.17.10: by him the relation of pervaded and pervader cannot even be understood. Therefore the nature of the paths, and likewise the relation of pervaded and pervader,
m.7.2.17.11: only after understanding them properly should one perform the purification of the paths. Having done everything there as before, up to preparing the fire-pit and the maṇḍala,
m.7.2.17.12: he should make in the east a maṇḍala for the pitchers, two cubits in measure. Then the Śaiva preceptor, having bathed and performed his daily rites, together with the disciple,
m.7.2.17.13: entering the maṇḍala, should perform the worship of Śambhu as before. There, milk-rice for the Lord, cooked from rice not less than an āḍhaka in measure,
m.7.2.17.14: having offered half of it, he should set aside the rest for the homa. Then, in a maṇḍala prepared in front, adorned with coloured powders,
m.7.2.17.15: the preceptor should place five pitchers, in the four directions and in the middle. In them he should install the five Brahma-mantras, with their root syllables joined with bindu and nāda,
m.7.2.17.16: beginning with namaḥ and ending with the syllable ya, the foremost knower of ritual should install them: Īśāna in the middle pitcher, Tatpuruṣa in the one placed in front,
m.7.2.17.17: Aghora in the southern one, Vāmadeva in the northern (left) one, and Sadyojāta in the western one. Having made the protection and formed the mudrā, the consecration of the pitchers
m.7.2.17.18: having done, he should begin the homa in the Śiva-fire as before. That half of the milk-rice which was earlier set aside for the homa,
m.7.2.17.19: having offered it, he should keep its remainder for the disciple to eat. Having performed the rite up to the tarpaṇa of the mantras as before,
m.7.2.17.20: and having offered the full oblation for them, he should then perform the kindling (dīpana). After oṃ, huṃ, then the root mantra ending in phaṭ,
m.7.2.17.21: and finally ending with svāhā — this they declare to be the formula for kindling, and likewise the aṅga mantras in due order. Three oblations of these are to be given in the kindling rite.
m.7.2.17.22: With those mantras, one by one, their blazing forms are to be contemplated. A white thread, spun by a brāhmaṇa maiden, made threefold and then threefold again,
m.7.2.17.23: that thread, having consecrated it with the root mantra, he should tie to the tip of the disciple's tuft, letting it reach to the big toe of the disciple standing with body erect.
m.7.2.17.24: Having let that thread hang down, he should join the suṣumṇā to it there. Taking it up with the Śānta mudrā, the knower of mantras, with the root mantra,
m.7.2.17.25: having offered three oblations, should establish its (the suṣumṇā's) presence in the thread. Striking the disciple on the heart by casting a flower, as before,
m.7.2.17.26: taking up his consciousness and placing it in the dvādaśānta, joining the thread with the suṣumṇā thread, protecting it with the astra mantra and the armour (varma) mantra,
m.7.2.17.27: and then having veiled that thread, he should regard it as the disciple's body. The bond made of the three root impurities, characterized by enjoyership and enjoyability,
m.7.2.17.28: which produces the sense-objects, senses, body and the rest — this he should imagine as his. The kalās beginning with Śāntyatīta, which have the forms of the elements beginning with ether,
m.7.2.17.29: are to be joined to the thread by their own names and worshipped with those names joined with namaḥ, or else with their seed-syllables. Having done in order what was stated before,
m.7.2.17.30: he should then observe the pervasion of mala and the rest in the tattvas and the rest, and the pervasion of the kalās in mala and the rest; and having offered oblations, he should kindle the kalās.
m.7.2.17.31: Striking the disciple on the head, and placing the thread on the body in due order, he should mark the thread at the position of Śāntyatīta while uttering the mantra.
m.7.2.17.32: Having done thus in sequence from Śāntyatīta down to Nivṛtti, and having offered three oblations, he should afterwards worship Śiva in the maṇḍala.
m.7.2.17.33: Seating the disciple to the south of the deity, facing north, in a maṇḍala strewn with darbha grass, the guru should give him the caru left over from the homa.
m.7.2.17.34: The disciple, honouring what was given by the guru and uttering Śiva's name first, having eaten it, should afterwards sip water twice and recite the Śiva-mantra.
m.7.2.17.35: Likewise, in another maṇḍala the guru should give him pañcagavya; he too, drinking it according to his capacity and sipping water twice, should remember Śiva.
m.7.2.17.36: Seating the disciple in a third maṇḍala as before, he should give him a tooth-stick having the characteristics stated in the scriptures.
m.7.2.17.37: With its soft tip, facing east or north, seated and restraining his speech, the disciple should clean his teeth.
m.7.2.17.38: Having washed the tooth-stick and thrown it away, and having sipped water, he should remember Śiva; then, instructed by the preceptor, with joined palms he should enter the Śiva-maṇḍala.
m.7.2.17.39: If the discarded tooth-stick is seen by the guru lying with its tip toward the east, north or west, it is auspicious; otherwise it is inauspicious.
m.7.2.17.40: If it points toward an unfavourable direction, the guru, to pacify that fault, should offer a hundred oblations with the root mantra, or half of that, or half of that again.
m.7.2.17.41: Then, having touched the disciple and having whispered the mantra of Śiva into his ears, the guru should have that disciple stay for the preparatory rite (adhivāsana) on the right side of the deity.
m.7.2.17.42: Pure, on a bed of darbha grass spread with an unworn (new) covering and consecrated with mantras, he should lie down at night with his head to the east, meditating inwardly on Śiva.
m.7.2.17.43: The guru, having bound with the śikhā-mantra the tuft of the disciple, to whose tuft a thread is tied, and having covered him with an unworn cloth with the armour-mantra (varman),
m.7.2.17.44: and having drawn three lines all around with ash, and with sesame and mustard seeds empowered by the astra-mantra, he should offer an oblation (bali) to the lords of the directions outside that boundary.
m.7.2.17.45: The disciple too, having thus undergone the adhivāsana and fasting thereafter, on waking and rising should report to the guru the dream he has seen.
m.7.2.17.iti: Thus ends the seventeenth adhyāya, named The rite of Śiva initiation, in the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.7.2.18.1: Upamanyu said: Then, having completed everything, such as bathing, and being urged by the preceptor, the disciple should go to the side of Śiva's maṇḍala with joined palms, meditating.
m.7.2.18.2: Then, having done everything as on the previous day, except the worship, up to the binding of the eyes, the guru should show him the maṇḍala.
m.7.2.18.3: When the scattering of flowers has been done by the blindfolded disciple, he should assign to him the name of that deity where the flowers fall.
m.7.2.18.4: And having brought him near, in this maṇḍala bearing the offered remains, as before, he should worship the god Īśāna and offer oblations into the Śiva-fire.
m.7.2.18.5: If a bad dream has been seen by the disciple, to pacify that fault he should offer a hundred oblations, or half that, or half of that, with the root mantra.
m.7.2.18.6: Then, having let the thread tied to the topknot hang down as before, whatever rite concerns the Nivṛtti kalā, beginning with the worship of the support (ādhāra)...
m.7.2.18.7: ...ending with the worship of Vāgīśvarī, he should perform, preceded by homa. Then, having bowed to Vāgīśā, the virtuous one who pervades Nivṛtti,
m.7.2.18.8: and having worshipped the god in the maṇḍala and offered three oblations, he should bring about the child's (disciple's) entry into all the wombs simultaneously.
m.7.2.18.9: Then, having performed striking, sprinkling and the rest on the disciple's thread-body, having taken up his self and placed it in the dvādaśānta,
m.7.2.18.10: then, taking it from there too with the root mantra and the mudrā seen in the scriptures, the preceptor should mentally join it simultaneously to all the wombs.
m.7.2.18.11: There are eight classes of gods and five classes of animals; with the single human class, the wombs are fourteen.
m.7.2.18.12: For the disciple's simultaneous entry into all of them, he should mentally place the disciple's self in Vāgīśānī, as is proper.
m.7.2.18.13: For the formation of the embryo, having worshipped the god, bowed down, and offered oblations as prescribed, he should contemplate it as formed.
m.7.2.18.14: Thus, through ritual action, he should bring about the birth and continued life of the one formed, his uprightness, the fulfilment of enjoyments, and likewise supreme delight.
m.7.2.18.15: For expiation, and for the perfection of class, life-span, enjoyment and saṃskāras, the best of preceptors, having offered three oblations, should pray to the god.
m.7.2.18.16: Having in just this way removed the impurity of being an enjoyer and of attachment to objects, that is, the purification of that body, he should then cut the disciple's three bonds.
m.7.2.18.17: By cutting, through the complete severance of the bond that bound him, having made the disciple's consciousness pure, he should regard it as alone (free).
m.7.2.18.18: Having offered the full oblation into the fire, he should then worship Brahmā; having offered him three oblations, he should convey Śiva's command to him:
m.7.2.18.19: O Grandsire, no obstruction is to be made by you for this one who is going to the supreme Śaiva abode; this command of Śiva is most weighty.
m.7.2.18.20: Having commanded thus, worshipped him and dismissed him according to rule, he should worship Mahādeva and offer three oblations.
m.7.2.18.21: Having drawn up the disciple's self, purified by Nivṛtti, as before, and placed it in his own self and in the thread, he should then worship Vāgīśa.
m.7.2.18.22: Having offered three oblations to her, bowed and dismissed her, he should make the joining of Nivṛtti with the Pratiṣṭhā kalā.
m.7.2.18.23: At the joining, having performed worship of both together and offered three oblations, he should then visualise the entry of the disciple's self into Pratiṣṭhā.
m.7.2.18.24: Then, having invoked Pratiṣṭhā and done all that was stated before, he should contemplate its pervasion and Vāgīśānī as its pervader,
m.7.2.18.25: her resembling the disc of the full moon; and having done the rest as before, he should convey to Viṣṇu the command of Śiva, the Supreme Self.
m.7.2.18.26: And having performed the dismissal of Viṣṇu and the rest, having joined Pratiṣṭhā with Vidyā, and in her too, as before,
m.7.2.18.27: having done the rites, having contemplated its pervasion and Vāgīśā in due order, having done all up to the full oblation in the blazing fire, and the rest as before,
m.7.2.18.28: having invoked Nīlarudra and likewise performed worship and the rest for him, he should give him Śiva's command in the manner stated before.
m.7.2.18.29: Then, having dismissed him as well, and having joined the Vidyā kalā to Śānti, he should observe its pervasion.
m.7.2.18.30: Likewise he should contemplate Vāgīśī, the pervader of his own self, whose form resembles the rising sun, illuminating the ten directions.
m.7.2.18.31: Then, having done the rest as before, having invoked and worshipped the god Maheśvara and offered oblations to him, he should mentally convey Śiva's command.
m.7.2.18.32: Having likewise dismissed Maheśvara and performed the rite for this other kalā, having led it to the Śāntyatītā kalā, he should observe its pervasion.
m.7.2.18.33: Likewise he should contemplate Vāgīśī, the pervader of his own self, resembling the expanse of the sky; and do everything up to the full oblation as before.
m.7.2.18.34: Having done this by the remaining procedure and worshipped Sadāśiva, he should impart to him the command of Śambhu of immeasurable deeds.
m.7.2.18.35: There too, as before, placing Śiva on the head as before, and having worshipped Vāgīśa and bowed, he should dismiss her.
m.7.2.18.36: Then, having sprinkled the disciple on the head with the Śiva mantra as before, he should contemplate the dissolution of Śāntyatītā into the Śakti-tattva.
m.7.2.18.37: On the far shore beyond the six paths, he should contemplate the supreme Śaiva Śakti, pervading all paths, shining like ten million suns.
m.7.2.18.38: Having brought the disciple, stainless as pure crystal, before her, and afterwards having washed the scissors according to the method stated in the Śiva scriptures,
m.7.2.18.39: the preceptor should cut his topknot together with the thread. Then, having placed it on cow-dung, he should offer the topknot into the Śiva-fire,
m.7.2.18.40: with the root mantra ending in vauṣaṭ. Having washed the scissors again and placed them in the disciple's hand, he should return the disciple's consciousness into his body.
m.7.2.18.41: Then, having led the disciple (śiśu), who has bathed, sipped water ritually and had the auspicious rites (svastyayana) performed for him, into the vicinity of the maṇḍala, and having made him prostrate like a staff,
m.7.2.18.42: and having performed worship according to rule, the guru should offer three oblations with the audible (vācaka) mantra itself, to purify any deficiency in the ritual acts.
m.7.2.18.43: He should offer three oblations by way of whispered (upāṃśu) utterance. Again, having worshipped the Lord of gods, to purify any deficiency in the mantras,
m.7.2.18.44: he should offer three oblations by way of mental utterance. Then, having worshipped Śambhu present in the maṇḍala together with Ambā, and having offered three oblations, the guru should afterwards pray with folded hands:
m.7.2.18.45: O Lord, by your grace the purification of his six paths (ṣaḍadhvan) has been accomplished; therefore lead him to your supreme, imperishable abode.
m.7.2.18.46: Having thus informed the god, and having performed, preceded by the joining of the nāḍīs, the rite ending with the full oblation (pūrṇāhuti) as before, he should then purify the elements.
m.7.2.18.47: Then, for purification, in the rite of purifying the elements, he should meditate on the stable and unstable, then on the cold and hot, and then on the corresponding stations, as having the form of oneness through pervasion.
m.7.2.18.48: Having severed the knots of the elements and having abandoned the elements together with their presiding deities, he who by the method of steadiness repeats the mantra in the supreme Śiva —
m.7.2.18.49: having purified him, burnt his body, and flooded it with drops of nectar, and having installed the self, he should then make his body consist of the purified paths.
m.7.2.18.50: There, first, he should place the all-pervading kalā Śāntyatītā of his own path, wholly pure, on the disciple's head, and likewise Śānti on the face;
m.7.2.18.51: Vidyā from the throat down to the navel, Pratiṣṭhā below that in order down to the knees, and below that he should place Nivṛtti, and contemplate them.
m.7.2.18.52: Having placed the root mantra with its own seed-syllables and with the limbs, and knowing him the disciple to be of the nature of Śiva, he should invoke the god in the lotus of his heart and worship him.
m.7.2.18.53: Having invoked the eternal presence and identity with Śiva in the disciple, the guru should bring about the qualities in this disciple who is full of Śiva's radiance:
m.7.2.18.54: the powers beginning with aṇimā; saying, be gracious, he should offer three oblations. In the same way he should again confer on him the qualities:
m.7.2.18.55: omniscience, likewise contentment, knowledge without beginning or end, undiminished power, independence, and infinite power.
m.7.2.18.56: Then, having taken leave of the god, he should consecrate him with the jars of Sadyojāta and the rest, meditating in his heart on the Lord of gods in due order.
m.7.2.18.57: Then, having seated that disciple and worshipped Śiva as before, having obtained permission from Śiva, he should impart to him the Śaiva vidyā.
m.7.2.18.58: There he should impart it preceded by Oṃkāra, enclosed (sampuṭa), ending with namaḥ, joined with Śiva and Śakti; and the Śakti-vidyā of the same kind.
m.7.2.18.59: He should teach the seer, metre and deity, likewise the Śiva-nature of Śiva and Śivā, the worship of Śambhu with its surrounding deities (āvaraṇa), and the seats.
m.7.2.18.60: Having worshipped the Lord of gods again, he should inform Śiva: Whatever has been performed by me, make all of it well-done.
m.7.2.18.61: The guru, together with the disciple, having bowed to the god, stretched like a staff on the ground, should then dismiss him from the maṇḍala and also from the fire.
m.7.2.18.62: Then all those in the assembly who are worthy of honour should be honoured in order.
m.7.2.18.63: The assembly members together with the officiating priests should be served according to one's means. One should not be miserly with wealth if one desires one's own welfare.
m.7.2.18.iti: Thus ends the eighteenth adhyāya, named The purification of the six paths and the rest, in the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.7.2.19.1: Upamanyu said: Next I shall explain the rite known by name as sādhaka initiation, and the greatness of the mantra of this sacrament, which I indicated earlier in my account.
m.7.2.19.2: Having worshipped the god in the maṇḍala and installed him in the jar as before, and having offered oblations, the preceptor should lead the disciple, without a turban, to the maṇḍala on the ground.
m.7.2.19.3: Having performed the rite up to the full oblation as before, and likewise having offered a hundred oblations, the best of preceptors, having gratified the deity with the root mantra by means of the jars,
m.7.2.19.4: and having kindled the fire as before, and done in order what was stated earlier, having consecrated the disciple by sprinkling as before, he should impart the supreme mantra.
m.7.2.19.5: There, having performed in detail and in order the rite up to the instruction of the vidyā, he should hand over the Śaiva vidyā into the disciple's hand with flower-water, saying:
m.7.2.19.6: By the grace of the Supreme Lord, this great mantra will surely be for you the bestower of the fruit of all attainments in this world and the next.
m.7.2.19.7: Having said this and worshipped the god, the guru, having obtained permission from Śiva, should teach the sādhaka the mantra practice and Śiva-yoga.
m.7.2.19.8: Having heard the guru's instruction, the practitioner of the mantra should, step by step, perform the mantra-practice prior to its application.
m.7.2.19.9: The practice of the root mantra is called puraścaraṇa, because it is to be performed before (puraḥ) the act called application (viniyoga).
m.7.2.19.10: Mantra-practice is not absolutely obligatory for one seeking liberation; but if performed, it would be beneficial for him too, here and hereafter.
m.7.2.19.11: On an auspicious day, in an auspicious place, or at a time free from defects, with teeth and nails clean, bathed, having performed the morning rites,
m.7.2.19.12: having adorned himself with such perfumes, garlands and ornaments as are available, wearing a turban and an upper garment, entirely in white, and composed,
m.7.2.19.13: in a temple, a house, or some other very charming place, seated on a comfortable posture practised beforehand,
m.7.2.19.14: having made his own body Śaiva by the method taught in the Śiva scriptures, having worshipped the Lord of the lord of gods, Īśvara Nakulīśvara,
m.7.2.19.15: having offered him milk-rice, having completed the worship in order, having bowed down to that god and having received permission from his mouth,
m.7.2.19.16: he should repeat the Śiva mantra ten million times, or half of that, or half of that again; or two million times, or else one million.
m.7.2.19.17: And then, eating only milk-rice free of salt and alkalis, in measured quantity, he should always be non-violent, forbearing, calm and self-controlled.
m.7.2.19.18: If milk-rice is not available, he may live eating fruits, roots and the like, which are prescribed by Śiva himself, each successive one being distinguished in order:
m.7.2.19.19: cooked oblation-rice (caru), alms-food, then grains of barley-meal, barley gruel, vegetables, milk, curd, ghee, roots, fruits, and then water.
m.7.2.19.20: And having consecrated with the mantra the foods to be chewed, eaten and so on, he should, especially during this practice, always eat in silence.
m.7.2.19.21: The observer of the vow should bathe in pure water from a river or stream, purified by a hundred and eight repetitions of the mantra, or else sprinkle himself, according to his ability.
m.7.2.19.22: Likewise he should daily offer libations and make oblations into the Śiva-fire with seven, five or three substances, or else with ghee alone.
m.7.2.19.23: For the Śaiva practitioner who thus propitiates Śiva with devotion, nothing whatever is hard to obtain here or in the hereafter.
m.7.2.19.24: Or else, even without the formal practice of the mantra, he should repeat the mantra a thousand times every day with one-pointed mind, while fasting.
m.7.2.19.25: Nothing is difficult for him to attain, nor is there anything inauspicious for him anywhere; having gained knowledge, prosperity and happiness here, he also attains liberation.
m.7.2.19.26: In the practice, in the application, and likewise in daily and occasional rites, he should do japa after bathing in order with water, with ash, and with mantra.
m.7.2.19.27: Pure, with tied tuft of hair, wearing the sacred thread, with a pavitra ring on the hand, bearing the tripuṇḍra and rudrākṣa, he should repeat the five-syllabled vidyā.
m.7.2.19.iti: Thus ends the nineteenth adhyāya, named The consecration of the sādhaka and the greatness of the mantra, in the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.7.2.20.1: Upamanyu said: Then the guru should consecrate as ācārya the disciple who has been thus purified and has performed the Pāśupata vow, because he is fit for it; and otherwise he should not.
m.7.2.20.2: Having made the maṇḍala as before and having worshipped the Supreme Lord, he should place five pitchers in the directions and in the centre, as before.
m.7.2.20.3: Having installed Nivṛtti in front (east), Pratiṣṭhā in the western pitcher, Vidyā in the south, Śānti in the north, and the supreme Śāntyatītā in the centre—
m.7.2.20.4: having performed the protective rites and so on there, having formed the cow-gesture (dhenu-mudrā), having consecrated the pots with mantras, and having made oblations up to the final full oblation as before—
m.7.2.20.5: the preceptor, having led the disciple into the maṇḍala without a turban, should perform the satiation (tarpaṇa) and other rites of the mantras, ending as before.
m.7.2.20.6: Then, having worshipped the Lord of gods and taken his leave as before, he should make that disciple mount the seat for the consecration.
m.7.2.20.7: Afterwards, having performed the sakalīkaraṇa on him—who embodies the five kalās and whose body has been invested with mantras—and having bound him, he should offer the disciple to Śiva.
m.7.2.20.8: Then, lifting the pots in order, beginning with the Nivṛtti pitcher and ending with the central one, he should bathe that disciple with the Śiva mantra alone.
m.7.2.20.9: Then the preceptor, having attained the state of Śiva, should place the Śiva-hand on the head of the novice and proclaim him a Śivācārya.
m.7.2.20.10: Then, having adorned him and worshipped the god in the Śiva-maṇḍala, having offered one hundred and eight oblations, he should then give the full oblation.
m.7.2.20.11: Again having worshipped the Lord of gods and prostrated on the ground like a staff, placing joined palms on his head, the guru should address Śiva:
m.7.2.20.12: O Lord, by your grace this man has been made a preceptor by me. O God, showing him favour, may your divine command be granted to him.
m.7.2.20.13: Having thus petitioned and again bowed together with the disciple, the guru should worship Śiva and the divine Śiva-scripture (Śivāgama) as he would Śiva.
m.7.2.20.14: Again taking Śiva's leave, the preceptor should then give the book of Śiva-knowledge to the disciple with both hands.
m.7.2.20.15: He (the disciple), placing that knowledge (the scripture) on his head, should set it upon the seat of knowledge, and, having saluted it properly, worship it.
m.7.2.20.16: Then the guru should also give him royal insignia, since one who has attained the rank of ācārya deserves even a kingdom.
m.7.2.20.17: Then he should give instruction, as practised by the ancients, as taught in the Śiva-scriptures, and as honoured among people.
m.7.2.20.18: Saying: Having carefully examined disciples by the marks stated in the Śiva-scriptures and having initiated them, the preceptor should impart Śiva-knowledge to them.
m.7.2.20.19: Likewise he should earnestly cultivate all this: freedom from strain, purity, forbearance, compassion, and also freedom from craving and from envy.
m.7.2.20.20: Having thus instructed that disciple and dismissed Śiva from the maṇḍala, he should worship the Śiva-pitcher, the fire and the rest, and also the assembly members.
m.7.2.20.21: Or else the guru together with his group may perform the saṃskāras simultaneously; in that case three or two stages of the procedure are taught to be combined.
m.7.2.20.22: At the very beginning he should arrange the pitchers as in the purification of the paths, having performed the whole samaya-saṃskāra except the consecration.
m.7.2.20.23: Having worshipped Śiva again and performed the purification of the paths, when that is completed he should worship the god once more.
m.7.2.20.24: Having offered oblations to the mantra, satiated it, kindled it, and invoked the blessing of the Lord, he should place the mantra in the disciple's hand and complete the rest.
m.7.2.20.25: Or else, having mentally gone through the entire mantra-saṃskāra in order, the guru should perform the purification of the paths ending with the consecration.
m.7.2.20.26: There, whatever procedure is prescribed for the kalās beginning with Śāntyatītā, all of it is to be performed in the purification of the three tattvas.
m.7.2.20.27: The triad of tattvas is declared to be named Śiva, Vidyā and Ātman. In Śakti arose Śiva, from him Vidyā, and from her the Ātman arose.
m.7.2.20.28: The path of Śāntyatītā is pervaded by Śiva; the higher one next to it by Vidyā; and the remaining path, in its entirety, by the Ātman, in order.
m.7.2.20.29: Considering the Śāmbhava initiation hard to attain, the wise who have mastered the meaning of the Śiva-scriptures should commend the Śākta saṃskāra, which has mantra as its root.
m.7.2.20.30: Thus I have told you everything—this fourfold nature of the rite called saṃskāra. O Kṛṣṇa, what more do you wish to hear?
m.7.2.20.iti: Thus ends the twentieth adhyāya, named The special and other consecrations, in the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.7.2.21.1: Kṛṣṇa said: O Lord, I wish to hear about the daily and occasional rites taught in the Śaiva scriptures for those who follow the Śaiva way of life.
m.7.2.21.2: Upamanyu said: Rising from bed at dawn, he should meditate on the God together with Ambā. After thinking over his duties for the day, he should leave the house when the dawn has risen.
m.7.2.21.3: Then he should relieve himself in an unobstructed, solitary place. After cleansing himself according to the rules, he should clean his teeth.
m.7.2.21.4: If tooth-sticks are not available, and on the eighth lunar day and similar days, he should cleanse his mouth with twelve mouthfuls of water.
m.7.2.21.5: Afterwards, having sipped water according to the rule, he should take the water bath (vāruṇa), in a river, in a temple tank, in a lake, or even at home.
m.7.2.21.6: Placing the bathing materials on its bank, he should remove the outer dirt, smear himself with earth and bathe, and then smear himself with cow-dung.
m.7.2.21.7: Having bathed again and again, and either discarding the cloth or washing it, well bathed, he should then put on a clean garment like a king.
m.7.2.21.8: A celibate student, an ascetic, and a widow should not take the cleansing bath, a bath with perfumes and the like, or cleaning of the teeth.
m.7.2.21.9: Wearing the sacred thread, tying his topknot and entering the water, he should immerse himself, sip water properly, and draw a triple circle in the water.
m.7.2.21.10: Submerged in the water, he should again repeat the mantra as far as he can and remember Śiva. Rising and sipping water, he should sprinkle himself with that same mantra.
m.7.2.21.11: He should do so with a cow's horn together with darbha grass, or with a palāśa leaf, or a lotus leaf, or with his two hands, five times or just three times.
m.7.2.21.12: In a garden and the like, or at home, he should bathe with a vardhanī vessel or a pitcher; at the time of immersion he should sprinkle himself with waters consecrated by mantras.
m.7.2.21.13: But if he is unable to take the water bath, he should cleanse his body from the soles of the feet to the head with a clean wet cloth.
m.7.2.21.14: Or he may take the fire bath (āgneya, with ash), or the mantra bath, or a bath with the Śiva mantra. A bath consisting of intent contemplation of Śiva is called the inner (ātmīya) bath of the yogin.
m.7.2.21.15: According to the procedure prescribed in his own sūtra, beginning with mantra-accompanied sipping of water, he should perform the rites ending with the brahmayajña, after offering libations to the gods and others.
m.7.2.21.16: Having meditated on Mahādeva residing in the solar disc and worshipped him according to rule, he should then offer the arghya to that Śiva in the form of the Sun.
m.7.2.21.17: Or else, having done this as stated in his own sūtra, he should cleanse his hands; then, performing the hand-placement (karanyāsa), he makes his body complete with the mantras.
m.7.2.21.18: Having sprinkled himself, with a bunch of kuśa grass, with water held in the left hand mixed with fragrance and white mustard seeds and accompanied by the root mantra,
m.7.2.21.19: with the mantras beginning āpo hi ṣṭhā, and having smelled the remaining water through the left nostril only, he should visualise the God within as white.
m.7.2.21.20: And taking up the sin residing in the body, expelling it through the other (savya) nostril, he should visualize it, black in colour, as lying outside, cast upon a stone.
m.7.2.21.21: Then he should offer libations to the gods and especially to the sages, and to the beings and the ancestors, and give the arghya according to rule.
m.7.2.21.22: With water mixed with red sandal he should make on the ground a well-rounded circle a hand's breadth in size, adorned with red powder and the like.
m.7.2.21.23: There he should worship the Sun together with his surrounding retinue, with the mantra khakholkāya along with its limbs, for the attainment of happiness.
m.7.2.21.24: Making a circle again and worshipping it with its limbs, he should place there a golden vessel measuring a Magadha prastha,
m.7.2.21.25: and fill it with fragrant water mixed with red sandal, with red flowers and sesame seeds, together with kuśa grass and unbroken rice,
m.7.2.21.26: with dūrvā grass, apāmārga and cow products, or with plain water alone. Kneeling on the ground and bowing to the God in the circle,
m.7.2.21.27: and placing that vessel on his head, he should offer that arghya to Śiva. Or else, with cupped hands, taking water with darbha grass, with the root mantra,
m.7.2.21.28: he should throw it up to Śiva, who dwells in the sky in the form of the Sun. Then, after cleansing his hands, he should again perform the hand-placement.
m.7.2.21.29: Understanding Śiva as consisting of the five Brahman mantras, from Īśāna to Sadyojāta, he should take the ash, rub it with the mantras, and touch his limbs,
m.7.2.21.30: with those mantras, down to the feet: head, face, heart, private parts and feet, in order. Then, rubbing the whole body with the root mantra, he should put on another garment,
m.7.2.21.31: Having put it on and sipped water twice, sprinkling himself with water consecrated by the eleven mantras, and covering himself with another upper cloth, he should sip water twice and remember Śiva.
m.7.2.21.32: Again having placed the mantras on his hands, the mantra-practitioner should draw the tripuṇḍra with ash, straight, oblong and distinct, on the forehead, with fragrant water.
m.7.2.21.33: Whatever mark has been drawn with ash on the forehead—round, square, a dot, or a half-moon—
m.7.2.21.34: he should draw the same on the arms, on the head, and between the breasts. Smearing the whole body with ash is not equal to these tripuṇḍra marks.
m.7.2.21.35: Therefore he should draw the tripuṇḍra alone, without smearing. He should wear rudrākṣa beads on the head, the neck, the ears and the hand.
m.7.2.21.36: A gold-coloured, unbroken, fine bead, not worn by others, is auspicious. For brāhmaṇas and the others in order, the best are white, yellow, red and then black.
m.7.2.21.37: If that is not available, whatever is available may be worn, provided it is undefiled. Even then, a bead proper to the higher should not be worn by the lower, nor the lower by the higher.
m.7.2.21.38: One who is impure should not wear the bead; he should wear it at all times. In this way, at the three junctures of the day, or at two, or just once,
m.7.2.21.39: having performed the bath and the rest according to his ability, he should worship the Supreme Lord. Going to the place of worship, he should settle into a pleasing seat,
m.7.2.21.40: and, facing east or north, meditate on the God and the Goddess. He should bow to the teachers from Śveta to Nakulīśa, to their disciples, and to his own guru.
m.7.2.21.41: Then, having again bowed to the god Śiva, one should recite the group of eight names: Śiva, Maheśvara, Rudra, Viṣṇu, Pitāmaha,
m.7.2.21.42: Saṃsāravaidya, Sarvajña and Paramātman — this is the group of eight. Or else, having recited the single name Śiva more than eleven times,
m.7.2.21.43: and having meditated on a mass of radiance at the tip of the tongue for the allaying of illnesses and the like, having washed the feet and made the hands anointed with sandal paste, one should perform the placing of mantras on the hands (karanyāsa), preceded by the purification of the hands.
m.7.2.21.iti: Thus ends the twenty-first adhyāya, named The daily and occasional rites, in the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.7.2.22.1: Upamanyu said: Nyāsa is said to be of three kinds, following the order of sustenance (sthiti), origination (utpatti) and dissolution (laya). The sthiti-nyāsa is for householders, and the utpatti nyāsa for celibate students (brahmacārins).
m.7.2.22.2: For renunciants (yatis) the dissolution-nyāsa, and likewise for forest-dwellers. That same dissolution-nyāsa is for a woman without a husband; for a married woman of the household it should be sthiti.
m.7.2.22.3: For a maiden, again, utpatti. I shall now state the defining feature of the nyāsa: placement from the thumb to the little finger is called the sthiti-nyāsa.
m.7.2.22.4: Beginning from the right thumb and ending at the left thumb is declared the utpatti-nyāsa; the reverse is the dissolution (saṃhṛti).
m.7.2.22.5: One should place in due order the syllables beginning with na, each with the bindu; one should place Śiva on the fingers, and also on the two palms and the two ring fingers.
m.7.2.22.6: Then, having performed the astra-nyāsa in the ten directions with the astra-mantra, one should contemplate the five kalās beginning with Nivṛtti, which embody the five elements,
m.7.2.22.7: together with the lords of the five elements, endowed with their respective emblems, residing in the heart, throat, palate, the middle of the brows, and the brahmarandhra;
m.7.2.22.8: one should contemplate them, with their knots, by their respective seed-syllables, within those respective seeds. For their purification one should recite the five-syllabled vidyā.
m.7.2.22.9: Having restrained the vital breath according to the number of the guṇas, one should then cut the knot of the elements with the astra mantra itself, by means of the astra-mudrā.
m.7.2.22.10: One should unite the self—driven by the vital breath through the suṣumṇā channel and issuing out through the brahmarandhra—with the radiance of Śiva.
m.7.2.22.11: Afterwards, having dried up the body with the wind, one should burn it with the fire of Time (kālāgni). Then, by the upward process, having withdrawn the kalās by means of the wind,
m.7.2.22.12: and having withdrawn the burnt body, touching the kalās together with their lord, one should flood the body with nectar and set each in its proper place.
m.7.2.22.13: Or else, the body having been withdrawn and burnt, without the re-creation of the kalās, one should then perform the flooding with nectar of what has become ashes.
m.7.2.22.14: Then, into that body made of the vidyā (mantra), one should join through the brahmarandhra the self, shaped like a lamp-flame, issuing forth from Śiva.
m.7.2.22.15: Having meditated on it as having entered within the body into the heart-lotus, one should again sprinkle the body made of vidyā with a shower of nectar.
m.7.2.22.16: Then one should perform the hand-nyāsa, preceded by purification of the hands; and after that perform the body-nyāsa with the great mudrā.
m.7.2.22.17: Then, having done the limb-nyāsa by the method taught by Śiva, one should perform the syllable-nyāsa on the joints of the hands, feet and so on.
m.7.2.22.18: Then, having placed the six limbs together with the six jātis, one should afterwards perform the binding of the directions in due order, beginning with the south-east (Āgneya).
m.7.2.22.19: Or else one may perform only the five-limbed nyāsa beginning with the head, and likewise the six-limbed nyāsa, without the purification of the elements and the rest.
m.7.2.22.20: Having thus, in abbreviated form, purified body and self, and having attained the state of Śiva, one should worship the Supreme Lord.
m.7.2.22.21: But one who has the time and no confusion of mind should perform the nyāsa rite according to the extended procedure.
m.7.2.22.22: Among these, the first is the mātṛkā-nyāsa, next after it the brahma-nyāsa, third the praṇava-nyāsa, and after that the haṃsa-nyāsa.
m.7.2.22.23: The fifth nyāsa is said by the wise to consist of the five syllables. Of these one may perform one or several in rites such as worship.
m.7.2.22.24: Having placed a on the head and ā on the forehead, likewise i and ī on the two eyes, and u and ū on the two ears,
m.7.2.22.25: ṛ and ṝ on the two cheeks, ḷ and ḹ on the two nostrils, e and ai on the two lips, o and au on the two rows of teeth, in order,
m.7.2.22.26: aṃ on the tongue, and then aḥ is to be applied on the palate, in due order. One should place the ka-group on the right hand, on its five joints.
m.7.2.22.27: And likewise one should place the ca-group on the joints of the left hand; and the ṭa-group and ta-group on both feet.
m.7.2.22.28: pa and pha on the two sides, then ba and bha on the back and the navel; one should place ma on the heart. Then in due order on the skin and the rest,
m.7.2.22.29: one should place the letters from ya to sa on the seven bodily constituents (dhātus); ha within the heart, and kṣa between the two brows.
m.7.2.22.30: Having thus placed the fifty letters by the method of Rudra, one should place the five Brahmans (brahma-mantras), according to the divisions of limbs, faces and kalās.
m.7.2.22.31: Having performed the hand-nyāsa and the rest with them, or not, in order, one should assign these to the head, face, heart, private parts and feet.
m.7.2.22.32: Then one should assign the faces, beginning with the upper and ending with the western; and the five kalās of Īśāna on these five, in order.
m.7.2.22.33: Then the four kalās of Puruṣa are to be placed on the four faces, following the order beginning with the east.
m.7.2.22.34: On the heart, throat, shoulders, navel, belly, back and chest—the eight kalās of Aghora; also on the feet and the hands.
m.7.2.22.35: Afterwards one should contemplate the thirteen kalās of Vāmadeva on the anus, penis, thighs, knees, shanks, buttocks, hips and sides.
m.7.2.22.36: The eight kalās of Sadyojāta too the best knower of ritual should assign to the feet, the hands, the nose, the head and the arms. Having thus performed in due sequence the nyāsa of the thirty-eight kalās,
m.7.2.22.37: afterwards the wise knower of the praṇava should perform the praṇava-nyāsa: on both arms, on the elbows and on the wrists,
m.7.2.22.38: on the sides, belly, thighs and shanks, on the feet and likewise on the back. Having thus performed the praṇava-placement, the one skilled in nyāsa
m.7.2.22.39: should perform the haṃsa-nyāsa as taught in the Śaiva scripture: dividing the seed-syllable of haṃsa, placing it on the eyes and on the nostrils,
m.7.2.22.40: dividing it, on the arms, eyes, mouth, forehead, and on the ears, on the armpits, the shoulders, the sides and likewise the breasts.
m.7.2.22.41: On the waist, the two hands and the two ankles, or else by the method of the five limbs (pañcāṅga) — having performed this haṃsa-nyāsa, one should then place the five-syllabled mantra (pañcākṣarī),
m.7.2.22.42: according to the method stated before, by which Śiva-hood arises. One who is not Śiva should not practise the worship of Śiva; one who is not Śiva should not worship Śiva; one who is not Śiva should not meditate on Śiva; one who is not Śiva cannot attain Śiva.
m.7.2.22.43: Therefore, having made the body Śaiva and having abandoned the notion of being a bound soul (paśu), and contemplating, I am Śiva, one should perform the Śaiva rite.
m.7.2.22.44: The sacrifice of ritual action, the sacrifice of austerity, the sacrifice of japa which is higher than that, the sacrifice of meditation and the sacrifice of knowledge — these are proclaimed as the five sacrifices.
m.7.2.22.45: Some are devoted to the sacrifice of action, others to the sacrifice of austerity, still others to the sacrifice of japa, and likewise some to the sacrifice of meditation,
m.7.2.22.46: and others are devoted to the sacrifice of knowledge; each successive one is superior. The sacrifice of action is said to be twofold, by the distinction of being done with desire and without desire.
m.7.2.22.47: The one with desire, having enjoyed the objects of desire, being attached to desires, is born again. The desireless one, having enjoyed pleasures in Rudra's abode, then falling from there,
m.7.2.22.48: is born as one devoted to the sacrifice of austerity — there is no doubt about this. And the ascetic, again having enjoyed pleasures there and then falling from there,
m.7.2.22.49: is born on earth as a man devoted to japa and meditation. The mortal devoted to japa and meditation, here, by virtue of the excellence of that,
m.7.2.22.50: having obtained knowledge, very soon attains union with Śiva (śiva-sāyujya). Therefore even the sacrifice of action of embodied beings, enjoined by Śiva, leads to liberation;
m.7.2.22.51: when desireless; joined with desire, it will lead only to bondage. Therefore, among the five sacrifices, one should be intent on meditation and knowledge.
m.7.2.22.52: He who has meditation and knowledge has crossed the ocean of worldly existence. Free from faults such as violence, pure, a means of purifying the mind,
m.7.2.22.53: the sacrifice of meditation is therefore supreme, granting the fruit of final liberation. Just as servants working outside are not great sharers in the reward,
m.7.2.22.54: as is seen in a king's palace, so too here are the ritualists. For to meditators the subtle form of the Lord becomes directly perceptible,
m.7.2.22.55: just as here, for ritualists, the gross form is fashioned from clay, wood and the like. Therefore those devoted to the sacrifice of meditation, regarding gods made of stone and clay,
m.7.2.22.56: do not wholly resort to them, because they know the true nature of Śiva. The man who, abandoning Śiva abiding in the self, worships him outside,
m.7.2.22.57: is like one who throws away the fruit in his hand and licks his own elbow. From knowledge comes meditation, and from meditation knowledge again arises;
m.7.2.22.58: through both of these comes liberation; therefore one should be devoted to meditation. At the dvādaśānta, likewise on the crown of the head, on the forehead, between the eyebrows,
m.7.2.22.59: or at the tip of the nose, or likewise in the mouth, at the neck, and in the heart, or at the navel — the eternal seat — with a mind pierced by faith,
m.7.2.22.60: one should worship the God and the Goddess with the offerings of external worship. Or else one should worship daily in a liṅga, or even in a man-made image,
m.7.2.22.61: or in the fire, or on a sacrificial ground, with devotion and according to one's means. Or else one should worship the Supreme Lord both inwardly and outwardly. One devoted to inner worship may or may not perform external worship.
m.7.2.22.iti: Thus ends the twenty-second adhyāya, named The daily and occasional rites taught in the Śaiva scriptures, in the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.7.2.23.1: Upamanyu said: I shall now briefly set out the explanation of the procedure of worship that was taught in the Śiva-scripture by Śiva himself to Śivā.
m.7.2.23.2: Whether or not one has first performed the inner worship as an auxiliary rite, ending with the fire-offering, one should afterwards perform the outer worship.
m.7.2.23.3: There, having mentally prepared the materials and purified them, having meditated on the god Vināyaka and worshipped him according to rule,
m.7.2.23.4: and having duly worshipped in the mind Nandīśa on the south and likewise Suyaśā on the north, the wise one should conceive a seat for the deity:
m.7.2.23.5: a seat furnished with the parts beginning with the ārādhana-seat — a lion-seat, a yoga-seat and the like, or a spotless lotus-seat endowed with the three tattvas.
m.7.2.23.6: Upon it one should meditate on Śiva together with Ambā, captivating to all, endowed with all auspicious marks, beautiful in every limb,
m.7.2.23.7: possessed of every excellence, adorned with all ornaments, with red lips, hands and feet, his face smiling white like jasmine and the moon,
m.7.2.23.8: resembling pure crystal, with three eyes like full-blown lotuses, four-armed, of noble limbs, bearing the lovely crescent of the moon,
m.7.2.23.9: with hands in the boon-giving and fear-dispelling gestures, Hara holding the deer and the axe, with serpents as necklace and bracelets, with a lovely blue region of the throat,
m.7.2.23.10: beyond all comparison, with his attendants and retinue. Then one should contemplate Maheśvarī on his left side,
m.7.2.23.11: lustrous like the petals of a full-blown lotus, with wide and long eyes, a face like the full moon, and dark curling hair,
m.7.2.23.12: resembling the petals of a blue lotus, wearing the half-moon as her crest, with breasts very round, firm, high, smooth and full,
m.7.2.23.13: slender-waisted, broad-hipped, clad in a fine, delicate yellow garment, furnished with all ornaments, radiant with the mark on her forehead,
m.7.2.23.14: graced by tresses strewn with varied flowers, fitting in form in every respect, her face slightly bowed with modesty,
m.7.2.23.15: holding a shining golden lotus in her right hand, placing the other hand straight like a staff, seated on the great seat,
m.7.2.23.16: the severer of bonds, manifestly of the nature of being, consciousness and bliss. Having thus meditated on the god and the goddess upon the auspicious excellent seat,
m.7.2.23.17: one should worship them with devotion, with flowers of the heart, as with all the offerings. Or else, having thus conceived any one of the forms of the Lord —
m.7.2.23.18: the Śaiva form called Sadāśiva, or likewise the supreme Māheśvarī form, or the one named Ṣaḍviṃśaka, or else the one called Śrīkaṇṭha —
m.7.2.23.19: and having also performed the placing of mantras (nyāsa) and the rest on it just as on one's own body, and in this form meditating on Śiva as embodied, beyond the existent and the non-existent,
m.7.2.23.20: having meditated thus, one should complete the worship mentally following the very order of the outer rite. Afterwards one should mentally perform the fire-offering in the navel with fuel-sticks, ghee and the rest.
m.7.2.23.21: And between the eyebrows one should meditate on Śiva in the form of a pure lamp-flame. Thus, whether the inner worship is done as an auxiliary or independently, in the auspicious meditative yoga,
m.7.2.23.22: ending with the fire-rite, the procedure is the same in every case. Then, having completed the entire mental sequence of worship,
m.7.2.23.23: one should worship the god in the liṅga, or on the sthaṇḍila (prepared ground), or even in the fire.
m.7.2.23.iti: Thus ends the twenty-third adhyāya, named The explanation of the rite of worship, in the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.7.2.24.1: Upamanyu said: For purification, one should sprinkle the place of worship with water using the root mantra, and with water scented with fragrance and sandal one should place a flower there.
m.7.2.24.2: Having driven away the obstacles with the astra mantra, and having enclosed the place with the varma (armour) mantra, and having placed the astra in the directions, one should prepare the ground for worship.
m.7.2.24.3: Spreading darbha grass there, one should wash the vessels with sprinkling and so on; having purified all the vessels, one should perform the purification of the materials.
m.7.2.24.4: The sprinkling vessel (prokṣaṇī), the arghya vessel, after that the pādya vessel, and likewise the vessel for ācamana water — this is the set of four.
m.7.2.24.5: Having washed, sprinkled and looked upon them, one should then pour pure water into them, and put in all the auspicious substances as available.
m.7.2.24.6: Gems, silver, gold, fragrances, flowers, unbroken rice and the like, fruits, sprouts and darbha grass — these are auspicious substances of many kinds.
m.7.2.24.7: Into the bathing water one should put fragrances and the like, and especially into the drinking water one should put cool and pleasing flowers and so forth.
m.7.2.24.8: One should put uśīra (vetiver) and sandal into the pādya water; and nutmeg, kaṅkola, camphor, bahumūla and tamāla —
m.7.2.24.9: — these, having been powdered, one should especially put into the ācamana water; and cardamom, camphor and sandal into all the vessels.
m.7.2.24.10: Into the arghya vessel one should put tips of kuśa grass, unbroken rice, barley, paddy and sesame too, ghee, white mustard, flowers and sacred ash.
m.7.2.24.11: Into the sprinkling vessel one should put kuśa, flowers, barley, paddy, bahumūla, tamāla and sacred ash, in due order.
m.7.2.24.12: Having placed the mantra in all the vessels, having enclosed them on the outside with the varma mantra, and afterwards protecting them with the astra, one should display the dhenu-mudrā (cow gesture).
m.7.2.24.13: Then, having sprinkled all the articles of worship with water from the sprinkling vessel, one should purify them duly with the root mantra.
m.7.2.24.14: If all the vessels are not available, the best of practitioners should prepare a single sprinkling vessel for all rites, and with water prepare that common arghya.
m.7.2.24.15: Then, having duly worshipped Lord Vināyaka in order with foods to be chewed and eaten and so on, then on the right side of the door —
m.7.2.24.16: — one should properly worship Nandin himself, lord of the inner apartments, resembling a mountain of gold, adorned with all ornaments,
m.7.2.24.17: wearing the crescent moon as a crown, gentle, three-eyed and four-armed, the lord bearing a blazing trident, a deer, an axe and a sharp cane,
m.7.2.24.18: with a face like the orb of the moon, or else lion-faced. And on the north side of the door, one should worship his wife, daughter of the Maruts,
m.7.2.24.19: Suyaśā, of good vows, the mother, intent on adorning the feet of the Goddess. Having worshipped her, and having entered the inner shrine of the Supreme Lord,
m.7.2.24.20: having worshipped the liṅga with those materials, one should remove the remnants of the previous offering (nirmālya); having washed it, one should place a flower on its top for its purification.
m.7.2.24.21: Holding a flower in hand, one should repeat the mantra according to one's capacity for the purification of the mantra. Having worshipped Caṇḍa in the north-east, one should have the nirmālya given to him.
m.7.2.24.22: Afterwards one should construct the seat, beginning with the support (ādhāra), in due order. Then one should meditate on the auspicious, dark Ādhāraśakti upon the ground.
m.7.2.24.23: In front of her, one should visualise Ananta with raised neck, coiled in form, white, five-hooded, as if licking the sky.
m.7.2.24.24: Above him is the auspicious seat with four lion feet; dharma, knowledge, detachment and sovereignty are indeed its feet.
m.7.2.24.25: Placed at the south-east and the other intermediate quarters, they are white, red, yellow and dark in colour; adharma and the rest are placed at the east and the other quarters, ending with the north, in order.
m.7.2.24.26: Having placed them, one should visualise the limbs of the seat as resembling lapis lazuli. Its upper covering is a lotus seat, spotless and white.
m.7.2.24.27: They declare its eight petals to be the eightfold powers beginning with aṇimā; and its filaments the Rudras beginning with Vāma, together with the śaktis beginning with Vāmā.
m.7.2.24.28: The seeds also are those very śaktis, within, up to Manonmanī; the pericarp is supreme detachment, and the stalk is knowledge of the nature of Śiva.
m.7.2.24.29: The bulb is the essence of Śiva-dharma. At the end of the pericarp are the three discs; above the three discs is the seat consisting of the triad of principles beginning with ātman.
m.7.2.24.30: Above all the seats one should imagine a divine seat, comfortable, spread with variegated coverings, shining with pure knowledge (śuddhavidyā).
m.7.2.24.31: One should perform invocation, installation, confinement, gazing and obeisance, forming the mudrās for each separately.
m.7.2.24.32: Having offered water for the feet, water for sipping, arghya, fragrance, and after that flowers, incense, a lamp and betel, one should then bathe Śiva and Śivā.
m.7.2.24.33: Or else, having thus arranged the seat and the image, and having made it complete with limbs (sakalīkṛtya) by the root mantra, by the Brahma-mantras and likewise by others,
m.7.2.24.34: one should then invoke, together with the Goddess, Śiva, the supreme cause, the god resembling pure crystal, unmoving and imperishable,
m.7.2.24.35: the cause of all worlds, supreme, consisting of all worlds, standing within and without, pervading all, subtler than the subtle and greater than the great,
m.7.2.24.36: the imperishable Lord, seen without effort by devotees, yet beyond the reach even of gods such as Brahmā, Indra, Viṣṇu and Rudra,
m.7.2.24.37: the essence of the Vedas, heard in scripture to be beyond the reach even of the learned, without beginning, middle or end, the medicine for those afflicted with the disease of worldly existence,
m.7.2.24.38: renowned as the Śiva-principle, established in the world for its welfare. With devotion one should worship the excellent liṅga with the five services.
m.7.2.24.39: The liṅga is the form of Maheśa, Śiva, the Supreme Self. At the time of bathing one should perform auspicious acts such as shouts of victory.
m.7.2.24.40: He should be bathed with the five cow-products, ghee, milk, curd, honey and the like first, with roots, with the juices of fruits, and with sesame, mustard and barley-meal,
m.7.2.24.41: Having bathed the deity with approved grains such as barley and with powders made from black gram and the like, and having smeared it with flour-pastes and so on, one should bathe it with warm water.
