m.7.2.24.42: One should rub it with bilva leaves and the like to remove the smell of the paste. Then, having bathed it again with waters, in the manner of service befitting an emperor,
m.7.2.24.43: one should offer fragrant āmalaka and turmeric in due order. Then, having cleansed the liṅga, or else the image, with waters,
m.7.2.24.44: one should bathe it with scented water, with water containing kuśa and flowers, and with waters containing gold and gems, consecrated by mantras, in due order.
m.7.2.24.45: But if the materials are unavailable, one should bathe Śiva with faith using whatever could be gathered, or with waters consecrated by mantras alone.
m.7.2.24.46: One should bathe him, preceded by mantras, with a pitcher, or with a conch, or with a vardhanī vessel, or with the hand, together with kuśa and flowers.
m.7.2.24.47: With the Pavamāna hymns, the Rudra hymn, the Nīla Rudra and the Tvarita Rudra, with hymns such as the Liṅga-sūkta, and with the Atharvaśiras,
m.7.2.24.48: with Ṛg verses, with Śaiva Sāman chants, and with the five Brahma-mantras, with the Śiva mantra and with the praṇava, one should bathe the Lord of the god of gods.
m.7.2.24.49: As one performs the bath and other rites for the God, so should one do for the Goddess; there is no difference whatsoever in that, since the two are equal.
m.7.2.24.50: Having first performed the bath and other rites for the God, one should afterwards perform them for the Goddess, by the command of the god of gods.
m.7.2.24.51: When Ardhanārīśvara is the object of worship, there is no order of before and after among the various services, whether in the liṅga or anywhere else.
m.7.2.24.52: Having performed the ablution of the liṅga and wiped it with a clean, fragrant cloth, one should offer a garment and a sacred thread.
m.7.2.24.53: Water for the feet, water for sipping, arghya, sandal paste, flowers, ornaments, incense, lamp, food offering, drinking water, and material for cleansing the mouth,
m.7.2.24.54: and again water for sipping, then after that mouth-perfume, and an auspicious, beautiful crown adorned with all kinds of gems,
m.7.2.24.55: pure ornaments and various garlands, two fans and two chowries, a parasol, a palm-leaf fan and a mirror,
m.7.2.24.56: Having offered these, one should perform the waving of lights (nīrājana), accompanied by the sounds of all auspicious instruments, by song, dance and the like, and with shouts of victory.
m.7.2.24.57: In a vessel of gold, silver or copper, or an auspicious earthen one, adorned with lotus designs, flowers, seeds, curd, unbroken rice and the like,
m.7.2.24.58: and marked with figures made of cow-dung—trident, a pair of conches, lotus, nandyāvarta, śrīvatsa, svastika, mirror, thunderbolt, fire and the like—
m.7.2.24.59: having placed eight lamps all around and one in the middle, one should meditate upon and worship in them the nine Śaktis beginning with Vāmā.
m.7.2.24.60: Having covered it with the Kavaca mantra and protected it on all sides with the Astra mantra, and having shown the cow-gesture (dhenumudrā), one should lift the vessel with both hands.
m.7.2.24.61: Or one may place five lamps on the vessel in order—in the intermediate directions and in the middle—or else just a single lamp.
m.7.2.24.62: Then, lifting that vessel, one should wave it in order above the liṅga and so on, circling three times clockwise, with the root mantra.
m.7.2.24.63: Then one should offer arghya and apply fragrant sacred ash on the head; having made an offering of a handful of flowers, one should afterwards present the food offerings.
m.7.2.24.64: Then one should give drinking water, and having again given water for sipping, one should present betel furnished with the five fragrant substances.
m.7.2.24.65: One should sprinkle what is to be sprinkled and have songs and dramatic performances conducted. Having meditated on Śiva and Śivā in the liṅga and so on, one should repeat the Śiva mantra according to one's capacity.
m.7.2.24.66: With humility one should perform circumambulation, prostration, praise, self-offering, and the submission of one's requests.
m.7.2.24.67: Having offered arghya and a handful of flowers and formed the mudrā according to rule, one should then beg the God's forgiveness and, having dismissed him from the external seat, meditate on him within oneself.
m.7.2.24.68: In great difficulty one may perform the services from pādya up to mouth-perfume, or just arghya and so on, or merely the scattering of flowers, with devotion foremost.
m.7.2.24.69: By that much alone, when done with devotion, supreme dharma is well accomplished. Without having worshipped Śiva, one should not eat as long as breath moves in the body.
m.7.2.24.70: If a sinful person eats willfully without worship, there is no expiation for him. But if one eats through negligence, one should vomit it out with effort,
m.7.2.24.71: bathe, worship the God and the Goddess twofold, fast, and practise ten thousand repetitions of Śiva's mantra, observing celibacy.
m.7.2.24.72: On the next day, having given gold and the like according to his means to Śiva or to a devotee of Śiva, and having performed a great worship, he becomes pure.
m.7.2.24.iti: Thus ends the twenty-fourth adhyāya, named The worship of Śiva taught in the scriptures, in the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.7.2.25.1: Upamanyu said: What was left unsaid here about worship, as if from fear of disrupting the sequence, that other matter I shall now explain, briefly and not at length.
m.7.2.25.2: Before the offering of the food oblation and after the offering of the lamp, one should perform the worship of the enclosures, or else when the waving of lights (nīrājana) has arrived.
m.7.2.25.3: There, in the first enclosure of Śiva or of Śivā, one should worship the mantras from Īśāna down to Sadyojāta, and also those from Rudra down to Astra.
m.7.2.25.4: They are placed in the northeast, in the eastern part, in the south, likewise in the north, and in the west; then in the southeast, in the northeast, likewise in the southwest,
m.7.2.25.5: in the northwest, again in the northeast, and after that in the four directions. This is called the inner enclosure (garbhāvaraṇa), or else the assemblage of mantras.
m.7.2.25.6: Or else one may worship the limbs from Hṛdaya up to Astra. Outside that, one should worship Śakra in the east and Yama in the south,
m.7.2.25.7: the wise one should worship Varuṇa in Varuṇa's quarter (west) and Dhanada in the north, Īśa in the northeast, Fire in his own quarter, and Nirṛti in the southwest;
m.7.2.25.8: Māruta in the northwest, Viṣṇu in the southwest, Vidhi (Brahmā) in the northeast. Outside the lotus one should worship also the weapons, beginning with the thunderbolt and ending with the lotus,
m.7.2.25.9: of well-known forms, belonging to the world-guardians, in their directions, in due order. All the deities of the enclosures, looking towards the god and goddess,
m.7.2.25.10: are to be meditated upon with palms joined in reverence, seated at ease. To all the enclosure deities, with their own names joined with namaḥ,
m.7.2.25.11: one should offer worship with flowers, having bowed to all of them in due order. Or one may worship only the inner enclosure, or with its own enclosure.
m.7.2.25.12: This holds in yoga, meditation, japa and homa, whether external or internal. The food offering to be given is of six kinds: plain rice, rice with mung beans,
m.7.2.25.13: milk-rice, rice mixed with curd, rice with jaggery, and rice steeped in honey. Of these, one or several, accompanied by various side dishes,
m.7.2.25.14: together with jaggery and sugar, one should offer; also excellent churned curd, eatables chiefly cakes, and sweet fruits;
m.7.2.25.15: and very cool drinking water, rich with red sandal and flowers; and soft pieces of areca nut steeped in cardamom juice;
m.7.2.25.16: and betel leaves combined with catechu and the like, pale, golden-coloured, properly prepared and auspicious; and white lime powder made from stone, not too dry and not spoiled;
m.7.2.25.17: and camphor, then cubeb, nutmeg and the like, fresh and fine. The unguent should be sandal, powdered from the root-wood;
m.7.2.25.18: musk, saffron, and a liquid made of musk. The flowers should be fragrant, pure and lovely.
m.7.2.25.19: Flowers that are scentless, strong-smelling, spoiled, stale, or fallen apart of themselves should not be offered in the worship of Śiva.
m.7.2.25.20: Garments should be soft, and ornaments especially made of gold, resembling rings of lightning.
m.7.2.25.21: All these should be fumigated with camphor, resin, aguru and sandal, and perfumed all around with masses of flowers.
m.7.2.25.22: Incense prepared with powders of sandal, aguru, camphor wood and guggulu, along with ghee and honey, is praised.
m.7.2.25.23: Lamps kept constantly burning with very fragrant ghee from a tawny (kapilā) cow, mixed with camphor, are commended.
m.7.2.25.24: The five cow-products, and sweet milk, curd and ghee likewise, from a tawny cow, are dear to Śambhu for bathing and for drinking.
m.7.2.25.25: And fine seats made of ivory, set with gold and gems, and colourful coverings;
m.7.2.25.26: and beds, high and low, lovely and comfortable, furnished with soft pillows and made of fine cotton.
m.7.2.25.27: Water brought from a river flowing to the ocean, or from a great stream, cool and strained through cloth, is especially good for bathing and drinking.
m.7.2.25.28: A parasol, moon-like and lovely, gleaming with strings of pearls, studded with the nine gems, divine, charming with its golden staff;
m.7.2.25.29: and two chowries, white and fine, adorned with gold, shaped like a pair of royal swans, beautified with jewelled handles;
m.7.2.25.30: and a mirror, very smooth, anointed with divine fragrance, covered all around with gems and adorned with fine garlands;
m.7.2.25.31: a conch of deep sound, resembling a swan, jasmine or the moon, inlaid with gems and gold at the mouth, the back and other parts;
m.7.2.25.32: and lovely trumpets (kāhala) producing various sounds, made of gold and adorned with pearls;
m.7.2.25.33: kettledrums, mṛdaṅgas, murajas, timicchas, paṭahas and the like, with a sound like the ocean, should be carefully provided.
m.7.2.25.34: Lovely utensils and vessels of every kind, and all their stands, one should have made of gold alone.
m.7.2.25.35: And the temple of Maheśa, Śiva, the Supreme Self, should be designed like a royal palace, with the features prescribed in the science of architecture (śilpaśāstra):
m.7.2.25.36: enclosed by high ramparts, with gateway towers shaped like mountains, covered with many gems, with golden doors and door-panels,
m.7.2.25.37: made of refined gold, surrounded by hundreds of jewelled pillars, rich with canopies of pearl strings, with arched gateways of coral,
m.7.2.25.38: its top adorned with divine golden crowning finials shaped like pots, and marked with the king of weapons (the trident),
m.7.2.25.39: and surrounded on all sides by residences fit for princes, beautified with royal roads and the like, and by mansions with lofty, towering spires,
m.7.2.25.40: and with excellent assembly halls standing in the directions and intermediate directions, its precincts exceedingly adorned, as though with inner enclosures.
m.7.2.25.41: The place should be attended by thousands of excellent women skilled in dance and song, and by many men accomplished in playing the flute and the vīṇā;
m.7.2.25.42: guarded by heroic guards equipped with elephants, horses and chariots; adorned with many flower gardens and many lakes,
m.7.2.25.43: and resplendent in the cardinal and intermediate directions with many long ponds; served by those who know the essence of the Vedas and Vedānta, devoted to the Śaiva scriptures,
m.7.2.25.44: by devotees delighting in the Śaiva way of life, bearing the marks taught in the Śaiva scriptures, tranquil, smiling-faced, prosperous, and devoted to right conduct,
m.7.2.25.45: served by illustrious twice-born Śaivas and Māheśvaras. Thus, whether inside or outside, in structures built according to one's means —
m.7.2.25.46: in a place made of stone, of ivory, of wood or of brick, or even simply of clay; or in a holy forest or on a mountain,
m.7.2.25.47: at a river, in a temple, in some other region, or in an auspicious house — whether rich or poor, without holding back his own capacity, one should worship the Lord with devotion using only wealth acquired by just means.
m.7.2.25.48: But even if one worships Śiva with devotion using wealth acquired by unjust means, there is no sin for him, since the Lord is subject to the devotee's feeling.
m.7.2.25.49: If one worships without devotion, even with wealth acquired by just means, he does not obtain its fruit; devotion alone is the cause here.
m.7.2.25.50: Whatever is done with devotion, according to one's wealth, with Śiva as its object — whether small or great — the fruit is equal for the rich and the poor.
m.7.2.25.51: A man, even of little wealth, should perform worship impelled by devotion; even one whose essence is great riches should not do it if devoid of devotion.
m.7.2.25.52: Even one who gives his entire possessions to Śiva, if devoid of devotion, does not by that become a partaker of the fruit; devotion alone is the cause here.
m.7.2.25.53: Not by extremely fierce austerities, nor by all the great sacrifices, can one reach the divine city of Śiva, leaving aside devotion directed to Śiva.
m.7.2.25.54: O Kṛṣṇa, more secret than the secret is devotion to Śiva, the Supreme Lord present everywhere; there is no doubt — one endowed with it is liberated.
m.7.2.25.55: Repetition of Śiva's mantra, meditation, fire-offering, sacrifice, austerity, scriptural learning, charity and study — all are for the sake of inner feeling; there is no doubt about this.
m.7.2.25.56: A man lacking devotional feeling is not liberated even after doing everything; but one possessed of feeling is liberated even without doing anything.
m.7.2.25.57: With thousands of Cāndrāyaṇa vows, likewise hundreds of Prājāpatya penances, month-long fasts and others — what more need has a devotee of Śiva of these?
m.7.2.25.58: Men without devotion perform austerities in this world and in mountain caves for the sake of meagre enjoyments; the devotee is liberated through his feeling.
m.7.2.25.59: Sāttvika action grants liberation; yogins are established in sattva. Ritualists enveloped by rajas would perform rājasa action, which grants powers (siddhi).
m.7.2.25.60: Asuras and rākṣasas, endowed with the quality of tamas, worship the Lord for worldly ends, and so do other men of that kind.
m.7.2.25.61: Whether resorting to a tāmasa, a rājasa or a sāttvika disposition, one who performs worship and the like with devotion attains welfare.
m.7.2.25.62: Since devotion has been fashioned like a boat to rescue one from the ocean of sin, what harm can rajas and tamas do to one endowed with devotion?
m.7.2.25.63: Whether an outcaste, a lowly person, a fool or one fallen, if he has taken refuge in Śiva, O Kṛṣṇa, he is worthy of worship by all gods and asuras.
m.7.2.25.64: Therefore, with every effort, one should worship Śiva with devotion alone, since for those without devotion there is no fruit anywhere.
m.7.2.25.65: I shall tell you a great secret; listen to my words, O Kṛṣṇa — a truth well established after deliberation by the Vedas, the śāstras and the knowers of the Veda.
m.7.2.25.iti: Thus ends the twenty-fifth adhyāya, named The worship taught in the Śaiva scriptures, in the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.7.2.26.1: Upamanyu said: Whether one is a slayer of a brāhmaṇa, a drinker of liquor, a thief, or one who has defiled his teacher's bed; or even a slayer of his mother, a slayer of his father, a slayer of a hero, or a slayer of an embryo —
m.7.2.26.2: — having worshipped with devotion Śiva, the supreme cause, even without mantras, he would be released from those various sins gradually, within twelve years.
m.7.2.26.3: Therefore even a fallen man should worship Śiva with every effort, if he is a devotee devoted to no other, living on alms, with senses subdued.
m.7.2.26.4: Even having committed a very great sin, if one worships the Lord of the gods with devotion using the five-syllabled mantra, he is freed from that sin.
m.7.2.26.5: Those who subsist on water, those who subsist on air, and others emaciated by vows — for them there is no reaching Śiva's world through these vows alone.
m.7.2.26.6: Whoever worships Śiva even once with devotion, using the five-syllabled mantra alone, he too goes to Śiva's abode, owing to the greatness of Śiva's mantra.
m.7.2.26.7: Therefore austerities and all sacrifices with one's entire property as fee — these are not equal even to a ten-millionth part of the worship of Śiva's image.
m.7.2.26.8: Whether bound or freed from the fetter, if the devotee worships with the five-syllabled mantra, he is released; there need be no deliberation about this.
m.7.2.26.9: Whether without the Rudra hymn or with the Rudra, one should worship Śiva with the Sūkta; the man who does so even once — though fallen or deluded — is liberated.
m.7.2.26.10: Or one should worship the god with the six-syllabled mantra or with the Sūkta-mantra — a devotee of Śiva who has conquered anger, whether he has not obtained or has obtained initiation.
m.7.2.26.11: Here the one who has obtained is superior to one who has not; of this there is no doubt. Or with that mantra together with the Brahma and Aṅga mantras and with the Haṃsa, one is liberated.
m.7.2.26.12: Therefore one should always worship Śiva with devotion using the Sūkta-mantra — once a day, twice, or three times, or constantly.
m.7.2.26.13: Those who worship Mahādeva are to be known as Maheśvaras themselves. But he by whom the blessed Śiva has not been worshipped with knowledge as his own helper —
m.7.2.26.14: — he wanders long in this saṃsāra, the ocean of sorrow. The fool who, having obtained the rare human birth, does not worship Śiva —
m.7.2.26.15: — fruitless is that birth of his, since it does not lead to liberation. Those who, having obtained the rare human birth, worship the Pināka-bearer —
m.7.2.26.16: — their birth is indeed fruitful; those best of men have attained their goal. And those who are intent on devotion to Bhava, whose minds are bowed to Bhava,
m.7.2.26.17: and engaged in constant remembrance of Bhava — they do not partake of sorrow. Charming mansions, women whose ornament is graceful charm,
m.7.2.26.18: and wealth beyond the point of satiety — these are the fruit of the rite of Śiva's worship. Those who desire great enjoyments and kingship in the abode of the gods,
m.7.2.26.19: they should long at all times for Hara's lotus feet. Good fortune, a lustrous form, strength, a disposition softened by generosity,
m.7.2.26.20: valour, and fame in the world come to one who worships Śiva. Therefore, abandoning everything, with mind fixed on Śiva alone,
m.7.2.26.21: one should perform the rite of Śiva-worship, if he desires his own welfare. Swiftly life departs, swiftly youth departs,
m.7.2.26.22: swiftly disease approaches; therefore the bearer of Pināka is to be worshipped. As long as death does not come, as long as old age does not overtake,
m.7.2.26.23: as long as the senses are not impaired, so long worship Śaṅkara. There is no other dharma in the three worlds equal to the worship of Śiva.
m.7.2.26.24: Knowing this, Sadāśiva should be worshipped with effort. The worship at the door, the curtain rite, the rite of bali to the retinue deities,
m.7.2.26.25: and the daily festival one should perform, if he worships in a temple. After the offering of the oblation-food, either he himself or an attendant
m.7.2.26.26: should give bali in due order to the retinue deities of the temple, going out with musical instruments and standing facing their respective directions.
m.7.2.26.27: He should offer flowers, incense, a lamp, and food along with water. Then, standing facing north, he should offer bali on the great pedestal.
m.7.2.26.28: Then whatever food and other things were offered earlier to the god — all of it, or what remains, he should offer to Caṇḍa.
m.7.2.26.29: Having then offered oblations into the fire duly, he should complete the rest of the worship. Having duly performed the application of the mantra, then the japa as prescribed for the mantra,
m.7.2.26.30: he should perform the daily festival as stated in Śiva's teaching. In a large vessel of metal, adorned with red lotuses,
m.7.2.26.31: having invoked there the divine Pāśupata weapon, he should worship it; and placing that vessel on the head of an adorned twice-born,
m.7.2.26.32: a twice-born whose body has the weapon placed on it by nyāsa and who holds a blazing staff — outside the temple's retinue deities, with auspicious sounds,
m.7.2.26.33: and with dancing, singing and the like, together with lamps, banners and so on, having made three circumambulations, neither hurried nor slow,
m.7.2.26.34: encircling the great pedestal by way of three circumambulations, the sacrificer, having entered again and standing at the door with joined palms, should take the vessel, bring it inside, and then dismiss the weapon.
m.7.2.26.35: Having performed the circumambulation and the rest in order, as stated before, and taking eight flowers, he should then conclude the worship.
m.7.2.26.iti: Thus ends the twenty-sixth adhyāya, named The rite of worship with all its parts and subsidiary parts, in the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.7.2.27.1: Upamanyu said: Now I shall describe the fire-rite, performed in a fire-pit, or on a prepared ground-altar, or on a vedi, or in an iron vessel, or in a new, auspicious earthen one.
m.7.2.27.2: Having installed the fire according to the rule and then having consecrated it, and having worshipped Mahādeva there, one should perform the homa rite.
m.7.2.27.3: One should make the fire-pit two hastas in measure, or only one hasta, either round or square; and likewise the vedi and the maṇḍala.
m.7.2.27.4: The pit should be as deep as it is wide; in its middle there should be an eight-petalled lotus, whose height is four aṅgulas, or just two aṅgulas.
m.7.2.27.5: They describe the navel (nābhi) within the pit with an elevation of twice a vitasti; and the aṅgula is reckoned as the space in the middle of the middle finger, between its middle and upper joints.
m.7.2.27.6: A hand (kara) is said by the wise to consist of twenty-four aṅgulas. Three girdles (mekhalā), or two, or else one —
m.7.2.27.7: one should make, as looks beautiful, smooth, pleasing and firm, with clay. The yoni should be made like an aśvattha leaf, or like an elephant's lip.
m.7.2.27.8: One should make it from the middle of the girdle, on the west or on the south, beautiful, slightly lowered towards the front, gradually opening out,
m.7.2.27.9: with its tip facing the pit, slightly leaving the girdle. For the vedi there is no rule of height; it may be of clay or of sand.
m.7.2.27.10: The maṇḍala is made with cow-dung water; the size of the vessel is not prescribed. One should smear the pit, the earthen vessel and the vedi with cow-dung water.
m.7.2.27.11: Having washed the metal vessel one should heat it; the others one should sprinkle with water. Then one should draw lines on the pit and the rest in the manner stated in one's own sūtra.
m.7.2.27.12: Having sprinkled it, one should prepare the seat for the fire with darbha grass or flowers, and should get ready all the materials for worship and for the oblation.
m.7.2.27.13: Having washed what is to be washed, one should purify it by sprinkling with the prokṣaṇī water. Fire produced from a gem, or produced from wood, or coming from a śrotriya's house,
m.7.2.27.14: or another honoured fire, one should then bring along with its container. Having circled it clockwise three times over the pit and the rest in due order,
m.7.2.27.15: and having uttered the fire-seed syllable, one should place the fire on its seat, either by way of the yoni, or likewise facing oneself.
m.7.2.27.16: The wise one, standing at the yoni area, should do this for the whole pit. The fire residing within his own navel, issuing like a spark from its aperture,
m.7.2.27.17: having come out, one should visualize it as merged into the outer fire, in the form of an orb. Everything up to the consecration of the ghee, beginning with the anvādhāna (adding fuel),
m.7.2.27.18: the knower of mantras should perform in the sequence stated in his own sūtra, with the root mantra. Having worshipped Śiva's form, then on the right side,
m.7.2.27.19: having placed the mantra in the ghee, one should show the mudrā called dhenu. The sruk and sruva to be used should be of bright metal, not of bell-metal, iron or lead,
m.7.2.27.20: or made of sacrificial wood, or as prescribed in smṛti and approved by craftsmanship; or a leaf of the palāśa (brahma-tree) and the like, without holes and raised in the middle.
m.7.2.27.21: Having wiped those two with darbha and heated them in the fire, one should sprinkle them again. Having sprinkled around in the order stated in one's own sūtra, with mantras preceded by Śiva,
m.7.2.27.22: one should offer with eight seed-syllables for the accomplishment of the fire's consecration: bhruṃ, stuṃ, bruṃ, śruṃ in order, and after that puṃ, ḍruṃ, druṃ.
m.7.2.27.23: These are the seven seed-syllables of the seven tongues in due order. The middle tongue, three-crested, is named Bahurūpā.
m.7.2.27.24: Of it, the flame on the south is Jvalantī, another on the left; the north-eastern tongue is Hiraṇyā; Kanakā stands in the east.
m.7.2.27.25: Raktā is in the south-east, Kṛṣṇā in the south-west; another is held to be Suprabhā; the tongue of the wind-quarter (north-west) is Atiriktā — each with a radiance matching its name.
m.7.2.27.26: Each is to be uttered after its own seed-syllable, ending with svāhā, in due order. Having offered ghee with the tongue-mantras into the tongues one by one in order,
m.7.2.27.27: and having offered three oblations in the middle with raṃ vahnaye svāhā, one should perform the sprinkling around, with ghee or with fuel sticks.
m.7.2.27.28: When this is done it becomes Śiva's fire; one should visualize Śiva's seat there. Having invoked the god Śiva, the Ardhanārīśvara, there, one should worship him, offering up to the lamp; then, having sprinkled around, one should perform the oblation of fuel sticks.
m.7.2.27.29: Those sticks should be of palāśa, or of other sacrificial trees, twelve aṅgulas long, not crooked, not dried of themselves, with bark, without blemish, and even.
m.7.2.27.30: Or ten aṅgulas long are prescribed, as thick as the little finger; or, if those are unavailable, a span (prādeśa) long; and all of them should be offered whole.
m.7.2.27.31: One should offer the ghee oblation shaped like a dūrvā leaf, four aṅgulas long; afterwards food in portions the size of an akṣa nut,
m.7.2.27.32: likewise parched grain, mustard seeds, barley and sesame, and, where possible, foods to be eaten, licked and sucked, smeared with ghee.
m.7.2.27.33: Ten oblations are to be offered there, or five, or three, according to one's capacity; or one may offer just a single oblation.
m.7.2.27.34: Ghee is offered with the sruva, fuel sticks and the like with the sruk, the rest with the hand; there one should offer by the divine tīrtha, or likewise by the sages' tīrtha of the hand.
m.7.2.27.35: If the others are unavailable, one may offer with a single substance, with faith. Again, for expiation one should offer three oblations after consecrating them with mantras.
m.7.2.27.36: Then, having filled the sruk with the ghee left over from the homa, and placed a flower at its tip, covering it with the sruva turned face down,
m.7.2.27.37: having covered it together with darbha, rising up with joined hands, one should offer with the root mantra ending in vauṣaṭ a stream of ghee as thin as a barley grain.
m.7.2.27.38: Having thus made the full oblation (pūrṇāhuti), one should sprinkle around as before. Then, having bidden farewell to the Lord of the gods, one should preserve the fire.
m.7.2.27.39: Or, having bidden farewell to that fire too, having united it in the navel, one should worship daily. Or else, having brought the fire by the method stated in the Śaiva scriptures,
m.7.2.27.40: one should duly consecrate and worship the fire born from the womb of Vāgīśī; having again done the anvādhāna and laid the enclosing sticks,
m.7.2.27.41: Having placed the vessels in pairs, and then having worshipped Śiva, having cleansed the sprinkling-vessel (prokṣaṇī) and sprinkled them with its water,
m.7.2.27.42: having set the praṇītā vessel, filled with water, in the north-east, having performed the rites up to the consecration of the ghee, and having cleansed the ladle (sruk) and spoon (sruva),
m.7.2.27.43: and then having performed the garbhādhāna, puṃsavana and sīmantonnayana rites, offering oblations separately for each, he should contemplate the fire as born.
m.7.2.27.44: He should contemplate him as three-footed, seven-handed, four-horned, two-headed, honey-tawny, three-eyed, crowned with matted locks and the moon,
m.7.2.27.45: red, with red garments and unguents, adorned with garlands and ornaments, endowed with all auspicious marks, wearing the sacred thread, with a triple girdle,
m.7.2.27.46: holding a spear (śakti) and the ladle and spoon in the right hands, and likewise with the others a javelin, a palm-leaf fan and a ghee vessel.
m.7.2.27.47: Having thus meditated on the born fire of this form, he should perform the birth-rite (jātakarma). Having done the removal of the navel cord, and then having cleared the birth-impurity,
m.7.2.27.48: having given it the name Śivāgniruci, preceded by an oblation, and having dismissed the parents, he should perform tonsure, initiation (upanayana) and the rest,
m.7.2.27.49: having performed its saṃskāras up to the conclusion of the Āptoryāma, and having done the homa beginning with the stream of ghee, then the sviṣṭakṛt oblation,
m.7.2.27.50: after that he should sprinkle around the fire with the seed-syllable raṃ. Of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva and Īśāna, and likewise of the guardians of the worlds,
m.7.2.27.51: and of their weapons, having performed worship all around in due order, the one who knows the rite, taking out fire for the purpose of incense, lamps and the like,
m.7.2.27.52: and having again prepared the materials beginning with ghee, having arranged a seat in the fire and invoked there as before,
m.7.2.27.53: and having worshipped the God and the Goddess, he should then perform the rite ending with the full oblation (pūrṇāhuti). Or else the fire-rite prescribed for one's own āśrama, as an offering to Śiva,
m.7.2.27.54: understanding it thus, the follower of the Śiva-āśrama should perform; there is no other rule there. Ash is to be collected from the Śiva-fire, or that arising from the agnihotra,
m.7.2.27.55: or even that produced from the wedding-fire, well-burnt, pure and fragrant. Dung of a tawny cow, caught in the air while falling, is recommended,
m.7.2.27.56: neither wet nor too hard, not foul-smelling nor dried out. If it has fallen to the ground, he should take it after discarding the top and bottom.
m.7.2.27.57: Having made it into balls, he should throw it into the Śiva-fire etc. with the root mantra. Rejecting the under-burnt and over-burnt, taking the white ash,
m.7.2.27.58: having taken it, or having stirred it well, he should deposit it in an ash-receptacle — of metal, wood, clay or stone,
m.7.2.27.59: or he should provide some other beautiful, clean ash-receptacle. He should deposit the ash, like wealth, in a level, auspicious, clean place.
m.7.2.27.60: When setting out, he should take the ash himself, or an attendant may. He should not give it into an unfit hand, nor drop it on an impure surface; he should not touch it with the lower limbs, nor neglect it, nor step over it.
m.7.2.27.61: Taking the ash from there, he should apply it with mantras at the prescribed times, not otherwise; nor should he have it given to the unworthy.
m.7.2.27.62: He should collect the ash while the deity has not yet been dismissed, because once the dismissal is done it becomes Caṇḍa's ash.
m.7.2.27.63: After the fire-rite is done, he should perform the bali offering according to the method taught in the Śiva scriptures, or in the manner prescribed in his own sūtra.
m.7.2.27.64: Then, placing the seat of knowledge on a well-smeared maṇḍala and installing the treasury of knowledge (the scripture), he should worship it in order with flowers and so on.
m.7.2.27.65: Making a maṇḍala for the guru too in front of the scripture, and setting an excellent seat there, he should worship the guru with flowers and so on.
m.7.2.27.66: Then he should honour those worthy of honour and feed the hungry; then he himself may eat pure food at ease.
m.7.2.27.67: Or he may eat what was offered to the God, its remainder, for self-purification, with faith and not from greed — but not what was offered to Caṇḍa.
m.7.2.27.68: For perfume, garlands and whatever else was offered, the same rule applies; but the discerning man should not there think, I am Śiva.
m.7.2.27.69: Having eaten and sipped water, meditating on Śiva in the heart, he should utter the root mantra, and spend the rest of the time in suitable pursuits such as discourses on the Śiva scriptures.
m.7.2.27.70: At night, when the first part has passed, having performed a charming worship, he should prepare a single, very beautiful bed for Śiva and Śivā,
m.7.2.27.71: and likewise food to chew and eat, garments, unguents, flowers, garlands and so on — making everything charming, either mentally or in actual deed.
m.7.2.27.72: Then, pure, he should sleep at the feet of the God and the Goddess — a householder together with his wife, and others alone.
m.7.2.27.73: Perceiving the time of dawn, he should utter the primal mantra, bowing mentally to the imperishable God with Ambā and with his gaṇas.
m.7.2.27.74: Having performed, as far as he is able, purification and the rest as befits place and time, he should awaken the God and the Goddess with divine sounds of conches and the like.
m.7.2.27.75: Then, having completed the worship of Śiva and Śivā with very fragrant flowers that have bloomed at that time, he should begin the rite described before.
m.7.2.27.iti: Thus ends the twenty-seventh adhyāya, named The fire rite, in the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.7.2.28.1: Upamanyu said: Hereafter I shall explain, according to the path taught in the Śaiva scriptures, the order of the occasional (naimittika) rites for those who follow the Śaiva way of life (śiva-āśrama).
m.7.2.28.2: In all the months, in both fortnights, on the eighth and the fourteenth lunar days, and likewise on the parvan days, in due order,
m.7.2.28.3: at the solstices and equinoxes, and especially at eclipses, a great worship should be performed, or even a greater one, according to one's ability.
m.7.2.28.4: Every month, having duly prepared the brahmakūrca, and having bathed Śiva with it, one who has fasted should drink the remainder.
m.7.2.28.5: For faults such as the slaying of a brahmin, however exceedingly great, no other expiation surpasses the drinking of the brahmakūrca.
m.7.2.28.6: In Pauṣa, under the asterism Puṣya, one should perform the waving of lights (nīrājana) for the Lord; in Māgha, under the asterism called Maghā, one should offer a ghee-blanket.
m.7.2.28.7: In Phālguna, at the end of Uttarā Phalgunī, one should begin the great festival; in Caitra, on the full moon of Citrā, one should perform the swing festival according to rule.
m.7.2.28.8: On the Vaiśākha full moon under Viśākhā one should make a great flower-pavilion; in Jyeṣṭha, under the asterism called Mūla, one should cause a cool water-pot to be offered.
m.7.2.28.9: In Āṣāḍha, under Uttarāṣāḍhā, likewise the placing of the pavitra threads; in Śrāvaṇa one should prepare other maṇḍalas made of natural materials.
m.7.2.28.10: Under the asterism called Śraviṣṭhā, and thereafter on the full moon of Prauṣṭhapada, one should perform the water-play with sprinkling, on the day connected with Pūrvāṣāḍhā.
m.7.2.28.11: Then on the Āśvayuja full moon one should offer milk-rice and newly cooked rice, and with that very food perform the fire-rite on the day of Śatabhiṣaj.
m.7.2.28.12: On the Kārttika full moon, in conjunction with Kṛttikā, one should offer a thousand lamps; likewise in Mārgaśīrṣa, under Ārdrā, one should bathe Śiva with ghee.
m.7.2.28.13: One who is unable to do these at those times may perform simply a festival, or an assembly (āsthāna), or a great worship, or an enhanced worship.
m.7.2.28.14: And when an auspicious event occurs, and in praiseworthy undertakings; in dejection, in misconduct, after a bad dream, or on seeing an evil sight,
m.7.2.28.15: in a portent or any other inauspicious thing, or in a severe illness, rites such as bathing, worship, japa, meditation, fire-offering and gifts
m.7.2.28.16: should be performed suited to the occasion, preceded by puraścaraṇa. And if the Śiva-fire is extinguished, one should kindle it again.
m.7.2.28.17: He who, firmly established in the dharma of Śarva, lives thus, ever diligent—to him Maheśvara grants liberation in a single birth.
m.7.2.28.18: Whoever performs this in ever-increasing measure in the daily and occasional rites goes to the divine, primal abode of Śrīkaṇṭhanātha.
m.7.2.28.19: There, having enjoyed great pleasures for a hundred crore kalpas, the man, falling from there in the course of time, reaches the world of Umā and that of Kumāra,
m.7.2.28.20: having attained the Vaiṣṇava and Brāhma worlds, and especially Rudraloka, and having dwelt there for a long time enjoying the pleasures described,
m.7.2.28.21: and again going upward from there, passing beyond the five abodes, he obtains knowledge from Śrīkaṇṭha and from there goes to the city of Śiva.
m.7.2.28.22: One devoted to half the practice likewise proceeds in the same way, but with two returns; afterwards, obtaining knowledge, he attains union (sāyujya) with Śiva.
m.7.2.28.23: But the embodied one who has practised a quarter (half of half), after the end of the body, passing beyond the two worlds—up to the end of the cosmic egg or upward to the Unmanifest—
m.7.2.28.24: having reached the Pauruṣa and Raudra abodes of the Lord of the mountain-king's daughter, and having enjoyed pleasures in many ways for many thousands of yugas,
m.7.2.28.25: when his merit is exhausted, reaches the earth and is born in a great family. There too, by the force of former impressions, he of great splendour
m.7.2.28.26: abandons the dharmas of the bound soul (paśu) and becomes devoted to Śiva's dharma; by the very weight of that dharma, meditating, he goes to the city of Śiva.
m.7.2.28.27: Having enjoyed various pleasures, he goes to the station of the Vidyeśvaras; there, having enjoyed many pleasures along with the Vidyeśvaras in succession,
m.7.2.28.28: he returns once more, whether within or outside the cosmic egg. Then, obtaining knowledge of Śiva and attaining supreme devotion,
m.7.2.28.29: and attaining likeness in nature to Śiva, he does not return again. And he who is intensely devoted to Śiva, as one whose mind is attached to sense-objects is attached to them,
m.7.2.28.30: he is liberated, whether he performs the Śiva-dharmas or not. The one who returns once, twice, or thrice is a returner;
m.7.2.28.31: one who has the qualification for Śiva-dharma would not again become merely a universal emperor. Therefore, taking refuge in Śiva for whatever reason,
m.7.2.28.32: one should set one's mind on Śiva-dharma, if one has made effort for the highest good. In this matter we shall not compel anyone by any means.
m.7.2.28.33: Through compulsion and excessive argument this does not, by their nature, appeal to some; but it does appeal to others through the weight of meritorious impressions—
m.7.2.28.34: to those in whom the cause of worldly existence is not able to sprout. Therefore, having fully considered this in accordance with one's nature,
m.7.2.28.35: one should take up Śiva-dharma, if one desires one's own welfare (śiva).
m.7.2.28.iti: Thus ends the twenty-eighth adhyāya, named The rules for daily and occasional rites, in the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.7.2.29.1: Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: O Lord, from your own mouth I have heard, equal to the Veda, the daily and occasional rites taught by Śiva for those who have taken refuge in him.
m.7.2.29.2: Now I wish to hear: if there is also a desire-motivated (kāmya) rite for those qualified for Śiva's dharma, please describe it now.
m.7.2.29.3: Upamanyu said: There is rite whose fruit is in this world, some whose fruit is in the next, and some for both this world and the next; and that again is fivefold.
m.7.2.29.4: Some rite consists of ritual action; some rite consists of austerity;
m.7.2.29.5: some consists of japa and meditation, and some of all these. The one consisting of ritual action is further divided according to the sequence of fire-offering, gift, and worship.
m.7.2.29.6: It becomes fruitful only for those endowed with full power, not for others; and that power is the command of Maheśa, Śiva, the supreme Self.
m.7.2.29.7: Therefore a twice-born who bears Śiva's command should perform the desire-motivated rites. Now I shall describe the kāmya rite that bestows fruit here and hereafter.
m.7.2.29.8: It is to be performed by Śaivas and Māheśvaras, internally and externally respectively. Śiva and Maheśvara are not absolutely different here.
m.7.2.29.9: Just so, Śaivas and Māheśvaras too are not different. Those men who depend on Śiva and delight in the sacrifice of knowledge are Śaivas;
m.7.2.29.10: those devoted to the sacrifice of action on earth are called Māheśvaras. Therefore Śaivas should perform the rite internally, Māheśvaras externally.
m.7.2.29.11: But the procedure of the rite about to be described does not differ. Having duly examined the ground by its smell, colour, taste and so on,
m.7.2.29.12: there, on a surface of the ground pleasing to the mind, with a canopy spread above, well smeared with cow-dung, resembling the inside of a mirror,
m.7.2.29.13: one should first determine the east by the method seen in the scriptures, and lay out a maṇḍala of one or two cubits.
m.7.2.29.14: One should draw a spotless eight-petalled lotus with its pericarp, with powders of gems, gold and the like, gathered as available,
m.7.2.29.15: furnished with five enclosures and full of great beauty. On the petals the siddhis are to be imagined; on the filaments, together with their śaktis,
m.7.2.29.16: the eight Rudras beginning with Vāma, in order from the eastern petal onward; in the pericarp, dispassion; in the seeds, the nine śaktis;
m.7.2.29.17: in the bulb, dharma of Śiva's nature; in the stalk, knowledge resting on Śiva; and above the pericarp, the circles of fire, sun and moon;
m.7.2.29.18: beyond that, the triad of principles called Śiva-, Vidyā- and Ātma-tattva; and above all the seats, a comfortable seat adorned with various flowers.
m.7.2.29.19: One should worship Śiva with the five enclosures, together with Ambā — him who resembles pure crystal, serene, of cool radiance,
m.7.2.29.20: adorned with a crown of matted locks like a ring of lightning, clad in tiger skin, his lotus-face slightly smiling,
m.7.2.29.21: whose soles, palms and lower lip are like red lotus petals, endowed with all auspicious marks, adorned with all ornaments,
m.7.2.29.22: bearing excellent divine weapons, anointed with divine fragrances, five-faced, ten-armed, with a crescent moon as crest-jewel.
m.7.2.29.23: His eastern face is gentle, with radiance like the rising sun, rich with three lotus-eyes, crested with the young moon.
m.7.2.29.24: The southern face has a lovely radiance like a dark rain-cloud, is crooked with frowning brows, fearsome, with three round red eyes,
m.7.2.29.25: dreadful with fangs, unassailable, with quivering bud-like lower lip. The northern face resembles coral, adorned with dark curls,
m.7.2.29.26: graceful, three-eyed, with the moon as ornament on its crest. The western face shines like the full moon, brilliant with three eyes,
m.7.2.29.27: bearing the crescent, gentle, charming with a soft smile. The fifth face resembles crystal, radiant with the lunar crescent,
m.7.2.29.28: exceedingly gentle, shining with three wide-open eyes. He is resplendent on the right with trident, axe, thunderbolt, sword and fire,
m.7.2.29.29: and on the left resplendent with serpent, iron arrow, bell, noose and goad. His form is enclosed up to the knees by Nivṛtti, up to the navel by Pratiṣṭhā,
m.7.2.29.30: likewise up to the throat by Vidyā, up to the forehead by Śāntā, and above that by the supreme kalā called Śāntyatītā,
m.7.2.29.31: pervading the five paths, his body directly made of the five kalās; the god whose crown is Īśāna, the ancient one whose face is called Puruṣa,
m.7.2.29.32: whose heart is Aghora, likewise whose secret part is Vāma, Maheśvara, whose feet are Sadya; his form consisting of thirty-eight kalās,
m.7.2.29.33: the Lord consisting of the Mātṛkā letters, likewise consisting of the five Brahmas, consisting of what is called Oṃkāra, and endowed with the Haṃsa-śakti,
m.7.2.29.34: likewise whose lap is occupied by the śakti whose nature is Will, with the śakti called Knowledge on the right and the one called Action on the left,
m.7.2.29.35: Sadāśiva, consisting of the three tattvas, the very embodiment of Vidyā — having conceived this form with the root mantra and having performed sakalīkaraṇa in due order,
m.7.2.29.36: and having worshipped duly up to the arghya with the root mantra, then invoking Śiva himself in embodied form together with the supreme Śakti,
m.7.2.29.37: having invoked there Mahādeva, who is free from manifestation as being or non-being, and having performed the five preparatory acts, one should worship the supreme Lord
m.7.2.29.38: with the Brahma mantras and the six limbs, then with the Mātṛkā, with the praṇava, and with the Śiva mantra joined with Śakti, in order,
m.7.2.29.39: or with the Śānta mantra, and likewise with other Vedic mantras in full; or one may worship the supreme God with the Śiva mantra alone.
m.7.2.29.40: Having made the offerings from foot-water up to mouth-freshener, without the dismissal, one should then begin the worship of the five enclosures in due order.
m.7.2.29.iti: Thus ends the twenty-ninth adhyāya, named Rites for desired ends, in the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.7.2.30.1: There, at the very beginning, one should first worship with fragrance and the rest the two gods Heramba and Ṣaṇmukha, beside Śiva and Śivā, on the right and on the left respectively.
m.7.2.30.2: Then, all around, in the first enclosure, one should worship the Brahmans, the five brahma-mantras, together with their Śaktis, in due order from Īśāna up to Sadyojāta.
m.7.2.30.3: There too one should worship, in sequence, the six limbs — the heart and the rest — of Śiva and of Śivā, beginning from the quarter of Agni.
m.7.2.30.4: There, afterwards, one may or may not worship the eight Rudras, Vāma and the rest, with the Śaktis Vāmā and the rest, all around in order beginning from the east.
m.7.2.30.5: I have told you the first enclosure, O delight of the Yadus; the second enclosure is now told out of affection — listen with faith.
m.7.2.30.6: One should worship Ananta on the eastern petal, with his Śakti to his left, and Sūkṣma on the southern petal together with his Śakti.
m.7.2.30.7: Then, on the western petal, one should worship Śivottama together with his Śakti; likewise, on the northern petal, one should worship Ekanetra.
m.7.2.30.8: Next one should worship Ekarudra and his Śakti on the north-eastern petal, and should worship Trimūrti and his Śakti on the petal of Agni's (south-east) quarter.
m.7.2.30.9: One should worship Śrīkaṇṭha on the south-western petal with his Śakti to his left; likewise one should worship Śikhaṇḍīśa on the north-western petal of the Wind.
m.7.2.30.10: In the second enclosure the sovereigns (cakravartins) are to be worshipped all around; in the third enclosure the eight Forms (aṣṭamūrtis) are to be worshipped along with their Śaktis.
m.7.2.30.11: In the eight directions in turn, all around in order beginning from the east: Bhava, Śarva, likewise Īśāna, Rudra, then Paśupati,
m.7.2.30.12: Ugra, Bhīma and Mahādeva — these are the eight Forms in order. Immediately after that, there the eleven Forms beginning with Mahādeva are to be worshipped in order together with their Śaktis.
m.7.2.30.13: Mahādeva, Śiva, Rudra, Śaṅkara, Nīlalohita, Īśāna, Vijaya, Bhīma, Devadeva, Bhavodbhava,
m.7.2.30.14: and Kapardīśa — these are named the eleven, and likewise the eleven Śaktis. Of them, eight are to be worshipped first, in due order beginning from Agni's quarter.
m.7.2.30.15: Devadeva on the eastern petal and Īśāna in Agni's region; Bhavodbhava between the two, and Kapālīśa beyond that.
m.7.2.30.16: In that enclosure, further, one should worship the lord of bulls in front, Nandin to his right, and likewise Mahākāla to his left (north).
m.7.2.30.17: Śāstṛ on the petal of Agni's quarter, the Mothers on the southern petal, the elephant-faced one on the south-western petal, and Ṣaṇmukha again on the western petal of Varuṇa;
m.7.2.30.18: Jyeṣṭhā on the Wind's petal, Gaurī in the north, Caṇḍa in the north-east of the Lord; between Śāstṛ and Nandīśa one should worship the chief of sages, Vṛṣabha.
m.7.2.30.19: To the north of Mahākāla one should worship Piṅgala; then, between Śāstṛ and the group of Mothers, Bhṛṅgīśvara.
m.7.2.30.20: Between the Mothers and Vighneśa one should worship Vīrabhadra; between Skanda and Vighneśa one should worship the goddess Sarasvatī.
m.7.2.30.21: Between Jyeṣṭhā and Kumāra, Śrī who worships Śiva's feet; between Jyeṣṭhā and Gaṇāmbā one should worship Mahāmoṭī.
m.7.2.30.22: Between Gaṇāmbā and Caṇḍa one should worship the goddess Durgā. In this same enclosure, further, the host of Śiva's attendants —
m.7.2.30.23: manifold, called Rudras, Pramathas and Bhūtas, together with their Śaktis — and the band of Śivā's female companions, one should worship with a composed mind, having meditated on them.
m.7.2.30.24: When the extensive third enclosure has thus been worshipped, one should meditate on the fourth enclosure outside it and worship it.
m.7.2.30.25: The Sun is to be worshipped on the eastern petal, the four-faced Brahmā in the south, Rudra on the petal of Varuṇa's quarter, and Viṣṇu on the petal of the northern quarter.
m.7.2.30.26: Now, each of these four gods has separate enclosures. For him the Sun, first come his six limbs alone, along with the Śaktis Dīptā and the rest:
m.7.2.30.27: Dīptā, Sūkṣmā, Jayā, Bhadrā, Vibhūti, Vimalā, Amoghā and Vidyutā, in order, stationed all around beginning from the east.
m.7.2.30.28: In the second enclosure the four Forms are to be worshipped in order, from the east up to the north, and after them the Śaktis.
m.7.2.30.29: Āditya, Bhāskara, Bhānu and Ravi, in sequence; or Arka, Brahmā, Rudra and Viṣṇu — these are the forms of Vivasvat.
m.7.2.30.30: Vistārā is in the eastern part, Sutārā stationed in the south, Bodhanī in the western part, and Āpyāyinī in the north.
m.7.2.30.31: Then, placing Uṣā, Prabhā, likewise Prājñā and also Sandhyā in the north-east and the other intermediate quarters, one should worship them in the second enclosure.
m.7.2.30.32: Soma, Aṅgāraka, Budha the best of the wise, Bṛhaspati of vast intellect, Bhārgava the treasure of splendour,
m.7.2.30.33: Śanaiścara, likewise Rāhu, and Ketu, smoky and fearsome — these one should worship all around in the third enclosure, in order.
m.7.2.30.34: Alternatively, one should worship the twelve Ādityas in the second enclosure, and in the third enclosure worship the twelve zodiac signs.
m.7.2.30.35: And outside that, all around, the seven groups of seven: sages, gods, Gandharvas, serpents, hosts of Apsarases,
m.7.2.30.36: Grāmaṇīs, likewise Yakṣas, Yātudhānas, and the horses made of the seven metres, and the Vālakhilyas — one should worship these.
m.7.2.30.37: Having thus worshipped the Sun in the third enclosure, one should next worship Brahmā together with three enclosures.
m.7.2.30.38: One should worship Hiraṇyagarbha in the east, then Virāj in the south, Kāla in the western part, and Puruṣa in the north.
m.7.2.30.39: Hiraṇyagarbha, the first Brahmā, resembles a lotus; Kāla looks like pure collyrium; Puruṣa is like crystal.
m.7.2.30.40: Triguṇa, Rājasa, Tāmasa and likewise Sāttvika — these four, in order, are stationed in the first enclosure.
m.7.2.30.41: In the second enclosure, Sanatkumāra, Sanaka, Sanandana and Sanātana are to be worshipped in order, all around, beginning from the east.
m.7.2.30.42: Then in the third enclosure one should worship the Prajāpatis: eight first, in the east and the other directions, and three in the east and west, in due sequence.
m.7.2.30.43: Dakṣa, Ruci, Bhṛgu, Marīci and Aṅgiras, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, Atri and Kaśyapa,
m.7.2.30.44: and Vasiṣṭha — these are renowned as the lords of creatures. Their wives too are to be worshipped together with them, in due order:
m.7.2.30.45: Prasūti and Ākūti, Khyāti and Sambhūti, Dhṛti, Smṛti, Kṣamā, Sannati and Anasūyā,
m.7.2.30.46: the Mother of the gods Aditi and Arundhatī — all of them devoted wives, ever intent on the worship of Śiva, splendid and lovely to behold.
m.7.2.30.47: Or else, in the first enclosure one should worship the four Vedas, and in the second enclosure, in turn, the Itihāsas and Purāṇas.
m.7.2.30.48: Then in the third enclosure all the Vedic branches of knowledge, headed by the Dharmaśāstras, are to be worshipped all around.
m.7.2.30.49: The Vedas are placed in front, beginning from the east, and the others as one likes, performing the worship all around in eight or in four divisions.
m.7.2.30.50: Having thus worshipped Brahmā, together with his three enclosures, in the south, one should then worship Rudra with his enclosures in the west.
m.7.2.30.51: His first enclosure is declared to be the six limbs of Brahman, and the second enclosure likewise consists of the Vidyeśvaras.
m.7.2.30.52: In the third enclosure there is a difference; that is now told. His four forms are to be worshipped in order, beginning from the east.
m.7.2.30.53: In front, in the east, is the god in the Sakala form, possessed of the three guṇas, called Śiva; in the south is worshipped the rājasic Brahmā, the creator, as Bhava.
m.7.2.30.54: In the west is to be worshipped the tāmasic Agni, Hara the destroyer; in the north the sāttvic Viṣṇu, bestower of happiness, lord of the universe, Mṛḍa.
m.7.2.30.55: Having thus worshipped in the western quarter Śiva, the twenty-sixth principle of Śambhu, one should then worship Vaikuṇṭha on the northern side.
m.7.2.30.56: Placing Vāsudeva in front, one should worship in the first enclosure; Aniruddha on the south, then Pradyumna in the west,
m.7.2.30.57: and afterwards Saṅkarṣaṇa in the north; or one may worship these two interchanged. The first enclosure has been told; now the auspicious second enclosure:
m.7.2.30.58: Matsya, Kūrma, Varāha, Narasiṃha, then Vāmana, Rāma and another Rāma, Kṛṣṇa, and also the venerable horse-faced one.
m.7.2.30.59: In the third enclosure one should worship the discus in the eastern part; in the south one should worship the missile named Nārāyaṇa, called in some places the Unobstructed.
m.7.2.30.60: In the west the Pāñcajanya conch, and then in the north the Śārṅga bow. Thus, with three enclosures, Hari himself, the supreme, called Viśva,
m.7.2.30.61: Mahāviṣṇu, Sadāviṣṇu, one should worship, having given him embodied form. Having thus worshipped the four forms of Viṣṇu in the order of the four vyūhas, one should worship their four Śaktis in order:
m.7.2.30.62: One should worship Prabhā in the south-eastern quarter, Sarasvatī in the south-west, Gaṇāmbikā in the north-west, and Lakṣmī in the north-east.
m.7.2.30.63: Thus, having performed the worship of the forms beginning with the Sun and, after that, of their Śaktis, one should worship the guardians of the worlds in that same enclosure:
m.7.2.30.64: Indra, Agni, Yama, Nirṛti and Varuṇa, Vāyu, Soma and Kubera, and then one should worship Īśāna.
m.7.2.30.65: Having thus worshipped the fourth enclosure according to rule, one should then worship the weapons of Maheśa in the outer enclosure:
m.7.2.30.66: The glorious trident in the north-east, the thunderbolt in Mahendra's quarter east, the axe in the quarter of Fire south-east; in the south one should worship the arrow.
m.7.2.30.67: In the south-west one should worship the sword, the noose in Varuṇa's region west, the goad in the Wind's quarter north-west, and the Pināka bow in the north.
m.7.2.30.68: One should worship Rudra's Kṣetrapāla facing west. Having worshipped the fifth enclosure, thereafter, outside —
m.7.2.30.69: outside the enclosures of all the enclosure-deities, or else in the fifth: in the fifth, together with the Mothers, one should worship the great Bull in front.
m.7.2.30.70: Then all the semi-divine beings are to be worshipped all around: sky-goers, sages, Siddhas, Daityas, Yakṣas and Rākṣasas,
m.7.2.30.71: the serpent-lords beginning with Ananta, together with the Nāgas born of their respective clans, the Ḍākinīs, and the chiefs of Bhūtas, Vetālas, Pretas and Bhairavas,
m.7.2.30.72: and others dwelling in the netherworld, born of various species; rivers, oceans, mountains, forests and lakes,
m.7.2.30.73: domestic animals, birds, trees, insects and other lowly creatures, humans of various forms, and wild beasts of lowly birth,
m.7.2.30.74: the worlds within the cosmic egg, then the millions of cosmic eggs, and the countless worlds outside the egg together with their rulers,
m.7.2.30.75: the Rudras who uphold the cosmic eggs, stationed in the ten directions; whatever belongs to the guṇas, whatever pertains to Māyā, or whatever is of Śakti, and what lies beyond that —
m.7.2.30.76: whatever exists that can be denoted by a word, whether sentient or insentient — understanding all that to be at the side of Śiva and Śivā, one should worship it collectively.
m.7.2.30.77: all of them with joined palms, inconceivable, with smiling faces, and ever gazing lovingly at the god and the goddess.
m.7.2.30.78: Having thus performed the worship of the enclosures, for the pacification of distraction one should again worship the lord of the gods and utter the five-syllable mantra.
m.7.2.30.79: Then, after that, one should offer to Śiva and Śivā a great caru, like nectar, accompanied by fine side dishes, pure and lovely.
m.7.2.30.80: The best is of thirty-two āḍhakas, and the lowest at least one āḍhaka; having prepared it according to one's means, one should offer it with faith.
m.7.2.30.81: Then, having offered drinking water and betel together with relishes, and having performed the waving of lamps (nīrājana) and the like, he should complete the rest of the worship.
m.7.2.30.82: He should procure only excellent articles suitable for the deity's enjoyment; a devotee should not be stingy with wealth when he has the means.
m.7.2.30.83: For one who is deceitful, or negligent, or who performs the rite defectively, desire-motivated rites do not bear fruit at all — such is the saying of the virtuous.
m.7.2.30.84: Therefore, completely abandoning negligence, he should perform desire-motivated rites with all their components, if he wishes for the attainment of the fruit.
m.7.2.30.85: Having thus completed the worship, and then having bowed to the God and the Goddess, and having concentrated the mind with devotion, he should afterwards recite the hymn.
m.7.2.30.86: Then, having worshipped with the hymn, at the end he should eagerly repeat the five-syllabled vidyā, at least one hundred and eight times, or over a thousand times.
m.7.2.30.87: Having performed worship of the vidyā and worship of the guru, afterwards, in due order, he should honour the members of the assembly too, according to his prosperity and his faith.
m.7.2.30.88: Then, having ritually dismissed the Lord of the gods together with all the enclosure deities, he should give the maṇḍala to the guru along with the implements of the sacrifice.
m.7.2.30.89: Or he should give everything, in due order, to those who have taken refuge in Śiva; or else he should offer it to Śiva alone in a shrine of Śiva.
m.7.2.30.90: Or he may worship the God in the Śiva-fire with the seven oblation substances, having duly worshipped all the deities of the enclosures.
m.7.2.30.91: This rite, named Yogeśvara, is renowned in the three worlds; there is no sacrifice anywhere in the world superior to it.
m.7.2.30.92: There is nothing in this world that cannot be accomplished by this, whether some fruit of this life or a fruit of the next world.
m.7.2.30.93: No restriction is laid down such as: this is its fruit, this is not; it is the supreme means to all that has the nature of the good.
m.7.2.30.94: It cannot be specified: whatever a person worships for, that fruit is obtained by him from this rite, as from the wish-fulfilling gem.
m.7.2.30.95: Even so, one should not employ this for the sake of a trivial fruit, because one who seeks a small thing from the Great becomes himself smaller.
m.7.2.30.96: Whether the fruit be great or small, a rite succeeds if it is done; so let the rite be performed directed toward Mahādeva.
m.7.2.30.97: Therefore the discerning one should perform this for fruits, visible and invisible, not obtainable by other means, such as victory over enemies and over death.
m.7.2.30.98: And in the case of great sins, fears of grave diseases and the like, famines and the like, one should perform the pacificatory rite by means of this, for the sake of appeasement.
m.7.2.30.99: What is the use of much talk? Maheśvara has declared this to be the Śaivas' own weapon, the averter of great calamities.
m.7.2.30.100: Therefore there is no greater protection for oneself here than this; thinking thus, one who employs this rite attains what is auspicious.
m.7.2.30.101: He who, having become pure and well-composed, recites merely the hymn, he too obtains one-eighth of the fruit of his most desired object.
m.7.2.30.102: One who, contemplating its meaning, recites it while fasting on a parvan day, or on the eighth or fourteenth lunar day, would obtain half the fruit.
m.7.2.30.103: But he who, contemplating the meaning and likewise observing a vow on parvan days and the like, recites the hymn for one month, obtains the complete fruit.
m.7.2.30.iti: Thus ends the thirtieth adhyāya, named The Śaivas' rites for desired ends, in the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa.
m.7.2.31.1: Upamanyu said: I shall tell you, O Kṛṣṇa, a hymn that follows the order of the five enclosures (pañcāvaraṇa). It is this holy hymn called Yogeśvara, by which the rite is brought to completion.
m.7.2.31.2: Victory, victory to you, O Śambhu, sole lord of the world, charming by nature, whose very nature is eternal consciousness, whose reality lies beyond the reach of speech and mind, even of those that have left behind the impure expanse of the world!
m.7.2.31.3: Victory to you, whose expanse is pure by nature, whose actions are beautiful! Victory to you, whose great power is equal to your own self, O ocean of pure qualities!
m.7.2.31.4: Victory to you, endowed with infinite radiance, whose form has no equal! Victory to you, support of an inconceivable greatness, whose auspiciousness is undisturbed!
m.7.2.31.5: O stainless one, O one without support, victory to you whose arising has no cause! O one of unbroken supreme bliss, victory to you, cause of liberation!
m.7.2.31.6: Victory to you of utterly supreme sovereignty! Victory to you, abode of boundless compassion! Victory to you, whose all is self-dependent! Victory to you of matchless glory!
m.7.2.31.7: Victory to you who envelop the great universe! Victory to you who are enveloped by nothing! Victory to you, higher than all! Victory to you, beyond whom there is absolutely nothing higher!
m.7.2.31.8: Victory, O wondrous one! Victory, O one not petty! Victory, O unimpaired one! Victory, O imperishable one! Victory, O immeasurable one! Victory, O one free of illusion! Victory, O one beyond mere being! Victory, O spotless one!
m.7.2.31.9: O mighty-armed one, O one of great essence, O one of great qualities, O one of great renown, O one of great strength, O great wielder of māyā, O one of great delight, O great warrior.
m.7.2.31.10: Salutation to the supreme god, salutation to the supreme cause. Salutation to Śiva, the tranquil one; salutation to you, the most auspicious.
m.7.2.31.11: For this entire world, together with gods and asuras, is dependent on you.
m.7.2.31.12: Therefore, who is able to transgress the command laid down by you?
m.7.2.31.13: Moreover, this person has you always as his sole refuge; therefore, having shown him grace, may you grant him what he prays for.
m.7.2.31.14: Victory to you, O Ambikā, O mother of the world! Victory to you who consist of all the worlds! Victory to you of limitless sovereignty! Victory to you of incomparable form!
m.7.2.31.15: Victory to you who are beyond speech and mind! Victory to you, destroyer of the darkness of unconsciousness! Victory to you, free from birth and old age! Victory to you, higher even than what is beyond time!
m.7.2.31.16: Victory to you who abide in manifold forms! Victory to you, beloved of the lord of the universe! Victory to you, to be worshipped by all the gods! Victory to you who unfold as the universe!
m.7.2.31.17: Victory to you of auspicious, divine limbs! Victory to you, lamp of auspiciousness! Victory to you of auspicious conduct! Victory to you, giver of auspiciousness!
m.7.2.31.18: Salutation to you, whose form is an assemblage of supremely auspicious qualities. From you indeed the world has arisen, and into you alone it dissolves.
m.7.2.31.19: Therefore, without you, even the Lord could not bestow the fruit. From birth onwards, O queen of the gods, this person has taken refuge in you.
m.7.2.31.20: Therefore fulfil the desire of this devotee of yours. Five-faced, ten-armed, resembling pure crystal—
m.7.2.31.21: the god whose body is made of the letters, the Brahma-mantras and the kalās, both with parts and without parts, mounted on the Śiva-form, transcending the Śānti kalā—may that Sadāśiva, worshipped by me with devotion, grant me the welfare I pray for.
m.7.2.31.22: May Śakti, the power of Will, called Śivā, seated on the lap of Sadāśiva, mother of all the worlds, grant my desire.
m.7.2.31.23: The two beloved sons of Śiva and Śivā, the gods Heramba and Ṣaṇmukha, possessed of Śiva's majesty, omniscient, feeding on the nectar of Śiva-knowledge,
m.7.2.31.24: contented, affectionate toward each other, ever honoured by Śiva and Śivā, and ever honoured too by the gods headed by Brahmā,
m.7.2.31.25: ever arisen to bring about the protection of all the worlds, taking incarnations at will in many ways through divisions of their own portions—
m.7.2.31.26: these two, thus worshipped by me constantly beside Śiva and Śivā—placing their parents' command foremost, may they grant me what I pray for.
m.7.2.31.27: He who is like pure crystal, named Īśāna, Sadāśiva, the form identified with the head of Śiva the supreme Self,
m.7.2.31.28: devoted to the worship of Śiva, tranquil, transcending Śānti, abiding in ether, the last seed-syllable of the five-syllable mantra, endowed with five kalās,
m.7.2.31.29: worshipped first in the first enclosure together with its Śakti—may that pure, supreme Brahman grant me what I pray for.
m.7.2.31.30: He who is like the rising sun, named Puruṣa, the ancient one, identified with the eastern face of Śiva the supreme,
m.7.2.31.31: of the nature of Śānti, abiding in wind, devoted to worship of Śambhu's feet, the first among Śiva's seed-syllables, and having four kalās among the kalās,
m.7.2.31.32: worshipped by me with devotion in the eastern part together with its Śakti—may that pure, supreme Brahman grant me what I pray for.
m.7.2.31.33: He who is like collyrium-mountain and the like, Aghora of fearsome form, the southern face of the god, worshipper of the feet of the god of gods,
m.7.2.31.34: mounted on the Vidyā level, situated in the middle of the fire-circle, the second among Śiva's seed-syllables, endowed with eight kalās among the kalās,
m.7.2.31.35: worshipped together with its Śakti in the southern region of Śambhu—may that pure, supreme Brahman grant me what I pray for.
m.7.2.31.36: He who is like saffron powder, named Vāma, wearing excellent attire, the northern face of the Lord, established in the Pratiṣṭhā level,
m.7.2.31.37: situated in the middle of the water-circle, devoted to the worship of Mahādeva, the fourth among Śiva's seed-syllables, endowed with thirteen kalās,
m.7.2.31.38: worshipped together with its Śakti in the northern region of the god—may that pure, supreme Brahman grant me what I pray for.
m.7.2.31.39: He who is white as conch, kunda-jasmine and the moon, named Sadya, of gentle features, the western face of Śiva, devoted to the worship of Śiva's feet,
m.7.2.31.40: established in the Nivṛtti level and situated in earth, the third among Śiva's seed-syllables, and endowed with eight kalās,
m.7.2.31.41: May the purifying supreme Brahman, worshipped together with Śakti on the western side of the deity, grant me what I pray for.
m.7.2.31.42: The two heart-forms of Śiva and of Śivā, filled with Śiva — placing the command of those two foremost, may they both grant me my desire.
m.7.2.31.43: The two auspicious forms of Śiva and of Śivā, resting in Śiva — honouring the command of the divine pair, may they both grant me my desire.
m.7.2.31.44: The two armours of Śiva and of Śivā, filled with Śiva — honouring the command of the divine pair, may they both grant me my desire.
m.7.2.31.45: The two eye-forms of Śiva and of Śivā, resting in Śiva — honouring the command of the divine pair, may they both grant me my desire.
m.7.2.31.46: And the two weapon-forms of the divine pair, ever intent on worship — honouring the command of the divine pair, may they both grant me my desire.
m.7.2.31.47: Vāma, Jyeṣṭha, and Rudra, Kāla and Vikaraṇa, Balavikaraṇa, and next Balapramathana,
m.7.2.31.48: and Sarvabhūtadamana, together with their eight Śaktis of like nature — may they grant me what I pray for, solely by the command of the divine pair.
m.7.2.31.49: Then Ananta and Sūkṣma, Śiva and also Ekanetra, Ekarudra and Trimūrti, Śrīkaṇṭha and Śikhaṇḍin,
m.7.2.31.50: and likewise their eight Śaktis, worshipped in the second enclosure — may they grant me my desire, solely by the command of the divine pair.
m.7.2.31.51: The eight forms beginning with Bhava and their Śaktis too, and likewise the other eleven forms beginning with Mahādeva —
m.7.2.31.52: all of them, together with their Śaktis, stationed in the third enclosure — honouring the command of the divine pair, may they bestow the desired fruit.
m.7.2.31.53: The king of bulls, of great splendour, with a voice like a great cloud, resembling the peaks of Meru, Mandara, Kailāsa and the Himālaya,
m.7.2.31.54: shaped like the crest of a white cloud, adorned with a hump, and resplendent with a tail resembling a great serpent-king,
m.7.2.31.55: with red mouth, horns and hooves, eyes mostly red, all limbs stout and tall, radiant with a most graceful gait,
m.7.2.31.56: bearing auspicious marks, glorious, with blazing jewelled ornaments, dear to Śiva, devoted to Śiva, the banner and the mount of the divine pair,
m.7.2.31.57: and whose other body is purified by the placing of their feet — the personified form of the king of bulls, glorious, bearing the splendid excellent trident as weapon — placing their command foremost, may he grant me my desire.
m.7.2.31.58: Nandīśvara, of great splendour, son of the daughter of the mountain-king, ever worshipped and saluted by the gods together with Nārāyaṇa,
m.7.2.31.59: stationed with his attendants at the door of Śarva's inner palace, equal in renown to the Lord of all, crusher of all asuras,
m.7.2.31.60: consecrated as overseer of all the Śiva-dharmas, dear to Śiva, devoted to Śiva, bearing the splendid excellent trident as weapon,
m.7.2.31.61: attached to those who take refuge in Śiva and loved by them in turn — honouring the command of the divine pair, may he grant me my desire.
m.7.2.31.62: Mahākāla, the mighty-armed, like a second Mahādeva — may he ever protect those who rely on Mahādeva.
m.7.2.31.63: Dear to Śiva, devoted to Śiva, ever the worshipper of the divine pair — honouring the command of the divine pair, may he bestow on me what I long for.
m.7.2.31.64: Śāstā, knower of the true meaning of all scriptures, the supreme body of Viṣṇu, son of Viṣṇu in the form of Mahāmoha, fond of honey, meat and liquor — placing their command foremost, may he grant me my desire.
m.7.2.31.65: Brahmāṇī and Māheśī, Kaumārī and Vaiṣṇavī, Vārāhī and Māhendrī, and Cāmuṇḍā of fierce valour —
m.7.2.31.66: these are the seven Mothers, mothers of the whole world; may they grant me what I pray for, by the command of the Supreme Lord.
m.7.2.31.67: He whose face is that of a rutting elephant, son of Gaṅgā, Umā and Śaṅkara, whose body is the sky, whose arms are the directions, whose eyes are the moon, sun and fire,
m.7.2.31.68: ever worshipped by the divine elephants of the quarters, Airāvata and the rest, bursting with the rut of Śiva-knowledge, the remover of obstacles for the gods,
m.7.2.31.69: and the creator of obstacles for the asuras and others — Vighneśa, devoted to Śiva — honouring the command of the divine pair, may he bestow on me what I long for.
m.7.2.31.70: The six-faced one, born of Śiva, the lord bearing the spear and the thunderbolt, the god who is son of Agni and again son of Aparṇā,
m.7.2.31.71: and son of Gaṅgā, of Gaṇāmbā, and likewise of the Kṛttikās, surrounded by Viśākha, Śākha and Naigameya,
m.7.2.31.72: conqueror of Indra, the moon-like commander, and likewise conqueror of the asura Tāraka, piercer by his own might of the mountains headed by Meru,
m.7.2.31.73: shining like molten gold, with eyes like lotus petals, Kumāra, the great model of beauty among the delicate,
m.7.2.31.74: dear to Śiva, devoted to Śiva, ever worshipping Śiva's feet — honouring the command of the divine pair, may he bestow on me what I long for.
m.7.2.31.75: Jyeṣṭhā, most excellent, the giver of boons, delighting in the worship of the divine pair — placing their command foremost, may she bestow on me what I long for.
m.7.2.31.76: Gaṇāmbikā, revered by the three worlds, manifest in the shape of a meteor, requested from Śiva by Brahmā for the creation and growth of the world,
m.7.2.31.77: the forms that issued from between the brows of Śivā when she divided herself: Dākṣāyaṇī Satī, Menā, and likewise Haimavatī Umā,
m.7.2.31.78: the mother of Kauśikī and likewise of Bhadrakālī, the mother of Aparṇā and likewise of Pāṭalā,
m.7.2.31.79: ever devoted to the worship of Śiva, Rudrāṇī, beloved of Rudra — honouring the command of the divine pair, may she bestow on me what I long for.
m.7.2.31.80: Caṇḍa, lord of all the Gaṇas, born from the mouth of Śambhu — honouring the command of the divine pair, may he bestow on me what I long for.
m.7.2.31.81: May Piṅgala, the glorious leader of the gaṇas, devoted to Śiva and dear to Śiva, grant me my desire, by the command of Śiva and Śivā alone.
m.7.2.31.82: May the leader of the gaṇas named Bhṛṅgīśa, intent on the worship of Śiva, grant me my desire, with the Lord's command going before.
m.7.2.31.83: Vīrabhadra, of great splendour, resembling snow, jasmine and the moon, ever dear to Bhadrakālī and protector of the Mothers,
m.7.2.31.84: remover of the head of the sacrifice and of the evil-minded Dakṣa, the hewer of the limbs of the gods beginning with Upendra, Indra and Yama,
m.7.2.31.85: the glorious attendant of Śiva, guardian of Śiva's command — may he bestow on me what I long for, by the command of Śiva and Śivā alone.
m.7.2.31.86: Sarasvatī, born from the lotus of Maheśa's speech, devoted to the worship of Śiva and Śivā — may she bestow on me what I long for.
m.7.2.31.87: Lakṣmī, abiding on Viṣṇu's chest, delighting in the worship of Śiva and Śivā — may she bestow on me what I long for, by the command of Śiva and Śivā alone.
m.7.2.31.88: Mahāmoṭī, wholly devoted to the worship of the Great Goddess's feet — may she, by that Goddess's own direction, bestow on me what I long for.
m.7.2.31.89: Kauśikī, mounted on a lion, the supreme daughter of Pārvatī, the sleep of Viṣṇu, the Great Illusion, slayer of the great buffalo demon,
m.7.2.31.90: destroyer of Niśumbha and Śumbha, fond of wine, meat and liquor — honouring her mother's command, may she bestow on me what I long for.
m.7.2.31.91: The Rudras, equal in renown to Rudra, the Pramathas of celebrated might, and those called Bhūtas, of great valour, equal in radiance to Mahādeva,
m.7.2.31.92: eternally liberated, incomparable, free from the pairs of opposites, free from calamity, accompanied by their Śaktis and attendants, saluted by all the worlds,
m.7.2.31.93: capable of creating and destroying all the worlds, devoted to one another and loyal to one another,
m.7.2.31.94: exceedingly affectionate toward one another, bowing to one another, ever most dear to Śiva, marked with the marks of Śiva,
m.7.2.31.95: gentle, terrible, and likewise mixed, having natures of the two intermediate kinds; ill-formed and well-formed, and bearing various forms likewise —
m.7.2.31.96: honouring the command of Śiva and Śivā, may they indeed grant me my desire. The group of the Goddess's dear companions, marked with the marks of the Goddess,
m.7.2.31.97: together with the daughters of Rudra and with Śaktis in many ways, ever worshipped with devotion in the third enclosure of Śambhu —
m.7.2.31.98: honouring the command of Śiva and Śivā, may it bestow auspiciousness on me. Divākara, the Sun, a form of Maheśa, with a beautiful orb of radiance,
m.7.2.31.99: without qualities, mixed with qualities, and likewise pure quality alone; of changeless nature, primal, one, with common modifications,
m.7.2.31.100: and of uncommon actions in the sequence of creation, maintenance and dissolution; thus divided threefold, fourfold and again fivefold,
m.7.2.31.101: worshipped together with his followers in the fourth enclosure of Śambhu, dear to Śiva, attached to Śiva, delighting in the worship of Śiva's feet —
m.7.2.31.102: honouring the command of Śiva and Śivā, may he bestow auspiciousness on me. The six limbs of Divākara, and the eight Śaktis beginning with Dīptā,
m.7.2.31.103: Āditya, Bhāskara, Bhānu and Ravi in order, Arka, Brahmā, likewise Rudra and Viṣṇu — these are the forms of Āditya;
m.7.2.31.104: Vistarā, Sutarā, Bodhinī, Āpyāyinī, and further the others — Uṣā, Prabhā, likewise Prājñā and Sandhyā — these too are the Śaktis;
m.7.2.31.105: and the planets from Soma to Ketu, imbued with Śiva, impelled by the command of Śiva and Śivā — may they bestow auspiciousness on me.
m.7.2.31.106: Or else the twelve Ādityas and likewise the twelve Śaktis, the sages, the divine Gandharvas, the hosts of serpents and Apsarases,
m.7.2.31.107: the Grāmaṇīs, likewise the Yakṣas, the Rākṣasas and the gods — these seven groups of seven — and the horses made of the seven metres,
m.7.2.31.108: and the Vālakhilyas and others — all worshippers of Śiva's feet — honouring the command of Śiva and Śivā, may they bestow auspiciousness on me.
